articles.title: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings.
articles.abstract: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

articles.title: Adjuvant capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab as adjuvant therapy in patients with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring 1 cm or smaller (ORCHID study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant treatment decisions for patients with small (T ≤ 1 cm), node-negative, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast tumors remain challenging, particularly regarding whether oral chemotherapy is comparable to intravenous regimens. We therefore conducted a phase II trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of an oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab regimen in this population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients received either single-agent capecitabine (1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 every 3 weeks) or vinorelbine capsules (60 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 3 weeks) plus trastuzumab, followed by trastuzumab monotherapy for a total of 12 months of therapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS). The secondary end points were distant disease-free survival (DDFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04296162).
RESULTS: The analysis population included 182 patients, of whom 81% had tumors measuring ≤ 0.5 cm and 74% had hormone receptor (HR)-negative disease. Of the 181 treated patients, 176 (97.2%) received capecitabine and 5 (2.8%) vinorelbine, with agent selection at the physician's discretion. After a median follow-up of 5.7 years (range, 1.0-6.2 years), the 5-year DFS rate was 97.3% (90% Confidence interval [CI], 94.4-98.7). The lower bound of the 90% CI exceeded the prespecified threshold of 92%, meeting the primary endpoint. Among the 6 observed invasive disease events, 2 involved distant metastasis, 3 involved local or regional recurrence, and 1 involved contralateral breast cancer. Among the secondary endpoints, the 5-year DDFS rate was 97.2%, with a 5-year OS rate of 100% (no deaths) during follow-up. Among the 176 patients treated with capecitabine, the most common capecitabine-related adverse event (AE) was hand-foot syndrome, which occurred in 66.5% of patients, with 8.0% of patients experiencing a grade 3 event.
CONCLUSIONS: Among women with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring ≤ 1 cm, capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab was associated with a low risk of cancer recurrence and favorable toxicity in this single-arm cohort, supporting further prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68.
RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

articles.title: A flexible wearable system for integrated sweat stimulation and chloride analysis in cystic fibrosis diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) diagnosis relies on quantitative sweat chloride testing, a process that requires highly trained personnel, bulky instrumentation, and a cumbersome workflow performed at specialized clinical centers with high per-test cost. Recent advances in wearable sweat biomarker sensors offer opportunities for the development of point-of-care CF sweat chloride analysis. This work presents a flexible, wearable platform for sweat chloride testing, based on miniaturized, automated iontophoresis stimulation, microfluidic sweat collection, and colorimetric chloride analysis. This system enables quantitative, visually interpretable chloride measurements without external instrumentation, requires only microliters of sweat to operate, and reduces the per-test cost to around 1 dollar. Clinical evaluation of the device with 55 subjects at a single pediatric CF center demonstrates strong agreement between chloride concentrations from standard-of-care sweat testing and this platform, with reliable operation across physiologically relevant chloride concentrations. This platform provides a practical, scalable alternative for CF diagnosis in a range of clinical settings with potential for use in the home.

articles.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress.
articles.abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to-central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

articles.title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict.
articles.abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination-as a proxy for health service delivery-and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement's association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

articles.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

articles.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans.
articles.abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c' and 32'. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c' and 32' significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

articles.title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa.
METHODS: This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing.
FINDINGS: The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia).
INTERPRETATION: SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden.
FUNDING: UK Medical Research Council and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.

articles.title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
articles.abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development. After birth, rapid microbial colonization occurs in the intestine and lungs. Through signaling molecules including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs), coupled with vagal nerve and mucosal immune pathways, the microbiota maintains intestinal and pulmonary immune homeostasis, preserves blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and modulates microglial activation, thereby regulating neurogenesis, synaptic pruning, and brain functional programming. Early-life dysbiosis is commonly associated with preterm birth, cesarean delivery, infection, and antibiotic exposure. In human observational studies, it accompanies disrupted organ homeostasis and neuroinflammatory signatures, and is linked to an increased long-term risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability; in neonatal animal models, it aggravates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and encephalopathy of prematurity. Because dysbiosis frequently co-occurs with prematurity, infection, and other confounders, these associations do not by themselves establish causality. This review summarizes early-life colonization patterns of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota and their underlying neuroimmune mechanisms, analyzes the impacts of dysbiosis on neuroimmunity and related diseases, and proposes intervention strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for neonatal health protection and neurodevelopmental disorder prevention.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for pediatric Clostridioides difficile infection: efficacy, challenges, and the path to next-generation microbiome therapies.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is an increasing cause of morbidity in children, with recurrent disease posing substantial therapeutic challenges. Antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of initial management; however, up to 30% of children experience recurrence, and those with underlying comorbidities face recurrence rates as high as 65%. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has demonstrated superior efficacy over antibiotics for recurrent CDI (rCDI) in adults and has emerged as the most effective available intervention for pediatric rCDI. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on FMT efficacy, microbiome changes, and safety in children with CDI. Data from large multicenter cohort studies demonstrate cure rates exceeding 80%, with comparable efficacy observed in high-risk subpopulations, including those with inflammatory bowel disease and immunocompromising conditions. Critical research gaps remain, including the absence of randomized controlled trials and limited long-term safety data in children. Despite demonstrated effectiveness, significant barriers limit FMT accessibility for children. The COVID-19 pandemic has substantially impacted availability, and current regulatory changes have further restricted access. The lack of FDA-approved live biotherapeutic products approved for CDI in children creates additional challenges. We critically examine the emerging pipeline of next-generation microbiome-based therapies and identify the steps required to ensure children with recurrent CDI have access to safe, effective, and approved treatments.

articles.title: Maternal BMI modulates cord plasma NT-proBNP in gestational diabetes linking cardiac stress to insulin-cortisol crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is an increasingly prevalent pregnancy disorder associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including an increased risk of early-onset cardiovascular disease in infants. GDM is associated with cardiac structural and functional changes as early as in utero. However, pathways linking maternal metabolic status to fetal cardiac stress remain poorly defined. We investigated N-teminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in umbilical cord plasma (UCP) as a candidate biomarker of fetal cardiac stress, together with additional cardiac, endocrine and endothelial biomarkers to identify novel links between fetal cardiac health and maternal and fetal metabolic, inflammatory and hormonal characteristics. UCP from 82 term pregnancies (57 controls, 25 GDM) was analyzed for NT-proBNP and complementary cardiac, endocrine, and endothelial markers. Associations with maternal metabolic parameters, neonatal outcomes, and other UCP parameters were assessed using correlation, regression, and mediation analyses, adjusted for gestational age and neonatal sex. NT-proBNP levels were elevated in the cord plasma of GDM pregnancies, specifically in the presence of increased maternal pre-pregnancy BMI. Across the cohort, NT-proBNP was further associated with maternal BMI at delivery, fasting glucose levels, placental weight, and neonatal C-peptide, while inversely associated with cord plasma cortisol. Mediation analyses identified a significant indirect association involving neonatal C-peptide and suggested a potential mediating role of NT-proBNP in the association between maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and cord plasma cortisol. These findings suggest that NT-proBNP may reflect fetal cardiac load in GDM and is associated with maternal metabolic status and fetal insulin secretion. The inverse association between NT-proBNP and cortisol raises the possibility of an interplay between natriuretic peptide signaling and glucocorticoid regulation, pointing towards a potential cardiac-endocrine adaptation to intrauterine metabolic stress. While these observations deserve further investigation, they provide new insights into cardiovascular programming.

articles.title: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase.
articles.abstract: Glutaric aciduria type I (GA-1) is a severe metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency of glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GCDH), leading to accumulation of organic acids in the brain and resulting in striatal injury and progressive movement disorders. Although early diagnosis and dietary management reduce risk, one-third of patients still develop debilitating neurological complications. We previously demonstrated that liver-specific deletion of aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase (AASS), an upstream enzyme in lysine degradation, is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here, we tested an N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated siRNA against Aass. Treatment of neonatal Gcdh-/- mice rescued lethality and improved the brain pathology while reducing toxic metabolites in the brain and other organs. Serum biomarkers, including glutaric acid, 3-hydroxyglutaric acid, and glutarylcarnitine, predicted neurological outcomes, supporting their use for therapeutic monitoring. Although systemic metabolite concentrations declined, their urinary excretion remained elevated, consistent with a renal washout phenomenon and preserved excretory capacity. These findings demonstrate the potential of liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy as a treatment for GA-1.

articles.title: RIPK1 inhibition limits expansion of pathogenic double-negative T cells in preclinical autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome models.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) is an immune disorder characterized by defective lymphocyte apoptosis, leading to lymphoproliferation, autoimmunity, and increased lymphoma risk. Although disease severity correlates with the expansion of double-negative T (DNT) cells, the mechanisms governing their aberrant generation and pathogenicity remain elusive. Through single-cell transcriptomics of peripheral blood from pediatric patients with ALPS, including patients harboring new FAS cell surface death receptor (FAS) mutations (FAS mutations), we identified a pathogenic effector DNT subset (GRANZYMEhiCXCR5hi) exhibiting cytotoxic and tissue-infiltrating features, a population conserved in ALPS mouse models. Using an apoptosis-defective murine model that develops early-onset ALPS with robust DNT cell expansion, we found that ALPS-associated caspase-8 functional impairment facilitates receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) activation to drive disease pathogenesis, a process exacerbated by receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) scaffold function. Peripheral CD8+ T cells from both patients with ALPS and mouse models exhibited increased susceptibility to activation-induced conversion into pathogenic DNT cells, which was effectively blocked by RIPK1 inhibition. Mechanistically, RIPK1 activation drove peripheral CD8+ T cells to adopt a pathogenic DNT fate via cAMP-responsive element modulator (CREM)-mediated CD8 silencing. Furthermore, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity reduced DNT cell generation and burden in target organs, reversed cytopenias, and alleviated autoimmune pathology in ALPS mouse models. Our findings establish RIPK1 as a critical driver of ALPS pathogenesis and identify RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Elucidating a potential role of the infant gut microbiome on L-tyrosine bioavailability in phenylketonuria using whole-body metabolic modelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inherited metabolic disorder caused by phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) deficiency, leading to elevated L-phenylalanine and severe neurological damage if untreated. While phenylalanine-based biomarkers are diagnostic and phenylalanine levels correlate with disease severity, the clinical manifestations of PKU are heterogeneous.
RESULTS: To identify additional reliable, potentially novel biomarkers, we used germ-free sex-specific, organ-resolved infant whole-body metabolic models (infant-WBMs) to simulate PAH deficiency and predicted elevated L-phenylalanine and its derivatives, alongside reduced L-tyrosine fluxes, as the product of phenylalanine hydroxylation. To test the reliability of these predicted biomarkers to variations in microbiome composition, we combined the infant-WBMs with gut microbiome models from 48 female and 42 male healthy infants. Upon integrating microbiome data, we found that microbial metabolism significantly increased the predicted L-tyrosine availability, obscuring its utility as a universal biomarker. In ~ 23% of microbiome-PKU models, L-tyrosine fluxes remained low, indicating insufficient microbial compensation. These cases were enriched in Firmicutes and lacked specific Bifidobacterium and Escherichia strains linked to L-tyrosine biosynthesis via the pretyrosine pathway. Shadow price analysis identified microbial species critical for host L-tyrosine metabolism. However, some, such as Bifidobacterium dentium, also contributed to L-phenylalanine synthesis, potentially worsening the PKU phenotype. In contrast, L-phenylalanine, phenylpyruvate, and hydroxyphenylacetic acid remained reliably elevated across all models, validating their diagnostic relevance.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates that microbiome composition can modulate biomarker reliability in PKU, particularly for L-tyrosine. Integrating microbial metabolic models with whole-body physiology enables assessment of biomarker reliability and reveals subpopulations for whom secondary biomarkers or targeted probiotics may be beneficial. This approach offers a powerful framework for refining diagnostics and therapy monitoring in rare metabolic diseases and the development of possible targeted microbiome therapies. Video Abstract.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors.
articles.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

articles.title: Respiratory Virus Activity - United States, July 2025-June 2026.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viral illnesses are common and can lead to severe outcomes, including hospitalization and death. U.S. trends in respiratory virus activity during July 2025-June 2026 were analyzed using data from six complementary public health surveillance systems. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity occurred unusually late in most U.S. regions. SARS-CoV-2 circulated nationally with typical bimodal peaks that occurred in August 2025 and January 2026. Annual RSV-associated hospitalization rates (number of hospitalizations per 100,000 persons) were highest among infants aged <12 months (790.2; 95% CI = 757.9-825.3), followed by children aged 12-23 months (611.9; 95% CI = 586.3-639.8) and adults aged ≥75 years (352.1; 95% CI = 309.9-407.7). Annual RSV rates overall and by age group did not exceed those observed during 2022-2025. COVID-19-associated hospitalization rates were highest among adults aged ≥75 years (361.2), infants aged <6 months (173.3), and adults aged 65-74 years (111.4). Newly established 2025-2026 national pediatric mortality surveillance provisionally identified 34 RSV-associated pediatric deaths from 35 reporting jurisdictions and 31 COVID-19-associated pediatric deaths from 43 reporting jurisdictions. RSV sequencing did not identify variant substitutions associated with reduced susceptibility to the available RSV monoclonal antibodies for infants. Most SARS-CoV-2 lineages were JN.1 descendants, but detections of BA.3.2, a highly divergent SARS-CoV-2 variant, increased. Circulation of other respiratory viruses followed usual historical patterns. Staying current with recommended RSV and COVID-19 vaccinations reduces the risk for severe illness and disease caused by these viruses.

articles.title: Stroke Death Rates Among Adults Aged ≥18 Years - United States, 2000-2024.
articles.abstract: In 2024, stroke was the fourth leading cause of death in the United States. A 2017 report found that beginning during 2013-2015, earlier declines in stroke death rates stalled or reversed among some populations of U.S. adults aged ≥35 years. This report examines 25-year trends in stroke death rates among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years across age, sex, and geographic areas, using 2000-2024 National Vital Statistics System mortality data. During 2000-2024, the age-adjusted stroke death rate among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years declined from 81.4 per 100,000 population to 51.9 (average annual percentage change = -2.0%), with declining trends across all age groups, sexes, U.S. Census Bureau regions, and U.S. jurisdictions except Delaware. Overall rates declined during 2000-2009 (annual percentage change [APC] = -5.2%), remained stable during 2009-2018, increased during 2018-2021 (APC = 4.0%), and declined again during 2021-2024 (APC = -2.4%). However, during the most recent trend periods, rates increased among adults aged 35-44 years, those aged ≥85 years, women, residents of the Midwest and South U.S. Census Bureau regions, and in 12 U.S. jurisdictions. Despite long-term declines in stroke death rates, the recent increase in trends in some demographic groups and geographic areas underscore the importance of continued surveillance to identify adults at increased risk for stroke and implement focused prevention and management efforts.

articles.title: Retinopathy of prematurity: causes, treatment and prevention.
articles.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is initiated at preterm birth. Vascular growth in the immature retina, conditioned to low intrauterine oxygen levels, is disrupted by rapid increases in oxygen which suppress oxygen-regulated growth factors. Maternally sourced essential lipids (ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids) and insulin-like growth factor-1 are also lost. Later, maturing (but avascular) retina becomes hypoxic and nutrient starved, driving a growth factor surge often causing destructive neovascularization. Current treatments address late-stage neovascular ROP by suppressing elevated vascular endothelial growth factor levels. Recent clinical studies address the initiating events, lack of specific maternally sourced lipids and growth factors, hyperoxia-induced metabolic changes, which induce suppression of normal retinal vascularization and retinal neural maturation. Early enteral supplementation with ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids reduces risk of neovascularization. Timed topical corticosteroids during early ROP which alter metabolism to promote normal vessel growth, show great promise in preventing severe disease. Risk algorithms with near 100% sensitivity and high specificity can reduce the number of screening examinations. AI-augmented photography and ultrawide field optical coherence tomography may further refine prediction, diagnosis and treatment. This review synthesizes recent clinical paradigm shifts toward early disease prevention, highlighting how novel metabolic, pharmacological, and digital health strategies can prevent ROP-related vision loss.

articles.title: Oveporexton: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Oveporexton (ORZEYFULTM) is an oral selective orexin receptor 2 agonist developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals Inc. for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Oveporexton received its first approval in China on 22 July 2026 for the treatment of adolescents aged ≥ 16 years and adults with NT1. Subsequently, oveporexton was approved on 5 August 2026 in the USA and on 24 August 2026 in Japan for adults with NT1. Targeting the underlying orexin deficiency in NT1, oveporexton is the first and only agent approved for the treatment of NT1 addressing the full range of symptoms which define the condition. Additional global filings and phase III clinical trials are ongoing. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of oveporexton leading to this first approval for NT1.

articles.title: Anxiety and depressive disorders among children and young people following a cancer diagnosis in England: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychiatric conditions are important survivorship outcomes among children and young people (CYP) diagnosed with cancer. However, many population-based studies have examined hospital contacts only, and estimates of absolute risk can be biased when competing mortality is not accounted for. We estimated absolute risks and relative hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based matched retrospective cohort study across 1474 general practices in England using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum primary care records linked to Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care and mortality records. CYP diagnosed with malignant cancer or any central nervous system tumour at ages 0-24 years between Jan 1, 2000, and Dec 31, 2022, were matched by age, recorded sex, and general practice to up to 20 comparators without cancer at the index date. Primary outcomes were first recorded anxiety and related disorders and depressive disorders; secondary outcomes were first-time psychotropic prescribing. Individuals with pre-index records of the respective outcome were excluded from that outcome analysis. Follow-up ended at outcome occurrence, death, practice deregistration, last data collection, or Dec 31, 2022. We estimated cumulative incidence using the Aalen-Johansen estimator and ethnicity-adjusted cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs) using matched-set stratified Cox models.
FINDINGS: There were 9145 CYP with cancer and 178709 comparators. Adjusted cause-specific HRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.61-1.88) for anxiety and related disorders, 1.16 (1.06-1.26) for depressive disorders, 1.27 (1.20-1.35) for antidepressant prescribing, 2.21 (2.05-2.38) for antipsychotic prescribing, and 2.69 (2.53-2.86) for anxiolytic prescribing. At 15 years, cumulative incidence was 14.1% (95% CI 13.0-15.3) versus 12.8% (12.5-13.1) for anxiety and related disorders, and 12.8% (11.6-14.0) versus 14.1% (13.8-14.5) for depressive disorders. Excess hazards were greatest in the early years after diagnosis.
INTERPRETATION: CYP diagnosed with cancer had higher hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing. These findings support proactive mental health monitoring and timely referral pathways within cancer and survivorship care, particularly early after diagnosis. Further research should evaluate whether timely assessment and tailored psychosocial support improve outcomes.
FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research Manchester Biomedical Research Centre and Greater Manchester Patient Safety Research Collaboration.

articles.title: Fatal and non-fatal health loss across 54 African Union member states, 1990-2023: a secondary analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to assess how the balance between fatal and non-fatal health loss changed between 1990 and 2023 across the 54 African Union member states, and whether countries converged.
METHODS: We analysed official Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 estimates of deaths, years of life lost (YLLs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), as counts and age-standardised rates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). The primary outcome was the YLD share of DALYs. We decomposed change into demographic and epidemiological components, attributed it to cause groups, and tested convergence between countries.
FINDINGS: Between 1990 and 2023, deaths rose by 2.09 million (24.9%), from 8.39 million (95% UI 8.33-8.46) to 10.48 million (10.39-10.58), while the population more than doubled, and the age-standardised DALY rate fell by 38.2%, from 83,519 to 51,656 per 100,000. YLDs accounted for 66.1 million (10.7%, 8.3-13.5) of 617.2 million DALYs in 1990 and 151.2 million (22.0%, 17.4-26.9) of 688.0 million in 2023, and the share rose in every country. Falling YLL rates from communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional diseases accounted for 10.20 (91%) of the 11.26 percentage point rise. Countries with lower initial shares gained faster proportionally (beta -1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.55 to -0.94) but not absolutely, and in 2023 the YLD share ranged from 2.453 million (11.5%) of 21.309 million DALYs in Niger to 1.543 million (42.4%) of 3.639 million in Tunisia. The share was higher among females than males in every country.
INTERPRETATION: Health loss in the African Union has shifted from premature death towards living with illness, mainly because fatal burden from communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional causes fell. Countries are converging in relative terms, but large differences remain. These modelled estimates should be interpreted with caution.
FUNDING: None.

articles.title: A phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial of the safety and efficacy of the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is characterized by strong immune dysregulation and hyperactive interferon/JAK/STAT signaling. We report a phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial testing the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in persons with DS and immune skin conditions. Participants received treatment for up to 9 months with extensive safety monitoring and assessments of biomarkers, skin pathology, and neuropsychological measures. The primary safety endpoint was met, with tofacitinib showing a safety profile similar to that observed in the general population. Tofacitinib decreases interferon scores, cytokine scores, and neurotoxic immunometabolites without overt immune suppression. Participants experienced benefits for immunodermatological conditions, most prominently hidradenitis suppurativa and alopecia areata, and improvements in multiple neuropsychological assessments. Multi-omics analyses reveal specific inflammatory pathways modulated by tofacitinib in DS. Given the lack of a placebo control arm, efficacy findings remain exploratory. These results support JAK inhibition as a safe strategy to attenuate immune dysregulation in DS. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04246372).

articles.title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
articles.abstract: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

articles.title: NOTCH3 deficiency contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE), a major cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity, is characterized by impaired trophoblast invasion and defective spiral artery remodeling. Although these pathological features are well-established, their underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. In this study, we identified a significant downregulation of NOTCH3 in PE placentas. Our findings demonstrated that NOTCH3 deficiency led to increased apoptosis of trophoblast cells and impaired their proliferation, migration, and invasion, which is associated with altered gene expression related to mitochondrial function, loss of mitochondrial mass, and disruption of mitochondrial biogenesis. Our mechanistic studies uncovered transcription factor A, mitochondrial (TFAM) and fructose-bisphosphatase 2 (FBP2) as target genes of NOTCH3 that are responsible for mitochondrial regulation. We demonstrated that NOTCH3 positively regulates TFAM and negatively regulates FBP2 through upregulating the expression of HEY1, a known NOTCH target gene. Therefore, NOTCH3 deficiency decreases TFAM expression and increases FBP2 expression, impairing mitochondrial biogenesis in trophoblast cells, which was rescued by TFAM overexpression in our in vitro model. This molecular mechanism was validated in an L-NAME-induced PE rat model, human PE placentas, and primary trophoblasts. Collectively, our findings define the role of NOTCH3 deficiency in the pathogenesis of PE. Through characterization of NOTCH3-HEY1-FBP2/TFAM axis, we provided new mechanistic insight into NOTCH3-regulated mitochondrial biogenesis and its relevance to human diseases like placenta disorders.

articles.title: Pediatric Tumor Immune Organoids Preserve Cellular Compartments and are Suitable for Preclinical Modeling of Emerging Immunotherapies.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic progress against pediatric solid tumors and brain tumors has stalled. Immunotherapies have shown promise, but additional optimizations are needed to overcome the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Cost-effective, reliable models that recapitulate the TME of solid tumors could accelerate development of novel immunotherapies. We developed and optimized Pediatric Tumor Immune Organoids (PTIOs), which grow intact fragments of tumors harvested from immunocompetent murine neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma (MB) and osteosarcoma tumor models in an air-liquid interface (ALI). PTIOs preserve tumor, immune and stromal cells for extended periods of time and recapitulate responses to immune-targeting agents and CAR T cells seen in vivo more accurately than traditional 2D in vitro models. Using a human patient-derived MB PTIO, we observed potent antitumor activity of GD2-CAR T cells. Our data suggest that PTIOs could provide an alternative and potentially more economical and informative platform than animal studies for preclinical modeling of immunotherapies for pediatric solid tumors.

articles.title: Colonic In Situ Microbiota Shows Greater Predictive Potential than Fecal Microbiota for Washed Microbiota Transplantation Response in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is increasingly linked to gut microbial dysbiosis, yet fecal microbiota may not adequately reflect host-microbe interactions at the intestinal mucosa. This study compares colonic in situ and fecal microbiota in children with ASD, evaluates their associations with clinical severity, and examines their responses to washed microbiota transplantation (WMT). Colonic in situ microbiota show marked structural and compositional divergence from fecal microbiota, with limited overlap between compartments. Despite lower microbial diversity, colonic microbiota exhibit broader and stronger associations with ASD severity, including Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) and Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) scores. In germ-free ASD model mice, transplantation of healthy donor microbiota alleviates autism-like behaviors. Consistently, WMT improves clinical symptoms in children with ASD and progressively shifts colonic microbiota toward donor-like configurations. Colonic microbiota changes are associated with symptom improvement, and exploratory predictive analyses suggest that integrating colonic in situ microbiota with clinical features may provide additional predictive information compared with fecal microbiota-based models. These findings suggest that clinically sampled colonic in situ microbiota may provide complementary information for understanding ASD heterogeneity and treatment response, although further validation is warranted.

articles.title: Reproductive History, Biological Indicators, and Pain Vulnerability in Aging Women: A Multi-Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain disproportionately affects women, yet the relationship between female reproductive history and long-term pain vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. Using three population-based cohorts from the UK, China, and the US, we evaluated associations between reproductive factors and pain-related phenotypes in aging women. Endogenous reproductive milestones showed nonlinear associations with pain risk. Specifically, both earlier and later ages at menarche and menopause, as well as shorter and longer reproductive lifespans, were linked to higher pain vulnerability. Childbirth-related characteristics, such as higher parity, earlier age at first birth, and longer interbirth intervals, were also associated with increased pain vulnerability. Reproductive surgeries and exogenous hormone use were consistently associated with pain phenotypes, with timing-dependent effects. In the UK Biobank, reproductive factors showed both shared and site-specific associations across seven chronic pain sites. These reproductive-pain associations were amplified among women with higher adiposity, greater socioeconomic deprivation, a history of depression or anxiety, and hypertension. Exploratory mediation analyses implicated inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators as potential biological correlates of several reproductive-chronic pain associations. Together, these findings highlight reproductive history as an important life-course factor associated with pain vulnerability and provide insights for future studies investigating mechanisms and risk stratification of chronic pain in women.

articles.title: Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation for bacterial infection: A multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Hyperammonaemia is traditionally linked to overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE), but growing evidence suggests it also contributes to cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction. We evaluated the association between plasma ammonia and bacterial infection and compared ammonia, the AMMON-OHE model and prognostic scores for predicting bacterial infection and other liver-related events in outpatients with cirrhosis.
APPROACH RESULTS: This is a multicentre, retrospective study in 1855 cirrhosis patients on prospectively followed cohorts from five European and one Singaporean centres. The primary endpoint was hospitalisation with bacterial infection. Within one year, 8% of European patients developed infection; these patients had higher ammonia (1.75 vs. 0.97 times ULN; p<0.001) and a sevenfold higher risk of liver-related death (37% vs. 5%; p<0.001). Ammonia remained associated with infection, each unit increase raising risk by 12-14%, and was selected by every variable-selection method. The 1.4 times ULN threshold identified patients at increased risk of infection and OHE (both p<0.001). Ammonia alone discriminated well for infection (C-index 0.725 in Europe, 0.877 in Singapore), and integration into the AMMON-OHE model improved prediction (C-index 0.805 in Europe), with good calibration and clinical utility comparable to Child-Pugh and greater than MELD. Both also predicted OHE (C-index up to 0.904), whereas performance was weaker for ascites and variceal bleeding.
CONCLUSION: Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation due to bacterial infection and predicts both infection and OHE. These findings support an ammonia-related vulnerability phenotype characterised by immune dysfunction and neurocognitive susceptibility, for which the AMMON-OHE model provides individualised risk stratification.

articles.title: KRAS and SKIL mutations synergistically promote pancreatic tumorigenesis through the ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of Smad4.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer development requires oncogenic KRAS plus additional genetic hits, yet these cooperating events remain poorly defined. Starting from a germline SKIL A512T mutation discovered in an infant with IPMN, we explored the synergistic role of SKIL and KRAS in tumorigenesis.
METHODS: HEK293T cells with engineered SKIL A512T and/or KRAS G12V mutations were analyzed for proliferation, tumorigenicity, and signaling. Transcriptomics, ubiquitination assays, and protein interaction studies (Co-IP, immunofluorescence) delineated the mechanism.
RESULTS: SKIL normally protects Smad4 by binding its MH2 domain; SKIL loss exposes this domain to ubiquitination, but degradation occurs only when KRAS mutation upregulates the E3 ligase SMURF2. Clinically, a significant positive correlation was observed between SKIL and Smad4 protein expression in KRAS-mutant IPMN tissues.
CONCLUSION: We identify a novel synergy between SKIL loss and KRAS activation that drives pancreatic tumorigenesis through targeted Smad4 degradation. This study aids in identifying high-risk populations for pancreatic cancer, specifically those harboring KRAS mutations.

articles.title: Brain somatic chromosome 1q gain causes focal cortical malformations and epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain somatic mutations are a major cause of epileptogenic focal cortical malformations. Hyaline astrocytic inclusions represent a rare neuropathological finding in epilepsy.
METHODS: We analyzed eight patients undergoing surgery for drug-resistant focal epilepsy associated with astrocytic inclusions, combining bulk and single-nucleus genomic analyses, cell-type-specific genetic profiling, neuropathological characterization, and electrophysiological recordings to establish genotype-neuropathology correlations.
RESULTS: Microelectrode array recordings from cortical slices from one patient revealed spontaneous abnormal network activity in regions without astrocytic inclusions. Multilayered genomic analysis of surgical brain tissue, including single-nucleus sequencing, identified mosaic chromosome 1q copy-number gains in all eight cases, with chr1q tetrasomies confirmed in six. In four cases, the supernumerary chromosome 1q was of maternal origin, and long-read haplotyping in a patient-parent trio supported a novel mechanism of meiosis II chromosome missegregation. Chr1q gains were enriched in inclusion-bearing astrocytes, linking chromosomal aneuploidy to neuropathology. Finally, we developed a targeted sequencing panel enabling the detection of chr1q gains in surgical brain samples, including samples obtained from presurgical stereo-EEG electrodes.
CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings support postzygotic rescue of a maternal meiotic error in non-neural lineages as a mechanism of pathogenic brain mosaicism and define mosaic chr1q gain as a distinct cause of epilepsy.

articles.title: Genetic variants in recurrent euploid pregnancy loss.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) affects ~ 5% of couples. Known causes of RPL include aneuploidies and unbalanced chromosome rearrangements, however the genetic basis of losses with normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray analysis remains unclear. We hypothesized that deleterious variants in genes essential for early development, including genes previously associated only with neonatal lethal disorders, contribute to RPL.
METHODS: Genome sequencing was performed on 118 families with unexplained, euploid RPL; 95% lacked major fetal structural anomalies on ultrasound. A tiered variant prioritization pipeline integrated model organism, human population databases, essential developmental pathways, and fetal transcriptomic profiles. Rare variants (allele frequency ≤ 0.1%) were assessed and confirmed by orthogonal methods. Parental samples were analyzed for mosaicism.
RESULTS: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in 18 families (15.3%) across 17 genes. These include six families with DHCR7, PIEZO1, PIGV, PRF1, SLC12A3, and SMN1 biallelic variants; two cases with ALAS2 and IKBKG hemizygous variants; and four pregnancies with heterozygous alterations inherited from affected parents with MYH3 and TNNI3 variants, and from asymptomatic parents with SCN5A and FLT4 variants. Additionally, four families had presumed de novo heterozygous variants in the EFTUD2, HNRNPK, FGFR2, and KAT6A genes (associated with autosomal dominant conditions), while two exhibited parental germline mosaicism in the FGFR2 and PORCN genes. Variants of uncertain significance were detected in 12 families (10.2%) across the ABCB7, CLPB, CRB2, FBN1, FLT4, GJA1, LYST, MAGED2, PTPN14, RNF213, TLR8, and VPS35L genes. Of 28 genes with plausible variants, 13 genes were previously implicated in perinatal lethality, whereas 15 were novel candidates. Overall, variants in candidate genes were inherited in 80% of families. Four additional families (3.4%) had biallelic ultra-rare variants in genes, which are involved in fundamental developmental pathways but not yet linked to human disease, pointing to a possible role in prenatal lethality. Transcriptomic analyses supported novel gene involvement in hematopoiesis, cardiovascular development, inflammation, and fluid homeostasis processes.
CONCLUSIONS: Genome sequencing revealed plausible monogenic etiologies for unexplained euploid pregnancy loss, providing new insights into the biology of early human lethality, phenotypic spectra, recurrence risks, and inheritance patterns. These findings support expanding RPL diagnostics beyond karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis.

articles.title: Necrotising enterocolitis triggers a TNF-driven gut-blood-brain cascade that disrupts the blood-brain barrier and induces TNFR1-skewed neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) in very-low-birthweight (VLBW) infants is associated with neurodevelopmental difficulties, but the mechanisms linking intestinal disease to brain injury remain unclear. We asked whether NEC propagates along a tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α)-centred gut-blood-brain pathway that compromises the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and activates inflammatory neuronal death programmes.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort, inflammatory biomarkers at symptom onset (C-reactive protein and procalcitonin) were related to Bayley-III composite scores at 24 months' corrected age. We then used a neonatal rat NEC model with daily oral etanercept, a soluble TNF receptor fusion protein, or saline from postnatal day 2 to day 14 to assess intestinal histopathology and permeability, circulating microbial products, inflammation, BBB permeability, early neurobehaviour, microglial activation, and neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis with TNF receptor (TNFR) localisation. An intestinal-epithelial cell-primary cortical neuron transwell co-culture tested whether LPS-injured epithelium was sufficient to release TNF-α, disrupt barrier integrity, and injure neurons, and whether etanercept mitigated these effects.
RESULTS: In infants, higher C-reactive protein and procalcitonin at NEC onset were associated with lower Bayley-III motor, cognitive, and language scores. In rats, NEC caused small-intestinal injury with tight-junction loss and permeability, elevated circulating microbial products and TNF-α, increased BBB leak, activated microglia, and induced neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis with a TNFR1-skewed and TNFR2-reduced profile. NEC also impaired early sensorimotor performance, and worse performance was associated with higher circulating C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, and TNF-α. Etanercept reduced inflammatory burden, improved intestinal and BBB integrity, and improved sensorimotor performance. In co-culture, LPS activated epithelial NF-κB and MAPK signalling, increased epithelial TNF-α, and reduced barrier resistance. Neurons exposed to this inflammatory milieu showed TNFR1 upregulation, TNFR2 downregulation, activation of apoptotic effectors, and NLRP1 inflammasome-linked pyroptotic signalling, accompanied by synaptic injury. Etanercept blunted upstream epithelial signalling, preserved barrier function, and reduced TNFR1-skewed neuronal injury programmes.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute inflammatory burden at presentation tracked with poorer 24-month neurodevelopment, and experimental data support TNF signalling as a plausible, modifiable relay linking barrier failure to BBB dysfunction, microglial activation, and TNFR1-skewed neuronal injury. These findings support risk stratification using routine biomarkers and motivate mechanism-informed trials targeting inflammatory amplification in NEC.

articles.title: Metabolomic signature of adiposity in preschool children: findings from the CORALS cohort.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is increasingly recognized as a condition characterized by excess adiposity and early metabolic dysregulation. However, evidence on metabolomic alterations during the preschool years remains limited. This study aimed to characterize circulating metabolomic profiles associated with body mass index (BMI) and examine their relationships with body composition. This cross-sectional analysis included 1200 children aged 3-6 years from the Childhood Obesity Risk Assessment Longitudinal Study (CORALS), of whom 1110 had complete covariate data. Circulating metabolic biomarkers were quantified in EDTA plasma using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) spectroscopy. Associations between BMI z-score (zBMI) and metabolites were assessed using multivariable linear regression with Bonferroni correction. Adjusted Spearman correlations were used to assess the relationships between metabolites and the z-scores for fat mass index (zFMI), fat-free mass index (zFFMI), and the waist-to-height ratio (zWtHR). Higher zBMI was associated with higher levels of branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, alanine and glycoprotein acetyls, and with lower levels of citrate and β-hydroxybutyrate. Children with a higher zBMI also had higher very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) concentrations and lower high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations and particle size. These metabolic differences showed consistent patterns across body composition indicators, particularly zFMI. These findings indicate that metabolic differences associated with higher BMI are detectable during the preschool years and involve multiple metabolic pathways. Body composition analyses suggest that individual metabolic features may relate differently to fat mass, fat-free mass, and central adiposity. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine their temporal and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Multi-Omics Gut Microbiome Species Communities and Functional Modules Linking Metal Exposures to Children's Neurodevelopmental Health in a Canadian Birth Cohort.
articles.abstract: Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. Here, we integrated stool metal measurements, shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and neurodevelopmental assessments in 116 children aged 8-12 years from the GESTE birth cohort in Sherbrooke, Canada. Nineteen metals were quantified in stool samples, and neurodevelopment was assessed using parent-reported behavioral scales, attention performance testing, and resting-state fMRI. Using network-based community detection, we identified 10 co-occurring species communities (SCs) from metagenomic data and 16 coexpressed functional modules (FMs) from metatranscriptomic data and evaluated their associations with metal exposures and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Higher levels of lead, cadmium, aluminum, zinc, copper, and magnesium were associated with lower abundance of Streptococcus- and Veillonella-dominated SCs, while multiple metals were associated with lower abundance of amino acid metabolism and carbohydrate degradation FMs. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested potential indirect associations between stool metals and parent-reported ADHD-related traits througha methionine cycle-related FM or sequentially through a Clostridium spp. SC and a Factor 420 biosynthesis FM. These findings suggest that stool metal concentrations are associated with community-level variations in gut microbial composition and function, some of which were further associated with parent-reported ADHD-related traits.

articles.title: Digital health infrastructure and research priorities across neonatal intensive care units in Germany: A nationwide cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract: Digital infrastructure increasingly determines whether clinical data can be reused for quality improvement, federated research, and population-level health surveillance, yet the digital maturity of neonatal intensive care has not been characterized at national scale. Neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) generate dense, continuous data for an extremely vulnerable population, a high-stakes exemplar of data-rich, high-acuity care. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional online survey of NICUs in Germany to map digital infrastructure and to capture respondents' attitudes, perceived barriers, and research priorities. Of 340 invited units, 136 (40%) began the questionnaire and 124 (36%) submitted analyzable unit-level responses between June and September 2025. Respondents were almost exclusively senior physicians, with no nurses or biomedical engineers, and responding centers were larger and more often university-affiliated than non-responders. Digitization was highly uneven: laboratory and imaging data were predominantly digital, whereas vital-sign, physician-note, medication, and nutrition documentation remained largely paper-based. A composite digitization score was apparently bimodal, suggesting a possible digital divide; only 33% of units operated a dedicated patient data management system at the bedside. Most respondents (83%) wanted further digitization, and demand was strongest in the least-digitized units (Spearman ρ = - 0.39, p < 0.001), although ceiling effects and common-method variance may contribute to this association. The dominant perceived barriers were shortages of information-technology personnel and the cost of software and hardware. These findings identify bedside documentation as the principal modernization priority and provide an exploratory indicator and baseline for tracking digital maturity over time. Mandated interoperability standards and targeted structural investment may be warranted to close the divide and to support more equitable and collaborative use of neonatal data across regions and health systems.

articles.title: Caregiver-Informed Safety and System Requirements for Real-Time Feedback During Pediatric Inhaler Use: Qualitative Concept-Elicitation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Correct use of a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI), usually with a valved holding chamber, depends on use-related conditions that caregivers may not observe directly, including inhalation pattern, actuation-inhalation timing, mask seal, and device orientation. Many digital inhaler systems emphasize actuation or adherence. Systems that infer technique-related conditions from proxy signals may add real-time feedback but also create false reassurance if a positive state is displayed when evidence is inadequate. Caregiver expectations for such feedback and its failure states remain poorly characterized before prototype development.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize caregivers' experiences of pediatric inhaler administration and translate responses to a proposed sensor concept into traceable candidate safety, system, and validation requirements.
METHODS: We conducted 23 semistructured concept-elicitation sessions through Zoom videoconference with 27 caregivers of children who currently or previously used a pMDI. Interviews consisted of 19 individual and 4 dyadic sessions pairing 2 caregivers from different households. Sessions were conducted remotely between April and July 2026 from the University of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Recruitment originated in Calgary and was not geographically restricted. A 6-phase guide examined current practices, difficulties, prior digital-tool use, and responses to a screen-shared clip-on concept incorporating airflow-, timing-, seal-, and orientation-related sensing; on-device feedback; an optional child-facing app; and a caregiver dashboard. No working prototype was evaluated. Approximately 86,000 transcript words underwent hybrid directed and conventional qualitative content analysis using an 18-category codebook. Two researchers independently coded the complete 27×18 matrix (486 paired decisions) across 2 rounds. Consensus categories were translated into candidate requirements and assigned an earliest verification or evaluation locus. Counts are descriptive caregiver-voice tallies, not prevalence estimates.
RESULTS: Persistent uncertainty about whether administration conditions were adequate was the dominant lived experience (19/27); for 5 caregivers, existing passive cues had not resolved it. A simple, real-time on-device signal was endorsed by 25 caregivers, but willingness to consider the concept was conditional on reliability (9 caregivers named reasons for abandonment, notably a "false green"), low-friction operation during acute symptoms (12/27), minimal added bulk and technique change, and one or more of clinical validation, clinician recommendation, or a trial pathway (composite category; 23/27). Stances on gamification (20/27), dashboard cadence (18/27), aesthetics (24/27), and privacy (18/27) supported an optional, configurable software layer. Intercoder agreement was 94% (Cohen κ=0.88). The analytic synthesis yielded a conceptual architecture separating observable proxy signals, an inference and data-quality gate, and positive, corrective, or uncertain feedback states.
CONCLUSIONS: Participating caregivers prioritized immediate and interpretable feedback about use-related conditions. The findings support conservative state assignment, an explicit uncertain state for indeterminate signals, and app-independent acute-use feedback. These are candidate requirements rather than validated device specifications; subsequent work should proceed through bench verification, simulated-use human factors evaluation, and prospective clinical or field validation.

articles.title: Parents' Perspectives on the Use and Development of Predictive AI in Neonatology: Focus Group Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictive AI models, such as AI-generated early warning systems for detecting critical conditions, are being praised as promising applications in neonatology. Despite technological advancements in predictive AI, the integration of AI at the bedside remains challenging, and few AI technologies are currently integrated into routine neonatal care. A better understanding of the wishes and barriers of patients and, in the case of neonatal patients, their parents, is essential to bridge this gap. Yet, parental perspectives on the use of AI remain underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored the perspectives of parents whose child had previously been admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit about the development and use of predictive AI in neonatal clinical settings.
METHODS: We conducted 3 focus groups with 18 Dutch parents of children admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit to explore their views on AI in neonatal care. Participants were purposively recruited via a neonatology parent and patient organization. Discussions focused on predictive AI in acute settings and on AI to predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in later life. A reflexive thematic analysis of the focus group data was performed.
RESULTS: Parents generally welcomed predictive AI as a supportive tool for the medical team, anticipating improvements in patient outcomes. AI for short-term predictions was especially appreciated, whereas longer-term predictions were received with some reservations. Overarching concerns regarding predictive AI systems included AI undermining parental intuition, overreliance on AI in decision-making, and undesirable ethical and psychological implications of long-term health predictions. Interestingly, in addition to predictive AI systems that support medical judgment, parents also hoped that other AI tools could be developed to better involve parental input in the decision-making process. Specifically, they envisioned applications that extend beyond clinical decision support to provide parents with information, emotional support, and tailored guidance on the right course of action.
CONCLUSIONS: Parental perspectives highlight both opportunities and challenges for predictive AI integration in neonatal care. Engaging parents in the design and implementation of AI informs the development of family-centered, ethically responsible AI solutions and may identify opportunities for developing parent-centered AI tools alongside systems designed to support clinicians.

articles.title: A Social Media Mining and Questionnaire Survey Hybrid Approach to Characterizing Caregiver Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices on House Dust Mite Control: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: House dust mite (HDM) sensitization commonly begins in early life and contributes to persistent allergic airway inflammation and asthma chronicity. Primary prevention via early-life environmental control is a potential pathway to reduce HDM sensitization and asthma risk.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize child caregivers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding pediatric HDM control using a hybrid literature/expert-driven and social media-driven approach and to examine associations between KAP levels, child age, and caregiver HDM-related online engagement.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study comprised two interconnected components: (1) mining of content published between August 2023 and July 2025 from 5 major Chinese social media platforms, analyzed via latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), and (2) a social media-enhanced web-based KAP survey administered in November 2025 to child caregivers in Chongqing, China. In total, 132,341 social media documents and 2275 caregivers of children younger than 18 years were included in the analysis. The main outcomes included social media discourse patterns and domain-specific KAP levels across 5 dimensions: foundational knowledge (K1), recommended control knowledge (K2), attitude toward social media topics (A1), attitude toward recommended methods (A2), and control practices (P). Stratified analysis was conducted by 2 exposure variables: child age (≤3 years vs >3 years) and caregiver HDM-related online engagement (engaged vs nonengaged).
RESULTS: LDA topic modeling identified 5 distinct topic clusters in the social media content. Commercial, emotional, and misleading content collectively dominated the information landscape, accounting for 83.3% (n=110,254) of the included documents (65.8% of the tokens), with commercial content often systematically conflating the concepts of "disinfection" and "mite elimination." Only 16.7% (n=22,087) of the documents (34.1% of the tokens) were classified as health educational content focusing on HDM allergy prevention, reflecting that this valid educational content is substantially longer and more information-dense than other social media posts. The average KAP levels of K1, K2, A1, A2, and P domains were 62.9%, 84.7%, 57.0%, 37.8%, and 25.8%, respectively. Social media emerged as the primary knowledge source (80.7%, n=1836), with methodological knowledge gaps (47.5%) being the top implementation barrier. Caregivers of children ≤3 years had significantly lower self-rated knowledge (23.5% vs 28.3%; P=.01), stronger endorsement of recommended methods, but also greater information overload (odds ratio [OR] 1.39, 95% CI 1.15-1.67; P<.001) and efficacy uncertainty (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.01-1.52; P=.04). Caregivers with HDM-related online engagement showed better performance across multiple items in 5 domains, but also increased traditional practice with uncertain evidence (ultraviolet irradiation: OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.35-2.53; P<.001) and misconception acceptance (allergy impact exaggeration: OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.04-1.87; P=.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Complex and suboptimal KAP levels exist, particularly among caregivers of young children (≤3 years). HDM-related online engagement is associated with both enhanced implementation of control practices and elevated misconception endorsement. These findings reveal critical educational gaps and the necessity of social media intervention.

articles.title: The Association Between Platform-Specific Social Media Use and Suicidal Ideation in Japan: Cross-Sectional Web-Based Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Japan, suicides among young women have recently increased; however, this trend's specific causes remain unclear. Concurrently, rising social media use has sparked concerns regarding its potential impact. However, findings on the association between social media use and mental health have been mixed, and platform-specific differences remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the cross-sectional association between current platform-specific social media use and retrospectively reported past-year suicidal ideation in Japan, as well as age- and sex-based differences.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed 2 linked nationwide internet surveys: the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey (December 2024-January 2025) and the Japan Society and New Tobacco Internet Survey (February 2025-March 2025). The analysis included 19,542 individuals aged 15 to 84 years who responded to both surveys. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the associations between the use of specific social media platforms (Facebook, X [formerly known as Twitter], Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok) and suicidal ideation, adjusting for covariates.
RESULTS: Suicidal ideation was reported by 10.8% (2118/19,542) of the participants. In the adjusted models, suicidal ideation was associated with the use of X (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.44, 95% CI 1.27-1.63), Facebook (aOR 1.33, 95% CI 1.18-1.49), and TikTok (aOR 1.33, 95% CI 1.19-1.50; P<.001 in all cases) but not Instagram (aOR 0.93, 95% CI 0.82-1.06) or YouTube (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 0.94-1.27). Exploratory stratified analyses (interpreted with caution given multiple comparisons) suggested that the association with X use was consistent across participants younger than 45 years.
CONCLUSIONS: The association between social media use and suicidal ideation varied across platforms and demographic groups. After adjusting for confounders, only instances of the use of X, Facebook, and TikTok were associated with higher odds of suicidal ideation. Thus, the relationship between social media use and suicidal ideation depends on platform characteristics and user attributes, thereby underscoring the need for platform-specific suicide prevention strategies. These cross-sectional findings do not permit directional inference and should be regarded as hypothesis generating.

articles.title: m6A epitranscriptomic regulation in acute myeloid leukemia: From leukemic dependencies to therapy resistance and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation has emerged as an important post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Dysregulated m6A writers, erasers and readers influence leukemic stem cell maintenance, myeloid differentiation, RNA stability, translation, metabolic adaptation and treatment response.
