CONCLUSION: The present study fills a gap in the field of A-T immunity, revealing exhaustion-associated features and functional impairment of NK cells correlated with increased plasma concentrations of sNKG2DLs and the immunosuppressive cytokines IL-6 and TGF-β. These findings indicate that NK defects can contribute to cancer and infection susceptibility and provide hints for improving current therapies for A-T.

articles.title: Giving Vulnerable Parents a Voice: A Qualitative Synthesis Review of Parent Engagement Experience in Child Maltreatment Prevention Programs.
articles.abstract: Recent child welfare policies in the United States prioritize child maltreatment prevention, making parent engagement in voluntary prevention services crucial to program effectiveness. However, engaging parents in high-risk families remains a significant challenge. This qualitative synthesis review examines parents' perspectives on factors influencing their engagement and identifies parent-recommended strategies to enhance engagement. A systematic search of multiple databases yielded 3,447 studies published between 1980 and 2022. Fifty-three peer-reviewed qualitative and mixed-methods studies published between 1991 and 2022 that explored parent engagement experiences in child maltreatment prevention programs met the inclusion criteria. We assessed study quality using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool and synthesized qualitative findings using thematic analysis. The qualitative synthesis identified three major domains influencing parent engagement: factors shaping parent engagement, engagement experiences, and parent-recommended strategies. Parents engaged more successfully when programs addressed contextual, internal, and external factors, including socioeconomic adversity, motivation, practical resources, program design, and provider relationships. Positive engagement fostered trust, support, parenting confidence, and stronger family relationships, whereas judgment, cultural mismatch, provider inconsistency, and logistical barriers hindered engagement. Parents recommended culturally responsive and father-inclusive services, flexible program delivery, practical supports, and strong provider-parent partnerships to strengthen engagement. Parent engagement in child maltreatment prevention programs is a dynamic process shaped by interactions among individual, programmatic, and broader contextual factors. Building trusting relationships, reducing structural barriers, and incorporating parents' perspectives into program design and delivery are essential for strengthening engagement and improving the effectiveness of child maltreatment prevention services.

articles.title: Ventilator-circuit configurations for noninvasive ventilation in infants with acute respiratory failure: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract: Patient-ventilator synchrony may differ across ventilator and circuit configurations during noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in infants. We compared an intentional-leak single-limb turbine configuration (SLC-turbine), a dual-limb turbine configuration with an active expiratory valve (DLC-turbine), and a dual-limb compressed-gas pediatric ICU configuration (DLC-PICU) in infants receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure METHODS: In this single-center randomized crossover physiological study, infants underwent three 30-minute NIV phases in randomized order with unchanged pressure support, PEEP, and FiO₂. Esophageal pressure was used to assess the asynchrony index (AI), individual asynchronies, and inspiratory effort. Primary and secondary endpoints were AI differences between DLC-PICU and SLC-turbine and between DLC-PICU and DLC-turbine, respectively RESULTS: Twenty infants entered stabilization, 13 were randomized, and 12 completed the protocol (age 10 [7-21] months; SpO₂/FiO₂ 185 [160-220]). AI differed across configurations: 8.6% [6.7-16.5] with SLC-turbine, 25.4% [16.3-35.0] with DLC-turbine, and 45.7% [30.5-63.8] with DLC-PICU (p=0.0023). AI was higher with DLC-PICU than with SLC-turbine (Hodges-Lehmann difference +32.0%, 95% CI +13.9 to +50.1; p=0.0015) and DLC-turbine (+18.4%, 95% CI +5.9 to +36.3; p=0.021). Auto-triggering showed the clearest configuration-dependent difference and was more frequent with DLC-PICU than with SLC-turbine (7.5 [0.6-11.4] vs 0 [0-2.5] events/min; difference +5.30 events/min; p=0.0039), without a significant difference between DLC-PICU and DLC-turbine. Ineffective efforts, double triggering, and premature cycling did not differ across configurations. All NIV configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, with no significant differences among NIV configurations CONCLUSIONS: AI was lower with SLC-turbine and DLC-turbine than with DLC-PICU and lowest with SLC-turbine. Auto-triggering showed the clearest configuration-dependent difference. All configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, without significant between-configuration differences. Because ventilator platform, circuit and expiratory architecture, and device-specific control functions differed, effects of individual components cannot be determined. These findings are specific to the ventilators and configurations evaluated. Further studies should determine whether these physiological differences translate into improved NIV tolerance or short- and long-term clinical outcomes TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04017780. Registered on 12 July 2019.

articles.title: Development and external validation of age-specific predictive models for sepsis in critically ill neonates and children using multidimensional hematological parameters: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICU/PICU). Given the rapid clinical deterioration of these vulnerable populations, shifting from reactive diagnosis to proactive prediction of sepsis onset is crucial. Multidimensional hematological parameters may provide new insights for risk stratification. While routine complete blood count (CBC) is widely used, the predictive potential of high-dimensional hematological cell morphology features that extend beyond traditional CBC remains under-investigated in large-scale pediatric cohorts.
METHODS: This multicenter study utilized a large-scale dataset from the CALM2302 project, encompassing 17,066 critically ill neonates and children across 30 Chinese hospitals between October 2020 and October 2023. We developed population-specific CatBoost models for NICU and PICU to predict sepsis onset. To mitigate class imbalance, random undersampling was applied to the training sets. From a candidate pool of 1,924 parameters (37 routine CBC and 1,887 research features), optimized signatures of approximately 200 features were selected for each population. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) across internal and dual external validation cohorts. Furthermore, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was performed to ensure model interpretability and identify key biological predictors.
RESULTS: Among the total cohort, 10,347 infants were categorized into the NICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 7.48%), while 6,719 children formed the PICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 10.92%). CatBoost was identified as the optimal architecture after benchmarking nine machine learning algorithms. The population-specific simplified 18-variable models demonstrated robust performance. In the NICU cohort, the model achieved an internal AUC of 0.846 and external AUCs of 0.742 and 0.827. For the PICU cohort, corresponding AUCs were 0.803, 0.717, and 0.811. These simplified models maintained highly comparable discriminative power to the full models (range of AUC attenuation: 0.005-0.027). SHAP analysis identified 18 key predictive features for each cohort, with only two shared features between the two populations and the remaining being cohort-specific. Notably, most of these 18 features were research parameters rather than traditional blood counts indices. Furthermore, most of these features remained statistically significant in multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, sex, and study sites.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, we developed and validated simplified 18-variable models that accurately predict sepsis in both neonatal and pediatric populations. By capturing early hematological morphological alterations beyond traditional blood counts, these models offer a robust, interpretable, and clinically accessible solution for proactive sepsis management in intensive care units.

articles.title: Medical Imaging and Pediatric and Adolescent Brain Tumor Risk.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Ionizing radiation from medical imaging may increase brain tumor risk.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify brain tumor risk associated with radiation exposure from medical imaging in children and adolescents.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Retrospective cohort study of children born from 1996 through 2016 who were enrolled from birth in 6 US health care systems or Ontario, Canada, and were alive and cancer-free at age 2 years, with follow-up through December 31, 2017 (US sites), and December 31, 2024 (Ontario).
EXPOSURES: Cumulative radiation dose to the brain from medical imaging, lagged by 2 years.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident brain or other central nervous system tumors. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models for categorical dose, and excess relative risks (ERRs) were estimated using linear dose-response models for continuous dose.
RESULTS: Among 3 704 860 children (1 900 285 [51.3%] male) followed up for 45 671 641 person-years (mean follow-up, 12.3 years), 1536 brain tumors were diagnosed. Mean radiation dose from 1 head computed tomography (CT) examination was 66.2 mGy (SD, 22.2). Among children with cumulative dose of 1 mGy or greater, mean cumulative dose was 73 mGy (SD, 95) overall and 100 mGy (SD, 105) among those diagnosed with brain tumors. Compared with no exposure, brain tumor risk increased with cumulative dose (>0 to <1 mGy: HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.26]; 1 to <5 mGy: HR, 1.71 [95% CI, 0.88-2.96]; 5 to <50 mGy: HR, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.16-2.81]; 50 to <75 mGy: HR, 2.30 [95% CI, 1.64-3.12]; 75 to <100 mGy: HR, 2.02 [95% CI, 1.13-3.30]; 100 to <150 mGy: HR, 2.81 [95% CI, 1.53-4.66]; ≥150 mGy: HR, 3.85 [95% CI, 2.43-5.75]). Cumulative dose was associated with brain tumor risk overall (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.27 [95% CI, 0.83-1.77]; P < .001), with stronger associations for aggressive histologies (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.51 [95% CI, 1.00-2.11]; P < .001). By age 21 years, exposure comparable to 1 head CT was associated with 7.9 excess brain tumors per 10 000 children, or approximately 1 excess tumor per 1266 head CT examinations. The estimated population-attributable fraction was 10.1% (95% CI, 5.8%-14.2%).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Medical imaging in children and adolescents was associated with a dose-related increase in brain tumor risk. These findings support careful clinical justification and dose minimization when pediatric imaging using ionizing radiation is indicated.

articles.title: Vaccines: The Best of Times, the Worst of Times: A Healthy Dialogue With Paul Offit.
Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias.
OBSERVATIONS: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

articles.title: Prognostic nomogram predicts postoperative mortality in children with brain tumors in a multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related death in children. Reliable tools for predicting postoperative mortality in children remain limited. The aim of the study is to develop and validate a clinically applicable prognostic nomogram.
METHODS: We developed and externally validated a prognostic nomogram using data from two prospective cohorts in South China. The model included 375 patients (internal cohort) and 224 patients (external validation). Multivariate Cox regression identified independent predictors, which were integrated into the nomogram to estimate 12-, 36-, and 60-month survival.
RESULTS: Here we show that five factors-age, World Health Organization classification, extent of resection, systemic immune-inflammation index, and Count of major neurological dysfunctions (muscle weakness, disorientation)-are independently associated with mortality. The model shows good discrimination with C-index values of 0.789 (training), 0.841 (test), and 0.789 (external). Area Under Curves at all timepoints exceed 0.80. Sensitivities and specificities ranged from 0.824-0.905 and 0.619-0.671, respectively. Calibration and clinical utility are satisfactory.
CONCLUSION: This nomogram enables individualized prediction of postoperative mortality in pediatric brain tumor patients, aiding surgical and perioperative decision-making.

articles.title: A low resource requirement molecular diagnostic and surveillance tool for Shigella in the era of vaccination.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infection with Shigella bacteria is one of the leading causes of diarrhoeal disease globally, with significant burden in low- and middle-income countries and rising incidence in high-income settings. Effective serotyping is essential for surveillance, outbreak investigation, vaccine targeting, and can inform clinical management. Current discriminative approaches, such as seroagglutination and whole genome sequencing, are constrained by cross-reactivity, infrastructure requirements, and cost.
METHODS: Here, we present the development of a nine-target multiplex PCR lateral flow device assay for the rapid, accurate identification of vaccine-prioritised S. flexneri serotypes 1b, 2a, and 3a, and S. sonnei, as well as clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes.
RESULTS: Validation using 138 DNA samples from clinical Shigella isolates showed 97.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity at the species level, performing comparably to in silico genomic prediction tools. Serotype classifications interpreted from the PCR assay also successfully aligned with the temporal and geographic trends observed in a large multi-country clinical dataset (n = 1,074), supporting its utility for temporospatial surveillance. To facilitate field-deployment of the PCR assay, we integrated an oligo-chromatographic dipstick method, enabling a simple, gel-free readout without need for specialised equipment.
CONCLUSION: This molecular dipstick assay provides a practical and scalable solution for Shigella serotyping and antimicrobial resistance profiling in support of vaccine implementation and surveillance efforts.

articles.title: Early-Age alcohol initiation increases the risk of mental disorders in children and adolescents: a longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract: Although alcohol use is proved to relate with poor psychiatric outcomes, the longitudinal impact of early-age alcohol initiation on youth mental health is poorly characterized. The current study analyzed semi-structured interview data on substance use collected at baseline and over two years of follow-up (6, 12, 18, and 24 months) as part of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study. Participants that reported having at least one sip were defined as alcohol experimenters. Latent class trajectory model (LCTM) was used to characterize sipping patterns over follow-up period. In this study, 1659 alcohol experimenters were identified (mean age at baseline, 9.55 ± 0.50 years; 944 males [56.9%]) and matched with 1659 controls without any alcohol use. Early-age alcohol initiation was associated with higher risk of developing mental disorders (MDs, OR 1.25, [95% CI, 1.03-1.52]). Subgroup analyses suggested that pre-baseline alcohol exposure could increase the risk of sleep-wake disorder (OR 1.39, [95%CI, 1.06-1.82]), bipolar disorder (OR 1.70, [95%CI, 1.10-2.67]), non-suicidal self-injury behavior (OR 1.91, [95% CI, 1.20-3.08]) and suicidal ideation (OR 1.51, [95% CI, 1.22-2.15]). Two sipping patterns were identified among follow-up alcohol experimenters: increased sipping (Class 1, 56.7%) and decreased sipping (Class 2, 43.3%) over the two-year follow-up period. Compared with controls, only Class 1 was significantly associated with increased risk of MDs (OR 1.48, [95% CI, 1.02-2.14]). Both Class 1 and Class 2 showed elevated risk of suicidal ideation (Class1: OR 2.38, [95%CI, 1.22-4.71]; Class2: OR 2.64, [95%CI, 1.29-5.44]). These findings suggest an association between early alcohol exposure and negative mental health conditions in children aged under 12 years, highlighting children as a potential priority population for alcohol prevention efforts.

articles.title: Estimating differing causal roles of glutamate and GABA genes on brain and behavior in autism.
articles.abstract: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) imbalance theory suggests that excitatory and inhibitory alterations underlies autism characteristics. However, genetic underpinnings of this imbalance and its impact on brain function and behavior remains unclear. We explored causal links between glutamate and GABA gene-set polygenic scores (PGS) for autism and core autism characteristics, putting particular attention on the restricted- and repetitive behaviors (RRBs) domain by including functional activity (fMRI) during inhibitory control (in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and striatum). Causal links between genes, brain and behavior was evaluated using Bayesian Constraint-based Causal Discovery (BCCD) algorithms, to build causal models of these relationships in a discovery sample (LEAP cohort: autistic = 343, neurotypical = 253) and two generalization cohorts with partially overlapping measures (TACTICS cohort: autistic = 60, neurotypical = 100, Simon Simplex Collection: autistic = 2756). In the discovery sample, we found a causal link between glutamate PGS and core clinical characteristics of autism, particularly the communication domain (Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised) in autistic participants, with 95% reliability. We did not find links between functional activity during inhibitory control and other measures. For one generalization cohort, we further report on the impact of 1H-MRS measures of glutamate, identifying a causal link between GABA autism PGS on ACC glutamate concentrations. Not all links were identified in the generalization cohorts, which may be due to clinical and genetic differences between the cohorts. While our results reinforce the previously found association between glutamate genes and core clinical autism behaviors, task-based functional activity may not be causally related to RRBs.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of non-pharmacological interventions on executive function and attentional control in children and adolescents with ADHD: a Bayesian network meta-analysis based on task-based cognitive outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) involves measurable impairments in executive functioning and attentional control, yet the relative efficacy of non-pharmacological treatments on objective, task-based performance in pediatric samples remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials enrolling children and adolescents with ADHD aged 6-18 years, identified from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL between 2000 and 2025. Interventions were aggregated into eight active categories plus Control, and task outcomes were prospectively assigned to seven executive/attentional task-family domains. Effect directions were harmonized, and the primary endpoint was defined as 0-2 weeks after treatment completion; models were fitted separately by domain. Additional exploratory post-intervention analyses examined study-level mean age and sex composition, indexed by male proportion, as aggregate-level moderators and complementary subgroup variables.
RESULTS: Eighty-six eligible randomized study reports involving 4628 participants met the inclusion criteria. For inhibitory control, Multicomponent interventions (Hedges' g = 0.63, 95% credible interval [CrI] 0.21-1.06), Cognitive Training (g = 0.61, 0.30-0.93), and Physical Activity/Motor Training (g = 0.46, 0.13-0.80) outperformed Control. Cognitive Training also improved working memory (g = 0.32, 0.01-0.63). For sustained attention, Multicomponent interventions showed the largest effects (g = 0.95, 0.36-1.55), with additional benefits for Cognitive Training (g = 0.50, 0.13-0.89) and Neurofeedback (g = 0.43, 0.02-0.85). Evidence for cognitive flexibility was attenuated, and planning/higher-order executive function and processing speed/reaction-time variability remained mixed or uncertain. Sensitivity analyses did not materially change the main ranking patterns. Exploratory aggregate-level analyses did not indicate clear systematic moderation of the better-powered domain-level effects by study-level mean age or male proportion.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent interventions and Cognitive Training showed the most consistent task-family-level improvements on objective executive and attentional tasks in pediatric ADHD, whereas evidence for higher-order executive function and processing speed/reaction-time variability remained uncertain. The exploratory age and sex-composition findings should be interpreted at the study level and do not establish individual-level developmental or sex-specific treatment effects.
PROSPERO: CRD420251129986.

articles.title: The longitudinal association of stress-response biomarkers on neurocognitive functioning in young adults at-risk for suicidal behavior.
articles.abstract: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, increased inflammation, and impaired neurocognitive processes have been observed across psychiatric disorders, yet their relationships in young adults at risk for suicidal behavior remain unclear. This study examined cross-sectional and prospective associations between biomarkers in these pathways and neurocognitive functioning in this population. A total of 254 participants aged 18-30 years were recruited from inpatient and outpatient settings, including individuals with a recent suicide attempt (SA; n = 66), suicide ideation (SI; n = 66), psychiatric controls (PC; n = 73), and healthy controls (HC; n = 49). Hair cortisol concentration, circulating inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, IL-10, IL-1ra, TNF-α), neurocognitive functioning, and clinical measures were assessed at baseline, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups. Of the sample, 110 (43.1%) contributed follow-up data. There was differential attrition in our sample and as such we used inverse probability-weighted analysis to adjust for this differential attrition in our longitudinal analyses. Cross-sectionally, higher CRP and IL-10 were associated with poorer executive functioning, however, these associations were not significant after adjusting for covariates. In longitudinal analyses, increases in CRP (β = 0.147, SE = 0.034, p < 0.001) predicted poorer executive functioning over time. In addition, increases in CRP (β = 0.328, SE = 0.114, p = 0.004) predicted reduced response inhibition over time. Results remained significant when adjusting for covariates. These findings highlight the role of inflammatory processes in cognitive impairments among young adults at risk for suicidal behavior.

articles.title: Usability of an artificial intelligence enabled Participation and Environment Measure prototype for family-centered goal setting support in pediatric rehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family-centered care coordination (FC-CC) in pediatric rehabilitation benefits from tools that support caregivers in contributing to personalized service planning for their children. Participation and Environment Measure (PEM) is a digital application that is being further developed to support FC-CC in early intervention (EI). PEM is being further developed to include the Young Children's Participation and Environment Measure (YC-PEM) electronic patient-reported outcome and a companion PEM-Plus (PEM+) goal setting intervention. This study examined usability of the first artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled PEM prototype.
METHODS: Caregivers from an urban EI program met these eligibility criteria: (1) were at least 18 years old; (2) identified as the parent or legal guardian of a child enrolled in EI services; (3) read, wrote, and spoke English; (4) had internet and telephone access; and (5) had a child 0-3 years old who received EI services for 3 or more months. Participants completed the AI-enabled PEM application with access to a debiased prototypic conversational agent. PEM usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and chatbot usability was assessed along four BOT Usability Scale (BUS-11) domains: 1) accessibility of chatbot functions; 2) functional interactive conversation; 3) privacy and security; and 4) timely response. Univariate logistic regression models were used to examine associations between each of the four BUS-11 domains and PEM+ engagement.
RESULTS: Eleven female caregivers of children (mean age: 24.5 months) enrolled, 66.7% of whom interacted with the prototypic chatbot during one or more iterations of the PEM+ intervention. Overall PEM usability remained acceptable. While overall chatbot usability was very poor (Mdn = 53.4%, IQR = 50.0, 55.4), caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability were average for accessibility of chatbot functions (Mdn = 3.8, IQR = 3.0, 4.0) and good for privacy and security (M = 3.1, Range = 2.0-5.0). Higher caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability did not significantly increase odds of PEM+ intervention use.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings indicate that an AI-enabled PEM retains adequate usability. A chatbot integrated within the PEM+ intervention is accessible and secure, though its functional interactive conversation and timely responses could benefit from further development to increase odds of its use in an EI service context.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06458959 (Registration date: 2024-06-14).

articles.title: Serum testosterone and uric acid: Key biomarkers for predicting response to drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) in adolescents polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) poses diagnostic and management challenges. Although combined oral contraceptives (COCs) can improve symptoms, treatment response varies.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy of drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) (DRSP/EE (II)) and explore predictors of therapeutic response.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective study.
METHODS: Adolescents with PCOS and healthy controls were retrospectively included. Among patients treated with DRSP/EE (II), clinical, biochemical, and sex-hormone indices were assessed at baseline and at 3 and 6 months, including total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), free androgen index (FAI), uric acid (UA), and lipid profile. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with treatment response, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess discriminative performance.
RESULTS: The PCOS group had higher androgen levels and lower SHBG than controls. TT and FAI decreased significantly after 3 and 6 months of DRSP/EE (II), while SHBG increased. Triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, and HDL-C increased. Responders had higher baseline TT (2.03±0.59 vs. 1.55±0.46 nmol/L; FDR P=0.009) and lower UA (314.43±61.33 vs. 372.16±77.16 μmol/L; FDR P=0.023) than non-responders. Multivariable logistic regression showed that TT (OR=6.893; P=0.004) and UA (OR=0.984; P=0.002) were independently associated with treatment response. ROC analyses showed AUCs of 0.716 for TT and 0.713 for UA, while the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.815, with 87.8% sensitivity and 75.0% specificity.
CONCLUSION: DRSP/EE (II) effectively improves hyperandrogenism in adolescent PCOS but may worsen lipid profiles. Baseline TT and UA are promising predictors of clinical response and may facilitate individualized management.

articles.title: Association between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and vaccine-induced antibody concentrations in five-year-old children from the Odense Child Cohort, Denmark.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental chemicals associated with lower vaccine-induced immune concentrations in children. Vaccine-induced antibody concentrations correlate strongly with time since vaccination, likely contributing to large variability in previous estimates. We investigated associations between prenatal and childhood PFAS exposure and antibody concentrations shortly after the five-year tetanus and diphtheria booster, with precise vaccination timing.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We included 259 children from the Odense Child Cohort, a background-PFAS-exposed Danish cohort. Exact vaccination dates from the Danish Vaccination Register determined time since vaccination. Child serum samples were collected a median of 5.9 weeks after the five-year booster (2015-2018). PFAS was quantified in maternal and child samples and antibodies in child samples. Generalized Linear Models were used to examine associations adjusting for maternal education and time since vaccination. Secondary analyses used logistic regression estimating odds of reaching protective antibody levels.
RESULTS: Generally consistent inverse, trends between childhood PFAS exposure and antibody levels were found, although most were not significant. The strongest association was observed for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), where a doubling was associated with a 38.4% lower tetanus antibody concentration (95% CI: -57.7%, -11.1%). The PFOS estimate was in the same direction, but weaker (-17.1; 95% CI: -37.6%, 10.2%). Similar non-significant associations were observed for other PFAS and diphtheria antibodies. Higher PFAS were associated with non-significantly lower odds of reaching protective antibody levels for both vaccines. No consistent patterns were observed for prenatal PFAS exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional study of low-exposed children, PFAS exposure was associated with lower antibody concentrations against tetanus and diphtheria. All estimates were inverse although not all significant, and associations appeared larger than in previous studies without exact vaccination dates. This is of public concern, as lower vaccine-induced antibody concentrations are considered critical adverse effect of PFAS.

articles.title: Markedly reduced skeletal muscle oxidative capacity with elevated circulating GDF-15 in children with cerebral palsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral palsy (CP) is associated with progressive skeletal muscle weakness and reduced physical capacity, yet the contribution of mitochondrial dysfunction to these impairments remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: We therefore evaluated skeletal muscle mitochondrial health in children with CP and typically developing (TD) children (12.9±3.4years) using a comprehensive approach integrating high-resolution respirometry, targeted protein analyses, circulating biomarkers, and plasma proteomics. Thirty-six skeletal muscle biopsies from 22 children with CP, and 15 muscle biopsies from TD children were collected during planned orthopedic surgery.
RESULTS: Skeletal muscle from children with CP exhibited markedly reduced oxidative capacity (-50% in CP vs TD, p<0.001), accompanied by broad reductions in mitochondrial and substrate transport proteins suggesting reduced mitochondrial content. Despite the absence of local or systemic inflammation, circulating growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), a biomarker of mitochondrial distress, was elevated in children with CP (337±53 vs 626±547pg·ml-1 for TD vs CP, p<0.05) and was highest among those with more severe motor impairments.
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that previously reported reductions in skeletal muscle mitochondrial protein content in CP translate into profound impairments in mitochondrial function. Moreover, the dissociation between mitochondrial dysfunction and inflammatory signaling suggests that mitochondrial insufficiency in CP occurs independently of inflammation. Elevated circulating GDF-15 further suggests that mitochondrial dysfunction in CP may extend beyond skeletal muscle and exert systemic effects. Together, our findings identify mitochondrial insufficiency as a prominent feature of skeletal muscle pathology in CP potentially acting as a contributor to secondary health complications across the lifespan.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
authors: Medauar Reis de Andrade Moreira F
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: Associations between ambient air pollutants and chronic pain prevalence in US children, 2023: A cross-sectional, national study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution poses increasing risks to pediatric health, yet associations between ambient air pollutants and chronic pain in children remain poorly described. This study examined whether ambient air pollutants are associated with chronic pain in a national sample of US children.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted linking data from 54,880 children aged 0-17 years in the 2023 National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH) to US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) state-level air pollution estimates. Parents reported whether their child experienced chronic or frequent pain in the past 12 months. Survey-weighted logistic regression was used to estimate associations between seven pollutants (PM2.5 PM10, PM10-2.5, O3, SO2, NO2, NO) and chronic pain, adjusting for age, sex, income, and asthma. Principal component analysis (PCA) characterized pollutant mixtures.
FINDINGS: Chronic pain prevalence was 5.1%, with higher rates among adolescents, females, and low-income households. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) was significantly associated with chronic pain after false discovery rate correction (aOR 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.13, p = 0.004, q = 0.028). PCA-derived mixture scores were not associated with chronic pain, and SO2 loaded weakly on both PCs (PC1-aOR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.87-1.04; PC2-aOR 0.98, 95% CI: 0.89-1.07), suggesting it captures independent variance from distinct industrial emission sources.
INTERPRETATION: SO2, a marker of industrial combustion and fossil fuel burning, was the only pollutant associated with pediatric chronic pain in this nationally representative sample. This association may reflect neuroinflammatory pathways linking combustion-derived pollution to pain sensitization. Future studies with finer-scale exposure assessment are needed to confirm these findings.
FUNDING: No direct funding for this project. Dr. Groenewald is supported by R01HL16637 from NHLBI.

articles.title: Strength Training in Youth: A Scoping Review with Evidence Gap Map.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strength training has gained increasing attention in youth athletic development due to its benefits in performance and motor competence. However, a comprehensive overview of the literature examining strength training in youth populations is lacking, and research remains fragmented across sex, maturation stages, and intervention characteristics.
OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic scoping review with an evidence gap map of studies on strength training in youth aged 6-18 years to provide evidence-based priorities for future research and practice.
METHODS: This scoping review followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Studies involving youth athletes exposed to structured strength training interventions (e.g., resistance, bodyweight, or combined methods) were included. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus was conducted up to April 20th, 2025. Data were descriptively summarized using pre-defined themes and tabulation procedures, and an evidence gap map was generated to depict how research is distributed across training variables, outcome domains, and population characteristics.
RESULTS: Out of 3770 records screened, 342 studies were included. Approximately 90% of trials assessed physical performance outcomes (e.g., strength, power, sprint speed), with limited focus on motor competence, injury prevention, or psychosocial factors. Male participants dominated the sample pool, while sex-specific analyses were uncommon. Studies involving biologically mature adolescents were scarce, and intervention durations varied widely, with numerous studies extending beyond eight weeks. A substantial proportion of studies failed to adequately report key training variables, such as frequency, intensity, supervision methods, limiting replicability, and comparability. Strength training was primarily studied in team sport contexts, especially soccer and rugby, with individual sports under-represented. Psychosocial outcomes, contextual factors (e.g., training environment), and follow-up beyond 6 months were absent in most studies. Technological and innovative approaches, including velocity-based and flywheel training, were limited to pilot studies. The evidence gap map revealed critical deficiencies in female representation, long-term follow-up, biological maturation assessment, and multidimensional outcome evaluation.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence indicates that youth strength training has been widely studied in relation to physical performance, injury-related outcomes, and neuromuscular development. However, important evidence gaps remain regarding biological maturity, sex-specific responses, psychosocial outcomes, long-term follow-up and context-specific applications. This scoping review identifies these gaps and highlights key priorities for future research rather than providing definitive recommendations for training practice or policy.
PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: OSF: https://osf.io/qnh25 , DOI: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QNH25 .

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Different Neuromuscular Training Modalities and Doses on Lower-Limb Injury Prevention in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower-limb injuries are common in athletes. Neuromuscular training (NMT) is widely promoted, but the comparative effectiveness of different modalities and the optimal dose remain uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library and Embase were searched to 1 August 2025. Eligible trials compared NMT with a control in athletes and reported lower-limb injury outcomes. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Two reviewers screened, extracted and assessed risk of bias. Prespecified subgroups examined modality and dose (frequency, session duration, intervention length), age, sex and sport. Certainty was rated with GRADE.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven RCTs (27,663 participants) were included. NMT was associated with reduced lower-limb injury risk (RR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82), although trim-and-fill adjustment attenuated the estimate. Structured (RR = 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.82) and multidimensional programmes (RR = 0.76, 95% CI 0.61-0.93) showed favourable pooled estimates, with no statistically significant between-modality difference. Favourable pooled estimates were also observed in adolescents (RR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.55-0.81) and young adults (RR = 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.99), and in football (RR = 0.71) and basketball (RR = 0.66); however, the between-age difference did not remain statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, and no statistically significant differences were detected between sport subgroups. Low-certainty, study-level subgroup analyses yielded favourable pooled estimates for programmes delivered 2-3 times per week, for 16-25 min per session, and over intervention periods of 1.5-12 months; however, these associations did not establish a causal or optimal dose. Certainty was very low overall and low to very low across dosage comparisons.
CONCLUSIONS: NMT may reduce lower-limb injury risk, but the magnitude of benefit remains very uncertain. Structured and multidimensional programmes, together with programmes delivered at moderate frequency and duration, showed favourable pooled estimates in exploratory subgroup analyses; however, the dose-related findings represent study-level associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal or optimal dose. These findings may inform the design of routine training programmes, while future high-quality RCTs should address adherence, long-term sustainability, and dose-response interactions across sports and populations.

articles.title: Internalizing and externalizing symptoms and social problem-solving difficulties in adolescents in residential care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents in residential care frequently present mental health and psychosocial adjustment difficulties. However, within this population, research comparing adolescents with documented maltreatment histories and those placed due to other documented inadequate-care or protection-related situations remains scarce. This study aimed to analyze emotional and behavioral problems and social problem-solving difficulties among adolescents in residential care and to examine, among those with maltreatment histories, their association with sociocognitive processes.
METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study included 84 adolescents aged 12-17 years in residential care, divided into a group with a documented history of maltreatment (n = 59) and a group placed due to other documented inadequate-care or protection-related situations (n = 25). The Child and Adolescent Assessment System (SENA) and the Social Cognitive Attitudes and Strategies Questionnaire (AECS) were used. Group differences were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U tests. Within the maltreatment group, partial Spearman correlations and linear regression models were performed, controlling for age, sex, polyvictimization, and length of stay in residential care. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: Adolescents with documented maltreatment histories showed higher scores in anxiety, posttraumatic symptomatology, attention problems, and global behavioral problems, with small to small-to-moderate effect sizes (all adjusted p = 0.032), whereas no group differences were found in social problem-solving difficulties. Within the maltreatment group, significant partial correlations showed that anxiety and social anxiety were associated with greater social problem-solving difficulties. Behavioral symptoms, particularly attention problems and antisocial behavior, showed significant associations with social problem-solving difficulties. The Emotional Index × Behavioral Index interaction was associated with difficulty obtaining information and difficulty generating solutions after adjustment for covariates and multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.048 for both). This association was strongest at low Emotional Index levels and weakened as the Emotional Index increased.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide a better understanding of the psychological vulnerability and sociocognitive functioning of adolescents in residential care with documented maltreatment histories. They suggest a differentiated pattern linking behavioral and anxiety-related symptoms, particularly social anxiety, to social problem-solving difficulties. Future studies should evaluate integrated interventions combining emotional regulation, behavioral regulation, and social problem-solving in residential care settings.

articles.title: Emotional childhood trauma, attachment dimensions, and depression severity in women with major depressive disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood trauma is a well-established risk factor for depression in adulthood. However, its clinical correlates may differ according to trauma subtype and patient population. In women with major depressive disorder, attachment-related interpersonal patterns may be relevant to understanding variation in depressive symptom severity. This study examined childhood trauma subtypes, attachment anxiety, attachment avoidance, and depression severity in adult women with major depressive disorder.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 120 adult women with major depressive disorder who had not yet initiated pharmacological or psychotherapeutic treatment for the current depressive episode. Participants completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-33, the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale-Short Form, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Spearman correlation analyses were used to examine bivariate relationships among study variables. Exploratory cross-sectional indirect association models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were estimated to examine whether attachment dimensions statistically accounted for the associations between childhood trauma subtypes and depression severity.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 35.85 years (SD = 12.53), and the mean PHQ-9 score was 16.48 (SD = 5.03). Overall childhood trauma was correlated with PHQ-9 scores (ρ = 0.246, p < 0.01). Among trauma subtypes, emotional abuse (ρ = 0.203, p < 0.05), physical abuse (ρ = 0.246, p < 0.01), and emotional neglect (ρ = 0.236, p < 0.01) were correlated with PHQ-9 scores. In exploratory indirect association models, attachment anxiety showed indirect estimates with confidence intervals excluding zero for emotional abuse (B = 0.042, 95% CI [0.003, 0.111]) and emotional neglect (B = 0.037, 95% CI [0.004, 0.101]). Attachment avoidance showed indirect estimates with confidence intervals excluding zero for emotional abuse (B = 0.037, 95% CI [0.001, 0.112]), physical abuse (B = 0.061, 95% CI [0.001, 0.177]), sexual abuse (B = 0.092, 95% CI [0.009, 0.228]), and emotional neglect (B = 0.030, 95% CI [0.001, 0.091]).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that attachment-related interpersonal processes may be relevant to the association between childhood trauma and depression severity in women with major depressive disorder. However, given the cross-sectional design and the exploratory nature of the indirect association analyses, the results should be interpreted cautiously and require replication in larger longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Associations between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying among adolescents: a three-wave longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Negative bystander behaviors significantly shape the trajectory of cyberbullying incidents. Previous research has established a link between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying. However, little is known about the longitudinal mechanisms underlying this relationship. To address this gap, the current study investigated the mediating role of callous‑unemotional traits and the moderating role of perceived social support in the longitudinal association between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying.
METHODS: A total of 1531 Chinese adolescents (49.8% female) with an average age of 16.12 years (SD = 0.34) participated in a three-wave longitudinal study with 6-month intervals. Validated self-report measures were used to assess childhood emotional maltreatment, callous‑unemotional traits, perceived social support, and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying. A moderated mediation model was tested using path analysis with bootstrapping (5000 resamples), after confirming the measurement model via confirmatory factor analysis.
RESULTS: The results revealed that childhood emotional maltreatment was positively associated with negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying 12 months later, and this association was mediated by callous‑unemotional traits. Perceived social support buffered the association between childhood emotional maltreatment and callous‑unemotional traits and mitigated the link between callous‑unemotional traits and negative bystander behavior. Further findings revealed that the indirect pathway of callous‑unemotional traits was more pronounced when levels of perceived social support were low, and higher levels of perceived social support could disrupt the mediating pathway of callous‑unemotional traits between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying.
CONCLUSIONS: This study enhances understanding of the longitudinal mechanisms linking childhood emotional maltreatment to negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying through callous‑unemotional traits. The findings highlight the importance of promoting perceived social support as a buffer that can disrupt this mediating pathway, providing empirical evidence for interventions aimed at reducing negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying among adolescents.

articles.title: The impostor phenomenon in Palestinian higher education: associations with self-esteem, anxiety, and competitiveness - a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Impostor syndrome (IS) is characterized by persistent self-doubt and feelings of intellectual fraudulence despite objective evidence of competence. Although IS has been widely studied among healthcare professionals and medical students, evidence among university students from diverse academic disciplines in Palestine remains scarce. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of IS among Palestinian university students and identify factors associated with its severity.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate students at An-Najah National University, Palestine, between March and May 2026. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire that included sociodemographic and academic characteristics, the Arabic Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS), the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7). Descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and multivariable linear regression were performed to identify factors associated with IS.
RESULTS: A total of 430 students participated (median age: 20 years; 77.9% female). The mean CIPS score was 56.2 ± 16.0. Based on established cutoffs, 47.2% of participants reported moderate impostor feelings, 29.3% frequent impostor feelings, and 6.5% intense impostor feelings, while only 17.0% reported few impostor feelings. CIPS scores were positively correlated with anxiety (ρ = 0.341, p < .001) and negatively correlated with self-esteem (ρ = -0.555, p < .001). In multivariable linear regression analysis, higher anxiety scores (β = 0.163, p < .001), lower self-esteem scores (β = -0.486, p < .001), age ≥ 20 years (β = 0.131-0.132, p ≤ .005), and competitiveness (β = 0.125, p = .016) were independently associated with higher IS severity. The final model explained 40.9% of the variance in CIPS scores (R² = 0.409).
CONCLUSIONS: Impostor syndrome was highly prevalent among Palestinian university students, with more than one-third reporting frequent or intense impostor feelings. Lower self-esteem, higher anxiety, older age, and competitiveness were independently associated with greater IS severity. University-based interventions aimed at enhancing self-esteem and addressing anxiety may help reduce impostor feelings and improve students' psychological well-being.

articles.title: A comparative study of network structures between different sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms in adolescents with and without non-suicidal self-injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine association networks between sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms among adolescents with and without non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), compare network structures and global connectivity between the two groups, and identify key bridge nodes within each network.
METHODS: A total of 8,102 Chinese adolescents were included, comprising 1,996 in the NSSI group and 6,106 in the Non-NSSI group. Nine types of sedentary behaviors and 20 depressive symptoms from the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) were assessed using self-reported questionnaires. Based on a mixed correlation matrix, sedentary behavior-depressive symptom networks were estimated separately for the two groups using the extended Bayesian information criterion graphical LASSO (EBICglasso), and bridge strength and one-step bridge expected influence were computed. A network comparison test was conducted to compare network structure and global strength between groups, along with covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Significant differences in network structure were observed between the two groups (M = 0.114, P < 0.001), indicating distinct conditional association patterns between sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms in adolescents with and without NSSI. The global strength was 11.913 for the NSSI group and 11.476 for the Non-NSSI group, with a non-significant difference of 0.437 (3.8%, P = 0.636). In the NSSI group, mobile phone/tablet use, offline classes/tutoring, and sitting and chatting showed higher bridge expected influence, while difficulty concentrating, reduced speech, and restless sleep emerged as prominent bridge symptom nodes. After covariate adjustment, the network structure differences remained statistically significant, whereas differences in global strength remained non-significant; core bridge nodes were largely preserved in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Although differences were observed in the specific association structures of sedentary behavior-depressive symptom networks between adolescents with and without NSSI, there was no evidence that the NSSI group exhibited significantly higher overall network connectivity. Mobile phone/tablet use, study-related sedentary behaviors, sitting and chatting, and symptoms related to attention, sleep, and social withdrawal may represent important candidate nodes for future longitudinal studies and risk screening; however, their causal roles and potential intervention value require further investigation.

articles.title: Exploring parents' experiences of palliative care in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU): a meta-synthesis of qualitative research.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When the goals of care for a critically ill child in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) shift from curative treatment toward palliative care, parents' experiences are often complex and multifaceted. This review aimed primarily to synthesize qualitative evidence on parents' experiences and, secondarily, to examine the interpretive relevance and boundaries of Weick's sensemaking framework after the data-driven synthesis had been completed.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative systematic review using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) meta-aggregation approach. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ProQuest were searched from inception to 2 February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted author-generated analytical findings and supporting participant illustrations, and appraised methodological quality. Findings were synthesized inductively; the 15 resulting subdomains were subsequently mapped to Weick's seven properties of sensemaking.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. Meta-aggregation generated five interrelated synthesized findings: (1) confronting and understanding the end-of-life reality; (2) finding recognition and support through relational networks; (3) maintaining the parental role; (4) safeguarding comfort, dignity, and farewell; and (5) continuing care and connection after the child's death.
CONCLUSIONS: Parents' experiences encompassed efforts to understand a changing clinical situation, rely on relationships with clinicians and others, remain involved as parents, protect the child's comfort and dignity, and sustain connection after death. Weick's framework helped interpret how parents used clinical cues, relationships, identity, and caregiving actions to construct a workable understanding of events, but gave less attention to grief-related emotions, surrogate decision-making burden, cultural and spiritual meaning, organizational constraints, and continuing bonds. The findings may inform family-centered communication, parental-role support, individualized end-of-life care, and bereavement services in the PICU.

articles.title: Metabolic and hormonal biomarkers in pregnancies with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (formerly polycystic ovary syndrome): a nested prospective cohort study with longitudinal sub-analysis.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do metabolic and hormonal biomarker profiles in early pregnancy and their longitudinal variations across gestation differ among women at high risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with and without polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly polycystic ovary syndrome [PCOS]), and are they associated with maternal and neonatal complications?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Among pregnant women at high risk of GDM, PMOS was associated with persistently elevated free androgen index (FAI) throughout pregnancy, whereas no interaction between elevated FAI and PMOS status on maternal and neonatal complications was identified.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Insulin resistance and hyperandrogenism are important pathophysiologic features of PMOS and are also part of the physiological changes during normal pregnancy. Pregnancies with PMOS have been associated with a higher risk of maternal and neonatal complications than those without PMOS.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Nested prospective cohort study with longitudinal sub-analysis using pooled data from two international multicentre clinical trials (TOBOGM study and B2B&Me trial). A total of 151 pregnancies at high risk for GDM were included from January 2018 to December 2021.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: At baseline (before 24 weeks' gestation), 151 pregnancies at high risk for GDM were included (65 PMOS and 86 non-PMOS). Longitudinal sub-analysis included 75 pregnancies (15 PMOS and 60 non-PMOS). Metabolic biomarkers (fasting plasma glucose [FPG], insulin, C-peptide) and hormonal biomarkers (testosterone, dihydrotestosterone [DHT], androstenedione [A4], sex hormone-binding globulin [SHBG], and anti-Mullerian hormone [AMH]) were measured to derive indices of insulin resistance (homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [HOMA-IR], quantitative insulin sensitivity check index [QUICKI], fasting glucose to insulin ratio [FGIR]) and FAI. These were assessed cross-sectionally and in exploratory longitudinal sub-analyses of a subset of participants across gestation using linear mixed-effects models. Interaction analyses explored whether biomarkers modified associations between PMOS and adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: PMOS was associated with higher pre-pregnancy and baseline BMI and greater insulin resistance (elevated fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and FGIR, and lower QUICKI). Androgen profiles differed significantly, with PMOS associated with higher DHT (167.8 vs 121.2 pg/ml, P = 0.003) and FAI (0.9 vs 0.5, P < 0.001) and lower SHBG (159.1 vs 215.3 nmol/l, P = 0.012), compared with non-PMOS controls. FAI in early pregnancy was independently associated with PMOS (geometric mean ratio 1.9, P = 0.003) and, in exploratory longitudinal sub-analyses, remained elevated throughout pregnancy in women with PMOS. Maternal and neonatal complications did not differ between groups, and no interactions between FAI, PMOS status, and composite adverse outcomes were identified.
LIMITATIONS REASONS FOR CAUTION: The selective inclusion of a high-risk cohort limited generalization. Minimized or neutralized differences in maternal and neonatal outcomes between groups may be observed due to timely screening, diagnosis, and intervention within the parent RCT protocols. Since this was a sub-study, no formal a priori power calculation was conducted. Consequently, the study may possess limited statistical power to identify smaller effect sizes, longitudinal changes, and interaction effects; therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: Persistently elevated FAI throughout pregnancy, potentially reflecting an inadequate protective SHBG response to pregnancy-induced androgen excess. Whether elevated FAI contributes to adverse pregnancy outcomes in PMOS warrants further longitudinal evaluation.
FUNDING: TOBOGM was funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council (NMHRC; grants 1104231 and 2009326), the Region Örebro Research Committee (grants Dnr OLL-970566 and OLL-942177), Medical Scientific Fund of the Mayor of Vienna (project 15205), the South-Western Sydney Local Health District Academic Unit (grant 2016), and a Western Sydney University Ainsworth Trust Grant (2019). B2B&Me was funded by the European Union Commission Horizon 2020 grant entitled 'Implementation Action to Prevent Diabetes from Bump 2 Baby (IMPACT DIABETES B2B&Me)' under grant agreement 847984, with collaborative NHMRC, Australia co-funding under grant number APP1194234. The project was sponsored by the University College Dublin. S.A., A.C.H.N., and T.M. are supported by Graduate Research Scholarships provided by Monash University. K.R. is supported by a scholarship from the NHMRC. S.J.E., H.T., and A.M. are supported by fellowships from the NHMRC.
DISCLOSURES: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBERS: ACTRN12616000924459 and ACTRN12620001240932.

articles.title: The management of endometriosis in adolescents and young adults: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: What evidence-based strategies are used in the treatment of endometriosis-associated symptoms in adolescents and young adults?
SUMMARY ANSWER: The use of hormonal therapies and surgery was associated with improvements in pain symptoms in most studies; however, the certainty of evidence was very low, meaning that the true impact of these treatments remains uncertain.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Endometriosis is a chronic condition estimated to affect 1 in 10 women, with symptoms commonly present during adolescence. Current management strategies for endometriosis include analgesia, hormonal suppression, and surgery, as well as non-pharmacological measures.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This is a systematic review of the literature. Six databases (CINAHL, Cochrane Central Database of Controlled Trials, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsychInfo, and Web of Science Core Collection) were searched from inception to May 2026. Search terms were related to endometriosis combined with terms regarding management and the adolescent age group.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Eligible studies included participants aged under 24 years with endometriosis and reported on outcomes in the management of endometriosis-associated symptoms. Only studies with full texts or data available in English were included. Screening and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two authors. Key outcomes included pain, quality of life, recurrence, and side effects. Data were reported narratively. Risk of bias was assessed according to study design (ROB2, NOS, and JBI tools) and quality of evidence with the GRADE system.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The search identified 14 376 records, of which 333 full texts were assessed for eligibility, and 23 studies, with a combined total of 1561 participants, were included. There were two randomised controlled trials, one single-arm open-label interventional study, eleven cohort studies, and nine case series. Five studies investigated hormonal treatments, one other study assessed other pharmacological treatments, sixteen studies assessed surgical management with or without hormonal treatment, and one study investigated non-pharmacological treatments. Most studies reported improvements in pain symptoms; however, there was heterogeneity in study design, length of follow-up, and outcome measures.
LIMITATIONS REASONS FOR CAUTION: There is limited evidence in this age group. Most studies had a moderate risk of bias, and the certainty of evidence was very low.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: The very low certainty of evidence limits the ability to draw inferences from the data. More high-quality research is essential to understand the effectiveness of current treatments and identify how they should be tailored for this age group.
FUNDING: No specific external or departmental funding was received for this systematic review.
DISCLOSURES: C.M.B. declares research grants from US DoD, NIH, EU Horizon 2020, Bayer AG, Aspira Ltd, Exeltis Ltd, Proteomics Inc, and Serac Healthcare Ltd, and consulting fees from Gedeon Richter, Theramex, Gesynta, and Roche (all paid to institution). S.A.M. is Field Chief Editor for Frontiers in Reproductive Health (personal fee) and is an advisory board member for the LIDEA Registry (personal fee) and has unpaid roles with Human Reproduction Statistical Advisory Board and the NextGen Jane Advisory Board, the Society for Women's Health Research, WERF, WES, ASRM, and ESHRE. K.V. reports research grants from the NIHR, NIH, UKRI, Medical Research Foundation, and EU IMI-2, consulting fees from Gesynta and Reckitts, and speakers' fees from Reckitts, Organon, Gedeon Richter, and Eli Lilly (all payments to institution). Some of the above companies manufacture treatments discussed in this review.

articles.title: Image-Based AI for the Diagnosis of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is one of the major causes of preventable blindness in premature infants. Early screening, accurate diagnosis, and severity classification are crucial for reducing irreversible visual impairment. Recently, image-based AI models have been widely applied to ROP screening, diagnosis, and severity classification. However, the model architecture, data source, validation method, and diagnostic task vary across studies. Consequently, the overall diagnostic efficiency and clinical utility of deep learning (DL) remain to be systematically assessed.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of image-based AI for ROP by disease type, validation method, model type, and use of transfer learning (TL).
METHODS: We performed a systematic search across Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Cochrane Library as of October 12, 2026, to identify studies investigating image-based AI for ROP detection or clinical subtype classification. The risk of bias (RoB) of included studies was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using bivariate mixed-effects models, with analyses stratified by diagnostic task and validation method.
RESULTS: Sixty-two studies contributed 185 contingency tables. For normal vs ROP, pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.96) and specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.97). For normal vs treatment-requiring ROP (TR-ROP), sensitivity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.91-0.99) and specificity was 0.74 (95% CI 0.66-0.80). For mild vs severe ROP, specificity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.59-0.90). In external validation, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.97) and 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.90), respectively, while the corresponding estimates were 0.95 (95% CI 0.93-0.96) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) in internal validation. For DL and conventional machine learning (ML) models, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98), respectively, while specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-0.94), respectively. With and without TL, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.97), respectively, while specificity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.95), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Image-based AI may have high sensitivity for ROP assessment, but its specificity is lower for identifying TR-ROP and in the external-validation subgroup. Given the predominance of retrospective studies, heterogeneity, and limited external validation, current evidence supports AI as an adjunct to screening and referral, with clinicians retaining responsibility for diagnostic and treatment decisions. Prospective, multicenter external validation is needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261418502; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418502.

articles.title: Digital health interventions for medication adherence and adherence-related outcomes in pediatric oncology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication non-adherence can compromise treatment outcomes in pediatric oncology. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may support medication-taking behavior and related skills. This review evaluated DHIs for medication adherence and adherence-related outcomes in pediatric oncology.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through December 2025. Study characteristics and outcomes were extracted into a shared spreadsheet. Direct adherence outcomes were distinguished from self-efficacy, knowledge, treatment intention, feasibility, and acceptability. Random-effects models were used for the quantitative syntheses, which were interpreted according to their underlying designs and measures.
RESULTS: After removal of 2,214 duplicates, 827 records were screened and nine reports were included. The pooled post-intervention objective adherence proportion was 76% (95% CI: 59%-87%; I2 = 76.0%); this descriptive proportion does not establish an intervention effect. Three studies contributed to the exploratory within-intervention standardized mean-change synthesis (0.46, 95% CI: 0.14-0.78; I2 = 84.0%). Because the underlying measures differed, this estimate was not interpreted as a single adherence effect. Randomized between-group findings and uncontrolled observations were reported separately.
CONCLUSION: DHIs may support medication adherence and related outcomes in pediatric oncology; however, the pooled post-intervention adherence proportion should not be interpreted as evidence of effectiveness. Heterogeneity in interventions, outcomes, and measurement methods warrants cautious interpretation.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420261510631.

articles.title: De-identification of child protection intake reports using relationship-based replacement (DI-REBAR).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child protection contacts are documented in the form of child protection intake reports detailing the child(ren) suspected to be at risk of harm, the notifier's concerns, the alleged person responsible, and other details. These narrative reports remain untapped for statistical reporting and research purposes due to being text-based as well as containing extremely sensitive content. Applying a contextual de-identification approach to child protection narratives opens up the possibility of large-scale automated analysis by external researchers while preserving data privacy and relational meaning.
DATA: 10,000 randomly selected South Australian Department for Child Protection intake reports were provided for this study. A total of 300 (200 development, 100 evaluation) were randomly selected, manually reviewed and annotated.
METHODS: We designed and implemented a context-preserving de-identification pipeline called De-Identification via Relationship-Based Replacement (DI-REBAR) on 10,000 reports while preserving the noted relationships between named individuals. A total of seven indirect identifiers (date, time, school, early learning centre, hospital, prison, sensitive reference numbers) and three direct identifiers (name, address, phone number) were selected for de-identification. A relationship table was temporarily created to map individuals and their relationship to the child of interest, with direct identifiers replaced. Indirect identifiers were replaced by list-based replacement and regular expressions.
RESULTS: DI-REBAR evaluation showed promising results in macro precision (>0.98), recall (>0.88), and F1-Score (>0.92) across nine out of the ten identifier classes (prison excluded). Each identifier had a range of precision (0.74-1.00), recall (0.61-1.00), and F1-Score (0.66-1.00). Address, phone number, and date have the best performances (>0.98) across precision, recall, and F1-Score.
CONCLUSION: This is the first Australian study to automatically de-identify sensitive child protection data whilst preserving relationship information, allowing large-scale text analysis by external researchers in a data custodian's controlled environment. This approach can be applied to other areas that rely on unstructured data such as court documents and police reports. However, human reviewers are still needed to ensure identifiable information is not disclosed.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stromal cells for periventricular hemorrhagic infarction in extremely preterm infants: a double-blinded randomized controlled phase IIa clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periventricular hemorrhagic infarction in extremely preterm infants (PVHI; the most severe form of intraventricular hemorrhage) are associated with a high risk of mortality and neurodevelopmental disability with no effective treatments. We aimed to assess the safety and potential efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) for PVHI in preterm infants.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, phase 2a double-blind randomized controlled trial at the Samsung Medical Center. Twenty-two preterm infants (23-31 weeks gestation) with PVHI were double-blindly randomized (1:1) to receive intraventricular MSCs (1 × 107 cells/kg) or normal saline within 7 days post-diagnosis. Primary outcome was combined rate of ventriculo-peritoneal shunt or death. Secondary outcomes included safety, mortality, cerebral palsy (CP), epilepsy, developmental delays.
RESULTS: The primary endpoint of shunt or death by 36 weeks' postmenstrual age did not differ between groups (relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.64 to 2.03). Among survivors assessed through 2 years' corrected age, the MSC group had lower observed rates of cerebral palsy, epilepsy, and microcephaly than the placebo group, although confidence intervals were wide; lower incidence of CP (relative risk 0.56, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.17), epilepsy (relative risk 0.38, 95% CI 0.10 to 1.36) and microcephaly (relative risk 0.30, 95% CI 0.08 to 1.07). No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred.
