CONCLUSIONS: DHIS2 data quality varies substantially across countries, with country-specific challenges in availability, completeness and consistency. Strengthening facility-level data capture and developing an MNCH data quality module are crucial for improving data reliability.

articles.title: Temporal trends and geospatial heterogeneity in Chagas disease in Mexico, 1998-2024: a multiscale cross-registry analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chagas disease evolves over decades, and notification, hospital-discharge, and mortality systems capture different points in its natural history. We evaluated their temporal concordance in Mexico and whether clustered registered mortality was associated with municipal social deprivation.
METHODS: We analysed notification, hospital-discharge, and mortality data through 2024. We used age-stratified quasi-Poisson models to estimate annual changes, a segmented model to describe notifications, and a registry-by-year model to compare slopes during 2005-2024. We age-standardised municipal deaths, tested for clustering, and modelled them against the 2020 Social Lag Index (SLI), 2019 healthcare supply, ascertainment proxies, and a state random intercept.
RESULTS: Hospital discharges decreased by 5.38% annually (95% confidence interval (CI) = -6.59, -4.16) and mortality by 2.49% (95% CI = -3.44, -1.54). Notification was not log-linear: it rose 10.50% annually to 2017, dropped 27.96% at the category split, then showed no detectable change (-2.26%; 95% CI = -4.77, 0.32). Slopes differed (P < 0.001), although notification's common-period change was indeterminate (1.25%; 95% CI = -0.79, 3.34). Among 2,475 municipalities, 253 recorded 735 deaths, with clustered residuals (Moran's I = 0.430). A 43-municipality High-High core remained after multiplicity correction; cluster death shares are post-selection statistics. A one-standard-deviation higher SLI was associated with registered mortality (incidence rate ratio = 1.48; dependence-robust 95% CI = 1.20, 2.08), but residual spatial autocorrelation persisted (Moran's I = 0.205); the interval included one after joint adjustment for two ascertainment proxies, and no spatial model met its reliability gate; the association is exploratory. Chronic disease predominated, and acute notification rates plateaued across 25-59 years. Infant notifications averaged 1.12 per year during 2017-2024, against 2,131 modelled congenital infections (563-4259 across parameter sets), which are different estimands.
CONCLUSIONS: Mexican registries showed no concordant temporal trend. Detection was adult-centred and chronic-dominant during 2005-2024. Registered mortality was spatially clustered; its association with deprivation remains exploratory and unresolved.

articles.title: Cystic fibrosis in China: addressing the cycle of underdiagnosis and treatment inaccessibility.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is substantially underdiagnosed in China, and access to targeted therapy remains limited. Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy has dramatically improved survival internationally, yet none has been approved or entered clinical trials in China. A circular problem contributes to this situation: CF is not included in newborn screening programmes because it has historically been considered extremely rare in East Asian populations. Yet, fewer than 300 patients have been genetically confirmed, in part due to limited diagnostic infrastructure. Epidemiological data based on carrier frequency suggest the true affected population exceeds 17,000 individuals. Patients who receive a molecular diagnosis face additional challenges, including a CFTR variant spectrum that differs from Western populations without established theratyping pathways, and the absence of regulatory submissions for CFTR modulators. Here, we discuss three potential approaches: expanding diagnostic capacity through standardised sweat chloride testing and clinician education, building theratyping infrastructure via patient-derived organoid biobanks, and applying existing rare disease regulatory pathways to facilitate drug approval.

articles.title: Future vaccine priorities in Cambodia: preparedness for emerging infectious diseases.
articles.abstract: Cambodia has achieved substantial progress in immunisation over the past two decades, culminating in one of Southeast Asia's most successful COVID-19 vaccination campaigns. However, the epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing. Climate change, environmental degradation, urbanisation, increasing regional mobility, and intensified human-animal interactions are increasing the risk of emerging infectious diseases, placing Cambodia at the frontline of future epidemic and pandemic threats. Although national vaccine policy has traditionally focused on childhood immunisation, preparedness for emerging infectious diseases requires a broader strategy that integrates pathogen surveillance, genomic monitoring, regulatory readiness, rapid vaccine platforms, and One Health collaboration. Here, we highlight the need for Cambodia to transition from a vaccine delivery agenda toward a broader vaccine preparedness agenda. We propose a national framework centred around surveillance-informed vaccine prioritisation, strengthened laboratory and genomic capacity, resilient vaccine delivery systems, sustainable financing, and regional partnerships. Such an approach could enhance Cambodia's preparedness for pathogens including H5N1, dengue, Japanese encephalitis, rabies, and future Disease X scenarios, while strengthening its contribution to regional health security.

articles.title: Underrecognised legacies of preeclampsia: a biosocial DOHaD perspective for research in sub-Saharan Africa.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is often approached as an acute obstetric complication, yet its longer-term implications for maternal and offspring health remain insufficiently understood, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Preeclampsia is a significant contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in SSA. Although its clinical management has improved, particularly in high-income countries, important questions remain regarding its causes, long-term consequences, and the extent to which existing evidence applies to SSA populations. In this viewpoint, we propose that conceptualising preeclampsia in SSA through a biosocial Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) lens provides a useful framework for investigating how biological, social, and environmental processes jointly shape maternal and offspring health across the life course. We review evidence and identify four priority domains for investigation: understanding context-specific causes and mechanisms; improving detection, care-seeking, and health system pathways; examining long-term maternal and offspring outcomes; and strengthening research infrastructures. We argue that advancing research on preeclampsia in SSA requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate biological, clinical, epidemiological, and qualitative research. Such a research agenda has the potential to improve understanding of preeclampsia beyond its acute manifestations and to inform more equitable strategies for maternal and child health across the life course.

articles.title: Expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wheezing is a very common symptom in preschool children. Compared with that of older children with wheezing or asthma, the morbidity and health care utilization of preschool are disproportionately high, imposing a heavy economic burden on the health care system and society. Furthermore, severe and frequent wheezing in early life is associated with a trajectory of poor lung function, which is associated with respiratory and non-respiratory health outcomes in later adulthood, including high-risk chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and high-risk cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in middle age. However, recurrent preschool wheezing, which is defined as two or more wheezing episodes in children younger than 6 years, excluding bronchiolitis, is highly heterogeneous in etiology and prognosis and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges for pediatricians.
METHODS: Thirty Chinese experts majoring in pediatric pulmonology and epidemiology were invited to write this practical consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children on the basis of evidence collection and experience. Elucidation and reviews were conducted using electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang databases. We used variations in terms for "wheezing", "asthma", "wheezing bronchitis", "preschool", "children", and "pediatric".
RESULTS: The etiology, evaluation, management of acute wheezing exacerbation, and strategy of long-term anti-inflammatory therapy in recurrent preschool wheezing are highlighted. The most common causes of preschool wheezing are virus-induced wheezing and asthma (typical wheezing), some of which require long-term anti-inflammatory therapy. Some other children had identifiable underlying diseases (atypical wheezing). On the basis of the confirmation of wheezing, the underlying diseases and phenotypes of typical wheezing should be carefully investigated. For acute wheezing, inhaled short-acting β₂-agonists are the first-line agents, and systemic corticosteroids should be reserved only for severe cases. Routine use of azithromycin is not recommended in acute wheezing. The decision to initiate long-term anti-inflammatory therapy for recurrent preschool wheezing should be based on a comprehensive evaluation of clinical risk indicators and treatable traits such as type 2 inflammation. Immunomodulators such as bacterial lysates may be considered for use in trials in preschool children with recurrent virus-induced wheezing.
CONCLUSIONS: This symptom-based, phenotype-oriented consensus provides practical guidance for the individualized management of heterogeneous recurrent wheezing in preschool children. Further studies are needed to identify clinical risk factors and biomarkers for persistent wheezing and asthma. More appropriate long-term treatment regimens should also be explored.

articles.title: Improved sleep and clinical outcomes following a single-session intervention among adolescents with borderline personality disorder features.
articles.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a serious mental illness that often emerges in adolescence. Although efficacious treatments have been developed, they are often lengthy, expensive, inaccessible, and require specialized training to deliver. Optimizing BPD prevention and early treatment is an important public health priority. Disrupted sleep is closely linked to key BPD features, and prior research has documented a range of sleep problems among BPD samples that appear to worsen symptom course and duration. This intervention trial (NCT04507308) assessed the effects of a single-session sleep-focused treatment on adolescent sleep and BPD-related symptoms. Fifty-seven adolescents (ages 13-18) with 3+ clinically impairing BPD features and at least some self-reported sleep-related difficulties participated with a caregiver. Participants completed baseline surveys, interviews, and 10-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) protocol to examine BPD symptoms and sleep in daily life. Youth also collected at-home ambulatory electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings before undergoing the treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention. Post-treatment, youth practiced their new sleep routine for approximately one month before undergoing reassessment (EMA, EEG, surveys). Many indices of sleep quantity and quality improved across both objective (EEG) and subjective assessments (EMA and self- and caregiver-report). Youth reported an earlier clock time at sleep onset and earlier waketime, more sleep, and fewer awakenings in daily life. Every sleep-related questionnaire score improved at post-intervention and was maintained at one-month follow-up. Multiple (though not all) indices of BPD symptoms also improved significantly. Findings suggest sleep may be a promising intervention target for at-risk youth.

articles.title: Adverse childhood experiences, social isolation and loneliness across adulthood: A nationwide cross-sectional study of Chinese adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loneliness and social isolation are distinct risk factors for depression and other affective disorders but are often conflated. Whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate differently to the two, and whether this varies across adulthood, is unclear.
METHODS: We analysed 24,219 adults from the nationwide 2024 Psychology and Behaviour Investigation of Chinese Residents. Seven ACE domains were assessed with items adapted from the WHO ACE-IQ. Social isolation (three-item structural index, score ≥ 2) and loneliness (two-item functional index, score 2) were defined using indices adapted from the UK Biobank. Adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated by modified Poisson regression with city-clustered standard errors; a stacked model compared the two outcomes.
RESULTS: Social isolation (30.0%) and loneliness (11.0%) overlapped weakly (kappa 0.17). Each additional ACE was associated with higher prevalence of loneliness (PR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.28) and, more weakly, isolation (PR 1.04, 1.01-1.08; ratio of PRs 1.19, 1.17-1.22). All seven domains were associated with loneliness; only emotional abuse, witnessed violence and, marginally, physical abuse were associated with isolation; sexual abuse, household substance use, household mental illness and parental incarceration were not. The association of ≥4 ACEs with loneliness strengthened with age (P for interaction <0.001; PR 2.71, 1.98-3.72, at ≥60 years).
LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design and retrospectively self-reported ACEs preclude causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: ACEs were more strongly associated with loneliness than with social isolation, particularly in later life. Among adults with ACE histories, asking about loneliness may capture disconnection that structural indicators such as living arrangements or contact frequency miss.

articles.title: Associations of academic time burden with depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents: A prospective multi-analytical study based on the Guangzhou Children and Adolescents Cohort.
articles.abstract: Academic pressure is a pervasive source of stress among secondary school students, and has been linked to higher risks of depression and anxiety. However, the association of academic time burden with depressive and anxiety symptoms, and the behavioral and symptom-level patterns involved, remain insufficiently understood. Using data from the Guangzhou Children and Adolescents Cohort, this study aimed to investigate whether self-reported academic time was longitudinally associated with elevated depressive and anxiety symptoms among adolescents. We curated the homework time, tutoring time, health-related behaviors, and depressive (CES-D-20) and anxiety (GAD-7) symptoms reported by participants, yielding depression (n = 9671, 44.7% girls) and anxiety (n = 4680, 41.1% girls) cohorts. Mixed-effects regression showed that longer homework time was significantly associated with both elevated depressive (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.03-1.15 per hour increase) and anxiety symptoms (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.19), with similar patterns for tutoring time (depressive: OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.08; anxiety: OR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.10-1.21). Sleep duration mediated 20.4% and 26.9% of the associations of homework time with depressive and anxiety symptoms, respectively. The corresponding proportions for tutoring time were 9.5% and 2.1%, with the latter being non-significant. Network analysis revealed that baseline academic time was associated with somatic symptoms and uncontrollable worry during follow-up, and that anxiety and depressive symptoms were reciprocally associated over time. These findings add to the rationale for policies that regulate academic time and highlight sleep protection as a promising target for adolescent mental health.

articles.title: WGS2IBI: a cloud-based workflow for individualized Bayesian inference from whole genome sequencing data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scalable and reproducible genomic workflows that support both individual- and population-level analyses are critically needed in precision medicine. We present WGS2IBI, a cloud-based, modular workflow that integrates whole-genome sequencing (WGS) preprocessing, population-level variant screening, and the previously developed Individualized Bayesian Inference (IBI) framework within a reproducible analysis pipeline. Implemented using the Common Workflow Language (CWL) and Docker, WGS2IBI ensures portability and reproducibility across computational environments.
RESULTS: Benchmarking on the Jackson Heart Study (JHS) TOPMed Freeze 9 cohort demonstrated efficient large-scale genomic processing and analysis. Preprocessing reduced 102 million variants to 18 million variants in approximately two hours at a total cost of $20.83. Population-level analyses using Global Search and Fisher's exact test (FET) were completed for $0.44 and $11.44, respectively. Individual-level analysis using IBIwas completed for $3.66. Analyses across additional TOPMed cohorts showed predictable scaling across cohort and chromosome sizes. Deployment on both BioData Catalyst (BDC) and the Gabriella Miller Kids First (KF) Data Resource Center via CAVATICA further demonstrated portability across two major NIH cloud ecosystems. To provide a biologically meaningful use case beyond workflow benchmarking, we also applied WGS2IBI to real hypertension data from 1,821 unrelated Framingham Heart Study (FHS) participants, where IBI-prioritized variants were enriched for lower minor allele frequency and included variants mapping to genes with prior blood-pressure relevance.
CONCLUSIONS: WGS2IBI provides a scalable, reproducible, and accessible workflow resource for WGS analysis, enabling efficient population- and individual-level genetic studies without local installation. Dual deployment on BDC and KF expands usability across diverse NIH genomic ecosystems, supporting both adult and pediatric research communities. This workflow lowers practical computational barriers for large-scale WGS studies and enables integrated evaluation of individual- and population-level genetic analyses.

articles.title: Rhabdomyolysis in Ugandan children with severe malaria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rhabdomyolysis is a serious clinical syndrome characterized by skeletal muscle injury, release of creatine kinase (CK) and increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). Few studies have examined rhabdomyolysis in severe pediatric malaria.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study. We examined the association of rhabdomyolysis with mortality (Cox proportional hazards models, complete case analysis and multiple imputation by chained equations). We also examined putative mediators of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality.
RESULTS: Of 600 patients in the cohort (median age 2 years, 44% female), 512 (85%) had at least one CK measurement. The median CK was 120 U/L (IQR 44-490) and 73/512 patients (14%) had rhabdomyolysis (CK>1000 U/L). There were 44 deaths in the cohort (case fatality rate 7.3%). Rhabdomyolysis was associated with an unadjusted 2.5-fold increased hazard of mortality (95%CI 1.1-6.1, p=0.038). This estimate remained statistically significant after adjustment for age and sex and after multiple imputation for missing CK values. The odds of AKI (OR 2.0, 95%CI 1.2-3.6, p=0.0085) and hyperkalemia (OR 2.7, 95%CI 1.3-5.5, p=0.0049) were higher among patients with rhabdomyolysis. AKI and hyperkalemia attenuated the effect of rhabdomyolysis in multivariable models. We estimated that the proportion of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality risk mediated by AKI and hyperkalemia was 23% (95% UI 12-41%) and 18% (95% UI 12-29%), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Rhabdomyolysis is common in children with severe malaria and is associated with elevated mortality. Rhabdomyolysis may be a marker of disease severity or may contribute to the pathogenesis of fatal malaria (e.g., via AKI and hyperkalemia).

articles.title: A Survey of Clinical Full-Time Equivalents in Academic Infectious Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No published definition currently exists for a 1.0 clinical full-time equivalent (cFTE) in academic infectious diseases (ID).
METHODS: The Infectious Diseases Society of America's member-led Academic Advisory Panel, with ECG Management Consultants, developed a cFTE work standards survey with questions on division demographics, inpatient shift commitments and patient volumes, and clinical leadership roles. ECG administered the survey via Cvent from August 2024 to February 2025 and employed descriptive analyses to summarize results.
RESULTS: A total of 155 academic ID divisions (109 adult and 46 pediatric divisions) were invited to participate. The global response rate was 65%, with 51% for adult divisions and 98% for pediatric divisions. Most divisions cover <3 facilities and utilize residents and fellows; advanced practice provider support is less common. The method of defining cFTE varied, with most divisions using time-based metrics like weeks on service; productivity measures were less frequent. Adult divisions reported managing more new patient consults and daily encounters. Over one-quarter of divisions reported uncompensated leadership responsibilities. Constructs for a 1.0 cFTE in academic ID for adult and pediatric divisions were developed based on survey results and reflect approximately 22 inpatient service weeks annually with three 4-hour outpatient clinics when off inpatient service.
CONCLUSIONS: We report the first survey of clinical work standards in academic pediatric and adult ID in the United States. ID leaders can utilize this information as a reference for clinical expectations, estimate work relative value unit generation, minimize un- or underfunded work, and negotiate effort and resources accordingly.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis of Standard- and High-Dose Rifampicin to Predict Safety, Completion, and Tolerability of Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy in the 2R2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rifampicin-based tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) may shorten treatment duration, but substantial interindividual pharmacokinetic variability may lead to different safety and tolerability profiles at the same dose. We performed pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analyses of standard- and high-dose rifampicin to predict safety, completion, and tolerability.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 1,368 adults and adolescents enrolled in the 2R2 trial comparing two months of rifampicin at 20 or 30 mg/kg/day with four months at 10 mg/kg/day. A population pharmacokinetic model developed from 440 participants was used to predict rifampicin exposure for all participants. Missing exposure metrics were imputed using 1,000 simulated datasets. Exposure-response relationships were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression models fitted within imputed datasets, with coefficients and standard errors pooled across imputations.
RESULTS: A two-fold increase in total rifampicin exposure (AUC0-24) was associated with higher odds of protocol-defined adverse events (AEs) requiring permanent discontinuation (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.25-2.81), discontinuation unrelated to AEs (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and tolerability symptoms potentially related to AEs without discontinuation (aOR 1.48, 95% CI 1.18-1.86); similar patterns were observed for peak concentration (Cmax). Higher AUC0-24 and Cmax were also associated with grade 1-2 and grade 3-4 AEs, rash/allergy/hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal intolerance, and early discontinuation, with no significant association for hepatotoxicity. Exposure-based models showed slightly better discriminatory performance than dose-based models in predicting safety.
CONCLUSION: Higher rifampicin exposure was associated with worse safety, completion, and tolerability in TPT. Larger efficacy trials are needed to determine the optimal dose to achieve sufficient exposure, alongside investigation of therapeutic drug monitoring to avoid excessive exposure.

articles.title: Prevalence of Powassan Virus Infection in Children with Suspected Lyme Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both Lyme disease and Powassan virus (POWV) are transmitted by the bite of the Ixodes tick. While severe POWV encephalitis cases are uncommon in children, milder infections may be underdiagnosed.
METHODS: We performed a case-control study nested within a prospective cohort of children < 21 years evaluated for Lyme disease at one of eight Pedi Lyme Net emergency departments. We selected children with early or early-disseminated Lyme disease (n=305) with age, sex, center and symptom matched clinical mimics (n=295). Using biobanked research specimens, we performed POWV two-tier serology with confirmatory focus neutralization testing (FNT) and a reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test. We defined a POWV infection with a positive two-tier serology or RT-PCR test. We compared the prevalence of POWV between children with Lyme disease and matched mimics.
RESULTS: Of the 600 included children, the median age was 9 years (interquartile range 6-14 years) and 377 (63%) were male. POWV infection was more common in the children with Lyme disease (8.5%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.4-11.7%) compared to matched mimics (0.7%, 95% CI 0.1-2.4%; difference 7.9%, 95% CI 4.6-11.1; adjusted odds ratio 5.0, 95% CI 1.2-21.9). Of the 28 children with a positive POWV two-tier serology test, 11 (39%) had a positive FNT test. None of the RT-PCR tests were positive (0%, 95% CI 0-0.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial minority of children with Lyme disease had serologic evidence of POWV co-infection compared with matched clinical mimics. Clinically unrecognized POWV infections were more common than previously acknowledged.

articles.title: Trial Endpoints for Aspergillus and Rare Molds: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold disease (IMD) remains a substantial cause of patient morbidity and mortality. Aspergillosis and mucormycosis remain the predominant infections encountered, although rare molds continue to emerge as important pathogens. Improvement in patient outcomes has been the result of progress in risk stratification, diagnostics, supportive care, antifungal therapy, and/or prophylaxis, yet substantial challenges remain, requiring the development of novel treatment strategies. Clinical trials evaluating treatment response are currently based on consensus criteria published in 2008. However, advances in clinical mycology and the broadening variety of mold diseases in clinical trials necessitate a revision of these criteria to ensure that adjudication of patient outcomes accurately captures responses to therapeutic intervention.
METHODS: To tackle this task, an international expert panel nominated by the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) was convened.
RESULTS: The panel produced updated consensus guidance for assessing treatment responses and defining study outcomes in clinical trials of IMD in both adults and children.
CONCLUSIONS: Along with guidance, potential pitfalls in assessing outcome, such as discordant clinical, radiologic, and/or mycologic data and areas for future research are discussed.

articles.title: An observational study of how staff organise daily activities in child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inpatient care within child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS) is provided in highly structured, safety-focused settings for young people with severe mental health conditions. In Sweden, minors receiving compulsory psychiatric care have had a statutory right to daily activities since 2020. However, national inspections have identified shortcomings in care environments and organisational conditions. This study aimed to explore how staff organise and enact daily activities for minors receiving compulsory care in inpatient CAMHS in Sweden.
METHODS: A qualitative observational design was used. Data were generated through 160 h of participant observation, evenly distributed across four Swedish inpatient CAMHS units, and through informal interviews with staff. Observations focused on how staff organised and facilitated daily activities involving minors receiving compulsory care. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis.
RESULTS: Findings revealed a tension between institutional control and staff efforts to enable meaningful daily activities. Three themes were identified: Control in tension with daily activities, Institutional work at a distance from minors' interests, and Cultivating engagement through activities. Safety, routines, and boundary-setting often took precedence over activities. Regulation of peer relationships shaped whether and how staff facilitated shared activities. Competing demands and limited organisational support restricted opportunities to identify and respond to minors' interests, while responsibility for initiating activities was often placed on minors. At times, staff fostered engagement by exploring interests, being available, participating, and creating opportunities for social connection. These enabling practices were less prominent than those centred on control and institutional demands. Access to activities varied with staff availability, competing priorities, and individual staff initiative.
CONCLUSIONS: Daily activities were organised through unit routines, staff initiatives, and available resources, without a distinct approach for minors receiving compulsory care. Similar activity provision in compulsory and voluntary care may not ensure equal opportunities for participation, given the greater restrictions of compulsory care. Realising the statutory right requires organisational structures, clear responsibilities, and integration of activities into unit routines and cultures, alongside staff engagement.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable. This qualitative observational study was not a clinical trial.

articles.title: Estimating the impacts of climate distress amongst an Australian youth population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change is widely recognised as the greatest threat to global health in the 21st century, with young people expected to bear a disproportionate share of its current and future impacts. Consistent with this heightened vulnerability, substantial proportions of young people worldwide report experiencing climate-related distress, yet the impact that climate change has on mental health remains underexplored.
METHODS: This study identified characteristics that were cross-sectionally associated with climate distress amongst a cohort of young Australians who had recently been exposed a series of climate-related events (N = 323, Mage= 20.26). Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were used for this cross-sectional analysis. Further, a longitudinal analysis was conducted using linear mixed models to estimate the impact that climate distress had on mental health symptoms (depression, stress, and anxiety), sleep quality, and substance use over a one-year period (2020-2021).
RESULTS: Cross-sectional analyses demonstrated that females, gender-diverse individuals, and those not engaged in employment, education, or training (NEET) reported significantly higher climate distress at baseline as compared to their respective counterparts. Further, those reporting greater altruism, elevated depression and stress, and lower anxiety also reported higher levels of climate distress at baseline. Linear mixed models (LMMs) revealed climate distress was linked to increasing depression and stress symptoms, but reductions in drug use. Climate distress was not associated with anxiety, sleep quality, or alcohol consumption in LMMs.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that amongst a sample of young Australians, higher climate distress tends to be experienced by those who are already disposed to poorer mental health. As such, mental health related consequences of climate change may be considered one way in which climate change exacerbates pre-existing inequalities. These findings also contribute to understanding of the potential impacts that climate distress has on mental health, justifying the need for interventions for climate distress to lessen its impact on vulnerable groups and the wider mental-health crisis as the climate crisis intensifies.

articles.title: Does mania lead to trauma in patients with bipolar disorder?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comorbidity between bipolar disorder (BD) and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is high. Although, the impact of childhood trauma on the development and course of BD seems to be very well established, less is known about the impact of BD on the development of trauma and PTSD. The aim of this study is to answer the following research question: What is known about the impact of a manic episode on the development of traumatic experiences or PTSD in patients with BD?
METHODS: A literature search for studies published to May 2026 was conducted.
RESULTS: Literature on this subject is scarce, only two articles were included. The first article showed that PTSD appeared to be a separate disorder in most bipolar patients. The second article showed that 15% of the subjects with BD experienced hallucinations and delusions during a manic episode as traumatic.
CONCLUSIONS: While it is plausible that, beyond childhood trauma, both the subjective experience of mania itself and its behavioural, psychosocial, and treatment-related consequences may give rise to traumatic experiences or even PTSD, empirical evidence remains too scarce to support definitive conclusions. Research is required in which the development of trauma and PTSD as a result of mood episodes in patients with BD has been studied.

articles.title: Assessing the global prevalence of depression symptoms between six weeks and six months postpartum: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum depression (PPD) and other perinatal mood and anxiety disorders are of critical importance given their symptom burden, association with impaired mother-infant bonding, and negative relationship impacts with support persons. However, PPD remains less studied beyond six weeks postpartum in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This is concerning because the risk of poor outcomes is high due to shifting provisions of care and surveillance challenges. The aim of this review was to understand the extent of the evidence around the global prevalence of PPD symptoms from six weeks to six months postpartum.
METHODS: A clinically-oriented search strategy was used to assess peer-reviewed articles published between 2019 and 2024 in PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. Studies were screened by two independent reviewers, with a third resolving discrepancies. Studies were included if they presented primary data around the prevalence of PPD from six weeks to six months postpartum (inclusive). Geographic and measurement characteristics were extracted along with PPD symptom prevalence rates using Covidence and Excel, with analyses in StataBE.
RESULTS: Most of the 78 included studies were from high- and upper-middle-income countries (76.93%) and over half measured PPD during the six-to-eight-week postpartum interval (53.85%). The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS; 83.33%) was the most utilized screening tool, with a median cut-off score of 11 (range 9 to 14). However, EPDS cut-off scores were reported inconsistently. There was methodological heterogeneity across studies, and rates of PPD symptoms ranged from 0.00% to 76.60% with a median of 16.00%.
CONCLUSIONS: This review found that PPD symptoms are common beyond the first six weeks postpartum, a time when care transitions and potential loss-to-follow-up may impact patient monitoring. However, more prevalence data are needed from LMICs, focusing beyond six-to-eight weeks postpartum, and at population levels, to establish rigorous global comparisons. More standardized reporting of screening tool cut-off scores are also needed to understand how PPD symptoms are measured.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Physical activity in Swedish 3-year-old children: associations with lifestyle and behavioral factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) positively affects children's health and well-being. Despite numerous studies on factors that influence PA in adults and older school-children, limited information exists about lifestyle factors, behavior, and neurodevelopmental predictors of PA in preschool children. This study aimed to (i) quantify the time spent in various activity levels (vigorous, moderate, light, and sedentary) among 3-year-old Swedish children, and (ii) examine associations between actigraphy-measured PA and various lifestyle, behavioral factors, and health in this age group.
METHODS: PA levels were measured using wrist-worn movement sensors (MotionWatch 8) in 497 3-year-old children in the ongoing NorthPop Birth Cohort in Northern Sweden. Motion data were collected over 24 h per day for eight continuous days and were classified into sleep, sedentary behavior, and PA intensities according to an age-, epoch-, and position-validated method. Children's lifestyle, health, and demographic data were collected using register data and parental questionnaires. Neurodevelopment and behavior were assessed using the Ages & Stages Questionnaire (ASQ) and Strength and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), respectively.
RESULTS: Swedish 3-year-old children spent an average of 163 min on moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) per day. Boys spent significantly more time at MVPA levels than girls (p < 0.001). Children with better gross motor function, older siblings in the household, and spending more time playing outdoors demonstrated longer time spent at higher levels of PA over 24 h per day. Children with hyperactivity problems were more physically active, whereas those with peer problems had lower PA levels. Children who were exposed to more time playing on computer/phone spent less time being physically active.
CONCLUSIONS: Three-year-olds in Sweden are generally highly active, with nearly all (99%) meeting the WHO recommendation of at least 60 min of MVPA per day and all (100%) meeting the recommendation of at least 180 min of total daily physical activity. The explanatory factors associated with particular PA levels are multidimensional, but the results suggest that behaviors such as playing outdoors and spending less time playing on computers/phones are associated with higher PA levels in this age group.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Retrospectively registered at Researchweb 11 November 2024 (project number 279272).

articles.title: Decomposition of age-specific income-related health inequalities: mobility around the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in Germany.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic caused major societal disruptions that may have altered existing health inequalities. This study examines how income-related inequalities in physical and mental health in Germany changed between 2018 and 2020, and whether these changes were driven by income-related health changes or by health-related income changes.
METHODS: Data from the 2018 and 2020 waves of the German Socio-Economic Panel were used to analyze physical and mental health outcomes derived from the SF-12 questionnaire. Age-specific mean levels were estimated, and a varying concentration index was applied to estimate smoothed, age-specific measures of income-related health inequality for men and women and for households with and without children. Changes in inequality were separated into income-related health changes and health-related income changes using a mobility decomposition.
RESULTS: Physical health declined significantly for working-age and older men, while remaining largely stable for women. Mental health decreased across most groups. The physical health advantage of higher-income individuals grew, while their mental health advantage shrank and disappeared among women in their 30s. Both shifts were driven by income-related health changes, while health-related income changes contributed significantly only to mental health inequality among women in their mid-30s.
CONCLUSIONS: The pandemic period did not uniformly exacerbate income-related health inequality but shifted its social distribution. In a crisis that affected both health and income, individuals in poorer health largely kept their income position, at least in the short term, whereas lower-income individuals experienced comparatively larger declines in physical health.

articles.title: Association between toileting behaviors and overactive bladder symptoms among female university students in Lebanon and Armenia: a comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a prevalent lower urinary tract symptom syndrome among young women, with potentially modifiable behavioral risk factors including toileting behaviors. This cross-sectional study investigated the association between toileting behaviors and OAB symptoms among female university students in Lebanon and Armenia.
METHODS: A total of 812 female university students (402 from Lebanon and 410 from Armenia) completed an online survey including the Toileting Behaviors-Women's Elimination Behaviors Scale (TB-WEB) and the 8-item Overactive Bladder Questionnaire (OAB-V8). Spearman correlation, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and descriptive statistics were used to analyze the data. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with screening-positive for probable OAB symptoms. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: 52.5% of Lebanese and 39.0% of Armenian participants screened positive for probable OAB symptoms based on the OAB-V8 cutoff. Lebanese students had higher TB-WEB scores (49.26 ± 8.77 vs. 44.82 ± 6.50) and OAB scores (8.01 ± 4.16 vs. 7.02 ± 5.48) (both p < 0.001). Total TB-WEB scores were positively correlated with OAB scores in both Lebanon (ρ = 0.680, p < 0.001) and Armenia (ρ = 0.312, p < 0.001). Delayed voiding showed the strongest association with OAB in Lebanon (ρ = 0.687, p < 0.001), whereas premature voiding was significantly associated with OAB only in Armenia (ρ = 0.264, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Unhealthy toileting behaviors were significantly associated with OAB symptoms in both countries, with notable differences in behavioral patterns. These findings suggest that toileting behaviors may represent a potentially modifiable factor worth exploring in future interventional studies on bladder health in young women.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized injury patients in a tertiary hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China: a retrospective single-center observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Injury is a substantial public health issue that ranks among the primary causes of mortality and disability globally. This study aimed to analyze the epidemiological characteristics and types of injury among hospitalized patients through a single-center hospital-based retrospective study conducted in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region in China.
METHODS: A total of 15,869 hospitalized injury patient records were retrieved from the Hospital Information System (HIS) of the People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region from 2018 to 2024.
RESULTS: Among the 15,869 hospitalized injury patients, 9,828 were male (61.93%) and 6,041 were female (38.07%). Most injuries occurred among individuals aged 30-69 years (57.37%). The top three external causes of injury were falls (41.84%), exposure to inanimate mechanical forces (21.96%), and transport accidents (18.06%). Overall, head injuries were the most common type of injury (20.20%), and were associated with significantly increased odds of in-hospital death. For length of stay, the long durations were observed for certain early complications of trauma (IRR: 1.65; 95% CI: 1.41, 1.92), injuries involving multiple body regions (IRR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.47, 1.81), and burns and corrosions (IRR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.22, 1.78). Regarding hospitalization cost, the high expenses were incurred for other and unspecified effects of external causes (ER: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.25, 2.01), injuries involving multiple body regions (ER: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.18, 1.55), and injuries to the neck (ER: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.09, 1.34).
CONCLUSION: This study clarifies the epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized injury patients in a tertiary hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Falls are the leading external cause of injury, and head injuries are ranked as the primary cause of injury-related deaths.

articles.title: Oral HPV prevalence and its associations with HIV, oral health, immune function, and behavioral factors among youth and mothers in Nigeria: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) are more susceptible to human papilloma virus (HPV) infection; however, data on the oral HPV burden among youth with or without perinatal HIV exposure or infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. This study described the distribution of oral HPV and examined demographic, dental, immune and behavioral characteristics of youth and mothers across HIV exposure groups in Nigeria and explored characteristics that co-occurred with oral HPV DNA detection.
METHODS: This baseline cross-sectional analysis leveraged data from a prospective cohort in Nigeria. At study enrollment, mothers were categorized as either HIV-infected (HI) or HIV-uninfected (HU), while youth participants were classified as HIV-infected (HI), HIV-exposed uninfected (HEU), or HIV-unexposed uninfected (HUU). Standardized questionnaires were used to capture behavioral data, and comprehensive dental examinations were used to assess decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), oral hygiene index simplified (OHIS), and gingival inflammation score (GIS). Oral rinse specimens were tested for oral HPV DNA and blood samples were collected for immune parameter assessment (CD4/CD8). The analysis was primarily descriptive given the small number of participants with oral HPV DNA detection. No inferential statistics were performed for HPV-stratified comparisons.
RESULTS: In our study, the overall oral HPV prevalence was low and was detected in 7/671 (1%) youth and 8/404 (2%) mothers. Among youth, oral HPV DNA was predominantly detected in HI and HEU groups and exclusively among HI mothers. In descriptive comparisons, youth with HPV DNA tended to have higher CD4 and lower CD8 counts and differences in oral health indices, whereas mothers with HPV DNA reported earlier sexual debut and lower CD4 counts. No inferential statistics were applied to these subgroups. These observations are hypothesis-generating given the small number of participants with detectable HPV DNA.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite its low prevalence, oral HPV was detected predominantly among PLWH and co-occurred with certain dental and immunological characteristics in this small number of cases. These findings highlight oral health as a potential area of interest in the context of oral HPV DNA detection and support further investigation into the relationships among oral health, the immune response, and viral detection within the HIV care setting in sub-Saharan Africa but cannot establish causal or predictive relationships.

articles.title: Neonatal admissions in a conflict-affected setting: an eight-year multi-center retrospective cohort study from Taiz, Yemen (2018-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal mortality in conflict-affected regions is a critical and under-documented public health issue. This study aimed to characterize admission patterns, diagnoses, and outcomes of neonates in Taiz, Yemen, over an eight-year period.
METHODS: We conducted a multi-center retrospective cohort study. All neonates (N = 1,936) admitted to five major hospitals in Taiz governorate between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2025, were included. Data were extracted from hospital registries. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and discharge against medical advice (DAMA). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of these outcomes.
FINDINGS: The cohort was 57.2% male. Most admissions (71.3%) occurred within 24 h of birth. The predominant diagnoses were birth asphyxia (27.8%), prematurity (24.3%), and neonatal sepsis (15.6%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 12.1% (235/1,936), with the highest rates among neonates with congenital anomalies (34.3%). However, in absolute terms, three preventable conditions-prematurity, birth asphyxia, and neonatal sepsis-accounted for 79.1% of all deaths. DAMA occurred in 19.8% (383/1,936) of admissions. Independent predictors of mortality were congenital anomalies (aOR 3.12, 95%CI 1.48-6.58) and admission at 8-27 days (aOR 1.89, 95%CI 1.16-3.08). Independent predictors of DAMA were admission at 1-7 days (aOR 1.58, 95%CI 1.21-2.06) and respiratory distress (aOR 1.86, 95%CI 1.15-3.01).
INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates a high burden of preventable neonatal conditions in conflict-affected Taiz. The findings highlight critical gaps in perinatal care and underscore the need for urgent, context-specific interventions, including scaling up neonatal resuscitation training, strengthening referral systems, and addressing the high DAMA rate through targeted family support. The results likely underestimate the true community burden of neonatal mortality, as they only capture facility-born infants.

articles.title: Knowledge and attitudes toward dementia and associated factors among residents in Wuhan, China: a cross-sectional community-based survey during the early implementation period of the National Dementia Action Plan (2024-2030).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia represents a major public health challenge in China, with the National Dementia Action Plan (2024-2030) aimed at improving awareness, facilitating early intervention, and reducing stigma. Despite this, empirical data on public dementia literacy during the early implementation period of the plan remain limited. This cross-sectional study described knowledge and attitudes toward dementia among urban residents in Wuhan, an early site for policy rollout, while identifying sociodemographic, experiential, and campaign-related factors associated with these outcomes.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, community-based survey was conducted in Wuhan, China, in 2025, employing multistage stratified random sampling to recruit 738 community-residing adults aged 18 years and older. Dementia knowledge was assessed using the Dementia Knowledge Scale (DKS; 22 items, scored as total correct responses), and attitudes were evaluated with the Scale of Attitudes toward Dementia (SATD; 4 items). Self-reported data included sociodemographic characteristics, contact with people living with dementia (PLWD), and participation in awareness campaigns (e.g., attending lectures, reading materials, watching videos).
RESULTS: The mean DKS score was 15.2 ± 6.5 (68.9% overall correct response rate), and the mean SATD score was 2.4 ± 1.5 (60% overall rate of positive attitudes). Significant knowledge gaps were evident, including uncertainty regarding disease prognosis (56.4%) and modifiable risk factors (36.7%), with only 46.2% correctly rejecting the misconception that healthy habits do not prevent dementia. Fatalistic attitudes persisted, as 25.2% viewed dementia as incurable and 33.2% as rendering old age meaningless, although 80.1% rejected the notion that dementia is a shameful condition. In multivariable analyses, higher knowledge scores were independently associated with female sex, higher education, contact with PLWD, and watching promotional videos (all P < 0.05). Positive attitudes were most strongly associated with higher knowledge scores, followed by video exposure, in multivariable logistic regression.
CONCLUSIONS: Dementia literacy in Wuhan was moderate but limited by gaps in prevention knowledge and entrenched fatalism. Given the cross-sectional study design, these findings only provide a cross-sectional snapshot and cannot establish causal improvements attributable to policy implementation. The results suggest that a dual-pathway intervention framework-combining scalable video-based education and intergroup contact via dementia-friendly communities-warrants consideration and formal evaluation to enhance China's national strategy, reduce stigma, and promote risk reduction behaviors.

articles.title: Toxoplasma gondii and gender equity: advocating for a one health approach in Lebanon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxoplasmosis, a zoonotic disease caused by the obligate intracellular protozoan Toxoplasma gondii, poses significant health risks, particularly for women of reproductive age, yet remains neglected in Lebanon's public health policies. This study aimed to assess awareness of toxoplasmosis among Lebanese participants and identify knowledge gaps about its prevalence, transmission routes, and health implications.
METHODS: The study involved 499 Lebanese participants across all provinces of Lebanon and examined factors influencing their awareness of toxoplasmosis, as well as related attitudes and readiness to act. Statistical analyses, including Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and regression models, were used to assess the relationship between education, gender, and geographic location on these outcomes.
RESULTS: Overall, > 80% of participants were classified as Unaware across prevalence, transmission, and clinical impact. Education was the only consistent determinant of awareness (Kruskal-Wallis H = 120.6, 98.2, and 87.5 for prevalence, transmission, and infection; all p < 0.001), whereas gender and location showed no significant effects. Among women, readiness to undergo serological testing had no significant predictors (logistic model pseudo R2 = 0.018, p = 0.226), with only a non-significant trend for higher transmission awareness (β = 0.067, p = 0.104).
CONCLUSIONS: The findings emphasize the urgent need for inclusive, gender-sensitive interventions that empower women and address disparities in public health outreach. The study, grounded in the One Health approach, offers actionable recommendations for improving disease awareness, establishing surveillance systems, and promoting preventive behaviors. These recommendations provide a comprehensive framework that can be adapted to similar global health challenges.

articles.title: Associations of 24-h movement behaviours and health-related physical fitness with educational outcomes among adolescents: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: The transition period of adolescence involves many changes regarding biology, cognition, and psychology that could influence health behaviour and educational outcomes. This systematic review sought to examine the relationship between various components of 24-h movement behaviours (physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep), health-related physical fitness, and educational outcomes in 9-19-year-old individuals. This review was registered on PROSPERO and performed following the PRISMA guidelines. Searching of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library databases revealed peer-reviewed studies published in English during 2005-2025. This search strategy led to a selection of 2,090 articles; 1,546 of them were duplicates and discarded, 544 records underwent title and abstract screening, 71 full-text papers were reviewed for inclusion criteria, and 22 studies were included into the narrative synthesis. Mainly, the evidence was related to physical activity and health-related physical fitness, which showed generally positive relationships with educational and learning-related cognitive outcomes. However, the results differed depending on the study design, population features, measures used, and educational outcomes. Evidence for sleep and sedentary or screen-based behaviours is scarce, as well as for all three types of movement behaviours assessed simultaneously. As a result, there is evidence of positive relationships between physical activity and physical fitness and some educational outcomes; however, there is no sufficient evidence of positive relationships of adherence to all 24-h movement behaviours to educational outcomes.

articles.title: Information-strained, social media-oriented, and patient-centered seekers: a latent profile analysis of health information seeking.
articles.abstract: This study explored latent profiles related to health information seeking (HIS), examined their associations between demographic characteristics and profile membership, and investigated differences in health-related outcomes among the identified profiles. Three indicators were used to identify latent profiles related to health information seeking: negative health information-seeking experience, use of health-specific social media, and patient-centered communication. Data were collected from the sixth cycle of the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 6), which investigates cancer-related information and health communication behaviors among adults in the United States (N = 1,614). This study identified three distinct profiles of health information seeking: information-strained seekers (n = 353, 21.9%), social media-oriented seekers (n = 681, 42.2%), and patient-centered seekers (n = 580, 35.9%). These three profiles demonstrated different patterns across the indicators of health information seeking, but were not associated with demographic characteristics such as gender, education, income, employment status, or history of cancer. Patient-centered seekers reported higher levels of patient activation, general health status, and trust in doctors and scientists as sources of health information compared to other profiles. The two profiles with higher levels of health-specific social media use, information-strained seekers and social media-oriented seekers, reported higher scores on cancer salience and beliefs about cancer. However, cancer screening intention and perceptions of the most responsible source to reduce misinformation did not differ among the three identified profiles. This study provides empirical evidence on subgroups of health information seekers that can inform the development of tailored strategies to enhance public health.

articles.title: Behavioral and structural determinants of HPV vaccination among adult men in China: a qualitative study using the COM-B model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is recommended for both males and females; however, uptake among adult men in China remains low. Understanding behavioral and structural determinants may inform gender-neutral HPV prevention strategies.
METHODS: This qualitative study used semistructured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model. Data were collected in February 2026 at a tertiary hospital health examination center in Qingdao, China. A purposive sample of 25 adult men aged 18-45 years attending routine health examinations was recruited. Interviews explored knowledge of HPV, attitudes toward vaccination, relational influences, and interactions with health services. Recruitment continued until data saturation was achieved, defined as the point at which no new themes or concepts emerged from successive interviews.
RESULTS: Among 25 participants (mean [SD] age, 31.5 [5.8] years; 14 [56%] married), 20 (80%) had heard of HPV, 4 (16%) knew that men could receive HPV vaccination, and 2 (8%) had been vaccinated. Three themes were identified. First, HPV was commonly framed as a women's health issue, limiting men's perceived susceptibility and reducing self-initiated motivation for vaccination. Second, vaccination motivation was often relationally mediated, with participants reporting willingness to vaccinate when encouraged by partners. Third, opportunity-related structural barriers, including limited clinician recommendation and perceived vaccine cost, constrained translation of vaccination intentions into behavior.
CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination decisions among Chinese adult men appear shaped primarily by motivational determinants, supported by limitations in HPV-related knowledge and perceived susceptibility, as well as opportunity-related structural barriers within the health system. Interventions to increase uptake may benefit from de-gendered public health communication strategies that move beyond the "cervical cancer vaccine" framing, alongside stronger clinician engagement and efforts to reduce structural barriers.

articles.title: Public preferences for mosquito-borne disease prevention interventions in metropolitan France: a discrete choice experiment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs), e.g., dengue, are an emerging public health threat in metropolitan France. While various preventive strategies exist, their real-world success depends on public uptake and adherence. However, research quantifying population preferences for these interventions remains scarce in non-endemic European settings. This study aimed to elicit preferences for key MBD preventive interventions to inform the design of acceptable health policies.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey in November 2023, recruiting a representative sample of adults aged 18-79 residing in metropolitan France (N = 2,087). We employed a discrete choice experiment (DCE) to elicit preferences. Participants completed ten unlabeled, forced-choice A vs. B tasks, selecting between two hypothetical intervention scenarios defined by four attributes: participation (e.g., government-led vs. individual), intervention frequency, environmental effects, and human health side effects. Average preferences and preference heterogeneity for each MBD attribute were retrieved from mixed multinomial logistic (MMNL) models with correlated random parameters. The drivers of preference heterogeneity were further assessed using interaction effects with respondents' characteristics and simulations were performed to assess optimal interventions that achieved greatest gains in aggregated utility.
RESULTS: All attributes influenced hypothetical decisions. Respondents exhibited the strongest aversion to interventions with systematic negative effects on animals and vegetation (β = -1.77), followed closely by those carrying risks of rare but serious human health side effects (β = -1.48). In terms of governance, government-led implementation was preferred over approaches relying on individual or community compliance. Notably, measures dependent on full community participation were disliked (β = -0.50). While interventions requiring greater time commitment reduced utility (β = -0.22), convenience was a secondary driver compared to health safety. Simulation analysis indicated that installing insect screens yielded the highest predicted utility, while chemical fumigation would generate highest welfare losses.
CONCLUSIONS: Public acceptability of MBD prevention in France hinges critically on environmental and health safety rather than convenience. The findings reveal a preference for centralized, government-managed interventions over those requiring coordinated community effort and compliance. To maximize uptake, policymakers should prioritize environmentally safe interventions and adopt transparent communication strategies that directly address public concerns regarding ecological impact and health side effects.

articles.title: Early-onset CVD at the intersection of sex, race/ethnicity, education, income, and health insurance in the US: a nationwide intersectional analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of early-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) is increasing, but how intersecting social determinants shape this risk in US young adults is unclear. We quantified intersectional inequities in early-onset CVD prevalence and examined their temporal changes following the COVID-19 pandemic in US.
METHODS: In this retrospective serial cross-sectional study of 1,030,504 US adults aged 18-44 (BRFSS 2015-2024), we employed Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA). Individuals were nested within 240 strata defined by sex, race/ethnicity, education, income, and insurance. The variance partition coefficient (VPC) and median odds ratio (MOR) quantified disparities. Models were stratified into pre- and post-pandemic periods.
RESULTS: The weighted prevalence of early-onset CVD was 2.1%. The variance components model revealed substantial between-stratum heterogeneity (VPC, 23.5%; MOR, 2.60). Predicted CVD probabilities ranged over 400-fold across strata (0.04%-15.91%), with the highest risk found in uninsured, low-income, low-education Asian males. Additive main effects explained only 44.6% of this inequality (PCV). Of 235 strata, 99 (42.1%) exhibited significant intersectional effects (58 penalties, 41 protections), with Asian adults featuring prominently at both risk extremes. From the pre- to post-pandemic period, intersectional inequities widened, with the MOR increasing from 3.43 (95% CI, 3.00-3.86) to 4.19 (95% CI, 3.55-4.84), a 22.2% relative increase (95% CI, - 0.4% to 44.7%).
CONCLUSION: Young US adults face vast, widening, and largely non-additive intersectional inequities in early-onset CVD. Risk is exceptionally concentrated in multiply-marginalized strata, and the post-pandemic exacerbation of these disparities demands a paradigm shift from individual risk management to structurally competent, equity-focused preventive strategies.

articles.title: A bivariate copula-geostatistical model for binary outcomes: joint spatial risk mapping of zero-dose and under-immunized children in Malawi, 2015-2016 MDHS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zero-dose and under-immunized children remain vulnerable, hindering progress toward Immunization Agenda 2030 and Sustainable Development Goals (SGDs). Although these outcomes are closely related, they are often analyzed independently, and conventional spatial models do not adequately capture their joint distribution and spatial dependencies. This study applies a copula-based geospatial model for binary outcomes to analyze these data in Malawi.
METHODS: Using 2015-2016 Malawi DHS data, we examined immunization status (zero-dose and under-immunization) among children aged 12-35 months. Covariates included maternal age, education, wealth, residence, and district. Exploratory spatial analysis mapped distributions, while copula-based joint modelling, through generalized joint regression model (GJRM) assessed dependencies. Markov Random Fields smoothed district-level estimates, and splines modelled maternal age effects.
RESULTS: Among the 5,668 children included in the analysis, 2.33% were zero-dose and 4.59% were under-immunized. The joint model revealed that children from the poorest families and those with parents having no education had higher odds of being zero-dose or under-immunized. Conversely, children from the northern region and rural residences had lower odds of being zero-dose or under-immunized. The spatial analysis revealed districts with more proportions of zero-dose and under-immunized children which included: Nsanje, Chikwawa, Thyolo, Phalombe. The joint modelling, using Frank copula, further revealed strong positive correlation between zero-dose and under-immunized.
CONCLUSION: The copula-based geospatial modelling framework provided a flexible approach for jointly analyzing zero-dose and under-immunization while accounting for their spatial dependence. The findings identified geographical hotspots and socioeconomic inequalities in childhood immunization, providing evidence to support geographically targeted and equity-focused interventions aimed at improving vaccine initiation and completion in Malawi.

articles.title: Retention in HIV care and acceptability of an adolescent and youth focused community‑based differentiated service delivery model in Ethiopia: a comparative mixed‑methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents and young people living with HIV (AYLHIV) aged 10-24 years continue to experience poorer outcomes across the HIV-care cascade than other age groups. Although differentiated service delivery models offer client-centered approaches to address structural and psychosocial barriers, evidence on adolescent and youth specific community-based models (AY- CDSDMs) in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. We assessed the association between enrollment in AY-CDSDM and retention in HIV care and evaluated the model's acceptability among AYLHIV in Ethiopia.
METHODS: We conducted a concurrent, comparative mixed-methods study in 20 purposively selected health facilities across eight high HIV burden regions of Ethiopia. Quantitative data were obtained through a retrospective review of medical records for 721 randomly selected AYLHIV aged 10-24 years who received HIV care between January 2024 and February 2025. We compared retention in care between those enrolled in AY-CDSDMs and those receiving conventional facility-based care. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with retention. Additionally, we conducted 54 key informant interviews and 11 focus group discussions to explore acceptability and implementation. Qualitative data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis guided by the theoretical framework of acceptability.
RESULTS: Among the 721 participants (mean age, 19 ± 3.4 years; 54% female), 359 (49.8%) were enrolled in AY-CDSDM and 362 (50.2%) received conventional facility-based care. Overall retention in care was 96.9% (95% CI: 96.5-97.3%). Retention was higher among AY-CDSDM participants (98.6%; 95% CI: 98.1-99.1%) than among those receiving conventional facility-based care (95.3%; 95% CI: 94.8-95.8%). Enrollment in AY-CDSDM was independently associated with higher odds of retention in care (AOR = 3.56; 95% CI: 1.20-10.58; p = 0.022). Qualitative findings indicated high acceptability of AY-CDSDM, highlighting perceived relevance and convenience, strengthened peer-support, reduced logistical and psychosocial barriers, and improved treatment-related confidence among participants. However, physical distance remained a minor barrier for a small subset of participants.
CONCLUSION: Enrollment in AY-CDSDM was associated with higher retention in HIV care and demonstrated high acceptability among AYLHIV in Ethiopia. By addressing structural and psychosocial barriers through peer-led, community-based approaches, AY-CDSDM represents a promising and scalable strategy to optimize retention in HIV care in resource limited settings.

articles.title: Why food stays contaminated: a COM-B framework analysis of child feeding practices in Dhaka's informal settlements.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foodborne diseases are the major public health concerns in low- and middle-income countries, particularly during the complementary feeding period. Children become increasingly exposed to environmental pathogens at this age. Food hygiene during this period is critical to prevent such diseases. This formative study aimed to identify the behavioral determinants of complementary food hygiene practices among caregivers of complimentary aged children using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, Motivation Behaviour) framework to develop food hygiene interventions.
METHODS: The study was conducted in the Korail slum, Dhaka, between August 2023 and March 2024. Multiple qualitative methods were employed, including semi-structured household observations (8 h per household, n = 32), semi-structured interviews (n = 16), and focus group discussions (3 groups, n = 24). Participant selection varied by method, such as observation; households were purposively selected to ensure contextual diversity; interview participants were selected based on observed hygiene practices to explore behavioral drivers; and FGD participants were recruited to capture variation by caregiving experience. Data were analyzed iteratively using thematic analysis guided by the COM-B framework, with triangulation across methods to enhance credibility.
RESULTS: Findings reveal that five key behaviors food reheating, food and water storage, utensil cleaning, surface cleaning, and hand hygiene are central to reducing microbial contamination and protecting children from enteric infections. Caregivers demonstrated strong psychological capability and reflective motivation, expressing awareness of recommended practices and concern for child health. However, physical opportunity constraints, including irregular fuel access, overcrowded shared kitchens, inadequate storage, distant communal washing areas, and the absence of designated handwashing facilities, consistently limited safe practice. Automatic motivation further shaped behavior, with reliance on visual cleanliness and sensory cues rather than microbial risk influencing routine decisions.
CONCLUSIONS: Food hygiene behaviors in low-resource urban settings are constrained by inadequate technical knowledge, structural barriers, and habitual practices. Interventions should address these limitations by combining enabling environments with behaviorally informed strategies that target routine practices. Integrated approaches are essential to improve complementary food hygiene and reduce child exposure to contamination in informal settlements.

articles.title: Contextual readiness assessment of CDC-recognized family healthy weight programs in Southwest Georgia Cooperative Extension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends all children with obesity receive Intensive Behavioral Lifestyle Treatment Programs, yet programs are not widely available. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is prioritizing dissemination of six programs known as Family Healthy Weight Programs (FHWP) and examining the potential role of community organizations like Cooperative Extension in implementation. This mixed-methods study conducts initial asset mapping and explores contextual readiness of implementing CDC-recognized FHWPs through Cooperative Extension in Southwest Georgia counties with a high obesity burden (> 40% adult obesity).
METHODS: We used descriptive statistics and bivariate analysis (chi-square tests) to explore the availability of healthcare and recreational resources and to compare across high-obesity and non-high-obesity counties, and by Extension districts (Southwest, Southeast, Northwest, Northeast). We additionally conducted a focus group with the potential implementing staff, Cooperative Extension agents, and thematically analyzed the data.
RESULTS: Only 72% of Georgia high-obesity counties have at least one physician (family medicine, pediatrician, or child psychiatrist) compared to 93% of non-high-obesity counties (χ² (1, n = 159) = 11.619, p < 0.001). Additionally, Southwest Georgia has significantly fewer counties with at least one physician (70.7%) than the other Extension districts (91.5%) (χ² (1, n = 159) = 9.360, p = 0.002), but there is no difference among high-obesity (66.7%) and non-high-obesity counties (76.5%) within the Southwest district (χ² (1, n = 41) = 0.110, p = 0.740). Less than half of the Southwest counties (46.3%) have a pediatrician to support participant recruitment, referral, and monitoring. Only one county had a YMCA in the Southwest district, and other recreational resources were limited. Extension agents perceived FHWPs to fit well with Extension's mission, structure, and participant needs, but echoed barriers revealed in the quantitative data, including a lack of local healthcare and recreational resources, and identified small eligible populations to recruit from and limited Extension staffing as additional implementation barriers.
CONCLUSION: If Extension proceeds with adopting FHWP in Southwest Georgia, administrators should select a program that can be delivered using appropriate partnerships, adaptations, and supports for staffing, recreational resources, and creative clinical support for recruitment, referrals, and patient monitoring.

articles.title: Physical and cognitive development in preschool children during and after COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-sectional cohort comparison.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted preschool children's routines, potentially affecting their fundamental movement skills (FMS), physical activity (PA), physical fitness (PF), and executive function (EF). This study compared these outcomes in preschoolers during and after the pandemic and investigated their associations.
METHODS: Two cohorts of 5-6-year-olds from four Chinese preschool centers were evaluated: one during the pandemic (2021, n = 174) and one post-pandemic (2023, n = 189). FMS were measured using the Test of Gross Motor Development Third Edition (TGMD-3), PA was monitored with accelerometers, PF was measured by field tests, and EF was assessed through computerized tasks. Multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) was used to compare outcomes between cohorts, and linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to examine associations between FMS, PA, PF, and EF components.
RESULTS: Post-pandemic participants demonstrated significantly better performance in locomotor skills, PF components (balance, flexibility, muscular strength, muscular endurance, speed-agility), and EF components (cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, working memory) compared to their pandemic peers. Conversely, pandemic participants exhibited higher scores in ball skills and spent more time in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). During the pandemic, better balance was associated with higher cognitive flexibility. Post-pandemic, muscular strength was positively associated with cognitive flexibility, and speed-agility with inhibitory control, while light PA was negatively associated with inhibitory control.
CONCLUSION: The findings reveal a mixed pattern of physical and cognitive outcomes between preschool children assessed during versus after the pandemic, with post-pandemic improvements in several domains but notable pandemic advantages in ball skills and MVPA. Furthermore, the associations between PF and EF were specific and context-dependent. These results provide descriptive evidence of developmental shifts associated with the pandemic context, though causal inferences are precluded by the cross-sectional design and small effect sizes.

articles.title: Prevalance and factors associated with cervical cancer screening uptake among HIV positive women in the rural communities of Alebtong district in Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) is the leading gynaecologic malignancy in Uganda and affects about 6959 women and 4607 die annually.
