CONCLUSIONS: Most pediatric patients with CCHF survive, but a severe hyperinflammatory course with frequent HLH can occur. Pediatric CCHF cannot be fully assessed with adult-derived frameworks, supporting pediatric-specific diagnostic and management strategies.

articles.title: Tailored Dosing Recommendations for Amikacin in Severely Ill Children: A Population Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Evaluation using Cmax/MIC and AUC/MIC-based Indices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Optimal amikacin dosing in severely ill patients remains challenging due to maturational and pathophysiological alterations affecting the pharmacokinetics (PK). This study aimed to develop a population PK model for amikacin, evaluate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) indices, and propose personalised dosing recommendations for this patient population.
METHODS: A prospective PK study was conducted in 38 severely ill children receiving intravenous 20 mg/kg amikacin every 24h. PK parameters were determined using nonlinear mixed-effects modelling (Monolix 2024R1). Probability of target attainment (PTA) was simulated for the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 mg/L and 8 mg/L for Enterobacterales. Evaluated PK/PD targets were a peak concentration (Cmax)/MIC ≥ 8 and a 24h area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-24h)/MIC ≥ 62.5h, in combination with a trough concentration (Ctrough) ≤ 5 mg/L toxicity threshold.
RESULTS: A two-compartment model with a priori allometric weight scaling on the PK parameters best described the data. Clearance was predicted using the Bouvet estimated glomerular filtration (eGFR) formula, combining creatinine and cystatin C. The central volume of distribution was 41% lower in oncology patients compared with intensive care patients. The population parameters for clearance and the total volume of distribution were 7.4 L/h/70 kg and 39.0 L/70 kg, respectively. AUC0-24h/MIC, as PK/PD index, was less frequently attained than the Cmax/MIC index. For a MIC of 2 mg/L, a dose of 20 mg/kg every 18h achieved a 100% PTA for the targets Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC0-24h/MIC ≥ 62.5h, and Ctrough ≤ 5 mg/L in typical patients with a 120-150 mL/min/1.73 m2 eGFR, compared with ≤76% for the current regimen. For a MIC of 8 mg/L, ≥80% PTA could not be achieved.
CONCLUSIONS: Current amikacin dosing regimens may result in subtherapeutic exposure, particularly in intensive care patients with high eGFR or when targeting higher MIC values or AUC/MIC targets. Optimised dosing regimens were proposed.

articles.title: Multicenter observational cohort study of clinical and viral features of human metapneumovirus infection in hospitalized children, Taiwan, 2023-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of respiratory tract infections (RTIs) in children. This study examined the circulation, seasonality, and clinical characteristics of pediatric hMPV infection in Taiwan during the three years following the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: We enrolled children hospitalized with molecularly confirmed hMPV infection at three hospitals in Taiwan between January 2023 and December 2025. The study comprised two periods: Period 1 (January 2023 to June 2024), a retrospective review of medical records, and Period 2 (July 2024 to December 2025), a prospective enrollment with written informed consent and collection of nasopharyngeal specimens. Genotyping was performed on a subset of respiratory samples collected during Period 2.
RESULTS: Of 3310 hospitalized children tested for RTIs, 390 (11.8%) were confirmed to have hMPV infection, of whom 342 were enrolled and analyzed. hMPV peaked from February to April. The median patient age was 2.77 years. Most patients presented with lower RTIs (93.6%); 41.5% had underlying conditions, 66.4% had antibiotic use, 43.9% had viral co-infection, 17.1% required intensive care, and 39.8% required respiratory support. The median hospital stay was 6 days. Four sublineages co-circulated, with A2.2.2 (51.6%) and B2 (24.2%) predominating. Clinical presentations did not differ significantly between hMPV subgroups A and B. A significant temporal shift toward younger patients was observed, driven mainly by an increase in infants aged 0-1 year (p for trend = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: hMPV contributes substantially to pediatric RTIs in Taiwan and shows distinct spring seasonality. Sublineage A2.2.2 predominated, whereas B2 increased during the 2024-2025 season. The shift toward younger affected children during the three-year observation period may suggest changing patterns of pediatric susceptibility but requires confirmation in large-scale, well-designed prospective studies.

articles.title: Increased incidence of group A streptococcal infections requiring hospitalization following the COVID-19 pandemic, with no change in the proportion of invasive disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections in hospitalized children and adults between pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods in Alicante, Spain.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study including all patients hospitalized with GAS infection between January 2015 and December 2025. Incidence rates were calculated per 10,000 hospital admissions and per 100,000 population. Temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson regression models and expressed as incidence rate ratios (IRR).
RESULTS: 456 hospitalized GAS infections were identified, 75 (16.4%) pediatric and 381 (83.6%) adult cases; 298 (65.4%) non-invasive and 158 (34.6%) invasives. The annual number of cases increased from 13 in 2015-84 in 2023. Overall incidence doubled in the post-pandemic compared with the pre-pandemic period (hospital-based IRR 2.53, 95% CI 2.05-3.12; population-based IRR 2.40, 95% CI 1.94-2.96). The increase was greater in adults (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.13-1.21) than in children (IRR 1.08; 95% CI 0.98-1.19). The proportion of invasive infections remained stable before and after the pandemic (35.0% vs 36.6%; RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79-1.39). Patients with invasive GAS infection were older and had a higher burden of comorbidity.
CONCLUSIONS: GAS infections increased markedly after the COVID-19 pandemic. It was not accompanied by an increase in the proportion of invasive infections.

articles.title: Age-Related Tibetan-Han Differences in Continuity of Care Among Insured Populations in High-Altitude Western China: Retrospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuity of Care (CoC) is an important dimension of health system performance and health equity, reflecting whether individuals can maintain stable and coordinated care relationships over time, rather than merely gaining access to services. Although ethnic differences in CoC have been documented, most existing studies have examined average group differences and have paid limited attention to whether such differences vary across the life course. Claims-based analyses can provide a population-level approach to monitoring CoC and identifying age-specific equity gaps in routine health service use.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether Tibetan-Han differences in CoC vary by age among insured populations in high-altitude western China and to assess whether these age-related patterns differ across outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease care settings.
METHODS: We used deidentified health insurance claims data from 3 major cities in high-altitude western China between January 1, 2021, and December 1, 2024. After data cleaning, we constructed a person-year dataset and restricted analyses to individuals with at least 3 annual health care encounters, yielding 850,469 person-years. The Bice-Boxerman CoC index was the primary outcome. Fixed-effects models with year and insurance-region fixed effects included ethnicity, age, age squared, and their interaction terms, adjusting for covariates derived from the Andersen behavioral model. SEs were clustered at the individual level. Subgroup analyses were conducted for outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease samples.
RESULTS: Mean CoC in the overall sample was 0.52 (SD 0.33). A significant nonlinear interaction between ethnicity and age was observed. Fixed-effects models showed a positive Tibetan coefficient (β=0.0582, P<.001), a negative ethnicity × age interaction (β=-0.0035, P<.001), and a significant ethnicity × age² interaction (P<.001). Outpatient results were similar. Inpatient analyses showed an overall disadvantage for Tibetans (β=-0.0795, P<.001) and a different age pattern. No significant age interaction was found in the chronic disease sample, whereas significant age heterogeneity remained in the nonchronic disease sample. Age-group analyses showed the largest Tibetan advantage at ages 20 to 25 and significantly lower continuity in most groups aged 35 to 75.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethnic differences in CoC were age-dependent and nonlinear rather than constant across age groups. Because the study covers 4 calendar years, these age-related associations may also reflect birth-cohort differences and should not be interpreted as within-person aging effects. Policies should pay greater attention to continuity barriers faced by middle-aged and older Tibetan populations.

articles.title: Machine learning-integrated full-length 16S rRNA gene profiling reveals early-life gut microbial signatures associated with subsequent infantile colic in Thai infants.
articles.abstract: Infantile colic develops after the neonatal period, but neonatal gut microbial patterns preceding symptom onset remain unclear. We examined early-life gut microbiome associations with subsequent infantile colic and internally evaluated microbiome-only prediction alongside retrospective metadata-containing comparisons. Stool samples collected 0-4 days after birth from 209 Thai infants (119 healthy and 90 who later met Rome IV diagnostic criteria for infantile colic) were profiled by Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing. Analyses included diversity and composition assessments, covariate-adjusted MaAsLin3 models, repeated nested cross-validation, and exploratory conditional association networks. Infants who subsequently developed infantile colic had lower Chao1 richness than healthy infants (q = 8.7 × 10-5), although delivery mode and collection day explained more community variation than outcome status. After covariate adjustment, Enterococcus faecium presence was associated with subsequent colic (odds ratio, 4.23; q = 0.021). The fully nested model-development procedure yielded participant-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) values of 0.773 and 0.740. In a secondary fixed-model comparison including feeding summarized through one month, a species-presence radial basis function support vector machine outperformed metadata alone (mean outer-fold AUROC/AUPRC, 0.780/0.764 vs. 0.539/0.484), while adding metadata produced only a small, uncertain improvement. Exploratory network analysis contextualized candidate taxa within group-specific conditional association modules. These findings support a focused early-life species-level pattern associated with subsequent infantile colic and prioritize candidate microbial features for external validation.

articles.title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
articles.abstract: Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in certain immunocompromised adults and adolescents. Here we show potent neutralization of this antibody against a broad range of emerging variants, including the recently dominant XFG. X-ray crystal structures of VYD222 in complex with the receptor-binding domains of prototype SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron BA.5 demonstrate the molecular basis of how VYD222 accommodates the mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants that escape other previous FDA-approved antibodies. Notably, many of the mutations between ADG20 and VYD222 occur in the second shell outside the paratope contact residues. Deep mutational scanning indicates that SARS-CoV-2's ability to escape VYD222 is constrained by structural compatibility and the need to maintain receptor binding. These findings provide crucial insights into the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants and offer valuable guidance for risk assessment of emergent variants.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype investigation of evolving mutations associated with antimalarial resistance among Senegalese Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites.
articles.abstract: Drug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum threatens malaria control and elimination efforts, particularly where sustained chemoprevention and treatment have driven parasite evolution. Senegal has implemented antimalarial strategies for two decades, including sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy and SP plus amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children. We analyzed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 2,805 monogenomic P. falciparum infections collected from febrile, treatment-seeking patients across Senegal between 2006 and 2022. Wild-type (WT), drug-sensitive alleles at four major resistance loci (Pfcrt, Pfmdr1, Pfdhfr, and Pfdhps) were rare, while resistance-associated variants, including Pfcrt K76T, the canonical Pfdhfr triple mutant (N51I, C59R, S108N), and Pfdhps A437G, predominated. To define how these genotypes shape drug response and parasite fitness, we cultured 33 clinical isolates representing 26 common combined haplotypes, which together accounted for 63.9% of infections in the WGS dataset. Multivariable mixed-effects models revealed drug- and background-dependent effects. Relative to the Pfcrt WT, the CVIET background increased monodesethyl-amodiaquine EC50 approximately 1.4-fold; adding N326S or I356T produced cumulative increases of approximately 2.6-fold and 3.2-fold, respectively. The Pfdhfr triple mutant increased pyrimethamine EC50 approximately 2,196-fold relative to Pfdhfr WT. For sulfadoxine, Pfdhps A437G was associated with an approximately 463,000-fold increase in EC50 relative to WT, while Pfdhps S436A had little effect. Pairwise competitive growth outcomes analyzed with a Bradley-Terry model showed reduced competitive ability for Pfcrt CVIET, partially rescued by Pfmdr1 Y184F; Pfdhps S436A increased whereas A613S reduced competitive ability. These findings reveal resistance-fitness trade-offs that may shape P. falciparum evolution as antimalarial policies change across Africa.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
articles.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating "late-small" and "early-large" epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

articles.title: Preliminary convergent validity and group discrimination of a serious game for assessing attention in children and adolescents with and without clinician-established ADHD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity. Diagnosis requires a comprehensive, multi-informant clinical assessment; performance on a single attention task is neither necessary nor sufficient. This cross-sectional study examined the preliminary convergent validity, reliability, and group discrimination of Attention Robots, a serious game designed to assess attention-related performance.
METHODS: Participants were 117 children and adolescents aged 6-18 years: 47 with a clinician-established ADHD diagnosis and 70 community comparison participants without a recorded ADHD diagnosis. Attention Robots scores were examined alongside CARAS-R and CogniFit measures using correlations, age- and sex-adjusted group comparisons, split-half reliability, and exploratory ROC analyses.
RESULTS: Attention Robots scores were associated with CARAS-R inhibitory-control and several CogniFit measures. After adjustment for age and sex and correction for multiple comparisons, participants with ADHD showed lower Attention Robots concentration and working-speed scores than community comparison participants, whereas error percentage did not differ between groups. Among the CogniFit outcomes, only visual perception remained significantly different between groups after Holm correction. The game-only ROC model showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.61; sensitivity = 0.28; specificity = 0.80). A model that also included sex yielded an AUC of 0.73, with sensitivity of 0.57 and specificity of 0.76; however, the higher AUC cannot be attributed to the game because sex was unevenly distributed between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Attention Robots may provide complementary information about attention-related performance, but the present two-gate, single-site findings do not support stand-alone screening or diagnosis. Independent validation with consistently verified, sex-balanced, clinically heterogeneous samples is required.

articles.title: Natural-abundance carbon isotope profiling of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplement incorporation in extremely preterm infants: a sub-study of the Mega Donna Mega randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extremely preterm infants are deprived of most third-trimester long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid accretion. In the Mega Donna Mega trial, enteral arachidonic acid (ARA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) supplementation reduced severe retinopathy of prematurity despite modest early changes in circulating levels.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated whether natural-abundance carbon isotope ratio (δ13C) profiling detects early entry of supplemented ARA and DHA into circulating phospholipids in extremely preterm infants.
METHODS: This sub-study of the randomized Mega Donna Mega trial included 25 infants born before 25+2 weeks' gestation who received standard-of-care nutrition (SOC, n=12) or enteral ARA+DHA supplementation (intervention, n=13; 100 and 50 mg/kg/day, respectively) from ≤3 days after birth until 40 weeks' postmenstrual age. Serum phospholipid fatty acid composition and δ13C values were determined at Day 0-3, 10-16, 34-47, and 75-87. Group differences were assessed with mixed models of treatment group by sampling window.
RESULTS: Between-group differences in ARA and DHA weight percent (wt%) emerged late in the intervention (Day 75-87, mean [SD]: ARA 10.1 [2.0] versus 6.9 [1.4]; DHA 3.3 [1.0] versus 2.3 [0.7]). ARA and DHA δ13C were similar between groups at Day 0-3 and higher in supplemented infants from Day 10-16 (difference [95% CI]: ARA 1.9 [0.9, 2.8] mUr; DHA 2.0 [0.3, 3.6] mUr). The group-by-window interaction was significant for ARA δ13C (p=0.007) but not for DHA δ13C (p=0.11; p=0.005 after excluding one infant with necrotizing enterocolitis and low compliance).
CONCLUSIONS: Natural-abundance δ13C profiling showed that supplemented ARA and DHA were bioavailable and entered circulating phospholipids within two weeks of birth, before clear separation in fatty acid composition. Concentration-based biomarkers may underestimate early exposure to supplemented fatty acids in extremely preterm infants.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03201588, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03201588.

articles.title: Pornography use in adolescence: a gender perspective on co-occurring behavioural, psychosocial, and health outcomes.
articles.abstract: This study examined associations between pornography use and gender identity, sexual attraction, sexual behaviours, substance use, adverse social experiences, and health and wellbeing among secondary school students from a gender perspective. This cross-sectional study used data from the 2025 FRESC Health Survey on Adolescence in Barcelona, Spain (3,690 students aged 13-19 years). Occasional or regular pornography use was contrasted with no use or one-time use. Sex-stratified survey-weighted complex-samples logistic regression models accounted for sampling strata and classroom clustering and were adjusted for age, family socioeconomic status, and family structure. Pornography use was more frequent among boys than girls (55.6% vs. 13.8%). Associations with ever having had sexual intercourse, daily smoking, recent drunkenness, lifetime cannabis use, peer aggression, and hyperactivity/inattention were observed in both sexes. Among girls, associations were additionally observed with transgender/nonbinary gender identity, non-exclusively heterosexual attraction, poor family relationships, peer victimization, sexual harassment, poor self-reported health, and life dissatisfaction; body dissatisfaction was significant only before correction for multiple testing. Among boys, conduct problems were also associated with pornography use. Following Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 21 outcomes per sex, seven of eight initially significant associations in boys and 13 of 14 in girls remained significant. Overall, these findings suggest that pornography use should not be understood as an isolated behaviour but rather in relation to a broader range of behavioural, psychosocial, and health characteristics during adolescence, although the cross-sectional design does not permit causal or temporal conclusions.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy and child internalising and externalising problems over time.
articles.abstract: Adequate gestational thyroid function is important for offspring neurodevelopment, yet behavioural implications of variation within the normal range are unclear. We examined associations with externalising and internalising problems across repeated assessments in childhood and adolescence. 2,606 mother-child dyads from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort with maternal free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurements in the first half of pregnancy and at least one child SDQ assessment. Primary analysis excluded women with overt thyroid disease or thyroid medication use and children born < 32 weeks or < 1500 g. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) scores at 5-6, 11-12 and 15-16 years, via mother-, teacher-, and self-report. Secondary analyses included logistic regression for borderline SDQ cut-offs, sex interactions, and effect modification by TSH. FT4 showed a U-shaped association with teacher-reported externalising problems (quadratic β = 9.49, FDR-adjusted p = 0.03), with higher scores at both low and high FT4. Higher FT4 was associated with lower child-reported internalising problems (β = -0.17, FDR-adjusted p = 0.04). For both primary associations, there was no evidence of FT4-by-age interaction, suggesting differences in problem levels rather than thyroid-related differences in symptom change over time. At age 5-6, FT4 showed a non-linear association with teacher-reported hyperactivity/inattention above the threshold, with a negative linear term (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.97) and a positive quadratic term (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.20). At age 11-12, higher FT4 was associated with fewer self-reported peer problems (OR = 0.84, 95% CI:0.71-0.99). In exploratory analyses, curvature of the FT4-externalising association varied by maternal TSH; no sex modification was detected. Within a cohort free of overt thyroid disease, maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy was associated with domain- and rater-specific differences in child internalising and externalising problems. We found no evidence that these associations changed across the available repeated assessments, suggesting differences in average problem scores rather than differences in how symptoms changed with age.

articles.title: Analysis of the placebo response model and its influencing factors in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a model-based meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: A robust placebo response continuously challenges the evaluation of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) therapies. This study utilized model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) to quantify the longitudinal trajectory of the placebo response, identify trial- and patient- level predictors, and compare response magnitudes between pediatric and adult populations to optimize future trial designs.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science identified placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials (RCTs) for ADHD. Longitudinal changes in placebo groups were mathematically modeled based on the ADHD Rating Scale (ADHD-RS) and Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S). Covariate modeling and subgroup analyses were applied to evaluate the impact of demographic and trial design factors.
RESULTS: Data from 79 RCTs were analyzed. Placebo responses exhibited non-linear dynamics, plateauing at approximately 6 weeks for the ADHD-RS and 10 weeks for the CGI-S. Larger trial sample sizes significantly predicted increased ADHD-RS placebo scores. Placebo magnitudes were also more pronounced in recent, multicenter, three more trial arms, industry-sponsored trials, trials using a stimulant as the active comparator, as well as in cohorts with fewer male or White participants and more severe baseline disease. Crucially, The time-course trajectories and amplitudes of the placebo response were similar in pediatric and adult populations.
CONCLUSION: This study provides a quantitative description of the placebo response trajectory in ADHD trials, together with the trial-level factors that modify it. The concordance between pediatric and adult placebo trajectories is supportive. These findings offer parameters for baseline-adjusted sample size estimation and endpoint selection in future trials. PROSPERO registration CRD420251171116.

articles.title: Neurocognitive profiles structure heterogeneous treatment response to bumetanide in neurodevelopmental disorders: secondary analysis of a multiple baseline single-case experimental design.
articles.abstract: We performed a secondary analysis of the Bumetanide for Developmental Disorders (BUDDI;EUDRA-CT-2020-002196-35) trial to examine whether baseline neurocognitive profiles are associated with differential behavioral and cognitive treatment response. Participants (7-19 years) with atypical sensory reactivity and ASD, ADHD, epilepsy, or TSC diagnoses received 6-months of bumetanide treatment (max 3.0 mg/day) within a multiple-baseline SCED. Neurocognitive functioning was assessed across multiple domains and used to derive subgroups via cluster analysis. Behavioral outcomes were captured using a parent-reported PROMset and standardized questionnaires. Linear mixed models and subgroup comparisons were used to evaluate change over time. Of 119 participants enrolled, 105 completed baseline and 85 follow-up assessments At the group level, memory improved after six months (B = 0.65, 95%CI = 0.45to0.85, pFDR < .001, d = 1.07), while processing speed decreased (B = - 0.25, 95%CI = - 0.42to - 0.07, pFDR < .001, d = - 0.49). Cluster analysis identified four neurocognitive subgroups with distinct baseline profiles and differential treatment responses: individuals with weaker functioning showed the largest memory improvements, whereas those with preserved functioning showed greater behavioral improvement alongside declines in processing speed and visuomotor integration. Across subgroups, neurocognitive and behavioral changes did not align, and correlations were small (r < 0.30). In this study, neurocognitive profiling based on a standardized test battery was associated with distinct patterns of change during treatment. The dissociation between neurocognitive and behavioral outcomes indicated domain-specific and non-linear treatment effects. These findings provide a basis for linking variability in real-world change to individual neurocognitive characteristics within a defined clinical context.Trial registration: EudraCT (2020-002196-35) registration date 24-04-2020. Protocol: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12888-022-04033-8.

articles.title: Parental experience of end-of-life care for their infant or child in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence confirms that provision of end-of-life care for infants, children and young people varies across the United Kingdom, however it is not clear how this variation impacts children and their families.
METHODS: This study aimed to assess parental outcomes and experiences of their infant, child or young person receiving end-of-life care in the United Kingdom through a cross-sectional mixed-methods survey. Bereaved parents were sent a survey, after their infant or child had died and had received end-of-life care in a neonatal or paediatric intensive care unit. The survey yielded qualitative and quantitative data, which were analysed using qualitative content analysis and graphical summaries of quantitative results. Data were integrated using joint display matrices.
RESULTS: One hundred sixty nine bereaved parents completed the survey, of which 60% were White British mothers of infants. Overall experiences were positive, however there were some differences between care settings and a minority reported mostly negative experiences. Key components of end-of-life care were not always available and choices over place of care were limited. Experiences of care as death approached were more positive. However, experiences of after death care, such as the use of cooling facilities, were highly variable with some parents expressing regret at not having the chance to have extended time with their child.
CONCLUSIONS: Parental experiences of end-of-life care varied widely, with key components often not available. Ensuring consistently high-quality care across all settings is essential to support parents' enduring wellbeing.

articles.title: Attitudes of registered nurses toward palliative and end-of-life care in Macao: a cross-sectional study in an east-meets-west context.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurses' attitudes toward palliative and end-of-life care may affect communication with patients and families, symptom support, and willingness to provide care for dying patients. Evidence from Macao remains limited despite its ageing population and healthcare context shaped by Chinese cultural traditions and Western medical practice.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to August 2021 in the main public hospital in Macao. Registered nurses completed an anonymous online questionnaire containing demographic/professional items and the Chinese version of the Frommelt Attitude Toward Care of the Dying scale. Negatively worded FATCOD items were reverse-coded before total scores were calculated. Welch tests, Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons, effect sizes, and multivariable linear regression with robust standard errors were used.
RESULTS: A total of 282 nurses completed the survey. Most were female (88.3%), held a bachelor's degree (75.5%), and had no palliative care training (61.0%). The mean FATCOD score was 110.45 (SD = 8.22), and internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.804). In adjusted analysis, prior palliative care experience was associated with higher FATCOD scores (B = 4.22, robust SE = 1.22, p < .001). Work unit also remained associated with scores; compared with Surgery, Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, and Orthopedics/Rehabilitation had higher adjusted scores. The model explained 22.6% of the variance.
CONCLUSIONS: Registered nurses in Macao reported moderately favorable attitudes toward palliative and end-of-life care. Training and experience should be strengthened, but cultural explanations should be interpreted cautiously because cultural beliefs were not directly measured.

articles.title: Bereaved mothers' and nurses' experiences of neonatal palliative and bereavement care in Iran: a qualitative content analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The death of a newborn in a neonatal intensive care unit is a profound experience for parents and nurses. Understanding how bereaved mothers and nurses experience communication, parental participation, farewell practices and continuing support can inform care that is responsive to families' individual and cultural preferences. This study explored bereaved mothers' and neonatal intensive care unit nurses' experiences of neonatal palliative and bereavement care in Iran and examined similarities and differences between their accounts.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study using conventional content analysis was conducted in the neonatal intensive care units of two tertiary university hospitals in Iran. Participants were selected through purposive sampling with maximum variation. Individual, semi structured, face to face interviews were conducted with mothers who had experienced the death of a newborn during the previous 12 months and nurses with experience caring for newborns and families during end-of-life care. Data were collected from March 2024 to January 2025. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim, anonymized and analyzed inductively using MAXQDA Analytics Pro 2020. Credibility, dependability, confirmability and transferability were supported through transcript review, independent coding, participant feedback, research team discussions, reflexive memo writing and maintenance of an audit trail.
RESULTS: Fifteen bereaved mothers and 18 neonatal intensive care unit nurses participated. Analysis generated three themes: losing and reclaiming maternal agency during neonatal end of life care, nurses' emotional labor in sustaining compassionate bereavement care and building a culturally responsive continuum of neonatal palliative and bereavement care. Mothers described receiving fragmented or indirect information, having restricted opportunities for presence and participation and seeking meaningful ways to acknowledge and remember their newborn. Nurses described providing emotional support while managing their own responses, professional responsibilities, educational preparation and organizational conditions. The accounts of both groups emphasized compassionate communication, respectful recognition of the newborn, individualized memory making, spiritual sensitivity and continuing support. Differences between their accounts concerned family mediated disclosure, maternal participation, opportunities for presence and touch, professional emotional expression and responsibility for follow up care.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants' accounts suggest that neonatal palliative and bereavement care may be strengthened by directly assessing each mother's preferences for communication and participation, sensitively offering individualized opportunities for farewell and memory making, and establishing clearly coordinated follow-up care. Education, reflective support and supportive organizational processes may assist nurses in providing compassionate care to newborns and bereaved families.

articles.title: Evaluation of spirituality among primary caregivers in a perinatal palliative care program in Mexico.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal palliative care seeks to maximize quality of life through physical, social, psychological, and spiritual care, supporting families from diagnosis through bereavement. Spirituality (the search for meaning and connection, and religiousness, a system of beliefs and rituals linked to the divine) shape the experience of illness and death, yet are often sidelined in medical care. Evaluating spirituality is essential but complex, as it requires translating an abstract concept into a socio-clinical measure and is limited by health professionals' lack of training. Tools such as FICA (Faith, Importance, Community, and Address in care) can facilitate this process.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the spiritual dimensions and needs of caregivers of newborns in palliative care, using the FICA tool as an evaluation guide.
METHODOLOGY: Semi-structured interviews with primary caregivers, guided by the FICA dimensions, were recorded and transcribed for thematic narrative analysis. Participants provided informed consent.
RESULTS: Caregivers of nine newborns were invited; seven caregivers of five newborns accepted. Ages ranged from 18 to 53 years; most belonged to extended nuclear families, lived in urban areas, and were traditionally Catholic. Most recognized their spiritual beliefs and needs and the importance of spirituality in their lives; six of seven belonged to informal spiritual communities. The affective dimension predominated, and anguish and abandonment emerged as spiritual symptoms.
CONCLUSION: FICA helps identify caregivers' spiritual dimensions, their community support, and how prayer, ritual, and family support provide comfort. Routine spiritual evaluation could help detect spiritual suffering and guide better support strategies from health professionals in perinatal palliative care.

articles.title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE for Targeted Alpha Therapy of Neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: High-risk neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of pediatric cancer mortality. Radioligand therapy targeting somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) with the β-emitter [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE) is under clinical investigation. Alpha-emitters such as actinium-225 (²²⁵Ac) cause more potent, localized DNA damage owing to higher linear energy transfer and shorter path length. We aimed to establish a robust labeling protocol for [²²⁵Ac]Ac-DOTATATE (²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE) for preclinical use and to compare its in vitro cytotoxicity with ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE in neuroblastoma cell lines.
METHODS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was synthesized using 5 µg DOTATATE per MBq ²²⁵Ac, and ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE at 60 MBq/nmol in 25 mM sodium ascorbate/50 mM sodium acetate (pH 5). SSTR2-mediated binding of ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE to IMR-32, SK-N-AS and BON cells was measured in real time (LigandTracer). Cytotoxicity was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® viability assay and DNA double-strand breaks by γH2AX immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was obtained with >95% radiochemical purity and remained stable for at least 48 h. ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE bound specifically to SSTR2-positive IMR-32 cells, with low binding to SSTR2-low BON and minimal binding to SSTR2-negative SK-N-AS cells. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) was 0.0049 kBq/mL for ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE and 5.4 kBq/mL for ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE, an approximately 1000-fold lower activity concentration required for alpha as compared with beta emitter. γH2AX analysis indicated a trend toward greater DNA damage with ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE. These findings support further development of SSTR2-targeted alpha therapy for high-risk neuroblastoma.

articles.title: Open fractures in children: a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractures are among the most common traumatic musculoskeletal injuries in children. A small fraction of these are open fractures. The risks of complications such as infection and soft tissue damage are suggested to be higher than closed fractures. The aim is to describe the characteristics, treatment, and outcomes of paediatric open fractures treated at a single level-1 trauma centre in the Netherlands.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patient and trauma characteristics were extracted from the Dutch National Trauma Registry, whereafter the data were completed with treatment and outcome information obtained from clinical patient records. Descriptive statistics were performed.
RESULTS: Overall, 52 cases of paediatric open fractures were identified. The majority was male (73.1%) and the most common injury cause was a road traffic accident (55.8%), followed by low-energy falls (11.5%). Only 27.0% had an Injury Severity Score (ISS) > 15. The most frequently fractured bones were tibia (38.5%), fibula (25.0%), hand (21.2%), radius (7.7%) and ulna (7.7%). Physeal involvement was seen in 9.5%. Complications were documented in 26.9% of all patients. Infections were seen in 15.4%, malunion and non-union in 3.8% of the research population.
CONCLUSIONS: Paediatric open fractures are relatively rare and most often occur after road traffic accidents with mostly ISS scores below 15. Physeal involvement is rare. Bone healing problems seem to be infrequent in the paediatric population.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4.

articles.title: Evolution of bilirubin detection: analytical strategies, sensing platforms, and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: Liver diseases, including fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, and cholestatic disorders, leading to hyperbilirubinemia contribute substantially to the global burden of morbidity and mortality. It is also a major clinical concern in neonates, with neonatal jaundice occurring in approximately 60% of term and 80% of preterm newborns during the first week after birth. Over the past decades, bilirubin detection has evolved from conventional laboratory-based methods to advanced sensing technologies designed for rapid, sensitive, and decentralized analysis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of bilirubin sensing, with emphasis on well-established electrochemical and optical sensing to integrated paper-based, smartphone-assisted, and wearable sensor technologies. Recent advances in functional materials, miniaturized sensors, digital analysis, and integrated sensing platforms have expanded the potential for portable bilirubin testing across diverse diagnostic and monitoring settings. These advances hold promise for applications in point-of-care (POC) testing, resource-limited settings, and neonatal care units, where timely and accessible bilirubin assessment is essential for informed clinical decision-making. Established bilirubin-sensing techniques and emerging technologies are critically evaluated to highlight novel approaches, compare analytical performance, and assess translational potential. Alternative sample matrices, which offer considerable potential for diverse applications, are also evaluated to distinguish exploratory demonstrations from clinically validated applications. Furthermore, matrix effects, sensor drift, storage stability, reproducibility, and variations across devices and fabrication batches are critically examined in relation to their implications for measurement reliability and clinical applicability. By integrating advances in sensing mechanisms, functional materials, and device architectures, the discussion provides a foundation for understanding bilirubin-sensing principles, critically evaluating reported approaches, and addressing existing challenges, while offering insights into sensor design and technology selection and identifying key priorities for developing reliable, accessible, and clinically translatable bilirubin-sensing platforms.

articles.title: Clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic effects of congenital DLK1 deficiency in women who had central precocious puberty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loss-of-function mutations in Delta-like Noncanonical Notch Ligand 1 (DLK1), a maternally imprinted gene at chromosome 14q32.2, are rare causes of central precocious puberty (CPP) associated with metabolic dysfunction in both sexes.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic consequences of congenital DLK1 absence in women who had CPP in their childhood.
METHODS: Peripheral blood from eight women from three distinct families who carried DLK1 deletions and exhibited undetectable circulating DLK1 serum levels were evaluated. 3T3-L1 cell differentiation into adipocytes was induced using DLK1-deficient serum from these women. In addition, mitochondrial function, cellular metabolism (Seahorse XL Analyzer), and whole blood transcriptomic profiling (RNAseq) were evaluated.
RESULTS: Women with congenital DLK1 deficiency had increased visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue on abdominal computed tomography. DLK1-deficient serum promoted greater adipogenesis of 3T3-L1 cells compared with control subjects serum. Flow cytometry revealed increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative stress in leukocytes in the patients. In addition, their leukocytes had decreased oxygen consumption and increased extracellular acidification. Whole blood transcriptomic profiling identified upregulation of several genes involved in neutrophil activation and inflammatory signaling, including obesity-associated genes (OLFM4 and LCN2).
CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrated distinct metabolic profiles in women with congenital DLK1 deficiency. The absence of DLK1 leads to increased adiposity, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and upregulation of genes involved in immune-related pathways, particularly neutrophil activation.

articles.title: Ocular Screening in Children With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis or Treated With Hydroxychloroquine: Clinical Report.
authors: AMERICAN ACADEMY OF PEDIATRICS, Section on Rheumatology
articles.abstract: Ophthalmic screening examinations are critical in children at risk for inflammatory ocular diseases or toxicity from medication use. Children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) who are at risk for or have had a diagnosis of uveitis require scheduled ophthalmic examinations. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is a treatment for several pediatric diseases and has a risk for retinal toxicity. Guidance is needed on the frequency of ophthalmic screening and the critical tests to be performed in both settings. Clinicians are highly encouraged to follow adult HCQ dosing recommendations (<5 mg/kg actual weight) until there are more specific data for children. This clinical report addresses recommendations for ophthalmic examinations in children with JIA, children with JIA-associated uveitis, and children receiving HCQ treatment. Families should be counseled about the critical importance of regular screening examinations for reducing the risk of visual impairment from disease-associated complications or medication toxicity. They can be reassured about the relative safety of medical therapy for these conditions if screening guidelines are followed.

articles.title: A National Pediatric Primary Care Research Agenda.
articles.abstract: Pediatric primary care (PPC) promotes child wellbeing through health supervision, anticipatory guidance, screening, and intervention. Given an evolving PPC landscape, content experts collaborated with the American Academy of Pediatrics Pediatric Research in Office Settings network in an iterative, multiyear process to create a PPC research agenda to advance child health that reflects professional and family priorities. Using an adapted nominal group technique, we identified research areas of focus based on (1) what PPC clinicians said they frequently encounter in practice; (2) the extent of the problem for families nationally; (3) evidence gaps; and (4) areas in which research could have the highest impact on child health. From 2022 to 2024, we synthesized contributor feedback from 8 key content expert sessions. This process resulted in 6 interconnected domains of highest priority for PPC research: (1) child mental health, (2) obesity, (3) communicating science to support families, (4) pediatric workforce, (5) injury prevention, and (6) adolescent health. We identified cross-cutting themes that warrant research in connection with these 6 prioritized domains. Examples of such themes include removing barriers to access and ensuring quality services for all children; under-resourced communities; care coordination and linkages within and outside PPC; supporting parents/caregivers; and technology and social media, which can serve as tools to enhance practice and can be assets or threats to child wellbeing. This manuscript details a vision for a national, coordinated PPC research agenda to inform investigators' and funders' efforts to advance primary health care and the health of all children based on our results.

articles.title: Interstitial Lung Disease in Term Born Neonates.
articles.abstract: Congenital panhypopituitarism, also referred to as combined pituitary hormone deficiency (CPHD), is a rare endocrine disorder characterized by deficiency of multiple pituitary hormones, including somatotropins, thyrotropins, lactotropins, gonadotropins, and corticotropins. Neonates with CPHD may initially be asymptomatic or present with nonspecific clinical features, frequently resulting in delayed diagnosis of this potentially life-threatening condition. This article presents 3 cases of term-born neonates in whom early diagnosis of CPHD was established during the investigation of atypical neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, presenting with radiological features suggestive of interstitial lung disease (ILD). All 3 infants exhibited persistent oxygen dependency. Etiological work-up of the ILD revealed central hypothyroidism and cortisol deficiency, consistent with CPHD. Brain magnetic resonance imaging in all cases confirmed ectopic posterior pituitary with pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. Initiation of hydrocortisone replacement therapy led to complete resolution of respiratory symptoms and successful weaning from oxygen. Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome with an ILD-like presentation in term infants may represent an early manifestation of CPHD. Further research into the prevalence of respiratory distress in affected neonates is warranted. A nationwide study across French reference centers for pituitary disorders is currently underway to explore this association.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.
articles.abstract: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend: EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should: ○ Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.○ Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include: ▪ External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquets▪ Airway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.▪ Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empirical bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.▪ External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.▪ Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.○ Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with: ○ Injuries that are incompatible with life (eg, decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).○ Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (eg, rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).○ Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.

articles.title: Acute Neurologic Decline in a Child With Unexplained Syndromic Features.
articles.abstract: A 17-year-old female patient was admitted for expedited neurologic examination after multiple falls. She had a history of 34-week prematurity, cognitive impairment, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and hypotonia without a unifying diagnosis. Over the past 2 months, she developed slurred speech, new extremity tremors, impaired concentration and memory, gait instability, and more frequent incontinence. Initial examination was notable for hypernasal, slurred speech, tremors, tongue fasciculations, and intrusion saccades. Imaging and laboratory analysis were inconclusive for a definitive diagnosis, and she was discharged with several genetic and metabolic panels pending. Five days later, she was readmitted with worsening headache, vomiting, and altered mental status. This case provides key insights into a rare pediatric neurologic disorder, as well as a potentially life-threatening complication early in the course of the disease.

articles.title: Changes in Childhood Food Allergy Following Implementation of Infant Feeding Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Since 2016, Australian infant feeding guidelines recommend introducing allergenic foods into the diet in the first year of life to prevent food allergy. Here, we evaluated whether the prevalence of food allergy in 6-year-old children changed following implementation of these guidelines.
METHODS: We conducted 2 population-based studies using the same methodology in Melbourne, Australia, before and after the guideline changes, recruiting 5276 12-month-old infants in 2007 to 2011 and 1933 infants in 2018 to 2019. Both studies followed up with children at age 6 years (2012-2016 and 2024-2025 respectively) with questionnaires, optional skin prick tests, and oral food challenges. Direct regression standardization compared prevalence estimates between cohorts, adjusting for demographic differences between the samples. Multiple imputation was used to handle missing data.
RESULTS: Participation at age 6 years in 2012 to 2016 was 84% and in 2024 to 2025 was 83%. After adjusting for temporal changes in food allergy risk factors, and applying multiple imputation, the prevalence of food allergy decreased: absolute reduction -2.0% (95% CI -3.4% to -0.6%, P = .005; n = 7209) and relative reduction -31% (95% CI -50% to -11%, P = .002). Findings were similar using complete cases (absolute reduction -2.9%, 95% CI -4.5% to -1.2%, P < .001; relative reduction -37%, 95% CI -57% to -18%, P < 0.001; n = 4173). This reduction was primarily driven by changes in cashew and peanut allergy; prevalence of milk and egg allergy did not change substantially in this age group.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide evidence that infant feeding guidelines recommending earlier allergen introduction may translate to measurable reductions in childhood food allergy at the population level.

articles.title: How Discrimination Shapes Care-Seeking for Black Caregivers of Children With Medical Complexity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Black children with medical complexity (CMC) experience a disproportionately high number of hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits. This disparity may reflect systemic and interpersonal racism and discrimination. Understanding Black caregivers' experiences is essential to designing programs that reduce acute care use. This study described caregivers' experiences of racism and discrimination and explored how these experiences influence care-seeking and communication among Black caregivers of CMC.
METHODS: In partnership with family advocacy organizations, we recruited Black caregivers of CMC via national advocacy groups, social media, and electronic health record messaging. Eligible caregivers had a child aged 0 to 21 years with a hospitalization or ED visit in the previous year and a score of 3 or more on the Children with Special Health Care Needs screener. Purposive sampling ensured that one-third of participants were from rural areas. Semistructured interviews, guided by Critical Race Theory, were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: Thirty-one caregivers completed interviews. Caregivers described discrimination in health care based on race and other characteristics. Five themes emerged in caregivers' experiences of racism: dismissal, stereotyping, fear of retaliation, dehumanization, and differential access to resources. These experiences contributed to distrust, caregiver burnout, and perceived negative health outcomes. Caregivers' responses to discrimination included withholding concerns, advocating, documenting, selecting specific clinicians, managing perceptions, and staying informed.
CONCLUSIONS: Perceived racism and discrimination shaped how Black caregivers of CMC communicated with clinicians and navigated health care, underscoring the need for health care systems and clinicians to foster trusting partnerships, address structural inequities, and provide equitable, family-centered care.

articles.title: ﻿Long-Term Efficacy and Tolerability of a Dermocosmetic Regimen in Mild-to-Moderate Facial and Truncal Acne: A 6-Month Clinical Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acne remains the most common inflammatory skin condition globally, with an increasing prevalence among adolescents and adults. Expert recommendations and clinical research indicate that dermocosmetic products can play an important role in the management of acne. The objective of this open-label, non randomized, single-center study conducted in Brazil was to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of an anti-acne dermocosmetic regimen combining a foaming cleansing gel, a multi-targeted cream, and a sunscreen for 6 months in subjects with mild-to-moderate acne on the face and trunk (chest and back).
METHODS: The investigation included 51 subjects (32 females and 19 males; mean age: 24 years). Subjects washed their face and trunk with the foaming cleansing gel and applied the dermocosmetic cream twice daily to the face and trunk, along with sunscreen at least once daily. The study included multi-zones (face and trunk) assessments, evaluation of clinical efficacy (inflammatory and non inflammatory lesions, acne-induced erythema [AIE], acne-induced hyperpigmentation [AIH]), objective skin barrier measurements, quality of life and stigmatization analysis, assessment of cutaneous tolerability, evaluation of cosmeticity/satisfaction with the cleanser and cream, and photography before/after treatment.
RESULTS: Multi-zone analysis of the combination dermocosmetic regimen demonstrated that the treatment led to improvement of acne on the face and trunk. The dermocosmetic regimen was linked to reductions in the number of inflammatory and non inflammatory acne lesions on the face and trunk. The AIE and AIH were statistically significantly improved on the back after 6 months. The regimen did not disrupt the skin barrier integrity. The stigmatization and skin discomforts associated with acne were significantly reduced. The subjects reported overall satisfaction regarding the efficacy and cosmetic properties of the regimen.
CONCLUSIONS: The use of a specific anti-acne dermocosmetic regimen was associated with improvement of mild-to-moderate facial and truncal acne.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06463925.

articles.title: Leukemia as the price of immunity? An evolutionary cost framework.
articles.abstract: Current evolutionary frameworks explain how leukemic clones are selected, diversify, and escape immune surveillance, yet they do not explain why leukemia-associated variants are so abundant in healthy individuals. We propose the evolutionary cost theory of leukemogenesis: driver mutations and oncogenic fusions are not random accidents but, in large part, recurring byproducts ("costs") of hematopoietic functions essential for survival. The same molecular machinery that enables V(D)J recombination, somatic hypermutation, APOBEC-mediated antiviral defense, stress-responsive hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) proliferation, and multilineage chromatin accessibility necessarily generates collateral genomic damage. These costs accumulate from development onward, creating a universal variant reservoir upon which selection, clonal evolution, and immunoediting subsequently act. Conversion from cost to clinical disease requires the convergence of four conditions: selection pressure, defense breach, failure of immune restraint-waning predation in aging, immature predation in early life-and time. This framework resolves several paradoxes, including the low mutation burden of infant MLL-rearranged acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), the accelerated risk in Fanconi anemia, and the single-driver sufficiency of chronic myeloid leukemia, and generates falsifiable predictions that distinguish it from multi-hit and selection-only models. Therapeutically, the goal shifts from eradication, which would require eliminating immunity itself, to ecological management: fortifying defenses, modifying the marrow microenvironment, breaking positive feedback loops, restoring immune predators, and establishing prevention windows in high-risk clonal hematopoiesis.

articles.title: Prevalence of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Associated with Congenital Heart Disease Following Defect Correction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Qual Care Clin Outcomes
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Understanding the disease burden of repaired pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) is essential for guiding healthcare strategies, yet data are lacking in this area.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) following defect correction in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).
DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed using PubMed, Embase and Cochrane databases.
STUDY SELECTION: Longitudinal cohort published between 1970-2023 involving CHD patients who underwent defect correction and were subsequently diagnosed with PAH were reviewed. Eligible studies reporting the prevalence of repaired PAH-CHD at least 3 months post-repair was included. Study selection was conducted independently by two reviewers. The primary outcome was the prevalence of PAH in patients following CHD defect correction.
RESULTS: Across 58 studies (7,036 participants), the random-effects pooled prevalence of reported post-repair PAH/PH was 10.8% (95% CI 7.3-15.0, I2 = 95.6%; prediction interval 0-50.1%). Prevalence was 9.0% (95% CI 3.3-17) in studies using right heart catheterisation, 19.3% (CI 10.6-29.7) in studies using echocardiography and 16.1% (CI 8.6- 25.1%) in studies using both modalities (p=0.19). Prevalence was highest in the adult-only cohort (18.5%, 95%CI 11.8-26.2) and lower in paediatric only (7.6%, 95%CI 3-13.5) and mixed-age cohorts (7.5%,95%CI1.7-16.3), p=0.039. Preoperative pulmonary hypertension (PH) was the strongest predictor of post-repair PAH and remained predictive on adjusted meta-regression (p<0.01).
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: PAH following defect repair remains a significant clinical dilemma requiring standardised diagnostic criteria and robust risk stratification tools to guide management.

articles.title: Neisseria meningitidis carriage in university students following a group B invasive meningococcal disease outbreak in Kent, England.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In March 2026, an invasive meningococcal disease outbreak in South-East England included 21 cases in young adults. In May 2026, we aimed to investigate carriage of meningococci in nearby universities, including the outbreak strain group B (MenB) ST-485 subtype P1·12-1,16-183.
METHODS: Students aged ≥18 years attending three university campuses completed a risk factor questionnaire and oropharyngeal swab for culture. Meningococcal isolates underwent serogrouping and whole genome sequencing. Carriage prevalences were estimated using the Clopper-Pearson exact binomial method. Associations between demographic or behavioural characteristics and carriage were assessed using modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Among 1991 participants, 76 meningococcal isolates were identified, including 18 (23·7%) genogroup B. Three isolates (3·9%) were ciprofloxacin resistant. The outbreak strain was not detected. Overall meningococcal carriage was 4·8% (95% CI 3·6-6·1%) among 1242 non-prophylaxed participants and 2·3% (1·3-3·6%) among 747 participants who received ciprofloxacin prophylaxis 6-9 weeks earlier. Higher carriage was associated with residence in shared accommodation (prevalence ratio 2·21, 95% CI 1·19-4·41) compared to a family home and combined smoking/vaping (1·90, 1·10-3·25), while chemoprophylaxis (0·27, 0·15-0·46) and Asian (0·44, 0·22-0·85) or Black (0·17, 0·05-0·42) compared to White ethnicity were associated with lower carriage.
CONCLUSION: Lack of outbreak strain carriage may reflect a highly virulent strain and the impact of outbreak control measures. The low overall meningococcal carriage rate continues a decline in carriage among adolescents and young adults over the past 25 years. Meningococcal carriage was lower in chemoprophylaxed students but rapid recolonisation suggests short-lived protection in semi-closed populations with ongoing mixing.

articles.title: Predicting adolescent physical activity beyond recent behavior: domain-level incremental prediction from motivation measures in two windows.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: An indicator can appear prominent in a fitted model without its wider domain adding distinct predictive information. We examined both repeated indicator prominence and domain-level incremental prediction of later adolescent physical activity beyond recent participation.
METHODS: Four assessments from 3755 Grade 7-8 adolescents at nine schools supported two approximately 3-month prediction windows: June-September (across summer vacation) and September-December. Participant-blocked rolling validation kept each adolescent in one fold and used earlier transitions to predict later activity. Elastic net and XGBoost compared 12 candidate characteristics in five domains with recent-activity-plus-sex baselines.
RESULTS: The recent-activity-plus-sex linear comparator explained 55.4% and 64.9% of held-out variance. Adding all characteristics increased elastic-net R² to.588 and.665 (absolute gains.034, 95% CI [.025,.043], and.017 [.008,.026]). Removing the motivation domain reduced R² across the two windows by.037 and.024 for elastic net and.039 and.026 for XGBoost (2.4-3.9 %age-point losses). Intentions, beliefs about capabilities, and affective appraisal were recurrent prominent indicators; removing the wider affective domain changed R² by approximately zero.
CONCLUSION: Motivation-related measures contributed domain-level predictive information in both windows, whereas prominent affective appraisal did not imply a comparable contribution from its wider domain. Independent school-based replication should assess generalisability, calibration, assessment burden, and decision utility.

articles.title: Medication Administration Errors Reported to a Poison and Medicines Information Center in Sudan: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Medication administration errors are a preventable category of iatrogenic harm, distinct from prescribing and dispensing errors. Case-level descriptions from Sudanese Poison and Medicines Information Center (PMIC) enquiries may help characterize the events that prompt requests for advice, although they cannot estimate population risk.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 553 enquiry narratives recorded in a Sudanese Poison and Medicines Information Center (PMIC) register between July 2022 and December 2023. Candidate cases (n = 27) comprised eight enquiries coded as medication error in the register and 19 classified as involving an iatrogenic administration-error route in a separate poisoning-focused analysis of the same register. Cases were eligible when the narrative described an administration-stage error involving dose, drug, route, rate, interval, diluent, or substance. Case ascertainment relied on these existing classifications; unflagged records were not independently rescreened.
RESULTS: Twenty cases met inclusion criteria. Fifteen (75%) involved a patient younger than 18 years. Healthcare workers were the documented error source in 13 cases (65%) and caregivers in 7 (35%). Wrong dose was the most common error type (8, 40%), followed by wrong drug (5, 25%) and wrong rate (2, 10%). Antimicrobials were the most frequently implicated drug class (6, 30%), followed by antimalarials (3, 15%) and cardiovascular agents (2, 10%). Five cases were documented as asymptomatic/stable, six as symptomatic/non-severe, two as symptomatic/severe, and seven had no status documented. Both severe-status cases involved a separate, serious clinical circumstance; causation could not be determined.
CONCLUSION: These descriptive cases represent enquiries reaching one PMIC, not population incidence or risk. They identify error patterns that may inform local review of dose verification, infusion-rate safeguards, and caregiver guidance.

articles.title: Dietary lactoferrin supplementation enhances immune function, improves intestinal integrity and reshapes gut microbiota in kittens.
articles.abstract: Lactoferrin is a natural iron-binding glycoprotein with barrier-protective, immunomodulatory, and antimicrobial activities, which is widely applied in human nutritional supplements and infant food additives. The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of dietary lactoferrin supplementation on immune parameters, intestinal barrier function, serum metabolome, and fecal microbiota in kittens. In this study, a total of 24 healthy kittens were divided into three groups and fed a commercial basal diet (CON) and the basal diet supplemented with 500 or 1000 mg/kg lactoferrin (L-LF or H-LF), respectively, for 42 days. Blood samples were collected on day 21 and 42 for measurement of immune and intestinal barrier markers. A repeated-measures mixed-effects model was used for data analysis. Serum and fecal samples were collected on day 42 for untargeted metabolomics and metagenomic analysis, respectively. Compared with CON, serum IgA level in the H-LF group was significantly higher on day 21 and day 42 (p < 0.05). The H-LF group showed higher serum IgM and lower IL-6 levels than CON on day 21, and both lactoferrin groups reduced IL-1β concentration on day 42 (p < 0.05), in contrast with the CON. Additionally, serum lipopolysaccharide and zonulin were decreased by H-LF relative to the CON on day 42 (p < 0.05). Untargeted metabolomics analysis revealed that lactoferrin altered serum metabolite profiles and increased levels of proline betaine, L-argininium(1+), and carnitine in H-LF (p < 0.05). Metagenomic analysis indicated that both L-LF and H-LF had a higher relative abundance of Bacteroidota but lower Escherichia coli than CON (p < 0.05). The H-LF group also increased the abundance of Prevotella, Bifidobacterium and Segatella copri in the feces of kittens (p < 0.05). Furthermore, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways of biosynthesis of secondary metabolites, biosynthesis of various nucleotide sugars, and sphingolipid metabolism were significantly enriched in kittens fed with H-LF (p < 0.05). Overall, dietary lactoferrin enhanced immune function, improved intestinal barrier integrity, and remodeled the gut microbiota of kittens, with the higher dose (1000 mg/kg) showing more pronounced benefits.

articles.title: Barriers to Effective Pain Management Among Pediatric Nurses Caring for Children With Sickle Cell Disease at a Public Health Facility.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sickle cell disease (SCD) imposes a significant public health burden in Ghana, with an estimated 2% of newborns (≈15,000 annually) affected and approximately 25% of the population carrying the sickle cell gene. The condition is characterized by recurrent episodes of severe pain requiring hospitalization. Pediatric nurses are pivotal in managing these crises; however, barriers such as limited pediatric specialization and inadequate institutional support constrain effective pain management.
OBJECTIVE: To describe barriers pediatric nurses encounter in managing pain among children with SCD.
METHODS: An exploratory descriptive qualitative design was conducted with 15 purposively sampled nurses. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using content analysis.
RESULTS: Nurses reported routine responsibilities such as hydration and pain relief, while noting resource-driven improvisations, like hot water bottles and room-temperature adjustments, rather than endorsed interventions. Most nurses lacked training in pediatric SCD pain management and had limited knowledge of the WHO analgesic ladder. Barriers included inadequate resources, absence of in-service training, and parental knowledge gaps. Some nurses expressed satisfaction with morphine use, noting improved pain control in children.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric nurses face significant barriers to effective SCD pain management, including limited training, scarce resources, and deficits in parental education. Strengthening protocols, increasing staffing, and implementing regular training are recommended to enhance pediatric pain care.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Web-Based Educational Intervention on Parental Knowledge, Attitudes, and Vaccine Hesitancy Toward Childhood Immunization: A Pre-Post Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaccine hesitancy remains a significant public health concern that may contribute to delayed childhood immunization. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a web-based educational intervention on parental knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine hesitancy toward childhood immunization among Saudi parents.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental single-group pre-post intervention study was conducted. Parents or primary caregivers of children aged 0-24 months completed an online questionnaire immediately before and immediately after exposure to a culturally adapted web-based educational intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 360 parents participated in the study. The intervention was associated with significant short-term improvements in parental knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine confidence immediately following exposure to the educational intervention. Parents demonstrated greater confidence in vaccine safety and effectiveness, increased trust in vaccine-related information, and fewer misconceptions regarding vaccination timing and common post-vaccination reactions. High levels of participant satisfaction with the intervention were also observed.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that the culturally adapted web-based educational intervention was associated with immediate improvements in parental knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine confidence among Saudi parents. Because the study employed a single-group pre-post design with immediate post-intervention assessment, further randomized controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these improvements are sustained over time.

articles.title: The Effect of Nursing-Implemented Swaddling and Dim Light on Sleep Patterns and Weight Gain in Preterm Infants: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPreterm infants admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are highly vulnerable to sleep disruption caused by environmental stressors such as excessive light exposure, frequent handling, and routine caregiving procedures. Disturbed sleep may negatively affect neurodevelopment, physiological stability, and growth. Developmentally supportive nursing interventions, including swaddling and environmental light reduction, are intended to minimise sensory stress and support behavioural regulation. ObjectivesTo evaluate the association of nursing-implemented swaddling combined with dim light exposure with sleep patterns and short-term weight gain among preterm infants. DesignQuasi-experimental controlled study with repeated measurements. MethodsThe study was conducted on a purposive sample of 60 preterm infants allocated to an intervention group (n = 30) and a control group (n = 30). Infants in the intervention group received standardised swaddling and dim light exposure during designated rest periods in addition to routine NICU care, whereas the control group received routine care only. Sleep-wake behavioural organisation was assessed daily for five consecutive days using the Anderson Behavioral State Scoring System (ABSS), and body weight was measured daily using a calibrated electronic infant scale. Data were analysed using non-parametric statistical tests, including the Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and Friedman tests.
