ResultsBaseline characteristics were comparable between groups for gestational age, birth weight, baseline weight, and APGAR scores; however, postnatal age was significantly higher in the intervention group (p = .004). Infants receiving swaddling and dim light demonstrated significantly greater improvements in sleep-wake behavioural organisation across the five-day study period than infants receiving routine care (all p < .001). The intervention group also showed significantly higher mean body weight at Day 5 (p = .009) and a higher mean discharge weight. ConclusionNursing-implemented swaddling combined with dim light exposure was associated with improved sleep-wake behavioural organisation and higher mean body weight at Day 5 and discharge among preterm infants, supporting the incorporation of developmentally supportive nursing practices into routine NICU care.

articles.title: Defending the vulnerable: current evidence and future priorities for maternal vaccination against Rift Valley fever virus.
articles.abstract: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) causes high rates of spontaneous in utero fetal death and neonatal mortality in pregnant ruminants and may pose an underestimated risk to pregnant people. There are currently no licensed vaccines available for human use, and existing veterinary platforms have substantial limitations in the context of pregnancy, underscoring the urgent need for countermeasures to protect these vulnerable animal and human populations. While significant progress has been made in RVFV vaccine development, the historical exclusion of pregnant people from vaccine clinical trials remains a barrier to access to vaccines. Recent draft guidance from the International Council for Harmonisation indicates that regulatory agencies will soon be expecting pregnancy-specific data during vaccine development. The recent advancement of several RVFV vaccine candidates to clinical trials provides an opportunity to address this unmet need in vaccine access for pregnant people. In this review, we synthesize the existing pregnancy-specific data for RVFV vaccines, including candidates currently in clinical trials. These data can potentially inform benefit-risk decision-making on RVFV vaccine use during pregnancy, and highlight potential evidence gaps ahead of future outbreak responses.

articles.title: Markers of Cardiovascular Risk Associated With Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: We sought to provide a brief review of available scores and factors to consider when assessing cardiovascular risk of pregnancy. We also discuss maternal cardiovascular risk stratification of survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer and congenital heart disease and identify gaps in knowledge.
RECENT FINDINGS: The modified WHO 2.0 I-IV in conjunction with the CARPREG II provides the most robust risk score to date but still has shortcomings. No score specifically addresses cardiovascular risk of pregnancy in survivors of cancer. While several tools for assessing risk exist, consideration of patient-specific factors also play an important role. Moderate and high-risk patients may be best cared for by multidisciplinary teams.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province, China, 2021-2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province of China, and to provide localized epidemiological data for the prevention and treatment of cervical cancer and related diseases.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on HPV genotyping data from 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital from 2021 to 2025. Overall infection rate, genotype distribution, age-specific positivity, and longitudinal trends were evaluated.
RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 18.57% (9,336/50,279), increasing from 15.30% in 2021 to a peak of 21.18% in 2023 but adjusting to 19.84% by 2025. Single infections were the predominant infection pattern (75.83%, 7,080/9,336). Age-specific prevalence exhibited a bimodal distribution, with the first peak in the ≤ 25 years group (23.56%, 810/3,438) and a second peak in the ≥ 56 years group (1,017/3,904, 26.05%). The five most prevalent genotypes were HPV52 (1,822/50,279, 3.62%), HPV16 (3.01%, 1514/50,279), HPV58 (2.46%, 1,239/50,279), HPV53 (1.97%, 989/50,279), and HPV39 (1.72%, 864/50,279), while HPV81 (1.70%, 856/50,279) were the most prevalent LR HPV genotypes. Annual analysis revealed HPV53 prevalence increasing significantly from 1.51% in 2021 to 2.72% in 2025 (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study provides the largest-scale data on the recent epidemiological characteristics of HPV infection in Lianyungang, China, which will guide the development of local cervical cancer prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes by maternal anxiety disorder during pregnancy occurring with and without other mental health conditions: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety disorders during pregnancy are common. Understanding whether the presence of anxiety with comorbid mental health conditions confers an increased risk to pregnant people and their infants is understudied.
METHODS: The sample included singleton liveborn infants in California from 2007-2020. Mental health conditions during pregnancy were obtained from discharge records. Adverse pregnancy outcomes examined included placental abruption, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), small or large for gestational age infant, preterm birth, or early term birth. Relative risks and 95% confidence intervals for each adverse outcome were estimated using modified Poisson regression with a log link and robust sandwich standard errors for people with an anxiety disorder diagnosis versus people without a mental health diagnosis. Calculations were made for people with any anxiety disorder, anxiety disorder only, anxiety disorder with comorbid depression, anxiety disorder with a comorbid non-depression mental health diagnosis, and anxiety disorder with comorbid depression and another mental health diagnosis. Four different models were considered: 1) unadjusted, 2) adjusting for racial/ethnic group, education, insurance, participation in Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), adequacy of prenatal care, age, and parity, 3) adjusting for model two plus infection, smoking, and drug/alcohol use, and 4) adjusting for model three plus diabetes and hypertension.
RESULTS: Of 5,836,541 maternal-infant pairs, 2.2% pregnant people had an anxiety disorder diagnosis during their pregnancy or at the birth admission. Of those with anxiety, 29.4% had a comorbid mental health diagnosis. People with an anxiety disorder during pregnancy were at increased risk of nearly all the adverse pregnancy outcomes examined. In fully adjusted models, individuals with anxiety and depression were 1.7-times more likely to have a provider-initiated birth before 32 weeks and were 1.5-times more likely to have SMM.
CONCLUSION: Maternal anxiety disorder diagnosis during pregnancy was associated with an elevated risk of an adverse pregnancy outcome even after adjustment for maternal factors. Rates of adverse outcomes were higher among individuals with a comorbid mental health diagnosis than those with an anxiety disorder alone. These findings indicate that individuals with anxiety disorders are at increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, highlighting the importance of prioritizing mental health support during pregnancy.

articles.title: The effects of different types of hormonal contraception on bone mineral density in women of reproductive age: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 150 million women worldwide use hormonal contraceptives; however, formulation-specific effects on bone mineral density (BMD) during the reproductive years remain poorly characterized. Prior meta-analyses are limited by the absence of untreated control groups and inadequate heterogeneity quantification, leaving clinicians without reliable guidance.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the effect of hormonal contraceptives on lumbar spine and femoral neck bone mineral density (BMD) in reproductive-aged women relative to untreated non-user controls stratified by contraceptive category, progestin class, and ethinylestradiol (EE) dose.
METHODS: This was a pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD420250640432; PRISMA, 2020). The MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL of Controlled Trials databases were searched from inception to December 2024. Eligible studies required a mandatory untreated control arm and ≥ 12-month DXA follow-up in women of reproductive age. Effect sizes were pooled as weighted mean differences (WMD) using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Evidence certainly was rated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Seven studies (k = 15 comparisons; n = 1,488 completers) met all inclusion criteria. The pooled WMD for lumbar spine BMD at 12 months was - 0.003 g/cm² (95% CI: -0.010 to + 0.005; p = 0.470; I² = 38.7%), below DXA precision limits and representing less than 0.3% of mean baseline BMD. COC users showed no significant BMD difference from controls across all progestin classes (WMD = - 0.0004 g/cm²; p = 0.925). A clinically interpretable EE-dose gradient emerged: low-dose formulations (≤ 20 µg; k = 8) showed a small but significant homogeneous reduction (WMD = - 0.011 g/cm²; 95% CI: -0.016 to - 0.005; p < 0.001; I² = 0%), while standard-dose formulations (30-35 µg) did not (WMD = + 0.009 g/cm²; p = 0.193). DMPA demonstrated a significant 2.0% lumbar spine BMD reduction (WMD = - 0.020 g/cm²; 95% CI: -0.038 to - 0.002; p = 0.030). RCT-only sensitivity analysis (k = 10) yielded WMD = - 0.006 g/cm² (p = 0.002; I² = 0%). The GRADE certainty was moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: COCs do not materially alter BMD over 12 months in reproductive-age women, with consistent null effects across all progestin classes. A biologically plausible EE dose gradient was identified; DMPA use warrants individualized counselling given clinically relevant, though reversible, bone loss. Adequately powered long-term randomized trials targeting low-dose formulations, adolescents, and DMPA continuers are urgently needed.

articles.title: Maternal and obstetric determinants of cesarean section delivery among mothers in public hospitals of Burao, Somaliland: an unmatched case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cesarean section (CS) is a critical obstetric intervention that reduces maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality when medically indicated. However, the increasing rate of cesarean delivery has become a major public health concern worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Evidence regarding the determinants of cesarean section delivery in Somaliland remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to identify maternal and obstetric determinants of cesarean section delivery among women delivering in public hospitals of Burao, Somaliland.
METHODS: An institution-based unmatched case-control study was conducted from April 15 to May 15, 2026, among 246 women (82 cases and 164 controls) who delivered in Burao General Hospital and Al-Khalifa Hospital. Cases were women who delivered by cesarean section, while controls were women who delivered vaginally. Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire and medical record review through KoboToolbox. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with cesarean section delivery. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to measure associations, and statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Previous history of cesarean section, non-cephalic fetal presentation, prolonged labor duration, and pregnancy-related complications were independently associated with cesarean section delivery. Women with a previous history of cesarean section were approximately nineteen times more likely to undergo cesarean delivery than those without a previous cesarean section (AOR = 19.35, 95% CI: 7.98-46.93). Mothers with non-cephalic fetal presentation were four times more likely to deliver by cesarean section compared with those with cephalic presentation (AOR = 4.05, 95% CI: 1.61-10.20). Women who experienced prolonged labor (≥ 12 h) were nearly nine times more likely to undergo cesarean section delivery than those with shorter labor duration (AOR = 8.92, 95% CI: 3.10-25.63). Similarly, women with pregnancy-related complications were approximately twelve times more likely to deliver by cesarean section than those without complications (AOR = 11.59, 95% CI: 4.60-29.18).
CONCLUSION: Previous cesarean section, non-cephalic fetal presentation, prolonged labor duration, and pregnancy-related complications were significant determinants of cesarean section delivery among women in public hospitals of Burao, Somaliland. Strengthening antenatal care services, improving labor monitoring, promoting early detection and management of pregnancy complications, and ensuring timely referral of high-risk pregnancies may contribute to appropriate utilization of cesarean section and improved maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: The effect of the centering pregnancy model on diabetes self- management, self-efficacy, pregnancy experience, and perinatal outcomes in women with diabetes: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes in pregnancy pose significant maternal and perinatal risks. The Centering Pregnancy group care model may improve diabetes self-management and pregnancy experience, but its effectiveness in Iran-particularly on perinatal outcomes-remains unproven. This trial evaluated whether Centering Pregnancy improves diabetes self-management, self-efficacy, and pregnancy experience (primary outcomes), and secondary outcomes including maternal satisfaction, breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum, preterm delivery, NICU admission, and cesarean section, compared with standard care in Iranian women with GDM or type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 100 women (50 per group) from Tabriz clinics. The intervention group received four bi-weekly group sessions plus standard care; controls received routine care. Primary outcomes (diabetes self-care activities [SDSCA], self-efficacy [DMSES], and pregnancy experience [PES]) were measured at baseline and 36-39 weeks. Secondary outcomes included satisfaction (Visual Analogue Scale), breastfeeding performance (Agunbiade instrument) at 6 weeks postpartum, and perinatal outcomes including preterm delivery, NICU admission, and cesarean section. from medical records. Analysis followed intention-to-treat principles using ANCOVA, with 6-week postpartum follow-up.
RESULTS: The intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in SDSCA (MD = 0.9, 95% CI: 0.3-1.4, p = 0.002), DMSES (MD = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.3-1.2, p = 0.001), and PES Uplifts (MD = 2.2, 95% CI: 0.3-4.1, p = 0.026) compared to the control group. Breastfeeding performance was significantly better in the intervention group compared to the control group (MD = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.4-1.3, p < 0.001). Perinatal outcomes showed lower rates in the intervention group but these differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed for PES Hassles, or satisfaction (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The Centering Pregnancy model is an effective patient-centered strategy for enhancing diabetes self-management, self-efficacy, and positive pregnancy experiences in Iranian women with diabetic pregnancies. Favorable but non-significant trends in perinatal outcomes warrant investigation in larger trials. This approach may be considered for integration into standard care protocols.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: IRCT20220718010324N70.

articles.title: Whole-body vibration training in addition to muscle-strengthening exercises alone in improving muscle function in children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 - a preliminary randomised interventional trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Identify whether whole-body vibration additionally to muscle-strengthening exercises improved muscle function in children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and muscle weakness, compared to muscle-strengthening exercises alone.
MAIN RESULT: No difference was noted in outcomes between the two groups.
SIGNIFICANCE: The interventions did not improve muscle function, albeit with low adherence.
PURPOSE: Children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) can have impaired muscle function. This preliminary randomised interventional trial investigated whether whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy in combination with muscle-strengthening exercises would improve muscle function compared to muscle-strengthening exercises alone, and their feasibility, in this cohort.
METHODS: Children with NF1 aged 6-16 years with muscle weakness were randomised to daily muscle-strengthening exercises for 6 months, or these daily exercises plus a WBV therapy programme for 6 months. The primary outcome was jumping power standard deviation score (SDS). Secondary and pre-determined exploratory outcomes included other measures of muscle function, balance, physical activity, fatigue and quality of life. Qualitative data regarding safety, feasibility and adherence were collected.
RESULTS: Forty-four children were recruited into the trial, with equal allocation to both groups. There was no effect on jumping power SDS between the two groups at the end of the trial (absolute effect size = -0.1, 95% confidence interval -0.5 to +0.3, P = 0.53). Similarly, no difference was detected with regard to secondary and exploratory outcomes. No significant changes in muscle function SDS were noted from baseline. The regimes within both groups were reported to be feasible. Adherence was low, affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and decreased enthusiasm over time. No adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: Six months of daily muscle-strengthening exercises alone or in combination with a WBV therapy programme is safe, although adherence was low. No difference in muscle function, balance, physical activity, fatigue or quality of life was detected when WBV therapy was added to daily muscle-strengthening exercises.

articles.title: Postoperative Sleep Quality in Children: Development and Psychometric Evaluation of a Questionnaire.
articles.abstract: Sleep in the immediate postoperative period is influenced by multiple perioperative factors. A key limitation in current research and clinical practice is the lack of brief, psychometrically robust instruments specifically designed to assess postoperative sleep. The aim of this study is to evaluate the psychometric properties of a short questionnaire assessing postoperative sleep quality in children and adolescents. The questionnaire was developed based on a literature review and 48 semi-structured interviews. This is a retrospective analysis. Out of 685 postoperative paediatric patients included across three studies (Study 1: n = 120; age: 14.7 ± 1.9 years, female: 43%; Study 2: n = 249; age: median 5.5, IQR: 4.5-6.5, female: 44%; Study 3: n = 312; age: median 12.0, IQR: 9.3-14.0, female: 38%), 88.5% (n = 609) could be included in the final analysis. Item response theory analysis was used to analyse factorial structure, reliability and measurement invariance (differential item functioning-DIF). A two-factor structure was identified: F1: Pain related impaired sleep quality and F2: General sleep quality with three items loading high on each factor could be identified (RMSEA: 0.01, 90% CI: < 0.01 to 0.06; CFI: 0.997, TLI: 0.996). Reliability was good (< 0.8) for relevant sleep quality ranges. No relevant DIF was observed with respect to sex or response mode. The Post-operative Sleep Questionnaire for children (Po-S-C) is a new short questionnaire for assessing postoperative sleep quality in children and adolescents showing good reliability and no measurement invariance. Further studies are needed to replicate these results in other samples.

articles.title: Experiences of parents during their intrauterine or perinatal child loss - a qualitative narrative interview study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the psychological consequences of intrauterine or perinatal child loss have been extensively studied, little is known about how parents experience the immediate period from the first suspicion of pathological alterations through pregnancy to birth. A deeper understanding of these experiences is essential for developing evidence-based recommendations for healthcare professionals.
AIM: To explore and organize parents' experience of child loss during pregnancy or at birth.
METHODS: This qualitative study represents the second phase of an exploratory, sequential, participatory mixed-methods project aimed at developing recommendations for healthcare professionals caring for families following intrauterine or perinatal loss. Twelve parents (nine mothers and three fathers) participated in nine narrative interviews in 2025. Data were analyzed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke within a phenomenological framework.
FINDINGS: Parents´ experiences were organized into two interwoven dimensions. The first dimension describes a chronological trajectory comprising five themes: living in suspended uncertainty, the collapse of normality, carrying the burden of decision-making, being held or dropped by the system, and becoming parents under impossible circumstances. The second dimension consists of four overarching themes accompanying the entire experience: contextual factors of child loss, preparing and adjusting, need time to process and grieve, and experiencing an inner conflict. Together, these dimensions demonstrate that parents´ experiences extend far beyond the moment of diagnosis or birth and evolve through continuously changing emotional, relational, and organizational demands.
CONCLUSION: Parents experience intrauterine or perinatal child loss as a dynamic process rather than a single event. Their experiences are shaped by both phase-specific challenges and overarching processes that persist throughout the trajectory loss. Healthcare professionals should therefore provide continuous, individualized, and coordinated support across all stages of care. The conceptual model developed in this study offers a foundation for developing evidence-based recommendations to improve compassionate and family-centered care following intrauterine or perinatal child loss.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered in the National Library of Medicine on January 13th, 2025 with the unique ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT06771661 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06771661).

articles.title: Effects of the maternal-free healthcare pilot policy on infant deaths in Ghana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: User fee elimination policies have been implemented in developing countries to eliminate financial obstacles that limit pregnant women's access to healthcare services. Numerous studies have revealed a positive association between the elimination of delivery fees and the uptake of maternal health services. However, only a few studies have examined its impact on neonatal and infant mortality rates (NIMRs).
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effect of the maternal-free healthcare pilot policy implemented from 2003 to 2005 in the Northern, Upper West, Upper East, and Central regions of Ghana on neonatal and infant mortality.
METHODS: We used the Ghana Demographic and Health Survey datasets for 2003 and 2008 and a difference-in-difference estimation approach for analysis.
RESULTS: The maternal-free healthcare pilot policy was associated with a 3.3 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points reduction in neonatal and infant deaths in the treatment regions.
CONCLUSIONS: The likelihood of infant death in the treatment regions was lower than that in the comparison regions during the pilot period. Neonatal and infant health policies should incorporate maternal health components to ensure the maximum benefit for the child from conception to less than one year.

articles.title: Errors in maternity settings: a systematic review of causes, contributing factors, and prevention strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Errors in maternity settings can significantly affect maternal and neonatal safety; however, they remain less explored than surgical or medication errors. Aligning with international safety initiatives, this systematic review aims to identify the causes, contributing factors, and prevention strategies for errors within maternity care environments to inform systemic safety improvements.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of international and Iranian databases was conducted for peer-reviewed studies published in English or Persian between 2008 and 2024. In accordance with PRISMA guidelines, study selection was performed through a structured screening process. Methodological quality was appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Given the methodological heterogeneity among the included studies, data were synthesized using a narrative thematic approach, mapping findings across the individual, team, administrative, and organizational levels of the healthcare system.
FINDINGS: Nineteen studies, 18 of which demonstrated high methodological quality, were included in the review. The synthesis revealed that errors in maternity settings result from a dynamic interaction of multi-level factors. Organizational and policy-level vulnerabilities were the most frequently identified contributing factors (57.9%), followed by individual-level factors (42.1%), administrative stressors (26.3%), and team-level dynamics (15.8%). Primary drivers included punitive safety cultures, staff shortages, and clinical knowledge gaps, highlighting that these errors are predominantly consequences of systemic weaknesses rather than isolated incidents.
CONCLUSION: Enhancing safety in maternity settings requires a multi-level paradigm shift from "person-centered blame" to "systems-oriented learning." By directly mapping actionable interventions to their root causes-such as implementing non-punitive Root Cause Analysis (RCA), optimizing staffing ratios, and providing targeted clinical training-healthcare institutions may achieve more sustainable approaches to error prevention.

articles.title: Adherence and clinical outcomes among patients with sickle cell disease receiving prophylactic therapy in Bamenda, Cameroon: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term prophylactic therapy is central to sickle cell disease (SCD) care, but evidence on medication adherence and patient-reported outcomes in Cameroon remains limited. We assessed SCD medication adherence and compared clinical outcomes before and during clinic-based prophylactic therapy.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at St Maria Soledad Catholic Hospital in Bamenda, Cameroon, from August to October 2024. Participants with SCD who had received hydroxyurea and folic acid, with age-appropriate penicillin prophylaxis, for at least 12 months were consecutively recruited. An adapted Hill-Bone medication adherence scale questionnaire was scored from 0 to 7, with higher scores indicating better adherence. Self-reported outcomes during the 12 months before enrollment in the prophylaxis program and the subsequent 12 months in the program were compared using paired McNemar tests. Factors associated with medication adherence score were examined using linear regression with Huber-White robust standard errors. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: Among 105 participants, the median age was 11 years (interquartile range [IQR], 7-16), and the median age at SCD diagnosis was 5 years (IQR, 2-6). The median adherence score was 5 (IQR, 5-6); 80 participants (76.2%) had a score of at least 5. Forgetting medication was reported by 59.0%, intentional nonuse by 30.5%, and running out of medication by 21.0%. Compared with the preceding 12 months, the proportions requiring transfusion (65.7% vs. 14.3%), experiencing at least three pain crises (67.6% vs. 30.5%), having at least three SCD-related hospitalizations (71.4% vs. 31.4%), having at least three non-SCD physician consultations (66.7% vs. 29.5%), and having a maximum hospital stay of at least 5 days (81.0% vs. 49.5%) were lower during prophylaxis (all p < 0.001). Age 10 years or younger was associated with a higher adherence score only in univariable analysis; no covariate was independently associated with adherence after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Within this single-center clinic cohort, medication adherence to SCD prophylaxis was generally favorable, although forgetfulness, intentional nonuse, and medication supply interruptions remained significant barriers. The marked reductions in selected clinical and healthcare-utilization outcomes during prophylaxis highlight the potential value of sustained, comprehensive SCD care. Strengthening access, continuity of treatment, and adherence support should remain clinical and public health priorities, while prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm causality.

articles.title: Health worker perspectives on the screening and management of hypertensive disorders and diabetes in pregnancy in Uganda: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and diabetes in pregnancy (DIP) are leading contributors to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet effective management depends on health workers having the knowledge, attitudes, and practices to screen, diagnose, and treat these conditions. Evidence on these provider-level factors remains limited in Uganda.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional survey among health workers in Uganda (November-December 2025), disseminating a structured questionnaire on HDP and DIP knowledge, attitudes, practices, prescribing, and task shifting via WhatsApp-based Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) networks and professional association platforms, hosted on REDCap. We analysed data in STATA 17 using descriptive statistics and comparisons across health worker groups.
RESULTS: Of the 690 eligible health workers, 577 completed the survey (83.5%). Midwives comprised the largest group (341, 59.1%) and most worked in public facilities (425, 73.7%). Knowledge and protocol integration were substantially stronger for HDP than DIP: CPD attendance was 70.9% for HDP versus 36.4% for DIP, self-reported protocol familiarity was 90.1% versus 38.6%, and routine BP screening was near-universal (538, 93.2%) while only 122 (21.1%) always screened for diabetes in pregnancy. Correct oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) thresholds were identified by only 186 (32.2%). Attitudes reflected strong support for patient involvement in treatment decisions and consistent treatment targets, with moderate confidence in guideline-based adjustments (279, 48.4%). Prescribing prioritised affordability (438, 75.9%) and reliable drug supply (473, 82.0%). Task shifting was widely accepted for basic functions including BP measurement (538, 93.2%) and lifestyle counselling (514, 89.1%), but less so for algorithm-based prescribing (170, 29.5%). Cadre differences were consistent across domains: for HDP, correct identification of severe preeclampsia features and use of advanced diagnostics were significantly lower among midwives than specialist cadres (p < 0.001); for DIP, gaps were most pronounced among midwives, with the lowest DIP CPD attendance (105, 30.8%) and OGTT endorsement (186, 54.5%) of all cadres (p < 0.001). Advanced diagnostic use and OGTT endorsement also increased progressively with facility level (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Health workers in Uganda demonstrate substantially stronger knowledge, attitudes, and practices for HDP than for DIP, with consistent cadre-related differences. Under-recognition of DIP likely contributes to missed opportunities for timely intervention. Targeted CPD on DIP, wider protocol dissemination, and system-level support for diabetes screening are urgently needed. Leveraging existing RMNCAH networks offers a practical pathway for integrating DIP into routine antenatal care.

articles.title: Metabolic profiling of brain and cerebrospinal fluid in cerebral malaria.
articles.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM), a severe neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, is a common cause of pediatric mortality and long-term cognitive impairment in endemic regions. The mechanisms driving CM-associated coma and neuropathology are not fully understood. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of brain tissue from experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) mouse models and brain autopsy tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from children with CM and non-malarial coma (NMC). ECM brain samples exhibited significant metabolic alterations, including differences in energy metabolism and amino acids and elevated pipecolic and lactic acids. In contrast, CM and NMC brain metabolomes showed limited differences. CSF metabolomes from cohorts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Malawi showed elevated glyceric acid in CM compared with NMC. Together, these findings highlight metabolic perturbations in CM across species and sample types and identify glyceric acid as a potential CSF biomarker.

articles.title: Gamma-delta T cells in neuroblastoma: Exploiting MHC-independent recognition to overcome the barriers of high-risk disease.
articles.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most frequent extracranial solid tumor in children and the main cause of early childhood cancer deaths. Relapse occurs in more than half of high-risk patients despite rigorous multimodal therapy, and four-year overall survival in relapsed disease is approximately 20%. Anti-GD2 monoclonal antibodies and GD2-directed CAR T cell treatment have advanced the field, although neither has eliminated neuroblastoma's immune resistance. Current immunotherapy has three interrelated challenges. GD2 heterogeneity lets antigen-negative subclones escape and cause recurrence. Inhibitory cytokines, regulatory T cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells dominate the TME. MHC class I downregulation frequently renders traditional αβ T cell methods ineffective, even with the target antigen present. Gamma-delta (γδ) T cells offer a distinct mechanism. They recognize tumor targets without antigen presentation by sensing stress-induced ligands through NKG2D and DNAM-1 and phosphoantigens through butyrophilin proteins BTN3A1 and BTN2A1. This recognition holds regardless of MHC class I status. In conjunction with anti-GD2 antibodies, CD16 expression boosts antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In neuroblastoma lesions, γδ T cells are the primary antitumoral fraction in tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte products, indicating compatibility with the disease's immune system. This study examines neuroblastoma immunotherapy failure mechanisms and innovative γδ T cell platforms, such as non-engineered allogeneic products, composite γδ T plus NK cell techniques, and CAR- and AbTCR-modified designs. A biomarker-driven patient selection paradigm and product standardization, in vivo persistence, and TME suppression are examined. NCT05400603, the first trial of adoptive transfer of ex vivo-expanded allogeneic γδ T cells in a population that includes pediatric neuroblastoma patients, is crucial for proving the mechanism.

articles.title: Culture-independent identification and serotyping of Streptococcus pneumoniae by targeted metagenomics in pleural fluid samples.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the leading cause of empyema and pneumonia in children and monitoring of effectiveness of polyvalent pneumococcal vaccines has been essential for controlling invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in children and elderly adults. Conventional serotyping of pneumococci has relied on Quellung reaction following laboratory culture; however, more recently whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has been implemented in many reference laboratories to enhance traditional typing. Pleural fluid samples from cases with empyema are often culture negative, limiting the utility of WGS and requiring PCR or 16S rRNA sequencing to detect S. pneumoniae. These molecular methods have limited sensitivity and capacity to characterize pneumococcus in clinical samples, especially in specimens with a low pathogen abundance. This study applied capture-based enrichment [(targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS)] to identify and characterize S. pneumoniae directly from pleural fluid samples. A total of 50 pleural fluid samples were subjected to tNGS with a custom probe panel, including 39 known positive fluids collected from IPD cases between 2018 and 2025 in New South Wales, Australia. tNGS results were benchmarked against molecular-based serotyping. Our tNGS achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity in detecting S. pneumoniae. Serotyping results were concordant with PCR, and 95% (37/39) of S. pneumoniae PCR-positive pleural fluid cases could be serotyped using tNGS. Standard molecular methods, however, could only determine serotype in 56% (22/39) of samples. This tNGS enabled 39% improvement in ability to directly identify and serotype IPD-associated serotypes of S. pneumoniae in difficult-to-culture pleural fluids, which can significantly enhance laboratory surveillance of IPD as well as our understanding of vaccine effectiveness.

articles.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep condition that has a harmful impact on one's quality of life and presents considerable health hazards, especially for pregnant women in their third trimester. It can lead to stress, postpartum depression and negative fetal outcomes. The prevalence and contributing variables of insomnia among pregnant women in Egypt have not been adequately studied. This study evaluated the prevalence of insomnia among third trimester pregnant women in Egypt and analyzed the associated risk factors.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This is a cross-sectional study of pregnant women in the third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital. The study included 390 participants. The study employed a pre-structured questionnaire that includes questions about sociodemographic and lifestyle attributes, accompanied by the ISI questionnaire used to diagnose and assess insomnia severity.
RESULTS: A total of 390 pregnant women in the third trimester completed the questionnaire. The prevalence of insomnia was 75.4% (n = 294), with 33.1% categorized as sub-threshold, 26.2% as moderate, and 16.2% as severe. Multivariate logistic regression identified maternal age 25-35 years (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.50-8.36) and age > 35 years (AOR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.01-9.70) as significant risk factors. Conversely, university education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11-0.61), overweight BMI (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.16-0.62), and rural residence (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95) were significant protective factors. Linear regression further confirmed that higher insomnia severity scores were predicted by increased maternal age, while overweight BMI (B = -3.10), rural residence (B = -1.98), and nulliparity (B = -3.69) were significant negative predictors of severity (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Insomnia is highly prevalent among pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester. Advanced maternal age and urban residence were associated with a higher risk and severity of insomnia, while higher education and nulliparity appear protective. Further research is needed to develop strategies to improve maternal well-being and reduce adverse outcomes for mothers and infants.

articles.title: Investigation of the relationship between breastfeeding myths and breastfeeding adaptation: a correlational survey study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early postpartum period is a critical time frame in which mothers' adaptation to breastfeeding is shaped and breastfeeding-related beliefs become evident. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between the level of belief in breastfeeding myths and breastfeeding adaptation among breastfeeding mothers in the early postpartum period.
METHODS: This correlational, cross-sectional study was conducted between December 2024 and June 2025. The study data were collected using the Introductory Information Form, the Breastfeeding Myths Scale, and the Breastfeeding Adaptation Scale. The sample of the study consisted of 181 mothers who agreed to participate in the research, had infants aged 2-4 weeks, and were breastfeeding their babies. Descriptive statistics, t-test, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation analysis were used for data analysis, and p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: In the study, it was determined that mothers' levels of belief in breastfeeding myths were low, while their breastfeeding adaptation levels were high. A statistically significant difference was found between breastfeeding myths scores and women's employment status and the place where they had lived for the longest period (p < 0.05). A statistically significant difference was found in total Breastfeeding Myths Scale scores according to prenatal breastfeeding education status (p = 0.002), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in total Breastfeeding Adaptation Scale scores (p = 0.092). Mothers who received prenatal breastfeeding education were found to have significantly higher scores in the "Infant's Feeding Capacity and Growth" sub-dimension of the Breastfeeding Adaptation Scale (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSION: According to the results of the study, although breastfeeding myths are still prevalent in the early postpartum period, mothers'breastfeeding adaptation levels were found to be high. Mothers who received prenatal breastfeeding education had higher Breastfeeding Myths Scale scores, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in total Breastfeeding Adaptation Scale scores between mothers who received prenatal breastfeeding education and those who did not. These findings indicate that breastfeeding counseling should be conducted with a holistic approach that takes cultural context into account and targets erroneous beliefs.

articles.title: U.S. preterm birth rates reduced nationwide, particularly among medically-induced deliveries, during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown period.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, many studies-particularly from wealthy nations-reported a drop in preterm birth rates. Our goal was to examine nationwide changes in U.S. preterm births in relation to a range of sociodemographic, perinatal conditions, and obstetric care factors.
METHODS: Using data from the publicly available natality files from the National Center for Health Statistics, we examined 25,767,850 observations of all U.S. registered singleton births during the months of April to June (i.e. early pandemic lockdown months) for the years 2015 to 2021. To control for seasonal shifts and focus on the early onset of the pandemic, we calculated average annual preterm birth rates (< 37 weeks gestation) between the months of April to June. We used these observed rates to generate predicted rates for 2020 and 2021, and stratified by sociodemographic and medical characteristics of interest.
RESULTS: The nationwide preterm birth rate has been increasing since 2015, but this trend was temporarily interrupted by a significant decrease in the early months of the pandemic. Preterm birth rates dropped for nearly everyone regardless of their sociodemographic characteristics. Additionally, there was a significant and steeper drop for late compared to early preterm births, for preterm home births compared to preterm hospital births, and significantly lower rates of preterm birth among those with induced births (c-section or vaginal). The average number of prenatal visits decreased in these months, and preterm birth rates significantly decreased among those with low (0-10) and average (11-15) number of prenatal visits. The decrease in preterm birth rates during this period was also accompanied by a decrease in fetal death rates, and decreases in neonatal and maternal intensive care admissions.
CONCLUSION: Our analyses indicate a potentially unintended interim health benefit of the pandemic across nearly all sociodemographic groups, with significant decreases particularly among induced preterm births. These findings, paired with reduced rates of fetal deaths and maternal and neonatal ICU admissions, suggest that in some cases, less intervention may have served as a benefit to reproductive outcomes. These results support the reduction in prenatal visits recommended by the 2025 national obstetric guidelines.

articles.title: Interactive effects of advanced maternal age and antral follicle count on preterm birth in women undergoing ART.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between advanced maternal age (AMA) and preterm birth (PTB) in assisted reproductive technology (ART) pregnancies remains inconsistent. We examined whether ovarian reserve, indexed by antral follicle count (AFC), modifies the association between maternal age and singleton PTB in women undergoing autologous frozen embryo transfer (FET).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted within the Anhui Maternal-Child Health Cohort Study in China. A total of 2,198 infertile couples who underwent ART treatment with autologous gametes were consecutively recruited between May 2017 and April 2021. Maternal age at embryo transfer was analyzed as both a categorical and a continuous variable. AFC was measured on cycle day 2-5 by transvaginal ultrasonography and categorized as ≤ 10 or > 10. Multiple adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for PTB in relation to maternal age were calculated and the interactive effects between maternal age and AFC on PTB were evaluated in logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Among 1,035 women, 123 (11.9%) experienced singleton PTB. Maternal age alone was not independently associated with PTB after multivariable adjustment, although women aged 40-45 years had higher PTB odds than those aged 20-<30 years in the fully adjusted model (OR 3.45, 95% CI:0.85-13.98), with borderline statistical significance. A potential interaction between maternal age and AFC was observed (3.69, CI 1.03-13.21). Among women aged 35-45 years, AFC ≤ 10 was associated with increased PTB risk (3.70, 1.03-13.30).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal age alone was not independently associated with PTB in this autologous FET cohort. Increased PTB risk appeared to be concentrated among older women with low AFC, suggesting that ovarian reserve may modify age-related PTB risk in ART pregnancies.

articles.title: Geographic variations and factors associated with breastfeeding counseling during the first 2 days of birth in Ethiopia: spatial and multilevel analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding improves child health, and counseling during pregnancy and after delivery supports early initiation and exclusive breastfeeding. However, coverage remains uneven in many low- and middle-income countries, and relatively little work has sought to use multilevel and spatial variability. Therefore, this study aimed to assess geographical variations and individual- and community-level determinants of breastfeeding counseling in Ethiopia.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis was conducted on 3,979 mothers using the 2019 Ethiopian Mini Demographic and Health Survey. Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi* statistics were used to identify clustering and hotspot areas, while SaTScan was applied to detect statistically significant clusters. Multilevel logistic regression was then used to examine the associations between breastfeeding counseling and its determinants. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals were estimated after adjusting for both individual-level variables (socio-demographic, infant and obstetric related variables) and community-level variables (aggregated from individuals).
RESULTS: The overall coverage of breastfeeding counseling within 48 h of postpartum was 39.6% (95% CI: 38.06%-41.10%) with marked regional disparities. The highest coverage was observed in Addis Ababa, Bahir Dar, Assosa, central Gambella, and northern SNNP, whereas the lowest coverage was observed in eastern SNNP, northern Somali, and southeastern Gambella. Mothers delivering in health institutions- (AOR = 5.20; 95% CI: 1.68-16.06), receiving postnatal checkups before discharge (AOR = 2.46; 95% CI: 1.51-4.00), and residing in communities with high antenatal care coverage (AOR = 2.12; 95% CI: 1.10-4.07) significantly increased the likelihood of receiving breastfeeding counseling.
CONCLUSIONS: Breastfeeding counseling coverage in Ethiopia is low with substantial regional inequalities, particularly poor access in the Somali, SNNP, and Gambella regions. Women were more likely to receive breastfeeding counseling when they delivered in health facilities, had postnatal checkups before discharge, and lived in communities with high antenatal care coverage. Integrating standardized breastfeeding counseling into all facility-based deliveries and postnatal contacts alongside targeted outreach services is recommended for low-performing regions.

articles.title: The impact of E-Coach nursing management on enhancing exclusive breastfeeding among puerperal women in China: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several puerperal women face challenges in maintaining exclusive breastfeeding, particularly in the early postpartum period. Encouraging puerperal women to align their intentions with their actions and guiding them to actively breastfeed for up to six weeks postpartum is crucial. The aim of the study was to enhance breastfeeding rates from 0 to 6 weeks postpartum by promoting the alignment of cognition and behavior regarding breastfeeding.
METHODS: A total of 169 puerperal women were recruited from a pregnancy hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either the intervention group (IG), which received E-Coach nursing management, or the control group (CG), which received routine antenatal and postnatal obstetric care. Data on puerperal women, infants, and breastfeeding were collected at baseline and six weeks postpartum.
RESULTS: The breastfeeding rate within 6 weeks was 20.73% in the IG and 8.64% in the CG (P = 0.0294). The breastfeeding rate during hospitalization was 39.51% in the IG and 23.46% in the CG (P = 0.0279). The median duration of accumulated exclusive breastfeeding after delivery was 7 (4, 14) days in the IG and 14 (7, 42) days in the CG (P = 0.0362), indicating earlier initiation of exclusive breastfeeding in the IG.
CONCLUSION: The E-Coach nursing management provides puerperal women with strategies to address breastfeeding challenges, enabling them to prolong breastfeeding as desired by expressing their feelings, concerns, and needs to obstetric nurse coaches. The program demonstrated a positive impact on improving exclusive breastfeeding rates in the later postpartum period.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study has been registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry database (Registration No. ChiCTR2300070672, Registration Date: April 19, 2023).

articles.title: Increased number of cells in day 3 embryosis associated with higher live birth rate in D5 vitrified-thawed single blastocyst transfer cycles.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cell number in 3-day-old (D3) embryos influences pregnancy outcomes in patients undergoing cleavage-stage embryo transfer. However, the association between D3 cell number and pregnancy outcomes following 5-day-old (D5) vitrified-thawed single blastocyst transfer remains underexplored.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort follow-up study included 2035 cycles of D5 vitrified-thawed single blastocyst transfer. Patients were divided into six groups according to D3 embryo cell number: ≤5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and ≥ 10. Live birth rate (LBR), clinical pregnancy rate, miscarriage rate, and neonatal outcomes were compared across the groups. Statistical analyses were conducted using a multivariate logistic regression model. Furthermore, mediation analysis was performed to explore the association between D3 embryo cell number and LBR.
RESULTS: LBR markedly increased with the D3 embryo cell number (p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis of high- and low-quality blastocysts also revealed significant differences in LBR across the groups (p < 0.05). Conversely, the miscarriage rate markedly decreased as the D3 embryo cell number increased (p < 0.05). The D3 embryo cell number and perinatal outcomes did not show an association. Compared with the 8-cell group, the ≤ 5-cell group had significantly lower LBR [aOR: 0.681, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.468-0.991, p < 0.05], whereas the ≥ 10-cell group had a significantly higher LBR (aOR: 1.632, 95% CI: 1.214-2.159, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed that D3 embryo cell number provides unique prognostic information for live birth outcomes beyond blastocyst quality metrics. Furthermore, the inclusion of D3 embryo cell number improved the predictive performance of the ROC model (ΔAUC = 0.012, 95% CI: 0.004-0.023, p = 0.007).
CONCLUSION: D3 embryo cell number is a valuable supplementary indicator for selecting D5 blastocysts in vitrified-thawed single blastocyst transfer cycles. Among blastocysts with comparable morphological quality, those derived from fast-cleaving D3 embryos were associated with a lower miscarriage rate and a higher likelihood of live birth, specifically when transferring lower-quality blastocysts.

articles.title: Maternal obesity, overweight, and pregnancy outcomes: a cross-sectional study at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Obesity and overweight remain rising public health challenges globally, with worse outlook in low-resource settings. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of obesity and overweight, the associated sociodemographic characteristics, and the maternal and neonatal pregnancy outcomes at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
METHOD: This hospital-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the maternity block of Korle Bu Teaching Hospital between March and June 2024. Participants were postpartum women aged 18 years and above who had singleton pregnancies, delivered after 28 weeks of gestation, had booking weight and height recorded in their antenatal records, and were enrolled within 24-72 h after delivery. Data collection utilized pretested questionnaires, and Body Mass Index was calculated using antenatal booking weight and height. Descriptive statistics, including mean (with standard deviation), frequency tables, charts, and graphs, were used to summarize the results. A chi-square test was used to determine the possible association between independent variables and BMI categories. Fisher's exact test was utilized when any of the categories had fewer than five participants. All associations were evaluated at a 95% confidence interval and a 5% significance level.
RESULTS: The average age of the respondents was 31.1 ± 5.9years, with modal age-group of 30-34; and average gestational age at booking was 10weeks 3 days(± 1week4days). Overall, 30.3% of participants were obese and 27.8% overweight. Although obesity and overweight appeared more frequent among participants with hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, and caesarean deliveries, none of these associations reached statistical significance (all p > 0.05). Majority (81.3%) had term delivery; 94% of infants had normal Apgar scores at both 1 and 5 min, while at 5 min 3.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% had mild, moderate, and severe asphyxia, respectively. An estimated 63.6% of obese mothers had macrosomic infants.
CONCLUSION: We found a high prevalence of obesity and overweight among pregnant women. Higher BMI was more common among women who were married, multiparous, unemployed, or had no formal education. It was also more common among those with hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, postpartum haemorrhage, caesarean delivery, and macrosomia. However, none of these associations reached statistical significance in this sample. Interventions focusing on promoting healthy weight management and physical activity during pregnancy are essential.

articles.title: "I do not want to do that alone": couples' experiences navigating hybrid perinatal care during a public health crisis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic challenged healthcare systems to balance infection prevention with equitable, patient-centered perinatal care. Risk-mitigation policies including restricted visitor access and rapid adoption of telehealth were intended to protect maternal and infant health. While many studies focus on the birthing individual, few studies have examined the perspectives of both members of a couple or how hybrid models of care may address gaps exposed during a public health crisis.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study of couples early in the pandemic to examine perinatal care experiences among pregnant/postpartum women and their partners. Participants were drawn from a prior pilot study focused on reducing anxiety and depression; eligible pregnant women screened positive for elevated symptoms (GAD-7 or PHQ-9 ≥ 10) and were cohabiting with a consenting partner. All trial participants were invited to an interview; data were collected from all who accepted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted individually via Zoom and explored experiences of healthcare engagement, perceptions of pandemic-related policy, and the role of perinatal support people. Forty-two interviews with 20 women and 9 partners were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis supported by team-based coding and a consensus-driven analytic process.
FINDINGS: Three major themes emerged with virtual care functioning as a crosscutting element across themes: (1) Inclusion of Support People, including isolating experiences, fear of receiving traumatic news, partner perspectives, and the role of doulas; (2) Virtual Care: Necessity and Promise, highlighting both the benefits and limitations of telehealth; and (3) Navigating Perinatal Care, encompassing perceptions of care quality, policy inconsistencies, and adaptations to safety measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Emergency perinatal policies must be clear, consistent, and adaptable to meet patient needs while preserving the presence of essential support people. In this study we found hybrid prenatal care models that combine telehealth and in-person support were valued for clear communication, and support presence. However, their effects on experience, satisfaction, and preparedness cannot be assumed from these data and require further study among perinatal couples.

articles.title: The association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and risk of small for gestational age in China: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify the relationship of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) with the occurrence risk of small for gestational age (SGA) in China.
METHODS: The Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Medline and Web of Science databases were searched for available studies. Relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were combined and subgroup analysis based on the specific comorbidity was conducted.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies with 24712 cases were included. The incidence rates of SGA among the ICP and non-ICP patients were 14.04% (294/2094) and 4.66% (1053/22618), respectively. Pooled results demonstrated that ICP was significantly related to the occurrence of SGA (RR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.99-4.88, P＜0.001) in Chinese pregnant women. Subgroup analysis based on specific comorbidity also showed the relationship between ICP and SGA among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (RR=6.09, 95% CI: 2.96-12.55, P＜0.001) and hepatitis B virus infection (RR=3.22, 95% CI: 1.69-6.12, P＜0.001).
CONCLUSION: In China, ICP was associated with the occurrence of SGA in China and pregnant patients with ICP experienced a significantly higher risk of SGA.

articles.title: Pregnancy and neonatal outcomes of sequential embryo transfer versus double cleavage-stage embryo transfer and double blastocyst transfer in frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sequential embryo transfer (Seq-ET), involving the transfer of a cleavage-stage embryo followed by a blastocyst within the same frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) cycle, has been proposed as an alternative strategy to improve reproductive outcomes. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness and neonatal safety compared to the traditional double embryo transfer (DET) in the general infertile population remains limited.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study incorporated 2,959 FET cycles, using Seq-ET (n = 165), and DET strategies at Day 3 cleavage (D3-DET, n = 1,043) or Day 5/6 blastocyst (D5/6-DET, n = 1,751) stage in our reproductive center (2023.07-2025.01). The Seq-ET group was separately matched with the D3-DET or D5/6-DET group by propensity score matching (PSM). Propensity score-adjusted logistic regression analyses were used to control for confounding factors. The live birth rate (LBR), biochemical pregnancy rate, clinical pregnancy rate (CPR), implantation rate, miscarriage rate, multiple pregnancy rate, multiple live birth rate and neonatal outcomes were analyzed between groups.
RESULTS: Seq-ET had significantly higher biochemical pregnancy rate (81.99% vs. 63.52%, P < 0.001), CPR (67.08% vs. 43.57%, P < 0.001), and LBR (51.55% vs. 33.86%, P < 0.001) than D3-DET. Compared with D5/6-DET, Seq-ET showed comparable biochemical pregnancy rate, CPR, and LBR, but was associated with a significantly lower multiple pregnancy rate (20.91% vs. 33.94%, P = 0.014) and higher miscarriage rate (22.73% vs. 13.94%, P = 0.048). Neonatal outcomes were analyzed separately for singleton and twin live births. No significant differences were observed among singleton live births. Among twin live births, D5/6-DET had shorter gestational age at delivery, while other neonatal outcomes did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Seq-ET yielded superior pregnancy outcomes compared with D3-DET and achieved pregnancy outcomes comparable to D5/6-DET while reducing the risk of multiple pregnancy, although a higher miscarriage rate was observed in the Seq-ET group. Neonatal outcomes were generally comparable between groups, with the except of shorter gestational age at delivery for twin live births in D5/6-DET group. These findings indicate that Seq-ET may serve as a viable alternative double embryo transfer strategy in FET cycles.

articles.title: Assessing prevalence, risk factors, and the association between trichomonas vaginalis and urine glucose and albumin in pregnant women at Bamenda III, Cameroon.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Trichomoniasis in pregnancy is associated with poor reproductive outcomes, including pelvic inflammatory disease, preterm delivery, and low birth weight. Urine albumin and sugar in pregnancy are major complications that might arise during pregnancy and are a cause for concern. This study aims to assess the prevalence and risk factors of Trichomonas vaginalis among pregnant women and their impact on urine glucose and albumin.
METHODOLOGY: The study was a cross-sectional study involving pregnant women at first antenatal visits from March to May 2024. A total of 200 pregnant women were recruited for the study. Vaginal swab samples were collected for the identification of Trichomonas vaginalis. Risk factors were identified using a closed-ended questionnaire, and the presence of albumin and glucose was identified using dipstick test strips.
RESULT: A total of 200 participants were recruited; the age ranges from 18 to 35 years, with a mean of 26.4± (4.5) years. The overall prevalence of T. vaginalis was 6.5% (13). The prevalence of urine albumin was insignificantly (p = 0.37) low 0 (0.0%) among those who were positive for T. vaginalis. Urine glucose was significantly higher (p = 0.001) in women who had trichomoniasis 10 (71.4%). Our data showed that women who had more than one sex partner [20.0%, Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR) 0.158 (0.031-0.796); p = 0.025] and women with a previous history of STI [10.2%, AOR 5.261(1.282-21.585); p = 0.021] were at higher risk of acquiring T. vaginalis infection.
CONCLUSION: The high frequency of trichomoniasis requires that this test be made a routine test for pregnant women. The results report for the first time that glucose was high in pregnant women who were positive for trichomoniasis, thereby showing a need for further research considering the effects of gestational diabetes.

articles.title: PROTECT: PRegnancy Outcomes using continuous glucose monitoring TEChnology in pregnant women with early-onset Type 2 diabetes: a multicentre randomised controlled trial - study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset type 2 diabetes (EOT2D), meaning type 2 diabetes diagnosed before the age of 40 disproportionately affects women from socially deprived and minority ethnic groups. EOT2D is now the most common form of pre-existing diabetes complicating pregnancy. These pregnancies carry high risks of congenital anomalies, stillbirth, neonatal death, and of both maternal and neonatal morbidity. Maternal glycaemia is the key modifiable risk factor yet remains suboptimal and is often accompanied by limited self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG). Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) offers continuous real-time glucose profiles, potentially enabling better dietary, lifestyle and therapy adjustments.
METHODS / DESIGN: The PROTECT trial is a multicentre, randomised controlled trial designed to evaluate whether CGM improves maternal glucose and neonatal outcomes in women with EOT2D. The trial will recruit 422 pregnant participants (≤ 16 weeks 0 days' gestation, HbA1c ≥ 43 mmol/mol) from around 20 UK NHS antenatal diabetes clinics. After a run-in phase with masked CGM, participants will be randomised to either real-time CGM (FreeStyle Libre 3) or standard SMBG. The primary maternal outcome is percentage of time in pregnancy-specific glucose target range (3.5-7.8 mmol/L). The primary neonatal outcome is a composite of neonatal care unit admission or death. Secondary outcomes include maternal HbA1c, glycaemic variability, insulin use, obstetric complications, neonatal morbidity, psychosocial measures, and cost-effectiveness. An internal pilot will assess recruitment feasibility, before proceeding to the full trial. Qualitative interviews with women and healthcare professionals will explore barriers and facilitators to CGM use. Statistical analyses will follow intention-to-treat principles.
DISCUSSION: This is the largest trial to date investigating CGM in EOT2D pregnancy, aiming to generate robust evidence on clinical efficacy, lived experiences, and economic impact, informing future NHS policy and practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN12804317 Registration Date: 23/10/2023.

articles.title: Maternal - fetal outcomes and risk factors of uterine rupture in the setting of pregnant women with scarred versus unscarred uterus: a systematic review and meta - analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare risk factors and outcomes of uterine rupture among patients with a scarred versus an unscarred uterus.
METHODS: In this meta - analysis, we analyzed studies published in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and Clinical Trials. gov that appeared in our search from inception to 18/03/2024.
RESULT: This study included a total of 15 studies (1 prospective study and 14 retrospective studies). It comprised 914 cases of patients with scarred uterus and 468 cases of patients with unscarred uterus. Among the 914 scarred uterus cases, 861 (94.2%) were due to prior cesarean section, and the remaining 53 (5.8%) were attributable to other uterine surgeries. The meta - analysis demonstrated that the rates of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage were higher in women with unscarred uterine rupture than in scarred group. Although maternal mortality was also elevated in the unscarred group, the difference did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, compared with scarred uterine rupture, cases of unscarred uterine rupture were more frequently associated with advanced maternal age, oxytocin use, induction of labor, and malpresentation.
CONCLUSION: Compared to patients with scarred uterine rupture, unscarred uterine rupture is associated with significantly higher risks of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, advanced maternal age, a higher incidence of oxytocin, induction of labor, and malpresentation were associated with rupture in the unscarred uterus group. These factors should be taken seriously. Early identification of relevant risk factors is crucial to avoid potential obstetric emergencies, prevent diagnostic delays, and allow timely surgical intervention to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate in Paediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Assessed by Physicians and School Teachers: A Post-marketing Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate (LDX) is a long-acting prodrug approved for the treatment of paediatric attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in Japan. This multicentre, prospective, post-marketing surveillance study evaluated real-world safety and effectiveness of LDX in children and adolescents with ADHD in Japan.
METHODS: Patients aged 6 to < 18 years initiating LDX between April 2021 and September 2023 were enrolled across 24 medical institutions in Japan. Safety was assessed over 24 weeks by monitoring adverse drug reactions (ADRs), including dependence/abuse events. Effectiveness was evaluated by physicians and school teachers at baseline, and weeks 12 and 24 using the Japanese ADHD rating scale IV (ADHD-RS-IV) questionnaire.
RESULTS: Of the 88 enrolled patients, 73 were included in the safety analysis and 57 in the effectiveness analysis. The mean (standard deviation [SD]) age was 10.4 (2.6) years; 79.5% were male and 20.5% were female. Most patients (90.4%) had received prior ADHD treatment. LDX was initiated at a mean (SD) dose of 26.8 (4.7) mg, with 72.6% continuing treatment at week 24. ADRs occurred in 30.14% of patients; the most common (in ≥ 2 patients) were decreased appetite (17.81%), weight decrease (4.11%), and aggression, insomnia, irritability, middle insomnia, and abdominal pain (each 2.74%). One serious ADR (suicide attempt with methylphenidate overdose, also considered a dependence/abuse event) was reported; LDX was discontinued and the patient recovered the following day. No other dependence/abuse events were reported. Physician- and teacher-rated ADHD-RS-IV total scores improved significantly from baseline: mean (SD) changes were - 10.1 (8.0; p < 0.0001) at week 12 and - 9.7 (8.5; p < 0.0001) at week 24 for physician-rated scores, and - 4.9 (8.5; p < 0.001) at week 12 and - 5.1 (9.7; p < 0.01) at week 24 for teacher-rated scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this post-marketing surveillance study of LDX in paediatric patients with ADHD in Japan were consistent with its established safety profile. Patients' ADHD symptoms improved according to both physician and teacher assessments.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) Clinical Trials Registry (identifier UMIN000046038).

articles.title: The Societal Burden of Sickle Cell Disease: A Life Course Perspective.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sickle cell disease (SCD) places a lifelong burden on patients and family members. Our objective was to review the available evidence to understand the impact of SCD across the life course, including childhood development, education, employment, quality of life, and life expectancy.
METHODS: This targeted literature review examined empirical studies from 2001 to 2026 that assessed the burden of SCD among patients and family caregivers across different life stages, including childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Outcomes included early childhood development, education, labor market outcomes, life expectancy, and impact on family caregivers.
RESULTS: Overall, 23 unique studies were included. Studies consistently demonstrated that SCD places a large burden on patients and family caregivers across all life stages, especially for those with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises. Many children with SCD experience significant developmental delays in cognition, while adolescents often experience greater school absenteeism, worse academic performance, and a higher likelihood of school dropout. Caregivers for children with SCD experience lost labor market opportunities and diminished mental health. Adults with SCD are less likely to work (unemployment), and when they do, they often have greater work absenteeism and presenteeism, worse job opportunities, and less income. Ultimately, people with SCD experience both lower overall life expectancy and lower quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Patients with SCD experience a burden associated with the disease across the life course. These outcomes should inform future evaluations of treatment and supportive services for SCD, which have the potential to generate substantial societal value.

articles.title: Vamorolone for DMD: Clinical Pharmacology of a Novel Dissociative Corticosteroid, A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Vamorolone is a dissociative corticosteroid approved for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). This review presents the clinical pharmacology program in support of its development, including dose rationale, pharmacokinetics-pharmacodynamics (PK-PD) modeling, and regulatory alignment. Key findings from early-phase studies, food effect evaluation, special population modeling, bioequivalence assessments, and comparative pharmacology evaluation are summarized. This narrative review synthesized 15 studies/investigations from peer-reviewed publications, regulatory documents, and unpublished sponsor data. Particular attention is given to the evaluation of PK in the target pediatric population across age groups, using population modeling to support individualized dosing. Vamorolone demonstrated dose-proportional PK (i.e., exposure increased in proportion to dose) in the therapeutic range, increased bioavailability with food intake, and a favorable safety profile at doses up to 6 mg/kg/day. PK-PD modeling supported individualized dosing in pediatric patients. In clinical trials and indirect treatment comparisons, vamorolone efficacy was broadly comparable to standard corticosteroids with a differentiated safety profile in which some corticosteroid-class adverse effects (notably effects on bone and growth) appeared attenuated. Clinically relevant, dose-dependent corticosteroid-class-related effects, including hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal-axis suppression, Cushingoid features, increased weight and appetite, behavioral/mood disturbances, headache, and gastrointestinal disorders remain at therapeutic doses. The vamorolone clinical pharmacology program demonstrates how mechanistic innovation related to dissociative glucocorticoid‑receptor signaling, modeling, and strategic regulatory alignment can inform corticosteroid therapy in DMD. The differentiated mechanism of action, efficacy, individualized dosing approach, and differentiated safety profile of vamorolone make it a promising option in DMD care.

articles.title: Gender bias in stereotypes of autism: Assessing the non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic group.
articles.abstract: Autistic women face specific challenges and feel they do not fit the autistic prototype. This paper examines the gendered nature of stereotypes towards autistic individuals as a possible underlying mechanism, owing to the apparent incompatibility between stereotypes on autistic individuals and stereotypes on women. In four studies, stereotypes about autistic individuals were analysed through a gendered (Studies 1 and 2) or intersectional lens (Studies 3 and 4). The first two studies used a trait nomination task (Study 1) or ecological traits (Study 2). Contrary to expectations, in these studies, stereotypes towards autistic individuals were represented by traits that are more predominantly perceived as feminine. However, more detailed analysis suggests that this varies according to facets of social evaluation. To deepen these results, two other studies focused on perceptions within the intersectional space. Study 3 underlined that core characteristics associated with autistic individuals are perceived as more representative of autistic men than of autistic women. Finally, a fourth study suggests that autistic women are being perceived differently than the average of autistic individuals and autistic men. These findings suggest that core facets of the stereotypes of autism are more masculine, suggesting a non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic community.

articles.title: Study of 34 prospective pregnancies in women receiving IL-1 inhibitors for autoinflammatory diseases and comparison to unexposed pregnancies (GR2 study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors are widely used in autoinflammatory diseases (AID) such as Still’s disease and monogenic inflammasomopathies, including cryopyrinopathies (CAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. As these conditions frequently affect women of reproductive age and data are limited, concerns remain regarding anti-IL-1 therapy safety during pregnancy. We aimed to evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes in women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception and pregnancy.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included pregnant women from the Groupe de recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares (GR2) prospective cohort, spanning 76 French centres before September 2024. Women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception or pregnancy were selected. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched control group of unexposed women with similar conditions and with the nationwide 2021 French National Perinatal Survey.
RESULTS: Thirty-four pregnancies (three twin pregnancies) in 31 women were exposed to anakinra (n=30) and/or canakinumab (n=5) for Still’s disease (n=15), familial Mediterranean fever (n=15), CAPS (n=3), undifferentiated systemic AID (n=2), tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome and recurrent pericarditis (n=1 each). Reported outcomes included infections (n=6), intrahepatic cholestasis (n=3), gestational diabetes (n=2), gestational hypertension (n=1) and intrauterine growth restriction (n=1). Median gestational age was 39 weeks with five preterm births between 32 and 37. One baby was diagnosed with laryngomalacia but did not require surgery.
