RESULTS: A total of 37 eligible studies, involving 466,995 reproductive-aged women, were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. The pooled estimate of women's knowledge on prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (PMTCT) was 56.97% (95% CI: 52.37%, 61.56%), indicating nearly half of reproductive-age women in Africa lacked adequate knowledge of PMTCT. Significant factors associated with higher knowledge of PMTCT included urban residence (AOR = 1.20; 95% CI: 1.12, 1.28), attainment of primary education (AOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.44), secondary education (AOR = 1.66; 95% CI: 1.38, 2.01), tertiary or higher education (AOR = 1.98; 95% CI: 1.59, 2.46), being aged 25-34 (AOR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.32, 1.41) or 35-49 (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.15, 3.36), exposure to mass media (AOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.44), having adequate knowledge of HIV (AOR = 1.964; 95% CI: 1.45, 2.66), history of maternal HIV infection and HIV-infected child (AOR = 2.19; 95% CI: 1.04, 4.60), and higher women's wealth index categories: poorer (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.05-1.62), middle-income (AOR = 1.29; 95% CI: 1.11, 1.50), and richer groups (AOR = 1.93; 95% CI: 1.32, 2.81).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite substantial progress in HIV prevention efforts, knowledge of PMTCT among reproductive-age women in Africa remains suboptimal, with considerable disparities across settings. The findings highlight persistent inequalities related to education, socioeconomic status, age category, geographical location, and access to health information. Thus, strengthening PMTCT knowledge requires tailored, integrated, and context-specific strategies that expand women's educational opportunities, improve access to reliable HIV-related information through media and comprehensive maternal health services, and prioritize underserved rural and socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. These proactive efforts are crucial to encouraging women for primary prevention of HIV, empowering women to make informed decisions, improving engagement with PMTCT services, and accelerating progress toward the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV in Africa.

articles.title: Progress toward poliomyelitis eradication - January 2023-December 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since the establishment of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) in 1988, wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) remains endemic in only Afghanistan and Pakistan. However, outbreaks of paralytic polio caused by circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses (cVDPVs) emerge in areas with low vaccination coverage and continue to challenge polio eradication goals. As the Global Polio Eradication Initiative extends its eradication target to 2029, understanding the epidemiologic, surveillance, and operational factors associated with persistent transmission is critical for informing policy decisions and targeting limited resources. This report describes global polio immunization efforts, surveillance activities, and epidemiology during January 2023-December 2024.
METHODS: Surveillance and virologic data were obtained from the World Health Organization's (WHO) global Polio Information System (POLIS), and immunization coverage estimates were sourced from WHO's Immunization Dashboard, which incorporates administrative and survey-based data from WHO and UNICEF. A cVDPV outbreak was defined using standardized acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) and environmental surveillance criteria; analyses were conducted in R (version 4.4.1).
RESULTS: Afghanistan and Pakistan reported 99 WPV1 cases in 10 provinces in 2024, compared with 12 cases in 3 provinces in 2023. cVDPV cases decreased 12% from 529 in 2023 to 464 in 2024. However, cVDPV detections from AFP and environmental surveillance expanded geographically, with detections in 40 countries in Africa, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe in 2024, including 14 countries with no detections in 2023. The resurgence of WPV1 in polio-free regions in Afghanistan and Pakistan and the spread of cVDPVs challenge global polio eradication.
CONCLUSIONS: Achieving global polio eradication will require reaching persistently missed children in remote and insecure areas, strengthening vaccination and surveillance systems, and reinforcing accountability to improve campaign quality. The geographic expansion of cVDPV type 2 (cVDPV2) underscores the need for rapid detection, expanded nOPV2 use in areas with prolonged transmission, and sustained partner engagement and strategic resource allocation amid declining global health funding.

articles.title: The social production of silence and vulnerability after child sexual abuse: A qualitative study of young women from the Romanian child protection system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is often embedded in broader contexts of cumulative victimization, while opportunities for disclosure and protection are shaped by familial, relational, and institutional conditions. These processes remain insufficiently understood among young people with histories of placement in child protection systems.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored young women's retrospective accounts of CSA and how they understood the conditions shaping silence, vulnerability, disclosure, and recovery in the context of their histories of placement in the Romanian child protection system.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Seven women aged 19-27 participated in semi-structured telephone interviews. The interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed in Romanian using a hybrid inductive and theoretically informed thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Participants situated CSA within broader experiences of physical and emotional abuse, neglect, family violence, parental alcohol misuse, and the absence of protective adults. They described silence as shaped by threats, fear, shame, self-blame, dependency, the normalization of violence, uncertainty about institutional responses, and experiences of invalidation. Their accounts presented vulnerability as relationally and structurally conditioned, including through limited or uneven access to protection and support. Trusted adults, educators, psychologists, supportive partners, and educational opportunities were described by participants as supportive resources in relation to disclosure, emotional well-being, autonomy, and the reinterpretation of traumatic experiences.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants' retrospective accounts suggest that silence and vulnerability following CSA cannot be understood solely as individual responses to trauma. They were experienced as shaped by relationships of dependency, normalized violence, responses to disclosure, and access to protective and supportive resources within and beyond the child protection system.

articles.title: Psychotherapy in routine clinical practice in Chile with children who have been sexually abused: Factors associated with initial symptoms and trajectory of symptomatic change.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy of child sexual abuse treatment has been demonstrated. Nonetheless, a gap persists in understanding how different factors are associated with treatment outcomes. Furthermore, evidence in non-high-income countries and in routine clinical practice is scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the children's symptoms trajectories over the course of treatment for child sexual abuse, and whether child and caregiver characteristics, the nature of the abusive experience, and caregiver session attendance are associated with initial symptom severity and symptomatic change.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The sample comprised 78 children aged 4 to 9 (x̄ 6.6; SD 1.6) who were referred to specialized treatment centres for sexual abuse in Santiago, Chile.
METHODS: Children's primary caregivers and professionals leading their treatment completed questionnaires at the beginning, middle and end of treatment. Multilevel models were utilized to analyse changes in the child's symptomatology.
RESULTS: Internalizing, externalizing and post-traumatic stress symptoms decreased during treatment (p < .001). Children whose caregiver reported a history of child sexual abuse had higher initial scores across all three types of assessed symptoms (p < .05 or less), and those whose caregiver reported higher post-traumatic stress had higher initial internalizing and post-traumatic stress scores (p < .001). Caregiver session attendance was the only factor linked to change, with more sessions associated with a steeper reduction in post-traumatic symptoms (p < .01).
CONCLUSIONS: Children receiving treatment as usual in Chile showed symptom reduction over the course of the intervention, although the observational design precludes attributing this change to treatment. Caregiver-related factors were consistently associated with children's symptoms, with potential implications for clinical practice and for research using an intergenerational approach.

articles.title: Configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances and registered outcomes among children investigated by child welfare services in Sweden: A latent class analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children investigated by child welfare services (CWS) are often exposed to multiple, co-occurring family and socioeconomic difficulties. Less is known about how such circumstances cluster within this population and whether different configurations are associated with different outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To identify profiles of family and socioeconomic circumstances among children investigated by CWS and examine their associations with criminal justice involvement, mental health-related medication use, and school performance.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The source cohort comprised 1764 children aged 7-12 years investigated by CWS in Stockholm, Sweden, in 2019 following concerns of maltreatment. The latent class analytic sample included 1660 children with complete data on six class indicators.
METHODS: Latent class analysis was conducted using indicators of foreign background, single-parent household, large household size, low income, persistent parental unemployment, and parental criminal conviction. Associations with distal outcomes were estimated using two-step maximum-likelihood models that retained uncertainty in latent class membership and adjusted for age or birth cohort and sex, as appropriate. Confidence intervals were obtained using 600 nonparametric bootstrap replications.
RESULTS: Three partly overlapping profiles were identified: Multiple adversity (38.3%), Low income and foreign background (21.1%), and Lower adversity (40.6%). In outcome-specific analyses, the Multiple adversity profile had higher odds of antidepressant medication use (OR = 1.79, 95% CI [1.27, 2.69]) and ADHD medication use (OR = 1.53, 95% CI [1.07, 2.45]) than the Lower adversity profile. The Low income and foreign background profile had higher odds of low school performance (OR = 1.96, 95% CI [1.09, 3.12]) than the Lower adversity profile. Associations with criminal justice outcomes were imprecise. None of the 15 pairwise outcome-profile contrasts remained statistically significant after Holm correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Children investigated by CWS showed heterogeneous and partly overlapping configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances. Outcome-specific patterns suggest that different configurations may be associated with different domains of functioning, but the findings should be considered exploratory given the multiple-testing results. Replication with longer follow-up and richer measures of family processes and child functioning is needed.

articles.title: Extreme temperatures and child neglect: A nationwide case-crossover study of Brazilian children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neglect is the most frequently reported but least studied form of child maltreatment. Because it arises in part from the conditions under which care is provided, neglect may be sensitive to environmental stressors associated with a warming climate. As an act of omission, it may also respond to heat through pathways distinct from those implicated in abusive behavior. However, population-level evidence on this association remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between heat and child neglect in a middle-income setting and examine heterogeneity across child and case characteristics.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: 150,163 notifications of neglect or abandonment involving children aged 0 to 9, recorded in Brazil's national violence notification system across 3428 municipalities, 2012 to 2019.
METHODS: Time-stratified case-crossover analysis with conditional logistic regression. Each child served as their own control, matched on municipality, calendar month, year, and day of week. Exposure was municipal daily maximum temperature, categorized with 27 to 30 °C as reference.
RESULTS: Odds of child neglect increase with temperature. On days of 33 °C or above, odds were 6.0% higher than at 27 to 30 °C (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). Below 24 °C, they were 6.0% lower (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96). Findings were robust to alternative event dates, reference categories, and municipality exclusions. No variation appeared by sex or race. Exploratory age comparison suggested a larger association among children aged 5 to 9 than among those aged 0 to 4 (ratio of odds ratios 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.017), although the difference did not meet the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold.
CONCLUSIONS: Heat is measurably associated with child neglect. Exploratory analyses suggest that these associations are larger in older children, though this effect does not persist after correction for multiple comparisons. Child welfare research and practice should consider environmental conditions as a potentially relevant and modifiable context.

articles.title: "It is worth seeing this, and it is never too late": Survivors' expectations of significant others during intrafamilial child sexual abuse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research on child sexual abuse has largely examined children's needs and expectations after disclosure. Less is known about how survivors retrospectively understand their expectations of significant others who were present during intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA), before disclosure became possible.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined what adult survivors of IFCSA expected from significant others during and after the abuse, and how these expectations were shaped by others' relational roles, authority, and capacity to intervene.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The study included 18 adult survivors of intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA) who reported the presence of significant others during abusive incidents. Participants were recruited through online support groups for adults with histories of childhood abuse.
METHODS: Guided by Denzin's interpretive paradigm and reflexive thematic analysis, the study draws on semi-structured, in-depth interviews to examine survivors' expectations of significant others and the meanings attributed to their presence.
RESULTS: Participants' expectations clustered around three relational demands: to be witnessed, to be protected, and to be stood with. Expectations differed according to relational role and capacity, with mothers, adults, siblings, and professionals each assigned distinct forms of responsibility.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings show that the presence of others may shape survivors' traumatic meaning-making before, during, and long after the disclosure. Practice and policy should support earlier recognition, protective action, and long-term acknowledgment.

articles.title: Beyond adversity: Resilience and benevolent childhood experiences in the link between adverse childhood experiences and psychological maladjustment during pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have been associated with psychological maladjustment during pregnancy, with potential implications for maternal well-being and child development. Although traditional ACE frameworks primarily focus on family-related adversities, expanded models incorporate a broader range of experiences, including peer victimization and parental absence. However, few studies have simultaneously examined the associations between traditional and expanded ACEs and psychological adjustment during pregnancy while also considering potential protective factors, such as resilience and benevolent childhood experiences (BCEs).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether maternal ACEs are associated with psychological maladjustment during pregnancy and to assess whether BCEs and resilience may serve as protective factors.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: A total of 454 pregnant women (Mage = 34.70, SD = 3.94) participated in the study and completed measures assessing traditional and expanded ACEs, BCEs, resilience, and psychological maladjustment.
METHODS: Mediation and moderation analyses were conducted to examine the roles of resilience and BCEs in the association between maternal ACEs and psychological maladjustment during pregnancy.
RESULTS: Resilience partially mediated the relationship between specific ACEs and maladjustment to pregnancy. Significant indirect effects through resilience were observed for emotional neglect, parental or sibling death, unsafe neighborhoods, and bullying. BCEs did not buffer the association between ACEs and maladjustment to pregnancy. Instead, higher levels of BCEs were associated with stronger ACE-maladjustment associations for emotional neglect and parental absence.
CONCLUSIONS: Resilience appears to be an important pathway linking specific childhood adversities with psychological maladjustment during pregnancy, with the most consistent evidence observed for emotional neglect, parental or sibling death, unsafe neighborhoods, and bullying. BCEs did not show a consistent buffering effect and were associated with stronger ACE-maladjustment associations for specific adversity types. Assessing a broader range of ACEs alongside resilience may improve the identification of women at risk and inform trauma-informed perinatal interventions.

articles.title: Pancreatic surgery in children: nationwide retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric patients differ in various ways from adult populations, but comprehensive multicentre or population-based data are missing for paediatric pancreatic surgery. This study evaluated indications, procedures, complications, and mortality in paediatric patients undergoing pancreatic surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective observational population-based cohort study queried the German Diagnosis-Related Group database for all patients aged < 19 years who underwent pancreatic surgical procedures between 2010 and 2023. The primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and complication rates. Sex- and age-based differences in surgical indications and procedures were explored as secondary outcomes. Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify risk factors for mortality and perioperative complications.
RESULTS: Among the 761 patients identified, indications for pancreatic surgery encompassed chronic pancreatitis (284 patients, 37.3%), pancreatic tumours (221, 29.0%), trauma (127, 16.7%), extrapancreatic tumours (70, 9.2%), and other diseases (59, 7.8%), with significant sex- and age-based differences (P < 0.001). Distal pancreatectomies (281, 36.9%) and pancreatoduodenectomies (125, 16.4%) were the most commonly performed operations. The mortality rate in the overall cohort was 2.8% (21), with no deaths recorded in the subgroup of patients with pancreatic tumours. The overall complication rate was 41.9% (319 of 761 patients), and varied depending on the surgical procedure, spanning from 28.6% for pancreatic cyst marsupialization to 92.9% for total pancreatectomy. Severe complications occurred in 244 patients (32.1%), and were again more common after total pancreatectomy (85.7%). In multivariable analyses, a higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (odds ratio (OR) 1.27; 95% confidence interval (c.i.) 1.12 to 1.44) and undergoing surgery for trauma (OR 5.22; 95% c.i. 1.96 to 13.89), other pancreatic diagnoses (OR 3.13; 95% c.i. 1.30 to 7.17), or chronic pancreatitis (OR 2.56; 95% c.i. 1.08 to 6.25) were identified as independent risk factors for the occurrence of complications, as were receiving total pancreatectomy (OR 8.42; 95% c.i. 1.38 to 51.16) and concomitant splenectomy (OR 1.82; 95% c.i. 1.10 to 3.00).
CONCLUSION: Pancreatic surgery in children is most commonly performed for chronic pancreatitis or tumours, with specific sex and age differences in indication. Pancreatic procedures in children are rare, but can be performed with low in-hospital mortality. However, morbidity remains substantial, particularly after extensive procedures.

articles.title: Hepatic Macrophages Depletion by Clodronate Liposomes Alleviates RRV-Induced Biliary Injury via Targeting the Notch3/PPAR Signalling Pathway.
articles.abstract: Biliary atresia is a rare obliterative cholangiopathy in neonates, and hepatic macrophages participate in biliary atresia pathogenesis. The study aimed to reveal the regulatory mechanism of macrophages in the progression of biliary atresia. Hepatic macrophages were co-cultured with vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Delta like canonical notch ligand 4 (DLL4) and neurogenic locus notch homologue 3 (Notch3) were quantified in rhesus rotavirus (RRV)-treated cells following anti-DLL4 antibody REGN1035. In RRV-challenged mice, Notch3 was activated by Ade-NICD3, while macrophages were depleted by clodronate liposomes (Clo-Lip) to compare intervention effects on RRV-induced biliary injury, hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), Notch3, CD68 and CD163. Notch3 knockout mice were used to verify the effect of Notch3 on RRV-induced injury. Transcriptome sequencing screened Notch3-related differentially expressed genes, and downstream pathway regulation was further verified. Macrophages upregulated DLL4, while REGN1035 treatment inhibited DLL4 and Notch3 expression. In RRV-infected mice, Clo-Lip-mediated macrophage depletion alleviated biliary injury, repressed Notch3 signalling and downregulated HIF-1α, CD68 and CD163. In RRV mice with NICD3 overexpression, macrophage depletion alleviated Notch3 activation-triggered biliary lesions, inhibited inflammation and downregulated HIF-1α, CD68 and CD163. Transcriptomic analysis identified 715 upregulated and 585 downregulated genes, confirming the peroxisome proliferators-activated receptor (PPAR) signalling pathway as a downstream pathway of Notch3. Compared with RRV-infected wild-type mice, Notch3 knockout alleviated RRV-induced biliary injury and abnormal macrophage polarization, downregulated HIF-1α and CYP7A1, but upregulated PPARα. This protective effect was abolished by the PPARα inhibitor GW6471. Macrophage depletion ameliorates RRV-induced biliary injury via regulating the Notch3/PPAR signalling pathway.

articles.title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
articles.abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more pronounced effects in females. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing identified a specific, lasting dysbiosis in the overweight female mice, characterized by reduced alpha diversity and species-level shifts in Lactobacillus, Muribaculum and Bacteroides. Crucially, upon allergic sensitization in adulthood, these animals displayed an exacerbated disease state consistent with an 'obese-asthma' phenotype, marked by heightened airway inflammation, intense eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltration, higher Type 2 cytokine levels (i.e., IL-4, IL-5) and altered bronchoalveolar immune profiles. These findings suggest that early-life nutritional imbalance establishes an altered immunometabolic trajectory via the gut-lung axis, providing a mechanistic basis for the increased severity observed in obesity-associated asthma.

articles.title: Impact of antimicrobial processing interventions on Salmonella prevalence, load, and serovar early and late within the same shift on two broiler part types.
articles.abstract: Salmonellosis linked to chicken products has not decreased despite successful reduction of Salmonella prevalence in raw poultry products in the United States. Interventions during immersion chilling reduce Salmonella on the carcass surfaces it can reach, such as the outside and internal cavity. Other potential Salmonella reservoirs such as the connective tissue or bone are inaccessible to the antimicrobial and could be released during second processing. The objectives in this study were two-fold: i) assess the efficacy of interventions on two different part types, specifically comparing skin-on, bone-in parts (whole and cut wings) with skinless, boneless parts (tenders), by assessing Salmonella status (prevalence, load, and serovar complexity) and ii) determine any association between Salmonella status between the beginning and end of a single shift. Twenty broiler processing facilities were visited in five states. Tenders and wings were collected pre- and post-intervention. Samples were collected at the start and end of the first shift to determine if cross-contamination would influence Salmonella prevalence, load, or serovar complexity later in the shift. Prevalence decreased from 27.4% (164/599) to 12.4% (74/599) in tenders (OR=0.24, p<0.001), from 13.9% (40/288) to 8.98% (23/256) in whole wings (OR=0.36, p=0.015), and from 22.8% (78/342) to 8.8% (33/375) in cut wings (OR=0.26, p<0.001) following antimicrobial application. Sample timepoint or intervention status had no impact on Salmonella load on either wing type. Eight serovars were detected; serovar Infantis was most prevalent in tenders 69.2% (164/237) and cut wings 61.3% (68/111). The presence of mixed serovar populations numerically decreased post-intervention in tenders (19.6% to 5.4%) and cut wings (5.1% to 0%), but was not significant in the mixed model (p=0.077). Overall, antimicrobial interventions in broiler processing establishments are associated with reduced Salmonella on parts.

articles.title: Latent profiles of addictive-like behaviors: a person-centered analysis of risk and protective factors among adolescents.
articles.abstract: Addictive-like behaviors are common during adolescence and are associated with a broad range of emotional, behavioral, and social outcomes. Using a person-centered framework, the present study aimed to identify distinct profiles of adolescents based on the frequency and severity of addictive-like behaviors and to examine how these profiles differ in key risk and protective factors. A large community sample of 6,849 adolescents aged 12-18 completed self-report measures assessing alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, and cocaine use, gambling, shopping, gaming, disordered-eating, sexual-activity, and social-networking behaviors. Risk and protective-factor measures were available in a 6,031-participant study component and included impulsivity, reward deficiency syndrome (RDS), meaning in life (presence and search), psychological flexibility, eudaimonic well-being, perceived acceptance and rejection from teachers, and parent-adolescent communication. Latent profile analysis identified three distinct behavioral profiles: Normal Engagement (n = 6,164; 90.00%), Tobacco-Dominant (n = 511; 7.46%), and Substance and Gambling Vulnerability (n = 174; 2.54%). The profiles differed significantly across sociodemographic characteristics and across the examined risk and protective factors. A clear and consistent directional pattern emerged, with Normal Engagement generally showing higher protective and lower risk characteristics, Substance and Gambling Vulnerability generally showing the reverse pattern, and Tobacco-Dominant frequently falling between them. Omnibus effects were very small to small. Overall, the findings are consistent with transdiagnostic risk and protective processes across adolescent addictive-like behaviors, while the modest effect sizes indicate substantial overlap between profiles.

articles.title: Integrin-Related Gene Signatures in Ewing Sarcoma Prognosis and Immune Microenvironment Analysis Using Bioinformatics and LASSO Regression.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify integrin-related genes (IRGs) as potential prognostic indicators for Ewing sarcoma (ES), a rare, aggressive malignancy of children and adolescents associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment efficacy, particularly in metastatic disease.
METHODS: The Gene Expression Omnibus datasets GSE17674 and GSE17679 were used for bioinformatics analyses as the training and validation datasets, respectively. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened and subjected to functional enrichment analysis. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to identify characteristic genes, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis to assess diagnostic potential, and CIBERSORT to analyze immune cell infiltration.
RESULTS: Of the 9,846 DEGs identified in GSE17674, 15 were IRGs with significant differences in expression (p < 0.05) and enrichment in integrin-mediated signaling pathways. LASSO regression identified 6 key genes; ITGA4, ITGAE, and ITGB7 had areas under the curve >0.9, indicating high diagnostic value. Immune cell infiltration analysis showed increased M0 macrophages and activated mast cells in ES samples.
CONCLUSIONS: IRGs play a pivotal role in ES progression and regulation of the immune microenvironment; these findings provide insight into the molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets. Reliance on public databases and the absence of in vitro and in vivo experimental validation are limitations shared by retrospective bioinformatics studies. Further experimental validation is needed.

articles.title: Navigating Childhood Cancer Care: Exploring the Experiences of Mothers in Ghana.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to explore and understand the lived experiences of mothers caring for children diagnosed with cancer in Ghana, with particular attention to how they perceive, make sense of and navigate their experiences throughout their child's cancer journey.
DESIGN: A qualitative phenomenological study.
METHODS: Eighteen mothers whose children were receiving cancer treatment at a tertiary health facility in Ghana were purposively recruited for the study. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews conducted between September and December 2025. The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Four major themes and eight subthemes emerged from the analysis: (1) emotional turmoil and psychological distress, (2) caregiving burden and lifestyle disruption, (3) coping mechanisms and resilience and (4) healthcare system challenges. Mothers reported persistent fear, anxiety, emotional exhaustion and financial strain associated with prolonged caregiving. Participants relied on spirituality, social support and personal resilience as coping strategies. Healthcare system barriers, including inadequate information and limited psychosocial support, further intensified caregiving stress.
CONCLUSION: Mothers caring for children with cancer experience multidimensional challenges that significantly affect their psychological, social and economic well-being. Strengthening psychosocial support systems and implementing caregiver-inclusive healthcare policies are essential for improving the well-being of both caregivers and children undergoing cancer treatment.
IMPACT: The findings underscore the need for family-centred paediatric oncology care that addresses both the medical needs of children with cancer and the psychological and social well-being of their caregivers. Integrating psychosocial support services, caregiver counselling and improved communication between healthcare providers and families may help reduce caregiver burden and enhance treatment experiences.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public involvement occurred in the design of the study.
NURSING IMPLICATIONS: Paediatric oncology nurses can strengthen caregiver-inclusive care by assessing maternal distress, explaining treatment and side effects in clear language, checking understanding, providing opportunities for emotional expression and linking mothers with psychosocial, peer, spiritual and financial-support resources.

articles.title: Early motor development in ADHD: monogenic and polygenic trajectories using NF1 as a model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ADHD is often accompanied by motor difficulties in childhood, yet little is known about how these traits emerge in early life or the genetic pathways that contribute to their development. Studying infants with an elevated familial likelihood of ADHD (EL-ADHD) alongside those with a monogenic condition associated with ADHD, such as Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), provides a unique opportunity to compare polygenic and monogenic influences on early motor development and its relationship to later ADHD traits. Accordingly, this study examined motor profiles in EL-ADHD, NF1, and typically developing (TD) infants, and investigated how early motor behaviour relates to emerging ADHD characteristics.
METHODS: The motor behaviour of infants with EL-ADHD, NF1, and TD were assessed at 10 and 14 months using a multimodal approach that included standardized motor assessments, parent reports of activity levels, behavioural coding of movements during free play, and accelerometery. Early ADHD traits were subsequently evaluated at follow-up visits at ages 2 and 3 years using the Child Behaviour Checklist (CBCL).
RESULTS: Across infancy, EL-ADHD infants exhibited higher gross motor scores on standardised assessments compared to TD and NF1 infants, although they did not differ from either group in their fine motor scores. In contrast, NF1 infants showed both lower gross and fine motor scores relative to TD and EL-ADHD peers. During free play, EL-ADHD infants displayed more mature motor behaviours and marginially higher mean acceleration levels compared to TD and NF1 infants, whereas only minimal free play differences were observed between TD and NF1. Additionally, group-specific relationships emerged between motor behaviour and later ADHD traits. In the EL-ADHD group only, 14-month gross motor skills showed a trend-level positive association with ADHD traits at 36 months, and 14-month parent-reported activity levels significantly predicted ADHD traits at both 24 and 36 months.
CONCLUSION: This study is the first to examine the relationship between motor development and ADHD traits in both polygenic and monogenic contexts. Our findings show that motor difficulties emerge early in infants with NF1, whereas such difficulties are not evident in those at elevated likelihood of ADHD in the general population. Moreover, early motor behaviour predicts later ADHD traits in ways that are specific to both developmental context and population. These results suggest that ADHD phenotypes can arise through distinct neurodevelopmental trajectories across different atypically developing populations.

articles.title: Criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, and misclassification patterns of the International Fitness Scale in adolescents from a rural Mediterranean region of Spain: The EHDLA study.
articles.abstract: Self-reported fitness instruments provide a scalable surveillance solution when objective testing is impractical, yet the nature of perception-accuracy discordance in adolescents is not well understood. This study examined criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, convergent construct validity against the Spanish Perceived Physical Literacy Instrument (S-PPLI), and misclassification patterning of the International Fitness Scale (IFIS) in a community sample of adolescents from the Valle de Ricote (Region of Murcia, Spain). Cross-sectional data from 1017 Spanish adolescents (471 boys, 546 girls; median age 14 years) from the Eating Healthy and Daily Life Activities (EHDLA) study were analyzed. IFIS overall correlated with the Assessing the Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA-Fit) composite (Spearman rho [ρ] = 0.369; partial ρ = 0.377, p < 0.001), with flexibility showing the strongest domain-specific validity (Spearman ρ = 0.635; partial ρ = 0.592, p < 0.001). Using the full five-level IFIS score, the area under the curve (AUC) for identifying the lowest fitness tertile was 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.63-0.69). At the primary screening cut-off (IFIS ≤ 3), sensitivity was 0.68, specificity was 0.59, and negative predictive value was 0.80, while a stricter threshold (IFIS ≤ 2) increased specificity (0.94) at the cost of sensitivity (0.16). Convergent validity with S-PPLI was supported (partial ρ = 0.56, p < 0.001). Misclassification profiling identified 18.5% of participants as underestimators and 17.6% as overestimators; underestimation was associated with shorter sleep, while concordant-low membership was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), lower activity, and more sedentary time. In conclusion, IFIS showed weak-to-modest criterion-related validity and limited discriminative accuracy. Therefore, IFIS may serve as a low-burden adjunct to objective testing for population-level prioritization, but its performance relative to other brief instruments or low-burden measures, including BMI, remains untested. Discordance between perceived and objective fitness was common (36.1%) and co-occurred with lifestyle and adiposity characteristics, supporting consideration of perception-accuracy profiling in school-based and public health surveillance. Findings pertain to a single rural region and require replication in urban, regional, and socioeconomically diverse samples before broader generalization.

articles.title: New evidence on pathogenesis, clinical features, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies in patients with autoimmune encephalitis.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) refers to a group of rare autoimmune diseases that affect the central nervous system, characterized by diverse clinical presentations and major challenges in diagnosis and treatment. Delayed diagnosis is an important predictor of poor clinical outcomes. Additionally, a subset of patients has shown limited response to conventional immunotherapy, and the development of novel treatment strategies remains insufficient. This review aims to summarize recent advances in the understanding of AE, focusing on its classification, pathophysiological mechanisms, the heterogeneous clinical manifestations associated with different AE antibody subtypes, diagnostic tools, and emerging therapeutic approaches. The diagnostic landscape of AE has expanded with the widespread application of tissue-based assays (TBAs) and live cell-based assays (live-CBA), facilitating the identification of neural autoantibodies and broadening the well-established antibody spectrum. State-of-the-art neuroimaging techniques-such as 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) and 18F-DPA714 positron emission tomography-offer more specific visualization of intracranial inflammation in AE. Moreover, deeper insights into AE pathogenesis have promoted the development of novel therapeutic targets, particularly monoclonal antibodies against neonatal Fc receptors and cluster of differentiation 20 (CD20). Notably, chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR-T) has emerged as a potential option for treatment-refractory AE by targeting key inflammatory pathways such as B cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and CD19. Despite significant advances in understanding AE pathogenesis and diagnostic landscape of AE, early detection and timely therapeutic intervention remain challenging. Emerging developments in antibody detection technologies, advanced neuroimaging modalities and immunotherapeutic strategies-particularly targeted and cell-based approaches-hold promise for improving long-term neurological outcomes, especially in patients with refractory or atypical AE.

articles.title: Oral-gut-vaginal microbiota crosstalk with host immunity and metabolism in pregnancy disorders.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy represents a critical stage in which both maternal and fetal health are of paramount importance. This review systematically examines the temporal dynamics of maternal microbial communities across multiple anatomical niches-including the vaginal, intestinal, and oral ecosystems-during pregnancy, and explores their profound connections with gestational health. We highlight the specific associations between site-specific microbial dysbiosis and adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. In addition, we delineate the mechanisms by which the immune microenvironment at the maternal-fetal interface maintains dynamic equilibrium under microbial regulation, and underscores the role of microbial metabolites as transgenerational signaling molecules critical for fetal development. Furthermore, we dissect the pathological disruption of the "microbiota-immune-metabolism" network in pregnancy-related disorders and evaluate the potential of targeted strategies-including probiotic supplementation and nutritional interventions-to restore microbial homeostasis and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. Finally, we emphasize the contribution of breast milk microbiota and immune components to offspring immune programming and outline future translational research directions, aiming to provide a scientific foundation for microbiota-based monitoring and early intervention in pregnancy health.

articles.title: Levels of Psychological Detachment in Nurses: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Psychological detachment among nurses, a critical component of professional recovery, plays a vital role in stabilizing the nursing workforce and expanding clinical human resources. This review aims to assess the level of psychological detachment among nurses and evaluate the impact of data collection periods (during and outside the COVID-19 pandemic), gender, and department. Computerized searches were conducted across 10 databases: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Medline, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed. The search period spanned from the inception of each database to January 7, 2026. A random-effects model was used to pool the total mean scores for psychological detachment, and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore sources of heterogeneity among studies. A total of 34 studies involving 20 517 nursing staff from six countries were included in the meta-analysis. Results showed that the overall mean score for nurses' psychological detachment was 2.68 (95% CI: 2.53, 2.82), indicating a low-to-moderate level. Subgroup analyses revealed relatively higher total mean psychological detachment scores among male nurses and during the COVID-19 pandemic, while paediatric nurses exhibited lower levels compared to other departments. Future efforts should prioritize the development of targeted clinical management systems to systematically enhance psychological detachment levels across diverse nursing populations. Trial Registration: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261304558).

articles.title: A multilevel analysis of demographic and contextual factors associated with emergency department visits and access block in Queensland.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies on factors associated with emergency department (ED) use, including demographic and contextual factors such as the remoteness of the area of residence and the availability of home support programs, are scarce but may better explain ED demand than studies based only on demographic factors. Furthermore, most studies are based on the nonplausible assumption that there is no geographical variation in factors associated with ED use across states or territories.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess whether contextual factors related to context or the environment, in addition to demographic factors, can improve our understanding of ED use in Queensland, Australia. Spatial analyses were performed to understand the factors more likely to drive ED demand and access block (AB) in different areas of the state.
METHODS: Data on all ED visits in Queensland in 2021 were aggregated by 1-year age groups for each postcode of patients' residential area and matched to the corresponding denominator population as well as to demographic and contextual factors.
RESULTS: When assessing factors associated with ED demand and AB, including contextual factors improved model fit compared with models comprising demographic factors only. The associations between ED visits and age appeared nonlinear. The highest rates of ED visits were observed among residents aged > 75 years, followed by those aged < 5 years and those aged 20-35 years. Across the state, a 1-year increase in patient age was associated with a 2% increase in the rates of AB. Queenslanders with low education levels are more likely to experience ED visits and AB. Residents living outside of metropolitan areas were less likely to access the ED but were more likely to experience AB when they attended the ED. Interestingly, increased numbers of Prolonged Level D GP visits (40 + minutes) and aged care places were associated with decreased rates of ED visits. Prolonged Level D GP visits were substantially more likely to be associated with reduced ED visits outside of the capital city and its neighbouring areas.
CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged GP visits (especially in remote areas), multidisciplinary case conferences and other forms of integrated care should be considered in policies aimed at reducing ED demand.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Topographic Ellipsoid Zone Reflectivity in Hereditary Optic Neuropathies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantitatively map topographic alterations in ellipsoid zone (EZ) optical coherence tomography signal intensity and investigate the subclinical photoreceptor involvement in hereditary optic neuropathies.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 170 eyes from 155 participants: 35 eyes with dominant optic atrophy, 35 with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), 35 from asymptomatic LHON carriers, 30 eyes from 15 participants with Wolfram syndrome, and 35 healthy control eyes. Swept-source optical coherence tomography en face images were analyzed, and the raw EZ signal intensity was measured in the foveal, parafoveal, and perifoveal regions. A linear mixed-effects model included the clinical group, the retinal region, and their interaction, with random intercepts for participant and eye nested within participant.
RESULTS: The Group × Region interaction was significant (likelihood-ratio P < 0.001), whereas the absolute foveal signal intensity did not differ significantly among the groups (P = 0.191). The model-estimated fovea-to-parafovea difference was 14.89 grayscale intensity units in healthy controls, 9.34 in LHON, 5.06 in carriers, 9.64 in dominant optic atrophy, and 14.15 in Wolfram syndrome. Compared with controls, the fovea-to-parafovea EZ signal intensity difference was reduced in LHON (Holm-adjusted P = 0.029) and asymptomatic carriers (Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). The Group × Region interaction remained significant in a sensitivity model including the vitreous and the retinal nerve fiber layer signal intensity (P = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: LHON patients and asymptomatic carriers showed a flatter fovea-to-parafovea EZ signal profile despite having a broadly similar absolute foveal signal intensity, consistent with subclinical outer retinal involvement associated with mitochondrial disease.

articles.title: Contrast Sensitivity Across the Visual Field in Children With Amblyopia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adults with amblyopia exhibit reduced contrast sensitivity, primarily at high spatial frequencies in central vision. Little is known regarding contrast sensitivity deficits in the peripheral visual field of amblyopic children. In the present study, we assessed monocular contrast sensitivity at three retinal eccentricities in children with anisometropic or strabismic amblyopia.
METHODS: Contrast sensitivity was measured at 0°, 4°, and 8° of retinal eccentricity in children ages 6 to 16 years with anisometropic amblyopia (n = 10) or strabismic amblyopia (n = 9), and age-matched controls (n = 11). Bandpass-filtered Auckland Optotypes were monocularly presented at each eccentricity, and spatial frequency was scaled accordingly. Contrast levels were determined using a QUEST adaptive staircase procedure, and fixation was monitored with a Gazepoint eyetracker. Thresholds and fixation compliance were compared across eccentricity, group, and eye using a linear mixed-effects model.
RESULTS: Collapsed across eccentricities, amblyopic eyes in the amblyopic groups had reduced contrast sensitivity compared to fellow eyes (P < 0.001 for anisometropic, P = 0.045 for strabismic) with no significance between eyes in controls (P = 0.56). When comparing across eccentricity, both amblyopic groups showed centralized contrast sensitivity deficits in the amblyopic eye as compared to the fellow eye at 0° and 4°.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings confirm that both anisometropic and strabismic amblyopic children demonstrate centralized contrast deficits in their amblyopic eye. In the periphery, these deficits were reduced for both groups, but with a more pronounced effect of eccentricity for anisometropic amblyopes. These findings may inform our understanding of dichoptic therapies for amblyopia that target central or peripheral areas of the visual field.

articles.title: Impairment of Contrast Sensitivity Function and Stereopsis in Successfully Treated Bilateral Pediatric Cataract Patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate postoperative contrast sensitivity function (CSF) and stereoacuity in children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts who achieved excellent best-corrected visual acuity (≤0.00 logMAR), and to assess the impact of age at surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 45 children with bilateral pediatric cataracts (90 eyes) and 45 controls. Monocular CSF and stereoacuity were measured. Patients were stratified by age at surgery (<2, 2 to <4, 4 to <6, and ≥6 years) to analyze the effects of surgical timing.
RESULTS: Despite a normal best-corrected visual acuity, the cataract group exhibited a lower area under the log CSF than controls (1.42 ± 0.20 vs. 1.49 ± 0.20; P = 0.04) and reduced CS at low-to-medium spatial frequencies (SFs) (1.0, 1.5, 3.0, and 6.0 cycles per degree; all P < 0.05). High SFs (12 and 18 cycles per degree) and cutoff SF were comparable between the groups (all P > 0.05). Age- and sex-adjusted CSF deficits differed across surgical-age subgroups for area under the log CSF, cutoff SF, and several CSF parameters (all P < 0.05), with the ≥6-year-old group showing deficits closest to zero. Stereopsis was significantly impaired in the pediatric cataract group (P < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts may exhibit persistent deficits in low-to-medium SF CS and stereopsis despite excellent visual acuity. This pattern may suggest differential developmental trajectories or vulnerability of visual pathways involved in contrast processing. Comprehensive functional assessment and individualized visual rehabilitation are recommended.

articles.title: Early labor and its long-term impact on cancer risk among older adults in Ecuador: a cross-sectional study analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The long-term health consequences of early labor remain insufficiently understood. This study explores the association between age at labor onset and cancer risk among older adults in Ecuador.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the 2009 Health, Well-being, and Aging Survey (SABE), including 3,791 adults aged 60 and older from mainland Ecuador. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the association between age at first work (5-12, 13-17, 18-25 [reference group], and 26-35 years) and self-reported cancer, adjusting for sociodemographic and early-life factors.
RESULTS: Compared to those who began working at ages 18-25, individuals who started between 5 and 12 years had 1.087 times higher odds of cancer (≈ 4% increased risk), while those starting at 13-17 years had 1.156 times higher odds (≈ 7% increased risk). Those who entered the workforce at 26-35 years showed 3.477 times higher odds. Although statistically significant, the effect sizes for early starters were modest.
CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of labor was modestly associated with increased odds of cancer in older Ecuadorian adults. This study should be viewed as a first step in exploring potential long-term consequences of child labor on chronic disease. Findings emphasize the importance of preventing child labor and highlight the need for further research with longitudinal data to clarify mechanisms and strengthen causal inference.

articles.title: The CAUSAL study: a prospective cohort of sarcoma survivors across the lifespan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcomas affect individuals across the lifespan, yet no cohort study exists evaluating contributors to treatment response, survival and health outcomes among contemporarily treated sarcoma patients. Determining disease, treatment, lifestyle, and genomic factors that contribute to oncologic and non-oncologic outcomes and survival in sarcoma patients is critical for strategic surveillance for current survivors and to inform future therapies. Furthermore, strategies to monitor disease through circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) approaches have tremendous potential as both a prognostic and predictive biomarker, to guide therapeutic interventions.
METHODS: This cohort is designed as a mixed retrospective and prospective study of sarcoma patients across the lifespan, treated with contemporary therapies, in the Sarcoma Treatment Center at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center. Data are systematically being collected on disease, treatment, response, relapse, treatment-related toxicity, sociodemographic, lifestyle, functional status, quality of life, physical health outcomes, and survival, together with tumor and germline biospecimens to evaluate oncologic and non-oncologic health outcomes among sarcoma patients seen for follow up or treatment since 2012 to present. At enrollment and annually, participants complete patient reported outcome (PRO) measures as well as health history and lifestyle surveys. In addition to general demographics, surveys provide data regarding family history, medication, and general health history. PROs assess financial toxicity, psychosocial and functional wellbeing, caregiver quality of life and function, post-traumatic stress, and physical symptoms. Lifestyle surveys describe participants' diet, physical activity, and substance use. Permission is secured to bank tumor specimens and germline samples, as well as for medical record review and ongoing follow up. Germline whole genome sequencing is conducted at 30X coverage. Tumor tissue sequencing is carried out by the Tempus xT, a panel of 648 cancer related genes at Tempus, Inc.
DISCUSSION: Establishment of a cohort of sarcoma survivors across the lifespan, with extensive and well characterized clinical and epidemiologic data, patient reported outcomes, tumor tissue, germline DNA, and serial blood samples builds a foundation for a long-term prospective investigation on life after sarcoma. Identification of health outcomes and their predictive and prognostic factors can lead to precision treatment and survivorship care, which are currently clinically unmet needs.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT06482957, Registered June 12, 2024.

articles.title: Transcriptome-based machine learning classification of pediatric germ cell tumors using nanopore RNA sequencing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood cancer comprises a heterogeneous group of diseases, with disproportionately higher mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) due to limited access to molecular diagnostics. Pediatric germ cell tumors (GCTs) are rare and represent 3% of childhood cancers, showing substantial clinical and biological heterogeneity, which makes accurate subtype classification challenging. As part of an ongoing multicentric collaboration, we evaluated nanopore whole-transcriptome sequencing as a scalable approach for differentiating pediatric GCTs from other solid tumors and distinguishing their histological subtypes using a nanopore-based transcriptomic classifier.
METHODS: Nanopore RNA-seq was performed on 56 pediatric tumors, including 14 germinomas/dysgerminomas/seminomas, 13 yolk sac tumors, 11 mature teratomas, seven immature teratomas, eight mixed tumors, and three embryonal carcinomas. A machine learning model was trained using their gene expression profiles and followed by independent validation.
RESULTS: Transcriptome data enabled molecular classification, achieving 98.9% overall accuracy in distinguishing GCTs from other previously sequenced pediatric solid tumors, and 100% accuracy above the established confidence threshold of 0.8. GCT subtype classification achieved 90.3% overall accuracy and 89.8% above 0.8 prediction probability. The model showed high F1-scores and AUC values above 0.86. Consistent performance was maintained in an independent cohort, and transcriptomic profiles derived from FFPE samples showed high concordance with cryopreserved tissues, supporting the method's applicability in routine clinical specimens.
CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the developed pipeline for GCT subtyping and support its future application in decentralized or resource-constrained healthcare systems. By enabling transcriptome-based classification with minimal infrastructure, nanopore platforms offer a promising solution for improving cancer diagnostics in LMICs.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors in pediatric atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (AT/RT) is a highly aggressive embryonal central nervous system tumor that predominantly affects young children. Despite progress in multimodal therapy, optimal treatment strategies remain controversial, especially for patients with metastatic disease.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical data from 22 pediatric patients with AT/RT treated at our center between November 2017 and April 2025. We evaluated demographic characteristics, extent of surgical resection, chemotherapy regimens, radiotherapy strategies, and survival outcomes. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. Prognostic factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 33 months (range, 7-110). Twelve patients (54.5%) presented with metastatic disease, and gross total resection(GTR) was achieved in 12 patients (54.5%). Eleven patients (50.0%) completed the initially planned chemotherapy regimen. At a reverse Kaplan-Meier median follow-up of 38 months (95% CI, 19-46 months), the 2-year OS and PFS rates were 64.3% (95% CI, 42.7%-85.9%) and 27.3% (95% CI, 9.7%-44.9%), respectively. In univariate analysis, radiotherapy and gross total resection were significantly associated with improved progression-free survival (PFS). In exploratory multivariable Cox regression analysis, metastatic disease and elevated lactate dehydrogenase(LDH) levels remained associated with inferior OS, whereas no variables retained independent significance for PFS.
CONCLUSIONS: Metastatic presentation and elevated LDH levels were associated with poorer overall survival in this exploratory single-center analysis. These findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: A large-scale multi-center analysis reveals that HNRNPA2B1 variants increase neuroblastoma risk in Chinese children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroblastoma has significant clinical heterogeneity, more precise genetic biomarkers are needed for early risk stratification. Although m6A modification has been reported to affect tumor development, the epidemiological impact of HNRNPA2B1 polymorphisms on neuroblastoma susceptibility remains to be determined.
METHODS: We recruited 1300 children with neuroblastoma and 2207 cancer-free controls across 9 Chinese hospitals to investigate the genetic contribution of HNRNPA2B1 variants (rs17153396 T > A and rs4273 C > T). Genetic associations were assessed through logistic regression and stratified risk analysis, and the robustness of the results was tested by false-positive report probability (FPRP) assessments. We integrated how HNRNPA2B1 affects survival and its interactome network by combining data from two public sets (GSE45547 and GSE16476) with protein‒protein interaction (PPI) network analysis.
RESULTS: The rs4273 C > T polymorphism increased neuroblastoma risk [adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 1.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.03-1.57, P = 0.023], and showed cumulative allelic effects (adjusted OR = 1.25, 95% CI = 1.02-1.53, P = 0.029). This genetic susceptibility was mainly manifested in female patients, infants (≤ 18 months), and early-stage patients [International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS) I + II+4s]. Transcriptome analyses revealed that upregulation of HNRNPA2B1 was correlated with advanced INSS stage, MYCN amplification, and poor prognosis, and its corresponding protein functioning as a critical hub in oncogenic PPI network.
CONCLUSIONS: The rs4273 variant emerges as a novel genetic determinant of neuroblastoma risk. The association between HNRNPA2B1 abnormalities and aggressive clinical phenotypes suggest that HNRNPA2B1 is both a potential risk indicator and a promising target for neuroblastoma treatment.

articles.title: Determinants of breast and cervical cancer screening uptake among women in Zambia: analysis of the 2024 Zambia demographic and health survey.
articles.abstract: Breast and cervical cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women globally, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The World Health Organization (WHO) has prioritised both cancers through the Global Breast Cancer Initiative and the global cervical cancer elimination strategy, which targets 70% screening coverage using high-performance tests among women aged 35 and 45 years. Despite Zambia's expansion of cervical cancer prevention services, little is known about the population-level uptake of breast and cervical cancer screening and the sociodemographic factors that drive it. This study assessed the determinants of breast and cervical cancer screening uptake among women aged 15-49 years using data from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS).We categorised the women into four mutually exclusive groups: no screening, breast-only screening, cervical-only screening, and breast and cervical screening. Survey weights were applied to account for the complex sampling design of the survey. Associations were examined using survey-adjusted multinomial logistic regression. All analyses were conducted using Stata 14.2.Among the 13,876 women included in the analysis, 68.84% reported no cancer screening, 4.67% reported breast-only screening, 17.87% reported cervical-only screening, and 8.63% reported both breast and cervical screening. Screening uptake increased with age but remained below recommended targets even among priority age groups: 43.8% of women aged 35-39 years and 51.3% of women aged 45-49 years reported any cervical cancer screening (cervical-only or combined). In multivariable adjusted analyses, these patterns were largely confirmed. Women aged 45-49 years were significantly more likely to undergo cervical-only screening (RRR 9.64; 95% CI 6.66-13.96) and combined screening (RRR 12.01; 95% CI 7.35-19.63) compared with adolescents aged 15-19 years. For breast-only screening, older age (35-44 years) and higher parity were the principal significant determinants, with women of parity 6 or more nearly twice as likely to report breast-only screening compared with nulliparous women (RRR 2.22; 95% CI 1.25-3.93). Higher education was associated with increased cervical-only (RRR 1.36; 95% CI 1.03-1.79) and combined screening (RRR 1.43; 95% CI 1.03-2.00). In contrast, rural residence was associated with lower cervical-only screening uptake (RRR 0.76; 95% CI 0.63-0.93), and high community poverty was associated with lower cervical-only (RRR 0.44; 95% CI 0.33-0.59) and combined screening (RRR 0.63; 95% CI 0.44-0.92).Breast and cervical cancer screening coverage among women aged 15-49 years in Zambia remains low, with substantial socio-demographic and geographic inequities. Screening uptake was strongly associated with age, parity, educational attainment, contraceptive use, and media exposure, while rural residence and high community poverty were consistent barriers across screening outcomes. Coverage remains markedly below the WHO 70% cervical cancer screening target, and no structured breast cancer early detection programme currently exists to address the growing burden of breast cancer among reproductive-age women in Zambia. Strengthening integrated screening strategies within reproductive health, primary care, and HIV service platforms, alongside targeted community-based outreach and health education, is essential for improving early detection and reducing the burden of women's cancers in Zambia.

articles.title: Online Physical Activity and Health Counseling for Survivors of Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (OPAC-ALL)- a study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia face an elevated risk of treatment-related late effects, including reduced cardiorespiratory fitness, musculoskeletal impairments, and metabolic syndrome. Effective, accessible interventions are urgently needed to promote physical activity and improve long-term health outcomes in this population. This trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a 26-week online high-intensity functional training program combined with health counseling and access to a lifestyle education website on cardiorespiratory fitness. The study will also assess the long-term impact on physical activity compared with WHO's physical activity guidelines.
METHODS: This single-center, two-arm randomized controlled trial will enroll 82 childhood ALL survivors aged 10-21 years who are at least one-year post-treatment and do not meet WHO physical guidelines. Participants will be randomized to an intervention group or a waitlist control group. The assessment time points for participants allocated to the intervention group will be at baseline and 26- and 78 weeks after baseline assessment. The assessment time points for participants allocated to the waitlist control group will be at baseline and at 26-, 52-, and 104 weeks after baseline assessment. The primary outcome is cardiorespiratory fitness. Secondary outcomes include physical activity levels, muscle strength, body composition, quality of life, fatigue, and markers of metabolic syndrome. Qualitative interviews will explore participant experiences and intervention feasibility.
DISCUSSION: This trial will provide critical evidence on the efficacy and feasibility of a digitally delivered, multicomponent intervention for improving physical fitness and health in childhood ALL survivors. If effective, the OPAC-ALL program could be integrated into routine follow-up care to address unmet rehabilitation needs in this growing survivor population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07042932. Registration date: 2025-06-17.

articles.title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index with multiple colorectal polyps as a precursor-lesion burden phenotype in adults undergoing diagnostic colonoscopy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer prevention depends on detection of precursor lesions, and metabolic dysfunction may shape early colorectal neoplasia before invasive cancer develops. Evidence linking the fasting triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with colonoscopy-defined polyp burden in younger and middle-aged diagnostic populations remains limited.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cross-sectional study included 169 adults aged 18 to 59 years who underwent complete diagnostic colonoscopy and had fasting triglyceride and glucose measurements within 90 days beforehand. Patients had no polyps (n = 58), 1 to 2 polyps (n = 60), or 3 or more polyps (n = 51); the primary outcome was 3 or more polyps. Logistic regression assessed TyG continuously and by tertiles, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index category, hypertension, and ever smoking. Spline modeling, discrimination, calibration, and E-value analyses were performed. Sensitivity analyses added diet, physical activity, alcohol use, family history, and colonoscopy-quality indicators; exploratory analyses examined incremental value over conventional risk factors and 2-hour postprandial glucose.
RESULTS: Mean TyG increased across polyp-burden groups (8.44 +/- 0.52, 8.72 +/- 0.51, and 8.90 +/- 0.49; P < 0.001). Each 1-unit increase was associated with higher adjusted odds of multiple polyps (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54 to 3.77; P = 0.002), and the highest tertile with substantially higher odds than the lowest (aOR, 4.78; 95% CI, 2.00 to 11.41; P = 0.005). Discrimination was only fair (area under the curve, 0.678). After further adjustment for diet, physical activity, alcohol use, family history, and colonoscopy-quality indicators, the association attenuated and lost significance (aOR, 1.63; 95% CI, 0.97 to 2.73; P = 0.064). Adding TyG to conventional risk factors raised discrimination only from 0.754 to 0.781.
CONCLUSION: Higher fasting TyG was associated with multiple colorectal polyps in adults undergoing diagnostic colonoscopy, although much of this association was shared with dietary pattern and physical activity. TyG is best regarded as a metabolic correlate of precursor-lesion burden rather than an independent determinant, and its fair discrimination and small incremental value preclude stand-alone triage use. Prospective multiethnic validation with standardized lifestyle assessment and dynamic glycemic measures is warranted.

articles.title: Intracranial metastases in sarcoma: a (not so) rare localization, experience of a sarcoma reference center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial metastases (IM) in patients with soft tissue sarcomas (STS) and bone sarcomas (BS) are uncommon. The reported incidence ranges from 1% to 3%, although it varies according to histological subtype, with alveolar soft part sarcoma and Ewing sarcoma showing the highest propensity for central nervous system (CNS) involvement. The development of IM is associated with a poor prognosis.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study including patients with STS and BS treated at the Veneto Institute of Oncology between 2010 and 2024. Data collected included age at diagnosis, sex, primary tumor characteristics, date and site of first metastasis, time to IM, and radiological characteristics of IM (number, location, and presence of peritumoral edema). Information on neurological symptoms, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes was also retrieved. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
RESULTS: Among 1,870 patients, including 801 with advanced disease, 30 developed IM, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.6% and 3.7% among patients with advanced disease. The most frequent histological subtypes were Ewing sarcoma (16.7%), undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (16.7%), and chondrosarcoma (13.3%). The median time from sarcoma diagnosis to IM was 30 months, while the median interval from the onset of metastatic disease to IM was 7 months. Most IM were diagnosed following the onset of neurological symptoms (70%), which were more commonly related to lesion location than to intracranial hypertension. The cerebrum was the most frequent site of involvement (66.7%), followed by the meninges (20.0%) and cerebellum (13.3%). Overall, 23 patients (76.7%) received at least one treatment for IM: 40.0% underwent local treatment alone, 20.0% received systemic therapy alone, and 30.0% received a combination of local and systemic treatments. Among patients receiving local treatment, radiotherapy alone was administered in 57.2% of cases, surgery alone in 21.4%, and combined surgery and radiotherapy in 21.4%. At the time of analysis, 25 of the 30 patients had died. Median OS after IM diagnosis was 2 months (95% CI, 1.14-2.85).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center series of patients with STS and BS, the overall incidence of IM was low, although certain histological subtypes showed a higher risk of CNS involvement. Most IM were solitary and potentially amenable to local treatment. Despite multimodal management, IM remained associated with a dismal prognosis. Further studies are needed to better understand the biological mechanisms underlying CNS dissemination and to identify more effective therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Trends in breast cancer incidence in Ethiopia, 2012-2022: a population-based study from a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer is uncontrolled abnormal cell growth. In 2022, an estimated 19.3 million new cancer diagnoses and 10 million cancer deaths were recorded globally. Breast cancer is among the leading cancers that result in death in Ethiopia. This study analyzed trends in breast cancer incidence in Ethiopia.
METHODS: Data were extracted from the Addis Ababa population based cancer registry. Of the 28,108 registered cancer patients, 7,160 were breast cancer cases. Crude, age-standardized incidence rate (ASR), annual percentage change (APC), and the Mann-Kendall trend test were utilized using R and Joinpoint regression software.
RESULTS: Breast cancer accounted for more than 25% of all cancers between 2012 and 2022. While the overall trend in incidence was not statistically significant, large fluctuations were observed. Incidence was highest in 2022 and in 2016 for the crude rate and ASR, respectively. Among females, breast cancer incidence increased non-significantly until 2016 (APC = 2.8), after which it showed a non-significant decline or remained relatively stable (APC = -0.7). In males, the incidence demonstrated a non-significant increasing trend till 2020 (APC = 6.5), followed by a non-significant decline thereafter (APC = -6.09). Overall, the APC was 0.43 among females and 4.48 among males .
CONCLUSION: Breast cancer accounts for one-fourth of all cancers diagnosed. While overall trends in incidence are statistically not significant, segmented analysis indicates non-significant over all trends with observed temporal fluctuations identified in segmented analyses, with a joinpoint detected in 2016 for females and 2020 for males. These findings emphasize the need for more breast cancer control, and public health education programs.

articles.title: Vonoprazan in school-aged children and adolescents: A narrative review of emerging evidence for gastroesophageal reflux disease and Helicobacter pylori infection.
articles.abstract: This narrative review synthesizes available evidence on vonoprazan (VPZ), a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB) that achieves rapid, potent gastric acid suppression with minimal CYP2C19 dependence, in pediatric patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) or Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. VPZ has been approved for adult indications in Japan (2014) and the United States (2022-2023) but has not received pediatric approval in any country or region as of mid-2026. Current clinical data derive almost exclusively from adolescents (12-17 years) and children aged ≥6 years weighing ≥30 kg; evidence in younger children (<6 years or <30 kg) is essentially absent, and this gap is highlighted throughout. Following the SANRA guidance for narrative reviews, PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through July 2026, supplemented by conference abstracts, reference lists, and regulatory documents, with adult data included where required for pharmacological or bridging rationale. For GERD, clinical evidence remains limited to Phase 1 pharmacokinetic/safety studies in adolescents (VPED-102) and children ≥6 years/≥30 kg (VPED-103), now reported in a peer-reviewed pooled analysis and integrated into a population pharmacokinetic (popPK) model; these confirm adult-concordant VPZ exposures at 10 and 20 mg with acceptable short-term tolerability and no age- or weight-related differences in clearance across 6-54 years, and model-based simulations support the same fixed doses in children as young as approximately 1 year, though no efficacy randomized controlled trial has been completed. For H. pylori eradication, prospective data from Japanese adolescents (n = 645) report a first-line VPZ triple-therapy intention-to-treat eradication rate of 73.6%, below the ≥90% guideline threshold, with clarithromycin resistance identified as a key contributor, while VPZ-based rescue therapy achieved 100% eradication in a small retrospective Western series (n = 11). Pediatric safety data are limited to short-term exposure; long-term effects on growth, bone metabolism, and the gut microbiome remain unstudied. Overall, VPZ is a pharmacologically promising alternative to proton pump inhibitors in pediatric acid-related disease, but current evidence is insufficient to support routine use outside clinical trials, and completion of ongoing randomized controlled trials, pediatric dose optimization, age-appropriate formulations, and long-term safety studies are prerequisites for guideline-level recommendations.

articles.title: "Time is of the essence": physician challenges impact patient access to chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CART) is a life-saving regimen for children with relapsed/refractory (r/r) B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), yet children from lower socioeconomic and historically marginalized backgrounds are less likely to receive it. Understanding the provider experience of CART referral and post-CART clinical management is critical for designing effective interventions to improve access.
OBJECTIVE: To explore physicians' experiences identifying and referring pediatric patients with r/r B-ALL for CART across diverse hospital settings, and to identify physician-perceived facilitators and barriers to CART treatment.
STUDY DESIGN: Focus groups using a semi-structured guide were conducted with pediatric oncology physicians, recruited via email and at a national conference, with targeted recruitment of National Cancer Institute Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP) site providers.
