Questions explored identifying pediatric patients with r/r B-ALL as CART candidates, referring them for CART, and accessing institutional infrastructure to support referral.
RESULTS: Analysis revealed six domains spanning referral to CART and subsequent CART treatment: identification of potentially eligible patients; complexity of CART referral; barriers to insurance approval; physician perception of patients' social/financial circumstances; and variability in pre- and post-CART management guidelines. Health system-level facilitators and barriers included patient identification and referral processes to tertiary care centers, guidelines for bridging therapy and post-CART toxicity management, and navigation support for patient care and insurance approval.
CONCLUSION: Findings highlight challenges in community-based settings where resources, infrastructure and geographic availability for CART are variable. Standardizing referral pathways, centralizing trial information, and streamlining CART-center intake process and communication are of immediate importance.

articles.title: Kcnq3 channels shape active membrane properties and firing signatures of thalamocortical neurons during postnatal development.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascending somatosensory pathways are formed before birth and refined in the early postnatal stages through activity-dependent mechanisms. In this context, the electrophysiological maturation of thalamocortical (TC) neurons is crucial to tune growing circuitry and ensure the fidelity of information processing. Accordingly, perturbations in ionic homeostasis during this vulnerable period might result in neurodevelopmental disorders. Encoded by Kcnq2 and Kcnq3, Kv7 or M-channels primarily assemble into hetero-tetramers under physiological conditions to mediate a subthreshold potassium current, termed M-current (IM), that regulates intrinsic excitability and neuronal firing signatures. Yet, how partial or complete absence of Kcnq3 subunits affects active and passive properties of developing TC neurons has hitherto not been fully elucidated.
METHODS: Here, by performing patch-clamp recordings in the mouse ventrobasal thalamic complex (VB), we provide a comprehensive electrophysiological characterization of the IM during postnatal development. We used transgenic mice carrying Kcnq3 mutations, corresponding to human orthologous variants associated with childhood forms of epilepsy, to investigate the impact of Kcnq3 full deletion and haploinsufficiency on the membrane properties and specific firing pattern of TC neurons. Furthermore, we determined the differential contribution of KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 channels to IM generation by expressing the human gene plasmids in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells at defined subunit ratios.
RESULTS: Pharmacological modulation with the Kcnq opener retigabine (RTG) revealed a gradual increase in IM magnitude during the first 30 postnatal days, whereas relative Kcnq2 and Kcnq3 transcripts remained unchanged across development. In the partial or complete absence of Kcnq3 channels, TC neurons exhibited hyperexcitability, characterized by enhanced burst firing and altered single action potential waveform. In accordance with these findings, equimolar KCNQ2/KCNQ3 expression evoked larger currents compared to either KCNQ2-dominant or KCNQ3-dominant subunit compositions.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest a central role for the Kcnq3 channels in stabilizing the membrane properties and firing mode of developing TC neurons, thus ensuring the faithful transmission of peripheral input to the cerebral cortex.

articles.title: Aetiological diagnosis of pneumonia: advances, limits and unresolved questions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the past 10 years, rapid molecular panels, point-of-care tests, host-response assays and sequencing have broadened and accelerated testing for pneumonia etiology. Yet detecting an organism remains different from showing that it caused disease, and more detections have not consistently improved patient outcomes. This review assesses what has changed in etiological diagnosis of pneumonia and where important uncertainties remain.
AREAS COVERED: Developments in adult and pediatric community-acquired pneumonia, hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia, and immunocompromised hosts are considered across syndromic molecular testing, clinical impact trials, host-response assays, sequencing and faster antimicrobial susceptibility testing. All specimens are considered, and conventional methods are discussed where they remain important to interpretation, treatment or surveillance. The evidence is assessed from detection through attribution and management to patient outcomes.
EXPERT OPINION: Progress is clearest in speed and breadth of detection; gains in clinical decision-making are promising but selective, and better outcomes are not established consistently. The central problem remains: a positive test result does not necessarily indicate the cause of pneumonia. We also lack reliable answers about whom to test, which specimens best represent disease, how to interpret mixed findings, and which test-guided decisions are safe and beneficial. Technology has advanced faster than clinical validation.

articles.title: Intraoperative serum sodium variation and postoperative complications: a single-center prospective cohort study in pediatric cardiac surgeries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess intraoperative serum sodium variation in children undergoing low- to moderate-risk cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and examine its association with a composite postoperative outcome.
METHODS: A total of 214 children were evaluated. Intraoperative serum sodium variation was defined as the difference between the highest and lowest observed concentrations. Its association with the composite outcome - defined as neurological, renal, cardiac, or pulmonary complications and/or death - was assessed using univariate and multivariable analyses. Mortality was additionally evaluated in exploratory unadjusted analyses.
RESULTS: Eighty-three children (38.8%) experienced the composite postoperative outcome. Median (interquartile range) intraoperative serum sodium variation was greater in patients with the composite outcome than in those without it (15.0 [10.2-20.0] vs. 8.0 [[5.0-12.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, variation was also greater among non-survivors than survivors (24.0 [20.0-26.5] vs. 10.0 [6.0-15.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, sodium variation remained independently associated with the composite outcome (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.06-1.19), together with CPB duration, peak intraoperative arterial lactate level, and body weight.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater intraoperative serum sodium variation was independently associated with a higher probability of the composite postoperative outcome in children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Exploratory unadjusted analysis also demonstrated greater sodium variation among non-survivors; however, the limited number of deaths precluded adjusted mortality analysis.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of IRT/IRT, IRT/PAP and IRT/PAP/IRT in cystic fibrosis newborn screening: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cystic fibrosis (CF) newborn screening (NBS) is used for early diagnosis, but conventional immunoreactive trypsinogen (IRT)/IRT protocols have high false-positive rates and low accuracy in diverse populations. Pancreatitis-associated protein (PAP) is a promising DNA-free biomarker.
METHODS: Systematic review registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023395880). Embase, LILACS (BIREME/BVS), Cochrane Library, PubMed and SciELO were searched from 2000 to May 2023, together with gray literature. Studies comparing at least two of these protocols (IRT/IRT, IRT/PAP or IRT/PAP/IRT) in the same newborn population were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, reconstructed 2 × 2 tables, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2) and certainty of evidence (GRADE).
RESULTS: Of 209 records, three prospective paired-comparison studies were included (Spain, n = 2; Argentina, n = 1; 198,728 newborns; 31 CF cases). Meta-analysis was not feasible. In the Spanish studies, IRT/PAP/IRT reduced false-positive results compared with IRT/IRT (22 vs. 79 and 11 vs. 26) and increased the positive predictive value (37.1%vs. 15.1% and 42.1% vs. 23.5%), with similar or lower sensitivity (92.9%vs. 100% and 88.9% vs. 88.9%). In Argentina, IRT/PAP eliminated the second sample, reducing incomplete screening from 22.5% to 0.2%, but the positive predictive value remained low (about 4%). All studies had a high risk of bias in at least one domain; certainty of evidence was low for false-positive results and very low for sensitivity.
CONCLUSIONS: PAP-based protocols may reduce false-positive results and, when no second sample is required, incomplete screening, but their effect on sensitivity is uncertain. A prospective pilot study within the Brazilian program newborn screening is needed before any protocol change.

articles.title: The burden, temporal patterns, and projected burden of asthma attributable to high BMI among children in China, 1990 - 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Childhood asthma and obesity represent two converging public health crises in China. High body mass index is an established modifiable risk factor for asthma, yet its specific epidemiological burden among Chinese children remains insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: Data on deaths and disability-adjusted life years attributable to high body mass index-related asthma among children aged 0 to 14 years in China from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study. Average annual percent change was used to assess temporal trends, an age-period-cohort model was applied to disentangle the independent effects of age, period, and birth cohort, and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was employed to project the burden through 2050.
RESULTS: In 2023, high body mass index-related asthma caused 8 deaths and 40,251 disability-adjusted life years among Chinese children, with males bearing a consistently higher burden. From 1990 to 2023, the age-standardized mortality rate declined significantly (average annual percent change: -4.26), while the disability-adjusted life year rate increased (average annual percent change: 1.62). Age-period-cohort analysis revealed declining mortality risk across successive periods and cohorts, whereas the risk of disability-adjusted life years increased markedly in recent birth cohorts (relative risk 1.81 for the 2014 to 2023 cohort). Projections indicate that total disability-adjusted life years will nearly triple to 102,393 by 2050.
CONCLUSION: While mortality from high body mass index-attributable asthma has declined, the morbidity burden is escalating and projected to worsen substantially by 2050. Integrated strategies targeting childhood obesity are urgently needed to mitigate this growing threat.

articles.title: Growth trajectories and metabolic profiles of low-birth-weight term and preterm infants: a 4-year longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare growth and metabolic outcomes during the first four years of life among low-birth-weight infants born moderately preterm, late preterm, and at full term.
METHODS: Cohort of singleton infants without malformations or congenital infections, weighing 1500-2499 g, followed in an outpatient clinic during the first four years of life, from 2014 to 2019. Three groups were compared: G1 (moderate preterm, n = 76), G2 (late preterm, n = 107), and G3 (term, n = 98). Weight, length, and head circumference were assessed using Z-scores. Metabolic assessment (cholesterol, triglycerides, fasting blood glucose) was performed once a year from the 2nd year onwards. Outcomes included growth failure, overweight/obesity risk, dyslipidemia, and glucose disorders. Group comparisons used ANOVA, Chi-square test, and repeated-measures ANOVA.
RESULTS: Growth Z-scores remained within normal limits but differed among groups, as moderate preterm infants maintained consistently higher Z-scores through the third year of life. Weight growth failure was more frequent in late preterm and term infants, with term infants showing a higher prevalence of thinness at 36-48 months and moderate preterm infants showing a higher risk of overweight at 24 months. No intergroup differences were found in lipid profiles, although triglycerides remained above recommended levels across all groups and time points, and preterm infants showed elevated total cholesterol at 4 years.
CONCLUSION: Growth patterns differed across groups in the first 4 years, with moderate preterm showing catch-up and higher Z-scores, while late preterm and term infants had more weight growth failure. Lipid profile abnormalities were observed in all groups from the second year of life onward.

articles.title: Assisted reproductive technology and the risk of urinary tract infection in offspring: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) increases the risk of certain childhood illnesses. However, its specific relationship with UTI in offspring remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the risk of UTI in ART offspring.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study linked Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database and Maternal and Child Health Database between 2004 and 2020. First live-born children conceived via ART were matched 1:2 with naturally conceived children based on maternal age, infant sex, and birth date. Pediatric UTI was defined as a hospitalization with a newly diagnosed UTI and concurrent antibiotic prescriptions before three years of age.
RESULTS: A total of 89,520 children were evaluated (29,840 in the ART group; 59,680 in the non-ART group). The cumulative incidence of UTI was significantly higher in the ART group (5.8% vs. 5.0%, p < 0.001). After adjusting for potential confounders, the ART group demonstrated a higher risk of UTI (aHR 1.16, 95% CI 1.09-1.24, p < 0.001). Notably, among children without genitourinary tract anomalies, ART remained significantly associated with offspring UTI (aHR 1.17, 95% CI 1.10-1.25, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Children born via ART carry an increased risk of developing UTI that is independent of known congenital structural anomalies.

articles.title: Infant mortality due to congenital heart disease in Brazil: a nationwide study of regional inequality and diagnostic imprecision, 2010-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of congenital anomaly-related deaths. In Brazil, a country marked by heterogeneous access to specialized care, mortality due to CHD may reflect disease severity and regional differences in diagnosis, screening, and treatment.
METHODS: The authors characterized temporal trends, regional and federative-unit patterns of CHD-related infant mortality in Brazil from 2010 to 2024 using data from the Mortality Information System (SIM) and Live Birth Information System (SINASC). The primary case definition was restricted to ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Temporal trends were evaluated via Prais-Winsten regression and linear regression with Newey-West standard errors to calculate the Annual Percent Change (APC) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, Brazil recorded 45,543 CHD deaths in children under one year (108.3 deaths per 100,000 live births). The Central-West and the Southeast had the highest and the lowest regional rates (125.70 and 104.38 per 100,000). National mortality notification increased (APC was 0.623%; 95% CI: 0.201 - 1.047; p = 0.012), with significant increases in the North (APC, 2.363%; p < 0.001) and Northeast (APC, 0.994%; p = 0.007), while other regions remained stationary. Over half of the deaths occurred in the neonatal period (52.8%).
CONCLUSION: Infant mortality notification due to CHD in Brazil increased from 2010 to 2024, showing marked regional inequalities. Rising trends in the North and Northeast and the high proportion of post-neonatal deaths suggest that delayed diagnosis, referral limitations, continuity-of-care gaps, and diagnostic imprecision in death certification influence preventable mortality.

articles.title: Real-world glycemic monitoring in pediatric cystic fibrosis: implementation of OGTT screening and multidisciplinary endocrinology care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess OGTT screening, glycemic abnormalities, HbA1c, and endocrinology follow-up in pediatric cystic fibrosis (CF).
METHODS: This retrospective study assessed 83 patients aged 10-18 years during 2024-2025; 20 younger patients were analyzed separately. Five with established CF-related diabetes (CFRD) were excluded from screening analyses. Historical OGTT findings were assessed separately. OGTT and HbA1c results within 90 days were compared descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 78 eligible patients, 45 (57.7%) had OGTT, 65 (83.3%) had HbA1c, and six (7.7%) had neither documented during 2024-2025. Historical OGTT results (n = 69) included normal glucose tolerance (n = 36), impaired glucose tolerance (n = 19), indeterminate glycemia (n = 10), and CFRD (n = 4). Among 26 paired results, three patients with impaired glucose tolerance had HbA1c < 5.7%, while ten with normal glucose tolerance had HbA1c 5.7-6.4%. Endocrinology follow-up was documented for 27/83 patients, including all five with CFRD.
CONCLUSIONS: OGTT documentation was incomplete, and HbA1c and OGTT categories differed. Improving OGTT completion and coordinated care remains important.

articles.title: Developmental hemostasis and coagulation disorders in neonates and infants: diagnostic challenges and modern clinical management.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To provide an updated overview of developmental hemostasis, diagnostic methodologies, hereditary and acquired coagulation diseases, and novel laboratory instruments pertinent to neonatal and infant care.
SOURCES: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. The review included relevant original studies, reviews, guidelines, and consensus statements on developmental hemostasis, neonatal coagulation abnormalities, thrombosis, and laboratory diagnostics.
SUMMARY OF THE FINDINGS: Coagulation factors, natural anticoagulants, fibrinolysis, platelet function, and fibrin structure change with gestational and postnatal age. Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen, platelet count, and D-dimer therefore require age- and assay-appropriate interpretation. The review distinguished inherited bleeding disorders from acquired coagulopathies, including disseminated intravascular coagulation, vitamin K deficiency bleeding, and sepsis-associated coagulopathy. It also discussed neonatal thrombosis and the complementary roles of thromboelastography, rotational thromboelastometry, and thrombin-generation testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Accurate recognition of coagulation abnormalities in neonates depends on understanding developmental hemostasis and using age-appropriate laboratory reference ranges. Clinical findings should be interpreted together with conventional coagulation tests and, where appropriate, newer diagnostic methods.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into benzoxaborole activity against Cryptosporidium parvum: CPSF3 targeting genetically validated for AN3661, with implications for resistance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryptosporidiosis is a major enteric disease affecting humans and animals worldwide, with severe consequences in young children and neonatal livestock, yet treatment options remain extremely limited. Benzoxaboroles have emerged as promising broad-spectrum antiparasitic compounds, but their mechanisms of action, molecular targets, and resistance pathways in Cryptosporidium spp. remain incompletely understood, limiting their optimal therapeutic deployment. We previously showed that the benzoxaborole AN3661 inhibits the endonuclease Cleavage and Polyadenylation Specificity Factor 3 (CPSF3) in Cryptosporidium hominis, likely by disrupting pre-mRNA processing and restricting parasite growth. Here, we further investigated the mode of action of AN3661 and compared it with two additional benzoxaboroles, AN13762 and AN7973.
METHODOLOGY: Cell culture assays combined with imaging-based quantification were used to assess drug activity and determine the impact of treatment on parasite growth and development. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was used to introduce a point mutation into Cryptosporidium parvum CPSF3 and evaluate resistance to benzoxaboroles in vitro and in vivo. Nanopore sequencing was performed to examine the effects of drug exposure on parasite mRNA processing.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We identified a single mutation in C. parvum CPSF3 (Y385N) that conferred strong resistance to AN3661. In contrast, this mutation did not reduce sensitivity to AN13762 or AN7973, which are also suspected to target CPSF3. All three benzoxaboroles impaired mRNA processing, a process mediated by the CPSF machinery, and exhibited parasiticidal activity, with pronounced effects during late-stage maturation of first-generation meronts, including inhibition of parasite egress; two compounds also affected gametogenesis. Notably, AN7973 controlled severe infection in susceptible mice challenged with the AN3661-resistant C. parvum CPSF3 Y385N mutant. In Toxoplasma gondii, AN7973 remained active against strains resistant to AN3661 and AN13762, supporting a distinct mechanism of action. Finally, AN3661 and AN7973 were active against Eimeria tenella, and AN3661 against Giardia duodenalis.
CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Together, these results identify a resistance mechanism affecting AN3661 in Cryptosporidium, and highlight AN7973 as a promising alternative compound with broad antiparasitic activity and efficacy against AN3661-resistant parasites.

articles.title: Exploring the Utility of the Quick Interactive Language Screener in Young Autistic Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Measuring emerging language in young autistic children is notoriously difficult. Conventional approaches-including standardized assessment, caregiver report, and natural language samples-offer valuable information but also have their respective limitations. The Quick Interactive Language Screener (QUILS) is a newer approach that has proven useful in non-autistic children. It is a computer-based tool designed to screen early language comprehension skills in vocabulary and syntax, as well as the processes underlying word learning. The present investigation aims to explore the usefulness of the QUILS when used with young autistic children, in terms of (1) correlations across the QUILS subtests and (2) correlations between the QUILS and other frequently used language measures (CDI-III vocabulary, CDI-III sentences, natural language sample metrics including lexical diversity and MLU, and Vineland-3).
METHODS: Secondary data analysis was used to explore a subset of participants derived from a national remote (i.e., Zoom-based) study on language development in children with autism. Participants (N = 54) aged 38-71 months (M = 56.2, SD = 8.8) were administered the QUILS; their caregiver completed the CDI-III and Vineland-3 about their development, and caregivers and children completed a brief caregiver-child interaction, from which natural language samples were transcribed.
RESULTS: The three subtests of the QUILS showed high correlations with each other (all ps < .001). Similarly, a QUILS composite score was highly correlated (all ps < .001) with words and sentences produced on the CDI-III, two metrics derived from our natural language sample (lexical diversity and MLU), and the Vineland-3 Communication Domain raw score.
CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that with young autistic children, the subtests of the QUILS cohere with each other, and the QUILS (overall) converges with other measures of emergent language.
IMPLICATIONS: These findings indicate that the QUILS may be a useful addition to the toolbox of early language assessment in autism. Our preliminary findings suggest that the QUILS is feasible for use with young autistic children and that it may be a useful complement to other instruments, providing promising directions for quantification of language skills using computer-based, remote administration.

articles.title: What Characterises the Communication of Three-Year-Olds with Suspected Autism?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The current study aimed to examine the communicative level of 3-year-old children with suspected autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in a population-representative sample focusing on communication initiation, communication modes and communication functions. Potential differences in communication between children who later met diagnostic criteria for ASD and those who did not, and possible differences between girls and boys were analysed.
METHODS: Video recordings from a standardised play observation of 75 children (14 girls, 61 boys, M age = 3.2), of whom 59 were diagnosed with ASD and 16 did not receive such a diagnosis, were analysed using the Modified - Classroom Observation Schedule to Measure Intentional Communication.
RESULTS: The whole group of children (n = 75) were more likely to respond to others than to take their own communicative initiatives. The most frequent communicative functions were confirming and requesting, often expressed through vocalisations or actions. No significant differences between girls and boys could be detected. Children without ASD (n = 16, all boys) gave more responses, used more verbal communication forms and more frequently established joint attention and dyadic social interaction than children with ASD (n = 59).
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced use of conventional spoken and gestural forms, as well as lower rates of contingent responding, distinguished children who later received an ASD diagnosis. Although results need to be interpreted cautiously, findings indicate that gender-related communicative differences associated with ASD may not be apparent in very early childhood.
IMPLICATIONS: This study contributes to understanding communication in suspected ASD. Future studies should examine longitudinal trajectories of communication functions, forms and initiative/response in children with ASD.

articles.title: Quick Reference Guide: An Umbrella Review of Speech-Language Interventions to Support Autistic Children and Youth.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Speech-language pathologists (SLPs) have reported using over 30 interventions to support autistic children and youth, but large caseloads limit time to review relevant research for informed clinical decision-making. To support the implementation of evidence-based practice, this umbrella review evaluates and compares the evidence for these interventions to provide clinicians, researchers and policymakers with an easy-access guide summarizing the existing evidence.
METHODS: The protocol was pre-registered in PROSPERO. Eight databases were searched to identify systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for Systematic Reviews. Summary tables were developed synthesizing the outcomes relevant to the field of speech-language pathology.
MAIN CONTRIBUTIONS: Twenty-three systematic reviews of interventions used by SLPs met our inclusion criteria and were categorized as either general intervention approaches or specific manualized interventions. Seven intervention approaches were identified (joint attention, caregiver-delivered, technology-assisted caregiver-delivered, play-based, pragmatic, social pragmatic, social skills), and all had consistent evidence for at least one positive outcome. Four of six manualized interventions had consistent evidence of a positive effect for at least one outcome (Early Start Denver Model; Joint Attention, Symbolic Play, Engagement, Regulation; PEERS®; Social StoriesTM).
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This umbrella review generated an overview of the existing evidence for interventions that may be used by SLPs to support autistic children and youth. Variability in evidence quantity and how outcomes were synthesized prohibited assessing relative efficacy or providing clinical recommendations on which interventions have the best evidence to support their use in practice; however, SLPs will be able to use the quick reference guide in conjunction with their clinical experience and client preferences to provide evidence-based practice. For researchers, results highlighted a need for the use of a consistent outcome measure to support comparison between interventions, describe participants in further detail and prioritize systematic reviews of interventions that are sufficiently similar in format and goals.

articles.title: An In Silico-In Vitro Framework for Model-Informed Precision Dosing in Oncology: Proof-of-Principle for Doxorubicin in Patient-Derived Sarcoma Spheroids.
articles.abstract: Drug dose and drug exposure time are important factors influencing the tumor-specific response to pharmacological agents. These parameters are only minimally reflected, if at all, in current functional precision medicine platforms and general prediction algorithms. In this study, we combined individualized pharmacokinetic modeling with functional long-term in vitro testing in patient-derived tumor spheroids to allow design of effective dosing regimens for solid tumors. Doxorubicin (DOX), which is used as a standard of care in the treatment of solid tumors such as soft tissue and bone sarcomas, served as a model drug. Based on an individualized physiologically-based pharmacokinetic DOX model for a 16-year-old woman, a series of study conditions were defined using the computationally modeled human area under the curve (AUC) for in vitro testing design. The different conditions spanned a range of treatment conditions from long-term exposure at low concentrations to short-term exposure at high concentrations, using patient-derived soft-tissue rhabdoid myosarcoma tumor spheroids derived from a 16-year-old cancer patient. Consistent with clinical observations, our results indicate that the outcome depended mainly on DOX concentration, while the exposure time was almost insignificant. Moreover, our study showed that the inhibitory DOX effect reaches saturation despite the AUC being linearly dependent on the administered dose such that lower DOX doses with similar antitumoral efficacy, yet lower systemic toxicity, can be achieved. The concept presented here is intended to serve as a foundation for in silico-in vitro research, with the aim of enhancing precision dosing in oncology.

articles.title: L-Asparaginase exposure and immune fitness in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia: A critical evidence appraisal for immunotherapy integration.
articles.abstract: L-asparaginase (L-ASP) is indispensable in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but circulating and marrow-resident immune cells encounter the same systemic amino-acid perturbation as leukemic blasts. Whether this exposure modifies the fitness of cells required for immunotherapy remains unresolved. This critical narrative review evaluates L-ASP and amino-acid-restriction evidence across T cells, natural killer cells, B cells, macrophages, and the bone-marrow niche, and relates it to blinatumomab, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, and checkpoint blockade. We assess intervention directness, clinical relevance, and study quality separately. T-cell studies show that asparagine supports early activation, whereas selected activated CD8⁺ states can mount an activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4)-dependent nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) response under defined restriction conditions. Direct in-vitro asparaginase studies report differing effects on human natural killer-cell killing and should be distinguished from glutamine withdrawal or intracellular glutaminase inhibition; direct enzyme-exposure studies also identify B-cell and macrophage effects in non-pediatric-ALL models, while local marrow effects remain uncertain. Clinical regimens establish that L-ASP and immunotherapies can be used within the same treatment program, but they do not define a metabolic washout interval. We therefore distinguish serum enzyme activity, biochemical substrate recovery, and functional immune recovery. Prospective studies should link these measures to partner-specific cellular, manufacturing, and clinical endpoints. Current evidence supports testable compatibility hypotheses, not fixed scheduling rules.

articles.title: Correlation between maternal serum pgRNA levels during pregnancy and neonatal virological characteristics at birth in HBV-infected pregnant women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between serum pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) in pregnant women with chronic HBV (CHB) infection during pregnancy and maternal clinical characteristics, virological characteristics of newborns at birth, and mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) outcomes.
METHODS: 312 pregnant women with CHB and their newborns were followed up for 12 months, and their clinical data were collected. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between maternal indicators and neonatal outcomes, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with neonatal HBeAg positivity.
RESULTS: Maternal HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels were significantly higher in the pgRNA-positive group. All infants followed up to 12 months were negative for both HBsAg and HBV DNA, yielding a 100% success rate of MTCT prevention. Neonatal HBeAg levels at birth were associated with maternal pgRNA levels. Maternal pgRNA levels were significantly higher in mothers of HBeAg-positive newborns than in those of HBeAg-negative newborns, whereas no significant association was found between maternal pgRNA levels and neonatal HBsAg or HBV DNA status. Neonatal HBeAg level was weakly positively correlated with maternal pgRNA levels (r = 0.17, P < 0.01) and maternal HBeAg levels (r = 0.12, P < 0.05). Maternal pgRNA, HBeAg, HBsAg, HBV DNA, age, and treatment were identified as factors associated with neonatal HBeAg status, whereas multivariate analysis showed that only maternal HBeAg remained an independent associated factor.
CONCLUSION: Maternal serum pgRNA is associated with neonatal HBeAg status at birth. However, under standardized combined immunoprophylaxis, maternal pgRNA was not associated with MTCT failure.

articles.title: HHV-7 positivity in hospitalized children with acute respiratory tract infections: co-detection patterns and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To analyze the epidemiology, co-detection patterns, and clinical features associated with Human Herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) positivity in children with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 9,521 pediatric inpatients with ARTIs using targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) to detect HHV-7 and co-detected microbes. False discovery rate (FDR) correction (Benjamini-Hochberg procedure), age-matched sensitivity analysis, and multivariable logistic regression were applied to control for multiple testing and confounding.
RESULTS: The overall HHV-7 detection rate was 3.3% (315/9,521; median age: 5 years) with an extremely high co-detection rate (99.0%), predominantly Streptococcus pneumoniae (32.1%), rhinovirus (30.8%), EBV (30.5%), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (30.2%). Bronchial wall thickening (81.1%) and ground-glass opacities (74.8%) were main CT findings. Notably, a subset of patients exhibited substantial clinical severity, with 16.8% (53/315) requiring respiratory support and 4.8% (15/315) admitted to the ICU. Regarding discharge outcomes, in-hospital mortality was zero, with 96.8% (305/315) achieving clinical recovery, while 3.2% (10/315) underwent voluntary discharge prior to full recovery. Although HHV-7-positive children (without CMV co-detection) initially presented with lower unadjusted respiratory support rates than CMV-positive children without HHV-7 co-detection (16.5% vs. 38.7%; FDR-adjusted q < 0.001), this difference lost significance in age-matched sensitivity analysis (q > 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that HHV-7 positivity was not independently associated with respiratory support (aOR = 0.57, P = 0.081). Younger age (aOR = 0.98, P < 0.001), elevated procalcitonin (aOR = 1.26, P = 0.047), and non-respiratory specimens (aOR = 5.19, P = 0.026) were identified as independent risk factors, whereas autumn admission was protective (aOR = 0.60, P = 0.045).
CONCLUSIONS: HHV-7 exhibits a low detection rate (3.3%) in pediatric ARTIs. The high co-detection rate (99.0%) suggests that HHV-7 positivity commonly occurs within polymicrobial respiratory infection contexts; its independent clinical contribution remains uncertain. Baseline clinical severity disparities between HHV-7 and CMV cohorts are primarily driven by host age rather than intrinsic viral pathogenicity.

articles.title: Nationwide surveillance of blood lead levels in Georgian children: insights from the state program "Early Detection and Screening of Diseases" (2020-2023).
articles.abstract: Lead is a toxic heavy metal associated with significant health risks, particularly in children, due to its neurotoxic effects and lack of a safe exposure threshold. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of blood lead levels (BLLs) in children aged 0-18 years screened under Georgia's national program, utilizing data from Georgia's State Program for Early Detection and Screening of Diseases collected between 2020 and 2023. The dataset includes 31,979 children, providing a robust foundation for evaluating temporal trends and regional disparities in lead exposure. A nationwide decline in elevated blood lead levels (BLLs) was observed during the study period, with an overall mean BLL of 4.75 µg/dL (SD 4.16); however, substantial regional variations persist, with Adjara (mean BLL 5.26 µg/dL, 11.66% with BLL ≥ 10 µg/dL) and Guria (mean BLL 5.02 µg/dL, 8.27% with BLL ≥ 10 µg/dL) reporting the highest levels. BLL was weakly associated with age, reflecting indication-based screening outside the target age range, and differed minimally between boys and girls. In a subgroup restricted to children aged 2-7 years, 31.32% had BLLs at or above 5 µg/dL. These findings underscore the critical need for targeted, region-specific environmental health interventions and policies to address persistent lead exposure risks. This analysis contributes valuable epidemiological insights into childhood lead exposure in Georgia, informing future public health strategies and resource allocation. This study represents the first nationwide descriptive analysis of blood lead surveillance data collected through Georgia's State Program for Early Detection and Screening of Diseases (2020-2023).

articles.title: Risk of exposure to heavy metals and hepatic renal profile in children from a rural Peruvian community.
articles.abstract: Children living in rural communities may be particularly vulnerable to chronic exposure to heavy metals through drinking water. This study evaluated the non-carcinogenic health risk associated with arsenic, lead, and mercury exposure and assessed renal and hepatic function biomarkers in children from a rural Peruvian community. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 50 children younger than 5 years from Rica Playa, northern Peru. Arsenic, lead, and mercury concentrations were measured in treated drinking water and untreated river water. Chronic daily intake and target hazard quotient (THQ) were estimated using deterministic methods and Monte Carlo simulation. Renal function was assessed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and hepatic function by serum transaminases. Arsenic concentrations exceeded regulatory limits in untreated water and generated THQ values above 1 in both treated and untreated water, with 100% of deterministic and probabilistic estimates exceeding the non-carcinogenic risk threshold. Lead exceeded the risk threshold only in a proportion of children consuming untreated water, particularly among those younger than 1 year. Reduced eGFR was identified in 72.7% (24/33) of evaluated children and elevated transaminases in 9.1%, although neither outcome was significantly associated with drinking water source. Arsenic was identified as the principal contributor to the estimated non-carcinogenic risk under the evaluated drinking water exposure scenarios. These findings support strengthening drinking water quality surveillance and implementing longitudinal biomonitoring in vulnerable pediatric populations.

articles.title: Umbrella review of the effectiveness of probiotic supplementation on oxidative stress markers, inflammatory biomarkers, and pregnancy outcomes in pregnant women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Probiotics are considered safe for reducing oxidative stress and inflammation in pregnancy, but meta-analytic findings are inconsistent. This study summarizes evidence on the effects of probiotic/synbiotic on oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: An umbrella review was conducted using PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to April 2025. Outcomes assessed included malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), glutathione (GSH), nitric oxide (NO), interleukin‑6 (IL‑6), tumor necrosis factor‑alpha (TNF‑α), C-reactive protein (CRP), high-sensitivity CRP (hs‑CRP), GDM, preeclampsia, preterm birth, cesarean section, birth weight, and gestational age.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight meta-analyses involving 37,195 participants were included. Probiotic supplementation consistently reduced MDA and improved antioxidant capacity (TAC, GSH), though findings for NO were mixed. Several meta-analyses reported significant reductions in IL-6, TNF-α, and hs-CRP. However, probiotics showed no consistent effect on clinical outcomes such as GDM, preeclampsia, preterm birth, cesarean section, or birth weight. Considerable heterogeneity was observed across probiotic strains, dosages, and intervention durations.
CONCLUSION: Probiotic supplementation during pregnancy appears to improve several biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation. However, current evidence does not consistently demonstrate beneficial effects on major clinical pregnancy outcomes. These findings suggest that while probiotics may influence biological pathways related to oxidative balance and inflammation, further high‑quality randomized controlled trials are needed to determine whether these biochemical effects translate into meaningful clinical benefits for maternal and neonatal health.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Tracking respiratory syncytial virus dynamics in wastewater during the 2024-2025 season in Switzerland.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is responsible for a substantial health burden worldwide, particularly among children and older adults. In 2023, novel immunoprophylactic interventions for RSV were approved, underscoring the need to monitor circulating RSV lineages and detect mutations that could compromise intervention effectiveness. Here, we implemented wastewater-based genomic RSV surveillance by integrating digital PCR and amplicon-based sequencing within Switzerland's national wastewater monitoring program. We tracked RSV subtypes and individual mutations across the 2024-2025 peak season in six Swiss cities. RSV-A and RSV-B co-circulated nationwide, and both exhibited similar epidemiological dynamics estimated from their subtype-specific effective reproduction numbers. No previously reported F protein mutations relevant to prophylaxis efficacy were identified. Genetic diversity analysis of wastewater-derived sequences reflected patterns previously reported in clinical data, with higher diversity in RSV-A than RSV-B, and greater variability in the G compared to the F gene. These findings demonstrate the potential of wastewater-based RSV surveillance for monitoring RSV dynamics and diversity and establish a national baseline for RSV evolution during the first season following vaccine implementation in Switzerland.IMPORTANCERespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory virus that can cause serious illness in vulnerable populations. The recent development of RSV immunoprophylaxis products has increased the importance of monitoring viral evolution. Standard surveillance based on clinical testing captures only a fraction of infections. Our findings demonstrate that wastewater-based genomic surveillance, using regularly collected samples throughout the peak RSV season, can provide a cost-effective and representative picture of viral dynamics. Expanding this approach into future RSV seasons and across a broader geographic scope will enable continuous tracking of viral evolution, including detection of novel mutations, which is particularly important given the widespread introduction of new vaccines and preventive treatments.

articles.title: Perinatal influences on the gut resistome and bacteriome in South African infants from birth to 6 months of life: insights from a shotgun metagenomics study.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AR) is a major global health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where neonatal infections remain a leading cause of death, compounded by limited surveillance and uncontrolled antibiotic use. The neonatal gut is a reservoir for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet LMIC data remain scarce. Using shotgun metagenomics, we investigated gut resistome and bacteriome dynamics in infants during their first 6 months of life. Analysis of 68 longitudinal fecal samples from 17 infants revealed 211 ARGs across 7 antibiotic classes. Beta-lactam genes (blaTEM-1 and blaTEM-10-MGH-1) dominated, accounting for 64.0% of detections and indicating substantial early-life resistance load. Non-blaTEM ARGs (e.g., cat4, tetC, aphA2) emerged between 16 and 26 weeks, reflecting ongoing microbial evolution. In this small, exploratory cohort, infant antibiotic exposure, maternal HIV with highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), and cesarean delivery with maternal antibiotics were associated with higher ARG diversity; given the small, uneven subgroups, this pattern is hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive, suggesting a role for clinical and maternal factors in resistome development. The bacteriome featured diverse, resilient taxa with persistent opportunistic pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus aureus, which are potential ARG reservoirs. Despite sample size limitations, these findings offer valuable insight into neonatal ARG acquisition, persistence, and bacterial profiles in an LMIC setting, and point to a plausible, multifactorial interplay of maternal, clinical, and environmental influences on resistome dynamics requiring confirmation in larger cohorts. This early, pervasive resistance reservoir supports tailored antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention, and microbiome-informed strategies, alongside future genotypic-phenotypic surveillance.IMPORTANCEThis study provides region-specific insight into the early-life gut resistome and bacteriome of infants from a low- and middle-income setting, addressing a gap in global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance. Universal detection of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) from birth highlights the establishment of a genetic resistance reservoir, even in antibiotic-naïve populations. In this small, exploratory cohort, perinatal factors, including antibiotic exposure, maternal HIV/HAART status, and delivery mode, showed patterns associated with resistome diversity and microbial succession. Although not statistically definitive, these findings suggest multifactorial drivers of early AMR emergence warranting confirmation in larger studies. Persistence of clinically important ARGs alongside opportunistic pathogens raises questions for neonatal infection management; however, these genotypic findings indicate potential rather than confirmed resistance, underscoring the need for paired phenotypic susceptibility data. This work establishes foundational longitudinal data for South Africa, informing antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention, and microbiome-informed interventions to mitigate AMR risk and improve infant health outcomes.

articles.title: An engineered Zika virus recombinant adenovirus vaccine induces protective immune response in mice.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in many countries/territories. Our previous publication reported that the antibodies (Abs) induced by ZIKV infection could exacerbate the mortality of JEV-infected mice, bringing challenges to the development of traditional Zika vaccines. Here, we developed two recombinant adenoviruses (Ad5-ZIKV-EWT and Ad5-ZIKV-Emut) encoding the ZIKV wild-type E protein and an E protein mutant carrying five amino acid substitutions (replaced by alanine) in the bc loop and fusion loop regions of the E protein, respectively. The levels of JEV-cross-reactive or DENV-cross-reactive Ab responses induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut immunization in mice are lower than those induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The level of ZIKV-neutralizing Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is comparable to that elicited by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The ability of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut to enhance JEV or DENV infections in vitro is attenuated as compared with that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The in vivo protective role of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is similar to that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. Mice receiving Ad5-ZIKV-EWT-immune mouse sera exhibited antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) post-DENV challenge, whereas passively transferred Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immune mouse sera did not lead to obvious ADE of DENV infection in recipient mice. Notably, maternally acquired Abs did not enhance the mortality of 2-day-old neonates born to Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immunized mice post-JEV challenge. These results suggest that optimizing the E protein amino acid sequence of ZIKV could significantly reduce the level of cross-reactive Abs to JEV and DENV, and abrogate the ADE of JEV and DENV infections, providing a promising strategy to develop an effective and safe ZIKV vaccine.
IMPORTANCE: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in some countries or territories. The results of preliminary animal experiments and clinical cohort studies support that antibodies induced by ZIKV infection can enhance JEV or DENV infection in vitro and in vivo. Therefore, the ZIKV vaccine encoding the wild-type E protein constructed by conventional methods has the antibody-dependent enhancement risk against JEV and DENV infections. In this study, we obtained an E protein mutant by mutating key amino acids in the bc loop and FL sequences of the ZIKV wild-type E protein to alanine. The recombinant adenovirus vaccine based on this E protein mutant is not only effective but also safer in preventing ZIKV infection in the future.

articles.title: Elucidating mechanisms associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress at the placental and fetal brain axis in response to oxycodone exposure.
articles.abstract: Prenatal oxycodone (Oxy) exposure has been associated with several neurodevelopmental outcomes in newborns. However, the molecular mechanisms involved in Oxy-induced placental and fetal brain damage during gestation remain unknown. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is a cellular stress response triggered by the accumulation of unfolded proteins, which activates the unfolded protein response. Here, we hypothesized that Oxy exposure induces ER stress in the fetal brain-placental axis. To test this hypothesis, we used three model systems: in vitro primary neurons, primary mixed neuroglial cells, and an in vivo model of maternal Oxy exposure. Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) was employed to detect mRNA expression of ER stress mediators, such as Binding Immunoglobulin Protein (Bip), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), spliced X-box binding protein 1 (sXBP1), and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP). Immunoblot analysis was also used to detect protein expression of ER stress mediators, such as Bip; phosphorylated and total forms of inositol-requiring transmembrane kinase/endoribonuclease 1α (p-IRE1α and t-IRE1α) and protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase α (p-PERKα and t-PERKα); phosphorylated eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (p-eIF2α); and sXBP1. Further, we detected pro-apoptotic markers such as Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim), p53 upregulated modulator of apoptosis (PUMA), and cleaved poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP). Exposure of Oxy to rat primary fetal neuronal cells increased mRNA expression of Bip and ATF4. sXBP1 and CHOP mRNA levels were upregulated in both rat primary fetal neuronal cells and mixed neuroglial cells. Prenatal Oxy exposure resulted in increased mRNA expression of all ER stress markers tested in both the placenta and fetal brain. We also observed that Oxy exposure increased protein levels of ER stress markers (Bip, p-IRE1α, t-IRE1α, p-PERKα, t-PERKα, p-eIF2α, and sXBP1), as well as pro-apoptotic and apoptotic markers (Bim, PUMA, and cleaved PARP). In conclusion, Oxy exposure increases ER stress mediators in both the placental and fetal brain compartments, which could further lead to apoptosis.

articles.title: Cross-protective immune responses to pneumococcal serotype 6A following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: India bears a pneumococcal disease burden, with serogroup 6 contributing to invasive pneumococcal disease, acute otitis media, and nasopharyngeal carriage. Serotype 6B is included in several pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with evidence suggesting cross-protection against serotype 6A. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated serotype 6A-specific immune responses following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines. Databases were searched for studies reporting IgG geometric mean concentrations, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL, and opsonophagocytic activity titers. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria; eight contributed quantitative data. Overall, 6B-containing vaccines elicited measurable cross-reactive IgG and functional responses against serotype 6A. Booster-containing 3 + 1 schedules showed numerically higher responses than 3 + 0 schedules, with pooled IgG GMCs of 1.63 vs. 0.59 µg/mL, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL of 92.78% vs. 65.38%, and OPA GMTs of 984.6 vs. 169.2, respectively. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251134118). These findings support 6B-mediated cross-reactive immunogenicity, particularly following booster dosing in vaccinated children.

articles.title: Exploring RSV prevention among pregnant people and healthcare professionals in Aotearoa, New Zealand.
articles.abstract: In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), RSV causes severe disease in infants, particularly Māori and Pacific infants, and is a high burden on the health system. Although an antenatal RSV vaccine and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are available internationally to prevent disease, they are not yet available in NZ. This study aims to explore the knowledge and perceptions of pregnant people and health care providers regarding RSV preventative options, and strategies for supporting a potential future immunization rollout in NZ. In this mixed-methods study, a cross-sectional survey of health care professionals (HCPs) across NZ and qualitative interviews with recently/pregnant Māori, Pacific, or ethnic minority migrants were conducted. A directed content analytic approach was used for analysis. Most HCPs (79.5%; 159/200) thought there was a high need for universal antenatal RSV vaccination, and 73.5% (147/200) ranked antenatal vaccination as their preferred prevention strategy over either targeted or universal infant monoclonal antibody. However, pharmacists comprised 63% of respondents. Interviewed caregivers (n = 13) would prefer to be offered whichever option had the longest duration of protection. If effectiveness and length of protection were similar, most preferred the antenatal vaccine so their infant was not injected to avoid discomfort or potential side effects their infant may experience. Recommendation from trusted HCPs, access to clear information from credible sources, and accessible and trusted administration settings are critical to supporting immunization acceptance. These insights can inform future implementation of a comprehensive rollout of an equitable preventative immunization program, reducing the risk of severe infant RSV disease.

articles.title: The importance of RSV vaccination for at-risk adults aged 18-59: An expert opinion with an Italian perspective.
articles.abstract: This expert opinion reviews the burden of RSV in at-risk adults aged 18-59 years and summarizes available evidence to provide expert considerations that may inform prevention strategies. Adults with comorbidities or immunocompromise frequently experience severe RSV infection, with annual and seasonal rates of 37.6 per 1000 persons/year and 28.4 per 1000 persons/season, respectively. Clinical presentation ranges from being asymptomatic through to acute respiratory distress, with 6.5-32.8% at-risk adults requiring hospitalization for RSV disease. Three preventative vaccines (RSVpreF, mRNA-1345, RSVPreF3) are currently approved in Europe for adults ≥18 years and in the United States for adults ≥60 years and 18-59 years at increased risk. The panel supports RSV vaccination in adults 18-59 years with severe forms of immunocompromise, respiratory disease, cardiovascular disease, neurological/neuromuscular disease, or renal disease. Higher vaccination rates in this population can be achieved by enhancing awareness, empowering health-care professionals, developing consistent policies, and improving access.

articles.title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.
STUDY DESIGN: In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.
RESULTS: Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420261355711.

articles.title: Efficacy of a nurse-facilitated mindfulness-based management program on severity of childhood cancer symptom cluster-leukemia in adolescents with leukemia receiving chemotherapy: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the efficacy of a mindfulness-based symptom cluster management program on CCSC-L severity and HRQoL.
METHODS: A two-arm multicenter randomized controlled trial with repeated outcome measurements was conducted among 60 adolescents receiving induction chemotherapy at three tertiary hospitals in Thailand. Participants were stratified by hospital and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either the program based on the Individual and Family Self-Management Theory plus usual care or usual care alone. The symptom cluster severity was assessed immediately after completion of the four-week structured intervention and at Weeks 4 and 8, and HRQoL at Week 12. Linear mixed-effects models and between-group comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant group × time interaction for overall symptom cluster severity (p < .001). Compared with usual care, adolescents receiving the intervention demonstrated significantly lower overall symptom cluster severity at Week 4 (model-estimated mean difference = -0.90) and Week 8 (model-estimated mean difference = -1.63). Significant between-group differences favoring the intervention were observed across all five symptoms at both assessments (all unadjusted p ≤ .001). At Week 12, the complete-case analysis (intervention, n = 30; control, n = 28) showed higher overall HRQoL in the intervention group (mean difference = 11.59, 95% CI [8.56,14.62], unadjusted p < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: The program reduced symptom cluster severity and improved HRQoL. These findings suggest that the intervention could be considered for integration into routine pediatric oncology nursing practice in similar clinical settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20250608004); prospectively registered on 8 June 2025, before the first participant was enrolled on 20 June 2025.

articles.title: A completely unpredictable life - parents' lived experiences of transitioning between hospital and home in paediatric oncology.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hospital-to-home transitions are critical for continuity and safety in childhood cancer care, but little is known about how parents experience them in the context of everyday family life. This study explored parents' lived experiences of the transition between a paediatric oncology centre and home during their child's cancer treatment.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve parents of children receiving active treatment at a single Danish paediatric oncology centre. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using a phenomenological-hermeneutic approach inspired by Paul Ricoeur, comprising naïve understanding, structural analysis, and comprehensive interpretation. Data management was supported by NVivo QSR.
RESULTS: Three themes described parents' experiences of transitions. First, everyday rhythms were disrupted, producing instability and unpredictability in family life. Second, responsibility shifted from professionals to parents, who undertook complex care tasks while questioning their competence. Third, parents experienced emotional vulnerability and strain, balancing exhaustion, uncertainty, and guilt with the need to remain strong. These findings demonstrate that transitions extend beyond logistical movement and encompass temporal, practical, and existential challenges.
CONCLUSION: Hospital-to-home transitions, embedded in the ongoing lives of families during childhood cancer treatment, require parents to sustain care and family life across changing settings and conditions. Transitional care should incorporate structured follow-up, assessment of family readiness, and support that is more responsive to families' needs throughout treatment.

articles.title: Do You See Me How I See Myself-and Does It Matter? Parent-Child Agreement on Symptom Ratings after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Its Association with Recovery: An A-CAP Study.
articles.abstract: Current methods for diagnosing and monitoring recovery of pediatric mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) rely heavily on both self-report and parent-proxy symptom inventories. Yet little is known about parent-child agreement and the clinical relevance of (dis)agreement on symptom inventories commonly used in pediatric mTBI. The current study thus aimed to (1) quantify parent-child agreement on an mTBI symptom inventory; (2) investigate which sociodemographic, clinical, psychosocial, and study-related factors are associated with agreement; and (3) finally explore whether early parent-child difference in symptom report is associated with symptom reporting over time. We conducted a secondary analysis of data collected from the Advancing Concussion Assessment in Pediatrics (A-CAP) study, a large-scale prospective longitudinal cohort study. Participants were children between ages 8 and 16.99 years with mTBI (n = 633) or orthopedic injury (OI; n = 334). Parent-child dyads completed symptom ratings using the Health and Behavior Inventory (HBI; cognitive and somatic symptom subscales) weekly or biweekly over the first 6 months post-injury and completed a series of questionnaires assessing sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial variables. Parent-child agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman (BA) plots. Two ordinary least squares linear regression models were used to assess factors associated with parent-child directional differences (i.e., parent minus child rating scores) on cognitive and somatic ratings. To investigate whether parent-child directional differences were associated with symptom trajectories, four generalized least squares models were used, with parent-reported cognitive and somatic and child-reported cognitive and somatic symptoms as the outcomes. Parent-child agreement was moderate for both cognitive (ICC = 0.67) and somatic (ICC = 0.65) symptoms. Visual inspection of BA plots showed somewhat better agreement for somatic symptoms. Number of days post-injury, sex, race, and parent-reported pre-injury report of symptoms, but not group (mTBI vs OI), were associated with cognitive and somatic parent-child difference scores. Parent-child differences early after injury were associated with both parent (χ2(3) = 38.11, p < 0.001) and child (χ2(3) = 27.16, p < 0.001) cognitive and parent (χ2(3) = 11.11, p = 0.011) and child (χ2(3) = 42.36, p < 0.001) somatic symptom trajectories. Parent-child agreement on the HBI is consistent with the broader psychopathology and health literature. Factors such as time since injury, sex, race, and pre-injury symptoms may be particularly important for understanding parent-child agreement on the HBI. Early disagreement, especially for cognitive symptoms, was relevant to later recovery trajectories, with dyads "coming together" over time. Findings highlight the importance of multi-informant assessment after mTBI.

articles.title: Substance use and recovery in the perinatal period: A cracked window of opportunity?
articles.abstract: Pregnancy and early parenthood are increasingly framed as a 'window of opportunity' for engaging women with substance use (SU) problems in treatment and recovery. Yet, when support becomes organized around the perinatal period and child, important questions arise regarding how recovery is understood and sustained. This qualitative study explored which factors shape women's trajectories of SU and recovery, and the role of the perinatal period and child within these processes. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 mothers in Flanders (Belgium) who initiated recovery during pregnancy or early parenthood, and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Findings indicate that women's trajectories were embedded in longstanding experiences of childhood adversity, mental health problems, and relational vulnerability. Both intimate relationships and SU frequently functioned as ways of coping with distress and unmet relational needs. Against this background, the child emerges as an ambivalent subject at the personal level, in intimate relationships, in family relations, and in recovery and care trajectories. While the child often provided meaning, hope, and motivation for change, women also projected expectations of connection, security, stability, and recovery onto the child. The findings suggest that emotional and relational needs previously sought through intimate relationships and SU were often reorganized around the child. Care practices may unintentionally reinforce this when treatment engagement becomes closely linked to child welfare and the prevention of child removal. The perinatal period may therefore be better understood as a 'cracked window of opportunity': while it can facilitate treatment engagement, overemphasizing the child as the primary catalyst for change, without simultaneously addressing underlying relational and trauma-related vulnerabilities, may contribute to the intergenerational transmission of relational vulnerability. Sustainable recovery requires additional trauma-informed, systemic, and life course-oriented care that attends to women's relational histories, supports them in developing and maintaining safe relationships, and extends from preconception to well beyond the perinatal period.

articles.title: A computational report on Fibrocystin structure via AlphaFold2: considerations and limitations for ARPKD research.
articles.abstract: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) is a rare, genetic disease that often occurs during early childhood and can be lethal at its most severe presentation. ARPKD is caused by biallelic variants in PKHD1 which encodes Fibrocystin, a large receptor protein. The disease presentation and progression of ARPKD is highly variable, the reason for this is currently unknown. To address this, AlphaFold2 was employed to generate a model of Fibrocystin which was used to establish spatial relationships between compound heterozygous pairs in ARPKD patients. AlphaFold2 was used to generate a model of full-length human Fibrocystin which was assessed for structural similarities to known protein structures. Compound heterozygous variant pairs and disease outcomes were acquired from previously published work and annotated onto the three-dimensional Fibrocystin model to identify spatial relationships. AlphaFold2 predicted the full-length of Fibrocystin with varying confidence. Globally, average modelling confidence was low, with more confident modelling around the G8 and PBH1 domains. Confidence was lowest around the transmembrane region and intracellular tail, which modelled poorly. FoldSeek identified structural similarities to other proteins; however, these had similar structures to those already predicted present in Fibrocystin. No new structural elements were detected. Spatial relationships between compound heterozygous variants did not correlate with disease outcomes. There are limitations to AlphaFold2 which limits its ability to accurately model a protein like Fibrocystin. These limitations may hinder the tools application in determining genotype-phenotype relationships in ARPKD. Currently, Fibrocystin models produced by AlphaFold2 are unable to identify genotype-phenotype relationships.

articles.title: Neonatal oxytocin administration restores impaired ultrasonic vocalizations in a mouse model of 3q29 deletion syndrome.
articles.abstract: The 3q29 microdeletion is a highly penetrant genetic risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. Although adult mouse models (Df/+) with this deletion exhibit robust social deficits, their early developmental trajectories are unknown. Here, we investigated neonatal communicative behaviors and the underlying oxytocin (OXT) system in Df/+ pups. On postnatal day 7, Df/+ pups emitted significantly fewer isolation-induced ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) than did their wild-type littermates. This behavioral deficit was accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of oxytocinergic neurons within the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus, as identified by Neurophysin 1 and OXT immunoreactivities. Notably, acute exogenous OXT restored the impaired USVs to normal levels, whereas arginine vasopressin did not. Furthermore, the baseline OXT receptor expression remained unaltered. These findings suggest that a deficiency in endogenous OXT, rather than receptor dysfunction, may drive impaired USVs in this model. As the early OXT system is essential for the maturation of social circuits, our results suggest that the neonatal period is a critical developmental window. Deficient OXT signaling during this specific stage may fundamentally alter the developmental trajectory of patients with ASD.

articles.title: Neuroimmune-endocrine interactions in perinatal asphyxia: from brain injury to neuroprotection.
articles.abstract: Perinatal asphyxia (PA) remains a major cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability worldwide. Although hypoxic-ischemic brain injury has traditionally been attributed to oxygen deprivation, excitotoxicity, and oxidative stress, accumulating evidence indicates that neurological outcomes are determined by complex interactions among metabolic, mitochondrial, neuroimmune, and neuroendocrine mechanisms. Following hypoxic-ischemic injury, primary energy failure rapidly triggers excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium dysregulation, and oxidative damage, leading to activation of microglia and astrocytes, release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, disruption of blood-brain barrier integrity, and recruitment of peripheral immune cells. These events contribute to the development of secondary energy failure and persistent neuroinflammation. Simultaneously, activation of hypoxia-responsive pathways, including hypoxia-inducible factor-1 (HIF-1), heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), glutathione-dependent antioxidant defenses, and neuroendocrine stress responses involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, promote endogenous adaptation and neuroprotection. Nitric oxide signaling further links mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrosative stress, inflammatory activation, and neuronal injury. Together, these mechanisms form an integrated neuroimmune-endocrine network that influences both injury progression and tissue repair. In this review, we propose Brain Energy Failure as a unifying conceptual framework linking mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrosative stress, neuroinflammation, endocrine adaptation, and endogenous neuroprotective responses following perinatal hypoxia. We further discuss the role of biomarkers associated with neuro-immuno-endocrine dysfunction, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress markers, endocrine factors, and indicators of neuronal and glial injury. Recent evidence has highlighted the therapeutic potential of multimodal neuroprotective approaches, including endogenous lipid mediators such as palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), which exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and mitoprotective effects. We also review current and emerging neuroprotective strategies targeting mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and bioenergetic instability, and discuss their translational implications. Understanding the interactions among these interconnected pathways may facilitate biomarker-guided diagnosis, personalized neuroprotection, and the development of more effective therapies aimed at improving long-term neurological outcomes following perinatal asphyxia.

articles.title: Fertility Treatment with Ovulation Induction or Intrauterine Insemination and the Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Offspring.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination and cerebral palsy in offspring, and to examine the potential mechanisms underlying an association, including specific treatment regimens, mediation by preterm birth, confounding by indication, and the association with specific subtypes of cerebral palsy.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study included all liveborn, singleton children in Denmark conceived from July 1995 and born before January 2017. The children were followed until March 2022. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination were identified from redeemed prescriptions for the specific hormones used for these treatments, recorded in the Danish National Prescription Registry. Children with cerebral palsy were identified from the Danish Cerebral Palsy Registry and the Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-up Program.
RESULTS: The study included 1,231,058 singleton children; 47,017 children were conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination, and 2,104 children were diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination had an increased risk of cerebral palsy compared to spontaneously conceived children (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.36; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.66). The point estimate remained similar in a sibling analysis. The risk was primarily related to the use of clomiphene citrate (aOR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.16-1.80). A mediation analysis showed that most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors (proportion eliminated: 87%; 95% CI: 36-137%). In line with this, the risk was highest for spastic bilateral cerebral palsy (aOR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.33-2.34), severe motor impairment (aOR: 1.66; 95% CI: 1.17-2.35), and for cerebral white matter lesions (aOR: 1.70; 95% CI: 1.24-2.33).
CONCLUSION: Ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination was associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in offspring. The risk was related to treatment with clomiphene citrate, and most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors.

articles.title: Neuro-adaptive predictive control for upper-limb rehabilitation using EMG and intention-aware assistance.
articles.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairments associated with neurological disorders such as cerebral palsy (CP) are characterized by abnormal muscle coordination, spasticity, fatigue, and highly variable electromyographic (EMG) patterns, posing significant challenges for rehabilitation exoskeleton control.
