OBJECTIVES: To analyze age distribution pattern, evolution trend and variations over time of hand foot and mouth disease(HFMD) incidence rate, in Dalian city, from 2009 to 2024.
METHODS: HFMD case data in Dalian from 2009 to 2024 were collected. Joinpoint regression was used to analyze trend in incidence rates as age increases among children aged 0-14 years across three periods, and an age-period-cohort (APC) model was constructed to assess effects of age, period, and birth cohort.
RESULTS: 1)From 2009 to 2024, there were 110117 HFMD cases reported in Dalian. (2)Age group 0-4 years consistently had highest annual incidence of HFMD, since 2023, proportion of cases in age group 10-14 years has increased. (3)Joinpoint regression analysis showed that during 2009-2019, HFMD incidence decreased significantly with increasing age in most age-sex groups.Except for 2023-2024 for female, age-specific trends was significant heterogeneity. (4) APC analysis showed that net drift test was statistically significant, with an estimated net drift of -6.848%(95%CI: -13.097%~-0.15%)and - 8.739%༈95%CI༚-14.208%~-2.921%༉respectively in males and females. The Cohort RR curve showed that, rate ratio of 2016-2020 birth cohort were 0.182 (95% CI:0.098-0.337) and 0.17 (95% CI:0.1-0.289)) respectively in males and females.For male, The local drift values in the age group 0-4 years,5-9 years and 10-14 years were - 15.681%(95% CI:-20.736%--10.304%༉, -5.401%༈95% CI:-12.158%-1.874%༉ and 1.335%༈95% CI:-15.137%-21.006%༉per year of age respectively, that for female were - 16.232% ༈95% CI:-20.569%--11.659%༉, -7.377%༈95% CI:-13.378%--0.961%༉ and - 2.037%༈95% CI:-6.179%-14.491%༉per year of age respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Since 2023, the proportion of HFMD cases in age group 10-14 years increased, likely driven more by declining cases in 0-4 years children than by increased in risk among age groups 10-14 years. Significant age-period‑cohort effects were observed in both sexes, with the 2016-2020 birth cohort having the lowest risk, but these findings are exploratory due to APC analysis limitations and require further validation.

articles.title: Cysticercosis-related benefits in Brazil: an epidemiological analysis of National Institute of Social Security data (2012-2024).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the sociodemographic, social security, and spatiotemporal patterns of benefits granted for cysticercosis (ICD-10 B69) in Brazil between 2012 and 2024, and to explore the potential contribution of social security databases as complementary sources for disease surveillance.
METHODS: A population-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using retrospective secondary data from the Brazilian National Social Security Institute (INSS) from January 2012 to December 2024. Benefits granted with a primary diagnosis of cysticercosis (ICD-10 codes B69, B69.0, B69.1, and B69.8) were included. Variables analyzed included benefit type, beneficiary demographics, insurance category, residence area, geographic distribution, and initial monthly income. Spatial-temporal clusters were identified using a discrete Poisson model.
RESULTS: A total of 2,313 benefits were granted. Sickness aid/Temporary Incapacity Aid accounted for 84.14% of concessions, followed by disability retirement (8.43%). Beneficiaries were predominantly male (63.20%), urban residents (82.60%), and aged 30-50 years. Most individuals received low-income benefits, with 51.36% earning one minimum wage. Concessions were concentrated in the Southeast and South regions, particularly in São Paulo (18.29%) and Minas Gerais (15.00%). A decline in concessions was observed between 2019 and 2022, followed by a slight increase in 2023-2024. Two significant high-risk spatial-temporal clusters were identified (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Cysticercosis imposes a measurable burden on social protection systems through work disability. Social security administrative data may complement traditional surveillance strategies, supporting targeted intersectoral policies to address regional disparities in diagnosis, access to care, and social protection.

articles.title: Immune response and durability of human papillomavirus antibodies in vaccinated adolescents after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), preceded by chemotherapy and/or total body irradiation, eradicates hematopoietic cells, including vaccine-primed memory cells. Revaccination is therefore required after HSCT. Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is particularly important in this population because of the increased risk of HPV-associated anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. While the World Health Organization (WHO) currently recommends a single HPV vaccine dose for immunocompetent adolescents, 3 doses are recommended for immunocompromised individuals.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the immunogenicity of HPV vaccination in adolescents following HSCT.
METHODS: Two cohorts were studied. Cohort 1 was a quasi-experimental study assessing seroconversion after a 2-dose schedule of HPV vaccination in post-HSCT adolescents aged 9-15 years. Eligible participants were ≥ 1 year post-HSCT and had discontinued immunosuppressive therapy for ≥ 6 months. Participants received 2-dose quadrivalent HPV (qHPV) vaccine at 0 and 6 months. Anti-HPV16 L1 IgG and anti-HPV18 L1 IgG levels were measured 6 months after the first dose and 1 month after the second dose. Cohort 2 was a cross-sectional study evaluating the persistence of anti-HPV16 and anti-HPV18 antibodies in vaccinated post-HSCT adolescents at varying intervals after completion of the vaccination series.
RESULTS: Twenty-three participants were enrolled in Cohort 1. Six months after the first vaccine dose, the proportions who seroconverted were 54.5% for HPV 16 and 68.2% for HPV 18. One month after the second dose, the proportions who seroconverted increased to 95.5% for HPV 16 and 90.9% for HPV 18. Local adverse events occurred in 22-39% of participants within 48 h after vaccination, whereas systemic adverse events were infrequent. No serious adverse events were observed. In Cohort 2, 15 participants were included. The interval since the last vaccine dose ranged from 6 to 62 months. All participants had detectable antibodies against HPV16, and all but one had detectable antibodies against HPV18.
CONCLUSION: The findings from this pilot study provide preliminary evidence that a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule may induce a better antibody response in adolescents after HSCT; however, further studies with larger sample sizes and serial assessment of antibody titers are needed to determine the optimal dosing strategy and long-term durability of immunity.

articles.title: Bacterial isolates and antimicrobial resistance patterns in ear infections: a multicenter study from medical laboratories in Sana'a, Yemen.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ear infections are a major public health concern globally, with a disproportionate burden in low and middle-income countries.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the bacterial profile, antimicrobial susceptibility, and age- and gender-related patterns of ear infections in patients attending multiple laboratories and hospitals in Sana'a, Yemen.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2022 to December 2023 in Sana'a, Yemen. Data were collected from four medical laboratories and two referral hospitals. Ear discharge samples from 313 patients were cultured, and bacterial isolates were identified using standard microbiological techniques. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the KirbyBauer disk diffusion method, and results were interpreted according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. Statistical analysis was carried out using SPSS v22.
RESULTS: Of the 313 patients, 271 (86.6%) had positive bacterial cultures. The majority of infections occurred in males (50.2%) and in the 21-30year age group. Staphylococcus aureus (54.6%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (15.9%) were the most frequently isolated organisms. High levels of resistance were observed to amoxicillin (96.8%), cefoxitin (70.3%), and amoxiclavulanic acid (58.6%). In contrast, clindamycin (83.5%), ofloxacin (75.6%), and levofloxacin (70.5%) demonstrated higher sensitivity. Overall, 48.8% of the 2,644 antibiotic susceptibility tests performed showed resistance.
CONCLUSION: This study found a significant prevalence of bacterial ear infections in Sana'a, Yemen, along with widespread resistance to routinely used medicines, particularly beta lactams. The prevalence of S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, as well as the reported resistance trends, point out the critical need for local antimicrobial stewardship programs. Regular surveillance and updated empirical treatment guidelines are critical for slowing the spread of AMR and improving clinical outcomes in the region.

articles.title: A nationally representative One Health multi-pathogen serosurvey in Cambodia: study protocol for the RACSMEI mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cambodia faces a high and complex burden of zoonotic, vector-borne, vaccine-preventable and environmentally transmitted infections, driven by intensive human-animal-environment interactions. However, nationally representative data integrating human, animal and environmental dimensions of pathogen exposure remain limited. The RACSMEI (Risk Assessment of Community Spread of Multiple Endemic Infectious Diseases in a One Health Perspective) study aims to address this gap through a nationwide One Health serosurvey designed to generate policy-relevant epidemiological evidence for precision public health and integrated surveillance.
METHODS/DESIGN: RACSMEI is a nationwide, cross-sectional, mixed-methods study conducted across all 25 provinces of Cambodia. Using a stratified, multi-stage cluster sampling design, approximately 15,000 individuals aged 2-75 years will be enrolled from 4,160 households in 104 randomly selected villages. Human, animal (poultry, pigs, dogs, cattle, small ruminants, rodents) and environmental (water, soil, air, surface swabs) samples will be collected. Exposure to more than 50 endemic, emerging, vaccine-preventable and elimination-targeted pathogens will be assessed using multiplex serological assays, molecular diagnostics and metagenomics sequencing approaches. Quantitative surveys will be complemented by semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions to explore social, behavioural and health system determinants of infection risk and care-seeking behaviours. Analyses will account for the complex survey design and integrate epidemiological, environmental and social science data.
DISCUSSION: By combining nationally representative sampling with integrated human, animal, environmental and social science data, RACSMEI aims to generate comprehensive evidence on infectious disease exposure and transmission risks across diverse socio-ecological contexts in Cambodia. The study will provide policy-relevant insights to support One Health surveillance strategies and targeted public health interventions. The protocol was approved by the Cambodian National Ethics Committee for Health Research and the Institutional Review Board of Institut Pasteur Paris.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07358910). It was retrospectively registered on 14 January 2026.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a clinical score with a rapid diagnostic test for enteric fever in Nepal, Bangladesh and Cambodia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distinguishing enteric (typhoid and paratyphoid) fever from other causes of fever is challenging. The diagnostic accuracy of Typhoid Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDT) are suboptimal but might improve if combined with a clinical score. We aimed to develop a clinical score, incorporating a point of care C-reactive protein (CRP) and Typhoid RDT, that could be used for febrile patients attending a health facility with limited laboratory capability, to identify those suitable for further investigations such as a blood culture, an empirical antimicrobial choice that covers enteric fever, or to rule out enteric fever as a likely diagnosis.
METHODS: Overall, 1168 Bangladeshi, Cambodian and Nepali children and adults attending hospital with fever were randomly split (80:20) into derivation and validation cohorts. There were 208/1168 (18%) with blood-culture-confirmed enteric fever. In the derivation cohort we studied the association of symptoms, signs, CRP, laboratory results, and the Test-it™ typhoid IgM RDT with blood culture confirmed enteric fever using logistic regression and developed several clinical scores. We determined the diagnostic accuracy of the clinical scores in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: The Typhoid RDT had a sensitivity of 63% and specificity 73% in the validation cohort. A basic clinical score including fever ≥ 3 days, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, absence of cough, and CRP ≥ 10 mg/L had a sensitivity of 80% and specificity 56%. Adding the Typhoid RDT result to the clinical score resulted in a sensitivity of 87%, a specificity of 58%, a PPV of 34%, and a NPV of 95%.
CONCLUSIONS: The diagnostic accuracy of a Typhoid RDT was only marginally improved by combining with a clinical score. Enteric fever was very unlikely with a negative clinical score.

articles.title: Pooling poo for Strongyloides PCR screening in communities in South-eastern Ghana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strongyloidiasis, caused by Strongyloides spp., is a neglected tropical disease with significant but underreported public health impact. In Ghana, particularly in the Volta and Oti regions, data on prevalence is limited due to inadequate surveillance and low sensitivity diagnostics.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed 1,392 archived human stool samples from seven communities across three districts (Adaklu, Hohoe, Nkwanta North). Samples were pooled (up to 10 samples per pool) for DNA extraction and PCR targeting the 18 S rRNA gene. Samples from positive pools were tested individually.
RESULTS: Overall pooled prevalence was 7.2% (95% CI: 5.5-9.3), while individual prevalence was 18.5% (95% CI: 16.5-20.6), with notable variation across communities. Lancha (27.9%) and Dawanu (27.4%) showed the highest rates. Logistic regression found no significant associations with sex, age, or district.
CONCLUSION: The pooling strategy proved sensitive and resource efficient, supporting its use in Strongyloidiasis surveillance, despite underestimating the prevalence of infection. This study highlights the need for sensitive diagnostics and integrated surveillance to guide targeted public health interventions.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, etiology, and treatment strategies for renal and perinephric abscesses in adults: a single-center, descriptive, 10-year retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, etiology, and antimicrobial resistance patterns of renal abscesses (RAs) and perinephric abscesses (PNAs) in adults and to analyze the associated treatment outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 40 adults who were diagnosed with RAs or PNAs at our institution between October 2014 and December 2024. The data collected included demographics, risk factors, clinical presentations, laboratory/imaging findings, microbiology, treatment modalities, and outcomes.
RESULTS: The median age of the patients was 51 years (IQR: 38-63 years; range, 18-84 years), with a male-to-female ratio of 1:2.1. Diabetes mellitus (50%) and urinary tract calculi (35%) were the most common risk factors. The predominant clinical manifestations included fever (72.5%), chills (37.5%), and flank pain (35%). Laboratory findings frequently revealed leukocytosis (87.5%), markedly elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) (median, 174 mg/L; IQR: 124.5-214.5 mg/L), and elevated procalcitonin (67.5%). Escherichia coli (E. coli) was the predominant pathogen, identified in 28 out of 39 positive cultures (71.8%), with a high proportion (53.57%) being extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producers.Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) was the most frequently used and clinically most useful diagnostic tool, establishing or strongly supporting the diagnosis in 62.5% of patients. Treatment included antibiotics alone (55%), antibiotics combined with drainage (42.5%), and nephrectomy (2.5%). All patients showed clinical improvement at discharge after a median hospital stay of 12 days (IQR: 8-16 days). During follow-up among the 30 patients who had regular outpatient visits, 83.33% (25/30) experienced resolved infections, whereas 16.67% (5/30) experienced recurrence. The outcomes for the remaining 10 patients who did not complete regular follow-up were not captured.
CONCLUSIONS: RAs and PNAs often present with nonspecific symptoms, underscoring the importance of early diagnosis and management. Diabetes is a major risk factor, and infections are predominantly caused by highly resistant E. coli. Contrast-enhanced CT is essential for diagnosis, but combination antibiotic and drainage therapy effectively improves patient prognosis. Optimizing antibiotic selection and intervention timing should be future priorities.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Assessing the association between compliance to intensive adherence counselling and viral suppression among children and adolescents living with HIV in Karamoja sub region, Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viral load suppression (VLS) among children and adolescents living with HIV (CALHIV) remains below the 95% target in many settings; in Uganda, only about 60% of CALHIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) are suppressed. Intensive adherence counselling (IAC) is recommended for non-suppressed patients, but evidence on its effectiveness in pastoralist, resource-limited settings such as Karamoja is limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study had two complementary objectives. The quantitative objective was to assess the association between compliance to IAC and viral load suppression among CALHIV at ART-accredited health facilities in Karamoja sub region, Uganda. The qualitative objective was to explore the perceived barriers and facilitators to completing IAC in the same setting.
METHODS: This mixed-methods cohort study combined retrospective chart review with key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs), conducted across 36 ART-accredited Karamoja facilities (January-December 2023; data abstracted January-March 2024). All eligible CALHIV aged 0-19 years with a documented high viral load (> 200 copies/mL plasma; >400 copies/mL dried blood spot, DBS) who were initiated on IAC were enrolled. Compliance to IAC was defined, using session-attendance records, as receipt of three or more consecutive monthly sessions. Modified Poisson regression was used to estimate the association between IAC compliance and viral load suppression, reported as crude and adjusted prevalence risk ratios (PRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Thematic analysis of the KIIs and FGDs was used to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to completing IAC.
RESULTS: Of the CALHIV assessed for eligibility, 154 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. Participants' mean age was 12.0 years (SD 4.2); 53.2% were female; mean ART duration was 12.3 months. Most (83.8%, n = 129) received three or more sessions. Suppression reached 41.1% (n = 53) among compliant versus 8.0% (n = 2) of non-compliant participants (crude PRR 5.14, 95% CI 1.34-19.72, p = 0.0016). After adjustment for facility level, age, ART duration, and HIV disclosure status, compliance to IAC remained independently associated with suppression (adjusted PRR 4.78, 95% CI 1.26-18.10, p = 0.021); the hospital-level association attenuated and was no longer significant (adjusted PRR 3.30, 95% CI 0.91-12.04, p = 0.071). Both confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small non-compliant group, so the magnitude of the effect should be interpreted with caution. Qualitative analysis identified perceived barriers (food insecurity, caregiver alcohol use, boarding-school attendance) and facilitators (caregiver meetings, peer support) to completing IAC, alongside perceptions of IAC effectiveness, health-system readiness for delivery, and improved quality of life.
CONCLUSIONS: Compliant CALHIV were more likely to achieve suppression than non-compliant CALHIV, although the wide confidence interval means the size of this association is uncertain; 58.9% of compliant participants nonetheless remained non-suppressed. IAC is necessary but insufficient; complementary interventions addressing structural barriers and clinical factors including drug resistance screening are required.

articles.title: Development and validation of a decision tree model to distinguish bacterial meningitis from viral meningitis and/or encephalitis in children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early differentiation between bacterial meningitis (BM) and viral meningitis and/or encephalitis (VM/E) in children remains challenging due to overlapping clinical features and limited availability of rapid aetiological diagnosis. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable decision tree model based on routinely available variables for early discrimination between BM and VM/E.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study in which paediatric patients were classified as BM or VM/E according to predefined criteria. Candidate variables were first identified through univariate analysis and subsequently incorporated into a decision tree model. Model performance was evaluated in both the training and test sets.
RESULTS: A total of 149 children were included, comprising 94 (63.09%) BM and 55 (36.91%) VM/E cases. The decision-tree model included three predictors, with procalcitonin (PCT) as the primary splitting variable, followed by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein and C-reactive protein (CRP). In the training set, the model demonstrated excellent performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.979 (95% CI: 0.912-0.994), sensitivity of 96.97%, and specificity of 97.44%. In the test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.753 (95% CI: 0.622-0.885), with sensitivity of 82.14% and specificity of 68.75%. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was frequently initiated prior to definitive diagnosis, with a substantial proportion of patients with VM/E receiving antibacterial treatment and some patients with BM receiving antiviral therapy.
CONCLUSION: We developed an interpretable and parsimonious decision-tree model based on routinely available clinical variables for early differentiation between BM and VM/E in children. This model may serve as a practical tool for early clinical assessment before microbiological confirmation.

articles.title: Comparison of diarrheagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes in diarrheic and non-diarrheic under-five children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diarrhea remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in under-five children (UFC). Diarrheagenic Escherichia coli (DEC) is associated with UFC diarrhea. Clear diagnosis of DEC is limited due to shared virulence genes with non-pathogenic strains. The study aimed to assess if or whether DEC is more associated with diarrheic than non-diarrheic UFC.
METHODS: The updated PRISMA guideline was followed for this systematic review and meta-analysis. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261294236). The aim of the study was to assess the role of DEC pathotypes in diarrhea of UFC globally. Major databases using predetermined criteria were used to identify relevant articles and managed by EndNote. The statistical analysis was done using STATA 17.0. Pooled effect (Log (OR), heterogeneity evaluation, and publication bias were done. Cumulative meta-analysis with prediction intervals was also done.
RESULTS: A total of 15 studies involving 15,815 participants (7,849 diarrhea cases and 7,766 controls) were included in this review. EIEC was significantly associated with UFC diarrhea (OR = 1.54 with 95% CI: 1.02-2.32) in the present study. EAEC, EPEC, ETEC, and STEC showed positive association but largely were non-significant. Minimal effect (OR = 0.96), heterogeneity (I² = 88%), and wide prediction intervals (PI) was for EAEC revealing variable impacts across populations. EPEC (OR = 1.11), STEC (OR = 1.11), and ETEC (OR = 1.25) showed non-significant association with moderate to high heterogeneity. Context-specific association was seen for all the DEC pathotypes in the subgroup analysis. The heterogeneity and inconsistent finding could be due to variation in publication year, geographic location, detection methods, and virulence gene targets.
CONCLUSION: Only EIEC was significantly and consistently associated with UFC diarrhea. Strengthened surveillance system and the implementation of targeted diagnostic methods are strongly recommended.

articles.title: Global paediatric drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance after the removal of age-disaggregated WHO reporting fields: a cross-national analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) is one of the most poorly documented dimensions of the global TB epidemic. In 2020, the World Health Organization removed age-disaggregated rifampicin-resistant TB (RR-TB) fields from its standard reporting format. No country has since resubmitted these fields to WHO, although some may continue to collect paediatric age-disaggregation through national or sub-national systems that are not reflected in the global dataset. This study analyses 2017-2019, the only three years for which age-disaggregated data exist in the WHO database, to quantify what has been lost from routine global surveillance and to inform discussion of reinstating standardized age-disaggregated reporting.
METHODS: We analysed WHO drug resistance surveillance data for 215 countries and territories over 2017-2019. Generalised estimating equations (GEE) with a Poisson family were used to describe year-on-year paediatric and adult notification patterns; because only three annual data points are available, these are descriptive comparisons rather than evidence of an underlying temporal trend, and no inferential trend claim is drawn from them. We constructed an Under-Reporting Index (URI) as a measure of each country's deviation from the reporting pattern of its own WHO region, not as a direct or externally validated measure of the true extent of under-reporting, to identify countries whose notified paediatric caseload deviates most from regional norms. A gradient-boosted ensemble trained on approximately 87 country observations was interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME); given the small sample size relative to the number of candidate predictors and the absence of an independent external validation dataset, the machine-learning component of this study is exploratory and hypothesis-generating throughout, and none of its outputs should be read as confirmatory or as demonstrating causal relationships.
RESULTS: Among 87 countries with any paediatric RR-TB data, 6,846 children under 15 were notified with RR-TB during 2017-2019. The global paediatric fraction rose from 1.82% in 2017 to 3.28% in 2018 before falling to 2.52% in 2019 (three-year mean: 2.54%; a descriptive pattern across three annual observations, not a statistically evaluated trend). Africa (3.64%) and South-East Asia (3.57%) carried the highest regional fractions. Notified paediatric counts fell well short of regional benchmarks in many countries: 209 country-years recorded zero paediatric RR-TB notifications despite non-zero adult caseloads. Among the exploratory machine-learning features, log-transformed total RR-TB burden had the largest mean absolute SHAP value (2.81; bootstrap 95% CI: 1.94-3.60), followed by retreatment fraction (1.17; 95% CI: 0.61-1.79); confidence intervals across features overlapped substantially, so these rankings are exploratory correlational associations from a small-sample model and should be read as directional and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive or causal.
CONCLUSIONS: Notified paediatric RR-TB fell well below regional reporting benchmarks before 2020, indicating a substantial gap between the paediatric and adult evidence base rather than establishing the true size of undetected paediatric disease. WHO's removal of age-disaggregated RR-TB fields from the standard reporting format that year has left a surveillance data gap that, as of this analysis, spans five consecutive years. Reinstating standardized age-stratified reporting, extending drug susceptibility testing to paediatric patients, and investing in community-based case-findingan approach supported by evidence from multiple African settings, not only the single country highlighted in our own data are among the actionable responses this descriptive and exploratory analysis can support.

articles.title: Nasal colonization and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of Staphylococcus aureus among healthcare workers at selected health institutions in Bahir Dar, Northwest Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a leading cause of healthcare- and community-acquired infections, ranging from mild skin conditions to severe systemic disease. Healthcare workers are frequently colonized, serving as potential reservoirs for transmission to patients, attendants, and colleagues. Nasal screening is a key strategy in controlling Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), yet data remain scarce in the study area. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of nasal colonization and the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of S. aureus among healthcare workers in selected health institutions in Bahir Dar, Northwest Ethiopia.
METHODS: An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted from April to July 2023 among 249 Healthcare workers. A systematic random sampling was employed to include study participants. The nasal samples were collected and processed following standard bacteriological procedures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using a disk diffusion method on Mueller Hinton Agar. Data were coded, entered, and analyzed using the SPSS version 27 statistical package. Logistic regression analysis was done to identify factors associated with nasal colonization by S. aureus and p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Colonization with S. aureus and MRSA was 15.7% (39/249) and 3.2% (8/249); respectively. From the S. aureus isolates, 20.5% (8/39) were MRSA. Of the S. aureus isolates, 82.1% (32/39) were resistant to Penicillin. About 30.8% isolates were multi-drug resistant (MDR). On the other hand, 89.7% (35/39) of the isolates were sensitive to Clindamycin, 89.7% (35/39) to Chloramphenicol, and 87.2% (34/39) to Ciprofloxacin. Infrequent hand-washing habits after patient contact (AOR = 6.770, 95% CI: 2.054-22.311; p = 0.002), Working in health center (AOR = 4.125, 95% CI: 1.390-12.245; p = 0.011) and frequent nose-picking habits (AOR = 3.378, 95% CI: 1.276-8.949; p = 0.014) were significantly associated with nasal colonization with S. aureus.
CONCLUSION: The nasal colonization rate of S. aureus and MRSA was lower than previous studies in the Amhara region. The isolates were relatively susceptible to Clindamycin, Chloramphenicol, and Ciprofloxacin. Infrequent hand-washing habits after patient contact, working in the health center and frequent nose-picking habits were significantly associated with nasal colonization with S. aureus. Hygienic activities should be practiced to prevent colonization and cross-transmission.

articles.title: Magnitude and longevity of antibody responses to key Plasmodium vivax Erythrocyte Binding-Like proteins in an amazonian cohort: a long-term follow-up study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plasmodium vivax, the second most common cause of malaria, remains a significant public health concern, with no vaccine approved to date. Although the DBL domain of Duffy binding protein (DBPII) is a leading blood-stage candidate, its extensive polymorphism, allele-specific immune responses, and low immunogenicity limit its effectiveness. In contrast, EBP2, a DBP homologue, emerges as a promising vaccine target due to its lower genetic variability and potential role in a distinct invasion pathway. Here, a long-term cohort of malaria-exposed individuals from the Amazon enabled the comparison of the magnitude and longevity of naturally acquired antibody responses to the DBL domains of EBP2 and DBP.
METHODS: A 15-years follow-up study was carried out among long-term P. vivax exposed Amazonian individuals (363, median age 36 years) and included 10 cross-sectional surveys at periods of high and low malaria transmission. The experimental approach focused on the longitudinal monitoring of IgG antibodies against the full DBL domains of EBP2 and DBP, as assessed by conventional serology (ELISA). Antibody durability was estimated by time to the first documented loss of seropositivity (Kaplan-Meier), while repeated serological measurements over follow-up (GLMM) identified factors associated with seropositivity.
RESULTS: Regardless of the malaria transmission period, IgG reactivity and seroprevalence were consistently higher for EBP2 than DBPII. EBP2-dominant IgG antibody profile was detected in 68-88% of individuals, compared to 9-30% for DBPII. The median time of the first loss of DBPII seropositivity was estimated at 72 months, with EBP2 seropositivity remained above 50% throughout the 180-month follow-up period. Although time living in the study area was associated with antibody response to both antigens, malaria infection - predominantly submicroscopic - was identified as an independent predictor of anti-EBP2 IgG seropositivity.
CONCLUSION: EBP2 induces more robust and long-lasting IgG antibody responses than DBPII, even in the absence of frequent reinfection-induced boosting. Further studies are warranted to determine the protective role of naturally acquired anti-EBP2 antibodies in the Amazonian population.

articles.title: Co-designing clinical decision support to enable proactive HPV vaccination in community pharmacies: a qualitative study using behavioral and implementation science theory and process frameworks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community pharmacies are accessible, acceptable venues to address suboptimal HPV vaccination among U.S. adolescents, especially in medically underserved populations. Yet awareness gaps, variable staff engagement, and workflow integration challenges limit uptake. We sought to identify and specify clinical decision support systems (CDSS)-operationalized as implementation strategies-to enable proactive delivery of HPV and other adolescent vaccines in pharmacies.
METHODS: From May-September 2023, we conducted eight virtual, audio-recorded focus group discussions with representatives of three Washington State independent pharmacies and two technology companies: PioneerRx (pharmacy software system) and STChealth (immunization information systems). The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05831540) on March 20, 2023. Semi-structured guides were informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research to elicit determinants across workflow steps mapped to the 5 A's Behavioral Counseling Framework (Assess, Advise, Agree, Assist, Arrange). Sessions (~ 60 min, biweekly) addressed: Immunization Information System (IIS) use; vaccination prompts; screening/consent integration; scheduling; reminder/recall; reporting; and population coverage assessment. We used a framework-guided rapid analysis approach to summarize barriers, facilitators, and recommendations. We catalogued proposed CDSS changes in a modified Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications to Evidence-based Implementation Strategies (FRAME-IS) matrix. Technology company readiness to develop/deploy proposed CDSS was captured at study close.
RESULTS: We identified nine priority pharmacy staff behaviors required for a proactive vaccination workflow and specified 19 CDSS to support these vaccination behaviors. Proposed tools included vaccine coverage dashboards, predictive inventory management, expanded health-information fields, tailored provider/patient prompts, digital screening/consent, documentation of refusal/delay, streamlined access to vaccination records, and integrated scheduling and reminder/recall. Technology companies indicated near-term feasibility for a subset of proposed CDSS: PioneerRx deemed 8/11 proposed tools were ready for implementation and 4/11 potentially feasible but not immediately available; STChealth committed to training on 2/8 CDSS with others outside short-term development scope. Tools were explicitly linked to targeted, operationalized implementation outcomes (e.g., adoption, feasibility, fidelity, reach) to support future evaluation.
CONCLUSIONS: Co-designing and refining CDSS within community pharmacy systems appears promising for shifting vaccination workflows from reactive to proactive, thereby reducing missed opportunities for HPV and other adolescent vaccinations. By coupling tool specifications to behavior targets and implementation outcomes, this formative work delivers turnkey strategies for subsequent hybrid implementation-effectiveness studies.

articles.title: A high-throughput rotavirus neutralization assay quantifies antibody responses beyond serum IgA in human infants.
articles.abstract: Rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe childhood gastroenteritis worldwide, yet the immune correlates of protection have been challenging to define. Here, we present an updated, high-throughput fluorescent imaging-based assay to quantify neutralization of rotavirus by antibodies prior to virus entry into cells. This methodology enables sensitive and reproducible assessment of rotavirus-specific antibody function in clinical samples within 24 h. By coupling fluorescent-focus detection after a single round of viral replication with automated multi-channel high-content imaging and cell-counting pipelines, this methodology significantly increases throughput, accuracy and cellular quality control compared to traditional neutralizing ELISAs (nELISAs). We also verified that widely accessible fluorescent ELISpot plate readers can accurately quantify fluorescent foci, expanding the potential availability of this methodology. We validated the technical performance and practical utility of this assay using 142 archived serum samples from a clinical trial cohort of Zambian infants vaccinated with either oral Rotarix (G1P[8]) or a parenteral non-replicating rotavirus vaccine candidate. The automated fluorescent-focus readout demonstrated high reproducibility (R2§amp;gt;0.90), extended dynamic range and strong comparability to standard nELISA outputs. Parallel evaluations against serum IgA titres confirmed that high-throughput neutralization measurements capture functional antibody dynamics distinct from total binding IgA. This highlights the assay's value as a robust tool for comprehensive immunogenicity profiling and vaccine candidate evaluation.

articles.title: Sustained Improvement in Time in Range After Automated Insulin Delivery Initiation in Adolescents and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A 12-Month Prospective Observational Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) improves glycemic outcomes in trials, but long-term real-world data on comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics remain limited in the Middle East.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) initiating Control-IQ (CIQ) or MiniMed 780G (MMG) at King Fahad Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between December 2023 and November 2025. Participants were followed for 12 months. Continuous glucose monitoring outcomes included time in range (TIR: 70-180 mg/dL), time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), glycemic management indicator (GMI), mean sensor glucose, and coefficient of variation (CV) and assessed at baseline and 6 post-initiation time points. Glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was assessed using paired pre- and post-AID values.
RESULTS: A total of 132 adults were included: 76 using CIQ and 56 using MMG. Mean age was 27.2 ± 7.7 years, 68.9% were female, and mean diabetes duration was 14.5 ± 7.9 years. Time in range increased from 59.0 ± 15.4% at baseline to 72.3 ± 10.2% at 2 weeks and remained sustained at 12 months (73.5 ± 11.5%; +15.1 percentage points; P < .001). Time below range <70 mg/dL decreased from 5.3 ± 5.3 to 1.4 ± 1.2%. Glycated hemoglobin A1c decreased from 7.42 ± 1.13 to 6.52 ± 0.73% (P < .001; n = 106). Time in range ≥70% increased from 29.0% to 71.0%, and HbA1c <7% increased from 30.3% to 74.5%. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis rates were significantly reduced.
CONCLUSION: In a Saudi tertiary diabetes center, AID initiation was associated with rapid and sustained 12-month improvements in TIR, HbA1c, hypoglycemia exposure, and acute diabetes-related events.

articles.title: Reduced Hippocampal Subfield Volumes in Neonates with Low 1-Minute Apgar Scores Correlate with Umbilical Artery Blood Gas Parameters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perinatal asphyxia may induce brain injury, while the effects of transient hypoxia on hippocampal subregions remain unclear. Using the 1-minute Apgar score, this study examined its effects on hippocampal volumes and correlations with umbilical artery blood gas parameters (UABG), providing imaging evidence to evaluate hypoxia-related brain injury.
METHODS: Neonates were assigned to the low Apgar score (LAS) group and the normal Apgar score (NAS) group. All subjects underwent 3D T1-weighted brain MRI for hippocampal volumetry. UABG indices, including pH, lactate (LAC), and base excess (BE), were collected. We performed an analysis of covariance with sex, postmenstrual age at MRI, and total brain volume as covariates, followed by correlation analysis.
RESULTS: Multiple hippocampal subfields exhibited significantly smaller volumes in the LAS group (all FDR-corrected q < 0.05). Within-group analyses identified correlations between hippocampal volumes and UABG parameters. In the LAS group, left parasubiculum volume was correlated with pH and base excess, and in the NAS group, left parasubiculum volume correlated with the two indicators, while right tail volume correlated with pH.
CONCLUSION: Neonates with lower 1-minute Apgar scores exhibit reduced volume of specific hippocampal subregions, correlating with umbilical artery blood gas parameters. These findings link transiently low 1-minute Apgar scores with hippocampal subregional morphology during the neonatal period.
ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: We investigated neonates with low 1-minute Apgar scores that normalized at 5 minutes and found their hippocampal subregional structural changes correlated with umbilical artery blood gas parameters.

articles.title: Detailed Memory and the Self: Examining the Development of the Self-Referential Effect in Autism.
articles.abstract: The self-referential effect (SRE), better memory for self-related information, strengthens with age and includes certain source details. In autism, altered self-referential processing may reduce the SRE, though findings remain mixed. Further, the effect of self-referencing on source details is understudied in autism. We studied 37 (10 female) autistic and 64 (35 female) nonautistic children between the ages of 7 and 17 years using a self- vs. other-referential encoding paradigm and a recognition task. Both groups showed stronger memory for self-encoded words, but nonautistic children had higher average SRE. The SRE emerged for inherent (referent type) but not peripheral (word location) source memory in both groups. In nonautistic children, the SRE increased with age. Findings suggest self-referential encoding can support memory and social learning in both autistic and nonautistic children.

articles.title: Multimodal Communication in Early Autism: A Microanalytic Investigation of Gesture, Speech, and Temporal Synchrony During Parent-Child Interaction.
articles.abstract: Early communication is inherently multimodal, relying on the coordination of gestures, speech, and gaze in time. While differences in gesture and speech production have been widely documented in autism, far less is known about how these communicative modalities are integrated and temporally organized during early interactions, especially in very young children with a confirmed diagnosis. The present study investigated multimodal communication in 30 autistic and 26 neurotypical toddlers and young children during naturalistic parent-child play interactions, using a fine-grained microanalytic coding approach. We examined gesture and speech production, their integration with gaze and with each other, and critically, the temporal synchrony between gesture and speech. Relative to neurotypical peers, autistic children produced fewer gestures and less spoken language, while relying more heavily on non-word vocalizations. Beyond these modality-specific differences, autistic children displayed lower rates of gesture-gaze and gesture-speech integration. Most notably, they exhibited a reduced temporal alignment between gesture and speech, indicating diminished gesture-speech synchrony during spontaneous interaction. These findings suggest that early autistic communication differs not only in the frequency and distribution of communicative behaviors, but also in how and when these behaviors are coordinated in time. By suggesting that temporal organization may be an important dimension of early multimodal communication, this study extends current work on early social communication in autism and underscores the value of temporally sensitive, interaction-focused approaches.

articles.title: Association of Antenatal Corticosteroid Administration-to-Birth Intervals With Mortality and Morbidity Among Extremely Preterm Infants: Multicenter Data from Shenzhen, China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The optimal interval between antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) administration and birth remains uncertain, and Chinese multicentre data are scarce.
METHODS: In this multicentre retrospective cohort, 1,328 infants born before 32 weeks were classified by ACS-to-birth interval: none, <24 hours, 24 hours-7 days or >7 days. The primary outcome was survival without major morbidity (SWMM).
RESULTS: Only the 24 hours-7 days interval was associated with lower pre-discharge death, treated patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and severe brain injury, and higher SWMM. Intervals <24 hours reduced death and severe retinopathy of prematurity (sROP) only; intervals >7 days improved SWMM, severe brain injury and sROP without survival benefit. Severe intraventricular hemorrhage risk rose nonlinearly at short intervals. A single complete course conferred the broadest protection, with graded reductions in treated PDA.
CONCLUSION: ACS benefits are interval- and outcome-specific; 24 hours-7 days provided the broadest protection, supporting individualized regimens.

articles.title: Subfield-specific hippocampal enlargement in high-functioning autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although previous studies have reported abnormal hippocampal volumes in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the specific alterations in hippocampal subfields and their relationships with clinical symptoms in high-functioning ASD (HF-ASD) remain unclear.
METHODS: In this study, we analyzed T1-weighted structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I), including 182 children and adolescents with HF-ASD and 213 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Using a linear mixed-effects model, we compared hippocampal volumes between groups, and examined associations between volumes and clinical measurements.
RESULTS: Compared to TDC, the children and adolescents with HF-ASD exhibited significantly increased volumes in the right entire hippocampus, presubiculum, subiculum, and granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus (GC-DG). No significant volumetric differences were observed within the child or adolescent subgroups, nor between these age groups. Notably, presubiculum volume showed a positive correlation with verbal scores and a negative correlation with social scores in the HF-ASD group.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate subfield-specific hippocampal overgrowth in children and adolescents with HF-ASD and presubiculum volume alteration may be a potential neuroanatomical correlate underlying verbal and social dysfunctions.

articles.title: Associations of autism spectrum disorder and male sex with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents: Findings from a tertiary intensive care setting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify key clinical and demographic factors associated with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents admitted to a tertiary intensive care setting, with a particular focus on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and sex differences.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive adolescents aged 10-19 years admitted to a tertiary emergency intensive care center following suicide attempts between February 2012 and April 2023 (N = 113). Violent methods were defined as physical modalities associated with high somatic lethality, distinct from standard pharmaceutical drug overdoses. Psychiatric diagnoses were evaluated post-resuscitation by dedicated on-site psychiatrists and clinical psychologists using DSM criteria and standardized clinical assessments when indicated.
RESULTS: Among 113 participants (33 violent attempts), an ASD diagnosis and male sex were significantly and independently associated with violent suicide attempt methods. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that adolescents with ASD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 6.96, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.48-19.50, p = .002) and male patients (aOR = 4.31, 95% CI: 1.38-13.50, p = .012) had significantly elevated odds of employing violent attempt methods. Jumping from heights was the predominant violent modality (66.7%), while rare fatal methods, such as lethal substance ingestion and self-immolation, were descriptively observed only in the ASD subgroup. Exploratory sensitivity analyses supported the empirical consistency of these main associations.
CONCLUSIONS: An ASD diagnosis and male sex are independently associated with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents in tertiary intensive care. Clinical management should integrate acute-phase behavioral safety planning and emotion-regulation support for neurodivergent youth with proactive outreach for adolescent males. In addition, environmental lethal means restriction remains vital to mitigating severe, life-threatening suicide attempts across clinical, educational, and community systems.

articles.title: Perinatal risk factors associated with autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition with multifactorial etiology, resulting from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures. Although numerous studies have identified individual perinatal risk factors for ASD, most have examined these exposures in isolation, limiting understanding of how perinatal complications cluster and jointly influence neurodevelopment. Evidence from Latin America also remains scarce. This study aimed to identify multivariate perinatal risk patterns associated with ASD in a Chilean population, addressing gaps in regional representation and methodological approaches. We conducted a population-based analysis of mothers of children with and without ASD in Chile. A broad set of medical and psychosocial perinatal variables was jointly analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) to characterize interrelated risk structures. MCA revealed a clear separation between ASD and non-ASD groups along the first dimension, suggesting that ASD diagnosis is embedded within structured perinatal patterns rather than isolated exposures. MCA-derived, stepwise, and LASSO-penalized logistic regression models were then compared. The most parsimonious model identified maternal vaginal bleeding during pregnancy, prenatal maternal stress or anxiety, and negative pregnancy intention or perception as the strongest factors jointly associated with increased odds of ASD, with a dose-response pattern observed for maternal stress. An unexpected inverse association with neonatal cyanosis may reflect enhanced medical surveillance and warrants cautious interpretation. These findings underscore the importance of integrated perinatal care addressing both obstetric and maternal mental health, and demonstrate the value of multivariate approaches for elucidating complex developmental risk pathways.

articles.title: Effects of SMOFlipid-based versus soybean oil-based high-protein parenteral nutrition on hematologic, biochemical, and clinical outcomes after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in children with acute leukemia: a randomized double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal parenteral nutrition (PN) strategies, especially the parenteral lipid composition, for children undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remain uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a randomized double-blind trial comparing high-protein PN containing SMOFlipid with soybean oil-based PN (Intralipid) in pediatric patients undergoing allo-HSCT for acute leukemia. Forty-six participants completed the study (SMOFlipid, n = 22; Intralipid, n =24). Primary outcomes were neutrophil and platelet engraftment; secondary outcomes included anthropometric, biochemical, inflammatory, and clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Neutrophil engraftment was similar between groups, whereas platelet engraftment occurred later in the SMOFlipid group. Both groups experienced nutritional deterioration during the early post-transplant period; however, SMOFlipid was associated with better preservation of anthropometric measures and more favorable metabolic trajectories, including lower triglyceride excursion and improved glycemic patterns. Adjusted interleukin-6 concentrations were higher in the SMOFlipid group. Although infection rates were similar, adjusted analyses suggested lower hazards of acute graft-versus-host disease and 100-day mortality with SMOFlipid. Kaplan-Meier analysis also demonstrated improved in-hospital survival.
CONCLUSION: SMOFlipid-based PN was associated with favorable metabolic and body-composition outcomes during early recovery after pediatric allo-HSCT, although platelet engraftment was modestly delayed and inflammatory markers were higher. Larger multicenter studies are required to confirm these findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06625372.

articles.title: Preliminary findings of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation on depressive symptoms and cognitive function in adolescents with mood disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mood disorders in adolescents significantly impair their educational attainment and daily functioning. Nevertheless, there is a paucity of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pharmacological interventions specifically for adolescents, and pharmacological interventions often require a considerable duration to achieve therapeutic efficacy. High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS), a non-invasive and safe neuromodulation technique, has demonstrated promising outcomes in the treatment of depressive symptoms in adults. Given its favorable efficacy and safety profile, Hi-tACS warrants investigation as a potential therapeutic strategy for adolescent mood disorders.
METHODS: A total of 27 adolescents (aged 14-18 years) diagnosed with a depressive episode of a mood disorder were enrolled and assigned to either a Hi-tACS intervention group (tACS group) or a medication treatment management group (MTM group). The tACS group received ongoing pharmacotherapy concomitant with 20 sessions of Hi-tACS intervention, administered twice daily over 10 days. The MTM group received ongoing pharmacotherapy alone. Baseline data were collected at enrollment, and follow-up assessments were conducted at 10- and 30-day post-baseline, encompassing measures of clinical symptoms (e.g., depression, anxiety, sleep quality) and cognitive function.
RESULTS: The tACS group demonstrated significantly greater and more rapid reductions in both Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) scores (P = 0.001) and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores (P = 0.002) compared to the MTM group. Regarding cognitive function, although the time × group interaction effect for the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) total score (P = 0.113) did not reach statistical significance, the tACS group exhibited a notable but non-significant trend toward superior cognitive improvement relative to the MTM group.
CONCLUSION: As a novel, safe, and efficient neuromodulation technique, Hi-tACS may offer enhanced efficacy in ameliorating symptoms of depression and anxiety among adolescents compared to medication alone. Furthermore, it demonstrates a potential trend toward superior cognitive enhancement, particularly in memory function.

articles.title: Working memory and BMIz in preschool children: an indirect association involving insufficient healthy food intake.
articles.abstract: Executive function and health behaviors may be relevant to obesity in preschool children, a critical period for obesity prevention, but their associations remain unclear. Our cross-sectional study investigated these associations in 1,557 preschool children from Wuhan, China. The primary adiposity outcome was body mass index z-score (BMIz). Executive function was assessed using seven tasks, from which standardized task scores were averaged to derive working memory and inhibitory control composite scores. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire. The insufficient healthy food intake and excessive unhealthy food intake scores were summed to derive an overall dietary risk score. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for kindergarten showed that working memory composite score was inversely associated with BMIz. This association was not observed in inhibitory control composite score. Both insufficient healthy food intake score and overall dietary risk score were positively associated with BMIz. The indirect association analysis indicated that insufficient healthy food intake accounted for 4.94% of the total association between working memory composite score and BMIz. These findings indicate an inverse association between working memory and BMIz in preschool children and suggest a potential indirect association through insufficient healthy food intake. Given the cross-sectional design, prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal ordering and directionality of these associations.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Childhood Vaccination Among Mothers in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood vaccination is a cost-effective public health intervention that prevents vaccine-preventable diseases and reduces child morbidity and mortality. However, vaccination uptake remains suboptimal in many low-resource settings, including Somalia. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding childhood vaccination among mothers in Mogadishu, Somalia, and identified factors associated with good vaccination practices.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 461 mothers in Mogadishu, Somalia. Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire with binary response items. Knowledge was summarized from six items, attitude from six directionally coded items, and vaccination practice from two direct behavioral items; service-related barriers were analyzed separately. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with good vaccination practice, with adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported.
RESULTS: Of 461 participants, 35.1% had good knowledge, 41.4% moderate knowledge, and 23.4% poor knowledge. After directionally coding attitude items, 10.0% had positive attitudes, 70.5% intermediate/neutral attitudes, and 19.5% negative attitudes. Using the revised behavioral definition, 20.4% demonstrated good vaccination practice. Positive attitude was independently associated with good practice (AOR = 2.86, 95% CI: 1.16-7.04, p = 0.023). Primary-school education was also associated with higher odds of good practice compared with a bachelor's degree or higher (AOR = 3.22, 95% CI: 1.45-7.17, p = 0.004). Knowledge level was not independently associated with practice after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Favorable maternal attitudes were associated with better childhood vaccination practice, while substantial gaps in adherence and service access remained. Interventions in Mogadishu should combine clear vaccine communication with practical measures to reduce missed appointments, travel barriers, waiting times, and vaccine shortages. The unexpected association with educational level should be interpreted cautiously and investigated in future studies.

articles.title: Bacterial Etiology and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Patterns of Clinical Isolates Among Infants in Tigray, Ethiopia: A Cross-Sectional Hospital-Based Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In settings with inadequate resources, when delayed diagnosis and empirical treatment are widespread, bacterial infections continue to be a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among infants. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) affects treatment efficacy and complicates therapeutic management.
AIM: The aim of this study was to determine antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and bacterial profiles among infants aged ≤ 12 months at a tertiary hospital in Tigrai, Ethiopia.
METHODS: Over the course of a year from July 2021 to June 2022, infants aged ≤ 12 months participated in a hospital-based retrospective study at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Ethiopia. Isolation and identification of bacterial infections from clinical specimens were based on standard microbiological methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method was performed based on the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute standards (CLSI 2024). Susceptibility patterns were reported as susceptible, intermediate, and resistance. Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS-23) was included for descriptive analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 271 samples taken, 101 (37.3%) bacteria were identified. Eighty-one (80.2%) of the isolates were Gram-negative including Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter species, and Klebsiella pneumoniae whereas 20 (19.8%) were Gram-positive bacteria, particularly, Enterococcus spp, S. aureus and Coagulase Negative Staphylococcus aureus (CoNS). Blood specimens were collected from 188 (69.4%) infants. The isolates showed resistance to tetracycline, ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and ceftriaxone. The multidrug resistances (MDR) of Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria were 59 (74.7%) and13 (65%) with total MDR of 72 (72.7%).
CONCLUSION: There are distressing levels of antibiotic resistance and a substantial prevalence of Gram-negative bacterial infections among infants in the study area. The findings emphasize the importance of stringent antimicrobial stewardship, constant monitoring for antibiotic resistance, and improved infection prevention and control techniques. To improve clinical results in this susceptible population, empirical treatment guidelines should be updated based on local resistance patterns.

articles.title: Effects of L-Carnitine Supplementation on Clinical Outcomes, Metabolic Profile, and Organ Function in Critically Ill Children: A Triple-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Critically ill children often develop relative l-carnitine deficiency due to hypermetabolism, which can impair mitochondrial energy production and exacerbate organ dysfunction. While adult data suggest that l-carnitine supplementation improves metabolic and clinical outcomes, robust randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in the pediatric intensive care population are lacking.
METHODS: This double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). Critically ill children aged 1 month to 12 years were randomly assigned to receive enteral l-carnitine (50-100 mg/kg/day, maximum 2000 mg/day) or placebo for seven consecutive days. The primary outcome was change in serum total protein. Secondary and exploratory outcomes included changes in glycemic profile, lipid profile, liver function tests, renal function tests, coagulation parameters, blood gas parameters, and clinical outcomes including 28-day mortality and Glasgow Coma Scale.
RESULTS: The l-carnitine group showed between-group improvements in liver and tissue injury markers compared to placebo, with reductions in ALT (p = 0.01) and LDH (p = 0.002). While serum albumin improved in both groups, between-group differences were non-significant. Within-group increases were observed for HDL (p < 0.001) and TG (p = 0.03) in the l-carnitine arm. No significant between-group differences were observed for blood sugar, renal function, or coagulation parameters. Notably, the l-carnitine group showed less favorable median shifts in PCO2 and pH (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). 28-day mortality was numerically lower in the l-carnitine group than in the placebo group; however, this difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Enteral l-carnitine supplementation for 7 days was associated with exploratory reductions in biomarkers of tissue and hepatocellular injury (LDH and ALT). However, it did not improve lipid profiles, clinical outcomes, or mortality, and was associated with less favorable acid-base alterations. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these exploratory findings and clarify the clinical relevance of these effects in critically ill children.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT: IRCT20221206056734N3).

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of HBsAg Positivity Among Pregnant Women Attending the Antenatal Care Clinic at Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Bahir Dar, Northwest Ethiopia, October-December 2025: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus infection remains a major public health concern, particularly in highly endemic settings, where mother-to-child transmission is an important route of infection. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen positivity and identify factors associated with HBsAg positivity among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital in Bahir Dar, Northwest Ethiopia.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 524 pregnant women attending the antenatal care clinic at Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital from October 1 to December 30, 2025. Participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire covering sociodemographic, obstetric, and behavioral characteristics. Five milliliters of venous blood were collected from each participant, and serum was tested for HBsAg using the SNIBE MAGLUMI chemiluminescence immunoassay. Data were entered into EpiData version 3.1 and analyzed using SPSS version 26.0. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Variables with p < 0.25 in the bivariable analysis were considered for the multivariable model. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The prevalence of HBsAg positivity was 11.1% (58/524; 95% CI: 8.4%-13.8%). HBsAg positivity was associated with being divorced or widowed (AOR = 2.05; 95% CI: 1.02-4.13; p = 0.044), a history of sexually transmitted infection (AOR = 2.55; 95% CI: 1.38-4.71; p = 0.003), having one current sexual partner (AOR = 0.48; 95% CI: 0.26-0.87; p = 0.016), and a family history of HBV infection (AOR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.18-5.08; p = 0.016). Only 140 participants (26.7%) reported having previously received information about HBV.
CONCLUSION: HBsAg positivity was prevalent among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital. The observed associations with marital status, STI history, number of current sexual partners, and family history of HBV infection highlight the importance of strengthening HBV screening and prevention services within antenatal care.

articles.title: Food Consumption Score and Associated Factors Among Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care Services in Guangua Woreda Public Health Facilities, Northwest Ethiopia, 2024: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Maternal under nutrition during pregnancy leads to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although assessing nutritional status is common, evidence regarding individual-level Food Consumption Score (FCS) and its determinants among pregnant women in rural settings like Guangua Woreda is limited. This study evaluated FCS and its associated factors among pregnant women in Northwest Ethiopia.
METHODS: A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 411 pregnant women attending ANC from July 20 to September 20, 2024. A systematic random sampling technique was used. Data were gathered via interviewer-administered structured questionnaires. Multivariable logistic regression was executed to identify associated factors, reporting Adjusted Odds Ratios (AOR) with 95% Confidence Intervals.
RESULT: A total of 411 women participated (96.9% response rate). The mean FCS was 48.2 (±12.4). Overall, 82.48% (95% CI: 78.80%-86.16%) of participants had an acceptable FCS, while 17.52% (95% CI: 13.84%-21.20%) had an unacceptable FCS. In the multivariable analysis, rural residence (AOR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.21-0.84), lowest wealth quintile (AOR = 3.89, 95% CI: 1.33-11.36), and poor maternal nutritional knowledge (AOR = 0.05, 95% CI: 0.01-0.22) were independently associated with unacceptable FCS.
CONCLUSION: While most pregnant women exhibited an acceptable FCS, nearly one-fifth presented with inadequate dietary consumption. Socioeconomic disparities, rural residency, and lower nutritional knowledge were significant predictors. ANC services should integrate targeted counseling and facility-level micro-economic support.

articles.title: Assessing the Risk of Neonatal Opioid Toxicity from Breastfeeding: Challenge to the Pediatric Clinical Pharmacology Modeling and Simulation Community.
articles.abstract: The safety of maternal codeine use during breastfeeding remains controversial, largely due to debate surrounding the "Toronto Case," in which a neonatal death was associated with elevated morphine exposure following maternal postpartum codeine therapy. Critics have argued that this outcome requires an exceptionally unlikely combination of several factors. This review details the physiological and pharmacokinetic complexities of infant opioid exposure and toxicity in breastfed infants by reexamining assumptions underlying the physiology-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model frequently cited to challenge the plausibility of the Toronto Case. When advances in developmental pharmacology, pharmacogenomics, and maternal and neonatal drug disposition that have occurred over the past 15 years are considered, an integrated mother-milk-infant system emerges in which individualized risk assessment can be conceptualized as the convergence of multiple factors, each of which contributes to the overall risk for a given mother-child dyad. Future modeling and simulations must include the maternal and neonatal determinants that predispose specific breastfeeding mother-newborn pairs to excessive sedation and respiratory failure after codeine administration, and generate evidence to support safer opioid therapy in breastfeeding mothers, breastfed infants, and older children.

articles.title: Measuring school wellbeing in neurodivergent children: Exploring the suitability of a self-report measure with primary school children with Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: The current study examines the suitability of a self-report measure of school wellbeing for primary school-aged children with Down syndrome. The sample comprised 48 children with Down syndrome aged between 6 and 10.75 years (M = 8.4 years, SD = 1), of whom 43 had both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour measures. Children and parents completed parallel versions of the How I Feel About My School (HIFAMS; Allen et al., 2018) measure of school wellbeing; classroom teachers completed the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (Goodman, 2001) and the Brief Early Skills and Support Index (Hughes et al., 2015). Properties of the child-reported HIFMAS were broadly similar to those for neurotypical children. Notably, however, both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour showed limited association with child-reported school wellbeing, highlighting the need for further research to evaluate this measure's sensitivity to variation in the school experiences of children with Down Syndrome.

articles.title: Coping with developmental coordination disorder: A comparative study of adults and parents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD/Dyspraxia) is a common, yet under-recognised lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterised by motor coordination difficulties affecting daily functioning and psychosocial wellbeing. Coping plays an important role in wellbeing, yet little is known about how adults with DCD manage ongoing challenges or how their coping compares with that of parents of individuals with DCD.
METHODS: One hundred and fourteen participants (90 adults with DCD; 24 parents who raised a child with DCD for at least 16 years) completed an online survey assessing coping, acceptance, optimism, resilience, condition perceptions and life satisfaction. Group differences were examined using MANCOVA and t-tests.
RESULTS: Parents reported greater use of adaptive coping, particularly acceptance, and planning, alongside higher optimism, resilience, and life satisfaction. Adults with DCD relied more on maladaptive coping, notably mental disengagement, which was associated with poorer wellbeing. Acceptance-based coping was a protective factor in both groups. Social support and humour showed no clear association with wellbeing. Greater motor coordination difficulties were associated with increased disengagement and reduced humour use.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with DCD and parents show distinct coping and wellbeing profiles. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions that promote adaptive coping and acceptance in adults with DCD overall.

articles.title: The effect of multi-site repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on executive functions and reading abilities in adolescents with comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and developmental dyslexia: A randomised controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occurs with developmental dyslexia (DD), and this comorbidity in children and adolescents is associated with pronounced cognitive and academic impairments. Current treatment approaches for ADHD + DD remain suboptimal, particularly in addressing the combined deficits. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory intervention, yet its therapeutic potential in this comorbid population has not been systematically evaluated.
METHODS: In a randomized controlled trial, 60 children diagnosed with ADHD + DD were assigned to either the rTMS group (receiving 40 high-frequency sessions over 8 weeks) or the sham rTMS group. Primary outcomes included executive function measures (n-back task, Go/No-go task) and reading-related tasks (phonological, morphological, and orthographic awareness). Safety and tolerability were closely monitored throughout the intervention.
RESULTS: Using mixed-design repeated measures ANOVA, compared with the sham group, the rTMS group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in verbal working memory accuracy (p < 0.05), response inhibition accuracy (p < 0.001), and processing speed across multiple tasks (p < 0.05). Reading performance also improved, with enhanced phonological awareness accuracy (p < 0.05) and faster morphological processing (p = 0.028). Correlation analyses indicated that improvements in executive function were significantly associated with gains in reading ability. Both interventions were well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported.
CONCLUSION: Multi-site high-frequency rTMS significantly enhances executive function and reading skills in children and adolescents with ADHD + DD, with a favorable safety profile. These findings provide novel evidence supporting rTMS as a neuromodulation-based intervention for this comorbid condition and highlight the therapeutic relevance of targeting the prefrontal-parietal network within an integrative treatment framework.

articles.title: Diagnostic outcomes of adolescents and adults presenting for an autism evaluation who do not meet criteria for autism: A retrospective chart review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Increased autism awareness and evolving diagnostic criteria have led more adolescents and adults to seek formal autism evaluations. This study examined the characteristics and diagnostic outcomes of adolescents and adults presenting for an autism evaluation at an academic autism center who did not receive an autism diagnosis.
METHODS: Electronic health records of patients meeting eligibility criteria (age ≥16 years, evaluation between January 2017 and November 2022, no prior center visits, no known genetic conditions, and not meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders [DSM-5] criteria for autism) were reviewed for demographic and clinical characteristics and DSM-5 diagnostic outcomes. Diagnoses were coded into DSM-5 categories. Diagnostic outcomes were compared across evaluation type, sex, and age groups using Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: A total of 121 patients met eligibility criteria (Mage = 28.1 [12.3] years, 57.0% male, 82.1% White). Most patients received multiple DSM-5 diagnoses (M = 2.2 [1.2]). The most common DSM-5 categories were other neurodevelopmental disorders (53.7%), anxiety disorders (47.1%), depressive disorders (28.9%), and trauma- and stressor-related disorders (13.2%).
