Females were more likely than males to receive an anxiety disorder diagnosis, and males were more likely to receive substance-related diagnoses. There were no differences in diagnostic outcomes across age groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents and adults presenting for a first-time autism evaluation who did not meet DSM-5 criteria for autism demonstrated diverse psychiatric and neurodevelopmental presentations and frequently received alternative DSM-5 diagnoses.

articles.title: Early intervention in children with fragile X syndrome: Prevalence, timing, and family perception.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic disorder that commonly leads to intellectual and developmental delays and disabilities. Early intervention (EI) services and therapies provided to children under 3 years of age aim to improve developmental outcomes. This analysis examines the prevalence of EI receipt among children with FXS, enrollment timing, services used, and parental satisfaction with EI services.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Fragile X Online Registry With Accessible Research Database (FORWARD), collected from 2011 to 2021. Participants aged 3-21 years during at least one clinic visit were included. EI receipt and enrollment age were assessed overall and by demographic characteristics; services used and satisfaction with services were assessed in relation to EI enrollment age. All analyses were stratified by sex.
RESULTS: Among 1114 participants, 86.0% of males and 59.6% of females received EI, with over 80% of parents reporting some level of satisfaction with services. EI receipt varied by household income, parental education, race/ethnicity, household language, and insurance. Among participants diagnosed with FXS at < 3 years, only 8.6% of males and 13.3% of females had a diagnosis before starting EI. Most EI participants received speech and language therapy (93.5% males, 90.3% females), occupational therapy (89.2% males, 72.4% females), and physical therapy (72.5% males, 50.3% females).
CONCLUSION: Most children began early intervention before FXS diagnosis, showing that EI receipt may depend more on recognition of developmental delays than genetic diagnosis. Parental satisfaction with EI was high, though receipt varied substantially by demographic factors, identifying opportunities for targeted outreach.

articles.title: Parental awareness, trust, and willingness to accept RSV immunization: A mixed-methods study in Chile.
articles.abstract: This study examines parental awareness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and the determinants of trust in-and willingness to accept-RSV immunization in Chile using a sequential mixed-methods design. We conducted a national online survey of parents aged 18-44 years (n = 510) and qualitative fieldwork with 74 parents across three regions of the country, including 44 in-depth interviews and 7 focus groups with 30 participants. Findings from the online survey indicate uneven awareness and perceptions: 62.9% (95% CI: 58.7-67.1) reported awareness of RSV, 53.5% (95% CI: 49.2-57.8) knew of available RSV immunization options, 88.6% (95% CI: 85.8-91.4) perceived RSV as severe, yet only 48.6% (95% CI: 44.3-52.9) perceived a high susceptibility to child contagion. High trust in and willingness to accept RSV immunization were reported by 72% (95% CI: 68.1-75.9) and 78% (95% CI: 74.4-81.6), respectively. Confidence in RSV immunization emerged as the strongest predictor of willingness to accept it, whereas perceived effectiveness of RSV immunization was the strongest predictor of confidence. Overall, willingness to accept RSV immunization is linked to the evaluation of its specific benefits, whereas confidence in RSV immunization is related to more general perceptions and positive intentions toward routine childhood vaccination. Qualitative data confirmed persistent knowledge gaps about RSV and underscored the role of emotions in shaping both trust in and willingness to accept immunization. Taken together, these findings suggest that RSV immunization strategies in Chile should simultaneously strengthen messages about the effectiveness of available tools and explicitly address parents' broader concerns and past experiences with vaccination, offering concrete priorities for the design of future RSV communication campaigns in Chile and similar settings.

articles.title: Myocardial Work Analysis: A Novel Echocardiographic Approach for Early Detection of Myocardial Fibrosis in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Preserved LVEF-A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While myocardial work (MW) indices have shown diagnostic and prognostic value in various cardiovascular diseases, their role in detecting myocardial fibrosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unexplored. This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.
METHODS: In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up.
RESULTS: Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P<0.01). Notably, MW abnormalities preceded global longitudinal strain reduction, with significant differences even in patients with DMD with normal global longitudinal strain (≥18%). Global work efficiency showed moderate diagnostic accuracy for baseline late gadolinium enhancement (area under the curve, 0.618) and was associated with subsequent late gadolinium enhancement development in exploratory longitudinal analysis (area under the curve, 0.798; cutoff of 95.85%), providing complementary information beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, given the limited number of progression events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Neonatal sevoflurane exposures induced cognitive impairment via Satb2-mediated synaptic deficits.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (Satb2) is a DNA binding protein, and involved in transcription regulation and chromatin remodeling. Studies demonstrated that the absence of Satb2 mediated cognitive impairments in humans and rodents. Moreover, animal research reported that neonatal exposure to sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in adolescent period, along with damage of synaptic plasticity, but the mechanisms are still not clear. Herein, we aimed to determine the role of Satb2 in neurotoxicity caused by sevoflurane.
METHODS: A total of 254 neonatal male Sprague-Dawley rats were used in this study. Neonatal rats were exposed to 30% O2 or 3.0% sevoflurane delivered in 30% O2 for 3 h on postnatal day 7 (P7). Cognitive function was evaluated through open field, Y maze, and novel object recognition tests from P28 to P35. The hippocampi were harvested on P14, P21, and P35. Effects of sevoflurane on Satb2, and synapse in the hippocampus were investigated by western blot, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and Golgi staining. To further screen key molecules, another batch of hippocampi were harvested immediately and 24 h after gas exposure, and subjected to RNA sequencing. Finally, Satb2 overexpression was induced by lentivirus injection into the lateral ventricle on P1, followed by gas exposure on P7. Next, some rats underwent behavioral tests on P28-P35. Hippocampi from another group of rats were harvested on P35 for Western blot, qRT-PCR, and Golgi staining.
RESULTS: Y maze test showed that sevoflurane reduced the spontaneous alternation ratio in young rats. Novel object recognition test also revealed that sevoflurane decreased recognition index, the entries, and duration in novel arm, along with prolonged the latency to novel arm. Persistent decrease in Satb2, postsynaptic density protein-95 (PSD95), and spine density were observed. Moreover, RNA sequencing also revealed the decrease in Satb2 mRNA caused by neonatal exposure to sevoflurane. Furthermore, we found that lentivirus (LV)-induced Satb2 overexpression partially restored the decreases in the PSD95, spine density, spontaneous alternation ratio, recognition index, the entries, and duration in novel arm, and the increase in latency to novel arm caused by sevoflurane exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that decreased Satb2 may contribute to cognitive disorders by reducing PSD95 levels, resulting in synaptic deficits. Meanwhile, this emphasizes that Satb2 was a potential target to intervening cognitive impairment caused by sevoflurane exposure.

articles.title: Transfusion-sparing anesthetic management and immediate extubation in pediatric liver transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood-sparing anesthesia and rapid recovery are central in pediatric liver transplantation (PLTx). The aim of this study was to describe the intraoperative anesthetic management adopted by a dedicated team.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study performed at IRCCS-ISMETT, a transplant center specialized in all solid organ transplantation. Main anesthetic strategies were restrictive crystalloid administration, multifactorial assessment for blood-products transfusion, and planned immediate extubation (IE). Pre-, intra-, and postoperative variables were extracted. Logistic regressions were applied to explore variables associated with PRBC transfusion and IE and subsequent multiple analyses on select variables.
RESULTS: Ninety-nine consecutive recipients (0-17 years) between January 2018 and July 2023 were reviewed (75% living-related). Median fluid rates were respectively 9, 14, and 9 ml/kg/h during the pre-anhepatic, anhepatic and neohepatic phases. 34% of recipients required no PRBC, and 77% received < 20 ml/kg. Plasma or platelets were administered to 17 children. IE succeeded in 89 patients (90%). Median hospital stay was 18 days. One-year graft and patient survival were 99%. Transfusion-free PLTx was associated with lower tolerated intraoperative hemoglobin and higher mean arterial pressure, greater weight, and lower preoperative international normalized ratio (INR) or pediatric end-stage liver disease score. IE was associated with no requirement for vasopressors, shorter surgical time, and lower lactate levels at the end of operation.
CONCLUSIONS: Blood-sparing anesthetic strategies and IE are feasible in PLTx within an experienced multidisciplinary program, and are associated with favorable early postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Combined Associations of Maternal Sleep Quality and Prenatal Negative Life Events with Childhood Parasomnias.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parasomnias are common in early childhood and are increasingly linked to later behavioral and neurodevelopmental vulnerability. Although prenatal determinants of childhood parasomnias are recognized as an emerging research focus, evidence remains limited. Maternal sleep disturbances and psychological stress frequently co-occur during pregnancy and may have long-term implications for offspring health. This study examined the combined associations of maternal prenatal sleep quality and stress exposure with childhood parasomnias.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6236 preschool-aged children, with maternal prenatal negative life events (NLEs) and sleep quality retrospectively assessed across three gestational periods. Childhood parasomnias were assessed using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to reduce group differences across exposure groups. Associations were examined using logistic regressions, and path analysis was performed to estimate direct and indirect effects.
RESULTS: Overall, 25.7% of children had parasomnias, with the highest prevalence in the co-exposure group (37.3%), followed by the poor-sleep-only (29.6%), NLEs-only (23.1%), and no-exposure groups (22.8%). After IPTW, maternal poor sleep quality during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of childhood parasomnias (aOR = 1.402, 95% CI: 1.231-1.596). While NLEs alone were not independently associated with parasomnias, co-exposure to poor sleep quality showed an even stronger risk (aOR = 1.778, 95% CI: 1.122-2.816). Associations appeared stronger among children whose mothers reported lower perceived family support. Path analysis revealed a direct association between maternal sleep quality and childhood parasomnias (β = 0.127, 95% CI: 0.083-0.172).
CONCLUSION: Poor maternal sleep quality during pregnancy was directly associated with increased risk of childhood parasomnias, and co-occurring NLEs further amplified this risk. These findings highlight the importance of jointly assessing maternal sleep quality and psychosocial stress during pregnancy to identify children who are susceptible to developing parasomnias.

articles.title: The Association Between Parent-Reported ADHD-Related Symptoms and English Word Reading in Syrian Refugee Children.
articles.abstract: The purpose of the present study was to examine child-level and family-level factors associated with English word reading in a sample of 133 Syrian refugee children aged 6-13 years resettled in Canada, 35% of whom had resided in refugee camps before resettlement. Using multilevel modeling to account for children nested within families, we examined whether parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were associated with English word reading after accounting for age, nonverbal reasoning, receptive vocabulary, and phonological awareness, and whether time spent in refugee camps was associated with word reading at the family level. Parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were assessed using the Hyperactivity/Inattention subscale of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), a behavioral screening instrument rather than a diagnostic assessment of ADHD. Findings indicated that older age and stronger phonological awareness were associated with higher English word reading scores, while parent-reported ADHD-related symptom scores were associated with lower word reading performance after accounting for the other predictors. In contrast, time spent in refugee camps was not significantly associated with English word reading. These findings highlight the importance of considering attentional and behavioral functioning alongside established cognitive and linguistic correlates when examining English literacy development among Syrian refugee children following resettlement.

articles.title: The Long-term cognitive and mental health impacts of pandemic-induced social isolation: a trajectory analysis.
articles.journal: J Gerontol B Psychol Sci Soc Sci
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The COVID-19 pandemic imposed social deprivation on older adults, offering a natural experiment to test trajectories of cognitive vulnerability and psychological resilience. Guided by a Dual-Pathway Framework, we investigated how pandemic-era community-based social participation trajectories predicted 2022 cognitive and mental health outcomes, and whether childhood adversity (CA) moderated these effects.
METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Study, with final analytic samples of 2,457 for depressive symptoms and 1,679 for cognitive function. Survey-weighted multivariable regressions using baseline-adjusted change scores evaluated how 2016-2020 social participation trajectories (Consistently Isolated, Pandemic Drop-off, Consistently Engaged, Pandemic Initiators) predicted changes in cognitive function and depressive symptoms from 2016 to 2022. Models adjusted for 2016 baselines, sociodemographic disadvantages, and physical health constraints, while testing moderation by cumulative CA.
RESULTS: Compared with Consistently Engaged peers, the Pandemic Drop-off cohort showed significant cognitive decline by 2022, resembling the Consistently Isolated. This drop-off did not predict worsened long-term depressive symptoms. CA independently predicted poorer mental health. Binary models showed no moderation, while continuous sensitivity analyses suggested a potential protective interaction between late-life social initiation and cumulative early-life trauma for cognitive preservation. Pandemic Initiators preserved cognitive function comparable to consistently engaged adults.
DISCUSSION: Findings support the Dual-Pathway Framework: the aging mind demonstrates emotional adaptation, whereas the aging brain may show accelerated aging after abrupt community-level social deprivation. Social participation may be important for cognitive health. Mitigating post-pandemic cognitive decline may require treating social isolation as a clinical vital sign and supporting social prescribing.

articles.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women.
METHODS: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.
RESULTS: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with post-tuberculosis lung disease among children and adolescents in Kenya: A multi-centre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most patients survive tuberculosis (TB) with treatment. However, emerging evidence reveals occurrence of a post-TB sequelae termed post TB lung disease (PTLD) that affects survivor's long term lung health. Evidence on PTLD in children and adolescents is limited. We evaluated the prevalence and factors associated with PTLD in children and adolescents completing treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi, Kenya.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study done on participants<20 years at the end of treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi. After obtaining informed consent and assent, we interviewed and examined participants, reviewed their medical records, and conducted a six-minute walk test (6MWT) for children >5 years. Post-TB sequelae was defined as persistent respiratory symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs after TB treatment. Descriptive statistics were computed for prevalence of post-TB symptoms and signs, and logistic regression analysis performed to evaluate factors associated with post-TB sequelae.
RESULTS: We enrolled 107 participants, of median age 6.3 years; 59% were female and 12% had Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Persistent respiratory symptoms were present in 29%; commonest being cough (21.5%). Abnormal respiratory signs were present in 51%; commonest being tachypnea (27%). Of 56 participants who did the 6MWT, 58% walked <70% of their expected distance. Overall, 57.0% (95% CI 47.1-66.5) had at least one while 33.6% (95% CI 23.8-41.6%) had two or more persistent symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs. Hospitalization at diagnosis (aOR 10.26 (1.76-59.79) and older age (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26) were independent predictors of PTLD.
CONCLUSION: A significant number of children and adolescents have persisting respiratory disease post-TB and it is more common among older children, and those with severe disease at TB diagnosis. There is need to institute routine assessment of children and adolescents at the end of TB treatment to identify those with sequelae, and provide post-TB care.

articles.title: High blood pressure among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus in Uganda: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coexistence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) worsens the clinical outcomes of children with diabetes concerning both microvascular and macrovascular disease. It increases mortality risk by 5 times, with a higher risk of death in developing countries. Therefore, comprehensive care for patients with diabetes, including hypertension screening, must be provided.
METHODS: This multicenter health facility-based cross-sectional study included 150 children and adolescents aged from 6 months to 18 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were treated at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH), Mbale Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH) and Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH). Interviewer-administered questionnaires were used to obtain data, which were then analyzed according to the study objectives using STATA® version 18. High blood pressure diagnosis was based on blood pressure (BP) above or equal to the 90th percentile for <13 years and either systolic BP ≥ 120 mmHg or Diastolic BP ≥ 80mmhg for 13 years and older for age, sex and height. The prevalence of high BP was determined as a percentage, whereas associated factors were analyzed at both bivariate and multivariable logistic regression. The significance of associations was set at a p-value <0.05 and a 95% confidence interval.
RESULTS: Of the 150 participants, 115 (76.7%) were above 12 years of age, and the median age was 15 years (IQR 13-17). There were more females [81/150 (54%)] than males. The majority were attending school [130/150 (86.7%)], with a few attending boarding school [26/130 (20%)]. Sixty-one participants (40.7%, 95% C.I 33%-49%) had high BP, and 53 (86.9%) of these patients had poor glycemic control. The factors associated with high BP among T1DM participants included having diabetes for 4-8 years (aOR= 2.23 [95% CI: 1.05-4.75]; p = 0.037), and 9-12 years (aOR= 4.545 [95% CI: 1.075-19.221]; p = 0.040) respectively compared to those less than 4 years. Additionally, having Poor glycemic control (HBA1C ≥ 7%) increased odds for high BP by 2.905 [95% CI: 1.149-7.342]; p = 0.024) times compared to their counterparts with good glycemic control.
CONCLUSION: There was a high prevalence of high blood pressure among children with type 1 diabetes. Factors associated with high blood pressure included disease duration of more than 4 years and poor glycemic control.

articles.title: Co-developing a women-centered HIV prevention intervention to reduce stigma, increase HIV self-testing, and improve pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake in Ghana (WISE WOMAN): A study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young women in Ghana (18-35 years) remain disproportionately affected by HIV due to intersecting structural and social challenges, including stigma, gendered power dynamics, and limited access to women-centered prevention services. Although HIV self-testing (HIVST) and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) are effective biomedical prevention strategies, uptake among young Ghanaian women remains low. Barriers include limited awareness, persistent stigma, and a lack of culturally relevant, youth-responsive prevention approaches. The WISE WOMAN study aims to address these gaps by developing and piloting a women-centered HIV prevention intervention co-created with young women in Ghana.
METHODS: This protocol describes a pilot implementation study of a women-centered HIV prevention intervention that will be delivered via WhatsApp. The intervention is informed by community-based participatory research and human-centered design approaches to enhance cultural relevance and responsiveness to young women's lived experiences. The study will enroll 50 young women aged 18-35 years who will participate in a four-week WhatsApp-based intervention designed to increase HIV prevention knowledge, reduce stigma, and support engagement with HIVST and PrEP. Implementation outcomes, including feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness, will be assessed using mixed methods. Quantitative data will be collected through baseline and post-intervention surveys, including the PIERS-22 engagement scale, and will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired comparisons. Qualitative data from group interactions and post-intervention interviews will be analyzed using thematic analysis. The study has received ethical approval from the University at Buffalo Institutional Review Board (STUDY00009328) and the Ensign Global College Ethics Committee (IRB/EL/AF-02/2025) and is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07003789).
DISCUSSION: This protocol outlines the design and methods for a digitally delivered, women-centered HIV prevention intervention grounded in participatory approaches. The planned pilot study will generate critical implementation evidence on the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of a WhatsApp-based, co-designed intervention, informing future adaptation, scale-up, and integration of culturally grounded HIV prevention strategies for young women in Ghana and similar settings.

articles.title: Visuo-spatial perception deficit in ophthalmological disorders: Visual field extent matters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Persons with Visual Impairment (VI) are more at risk to be without academic qualification. This is classically attributed to limited access to visual information, considered difficult due to reduced visual acuity. However, in some cases, visual acuity is preserved but visual field is reduced. Given the importance of visuo-spatial skills in learning, we assessed the accuracy of perceptual visuo-spatial judgements relative to visual field extent and visual acuity to question their respective contribution to the functional repercussions in VI.
METHODS: 97 patients were administered the elementary visuo-spatial perception (EVSP) test during their clinical assessment. We put a focus on two diseases of our sample: Retinitis Pigmentosa (N = 19) and Albinism (N = 18), with mainly restriction of visual field extent in the former, and visual acuity loss in the latter. In addition, we investigated the correlation between the visuo-spatial performance and these two distinctive factors of VI in the whole sample.
RESULTS: The results indicated higher prevalence of visuo-spatial perception deficit in the whole sample of VI compared to typically developing individuals. Even if most pathologies affect both peripheral and central vision, which makes it complicated to fully disentangle between these two factors, the focus on the Retinitis Pigmentosa and the Albinism groups suggested that visuo-spatial perception is less impacted by a low visual acuity than by peripheral visual field restriction. Additionally, we found that visuospatial perception performance was significantly correlated with visual field extent and not with visual acuity in the whole sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Visual field extent matters for visuo-spatial processing and probably for academic achievement. Further investigations are needed to understand how impaired visuo-spatial perceptual skills may explain academic difficulties in VI.

articles.title: Sociodemographic characteristics of pre-XDR-TB among patients with MDR/RR-TB in Central and Eastern Oromia, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-XDR-TB is a type of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains that meet the definition of multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB) and are also resistant to any fluoroquinolone. An estimated 1,800 MDR/RR-TB cases emerged in Ethiopia in 2021. The objective of the study was to determine the sociodemographic characteristics and associated factors of pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (pre-XDR-TB).
METHODS: The study was specifically conducted in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis Treatment Initiation Centers in these regions Central and Eastern Oromia, Ethiopia. The study was conducted from September 2025 to December 2025. A facility-based retrospective cross-sectional study design was employed. Total sample size for the study of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis was 445, While sample size fo the characterization of Pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis was 21. Data was collected from Adama, Robe Dida, Bishoftu, Chiro, Ginnir, Goba, and Shashemene treatment centers. The sample size was allocated proportionally based on the total number of MDR-TB patients receiving treatment and care at each facility. Sample was collected from simple random sampling procedure. Data were entered, cleaned, and analyzed using Microsoft Office Excel 2024 and R statistical software.
RESULTS: Pre-XDR TB patients in Central and Eastern Oromia were predominantly male (71.4%), married (71.4%), and from rural areas (52.4%), with the majority (76.2%) originating from the Oromia region. Socioeconomically, most patients had low educational attainment, with 47.6% having only primary education and 33.3% having no formal education at all. Farming was the dominant occupation (47.6%), followed by daily labor (28.6%), and 76.2% of patients earned less than 3000 USD per month, indicating that pre-XDR TB was concentrated among the lowest income groups. Access to healthcare was severely limited, as 61.9% of pre-XDR TB patients traveled more than 10 km to reach the nearest health facility. Taken together, these findings reveal that pre-XDR TB in this setting disproportionately affects young adult married males engaged in low-income farming and daily labor occupations, with low educational attainment, predominantly rural residence, and markedly limited geographic access to healthcare services a convergence of socioeconomic and structural vulnerabilities that likely contributes to delayed diagnosis, treatment interruption, and ongoing transmission of fluoroquinolone-resistant strains in the study area.
CONCLUSION: Pre-XDR TB in Central and Eastern Oromia predominantly affects young adult male farmers and daily laborers with low income, low education, rural residence, and limited healthcare access. Living or working in crowded environments was the only independent modifiable factor significantly associated with pre-XDR TB development (AOR = 2.68; 95% CI: 1.12-6.42), underscoring the critical role of structural and environmental determinants in the epidemiology of advanced drug-resistant tuberculosis. These findings highlight the urgent need for targeted public health interventions addressing both the clinical management and the underlying socioeconomic and environmental drivers of pre-XDR TB in Ethiopia.

articles.title: Regional variation in adolescent births and associations with adverse perinatal outcomes in Georgia: A birth registry-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Georgia, approximately 2,700 (5.8%) adolescents give birth every year. Adolescent births are a public health concern due to an increased risk of various adverse maternal and newborn outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the regional variation of adolescent births and also the associations between maternal age and preterm birth (PB), neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and perinatal death (PD) in Georgia.
METHODS: The study population included all childbirths in women aged <30 years between 2017 and 2022, comprising 173,238 women and their 175,213 newborns. We used three age groups: adolescents aged <18, and 18-19 years, and adults aged 20-29 years (reference group). Logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the associations between maternal age and PB, NICU admission, and PD. Population attributable fractions and absolute numbers of the selected adverse outcomes attributable to adolescent births were estimated.
RESULTS: The adolescent birth rate (ABR) was 22.2 per 1000 adolescents in Georgia in 2022. Most of the adolescents aged <20 years lived in the regions of Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti with an ABR of 70.3 per 1000, 35.3 per 1000, and 26.4 per 1000, respectively. Newborns born to adolescents aged <18 (PB adjusted odds ratio [aOR]= 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.41; NICU aOR= 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.33; PD aOR= 1.33, 95% CI: 0.99-1.80) and 18-19 years (PB aOR= 1.04, 95% CI: 0.98-1.11; NICU aOR= 1.08, 95% CI: 1.01-1.16; PD aOR= 1.17, 95% CI: 0.98-1.40) had higher odds for almost all the selected perinatal outcomes than newborns born to the reference group of 20-29-year-old women. If adolescents <20 years had postponed childbirth until they were between 20 and 29 years old, approximately 14 cases of singleton preterm birth (1%), 16 NICU admissions (1%), and 4 perinatal deaths (2%) occurring between 2017 and 2022 could have been prevented.
CONCLUSION: Our findings revealed large geographical differences in adolescent births across Georgia, with the highest rates in Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti. Adolescent childbirth, particularly among those <18 years, was linked to higher risks of PB, NICU admission, and PD compared to adults aged 20-29 years. Targeted interventions, such as improved access to reproductive health education and family planning, are needed, especially in high-burden regions.

articles.title: Maintaining integrity amidst turmoil: A qualitative exploration of parental coping process during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for pediatric cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood cancer, particularly pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), imposes profound psychosocial and socioeconomic challenges on parents. This study aimed to develop a grounded theory explaining the dynamic coping process experienced by parents during their child's HSCT journey.
METHODS: This qualitative study used Corbin and Strauss's (2015) grounded theory approach to develop an explanatory account of the parental coping process during pediatric HSCT. Twenty Persian-speaking parents of children undergoing HSCT at a tertiary care center in Iran were recruited through purposive and theoretical sampling. Data collection began with unstructured interviews and progressed to in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed through constant comparative analysis, including open, axial, and selective coding.
RESULTS: Parental coping during pediatric HSCT was a multifaceted, non-linear process shaped by evolving stressors and adaptive responses. The analysis generated a grounded theory centered on the core category, "maintaining integrity amidst turmoil," which reflected parents' efforts to manage their central concern, "entrapment in adversity," arising from perceived threats and trapped in suffering. Coping was mediated through two key strategies: "health-seeking behaviors" and "emotional and cognitive coping efforts". Contextual factors, including a "continuum of support systems" (ranging from empowering healthcare interactions to systemic inadequacies) and "beliefs and individual situation" (cultural, spiritual, and personal values), significantly influenced coping trajectories. Outcomes included "relative adaptation" and "self-actualization".
CONCLUSIONS: Tailored support systems that address systemic gaps and cultural beliefs are essential for fostering adaptive coping. Strengthening health-seeking and emotional-cognitive strategies can promote functional stability and personal growth among parents.

articles.title: Association between active helicobacter pylori infection and Iron Deficiency Anemia among pregnant women attending antenatal care in Uganda: An analytical cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori infection has been associated with iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) during pregnancy, but evidence from Uganda remains limited. This study compared IDA prevalence by H. pylori status, assessed the adjusted association between H. pylori positivity and IDA, and explored factors associated with IDA among infected pregnant women.
METHODS: A facility-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 pregnant women attending antenatal care at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda, from August to December 2025. Participants were systematically recruited into H. pylori-positive and -negative analytical groups (196 each). Active H. pylori infection was determined using stool antigen testing, and IDA was defined by concurrent anaemia and serum ferritin <15 µg/L. Prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated for the H. pylori-IDA association, while logistic regression explored factors associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women.
RESULTS: IDA was more prevalent among H. pylori-positive than -negative women (14.8% [29/196] vs 6.6% [13/196]). H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA (cPR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.20-4.16; p = 0.012), including after adjustment for residence, iron-rich food consumption and household income (aPR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.16-4.24; p = 0.016). Median haemoglobin was lower among H. pylori-positive women (11 vs 12 g/dL; p < 0.001). Among H. pylori-positive women, lack of deworming (aOR=4.88, 95% CI: 1.73-13.79), tea or coffee consumption with meals (aOR=4.31, 95% CI: 1.22-15.20), and inadequate handwashing (aOR=3.18, 95% CI: 1.15-8.76) were associated with higher odds of IDA.
CONCLUSIONS: H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA among pregnant women attending ANC at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital. Lack of deworming, tea or coffee consumption with meals, and inadequate handwashing were associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of IDA cases.

articles.title: Comparing the effects of biological nurturing versus the WHO/UNICEF 20-hours course method on early breastfeeding problems: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biological nurturing (BN) is a neurobehavioral approach to breastfeeding that promotes a comfortable, laidback maternal position to facilitate effective attach and reduce breast problems. Although BN has shown to be effective in a variety of settings, its implementation in hospital context has not been thoroughly evaluated. The aim of this observational study was to evaluate the effectiveness of BN, compared to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method, on the occurrence of breast problems and the prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding during hospital stay and the 24 hours before discharge, and to compare these results with those obtained from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) conducted in the same hospital in 2018.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at IRCCS Burlo Garofolo Pediatric Hospital (Trieste, Italy) between June and September 2022. Ninety women who gave birth at the hospital and were breastfeeding during hospital stay after delivery were enrolled in the study and asked to complete a questionnaire. The primary study outcome was the frequency of women who were breastfeeding according to the BN approach (BN group) or according to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method (WHO/UNICEF group) during hospital stay, and to compare the prevalence of breast problems between the two groups.
RESULTS: Sixty-five out of 90 women (72.2%) breastfed according to the BN approach and 25 (27.8%) to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method. During hospital stay, 55.4% of women (n = 36) experienced breast problems in the BN group and 76.0% (n = 19) in the WHO/UNICEF group. The prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding was significantly higher in the BN group than in the WHO/UNICEF group during hospital stay (86.2% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.02) and in the 24 hours prior to hospital discharge (81.5% vs. 56.0%; p = 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: The BN approach applied in the real-life situation of a paediatric hospital was effective in preventing breast problems and increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates.

articles.title: Untargeted plasma metabolomics reveals metabolite alterations and pathway perturbations in gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first detected during pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Metabolomics provides a system-level approach to characterize metabolic alterations associated with gestational insulin resistance. This study aimed to identify plasma metabolite differences between women with GDM and normal glucose tolerance (NGT) and to evaluate the discriminatory performance of a metabolite-based panel.
METHODS: Plasma samples from 270 pregnant women (169 GDM and 101 NGT) were analyzed using an untargeted 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR)-based metabolomics approach. Differential metabolites were identified using univariate, followed by multivariate modeling and regression adjustment for maternal age and pre-pregnancy body mass index. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using Random Forest (RF), Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), and Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear-SVM) models with Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using KEGG and SMPDB, and disease-based enrichment was assessed using HMDB.
RESULTS: Among 31 identified metabolites, 14 differed significantly between GDM and NGT. Integration of univariate and multivariate analyses prioritized nine metabolites-acetone, citrate, glucose, succinate, glycine, 3-hydroxybutyrate, leucine, phenylalanine, and the CH = CH bond of unsaturated lipids-that remained independently associated with GDM after covariate adjustment. All nine metabolites were elevated in the GDM group. A nine-metabolite panel achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.70-0.81) using the RF model. Pathway enrichment identified valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis and ketone body metabolism as significantly enriched pathways. HMDB-based disease enrichment showed overlap with preeclampsia-related metabolic signatures.
CONCLUSION: Untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, combined enrichment analyses, identified coordinated metabolic disturbances in GDM involving amino acid and ketone body metabolism. A nine-metabolite panel demonstrated moderate discriminative performance and provides mechanistic insight into GDM-associated metabolic adaptations, supporting their potential utility for future biomarker validation and translational studies.

articles.title: Perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum and its correlates in Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal and newborns care continuum completion decision making process is influenced by seeking validation and the sole approval from significant others. Evidences have shown that community acceptance is one of the bottlenecks hindering the completion of the maternal and newborns care continuum and their retention in the care. It is also among the critical determinants for the success of the paradigm shift on the maternal, newborns and child health (MNCH) care continuum completion. However, this area is understudied, leading a dearth of evidence in Ethiopia. Hence, this study aimed at documenting the level of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum and identifying associated factors among pregnant women. The findings could provide actionable evidence for the Ethiopian Health Ministry and relevant developmental partners to improve maternal and newborns health outcomes.
METHODS: This study has used the baseline cross sectional data form the Ethiopian Performance Monitoring for Action (EPMA) cohort one survey. The study screened, enrolled and collected data from pregnant and six week postpartum women. However, the analytic sample were 2,219 pregnant women. Frequencies were computed to describe the pregnant women. Multinomial logistics regression statistical modeling was fitted to identify correlates of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum. Results were presented in the form of percentages and odds ratio with 95% Confidence Intervals. Statistical significance was declared at p-value of 0.05.
RESULTS: The overall proportion of perceived maternal and newborns care continuum community acceptance was 93.30% (95%CI: 91.61%, 94.41%). However, only 1/3 of women, i.e., 33.66% (31.42%, 35.96%) and 31.93 (29.60%, 34.36%) respectively perceived that most and few people in their community encourage women to obtain the three domains of maternal and newborns care continuum. Women age, secondary educational status, contraceptive ever use history, health facility as desired place of delivery and residing in Oromiya regional state were found to increase the likelihood of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum. On the contrary, higher birth order, rural residence, higher wealth index and family member as desired birth attendant were factors lowering this likelihood.
CONCLUSIONS: This suboptimal level of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum by most people in the community signals that interventions and programs are required to nurture a positive influence of the community on women to complete the care continuum. Context specific and age sensitive programs and interventions which aimed in choice based contraceptive provision, empowering women to choose their childbirth attendant and place; and postpartum contraceptive use counseling are imperative to improve perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum. These interventions need to target younger, less educated, economically disadvantage, rural women and those with polygamous marriage. Improving birth preparedness and complication readiness and installing the inter-pregnancy preconception care packages are imperative in this regard. Enhancing mechanisms for incorporating community input is the core implication. These include strengthening the implementation of community score cards; and testing and scaling up the community maternal and newborns health family meetings.

articles.title: Five-year trends in Malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation at Yejube health center, Baso Liben district, East Gojjam zone, Ethiopia, 2020-2024: Implications for Malaria elimination.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains a major global public health problem, with an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly in the WHO African Region. Ethiopia continues to face substantial malaria transmission and has adopted an elimination strategy emphasizing surveillance, early diagnosis and treatment, and integrated vector control. Assessing local temporal, species-specific, demographic, and seasonal patterns is essential to guide targeted malaria elimination efforts.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the five-year temporal trend of malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation among patients attending Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A facility-based retrospective study was conducted in Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia, using laboratory records from January 2020 to December 2024. All individuals tested for malaria by microscopy during this period were included. Data on test results, Plasmodium species, age, sex, year, and month of diagnosis were extracted from laboratory logbooks. Data were entered in EpiData 4.2, then analyzed using SPSS 24. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression were used to assess malaria test positivity and associated factors. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 7,806 blood films were examined from 2020 to 2024, of which 1,066 were positive for malaria, yielding an overall test positivity rate of 13.65% (95% CI: 12.91-14.44%). Annual positivity declined from 20.08% in 2020 to 4.95% in 2023, followed by a resurgence to 14.66% in 2024. Plasmodium falciparum accounted for 49.6% of confirmed cases, followed by P. vivax (43.3%) and mixed-species infections (7.0%). Although P. falciparum predominated in 2020, P. vivax predominated from 2021 onward. Malaria test positivity was significantly higher among males than females (16.7% vs. 10.1%; p < 0.001) and differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001). Monthly positivity peaked in October (21.5%) and November (20.3%), with the lowest rate in February (3.9%). In multivariable logistic regression, males had higher odds of malaria positivity than females (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.56-2.06). Compared with individuals aged ≥60 years, the odds were higher among children aged under five years (AOR = 9.27, 95% CI: 1.27-67.77), individuals aged 15-29 years (AOR = 8.39, 95% CI: 1.15-61.27), and those aged 30-59 years (AOR = 9.60, 95% CI: 1.31-70.25). Compared with August, the odds of malaria positivity were significantly higher in September, October, November, and May, but significantly lower in February.
CONCLUSION: Malaria test positivity at Yejube Health Center declined from 2020 to 2023 before resurging in 2024. Although P. falciparum predominated overall, P. vivax was the leading species from 2021 onward. Positivity was associated with sex, age, and month of diagnosis, with peaks in October and a secondary increase in May. These findings underscore the need for sustained surveillance and locally tailored malaria control strategies.
RECOMMENDATIONS: Strengthen malaria surveillance and seasonal preparedness, particularly before peak-positivity periods. Tailor prevention and health education to males and higher-risk age groups, and improve P. vivax diagnosis, treatment, and relapse prevention. Further studies incorporating population-based, meteorological, and entomological data are recommended to clarify transmission patterns and guide malaria control and elimination efforts.

articles.title: Clinical features, first aid practices, and hospital management of snakebites in Northern Uganda: A multi-facility cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Snakebite envenoming is a neglected tropical disease with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa, where weak surveillance, limited antivenom availability, and reliance on traditional remedies compound morbidity and mortality. Evidence on how snakebite cases are clinically managed in routine practice in Uganda remains scarce. We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study with retrospective abstraction of records from four purposively selected health facilities in Gulu and Arua Districts of Northern Uganda. Snakebite case records from outpatient, inpatient, paediatric, and intensive-care service points covering the period 2017-2021 were reviewed using a standardised abstraction tool. Descriptive statistics were computed in Stata version 14, with frequencies and proportions for categorical variables and medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) for continuous variables, both of which were right-skewed. All analyses were complete-case, and the denominator is reported wherever it differs from the full sample. We analysed 227 snakebite case records. Of these, 58.6% were female and the median age was 21 years (IQR 13-38); students or pupils accounted for 26.6% of the 192 records in which occupation was described. Most bites involved the lower limb (85.9%) and occurred in the second and third quarters of the year (59.9%). Snake species was undocumented in 76.2% of records. No pre-hospital first aid was recorded in 59.1% of cases; where first aid was documented it was usually harmful, most often a tourniquet (29.3%) or a herbal remedy (8.9%). The dominant clinical manifestations were pain (60.8%), swelling or blisters at the bite site (68.7%), and fang marks (26.9%). One or more features suggestive of systemic envenoming were documented in 18.5% of cases, of whom 33.3% received antivenom. Overall, only 15.0% of cases received antivenom, while supportive care predominated (intravenous fluids 68.1%, analgesics 64.2%, antibiotics 53.1%). Coagulation testing was rare (20-minute whole blood clotting test 17.3%; INR 12.0%). Overall, 93.4% of patients recovered, 3.1% died, 0.9% were referred to other healthcare facilities, and the rest (2.6%) had missing information on the outcomes. Snakebite management in Northern Uganda is largely symptomatic, with critical gaps in species identification, syndromic assessment, coagulation testing, antivenom utilisation, and pre-hospital first aid practices. Strengthening health-worker training, improving documentation and surveillance, and community education on appropriate first aid are urgently needed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Health facility support and its influence on weight gain for neonates under Kangaroo Mother Care in Western Kenya.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) is a proven, low-cost intervention that enhances survival and growth among low-birth-weight (LBW) infants. This study assessed facility-level factors influencing neonatal weight gain during KMC in Western Kenya.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 275 mothers and caregivers of LBW infants across nine public health facilities. Data was collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed with SPSS v26. Binary logistic regression identified facility predictors of adequate daily weight gain (≥15 g/kg) at α = 0.05.
RESULTS: Only 38.2% of neonates achieved the recommended daily weight gain (mean = 12.96 ± 4.85 g/kg). The mean facility KMC implementation score was 10.78 ± 2.59 out of 19 (56.7 ± 13.7%). Factors independently associated with adequate weight gain included availability of breast pumps (AOR = 2.81, p = 0.009), milk banks (AOR = 3.22, p = 0.004), adequate food for mothers (AOR = 5.32, p < 0.001), seating for mothers (AOR = 3.72, p = 0.001), rooms for breast milk expression (AOR = 4.77, p < 0.001), easy-to-read KMC information (AOR = 2.86, p = 0.007), family-centered KMC support (AOR = 2.41, p = 0.032), and adequate staffing (AOR = 3.44, p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Effective facility support, particularly; maternal nutrition, infrastructure, comfort, family involvement, and staffing, is essential for improving neonatal outcomes under KMC. Strengthening these areas can enhance implementation quality and optimize weight gain among LBW infants in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Sensorimotor representation in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis compared with healthy controls: Proprioception, tactile acuity, left-right judgment, and motor imagery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is increasingly recognized as involving central sensorimotor alterations beyond structural spinal deformity, yet multiple sensorimotor domains have not been assessed comprehensively within a single AIS sample. This study aimed to compare tactile acuity, proprioception, left/right judgment, and motor imagery between adolescents with AIS and healthy controls, and to explore the associations of these sensorimotor domains with postural, body image, and health-related quality-of-life outcomes.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional case-control study, 41 adolescents with AIS and 42 healthy controls were assessed for tactile acuity, proprioception, left/right judgment, motor imagery, and pressure pain threshold, alongside body image, perceived spinal appearance, and quality of life.
RESULTS: Adolescents with AIS showed elevated paraspinal two-point discrimination thresholds at right T10, right L4, and left L4 (all adjusted p ≤ 0.040), but not at left T10, greater spinal repositioning errors in all four tested directions (all adjusted p ≤ 0.005), and poorer external visual motor imagery (adjusted p = 0.023). No between-group differences were found for left/right judgment or pressure pain threshold (all adjusted p > 0.05). Proprioceptive measures showed the strongest discriminative ability (lumbar right lateral flexion and lumbar flexion repositioning errors: AUC = 0.802 and 0.794, both p < 0.001), and a three-variable exploratory model correctly classified 82.9% of participants in the original sample and 81.7% after leave-one-out cross-validation. Body image disturbance and perceived spinal appearance were also worse in the AIS group, as were SRS-22 function, self-image, and subtotal scores (all adjusted p ≤ 0.012).
CONCLUSION: Adolescents with AIS showed impairments in tactile acuity, proprioception, and external visual motor imagery relative to healthy controls. These cross-sectional findings suggest that sensorimotor alterations may be relevant when designing rehabilitation strategies for this population, but they should be interpreted cautiously and do not establish causality. Larger longitudinal and neuroimaging-based studies are needed to clarify these relationships.

articles.title: Developing a syndromic case definition for timely surveillance of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) based on financial claim codes in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To improve pandemic preparedness, a sustainable and timely surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) is crucial. We developed and evaluated a proxy for syndromic SARI-surveillance using financial claim codes (DTC-codes).
METHODS: With data from 2016-2020 we compared DTC-codes with primary discharge diagnosis classified by ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as comparative benchmark for SARI, distinguishing between paediatric and adult populations, and pre- and during COVID-19-pandemic periods. To establish DTC-based proxies for SARI, accuracy metrics of individual and combinations of DTC-codes, and temporal trends were assessed. We retrospectively assessed its ability to detect COVID-19 epidemic patterns and its relationship with outcomes of existing respiratory surveillance systems.
RESULTS: For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections served as proxy for SARI. In the paediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory tract infection were used. While trends in DTC-based SARI proxies correlate with trends in ICD-10-coded SARI, the accuracy relative to this benchmark was moderate. The adult DTC-based SARI proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalisations during the pandemic and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections in the pre-pandemic period. The paediatric DTC-based SARI proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections.
CONCLUSION: We established DTC-based proxies for syndromic SARI-surveillance that appeared suitable to monitor SARI-trends. However, on the patient level the accuracy for ICD-10-coded SARI appeared moderate. Accuracy of the DTC-based SARI proxy and its ability to detect relevant epidemic signals, should be assessed prospectively with real-time data.

articles.title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Widespread misinformation influenced public understanding of disease risk and preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings such as Myanmar. Although preventive behaviors were generally protective, some actions driven by misinformation may have been ineffective or harmful. Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited. This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024. Participants were asked to retrospectively report their preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020-2022). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previous COVID-19 studies. The outcome variable was misinformation-based preventive behaviors, categorized as low (0-2 behaviors) and high (3-4 behaviors) engagement. Independent variables included sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media platform use, and selected health belief variables based on the Health Belief Model (HBM). A total of 434 respondents were included in the analysis, of whom 106 (24.4%) reported high engagement in MPB. Use of social media platforms other than Facebook was associated with higher engagement (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22-4.35). Participants reporting ≤3 hours and 4-6 hours of daily social media use had lower odds of MPB engagement compared with those reporting >6 hours (AOR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25-0.86; AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.24-0.95, respectively). Higher self-efficacy was independently associated with greater engagement in MPB (AOR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.03-2.82). MPB were more strongly associated with information environments and specific health beliefs than with sociodemographic characteristics alone. These findings underscore the importance of addressing misinformation and improving access to reliable health information to reduce engagement in non-evidence-based practices.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of Jordanian mothers regarding acute gastroenteritis in children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices of mothers living in Jordan regarding childhood acute gastroenteritis and to identify factors associated with poor knowledge, poor practice, lack of oral rehydration solution (ORS) awareness, and antibiotic use without medical consultation.
METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 730 mothers living in Jordan using a structured Arabic-language questionnaire. Participants were recruited through paediatric hospital settings and social media using convenience sampling. Composite knowledge and practice scores were calculated, and four multivariable binary logistic-regression models were fitted to examine factors associated with the prespecified outcomes.
RESULTS: The mean composite knowledge score was 15.73 ± 6.83 out of 28, corresponding to 56.18% of the maximum score, and 31.37% of participants were categorized as having poor knowledge. The mean composite practice score was 4.58 ± 1.71 out of 10, corresponding to 45.84% of the maximum score, and 61.23% were categorized as having poor practice. Overall, 54.52% identified three or fewer of the eight dehydration signs assessed, 59.59% were aware of ORS, and 3.15% selected ORS as their intended first action. Compared with residence in Central Jordan, residence in North Jordan was associated with higher adjusted odds of poor knowledge (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.38-3.45), poor practice (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.55), lack of ORS awareness (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.28), and antibiotic use without medical consultation (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.12-2.91). University-level education was associated with lower odds of poor knowledge and poor practice, while healthcare employment was associated with lower odds of poor practice and lack of ORS awareness.
CONCLUSION: Important gaps were identified in dehydration-sign recognition, ORS-related intended practices, and overall reported home-management practices. These findings support the development and evaluation of targeted caregiver-education initiatives emphasizing dehydration recognition, appropriate ORS use, safe medication practices, and timely care-seeking. Regional and educational differences may help identify groups requiring additional support; however, the observed associations should not be interpreted causally because of the cross-sectional design.

articles.title: Neurodevelopment among children under five years with sickle cell disease in Eastern Uganda: A propensity score analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We compared neurodevelopment among children under-five years with and without sickle cell disease in eastern Uganda.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study between March and September 2025 at the pediatric sickle cell clinic of Mbale Regional Referral Hospital. We included 350 children under five years (117 with sickle cell disease and 233 without sickle cell disease). The primary outcome was neurodevelopment assessed using the Malawi Development Assessment Tool. We performed independent sample t-tests to compare development for age z-scores between children with and without sickle cell disease. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses to calculate the effect of sickle cell disease on neurodevelopment.
RESULTS: The median age of the children was 40.9 months (interquartile range 27.8 to 54.3 months). Children with sickle cell disease had 0.89 lower DAZ scores compared to their peers without sickle cell disease. Among the children with sickle cell disease, those not enrolled on hydroxyurea had 0.4 lower DAZ scores in the social and language domains compared to those on hydroxyurea. The average exposure effect, obtained from the inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses, was -0.87, 95% CI [-1.19, -0.55] and the average exposure effect among the exposed was - 0.62 95% CI [- 1.01, - 0.23].
CONCLUSION: Children with sickle cell disease had lower developmental scores across all domains (social, gross motor, fine motor and language) compared to community controls. These findings highlight the developmental vulnerability associated with sickle cell disease in early childhood. Efforts towards timely screening and management of developmental delays among children are needed to improve their quality of life and long-term development. This may be through integration of neurodevelopmental screening into routine sickle cell disease care.

articles.title: A cross-sectional survey investigating norms and opinions concerning unvaccinated and vaccinated individuals (INOCU-VAX).
articles.abstract: Vaccine hesitancy remains a major public health concern, yet limited attention has been given to how individuals judge vaccine refusal versus acceptance. Clarifying how people judge the vaccination decisions of others may help identify the social norms that shape vaccination attitudes. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 2,115 adult patients within a large integrated US healthcare system from January 29 to February 19, 2025. Respondents rated their agreement with two statements regarding adult and parental vaccine refusal using a 5-point Likert scale. Responses were categorized as disagree/strongly disagree, neutral and agree/strongly agree for analysis. Additional measures included agreement with additional vaccine-related attitude items and demographic characteristics. Most respondents agreed or strongly agreed that people who refuse recommended vaccines for themselves or their children are making a bad decision, while very few agreed or strongly agreed that accepting recommended vaccines is a bad decision. Refusal-disapproving respondents were more likely to endorse vaccine benefits, support physician encouragement of vaccination, and report receiving recommended vaccines. They were also more likely to be older and report higher educational attainment, income, and liberal political views. Most respondents (even those who were refusal-approving) agreed that vaccines are beneficial. Although respondents differed markedly in how they judged vaccine refusal, most viewed vaccine acceptance positively. Normative disagreement appears to center on refusal rather than vaccination itself. Interventions that recognize this asymmetry may strengthen the design of communication and public health messaging strategies.

articles.title: Association between late-pregnancy household food insecurity and birth weight: Evidence from Propensity Score Matching.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food insecurity, a situation characterized by the absence or limited access to sufficient quality and quantity of food to meet dietary needs, exposes mothers to adverse pregnancy outcomes such as birth defects and low birth weight. Nevertheless, despite the massive burden of food insecurity among pregnant and lactating women residing in resource-limited and war-affected settings like Tigray, Northern Ethiopia, there is a scarcity of evidence on the effect of food insecurity on pregnancy outcomes, more specifically, birthweight. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the association between late-pregnancy household food insecurity and birthweight using propensity score matching.
METHOD: A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Northern Ethiopia, from December 2024 to March 2025. The study included 286 mother-newborn pairs recruited using systematic random sampling. Data were collected by trained midwives using a structured questionnaire and checklist. Food security status was assessed using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale. Data were analyzed in STATA version 19. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to assess the effect of household food insecurity on birth weight. Results of PSM are reported using the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) and the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATET). In addition, crude comparisons of mean differences were made using either the Independent-Samples T-Test or One-Way ANOVA. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05. In addition, subgroup, sensitivity, and robust multiple linear regression analyses methods are used to assess effect robustness and detect a dose-response relationship.
RESULT: The mean age of the mothers was 28.7 years (SD = 3.9). Of the total participants, 177 (61.9%) were food-secure, while the remaining 109 (38.1%) were food-insecure. Among the food-insecure group, 49 (17.1%) experienced mild food insecurity, 40 (14.0%) moderate food insecurity, and 20 (7.0%) severe food insecurity. The magnitude of low birthweight (LBW) among food-insecure mothers was 48.6%, compared to 11.3% among food-secure mothers. Overall, the prevalence of LBW was 25.5%. On average, the birthweight of newborns born to food-insecure mothers was 204 grams lower (ATE = -204.0, 95% CI: -289.3 to -118.7, p < 0.001) than that of newborns born to food-secure mothers. Furthermore, the birthweight of newborns born to food-insecure mothers was 218 grams lower compared to the birthweight they would have had if their mothers had been food secure (ATET = -218.3, 95% CI: -411.2 to -25.3, p = 0.027).
CONCLUSIONS: Late-pregnancy maternal food insecurity was significantly associated with decreased neonatal birthweight and an increase in the magnitude of LBW. Hence, addressing maternal food access could substantially decrease the burden of LBW and its related complications. During antenatal care, emphasis should be placed on assessing a pregnant woman's nutritional and food security statuses, and on integrating social and behavioral nutrition interventions to promote food security. In addition, a focus should be given to nutrition education before and during pregnancy. Policymakers should also ensure food security and improve nutritional conditions by empowering women.

articles.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Drought poses multiple health risks that may affect children both prenatally and during early childhood, yet the evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence from observational studies assessing the association between drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life and child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD4202338273). We searched 18 databases and complemented the search with grey literature and manual reference screening. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed risk of bias. Studies were eligible if they evaluated drought exposure during the prenatal period or childhood up to 5 years of age using any drought assessment method. Sixty-one publications met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were conducted in Africa (47.5%), and cross-sectional designs predominated (47.5%). Prenatal drought exposure was most consistently associated with adverse birth outcomes, low birthweight, impaired child growth, and increased infant mortality. Evidence for other outcomes, including anaemia and alterations in gut microbiota composition, was limited or inconclusive. Postnatal drought exposure was consistently associated with acute and chronic malnutrition and increased mortality risk, whereas evidence for infectious diseases and micronutrient deficiencies was more heterogeneous across studies. Across studies, the magnitude of these effects varied according to drought severity, socioeconomic conditions, and access to health services. Overall, the evidence suggests that drought exposure from pregnancy through early childhood is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes. Strengthening social protection, food security, and health interventions in drought-prone settings may help reduce the burden of these impacts on child health.

articles.title: Population-level associations of interpersonal trauma during childhood and adulthood with mental health and addiction problems.
articles.abstract: Interpersonal trauma during childhood and adulthood is associated with many adverse mental health and addiction outcomes. However, methodological issues of previous studies make it difficult to estimate and compare these associations at the population level. The objective of this study was to estimate and compare associations of self-reported interpersonal trauma during childhood and adulthood with several adverse mental health and addiction-related outcomes using population-based data. Using general population survey data among adults aged 18 + years (n = 4,016), we conducted logistic regression analyses to estimate the association between interpersonal trauma (never, childhood only, adulthood only, childhood and adulthood) and seven outcomes including psychological distress, suicidal ideation, ADHD symptoms, hazardous drinking, daily cannabis use, problematic electronic device use, and problem gambling. We also estimated population attributable fractions for any lifetime trauma in the seven outcomes. Overall, 18.3% of adults reported interpersonal trauma (9.2% childhood only, 5.0% adulthood only, and 4.1% both childhood and adulthood). In our main models, interpersonal trauma was significantly associated with psychological distress, suicidal ideation, ADHD symptoms, hazardous drinking, daily cannabis use, and problematic electronic device use, but not problem gambling. There was no evidence of interaction between childhood trauma and adulthood trauma for any of the outcomes either on the multiplicative or additive scale. Population attributable fraction estimates of lifetime trauma were significant for all seven outcomes ranging from 5.5% to 12.4%. Interpersonal trauma during either childhood or adulthood is strongly associated with, and may account for a significant proportion of, mental health and addiction problems at the population level. Based on current evidence, policymakers should place a higher priority on developing prevention strategies for interpersonal trauma to reduce the burden of mental health and addiction problems.

articles.title: Latent profiles of parental discipline in Singapore: Intergenerational patterns and links to adjustment in young adulthood.
articles.abstract: Using a person-centered approach, this paper examined parental discipline profiles in Singapore from parents' and young adults' perspectives, and how these were linked to young adults' adjustment. Two quantitative studies were conducted to explore parents' experiences of disciplining their children (Study 1) and young adults' experiences of receiving discipline (Study 2). Study 1 utilized the self-reported ISPCAN Child Abuse Screening Tool for Parents (ICAST-P) to document the frequency of use of 36 discipline methods. The ICAST-P was reworded for Study 2 to assess young adults' experiences of being disciplined. Latent class analysis identified three groups of disciplinarians in each study. Study 1 (N = 747 parents; 80.7% mothers) showed that 14.6% of participants were harsh disciplinarians (high psychological-physical/violent discipline), 54.5% were high psychological-low physical/violent disciplinarians, and 30.8% were low psychological-physical/violent disciplinarians. Parents who endorsed physical discipline and had been physically punished during childhood were more likely to be harsh disciplinarians. Study 2 (N = 667; 74.3% females; age 18-25) showed three similar groups: harsh disciplinarians (4.0% mothers; 6.1% fathers), the high psychological-moderate physical/violent discipline group (34.0% mothers; 37.7% fathers), and the moderate psychological-low physical/violent discipline group (62.0% mothers; 56.1% fathers). Young adults whose parents used moderate psychological and low levels of physical/violent discipline had the least emotion dysregulation, the best parent-child relationship, and the highest self-esteem. The potential long-term impact of harsh discipline and intergenerational transmission of harsh discipline are discussed.

articles.title: Beyond generalizations: Understanding adolescent social networks in American Indian communities.
articles.abstract: American Indian (AI) adolescents experience disproportionately high rates of substance use, yet the role of substance use and other individual characteristics in friendship network formation within AI-majority reservation schools remains understudied.
