Disruption of circadian rhythms and mitochondrial transport, 2 fundamental homeostatic systems, are increasingly recognized as independent contributors to vascular pathology. However, their integrated molecular crosstalk in KD remains completely uncharted.
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to identify and validate a mitochondrial transport andcircadian rhythm (MRC)-related molecular signature in KD. The secondary objectives were to resolve MRC-defined molecular subtypes, to nominate and characterize a candidate hub gene, to define its cellular distribution, and to prioritize candidate therapeutic compounds.
METHODS: First, Peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic datasets of KD patients were analyzed. GSE68004 was interrogated via Limma, GSVA, and WGCNA to isolate MRC-associated shared DEGs. Second, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and 3 machine learning algorithms (RF, Lasso and SVM-RFE) were deployed in GSE63881 for molecular subtype identification and diagnostic model construction, with independent diagnostic validation in integrated GSE73463 and GSE73462. Next, leveraging single-cell transcriptomic data from peripheral blood samples of KD patients (GSE24757), we resolved the spatiotemporal dissemination and functional evolution of the hub gene. In addition, deep learning-driven drug screening (DrugReflector) and molecular docking nominated a candidate compound in GSE18606. Finally, differential expression of the hub gene was validated using q-RT-PCR in clinical samples from KD patients.
RESULTS: The integrated MRC-related signature robustly stratified KD patients into 2 distinct molecular subgroups. FNDC5 was identified as an NK-distributed and MRC-related pathogenic factor in KD. BRD-K10482608 was nominated as a computationally predicted candidate targeting FNDC5 for KD.
CONCLUSION: This study provides the first pathway-anchored MRC-related signature in KD together with a validated framework for molecular stratification. FNDC5 is put forward as a prioritized, hypothesis-generating candidate of KD vasculopathy, and BRD-K10482608 as a computationally nominated starting point for future functional and nursing pharmacological testing.

articles.title: Challenges in left bundle branch area pacing in children and congenital heart disease: technical limitations, diagnostic pitfalls, and physiologic insights.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) in children is complicated by small cardiac dimensions, congenital heart disease (CHD), and the uncertain applicability of adult diagnostic criteria. This study evaluated paediatric LBBAP procedural success, technical adaptations, and diagnostic challenges.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Retrospective analysis of consecutive patients ≤ 18 years of age undergoing attempted LBBAP between January 2021 and June 2025. Sixteen patients (median 13.3 years) were included; three of them had CHD. Transoesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) was used to guide most procedures (15 out of 16). In structurally normal hearts, LBBAP success was 61.5%, correlating with older age (P = 0.048). Standard adult-configured sheaths caused oblique septal trajectories; conversely, atrial-septal-oriented sheaths (C315-S4/S5) ensured perpendicular fixation, enabling success in children weighing as little as 20.2 kg. Final V6 R-wave peak time (V6RWPT) < 75 ms had a poor specificity (11%) in confirming left bundle branch capture, with 53.8% of the patients met this threshold during right ventricular septal pacing. Similarly, the adult V6-V1 interpeak interval criterion (>44 ms) yielded a suboptimal overall diagnostic accuracy of 37.5%. Successful LBBAP was associated with reduced left ventricular end-diastolic dimension Z-scores (P = 0.045) and septal-to-posterior wall motion delay (P = 0.048). In CHD cases, scarring and cardiac rotation rendered standard electrical criteria non-diagnostic; however, TEE-guided left ventricular subendocardial placement maintained stable pacing and preserved synchrony.
CONCLUSION: Paediatric LBBAP requires adapted delivery sheaths to overcome geometric mismatches. Adult electrocardiographic criteria, including V6RWPT and V6-V1 interpeak difference, lack accuracy to define LBB capture in children. Clinically, LBBAP effectively improves left ventricular dyssynchrony.

articles.title: Psychometric properties of the Peruvian version of the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal problems are frequent in the adult population. The Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) assesses the presence of musculoskeletal symptoms across nine body regions, and its total score represents an index of symptom burden across regions; however, psychometric evidence for its use in Peru is lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To translate the NMQ into Peruvian Spanish and evaluate its structural validity, internal consistency, measurement invariance, and validity based on relationships with external variables in a sample of Peruvian adults.
METHODS: A psychometric study was conducted with 1,215 participants. The mean age was 22.7 years (SD = 8.3), and 73.0% were women. The NMQ was translated and back-translated into Peruvian Spanish. Structural validity was evaluated through confirmatory factor analysis using the WLSMV estimator. Internal consistency was estimated using McDonald's omega and Cronbach's alpha. Measurement invariance according to sex and age was examined using multigroup CFA and MIMIC models, respectively. Validity based on relationships with external variables was evaluated through correlations with sleep problems, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: The one-factor scoring model showed sufficient structural validity: χ²(27) = 210, CFI = 0.957, TLI = 0.942, SRMR = 0.067, and RMSEA = 0.075 (95% CI: 0.065-0.084). Standardized factor loadings ranged from 0.67 to 0.77. Internal consistency was sufficient (ω = 0.794; α = 0.799). The NMQ symptom-burden index showed moderate positive correlations with sleep problems (ρ = 0.465), anxiety symptoms (ρ = 0.458), and depressive symptoms (ρ = 0.402), all p < .001. Measurement invariance according to sex and age was supported.
CONCLUSION: The Peruvian version of the NMQ showed psychometric evidence for its one-factor model, supporting its use for accurately assessing musculoskeletal symptoms in Peruvian adults.

articles.title: A matched, real-world observational study of the burden of osteogenesis imperfecta and healthcare resource utilization in Ontario, Canada.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by bone fragility and deformity. This study aimed to estimate the incidence and prevalence of OI in Ontario, Canada, and to describe the burden of illness (BOI) among patients with OI.
METHODS: A retrospective, population-based, matched observational study was conducted using Ontario health administrative data from ICES (formerly Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences). Patients with OI were identified using ICD-10-CA codes from hospital and emergency department records between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2021. The study included an incidence and prevalence cohort and a BOI cohort, with the latter exact-matched to controls (general population without OI) on age, sex, and geography. The BOI cohort was followed for one to three years. Outcomes included OI incidence and prevalence, patient demographics, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), direct healthcare costs, and fracture rates.
RESULTS: The study identified 565 patients with OI, with a median (IQR) age of 14 (5-37) years (57% children aged 1-17) and 48% male. The annual incidence of OI ranged from 0.14 to 0.46 per 100,000, while prevalence stabilized at 3.9 per 100,000 over the study period. Fracture rates were higher among patients with OI than controls, with a mean (SD) rate of 0.7 (0.9) fractures per person per year. Rates were particularly high among children, at 0.8 (0.9) fractures per person per year. Patients with OI had significantly higher HCRU compared to controls, with greater mean numbers of specialist visits (29.1 [35.8] vs. 4.9 [12.4]), general practitioner visits (18.8 [32.1] vs. 7.6 [9.7]), emergency department visits (4.9 [10.1] vs. 1.1 [2.1]), and hospitalizations (1.7 [2.0] vs. 0.1 [0.5]) (all p < 0.001) over the follow-up period. The mean total cost (excluding Ontario Drug Benefit costs) per OI patient over the three-year follow-up was also higher than controls ($47,348 [$77,161] vs. $4,667 [$16,480]; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first real-world estimates of OI incidence and prevalence in Ontario, highlighting its significant healthcare burden, as well as the need for improved interventions to reduce fractures and associated burden and further research to improve the management and outcomes of OI patients.

articles.title: Effect of six weeks of ankle stretching exercises on ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated the effect of six weeks of ankle-stretching exercises on anterior knee pain (primary outcome) and ankle dorsiflexion range of motion, genu recurvatum, stride length, and walking speed (secondary outcomes) in children. The study was motivated by the role of ankle dorsiflexion range of motion in lower-limb function.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial with pre-test-post-test design, 40 children aged 6-10 years were assigned to an intervention group (n = 20) or a control group (n = 20). The intervention group performed ankle-stretching exercises for six weeks; the control group continued usual activities without intervention. Ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and genu recurvatum angle were measured with a goniometer, anterior knee pain was assessed using the Wong-Baker FACES Scale, and stride length and walking speed were recorded with the Kinova tool. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to assess between-group effects at a significance level of 0.05.
RESULTS: The Mann-Whitney U test showed significant between-group differences at post-test for dorsiflexion range of motion of the soleus and gastrocnemius, anterior knee pain severity, and genu recurvatum angle (P < 0.05). Marginal means analysis confirmed the effectiveness of the exercises on dorsiflexion (soleus and gastrocnemius) and anterior knee pain (P < 0.05). ANCOVA indicated no significant change in stride length or walking speed after six weeks (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Six weeks of ankle-stretching exercises significantly improved ankle dorsiflexion, anterior knee pain, and genu recurvatum in children with ankle pronation. This low-cost intervention may be a useful component of clinical management; however, because walking speed and stride length did not improve, combining stretching with strengthening or gait-specific training may be required for broader functional gains.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: IRCT20240306061185N7, retrospectively registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials on 2026-06-09.

articles.title: Cognitive Enhancement in Neurodevelopmental Disorders Through a Dimensional Lens: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Research on cognitive interventions in neurodevelopmental disorders has largely been organized by diagnosis. This scoping review took a dimensional perspective instead. It examined which cognitive dimensions these interventions target in different diagnostic groups, what kinds of intervention are used, and whether cognitive gains are accompanied by changes in everyday functioning.
METHODS: Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for studies published up to 29 September 2026. Primary intervention studies in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism, specific learning disorder, intellectual disability or related conditions were eligible if they reported both cognitive and functional outcomes. Interventions were classified with a five-category taxonomy, cognitive outcomes were grouped by dimension, and study quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.
RESULTS: Of 1868 screened records, 167 studies (173 reports) were included. Most evaluated remediation (80.2%), usually in school-aged children. Working memory, attention and inhibition were measured in all major diagnostic groups, whereas social cognition was studied mainly in autism and phonological processing mainly in specific learning disorder. Cognitive outcomes improved in 52.7% of studies and functional outcomes in 44.3%. Functional improvement was reported by 68.3% of uncontrolled studies, 36.5% of controlled studies and 26.5% of studies meeting at least four appraisal criteria. Academic achievement was the functional outcome in 64.7% of studies, and only 15.0% followed participants for six months or longer.
CONCLUSION: Several cognitive targets are shared across diagnoses, which is consistent with a dimensional view. The current evidence, however, cannot show that choosing interventions by cognitive profile works better than diagnosis-based care. Improvements on cognitive tasks carry over to daily functioning only inconsistently, and less often in well-controlled studies. Future trials should recruit participants by cognitive profile, measure functional outcomes beyond academic achievement and include longer follow-up.

articles.title: Associations of Serum Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid and Docosahexaenoic Acid Levels with Pediatric Sleep Disorders: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study investigates the serum levels of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) among children with sleep disorders, to generate preliminary hypotheses for future research.
METHODS: A total of 95 consecutively enrolled children newly diagnosed with sleep disorders from January to July 2024 were included in this cross-sectional observational study. Blood GABA and DHA levels were measured using API 4500 liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry system. Sleep disorders were classified by physicians according to ICSD-3 criteria based on structured parental interviews supplemented by brief sleep habit questions, without objective sleep monitoring such as polysomnography or actigraphy.
RESULTS: No significant differences in GABA and DHA serum levels were found between genders. Within these children diagnosed with sleep disorders, significant inter-age differences in serum GABA and DHA were observed, younger patients exhibited higher serum GABA and DHA relative to older patients in the same clinical sample. Children with insomnia showed lower serum GABA than those with parasomnia (unadjusted for age confounding). A positive correlation between GABA levels and maternal education was observed. No significant difference in DHA was observed between insomnia and parasomnia. Maternal education was positively correlated with GABA in univariate analysis, but this association did not remain significant in multivariable models.
CONCLUSIONS: Younger children with sleep disorders had higher GABA and DHA serum levels, and children with insomnia had lower GABA than those with parasomnia, whereas no significant difference in DHA was observed between these two groups. These cross-sectional correlational findings cannot establish causality. Definitive evaluation of serum GABA and DHA as candidate biomarkers requires further studies.

articles.title: Addressing loneliness and social isolation in at-risk groups during COVID-19 and beyond: a qualitative study in Switzerland.
articles.abstract: When Switzerland implemented public health measures against COVID-19, certain populations were particularly at risk of loneliness and social isolation, e.g., adolescents and young adults, older people, and migrants. This retrospective qualitative study aimed to explore stakeholders' experiences and perspectives on addressing loneliness and social isolation among these at-risk populations, with particular attention to the contextual, protective, and barrier factors shaping these experiences. It included 36 participants across six focus groups who provided social support to at-risk groups during COVID-19 in both the German- and French-speaking parts of Switzerland. The data were analysed using applied thematic analysis. Three overarching themes were developed: (1) communication and design of public health measures, (2) seizing and adapting existing resources, and (3) establishing a culture of social relationships. According to a socio-ecological framework for loneliness and social isolation during COVID-19, this study shows the interplay between the organisational and institutional levels to which participants belonged and different levels of the social system. Stakeholders perceived that their provision of social support was connected to individual initiatives, pre-existing interpersonal relationships and community support networks. Further, poor policy communication and a lack of acknowledgement of at-risk groups' social needs impacted the ability to address loneliness and social isolation. Stakeholders described opportunities to maintain social support within pandemic restrictions, noting that Swiss public health measures provided some room to meet social needs. Their accounts suggest that future preparedness should consider social relationships alongside infection prevention, pointing to specific approaches that require further safety evaluation and ethical assessment.

articles.title: Communicating dermatologic drug safety: a comparative evaluation of United States and United Kingdom pharmacovigilance systems using dapsone as a model medication.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance systems are essential for identifying adverse drug reactions (ADRs) that may not be recognized during premarketing clinical trials. Although the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS) and the United Kingdom Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) Yellow Card Scheme share the common objective of medication safety surveillance, little is known about how these systems differ in organizing and communicating postmarketing safety information to clinicians. This study compared the clinician-facing organization, accessibility, and communication of postmarketing safety information between the FDA AEMS Public Dashboard and the MHRA Yellow Card Interactive Drug Analysis Profile (iDAP) using dapsone as a representative dermatologic medication.
METHODS: A cross-sectional comparative pharmacovigilance study was conducted using publicly available FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card data extracted on June 29, 2026. Descriptive analyses characterized adverse-event reports, patient demographics, clinical outcomes, MedDRA Preferred Terms, and System Organ Class distributions. The two pharmacovigilance platforms were qualitatively compared using a predefined framework assessing data accessibility, organization, clinical usability, and research utility.
RESULTS: The FDA AEMS identified 4,793 reports associated with dapsone-containing products, including 3,686 (76.9%) classified as serious and 280 (5.8%) reporting death. The MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identified 699 reports comprising 1,701 adverse reactions, including 559 (80.0%) serious reports and 25 (3.6%) fatal outcomes. Both systems demonstrated overlapping patterns of reported adverse reactions. Despite similar pharmacovigilance outputs, substantial differences were observed in the communication of safety information. The FDA emphasized downloadable datasets, customizable searches, and case-level transparency to facilitate secondary pharmacovigilance analyses, whereas the MHRA prioritized standardized, drug-specific summaries, hierarchical MedDRA organization, integrated visualizations, and contextual guidance to support rapid clinical interpretation.
CONCLUSIONS: The FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identify similar postmarketing safety profiles for dapsone while employing distinct approaches to communicating pharmacovigilance information. These complementary strengths suggest that future clinician-facing pharmacovigilance platforms should integrate the analytical flexibility of the FDA with the standardized, medication-specific communication strategies of the MHRA to improve the translation of postmarketing safety data into dermatology practice while preserving scientific transparency.

articles.title: Insights into the Genomic Characteristics of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from Pediatric Bloodstream Infections in Beijing, China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bloodstream infection (BSI) caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a serious and urgent threat for hospitalized patients. While the epidemiological characteristics of pediatric CRKP have been increasingly reported, the genomic architecture, plasmid replicon profiles, and mobile genetic environments underlying carbapenemase dissemination in pediatric bloodstream isolates remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing on 91 non-duplicate CRKP isolates recovered from pediatric bloodstream infections to characterize their genetic features.
RESULTS: The CRKP population showed a highly structured lineage distribution, dominated by ST11-KL47 and ST20-KL28. Five isolates co-harboring bla KPC-2 and bla NDM-5 were identified. ST11 isolates were characterized by the frequent co-occurrence of bla KPC-2, bla CTX-M-65, rmtB, and IncFII(pHN7A8)/IncR replicons, whereas ST20 isolates were consistently associated with bla NDM-5, bla CTX-M-15, and the IncX3 replicon. Phylogenetic comparison with publicly available ST11 genomes showed that most local ST11 isolates clustered within a locally enriched ST11 subclade, suggesting local persistence or expansion of this clade in the pediatric setting. Analysis of carbapenemase genetic environments revealed that bla KPC-2 was located within a conserved Tn6296-like structure, ISKpn27-bla KPC-2-ISKpn6-korC, in most bla KPC-2-positive isolates. In contrast, bla NDM-5 showed a conserved core structure, bla NDM-5-bleMBL-trpF, followed by three downstream structural variants.
CONCLUSION: This study reveals lineage specific resistance architectures among pediatric CRKP bloodstream isolates. The dominant ST11-KL47 lineage was associated with a KPC-2-centered resistance profile and IncFII/IncR replicons, whereas ST20-KL28 was associated with NDM-5, CTX-M-15, and IncX3. The conserved Tn6296-like bla KPC-2 context and the heterogeneous downstream structures surrounding bla NDM-5 highlight differences in the local genetic environments of the two major carbapenemase determinants. These findings emphasize the importance of genomic surveillance to track lineage-associated resistance architectures and monitor high-risk clones in pediatric CRKP infections.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Genomic Comparison Study on Streptococcus agalactiae Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance Determinants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Group B Streptococcus (GBS), primarily Streptococcus agalactiae, is a significant opportunistic pathogen responsible for neonatal sepsis, meningitis, and infections in immunocompromised individuals. The C5a peptidase, encoded by scpB, represents a key invasin potentially involved in GBS colonization of damaged epithelium. However, the distribution and genomic context of the bca-cfb-scpB-lmb virulence cluster across diverse GBS isolates remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: In this study, a clinical GBS strain Guangzhou-SAG092 isolated from a patient with invasive infection in 2018 underwent complete genome sequencing using PacBio technology. We performed comparative genomic and SNA-based genome phylogenetic analyses of 85 complete GBS genomes, comprising 83 publicly available NCBI complete genomes plus Guangzhou-SAG036 and Guangzhou-SAG092. The dataset included isolates from 11 countries; host metadata were available for 77 isolates (41 human and 36 non-human), and 8 unknown-host isolates were excluded from host comparisons. Virulence factor distribution, especially the invasion-associated gene scpB, was analyzed. Statistical comparisons were performed to assess differences in virulence gene distribution between human and non-human isolates.
RESULTS: Strain Guangzhou-SAG092 was identified as sequence type ST-885, with a genome size of 2,265,243 bp containing 2,230 predicted genes. The genome harbors 19 identified virulence factor genes, including the bca-cfb-scpB-lmb cluster. The scpB gene was present in 84 of 85 Strains, with only strain YZ1605 lacking this gene. Significant differences were identified in the distribution of certain virulence genes between human and non-human isolates. All 85 Strains carried macrolide resistance genes, 40 carried tetracycline resistance genes, 8 carried aminoglycoside resistance genes, 2 carried phenolic resistance genes, and 3 carried glycopeptide resistance genes. Guangzhou-SAG092 carried aph(3')-IIIa, tetO, tetM, ermB, and cat but was phenotypically susceptible to all 10 tested antibiotics, indicating a genotype-phenotype discordance.
CONCLUSION: This genomic characterization provides a foundation for understanding the distribution of the bca-cfb-scpB-lmb virulence cluster in GBS. However, gene carriage alone does not establish pathogenicity or host adaptation, functional and expression studies are required to determine the biological significance of these associations.

articles.title: Fever management and parental anxiety in a pediatric emergency department: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fever, often associated with considerable parental anxiety, is one of the most common reasons for pediatric emergency department visits. Parental anxiety could be related to how parents manage childhood fever. This study aims to describe parental fever management practices and state anxiety among parents presenting to a pediatric emergency department and investigate the relationship between these variables.
METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2025 and February 2026 in the pediatric emergency department of a state hospital. The sample consisted of 360 parents of children aged 0-6 years who presented with fever and met the inclusion criteria. Data were collected through the Personal Information Form, the Parent Fever Management Scale, and the State Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The relationship between parental state anxiety and fever management scores were analyzed using Pearson's correlation and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses.
RESULTS: While the Parent Fever Management Scale mean score was 31.37 ± 6.82, the State Anxiety Inventory mean score was 48.47 ± 16.36. A significant positive correlation was found between fever management scores and parental state anxiety (r = 0.471, p < .001). Hierarchical regression analysis showed that after adjustment for the variables was included in the model, state anxiety was positively associated with fever management scores (β = 0.315, p < .001).
CONCLUSION: Parental fever management practices were positively associated with state anxiety levels. Healthcare professionals should consider parental anxiety when providing education and counseling about childhood fever management. Further intervention studies are needed to determine whether interventions addressing parental anxiety can improve the appropriateness and evidence-based nature of fever management practices.

articles.title: Epidemiology, risk factors, and antimicrobial susceptibility of nasopharyngeal bacterial colonization in children: A prospective study using culture and PCR.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSES: To investigate bacterial carriage among Taiwanese children, focusing on colonization patterns, risk factors, and antibiotic susceptibility.
METHODS: In this prospective hospital-based study, children aged 1 month to <13 years were recruited from well-child/vaccination clinics, general pediatric outpatient clinics, and pediatric inpatient wards from March to November 2025. Nasopharyngeal specimens were analyzed using culture and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed for cultured isolates. Risk factors for carriage were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 346 children, carriage of Moraxella catarrhalis (59%) was most prevalent, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae (35.8%), Haemophilus influenzae (23.1%), and Staphylococcus aureus (15.6%), as determined by combined culture and qPCR results. PCR increased detection and identified frequent co-colonization (42.5%). S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae carriage peaked at 1-2 years, whereas S. aureus showed a U-shaped distribution. Daycare attendance (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 7.761, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.396-17.738), recent upper respiratory tract infection (aOR = 4.704, 95% CI: 2.626-8.428), allergic diseases (aOR = 3.441, 95% CI: 1.857-6.379), and prior otitis media (aOR = 2.385, 95% CI: 1.151-4.943) were independently associated with carriage. Penicillin resistance in S. pneumoniae was low (5.3%, non-meningitis breakpoints). Ampicillin resistance was common in H. influenzae (63.8%) and M. catarrhalis (54.3%), but both remained susceptible to amoxicillin-clavulanate (93.6% and 100%).
CONCLUSIONS: Nasopharyngeal carriage in children is common, often polymicrobial, and age-dependent. PCR improves detection over culture. Local carriage surveillance may complement clinical isolate data and help monitor antimicrobial resistance trends.

articles.title: Metabolic-reproductive axis in normogonadotropic anovulation: a comparative study of polycystic ovary syndrome and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare hormonal and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction (HPOD), with particular emphasis on kisspeptin and ghrelin concentrations and on PCOS subsets characterized by hyperandrogenemia (HA), insulin resistance (IR), and obesity.
METHODS: The prospective study involved women aged 18-45 with menstrual irregularities. Participants underwent gynecological evaluations, including pelvic ultrasound, and biochemical serum analyses to assess hormonal and metabolic parameters.
RESULTS: Kisspeptin (p = 0.003) and ghrelin (p = 0.006) concentrations were significantly higher in PCOS than in HPOD. Distinct hormonal and metabolic profiles characterized PCOS, HPOD, and PCOS phenotypes. In PCOS, kisspeptin concentrations were higher in women with IR (p < 0.001) and HA (p = 0.003), whereas ghrelin concentrations did not differ by IR (p = 0.611) or HA (p = 0.153). Neither kisspeptin (p = 0.428) nor ghrelin (p = 0.240) differed by BMI category. Kisspeptin concentrations were positively correlated with ghrelin, thyroid-stimulating hormone, IR indices, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6, and negatively with sex hormone-binding globulin and free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). Ghrelin concentrations positively correlated with dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate and negatively with free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). There were fewer significant correlations in HPOD. In multiple regression, ln(IL-6) was an independent positive predictor of ln(kisspeptin) (β = 0.296, p = 0.027) and fT4 a negative predictor (β=-0.059, p = 0.027), while for ln(ghrelin) only 17-OH-progesterone remained a positive independent predictor (β = 0.042, p = 0.019), with metabolic markers losing significance.
CONCLUSIONS: The lack of classical PCOS markers as independent predictors suggests that kisspeptin and ghrelin are regulated by primary inflammatory, thyroidal, and steroidogenic axes, with kisspeptin appearing inflammation-sensitive and ghrelin steroidogenesis-related, supporting a multi-axial model of PCOS.
STUDY REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov(NCT06793098), on January 20, 2025.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype spectrum of ACAN variants in children with short stature: a national cohort and literature review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heterozygous ACAN variants have been reported in cases with short stature, mild skeletal dysplasia, and advanced bone age. The purpose of this study is to examine the phenotypic features of pediatric cases with ACAN gene variant in Turkey.
MATERIALS-METHOD: The is a retrospective design study, includes short stature children with ACAN gene variants. Anthropometric data, dysmorphic findings, bone age and genetic analysis results of the cases were examined.
RESULTS: A total of 29 pediatric cases with ACAN gene variants, were included. The median age at presentation was 5.4(1.2-14.8) years. At admission, median height SDS was - 2.98(-1.14, -6.34), 26 cases (89.6%) were prepubertal and 3 cases (10.6%) were pubertal. Dysmorphic findings were frontal bossing, relative macrocephaly, flat nasal root, bulbous nasal tip, high-arched palate, midfacial hypoplasia, coarse face, short neck, and ptosis. Bone findings included genu varum deformity, short extremities, brachydactyly, pre-axial polydactyly, chest deformities, scoliosis, coxa valga, lordosis, metaphyseal irregularity, epiphyseal irregularity and platyspondyly on radiographs. The accompanying diseases were Chiari type 1 malformation, tethered cord, syringomyelia, and nonossifying fibroma. Advanced bone age at presentation was detected in 15(51.7%) cases. A total of 12 cases were given rhGH treatment, median Δheight SDS was + 0.29 (- 0.58;+1.86).
CONCLUSION: Aggrecanopathy/aggrecan-related dysplasia is one of the skeletal dysplasias that cause short stature. Contrary to common findings, advanced bone age and osteo-articular complications are not mandatory and have not been demonstrated in every case. ACAN gene variants should also be taken into consideration in the differential diagnosis of cases with proportionate, and familial short stature.

articles.title: Phenotype-guided multiplex molecular profiling in children with food-associated anaphylaxis of unknown trigger.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Identifying the culprit allergen remains challenging in some children with food-associated anaphylaxis despite comprehensive routine evaluation. This study evaluated the clinical contribution of phenotype-guided interpretation of multiplex molecular allergen profiling in children whose reactions remained unexplained after conventional assessment. This retrospective study included children aged 1-18 years evaluated at a national tertiary pediatric allergy center between January 2020 and January 2026. ALEX2 profiles were interpreted alongside exposure history, reaction phenotype, cofactors, conventional allergy investigations, and clinical follow-up. Diagnostic certainty was categorized as confirmed, probable, possible, or unresolved. Among 1640 food-associated anaphylactic episodes, 53 episodes in 33 children remained unexplained after routine evaluation. ALEX2 testing was performed in 30 children, representing 49 episodes. Overall, 26/30 children (86.7%) received a molecularly supported clinical classification: 7 confirmed, 10 probable, and 9 possible; four remained unresolved. Seven classifications were challenge-confirmed, including six nsLTP-associated phenotypes confirmed by supervised food-exercise challenge and one poppy seed allergy confirmed by oral food challenge. The most frequent phenotype was nsLTP-associated food allergy (11/30, 36.7%), accounting for 22 episodes. Other classifications included oral mite anaphylaxis, shrimp allergy, Alternaria-associated food allergy, wheat-dependent exercise-induced anaphylaxis, serum albumin-associated food allergy, and profilin-associated food allergy.
CONCLUSION: Phenotype-guided interpretation of multiplex molecular allergen profiles supported clinically meaningful classification in most children with unexplained food-associated anaphylaxis. Molecular diagnostics should be used to generate clinically testable hypotheses and guide targeted confirmation rather than to establish causality from sensitization alone.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Conventional allergy testing may fail to identify the trigger in a small subset of children with food-associated anaphylaxis. • Multiplex molecular testing can detect sensitizations not captured by routine diagnostic evaluation.
WHAT IS NEW: • Phenotype-guided molecular profiling identified clinically relevant patterns, particularly nsLTP and oral mite anaphylaxis, in children with previously unexplained food-associated anaphylaxis. • Challenge-confirmed cases demonstrate that molecular findings are most informative when interpreted alongside clinical phenotype and cofactors.

articles.title: Theory of mind, autism-like traits, executive functions, and structural brain MRI findings in children with neurofibromatosis type 1.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aimed to examine social-cognitive difficulties in children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) by jointly investigating theory of mind (ToM), executive functions, and autism-like traits and to explore whether children with NF1 show structural differences in brain regions commonly implicated in social cognition and executive functioning. In this two-center cross-sectional study, 41 children aged 8-18 years were included, comprising 21 children with NF1 and 20 age- and sex-matched typically developing children. Participants underwent behavioral assessment, including parent-reported autism-like traits, everyday executive functioning, and direct measures of ToM. Structural brain MRI data were analyzed using automated volumetric and cortical thickness measures, focusing on these regions. Children with NF1 showed higher autism-like traits, lower everyday executive functioning in play and social routines, and poorer performance on an advanced ToM task. The NF1 group also had larger global brain volume reflecting widespread white matter expansion; lower cortical gray matter proportion and thickness in frontal, temporal, parietal, cingulate, and limbic regions; and larger subcortical structures including the amygdala, hippocampus, and thalamus. Exploratory within-group brain-behavior correlations were few and selective, none survived multiple-comparison correction, and none involved autism-like traits.
CONCLUSION: Children with NF1 display a multidimensional profile of social-cognitive difficulties together with structural differences indicating an imbalance between cortical and subcortical regions typically involved in social cognition. These structural differences offer a possible neurobiological substrate for the social-cognitive difficulties observed in NF1. Whether they account for these difficulties remains to be tested in samples powered to examine brain-behavior associations directly.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) frequently show executive dysfunction, autism-like traits, and theory of mind (ToM) difficulties. • These domains have rarely been examined jointly, or alongside brain structure, in the same children.
WHAT IS NEW: • Autism-like traits, everyday executive difficulties, and poorer ToM co-occurred in children with NF1. • The same children showed reduced cortical thickness and proportion with enlarged subcortical structures in regions implicated in social cognition, a candidate substrate for future brain-behavior studies.

articles.title: Predictors of anemia among children 6-59 months of age in Tanzania: a multilevel analysis of TDHS-MIS 2022.
articles.abstract: Anemia remains a major public health problem among children in developing countries, including Tanzania, despite ongoing nutritional and health interventions. This study aimed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with anemia in children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania. The study used data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS), a nationally representative cross-sectional survey conducted between February and July of 2022. Multilevel logistic regression was performed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with childhood anemia. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. A total of 4334 children aged 6-59 months were included in the analysis. The overall prevalence of anemia among children aged 6-59 months was 59.9% (95% CI: 58.48-61.39). Of these, 1.9%, 32.4%, and 25.6% had severe, moderate, and mild anemia, respectively. In the final multilevel model, children aged 6-23 months (AOR = 2.48; 95% CI: 2.01-3.07), those who were fourth or fifth born (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.25-2.52), those having recent diarrhea (AOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.11-2.21), those with stunting (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08-1.59), and those with positive malaria test results (AOR = 4.87; 95% CI: 3.06-7.75) had significantly higher odds of anemia. Maternal age of 15-24 years (AOR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05-2.27), maternal anemia (AOR = 1.74; 95% CI: 1.44-2.10), and lack of health insurance (AOR = 1.67; 95% CI: 1.09-2.55) were also associated with increased odds of childhood anemia, whereas maternal overweight was associated with lower odds of anemia (AOR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.59-0.96). Significant geographical disparities in childhood anemia were also observed across zones. Conclusion: Anemia affects approximately six out of ten children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania, indicating that it remains a public health concern in the country. Both individual- and community-level factors contribute to childhood anemia. Integrated interventions targeting child nutrition, malaria and diarrheal disease prevention, maternal anemia, and geographically tailored strategies are needed to reduce the burden of childhood anemia in Tanzania. What is known: • Anemia is a persistent public health problem among children under five years of age in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, with several individual-level risk factors (nutritional status, infections, and maternal characteristics) previously documented. What is new: • Using nationally representative data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS) and a multilevel logistic regression model, this study found that childhood anemia remains highly prevalent. • In addition to confirming established child-related predictors (younger child age, higher birth order, diarrhea, stunting, malaria infection, younger maternal age, and maternal anemia), this study demonstrated the independent influence of household factors (lack of health insurance) and community-level geographic disparities on childhood anemia.

articles.title: Early childhood outcomes in survivors of congenital chylothorax: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition and the most common cause of pleural effusion in neonates. Although neonatal morbidity and mortality have been described, outcomes beyond the neonatal period remain incompletely characterised. This study aimed to describe respiratory, developmental, and feeding outcomes during early childhood after congenital chylothorax. We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study including infants with congenital chylothorax managed at Lille University Hospital between 2011 and 2023. Cases were identified through an electronic database search and confirmed by individual medical record review. Follow-up data between 1 and 3 years of age included growth, respiratory symptoms and healthcare use, chylothorax recurrence, developmental outcomes, and feeding difficulties. Among 260 medical records screened, 34 infants with congenital chylothorax were included. Four died during the neonatal period. Follow-up data were available for 26 of the 30 survivors (87%) at a median age of 2.0 years [1.5-2.0]. Chylothorax recurred in one child (4%). Seventeen children (65%) received inhaled respiratory medications, 11 (42%) had respiratory symptoms, and 14 (54%) required hospital readmission. Developmental delay was identified in six children (23%) and feeding difficulties in four (15%). Nine children (35%) had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory medication use and hospital readmissions were frequent. Developmental and feeding difficulties were also documented in a subset of survivors. Although these outcomes cannot be attributed solely to congenital chylothorax, the findings highlight the importance of structured multidisciplinary follow-up.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition associated with substantial neonatal morbidity and variable outcomes. • Data beyond the neonatal period remain limited and are derived mainly from small cohorts, with respiratory and neurodevelopmental outcomes incompletely characterised.
WHAT IS NEW: • Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory symptoms and healthcare use remained frequent. • Developmental and feeding difficulties affected a subset of survivors, while 35% had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up.

articles.title: Admission systemic inflammatory response index and prognostic nutritional index in children with diabetic ketoacidosis-associated acute kidney injury: an exploratory retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Early identification of acute kidney injury (AKI) in children with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is important to enable timely management, but conventional markers based on serum creatinine may delay detection. The Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI) and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) have been associated with adverse outcomes in various clinical settings, but their association with DKA-associated AKI in children has not been investigated. This retrospective study included 122 children with type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by DKA. SIRI and PNI were calculated from admission blood samples. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, and multivariable logistic regression was performed. A nomogram was constructed and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. AKI occurred in 36 children (29.5%). Spearman correlation analysis showed that SIRI was positively correlated with creatinine, uric acid, and BUN, and negatively correlated with pH and bicarbonate, while PNI showed only weak correlations with these variables. In the fully adjusted model, admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration, remained independently associated with AKI (OR 1.132, 95% CI 1.051-1.243, P = 0.003), whereas SIRI showed a positive but non-significant association (OR 1.066, 95% CI 0.981-1.166, P = 0.143). PNI remained significant after adjustment for hydration-related variables and when post-rehydration PNI was used. In an exploratory analysis, the combined SIRI-PNI model achieved an AUC of 0.845 (95% CI 0.765-0.925), which was higher than that of SIRI alone (0.752) and PNI alone (0.746) (DeLong test, both P < 0.05). The nomogram showed acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ2 = 3.617, P = 0.890) and potential net clinical benefit. Conclusion: Admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration and disease severity rather than nutritional immune reserve, was associated with AKI in children with DKA In an exploratory analysis, the combination of SIRI and PNI provided moderate discriminative ability , supporting further evaluation of these routinely available indices for early risk assessment.

articles.title: Paired independent child-parent symptom reporting using the Turkish SSPedi and mini-SSPedi: psychometric evaluation and discordance patterns in pediatric oncology.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The Symptom Screening in Pediatrics Tool (SSPedi; ages 8-18) and mini-SSPedi (ages 4-7) are validated pediatric oncology symptom-screening instruments. Turkish versions are available, but paired independent child self-report and parent proxy-report within the same assessment have not been systematically evaluated in Türkiye. This study assessed the psychometric properties of paired SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting and characterized child-parent discordance. In this prospective observational study, conducted from January to December 2025 at Istanbul University pediatric hematology-oncology inpatient and outpatient clinics, child-parent dyads aged 4-18 receiving cancer treatment or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation were enrolled. Children completed SSPedi or mini-SSPedi independently, followed by an independent parent proxy-report on the same items. This approach differs from consensus-based co-SSPedi, which produces a single joint score through structured child-parent discussion. Psychometric evaluation included internal consistency, test-retest reliability, known-groups validity, convergent validity, and responsiveness. Convergent validity was examined using ChIMES, PeNAT, and FPS-R. Among 131 dyads, child self-report showed high internal consistency (α = 0.884-0.956; overall α = 0.922), as did parent proxy-report (α = 0.852-0.911). Combined child-parent scores correlated significantly with ChIMES (ρ = 0.268), PeNAT (ρ = 0.263), and FPS-R (ρ = 0.270). Known-groups validity and responsiveness were supported. Discordance varied systematically by symptom domain and developmental age: parents more often overestimated emotional distress, whereas children rated internal physical symptoms as more bothersome. Several individual correlations were marginally below the prespecified r ≥ 0.25 threshold. Future studies should determine whether consensus-based co-SSPedi provides additional clinical value beyond paired independent reporting in routine practice.
CONCLUSION: Paired independent SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated acceptable-to-strong psychometric properties and supports simultaneous child-parent symptom assessment in Turkish pediatric oncology.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Child self-report is the preferred approach for assessing subjective symptoms in pediatric oncology, but parent proxy-reports are often needed and may differ from children's perceptions.
WHAT IS NEW: • Paired independent Turkish SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated high internal consistency, acceptable convergent validity, and supported known-groups validity and responsiveness, and revealed systematic child-parent discordance, with parents rating emotional symptoms higher and children reporting greater burden from internal physical symptoms.

articles.title: Paediatric complex regional pain syndrome type 1 in Italy: a national survey of diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Complex regional pain syndrome type 1 (CRPS-1) is a rare but potentially disabling condition, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide clinical management. This study aimed to describe diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to paediatric CRPS-1 among Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to 34 Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. The questionnaire explored referral patterns, diagnosis, management strategies, availability of formal management protocols, disease burden, and follow-up procedures. Data were analysed descriptively. Twenty-three of 34 centres participated (67.6%). In most centres (17/23, 73.9%), the majority of patients were referred without a prior diagnostic suspicion of CRPS-1, and paediatric rheumatologists most frequently established the diagnosis. In 9/23 centres (39.1%), CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than 3 months after symptom onset in the majority of patients. Multidisciplinary care was widely adopted, with physiotherapy and psychological support routinely incorporated into clinical care in 22/23 (95.7%) and 21/23 (91.3%) centres, respectively. Initial management most commonly combined pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions (14/21, 66.7%). Pharmacological strategies were heterogeneous, with only 2/23 centres (8.7%) having a formal protocol. More than 90% of centres (21/23) rated the impact of CRPS-1 on patients and their families as severe or very severe.
CONCLUSION: This national survey shows substantial convergence in the core principles of multidisciplinary paediatric CRPS-1 management despite the absence of specific guidelines. Future collaborative research should strengthen the paediatric evidence base to support more robust clinical recommendations, while improving awareness among primary care paediatricians and other frontline clinicians should remain a priority to facilitate earlier recognition and timely referral.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Paediatric CRPS-1 is uncommon and potentially disabling, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide diagnosis and treatment. • Multidisciplinary rehabilitation and psychological support are key components of treatment, whereas pharmacological management remains poorly standardised.
WHAT IS NEW: • This first Italian multicentre survey shows substantial agreement on the core principles of multidisciplinary care, despite heterogeneity in pharmacological treatment and the limited availability of formal management protocols. • Delayed recognition remains a relevant challenge: in nearly 40% of participating centres, CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than three months after symptom onset in the majority of patients.

articles.title: Clinical analysis of rare chylous mesenteric cyst in children.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chylous Mesenteric Cysts (CMCs) are rare intra-abdominal masses in children, and definitive preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. This study reviews the diagnosis and management of CMCs at a single institution, with particular attention to clinical characteristics and the effectiveness of laparoscopic surgery. A retrospective analysis was performed on the records of all patients diagnosed with CMCs and treated with laparoscopic surgery at our institution between January 2020 and May 2026. Clinical manifestations, preoperative imaging data, surgical techniques, postoperative complications, and patient outcomes were evaluated. The study cohort included three girls and five boys. The median age was 4.2 years (range, 0.1 to 9.0 years), and the median weight was 14.5 kg (range, 4.9 to 32.5 kg). Abdominal pain and vomiting were the most common symptoms, occurring in 62.5% of cases. Four patients experienced cyst-related complications: three developed intestinal volvulus, and one presented with intestinal volvulus accompanied by intestinal obstruction. Sole cyst excision was conducted in two cases, while en bloc resection of the cyst with bowel was performed in six cases. Laparoscopic surgery was completed successfully in seven patients; one case required conversion to open surgery. The mean operative time was 103 ± 31 min. Pathological examination identified lymphatic malformation containing chylous fluid in all patients, findings consistent with mesenteric chylous cyst. No peritoneal infection, anastomotic leakage, or cyst recurrence was observed during short and medium term follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Chylous mesenteric cysts are most often definitively diagnosed during surgery. Once confirmed, prompt removal is recommended to prevent complications. Laparoscopic cyst excision or cyst excision with bowel resection appears to be a feasible approach for pediatric patients with uncomplicated chylous mesenteric cysts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • CMCs are rare, benign lymphatic malformations of the small-bowel mesentery in children that can result in severe complications such as intestinal volvulus and obstruction. Definitive pre-operative diagnosis of CMC is challenging, with most cases confirmed during surgery. • Surgical resection is the standard treatment. Open surgery has long been mainstream, while laparoscopy is increasingly applied.
WHAT IS NEW: • Transumbilical single-port laparoscopy appears feasible in selected paediatric patients with uncomplicated CMC. Extensive or poorly demarcated lesions may require conversion to open surgery. • Definitive preoperative diagnosis was uncommon in this small cohort and in the limited literature reviewed. The transumbilical approach may offer a cosmetically favourable incision and facilitate specimen extraction. Complete resection was followed by favourable short and medium term outcomes in this series; however, the small sample size and absence of a comparator group preclude firm conclusions.

articles.title: Lung ultrasound in congenital heart disease: from physiology to precision medicine.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 8 per 1000 births worldwide. Approximately 25% are classified as critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), requiring early diagnosis and neonatal intervention. Management of these patients is complex, dynamic and multiparametric. Respiratory complications are common during the hospitalization of patients with CHD. Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a valuable bedside tool to accurately assess lung aeration, particularly in critically ill patients in whom conventional imaging techniques may be difficult to obtain, impractical, or challenging to interpret. Although growing evidence supports the use of LUS throughout the perioperative and postoperative period, its application remains insufficiently characterized. LUS is evolving beyond its traditional role as a diagnostic imaging modality toward a dynamic bedside monitoring tool, with the potential to guide and optimize respiratory management before, during, and after cardiac surgery.
CONCLUSION: This review aims to summarize the current evidence regarding the use of LUS in this population and to highlight its potential role in the assessment and management of preoperative and postoperative respiratory complications.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Lung ultrasound (LUS) is a bedside, radiation-free imaging technique that provides real-time information on pulmonary aeration, interstitial edema, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and pneumothorax in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). • Pulmonary abnormalities in CHD are closely related to the underlying hemodynamic physiology and may change dynamically throughout the preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative periods. However, the clinical application of LUS in this population remains heterogeneous and is not yet routinely integrated into CHD management.
WHAT IS NEW: • This review summarizes the current evidence on LUS in CHD from a pathophysiological perspective, linking ultrasound findings to the underlying cardiac physiology and highlighting potential pitfalls in their interpretation. • LUS may contribute to a precision-medicine approach in children with CHD by integrating bedside pulmonary phenotyping with clinical and echocardiographic assessment, while identifying key areas where prospective studies are needed to establish standardized protocols and determine whether LUS-guided management improves clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and lipid parameters in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: systematic review & meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.

articles.title: Metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder regarding the caregiving process.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) regarding the caregiving process. The study was conducted with 46 participants responsible for the care of children with ASD. Data were collected between March and April 2026 using a metaphor form. The first part of the form included questions regarding sociodemographic characteristics, while the second part included the statement, "Caring for a child with autism spectrum disorder is like … because …" to identify participants' metaphorical perceptions of the caregiving process. Participants produced 46 metaphors, which were analyzed using content analysis and grouped into five themes: love, belonging, and hope; struggle and resilience; patience, acceptance, and adaptation; uncertainty, learning, and discovery; and intensive care and dependency. Regarding emotional valence, 28.3% of the metaphorical expressions were classified as positive, 37.0% as negative, and 34.7% as mixed. The theme of love, belonging, and hope had the highest frequency (28.3%). Descriptive cross-tabulations were also used to present the distribution of metaphor themes according to caregiving support, psychological support, and education about ASD. As no inferential statistical tests were performed, these distributions were interpreted descriptively and were not considered evidence of statistically significant differences, associations, or causal effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that caregivers' metaphorical perceptions of caring for a child with ASD reflect a multidimensional experience encompassing emotional attachment and hope as well as struggle, adaptation, uncertainty, and dependency.

articles.title: Ten myths about milrinone in pediatric cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe and increasingly common condition in children, representing a global health and economic burden. Inodilators (i.e., vasoactive agents with inotropic and vasodilator effects), most commonly dobutamine and milrinone, are the cornerstone of pharmacological treatment for CS in children. Although pediatric guidelines still recommend dobutamine as the first-line inodilator in CS, the use of milrinone has become predominant in this indication. Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase - 3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects and is commonly regarded as offering several theoretical advantages over dobutamine. Based on a critical review of current evidence, we examine here ten myths about milrinone in pediatric CS. The hemodynamic profile of milrinone in CS appears to rely primarily on vasodilation, with limited evidence for clinically meaningful inotropic or lusitropic effects. Current data support a neutral effect on myocardial oxygen consumption and an efficacy in preventing low cardiac output syndrome after pediatric cardiac surgery, while milrinone clearance is reduced in acute kidney injury with unclear clinical significance. However, no consistent evidence demonstrates milrinone's superiority over dobutamine in reducing mortality, length of hospital stay, or tachyarrhythmia, nor its greater efficacy in patients receiving beta-blockers. Its presumed benefits in newborns and in patients with right ventricular failure or pulmonary hypertension remain uncertain and warrant further investigation. What is known: • Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects. • Milrinone has become the preferred inodilator over dobutamine in pediatric cardiogenic shock. What is new: • Milrinone's efficacy appears to stem from vasodilation rather than significant inotropy or lusitropy. • No consistent evidence shows its superiority over dobutamine; further study is warranted.

articles.title: Gynecologic problems in adolescents and young adults: a 30-year referral cohort from a tertiary pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic in Korea.
articles.abstract: Adolescent gynecologic practice relies largely on adult-derived evidence, as age-specific data remain limited. We compared the spectrum of gynecologic problems in Korean adolescents and young adults and, as a secondary analysis, examined whether the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea has changed over three decades. We retrospectively reviewed 6,350 patients (adolescents aged 10-19 years, n = 2,841; young adults aged 20-29 years, n = 3,509) who attended a pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic between January 1995 and December 2024. Chief complaints, final diagnoses, and trends in age at diagnosis across three 10-year periods were analyzed. Menstrual disorders were the most frequent complaint in both groups but were more prevalent in adolescents (74.4% vs. 64.7%, p < 0.001). Endocrine disorders were the leading diagnosis, again more frequent in adolescents (36.4% vs. 28.2%, p < 0.001). Turner syndrome was the predominant cause of primary amenorrhea in adolescents (39.8%), and Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome in adults (62.0%). Polycystic ovary syndrome appeared more prevalent among adolescents with secondary amenorrhea (51.1% vs. 37.8%, p = 0.019), but this difference did not persist after applying adolescent-specific criteria (33.3% vs. 37.3%, p = 0.516). The median age at diagnosis of Turner syndrome decreased from 18 to 13 years (ρ =- 0.580, p < 0.001), whereas that of MRKH syndrome was unchanged (median 20 years; ρ =- 0.033, p = 0.731).Conclusion: Within the limits of a single-center referral cohort, the gynecologic disease spectrum is age-specific. Despite improved imaging access, diagnostic delay in MRKH syndrome showed no detectable improvement, supporting proactive pelvic imaging in adolescents with primary amenorrhea. What is Known • Adolescent gynecologic care is largely extrapolated from adult evidence, and long-term trends in the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea have not been characterized. What is New • Over 30 years, median age at Turner syndrome diagnosis fell from 18 to 13 years, whereas MRKH syndrome showed no detectable change from 20 years, indicating persistent diagnostic delay.

articles.title: Transpulmonary pressure monitoring in neonates and infants.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Transpulmonary pressure (PL) monitoring has been extensively studied in adult critical care, but evidence remains limited in neonates and infants despite their high vulnerability to lung and cardiac injury. This narrative review summarizes the physiological rationale, measurement techniques, and clinical evidence for PL monitoring in neonates and infants. PL is the distending pressure of the lungs. PL monitoring may help characterize lung stress and strain, assess respiratory effort, guide PEEP selection, and better understand cardiopulmonary interactions. Esophageal pressure monitoring remains the reference method for estimating PL, but its invasiveness and technical limitations restrict its use, particularly in extremely preterm neonates. Alternative approaches, including diaphragmatic electrical activity or airway occlusion maneuvers, may provide less invasive estimates, although most remain insufficiently validated in neonates. Current clinical evidence is scarce but suggests that excessive respiratory effort and elevated lung stress may occur in preterm infants, including during non-invasive respiratory support. PL monitoring may also help to optimize lung recruitment and cardiopulmonary interactions in infants with congenital heart disease or right ventricular failure.
CONCLUSIONS: PL monitoring offers a promising physiological approach to individualize respiratory support in neonates and young infants. Further studies are needed to validate minimally invasive or non-invasive surrogates of PL and to determine their clinical relevance in this population. Integration of automated occlusion maneuvers and other advanced monitoring tools into neonatal ventilators may facilitate the transition towards physiology-based, individualized respiratory and cardioprotective strategies.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Neonates' physiology may increase their vulnerability to ventilator-induced injuries. • Transpulmonary pressure (PL) reflects the true lung distending pressure, but neonatal evidence remains limited and esophageal pressure monitoring is challenging.
WHAT IS NEW: • Emerging alternatives (diaphragmatic electrical activity and airway occlusion maneuvers) could provide emerging approaches to estimate lung stress and respiratory effort. • PL-informed PEEP titration may help optimize lung recruitment to optimize hemodynamics in neonates with our without congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Association between breakfast frequency, school commuting mode, and psychological symptoms: a cross-sectional study of Chinese adolescents.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Psychological symptoms among adolescents are a rising global public health concern. Irregular breakfast habits and passive commuting may be associated with these symptoms, but large-scale national evidence from China is scarce. We examined independent and joint associations using nationwide Chinese adolescent data. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2025 among 52,035 adolescents aged 12-17 (26,104 boys, 25,931 girls) from 27 regions in China, using a multistage stratified cluster random sampling. Breakfast frequency and school commuting mode (active: walking or cycling; passive: motorized transport) were assessed via self-report questionnaires. Subclinical psychological symptoms were evaluated using the Multidimensional Subhealth Questionnaire for Adolescents (MSQA). Covariates included age, sex, monthly household income, sleep duration, body mass index, and grip strength. t-tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression are used to explore the associations. The proportions of adolescents breakfast frequency ≤ 1, 2-4, and > 4 times per week were 4.0%, 12.5%, and 83.4% and active and passive commuting accounted for 43.1% and 56.9%. The prevalence of emotional problems, behavioral problems, social adjustment difficulties, and subclinical psychological symptoms were 27.5%, 26.6%, 17.6%, and 20.8%. Fully adjusted models found independent associations of low breakfast frequency (≤ 1/week: OR 2.58, 95%CI 2.35-2.82) and passive commuting (OR 1.18, 95%CI 1.13-1.24) with symptoms; the combined category had the highest OR (OR 3.04, 95%CI 2.66-3.49, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Low breakfast frequency and passive commuting were associated with higher prevalence of subclinical psychological symptoms, with the highest OR in the combined category but no evidence of multiplicative interaction. Related interventions warrant evaluation.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Low breakfast frequency and passive school commuting are separately associated with adverse psychological outcomes in adolescents, but large nationwide evidence from China is limited.  • The joint association of these two modifiable daily behaviors with adolescent psychological symptoms remains unclear, including whether the association of one behavior varies according to the other.
WHAT IS NEW: • This large nationwide study found independent associations of low breakfast frequency and passive commuting with higher odds of subclinical psychological symptoms among Chinese adolescents. • Adolescents with infrequent breakfast consumption and passive commuting had the highest odds of psychological symptoms, with no statistical evidence of multiplicative interaction.

articles.title: Early-stage tendon stiffening precedes morphological thickening in pediatric type 1 diabetes: a quantitative shear wave elastography study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to comparatively evaluate Achilles tendon thickness and elastographic tissue stiffness in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) versus healthy controls, demonstrating the early radiological reflections of chronic hyperglycemia on pediatric tendon histomorphology. This prospective cross-sectional study included 60 pediatric T1DM patients and 60 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (mean age, 11.82 ± 4.02 years; range, 7-16 years). Glycemic control was evaluated using mean HbA1c levels. Anteroposterior Achilles tendon thickness was measured via B-mode ultrasonography. Quantitative tissue stiffness was assessed using Shear Wave Elastography (SWE), recording Young's modulus (kPa) and shear wave velocity (m/s) guided by motion stability and reliability indices. Bilateral Achilles tendon thickness did not differ significantly between the diabetic and control groups (p > 0.05). However, SWE revealed a highly significantly increased Young's modulus and shear wave velocity in the diabetic group compared to healthy controls (p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression identified diabetes duration as a significant independent predictor of increased tendon thickness (p < 0.05). Furthermore, left Achilles tendon velocity demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.940) in distinguishing diabetic tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: In children with T1DM, quantitative SWE detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness before macroscopic morphological thickening occurs on B-mode ultrasonography. While histopathological confirmation is lacking, this imaging-based observation of early-stage stiffening may serve as a non-invasive surrogate marker reflecting putative glycation-related microstructural alterations within the tendon matrix, presenting a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically reported in adult diabetic cohorts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • In adult diabetic cohorts, chronic hyperglycemia leads to macroscopic Achilles tendon thickening and biomechanical softening due to long-term collagen degradation. • The subclinical effects of type 1 diabetes on connective tissue histomorphology in the early pediatric stage remain largely unexplored.
WHAT IS NEW: • Quantitative Shear Wave Elastography detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness in pediatric type 1 diabetes before any macroscopic morphological thickening occurs.  • This early-stage tissue stiffening reveals a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically observed in adult diabetic patients.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of HPV vaccination in parents and patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection and a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers. Children with rheumatologic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy are at increased risk for persistent HPV infection, making vaccination a critical preventive strategy. The HPV vaccine is not included in Türkiye's National Immunization Program (NIP). This study aimed to assess HPV awareness, vaccine acceptance, and factors contributing to vaccine hesitancy among children with rheumatologic conditions and their parents. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 156 parent-child pairs attending the Pediatric Rheumatology Department at Dokuz Eylul University between August 2024 and August 2025. The survey was offered to 178 eligible parent-child pairs, of whom 156 agreed to participate (response rate, 88%). Inclusion criteria were ages 9-18 years, confirmed rheumatologic diagnosis, and current immunosuppressive therapy. Separate structured questionnaires were administered to parents and children to assess demographic characteristics, disease characteristics, immunization history, HPV knowledge, vaccine awareness, attitudes, and actual vaccination status. Median child age was 13 years; 81% of parents were female. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis was the most common diagnosis [87%]. HPV vaccine coverage was low [3% in both children and parents]. Among parents, 48% had heard of HPV and 47% were aware of the HPV vaccine. The most commonly reported barriers to HPV vaccination were insufficient knowledge [65% of children and 58% of parents], safety concerns [38% of children and 39% of parents], and lack of physician recommendation [63% of parents]. Logistic regression showed that female parent respondent status [OR = 7.3, 95% CI 2.2-24.6; p = 0.001] and university education compared with primary school education [OR = 12.9, 95% CI 1.8-90.4; p = 0.010] were associated with higher HPV awareness. Parents who had not previously obtained optional vaccines [not included in the NIP] for their children had lower odds of HPV awareness than those who had [OR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.69; p = 0.010]. Conclusions: HPV vaccination rates were very low among children with rheumatic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Higher parental HPV awareness was associated with female parent sex, higher parental education, and previous uptake of optional vaccines. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included insufficient knowledge, safety concerns, and lack of physician recommendation. These findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions and stronger physician-family communication regarding HPV vaccination.

articles.title: Prevalence and pretreatment predictors of acetaminophen treatment failure for patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of acetaminophen-induced patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) closure failure and evaluate pretreatment predictors of non-response in preterm infants.
