This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261472267). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Epistemonikos, and ProQuest were searched from inception to August 2026. Randomized and observational studies reporting PDA closure outcomes following acetaminophen treatment were included. Random-effects models pooled study-defined failure prevalence and crude odds ratios (ORs). Subgroup analyses and exploratory univariable meta-regression examined heterogeneity. Analyses used R version 4.4.1 with the meta and metafor packages. Twenty-eight studies contributed 1559 evaluable infants. The pooled failure prevalence was 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 85.8%; τ2 = 0.5886). Crude analyses linked extreme prematurity (OR, 2.97; 95% CI, 1.44-6.13) and female sex (OR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.05-2.55) to higher failure odds. Treatment context, dose, and duration showed significant subgroup differences; administration route did not. Meta-regression identified study-level associations involving birth weight, gestational age, small-for-gestational-age status, 1-min Apgar score, preterm premature rupture of membranes, and antenatal corticosteroid exposure. Individual adjusted analyses identified greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia as potential predictors.  Conclusion: Overall, approximately one-third of treated preterm infants met study-defined criteria for acetaminophen treatment failure. Extreme prematurity, greater ductal severity, and thrombocytopenia warrant further evaluation as prognostic factors. Prospective studies should standardize outcome definitions and validate prediction models. What is Known: • Acetaminophen is used for PDA closure in preterm infants, particularly when cyclooxygenase inhibitors are contraindicated. • Treatment response varies substantially, but acetaminophen-specific predictors of failure remain poorly defined. What is New: • Across 28 studies involving 1559 infants, acetaminophen treatment failed in 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%). • Extreme prematurity showed higher failure odds, while greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia emerged as potential predictors requiring validation.

articles.title: Familial Mediterranean fever across the age spectrum: pediatric and adult-onset differences in phenotype, diagnosis, treatment response, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an auto-inflammatory disease caused by pathogenic variants in the MEFV gene, leading to dysregulated pyrin inflammasome activation and excessive IL-1β-mediated inflammation. FMF is characterized by recurrent fever, serositis, and musculoskeletal manifestations, with substantial interindividual variability. Although traditionally considered a pediatric disease, FMF is now recognized as a lifelong condition extending into adulthood, with age-related differences in clinical presentation, genetics, treatment response, and long-term outcomes. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence comparing pediatric-onset disease, adult-onset FMF, and adults with childhood-onset disease across these domains. A structured narrative search of current evidence on FMF was conducted using different platforms, highlighting differences in clinical presentation, genotype-phenotype correlations, treatment response, and quality of life. Research indicates that pediatric-onset FMF is typically associated with earlier and more severe disease, higher attack frequency, and a stronger association with high-penetrance pathogenic variants, particularly M694V. In contrast, adult-onset FMF patients often exhibit milder and atypical manifestations, lower inflammatory burden, and a higher prevalence of heterozygous or low-penetrance variants, although diagnostic delays remain common in this population. Adults with childhood-onset FMF represent a distinct subgroup with cumulative inflammatory exposure and a higher risk of complications, including AA amyloidosis. Across all age groups, colchicine remains the cornerstone of therapy, although treatment challenges differ, with higher rates of colchicine resistance in children and greater intolerance and comorbidity-related constraints in adults.
CONCLUSION: Recognizing FMF as a disease continuum may enhance clinical awareness, facilitate earlier diagnosis, and support age-adapted, proactive management strategies aimed at reducing long-term complications and preserving quality of life.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FMF is clinically and genetically heterogeneous, with established differences between pediatric- and adult-onset disease. Delayed diagnosis and persistent inflammation contribute to preventable disease burden and complications.
WHAT IS NEW: • This review directly compares pediatric-onset, adult-onset, and adult with childhood-onset FMF across multiple domains. This distinction highlights how age at onset and cumulative inflammatory exposure may lead to different disease trajectories in adulthood, linking phenotype, diagnostic recognition, genotype, treatment timing, and long-term outcomes within an age-continuum framework.

articles.title: Association between neonatal phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Phototherapy has been widely used for the treatment of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia. However, concerns persist about its long-term neurological effects. While some studies report an increased risk of epilepsy after phototherapy, others found no association. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to examine the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. We followed the PRISMA guidelines for our meta-analysis. We searched six databases for studies investigating the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for quality assessment. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effect model in R software. Three studies with 632,227 participants met our inclusion criteria. Phototherapy was associated with a 37% higher risk of childhood epilepsy (HR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.13-1.67, p < 0.01; I2 = 30%). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant risk in boys (HR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.17-2.24, p < 0.01) but not girls (HR = 1.14, 95% CI = 0.92-1.41, p = 0.23). No association was found with febrile seizures (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 0.99-1.15, p = 0.09).
CONCLUSION: In this meta-analysis of three observational cohorts, neonatal phototherapy was associated with a possible increase in the risk of childhood epilepsy, particularly in boys; this finding depends on a small and methodologically heterogeneous evidence base, and residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded. Given the limited number of studies, the conflicting result from the most methodologically rigorous study, and the exploratory nature of the sex-stratified analysis, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as grounds to alter current phototherapy practice. Further well-designed studies controlling for confounders are needed.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Phototherapy is standard treatment for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and is generally considered safe. • Prior studies on phototherapy and childhood epilepsy have shown conflicting results.
WHAT IS NEW: • Pooled analysis of 632,227 infants show an association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy, particularlyin boys, but not febrile seizures. • The association may reflect residual confounding rather than a causal effect, and does not currently justify changingphototherapy practice.

articles.title: Association of differential growth and the incidence of respiratory distress in twins with birth weight discordance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Birth weight is linked to neonatal lung morbidities, including respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). Studies in singletons are often limited by confounding factors. Birth weight discordant (BWD) twins eliminate these biases, providing a unique model to isolate the impact of differential growth. Our aim is to compare the risk of RDS in the smaller twin versus the larger twin within discordant pairs. PubMed and preprint servers (medRxiv and Research Square) were systematically searched using a Boolean phrase combining terms such as twin, birth weight discordance, respiratory distress, and RDS, retrieving all relevant articles from August 21st 2025 to July 30th, 2026, with no language, geographical, or time restrictions. All studies reporting on the correlation of birth weight and the incidence of RDS in BWD twins were included in our review. The systematic review and meta-analysis is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251135439). A total of 21 studies were included in our review. RDS incidence was found to be lower in the lighter twin compared to its heavier co-twin (11.44% vs 14.67% respectively, RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.95, p = 0.01) with lower need for surfactant administration, a result which was reversed in the analysis for BPD incidence where the lighter twin was at greater risk (5.71% vs 2.76% in the heavier twin, RR 2.04, 95% CI 1.11-3.72, p = 0.02). Although the individual studies had contradicting findings, our study revealed no difference in all-cause mortality and the NICU length of stay.
CONCLUSION: Birth weight is an important risk factor for neonatal morbidities. Our review revealed that the lighter twin in BWD pairs is at a significantly lower risk of RDS and need for surfactant. On the contrary, the smaller twin demonstrated a statistically significant higher prevalence of BPD.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The impact of intrauterine growth restriction on neonatal lung maturation remains controversial, with singleton studies often limited by genetic, maternal, and environmental confounders. Birth weight discordance in twins offers a unique naturally controlled model to isolate the effect of growth restriction on respiratory outcomes.
WHAT IS NEW: • In birth weight discordant twins, the lighter co-twin faces a significantly lower risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and a lesser requirement for surfactant administration. Conversely, this risk profile reverses for chronic lung disease, where the smaller growth-restricted twin exhibits a significantly higher incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD).

articles.title: Changes in neuroinflammatory and blood-brain barrier-related markers during methylphenidate treatment in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to investigate within-participant changes in serum IL-6, S100B, and Claudin-5 levels during 3 months of methylphenidate treatment in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and to examine whether biomarker changes were associated with changes in ADHD symptom severity. This single-center, uncontrolled prospective observational study included 42 medication-naïve children aged 6-11 years with ADHD who completed 3 months of methylphenidate treatment. Serum IL-6, S100B, and Claudin-5 levels were measured at baseline and month 3. ADHD symptom severity was assessed using the Conners Parent Rating Scale-Revised: Short Form (CPRS-R:S) and the Conners Teacher Rating Scale-Revised: Short Form (CTRS-R:S). Associations between percentage changes in biomarkers and symptom scores were examined, with correction for multiple testing. Parent- and teacher-rated ADHD symptom severity decreased significantly over 3 months. Serum IL-6 and S100B levels also decreased significantly, whereas the change in Claudin-5 was not significant. A nominal inverse association was observed between percentage changes in IL-6 and teacher-rated symptom severity, but this association did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction.
CONCLUSION: Among children who completed the 3-month treatment period, methylphenidate was associated with reductions in selected peripheral biomarkers associated with inflammatory and glial processes. However, biomarker changes were not significantly associated with symptom changes after correction for multiple testing, and the uncontrolled observational design does not establish a causal effect of methylphenidate on these biomarkers.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07041333, registered on 19 June 2025. Prospectively registered.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Neuroinflammatory and blood-brain barrier-related alterations have been implicated in ADHD, but most available evidence is cross-sectional. • Longitudinal data on biomarker changes during methylphenidate treatment in medication-naïve children are limited.
WHAT IS NEW: • Three months of methylphenidate treatment was accompanied by reductions in peripheral serum IL-6 and S100B, whereas Claudin-5 did not change significantly. • Within-participant biomarker changes were largely unrelated to symptom changes after correction for multiple testing.

articles.title: How far have we come? Experiences and needs of parents of children with developmental disabilities in a Northeastern German region more than a decade after Germany's ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Appropriate support measures can help children with developmental disabilities participate in society. However, little is known about how these measures are perceived by their families. This study aimed to explore parents' experiences, challenges, and needs regarding existing support measures. Structured interviews were conducted with 68 parents of children aged 3-18 years with developmental disabilities in Northeastern Germany. The qualitative interview study included open-ended questions and one supplementary closed-ended question comprising several statements, each to be rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Responses from the open-ended questions were categorised inductively; rating responses were summarised descriptively. All parents gave specific descriptions of what they considered "good integration", most frequently mentioning growing up together, equal rights, and the removal of barriers. For motor impairments, visual impairments, and behavioural difficulties, more than half of responding parents rated the implementation of accessibility measures in their region as somewhat inappropriate or absolutely inappropriate. About one-third of parents mentioned authorities or service providers, such as the Youth Welfare Office or care services, as helpful, whereas almost one out of five did not mention any governmental measure they considered helpful. The most frequently mentioned wishes for improvement were less bureaucracy and easier access to information about support options.
CONCLUSION: Although many parents mentioned helpful support measures, important gaps remain. The findings highlight the need for improved information, tailored support, and efforts to ensure that existing policies and support measures have a more tangible impact on the daily lives of these families.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Participation of children with developmental disabilities and their families relies on the availability of appropriate support measures.
WHAT IS NEW: • Accessibility remains a challenge for children with development disabilities and their families, especially for motor and visual impairments and behavioural difficulties. Despite existing support measures in Germany, some parents did not identify any measure as helpful.

articles.title: KAWACALP study: the utility of serum calprotectin as a prognostic biomarker in Kawasaki disease.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess if serum calprotectin (sCP) can be used as a predictor of resistance to intravenous immunoglobulin treatment (IVIG) and coronary artery aneurysms (CAA) in Kawasaki disease (KD). A multicenter, observational, cohort study was conducted prospectively between September 2018 and February 2023. sCP was analyzed at four points in the evolution of KD in 74 patients from four Spanish hospitals. The sCP and other clinical and analytical values were compared between groups: IVIG responders or sensitive KD patients (SKD) versus IVIG nonresponders or refractory KD patients (RKD), and KD patients with CAA versus those without CAA. In refractory KD patients and in those who developed CAA, sCP was higher at the moment of diagnosis and remained elevated after treatment with IVIG, unlike what happened in sensitive KD patients and in those without CAA. A post-treatment sCP level ≥ 14.09 μg/ml predicted RKD with Sn 75% and Sp 72.97% (AUC 0.75). A pre-treatment sCP cutoff of ≥ 21.49 μg/ml predicted CAA with Sn:100% and Sp 71.05% (AUC 0.86). A post-treatment sCP value ≥ 14.76 μg/ml predicted CAA with S 71.43% and Sp 76.32% (AUC 0.74).
CONCLUSIONS: Serum CP at the time of diagnosis ≥ 21.49 μg/ml has a sensitivity of 100% to detect CAA. Therefore, if these results are confirmed in larger studies, sCP may be used as a prognostic biomarker in patients with Kawasaki disease, to detect early patients with a higher probability of CAA occurrence, guide treatment decisions and ultimately reduce cardiac complications.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • At present, no validated biomarkers allow early identification of IVIG resistance or predict coronary involvement in KD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • High serum calprotectin level at the diagnosis of KD and persistently elevated levels after IVIG treatment may identify patients at risk for IVIG resistance and coronary complications.

articles.title: Functional echocardiography for management of shock in neonates- a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neonatal shock is associated with a high case fatality rate. Detection and management of shock by monitoring only clinical parameters may be inadequate due to inconsistent association with tissue perfusion. We evaluated the efficacy of adding functional echocardiography to standard clinical assessment in improving short-term outcome in neonates with shock. This was an open-labelled randomized clinical trial conducted in level III NICU of a tertiary care hospital in India. Neonates born at 28-42 completed weeks of gestation and developing shock defined by presence of at least two of seven prespecified criteria: tachycardia, hypotension, prolonged capillary refilling time, low perfusion index, increased central-to-peripheral temperature difference, oliguria and metabolic acidosis were randomized into two groups: Echo group-shock managed using both standard clinical assessment and functional echocardiography and, Clinical group- shock managed using only standard clinical assessment. Primary outcome was survival without inotropic support at 72 h post-randomization. Secondary outcomes were time to hemodynamic stability, survival to discharge and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable in the two groups. Survival without inotropic support at 72 h was observed in 28 (73.7%) of 38 neonates in the Echo group and 13 (33.3%) of 39 neonates in the Clinical group (RR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.36-3.58, P = 0.0004; adjusted RR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.33-3.59). Hemodynamic stability was reached earlier in the Echo group (median, 3 vs. 5 h; P =  .001). Survival to discharge (73.7% vs. 59.0%; RR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.90-1.73) and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia (10.5% vs. 7.7%) did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, open-label trial, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h after randomization. Survival to discharge and severe brain injury did not differ significantly; the trial was not powered for these outcomes. Multicenter trials with blinded outcome assessment are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry of India Identifier (CTRI/2023/08/056672), registered on 21st august 2023.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Diagnosis of neonatal shock and initiating inotropes solely on the basis of clinical parameters like low BP or isolated tachycardia does not address the underlying physiology. • This practice may not help match the pharmacological action of drug to underlying cause.
WHAT IS NEW: • In a randomized trial of neonates with shock, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h (74% vs. 33%). • Effects on survival to discharge (74% vs. 59%) and severe brain injury were imprecise; multicenter trials are needed before routine use.

articles.title: Bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants: a prospective ultrasound study of intestinal structural development.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The preterm intestine undergoes rapid structural and functional maturation during late gestation and early postnatal life. Although abdominal ultrasound is increasingly used in neonatal care, quantitative descriptions of developmental variation in bowel wall structure and motility remain limited. In this prospective observational study, preterm infants born at ≤ 34 weeks' gestation underwent serial abdominal ultrasound examinations in a level III neonatal intensive care unit. A total of 260 longitudinal ultrasound scans were performed from early postnatal life through term-equivalent age. Bowel wall thickness (BWT) was measured in four abdominal quadrants using a standardized high-frequency ultrasound protocol. Small-bowel loops were identified using established sonographic criteria. Peristaltic activity was graded semi-quantitatively (0 = absent, 1 = intermittent, 2 = active) during standardized cine observation. Associations between postmenstrual age and ultrasound measures were evaluated using regression and correlation analyses accounting for repeated measurements within infants. Fourteen preterm infants contributed serial examinations spanning 26 to 37 weeks' postmenstrual age. BWT demonstrated a progressive increase with advancing maturity and consistent regional variability across abdominal quadrants. Peristaltic activity similarly increased with postmenstrual age, with a transition from absent or intermittent motility in earlier scans to active peristalsis at later ages. Structural and functional findings showed parallel maturational trends.
CONCLUSION: Bedside ultrasound enables quantitative assessment of intestinal structure and motility during preterm development. These findings provide longitudinal developmental imaging data describing intestinal maturation and support future studies examining intestinal adaptation and clinical outcomes in preterm infants.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Real-time assessment of neonatal bowel health remains a major clinical challenge with important knowledge gaps. Reliance on nonspecific clinical signs, delayed laboratory changes, and adjunctive abdominal radiographs often leads to late recognition of bowel injury, reducing opportunities for timely and targeted intervention. Abdominal ultrasound is emerging as a valuable tool for early detection of gut injury and for real-time monitoring, offering neonatologists a way to guide bedside decision-making more precisely..
WHAT IS NEW: • Provides prospective ultrasound characterization of bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants. • Demonstrates maturational and regional variation in intestinal wall structure during early life. • Establishes foundational developmental imaging data to support future longitudinal and outcome-based studies.

articles.title: Urinary exosomal C5b-9 as a non-invasive biomarker for diagnosis and monitoring of pediatric IgA nephropathy: a single-center prospective study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This exploratory study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and predictive value of urinary exosomal C5b-9 in children with IgA nephropathy (IgAN). A total of 70 children with biopsy-proven IgAN, 43 with non-IgAN glomerulopathies, and 30 healthy controls were enrolled. Urinary exosomal C5b-9 levels were measured at baseline and at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after renal biopsy. The diagnostic performance of baseline C5b-9 was assessed using ROC curve analysis. Multivariate logistic regression models were constructed to evaluate its independent association with 12-week remission. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using a repeated-measures mixed-effects model, and the predictive value of the early decline rate was assessed by ROC analysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were also performed. Baseline urinary exosomal C5b-9 levels were significantly higher in IgAN patients compared with non-IgAN patients and healthy controls (both p < 0.01). The area under the curve (AUC) for distinguishing IgAN from non-IgAN was 0.942, with an optimal cutoff of 227.36 ng/mL (sensitivity, 92.9%; specificity, 83.7%). The optimal cutoff for predicting 12-week non-remission was 287.90 ng/mL (AUC = 0.819; sensitivity, 75.7%; specificity, 71.9%). Low baseline C5b-9 (< 287.90 ng/mL) was associated with significantly higher cumulative remission rates (log-rank p < 0.01). Across three multivariate models, baseline C5b-9 remained independently associated with 12-week remission (OR range, 0.599-0.623, all p < 0.01). Longitudinal analysis revealed a significant time × group interaction (p = 0.002), indicating greater C5b-9 decline in remitted patients. The early decline rate (> 8.15% reduction by week 4) predicted remission with an AUC of 0.754 (sensitivity, 63.9%; specificity, 84.4%). Combination therapy showed a trend toward faster remission (HR = 1.856, p = 0.056).
CONCLUSION: Urinary exosomal C5b-9 may have potential as a non-invasive biomarker for diagnosing IgAN and predicting early treatment response in children. These exploratory findings suggest clinical utility and require external validation in larger cohorts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • IgAN is the most common childhood glomerulonephritis; diagnosis needs invasive biopsy. Complement activation (C5b-9 deposition) is involved. • Whole-urine C5b-9 has given inconsistent results, limiting its clinical use.
WHAT IS NEW: • Urinary exosomal C5b-9 may offer a stable, kidney-specific option. This pediatric study explored its potential in IgAN. • Urinary exosomal C5b-9 helped distinguish IgAN from other glomerulopathies (AUC = 0.942). Levels were linked to 12-week remission. An early decline by week 4 predicted later remission with 84.4% specificity.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and diagnostic challenges of Kawasaki disease in infants younger than 3 months: a 21-year single-center retrospective study from China.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) in infants younger than 3 months is uncommon but poses substantial diagnostic challenges because classical clinical manifestations are frequently incomplete during the early phase of illness. Delayed diagnosis increases the risk of coronary artery abnormalities (CAA), yet the clinical characteristics and diagnostic evolution of this age group remain insufficiently understood. We retrospectively reviewed all infants younger than 3 months diagnosed with KD at Peking University First Hospital between January 2005 and January 2026. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, echocardiographic features, treatment, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed. Particular attention was paid to the temporal evolution of clinical manifestations and coronary artery abnormalities during the diagnostic process. Fifteen infants were included in the study. Incomplete KD accounted for 86.7% (13/15) of cases. Gastrointestinal manifestations (53.3%), bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scar reactivation (60.0%), and respiratory symptoms (40.0%) were common and frequently resulted in an initial diagnosis of infection. Coronary artery abnormalities developed in ten patients during the disease course. Three infants had normal initial echocardiographic examinations but subsequently developed coronary artery abnormalities on repeat evaluation between fever days 7 and 10. Fourteen patients responded to initial intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment, whereas one patient was IVIG-resistant. Coronary artery abnormalities and other cardiac echocardiographic involvement resolved in all patients during follow-up.Conclusion: KD in infants younger than 3 months is characterized by an evolving clinical presentation in which classical clinical manifestations and echocardiographically detectable coronary artery abnormalities emerge sequentially rather than simultaneously. Recognition of this evolving diagnostic process may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Persistent clinical suspicion, together with longitudinal clinical reassessment and appropriately timed repeat echocardiography, may improve recognition before clinically significant coronary injury develops.

articles.title: Latent tuberculosis infection conversion and TST-IGRA agreement in BCG-vaccinated children with rheumatic diseases receiving biologic therapy: a 10-year single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess agreement between the tuberculin skin test (TST) and QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube (QFT-GIT) assay and describe latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening conversion during biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs). This 10-year retrospective cohort included children receiving bDMARDs. Baseline screening comprised TST and/or QFT-GIT and chest radiography, with follow-up testing as available. TST positivity was defined as ≥ 5-mm. Agreement and paired TST positivity were assessed using Cohen's kappa, and McNemar's test, respectively. Among 106 patients (49.1% female), median age at bDMARD initiation was 11.6 years. New LTBI screening positivity occurred in 14/87 (16.1%) with no positive baseline result. Overall, 31 (29.2%) received isoniazid, 19 before bDMARD and 12 during follow-up. TST-QFT-GIT agreement was moderate at baseline (n = 90; κ = 0.472) and fair at follow-up (n = 76; κ = 0.213). Paired TST positivity increased from 8.8% to 20.0% (n = 80; p = 0.012). New QFT-GIT positivity occurred in 6/74 patients (8.1%) with negative or indeterminate baseline results. Of 14 conversions, two were detected by both tests, eight by TST only, and four by QFT-GIT only. Conversion occurred with both tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors and non-TNF biologics, without significant between-group differences. No active tuberculosis developed during available follow-up.
CONCLUSION: New LTBI screening positivity occurred after initiation of both biologic classes in BCG-vaccinated children. Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at first follow-up. The clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain and requires interpretation in the context of BCG vaccination, prior tuberculin testing and TB exposure risk.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children receiving biologic therapy require LTBI screening because of risk of active tuberculosis. • BCG vaccination, immunosuppression, and the absence of gold standard complicate interpretation of TST and IGRA results.
WHAT IS NEW: • Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at follow-up, the clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain. • New LTBI screening positivity was documented during follow-up, after initiation of both anti-TNF and non-anti-TNF biologic agents.

articles.title: Image quality and procedural safety in neonatal brain MRI with and without sedation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neontal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is susceptible to motion artefacts, whereas pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia may cause cardiorespiratory adverse events. We compared image quality and adverse events across three MRI strategies in newborns: natural sleep without sedation, pharmacological sedation, and imaging during mechanical ventilation. We retrospectively analysed 151 brain MRI examinations performed in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between August 2013 and August 2024. Examinations were classified as non-sedated using a feed-and-swaddle approach (n = 21), pharmacologically sedated without intubation (n = 67), or performed in intubated and mechanically ventilated infants (n = 63). Motion artefacts and documented adverse events were compared between groups. Motion artefacts were more frequent in non-sedated examinations than in sedated or intubated examinations (85.7% vs. 32.8% and 25.4%, respectively; p < 0.001). Moderate/severe artefacts occurred in 14.3%, 7.5%, and 0%, respectively. No adverse events were documented in the non-sedated group, compared with 8/67 (11.9%) in sedated and 7/63 (11.1%) in intubated infants; this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.275). Within the sedated cohort, artefacts were more frequent with chloral hydrate, whereas respiratory complications occurred predominantly with propofol-based sedation.
CONCLUSION: Neonatal MRI strategies involve a clinically relevant trade-off between image quality and procedural safety. Natural-sleep MRI avoids pharmacological exposure and was not associated with documented adverse events but resulted in more motion artefacts. MRI strategies should therefore be individualized according to clinical condition and required diagnostic image quality.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Motion artefacts may compromise neonatal MRI, and pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia is frequently used to improve image quality. • Feed-and-swaddle MRI can avoid drug exposure, while sedative and anaesthetic agents may cause respiratory and haemodynamic adverse events.
WHAT IS NEW: • Direct comparison of three real-world neonatal MRI strategies demonstrates a trade-off between image quality and procedural safety: sedation and controlled ventilation reduced motion artefacts, whereas no adverse events were documented during natural-sleep MRI. • Exploratory analyses suggest differences between sedation regimens, with more artefacts after chloral hydrate and respiratory events occurring predominantly with propofol-based sedation.

articles.title: Kidney involvement is associated with glucose-insulin homeostasis in adolescents with newly diagnosed anorexia nervosa: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with multisystem medical complications, although kidney involvement (KI) remains an underrecognized component of the medical burden of the disease, particularly in adolescents. We aimed to characterize the spectrum of KI in adolescents with newly diagnosed AN by assessing both glomerular and tubular function and exploring clinical and metabolic correlates of renal abnormalities, including glucose-insulin homeostasis alterations. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 125 adolescents with newly diagnosed AN that underwent clinical evaluation, biochemical testing, and abdominal ultrasonography. KI was defined by the presence of reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), calculated using the modified Schwartz equation, and/or albuminuria, and/or renal tubular dysfunction. Glucose-insulin homeostasis was assessed using the Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). The cohort (75.2% female, mean age of 13.8 ± 2.3 years) showed KI in 31.2% of patients. Both urinary β2-microglobulin and eGFR were independently associated with HOMA-IR after adjustments (both p < 0.05). Renal parameters were not significantly associated with body mass index, heart rate, or FT3 concentrations (all p > 0.05). Urinary β2-microglobulin was positively associated with HOMA-IR (R2 = 0.12, p < 0.001), whereas eGFR was inversely associated with HOMA-IR (R2 = 0.06, p = 0.006). In adjusted analyses, both urinary β2-microglobulin and eGFR remained independently associated with HOMA-IR (both p < 0.05). Renal parameters were not significantly associated with body mass index, heart rate, or FT3 concentrations (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: KI was identified in nearly one-third of adolescents with newly diagnosed AN and involved both glomerular and tubular compartments. The association between renal parameters and HOMA-IR, together with the absence of associations with conventional markers of disease severity, suggests that renal abnormalities may coexist with alterations in glucose-insulin homeostasis at diagnosis. Comprehensive kidney assessment at diagnosis may improve the identification of KI and support individualized clinical monitoring in adolescents with AN.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Kidney involvement is an underrecognized complication of anorexia nervosa, although pediatric data remain limited, particularly regarding tubular abnormalities. • Creatinine-based assessment may not fully capture renal alterations in adolescents with anorexia nervosa.
WHAT IS NEW: • In adolescents with newly diagnosed anorexia nervosa, kidney involvement was detectable before nutritional rehabilitation and involved both glomerular and tubular compartments.  • Renal parameters were associated with glucose-insulin homeostasis alterations, suggesting coexistence of renal and metabolic abnormalities at diagnosis.

articles.title: Fetal hemoglobin fraction: a potential predictor of late-onset sepsis in very preterm infants.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Late onset sepsis (LOS) is included between the so-called oxidative stress-related diseases in preterm infants. Increasing evidence supports a protective role of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) against oxidative stress. We hypothesized that HbF blood fractions measured during the first weeks of life may be associated with the risk of developing LOS. We carried out a retrospective observational study on 166 preterm infants with gestational age <30 weeks. The primary endpoint of our study was the comparison of HbF fraction values between infants who developed LOS and those who did not during the first week of life. Fifty-six (34%) infants had LOS at the mean age of 14±8 and 22±15 days of life. Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life (HbF14) to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF14 decreased (OR 0.974, 95% CI 0.956-0.992; P=0.004) the risk of LOS. In ROC analysis, HbF14 showed moderate discriminative ability in predicting LOS, with an AUC of 0.676 and 95% CI 0.593-0.758.
CONCLUSION: Lower HbF fractions during the first weeks of life were associated with an increased risk of LOS, with HbF14 emerging as an independent protective factor. These findings confirm the role of HbF in modulating susceptibility to oxidative stress-related complications in this vulnerable population and the importance of maintaining its levels high.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Low fetal hemoglobin (HbF) fractions are associated with increased risk of oxidative stress-related complications of prematurity. Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is included among oxidative stress-related diseases.
WHAT IS NEW: • Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF fraction at 14 days of life is associated with decreased risk of LOS.

articles.title: Associations of intolerance of uncertainty, cyberchondria, and e-health literacy with parents' attitudes toward childhood vaccination.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study examined the associations of intolerance of uncertainty, cyberchondria, and e-health literacy with parents' attitudes toward childhood vaccinations. This descriptive and correlational study was conducted with 471 parents of children aged 0-5 living in eastern Turkey between February and July 2025. Data were collected using the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale, the Short Form of the Cyberchondria Scale, the e-Health Literacy Scale, and the Parental Attitudes about Childhood Vaccines Scale. Thirty-one percent of participants were vaccine hesitant. Parents with vaccine hesitancy had significantly higher intolerance of uncertainty and cyberchondria scores than those without vaccine hesitancy (p < .001). Correlation analysis revealed that parental vaccination attitude scores were positively correlated with intolerance of uncertainty (r = .277) and cyberchondria (r = .328), but negatively correlated with e-health literacy (r = -.239; p < .001). In the final hierarchical regression model, intolerance of uncertainty, cyberchondria, and e-health literacy collectively explained 13.7% of the variance in parental vaccination attitude scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher intolerance of uncertainty and cyberchondria scores were associated with less favorable attitudes toward childhood vaccinations, whereas higher e-health literacy scores were associated with more favorable attitudes.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: From a primary healthcare perspective, these findings highlight the potential role of family physicians, nurses, and midwives in addressing parents' concerns about vaccination, particularly those related to uncertainty, online health information seeking, and e-health literacy.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Intolerance of uncertainty and cyberchondria have been associated with parental vaccine hesitancy. • Previous studies have reported associations between e-health literacy and vaccination attitudes, although findings have varied across populations.
WHAT IS NEW: • In a sample of parents in Turkey, cyberchondria showed the strongest association with childhood vaccination attitude scores (β =.228), followed by intolerance of uncertainty (β =.127). • E-health literacy showed a weaker, negative association with vaccination attitude scores (β = -.115). Together, the three variables accounted for 13.7% of the variance in vaccination attitude scores.

articles.title: Polypharmacy and use of prescription medication in children and adolescents with life-limiting conditions-a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Children and adolescents (CA) with life-limiting conditions (LLC) are living longer thanks to better treatment but face substantial medication burden. We investigated polypharmacy and use of prescription medication in CAs with LLC compared to a comparison population of CAs with no LLC up to 25 years after diagnosis. This retrospective nationwide cohort study included all patients aged 0-21 years born in Denmark and diagnosed with an LLC between January 1, 1996, and December 31, 2021. Sociodemographic and prescription data were obtained from national registries. We assessed polypharmacy and the mean cumulative number of prescriptions at 1, 5, 10 and 25 years after diagnosis. We assessed concurrent polypharmacy (≥ 5 different prescriptions within 120 days before a follow-up time) and sequential polypharmacy (≥ 4 regularly dispensed prescriptions, defined as at least three prescriptions within 12 months before a follow-up time). We identified 98,508 CAs with LLC and 492,540 CAs with no LLC matched 1:5 on sex and age at diagnosis. Median follow-up was 9.4 years (interquartile range 4.8, 15.5) with 3608 deaths. One year after diagnosis, 4.53% of CAs with LLC were using ≥ 5 unique medications compared to 1.57% of population controls, while 2.1% of CAs with LLC were using ≥ 4 medications regularly compared to only 0.1% of population controls. CAs with a neurological or neuromuscular diagnosis and from families with lower education levels had the highest medication use.
CONCLUSIONS: Healthcare providers of CAs with LLCs must be aware of the impact of long-term polypharmacy and balance symptom control with the complexity of medication regiments, especially in children from families with lower educational levels.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children and adolescents (CA) with life-limiting conditions (LLC) are living longer and often receive multiple medications for long-term symptom management. • However, the prevalence of polypharmacy and patterns of prescription medication use over time across diagnostic groups and sociodemograpic factors in this population compared to the general pediatric population are unknown.
WHAT IS NEW: • The prevalence of polypharmacy was almost threefold higher among CAs with LLC compared to the general pediatric population at one year after diagnosis, with smaller yet elevated differences up to 25 years after diagnosis. • Anti-infectives, anti-epileptics, respiratory drugs, and anxiolytics/sedatives were most prescribed, and the highest overall medication use was observed among CAs with a neurological or neuromuscular diagnosis and those from families with lower parental educational attainment.

articles.title: Monitoring of pulmonary outcomes in paediatric cystic fibrosis patients treated with modulator therapy-a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Recently introduced CFTR modulator drugs have transformed the disease trajectories in people with cystic fibrosis. Children with cystic fibrosis, who would once have experienced progressive lung damage and pulmonary function decline from early life onwards, now, when treated with effective modulators, appear to have preserved lung structure and pulmonary function using conventional monitoring tools. However, since cystic fibrosis lung disease may still progress despite effective therapy, early detection of disease manifestation, disease progression, and the tracking of treatment responses remain crucial. Monitoring of lung disease in the current era of CFTR modulators, therefore, poses a fundamental challenge for cystic fibrosis clinicians and researchers. This narrative review summarises currently available monitoring tools for paediatric cystic fibrosis patients.
CONCLUSION: In children with cystic fibrosis receiving effective CFTR modulator therapy, spirometry remains an important component of pulmonary monitoring but may be insufficient to detect early or residual lung disease. Complementary approaches, including multiple-breath washout, oscillometry, and structural and functional lung imaging, can provide more sensitive assessment of pulmonary abnormalities and treatment responses. Further development of sensitive, non-invasive biomarkers of airway infection and inflammation, alongside evidence to guide the integration of these tools into routine clinical care, remains an important priority.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • CFTR modulator therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in cystic fibrosis, and children initiating effective modulators early in life frequently maintain normal or near-normal pulmonary function. • Conventional monitoring with spirometry, particularly FEV₁, has limited sensitivity for detecting early or residual cystic fibrosis lung disease.
WHAT IS NEW: • Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

articles.title: Evaluation of pediatric patients diagnosed with food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Food Protein-Induced Enterocolitis Syndrome (FPIES) is a non-IgE-mediated food allergy typically presenting in infancy with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. The absence of specific biomarkers complicates diagnosis and management. This study aimed to evaluate demographic characteristics, trigger food distribution, clinical phenotypes, and tolerance development in pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES. This cross-sectional study included pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES and followed at Ankara Etlik City Hospital between October 2022 and December 2025. Patients were re-evaluated for demographic data, trigger foods, phenotypic features, oral food challenge (OFC) outcomes, and tolerance development. A total of 63 patients were included (63.5% male), with a median age of 26 months (IQR 16-37). A total of 134 reactions were documented, with a median age at first reaction of 7 months (IQR 6-8). During first acute episodes, 19 patients required emergency care; three were hospitalized, and two required intensive care unit admission. Egg yolk was the most common trigger (51.5%), followed by cow's milk (21.2%), fish (18.1%), egg white (6%), and red meat (3%). Multiple trigger foods were identified in three patients. Phenotypic analysis revealed atypical FPIES in 10 patients and chronic FPIES in one patient. A total of 34 OFCs were performed for diagnostic confirmation and tolerance assessment. Reactions occurred in 11 tests, and eight required medical treatment. During follow-up, tolerance developed in 47.6% (n = 30) of patients, with a median tolerance age of 18 months (IQR 14-26). Tolerance was confirmed by OFC in 18 patients and by successful home reintroduction in 12.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, egg yolk was the predominant trigger food. Nearly half of the patients achieved early tolerance. Given the heterogeneous phenotypic spectrum of FPIES, increased clinical awareness and standardized management approaches are essential for optimal follow-up and prognosis assessment.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FPIES shows geographic variation in trigger foods and clinical presentation, and tolerance acquisition may differ according to the culprit food.
WHAT IS NEW: • Egg yolk was the predominant trigger in this cohort, while fish-induced FPIES showed significantly later tolerance acquisition, supporting food-specific timing of follow-up and re-evaluation.

articles.title: India's rising palliative care needs and the policy response: A review of state palliative care policies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The need for palliative care is increasing in India. As health is primarily a state responsibility, state governments play a key role in translating national priorities into policies. This study examined how national and state palliative care policies address these challenges.
METHODS: A documentary analysis of palliative care policies in India was conducted. Documents were identified through Google search, government website searches and expert consultation. Documents were reviewed against a framework based on the World Health Organisation public health model for palliative care development. Additional domains included paediatric palliative care, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, governance, financing, and cross-sectoral interventions.
RESULTS: The analysis included the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC) and policies from Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Goa. All policies supported institution and home-based care, emphasised opioid availability, promoted health-system integration, and included workforce training and community engagement. Kerala and Tamil Nadu provided the most comprehensive approaches to health-system integration, community participation, and implementation planning, while Kerala demonstrated the strongest commitment to research and diversified financing. Considerable variation existed in implementation readiness, monitoring and evaluation frameworks, governance arrangements, and financing mechanisms. Most policies incorporated monitoring structures, although only some specified indicators, targets, or review processes. Paediatric palliative care was inconsistently addressed, with most policies lacking actionable implementation strategies. Despite increasing needs associated with population ageing and chronic disease, only Goa explicitly identified older adults as a vulnerable population, and no policy addressed advance care planning. Cross-sectoral approaches were limited; only Kerala and Tamil Nadu included explicit mechanisms linking palliative care with social welfare and community support systems.
CONCLUSIONS: Indian palliative care policies align with core palliative care development domains but remain insufficiently responsive to demographic and epidemiological transitions. Strengthening age-responsive planning, paediatric palliative care, financing, and intersectoral social support could improve preparedness for future palliative care needs.

articles.title: Co-creating death and grief literacies with young people: A case-based example of youth engagement in research in Canada.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Death literacy refers to the knowledge and skills that make it possible to understand, gain access to, and act upon end-of-life and death care options. Grief literacy focuses on the capacity to access, process, and use knowledge related to experiences of loss. Despite growing attention to death and grief literacies in public health research, theory, and practice, young people are rarely involved as active contributors to their development, and often remain passive recipients of education about death, dying, and grief.
OBJECTIVE: Grounded in Childhood Ethics scholarship, this project aimed to explore: (a) how a multigenerational research team involving youth researchers and non-youth researchers experienced conducting a study on youth engagement in palliative and end-of-life care; and (b) the ways in which the research process could support the co-creation of knowledge on death and grief literacies.
DESIGN: A case-based approach was used to explore the experiences of multigenerational research team members involved in a national study on pediatric palliative and end-of-life care in Canada.
METHODS: Reflexive accounts from youth researchers (n = 2) and non-youth researchers (n = 4) were gathered during multiple reflexive team conversations.
RESULTS: Analysis of team member accounts identified five themes regarding the co-creation of death and grief literacies within a multigenerational research team, including: (1) challenging societal silences around death, dying, and grief among young people; (2) expanding death and grief literacies into social networks; (3) fostering trust and intellectual humility; (4) legitimizing youth researcher contributions; and (5) engaging in reciprocal learning.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that engaging young people in research on palliative and end-of-life care can function as a way of reflecting upon, expanding, and advancing death and grief literacies. We propose that death and grief literacies may be understood as participatory, relational, and multigenerational practices, and suggest implications for public health, palliative care, and youth engagement research and practice.

articles.title: Symptom burden and support needs of children with cancer at home: A creative qualitative study during treatment and end of life.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children with cancer experience distressing symptoms at home, but research on their experiences and needs is scarce. To inform the development of a new home-based symptom app, we aimed to gain insight into the symptoms, symptom bother, and experiences and needs of children and their families during treatment and end of life.
METHODS: A qualitative study design was applied. We conducted 11 generative interviews supported with LEGO® as engaging method to help participants visualize and talk about their experiences. Participants were five children (≥ 8 years) and ten parents of children (≥ 0 years) undergoing cancer treatment or receiving palliative care. End-of-life symptom experiences and needs were explored in a focus group with seven bereaved parents. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the data of interviews and focus group separately.
RESULTS: Participants reported a wide range of symptoms. The most bothersome physical and psychological symptoms reported in the interviews were nausea and feeling scared or worried. Bereaved parents identified nausea, fatigue, pain, and behavioral changes as the most bothersome symptoms during the last phase of life. Children and parents faced uncertainty in determining the cause and severity of symptoms, as well as how to manage them at home. They emphasized the need for clear guidance on when to seek medical support. Over time, children and parents became experts in managing symptoms. Bereaved parents highlighted the intense symptom burden in their child's final weeks and stressed the importance of swift and effective communication with healthcare professionals. Despite facing severe symptoms and the approaching end of life, families remained focused on making the most of each moment.
CONCLUSIONS: Families require clear guidance on recognizing and managing symptoms at home across the entire care continuum. Especially in the last phase of life, rapid communication between parents and healthcare professionals is crucial to alleviate distress and maximize comfort.

articles.title: Global research trends in Scopus-indexed literature on parental cancer and children's psychosocial adjustment to parental cancer: a bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to provide a bibliometric overview of the Scopus-indexed literature on parental cancer and children's psychosocial adjustment across time.
METHODS: The Scopus database was searched for all related documents from the inception of this research field through November 25, 2025. Retrieved records were refined and analyzed using multiple tools, including OpenRefine, Bibliomagika, Biblioshiny (Bibliometrix), and VOSviewer.
RESULTS: A total of 449 relevant articles were published by 2446 authors from 1983 to 2025, with the USA being the leading country in terms of productivity and the Journal of Psycho-Oncology having the greatest output and greatest citation impact. The findings demonstrate sustained growth in research focusing on parental cancer and its impact on children, indicating that cancer is a family crisis with psychological consequences rather than an individual experience.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a bibliometric overview of research productivity and thematic trends in parental cancer and children's psychosocial adjustment. The findings indicate growth in Scopus-indexed literature focused on psychosocial outcomes, family dynamics, and communication but highlight a persistent gap in interventions and international collaboration.

articles.title: Game-based digital interventions in pediatric hematologic oncology: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This review aims to map game-based digital interventions in pediatric hematologic oncology, describe their technological platforms and game elements, and identify the reported health-related and implementation outcomes.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and was reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guideline. The Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework guided the definition of search terms and the development of the search strategy for PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database.
RESULTS: This review included 19 studies from 12 countries, involving 932 participants, of whom 756 had hematologic malignancies. The studies evaluated game-based digital interventions in three formats: screen-based (n = 7), motion-based (n = 6), and virtual reality-based (n = 6). Applications included procedural distraction, treatment-related education, symptom management, and physical or cognitive rehabilitation. The studies reported symptom and psychological, functional, health-related quality of life, and implementation-related outcomes (feasibility, usability, and acceptability).
CONCLUSION: Game-based digital interventions have been applied across diverse supportive care contexts for children with hematologic malignancies. Although a range of applications has been explored, current evidence is insufficient to determine which intervention formats or game elements are most appropriate for particular age groups or clinical contexts. Future research should focus on theory-informed intervention development, evaluate implementation in practice, and explore the potential of these interventions in long-term care.

articles.title: Severe oral mucositis and healthcare utilization in adults with acute lymphoblastic leukemia receiving myeloablative total body irradiation-based conditioning.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We evaluated the association between total body irradiation (TBI) dose and severe oral mucositis (OM) in adults with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) undergoing myeloablative allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).
METHODS: We analyzed 101 adults receiving 8 or 12 Gy TBI. Severe OM was defined as WHO grades 3-4. TBI allocation was non-randomized, with 8 Gy more frequently used in older patients and those with a Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Comorbidity Index (HCT-CI) > 3. Multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with severe OM, with the Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) included in the primary model; sensitivity analyses evaluated alternative models.
RESULTS: Severe OM occurred in 48 patients (47.5%) and was more frequent after 12 than 8 Gy (62.0% vs. 33.3%, P = 0.005). In the primary model, 12 Gy TBI was associated with higher odds of severe OM (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.17-6.78; P = 0.022). The association between 12 Gy TBI and severe OM remained significant when HCT-CI replaced KPS and after calendar-year adjustment. After age adjustment, the estimate was similar, but the confidence interval widened and included the null (OR 2.63, 95% CI 0.90-8.06; P = 0.081). Severe OM was associated with a 4-day longer median hospital stay (41 vs. 37 days, P = 0.001) and a 5-day longer median duration of systemic therapeutic antibiotic treatment (20 vs. 15 days, P = 0.002). Neither measure differed significantly by TBI dose.
CONCLUSION: Higher TBI dose was associated with severe OM; severe OM was associated with longer hospital stays and systemic therapeutic antibiotic treatment. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given non-randomized TBI allocation.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is a retrospective analysis and was not registered as a clinical trial.

articles.title: Perceptions and Barriers to the Use of Modern Contraceptive Methods and HIV Prevention Among Youth Aged 16-20 in Rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study explored young people's perceptions of modern contraceptive methods and HIV prevention, alongside the socioeconomic and cultural barriers they encounter three years post-implementation of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Evaluating this curriculum exposes critical implementation gaps.
METHODS: A qualitative cross-sectional study using semi-structured, face-to-face in-depth individual interviews was conducted in January 2025 among 64 students aged 16-20 across four secondary schools (two public, two faith-based) in South Kivu. A purposive stratified sampling strategy enabled intra-sample comparative analysis across genders and institutional models. Transcribed data underwent inductive thematic open coding with double independent coding to ensure inter-rater reliability.
RESULTS: Our findings expose a significant public health paradox. On one hand, an absolute semantic disconnect exists where 100% of interviewed youth were unfamiliar with the term "contraception", coexisting with a low rate of consistent condom use (17.7%) among sexually active participants, despite comprehensive theoretical mastery of HIV transmission pathways. On the other hand, constrained by community taboos and the fear of parental or religious sanctions, these adolescents underutilize formal youth-friendly healthcare channels. Instead, they engage in alternative risk behaviors, specifically the post-coital utilization of high-dose quinine and aspirin (reported by 40.9% of sexually active girls) as makeshift emergency contraceptives, inducing clinical side effects. Conservative religious leaders and parents with low formal education levels constituted the primary socio-cultural barriers, whereas schoolteachers were supportive.
CONCLUSION: Rural youth remain vulnerable to unintended pregnancies and HIV due to community-enforced silence and institutional linguistic barriers. Effective interventions must transcend classroom education to engage religious and parental gatekeepers, de-stigmatize family planning services, and adapt formal medical terminologies to local daily vernacular languages to align theoretical knowledge with behavioral change.

articles.title: Early-Life Thyroid Hormones Promote Telomere Elongation and Link Telomere Dynamics to Long-Term Behaviour and Performance.
articles.abstract: Telomeres are essential chromosomal structures that safeguard genome integrity. Telomere length (TL), which often shortens with age and stress exposure, is increasingly viewed as an index of life prospect. Within a pace-of-life framework, telomere dynamics can be defined as integrative markers of somatic state and expected lifespan, potentially linking early environments to later life-history strategies. Because telomere dynamics can be tightly coupled to metabolic state-especially during early growth-thyroid hormones (THs), key promoters of growth and metabolism, are prime candidates for mediating these effects. Here, we test whether experimentally elevated early-life thyroid hormone levels promote telomere maintenance during the main post-hatching growth phase in zebra finch (Taeniopygia guttata) nestlings, and whether early-life telomere dynamics predict adolescent and adult performance. By administering TH (T3) throughout the main growth phase until fledging, we analysed TL dynamics longitudinally at 'adolescence' (day 186 post-hatching) and 'adulthood' (day 316 post-hatching). We focused on TL distribution metrics, considering the shortest and the longest TL classes, as well as mean TL, calculated across all telomere length values. We then assessed the consequences of TH-mediated TL dynamics for vertical escape flight and exploratory behaviour, two traits related with fitness and life-history. Irrespective of the TH treatment, we observed (1) TL elongation during the main growth phase, driven by the longest TL, which challenges the prevalent notion that TL shortens in early life; (2) TL attrition only during adolescence and only in the shortest class of telomeres; (3) the TH treatment during early life led to TL elongation of the longest TL in adolescence; (4) this TL elongation, measured as the change in TL from fledgling to adolescence, was positively associated with exploratory behaviour and escape vertical flight in adulthood. Our findings indicate that early-life THs can alter TL dynamics and that these telomere changes are associated with later behaviour and performance. They also highlight the importance of considering different classes of TL rather than relying solely on average TL measures, as short telomeres did not elongate whereas long telomeres changed in both directions and largely accounted for the patterns observed at the average TL level, raising questions about the biological meaning of variation among telomere classes.

articles.title: The role of parent-child relationship quality in socioeconomic inequalities in unintentional injuries and alcohol poisonings among adolescents: A Danish cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Low socioeconomic position is associated with unintentional injury in adolescents. We examined whether parent-child relationship quality mediates the association between low parental socioeconomic position (SEP), unintentional injuries, and alcohol poisonings.
METHODS: The Danish National Youth Cohort 2014 (15-19 years old) was linked to nationwide registers (n = 65,851). Outcomes were unintentional injuries and alcohol poisonings. Logistic regression assessed associations between parental SEP, parent-child relationship quality, and outcomes. Mediation analysis assessed if relationship quality accounted for socioeconomic differences in risk of harm.
RESULTS: Lower SEP associated with higher risk of unintentional injury and alcohol poisonings and dose-dependent associations were observed between lower SEP and lower parent-child relationship quality. For instance, the odds ratios (95% confidence interval) of low parental interest were 1.13 (95% CI 1.04,1.22), 1.40 (1.29,1.52), and 1.92 (1.64,2.24) for medium, short, and elementary education, respectively, compared with long education. Low relationship quality was in turn associated with higher odds of unintentional injury and alcohol poisoning. No statistically significant effect operated through the parent-child relationship pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the potential importance of socioeconomic hardship in shaping parent-child relationships and injury risk however more research is needed to elucidate underlying causal mechanisms.

articles.title: Impulse Oscillometry Reveals Altered Airway Mechanics in Children with Alternaria alternata Sensitization and Allergic Respiratory Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Alternaria alternata is an important fungal aeroallergen associated with allergic respiratory disease, but airway mechanics in sensitized children have not been well characterized using impulse oscillometry (IOS). This study evaluated respiratory system resistance and reactance in children with Alternaria alternata sensitization and allergic respiratory disease compared with healthy controls.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 75 children aged 3-18 years with asthma and/or allergic rhinitis and Alternaria alternata sensitization confirmed by skin prick testing, together with 69 healthy controls. Diagnoses were established according to the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) and Allergic Rhinitis and its Impact on Asthma (ARIA) criteria. The required sample size was determined a priori using an assumed effect size of 0.50, α=0.05, and 80% power. Baseline IOS measurements were obtained using a Jaeger MasterScreen IOS system in accordance with European Respiratory Society technical standards. Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U-test for two-group comparisons and the Kruskal-Wallis test for comparisons across three diagnostic subgroups.
RESULTS: The median age of the study population was 11 years (interquartile range [IQR], 9-13 years), and 53.3% were male. Compared with healthy controls, children with Alternaria alternata sensitization and allergic respiratory disease had higher R5-20 and zR5 values (P<0.001 and P=0.006, respectively), as well as higher Fres, AX, and zX5 values (P<0.001, P<0.001, and P=0.017, respectively). Among the allergic respiratory disease subgroups, zR5 was significantly higher in children with asthma than in those with allergic rhinitis (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Children with Alternaria alternata sensitization and allergic respiratory disease showed higher airway resistance and altered respiratory reactance on IOS than healthy controls. IOS may provide complementary information about airway mechanics in this population.

articles.title: Occurrence of Toxocara spp. in companion animals and serological evidence of human exposure at the human-companion animal interface in Giza, Egypt.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxocariasis, caused by Toxocara spp., is one of the most neglected zoonotic parasitic diseases worldwide. In Egypt, integrated One Health studies investigating human, animal, and occupational risk factors remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of zoonotic Toxocara spp. in companion animals and to identify associated risk factors within a One Health framework.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Giza, Egypt, including dogs (n = 70) and cats (n = 35) from animal shelters and veterinary clinics, eosinophilic children (n = 227), and shelter workers (n = 22). Animal fecal samples were examined microscopically for intestinal parasites, while human serum samples were tested for anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Demographic characteristics and potential risk factors were collected through standardized questionnaires. Associations were evaluated using Pearson's Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, followed by binary logistic regression to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Toxocara canis-like eggs were detected in a percentage of 17.1% in canine cases, with no significant difference in positivity rates regarding sex. In contrast, T. canis positivity rate was significantly correlated with younger age, lack of anthelmintic medication, and concurrent detection of Cystoisospora species. Among the studied eosinophilic children, anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies were detected in 41/227 (18.1%). In the univariable analysis, rural residence was significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (COR = 2.08, 95% CI: 1.00-4.32; P = 0.047). Similarly, contact with soil (COR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.17-5.42; P = 0.02), consumption of unpurified water (COR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.15-6.82; P = 0.02), and interaction with pets (COR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.48-6.87; P = 0.002) were significantly associated with anti IgG seropositivity. In the multivariable binary logistic regression model, contact with soil remained significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (AOR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.17-8.66; P = 0.02). Consumption of unpurified water (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.03-6.78; P = 0.04) and interaction with pets (AOR = 3.60, 95% CI: 1.60-8.10; P = 0.002) were also independently associated with seropositivity. In contrast, the association with rural residence was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the other variables included in the model (AOR = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.25-1.17; P = 0.12).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates substantial exposure to T. canis-like eggs among companion animals and children in Giza, Egypt, highlighting the need for integrated One Health interventions. Regular deworming of pets, public health education, and coordinated veterinary-medical surveillance are recommended to reduce toxocariasis at the human-companion animal interface.

articles.title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Assessing the need for reproductive genetic counseling among adults with cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reproductive health has become an increasingly important focus for people with cystic fibrosis (CF), and guidelines have recommended routine inclusion of genetic counselors on care teams to address questions regarding infertility, pregnancy planning, prenatal diagnosis, and other reproductive health considerations. Despite this, implementation of genetic counseling is still lacking, and there is limited literature documenting patient perspectives on reproductive genetic counseling, particularly in the era of highly effective cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators that have transformed the landscape of clinical care.
METHODS: An electronic REDCap mixed-methods survey was distributed to adults with CF at our center to assess the need for reproductive genetic counseling and to understand current reproductive health concerns. Descriptive statistics were used to report quantitative and demographic data, and a thematic analysis was performed for free-response data.
RESULTS: A total of 237 patients were surveyed, and 116 (49%) responded. Of the 116 respondents, 31 (27%) had never heard of genetic counseling, and 82 (71%) had not previously received it. Forty-four of these 82 (54%) reported that they would find genetic counseling moderately or very helpful. The most important reproductive health topics included the effect of CFTR modulators on fertility and pregnancy, and carrier screening for partners and family members. Qualitative analysis revealed key content categories, including fertility status, concerns and uncertainty with personal health, and lack of informed discussions with providers. Multiple respondents also highlighted not wanting to pass CF onto a child.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight a need and desire in the modern era among adults with CF for improved education regarding reproductive health.

articles.title: Determinants of birth asphyxia among new-borns delivered at Yirgalem general hospital, Sidama Regional State, Southern Ethiopia: Unmatched case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence from the World Health Organization, 4 million infants is born each year with asphyxia resulting as the leading cause of death in low- and middle-income countries including Ethiopia. Despite of this fact, there is little known about risk factors in the study area. There is little context-specific evidence in the Sidama Regional State, especially from facility-based analytical studies. In order to guide focused interventions and enhance neonatal outcomes in this context, local evidence generation is crucial.
OBJECTIVE: aimed to identify determinants of birth asphyxia among new-borns delivered at Yirgalem General Hospital, Sidama regional state, Southern Ethiopia.
METHODS: A facility based unmatched case-control study was conducted from April 15- July 25/2023 among 106 cases and 214 controls. All asphyxiated new-borns were enrolled as cases and every two other non-asphyxiated new-borns were taken as controls. Those new-borns with an Apgar score of < 7 at the fifth minute were taken as cases, and those with ≥7 were taken as controls. Data was collected through the Kobo collection toolbox. The data were exported to statistical package for social science(SPSS) version 27 for analysis, the descriptive analysis was conducted for continuous and categorical variables and the finding was presented using text, tables, and figures. Then, Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess the association between independent variables and birth asphyxia. Hence, variables with a p-value of < 0.25 in the bivariable analysis were included into the multivariable logistic regression model to control for potential confounding. Finally, in the multivariable analysis, variables with a p-value of < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 320 (106 cases and 214 controls) were included in the study. About, 36.8% of mothers with cases and 14.5% of mothers with controls were not followed by partograph. In multivariable model, mothers who faced complications of labor [AOR=3.6; 95% CI: 1.68, 7.90], vaginal discharge [AOR=5.58; 95% CI: 2.73, 11.42], have not followed by partograph [AOR =4.48; 95% CI:1.99, 5.95], and non-cephalic foetal presentation[AOR=2.32; 95%CI: 1.10, 4.90] were statistically significant associated with birth asphyxia.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reported key determinants of asphyxia namely complications of pregnancy, non-cephalic fetal presentation, not use of partograph, vaginal discharge during pregnancy, gestational age (preterm), low birth weight, and mode of delivery. Therefore, findings underscore consistent use of partograph is a key to identify complication early.
