Midwifes and other health professionals need to work on antenatal care in order to monitor baby presentation and mother health conditions.

articles.title: Automated Control of Oxygen Therapy: A State-of-the-Art Review of Closed-Loop Devices, with a Rule-Based, Network-Independent System (EMILY) as a Working Exemplar.
articles.abstract: Supplemental oxygen is among the most widely administered hospital therapies, yet it remains one of the least precisely controlled. Both hypoxemia and hyperoxemia are independently associated with adverse outcomes, and the decade of pragmatic oxygen-target trials has shifted attention from the numeric choice of target toward the fidelity with which any chosen target is sustained. Manual titration is intrinsically episodic and cannot close this fidelity gap, particularly outside high-intensity monitored environments. Automated closed-loop oxygen control has matured rapidly across four delivery paradigms-conventional oxygen flow (low-to-moderate flow up to 15-20 L/min via nasal cannula or mask), high-flow nasal cannula, invasive ventilation, and neonatal respiratory support-with consistent gains in time-in-target and reductions in extremes of oxygenation across all classes. This review surveys the contemporary device landscape (FreeO2, O2matic, iPOC, the Hamilton O2 assist controller evaluated in the HILOOP study, and the TSF high-flow controller, INTELLiVENT-ASV, and the neonatal CLiO2/OxyGenie/PRICO/SPOC/IntellO2/CLAC family), compares control architectures (proportional-integral-derivative, rule-based, and emerging machine-learning approaches), and synthesizes the efficacy, safety, workload, and economic evidence. We then use EMILY, a rule-based, network-independent, source-agnostic, closed-loop flow controller deployed in an intermediate respiratory care unit as a working exemplar to illustrate where the field is heading: multi-parameter inference, network-independent operation, portability across oxygen sources, and instrumented clinician override. We discuss its specific advantages and limitations in detail, and close with an agenda for the outcome trials, interoperability standards, and equity safeguards the field now requires.

articles.title: Guidance documents for the conduct of vaccine clinical trials in pregnant and lactating women: A tool from the CEPI-SPEAC-Brighton Collaboration project.
articles.abstract: As infectious diseases continue to pose risks globally, the inclusion of pregnant and lactating women in vaccine clinical trials is crucial to ensure that mothers and newborns have the option to benefit from potentially life-saving vaccinations. Pregnant and lactating women face unique risks from some infectious diseases and the potential benefits of vaccinating them during pregnancy or lactation can extend to newborns through the transfer of maternal antibodies. Vaccination during lactation raises a distinct set of scientific questions, including transfer of vaccine components and of antigen-specific antibody into milk, the isotype and functional profile of that antibody, and its contribution to infant mucosal protection. Conducting vaccine clinical trials in these populations requires careful attention to regulatory and ethical considerations, study design, data collection and analysis, safety monitoring, and the assessment of efficacy and effectiveness throughout the life cycle of the vaccine. Unique challenges exist, such as distinguishing vaccine-associated adverse events from background pregnancy- and obstetric-related events, fear of harming the fetus, and addressing real and perceived risks to mitigate study recruitment hesitancy and ensure the safety of participants and their unborn infants and the success of the clinical trial. With the exception of first-trimester studies, substantial progress has been made over the last three decades to ensure pregnant and lactating women are included in vaccine studies. Collaboration with experts in vaccine research and ethics, obstetric and maternal-fetal medicine specialists, pediatricians, neonatologists, and other pertinent experts is essential to ensure these studies are properly and successfully conducted. This document compiles published global guidelines and relevant literature concerning the conduct of interventional or observational vaccine studies in pregnant and lactating women.

articles.title: Post-authorization safety surveillance of RSV vaccinated U.S. pregnant women reporting to V-safe.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of US infant hospitalizations. In 2023, the Food and Drug Administration approved an RSV vaccine (Pfizer, Abrysvo) for administration to pregnant women to prevent severe RSV disease in their infants. V-safe collects information about events experienced shortly after vaccination. Vaccinated women who enrolled in V-safe completed web-based surveys about injection site and systemic reactions, their severity, and health impacts (i.e., interference with normal daily activities, missing work or school, or receipt of healthcare) daily for 7 days and then weekly during weeks 2-6 post-vaccination. During October 12, 2023-March 21, 2025, 1200 pregnant women reported RSV vaccination and completed at least one health survey. Median age was 34 years. Common symptoms reported on 0-7 days post-vaccination surveys included injection site pain (32.5%), fatigue (27.7%), and muscle aches (20.5%). Reactions were most frequently reported the first day post-vaccination, and most were self-categorized as mild or moderate. A health impact was reported by 12.5% of participants during the first week after vaccination. Preterm delivery was reported by 59 (6.1%) of 971 participants vaccinated 32-36 weeks of gestation who provided a delivery date. In clinical trials, 5.7% of vaccinated women had preterm delivery. However, more V-safe participants had risk factors for preterm delivery. Based on reports from vaccinated women, short term reactogenicity of mild or moderate severity was common after maternal RSV vaccination. Our findings were generally consistent with safety data from pre-licensure randomized clinical trials of RSV vaccines administered to pregnant women.

articles.title: A quarter-century of pneumococcal protection: estimated global impact of PCV7, PCV13, and PCV20 in children <5 years old.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumococcal diseases, disproportionately affecting children aged <5 years. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) have been implemented globally, substantially reducing the disease burden. This study estimated the global public health impact of PCV7, PCV13, and PCV20 in children aged <5 years over 25 years (2000-2025).
METHODS: The vaccine-specific direct effects of PCV7, PCV13, and PCV20 on invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), pneumonia, and acute otitis media (AOM) in children aged <5 years were estimated over a 25-year period using a previously described PCV impact model. The model was parameterized using epidemiology data, population estimates, and published literature providing vaccine effectiveness, incidence, and mortality estimates.
RESULTS: Between 2000 and 2025, approximately 682 million children aged <5 years were vaccinated globally with PCV7, PCV13, or PCV20, preventing an estimated ~451 million cases of pneumococcal disease and ~1.8 million deaths. AOM accounted for approximately 91% of cases prevented, followed by pneumonia (8%) and IPD (1%), while pneumonia prevention accounted for the majority of deaths averted. PCV13 contributed to more than 95% of the total estimated cases prevented, reflecting its widespread global adoption. The contribution of PCV20 was limited both by its recent introduction and low uptake to date.
CONCLUSIONS: PCV7, PCV13, and PCV20 implementation was estimated to have reduced pneumococcal disease and mortality among young children worldwide. Continued use of effective vaccines such as PCV13 remains critical, while broader adoption of higher-valency options, when feasible, may provide additional public health benefits by addressing evolving pneumococcal serotype epidemiology.

articles.title: Differences in patient attitudes on respiratory syncytial virus immunization among Canadian jurisdictions with and without publicly funded universal nirsevimab programs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, Canada introduced two strategies to prevent severe infant RSV infection: maternal vaccine (RSVpreF) and infant monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab). Although Canadian guidelines recommended universal seasonal nirsevimab, implementation varied across provinces/territories. We compared attitudes and preferences towards RSV immunization in jurisdictions with and without publicly funded universal nirsevimab programs.
METHODS: Between November 2024 and March 2025, we conducted a national prospective cohort study recruiting pregnant or recently pregnant participants through social media. Participants completed a baseline survey, with follow-up at 3 and 6 months postpartum. Surveys collected demographic data, obstetrical outcomes, reported receipt of immunization products, and attitudes towards RSVpreF and nirsevimab, including perceived barriers. Participants were analyzed by residence in provinces/territories with versus without universal nirsevimab programs.
RESULTS: Among 1008 participants included in the analysis, 40.6% resided in jurisdictions with funded universal nirsevimab programs. If both immunization products were free and available, in jurisdictions with universal nirsevimab, 78.5% would accept nirsevimab, while 72.4% would accept RSVpreF. In provinces without funded nirsevimab programs, 73.9% of participants would accept nirsevimab with an 89.8% acceptance rate for RSVpreF (p < 0.001). In jurisdictions with universal nirsevimab programs, nirsevimab was perceived as more beneficial (p < 0.001) and more effective (p = 0.02) at preventing RSV disease than RSVpreF. Approximately 96% of participants agreed that the decision to obtain RSVpreF was up to them, however, fewer felt the same about nirsevimab (84.6%). When ranking vaccines in pregnancy, 43.9% of participants ranked Tdap as their top priority, while 21% ranked RSV vaccination first. Tdap was ranked higher than RSVpreF by 60.5% of participants, with no significant differences between jurisdictions.
CONCLUSIONS: During the 2024/2025 RSV season, preferences between RSVpreF and nirsevimab were associated with provincial/territorial public funding for infant monoclonal antibodies. As RSV immunoprophylaxis programs evolve, policymakers should recognize that funding decisions can influence public attitudes and preferences towards available immunization products.

articles.title: Epidemiology of influenza C in Hong Kong inferred from pediatric hospitalization data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza C virus (ICV) circulates globally causing generally mild respiratory infections. Limited data have been reported, including epidemiologic features and its potential interactions with other influenza viruses and respiratory pathogens.
METHODS: We analyzed laboratory-confirmed pediatric influenza hospitalizations in Hong Kong from October 2015 to March 2025. Respiratory specimens were tested by multiplex RT-PCR for influenza A, B, and C viruses and other respiratory pathogens. We described the seasonality, age distribution, co-detections, hospitalization burden, and explored effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccines against ICV-associated hospital admissions in comparison with seasonal influenza A and B viruses using the test-negative analysis.
RESULTS: Of a total of 39,146 admissions, 356 (0.9%) tested positive for influenza C, and 4554 (11.6%) and 1600 (4.1%) for influenza A and B, respectively. A high proportion of ICV cases (64.3%) had at least one co-detected respiratory pathogen, compared with influenza A (18.4%) and influenza B (15.3%). Seasonal influenza vaccination was not effective against ICV-associated hospitalization (vaccine effectiveness: -6.2%, 95% confidence interval: -44.6% to 22.0%) but effective for influenza A (58.2%, 54.3% to 61.8%) and influenza B (68.7%, 63.0% to 73.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provided important epidemiologic information on ICV infections in pediatric patients. The estimated null protection against influenza C from seasonal influenza vaccination implied the potential immunological relationship between seasonal influenza viruses and underscored the importance of continuous surveillance on influenza viruses.

articles.title: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination: A systematic review and meta-analysis of determinants of vaccine acceptability and uptake.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination has potential to prevent infant respiratory morbidity. We identified sociodemographic factors influencing the acceptability and uptake of RSV vaccination among pregnant individuals.
METHODS: We carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis of sociodemographic factors associated with maternal RSV vaccination behavior. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science for observational studies of RSV vaccination in pregnant women published before September 10, 2025. We included articles that examined how maternal race/ethnicity, education, employment, age, and marital status were related to RSV vaccine intention and uptake. We performed a meta-analysis using random effects models with inverse-variance weighting to estimate pooled odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the association between sociodemographic factors and RSV vaccination intention and uptake.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies comprising 15,275 individuals met inclusion criteria. Black race was the strongest determinant of vaccination behavior during pregnancy, followed by socioeconomic factors. In meta-analysis, Black race was associated with more than 50% lower odds of RSV vaccine uptake compared with White race (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.32-0.57; 6 studies). Low educational attainment (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45-0.76; 8 studies) and unemployment (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.96; 7 studies) were associated with >20% less intention to be vaccinated compared with higher education or employment. Maternal age and marital status were not associated with RSV vaccination intention.
CONCLUSION: Black patients and patients from low socioeconomic backgrounds should be a primary focus of obstetric RSV vaccination efforts.

articles.title: Quality, tone, and misinformation in TikTok content about RSV immunization for pregnant people and infants (2023 to 2025): a cross-sectional content analysis.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of infant hospitalization. Since 2023, families have had two prevention options: a maternal vaccine given in pregnancy or an antibody shot, nirsevimab, given to infants. Many parents use social media to help decide. We reviewed 169 public TikTok videos about RSV immunization posted between July 2023 and November 2025, rating quality on a 1 to 5 scale and coding creator type, misinformation status, tone, and narrative framing. Median quality was 3, and 47% of videos were high quality. Health professionals made half of all videos and most evidence-consistent content, while parents and caregivers made a larger share of mixed-or-uncertain content. Mixed-or-uncertain videos (20%) were more than six times as common as outright misinformation (3%). Most videos (73%) used a protective, child-focused frame, regardless of accuracy. Clinicians should ask families what they have seen online and be ready to offer reliable resources.

articles.title: Estimating the global and regional impact of introducing typhoid conjugate vaccination schedules: a modelling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2018, WHO recommended single-dose typhoid conjugate vaccines (TCVs) for typhoid-endemic countries. Emerging evidence of waning immunity has raised questions about optimal vaccination age and booster doses. A follow-up multi-model study evaluated vaccination schedules, focusing on booster strategies. Here, we expand findings from one of four modelling groups, estimating the global and regional health impact of TCV schedules.
METHODOLOGY: We developed an agent-based typhoid transmission model using the open-source Starsim toolbox. The model captures subclinical and acute infections, chronic carriers, and natural and vaccine-derived immunity, with age- and sex-specific parameters and outcomes. The model was calibrated to three incidence archetypes (medium, high, and very high) and two vaccine-derived immunity durations (fast and slow waning). Countries were mapped to archetypes based on national typhoid burden. We compared no vaccination with four strategies: routine vaccination at 9 months, 9 months with a booster at 5 years, 2 years, and 5 years, each with a catch-up campaign. Cases, deaths, and DALYs averted were estimated globally and across GBD super-regions over 10 years.
RESULTS: Globally, up to 29.5 million cases and 8.2 million DALYs could be averted with routine vaccination at 9 months plus a 5-year booster. Earlier vaccination and longer-lasting immunity generally increased impact. Under fast waning, vaccination at 2 years averted more cases and DALYs than vaccination at 9 months or 5 years, particularly in high-incidence settings where burden was greatest among children aged 2-<5 years. Boosters provided additional benefits, especially with fast waning. South Asia accounted for the largest share of global impact, followed by Sub-Saharan Africa.
CONCLUSION: TCV could avert substantial typhoid burden. The optimal age for a single dose depends on how quickly protection wanes, and boosters add benefit where waning is rapid. Better evidence on the protection duration, and country-specific analyses, are needed to guide schedule choices.

articles.title: A next generation vaccine to prevent disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B (MenB).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: OMVax has developed a meningococcal native outer membrane vesicle (NOMV) vaccine containing overexpressed, mutant Factor H binding proteins (FHbps) from subfamilies A and B with reduced FH binding and attenuated endotoxin (NOMV-FHbp). In previous studies, NOMV presented surface antigens in a native environment that elicited high titers of serum bactericidal activity (SBA) in mice and infant macaques. However, the relatively low amounts of NOMV produced by MenB strains has limited vaccine development.
METHODS: We describe here a culture medium enabling commercial scale production of NOMV. We investigated the ability of antibodies elicited in mice by NOMV-FHbp alone or in combination with a MenACWY capsular polysaccharide conjugate vaccine to elicit human complement-mediated serum bactericidal activity (SBA) against strains from each capsular group.
RESULTS: In CD1 wild-type (WT) mice, anti-NOMV-FHbp antibodies showed significantly greater SBA than those elicited by marketed MenB vaccine MenB-FHbp against five out of six representative MenB strains currently causing disease. The combination NOMV-FHbp+MenACWY vaccine maintained high SBA activity against strains from the different serogroups compared to each individual vaccine. In CEACAM1/FH human transgenic mice, anti-NOMV-FHbp antibodies showed greater or comparable SBA than those elicited by MenB-4C licensed vaccine against two MenB strains expressing FHbp ID 1, an amino acid sequence identical to FHbp ID 1 in the MenB-4C vaccine.
CONCLUSIONS: The results show that NOMV-FHbp alone or in combination with MenACWY vaccines has the potential to broaden protection against MenB strains that are not optimally covered by existing vaccines.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese Manual Therapy (Tuina) Alleviates Cerebral Palsy by Enhancing PARP1 SUMOylation to Suppress Parthanatos.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) often suffer from sensorimotor dysfunction. Tuina has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in CP rehabilitation. This study aimed to elucidate whether Tuina ameliorates motor deficits in hypoxic-ischaemic (HI)-induced CP mice by suppressing PARP1-mediated parthanatos through modulation of the PIAS4-PARP1-SUMOylation axis.
METHODS: A neonatal HI brain injury model was established in postnatal day 7 (P7) C57BL/6 mice via right common carotid artery ligation. Mice were randomised into three groups: Sham, Model and Model + Tuina. A 42-day acupoint massage protocol was administered following modelling in the Tuina group. Motor function was assessed using righting reflex, grip strength, balance beam, rotarod and CatWalk gait analyses. PARP1 activity and parthanatos markers were assessed by western blotting and immunofluorescence. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and proximity ligation assay (PLA) were performed to evaluate PIAS4-PARP1 binding and PARP1-SUMO2/3 interaction.
RESULTS: Tuina significantly promoted body weight gain and improved grip strength, coordination, balance and gait parameters in CP mice. At the molecular level, Tuina inhibited PARP1 hyperactivation, reduced PAR accumulation and apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) nuclear translocation and upregulated PIAS4 expression. Moreover, Co-IP and PLA analyses revealed decreased PIAS4-PARP1 binding and reduced PARP1-SUMO2/3 conjugations in CP mice, whereas Tuina significantly restored both interactions indicating enhanced PARP1 SUMOylation.
CONCLUSIONS: Tuina was associated with improved motor function, increased PIAS4 expression, enhanced PARP1 SUMOylation and suppression of parthanatos in CP mice. These findings suggest a potential role of the PIAS4-PARP1 SUMOylation axis in the neuroprotective effects of Tuina, although the causal relationship between this pathway and the therapeutic effects of Tuina requires further investigation.

articles.title: Improving Assessment Practices With Autistic Girls: Views and Experiences of Psychologists in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The role of sex and gender warrants careful consideration in autism identification. Studies focusing on prevalence rates consistently report higher numbers of autistic boys compared to autistic girls, and there is increasing awareness autistic girls may be under-identified within the general population. Different reasons have been cited, including issues with assessment practices and behavioural differences between autistic girls and autistic boys.
METHODS: In attempting to understand and improve assessment practices with autistic girls, 91 psychologists working in publicly funded services in the Republic of Ireland involved in autism assessments with children completed a survey focused on their autism assessment experiences, with an emphasis on autistic girls. Survey questions were designed to gather quantitative and qualitative data, with descriptive statistics and content analysis used to provide an overview of participants' responses.
RESULTS: Psychologists reported gender-related differences in autism assessments, highlighting diverse expressions of autistic differences and different referral reasons. Specific gender-based assessment practices were noted, resulting in lengthier assessments with autistic girls. Most psychologists engaged in 'upgrading' (autism identified in cases where presentations are less clear and/or where individuals do not meet thresholds on standard diagnostic tools (Rogers et al., 2016), with nearly half reporting that it happens more frequently with autistic girls compared to autistic boys.
CONCLUSION: Further research is needed to explore the role of clinical judgement in autism assessment and identification, as well as parental and autistic girls' experiences of assessments. From a practice-based perspective universities offering psychology professional training need to develop curricula of learning in autism assessment and identification to include experiences of autistic females.

articles.title: Mapping the Interplay of Depression and Autism-Related Traits in Adolescents: A Network Analysis Approach.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Autistic adolescents are at increased risk of developing depression but overlapping presentations of the two conditions and atypical symptoms complicate accurate identification and treatment. This study applied network analysis to investigate how autism traits relate to specific depressive symptoms in autistic and non-autistic adolescents.
METHODS: Participants were 474 adolescents aged 12-17 years (128 autistic; 346 non-autistic) recruited from a multi-site study. Depressive symptoms were assessed via child- and parent-report using the Patient Health Questionnaire for Adolescents (PHQ-A), and autism traits were measured using the Social Responsiveness Scale-2 (SRS-2). Bayesian network analysis was conducted to identify central depressive symptoms and to examine links between autism traits and depressive symptom nodes across informants.
RESULTS: Child- and parent-reported PHQ-A networks showed distinct informant-specific patterns. Depressed mood and psychomotor disturbance were the most central symptoms in the child-reported depression network, whereas parent reports identified anhedonia and appetite/weight change as most central. Autism traits when added to the networks were linked to psychomotor disturbance in the adolescent- and parent-reported networks, and to low self-worth in the parent-reported network.
CONCLUSION: Findings indicate that autism traits are linked to depression through specific pathways. Psychomotor disturbance and low self-worth emerged as key bridges between autism and depression, highlighting the importance of multi-informant assessment, contextual interpretation of psychomotor changes, and targeted support for item-level depressive symptoms during intervention.

articles.title: An Interactive Booklet for Addressing Postpartum Mood and Anxiety Disorders: Feasibility Assessment Using the APEASE Criteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal mood and anxiety disorders occurring at any time during the perinatal period affect 15% to 20% of birthing parents in the United States and are frequently underdiagnosed. Technology-based tools may improve early detection of mental health issues, expand access to support, and reduce barriers to help-seeking behaviors.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and practicability of "Be Well, Mommy," a mobile interactive booklet designed to support postpartum mental health, developed using a 10-step social marketing framework. Secondary objectives included assessing its potential to raise mental health awareness, normalize postpartum emotional challenges, and facilitate help-seeking with patients, as well as assessing health care provider perspectives to inform refinements. Insights from this feasibility trial will guide improvements and future large-scale implementation.
METHODS: Researchers conducted a qualitative feasibility project in Southeast Georgia with 15 first-time female parents and 5 health care providers. Participants were asked to use the booklet for 2 weeks, followed by 3 focus groups with mothers and 5 in-depth provider interviews. Researchers analyzed the data thematically using NVivo 15 and the APEASE (acceptability, practicability, perceived effectiveness, affordability, side effects, and equity) criteria.
RESULTS: Findings revealed mixed acceptability. Birthing parents described the booklet as supportive, easy to navigate, visually appealing, and helpful in normalizing emotional challenges after childbirth. Experts, however, expressed concerns about limited clinical depth and difficulties in integrating it into practice. Practicability was generally high, though minor navigation and technical issues were identified. The free, mobile-friendly format enhanced affordability and equity. No major safety concerns emerged, although some participants found celebrity stories less relatable.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, "Be Well, Mommy" demonstrates preliminary feasibility as an accessible, awareness-raising tool that may support early recognition of postpartum mental health concerns and encourage help-seeking. Refinements, including expanded evidence-based content, improved navigation, and enhanced provider engagement, are recommended prior to large-scale implementation. Further longitudinal and quantitative research is needed to assess effectiveness and scalability.

articles.title: Electronic Screen Exposure and Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review examined the association between early childhood electronic screen exposure and ASD or ASD-like characteristics in preschool children, whether reducing screen exposure changes those characteristics, and whether genetic/familial vulnerability moderates the association.
METHODS: Nine databases were searched to December 2024. After screening 650 records, 11 studies (124,913 participants) met inclusion criteria. Quality was assessed using Kmet criteria. Given substantial heterogeneity in design, exposure definitions, outcomes, and reporting, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Studies fell into three domains: (1) screen exposure and ASD-like characteristics; (2) screen reduction and changes in these characteristics; and (3) genetic/familial vulnerability as a moderator. Greater early screen exposure was frequently associated with ASD-like characteristics and related developmental concerns, including language and attentional difficulties. However, evidence was heterogeneous, and findings varied in quality and directness. Evidence on clinically diagnosed ASD was limited, and improvement after screen reduction rested mainly on uncontrolled case observations, often alongside increased caregiver-child interaction.
CONCLUSION: Evidence suggests an association between greater early screen exposure and ASD-like characteristics but does not establish that screen exposure causes ASD or that reducing it treats such characteristics. Confounding, reverse causation, caregiver-report bias, inconsistent measurement, and limited high-quality evidence restrict causal interpretation. "Virtual autism" and "Post-Digital Nannying Autism Syndrome" are not recognized diagnostic categories. Prospective longitudinal and quasi-experimental studies using standardized measures of content, context, timing, caregiver involvement, and outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Growing Through Challenge: Attitudes Towards Autism Mediate the Li​nk Between Caregiving Strain and Personal Growth in Mother​s.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study investigated whether attitudes towards autism mediated the relationship between the level of caregiver strain and psychological outcomes (personal growth and mental health) in mothers of children with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). We examined how conceptual frameworks ranging from the medical model to the neurodiversity perspective are related to mothers' capacity for positive transformation in the face of caregiving strain.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 449 mothers of children with ASC (aged 2-18 years). Participants completed measures of caregiver burden (CBI), post-traumatic growth (PTGI), mental health (MHC-SF), and attitudes towards autism (ATA-Q). Mediation analyses were performed using bootstrapping procedures with 5000 replications to test indirect effects.
RESULTS: Attitudes towards autism statistically mediated the relationship between caregiver strain and personal growth (indirect effect: b = -0.19, 95% CI [-0.29, -0.11], p < .001; 60% of total effect), with the direct effect becoming non-significant when attitudes were included (b = -0.13, p = .185). For mental health, attitudes showed partial mediation (indirect effect: b = -0.06, 95% CI [-0.10, -0.02], p = .005; 16% of total effect),​ with the direct effect remaining significant (b = -0.29, p < .001).
CONCLUSION: Medical-model perspectives, associated with higher strain, corresponded to lower personal growth, whereas neurodiversity-aligned attitudes corresponded to higher growth. Notably, mothers facing the greatest caregiving strain were most aligned with the medical perspective, suggesting that those in the most demanding situations may be particularly vulnerable to poorer psychological adjustment. These findings may inform work addressing both practical support needs and conceptual frameworks of autism.

articles.title: Association Between Cancer Stage and Parenting Self-Efficacy in Breast Cancer Survivors: A Survey of a Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Community.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer substantially affects women's health and survivorship, with an increasing number of survivors. However, research on social reintegration into family and work roles after cancer remains limited. This study aimed to examine the association between breast cancer-related clinical indicators and parenting self-efficacy among survivors who were working mothers before diagnosis, thereby enhancing understanding of post-cancer social reintegration into parenting.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 357 women who completed their last treatment between 2018 and 2022 and had at least one dependent child aged 12 years or younger. Participants were recruited from an online patient community in Republic of Korea (= South Korea) in October 2023, which predominantly consisted of survivors of triple-negative breast cancer. Parenting self-efficacy was the primary outcome. Clinical characteristics, return-to-work-related factors, and sociodemographic variables were included as independent variables and covariates. Multivariate linear regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Higher breast cancer stages were associated with lower parenting self-efficacy compared with Stage 0. Undergoing breast-conserving surgery and longer time since the completion of the last treatment were positively associated with parenting self-efficacy. Overall patterns were similar in the total sample and among participants who had returned to work (n = 229), although some associations varied in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Advanced cancer stages may be associated with lower parenting self-efficacy among breast cancer survivor mothers. However, this association appears sensitive to stage grouping and warrants cautious interpretation. These findings may provide preliminary insights into post-cancer parenting experiences, although the specific study population and cross-sectional design limit generalizability. Greater attention may be needed for social reintegration into parenting for young women with breast cancer, who play critical roles in both the workforce and childcare.

articles.title: The Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of Self-Help Mindful Parenting Intervention for Mothers of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder and Developmental Delay in China: A Multicenter Feasibility Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and developmental delay (DD) experience great parenting stress; meanwhile, effective interventions to manage parenting stress are lacking. To examine the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of a self-help mindful parenting intervention among parents of children with ASD/DD.
METHODS: A total of 30 mothers of children with ASD/DD were recruited and randomized 1:1 to the intervention group receiving a six-week self-help mindful parenting program (n = 15) or the waitlist-control group (n = 15). Feasibility was assessed based on recruitment, retention, data completion, and intervention completion, and acceptability was derived from self-perceived burden and satisfaction. Preliminary efficacy was analyzed by mixed effect models, with effect sizes described using Hedge's g.
RESULTS: High feasibility was suggested by the 66.7% completion rate among mothers in the intervention group. The mothers also in the intervention group reported a low mean score of self-perceived burden (8.09 ± 2.02 out of 10.00) and a high median satisfaction score (8.00 out of 10.00), indicating high acceptability. Compared with the control group, the intervention group reported a medium magnitude reduction in parenting stress (t = 3.46 ~ 4.08, P = 0.003 ~ 0.006, Hedges' g = 0.50 ~ 0.82).
CONCLUSIONS: Self-help mindful parenting is feasible and acceptable, and shows preliminary efficacy. This highlights the need for a full-scale randomized controlled trial to further examine its efficacy.

articles.title: Perceived Health in Mothers of Children With Neuropsychiatric Conditions: The Role of PTSS From Child-Related Trauma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Mothers raising children with neuropsychiatric conditions, such as autism or other mental health disorders, encounter unique caregiving challenges that can adversely affect their psychological and physical health. While research has documented poorer perceived health among these mothers and identified elevated posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) related to their children's upbringing, no study has explored how PTSS specifically contributes to perceived health in this population.
METHODS: This study aimed to address this gap by examining 635 mothers, including 169 mothers of children with autism or mental health disorders and 466 mothers of children without disabilities. Participants completed self-report measures online. Analyses included permutation-based ANCOVAs, correlation analyses, and hierarchical regression analyses.
RESULTS: Results showed that mothers of children with autism or mental health disorders reported worse self-rated health (SRH), more somatic complaints, and a higher number of health problems compared to comparison mothers. PTSS was negatively associated with perceived health, while perceived social support was positively associated. However, regression analyses indicated that PTSS was a significant predictor of all three health indicators, independent of age, substance use, and perceived social support. After including PTSS in the regression models, the effect of perceived social support on SRH and somatic complaints became non-significant.
CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the role of posttraumatic distress from child-rearing trauma in shaping perceived health among mothers of children with neuropsychiatric conditions and underscores the need for trauma-focused interventions to mitigate the negative impact of PTSS on their health perceptions.

articles.title: Validity and Reliability of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract: Handedness is a key behavioral marker of hemispheric specialization and is closely associated with motor, perceptual, and cognitive development. Although standardized questionnaires such as the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory-Short Form (EHI-Short) provide indirect measures of manual lateralization, observational tools are needed to capture children's functional hand use in everyday activities. This study evaluated the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in 188 children aged 5-12 years, including 81 children with ASD and 107 typically developing (TD) peers. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa, and convergent validity was evaluated through agreement analyses, classification accuracy, and correlations with the EHI-Short. Inter-rater agreement was almost perfect (κ = 0.885, p < .001) and test-retest agreement over a 14-day interval demonstrated excellent stability in the ASD group (κ = 0.870) and perfect agreement in an availability-based TD subsample (n = 50; κ = 1.000). AHA and EHI-Short handedness classifications showed strong categorical agreement (ASD: κ = 0.914; TD: κ = 0.868), and AHA laterality indices were strongly correlated with EHI-Short laterality coefficients (ASD: r = .939; TD: r = .982). Children with ASD showed a higher prevalence of atypical handedness than TD peers, and ASD status remained associated with atypical handedness after adjustment for age and gender. Category-specific estimates for mixed-handedness in the TD group should be interpreted cautiously because no TD children were classified as mixed-handed by the AHA. Overall, the Turkish AHA demonstrated good reliability, with evidence of convergent validity, and agreement with the EHI-Short. These findings should be regarded as preliminary psychometric evidence, and further validation in larger and more diverse samples is warranted.

articles.title: The apelin-APJ axis in infantile hemangioma: Emerging evidence and potential links to propranolol response.
articles.abstract: Propranolol is the standard first-line systemic therapy for infantile hemangioma (IH), but its antiangiogenic mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Emerging evidence implicates the apelin-APJ system in IH endothelial biology. APJ is enriched in hemangioma-derived endothelial cells (HemECs), and pharmacological inhibition suppresses proliferation, migration and angiogenic behavior, with genetic experiments supporting an APJ-dependent component. Separately, propranolol reduces APLN transcription in IH-derived models, and circulating apelin declines during treatment. These findings motivate investigation of an indirect link through ligand regulation, but do not establish APJ-dependent mediation of propranolol efficacy. This review distinguishes ligand transcription, ligand abundance, receptor expression and receptor-dependent function, integrating IH observations with mechanistic evidence from other vascular and disease models. We examine endothelial cell states, HIF-1α-dependent transcription, and the distinct SOX18-mevalonate mechanism of R(+)-propranolol. Cross-disease intervention studies provide a rationale for investigating treatment responsiveness. Priorities include defining functional ligand sources and recipient cells, testing receptor-dependent effects on drug response, validating circulating biomarkers, and establishing developmental safety before therapeutic translation.

articles.title: Bacterial spectrum, age and calendar-quarter distribution, and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of isolates recovered from respiratory specimens of children hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia in Chongqing, China: a three-year retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Community acquired pneumonia (CAP) continues to be an important cause of admission of children in hospitals. This study focused on bacterial isolates from respiratory samples, age distribution and antibiotic resistance patterns of children below seven years admitted with CAP in Chongqing, China from January 2023 to December 2025. Of the 2,988 patients included in the study, 884 (29.59%) were positive for bacterial culture, with 930 isolates. The predominant species were Haemophilus influenzae (43.01%), Moraxella catarrhalis (22.80%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (14.84%), and Staphylococcus aureus (10.32%). The distribution of recovered isolates differed significantly across age groups (P < 0.01). After adjustment for calendar year, overall culture positivity did not differ significantly across quarters (P = 0.085), although a significant quarter-by-year interaction was observed (P = 0.005), indicating that quarterly patterns varied between years. Year-adjusted quarterly associations were also observed for H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, and S. aureus. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing showed high non-susceptibility to ampicillin (65.25%) and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (62.33%) among H. influenzae isolates, and to erythromycin and clindamycin (99.19% for each) among S. pneumoniae isolates. Oxacillin non-susceptibility was observed in 20.25% of tested S. aureus isolates, while imipenem non-susceptibility was uncommon among tested Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. These findings support continued regional microbiological surveillance and may inform institutional antimicrobial stewardship. Because nasotracheal suction specimens may contain colonizing organisms, culture recovery alone does not establish the bacterial causes of CAP.

articles.title: Youth perspectives on tuberculosis prevention in South Africa: A qualitative study in faith-based organisations.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading public health challenge in South Africa, with high rates of co-infection with HIV. Faith-based organisations (FBOs) have untapped potential to support TB prevention, particularly by engaging youth who are often overlooked. This study explored youth perspectives on TB prevention and FBOs' roles in advancing youth-led, culturally grounded health promotion strategies in Johannesburg, South Africa. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using five focus group discussions with youth aged 18-30 years from Christian, Muslim, and Rastafarian faith communities. The study was guided by principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and Human-Centered Design, applying the 'Define' and 'Develop' phases of the Double Diamond model. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants demonstrated a blend of biomedical knowledge and persistent TB myths. Youth identified FBOs as trusted yet underutilised platforms and proposed strategies including music, storytelling, drama, peer-led health clubs, and digital campaigns. They expressed readiness to lead within faith institutions but noted barriers, including resistance from traditional hierarchies and limited resources. Youth in faith communities possess the creativity, insight, and commitment to transform TB prevention efforts. Strengthening partnerships between youth and FBOs, and investing in participatory, faith-aligned health promotion models, could yield more equitable and sustainable public health outcomes in high-burden settings.

articles.title: Reduction in Emergency Department Attendances for Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants Aged Under 1 Year in England During Winter 2025/2026 Following Introduction of Maternal RSV Vaccination.
articles.abstract: In September 2024, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) maternal vaccination was introduced to the UK schedule. Monitoring acute bronchiolitis emergency department (ED) attendance levels may provide a 'real-world' assessment of the likely impact. ED acute bronchiolitis attendances in England were substantially lower (-23%) in infants aged under 1 year in 2025/2026 compared to preceding seasons, consistent with bronchiolitis aetiology, vaccine efficacy and uptake and RSV immunisation programme impacts elsewhere. This work contributes to the evidence that maternal RSV vaccination is bringing about reductions in the RSV burden in young infants.

articles.title: Impact of consolidative HSCT after CAR T-cell-induced remission in pediatric relapsed/refractory B-ALL: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is required after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T)-induced remission in pediatric relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B-ALL) remains unresolved. We report single-center outcomes of CAR-T therapy with or without subsequent HSCT, evaluated using current consensus response criteria.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 34 pediatric patients with R/R B-ALL who received investigational autologous CAR-T products (CD28- or 4-1BB-based; single- or dual-target) between June 2018 and December 2023. Response was assessed per National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines and international consensus definitions; survival by Kaplan-Meier estimation. The HSCT comparison was descriptive, complemented by a 6-month landmark analysis, a time-dependent Cox analysis restricted to patients transplanted at our center, and event-free survival (EFS) with in-remission HSCT censored at transplant.
RESULTS: Median age was 7.3 years; 26 patients were relapsed and 8 refractory. CR or CRi (CR/CRi) was achieved in 26/34 (76.5%), all MRD-negative. Grade ≥3 CRS occurred in 11.8% and grade 3 ICANS in 2.9%. At a median follow-up of 21.4 months, 2-year OS and EFS were 57.4% (95% CI, 38.8-72.3) and 43.2% (26.2-59.1). Among 24 patients with marrow-involved disease achieving MRD-negative CR, 20 underwent HSCT and 4 did not; 2-year OS was 79.3% versus 25.0% (descriptive log-rank P = 0.006), and all 4 non-HSCT patients relapsed and died. In the 6-month landmark analysis (n=21), HSCT by landmark remained associated with superior OS (P = 0.047); the time-dependent Cox analysis showed a consistent association (OS: HR, 0.19 (0.04-0.90); P = 0.036). With in-remission HSCT censored, no patient remained event-free beyond 12.1 months, versus a conventional 2-year EFS of 61.8%. Two of 4 patients with isolated testicular relapse achieved durable remission without HSCT.
CONCLUSIONS: CAR-T therapy induced high rates of MRD-negative remission with manageable toxicity in pediatric R/R B-ALL, but rarely produced durable survival without HSCT in marrow-involved disease. Post-remission HSCT was associated with improved survival; salvage HSCT after relapse also appeared effective in a few patients. These associations are limited by the retrospective design and small sample size and require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia: a descriptive single-centre case series from a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia (JMML) is a rare myeloproliferative neoplasm of early childhood driven by RAS-MAPK pathway activation, for which allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is the only established cure. Data from low- and middle-income countries, where donor access, drug availability and monitoring capacity differ from the settings that generate most published evidence, are scarce.
METHODS: We reviewed all consecutive children with JMML who underwent allogeneic HSCT at a single tertiary centre in northern India between January 2019 and August 2025. Engraftment, graft failure, poor graft function and transplant complications were classified by pre-specified consensus criteria. The analysis is descriptive: proportions are reported with exact 95% confidence intervals (CI) and survival as Kaplan-Meier estimates, without hypothesis testing.
RESULTS: Eight children (seven boys; median age 19.5 months) received myeloablative fludarabine-busulfan-melphalan conditioning and fresh peripheral blood stem cells from four HLA-matched siblings and four haploidentical parents. Initial neutrophil engraftment occurred in six (75%; 95% CI 34.9-96.8) at a median of 17.5 days, and sustained engraftment in five (62.5%; 95% CI 24.5-91.5). Primary graft failure, secondary graft failure and poor graft function occurred in one patient each, all haploidentical recipients; all four matched-sibling recipients engrafted durably. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1-2) occurred in three haploidentical recipients and skin-limited grade I-II acute graft-versus-host disease in two patients. Three children died without relapse: two after graft failure (days +28 and +41) and one of a COVID-19/MIS-C-like illness 28 months after transplantation. No relapse occurred. At a median follow-up of 35 months among survivors, five of eight children were alive (62.5%; 95% CI 24.5-91.5); Kaplan-Meier overall and event-free survival at 36 months were 60% (95% CI 19.5-85.2) and 46.9% (95% CI 12.0-76.3), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Allogeneic HSCT for JMML, including haploidentical transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide, was feasible in a resource-limited setting, and no patient relapsed. However, graft failure or poor graft function affected three of four haploidentical recipients, and this cohort is far too small to support any comparison between donor types. Donor-specific antibodies, HLA disparity, splenic disease burden, conditioning exposure and graft composition warrant systematic attention in alternative-donor transplantation for JMML in similar settings.

articles.title: Impact of cervical cancer education on knowledge, attitudes and preventive practices among adolescent girls in secondary schools: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains one of the most preventable yet deadliest cancers affecting women in Africa. Despite global advances in prevention through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screening, and early treatment, Sub-Saharan Africa continues to experience disproportionately high incidence and mortality rates because of limited health infrastructure, inadequate awareness, and delayed diagnosis. Given that adolescence represents a critical window for establishing lifelong health behaviors, school-based cervical cancer education may provide an effective platform for improving knowledge and promoting preventive practices in line with the World Health Organization's (WHO) cervical cancer elimination strategy.
METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, African Journals Online (AJOL), the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was undertaken for studies published up to 2026. A total of 1,700 records were identified and screened, resulting in the inclusion of 20 eligible studies. Data were extracted, charted, and synthesized using a narrative approach.
RESULTS: Evidence suggests that baseline knowledge of cervical cancer and HPV among adolescent girls in African secondary schools remains generally low to moderate. A consistent knowledge-attitude gap was identified, whereby positive attitudes toward prevention frequently coexisted with limited factual understanding of cervical cancer risk factors, screening, and HPV vaccination. Educational interventions, including peer-led programmes, classroom-based teaching, health campaigns, and multimodal educational strategies, consistently produced significant improvements in knowledge and awareness. However, improvements were less pronounced for more complex concepts, including disease curability, recommended screening intervals, and vaccine mechanisms. Furthermore, an intention-behavior gap was observed, as high levels of vaccine acceptance rarely translated into actual uptake because of parental, sociocultural, and health system barriers. Geographical analysis revealed a substantial concentration of studies in a limited number of Anglophone countries, particularly Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda, highlighting important gaps in evidence across many African settings.
CONCLUSION: School-based cervical cancer education represents a feasible and scalable strategy for improving cervical cancer literacy among African adolescents. However, achieving the WHO's cervical cancer elimination targets will require a shift from isolated educational sessions toward sustainable, curriculum-integrated, multilevel interventions involving schools, families, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Future research should prioritize the evaluation of long-term behavioral outcomes, particularly HPV vaccine uptake and participation in cervical cancer screening programmes.

articles.title: Factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of cervical cancer is highest in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet the region's coverage of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is still low and varies greatly between and within nations. HPV vaccination targets adolescents, making parental and caregiver consent and decision-making essential to vaccination program success. Parental hesitancy is a major determinant of whether national vaccination programs result in population-level protection, and a range of factors have been identified as drivers of parental reluctance.
OBJECTIVES: This scoping review aims to map and synthesize the evidence on factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa, including individual, household, sociocultural, informational, and health-system determinants, while identifying gaps for future research.
METHODS: An initial multi-database search (PubMed/MEDLINE, SpringerLink, ProQuest and ScienceDirect; May to June 2026) identified 236 records, of which 79 unique records were screened and 36 studies met the eligibility criteria. An updated search with expanded terms was then run in PubMed, ScienceDirect and SpringerLink and a new database, AJOL; (200 records), which added 22 eligible studies, giving 58 studies in total. Hesitancy was defined as delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite service availability; studies of acceptance, willingness, knowledge, attitudes or perceptions were eligible when they also reported determinants of hesitancy. Data were charted and synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: The 58 included studies spanned ten Sub-Saharan African countries namely Nigeria, Cameroon, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi, and Zambia, published between 2016 and 2026, and comprised cross-sectional surveys, qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, a randomized survey experiment, quasi-experimental studies, and programmatic/stakeholder assessments. Recurring factors included wide variation in HPV/cervical cancer awareness, safety and side-effect concerns (including fears of infertility and conspiracy beliefs), cost and geographic access barriers, religious and cultural beliefs, the paradoxical relationship between caregiver education and hesitancy, and the influence of health workers, social media, and community/religious leaders.
CONCLUSION: Parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination across Sub-Saharan Africa is shaped by overlapping informational, sociocultural, economic, and trust-related factors that vary substantially by country, delivery platform, and rollout maturity. Closing the region's HPV vaccination gap may require country and community-tailored, multicomponent strategies combining trusted-messenger communication, dedicated safety-concern counseling, and continued attention to cost and access barriers, particularly in under-studied countries and rural settings.

articles.title: Race-Neutral Spirometry Equations and Functional Classification of Latin American Children and Adolescents: A Multinational Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Race-neutral Global Lung Function Initiative (GLI)-Global spirometry equations are increasingly adopted, but their impact on the functional classification of children in Latin America has been examined only in single-country studies, leaving the region without multinational data.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of different spirometry reference equations on functional classification in Latin American children and adolescents, to characterize the physiological and demographic determinants associated with reclassification relative to GLI-Global, and to relate the reclassification of obstruction to bronchodilator responsiveness.
METHODS: Retrospective, cross-sectional study of spirometry in participants younger than 20 years at four Latin American sites (2009-2025). One test per individual was analyzed. Z-scores and functional patterns (normal, obstructive, non-specific, mixed; ATS/ERS 2022) were derived for Martínez-Briseño (a regional reference equation), NHANES-Hispanic, Knudson, GLI-2012 (Caucasian), and GLI-Global equations. Agreement (kappa) and logistic and multinomial models characterized reclassification relative to GLI-Global.
RESULTS: Among 13,171 children (median age 10.2 years; 56.4% male), GLI-Global classified 74.6% as normal versus 61.4% (Martínez-Briseño) and 64.4% (NHANES-Hispanic) in those ≥8 years, with the non-specific and mixed categories becoming uncommon. Relative to the regional equations, GLI-Global assigned higher FEV1 and FVC z-scores (by ∼0.95 SD versus Martínez-Briseño and ∼0.65 SD versus NHANES-Hispanic) while leaving the FEV1/FVC z-score little changed. Agreement with GLI-Global was 84.3% for Martínez-Briseño (kappa 0.65) and 88.7% for NHANES-Hispanic (0.75); GLI-2012 (Caucasian) agreed in 96.6%, although non-specific results still shifted to normal. GLI-Global reclassified about one in six tests-mostly low-FVC patterns moving to normal-with a net shift toward normal of + 7 to + 15 percentage points across sites. Among 11,621 children with post-bronchodilator testing, GLI-Global identified more bronchodilator-responsive children than Martínez-Briseño (24.1% versus 19.8%) but identified fewer with any abnormal finding (37.6% versus 42.3%; difference -4.7 percentage points, 95% CI - 5.4 to - 4.1); about one in eight bronchodilator-responsive obstructive children was relabeled as normal.
CONCLUSIONS: Relative to the equations in regional use, GLI-Global mainly relabels low-FVC patterns as normal in these referred children-a change in classification, not resolved disease. It identified more bronchodilator-responsive children but identified fewer children with any abnormal finding, and a larger share of responders had a baseline read as normal.

articles.title: Pharmacological considerations in opioid use disorder treatment in pregnant and postpartum patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Untreated perinatal opioid use disorder (OUD) is a major contributor to maternal and infant morbidity and mortality, worsened by an often adulterated fentanyl-dominant drug supply. Medication for OUD (MOUD) is standard of care, yet evidence guiding selection, initiation, dosing, pain management, neonatal withdrawal, breastfeeding, and postpartum continuity is evolving.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review with expert opinion synthesizes five years of literature, alongside foundational trials, on MOUD treatment across pregnancy, delivery, and the first postpartum year, prioritizing shared decision-making and trauma-responsive care. Topics include MOUD maternal dose and formulation, fentanyl-era induction, adulterant-complicated withdrawal, peripartum pain management, neonatal considerations, medication-specific breastfeeding, postpartum co-occurring mental health and MOUD access challenges, and long-term child outcomes. A PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov search (2020-2026) supplemented foundational sources.
EXPERT OPINION: Treatment needs to center in trust, non-judgment, and shared decision-making. Extended-release buprenorphine is an emerging preferred option, especially for patients stabilized on buprenorphine, and buprenorphine-naloxone appears to be as good as, if not better than, buprenorphine alone. Withdrawal management must accommodate an increasingly adulterated drug supply, and breastfeeding is generally compatible with MOUD. Like all children, prenatally opioid-exposed children need nurturing care, developmental screening, and early intervention when indicated.

articles.title: Pharmacotherapy options for managing hepatitis B in children: an update.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may face decades of infection before developing advanced liver disease. Although antiviral options have expanded, pediatric management remains challenging because of age-dependent treatment eligibility, limited long-term evidence, and uncertainty regarding functional cure.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines treatment indications, international guidelines, and the efficacy and safety of interferon-based therapy and nucleos(t)ide analogues in children and adolescents. International guidelines were prioritized, supplemented by PubMed and Cochrane Library searches through September 2026 without a lower publication-date limit. We discuss treatment withdrawal and developmental safety, including management during immunosuppression, considerations for special populations and transition to adult care. Emerging therapies are assessed with particular attention to the limits of applying adult results to children.
EXPERT OPINION: In our view, earlier treatment deserves studies, but younger age alone is insufficient grounds for intervention. Favorable responses in selected childhood cohorts do not establish that treating all children with high viremia improves lifelong outcomes. Bepirovirsen offers a concrete route toward finite therapy by reducing HBV transcripts, yet adult efficacy cannot establish pediatric benefit. Over the next five years, adolescent trials should determine whether such treatment could achieve sustained HBsAg loss after withdrawal without unacceptable toxicity. Until then, effective NA suppression remains a clinically valuable option, even when cure is not achieved.

articles.title: Clinical Perspectives on Heart-Kidney-Brain Crosstalk.
articles.journal: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular, kidney, and neurological diseases are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur, reflecting an integrated heart-kidney-brain axis linked by shared hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory pathways. This crosstalk maintains perfusion, blood volume, and metabolic homeostasis through coordinate signaling via the circulation, autonomic nervous system, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. When dysregulated, these same pathways perpetuate injury across organs, transforming adaptive responses into maladaptive cycles of dysfunction.This review synthesizes current understanding of the physiology and molecular mechanisms underlying heart-kidney-brain interactions, emphasizing hypoperfusion, neurohormonal activation, and convergent pathways of oxidative stress and inflammation as central drivers. Key amplifiers, including iron dysregulation, uremic toxin accumulation, and disordered mineral metabolism, extend injury systemically, contributing to cardiac remodeling, kidney disease, progression, and neurological disease. Clinically, this axis manifests as interconnected syndromes such as cardiorenal syndrome, cerebrovascular disease, and cognitive impairment. Emerging biomarkers and imaging modalities reveal overlapping signals across organs yet are rarely integrated in practice. Notably, neurological outcomes remain underrepresented in cardiovascular and kidney research despite their profound impact on quality of life, particularly in the pediatric population where disease affects lifelong development. We highlight gaps in mutli-organ diagnostic frameworks, biomarker standardization, and translational models, and propose future research directions in the heart-kidney-brain axis. Recognizing the heart, kidney, and brain as a unified system is essential to improving risk stratification, preventing multi-organ injury, and advancing patient-centered care.

articles.title: Mapping research on suicide bereavement in older adults: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Suicide bereavement may impact individuals from different age groups in varying ways. Existing research has mainly focused on suicide bereavement in adolescents and adults. This review aims to understand suicide bereavement amongst older adults and identify existing evidence gaps.
METHOD: The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR. Peer-reviewed articles were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO (Ovid), Medline (Ovid), and Embase (Ovid). Grey literature was identified through Google Scholar and ProQuest Thesis and Dissertations. Protocol registration OSF: https://osf.io/ub524/.
RESULTS: The review identified 11 relevant publications, five of which originated from the United States. Suicide-bereaved older adults face diverse challenges, including concerns about rebuilding their lives as time and resources become increasingly limited, as well as prioritising others' needs while suppressing personal grief. The impacts of their loss included an increased risk of suicidal behaviour and psychosocial problems, and diminished social support and help-seeking.
CONCLUSIONS: Further studies are urgently needed to explore the experiences and interventions of suicide bereavement in older adults, with consideration of various context, such as non-western and low-and-middle-income countries.

articles.title: "Are monoclonal antibodies going to be used the same way they are currently prescribed in asthma?".
articles.abstract: Biologics targeting IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, TSLP, and IgE continue to expand the therapeutic options for patients with severe asthma. Although they reduce exacerbation frequency, lower systemic corticosteroid exposure, and improve symptom control in selected patients with T2-high severe asthma, their benefits are incomplete and are unevenly distributed across the whole spectrum of the severe asthma population. Several unmet needs exist with the current use of biologics in asthma including the need for development of validated biomarkers, the conduct of adaptive trials with multi-biomarker and omics-guided selection coupled with pharmacogenetic studies and interventions evaluating therapies for neutrophilic, pauci-granulocytic and mixed disease. Early interventions targeting immune hyperresponsiveness and structural remodeling coupled with pragmatic comparative trials, disease registries, multi-omic biomarkers, prevention trials for the pediatric population and with integrated severe-asthma/comorbidity models are also need and hold the potential to improve the impact of biologics in severe asthma. In this review, we discuss the limitations and opportunities for the use of current biologics and describe future research needs within the framework of achieving disease modification and complete remission.

articles.title: Epistemic mistrust as a correlate of general psychopathology (p-factor) in adolescence: Evidence from community and clinical samples.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The psychological processes underlying broad psychopathological liability in adolescence, indexed by the p-factor, remain underspecified. Within the mentalising framework, epistemic trust refers to the capacity to regard communicated information as reliable, personally relevant and generalisable; its disruptions, expressed as Epistemic Mistrust or Credulity, may limit adaptive social learning and contribute to transdiagnostic vulnerability. We examined whether epistemic stances were associated with the p-factor in adolescence and whether these associations differed between community and clinical samples.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study of 1073 Italian adolescents (846 community, 227 clinical; Mage = 15.30, SD = 1.89).
METHODS: General psychopathology was estimated via a bifactor model based on YSR syndrome subscales; Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity were assessed by self-report (ETMCQ). Structural equation modelling tested associations between latent epistemic dimensions and estimated p-factor scores in the full sample and across groups.
RESULTS: In the full model, lower Trust and higher Mistrust and Credulity were each significantly associated with higher general psychopathology. Multi-group analyses indicated non-equivalent associations across groups, and path-by-path tests located this difference in Trust alone (Δχ2(1) = 9.30, p = .002); the Mistrust and Credulity coefficients did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Epistemic mistrust was associated with general psychopathology to a comparable degree in both community and clinical adolescents, as was epistemic credulity. The association involving Trust was present only among community adolescents, and this was the single group difference that survived formal testing.

articles.title: The Solitary Functioning Kidney: From Pathophysiology to Long-Term Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Solitary functioning kidney (SFK) is a clinical condition characterized by the presence of a single functioning kidney, arising from either congenital anomalies or acquired causes. It is recognized as an important risk factor for chronic kidney disease and, in some patients, progression to end-stage kidney disease. Previous publications have often addressed pediatric congenital SFK, living kidney donors, and disease-related nephrectomy cohorts separately, limiting the translation of heterogeneous evidence into a common clinical approach.
SUMMARY: This review integrates evidence on congenital and acquired SFK across the life course, covering etiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic assessment, risk factors, and long-term management. Despite differences in developmental background, timing of adaptation, and comorbidity burden, both conditions involve reduced functional nephron mass and compensatory adaptations. Renal enlargement and glomerular hyperfiltration initially preserve kidney function but may become maladaptive, contributing to glomerular injury, proteinuria, tubulointerstitial inflammation, and fibrosis. Ultrasonography, blood pressure measurement, urinary albumin or protein assessment, and estimated glomerular filtration rate remain central to clinical evaluation, whereas most emerging biomarkers require further validation. Prognostic assessment should integrate established kidney injury with etiology-specific indicators of renal reserve and additional renal insults.
KEY MESSAGES: Persistent albuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension, and declining kidney function are the principal clinical indicators of adverse renal outcomes in SFK. We propose an evidence-informed, two-step framework that first identifies established kidney injury and then assesses residual renal reserve and additional "second hits" to guide dynamic risk stratification and individualized follow-up. Management should emphasize appropriate lifestyle measures, blood pressure and proteinuria control, and avoidance of additional nephrotoxic insults, with pharmacological therapy guided by kidney injury and comorbidities. The proposed framework complements established CKD classification and population-specific recommendations but remains conceptual and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis: a comparative DTI-ALPS study with healthy controls and epilepsy patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is characterized by pathogenic autoantibody-mediated synaptic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms facilitating antibody access to the brain parenchyma remain incompletely understood. The glymphatic system, which supports cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange along perivascular spaces, has been implicated in immune surveillance and waste clearance; however, its involvement in anti-NMDAR encephalitis has not been fully investigated in vivo.
METHODS: Glymphatic system-related function was assessed using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) in 15 patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis, 17 patients with epilepsy, and 18 healthy controls. Group differences in ALPS-index values were analyzed with adjustment for age and sex. Associations between ALPS-indexes, clinical severity, and regional brain volumes were further examined.
RESULTS: ALPS-index values were significantly reduced in both anti-NMDAR encephalitis and epilepsy compared with healthy controls. Across all groups, ALPS-indexes demonstrated strong bilateral correlations, with consistently lower values in the right hemisphere. In anti-NMDAR encephalitis, lower ALPS-index values were associated with longer hospitalization and higher modified Rankin Scale scores, whereas no associations were observed with cerebrospinal fluid anti-NMDAR antibody titers. In epilepsy, ALPS-indexes showed a distinct pattern of clinical and structural correlations, including associations with regional brain volumes that were absent in the NMDAR group. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated moderate-to-good discriminative performance of ALPS-indexes for both disease groups.
CONCLUSION: DTI-ALPS reveals altered perivascular water diffusivity in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, which correlates with clinical severity independently of antibody titers. These findings suggest glymphatic-related dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, and indicate that the ALPS-index captures disease-relevant pathophysiological processes beyond antibody burden, with potential utility as a noninvasive imaging marker for clinical assessment and prognosis in immune-mediated encephalitis.

articles.title: Clinical and treatment profiles of myasthenic crisis patients in a tertiary hospital in the Philippines: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myasthenic crisis is a life-threatening complication of myasthenia gravis. Data on its clinical profile and outcomes in resource-limited settings are limited.
METHODS: A retrospective review of pediatric and adult myasthenic crisis patients admitted at Philippine General Hospital from 2015 to 2024 was conducted. Sociodemographic, clinical, treatment, and outcome data were extracted from inpatient charts. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square, Fisher's exact, Wilcoxon rank-sum, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to analyze associations between clinical characteristics and outcomes.
RESULTS: Eighty-two patients were included, mostly female (n = 49, 59.8%) with peak onset in the third decade. Infection was the leading precipitant of crisis, while hypertension, diabetes, and tuberculosis were common comorbidities. Nearly all required ventilation (96.3%, median nine days). Mortality was 13.4% (n = 11), mainly due to sepsis and respiratory failure. Younger age (< 30 years, p = 0.021) was linked to improved survival, whereas absence of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) or therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) was associated with higher mortality (p = 0.012).
CONCLUSION: This study provided one of the largest descriptions of myasthenic crisis in the Philippines, demonstrating that infection remains the predominant inciting factor and timely rescue immunotherapy is associated with improved survival. These findings support strengthening access to specialized neuromuscular care and crisis-directed therapies in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Longitudinal exploration of auditory sensory-perceptual processing in CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (Batten disease)): A high-density auditory evoked potential (AEP) study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is currently limited information about sensory and perceptual abilities across the progression of CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis; Batten disease), a recessively inherited lysosomal storage disorder and a leading cause of childhood neurodegeneration. Clinical symptoms include vision loss, motor impairments, and cognitive challenges, making it difficult to accurately assess neurocognitive and perceptual abilities. Thus, there is a critical need to identify objective biomarkers that can be used to inform disease progression and track treatment response in this population.
METHODS: This exploratory case series investigates longitudinal changes in auditory sensory perceptual processing over several years in a small sample of individuals with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease (N = 4; 3 male) compared to a cross-sectional sample of 60 neurotypical (NT) controls using high-density electroencephalography (EEG). We utilized a duration mismatch negativity (MMN) paradigm, identical to what has been used in our previous cross-sectional study. We examined the auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) of the standard tones across three different stimulus onset asynchrony conditions and examined the N1 and P2 components of the AEP.
