RESULTS: Early evidence shows differences in the amplitudes of the N1 and P2 components in individuals with CLN3 disease relative to NT controls. These amplitude differences were most notable in CLN3 disease when participants were presented with standard tones that had the slowest presentation rate. Specifically, N1 and P2 amplitudes were more negative than NT controls in childhood and adolescence and as CLN3 disease participants aged, the amplitude of the AEPs was more positive than controls. Further, a more positive N1 amplitude during the longest stimulus presentation condition was associated with both reduced verbal intelligence and working memory abilities in CLN3 disease participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Our preliminary case-series findings parallel recently published work in a mouse model of CLN3 disease that showed both sex- and age-dependent disruptions in central auditory processing. Taken together, we demonstrate the utility of auditory EEG measures as a sensitive, objective and translational measure in CLN3 disease that may serve as a potential outcome measure useful in tracking disease progression. Continued work is needed in humans focused on sex-based differences and longitudinal changes of auditory processing in CLN3 disease.

articles.title: Mapping Gaps in the day of Birth Care Pathway: A Qualitative Birth Observation Study Informing Service Delivery Redesign in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improving maternal and neonatal health (MNH) care quality remains a critical challenge in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This study used a qualitative birth observation approach to identify operational and practice gaps across the institutional delivery continuum in five selected facilities to inform service-delivery improvements within a Service Delivery Redesign (SDR) framework.
METHODS: A descriptive qualitative study based on structured, non-participatory observations was conducted from September to November 2023. Professional clinicians documented 34 deliveries from admission through the immediate postpartum period across five health facilities. Data were analyzed using a hybrid deductive-inductive thematic approach mapped against the WHO quality of care domains. Data saturation was achieved through daily thematic debriefings and iterative analysis.
RESULTS: Quality gaps were observed at all stages of care within the studied facilities. At admission, initial assessment frequently relied on historical prenatal records rather than real-time triage. Labor monitoring was critically compromised; partographs were routinely populated retrospectively with fabricated parameters for audit compliance rather than real-time decision-making. Non-recommended practices, such as fundal pressure, were frequently performed, in some cases by unsupervised trainees. Essential newborn care revealed a near-total omission of immediate skin-to-skin contact, alongside delays in cord care and breastfeeding initiation. Active clinical surveillance during the first six hours postpartum was fundamentally non-existent.
CONCLUSION: Significant clinical and structural gaps across the maternal and newborn care pathway in the observed facilities are driven by weak organizational routines and fragmented workflows. While these findings cannot be statistically generalized to the entire DRC, they suggest that quality improvement within these contexts should shift from passive geographic coverage toward designated high-volume delivery hubs capable of ensuring safe and respectful care.

articles.title: Multiparametric Prediction for Histological Chorioamnionitis Stage in Preterm Premature Rupture of Membranes: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the predictive value of multiparametric combinations for discriminating histological chorioamnionitis (HCA) severity in women with preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) and histologically confirmed HCA.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 182 women with PPROM complicated by HCA, stratified into mild and moderate-to-severe HCA groups based on histological staging. Maternal and neonatal outcomes were compared between groups. Risk factors were identified through multivariable analysis, and a predictive model combining biomarkers and clinical characteristics was developed.
RESULTS: Women with moderate-to-severe HCA delivered at earlier gestational ages and had neonates with lower birth weights than those with mild HCA, along with significantly higher rates of clinical chorioamnionitis, neonatal complications, and prolonged neonatal hospitalization. After adjustment for gestational age at delivery, moderate-to-severe HCA remained independently associated with neonatal sepsis, acidosis, and anemia. C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, fibrinogen, alkaline phosphatase, globulin, and total bilirubin were identified as independent risk factors for severe HCA. The multiparametric prediction model demonstrated good discriminative ability (AUC = 0.870), which was marginally improved by inclusion of gestational age at PPROM onset (AUC = 0.878). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.856, and calibration assessment showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed probabilities.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, maternal and neonatal risks in PPROM are associated with the severity of HCA. A multiparametric prediction model combining biomarkers with clinical parameters showed potential for discriminating HCA severity; however, prospective external validation is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Dosing Evaluation for Sedation in Neonates Undergoing Therapeutic Hypothermia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recently, dexmedetomidine has replaced opioids for sedation in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). The study objectives were to describe dosing patterns, evaluate compliance, and compare effectiveness and safety between the original (pre-implementation) and revised (post-implementation) in-house dexmedetomidine dosing guidelines.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study that included neonates with HIE admitted to a level IV NICU for therapeutic hypothermia comparing two dexmedetomidine dosing regimens: (1) pre-implementation: starting dose of 0.05 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.05 μg/kg/h every 6 h as needed, and (2) post-implementation: 0.2 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.1 μg/kg/h every 30-60 min as needed.
RESULTS: A total of 106 neonates were included: 50 in the pre-implementation group and 56 in the post-implementation group. Compliance to post-implementation formulary recommendations was 69.6% for initial doses, 62.5% for dose increases, and 44.6% for dose decreases. An increased odds of opioid exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 7.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.59-51.5, p = 0.02) and greater proportion of bradycardia (21.4% vs. 4%, p = 0.03) were observed in the post-implementation group. No significant differences in effectiveness end points or hypotension were observed between groups (p ≥ 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Compliance with formulary-recommended dexmedetomidine dosing was variable and dose decreases were common in the post-implementation group. The post-implementation dosing approach was not associated with improved effectiveness outcomes (sedation) but was associated with greater opioid exposure and more bradycardia, supporting the need for further prospective evaluation to determine the optimal dexmedetomidine dosing in neonates undergoing HIE.

articles.title: Emerging antimicrobial resistance among uropathogens causing urinary tract infections in pregnant women: a retrospective study from Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract: It is evident that urinary tract infections (UTIs) can lead to poor maternal and perinatal outcomes. We designed this study to assess the susceptibility patterns of urinary pathogens to antimicrobials, along with their applicability for the mother and fetus, to ensure effective UTI treatment during pregnancy. This retrospective study was conducted to assess bacterial UTIs in the inpatient department of a tertiary care teaching hospital in Saudi Arabia. A total of 154 pregnant women with a confirmed case of UTI were included. Urine samples were collected by the midstream urine sampling method as per the standard procedure. We observed that around 52% of participants were in the 26-35 age group. The most common isolate was Escherichia coli (58.44%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (22.73%) and Streptococcus group B (3.90%). Considering the best choices in pregnancy for Escherichia coli isolates, nitrofurantoin (100%) showed the highest efficacy among participants, followed by fosfomycin (88.8%), amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (84.28%), and cefotaxime intravenously (90%). In prenatal care, it is of the utmost importance to regularly evaluate the susceptibility and resistance pattern of antimicrobials to UTI-related pathogens during the course of pregnancy in order to provide optimal therapy for both mothers and infants.

articles.title: Gut microbiome and fecal metabolome dysregulation in pediatric atopic eczema: a multi-omics correlation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic eczema (AE) is a highly prevalent inflammatory skin disorder in children, with growing evidence underscoring the role of gut microbiota dysbiosis in its pathogenesis. However, the specific mechanisms by which gut microbes and their metabolic products contribute to AE development remain poorly understood.
METHODS: This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach to investigate the gut ecosystem in pediatric AE. Fecal samples from affected children and matched controls were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing to profile the gut microbiota and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based metabolomics to characterize the fecal metabolome.
RESULTS: Significant gut microbial dysbiosis was observed in children with AE, marked by reduced species diversity and altered community structure. Specifically, the relative abundances of key genera such as Streptococcus, Enterococcus, and Bifidobacterium were significantly diminished. Correlation network analysis revealed the metabolite Fruleuile as a central hub in the microbe-metabolite interaction network, demonstrating significant associations with several bacterial genera, including Mycobacterium. Our findings confirm significant gut microbiota dysbiosis in pediatric AE and identify distinct microbial and metabolic signatures associated with the condition. The metabolite Fruleuile emerges as a potential key mediator in the gut-skin axis, highlighting the importance of host-microbiota metabolic interactions in the pathophysiology of AE patients.

articles.title: Geographical disparities in risks of emergency department visits due to intentional self-harm in Florida: a retrospective ecological study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intentional self-harm is a major and growing public health concern in Florida, contributing to thousands of emergency department (ED) visits each year. Although there is evidence that the burden of intentional self-harm varies by geographical location, little is known about disparities of intentional self-harm related ED visit risks in Florida. Understanding these disparities is important for guiding health planning, allocation of resources, and tailoring efforts to mitigate the problem. Therefore, the objectives of this study were to investigate county-level geographic disparities in intentional self-harm-related ED visit risks in Florida.
METHODS: Retrospective ED data were obtained from Florida Health Charts, a publicly available data dashboard maintained by the Florida Department of Health. County-level age-adjusted intentional self-harm-related ED visit risks were calculated for four time periods: 2016-2017, 2018-2019, 2020-2021 and 2022-2023. Tango's spatial scan statistics were used to identify high-risk clusters. Two sample tests of proportions were used to compare proportions of counties and populations in high-risk clusters between rural and urban areas.
RESULTS: Age-adjusted intentional self-harm-related ED visit risks decreased from 139.4 to 127.4 visits per 100,000 persons over the study period. Counties in the northwest, northeast, central, and southwest Florida tended to have high risks. Statistically significant high-risk clusters of intentional self-harm ED visits were detected in multiple predominantly rural areas, with seven clusters in 2016-2017 (relative risks (RR) = 1.2-2.2), nine clusters in 2018-2019 (RR = 1.2-2.8), five clusters in 2020-2021 (RR = 1.3-1.9), and six clusters in 2022-2023 (RR = 1.2-1.9). The proportion of counties in high-risk clusters increased from 46.3% in 2020-2021 to 61.2% in 2022-2023. While there were no significant (p > 0.05) differences between rural and urban counties in earlier periods (2016-2021), by 2022-2023 significantly (p = 0.001) more rural (81.3%) than urban (42.9%) counties were part of high-risk clusters. Over the study period, 34.3% of the counties were persistently part of high-risk clusters. There was a significantly (p < 0.0001) higher proportion of rural than urban residents living in high-risk clusters; increasing from 57.2% in 2016-2017 to 71.9% in 2022-2023 in rural areas compared to an increase from 35.0% in 2016-2017 to 41.8% in 2022-2023 in urban areas.
CONCLUSION: Despite the declining trend, geographic disparities of intentional self-harm related ED visit risks exist in Florida. Study findings may be useful for informing future studies, targeted intentional self-harm prevention strategies, and need-based resource allocation geared at reducing disparities and improving population health for all.

articles.title: Neuromuscular efficiency in schoolchildren: a 16-week structured exercise program improves plantar load distribution across static, dynamic and load-bearing tasks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular efficiency in children is associated with the control of postural and gait mechanics, which are dependent on physical activity levels. Alterations in plantar pressure distribution provide objective indices of load control and efficiency of movement under various functional conditions. The study aimed to explore the effects of a 16-week structured exercise program on plantar pressure distribution and neuromuscular efficiency in schoolchildren at static, dynamic, and load-bearing conditions.
METHODS: For a total of 147 schoolchildren, a controlled experimental design where pre-post measurements were conducted (experimental: n = 74; control: n = 73). Plantar pressure was evaluated during standing, ambulation, and walking with a schoolbag. Statistical analyses were conducted with paired and independent t-tests, and two-way mixed analysis of variance (ANOVA).
RESULTS: There was a significant reduction in plantar pressure in the experimental condition (standing: p = .024; walking: p = .017; load: p = .010), while there were no significant changes in the control group. Weight-bearing symmetry increased appreciably for the experimental group (p < .001). Group and condition effects were found to have significant main effects in ANOVA, alongside significant interaction effects (p < .05), showing that changes are felt more under the conditions of dynamic or load-bearing tasks.
CONCLUSIONS: The results show that systematic exercise increases neuromuscular utilization by optimizing distribution of loads, postural coordination and functional adaptation. The gradual improvement across all training conditions indicates that the greatest improvements occurred under dynamic and load-bearing conditions compared with quiet standing. These findings also support the development of a structured model of exercise at school for the promotion of postural health and optimal function of movement in children.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial Network Associations in Paediatric Chronic Pain: A Cross-Lagged Panel Network Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biopsychosocial models of chronic pain emphasize interactions between biological, psychological and social processes, yet little is known about their organization over time in paediatric chronic pain. This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal network associations among pain intensity, pain interference, pain extent, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, pain catastrophizing, sleep disturbance, fatigue and peer relationships in children and adolescents with chronic pain.
METHODS: The baseline network was estimated using a Gaussian graphical model with regularized partial correlations (N = 744). Cross-lagged panel network models were used to examine autoregressive and cross-lagged associations from baseline to 12 months (n = 357) and 24 months (n = 186) among youth with persistent chronic pain.
RESULTS: Pain interference had the highest cross-sectional strength centrality, followed by depressive and anxiety symptoms. Strongest baseline associations involved fatigue-pain interference, anxiety-depressive symptoms, pain catastrophizing-anxiety symptoms and sleep disturbance-pain interference. In the longitudinal models, pain interference showed the most consistent prospective pattern, with associations to later pain catastrophizing at 12 months and to later sleep disturbance and pain catastrophizing at 24 months. Depressive symptoms and pain catastrophizing were more often associated with prior levels of other domains.
CONCLUSION: Findings extend prior cross-sectional evidence by showing that pain interference was highly connected at baseline and prospectively involved among youth with persistent chronic pain. Pain interference may represent an informative functional domain for understanding how pain-related, psychological and physical difficulties are organized over time, supporting the clinical relevance of assessing interference with daily functioning.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study extends paediatric chronic pain research by examining cross-sectional and longitudinal associations among pain-related, psychological, physical and social domains. Pain interference showed the highest connectivity at baseline and was consistently involved in prospective associations, particularly with pain catastrophizing and sleep disturbance. These findings highlight multidomain assessment and suggest that interference with daily functioning may help identify broader pain-related difficulties that could otherwise be missed.

articles.title: MVCNN model for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea prediction via facial photos.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) diagnosis but is limited for large-scale screening and telemedicine by high costs and specialized requirements. Given the close correlation between craniofacial features and OSA, this study developed a non-invasive risk stratification model (non-OSA, mild OSA, and moderate-to-severe OSA) using two-dimensional multi-view facial photographs based on a Multi-View Convolutional Neural Network (MVCNN).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 212 children with frontal and lateral facial photographs linked to polysomnography. Models were evaluated at the patient level after aggregating each participant's available image records. The MVCNN was internally evaluated in 149 patients and externally evaluated in 63 patients. Patient-level discrimination and classification metrics were estimated with bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired bootstrap analysis compared models evaluated on common patients.
RESULTS: In the internal patient-level evaluation, MVCNN achieved a macro-AUC of 0.898 (95% CI, 0.863-0.930), macro-F1 of 0.839, balanced accuracy of 0.840, and overall accuracy of 0.846. Its macro-AUC exceeded those of ResNet-50 by 0.061 (95% CI, 0.022-0.106; P = 0.004) and VGG-16 by 0.104 (95% CI, 0.057-0.164; P < 0.001). In the external cohort, MVCNN achieved a macro-AUC of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.827-0.919), macro-F1 of 0.833, balanced accuracy of 0.826, and overall accuracy of 0.841.
CONCLUSIONS: Patient-level analyses support the discriminatory performance of multi-view facial photography for pediatric OSA risk stratification in the studied dental cohorts. Prospective validation, direct view-ablation studies, and calibration in broader clinical populations are required before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Seropositivity patterns of six epstein-barr virus antibodies among hospital attendees in suburban shanghai, China: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe the seropositivity patterns of six Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) antibodies among hospital attendees in Jinshan District, suburban Shanghai, and their distribution by sex and age group.MethodsThis retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 2,450 hospital attendees who underwent a six-marker EBV serology panel at Tinglin Hospital, Jinshan District, Shanghai, from July 2020 to May 2026. Counts, percentages and Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Group comparisons used Pearson chi-square tests, with Holm correction across 18 marker-specific comparisons. Pooled calendar-quarter comparisons and selected crude prevalence ratios (PRs) were exploratory.ResultsAt least one EBV antibody was detected in 2356/2450 (96.16%; 95% CI 95.33-96.85). VCA IgG was most frequent (93.67%; 95% CI 92.64-94.57), whereas EA IgA was least frequent (5.31%; 95% CI 4.49-6.27). After Holm correction, no marker-specific differences by sex or age group remained statistically significant.ConclusionsThis hospital-based study describes six-marker EBV seropositivity among clinically tested attendees. The findings should not be interpreted as community prevalence, incidence, active infection, or evidence of diagnostic or screening performance. Exploratory calendar-quarter differences are hypothesis-generating because clinical selection, incomplete calendar coverage, patient composition and testing practice may affect the observed distributions.

articles.title: Influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors, including asthma diagnosis, in Korea: analysis of the Korea national health and nutrition examination survey (2014-2021).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors in the South Korean population, focusing on individuals with asthma across age groups.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted using Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2014-2021) for 43,191 individuals (aged ≥6 years). Vaccination rates and predictors were examined in the general population and those with asthma across four age cohorts (6-13, 14-18, 19-64, and ≥ 65 years) using survey-weighted logistic regression.
RESULTS: Vaccination coverage was consistently higher among individuals with asthma than those without: 68.2% vs. 62.8% (ages 6-13), 36.8% vs. 27.1% (ages 14-18), 28.5% vs. 27.0% (ages 19-39), 48.2% vs. 32.1% (ages 40-64), and 85.3% vs. 82.5% (ages ≥65). Female sex and chronic comorbidities positively correlated with vaccination. Increasing age was linked to lower coverage in youth but higher coverage in adults. Notably, asthma history independently predicted vaccination in age groups with lower baseline coverage.
CONCLUSIONS: Although individuals with asthma showed higher coverage, vaccination rates remained suboptimal, particularly among adolescents and working-age adults. Proactive age-tailored vaccination strategies are needed.

articles.title: Validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the modified Yale food addiction scale for children 2.0 among adolescents in Istanbul, Türkiye.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study adapted and validated the Turkish Modified Yale Food Addiction Scale for Children 2.0 (mYFAS-C 2.0) in adolescents aged 13-17 years.
METHODS: Following World Health Organization guidelines, 532 adolescents (267 non-clinical, 265 clinical) in Istanbul, Türkiye completed the mYFAS-C 2.0, Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire Short Form, and Perceived Stress Scale. Construct validity and three-week test-retest reliability (n = 91) were evaluated.
RESULTS: Exploratory factor analysis supported a single-factor structure (46.11% variance). Confirmatory factor analysis showed good fit (χ2/df = 4.19, comparative fit index = 0.93, Tucker-Lewis index = 0.91, standardized root mean square residual = 0.04, root mean square error of approximation = 0.08; loadings: 0.58-0.74). Cronbach's α (0.90) and intraclass correlation coefficient (0.99) demonstrated high reliability. Total scores correlated with eating pathology (r = 0.68) and perceived stress (r = 0.32) (p < 0.01). Clinical participants scored higher than non-clinical controls (28.24 ± 11.16 vs. 20.37 ± 5.95, p < 0.01), peaking in adolescents with obesity (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: The Turkish mYFAS-C 2.0 is a valid, reliable instrument for assessing addictive-like eating behaviors among Turkish adolescents aged 13-17 years.

articles.title: Recreational opportunities and mentorship at Play Marin enhance health and well-being for adolescents in Marin City, CA.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Finding evidence-based interventions and community supported solutions to the mental health crisis among youth is imperative. We aimed to understand the impact of Play Marin (PM, a community-based organization) on overall well-being using data collected from current and former students and community members.
METHODS: The research methodology consisted of a mixed methods approach: interviews were conducted with students of PM, family members and coaches in the Spring of 2024. Quantitatively, the survey data were compared between former students of PM and the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS), collected in 2024.
RESULTS: Qualitatively revealed results that individuals associated with PM experienced recreational opportunities and mentorship, better mental and physical health, and increased feelings of belonging. Quantitative results suggested participants had better mental health, less screentime, competed on more sports teams, slept more on school nights, vaped less, and felt closer to other students at school (p < 0.05) as compared to the YRBSS.
CONCLUSIONS: The current mental health crisis may be alleviated with increased recreational opportunities and mentorship for adolescents and young adults through community engagement and positive interactions. Exposure to mentors with lived experiences help adolescents gain necessary tools and resources to make better health decisions than the YRBSS.

articles.title: Radiology-to-Surgical Consultation Timing for Suspected Appendicitis in the Emergency Department: Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute appendicitis is a common condition that typically requires surgery, yet the workflow linking diagnostic imaging to surgical consultation varies substantially across emergency departments (EDs). Delays between imaging completion and consultation ordering may prolong care and contribute to avoidable clinical and operational inefficiencies.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to quantify real-world consultation delays among patients with radiology-confirmed appendicitis, identify factors associated with prolonged delays, and establish a manually adjudicated dataset linking radiology impression language to consultation behavior as an empirical foundation for future workflow automation. This study did not develop or evaluate a natural language processing (NLP) system; rather, the NLP and automation applications discussed represent potential areas for future work.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational study of ED encounters at a single academic medical center from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2025, during which abdominal imaging was obtained to evaluate possible appendicitis (N=1422). All radiology impressions were manually adjudicated and classified as positive, indeterminate, or negative. The primary timing measure was the interval from imaging completion to the placement of a surgical consultation order, which was analyzed within a predefined plausible window of -60 to +360 minutes. Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare delays across imaging modalities and age groups. Logistic regression was used to assess predictors of prolonged delay (>30 minutes).
RESULTS: Among 1422 encounters, radiology findings were classified as positive for appendicitis in 566 (39.8%), indeterminate in 675 (47.5%), and negative in 181 (12.7%). Surgical teams evaluated 99.8% (565/566) of patients with radiology-positive findings. Among 524 radiology-positive encounters with complete time stamps within the plausible window, the median time from imaging completion to consultation order was 30.8 (IQR 17.8-48.5) minutes, and 268 (51.1%) encounters exceeded 30 minutes. Delays were longer for computed tomography (CT) than for ultrasound (median 34.9 [IQR 21.7-53.0] vs 21.2 [IQR 10.9-36.4] minutes; P<.001). In adjusted analysis, CT was associated with prolonged delay (odds ratio [OR] 2.29, 95% CI 1.08-4.86; P=.03), whereas adult age group was not (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.52-2.28; P=.81). Across a typical year, cumulative imaging-to-consultation waiting time totaled approximately 58 patient-hours.
CONCLUSIONS: Radiology-confirmed appendicitis reliably triggered surgical evaluation, yet meaningful delays remained. This foundational timing analysis and the accompanying adjudicated dataset quantify the opportunity for future workflow improvements and can inform the development and evaluation of NLP-driven tools to automate consultation activation following clear radiologic diagnoses. Prospective studies are needed to develop and validate such systems.

articles.title: Operating room extubation: experience from a public Brazilian pediatric cardiovascular center.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence and success of intentional postoperative operating room extubation after elective congenital cardiac surgery at a Brazilian federal referral center and identify factors associated with non-extubation and extubation failure.
METHODS: This historical cohort study was conducted in a pediatric and neonatal cardiac intensive care unit over five years. Patients aged 0-18 years with congenital heart disease who underwent elective corrective or palliative cardiac surgery without preoperative mechanical ventilation were included. The primary outcome was operating room extubation, and the secondary outcome was extubation success, defined as no reintubation within 48 postoperative hours. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance identified factors independently associated with nonextubation and extubation failure (p<0.05).
RESULTS: Among 637 patients, 37% were extubated in the operating room, with a 98% success rate. They were older, had higher body weight, shorter noninvasive ventilation duration, shorter intensive care unit stays, and lower mortality. Increasing age reduced the risk of non-extubation. The need for noninvasive ventilation and longer intensive care unit stay were independently associated with non-extubation and extubation failure, although only four failures occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Operating room extubation was feasible in a substantial proportion of pediatric patients and achieved a high success rate, supporting its safety in selected cases. Greater surgical complexity, need for noninvasive ventilation, and longer intensive care unit stay increased the risk of non-extubation, whereas increasing age reduced this risk.

articles.title: Delayed umbilical cord clamping in rooming-in term newborns: benefits and neonatal outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate neonatal outcomes associated with delayed umbilical cord clamping (DCC) in term newborns admitted to a rooming-in unit.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted at a university hospital (April-August 2023). Singleton neonates ≥37 weeks' gestation without congenital malformations or infections were included. Exclusion criteria were intermediate or intensive care admission, umbilical cord clamping time between 30-60 seconds, and hemolytic disease. Participants were divided into two groups based on clamping time: early (0-30 seconds) and delayed (1-3 minutes). Primary outcomes: jaundice requiring phototherapy and length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes: skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding within the first hour, hematological parameters, and polycythemia. Data were analyzed using Student's t-test, χ2, and odds ratio (OR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Among the 363 newborns studied (52.14% male; mean gestational age of 39 weeks±1.34 and weight 3240 g±422.54), 281 (77%) underwent DCC. The delayed clamping group showed a significantly lower requirement for neonatal resuscitation (4 vs. 18%), a lower incidence of Apgar scores < 7 at the first minute (0.5 vs. 17%), and a fivefold increase in skin-to-skin contact (IC95% 2.42-12.43). No significant differences were found between groups regarding five-minute Apgar scores, bilirubin levels, the need for phototherapy, weight loss and length of hospital stay. Polycythemia was rare in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: DCC is a beneficial and safe practice for healthy term newborns. It allows for immediate skin-to-skin contact without increasing the risk of jaundice requiring phototherapy or polycythemia, reinforcing its role as a fundamental component of humanized neonatal care.

articles.title: The Effect of ADHD Symptoms on the ND-PAE Diagnosis in Children with Heavy Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
articles.abstract: This study assessed the specificity of the Neurobehavioral Disorder Associated with Prenatal Alcohol Exposure (ND-PAE) diagnosis in individuals with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) and controls with and without symptoms of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Participants were recruited from six collaborative sites; data were analyzed using logistic regression. The results of study 1 showed that both ADHD symptomatology and PAE significantly increased the likelihood of ND-PAE categorization; however, the interaction between ADHD and PAE did not. Study 2 showed that in children with ADHD symptoms, PAE significantly predicted endorsement of the Adaptive Functioning diagnostic domain. Therefore, having ADHD does not differentially affect the likelihood of ND-PAE categorization in those with PAE, but adaptive functioning challenges set PAE apart from ADHD. Although confirmation of PAE is required for the diagnosis of ND-PAE, further research is needed to address the specificity of this diagnosis, potentially using adaptive functioning symptoms.

articles.title: Stable and Dynamic Influences of Parent Internalizing Symptoms and Parenting Stress on Psychopathology in Children with a Chronic Physical Illness: The Moderating Role of Child Hair Cortisol.
articles.abstract: Children with a chronic physical illness (CPI), such as diabetes, asthma, and epilepsy, experience significant stress and are at a greater risk of psychopathology. Parent distress strongly influences child psychopathology, and understanding stable and dynamic paths of transmission are critical for developing effective interventions. This study examined the between-dyad (stable) and within-dyad (dynamic) effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on psychopathology in children with a CPI. Additionally, we examined whether these associations were moderated by child hair cortisol concentration (HCC). Data come from 244 children (2-16 years at baseline) with a CPI, and their parents, who were followed for 48-months (assessments at baseline, 6, 12, 24, and 48 months). Parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress were assessed using self-report measures. Hair samples were collected from children, and parents reported child psychopathology symptoms. Previous work identified three HCC trajectories among children in this sample: Hypersecretion (68.0%), Hyposecretion (8.6%), and Hyper-to-Hypo (23.4%). There were significant between- and within-dyad effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on child internalizing and externalizing symptoms. Child HCC moderated the between-dyad effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on child internalizing symptoms. The combination of high average levels of parent internalizing symptoms or parenting stress and cortisol hypersecretion predicted greater child symptoms. Findings highlight the importance of considering parent distress, paired with child cortisol, to understand psychopathology risk in children with a CPI. Overall, HCC may be a promising biomarker for understanding heterogeneity in associations between parent distress and child psychopathology.

articles.title: Association of Pubertal Timing and Progression with Variation in the Dual Systems Imbalance Gap: The Moderating Role of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract: This study sought to examine the direct effects of puberty on dual systems imbalance for male and female youth and test for a moderating effect of autism spectrum disorder. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development data were analyzed. Ordinary least squares regression was used to test for direct and moderated effects of interest. Earlier pubertal development was associated only marginally significantly associated with greater dual systems imbalance characterized by greater sensation-seeking and lower impulse control for male youth. Autism spectrum disorder was significantly and negatively associated with dual systems imbalance, meaning lower sensation-seeking and greater impulse control. No significant direct effects were observed for female youth. No significant moderation effects were observed for either sex. Findings suggest the importance of autism and potentially pubertal developmental rate for understanding dual systems development for male youth, but not female youth.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Digital Interventions for Youth Anxiety, Depression, ADHD, and Misconduct: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) testing youth digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) typically evaluate one type of DMHI for one problem (e.g., computerized-CBT for depression); although DMHIs are diverse, few evaluations have examined a broad range of them to identify cross-cutting features associated with effectiveness. Searching PsycINFO and PubMed for RCTs testing DMHIs for pediatric anxiety, depression, ADHD, and/or misconduct, we identified 91 articles (35 testing ADHD interventions, anxiety = 29, depression = 14, misconduct = 8, multiple = 5 [102 treatment-control comparisons]). Robust variance estimation (RVE) analyses demonstrated pooled effect sizes (ES) of g = 0.29 (95% CI [0.24, 0.35], p < .001) at post-treatment and g = 0.21 (95% CI [0.12, 0.30], p < .001) at follow-up, with substantial between-study heterogeneity at post-treatment (I2 = 49.15%; τ2 = 0.05; 95% PI [-0.15, 0.74]) and follow-up (I2 = 54.96%; τ2 = 0.05; 95% PI [-0.25, 0.67]). We conducted bivariate moderator analyses (e.g., intervention target, content, administration method) and covariate-adjusted models. Sources of between-study heterogeneity include treatment type (e.g., larger effects for CBT than bio-/neurofeedback), therapist support (larger effects with vs. without), and control group (larger effects when compared against no-treatment controls vs. active controls). Treatment target also moderated ES (e.g., anxiety [g = 0.41] greater than ADHD [g = 0.16]). Future work should attend to publication and study-quality-related bias, and test promising DMHI features experimentally.PROSPERO Pre-Registration: CRD42022357707 ( https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42022357707 ).

articles.title: Evaluating the evidence of health consequences of celiac disease: an umbrella review of meta-analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Celiac disease (CeD) extends beyond the gastrointestinal tract and may affect multiple organ systems. However, the credibility of reported extra-intestinal associations remains uncertain.
METHODS: We searched PubMed and Scopus until August 2024 for systematic reviews and meta-analyses of observational studies evaluating associations between CeD and any health-related outcome. Each meta-analytic association was appraised using established credibility criteria.
RESULTS: Thirteen publications met eligibility, reporting 26 meta-analytic associations, 17 of which were nominally statistically significant (P < 0.05). One association achieved strong evidence: CeD and higher risk of thyroid disease evaluated across all ages (odds ratio [OR] = 3.09, 95% CI: 2.33-4.09, nstudies = 12, I2 = 40%). Three associations reached highly suggestive evidence: CeD and higher risk of pneumococcal infection at all ages (OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.43-1.92, nstudies = 3, I2 = 0%) and among children/adolescents, lower bone mineral content (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.65, 95% Cl: -0.83 to -0.48, nstudies = 15, I2 = 67%), and lower areal bone mineral density (SMD = -0.80, 95% Cl: -1.03 to -0.56, nstudies=15, I2 = 72%). Most meta-analyses were based on case-control or cross-sectional studies, while all studies contributing to pneumococcal infection had a cohort design. Suggestive evidence supported five associations, namely CeD and higher risk of any fracture and psoriasis (all ages), insomnia (children, adults), and lower height and body weight (children/adolescents). Eight associations showed weak evidence, and the remaining were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Four meta-analytic associations between CeD and higher risk of thyroid disease, pneumococcal infection, and lower bone mass and density reached high credibility, highlighting the potential systemic nature of CeD. Prospective studies are needed to strengthen this evidence. This synthesis may inform the future research agenda in this understudied field and prevention strategies aimed at mitigating CeD-related morbidity.

articles.title: Burden, etiology, and risk factors of diarrheal diseases among neonates in Eastern sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diarrheal disease is the leading cause of child morbidity and mortality. However, there are only limited studies available in Africa. This study determined magnitude, burden, etiology, and risk factors of diarrheal disease among neonates (aged 0-27 days) in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African (ESSA) region from 1990 to 2023.
METHOD: The Global burden of Diseases 2023 estimates and methods were used. The incidence rate estimated was the cumulative incidence over the entire neonatal period (0-28 days), representing the total number of diarrheal episodes per 100,000 neonates during this period.
RESULTS: There were an estimated 215,343 cumulative new cases of diarrheal disease per 100,000 neonates (95% UI: 186,566-240,723) in 2023. The highest incidence and prevalence rates were estimated in South Sudan, Madagascar, and Malawi, whereas the lowest prevalence rate was estimated in Mozambique. The highest years of life lost and disability-adjusted life years rates were estimated in Somalia, whereas the lowest were estimated in Uganda and Tanzania. Rotavirus, adenovirus, and shigella were the common causes of diarrheal disease, whereas unsafe water, poor sanitation, no access to hand-washing facilities, low birth weight, short gestation, and suboptimal breastfeeding were the leading risk factors.
CONCLUSION: This study has revealed that there was substantial reduction in the burden of diarrheal diseases among neonates in the ESSA region in 2023 compared to 1990. However, the rates remain high and heterogeneous across the region. Therefore, prevention activities should target high-risk populations, improving water, sanitation, and hygiene, infant nutrition, and vaccination.

articles.title: Maternal satisfaction with child immunization service, rural tigray after pretoria agreement: A community-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Maternal satisfaction with child immunization services is a vital indicator of healthcare quality and heavily influences service utilization. However, evidence regarding maternal satisfaction in the rural districts of Tigray remains scarce following the Pretoria Agreement. This study aimed to assess maternal satisfaction with childhood immunization services and its associated factors in rural districts of Tigray, Ethiopia. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 454 mothers in rural southeastern zone of Tigray from April to May 2025. Maternal satisfaction was evaluated using a five-point Likert scale. Respondents scoring <46 were categorized as 'dissatisfied', while those scoring ≥46 were categorized as 'satisfied'. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analyzed using SPSS version 27. We used descriptive statistics to summarize the data, and binary logistic regression analysis to identify factors significantly associated with maternal satisfaction. The overall prevalence of maternal satisfaction with child immunization services was 67.2% (95% CI: 62.8-71.6%). Maternal satisfaction was significantly associated with higher maternal education (AOR = 2.32; 95% CI: 1.04-5.18), receiving adequate information about vaccination (AOR = 2.60; 95% CI: 1.42-4.76), cleanliness of the waiting area (AOR = 2.33; 95% CI: 1.32-4.14), shorter distance to the health facility (AOR = 4.21; 95% CI: 2.26-7.84), and shorter waiting times (AOR = 4.58; 95% CI: 2.52-8.32). Approximately two-thirds of mothers were satisfied with childhood immunization services. Interventions aiming to optimize service utilization in rural Tigray should focus on improving facility cleanliness, reducing patient waiting times, enhancing maternal education, and providing comprehensive vaccination counseling.

articles.title: Housing Factors and Infant and Young Child Feeding Outcomes in the United States: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Housing insecurity is a pervasive social determinant of health that may influence infant and young child feeding (IYCF) outcomes, yet evidence from the United States (U.S.) has not been comprehensively synthesized. This scoping review examined associations between housing factors and IYCF outcomes among U.S. families with children from birth through 2 years of age. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Embase through June 2026. Twenty-three articles (19 primary studies and four reviews) met inclusion criteria. Findings were organized using Taylor's (2018) Four Pathways Connecting Housing and Health Framework, with findings categorized into four pathways: stability, affordability, quality and safety, and neighborhood context. Breastfeeding outcomes were assessed most frequently. Among the 19 primary studies, 16 used quantitative designs testing housing-IYCF associations; eight identified at least one statistically significant association, while eight reported none. Heterogeneous measurement approaches complicated interpretation, and associations that were significant before adjustment were often attenuated afterward, which may reflect the role of broader social and structural factors along mediating pathways rather than an absence of association. Authors commonly recommended multilevel approaches, including housing screening and referral, expanded lactation support, integrated housing and social-needs support, and structural investments in housing and communities. Further research should strengthen measurement of housing insecurity, broaden IYCF outcomes beyond breastfeeding, and evaluate housing-related interventions to support recommended IYCF outcomes.

articles.title: Fluzoparib combined with docetaxel followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide as neoadjuvant therapy in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a single-arm phase II study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most prevalent molecular subtype of breast cancer, yet overall pathological complete response (pCR) rates after neoadjuvant chemotherapy remain low. BRCA mutations and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) may sensitize tumors to PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality. We investigated the efficacy and safety of fluzoparib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with HRD-positive and/or germline BRCA (gBRCA)-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, prospective, open-label, single-arm phase II trial (NCT07162051) enrolled women aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. Patients received fluzoparib combined with docetaxel during cycles 1-4, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide during cycles 5-8. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving residual cancer burden (RCB) grade 0/I. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), pathological complete response (pCR) rate, and safety.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were enrolled between March 2023 and October 2025. Four patients (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0%-32.7%) achieved RCB 0/I, two patients (7.1%; 95% CI 0.9%-23.5%) achieved total pCR (tpCR), and six patients (21.4%; 95% CI 8.3%-41.0%) achieved breast pCR (bpCR). The ORR was 82.1%. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in four patients (14.3%). No treatment discontinuations, dose reductions, treatment delays, or treatment-related deaths were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of fluzoparib to standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve RCB 0/I rates in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, although the regimen was well tolerated. Future studies should focus on gBRCA-mutated or higher-risk populations and explore optimized combination strategies, including anti-angiogenic agents. REGISTRATION CENTER, TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER, AND REGISTRATION DATE: This is a prospective, open label, single arm phase II clinical trial. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; Trial registration number: NCT07162051; Registration date:2023-02-21.

articles.title: Human cytomegalovirus infection impairs axon formation by inducing inhibitory GSK-3β Ser9 phosphorylation and suppressing ATP synthesis.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a globally prevalent pathogen known to significantly impact neural development in embryos and young children. Despite its well-established association with neurological disorders, the precise mechanisms through which HCMV infection induces these diseases remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we show that HCMV infection impairs neural cell differentiation by perturbing adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production during the neurogenesis. HCMV infection disrupts the neural differentiation of stem cells derived from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) and the human neuroblastoma cell line (SH-SY5Ys), alternating the expression of neural cell markers and impairing axon formation. Moreover, under neurogenic inductive conditions, HCMV infection in SHEDs and SH-SY5Ys increases Ser9 phosphorylation levels of GSK-3β, which suppresses GSK-3β kinase activity. This inhibition of GSK-3β activity reduces mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis, disrupting energy support for neural differentiation. This study reveals a molecular cascade connecting HCMV infection to defective neural differentiation through crosstalk between GSK-3β phosphorylation and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, offering a potential therapeutic target for congenital HCMV infection.

articles.title: Disruption of histone 3-associated epigenetic mechanisms in paediatric high-grade glioma and posterior fossa group A ependymoma offers new therapeutic options.
articles.abstract: Paediatric high-grade glioma (pHGG) and posterior fossa group A (PFA) ependymoma are pathologically and molecularly different central nervous system malignancies that share two key traits: resistance to treatment and poor overall prognosis. Here, we describe the key epigenetic mechanisms that drive these tumour types. Specifically, we showcase how dysregulation of every aspect of the histone 3 life cycle is aberrantly regulated in pHGG and PFA. We discuss how histone 3 dysregulation may provide a therapeutic window for tailored precision epigenetic therapy. Finally, we discuss the state of epigenetic therapeutics by reviewing past and current clinical trials, and provide an outlook for optimization of future therapies for these devastating tumours.

articles.title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Hypoglycemia and Associated Factors Among Patients With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Attending Follow-Up Care at Bule Hora University Teaching Hospital, Southern Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Hypoglycemia is the most common acute complication of insulin therapy among individuals with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and remains a major barrier to achieving optimal glycemic control. Recurrent hypoglycemia is associated with increased morbidity, impaired quality of life, poor treatment adherence, and increased healthcare utilization. Despite the growing burden of T1DM in Ethiopia, evidence regarding the prevalence of hypoglycemia and its associated factors remains limited, particularly in resource-constrained settings. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of self-reported hypoglycemia and its associated factors among patients with Type 1 diabetes mellitus attending follow-up care at Bule Hora University Teaching Hospital, Southern Ethiopia.
METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 198 T1DM patients attending follow-up care at BHUTH from January 1 to march 31, 2025. A census sampling technique was employed to include all eligible participants. Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire and medical record review. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression models and statistical significance were declared at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 198 participants were included in the study. The prevalence of self-reported hypoglycemia was 42.0% (95% CI: 35.5%-49.3%). Participants living ≥ 5 km from the health facility had significantly higher odds of experiencing hypoglycemia than those living within 5 km (AOR = 3.15; 95% CI: 1.58-6.31; p = 0.001). Conversely, participants who practiced self-monitoring of blood glucose had significantly lower odds of hypoglycemia than those who did not (AOR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.06-0.26; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly half of the study participants experienced at least one episode of hypoglycemia. Regular self-monitoring of blood glucose was associated with a lower risk of hypoglycemia, whereas greater distance from the healthcare facility increased the risk.

articles.title: Co-administration of DTaP with COVID-19 mRNA vaccine in mice alters immune responses and induces increased protection from Bordetella pertussis challenge.
articles.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, children received COVID-19 mRNA vaccines alongside other regularly scheduled immunizations, such as the acellular Bordetella pertussis vaccine DTaP. It is known that mRNA vaccines are pro-inflammatory in nature, leading to protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 infection. The goal of this study was to investigate the potential adjuvanticity of co-administration of a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP. Mice were immunized with DTaP alone or with a co-administration of DTaP plus COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. To understand the impact of co-administration, we evaluated protection against B. pertussis aerosol challenge in mice and potential correlates of protection, including cytokine responses to vaccination, antibody responses, and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the draining lymph node. Three decreasing doses of each vaccine were used to simulate waning immunity. Overall, compared to mice immunized with DTaP, co-administration of DTaP + COVID-19 mRNA vaccines elicited higher pro-inflammatory cytokine responses, higher IgG2b antibody responses, and mice were afforded increased protection against aerosol challenge of B. pertussis. Single-cell transcriptomics studies on the lymph node of vaccinated mice at 1 day post-boost further characterized how co-administration of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP vaccine shapes immunity. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that co-administration of DTaP and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine generated populations of B and T cells with upregulated expression of interferon-stimulated genes, which were absent when vaccinating with DTaP alone. Altogether, these data suggest that administering DTaP alongside COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alters immune responses and provides increased protection from an aerosol challenge of B. pertussis compared to DTaP alone in mice.

articles.title: ETEC heat-labile toxin promotes β-catenin stabilization and transcriptional reprogramming to disrupt intestinal epithelial differentiation.
articles.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC), defined by its production of heat-labile (LT) and heat-stable (ST) enterotoxins, is a common cause of acute diarrheal illness in children from low- and middle-income countries and is also linked to long-term sequelae such as malnutrition and growth impairment. While the mechanisms underlying toxin-mediated acute diarrhea are known, the molecular events involved in ETEC-related sequelae remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the ETEC heat-labile toxin (LT) profoundly remodels intestinal epithelial composition and function through modulation of WNT/β-catenin signaling. Using human ileal enteroids, we demonstrate that LT stabilizes cytosolic β-catenin independently of endogenous WNT ligands, promotes its nuclear accumulation, and enhances TCF/LEF-dependent transcription. LT exposure led to robust upregulation of canonical WNT target genes and genes promoting cell-cycle entry and progression. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed increased proliferative activity across epithelial lineages with expansion of progenitor and intermediate cell populations. Concomitantly, LT reduced the abundance of differentiated absorptive enterocytes and suppressed transcriptional programs required for epithelial maturation, nutrient transport, and digestive function. Together, these findings identify LT as a potent driver of intestinal epithelial reprogramming, providing insight into how ETEC infection may contribute to long-term consequences beyond acute diarrhea. These findings may inform strategies to prevent major sequelae, including malnutrition, that affect millions of children worldwide.

articles.title: Clinical, Genetic, MR Spectroscopy characteristics and Response to Flunarizine in Episodic Ataxia Type 2: The Sheffield Ataxia Cohort.
articles.abstract: Episodic ataxia type 2 (EA2) is an autosomal-dominant calcium channelopathy caused by pathogenic mutations in the CACNA1A gene, characterized by episodic cerebellar symptoms and marked phenotypic heterogeneity. Data on real-world clinical features and treatment responses, particularly in the era of major genetic advances, remain limited. This is a retrospective observational single-centre case series of 58 individuals from 38 families with genetically confirmed EA2. Clinical, demographic, genetic, and treatment data were extracted from medical records using a standardized Excel-based data collection tool. Symptom patterns with associated neurological features, genetic characteristics, and treatment responses were analyzed descriptively. Paired MRI imaging including MR spectroscopy (MRS) of the cerebellum at baseline and follow up data, and medication efficacy were assessed using patient-reported benefit, and statistical analysis was performed using Wilcoxon signed rank test and Exact binomial testing respectively. The mean age at diagnosis was 35.2 ± 21.5 years, and a positive family history was identified in 48 patients (82.70%). The most frequent clinical manifestations were gait instability (87.93%), dysarthria (39.66%), headache (58.62%) and isolated dizziness (48.28%). Episodic symptoms predominated, with 33 patients (56.89%) experiencing discrete attacks. Amongst those with episodic symptoms, weekly attacks were the most common (42.4%), while 17 patients (29.31%) exhibited a non-episodic course with persistent symptoms. Interictal oculomotor abnormalities, including nystagmus, were noted in some individuals. Paired longitudinal MRS analyses for both vermis (W = 118.0, p = 0.67) and hemisphere (W = 122.0, p = 0.39) revealed no significant change over time. Flunarizine showed the highest rate of therapeutic benefit, with 76.5% of treated patients reporting improvement (p = 0.04), whereas other treatments demonstrated variable but non-significant effects. This study highlights the clinical heterogeneity and neuroimaging (MRS) insight of EA2 underscoring the predominance of episodic manifestations, while also recognizing a subset with non-episodic symptoms. Flunarizine appears to be an effective, accessible therapeutic option for reducing attack frequency and duration in EA2, though further studies are required to compare efficacy with alternative therapeutic options such as acetazolamide.

articles.title: Global Burden of Acne (1990-2021) and Projections for China's Disease Burden Over the Next 15 Years: A Comprehensive Study Based on Global Burden of Disease Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acne vulgaris is a common chronic inflammatory skin disease with a significant impact on the global health burden. Although acne vulgaris is more prevalent among adolescents, the incidence of adult acne is gradually increasing, imposing a severe psychological and social burden, particularly on women of reproductive age. China accounts for 18% of the global population, yet previous GBD studies have paid insufficient attention to the evolving burden of acne in the country. With China's Socio-demographic Index (SDI) rising rapidly, it serves as an ideal case for examining the relationship between socioeconomic transition and disease burden. This study aims to analyze trends in the global burden of acne vulgaris from 1990 to 2021, examine regional, national, age, and gender disparities, assess associations with sociodemographic indicators, and project future trends in China's acne vulgaris burden over the next 15 years. Prior studies have largely been confined to single continents or specific countries, with data typically limited to 2017 or earlier. In contrast, this study spans 204 countries and territories worldwide from 1990 to 2021, significantly expanding both temporal and spatial coverage. It is the first to systematically delineate nonlinear associations within the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) framework, revealing a distinctive epidemiological curve characterized by an initial decline followed by a subsequent rise. Furthermore, by incorporating projections of China's disease burden over the next 15 years, this research provides robust empirical evidence to inform public health policymaking across the Asia-Pacific region.
METHODS: Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 database, we extracted data on acne vulgaris incidence, prevalence, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and age-standardized rates from 204 countries and regions worldwide between 1990 and 2021. Trend analysis employed age-standardized rates, estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and Bayesian modeling, with socioeconomic factors assessed using the Socio-Demographic Index (SDI).
RESULTS: In 2021, 239.7 million prevalent cases and 124.3 million incident cases of acne vulgaris were reported globally, accounting for 5.126 million DALYs. The global age-standardized prevalence, incidence, and DALY rates for acne vulgaris were 3142.5 per 100 000 population (95% uncertainty interval: 2867.0 to 3500.6), 1645.2 (1459.7 to 1878.2), and 67.2 (42.3 to 105.8) per 100 000 population, representing increases of 12.2%, 14%, and 12.3% compared to 1990. In 2021, Germany (5688.4), Portugal (5475.1), and Luxembourg (5323.1) exhibited the highest age-standardized prevalence rates for acne vulgaris. Over the entire study period, Sudan (25.3), Equatorial Guinea (25.2), Iraq (24.9), and Oman (24.7) recorded the largest increases in age-standardized point prevalence rates. In 2021, Germany (2723) and Romania (821.7) had the highest and lowest age-standardized incidence rates, respectively, while Germany (121) and Romania (32.2) had the highest and lowest age-standardized DALY rates, respectively. Gender differences were pronounced, with women exhibiting higher standardized prevalence, incidence, and DALY rates than men. Among men, the global DALY rate for acne vulgaris increased between ages 15-19 and then declined with age, while for women, this rate also rose between ages 15-19. Regionally, a complex association exists between sociodemographic indices and the age-standardized DALY rate for acne vulgaris, characterized by an overall plateau followed by a steep upward trajectory. China's burden of acne vulgaris exceeds the global average and is projected to continue rising over the next 15 years.
CONCLUSION: Acne vulgaris represents a significant global dermatological burden, particularly in high-SDI regions, among children, and in female populations. Targeted prevention and treatment strategies are needed to mitigate its health impacts.

articles.title: Topical Epidermal Growth Factor in Acne Vulgaris and Acne-Related Sequelae: Mechanistic Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Formulation Challenges.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acne vulgaris (AV) is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder, particularly among adolescents and young adults, and its management remains limited by variable treatment response, poor adherence, and treatment-related adverse effects.
AIMS: This review critically evaluates the mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and formulation challenges relating to topical epidermal growth factor (EGF) in active acne vulgaris and acne-related sequelae.
METHODS: PubMed was searched from database inception through June 30, 2026, using predefined MeSH and free-text terms related to AV, acne scarring, epidermal growth factor, EGF receptor (EGFR) signaling, keratinocytes, sebocytes, inflammation, skin-barrier repair, wound healing, and topical delivery. PubMed-indexed articles were selected through title-and-abstract screening followed by full-text assessment. Human acne-related studies were prioritized, while relevant preclinical studies were included to evaluate mechanistic, safety, and formulation-related evidence. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in study design and indication, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively.
RESULTS: Preclinical studies suggest that EGF/EGFR signaling may influence keratinocyte inflammation, migration, proliferation, and tissue repair; however, most of this evidence derives from non-acne cellular or wound-healing models. Direct clinical evidence for active acne is limited to two small, short-term split-face studies that reported preliminary within-study improvements in lesion-related outcomes. Separate small studies have evaluated topical EGF-containing formulations for established atrophic acne scars or recombinant human EGF (rhEGF) as an adjunct to fractional laser treatment. These studies do not demonstrate prevention of new acne scars, and evidence from scar or post-procedural settings cannot be extrapolated to active acne treatment. Heterogeneity in study design, formulation, indication, outcome assessment, and follow-up prevents firm conclusions regarding clinically meaningful efficacy, comparative effectiveness, or long-term safety. The single-database, English-language narrative-review methodology also limits the comprehensiveness and certainty of the synthesis.
CONCLUSIONS: Available studies provide preliminary biological rationale and limited clinical signals for topical EGF in acne-related care, but the evidence is insufficient to establish clinically meaningful efficacy or an evidence-based therapeutic role in active acne vulgaris. Evidence for topical EGF serum used alone on established atrophic scars remains weak, whereas the comparatively broader evidence concerns rhEGF as an adjunct after fractional laser treatment for established scars. Even in this procedural setting, heterogeneous protocols and limited evidence certainty preclude routine recommendation. Topical EGF should therefore remain investigational, and larger randomized controlled trials using standardized formulations, active comparators, indication-specific outcomes, and longer safety follow-up are required.

articles.title: Cosmetic Outcomes and Safety of Hair Transplantation and Topical Minoxidil for Temporal Triangular Alopecia: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporal triangular alopecia (TTA) is a non-scarring alopecia affecting the frontotemporal region, with estimated prevalence of 0.11%. Despite recognized aesthetic and psychological impact, particularly among children and adolescents, no systematic evaluation has synthesized available evidence on its treatment.
AIMS: This systematic review synthesizes and evaluates surgical and medical management of TTA, with emphasis on cosmetic outcomes, durability, and safety.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, a systematic search was conducted from inception to December 30, 2025 using PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies reported cosmetic outcomes, adverse events, or patient satisfaction with hair transplantation or topical minoxidil for TTA.
RESULTS: Nine studies met inclusion criteria (n = 23 patients): three case reports of topical minoxidil and five case reports and one case series of hair transplantation (follicular unit transplantation or excision). Hair transplantation was associated with cosmetic improvement (20 patients, six studies), maintained up to 6 years in one case. Topical minoxidil (three cases) was associated with cosmetic improvement; relapse after discontinuation was reported in one case, with outcomes after discontinuation not assessed in the other two. Both interventions were associated with favorable safety profiles, with no serious adverse events across the included studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical minoxidil may be a non-invasive option for pediatric patients or those preferring non-surgical management, and hair transplantation for adults seeking durable cosmetic correction. These findings reflect low-level evidence from case reports and a case series (Level IV, Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine) and should be considered descriptive observations from a small evidence base. Given the scarce published evidence, higher-quality prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed, particularly in pediatric populations.

articles.title: Psychosocial Outcomes of Microwave Thermolysis for Axillary Hyperhidrosis and Bromhidrosis in Adolescents: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary axillary hyperhidrosis and bromhidrosis in adolescents cause significant physical discomfort and psychosocial distress, negatively impacting emotional well-being and social function. While microwave thermolysis is effective in adults, its psychological benefits in adolescents remain understudied.
AIMS: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of microwave thermolysis in adolescents and investigate its impact on quality of life, anxiety, and depression.
PATIENTS/METHODS: This retrospective study included 21 adolescents (mean age 15.21 years) treated with microwave thermolysis. Clinical severity was assessed using the Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Scale (HDSS) and a bromhidrosis grading scale. Psychosocial outcomes were evaluated using the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), a modified Quality of Life (QoL) questionnaire, and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) at baseline and 1 month post-treatment.
RESULTS: The treatment yielded significant clinical improvement, with HDSS scores decreasing from 3.19 to 1.33 (p < 0.0001) and bromhidrosis severity dropping from 4.19 to 0.48 (p < 0.0001). Psychosocial burden was markedly reduced: DLQI scores improved from 17.38 to 10.71 (p < 0.0001), and QoL scores increased from 52.10 to 84.95 (p = 0.027). Significant reductions were observed in HADS-anxiety (14.05 to 1.67, p < 0.0001) and HADS-depression scores (7.48 to 1.05, p < 0.0001). All cases reported no major side effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Microwave thermolysis is a highly effective treatment for adolescent axillary hyperhidrosis and bromhidrosis. Beyond symptom relief, it significantly alleviates anxiety and depression while enhancing quality of life and social function. These findings support its use as a primary therapeutic option for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Treatment Challenges of Acne, With Insights Into the Role of Dermocosmetics: An Expert Consensus From India-A Modified Delphi Method.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acne vulgaris is a common skin condition that typically begins in adolescence but can often persist in adulthood, contributing to significant physical and psychosocial burden. Despite the availability of multiple treatment options, challenges such as poor adherence, treatment-related side effects, and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation remain common in clinical practice. Dermocosmetics are increasingly used in acne management, either alone in mild cases or as adjuncts to medical therapy.
OBJECTIVES: To assess acne prevalence, treatment practices, and key management challenges, along with the role of dermocosmetics, based on expert consensus from India.
METHODS: A panel of 10 dermatologists participated in a modified Delphi process comprising a pre-meeting survey followed by a structured advisory board discussion, capturing clinical practice patterns, treatment approaches, and perspectives on dermocosmetic use in acne management.
RESULTS: Experts reported treating a high number of acne patients, primarily adolescents, with a higher proportion of females. Hyperpigmentation and scarring were common sequelae of acne, while treatment adherence and antibiotic resistance, particularly to erythromycin and azithromycin, were noted as key challenges. Procedural interventions, including chemical peels, lasers, and comedone extraction, were increasingly used in early acne management, especially in patients prone to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and relapse. Low-dose isotretinoin and hormonal therapies were commonly used in acne management, while dermocosmetics were utilized as monotherapy in mild cases and as maintenance therapy following treatment in more severe cases. Lifestyle factors such as high glycaemic diets, whey protein, multivitamins, and steroid-like drugs were identified as potential contributors to acne exacerbation.
LIMITATIONS: Findings are based on a small expert panel convened with industry support and reflect clinical opinion rather than primary patient data.
CONCLUSION: Procedural interventions are becoming more popular, thereby providing an opportunity to incorporate dermocosmetics into acne treatment regimens.

articles.title: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE.
OBJECTIVE: The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up.
RESULTS: Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula.
CONCLUSION: EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

articles.title: Breastfeeding interventions for low-birth weight and very low birth weight infants in South Asia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate interventions promoting breastfeeding practices among Low Birth Weight (LBW) and Very Low Birth Weight (VLBW) infants in South Asia.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in five databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINHAL, and the Cochrane library). Evidence was synthesized to estimate the duration to establish breastfeeding practices among LBW and VLBW infants. Meta-analysis was performed to estimate the effect size on breastfeeding practices using random effect model. Heterogeneity was explored by sub-group and meta-regression analyses. Risk of bias and strength of evidence was assessed by the RoB2, ROBINS-I and NIH Quality Assessment tools considering the study design of the selected articles.
RESULTS: From a pool of 2,524 records screened, 16 studies met the inclusion criteria. The systematic review revealed that various interventions aimed at improving breastfeeding practices among LBW infants largely resulted in positive breastfeeding outcomes such as initiation of breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding. The Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) care was intervened in most cases together with other interventions, including Non-nutritive suckling, Premature Infant Oromotor Intervention, Nutrition Education and Mother Baby Friendly Initiatives Plus. Meta-analysis showed mothers who received KMC demonstrated an earlier initiation of breastfeeding (pooled SMD: -1.08, 95% CI: -2.15, to -0.01) as compared to mothers who received conventional care.
