The prespecified primary outcome was persistent LV systolic dysfunction, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 55% at ≥6 months. Study-level events and denominators were extracted and harmonized using the number of children who underwent ≥6-month echocardiography as the endpoint-specific denominator. Pooled prevalence was estimated using an intercept-only binomial logistic-normal generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) fitted directly to study-level event counts and denominators without continuity correction. The originally prespecified random-effects logit model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, together with alternative continuity corrections and transformation-based approaches, was retained as sensitivity analysis under sparse-event conditions.
RESULTS: Ten cohorts met the inclusion criteria and contributed to quantitative synthesis, comprising 432 children with echocardiography at ≥6 months. Persistent LV systolic dysfunction occurred in 3 children, corresponding to a crude observed proportion of 0.69% (3/432). In the revised primary continuity-correction-free binomial logistic-normal GLMM, the pooled prevalence was 0.69% (95% CI, 0.22%-2.13%). Given that only three events were observed, this model-based estimate should not be interpreted as a precise estimate of the underlying population prevalence. Continuity-corrected sensitivity models yielded pooled estimates from 1.62% to 2.23%, further demonstrating numerical sensitivity to the treatment of zero-event cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Persistent LV systolic dysfunction was infrequently observed among children with MIS-C reassessed by echocardiography at ≥6 months. However, only three events were identified, so the available evidence is insufficient to determine the exact population prevalence with precision. Inference is further limited by heterogeneous follow-up and potential selection bias from nonuniform late imaging. Larger prospective cohorts with standardized long-term surveillance are needed.

articles.title: Restrictive lung function defined by body plethysmography is common in children with Fontan palliation and functionally relevant.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary dysfunction is common in single ventricle (SV) patients with Fontan circulation, yet the prevalence and clinical relevance of true restrictive lung disease remain poorly characterized as most studies relied on spirometry alone. This study comprehensively assessed lung function using spirometry and body plethysmography, examined its relationship with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived lung volumes, evaluated its impact on exercise capacity, and identified clinical correlates of restrictive physiology.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre study, 31 children and adolescents with Fontan circulation underwent spirometry, body plethysmography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), and CMR. Restrictive lung function was defined by reduced (<LLN) total lung capacity (TLC). Lung function, CMR findings, exercise performance, and clinical characteristics were compared between patients with and without restrictive physiology.
RESULTS: Restrictive lung function was identified in n = 8 (26%) participants. TLC correlated strongly with CMR-derived total lung volume (r = 0.889, p < 0.001). Patients with restrictive physiology demonstrated significantly reduced exercise capacity, including lower peak oxygen uptake, tidal volume, and minute ventilation, with reduced breathing reserve and higher peak respiratory rate, indicating clinically relevant ventilatory limitation. Restrictive physiology was associated with lower ventricular ejection fraction and impaired global circumferential strain. In multivariable analysis, TLC was the strongest predictor of peak oxygen uptake.
CONCLUSIONS: Restrictive lung physiology confirmed by body plethysmography is common in children and adolescents with Fontan circulation and associates with impaired exercise performance and reduced ventricular function. Comprehensive pulmonary function testing including body plethysmography may be considered in routine follow-up to identify patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Routine Prenatal Ultrasound at 36 Weeks: Impact on Obstetric Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of introducing a routine prenatal ultrasound scan at 36 weeks' gestation, integrated with a predefined clinical management pathway, on obstetric outcomes.
DESIGN: Single-centre retrospective study.
SETTING: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London, UK.
POPULATION: 37 001 singleton term pregnancies delivered between April 2016 and October 2024.
METHODS: From January 2020, universal 36-week ultrasound replaced targeted scanning within a predefined national management pathway; its impact was assessed using interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were gestational age at birth in SGA and LGA neonates, and prenatal detection rate of breech presentation. Secondary outcomes included rates of neonatal intensive care unit admission, severe perineal trauma, shoulder dystocia and stillbirth.
RESULTS: SGA infants delivered at 37-38 weeks' gestation increased from 18.7% to 38.1% post intervention (p = 0.04) with a concomitant overall reduction in NICU admissions (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.66-0.82). The prenatal detection rate of breech presentation increased significantly from 78% to almost 90% (p = 0.002). The intervention was also associated with a significant reduction in third- and fourth-degree perineal tears (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.65-0.84).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine 36-week scan embedded within a structured clinical management pathway was associated with significant changes in obstetric metrics and improved pregnancy outcome. Overall, these findings provide real-world evidence on how a universal third-trimester ultrasound may selectively influence obstetric management and inform the ongoing debate on routine prenatal screening strategies.

articles.title: Clustering of Maternal and Perinatal Complications Following Fresh and Frozen Embryo Transfer in First-Time Mothers: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess how often women who give birth following frozen-thawed embryo transfer (frozen-ET), fresh embryo transfer (fresh-ET) and natural conception (NC) have pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications, develop a single complication, or experience multiple complications.
DESIGN: A population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Denmark (2008-2014), Norway (2008-2015) and Sweden (2008-2015).
POPULATION: Restricted to singleton pregnancies among first-time mothers, this study included 6634 deliveries after frozen-ET, 25 660 after fresh-ET and 523 277 after NC.
METHODS: The following complications were studied: stillbirth, neonatal death (0-27 days after delivery), preterm birth (gestational age < 37 weeks), small for gestational age or large for gestational age (birthweight < -22% or > +22% from the expected birthweight according to sex and gestational age), low birthweight (< 2500 g), macrosomia (≥ 4500 g), Apgar score < 5 at 5 min, major birth defects, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, placenta previa and placental abruption.
RESULTS: In first-time mothers, three of every four singleton pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET were without maternal and perinatal complications, compared to four of every five pregnancies after NC. In pregnancies with neonatal survival ≥ 28 days (99.3% after frozen-ET, 99.3% after fresh-ET, and 99.5% after NC), two or more complications affected one in 11 pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET, compared to one in 16 after NC.
CONCLUSION: In this study, we observed that most first-time mothers experienced pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications following ART, and when complications occurred, they were typically without additional complications. Although single and multiple complications were more common following ART than after NC, the absolute differences were small. These findings may help set realistic expectations when counselling people who consider ART treatment, or those already in treatment.

articles.title: Exercise Test Findings in the Long-Term Outcomes After Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MUSIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) commonly presents with cardiovascular involvement, but the frequency of exercise-related arrhythmias and exercise capacity are poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe exercise stress testing (EST) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) after MIS-C.
METHODS: We summarized EST and CPET results from the MUSIC (Long-terM OUtcomes after the Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome In Children) study (1,204 participants, 32 North American sites). Demographics and details of hospitalization from participants undergoing clinical EST were compared to participants ≥5 years who did not undergo EST. Site reported results of EST and CPET were described.
RESULTS: EST was performed in 22% (208/932) at a mean of 150 ± 110 days after hospitalization. Compared with those who did not undergo EST (n = 724), the EST cohort was older (12.2 vs 10.5 years) and had higher rates of intensive care unit admission (77.4% vs 63.8%), vasoactive infusions (57.2% vs 46.1%), troponin elevation (64.4% vs 51.0%), and coronary artery aneurysm (22.7% vs 0.4%) (all P ≤ 0.01). During EST, only 1% (2/208; 95% CI: 0.1%-3.4%) exhibited premature ventricular contractions and no sustained ectopy. Among 160 participants undergoing CPET, 75.6% (121/160; 95% CI: 68.2%-82.1%) achieved oxygen consumption/kg ≥ 80% predicted, and 83.8% (134/160; 95% CI: 77.1%-89.1%) achieved an oxygen pulse ≥80% predicted.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing exercise testing after MIS-C, most had normal exercise capacity, no sustained arrhythmias occurred, and premature ventricular contractions were rare.

articles.title: Evidence-based expert consensus on long-acting injectable antipsychotics for bipolar disorder: Recommendations from the TSBPN.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based expert consensus recommendations from the Taiwanese Society of Biological Psychiatry and Neuropsychopharmacology (TSBPN) on the use of long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics in bipolar disorder.
METHODS: An eight-member working group and 12-member scientific committee formed a 20-member expert panel. A narrative review of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE from inception through February 2026 prioritized bipolar-specific evidence and incorporated relevant indirect evidence when necessary. Fourteen statements were graded using the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry framework for level of evidence (LoE) and acceptability. After expert review and revision, 18 panelists completed anonymous voting to determine the Taiwan recommendation grade (RG-T) and level of agreement.
RESULTS: The 14 statements covered LAI selection, clinical role, timing of initiation, special populations, and safety monitoring. Strong RG-T 1 recommendations supported prioritizing locally approved agents, individualized shared decision-making, use during mania as part of an acute-to-maintenance strategy, maintenance monotherapy or combination treatment, management of suspected nonadherence, earlier use in recurrent illness, use in patients with frequent manic episodes or comorbid substance use disorder, prevention of manic-spectrum recurrence, and combination with established bipolar-depression treatments when clinically indicated. RG-T 2 recommendations addressed older adults, children and adolescents, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and metabolic monitoring. Agreement ranged from 72.2% to 100%. Evidence was strongest for maintenance and manic-spectrum recurrence, but more limited for bipolar depression and several special populations.
CONCLUSION: This TSBPN consensus integrates available evidence with expert judgment to support individualized LAI use across bipolar-disorder treatment settings while highlighting areas requiring further research.

articles.title: Personal and environmental factors associated with allergic disorders among adolescents in Lusaka, Zambia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between wheezing, allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema and selected environmental, lifestyle and personal factors among school-going adolescents aged 13–14 years.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.
SETTING: Participants were enrolled from schools in Lusaka, Zambia.
PARTICIPANTS: Adolescents aged 13–14 years attending urban schools.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Three primary outcomes including symptoms of asthma (wheeze), rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema were determined using the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood–Global Asthma Network questionnaire. Multivariate mixed effect logistic regression models were used to assess the association between selected exposure variables and each outcome. The study was reviewed and approved by the Levy Mwanawasa Medical University Research Ethics Committee (ref: LMMU-REC 00003/21) and the Zambian National Health Research Authority (ref: NHRA 0000001/23/03/2022). The Ministry of Education, headquarters in Lusaka, gave permission to access the schools (ref: MOE/101/1/45). All participants assented while their guardians consented.
RESULTS: The prevalence of symptoms of asthma (current wheeze), allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema was 13.6%, 11.8% and 6.5%, respectively. In mixed-effect multivariable analysis, exposure to environmental pollutants including smoke from cigarettes, vehicle emissions, use of charcoal and pet exposure as well as lifestyle factors such as physical activity and frequent paracetamol intake were significantly associated with all the outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates a significant burden of allergic diseases among adolescents in this population. Additionally, the study reveals an association between these symptoms and modifiable environmental, lifestyle and personal factors. Although further studies are needed to elucidate the observed associations, the findings highlight the potential benefit of reduced exposure to indoor and outdoor air pollutants, promotion of healthier lifestyle choices among adolescents and encouraging cautious use of paracetamol

articles.title: An observational study protocol characterising pain trajectories, opioid use and predictors of chronic postsurgical pain in children with cerebral palsy undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) are likely at greater risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) due to their high prevalence of pre-existing pain and frequency of orthopaedic procedures. However, little is known about the prevalence, trajectories and risk factors of CPSP or persistent opioid use among children with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Understanding CPSP and patterns of postoperative opioid use in this population is crucial to optimise perioperative pain management, inform opioid stewardship practices, improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare use and costs.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multi-site, prospective, longitudinal study aims to recruit 450 children aged 5–17 years with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Participants will complete study assessments from 1 month before surgery to 12 months postoperatively. Study measures include preoperative quantitative sensory testing; caregiver-reported and child-reported (for participants ≥8 years who are cognitively able) assessments of pain and psychosocial factors at five time points; real-time postoperative text message assessments of pain and opioid use; and postoperative gait laboratory measures of functional outcomes. Demographic and surgical, and clinical data, including medical history, inpatient postoperative pain scores and analgesic medication use, will be extracted from the electronic medical record. Analysis will (1) characterise the postoperative pain and opioid use trajectories, (2) identify predictors of CPSP and persistent opioid use and (3) examine relationships between perioperative pain severity and the functional mobility outcomes achieved via orthopaedic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Central and local Institutional Review Boards at each site have approved the study. Study results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journal publications and presentations at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05764681.

articles.title: Efficacy of the consumption of traditional rice compared with that of normal rice in reducing obesity among children aged 10-14 years attending the paediatric endocrine clinic at Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Sri Lanka: a study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Childhood obesity is an emerging global public health concern, with a growing prevalence in Sri Lanka. Dietary management and physical activities play a vital role in the management and prevention of childhood obesity, as effective treatments for this metabolic risk are scarce. Sri Lankan traditional rice varieties, which are known for their low glycaemic index (GI) contributed by high amylose and resistant starch (RS), may offer potential benefits in reducing obesity. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of the consumption of traditional low-GI rice in reducing obesity among children.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-centre, parallel-group, superiority design, single-blinded, randomised controlled trial. The study population will include children aged between 10 and 14 years who are diagnosed with obesity (body mass index (BMI) over the 95th centile for age and sex (BMI between +2 SD and +3 SD)) and who are registered in the paediatric endocrine unit at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Colombo, Sri Lanka. Eighty children will be randomised into either the intervention group (consuming traditional rice as one main meal for 5 days per week for 6 months) or the control group (continuing their usual diet with normal rice) via covariate adaptive randomisation balanced for age and sex. Anthropometric parameters (weight, height, mid-upper arm circumference, waist circumference, body fat), and blood pressure will be assessed at baseline, at the midpoint (13 week) and at the final follow-up (26 week) whereas biochemical parameters (fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, lipid profile, liver function test, insulin, leptin) will be assessed at baseline and at the final follow-up. The frequency of single-nucleotide polymorphism in rs17782313 near the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) gene will also be determined. The primary outcome is the reduction in BMI z-score, whereas secondary outcomes include reduction in anthropometric measurements and improvements in biochemical parameters.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been granted ethical approval by the Research Ethics Committee, Faculty of Medical Sciences, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, Sri Lanka (application number 73/24). The results of this study will be published in peer-reviewed journals and presented at relevant scientific conferences.
REGISTRATION DETAILS: The trial has been registered in the Sri Lanka Clinical Trials Registry (Registration number-SLCTR/2025/022; Date of registration: 5 June 2025).
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: SLCTR/2025/022

articles.title: Experiences of late-diagnosed autistic women: a qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autism spectrum disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition with marked gender disparities in identification, leaving many women undiagnosed or misdiagnosed until adolescence or adulthood. Late-diagnosed autistic women frequently experience long-term mental distress, identity confusion, and inadequate support due to camouflaging behaviours, internalised symptoms and gender-biased diagnostic criteria. Although a growing number of qualitative studies have explored their experiences, findings remain fragmented and lack a comprehensive systematic synthesis. This qualitative meta-synthesis aims to systematically integrate existing qualitative evidence to clarify the lived experiences, diagnostic journeys and post-diagnostic adaptation of late-diagnosed autistic women.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol describes a planned qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) meta-aggregation approach. The protocol was developed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guideline. Systematic searches will be conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Database, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Web of Science. The formal literature search is planned to commence in January 2027 and be completed by March 2027 covering the period from database inception to March 2027. At the time of manuscript submission, the review remains at the protocol stage and the formal systematic literature search has not yet commenced. Peer-reviewed qualitative or mixed-methods studies focusing on the lived experiences of autistic women diagnosed in adolescence or adulthood will be included. Studies involving participants with diverse gender identities will be considered, and findings will be interpreted according to participants’ gender identities. Two independent reviewers will conduct study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist. Data synthesis will use a three-step meta-aggregation approach to categorise findings and generate integrated results. Confidence in the synthesised findings will be assessed using the ConQual tool.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: As this study is a secondary analysis of published data, ethical approval is not required. The findings will be disseminated through publication in a peer-reviewed journal and presentations at academic conferences.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261361996.

articles.title: Baseline immune profiles are associated with positive outcomes in young children with a peanut allergy, enrolled in a randomised clinical trial for oral immunotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peanut allergy affects around 3% of Australian infants, can cause life-threatening anaphylactic reactions and often persists throughout life. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) is a promising treatment to achieve desensitisation, but treatment outcomes vary. This study describes the immunological profiles associated with favourable OIT outcomes.
METHODS: This study assessed blood samples from 49 peanut-allergic children (1-4 years old) who participated in the Early Peanut Immunotherapy in Children (EPIC) randomised controlled trial. Children randomised to undergo peanut OIT (n = 24), or to follow the current recommended clinical practise of strict peanut avoidance (n = 25) for twelve months, were immunologically evaluated. Desensitisation outcomes were assessed using an end of treatment (EOT) oral food challenge, and blood samples were collected at baseline, 12-week follow-up (OIT only), and EOT. Thirty immune cell subsets were identified using an established immune cell flow cytometry panel and an FcεR1 expression panel.
RESULTS: As part of the clinical trial, OIT induced either partial or complete desensitisation in 91.3% of participants in the intervention group, compared to 20.8% in the avoidance group. After 12 weeks of treatment, OIT-treated patients displayed an expansion of basophils, monocytes and dendritic cells compared to levels at recruitment. At EOT, OIT increased the abundance of CD4- T effector memory cells and mast cell progenitors. Younger children with low levels of peanut-specific IgE were more likely to achieve complete desensitisation. Such outcome was also associated with low levels of CD4+ memory Tregs and CD4- central memory T cells at recruitment, whereas increased levels of basophils were associated with partial desensitisation. Differences between partial and complete desensitisation were also observed regarding dendritic cell activation and expression of the IgE receptor.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that immune signatures vary according to OIT clinical response and may have utility in monitoring treatment progress and in identifying children most likely to benefit from OIT in the future.

articles.title: Synergism of triggers for loss of asthma control in children during wartime.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with asthma living in areas affected by armed conflict are exposed to a unique combination of psychological stress, environmental hazards, healthcare disruption, and adverse social conditions that may contribute to poorer asthma control. Although these factors have been investigated individually, their integrated pathophysiological interactions have not been comprehensively synthesized.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize current evidence on the psychoneuroimmunological, environmental, and behavioral mechanisms that may contribute to loss of asthma control in children exposed to armed conflict and to summarize potential implications for clinical management.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A targeted narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine. Evidence from conflict-related asthma studies was integrated with mechanistic research on psychoneuroimmunology, environmental health, and pediatric asthma, together with current international clinical guidelines.
RESULTS: Available evidence suggests that asthma destabilization during armed conflicts is multifactorial. Chronic psychological stress may alter brain-lung axis signaling, contributing to neuroimmune dysregulation and reduced glucocorticoid responsiveness. Simultaneously, exposure to particulate air pollution, combustion products, indoor dampness, and shelter-associated allergens may amplify airway inflammation. Healthcare disruption, forced displacement, and family disorganization may further reduce treatment adherence and continuity of care. Together, these interacting factors may contribute to poorer asthma control and increased exacerbation risk in susceptible children.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports a multidimensional model in which psychological, environmental, and healthcare-related factors interact to influence asthma outcomes during armed conflicts. Asthma management in humanitarian settings should prioritize continuity of inhaled corticosteroid-containing therapy according to contemporary international guidelines, individualized asthma action plans, objective monitoring whenever feasible, and integration of psychological support into comprehensive pediatric asthma care. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the relative contribution of these mechanisms and to strengthen the evidence base for clinical recommendations.

articles.title: The Wide Phenotypic Spectrum of Adult-Onset Single Large-Scale Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndromes.
articles.abstract: Single large-scale mitochondrial DNA deletions (SLSMDs) give rise to a wide spectrum of clinical features, including Kearns-Sayre syndrome (KSS) and chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO). Because longitudinal data are scarce, the natural history remains poorly defined. This study was undertaken to describe the clinical spectrum in a large cohort of patients with clinical onset after 16 years of age. A retrospective multicenter study was performed in patients diagnosed and followed in seven European mitochondrial disease centers. Seventy patients were included. The median age at disease onset was 27 years, and the median age at last evaluation was 52 years, with a median follow-up duration of 19 years. Median survival from disease onset was 34 years. KSS spectrum disorder was present in 36% of the patients, while CPEO was identified in the remaining 64%. Among those with CPEO at onset, 27% progressed to KSS spectrum disorder. Multisystem involvement was present in 59%. The most frequently reported symptoms or signs were ptosis and/or ophthalmoplegia (100%), skeletal muscle weakness (56%), perceived fatigue (34%), visual impairment (30%), exercise intolerance (33%), pigmentary retinopathy (20%), hearing impairment (19%), cardiac conduction block (15%), ataxia (11%), epilepsy (14%), and cognitive impairment (11%). Our study gives further insight into the highly heterogenous clinical presentation and natural history associated with SLSMDs. The relevance of categorizing patients into classical syndromic phenotypes may be questioned, as the observed overlap in clinical manifestations and the frequent evolution of phenotype over time suggest a continuum of disease expression rather than clearly distinct syndromic entities.

articles.title: Untargeted Metabolomics of Dried Blood Spots for Inherited Metabolic Disorder Classification.
articles.abstract: Dried blood spots (DBS) are commonly used in specific clinical applications, most prominently the new-born screening. Their advantages include minimally invasive sampling, simplified transport and storage, and excellent metabolite stability. Despite their increasing application in metabolomics, the impact of the DBS matrix on metabolite recovery and diagnostic interpretation remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we evaluated DBS-specific analytical biases by comparing matched blood, serum, and plasma samples before and after spotting onto filter paper using targeted and untargeted metabolomics. Compound-specific matrix effects were observed in an extraction protocol-dependent manner, with the strongest differences affecting dicarboxylic acylcarnitines and selected amino acids. To assess the practical relevance of these findings, we analyzed 229 DBS samples from patients with inherited metabolic disorders or obesity, individuals following a ketogenic diet, and healthy controls. Untargeted metabolomics combined with random forest classification captured distinct metabolic signatures despite pre-analytical variability and filter paper-associated retention effects. Subset analyses revealed that classification remained accurate for several groups after excluding established diagnostic markers, amino acids, or acylcarnitines, indicating that discriminatory information extended beyond conventional biomarkers. However, in the case of selected fatty acid oxidation disorders the classification still depended strongly on acylcarnitines. Despite pronounced filter paper retention, C4DC-Acylcarnitine ranked among the 15 most important classification variables, while N-Hexosyl phenylalanine emerged as the second-ranked feature and a potential complementary biomarker for phenylketonuria. These findings support the potential of DBS-based untargeted metabolomics for broader metabolic phenotyping and warrant validation in larger, balanced and independent cohorts.

articles.title: Tracking Neurophysiological Trajectories in Adolescent Non-Suicidal Self-Injury During Mindfulness-Based Intervention: A Longitudinal Single-Channel EEG Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adolescent non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) remains a major clinical challenge, and objective neurophysiological monitoring during early intervention is lacking. This prospective longitudinal observational study characterized longitudinal EEG trajectories during an individualized home-based EEG biofeedback editation (H-EBM) intervention in hospitalized adolescents with NSSI and explored whether neurophysiological trajectory features were associated with emotional improvement.
METHODS: Fifty-two hospitalized adolescents with NSSI (DSM-5 criteria) who received routine inpatient psychiatric care together with daily H-EBM sessions over approximately 10 days were included in the per-protocol analysis. H-EBM integrated metaphor-guided therapeutic narratives with real-time EEG biofeedback via a single-lead device (Fp1, 512 Hz). Emotional states were assessed at admission and discharge using the profile of mood states (POMS). Participants were exploratorily classified into exploratory responder ( n = 36  ) and non-responder ( n = 16  ) subgroups based on total mood disturbance (TMD) improvement. Longitudinal alpha/beta power ratio trajectories were compared between subgroups, and associations between EEG trajectory slopes and TMD improvement were examined.
RESULTS: The exploratory responder subgroup showed significant reductions in TMD scores and core symptom subscales (depression and tension; all p < 0.001  ), whereas the exploratory non-responder subgroup showed no improvement. The alpha/beta ratio in the exploratory responder subgroup exhibited a progressive upward trajectory across training sessions, while this ratio remained stable or fluctuated in the exploratory non-responder subgroup. The alpha/beta ratio slope was positively associated with TMD improvement scores (Pearson r = 0.43  , 95% CI [0.18, 0.63], p = 0.002  ). Exploratory logistic regression suggested that the alpha/beta ratio slope was associated with exploratory responder status after adjusting for age and gender (OR = 9.49, 95% CI [1.01, 89.44], p = 0.049  ). Exploratory ROC analysis showed moderate apparent (in-sample) discriminative performance (AUC = 0.774, 95% CI [0.638, 0.899]).
CONCLUSION: Longitudinal neurophysiological trajectories during individualized H-EBM were associated with emotional improvement in hospitalized adolescents with NSSI. These preliminary findings suggest that EEG trajectory analysis may represent a promising objective monitoring approach during individualized mindfulness-based interventions. Given the observational design without a control group, future randomized controlled studies are warranted to examine potential therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Providing Social and Emotional Supports to Students With Intellectual and Developmental Disability in Post-Secondary Education Programs.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities are attending college more now than ever. The transition to college can be extremely challenging for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities due to limitations and/or struggles with various conceptual and social skill deficits. As individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities transition to inclusive post-school education (IPSE) programs, existing or new social and emotional issues may emerge or be exacerbated.
METHOD: In this secondary data analysis, the authors examine 35 students with intellectual and developmental disabilities to identify patterns and reasons for counseling sessions with an IPSE program counselor.
RESULTS: Over the course of one academic year (August through April), students attended 355 counseling sessions. Four themes (relationship skills, self-awareness, self-management, and social awareness) and 15 subthemes (codes) were identified as reasons for counseling sessions. Relationship skills (36%) and self-management (33%) were the most frequently identified themes. After accounting for repeated counseling sessions within students using generalized linear mixed models, relatively few participant or session characteristics were significantly associated with counseling themes or codes. Relationship Skills varied significantly by disability classification and year in program, while only a small number of significant associations were identified at the code level.
CONCLUSION: Students with IDD demonstrated social-emotional counseling needs across different years of participation in the IPSE program, particularly in the areas of relationship skills and self-management. The limited number of significant differences across participant and session characteristics suggests that counseling support needs were broadly present across students rather than concentrated within particular demographic groups or stages of the college experience.

articles.title: High HTLV Prevalence Among Female Sex Workers in Northeastern Pará, Brazilian Amazon.
articles.abstract: Human T-lymphotropic virus types 1 and 2 (HTLV-1/2) are endemic retroviruses in Brazil, particularly in the Amazon region. Female sex workers (FSWs) represent a key population with heightened vulnerability; however, data on prevalence and risk factors in this region remain limited. We conducted a cross-sectional study (August 2022-April 2024) using snowball sampling among FSWs in five municipalities in northeastern Pará. Participants provided blood samples for serological screening and molecular confirmation. Among 154 FSWs, the overall HTLV-1/2 prevalence was 4.5% (7/154; 95% CI: 2.2%-9.1%). HTLV-1 accounted for 3.9%, while HTLV-2 represented 0.6%. Phylogenetic analysis classified most HTLV-1 cases as belonging to the Cosmopolitan subtype (1a), predominantly the Transcontinental subgroup (1aA), with one case identified as subgroup 1aB. The single HTLV-2 case was confirmed as subtype 2c. Infection was concentrated among the most socioeconomically vulnerable individuals: all positive cases had ≤ 8 years of education and reported low family income. Illicit drug use was significantly associated with infection (OR = 7.33; 95% CI: 1.34-40.05; p = 0.01). All HTLV-positive FSWs expressed willingness to engage in condomless sex due to financial necessity or under the influence of substances, and none were aware of HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) or Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP). This study reveals a high HTLV-1/2 prevalence among FSWs in the northeastern Brazilian Amazon. The association of HTLV infection with poverty, drug use, and contextual risk factors underscores the urgent need for integrated public health strategies that combine screening, targeted education, and structural interventions to mitigate transmission in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Surrogate decision-making support in pediatric end-of-life care during infancy and early childhood: A case-derived conceptual framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reports on nursing support addressing changes in family functioning during surrogate decision-making in pediatric end-of-life care are limited. This case describes treatment and end-of-life care of an infant with atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (AT/RT).
METHOD: Clinical records and the primary nurse's recollections informed a four-phase account of the clinical course, surrogate decision-making, family situation, and nursing support. Family functioning was retrospectively analyzed using the structural, developmental, and functional dimensions of the Calgary Family Assessment Model.
RESULTS: At admission, the infant had repeated vomiting, minimal spontaneous movement, and an inability to roll over. Treatment included surgery, chemotherapy, autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplantation, and radiotherapy. Despite treatment, the disease progressed, and the infant died at home surrounded by family. The mother's surrogate decision-making evolved with changes in the child's condition, treatment limitations, and the increasing important of family time. She struggled to reconcile hope for continued treatment, treatment burden, and family time. Family roles, relationships, and support systems changed. The nurse helped the mother express her values and wishes and revisit decisions, without pressuring her toward a single conclusion. In parallel, nursing support addressed changes in family roles, caregiving responsibilities, and available support.
CONCLUSION: This case suggests the importance of attending to both surrogate decision-making and changes in family functioning in pediatric end-of-life care during infancy and early childhood. A case-derived conceptual framework illustrates these parallel aspects of nursing support and requires further examination across cases.

articles.title: High-alert medication safety in Pediatric critical care: A multinational analysis of nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-alert medications are frequently used in pediatric intensive care units and can cause serious harm when used in error. Multinational evidence on pediatric intensive care nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers remains limited.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional multinational study was conducted among 705 pediatric intensive care nurses from Egypt, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Iraq. Data were collected using a sociodemographic and professional form, a 10-item High-Alert Medication Knowledge Questionnaire, and a 23-item Attitudes Toward Medication Errors and Error Reporting Questionnaire. Descriptive, correlation, simple regression, and dummy-coded multiple regression analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.
RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 5.46 ± 2.69 on the 0-10 scale, corresponding to 54.55% of the maximum possible score. Professional and organizational consequences had the highest mean percentage among attitude domains (59.18%), followed by fear and punitive barriers (50.94%); beliefs about error prevention and safety culture had the lowest percentage (33.45%). Knowledge showed weak correlations with reporting-related attitude domains. Multiple regression showed that knowledge was associated with gender, country, and high-alert medication safety training, whereas total attitude was associated with country and total nursing experience.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric intensive care nurses showed important gaps in high-alert medication safety knowledge, while reporting attitudes reflected persistent organizational and professional barriers. Findings support competency-based education, just-culture reporting systems, feedback mechanisms, and work-system redesign.

articles.title: Changes in pediatric nurses' knowledge of autism spectrum disorder and alternative communication strategies before and immediately after a health education program: a one-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess changes in pediatric nurses' knowledge of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and alternative communication strategies before and immediately after a health education program.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest study was conducted among pediatric nurses from two teaching hospitals. Participants completed a knowledge questionnaire assessing ASD and alternative communication strategies immediately before and after the program; the questionnaire did not assess observed communication skills or clinical performance.
RESULTS: Baseline knowledge of ASD and alternative communication strategies was limited. Mean ASD knowledge scores increased from 5.92 ± 2.39 at pretest to 12.30 ± 1.38 at immediate posttest. Mean knowledge scores for alternative communication strategies increased from 6.66 ± 3.22 to 12.75 ± 1.39. Both pretest-posttest differences were statistically significant (p < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric nurses demonstrated higher questionnaire-based knowledge scores immediately after the health education program. However, the one-group pretest-posttest design does not establish that the program alone caused these changes or that the knowledge gains were sustained. Questionnaire familiarity, recall, and testing effects may also have contributed to the observed differences.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Structured health education may support pediatric nurses' knowledge of ASD and alternative communication strategies. Further evaluation should assess knowledge retention over time and include objective measures of practical communication skills to determine whether knowledge gains translate into clinical competence.

articles.title: Effect of an educational program on pediatric nurses' performance within the critical golden hour following pediatric trauma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Outcomes after pediatric trauma, a leading cause of childhood death and disability, depend substantially on care delivered during the first "golden hour". Nurses are the first to assess injured children, yet evidence shows persistent deficits in their trauma-specific preparation. This study evaluated the effect of a structured educational program on pediatric nurses' knowledge, practice, self-confidence, and attitudes regarding golden-hour trauma care.
DESIGN AND METHODS: A one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design was used. A convenience sample of 108 nurses in the pediatric emergency department of Beni-Suef University Hospital, Egypt, completed a five-part instrument covering the four outcome domains, received a structured researcher-delivered program on golden-hour pediatric trauma assessment and management, and were reassessed identically. Five pediatric nursing experts confirmed content validity, and internal consistency was acceptable (KR-20 = 0.86 and 0.79 for the dichotomous tools; Cronbach's α = 0.81 and 0.78 for the Likert tools). Paired t-tests and Spearman's correlations were used.
RESULTS: Before the program, 51.9% of nurses were unfamiliar with the golden hour and 88.9% had received no related training. Afterwards, mean knowledge rose from 66.3% to 85.9%, practice from 51.1% to 79.7%, self-confidence from 3.06 to 3.79, and attitudes from 2.48 to 2.76 (all p < .01). Knowledge correlated positively with practice (r = 0.684, p < .01), self-confidence, and attitudes.
CONCLUSIONS: The program was associated with significant improvement across all four domains.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Golden-hour training should be embedded in professional development for pediatric emergency nurses and reinforced with simulation, standardized protocols, and mentorship.

articles.title: Perfectionism and burnout among pediatric intensive care unit nurses: The mediation role of workaholism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) nurses work in high-acuity environments characterized by complex clinical demands, repeated exposure to critically ill children, parental distress, and pediatric death, placing them at increased risk of burnout. Perfectionistic tendencies may promote excessive and compulsive work patterns, or workaholism, that further deplete nurses' psychological resources. However, the pathways linking perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout remain insufficiently understood in pediatric critical care nursing.
AIM: This study examined the relationships among perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout among PICU nurses and investigated the mediating role of workaholism in the perfectionism-burnout relationship.
METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 431 PICU nurses recruited from eight hospitals across five Egyptian governorates. Data were collected using a web-based questionnaire including the Short Almost Perfect Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, and Dutch Work Addiction Scale. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, hierarchical multiple regression, and mediation path analysis.
RESULTS: Burnout was positively associated with workaholism (r = 0.218, p < 0.01) and perfectionism (r = 0.247, p < 0.01). A significant positive correlation was also observed between perfectionism and workaholism (r = 0.334, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect association between perfectionism and burnout through workaholism (standardized indirect effect = 0.051, bootstrap 95% CI [0.016, 0.089]), accounting for approximately 20.6% of the total association and supporting partial statistical mediation. Hierarchical regression analysis identified alternating shifts, perceived insufficient income, a nurse-to-patient ratio of 1:3, workaholism, and perfectionism as significant predictors of burnout.
CONCLUSION: Perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout were significantly interrelated among pediatric intensive care unit nurses. Workaholism showed a partial statistical mediating role in the association between perfectionism and burnout, suggesting that compulsive work behaviors may represent a relevant behavioral pathway linking these psychological characteristics. The findings highlight the importance of addressing both individual and organizational factors through strategies targeting maladaptive perfectionism, excessive work involvement, staffing adequacy, and psychological support. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal relationships and evaluate interventions aimed at reducing burnout.

articles.title: Children's and adolescents' experiences of returning to school after acquired brain injury: a qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize qualitative evidence on the experiences of children and adolescents returning to school after acquired brain injury (ABI).
BACKGROUND: Returning to school is critical for recovery and social reintegration after ABI. Although return-to-school support has increasingly emphasized individualized accommodations, multidisciplinary collaboration, and ongoing follow-up, existing evidence remains largely informed by clinical outcomes and the perspectives of parents or professionals. The lived experiences of children and adolescents themselves remain insufficiently synthesized.
METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted across multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, PsycINFO, CNKI, and VIP. This study adhered to the PRISMA and ENTREQ guidelines. Included literature was quality-appraised using the CASP checklist, and extracted data were analyzed using thematic synthesis.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies were included. Analysis yielded 12 subcategories grouped into 5 main themes: (1) Hinder learning effectiveness; (2) Psychological Distress; (3) Social Challenges; (4) Family support; (5) Support needs during return to school.
CONCLUSION: School reintegration after ABI is a complex, multidimensional process. Nursing and healthcare personnel should attend to children's perspectives, provide individualized support, and strengthen communication across families, schools, and healthcare. At policy level, formal information-sharing pathways and teacher training on ABI are needed to ensure consistent, appropriate support.

articles.title: "I hardly fall asleep because I keep thinking about my child": Psychosocial experiences of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James Centre Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, Malawi.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Admission of a child to a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is highly distressing for caregivers, who face uncertainty about the child's outcome and disruption of normal caregiving roles. In low-resource settings such as Malawi, where psychosocial support is limited, little is known about caregivers' experiences during their child's PICU admission.
OBJECTIVES: This study explored psychosocial experiences, coping mechanisms and support needs of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James PICU in Malawi.
METHODS: A qualitative exploratory-descriptive study was conducted between October and December 2024 at Mercy James PICU within Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre. Eleven caregivers of children admitted for over 48 h were purposively sampled for in-depth, semi-structured interviews, which were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated and analysed thematically. The transactional theory of stress and coping guided interpretation of findings.
RESULTS: Four themes were identified: emotional and psychological distress, caregivers' perceptions of care delivery, coping mechanisms and perceived support needs. Caregivers experienced both immediate and ongoing distress associated with sudden PICU admission, uncertainty, separation from family and financial strain. Perceptions of care were shaped by interactions with staff and hospital environment. Caregivers used both problem-focused strategies, like information seeking, and emotion-focused strategies like reliance on God, social support and acceptance. They reported unmet needs for psychological support, compassionate care and access to food.
CONCLUSION: Caregivers of children in PICU experience significant psychosocial challenges shaped by admission context, environment and limited support. Strengthening communication and information-sharing practices, compassionate care, structured emotional support and addressing basic needs is essential.

articles.title: Fathers' role conflicts and identity reconstruction in paediatric palliative care: A qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis of qualitative studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although family-centred care is the guiding model in paediatric palliative care, mothers are frequently assumed to be the primary caregivers, while fathers' role experiences and unique needs have long been neglected-rendering them "forgotten caregivers".
OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize qualitative studies on fathers' role experiences in paediatric palliative care and to gain an in-depth understanding of the challenges they face, coping strategies, and psychological growth trajectories.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across six databases. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) approach for qualitative synthesis was used for quality appraisal and data synthesis.
RESULTS: Eight studies were included. Four synthesized themes were identified: (1) Masculinity and the maternal-centric medical system intertwine, obscuring fathers' unique needs; (2) torn between economic provision expectations and caregiving desire, fathers fall into a deep role predicament; (3) confronted with structural exclusion, fathers adjust by seeking informational control and partnering with the mother; and (4) adversity catalyses transformation, leading to the reconstruction of fatherhood identity and meaning.
CONCLUSION: Fathers are systematically marginalized in paediatric palliative care, which conceals both their needs and vulnerabilities. Fathers possess caregiving willingness but develop instrumental coping pathways due to structural exclusion, ultimately transforming their identity.
IMPACT: Clinically, the default "mother-as-primary-carer" communication model should be disrupted, and father-friendly, skill-oriented, peer-supported services should be developed. At the policy level, fathers need to be recognized as core members of the care team, thereby advancing palliative care from "mother-centred" to truly family-centred care.

articles.title: Development and psychometric properties of the scale of perceived safe care among hospitalized children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a child-reported scale for assessing perceived safe care among hospitalized children aged 7-12 years and to examine its psychometric properties.
METHODS: This methodological scale-development study was conducted between 15 March and 15 June 2026 with 410 hospitalized children in pediatric clinics in three provinces. A 32-item pool underwent expert content review and pilot testing; the resulting 20-item draft was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 205) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 205) in non-overlapping analytic datasets.
RESULTS: EFA yielded a 13-item, two-factor structure. In the final Principal Axis Factoring solution, the two extracted factors accounted for 50.833% of the variance after extraction (43.812% and 7.020%, respectively); the first two initial eigenvalues were 6.182 and 1.385, whereas the third was 0.841. The correlation matrix was suitable for factor analysis (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.895; Bartlett's χ2 = 1279.755, df = 78, p < 0.001). CFA supported an acceptable-to-good fit (χ2 = 126.505, df = 60, χ2/df = 2.108, root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) = 0.074, 90% confidence interval (CI) 0.056-0.092, comparative fit index (CFI) = 0.951, incremental fit index (IFI) = 0.952, Tucker-Lewis index (TLI) = 0.937, standardized root mean square residual (SRMR) = 0.061). The two factors were named Perceived Safety and Protection and Information and Supportive Care. Internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.904; McDonald's ω = 0.903). The total score correlated positively with the Assessment of Care Quality Through Children's Eyes Scale (r = 0.709, 95% CI 0.657-0.754, p < 0.001) and negatively with the Perceived Stress Scale for Kids (r = -0.514, 95% CI -0.582 to -0.439, p < 0.001). Two of the three prespecified hypotheses were fully supported; the structural hypothesis received qualified support because the two-factor representation was supported, although evidence for factor distinctness was mixed.
CONCLUSION: The scale provided preliminary evidence of content validity, structural validity, hypothesis-based construct validity, and internal consistency for assessing hospitalized children's perceptions of safe care. Further testing of temporal stability, measurement invariance, responsiveness, and external validity in independent and diverse samples is warranted.
PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: The scale may be used as a child-reported measure to describe perceived safe care and to support pediatric nursing research and quality-improvement activities; it should not be interpreted as a substitute for objective patient-safety indicators.

articles.title: The effect of web-based education and therapeutic play methods provided to children undergoing elective surgery on preoperative anxiety and fear, and postoperative pain and sleep: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of combining web-based education provided at home with therapeutic play implemented in the hospital on preoperative anxiety and fear, as well as postoperative pain and sleep, in children aged 7-12 years undergoing elective surgery.
DESIGN: Randomized controlled experimental study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study included 78 children aged 7-12 years who underwent elective surgery. The children were randomly assigned to two groups: intervention (n = 37) and control (n = 41). Children in the intervention group received web-based education about the surgical process at home and information through therapeutic play at the hospital, whereas the control group received standard preoperative nursing care. Data were collected using the Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale-Short Form (mYPAS-SF), Child Fear Scale (CFS), Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale (WBFPS), and Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC).
RESULTS: The preoperative mYPAS-SF and CFS scores, as well as the postoperative WBFPS scores, were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (p < 0.05), with effect sizes indicating large clinical significance. No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of post-discharge SDSC scores (p > 0.05), and the effect size was clinically small.
CONCLUSION: Providing preoperative preparation education using a combination of web-based education and therapeutic play was effective in reducing preoperative anxiety and fear and postoperative pain in children undergoing elective surgery; however, it did not affect improving sleep.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Pediatric nurses can help reduce children's preoperative anxiety, fear, and postoperative pain in children scheduled for surgery by using effective, practical, web-based educational and therapeutic play methods tailored to the children's age and developmental characteristics in pediatric surgery clinics.

articles.title: Childhood obesity, ultra-processed foods, and the future of child health: Implications for pediatric nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is a serious pediatric issue with potential health effects across the life course. Although it is often framed as an individual or family problem, children's eating patterns are strongly shaped by food environments, commercial marketing, affordability, and access. In particular, the accessibility, low cost, palatability, and marketing of ultra-processed foods may contribute to childhood obesity. This commentary analyzes childhood obesity through the lens of ultra-processed food consumption and identifies practical, non-stigmatizing, and equity-oriented implications for pediatric nursing practice.

articles.title: Goal Management Training for Adolescents with ADHD: A Multi-Center Randomized Controlled Effectiveness Trial.
articles.abstract: Non-pharmacological interventions targeting executive functions (EF), such as Goal Management Training (GMT), may augment treatment as usual (TAU) for adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We examined whether GMT plus TAU improves EF, ADHD symptoms, and functional impairment more than TAU only. In this preregistered multi-center randomized controlled trial, 116 participants (Mage = 14.69 years; 66% female) were randomized to GMT plus TAU or TAU only. GMT comprised seven weekly 2-hour group sessions, supplemented by parent and teacher sessions. TAU was standard outpatient mental health services. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the parent-reported Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF-2), Global Executive Composite (GEC). Secondary outcomes were teacher-, self-, and parent-reported BRIEF-2 subdomains; parent- and teacher-reported ADHD Rating Scale-IV scores; and parent-reported functional impairment measured with the Weiss Functional Impairment Rating Scale-Parent Report (WFIRS-P). GMT plus TAU showed no additional benefit over TAU only. Intention-to-treat analyses showed no significant between-group difference in GEC (adjusted b = - 2.12, 95% CI [- 7.64, 3.41], p = .449, d = - 0.14), parent-reported ADHD symptoms (d = - 0.27, p = .323) or other secondary outcomes (all p > .10). Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05874791; registered April 14, 2023).

articles.title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

articles.title: Ferric derisomaltose for the treatment of iron deficiency with or without anemia in women's health: an expert review.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency (ID) with or without anemia is highly prevalent in women, and is commonly caused by abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB; including heavy menstrual bleeding), increased iron requirements during pregnancy, or postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). ID or iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in women of reproductive age has been associated with a substantial burden on quality of life, impaired physical and cognitive functioning, decreased productivity, and increased healthcare costs. The presence of ID/IDA during pregnancy has also been linked to poorer maternal outcomes and fetal developmental impairments, including an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in neonates. Despite the high prevalence of ID/IDA and negative impact on women's health, these conditions are frequently overlooked and undertreated, in part due to the nonspecific nature of symptoms, such as fatigue. There is an increasing body of evidence for the use of intravenous (IV) iron to treat ID/IDA in women. Although efficacy is largely comparable among IV iron formulations when equivalent doses are used, there are factors that distinguish certain IV iron formulations from others. This review aims to discuss available evidence for the treatment of ID/IDA in women with ferric derisomaltose (FDI; a high-dose IV iron formulation), focusing on AUB, pregnancy, and PPH. Based on existing data, FDI represents a clinically-effective option for iron repletion in these contexts, and a low risk of hypersensitivity reactions and hypophosphatemia. There is scope for further research within the field of ID/IDA in women's health to address unmet needs and evidence gaps across the patient care pathway.

articles.title: Non-invasive brain stimulation for motor rehabilitation in pediatric stroke: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric stroke is a leading cause of neurological disability, often resulting in hemiparetic cerebral palsy (HCP). Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS), including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), may enhance motor recovery due to the developing brain's neuroplasticity.
OBJECTIVES: To map the available evidence on the feasibility, safety, and clinical and neurophysiological outcomes of rTMS and tDCS in children and adolescents with hemiparesis secondary to pediatric stroke.
METHODS: A scoping review of 11 publications representing 8 independent controlled trials published between 2005 and 2025: 4 rTMS trials (6 reports) and 4 tDCS trials (5 reports) involving perinatal or pediatric stroke. Additional reports from the same cohorts were retained when assessing different outcomes or follow-up points but were not counted as independent cohorts. Clinical, neurophysiological, and safety outcomes were synthesized descriptively.
RESULTS: NIBS was feasible and generally well tolerated under the studied protocols, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. Some small rTMS trials reported benefits in selected upper-limb outcomes compared with sham, but effect magnitude and durability remain uncertain. Smaller tDCS trials yielded mixed findings, including improved subjective occupational performance without additional gains in objectively assessed hand function. The largest multicenter trial, involving 89 randomized children with perinatal stroke and unilateral cerebral palsy, found no additional benefit over sham in hand function or achievement of child-identified functional goals. One small rTMS trial included 10 participants with childhood-onset arterial ischemic stroke; no controlled tDCS trial specifically targeting childhood-onset stroke was identified.
DISCUSSION: NIBS appears feasible and generally well tolerated in children with stroke-related hemiparesis. Upper-limb motor recovery benefits have been reported, particularly alongside intensive rehabilitation, although the largest pediatric tDCS trial showed no additional motor benefit. Corticospinal and metabolic predictors remain exploratory. The small evidence base, methodological heterogeneity, and interindividual variability preclude definitive conclusions about clinical effectiveness. Evidence predominantly concerns perinatal stroke and unilateral cerebral palsy, limiting generalizability to childhood-onset stroke. Future research should standardize protocols and investigate whether individualized approaches incorporating neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers improve rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Dual-wavelength superpulsed photobiomodulation in children and adolescents with orofacial pain: clinical, thermal, and optical transmission outcomes in a pilot study.
articles.abstract: To report the preliminary results of a photobiomodulation protocol using a dual-emission diode laser (810 nm and 980 nm) in children and adolescents with orofacial pain, considering clinical findings, thermal behavior, and optical transmission in the region of the masseter muscle. An uncontrolled exploratory pilot study was conducted involving seven participants six to 17 years of age with orofacial pain submitted to photobiomodulation twice a week for four weeks, totaling eight sessions. Application was performed bilaterally in direct contact at four points per side: masseter muscle, temporalis muscle, cervical trapezius muscle, and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) region, totaling eight points per session. A 7-mm adapter was used, with an average power of 0.3 W, 3.9 J per point, and 13 s per point. Orofacial pain, regional temperature, skin phototype, power, and irradiance transmitted in the masseteric region were investigated. Mean age was 11.4 ± 3.6 years and the female sex accounted for 57.1% of the sample. Lower pain values were found over time. Mean optical power detected at the buccal mucosa after transmission in the masseteric region was 0.41 ± 0.10 mW, corresponding to mean irradiance of 0.64 ± 0.16 mW/cm². Exploratory correlations between irradiance and anthropometric variables, and between phototype and temperature, had wide confidence intervals, indicating substantial uncertainty regarding the direction and magnitude of these associations. In this pilot study, descriptive reductions in pain outcomes were found over the four-week intervention period. Given the uncontrolled design, these exploratory findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical efficacy or causality, but may assist in the design of future controlled clinical trials with larger samples.

articles.title: Effects of a preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes: secondary findings from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity rates are rising globally, and many females of reproductive age are physically inactive, which may adversely affect future maternal and neonatal health. In this secondary analysis, we investigated the effect of a combined preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks.
METHODS: This article reports analyses of secondary outcomes from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial, in which we randomised females who were planning pregnancy, at risk of gestational diabetes mellitus and did not have diagnosed diabetes 1:1 to intervention or control. The intervention consisted of time-restricted eating (TRE) and exercise training and spanned from preconception throughout pregnancy. TRE involved restricting energy intake to ≤10 hour/day on ≥5 days per week. Exercise volume was based on a heart-rate-based metric (Personal Activity Intelligence, PAI), with the goal of ≥100 weekly PAI-points. The main outcomes of interest in this secondary analysis were cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks of intervention in the preconception period.
RESULTS: Among 167 randomised participants, we included 166 in the intention-to-treat analysis. After 7 weeks of preconception intervention, there was no significant between-group difference in relative peak oxygen uptake (0.8 mL·kg-1·min-1; 95% CI -0.2 to 1.9, p=0.10) or glucose area under the curve (0.0 mmol·hour/L; 95% CI -0.1 to 0.2, p=0.76).
CONCLUSION: 7 weeks of preconception TRE combined with exercise training did not result in statistically significant improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness or glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04585581.

articles.title: Deep learning classification of children with autism spectrum disorder using short-duration center of pressure data.
articles.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often demonstrate impaired postural stability. However, assessment of postural stability in this population can be challenging because prolonged standing trials may increase spontaneous fidgeting and reduce data quality. Convolutional neural network (CNN) may offer a practical approach for identifying ASD-related postural control patterns using short-duration center of pressure (COP) data. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the classification performance of a CNN for distinguishing children with ASD from healthy controls using short duration COP data. 49 children, including 20 typically developing children and 29 children with ASD, completed quiet-standing trials on a force plate. COP data were analyzed using CNN models trained separately with 5 s, 10 s, and 15 s COP data inputs. Classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score were calculated to assess the model performance. In general, classification performance improved as COP input duration increased. Using 5 s COP data, the CNN model achieved a classification accuracy of 77.6 %. When the duration was increased to 10 s, accuracy improved substantially to 96.7 %. Extending the duration to 15 s resulted in a minor increase in accuracy to 98.8 %. These findings indicate that short-duration COP contains discriminative information in this sample. Larger multisite samples and external validation are required before clinical application.

articles.title: Whole-genome association scans and meta-analysis identify deletions or excess homozygosity associated with head and neck cancer susceptibility.
articles.abstract: Because currently identified genetic variants and exogenous risk factors explain only a modest proportion of susceptibility to head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and because deletion variants and copy number variants remain largely understudied for human complex diseases, we attempt to identify additional common genetic variants that influence HNSCC susceptibility by performing a whole-genome analysis of the association between deletions or excess homozygosity and susceptibility to HNSCC. The design of the standard genome-wide association studies is a point-wise approach to finding individual disease-associated SNPs. In contrast, we propose to use segment-wise approaches to finding small chromosomal segments of varying sizes that influence HNSCC susceptibility. We conducted two distinct whole-genome scans of associations using 733,202 SNPs, with 1,154 cases and 1,542 controls in batch 1 and 1,031 cases and 2,965 controls in batch 2, as well as the meta-analysis that synthesizes the association summary statistics from each batch. The method is designed for examining statistical evidence of marginal association of one SNP at a time in the first stage, followed by a cluster-based approach that combines the overall assessment of individual marginal associations of neighboring SNPs in distinct genomic regions in the second stage. We identified nine short candidate deleted segments in which at least 2 neighboring top SNPs (with p-value ≤1 × 10-4) were overly aggregated on chromosomes 3p22.2 (batch 1), 1p31.1, 5q33.2, 11q12.3 (batch 2), 5p15.2, 6p22.2, 9q21.31, 12q12, and 12q13.12 (from meta-analysis) at a corrected 0.05 nominal significance level, adjusted for multiple comparison procedures. These short segments contain or overlap several genes: SCN5A, AK5, CARMIL1, and MUC19, which are associated with various diseases, including cardiac events, sudden infant death syndrome, colon cancer, liver cancer, HNSCC, and Crohn's disease.

articles.title: Longitudinal characterization of a Leigh-like presentation associated with the MT-ND4 m.11470A>C variant.
articles.abstract: Leigh syndrome comprises genetically heterogeneous mitochondrial disorders, but interpretation of rare mitochondrial DNA variants is often limited by sparse longitudinal data. We report a male patient followed from childhood to age 16 with the MT-ND4 m.11470A>C (p. (Lys237Asn)) variant. Right-eye strabismus and optic atrophy appeared at age 3, followed by progressive limb weakness, gait instability, and dysarthria. At age 16, magnetic resonance imaging showed bilateral lesions involving the basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. The patient subsequently developed respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. The variant was detected in saliva at a pipeline-reported heteroplasmy level of 51.8% and was not detected by Sanger sequencing in saliva from the mother or dizygotic twin brother. APOGEE 2 predicted a potential deleterious effect, the affected residue was conserved, and static structural visualization suggested altered local contacts. A targeted review identified previous associations of m.11470A>C with MELAS and a Leigh syndrome record in a pediatric cohort. This detailed longitudinal case adds clinical and neuroimaging resolution to the reported m.11470A>C spectrum and supports integrating disease trajectory, tissue source, heteroplasmy, and family data when interpreting rare mitochondrial DNA variants.

articles.title: The neurodevelopmental model for schizophrenia: Leading to the conceptual logic of, and nascent evidence for, prenatal-perinatal early intervention?
articles.abstract: The neurodevelopmental model for schizophrenia looks rearwards from first episode psychosis (FEP), though clinical high risk for psychosis (CHRP), psychomotor abnormalities in childhood and delayed milestones in infancy, to origins in fetal brain dysmorphogenesis; in contrast, the early intervention model looks forwards from CHRP, through FEP, to course of illness and improvement in long-term outcome. This article considers emerging evidence for convergence in these models. It first considers recent incisive, physical evidence for disruption to fetal craniofacial morphogenesis and asymmetry in schizophrenia; these findings indicate a gestational 'window' for dysmorphogenesis and its association with genetic risk for schizophrenia. It then considers recent formulations of genetic risk as a dynamic, context-dependent process underlying fetal brain dysmorphogenesis that encompasses environmental-psychosocial factors known to influence the onset and course of psychotic illness. These formulations suggest that interventions during CHR-P may be 'too late'. Rather, they posit interventions during the prenatal and perinatal‑neonatal stages as reflecting the developmental pathobiology of schizophrenia and proffering prophylaxis through alleviation of disruption to the normal developmental programme. Using maternal folic acid supplementation as a model of prophylaxis for a neurodevelopmental disorder (neural tube defect), this article then considers recent evidence, across 194 global jurisdictions, that risk for schizophrenia may also be lower in those jurisdictions with mandatory maternal folic acid supplementation. It further considers the first evidence that multidomain perinatal‑neonatal public health interventions can lead to significant improvements in neurodevelopment. The neurodevelopmental model for schizophrenia leads to the conceptual logic of, and nascent evidence for, prenatal‑neonatal prophylaxis.

articles.title: Novel Breath Segmentation and Predictive Quality Classification Model for Pediatric Bag-Mask Ventilation Using Capnography Waveforms.
articles.abstract:
