BACKGROUND: Bag-mask ventilation (BMV) is a critical phase of pediatric airway management, yet objective feedback remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a two-stage, CO2-only framework for pediatric BMV assessment comprising automated breath segmentation and machine learning classification of breaths according to predefined low-quality criteria for insufficient ventilation. We hypothesized that our model would achieve area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) greater than or equal to 0.75 and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) greater than or equal to 0.75.
DERIVATION COHORT: We retrospectively analyzed capnography waveforms from 85 critically ill children receiving peri-intubation BMV in a quaternary-care PICU. Flow and pressure data established reference-standard low-quality criteria: expiratory tidal volume (VTE) less than 4 mL/kg of ideal body weight, mask leak greater than 40%, or upper airway obstruction (VTE < 4 mL/kg with peak inspiratory pressure > 30 cm H2O and leak > 80%).
VALIDATION COHORT: CO2-based segmentation was validated in 10 randomly selected patients comprising 605 manually adjudicated breaths. Classification performance was internally validated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation within the derivation cohort; no independent validation cohort was used.
PREDICTION MODEL: A rule-based algorithm segmented continuous CO2 waveforms into breaths. Deep learning architectures then used CO2 waveforms alone to classify breaths according to whether they met predefined low-quality criteria.
RESULTS: The CO2-only algorithm identified 6942 breaths (median, 66 per patient [interquartile range, 47-100 per patient]); 49.5% met at least one low-quality criterion. Segmentation achieved positive predictive value 0.95 (95% CI, 0.93-0.96) and sensitivity 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89). Twenty-seven breaths were adjudicated as false-positive detections (0.05; 95% CI, 0.036-0.074). CO2-only segmentation may miss ventilatory attempts with minimal or absent exhaled CO2. The best-performing classification model achieved AUROC 0.79 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89) and AUPRC 0.75 (95% CI, 0.57-0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: A CO2-only framework showed proof-of-concept feasibility for breath segmentation and quality classification during pediatric BMV, supporting further development of objective bedside feedback systems.

articles.title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors.
OBJECTIVES: To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain).
RESULTS: Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of FAS Sequencing in Suspected ALPS: Insights from a Large Clinical Cohort.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) is a rare immune dysregulation disorder most commonly caused by defects in the FAS-mediated apoptosis pathway. While germline FAS variants account for the majority of cases, somatic variants, typically restricted to double-negative T cells (DNTCs), may be under-detected in routine testing. We retrospectively analyzed FAS full-gene sequencing in 686 probands and 3 family members with suspected ALPS to assess diagnostic yield, variant spectrum, and clinical utility. Germline FAS variants were identified in 73/685 probands (10.7%) using whole blood or cytobrush samples. Somatic FAS variants were detected in 8/22 cases (36.4%) using sorted DNTCs, demonstrating a substantially higher diagnostic yield in patients with strong clinical suspicion but negative germline testing. A total of 65 unique diagnostic sequencing variants were identified, of which 49% were previously unreported. Variants were enriched in the intracellular domain (65%), with most disrupting the death domain. Three cases with copy number variants (CNVs) were identified, including deletions spanning intron 5 to exon 9, intron 6 to exon 9, and a partial exon 9 deletion involving the C-terminal region of FAS, expanding the known spectrum of structural variants. One case demonstrated a somatic FAS variant with a markedly higher level than wild-type allele in DNTCs, consistent with somatic loss of heterozygosity (sLOH), representing the second reported case of ALPS-sFAS/sLOH. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive FAS testing, including germline and somatic analysis with DNTC-based sequencing and CNV detection, to improve diagnostic accuracy and inform clinical management in suspected ALPS.

articles.title: SIMPATHY Study: Specific Antibody Response to Typhim Vi Polysaccharide as a Surrogate Marker of Infectious Risk in Secondary Immunodeficiency Associated with B Cell Cancer.
articles.abstract: Recurrent and severe infections represent a major cause of morbidity and mortality of secondary immunodeficiency (SID) associated with B-cell lymphoproliferative syndromes (B-CLPD). Nevertheless, immunological evaluation and prophylactic interventions are often delayed until infectious complications occur. Early vaccination is therefore relevant not only because it provides protection during the initial phases of B-CLPD, but also because it enables the identification of patients at higher risk of infection. In this context, assessment of antigen-specific humoral response has been proposed as a useful biomarker for identifying patients with greater clinical vulnerability. We conducted SIMPATHY (Secondary Immunodeficiency Multicentric study on the Antibody Production to Typhi vaccine), a multicentre, retrospective, observational study including 128 individuals with B-CLPD, classified according to the presence or absence of severe and/or recurrent infections, as well as healthy controls. Specific IgG antibody responses to Streptococcus pneumoniae (13-valent conjugate, Prevenar), Salmonella typhi (Typhim Vi), and tetanus toxoid vaccines were assessed at baseline and 4-weeks after vaccination. Among 128 individuals analysed, patients with B-CLPD showed significant immunological and clinical differences compared to healthy controls, particularly in vaccine-specific antibody responses and lymphocyte subsets. B-CLPD patients with recurrent or severe infections exhibited markedly reduced pre-vaccination anti-pneumococcal (p = 0.03) and post-vaccination anti-pneumococcal (p = 0.001) and anti-Salmonella typhi Vi titers (p = 0.1), highlighting impaired vaccine-specific antibody responses as potential predictors of infection risk. An immunological classification identified two subgroups within B-CLPD, predominant antibody defect and combined immune defect, with a trend toward higher respiratory infection rates in the latter, suggesting broader immune dysfunction.

articles.title: Photoacoustic imaging assessment of acute kidney injury associated with experimental necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal condition increasingly recognized to cause systemic complications, including acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the underlying mechanisms and variations in renal impairment remain largely unknown, and there is a lack of non-invasive imaging methods for detecting early kidney injury. Methods: We evaluated kidney injury through a multimodal approach, using a neonatal rat model of experimental NEC. Plasma and renal tissue were analyzed for pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) by ELISA. Histological analysis and immunofluorescence staining were used to identify renal abnormalities and expressions of KIM-1 and NGAL. Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) was used to assess renal oxygenation and total hemoglobin as functional imaging biomarkers of kidney injury. Results: NEC pups showed significant elevations of systemic and renal cytokines, as well as increased expression of KIM-1, NGAL and CD31 in proximal tubules of the kidney. Histological examination further confirms renal injury in the NEC cohort. PAI demonstrated reduction in renal oxygen saturation, offering non-invasive assessment of physiological kidney damage. Conclusion: This study characterizes AKI associated with NEC as an inflammatory and hypoxic response in the neonatal rat NEC model and introduces PAI as a promising imaging modality for non-invasive evaluation of renal injury in NEC.

articles.title: Age-Specific Self-Care, Psychosocial, and Coping Competencies in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: Development of a Competency Framework from Diabetes Camp Experiences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The progressive acquisition of self-care and coping competencies is essential for children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), as these skills support increasing autonomy in diabetes management. However, limited data are available regarding the ages at which these competencies are typically acquired. This study aimed to determine the ages at which key self-care and coping competencies are acquired among children and adolescents with T1D.
METHODS: We analyzed data from competency evaluations conducted in 943 patients aged 7-17.9 years during diabetes summer camp in France in 2021. A broad range of self-care and coping competencies was assessed in patients treated with either multiple daily injections (MDI) or insulin pump therapy. Age groups were defined as 7-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, and 15-17 years. Descriptive statistics were used to determine the proportion of patients acquiring each competency by age group, and treatment modalities were compared using univariate analyses.
RESULTS: Among the 114 self-care competencies classified into 14 domains, 94.1% were acquired by patients treated with MDI and 96.5% by those using insulin pump therapy by the age of 17.9 years. We established a detailed reference list of the ages at which at least 75% of patients had acquired each competency and developed a corresponding competency evaluation tool. Several competencies were acquired at younger ages in patients using insulin pump therapy than in those treated with MDI.
CONCLUSIONS: The age-specific reference list developed in this study may help healthcare professionals design and adapt therapeutic education programs to support the progressive development of autonomy in children and adolescents with T1D.

articles.title: JUVENILE IDIOPATHIC ARTHRITIS IN CHILDREN WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES: IMPACT OF CURRENT MEDICAL TREATMENT OPTIONS ON ANTHROPOMETRY AND METABOLIC CONTROL.
articles.abstract: Children with both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) face increased disease complexity due to overlapping autoimmune and inflammatory processes. This study aimed to assess anthropometric, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk factors compared to children with T1D alone. Data from the Diabetes Patient Follow-up (DPV) registry (1995-2023) were analyzed, comparing 489 children with T1D and JIA to 67,462 children with T1D only. Children with T1D and JIA used diabetes technologies (insulin pumps, CGM, AID systems) more frequently with similar HbA1c levels. Between 2014-2019 and 2020-2023, HbA1c levels significantly improved in the JIA group, while BMI and height approached the T1D only group. Despite increased disease burden, children with T1D and JIA achieve glycemic control comparable to those with T1D alone. Nonetheless, elevated cardiometabolic risks highlight the need for tailored, interdisciplinary care strategies.

articles.title: Evolution of POCUS in the NICU: From a diagnostic tool to an extension of clinical examination.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly transforming neonatal intensive care practice from a discrete diagnostic modality into an extension of the bedside clinical examination. Compared to traditional monitoring tools, POCUS provides rapid, real-time physiologic and anatomic information that may improve diagnostic precision, procedural safety, and individualized clinical decision-making in critically ill neonates. Over the past decade, expanding evidence and international consensus guidelines have supported a growing range of neonatal POCUS applications, including lung ultrasound for respiratory distress and pneumothorax, targeted cardiac assessment, bowel ultrasound for necrotizing enterocolitis, vascular access guidance, and evaluation of the acutely decompensating infant. Structured protocols such as SAFE-R, the Crashing Neonate Protocol, STEP, and NeoSONAR have further advanced the integration of ultrasound into neonatal emergency assessment and resuscitation. In parallel, formal recommendations from organizations including the European Society of Pediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care, the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Society of Echocardiography, and the National Neonatal POCUS Collaborative have accelerated the development of standardized training, credentialing, and quality assurance frameworks. This narrative review summarizes the evolving role of POCUS in neonatology, reviews current evidence supporting diagnostic and procedural applications, discusses emerging protocols for emergency and resuscitative care, and explores future directions including advanced training pathways, artificial intelligence integration, research interests, competency-based education and standardized training.

articles.title: Experiences of Families Receiving Regular Remote Review of CGM to Provide Targeted Supports: A mixed methods study evaluating a pilot model of care in children with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the experience of families of children (aged 7-14) with type 1 diabetes participating in a model of diabetes care that utilises regular remote review of CGM to prioritise contact and provide personalised and targeted support. This study focused on exploring the acceptability and impact of this model of care on participants and their families.
METHODS: This mixed-methods study used semi-structured interviews and a combined multiple-choice and free-text survey, completed by parents of children participating in a trial model of diabetes care. Qualitative data was analysed via reflexive content analysis to establish categories describing the experience and acceptability of the model of care. Quantitative data reflecting acceptability of the model of care were reported using frequency of response.
RESULTS: A sample of 15 surveys and 9 interviews were completed from 59 eligible participants who completed the model of care. The primary outcome, family experience of receiving contact, was most frequently referenced with 83% reporting positive personal impacts such as reassurance, support and validation, 46% reporting improved wellbeing and 70% reporting impacts on diabetes self-knowledge and management changes. Secondarily, the model was largely seen to be acceptable with 83% reporting convenient, positive and flexible communication and with potential to add-value to and reduce the requirement of traditional outpatient clinical care. Further, most participants reported a desire to continue the model of care. Participants also described potential revisions to improve the model and target specific populations who may benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggested acceptability and subjective benefit of regular review of CGM by the clinical team with targeted remote intervention in a group of children with T1D. It highlights the value that families place on support and communication, independent of glycaemic benefits. This insight may be used to guide clinical contacts and future trials.

articles.title: Hybrid Closed-Loop Use Mediates the Relationship Between Social Determinants of Health and Glycemic Outcomes in a Canadian Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Clinic.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sociodemographic disparities continue to impact people living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), despite advances like hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, which improve glycemic outcomes and quality of life. This study evaluated whether HCL system use mediates the relationship between social determinants of health (SDH) and glycemic outcomes in children living with T1D (CLWT1D).
METHOD: A retrospective chart review included CLWT1D followed at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario between May 2023 and May 2024. Demographics, management, and glycemic outcomes (hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and percent time in range (%TIR)) were collected. SDH were measured using the Canadian Index of Multiple Deprivation, which categorizes individuals into quintiles (Q1= least to Q5= most deprived) across four dimensions using postal codes. Regression models examined mediation effects.
RESULTS: Data from 581 children (mean age 13.4±3.8 years; 46.6% female; mean T1D duration 6.1±3.8 years; mean HbA1c 8.0±1.5%) were analyzed. Of these, 46% used HCL systems, while 54% used injections or stand-alone pumps. HbA1c was associated with situational vulnerability (p<0.001) and residential instability (p<0.001), with HCL system use significantly mediating differences in HbA1c between Q1-4 vs Q5. No mediation effect was found for economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. %TIR results were consistent with HbA1c findings.
CONCLUSION: HCL system use mediated the relationship between glycemic outcomes and residential instability and situational vulnerability, but not economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. Access to HCL systems may mitigate health inequities in CLWT1D; however, technology alone does not eliminate these disparities, and parallel interventions are needed to promote equitable care.

articles.title: Menarche in Young-Onset Type 1 Diabetes: Data from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) Registry.
articles.abstract: Aim Data on age at menarche in youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain limited. We examined factors associated with age at menarche and longitudinal trajectories of insulin dose, glycaemia, and body mass index (BMI) before and after menarche in an Australasian cohort. Method Longitudinal sociodemographic and clinical data for females with T1D and a documented menarche date were extracted from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) registry. Generalised estimating equations were used to examine factors associated with age at menarche (< vs. ≥ cohort median age), including Index of Relative Socioeconomic Disadvantage score, T1D duration, total daily insulin dose/kg (TDD/kg), HbA1c, insulin pump use, and BMI standard deviation score (SDS). Trajectories of TDD/kg, HbA1c, and BMI SDS across nine clinically defined pre- and post-menarche time intervals were analysed using linear mixed models with time modelled as a categorical fixed effect, accounting for repeated measures and within-subject correlation. Results Overall, 601 females from nine centres were included. Median (IQR) age at menarche was 12.6 (12.0, 13.3) years. Later menarche was associated with longer T1D duration (B = 0.10; 95% CI 0.01-0.19; p = 0.04), lower TDD/kg (-1.20; -2.00 to -0.42; p = 0.003), higher HbA1c (0.21; 0.02-0.39; p = 0.03), and lower BMI SDS (-0.48; -0.79 to -0.17; p = 0.002). TDD/kg increased in the pre-menarcheal period, peaking around menarche then declining; BMI SDS increased progressively from pre- to post-menarche; and HbA1c rose over time from pre- to post-menarche (all p < 0.001), demonstrating distinct trajectories. Conclusions Increasing insulin requirements preceded menarche, while HbA1c and BMI SDS continued to rise during the post-menarcheal period. These findings suggest that metabolic changes associated with pubertal maturation extend beyond menarche itself and highlight the importance of considering pubertal progression in diabetes care and anticipatory management during adolescence.

articles.title: Monitoring aeration during non-invasive ventilation in the delivery room: a narrative review of current and emerging methods.
articles.abstract: Ensuring effective lung aeration during non-invasive ventilation in the delivery room is a central challenge in neonatal resuscitation. Preterm neonates frequently require respiratory support at birth, yet it is difficult to assess whether delivered ventilation is effectively reaching the lungs. Currently recommended monitoring parameters reflect mostly indirect physiological responses to lung aeration and provide limited actionable guidance when values fail to improve. This narrative review evaluates nine monitoring methods for their ability to answer two key clinical questions: whether spontaneous breathing is present and effective, and whether positive pressure ventilation results in effective lung aeration. Methods are grouped by measurement modality: respiratory flow and pressure monitoring, exhaled carbon dioxide (CO2) detection, lung ultrasound, thoracic volume change, and transcutaneous diaphragmatic electromyography. Each method provides clinically relevant physiological information, yet for most, limitations in reliability, interpretability, or delivery room applicability constrain their use as an actionable guide during active resuscitation. Of all modalities reviewed, exhaled CO2 comes closest to addressing both clinical questions, as its presence directly confirms gas exchange and therefore lung aeration by either spontaneous breathing or ventilation, though evidence for its use to guide resuscitation remains limited. Delivery room evidence remains sparse across most methods, and where studies exist, they have largely been conducted for post-hoc physiological analysis rather than evaluation of real-time guidance. Future research should focus on prospective evaluation of monitoring-guided resuscitation strategies and on identifying which combinations of methods provide the most actionable information without adding unnecessary complexity.

articles.title: Japan society of clinical oncology clinical practice guidelines 2024 for fertility preservation in childhood, adolescent, and young adult cancer patients: part 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Japan Society of Clinical Oncology (JSCO) Clinical Practice Guidelines 2024 for Fertility Preservation in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult (CAYA) Cancer Patients and Related Diseases provide updated guidance for oncofertility care in Japan. This article, Part 2 of the guideline series, addresses gynecologic, breast, and urologic cancers; childhood cancer and related diseases; and hematologic malignancies.
METHODS: Background Questions (BQs), Clinical Questions (CQs), and Future Questions (FQs) were developed for each disease area. CQs were addressed through systematic reviews and resulted in evidence-based recommendations, whereas BQs summarized established clinical knowledge and FQs addressed important issues for which evidence-based recommendations could not be formulated. Recommendations were developed through systematic review and consensus processes using the Evidence-to-Decision framework, with consideration of the certainty of evidence, benefits and harms, patient values, acceptability, and feasibility.
RESULTS: Disease-specific recommendations, statements, and explanatory texts are presented for fertility preservation and reproductive support in the five clinical areas. Because evidence remains limited for several clinical issues, decisions should be individualized according to the patient's age, disease status, planned treatment, urgency of treatment initiation, and reproductive wishes.
CONCLUSIONS: These guidelines emphasize prioritization of cancer treatment, timely individualized counseling, and multidisciplinary collaboration among oncologists, reproductive medicine specialists, pediatricians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals. Such collaboration is essential to support informed decision-making and optimize oncofertility care for CAYA patients.

articles.title: Laparoscopic versus open appendectomy for appendicitis in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute appendicitis is among the most common pediatric surgical emergencies worldwide. Laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) has gained wide acceptance in recent years ; however, its superiority over the traditional open appendectomy (OA) is still a topic of debate, particularly regarding postoperative outcomes and recovery.
AIM: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare LA and OA in children with acute appendicitis, focusing on postoperative outcomes, recovery parameters, pain, cosmetic results, and cost-effectiveness to guide evidence-based surgical decision-making.
METHODS: The study followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025620445). A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Science Direct, Scopus, and Google Scholar in November 2024. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing LA and OA in patients aged ≤ 18 years were included. Data were extracted and analyzed using RevMan 5.0, applying fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Twenty-five studies involving 166,755 patients (7 RCTs and 18 observational studies) were included. LA significantly reduced surgical site infection (OR = 0.68), intestinal obstruction (OR = 0.24), and reoperation rate (OR = 0.53). It also shortened hospital stay (MD = - 1.16 days) and time to oral intake (MD = - 1.14). No significant differences were found in operative time, intra-abdominal abscess formation, or overall complications.
CONCLUSION: LA offers better postoperative outcomes and faster recovery than OA in pediatric appendicitis, with comparable operative time and abscess risk. These findings support LA as the preferred approach, although further multicenter RCTs are needed for long-term outcome validation.

articles.title: Hidden heterogeneity in complicated appendicitis: comparison of preoperative biomarker profiles across the histopathological spectrum of acute appendicitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complicated appendicitis, comprising gangrenous and perforated subtypes, is conventionally treated as a single category in biomarker studies. These subtypes may nonetheless represent distinct pathophysiological processes, and whether they exhibit different preoperative biomarker profiles has not been systematically investigated. This study compared preoperative biomarker profiles across the histopathological spectrum of acute appendicitis and evaluated the diagnostic role of immature granulocytes (IG).
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 363 appendectomy patients classified as acute appendicitis (n = 227), gangrenous appendicitis (n = 59), perforated appendicitis (n = 33), or negative appendectomy (n = 44). A three-tiered framework compared negative appendectomy versus true appendicitis, uncomplicated versus complicated, and gangrenous versus perforated appendicitis. Laboratory parameters and composite indices were analysed by ROC analysis with DeLong confidence intervals and Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons, and by multivariable logistic regression with Firth penalized and bootstrap-corrected sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Gangrenous and perforated appendicitis exhibited divergent biomarker profiles. Neutrophil-based indices did not discriminate between subtypes, all confidence intervals including 0.50 (AUC 0.449-0.547), whereas CRP-based parameters and IG retained discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.756-0.853). CRP increased monotonically across the spectrum (15.7 → 39.4 → 157.0 mg/L), whereas NLR rose from acute to gangrenous appendicitis and showed no further increase thereafter (p = 0.600). IG percentage outperformed neutrophil percentage (ΔAUC = 0.314, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). CRP (p < 0.001) and IG count (p = 0.010; Firth p = 0.012) were independent predictors of perforated appendicitis, and adding IG count to CRP improved model fit (p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Neutrophil-based indices fail at the gangrenous-perforated boundary, whereas CRP and IG retain diagnostic value across the spectrum. All findings are exploratory: they derive from a single operated cohort and require external validation before clinical application. The principal implication is methodological: pooling these subtypes under one complicated category may cause signal loss in biomarker studies.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: The global macroeconomic burden of idiopathic epilepsy: estimates for 2021 and projections to 2050.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic epilepsy imposes substantial health and economic burdens worldwide, yet evidence on welfare-based macroeconomic losses attributable specifically to idiopathic epilepsy remains limited. This study estimated the global, regional, and national welfare burden of idiopathic epilepsy across 190 countries and territories in 2021 and projected this burden to 2050.
METHODS: Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and healthy life expectancy were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021; gross domestic product (GDP) and GDP per capita from the World Bank's World Development Indicators database; and country-, sex-, and age-specific population estimates and medium-variant projections from the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024. VLW was estimated using the value of a statistical life and the value of a statistical life year and expressed in purchasing power parity-adjusted constant 2021 international dollars. Age- and sex-specific DALY rates were projected to 2050 using exponential smoothing state-space models and combined with the corresponding population projections.
RESULTS: In 2021, the global undiscounted VLW attributable to idiopathic epilepsy was Int$1,138.013 billion, equivalent to 0.737% of global GDP. By 2050, it was projected to reach Int$1,287.730 billion, equivalent to 0.834% of the 2021 global GDP benchmark and 13.156% above the 2021 level. Absolute VLW was concentrated in high-income and populous regions, particularly the United States, China, and India, whereas the relative burden was greatest in low-SDI regions and Sub-Saharan Africa. Higher VLW was observed among adolescents, young and middle-aged adults, and males.
CONCLUSIONS: Idiopathic epilepsy causes substantial and growing global welfare losses with marked inequalities. Strengthening prevention, diagnosis, affordable antiseizure medication access, primary care integration, and anti-stigma interventions is essential, especially in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Shared and Distinct Patterns of Grammatical Aspect Production and Prosody in Mandarin-Speaking Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder and Developmental Language Disorder.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study used the Mandarin perfective aspect marker le as a window into structural language to examine whether similarities between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and developmental language disorder (DLD) extend beyond morphosyntactic production to prosodic realization, and whether prosody provides ASD-specific linguistic markers.
METHOD: Preschool-aged Mandarin-speaking children with ASD, DLD, and typical development (TD) completed elicited production and comprehension tasks, and their speech was analyzed using acoustic and sentence-level prosodic measures.
RESULTS: Both ASD and DLD groups produced canonical le forms at rates comparable to TD children and showed similar atypical temporal modulation in short sentences, indicating shared vulnerabilities at the syntax-prosody interface. However, important divergences emerged. Only the ASD group showed reduced comprehension accuracy relative to TD peers, fewer alternative valid completive constructions, and more task-irrelevant responses. Moreover, ASD was associated with selective prosodic differences: elevated pitch and pitch variability, as well as abnormal lengthening and exaggerated intensity modulation in longer sentences.
CONCLUSIONS: These preliminary findings suggest that language profiles of ASD and DLD, particularly ASD, are characterized by atypical coordination between syntactic encoding and prosodic realization. Theoretically, the results support treating prosody as an integral component of structural language organization and highlight prosody as a key dimension for distinguishing ASD from DLD in tonal languages.

articles.title: Speech Sound Production in Children With and Without Elevated Familial Likelihood of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to characterize the speech production skills of 3-year-old children who have typical familial likelihood (TL) and elevated familial likelihood (EL) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) with diverse developmental outcomes (ASD, a history of non-autism language delays, or no delays or diagnoses) during spontaneous speech. Our research questions were as follows: (a) Do speech sound inventories and phonological processes differ across groups, and (b) do groups differ in the accuracy and consistency of repeated words?
METHOD: Spontaneous speech samples of TL children (n = 16), EL children with a subsequent ASD diagnosis (EL-ASD; n = 10), EL children with a history of non-autism language delay (EL-HLD; n = 21), and EL children with no ASD diagnosis or language delay (EL-ND; n = 16) at 36 months of age were analyzed for productive consonant and vowel inventories, phonological processes, and accuracy and consistency of repeated words. Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to examine potential group differences in sizes of phonetic inventories and proportions of repeated words. Fisher's exact tests were used to compare likelihoods of using individual consonants, vowels, and phonological processes.
RESULTS: EL-ASD children had significantly smaller consonant inventories than TL and EL-ND children and smaller vowel inventories than all other children. These differences did not hold when analyzing only those participants who produced at least 50 speechlike utterances in sensitivity analyses, although these analyses only included n = 4 EL-ASD participants. EL-ASD children showed a greater prevalence of glottalization. No group differences in the consistency or accuracy of repeated words were found.
CONCLUSIONS: Together, these results suggest that speech sound development in EL-ASD children may show subtle differences from that of TL, EL-ND, and EL-HLD children. Consonant development in EL-HLD children may also differ slightly from that in TL and EL-ND children. Clinically, these findings suggest that assessing speech skills may be warranted for some EL children and highlight the heterogeneity of speech and language skills among children with an elevated likelihood of ASD.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.35043553.

articles.title: Deictic Gestures and Developmental Skills in Down Syndrome: The Role of Hand Points.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize deictic gesture form and communicative intent in children with Down syndrome (DS) and address a clinically important limitation in how pointing is defined in assessment. Building on our prior work linking caregiver-reported total gesture use to language, motor, and pragmatic/social skills in toddlers with DS, we examined microcoded deictic gestures during naturalistic parent-child interactions, distinguishing hand points (multifinger or whole-hand points) from index-finger points and exploring associations with adaptive developmental skills.
METHOD: Participants were 41 children with DS (range: 36.3-88.8 months, M = 54.1 months) who completed a baseline 10-min remote in-home parent-child interaction. Gestures were coded for type, deictic form (reach, give, show, hand point, index-finger point), and communicative intent (behavioral request, joint attention). Rates were compared using Friedman tests (false discovery rate [FDR] corrected). Partial Spearman correlations examined associations between the three most frequent deictic forms (hand point, show, and give) and Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-Third Edition (Vineland-3) growth scale values across communication, motor, and interpersonal domains, controlling for chronological age with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (BH-FDR) correction.
RESULTS: Children produced higher rates of deictic than nondeictic gestures. Most gestures were spontaneous, and many co-occurred with speech. Index-finger points were uncommon; hand points were more frequent and clearly referential in context (serving both requesting and joint attention functions). After age control and BH-FDR correction, hand-point rate was positively associated with Vineland-3 Interpersonal Relationships.
CONCLUSIONS: Hand points were common, spontaneous, and communicatively meaningful in children with DS but may be overlooked when pointing is defined solely as an index-finger gesture. Measurement frameworks that credit functionally effective hand points may provide a more accurate representation of children's referential communication and inform clinical interpretation and intervention planning.

articles.title: Exploring the impossible: Prior sleep timing and infants' response to violation-of-expectation events.
articles.abstract: Infants actively explore their environment to learn. Events that contradict infants' prior experiences about how the world works are thought to serve as special learning opportunities. Infants preferentially explore objects behaving in an unusual way and test their properties related to the event. Given the critical role of sleep in infant cognition, we hypothesized that the exploratory response to events that violate basic physical principles would vary depending on prior sleep timing. Eight- to 12-month-old infants (n = 28) viewed televised events either shortly after a nap or following prolonged wakefulness. Each infant saw one object violate the law of object solidity and another object conform with it. Immediately afterward, infants showed targeted exploration of the object violating solidity: they explored it longer than the experience-conforming object and a novel distractor, and they were more likely to test its properties regarding the violated principle. Unexpectedly, there was no significant effect of prior sleep timing on how infants explored the objects. However, exploratory regression analyses revealed that longer prior wakefulness duration was associated with less targeted exploration of the object violating solidity. Additional studies are required to test if prior sleep timing is associated with how infants process and respond to physically impossible events in confirmatory analyses.

articles.title: Ritlecitinib for Alopecia Areata in Patients Under 18 Years of Age: A Single-Center Retrospective Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Alopecia areata (AA) in pediatric and adolescent patients can be severe and difficult to manage, and real-world data on targeted therapies in this population remain limited. Ritlecitinib, a selective JAK3/TEC inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy in adults with AA, but evidence in patients under 18 years of age is scarce. The purpose of this study is to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric and adolescent patients with alopecia areata.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective real-world study included patients aged <18 years with AA treated with ritlecitinib 50 mg once daily. Treatment response was assessed using changes in Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) scores and achievement of SALT50/75/90 at the last on-treatment observation. Safety outcomes were evaluated based on clinical records.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 9.3 years (IQR, 6.0-14.6), including patients younger than 12 years who received off-label treatment. The median baseline SALT score was 50. The median SALT score decreased to 0 at the last observation (p < 0.001). SALT50, SALT75, and SALT90 were achieved by 96.3%, 77.8%, and 55.6% of patients, respectively, and 51.9% achieved complete scalp regrowth. Treatment responses were observed in both patchy AA and AT/AU subgroups; however, interpretation of subgroup differences is limited by the small sample sizes. No serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were documented in the available medical records.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, ritlecitinib treatment was associated with substantial improvement in SALT scores and no documented serious adverse events during the observation period. These preliminary findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies, particularly in children younger than 12 years receiving off-label treatment.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of head lice infestation among schoolchildren in district 19, Tehran: A Cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Head lice infestation (Pediculus humanus capitis) remains a persistent global public health concern and is one of the most prevalent parasitic infections among school-aged children. Given that schools represent key institutional environments for the active identification and screening of infestations, combined with marked regional variability in epidemiological patterns, the lack of localized surveillance data in densely populated urban areas, such as southern Tehran, hampers the design of effective control and prevention strategies. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of P. h. capitis infestation and to identify its associated demographic and personal hygiene factors among students in District 19 of Tehran.
METHODS: This descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in autumn 2025 among 720 schoolchildren in District 19 of Tehran. Data were collected through direct scalp examination and a structured questionnaire. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test was used to assess normality. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical variables, while independent t-test and Mann-Whitney U test were applied for quantitative variables. Bathing frequency was analysed both as a continuous and categorical variable. To account for clustering within schools and adjust for potential confounders, a multivariable logistic regression model using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) was fitted.
RESULTS: Of the 720 students examined, 364 (50.6%) were female and 356 (49.4%) were male. The overall prevalence of P. h. capitis infestation was 5.0% (95% CI: 3.5-6.9%) [36/720]. Statistical analysis revealed a significant association between infestation and gender, with a markedly higher prevalence in girls (8.8%) compared to boys (1.1%) (P < 0.001). Furthermore, a significant relationship was observed between infestation and personal hygiene; mean weekly bathing frequency was significantly lower in infested students (2.44 ± 0.91) compared to non-infested students (3.15 ± 1.3) (P < 0.001, independent-samples t-test with unequal variances assumed).A history of scalp pruritus was also strongly associated with the diagnosis of infestation (P < 0.001). No statistically significant associations were found regarding age, educational level, or socioeconomic variables.
CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that P. h. capitis infestation remains a public health concern among schoolchildren in District 19 of Tehran. Female sex, and lower weekly bathing frequency were associated with higher infestation rates. Our data did not demonstrate statistically significant associations between the measured socioeconomic indicators and infestation; however, given the small number of positive cases, larger studies are needed before concluding that pediculosis is independent of socioeconomic status. These results support the implementation of universal school-based screening and hygiene education programs, with particular attention to primary and lower secondary schools.

articles.title: Pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To review visual, anatomical, microbiological, and management-related outcomes in pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through June 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261422377). We included cohort studies, case-control studies, and case series (five or more patients) of patients aged 18 years or younger with endophthalmitis after open-globe injury. We excluded postoperative or endogenous endophthalmitis and cohorts without separable pediatric post-traumatic data. Proportions were pooled using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey transformation. Risk of bias was assessed with JBI, Newcastle-Ottawa, or QUADAS-2 tools.
RESULTS: Fifty-seven studies (4,558 eyes) were included, 29 in quantitative synthesis. Pooled random-effects estimates are shown with crude event counts. Favorable final visual acuity (≥ 20/200) was achieved in 28% (95% CI 16-42%; 317/787 eyes) and no light perception in 27% (13-44%; 160/466). Globe retention was 98% (96-100%; 870/920), evisceration or enucleation 2% (0-4%; 50/920), and phthisis bulbi 14% (4-26%; 74/498). Culture positivity was 39% (27-52%; 442/976), with Gram-positive organisms predominating among 880 isolates. Pars plana vitrectomy, intravitreal therapy, and systemic antibiotics were used in 90% (883/1,085), 97% (775/907), and 81% (781/915) of eyes, respectively. Delay to presentation and to primary repair were the most consistent predictors of endophthalmitis and poor outcome.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis is associated with poor visual outcomes despite aggressive multimodal treatment, although globe preservation is achievable in most eyes. Early recognition, prompt antimicrobial therapy, and timely surgical intervention appear critical to optimizing outcomes, emphasizing the need for rapid referral and standardized management.

articles.title: Platelet parameters and treatment-requiring reactivation after intravitreal ranibizumab for retinopathy of prematurity: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether platelet parameters are associated with the need for retreatment in preterm infants with retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) after intravitreal ranibizumab (IVR).
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included preterm infants with zone II stage 3 + ROP who received primary IVR. Platelet count (PC), mean platelet volume (MPV), and platelet mass index (PMI) were collected at birth, at first treatment, and at 4 weeks post-treatment. Infants were divided into a retreatment group (n = 40) and a control group (n = 143, no retreatment). Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Of 183 infants, 40 (21.86%) required retreatment. The postmenstrual age (PMA) at retreatment was 41.09 ± 1.72 weeks, and the median time to retreatment was 7.36 weeks (interquartile range [IQR]: 6.47-8.00). Birth weight (BW), gestational age (GA), and PMA at initial treatment were significantly lower in the retreatment group (all P < 0.001). At birth, PC was lower and MPV was higher in the retreatment group (both P < 0.001), whereas PMI did not differ (P = 0.095). At first treatment, PC and PMI were lower in the retreatment group (both P < 0.001), while MPV did not differ (P = 0.319). At 4 weeks post-treatment, PC and PMI remained lower and MPV was higher in the retreatment group (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.039, respectively). In the multivariable model, PMA at initial treatment (odds ratio [OR] = 0.113, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.029-0.435, P = 0.002) and PC at birth (OR = 0.917, 95% CI: 0.870-0.966, P = 0.001) were independent protective factors, whereas MPV at birth (OR = 14.252, 95% CI: 2.340-86.791, P = 0.004) was an independent risk factor. The area under the curve (AUC) was 0.886 for PC (cut-off ≤ 271.50 × 10⁹/L; sensitivity 75.0%, specificity 99.3%) and 0.886 for MPV (cut-off ≥ 10.550 fL; sensitivity 70.0%, specificity 97.2%).
CONCLUSION: PC at birth and MPV at birth are independently associated with the need for retreatment after IVR for ROP. These readily available hematological markers warrant further investigation as potential indicators for identifying infants requiring closer follow-up.

articles.title: Risks of long-term ophthalmic complications in preterm and ROP: a 14-year population-based study in Taiwan.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the 14-year (2004-2017) epidemiology and newborn demographic risk factors for preterm- and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP)-associated ophthalmic complications using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD).
DESIGN: Retrospective Cohort Study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1,784,677 infants were recorded from the maternal and children database of the NHIRD.
METHODS: Data were retrieved from the NHIRD, and patients were stratified into full-term, preterm without ROP, and ROP groups. Six ophthalmic complications were recorded and compared, including myopia, amblyopia, glaucoma, strabismus, cataracts, and retinal detachment. The average follow-up time for the recorded ophthalmic complications was between 6.5 to 7.2 person-years. The hazard ratios (HRs) for patients with ROP were calculated for each complication, using full-term infants as the reference group.
RESULTS: A total of 1,784,677 infants born between 2004 and 2017 were enrolled, and 0.56% were diagnosed with ROP. ROP was identified as a risk factor for myopia, amblyopia, strabismus, cataracts, and retinal detachment (all p<0.05). ROP-associated glaucoma, cataracts, and retinal detachment showed extremely early onset within the first 2 years of life, identifying them as high-risk complications among patients with ROP. Multivariate analysis showed a trend of lower birth weight being associated with a higher risk of developing ROP-associated complications of myopia, amblyopia, glaucoma, and strabismus.
CONCLUSION: Prematurity, especially in the presence of ROP, carries a higher risk of ophthalmic complications, which often present early in the first decade of life. Low BW among patients with ROP is also associated with elevated risks of ophthalmic complications.

articles.title: Design priorities for paediatric walkers in India: professional perspectives.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Independent mobility is essential for children's participation in education, community life, and social activities. In India, no paediatric walker is specifically designed for Indian children or the contexts in which they live. This study explored rehabilitation providers' perspectives on the limitations of existing paediatric walkers and identified features that may optimise walker design for Indian settings.
METHODS: A qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis was conducted across four cities in India. Rehabilitation providers, orthotists and equipment vendors, involved in the assessment, prescription, and provision of paediatric mobility devices were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling. Data were collected through focus groups and individual interviews.
RESULTS: Fifty-eight participants shared their perspectives over nine focus groups and five individual interviews, in four different Indian cities. Six themes were identified (1): child-friendly design, emphasising attractive, engaging, safe, and easy-to-use walkers (2); customisation, including adjustability for age, diagnosis, growth, and terrain (3); durability, particularly for uneven rural environments and prolonged use (4); functional features, such as harnesses, splints, seating options, braking systems, and improved wheel designs (5); technology integration, including biofeedback, artificial intelligence, and GPS-enabled monitoring; and (6) lightweight construction, supporting portability, transportation, and everyday use.
CONCLUSIONS: Rehabilitation providers identified several design priorities for a paediatric walker tailored to Indian contexts. These findings provide foundational guidance for the development of paediatric mobility devices that better meet the needs of Indian children and their families.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Bedside Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score to Predict Mortality in Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a common but often overlooked complication of advanced liver cirrhosis and is independently associated with decompensation and mortality. Because CT-based muscle quantification is not always feasible in resource-limited settings, we developed and validated a bedside Cirrhotic Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score (CSNS) incorporating anthropometric, ultrasonographic, and metabolic variables to predict 12-month morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage liver disease.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 350 adult patients enrolled from December 2023 to April 2026. Patient selection was sequential and prospective into a development cohort (n = 250) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 100). All participants met sarcopenia criteria based on gait speed and handgrip strength. Six bedside parameters: triceps skinfold thickness, mid-upper arm circumference, mid-arm muscle circumference, mid-thigh circumference, ultrasound-derived psoas muscle thickness, and nitrogen balance were combined via penalized logistic regression to generate the CSNS on a 0-100 scale. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC and compared with MELD-Na and Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) scores. External validation was performed in the independent cohort.
RESULTS: Nitrogen balance and psoas muscle thickness contributed most strongly to the final model. At an optimal cutoff of 61.2, the CSNS showed good discrimination for 12-month mortality in both the development (AUROC 0.816) and validation (AUROC 0.803) cohorts, with higher AUROC values than MELD-Na and CTP. High CSNS remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR 1.023; p = 0.002) and was significantly associated with major cirrhosis-related complications, including hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, refractory ascites, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding (all p ≤ 0.003).
CONCLUSION: The CSNS is a simple, radiation-free bedside tool that improves prognostic assessment beyond conventional scores and may support risk stratification in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Chasing a Fox Tail-Red Fox as Environmental Sentinel in the One Health Salmonella Surveillance.
articles.abstract: Salmonella remains a major zoonotic hazard of global concern. While its occurrence in livestock and food is well documented, its environmental circulation in wildlife reservoirs remains poorly understood. Surveillance of free-living animals is essential for improving our understanding of transmission routes. Wide-ranging mesocarnivores such as red foxes (Vulpes vulpes) may contribute to the environmental persistence and spatial dissemination of Salmonella across natural and peri-urban ecosystems. This study assessed the prevalence, genomic characteristics, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles of Salmonella isolated from red foxes. Additionally, comparative genomic analyses with human-derived Salmonella strains were performed. A total of 300 intestinal samples (ceca) collected from hunted red foxes (2022-2023) in the Podkarpackie and Małopolskie Voivodeships were analyzed for Salmonella according to the ISO standard. Antimicrobial susceptibility of confirmed isolates was determined using the broth microdilution method. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed using the Illumina NextSeq platform. Salmonella was detected in 4.7% (n = 14) of samples. Identified serovars included S. Enteritidis (n = 12), S. Typhimurium (n = 1), and S. Infantis (n = 1), corresponding to the leading serovars associated with human salmonellosis in the European Union (EU). All S. Enteritidis isolates belonged to sequence type (ST) 11, while S. Typhimurium and S. Infantis were classified as ST19 and ST32, respectively. Six isolates exhibited AMR. Quinolone resistance in S. Enteritidis (n = 5) was associated with gyrA mutations, whereas the multidrug-resistant S. Infantis strain carried gyrA, parC, tet(A), sul1, and ant(3″)-Ia. Comparison of S. Enteritidis isolates from foxes and humans suggests potential genetic relatedness. The detection of clinically relevant and antimicrobial-resistant serovars in red foxes highlights that these animals may be useful sentinels for environmental Salmonella surveillance. These findings support the inclusion of wildlife in integrated environmental pathogen and AMR surveillance within a One Health framework.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Insulin Dosing in Gestational Diabetes: A Simulation Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Gestational diabetes (GDM) is a major contributor to maternal and neonatal morbidity, healthcare costs and a growing healthcare burden for clinicians. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications are increasingly used in healthcare, but data are lacking on their use in GDM management.
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate the proof of concept of utilizing a large language model (LLM) clinical decision support tool (CDST) in GDM care we conducted a study with an objective to compare ChatGPT management of insulin dependent GDM to clinician management. Our primary hypothesis was that ChatGPT would suggest starting insulin at a higher dose than the clinicians. Our secondary hypothesis was that clinician-prescribed doses would converge with the initially recommended ChatGPT dose by the first visit occurring more than 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
STUDY DESIGN: In a retrospective cohort of patients with insulin-dependent GDM, we compared a model using ChatGPT as a simulated CDST to traditional clinician-prescribed insulin. Gestational age (GA), weight, and glucose values were entered into ChatGPT with a request to create an initial insulin regimen, and subsequent log values were entered with a request to alter the regimen as appropriate. The primary outcome was total daily insulin dose (TDD) and the exposure was regimen source (ChatGPT vs clinician). We compared TDD at the initial visit and the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
RESULTS: A total of 60 patients were included. The initial clinician TDD of insulin was 13.3 units lower than the ChatGPT recommendation (95% CI: 7.7-18.9, p < 0.001). At the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation, clinicians increased their prescribed TDD by an average of 11.1 units (95%CI: 7.4-14.4, p< 0.001). At this subsequent time point clinician prescribed TDD was similar to the initial ChatGPT prescription (mean: [ChatGPT-CP]: 2.2 units (95%CI: -3.2-7.7), p=0.42), and concurrent visit (mean [ChatGPT-CP]: 1.6 units (95%CI: -0.2-3.4), p=0.08).
CONCLUSION: Clinicians initiate insulin at lower doses than recommended by ChatGPT. However, 2-3 weeks after insulin initiation, recommended doses were similar. These findings suggest the feasibility of prospective studies assessing the use of an AI-CDST in GDM management. This approach may complement clinicians as a co-management tool and expand access to earlier medical intervention, particularly in areas with limited access to high-risk obstetricians.

articles.title: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life Measure for Children/Adolescents With Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to adapt the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life for Adolescents with Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS) scale into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. It also explored oral health status and quality of life among children with Down syndrome (DS).
METHODS: The study included 100 children with DS and their mothers. Sociodemographic and oral health data were collected through structured questionnaires. The OH-QOLADS, comprising child and family forms with two timeframes, was translated and culturally adapted following international guidelines. Internal consistency, CFA, and item-total correlations were conducted to assess psychometric validity.
RESULTS: The Turkish OH-QOLADS showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α and McDonald's ω > 0.94) across all forms and timeframes. CFA supported the original four-factor structure (symptoms/functioning, emotional well-being, social participation, and family impact) with strong model fit indices (CFI > 0.98; RMSEA < 0.05). Most participants reported poor oral health, low tooth brushing frequency, and minimal preventive care. Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) scores were significantly associated with comorbidities like thyroid disease, diabetes, and hearing impairments.
CONCLUSION: The Turkish OH-QOLADS is a valid, reliable tool for assessing OHRQoL in children with DS. The findings highlight the need for better access to preventive dental services and caregiver support.

articles.title: From Skin Commensals to Bloodstream Pathogens: In Vitro Virulence Traits and In Vivo Pathogenicity of Malassezia Isolates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The lipid-dependent yeast genus Malassezia is composed of skin commensals that can become pathogenic. This genus can cause bloodstream infection in low-weight preterm neonates and immunocompromised adults. However, little is known about the virulence mechanism involved in the transition from commensal to pathogenic.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate and compare the in vitro and in vivo virulence of M. furfur, M. pachydermatis and M. sympodialis strains from fungemia cases and healthy skin or superficial clinical entities.
METHODS: Twenty-five isolates, along with three reference strains of the three evaluated species, were assessed in vitro for virulence traits, including phospholipase and hemolytic activity, thermotolerance, oxidative stress resistance and biofilm production. Those isolates that presented the highest or lowest in vitro virulence based on the evaluated traits were evaluated in vivo in the Galleria mellonella infection model.
RESULTS: Fungemia isolates of the three species showed higher phospholipase activity, biofilm formation, thermotolerance and oxidative stress resistance. Only for M. furfur, a high hemolytic activity was registered for the fungemia isolate. In vivo evaluation supported the previous in vitro results, in which larvae inoculated with isolates from fungemia and with high in vitro virulence were demonstrated to induce higher mortality and tissue burden, contrasting with isolates from healthy skin or skin clinical entities.
CONCLUSION: The evaluated isolates exhibited heterogeneous in vitro phenotypes and experimental pathogenicity. The findings support further investigation of relationships between these traits and infection outcomes. Finally, M. furfur showed a higher capacity to survive in the host, correlating with the Malassezia-fungemia epidemiology.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Husband-Involved Maternity Education on Skilled Delivery Service Utilization in Rural Communities of Central Ethiopia: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: In low-income countries, skilled delivery service utilization remains disproportionately low among rural women, resulting in a high rate of preventable maternal and neonatal mortality. Poor husband involvement in maternity care is one of the major contributing factors in Ethiopia. Hence, the purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of husband-involved maternity education on skilled delivery service utilization in rural communities of central Ethiopia. A two-arm parallel-group cluster-randomized controlled trial was carried out among couples in the rural community of Central Ethiopia. The intervention group received group maternity education and individual home visits. A total of 496 couples from 16 clusters were randomly assigned to either the intervention (n=248) or the control group (n=248). A generalized estimating equation analysis was done to evaluate the intervention effectiveness. At the end line, 97.9% of the couples in the intervention group and 98.7% of the couples in the control group were available for analysis. There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the control and intervention groups. SDSU was significantly higher among pregnant women who received HIME intervention than those who did not receive the interventions, with a net effect of 21% (95% CI 18.7% - 23.2%, p < 0.001). In the GEE model, the SDSU was a 2-fold increase compared to the control group (AOR: 2.435, 95% CI 1.531, 3.874). This research indicates that involving husbands in the maternity education has a great effect on improving skilled delivery service utilization among pregnant women.

articles.title: Child Sexual Abuse, Sexual Function, and Sexual Distress in Couples Coping with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder: A Dyadic Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract: Sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD), characterized by low sexual desire and high sexual distress, is the most common sexual dysfunction among women. Although current theoretical models support interpersonal conceptualizations of sexual desire, distal interpersonal factors that may underlie the sexual well-being of couples coping with SIAD, such as child sexual abuse (CSA), have not been thoroughly documented. Yet, difficulties with sexual desire and arousal are among the most frequently reported sexual dysfunctions among CSA survivors. Using a one-year longitudinal design among couples with SIAD, this study examined the associations between both partners' CSA and their sexual function and distress. Individuals with SIAD (N = 263; Mage = 34.16) and their partners (N = 263; Mage = 35.71) completed validated questionnaires at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Dyadic latent growth curve analyses were conducted within a structural equation model. Results showed that greater CSA among individuals with SIAD was associated with their own higher initial levels of sexual distress. Moreover, higher levels of non-SIAD partners' CSA were unexpectedly associated with lower initial levels of sexual function difficulties for individuals with SIAD. However, non-SIAD partners' CSA predicted greater increases in sexual function difficulties over time for individuals with SIAD. No other significant associations were found. Findings highlight the role of CSA in the sexual function and distress of couples coping with SIAD and point towards the value of couple-based interventions that acknowledge both partners' histories and their impact on mutual sexual experiences.

articles.title: Maternal hair glucocorticoids as indicators of HPA axis dysregulation in early preterm birth.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet its biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysregulation is implicated in PTB, and maternal hair glucocorticoids may reflect chronic HPA axis activity. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether hair cortisone (HCNC) and cortisol (HCC) concentrations measured during pregnancy were associated with early preterm birth (ePTB), birth after 20 weeks and at or before 34 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: This analysis used data (N = 309) from the Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study in Peru. Maternal hair collected at birth was divided into two 3-cm segments representing later pregnancy (0-12 weeks before birth) and earlier pregnancy (12-24 weeks before birth) to estimate HCNC and HCC. To address variation in glucocorticoid concentrations by gestational age at birth and differences in exposure windows between ePTB and term births, we used gestational age-standardized residuals as outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression procedures were used to estimate odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for ePTB.
RESULTS: Higher HCNC in later pregnancy was associated with lower odds of ePTB, corresponding to 20% (OR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.63-0.99) lower odds of ePTB per-one standard deviation increase in gestational-age standardized HCNC. In contrast, higher HCC in earlier pregnancy was associated with higher odds of ePTB (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.29-1.94).
CONCLUSIONS: Hair glucocorticoids may reflect HPA axis dysregulation during pregnancy, but imprecise temporal resolution and wash-out effects warrant further study of their predictive value for ePTB.

articles.title: Precision medicine in acute lymphoblastic leukemia: A narrative review of current strategies and future directions.
articles.abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a genetically heterogeneous hematologic malignancy and the most common cancer in children, with significant morbidity and mortality in adults. Advances in molecular diagnostics and targeted therapies have shifted treatment from uniform chemotherapy toward precision medicine approaches tailored to individual genomic and clinical profiles. To summarize these approaches, a narrative review was conducted following the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2015 and August 2026. Additional sources, including reference lists and clinical trial registries, were screened. Studies were selected based on relevance to precision medicine in ALL, including molecular diagnostics, pharmacogenomics, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Evidence was synthesized narratively without formal quality scoring. Key findings indicate that advances in next-generation sequencing have enabled the identification of clinically relevant molecular subtypes, including BCR-ABL1-positive, Philadelphia chromosome-like, and KMT2A-rearranged ALL, facilitating risk stratification and targeted treatment selection. Pharmacogenomic testing, particularly for TPMT and NUDT15 variants, supports individualized thiopurine dosing and reduces treatment-related toxicity. Targeted therapies and immunotherapies, including tyrosine kinase inhibitors, blinatumomab, inotuzumab ozogamicin, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and menin inhibition with revumenib for selected relapsed or refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemias, have significantly improved outcomes in relapsed and refractory ALL. However, variability in access to molecular diagnostics, lack of standardized biomarker panels, and limited long-term outcomes data remain key challenges. Overall, Precision medicine is transforming the management of ALL by enabling individualized, biomarker-driven treatment strategies that improve survival and reduce toxicity. Broader implementation will require standardized diagnostic approaches, improved access to advanced therapies, and integration of real-world evidence to support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Vascular maturation determines the susceptibility of retinal blood vessels to pharmacological depletion of pericytes in rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pericyte loss is a key pathological feature of diabetic retinopathy. However, the characteristics of vascular regions prone to functional and structural alterations following pericyte loss remain unclear. In neonatal rats, imatinib induces retinal pericyte depletion and subsequent vascular abnormalities. Using this model, we examined how vascular maturation affects vascular abnormalities following pericyte depletion.
METHODS: The rats were divided into five postnatal day (P) groups: P4, P7, P10, P13, and P21. (1) Acute effects of imatinib on pericytes and endothelial cells were assessed 6 and 12 h after treatment in P4 rats. (2) Pericyte depletion was evaluated 1 day after imatinib administration (100 or 300 mg/kg). (3) Retinal vascular alterations following imatinib treatment on P13 and P14 (P13/14) were examined. (4) Developmental changes in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) dependence of the retinal vasculature were assessed using the VEGF receptor inhibitor KRN633 in P4, P10, and P13 groups.
RESULTS: Imatinib increased cleaved caspase-3 immunoreactivity in pericytes, but not endothelial cells, and reduced pericyte coverage within 6 h after treatment. Pericyte coverage in superficial retinal vessels was significantly reduced in all groups except P21, with decreasing severity with age. Imatinib treatment on P13/14 reduced pericyte coverage in both the superficial and deep vascular layers, particularly at the vascular front and in the deep layer. Capillary dilation and dextran leakage were preferentially occurred in regions lacking pericyte coverage. KRN633-induced capillary degeneration decreased with vascular maturation.
CONCLUSION: Immature, VEGF-dependent blood vessels are more likely to develop morphological alterations in response to pericyte depletion.

articles.title: Identifying MRI-Defined Optic Pathway Glioma in NF1 Using Macular OCT and Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether macular optical coherence tomography (OCT) distinguishes eyes with versus without recorded magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined eye-level optic pathway glioma (OPG) status in neurofibromatosis type 1, and whether longitudinal OCT, visual/clinical variables, optic-nerve, or single-feature OCT add value.
METHODS: One study eye was selected per participant independently of OPG status. The retrospective cohort included 182 participants (58 OPG-positive and 124 OPG-negative eyes). Six primary feature sets compared baseline and longitudinal macular OCT, with and without clinical/visual variables, plus clinical/visual variables alone and visual acuity (VA) alone. Paired macular versus optic-nerve analyses used 141 participants with at least two paired examination dates.
RESULTS: Baseline macular OCT achieved pooled out-of-fold area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) 0.819 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) 0.870, versus 0.551 and 0.667 for VA alone. Longitudinal summaries and added clinical/visual variables provided no clear gain. Baseline macular and optic-nerve OCT showed similar discrimination in the paired cohort (PR-AUC 0.787 vs. 0.802). Macular ganglion cell complex (GCL++) alone achieved PR-AUC 0.819 and ROC-AUC 0.844. Of 58 OPG-positive eyes, 31 (53.4%) had preserved baseline VA; among participants with preserved VA, baseline macular OCT retained discrimination (PR-AUC 0.701; ROC-AUC 0.831).
CONCLUSIONS: Macular OCT provided structural information beyond VA and showed similar discrimination to optic-nerve OCT. Longitudinal summaries offered no clear gain over baseline OCT, while GCL++ alone showed strong discrimination.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: Simple macular OCT measures may complement clinical assessment and MRI surveillance but require external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Inferring basic and complex emotions across the lifespan: The influence of face masks and autistic traits.
articles.abstract: Since Covid-19, wearing face masks has been more commonplace. Mixed findings exist regarding the impact of face masks on emotion recognition. This study investigated the recognition of basic and complex emotions from dynamic facial expressions portrayed with and without a face mask across the life-span whilst also examining the influence of autistic traits. 376 participants (112 children, aged 6-11, 74 males, 38 females; 101 adolescents, aged 12-15, 62 males, 34 females; 163 adults, aged 16-87, 44 males, 119 females) completed an online facial expression recognition task with newly created and validated stimuli of five basic and five complex emotions. Findings revealed that participants had lower recognition accuracy for masked compared to unmasked faces overall, [Formula: see text]  = .18. Children and adolescents with a higher number of autistic traits were generally less accurate in both conditions, r = -.22 and -.30 respectively. Moreover, higher levels of autistic traits were linked to lower accuracy for masked faces in children, [Formula: see text]  = .07, but not in adolescents, [Formula: see text]  = .02, or adults, [Formula: see text]  < .001. These findings highlight the challenges face masks pose to emotion recognition, particularly for children with higher levels of autistic traits.

articles.title: A reversible neonatal transverse aortic constriction model prolongs cardiomyocyte proliferative activity beyond the early postnatal regenerative window in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The neonatal mammalian heart retains transient regenerative capacity during the first postnatal week, but this ability rapidly declines thereafter. Whether transient mechanical stress can prolong postnatal cardiomyocyte proliferative competence remains unclear.
