PURPOSE: Severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) in children is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, requiring reliable tools for early assessment and prognosis. While the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is the standard neurological evaluation tool, it has limitations in pediatric patients. The Eppendorf-Cologne Scale (ECS), originally developed for adults, emphasizes pupil size, reactivity, and motor response and may offer advantages in children.
METHODS: This multicenter cohort study analyzed TraumaRegister DGU® data from 5,851 pediatric patients (mean age 9.6 years). Documentation included prehospital and in-hospital assessments, injury characteristics, and outcomes. ECS and GCS scores were evaluated based on first recorded prehospital values. Predictive performance for mortality and severe TBI was assessed using AUROC analysis.
RESULTS: Among the cohort, 2,582 patients (44.1%) had severe TBI and 476 (8.1%) died in hospital. GCS showed slightly higher accuracy for predicting severe TBI (AUROC 0.778, 95% CI 0.766-0.791) than ECS (AUROC 0.745, 95% CI 0.731-0.758). For mortality prediction, ECS performed marginally better (AUROC 0.943, 95% CI 0.929-0.957) than GCS (AUROC 0.910, 95% CI 0.896-0.924). Mortality rates were 90% in the worst ECS category and 55% in the worst GCS category.
CONCLUSION: GCS showed higher discrimination for severe TBI, whereas ECS showed higher discrimination for in-hospital mortality among patients with severe TBI. ECS may provide complementary prognostic information, but its clinical utility and role alongside GCS require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Teletherapy for Adolescent Mental Health: A Scoping Review of Comparative Effectiveness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Teletherapy has become an increasingly common delivery format for adolescent mental healthcare, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Given adolescents' distinct developmental characteristics, its effectiveness requires evaluation against in-person treatment and alternative remote formats. The objective was to map the randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence on teletherapy for adolescent mental health and to conduct a quantitative synthesis where the evidence permits.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidance, six databases were searched for RCTs published from 2014 onward that evaluated therapist-delivered remote psychotherapy for adolescents (13-18 years) with diagnosed mental health conditions, compared with face-to-face treatment, an alternative teletherapy format, or a waitlist or minimal-contact control. Quantitative synthesis was stratified by comparator type.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs across eight diagnostic categories were included. Six compared teletherapy with face-to-face treatment, six compared two remote formats, and six used only waitlist or minimal-contact controls. Among face-to-face comparisons, two obsessive-compulsive disorder trials met noninferiority margins, two anxiety trials nonsignificantly favored face-to-face treatment (g = -0.54 and -0.45), and single tic-disorder and insomnia trials found no clear difference. Teletherapy was superior to waitlist or minimal-contact control for anxiety (k = 6, g = 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.75-2.38) and depression (k = 5, g = 1.14, 95% CI: 0.64-1.64). Risk of bias was low in 3 of 18 trials.
CONCLUSIONS: Teletherapy improves adolescent anxiety and depression relative to waitlist or minimal-contact controls, although the size of the benefit is uncertain. Face-to-face comparisons are few, and their findings differ by condition, so equivalence to in-person care cannot yet be established. Condition-specific trials with face-to-face comparators are needed.

articles.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
articles.abstract: Regarding circadian typology, the existence of a fourth category, the bimodal types, was previously proposed. Bimodal types would be those answering some questions as morning types, while others as evening types, resulting in a different sleep-wake cycle compared to intermediate types. The aim of this study was to further explore the plausibility of this new circadian typology category, attempting to determine whether it qualifies as a genuinely new category of individuals or merely a byproduct of another individual difference, namely ideal sleep duration. To this end, we reanalyzed data previously collected from 1583 children and adolescents (817 females, mean age of 13.13 ± 1.96) and 2115 adults (1144 females, mean age of 44.50 ± 5.64) who completed the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents (MEQ-CA) and the MEQ, respectively. The open-ended questions on the ideal bedtime and get-up time were used to compute the ideal total sleep time that was later grouped into three categories: short- (≤6 hours), medium- (6 < x < 12 hours), and long sleepers (≥12 hours). In children and adolescents, bimodal types were overrepresented in both short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers; separately considering the gender variable, the same pattern of results was detected in males only. Regarding adults, an overrepresentation of bimodal types was observed among long sleepers and their underrepresentation among medium sleepers; this same distribution was replicated only in males. It seems that the suggested fourth category of circadian typology, that of bimodal types, may be considered as a byproduct of the individual difference in ideal sleep duration.

articles.title: Association of First Trimester Maternal Prognostic Nutritional Index and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet Score with Preterm Birth and Low Birth Weight: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 6780 Pregnant Women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the associations between first trimester maternal prognostic nutritional index (PNI) and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score with preterm birth and low birth weight.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 6780 pregnant women, with PNI and HALP calculated using laboratory indicators obtained in the first trimester. Baseline clinical data and perinatal outcomes were extracted from the electronic medical records. Group comparisons were conducted using the χ2 test and Mann-Whitney U-test. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify independent associated factors. Receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the predictive performance of PNI.
RESULTS: Of the 6780 pregnancies, 841 (12.4%) were preterm births and 922 (13.6%) were low birth weight infants. For low birth weight subgroup analyses, 137 cases with macrosomic infants (birth weight ≥4000 g) were excluded, yielding a sample of 6643 for this sub-analysis. Maternal PNI and HALP levels were significantly lower in fetuses with preterm birth and low birth weight than in term birth and normal birth weight fetuses (all p<0.001). Logistic regression analysis showed that lower PNI was independently associated with preterm birth (adjusted odds ratios (OR) = 0.873, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.854-0.893, p<0.001) and low birth weight (adjusted OR = 0.882, 95% CI: 0.863-0.902, p<0.001), whereas HALP was not statistically significant. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of PNI for predicting preterm birth and low birth weight were 0.622 (95% CI: 0.600-0.644) and 0.608 (95% CI: 0.586-0.629), indicating modest discriminatory ability, with optimal cut off values of 39.65 and 39.45, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Low PNI was an independent factor associated with preterm birth and low birth weight, while HALP showed no independent association. Given its modest AUC values, PNI may serve only as an economical auxiliary complementary biomarker, rather than a standalone predictive tool, for antenatal risk stratification of preterm birth and low birth weight.

articles.title: Associations of Vaping and Smoking Expectancies and Subsequent E-cigarette Ever-Use among United States Adolescents: A Two-Year Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: E-cigarettes continue to be the most common tobacco/nicotine product among United States adolescents. Understanding the predictive value of vaping and smoking expectancies can help prevent youth e-cigarette use.
METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study analyzed the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study 6.0 data to examine vaping and smoking expectancies (15-item scales ranging 1-5) for adolescents aged 12-13 years (baseline) who had never used an e-cigarette. A dual vaping-smoking expectancy variable (low vaping/low smoking, low vaping/high smoking, high vaping/low smoking, high vaping/high smoking) was created, and multivariable regressions tested the association between vaping, smoking, and dual expectancies and e-cigarette use susceptibility as well as ever-use by age 14-15 (two-year follow-up).
RESULTS: Among 1,990 participants at baseline, the mean (interquartile range) vaping and smoking expectancies were 2.3(1.8-2.8) and 1.7(1.2-2.0). Both vaping expectancy and smoking expectancy at baseline were associated with e-cigarette use susceptibility at baseline (AOR[95%CI]=3.8[2.8-5.1],p<.001; 3.1[2.2-4.2],p<.001; respectively) and subsequent ever-use at two-year follow-up (3.0[1.9-4.8, p<.001); 2.5[1.6-3.9], p<.001; respectively). Dual vaping/smoking expectancy showed a dose-response relationship with susceptibility to e-cigarette use (high/high, 8.3[5.4-12.9]p<.001; high/low, 3.9[2.3-6.8],p<.001; low/high, 2.9[1.8-4.6],p<.001 vs. low vaping/low smoking) and ever-use (6.4[2.4-17.1], p<.001; 6.1[2.0-18.7],p=0.002; 3.9[1.4-10.9], p=0.01; vs. low/low). Adolescents with high vaping and high smoking expectancies tended to be older, female, and report lower parental monitoring and school environment scores(p<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Vaping, smoking, and dual expectancies were associated with risk of e-cigarette use susceptibility and ever-use within two years. Identifying adolescents with high vaping and smoking expectancies offers a crucial opportunity to implement targeted interventions aimed at preventing youth vaping.

articles.title: Longitudinal trends in early childhood sleep and napping behaviors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although most children discontinue daytime napping by six years of age, longitudinal evidence describing how napping changes over time remains limited. We examined 6-month changes in nap duration, frequency, timing, spontaneity, and proportion of daytime sleep in preschool-aged children.
METHODS: At baseline, 702 parents representative of the Canadian population completed surveys about their children aged 1 to 6 years, inclusive. Six months later, 162 parents reported on their child's napping (duration, frequency, timing, spontaneity, and proportion of daytime sleep) and nighttime sleep (duration and sleep problems). Children were categorized at baseline into nap profiles-regular, intermittent, spontaneous, or non-nappers-and changes were examined overall and within profiles.
RESULTS: Among children napping at baseline, 25.2% had ceased napping at follow-up, whereas 11% of baseline non-nappers resumed napping. Among children napping at both time points, nap duration and proportion of daytime sleep significantly decreased over 6 months. The largest reductions in nap duration were observed among regular nappers. Nap timing and spontaneity remained relatively stable. Nighttime sleep duration did not significantly change; however, nighttime sleep problems decreased over time.
CONCLUSION: Preschool nap behaviors are dynamic and vary by nap profile. Regular nappers exhibited the most pronounced reductions, while some non-nappers resumed napping. These findings support flexible, developmentally sensitive definitions of nap cessation and highlight the importance of individualized approaches to supporting sleep during early childhood.
CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Most research on preschool napping has focused on single sleep measures and has provided limited longitudinal evidence on how multiple nap behaviors change over time. This study examined 6-month changes in several dimensions of napping among children classified into distinct nap behavior profiles.
STUDY IMPACT: Preschool nap behaviors changed differently across nap profiles, with regular nappers showing the largest reductions in daytime sleep and some non-nappers resuming napping. These findings suggest that nap cessation is a dynamic process and support flexible, individualized approaches to defining and managing daytime sleep in early childhood.

articles.title: Histologic Patterns That Hinder Detection of Cirrhosis on Routine Abdominal Imaging: Steatosis, Centrizonal Sinusoidal Fibrosis, and Biliary-type Cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT.—: Early detection of cirrhosis is essential for guiding management and prognostic surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma. Although elastography-based techniques are increasingly used, abdominal computed tomography (CT) remains the most routinely performed imaging modality in chronic liver disease surveillance.
OBJECTIVE.—: To evaluate concordance between routine abdominal CT and histology for detection of cirrhosis and investigate potential drivers of discordance.
DESIGN.—: Surgical liver pathology specimens (2018-2019) with corresponding abdominal CT within 90 days were included. Radiology and pathology reports were analyzed for the presence or absence of cirrhosis; discordant cases underwent double-blinded rereview by subspecialists. Pathology rereview assessed fibrosis stage, pattern, and quality (progressive versus regressive; Beijing classification), as well as with secondary histologic findings.
RESULTS.—: Initial concordance for cirrhosis/no cirrhosis was 88.7% (754 of 850). Rereview improved concordance to 95.8% (786 of 820), with 3 "Rad-overcalls" and 17 "Rad-undercalls" corrected by radiology. Persistent "Rad-overcalls" (n = 17) were explained by reclassified pathology (n = 12; 70.5%) or centrizonal sinusoidal fibrosis (n = 4; 23.5%). Among 29 persistent "Rad-undercalls," underlying etiologies included steatotic liver disease (n = 7; 24.2%), biliary atresia (n = 4; 13.7%), active hepatitis (n = 3; 10.3%), primary sclerosing cholangitis (n = 2; 7%), and primary biliary cholangitis (n = 1; 3.5%). All discordant pediatric cases (n = 4) had biliary cirrhosis unrecognized on CT. Discordance was significantly higher in biliary cirrhosis from biliary atresia (100%) versus primary sclerosing cholangitis or primary biliary cholangitis (12.5% each; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS.—: Routine abdominal CT demonstrates high concordance with histology for detection of cirrhosis. Discordance arises mainly from centrizonal sinusoidal fibrosis, biliary atresia, and steatotic liver disease, underscoring limitations of CT in these settings.

articles.title: National survey of the clinical profile and management of patients with hereditary angioedema due to C1-inhibitor deficiency in Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare, often misdiagnosed disorder. Epidemiological data on this condition are scarce in Latin America, particularly in Colombia. This study aimed to describe the demographics, clinical features, and treatment of Colombian HAE patients in order to address data gaps.
METHODS: A web-based survey (Sept, 2021-Mar, 2023) of Colombian physicians managing HAE patients collected anonymous data on demographics, clinical features, and treatments. Statistical analyses compared patients receiving long-term prophylaxis (LTP) versus those who did not.
RESULTS: The survey included 42 physicians from 19 Colombian provinces, covering 274 HAE patients. Median age at symptom onset was 13 years, with a diagnostic delay of 8 years. Most patients were female (59.85%) and had a family history of HAE (83.58%). Attacks mainly affected peripheral, abdominal, and facial areas; common triggers included stress, trauma, and menstruation. Hospitalization was reported by 46.24% of patients, with 23.77% hospitalized in the preceding year and 4.96% requiring intubation. All received on-demand therapy, mainly icatibant (91.41%). Long-term prophylaxis was prescribed in 52.14% of cases, with danazol (66.67%), tranexamic acid (31.21%), and lanadelumab (17.02%). These patients had longer diagnostic delays and higher hospitalization rates compared to those not receiving prophylaxis (p < 0.01 and p = 0.01, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: This study shows significant diagnostic delays and treatment challenges for HAE in Colombia. Underreporting and geographic disparities suggest an underestimated prevalence. The findings underscore the urgent need for greater awareness, equitable access to therapies, and robust patient registries in order to address unmet needs and reduce the burden of HAE for affected individuals.

articles.title: Goat milk infant formula and gut health: from traditional nutrition to scientific innovation.
articles.abstract: When breastfeeding is not possible, goat milk-based infant formula (GMF) provides an alternative to cow's milk-based formula. This narrative review evaluates clinical, observational, and mechanistic evidence on the nutritional suitability of GMF and its potential relevance to infant gut health. Randomized trials and meta-analytic evidence support the safety and nutritional adequacy of GMF. Its distinct composition, including a higher β-casein-to-αs1-casein ratio and differences in the profile and concentrations of oligosaccharides and bioactive proteins compared with cow's milk, provides biological plausibility for differences in curd formation, protein digestion kinetics, and microbial fermentation. However, these mechanistic findings do not establish clinical benefit. Controlled evidence does not currently demonstrate that GMF prevents or treats feeding-related gastrointestinal symptoms, including infant colic and functional constipation, although observational studies suggest possible symptom differences in some infants. Well-designed randomized trials in symptomatic infants are needed to evaluate gastrointestinal outcomes, microbiota development, immune effects, and the potential value of emerging formula innovations. Future GMF development may combine the goat milk matrix with recombinant human milk proteins or microbiome-targeted ingredients to complement components that are absent, present at low concentrations, or altered during processing; however, their application and clinical benefits in GMF remain to be established.

articles.title: Overweight, obesity, and sex differences in the acquisition of aquatic motor competence among 4-5-year-old preschool children: a quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood overweight and obesity are associated with impaired motor competence, yet evidence on how weight status relates to structured aquatic motor skill learning in preschoolers-and whether sex moderates this relationship-remains scarce. This study compared changes in aquatic motor competence between overweight/obese and healthy-weight 4-5-year-old preschoolers following a common 8-week structured aquatic programme, and examined sex differences.
METHODS: Sixty 4-5-year-old children (30 overweight/obese, 30 healthy-weight; 15 boys and 15 girls per group) without prior systematic aquatic exposure were recruited from two kindergartens in Taiyuan, China. Weight status was classified using the Chinese Growth Standard for Children Under 7 Years (WS/T 423-2022) and WHO criteria. All children completed a 16-session, 8-week structured aquatic motor skill programme (45 min/session, 2 sessions/week, 1:5 instructor-to-child ratio). Aquatic motor competence was assessed pre- and post-intervention using the Actual Aquatic Skills Test (AAST; 17 items, range 17-51). The primary analysis examined differential change over time using a 2 (Group) × 2 (Sex) × 2 (Time) mixed-design ANOVA; estimated mean differences are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and effect sizes as Cohen's d and partial η 2. A 2 × 2 factorial ANOVA on post-intervention scores was retained as a secondary analysis.
RESULTS: Pre-intervention AAST scores did not differ between weight-status groups (t = -0.76, p = 0.448) or between boys and girls (t = -0.94, p = 0.353). The Group×Time interaction was significant (F(1,58) = 31.88, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.355): healthy-weight children showed greater mean improvement than overweight/obese children (mean Δ 27.50 vs. 23.40 points; mean difference 4.10, 95% CI 2.65-5.55; Cohen's d = 1.46, 95% CI 0.89-2.03). The Sex×Time interaction was also significant (F(1,58) = 5.15, p = 0.027, partial η 2 = 0.082): girls showed greater mean improvement than boys (mean Δ 26.43 vs. 24.47; mean difference 1.96, 95% CI 0.23-3.70; Cohen's d = 0.59, 95% CI 0.07-1.11). The Group×Sex interaction on post-intervention scores was not significant (F(1,56) = 0.22, p = 0.645, partial η 2 = 0.004; interaction contrast on change scores 0.34 points, 95% CI -1.10 to 1.78).
CONCLUSION: In this convenience sample of Chinese preschoolers, healthy-weight children and girls showed greater mean improvement in aquatic motor competence than overweight/obese children and boys, respectively, following a common structured aquatic programme. Because the design lacked a non-intervention control group, these findings are associative and do not establish that weight status caused the differential response. Longer and more individualised aquatic curricula, potentially combined with nutritional and psychological support, warrant prospective evaluation in randomised trials for overweight/obese preschoolers.

articles.title: Construction of a nomogram prediction model for symptom residue after tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in children with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome based on lasso-logistic regression analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify the factors associated with residual symptoms after adenotonsillectomy in children with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) using LASSO-logistic regression, and to construct a nomogram prediction model.
METHODS: A total of 324 children with OSAHS treated at our hospital from January 2023 to March 2024 were enrolled and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 227) and an internal validation cohort (n = 97) at a ratio of 7:3. According to the 1-year follow-up results, the training cohort was further divided into a recovery group and a residual symptom group. In addition, 175 children with OSAHS treated at our hospital from April 2024 to January 2025 were included as an external validation cohort. LASSO-logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative residual symptoms. A nomogram model was then established and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Compared with the recovery group, children in the residual symptom group were younger and had higher proportions of males, BMI > the 95th percentile, family history of OSAHS, asthma, rhinitis, >8 spontaneous awakenings per hour before surgery, AHI > 18 events/h before surgery, as well as higher preoperative mYPAS scores and postoperative Wong-Baker scores (all P < 0.05). LASSO-logistic regression identified sex, BMI, asthma, rhinitis, number of spontaneous awakenings before surgery, and preoperative AHI as independent predictors (all P < 0.05). The AUC values of the nomogram in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts were 0.874, 0.851, and 0.850, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: The nomogram showed good predictive performance and may help assess the risk of residual symptoms after adenotonsillectomy in children with OSAHS.

articles.title: When kidneys fail again: management of kidney allograft failure in children.
articles.abstract: Many children who receive a kidney transplant will require more than one transplant during their lifetime. When the first graft fails, decisions made during this transition may affect not only the return to kidney replacement therapy but also the chances of receiving a subsequent transplant. In particular, withdrawal of immunosuppression, development of HLA sensitization, graft intolerance, and the decision to remove or retain the failed allograft require careful consideration. In this Mini Review, we examine the epidemiology and causes of kidney allograft failure in children and discuss the practical challenges that follow graft failure. Evidence specific to children is scarce, especially regarding how and when immunosuppression should be withdrawn. Current data favor early preparation for retransplantation and avoidance of unnecessary sensitization. An asymptomatic failed allograft can generally remain in situ, whereas nephrectomy is reserved for specific indications. Despite greater sensitization after a first transplant, second kidney transplants in children can achieve good graft survival. Prospective pediatric studies are needed to determine how immunosuppression and the failed allograft should best be managed while preserving access to retransplantation.

articles.title: Could excessive infant mattress firmness contribute to positional plagiocephaly in Japan? An international comparison and hypothesis paper.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: International infant sleep-surface standards primarily address the prevention of overly soft sleep surfaces using pass/fail test methods rather than specifying a directly comparable consumer firmness value in Newtons. No international standard establishes an upper firmness limit for infant mattresses. Japan has no infant-specific national mattress firmness standard.
OBJECTIVE: To document the firmness (Newton value, N) of Japanese commercially available infant mattresses, compare these values against international regulatory frameworks and selected manufacturer recommendations, and propose a biomechanical hypothesis suggesting that excessive mattress firmness may contribute to the apparently higher prevalence of positional plagiocephaly (PP) reported in Japanese cohorts.
METHODS: Firmness values (N; JIS K6400-2 Method A, 40% compression) were collected from publicly available manufacturer or retailer specifications for ten Japanese infant mattress products satisfying pre-defined inclusion criteria (the primary analysis dataset). Two additional products, identified outside the original search during revision, are reported as a sensitivity check only. International reference values were obtained from regulatory documents, selected European manufacturer guidance, and product documentation. PP prevalence data were extracted from peer-reviewed literature; cross-national comparisons are presented as illustrative only.
RESULTS: Japanese infant mattress firmness ranged from 160 to 285 N (median 183 N, ten-product primary analysis). No direct numerical comparison with European density-based manufacturer recommendations is made, as no validated conversion between density (kg/m3) and ILD firmness (N) exists. Five products had firmness at or below 176 N; four products exceeded 190 N. Of the ten products, six fell within the Korean reference-test-mattress specification range (170 ± 20 N = 150-190 N), indicating that the Japanese market does not consist uniformly of extreme outliers. This preliminary survey is restricted to ten products identified through publicly accessible manufacturer or retailer specifications; independent laboratory verification was not performed.
SAFETY STATEMENT: Existing evidence strongly supports firm sleep surfaces as a key measure for reducing sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) risk. The present hypothesis concerns only the upper end of the firmness spectrum-specifically, whether surfaces that are excessively firm may carry biomechanical consequences distinct from those of appropriately firm surfaces. This paper does not recommend using softer mattresses, adding comfort toppers, or using positioning pillows or positioners.
HYPOTHESIS: Excessive mattress firmness may reduce occipital contact surface area (increasing interfacial pressure: P = F/A) and may reduce small spontaneous head-position changes during sleep (a direction that remains to be tested), thereby increasing sustained focal pressure on the immature, malleable calvaria and potentially contributing to the apparently higher PP prevalence reported in Japan.
CONCLUSIONS: Japanese infant mattresses surveyed had a median firmness of 183 N. Among the regulatory frameworks reviewed, Japan lacks an infant-specific national mattress firmness standard, and no international standard establishes an upper firmness limit. Independent market-wide testing and prospective outcome studies are warranted to determine whether an infant-specific upper firmness range should be considered.

articles.title: Exploring and interpreting how nurses experience and attribute meaning during pediatric emergencies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Appropriate and adequate use of clinical tools is important for achieving positive outcomes in patients during emergencies. This can be achieved when tools are understood based on their mode of Being and spatial value to Dasein rather being understood by the characteristics and properties they possess. However, there is little empirical research on how nurses deal with and encounter these tools, their lived experience of these tools, and their meaning-making of these tools in pediatric emergency care.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore and interpret how nurses experience and make meaning of the "mode-of-Being" and use of clinical tools in emergency pediatric care within the context of their everyday clinical practice.
METHODS: A phenomenological design was adopted to explore tool use among pediatric emergency nurses in a hospital emergency ward. Qualitative data were collected through interviews and analyzed using Diekelman-Allan-Tanner's method.
FINDINGS: Team application of the A, B, C, D, E (airway, breathing, circulation, dehydration, and exposure to trauma) protocol optimizes pediatric emergency care; work fashion as an ecosystem; human, institutional, and financial constraints; and three team-pillar approaches to professional development.
PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: This study will benefit children undergoing emergency treatment and enhance both experiential and theoretical knowledge of tools by nurses, thereby resulting in effective and efficient use of tools and higher-quality care outcomes.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: integrating clinician-performed evidence and nurse-led implementation.
articles.abstract: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), for which early identification, accurate assessment, and dynamic monitoring are critical for improving outcomes. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has emerged as a non-invasive, reproducible, and portable imaging modality with unique advantages for NEC assessment. However, direct evidence on nurse-led POCUS specifically in NEC remains scarce; most published ultrasound studies have been conducted by radiologists, sonographers, or neonatologists. This review synthesizes evidence from two sources: (1) clinician-performed POCUS technical evidence in NEC, including the detection of pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, and hemodynamic alterations; and (2) nurse-led implementation evidence derived from POCUS programs in other neonatal or critical care settings, including screening workflows, documentation standards, and training requirements. We discuss the current evidence base, highlight the gap between clinician-performed technical evidence and nurse-led implementation, and propose a framework for integrating POCUS into NICU nursing practice. By critically synthesizing the available evidence, this review aims to provide practical guidance for future nurse-led POCUS programs in NEC and to outline priority areas for prospective research.

articles.title: Knowledge-to-practice gaps in early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder: a cross-sectional study of Palestinian paediatricians.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is essential for timely intervention and improved developmental outcomes. This study assessed pediatricians' knowledge, attitudes, practices (KAP), and perceived barriers regarding early ASD identification in Palestine.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 123 pediatricians practicing in hospitals, primary healthcare centers, and private clinics across the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire comprising demographic characteristics, the validated Knowledge about Childhood Autism among Health Workers (KCAHW) scale, and sections assessing attitudes, clinical practices, and perceived barriers related to early ASD diagnosis. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Participants showed strong overall ASD knowledge (mean KCAHW score: 14.69 ± 2.50/19), scoring highest in social/communication domains but lower in etiology, comorbidities, and onset age. Attitudes were overwhelmingly positive, with 98.4% valuing provider awareness and 95.9% supporting multidisciplinary assessments. Clinically, 93.5% routine-referred suspected cases and 91.1% counseled families, but only 32.5% routinely used standardized screening tools (e.g., M-CHAT). Key barriers included high perceived lack of parental awareness (88.6%), absence of standardized diagnostic protocols (72.4%), social stigma (61.8%), and insufficient ASD-specific training (59.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Palestinian physicians exhibit good foundational knowledge and positive attitudes toward early ASD detection. However, low standardized screening rates, training gaps, and systemic and sociocultural barriers delay timely diagnosis. Enhancing professional training, implementing standardized screening pathways, and improving community awareness are vital to accelerate early intervention.

articles.title: Parental experiences of transition from tertiary neonatal care to a regional special care nursery in an Australian setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm infants from regional areas may require transfer to tertiary neonatal intensive care, followed by back-transfer to regional services after clinical stabilisation. Despite this common practice, there is limited research examining parental perceptions of care across tertiary and regional special care nurseries (SCNs), particularly within the Australian context. Understanding these experiences is essential to inform service improvements at a regional level.
AIM: This study aimed to explore parental perceptions of the transition from tertiary neonatal care to a regional SCNs.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study design was undertaken in Mackay, Queensland. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 parents of preterm infants who were back-transferred from tertiary to the regional SCN. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic methodology to identify key patterns and subthemes.
RESULTS: Five overarching themes were identified: experiencing acute emotional impact, adapting to transition of care, forming new social supports, managing finances, and bridging the care gap. Back-transfer brought relief but could also generate anxiety as parents adjusted to regional care.
CONCLUSION: Back-transfer from tertiary to regional neonatal care can be accompanied by parental anxiety despite the benefits of returning closer to home. Greater preparation, communication and continuity-of-care strategies may support families during this transition.

articles.title: Language outcomes in preschool children with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate language outcomes in preschool children with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) treated with therapeutic hypothermia and without major neurodevelopmental disabilities, and to identify early developmental and neonatal factors associated with language disorder at preschool age (LD).
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included children with moderate-to-severe HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia at a tertiary neonatal center and followed through preschool age. Children with cerebral palsy, intellectual disability (IQ <70), autism spectrum disorder, major genetic disorders, severe global developmental impairment, or other neurological conditions precluding reliable formal language assessment were excluded. Early developmental functioning was evaluated using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales at 24 months. Language skills were assessed between 30 and 76 months of age using standardized age-appropriate Italian instruments, and LD was identified on the basis of standardized assessment combined with clinical evaluation. Neonatal variables included cord blood pH, base excess, cerebral function monitoring, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
RESULTS: Seventy-five children completed language assessment. Nineteen children (25.3%) met criteria for LD. Difficulties were more frequent in expressive language domains, with naming deficits observed in 62.7% and articulation/repetition difficulties in 61.3% of participants. Children who subsequently developed LD had significantly lower Griffiths Hearing and Speech (Scale C) scores at 24 months compared with children without LD [median 75 [IQR 67-80] vs. 88 [81-95], p < 0.001]. In logistic regression, each 10-point decrease in Griffiths Scale C was associated with higher odds of later LD (unadjusted OR 3.85, 95% CI 1.84-8.06; p < 0.001; adjusted OR 3.78, 95% CI 1.78-8.02; p < 0.001). Severe neonatal acidosis was associated with poorer comprehension and articulation/repetition outcomes, whereas combined white and gray matter injury was associated mainly with poorer expressive language performance.
DISCUSSION: Language difficulties are common among preschool survivors of neonatal HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia, even in the absence of major neurological disabilities. Early language vulnerabilities are detectable at 24 months and may help identify children at increased risk of later LD, supporting the need for structured language surveillance within long-term follow-up programs.

articles.title: Sleep quality and physical fitness among Chinese adolescents: a multilevel cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep quality is an important component of adolescent health, but its association with physical fitness remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the association between sleep quality and physical fitness among Chinese adolescents.
METHODS: This school-based cross-sectional study included 5,018 adolescents from 18 schools in six Chinese cities. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The Physical Fitness Index (PFI) was the primary outcome, and estimated VO₂max was the secondary outcome. School-level random-intercept models adjusted for age, sex, school stage, BMI, socioeconomic status, and screen time. Sensitivity analyses examined school-clustered standard errors and exploratory models incorporating random intercepts for school and class within school.
RESULTS: Higher PSQI scores were associated with modestly lower PFI in the fully adjusted school-only model (β = -0.049, 95% CI: -0.079 to -0.019, P = 0.002). The PFI association remained significant with school-clustered standard errors (95% CI: -0.086 to -0.012, P = 0.013) and in the exploratory school-and-class model (β = -0.040, 95% CI: -0.068 to -0.012, P = 0.005). For estimated VO₂max, the association was non-significant in the fully adjusted school-only model (β = -0.036, 95% CI: -0.082-0.010, P = 0.125), but significant in the exploratory school-and-class model (β = -0.049, 95% CI: -0.092 to -0.005, P = 0.030), indicating sensitivity to the clustering specification.
CONCLUSIONS: Poorer sleep quality was modestly associated with lower PFI among Chinese adolescents. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and evaluate potential implications for health monitoring and fitness promotion.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, treatment modalities, and mortality in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs), but data from Turkey and comparable middle-income settings are limited. We aimed to describe the etiology, management and outcomes of children with PARDS in a tertiary PICU and to explore factors associated with PICU mortality, with particular attention to in-hospital complications.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, all 1,350 children admitted to a 20-bed tertiary PICU in Ankara, Turkey, between August 2019 and September 2021 were screened, and 38 children with PARDS defined by the PALICC-2015 criteria were included. The primary outcome was PICU mortality. Survivors and non-survivors were compared using non-parametric tests, and an exploratory multivariable logistic regression model, limited to three variables because of the small number of deaths, was fitted.
RESULTS: The median age was 30.5 months (IQR 6.8-79.8), and infectious pneumonia was the leading cause (29/38, 76.3%). Thirty-one children (81.6%) required invasive mechanical ventilation and were classified as having mild (n = 5), moderate (n = 9) or severe (n = 17) PARDS; seven were managed with non-invasive ventilation alone and could not be classified by severity. PICU mortality was 39.5% (15/38): 0/5 in mild, 2/9 in moderate and 13/17 in severe PARDS (p = 0.001). At least one selected in-hospital complication (pulmonary hemorrhage, air leak or hospital-acquired infection) occurred in 20 children, 13 of whom died. Pulmonary hemorrhage (11/11 died; p < 0.001) and air leak syndromes (9/12 died; p = 0.004) were associated with mortality, whereas hospital-acquired infections were not (p = 0.544). In the exploratory multivariable model, the composite of selected in-hospital complications was associated with mortality after adjustment for sex and prone positioning (adjusted OR 8.62, 95% CI 1.29-57.68; p = 0.026).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, PICU mortality was high and concentrated among children with severe PARDS. Pulmonary hemorrhage and air leak syndromes were frequent among non-survivors. Because complication timing was not available and the sample was small, these findings should be regarded as associations reflecting disease severity in our setting rather than as independent predictors of mortality.

articles.title: Solar-powered phototherapy for severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia in low-resource settings: a multicentre implementation study in Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progress in neonatal care in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains constrained by inequitable access to effective interventions, particularly in remote settings where unreliable electricity, limited specialist availability, and household poverty restrict treatment. Severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (SNH) exemplifies this challenge. We evaluated whether a fully solar-powered total-body phototherapy system could maintain effective treatment while progressively decentralising care from specialist tertiary practice to resource-poor grassroots facilities.
METHODS: A multicentre staged implementation study was conducted in Nigeria between February 2024 and January 2026. Implementation progressed through three phases: specialist-controlled deployment at a tertiary neonatal centre; corroborative deployment across additional tertiary centres in different geographic and climatic settings; and task-shifted implementation in grassroots hospitals. The PoliteUltraLumen system combines photovoltaic power generation, battery storage, and dual-surface total-body phototherapy. Grassroots implementation incorporated supplementary phototherapy devices, simplified operating procedures, community bilirubin screening, and treatment delivered predominantly by junior clinicians, nurses, and health assistants. Outcomes included bilirubin reduction to predefined treatment thresholds, treatment duration, safety, operational continuity, and feasibility of decentralised delivery.
RESULTS: More than 2,000 neonates underwent community bilirubin surveillance and 663 received phototherapy across the three implementation phases. All treated neonates achieved the predefined bilirubin treatment endpoints and were successfully discharged. Among cases with comprehensive treatment data, mean treatment duration was 16.5 ± 3.4 h. No treatment interruption due to power failure occurred. No treated neonate was reported to require subsequent exchange blood transfusion, and no device-related serious adverse event or treatment-related mortality was identified. Treatment remained feasible under task-shifted grassroots implementation.
CONCLUSION: Fully solar-powered phototherapy was successfully translated from specialist-controlled tertiary care to decentralised grassroots neonatal services while maintaining treatment effectiveness and operational independence from grid electricity. These findings suggest that progress in LMIC neonatal care should encompass not only advances in clinical technology, but also the capacity to redesign and deliver effective interventions equitably where infrastructure, specialist personnel, and family resources are most constrained.

articles.title: Healthcare practitioners' perspectives on barriers to early identification of refeeding syndrome in hospitalised children with severe acute malnutrition: a qualitative descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reducing severe acute malnutrition in children is central to the Sustainable Development Goals, yet severe acute malnutrition remains a leading cause of childhood mortality in developing countries. Refeeding syndrome in children with severe acute malnutrition is a poorly understood, potentially fatal complication during stabilisation. Early detection is essential to prevent adverse outcomes. However, healthcare practitioners inconsistently recognise refeeding syndrome, particularly in resource-limited public hospitals, where severe acute malnutrition is common, but the condition itself remains understudied. The objective of this study was to explore healthcare practitioners' experiences of identifying refeeding syndrome among hospitalised children aged 6 to 59 months with severe acute malnutrition in public hospitals in the City of Tshwane, South Africa.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study design was employed. Using purposive sampling, 20 healthcare practitioners (paediatricians, medical doctors, nurses, and dieticians) from paediatric wards in public hospitals within the City of Tshwane were recruited. Semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and anonymised. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's approach, supported by NVivo 15 software. An inductive coding strategy allowed themes to emerge. Trustworthiness was established using Lincoln and Guba's criteria. Ethical approval was obtained from the University's ethics committee, and all participants provided written informed consent.
RESULTS: Fivethemes were developed:: (1) Awareness vs. practice: "known on paper," but under-recognised; (2) Reactive rather than proactive identification; (3) Managing RFS through standard SAM care; (4) Interprofessional collaboration is essential but fragile; and (5) Health system constraints undermine early identification. Participants emphasised the need for clearer clinical guidance and strengthened multidisciplinary collaboration.
CONCLUSION: Participants' accounts suggest that knowledge, organisational and resource constraints may hinder early identification of refeeding syndrome in children with severe acute malnutrition. The findings identify priorities for developing and evaluating context-sensitive guidance, multidisciplinary training and service support; the effectiveness of these strategies was not assessed.

articles.title: Nonlinear evolution of acoustic characteristics of bowel sounds in preterm infants.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gastrointestinal function can be assessed through bowel sounds, which objectively indicate gastrointestinal movement. However, the conventional method of abdominal auscultation has considerable limitations. This study aimed to investigate the evolutionary patterns of acoustic characteristics of bowel sounds in preterm infants, explore their variation with postmenstrual ages (PMAs), and quantify the association between PMA and bowel sound maturity to characterize the developmental trajectory of intestinal motility in preterm infants.
METHODS: Twenty-seven preterm infants (gestational age: 30-36 + 6 weeks) were enrolled in this study. A convolutional neural network-based smart device was used to monitor bowel sounds 1-4 times weekly for ≥3 h from day 1 to 30 after birth. Parameters, including bowel rate (number of bowel sounds per minute), frequency, and number of durations >2 s per min, were collected. Loess regression and derivative analysis were employed to characterize the dynamic progression of the bowel sound parameters relative to PMA, whereas Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis H tests were utilized to assess between-group differences.
RESULTS: A nonlinear dynamic change was observed in the relationship between characteristic parameters of bowel sounds in preterm infants and PMA. A significant transition occurred at 33.1 weeks of PMA. The PMA groups showed a significant difference in both between-group and multiple comparisons (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Bowel sound parameters demonstrated a nonlinear evolution with PMA, with an inflection point at 33.1 weeks that was synchronized with the critical maturation period of the enteric nervous system/interstitial cells of Cajal network. These parameters may serve as objective markers for assessing the dynamic maturation of the gastrointestinal system in preterm infants.

articles.title: Effects of family-integrated care on weight gain, breastfeeding, hospital stay, and infection in NICU preterm infants: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of family-integrated care (FICare) on hospital stay, weight gain rate, breastfeeding rate, and nosocomial infection rate in premature infants in the NICU, given that existing individual studies have yielded inconsistent conclusions and no comprehensive meta-analysis has yet synthesized this evidence.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials and eligible non-randomized comparative studies on FICare for premature infants were searched from PubMed, Medline, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE. Two researchers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias-2 tool for randomized controlled trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for non-randomized studies. Meta-analysis used mean difference (MD) or standardized MD for continuous outcomes and odds ratio (OR) for dichotomous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using I2; sensitivity analysis examined whether effect directions were driven by single studies. Publication bias was not formally assessed due to the limited number of studies per outcome.
RESULTS: Six studies involving a total of 4,138 premature infants were included, with 2,010 infants in the FICare group and 2,128 infants in the conventional care group. Compared with conventional care, FICare significantly increased weight gain rate (pooled MD = 4.35, 95% CI [2.00, 6.69], P < 0.05; I2 = 98.55%; unit: g/day), and improved breastfeeding rate (pooled OR = 3.06, 95% CI [1.58, 5.99], P = 0.01; I2 = 91.82%). No significant differences were found in length of hospital stay (pooled MD = -3.63, 95% CI [-7.80, 0.54], P = 0.09; I2 = 99.79%; unit: days) or nosocomial infection rate (pooled OR = 0.90, 95% CI [0.68, 1.17], P = 0.41; I2 = 27.33%). Subgroup analysis showed that in Chinese studies, FICare significantly shortened hospital stay (pooled MD = -6.93, 95% CI [-7.22, -6.65], P < 0.05), but not in international multicenter studies. Weight gain rate improved in both severe and stable condition subgroups. Sensitivity analysis showed consistent direction of effects across all outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that FICare may be associated with improved weight gain and exclusive breastfeeding rates in NICU premature infants, but shows no significant effect on hospital stay duration or nosocomial infection rate. The findings are promising but should be interpreted with caution due to high heterogeneity and the limited number of included studies.

articles.title: The rising burden of chronic gastrointestinal diseases: the role of Mediterranean diet.
articles.abstract: Chronic gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic diseases represent a growing global healthcare burden, heavily influenced by environmental factors and the exposome. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic and preventative role of the Mediterranean diet (MD) as a potent non-pharmacological intervention in modulating gut health. A literature analysis was conducted focusing on the mechanisms of the MD-rich in polyphenols, monounsaturated fatty acids, and dietary fiber-and its clinical impact on pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), gluten-related disorders, functional GI disorders, and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD). The MD acts as a critical modulator of the gut microbiome, effectively reversing dysbiosis and promoting microbial diversity. Nutraceutical components of the diet significantly reduce systemic and localized inflammation by downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines. Furthermore, the MD reinforces the gut epithelial barrier and enhances mucosal immunity. Clinical data demonstrate that high MD adherence correlates with reduced disease activity in pediatric IBD, improved symptom management in functional GI disorders, and attenuated hepatic steatosis and metabolic syndrome markers in MASLD patients. The Mediterranean diet serves as a powerful, evidence-based strategy for mitigating chronic gastrointestinal and metabolic disorders. By directly targeting dysbiosis and inflammation, it offers an effective lifestyle-based modulation tool to alleviate the rising clinical burden of modern digestive pathologies.

articles.title: Recognizing pediatric post-intubation tracheal stenosis: lessons from delayed diagnosis and tissue-preserving endoscopic management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-intubation tracheal stenosis (PITS) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of endotracheal intubation in children. Because early symptoms often mimic common pediatric respiratory disorders, diagnosis may be delayed until critical airway obstruction develops. We aimed to characterize the diagnostic course, clinical presentation, and outcomes of pediatric PITS treated using a minimally invasive, tissue-preserving endoscopic strategy.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all children with endoscopically confirmed PITS treated at a tertiary pediatric airway center between 2019 and 2026. Clinical presentation, timing of diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Eight infants were included in this cohort, all of whom had subglottic PITS. Median age at intubation was 4.5 months and median duration of initial mechanical ventilation was 3.5 days. Respiratory symptoms developed after a median of 4.5 days following extubation, whereas PITS was diagnosed only after a median of 65 days, indicating substantial diagnostic delay. Six patients presented with stridor and dyspnea, while two developed severe respiratory failure requiring emergency intubation without preceding stridor. Six patients had Myer-Cotton grade III and two grade II stenosis. Morphology-guided endoscopic treatment included balloon dilation (n = 4), mechanical dilation (n = 3), or membrane resection (n = 1), combined with temporary postoperative airway stabilization through invasive ventilation as well as local and systemic anti-inflammatory therapy. No patient developed restenosis or required tracheostomy or open airway reconstruction during long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Delayed recognition appears to be a major challenge in pediatric PITS. Early endoscopic airway evaluation should be considered in children with persistent respiratory symptoms after intubation, even after short-term ventilation or in the absence of stridor. Selected patients may be successfully managed using a minimally invasive, tissue-preserving endoscopic approach.

articles.title: Quantitation and clinical implications of lactadherin in human breast milk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lactadherin (also known as milk fat globule-EGF factor 8, MFG-E8) is a major bioactive component of the milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) in human milk and plays important roles in immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and host defense. However, data regarding lactadherin concentrations in human milk and the maternal factors influencing its levels remain limited. This study aimed to characterize lactadherin concentrations across different lactation stages, identify potential determinants of lactadherin variation, and explore its associations with infant health outcomes.
METHODS: A total of 91 Chinese mother-infant pairs were enrolled in this prospective cohort study. Maternal and infant demographic characteristics and clinical information were collected through medical records and structured questionnaires. Colostrum and mature milk samples were collected, and lactadherin concentrations were quantified using a modified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Infants were followed up to 6 months after birth through telephone interviews to record feeding patterns and the occurrence of common infantile diseases.
RESULTS: Lactadherin concentrations were significantly higher in colostrum than in mature milk (median: 112.79 μg/mL vs. 10.51 μg/mL, respectively; P < 0.0001), indicating a substantial decline in lactadherin levels during lactation. Maternal allergy history was identified as an independent factor associated with lactadherin concentrations. Specifically, maternal allergy history was associated with lower lactadherin concentrations in colostrum (β= -53.16, P = 0.039) but higher concentrations in mature milk (β = 7.38, P = 0.024). Furthermore, a significant interaction between maternal allergy history and lactation stage was observed (P = 0.0007), suggesting a stage-dependent association between maternal allergy history and lactadherin levels. No significant associations were observed between lactadherin concentrations in human milk and the incidence of infantile diseases during the follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: Lactadherin concentration in human milk varies substantially across lactation stages and is influenced by maternal allergy history. Further studies are needed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms governing lactadherin dynamics and to determine their implications for infant health and nutritional applications.

articles.title: Advances in fecal biomarkers for necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a serious gastrointestinal disease in neonatal period. Early identification and early intervention are of great significance to improve the prognosis of children. At present, the diagnosis of NEC mainly depends on clinical manifestations, laboratory indicators and abdominal imaging examinations. However, the early symptoms lack specificity, and the blood test has certain trauma. The typical imaging signs suggest that the disease progresses to the middle and late stages, and there is a certain lag. In recent years, with the deepening of the research on the pathogenesis and detection technology of NEC, fecal markers have attracted attention because they may reflect pathological changes within the intestinal lumen and support early prediction, diagnosis, severity assessment, and prognostic evaluation of NEC. Existing studies have shown that fecal inflammatory proteins, barrier and mucosal injury-related indicators, intestinal flora and metabolic indicators can change during the development of NEC, which may support early prediction, diagnosis, severity assessment and prognostic prediction of NEC. Based on the main pathological processes of NEC, this review summarizes the research progress and current limitations of fecal biomarkers and discusses their potential clinical applications in NEC.

articles.title: The role of oxidative balance in the early diagnosis of oxidative stress-related diseases in infants born to mothers with preeclampsia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a major cause of preterm birth and is associated with increased oxidative stress. Alterations in oxidative-antioxidative balance may contribute to oxidative stress-related neonatal diseases in preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the oxidative and antioxidative status of preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia and investigate associations between oxidative stress biomarkers, particularly advanced oxidation protein products (AOPPs), and neonatal diseases.
METHODS: Thirty preterm infants (<37 weeks' gestation) requiring neonatal intensive care who were born to mothers with preeclampsia were enrolled in the preeclampsia group, and 30 gestational age-matched preterm infants born to normotensive mothers served as controls. Total oxidant status (TOS), total antioxidant status (TAS), 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), and AOPPs were measured in cord blood and serum samples collected on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7. Biomarker levels were compared between groups, and their associations with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) were evaluated.
RESULTS: RDS, NEC, and PDA were significantly more frequent in the preeclampsia group (all p < 0.05). AOPP levels were significantly higher in the preeclampsia group in cord blood and on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7 (all p < 0.001). TAS and 8-OHdG levels did not differ significantly between groups at any time point (p > 0.05). Cord blood TOS levels were significantly higher in the preeclampsia group (p = 0.005), whereas TOS levels on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7 did not differ significantly (p > 0.05). No significant associations were found between serial biomarker levels and RDS, BPD, NEC, ROP, IVH, or PDA (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: AOPPs may represent a potential biomarker of oxidative stress in preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia. Further prospective studies are needed to determine their role in the early diagnosis of oxidative stress-related neonatal diseases.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is one of the most common chronic respiratory complications in preterm infants. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential for individualizing preventive strategies and optimizing therapeutic decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have emerged as promising tools to improve predictive performance in this population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and synthesize the predictive performance of AI-based models for BPD development in preterm infants and to assess their methodological quality.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA recommendations. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library up to February 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-based models for predicting BPD in preterm infants born at <32 weeks of gestation and/or with a birth weight < 1,500 g were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in the analysis domain. Clinical applicability raised high concern in 38.9% of the studies due to a lack of external validation and heterogeneity in outcome definitions.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261466494, PROSPERO: CRD420261466494, registered retrospectively on August 4, 2026.

articles.title: Reference values for cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in preterm neonates.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this work is to establish reference values for cord blood N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in preterm neonates and to examine the associations between NT-proBNP concentrations and perinatal factors.
METHODS: Cord blood NT-proBNP levels were measured in 174 preterm infants born at 26-36 weeks of gestation. Infants were stratified by gestational age (GA), and reference intervals for cord blood NT-proBNP were calculated as the 5th-95th percentiles for each GA subgroup. Correlations between NT-proBNP concentrations and selected perinatal variables were also assessed.
RESULTS: The study revealed that NT-proBNP levels showed negative correlations with GA, birth weight (BW), and Apgar scores at 1 and 5 min, with correlation coefficients of -0.229, -0.278, -0.264, and -0.290, respectively, all statistically significant at P < 0.01. However, no significant associations were observed between NT-proBNP concentrations and infant gender, cord blood pH, premature rupture of membranes (PROM), mode of delivery, or early ejection fraction (EF).
CONCLUSION: Reference intervals for cord blood NT-proBNP in preterm infants should be stratified by GA, with levels decreasing as GA and BW increase. Neither vaginal delivery nor PROM was associated with elevated NT-proBNP levels, suggesting that these perinatal factors do not independently induce significant cardiovascular stress in the fetus.

articles.title: Maternal vitamin D concentrations during the second trimester and neurodevelopmental outcomes in preschool-aged children in the APrON cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy is a critical period for fetal brain development and is sensitive to maternal micronutrient status. Maternal vitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations have been associated with child neurodevelopmental outcomes, while biological aging processes reflected by epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) may contribute to these associations. This study examined associations between maternal vitamin D concentrations and neurodevelopmental outcomes in preschool-aged children and explored whether infant EAA mediated these associations.
METHODS: We included 252 mother-child pairs from the APrON cohort. Maternal second trimester plasma 25(OH)D3 concentrations were quantified, and children's cognitive, language, motor, and behavioural outcomes were assessed at 3-5-years. In a subsample of 130 children, buccal epithelial cells collected at 3 months were profiled using the Infinium HumanMethylation EPIC v1.0 BeadChip. EAA was estimated using the Pediatric-Buccal-Epigenetic clock. Adjusted linear regressions examined associations between maternal 25(OH)D3 and children's outcomes, including models using quartiles and a 30 ng/mL threshold. Mann-Whitney U-tests compared outcomes according to a 20 ng/mL sufficiency threshold. In the subsample, exploratory mediation analyses examined the potential mediating role of infant EAA.
RESULTS: No associations were found between maternal vitamin D and children's cognitive, language, or behavioural outcomes. Maternal vitamin D concentrations were positively associated with children's motor outcomes (B = 0.04; 95% CI = 0.004, 0.076, p = 0.03), although this small, nominal association did not survive correction for multiple comparisons (q = 0.18). This positive association was attenuated when vitamin D was modeled using quartiles or when "sufficiency" was defined as 30 ng/mL. No differences were found in neurodevelopmental outcomes based on vitamin D sufficiency defined as 20 ng/mL. No evidence of mediation via EAA was detected, although small indirect effects could have gone undetected due to the small sample size for this sub-analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides preliminary evidence that maternal vitamin D concentrations during pregnancy are associated with improved motor performance in children. A biomarker of biological aging, EAA, did not appear to play a role in this association. Examination of different forms of maternal vitamin D and statistical models that consider continuous measures and thresholds of "sufficiency" are needed to clarify associations between maternal vitamin D concentrations and children's neurodevelopment.

articles.title: Longitudinal perspective on the buffering effect of Tai Chi intervention against accumulated perceived stress and its sleep-improving effects among late adolescence.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: First-year university students stand at the close of WHO-defined adolescence (10-19 years), in mid-transition: leaving family, entering a new institution, and assuming adult academic and social roles. Stress during adolescence can have consequences that persist into adulthood. Most mental disorders begin by the mid-twenties, while higher levels of adolescent stress predict greater risks of adult anxiety and depression, academic dropout, and lower workforce participation and productivity. The 16-form simplified Tai Chi routine is easy to learn, but direct evidence of its effect in late adolescents is limited. This randomized controlled trial examined its effect on perceived stress and sleep quality.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: A total of 176 first-year undergraduates, all aged 18 years at baseline, at a university in Hangzhou, China, were randomly allocated 1:1 to a Tai Chi group (n = 88) or a no-intervention control group (n = 88). The Tai Chi group practiced the 16-form simplified routine three times weekly for 12 weeks (90 min per session: 30 min of warm-up and 60 min of guided practice); controls maintained their usual lifestyle. Perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale, PSS-14) and sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI) were assessed before and after the intervention. The primary outcomes (PSS-14 and PSQI global scores at week 12) were analyzed by baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance.
RESULTS: The groups had similar baseline characteristics. All 176 participants completed the PSS-14 and 168 had complete PSQI data. Within groups, both measures improved under Tai Chi (PSS-14 -3.28; PSQI -1.00; both P < 0.01), whereas perceived stress rose in controls (+4.47, P < 0.001) and sleep quality was unchanged. After baseline adjustment, PSS-14 scores were lower in the Tai Chi group (adjusted mean difference -7.48, 95% CI -8.80 to -6.17; P < 0.001), as were PSQI global scores (-1.17, 95% CI -1.87 to -0.46; P = 0.001). Exploratory component analyses gave nominal P < 0.05 for four PSQI components, none of which remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons.
CONCLUSION: Compared with no intervention, a 12-week 16-form Tai Chi program lowered perceived stress and improved sleep quality in late adolescents starting university, buffering the stress escalation of the academic semester, and merits multicenter testing against an active comparator.

articles.title: The impact of nesting care on the growth and neurological development of premature infants in neonatal intensive care units.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations of nesting care with growth, nighttime sleep-wake measures, and early neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study compared two noncontemporaneous cohorts at the Maternal and Child Health Hospital of Linping District, Hangzhou. Fifty preterm infants receiving nesting care from March 2024 to March 2025 and 50 receiving traditional care from February 2023 to February 2024 were manually selected from the eligible population to achieve approximate baseline comparability. Growth was assessed at birth and 3 months corrected age, sleep-wake activity by actigraphy at baseline and day 7, and neurodevelopment using the Gesell Developmental Schedules at 40 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) and 3 months corrected age. Longitudinal sleep and Gesell outcomes were analyzed using adjusted change-score regression models with HC3 robust standard errors and Holm correction.
RESULTS: At 3 months corrected age, the nesting-care group had higher body weight (difference, 195.12 g; 95% CI, 26.00-364.24), greater body length (2.04 cm; 95% CI, 0.68-3.40), and greater head circumference (median difference, 1.00 cm). From baseline to day 7, improvement in total sleep duration was greater in the nesting-care group (adjusted difference in change, 1.09 h; 95% CI, 0.36-1.81; Holm-adjusted P = 0.010), while mean awakening duration decreased more (-0.57 h; 95% CI, -0.70 to -0.45; P < 0.001). For neurodevelopment, adjusted improvements from 40 weeks PMA to 3 months corrected age were greater for fine motor (4.40 points), adaptive (3.95), language (2.18), and personal-social domains (1.60), whereas gross motor change was not statistically significant after adjustment (P = 0.054).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective comparison of noncontemporaneous cohorts, nesting care was associated with more favorable growth, nighttime actigraphy-derived sleep-wake measures, and several early neurodevelopmental outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because residual confounding and calendar-period effects cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of exome and chromosomal microarray analysis in cases of severe central nervous system structural anomalies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The central nervous system (CNS) is affected in 9% of fetal malformations but accounts for as much as one-third of all pregnancy terminations due to fetal anomaly. When applying chromosomal microarray (CMA) to the diagnosis of fetal CNS anomalies, the estimated diagnostic yield remains low. Recent study demonstrated that, in fetuses with major CNS anomalies, exome sequencing (ES) had an additional diagnostic yield of 44% over the 10% provided by CMA. We aimed to determine the cost effectiveness of the added value of ES in major CNS structural anomalies.
METHODS: We modeled costs, utility, and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) for CMA versus CMA + ES in prenatal testing. Two strategies were compared using the Markovian process decision analysis model: (1) CMA only, abnormal result culminating in termination of pregnancy (TOP); (2) ES after a negative CMA, where for positive result a TOP is conducted. The outcomes included health quality of life after TOP or having a disabled child, the costs of the CMA test, the ES test, and the health expenses of a disabled child. The time horizon of the model was 20 years. Sensitivity analysis including probabilistic sensitivity analysis of all parameters was conducted.
RESULTS: In the base-case model, the total expected cost per pregnancy was $US 91 059 for the CMA-alone strategy (driven largely by the expected long-term cost of raising a child with an undiagnosed disability) and $US 3101 for the CMA + ES strategy. The QALYs with a time horizon of 20 years were 11.84 and 13.84 for CMA and CMA + ES strategies, respectively, so CMA + ES dominated CMA alone (higher QALY value and cost saving). Sensitivity analysis revealed that the results were robust, and CMA + ES dominated the CMA with cost savings for all sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: We suggest that ES has the potential to be cost effective and should be considered as a first-tier test in the prenatal diagnosis of major CNS anomalies. The substantial increase in diagnostic yield offered by ES not only provides valuable information for the current pregnancy but also holds significant relevance for future pregnancies. These findings are pivotal in facilitating timely and evidence-based decision-making.

articles.title: Associations between cesarean delivery and adverse maternal and newborn outcomes by Robson Group: An analysis of the PRISMA study cohort in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Rising cesarean section (CS) rates in low- and middle-income countries may mask a triple burden of unmet need, overuse, and unsafe provision. Using the Robson ten-group classification, a global standard for monitoring institutional deliveries, we examined CS incidence and associations with adverse outcomes.
METHODS: Data were drawn from the Pregnancy Risk, Infant Surveillance, and Measurement Alliance Maternal and Newborn Health Study, an open cohort study in Kenya, Zambia, India, and Pakistan (2022-2025). We generated descriptive statistics for Robson groups and within-group relative risks of adverse events for CS versus vaginal delivery using multivariable adjusted log Poisson models.
RESULTS: Among 10 996 women, 29% delivered by CS. Group 5 (prior CS) and group 10 (preterm) were the largest contributors, accounting for 28% and 17% of all CS deliveries, respectively. Between-site differences in CS incidence were most pronounced for groups 2 and 4 (induced labor/pre-labor CS), ranging from 20% to 60% for nullipara and from 7% to 44% for multipara. Compared with vaginal delivery, CS was associated with an increased risk of maternal near miss, prolonged hospitalization, hemorrhage, and newborn intensive care unit admission. Stratified by Robson group, adverse outcome risk was concentrated among lower-obstetric-risk groups.
CONCLUSION: Repeat CS, preterm deliveries, labor induction, and pre-labor CS were drivers of CS. Although differences in risk magnitude associated with CS across Robson groups revealed important patterns for quality improvement, these estimates should not be interpreted as causal effects. Equipping facilities to manage labor induction, trials of labor after cesarean, and preterm deliveries is critical to improving quality of care.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding access to sexual and reproductive health and gender-based violence services in Brazil since the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: A multi-stakeholder qualitative analysis.
articles.abstract:
