OBJECTIVES: Understanding how disruptions to essential sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender based violence (GBV) services because of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-COV-2;COVID-19) pandemic were experienced across different population groups is critical to health system responses. The objective of this study was to explore how the pandemic influenced knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to access to SRH and GBV services in Brazil.
METHOD: A qualitative study was conducted in five healthcare facilities in Brazil between November 2022 and May 2023. Purposive sampling included pregnant and non-pregnant women, partners, and healthcare professionals. Pregnant women were interviewed at two time points. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using inductive thematic content analysis guided by Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory.
RESULTS: A total of 99 participants contributed to 120 interviews. Political-institutional mistrust, conflicting public messaging, and health system reorganization affected access to SRH and GBV services. Although healthcare professionals reported continuity of essential services, women described reduced availability of gynecological care and contraceptive services. Socioeconomic barriers, transportation difficulties, and poor coordination further limited access, particularly for vulnerable groups. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified GBV by increasing household stressors such as unemployment and alcohol abuse while weakening safety nets. Victim blaming and financial dependence hinder reporting. Over time, pregnant women's perceptions shifted from fear of COVID-19-related fetal outcomes to concerns about vaccination and newborn care.
CONCLUSION: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on SRH and GBV service access in Brazil was not solely due to service disruption but resulted from dynamic interactions across political, institutional, interpersonal, and temporal levels.

articles.title: The strategic integration of emergency obstetric and neonatal care with contraceptive services.
articles.abstract: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (CEmONC) indicators have strengthened health systems' capacity to manage acute obstetric emergencies and remain central to global maternal health monitoring. However, current EmONC frameworks omit contraception, despite its established role in preventing unintended pregnancy, supporting healthy interpregnancy intervals, and reducing recurrent exposure to obstetric risk. This gap reflects an artificial divide between emergency response and preventive care. This commentary argues that contraception should be recognized as an essential, integrated component of EmONC rather than a separate postpartum service. We outline the clinical rationale for embedding contraceptive counseling and provision within each EmONC signal function, noting that the nature of an obstetric emergency-hemorrhage, infection, hypertensive disease-often directly informs contraceptive eligibility and method selection. We further describe why the postpartum period after an obstetric emergency represents a critical, frequently missed opportunity for contraceptive counseling, particularly in low-resource and humanitarian settings where subsequent access to care is uncertain. We propose practical strategies for integration at the facility, health system, and global levels, including standardized counseling prompts, aligned supply chains, updated training curricula, and incorporation of contraceptive indicators into EmONC guidance and monitoring tools. Embedding contraception within EmONC would strengthen continuity across the maternal health continuum and better align global frameworks with the clinical realities of obstetric risk.

articles.title: Pre-eclampsia screening and prevention: Implementing FIGO guidelines in a Thai population.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world implementation, screening performance, aspirin uptake, and safety of a FIGO (the International Federation of Gynecology & Obstetrics)-based first-trimester pre-eclampsia screening and prevention program.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women initiating antenatal care before 14 weeks of gestation at a tertiary referral center in southern Thailand from 2021 to 2024. Screening incorporated maternal factors, mean arterial pressure, and uterine artery pulsatility index. Women with a calculated risk of 1:100 or greater were classified as being at high risk and offered aspirin 162 mg nightly. Outcomes included screening coverage, detection rates, aspirin uptake, pregnancy outcomes, and bleeding complications.
RESULTS: Among 1713 pregnancies, 71 developed pre-eclampsia (4.1%), including 49 with severe features. Overall, 1106 women were screened (64.6%), but coverage reached 93.6% by the end of implementation. The screen-positive rate was 11.3%. Detection rates were 61.7% for overall pre-eclampsia, 69.6% for delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, 87.5% for delivery before 34 weeks of gestation, and 100% for delivery before 32 weeks of gestation, with false-positive rates of approximately 9%-11%. Aspirin uptake among screen-positive women was 99.2%. Pre-eclampsia was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery, preterm birth, lower birth weight, and neonatal intensive care unit admission. No eclampsia, placental abruption, maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal death, stillbirth, or neonatal death occurred. After adjustment for potential confounders, aspirin was not associated with the risk of an estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and the risk of an estimated blood loss of 1000 mL or more did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: FIGO-based first-trimester screening was feasible in routine care, with increasing coverage as implementation matured, near-universal aspirin uptake, and clinically useful detection of preterm pre-eclampsia. Aspirin use was not significantly associated with severe bleeding.

articles.title: Birth and long-term health outcomes of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate treatment for heterotopic pregnancy: A retrospective study and focused literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report birth outcomes and long-term intellectual and physical development follow-up data of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate (MTX) injection for heterotopic pregnancy (HP), and to summarize relevant published cases.
METHODS: We included 29 patients with HP involving uncommon ectopic implantation sites who underwent transvaginal ultrasound-guided local MTX injection to treat the ectopic gestation (2006-2023). We evaluated birth outcomes and the intellectual and physical development in offspring aged 4-17 years, and conducted a focused review of published cases from 1990 to 2025 via PubMed.
RESULTS: Pregnancy outcomes were available for 27 of 29 patients. Twenty-four women delivered 26 live-born offspring, including 23 without and three with congenital anomalies (congenital heart disease, hypospadias, and multiple craniofacial and limb abnormalities, respectively). Matched comparative analyses included 11 preschool-aged, eight school-aged, and seven adolescent offspring. Across the cognitive, anthropometric, blood pressure, and laboratory outcomes assessed, three between-group differences showed nominal P-values of below 0.05, involving preschool uric acid, school-age systolic blood pressure, and adolescent blood urea nitrogen. Among these, the systolic blood pressure difference was accompanied by high-normal blood pressure or hypertension in some offspring in the MTX group. None of the three differences remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After the exclusion of overlapping observations, the focused literature review identified 14 independent live-born offspring from previously reported cases, of whom two had congenital anomalies.
CONCLUSION: Most live-born offspring following local MTX treatment for HP had no congenital anomalies, and no long-term offspring outcome comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. However, congenital anomalies were reported in both our cohort and the published literature, and the small sample size and limited evidence preclude firm conclusions regarding long-term safety.

articles.title: One-Year Survival After Hybrid Stage 1 Single Ventricle Palliation - The Impact of Institutional Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hybrid stage 1 palliation (HS1P), an alternative to the Norwood procedure for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), is often reserved for high-risk patients. We aimed to evaluate the survival of HS1P through one year when used as standard palliation strategy for HLHS and similar lesions and to assess changes in survival over time.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all infants who underwent HS1P for single ventricle palliation. A structured protocol for patient management was developed between 2009 and 2017, with all components implemented by June 2017. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on timing of HS1P: Era 1 (January 2002 - May 2017), and Era 2 (June 2017 - December 2024). The primary outcome was survival through one year.
RESULTS: A total of 281 infants underwent HS1P, 221 in Era 1 and 60 in Era 2. Median age at HS1P was 6 days for both groups. Balloon atrial septostomy at the time of HS1P was significantly more common in Era 2 (43% vs 4% in Era 1), as was use of smaller bands (p <0.001 for both). One-year survival was significantly higher in Era 2 compared to Era 1 (83% vs 65%, p=0.01), and this benefit persisted in multivariable analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study of HS1P used as standard palliation, contemporary survival was excellent with significant improvements in outcomes in more recent years. Further study is needed to understand longer-term outcomes and the interplay of patient risk factors, to help guide best practices.

articles.title: Atypical inflammatory bowel disease and multi-system inflammation expand the phenotype of inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B kinase subunit beta gain-of-function variants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gain-of-function (GoF) variants in the inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa-B kinase subunit beta (IKK2) protein, encoded by inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B kinase subunit beta (IKBKB), have previously been reported to cause autoinflammation with a progressive immunodeficiency. Genetic defects have not previously been described in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), although disruption of highly interacting proteins, such as IKBKG and RELA, are known causes of monogenic IBD.
METHODS: Using whole exome sequencing data, we screened a cohort of over 1250 adult and paediatric onset patients with IBD for deleterious variants (minor allele frequency < 0.0005, Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion [CADD] > 15) in IKBKB. We retrieved in-depth phenotypic data and performed peripheral blood mononuclear cell CD25/CD70 stimulation validation in patients with apparent IKBKB GoF variants.
RESULTS: We identified 11 patients with potentially pathogenic variants. Correlation with clinical and immunophenotypic data prioritised a rare, potential gain-of-function, variant in a patient and his affected parent, c.522T>G, p Asp174Glu. The proband had multi-system inflammation and severe atypical inflammatory bowel disease with rectal stricturing. We demonstrated impaired CD25/CD70 T- and B-cell responses in the patient, characteristic of the IKBKB defect, alongside hallmark immunological manifestations of reduced natural killer and B-cell numbers, and perturbed immunoglobulin titres. Treatment with a selective Janus kinase (JAK1)-inhibitor resulted in rapid clinical and biochemical improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: This study expands the phenotypic manifestation of IKBKB GoF variants to include IBD and demonstrates a biologically plausible targeted treatment. Further functional work is required to elucidate the precise mechanism of bowel inflammation and identify additional patients.

articles.title: Implementing intestinal ultrasound in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: Practical framework for program development: Perspectives from the Pediatric Committee of the Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada.
authors: Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada (iUSCAN)
articles.abstract: Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is a noninvasive, radiation-free tool that is well-tolerated and frequently preferred by children and families. Its ability to provide real-time assessments that facilitate timely decision-making is driving its adoption as an increasingly important monitoring standard in comprehensive pediatric inflammatory bowel disease care. IUS programs follow a common trajectory: begin by identifying and supporting a physician lead, then scale through additional trained physicians, a consultation service, and, where volume supports it, sonographer or hybrid models. Institutional planning should enable this growth while preserving the point-of-care delivery that defines IUS's clinical value. Sustainability requires institutional commitment to equipment, protected time, training (ideally embedded in fellowship), standardized documentation, and a reimbursement strategy. Equipment is attainable, not aspirational: a moderately priced cart-based system is sufficient and should be framed to leadership as essential infrastructure. Centers that adopt IUS with rigorous documentation and join collaborative registries from the outset will be positioned to generate the outcomes data needed to further advance the field.

articles.title: Central-line associated bloodstream infections in children on long-term parenteral nutrition: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central-line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality in children receiving long-term parenteral nutrition (LT-PN). This study aimed to assess CLABSI incidence rate, risk factors and taurolidine lock therapy (TLT) effectiveness.
METHODS: We conducted a 5-year, single-centre prospective cohort study of children on LT-PN. The primary outcome was CLABSI incidence, expressed as episodes per 1000 CL-days (with 95% confidence intervals).
RESULTS: Across 27,086 CL-days in 20 children (median age 44 months, interquartile range 88.25), 31 CLABSI episodes occurred, yielding an incidence of 1.14/1000 CL-days (0.80-1.62). Children with enterostomy had a higher incidence (2.24/1000 CL-days [1.33-3.78]) compared with those without (0.80/1000 CL-days [0.50-1.28]; p < 0.05). Subsequent CLABSI episode was more frequent in children with intestinal motility disorders (p = 0.049) and in those receiving total PN without enteral/oral intake (p = 0.049). In multivariable analysis, oral food intake was independently associated with a lower likelihood of CLABSI recurrence (odds ratio [OR] 0.01, 95% CI 0.00-0.68; p = 0.032). Compared with standard care (1.88/1000 CL-days [1.04-3.39]), children on TLT had a lower incidence (1.01/1000 CL-days [0.65-1.56]).
CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI incidence in children on LT-PN appears to be influenced by specific risk factors, including enterostomy, intestinal motility disorders, and exclusive PN. TLT was associated with a lower CLABSI incidence. Although statistical significance was not reached these findings suggest a potential benefit of TLT.

articles.title: The impact of highly effective modulator therapy on gastrointestinal, hepatic, and nutritional outcomes in cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a multisystemic disease that has implications throughout the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and is a significant cause of morbidity for people with CF (PwCF). The introduction of highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT) has led to major implications in the health and life expectancy of PwCF. However, the influence of HEMT on GI manifestations for PwCF is less clear and complex. This paper performs a review of the current literature assessing the impact of HEMT on GI manifestations related to CF. We review the implications of HEMT on the upper GI tract, pancreas, liver, lower GI tract, and nutrition. HEMT has a positive impact on overall weight and nutrition but may lead to greater than recommended weight gain. HEMT may also lead to improved pancreatic function when started at a young age, may improve meconium ileus in the neonatal period, and may improve intestinal inflammation. There is less clear evidence on the impact of HEMT on reflux, bloating, constipation, distal intestinal obstruction syndrome, and pancreatitis. There does not appear to be an improvement in CF hepatobiliary disease (CFHBI) with HEMT, and those taking it should be monitored for drug-induced injury (DILI). HEMT does show promising benefits for some GI manifestations of CF. However, there continues to be significant morbidity from GI manifestations in PwCF despite HEMT. Further research would benefit the understanding and implications of HEMT in this realm.

articles.title: BMI percentile trajectories and liver enzyme changes in children with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The incidence of pediatric obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are rapidly rising. However, the impact of dynamic body mass index (BMI) changes on liver chemistries remains understudied. We investigated the association between longitudinal changes in BMI percentile and changes in liver chemistries among children with MASLD.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, 1169 children with biopsy-confirmed MASLD enrolled in the Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network were followed for a mean of 4.0 years. BMI percentiles were calculated using the lambda-mu-sigma method with an extended metric to capture nuances at extreme values. Generalized linear mixed-effects models with random effects for patients and clinics were applied, and inverse probability treatment weighting adjusted for demographics and baseline histologic features. Sensitivity analyses stratified by sex and ethnicity assessed robustness.
RESULTS: Participants (mean age 13 years; 72% Hispanic) with higher BMI percentiles exhibited elevated blood pressures, increased insulin levels, and a lower frequency of the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) GG variant. Each 5-unit increase in BMI percentile was independently associated with a 23% increase in alanine aminotransferase (1.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-1.30), a 13% increase in aspartate aminotransferase (1.13; 95% CI, 1.09-1.17), and a 12% increase in γ‑glutamyl transferase (1.12; 95% CI, 1.08-1.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal increases in BMI percentile are independently associated with worse liver chemistry in pediatric MASLD. Routine monitoring of BMI trajectories, alongside early weight management strategies, may be critical to mitigating disease progression. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01061684, NCT04454463.

articles.title: Composite scores as a measure of cyclic vomiting syndrome burden: Preliminary validation in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cyclic vomiting syndrome (CVS) is a debilitating, episodic vomiting disorder. There are no validated outcome surveys quantifying the burden of CVS episodes. Recent data demonstrate that specific parameters such as episode timing, duration, and associated symptoms are key to diagnosing pediatric CVS. It is unclear if these specific parameters alone or in combination relate to the disabling nature of CVS. This study aimed to evaluate the strength of various CVS composite scores based on episode parameters compared to individual parameters in relationship to a proxy index of disability.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of data from 38 patients aged 3-18 years presenting with episodic vomiting at Children's Wisconsin hospital with a formal CVS diagnosis, including a migraine-associated CVS (mCVS) subgroup (n = 21), were analyzed. Patients and caregivers completed surveys on specific symptoms during vomiting episodes and the pediatric migraine disability assessment (PedMIDAS) tool as index of CVS-related disability burden. Pearson correlations were computed between PedMIDAS disability scores and seven different CVS composite scores including the following parameters of episodes: frequency (F), duration (D), nausea severity (Sn), headache pain severity (Sh), and abdominal pain severity (Sa).
RESULTS: For both CVS and mCVS, each composite score was more strongly associated with PedMIDAS than any individual parameter. For CVS patients, the F*D*Sn and F*D*Sn*Sa composite scores showed the strongest disability association (r = 0.628, p < 0.001 and r = 0.654, p < 0.001, respectively). For mCVS, the F*D*Sh composite score had the strongest association with disability (r = 0.731, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study provides preliminary validation of a pediatric CVS burden scale based on an index of disability. Composite scores that include several individual episode parameters have stronger associations with disability than any individual parameters alone.

articles.title: Short- and median-term disease outcome after Clostridioides difficile infection in paediatric inflammatory bowel disease patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a recognised complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In adults, CDI has been linked to increased long-term colectomy risk, but data on its impact in paediatric IBD remain scarce. We aimed to assess the medium-term course of IBD after CDI in children.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, case-control study in the paediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition Department at Necker-Enfants Malades Hospital. All paediatric IBD (pIBD) patients hospitalised with CDI between January 2008 and December 2020 were included. Each case was matched 1:3 with IBD controls by sex, age, IBD subtype, disease location, and year of diagnosis. Outcomes at 12, 24 and 36 months included disease activity scores, number of exacerbations, hospitalisations, digestive surgeries, and treatment escalation.
RESULTS: Forty-five pIBD patients with CDI were enrolled and matched with 152 pIBD controls. Compared with controls, children with CDI experienced a more severe disease course, characterised by higher mean activity scores each year of follow-up, more flares requiring hospitalisation at 24 and 36 months, and greater need for therapeutic escalation over time (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In paediatric patients, CDI is associated with a significantly more severe medium-term course of IBD. Early recognition and targeted management of CDI are therefore crucial in this population.

articles.title: Natural history and disease burden of biliary atresia in the United States: A systematic literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Biliary atresia (BA) is a rare and potentially fatal cholangiopathy affecting infants. The primary treatment approach for BA is Kasai hepatoportoenterostomy (KP); however, even with KP, many patients still require liver transplantation (LT). The objective of this systematic literature review (SLR) was to describe epidemiology, natural history, and native liver survival (NLS), as well as the humanistic and economic burden, in patients with BA in the United States (US).
METHODS: Embase and MEDLINE searches were performed; US-based, English-language publications from 2014 to 2024 were included. Additional searches were conducted for non-peer-reviewed publications, including congress abstracts. The SLR was conducted per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines.
RESULTS: Across epidemiology, natural history, and NLS, 38/3485 records were included; for the humanistic and economic burden outcomes, 16/1471 records were included. Sample sizes ranged from 10 to 4306 patients, and BA prevalence was 6.5-6.8 per 100,000 live births. Complications of BA included various hepatic, cardiovascular, and renal abnormalities, among others. Post-transplant graft survival rates ranged from 86.0%-96.0% and 79.0%-97.0% at 1 and 5 years post-LT, respectively. BA was also associated with high healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and disease costs. Overall, sample heterogeneity and study design differences made comparisons across studies difficult.
CONCLUSIONS: Although there are limited data on BA outcomes in the US, and the published BA studies are heterogeneous, this SLR reveals a substantial burden due to BA-related care and complications. Additionally, data on HCRU and costs highlight the unmet need for additional management and research in BA.

articles.title: An appraisal of the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition clinical practice guidelines.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical practice guidelines produced by the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) guide clinical decision-making across pediatric gastroenterology in North America, yet their methodological quality has not been systematically evaluated. We aimed to assess the quality of NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation II (AGREE-II) instrument.
METHODS: We identified 11 NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines published between 2005 and 2024. Each guideline was independently appraised by ≥4 reviewers using the AGREE-II tool, which evaluates six domains across 23 items on a 1-7 scale. Scaled domain scores were calculated according to the AGREE-II rubric. To assess reproducibility, domain-specific and pooled intraclass correlation coefficients were estimated using linear mixed-effects models with crossed random effects for raters and items.
RESULTS: Domain scores varied substantially across guidelines. Scope and Purpose (mean 83.8%, SD 7.6) and Clarity of Presentation (mean 80.4%, SD 9.9) received the highest ratings, reflecting clear objectives, defined target populations, and well-structured recommendations. Stakeholder Involvement (mean 58.1%, SD 7.8) and Applicability (mean 53.6%, SD 5.1) scored lowest, indicating limited reporting of patient or caregiver engagement, implementation tools, barriers, or resource implications. Inter-rater reliability ranged from poor to moderate across AGREE-II domains, consistent with the subjectivity inherent in AGREE II scoring and variability in guideline reporting detail.
CONCLUSIONS: NASPGHAN guidelines demonstrate strengths in defining scope and presenting recommendations clearly. Opportunities for improvement include greater stakeholder involvement, enhanced transparency in guideline development methodology and conflict-of-interest reporting, and clearer guidance on implementation and resource considerations.

articles.title: Relationship Between Timing of Surgery and Procedure-Specific Outcomes in Neonates and Infants for Congenital Heart Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Determining the right timing for neonatal heart surgery remains difficult. In a large multicenter cohort, we studied the relationship between birthweight, timing of surgery, and outcomes to identify optimal surgical timing.
METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database from 2010-2022, we retrospectively reviewed infants who underwent surgery within 90 days of birth. Procedures analyzed included coarctation of aorta (CoA), ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair, atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) repair, tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, Norwood procedure, and arterial switch operation (ASO). Birthweight, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were analyzed as predictors of operative mortality using categorical and continuous models, including nonlinear spline analysis. Patients were divided into five birthweight categories for risk comparison.
RESULTS: The cohort included 35,315 patients: 26,367(74.7%) neonates and 8,948(25.3%) infants. Low birthweight (<2500g) was present in 15.8% of neonates and 59.9% of infants. Operative mortality was highest in the 0-1kg group (9%, p<0.001). Continuous birthweight was a predictor of mortality (OR=0.45 per 100g increase; 95% CI: 0.40-0.51; p<0.0001). Neonatal age at surgery, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were independently associated with increased mortality. For Norwood procedures, mortality increased below 1.8kg and before 5 days of age; for ASOs, lowest risk occurred between 1.8-3.5kg and after 5 days of age. In AVSD, VSD, and CoA, neither birthweight nor timing significantly affected mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Except for Norwood and ASO procedures, weight and timing had limited impact on mortality, supporting individualized surgical decision-making rather than reliance on historical weight thresholds.

articles.title: Serum serotonin levels in children with functional constipation: A prospective case-control study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Functional constipation is a common pediatric functional gastrointestinal disorder, but data on circulating serotonin are limited. This study compared fasting serum serotonin levels between children with functional constipation and healthy controls and examined associations with clinical characteristics.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, case-control study included children aged 4-18 years with Rome IV-defined functional constipation and healthy controls. Fasting serum serotonin was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Clinical characteristics, including fecal incontinence, body mass index categories, and treatment response, were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed discriminatory performance.
RESULTS: Seventy-four children were included: 37 with functional constipation and 37 controls. Age and sex distribution were similar. Serum serotonin levels were higher in children with functional constipation (174.1 ng/mL [interquartile range, IQR, 161.1-188.3] versus 160.5 ng/mL [IQR, 149.5-181.9]; p = 0.048). Children with fecal incontinence had higher serum serotonin levels in the unadjusted analysis (p = 0.031), but this finding did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. After excluding children with fecal incontinence, the between-group difference was no longer significant (p = 0.134). Levels were numerically higher in children with obesity, but differences across body mass index categories were not significant. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.628 (95% confidence interval, 0.496-0.759; p = 0.062).
CONCLUSIONS: Serum serotonin was modestly higher in children with functional constipation, but diagnostic utility was limited. These exploratory findings do not support its use as a diagnostic marker. Further studies are needed to clarify serotonin-related pathways in pediatric functional constipation.

articles.title: Genetic testing strategies for neonatal cholestasis in the neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cholestasis in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) has a broad differential diagnosis, including genetic diseases. Advances in next generation sequencing (NGS) have expanded the ability to identify genetic etiologies. Studies evaluating testing strategies, diagnostic yield, and clinical characteristics of those undergoing genetic testing for cholestasis in the NICU are limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied patients at a single-center Level IV NICU with cholestasis, genetic testing and Hepatology consultation between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Microarray, targeted gene panel and exome or genome sequencing (ES/GS) results and clinical characteristics of those tested were reviewed. Diagnostic yield was defined as identification of pathogenic variants determined to be causative of cholestasis. Categorical variables were compared using Chi-squared test or Fisher's exact as appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Wilcoxon rank sum tests or Kruskal-Wallis tests as appropriate.
RESULTS: A total of 174 patients were included for analysis. Patients with three modalities of testing had higher peak direct bilirubin and alanine aminotransferase. Diagnostic yield increased by comprehensiveness: microarray 5% (3/54), targeted gene panel 10% (12/125) and ES/GS 33% (23/70). Seven patients with non-diagnostic targeted panels had diagnostic ES/GS. Those with diagnostic ES/GS were younger at Hepatology consultation, had higher peak direct bilirubin and were less likely to have sepsis compared to those with diagnostic targeted panels.
CONCLUSIONS: ES/GS demonstrated greater diagnostic yield for cholestasis in the NICU than other modalities. Confounding by year of testing is possible, but differences in yield support preferential use of ES/GS for neonatal cholestasis evaluation.

articles.title: Obesity in paediatric inflammatory bowel disease: The emerging double burden-A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Obesity is increasingly recognised in paediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), challenging the traditional view of paediatric IBD as a condition primarily associated with undernutrition, impaired growth, and delayed puberty. In parallel with the global rise in childhood obesity, overweight and obesity are now increasingly reported in children with IBD, particularly in ulcerative colitis. The coexistence of obesity, intestinal inflammation, altered body composition, and nutritional vulnerability creates new challenges for assessment and management. Body mass index (BMI) remains the most commonly used screening tool, but may not adequately reflect adiposity, muscle mass, fat distribution, pubertal status, growth trajectory, or metabolic risk. Paediatric studies suggest that overweight and obesity may influence disease presentation, diagnostic delay, disease activity, relapse or exacerbation risk, postoperative complications, bone health, and treatment response, particularly with anti-TNF therapy. However, available data remain limited and heterogeneous, with differences in study design, BMI definitions, disease subtype, and outcome measures. Lifestyle modification, including improvement of diet quality and promotion of physical activity, should be adapted to disease activity, nutritional status, growth needs, and psychosocial wellbeing. Key knowledge gaps include the need for harmonised obesity definitions, prospective studies incorporating body composition and patient-centred outcomes, and evaluation of obesity-targeted interventions in children and adolescents with IBD. This review summarises current evidence on the epidemiology, assessment, clinical relevance, therapeutic implications, and lifestyle management of obesity in paediatric IBD, and highlights future research priorities.

articles.title: The role of histologic remission as disease clearance: Emerging treat-to-target in pediatric ulcerative colitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: While clinical and endoscopic remission (ER) are established therapeutic targets in ulcerative colitis (UC), endoscopic healing may not fully reflect residual microscopic inflammation. Histologic remission (HR) has been proposed as a deeper marker of disease control and a potential predictor of long-term outcomes. We evaluated whether HR predicts relapses in pediatric UC patients who achieved ER.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included pediatric patients with UC (<18 years) who achieved ER (Mayo endoscopic subscore (MES) 0 or 1). HR was defined as a Nancy index score of 0. Patients were stratified into HR and non-HR groups. The primary outcome was clinical relapse, defined as a partial Mayo score ≥3, corticosteroid initiation, requiring treatment escalation, UC-related hospitalization, colectomy or death. Relapse-free survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among 111 pediatric UC patients with ER, 35 (31.5%) achieved HR. Patients with HR showed significantly improved relapse-free survival than non-HR (log-rank p = 0.015). Multivariable Cox regression demonstrated that both ER (MES 0 vs. 1; hazard ratio 0.57, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.28-0.94, p = 0.032) and HR (hazard ratio 0.39, 95% CI 0.17-0.91, p = 0.030) independently predicted reduced relapse risk. Notably, even among patients with ER, those with a Nancy index of 0 had superior relapse-free survival versus a score of 1 (p = 0.008).
CONCLUSIONS: HR was achieved in only one-third of pediatric patients with UC with ER but was strongly associated with reduced relapse, supporting HR as a treatment target beyond ER.

articles.title: Addition of Curcumin-QingDai correlates with clinical benefit in pediatric ulcerative colitis and inflammatory bowel disease-unclassified.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Composite remission remains hard to achieve for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Recently, a novel herbal-based combination therapy, Curcumin-QingDai (CurQD), has shown promise in improving rates of clinical remission for adults with ulcerative colitis (UC), however, experience in children is lacking. Here we describe efficacy and safety of CurQD in a pediatric cohort diagnosed with UC/IBD-unclassified (IBD-U).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of children with a diagnosis of UC or IBD-U beginning CurQD. Data collection included demographics, disease extent and severity, medication history, surgical history, biomarkers, endoscopic and histologic reports, and intestinal ultrasound. Clinical disease activity measured by the pediatric ulcerative colitis activity index (PUCAI) was recorded at baseline, Weeks 8-12 and Week 24.
RESULTS: A total of 35 patients with UC/IBD-U treated with CurQD met inclusion criteria, 28.6% were female and 62.9% had a diagnosis of UC. The median age at start of intervention was 14.0 years. Twenty-two (62.9%) were bio-experienced. Clinical response and clinical remission rates were 65.5% and 63.6%, respectively, by Week 24. Significant changes in calprotectin, ESR, albumin and hemoglobin were noted pre/post intervention. Side effects to CurQD were uncommon (14.2%) and mild in all cases.
CONCLUSIONS: As management options in the pediatric population are limited, adjunctive therapy is often a crucial consideration in achieving clinical response in children with IBD. Our data suggests that the addition of CurQD may offer a safe and effective option for children with UC/IBD-U when a primary agent has not resulted in a durable clinical remission.

articles.title: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Pediatric cholestatic liver diseases, such as Alagille syndrome and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, are rare genetic disorders characterized by impaired bile flow, systemic bile acid accumulation, and debilitating pruritus. Historically managed with supportive care or invasive surgical interventions, the therapeutic landscape has recently expanded with the introduction of ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitors. These luminal, ileum-targeted agents block bile acid reabsorption, thereby increasing fecal bile acid excretion and effectively reducing the systemic bile acid pool to relieve pruritus. However, this pharmacological blockade also attenuates the intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR)-fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19) feedback loop, leading to a compensatory increase in hepatic bile acid synthesis. Consequently, the clinical efficacy and safety of IBAT inhibitors are heavily dependent on a sufficiently preserved enterohepatic bile flow and canalicular export capacity. When luminal bile acid delivery is impaired, therapeutic benefits diminish, and the unchecked compensatory synthesis may contribute to hepatocyte stress and elevated transaminases. Thus, optimizing the use of these therapies will require a shift from broad disease-label indications toward precision, genotype- and physiology-informed patient selection, utilizing non-invasive biomarkers to assess target engagement and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Treatment of pediatric autoimmune liver disease beyond prednisolone and azathioprine in a cohort of 115 patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric autoimmune hepatitis (pAIH) is an acute or chronic inflammatory liver disease, caused by a dysregulation of the immune system. Autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis (ASC) additionally affects the bile ducts. Traditional first-line treatment (FLT) consists of prednisolone and azathioprine. If pAIH/ASC remains untreated or biochemical remission (BR) is not achieved, end-stage liver disease develops. We aimed to analyze the 6-months-outcomes of various second- and third-line therapies for pAIH/ASC.
METHODS: This is a retrospective single-center analysis, including all cases of patients with pAIH or ASC between 2000 and 2025. All patients were diagnosed based on published European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition diagnostic criteria.
RESULTS: Of 115 patients with pAIH or ASC, 26 patients required an alternative therapy (altT) other than prednisolone and azathioprine, most of them due to non-BR, including due to non-compliance. The 6-month outcome shows, that tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha inhibitors overall achieved the best results with a BR rate of 40% (n = 2/5). This was closely followed by cyclosporin A (CSA), with a BR rate of 36.4% (n = 4/11), which was the most commonly used drug in our study. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are significantly more likely to need altT.
CONCLUSIONS: The overall BR rate 6 months after start of altT is low and decreases with each stage of therapy, the TNF-alpha inhibitors demonstrated the highest BR rate for altT. Non-compliance is a significant problem in general, so it is unclear whether the success of this therapy is solely attributable to the drug's inherent immunomodulatory function or to its controlled administration via intravenous injection. The prospective evaluation of this novel, low-side-effect management option warrants further explorations.

articles.title: Baseline TNF-α in relation to inflammatory burden, infliximab pharmacokinetics, and dose intensification in pediatric Crohn's disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Crohn's disease (CD) is a systemic disorder in which conventional luminal endoscopic assessments may incompletely reflect overall inflammatory burden. We aimed to evaluate the associations between baseline inflammatory cytokines, disease phenotype, infliximab (IFX) pharmacokinetics, and the need for dose intensification (DI) in pediatric CD.
METHODS: This prospective study included pediatric patients with moderate-to-severe CD treated with IFX. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels were measured at diagnosis. Baseline imbalances were adjusted using propensity score matching and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses.
RESULTS: Of the 160 enrolled patients, 15 (9.4%) were not included in the 1-year analysis, and 145 (90.6%) completed the 1-year follow-up. Body mass index (BMI)-adjusted TNF-α levels correlated with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (R = 0.22, p = 0.008) and fecal calprotectin (R = 0.34, p < 0.001), but not with simple endoscopic score for CD. In contrast, IL-6 levels were not significantly associated with inflammatory biomarkers. Cytokine profiles and IFX trough levels were not associated with perianal disease status or disease location. DI was required in 94 of 145 patients (64.8%), and patients requiring DI demonstrated higher baseline TNF-α levels than those without DI (49.63 ± 29.09 vs. 40.14 ± 16.59 pg/mL, p = 0.046).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline TNF-α levels were associated with subsequent IFX DI, while also correlating with conventional inflammatory biomarkers but not with SES-CD or anatomical disease phenotype. These findings suggest that baseline TNF-α may reflect an aspect of inflammatory burden relevant to subsequent treatment requirements that is not captured by luminal endoscopic severity or anatomical disease classification alone.

articles.title: Faecal leucine levels differentiate paediatric inflammatory bowel disease from irritable bowel syndrome and functional abdominal pain.
articles.abstract: Diagnosing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is based on a combination of clinical symptoms, with laboratory tests and endoscopy, to distinguish IBD from other conditions. Faecal amino acids, particularly leucine, have shown promising results as noninvasive biomarker for this purpose. This cross-sectional study evaluated faecal leucine and the leucine/isoleucine ratio and its potential discriminative value between treatment-naïve IBD patients and patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and functional abdominal pain- not otherwise specified (FAP-NOS) patients, using a targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) technique. Absolute leucine concentration and the leucine/isoleucine ratio were significantly higher in IBD, with the leucine/isoleucine ratio showing an area under the curve of 0.75 (95%CI: 0.65-0.84) with a cut-off value of 1.44. Concluding, the leucine/isoleucine ratio can differentiate IBD from IBS and FAP-NOS, and provides insights into disease pathogenesis. These findings highlight its potential as a novel noninvasive biomarker, although further studies are warranted.

articles.title: High rates of flares after anti-tumor necrosis factor withdrawal in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: A multi-center study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Outcomes of anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) discontinuation in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remain unclear. We aimed to quantify relapse and biologic re-initiation rates following anti-TNF withdrawal in patients in sustained clinical remission for at least 6 months.
METHODS: Patients' characteristics were recorded at the time of anti-TNF discontinuation, at the time of flare, or at the end of follow-up, with a minimum follow-up of 1 year. A flare was defined as clinical, biochemical, or endoscopic activity leading to hospitalization, systemic corticosteroids, and/or initiation of a biologic.
RESULTS: This multicenter retrospective study from the Pediatric IBD Porto Group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) included 83 children from 21 centers (46 [55%] males, 59 Crohn's disease [CD], 24 ulcerative colitis [UC]), who discontinued anti-TNF. At the time of anti-TNF withdrawal, the median age was 14.8 years (interquartile range 12.4-16.9); 93% had biochemical remission, and 68% of those undergoing endoscopy were in endoscopic remission. Within 12 and 24 months, 45/83 (54%) and 56/74 (76%) experienced a flare, and 29/83 (35%) and 47/68 (69%) re-initiated a biologic, respectively. Overall, flare and biologic re-initiation rates were similar in CD and UC, between those with biochemical or endoscopic remission, and among those maintained on immunomodulators (n = 33) or 5-aminosalicylates (n = 20). Univariate and multivariable Cox models did not identify baseline predictors of relapse or biologic re-initiation.
CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing anti-TNF therapy in pediatric IBD patients in clinical remission is associated with high rates of disease flare and treatment re-initiation. This provides quantitative data to help balance the benefits and risks when considering anti-TNF withdrawal.

articles.title: Higher incidence of paediatric autoimmune liver disease post-COVID.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A higher incidence of autoimmune conditions with greater disease severity is reported post-Coronavirus Disease (COVID). The incidence and disease severity of paediatric autoimmune liver disease (AILD) post-COVID has not been assessed.
METHODS: Data on children <16 years of age diagnosed with AILD between 2015 and 2024 from a United Kingdom quaternary liver specialist centre was captured. Comparison of AILD incidence and presenting clinical characteristics in pre and post-COVID pandemic time-periods were made.
RESULTS: 199 patients were newly diagnosed with AILD within the study period (82 pre-COVID [2015-2019]; 47 autoimmune hepatitis type 1 [AIH-1], 11 AIH-2, 9 primary sclerosing cholangitis [PSC], 15 overlap/autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis [ASC], and 117 post-COVID [2020-2024]; 64 AIH-1, 10 AIH-2, 20 PSC, 23 overlap/ASC). A sharp rise in the incidence of AIH-1, PSC and overlap syndrome/ASC was observed post-COVID, being most marked in the AIH-1 cohort (p < 0.0001). Children were older at disease presentation for AIH-1, PSC and overlap/ASC compared to pre-COVID, particularly in AIH-1 (p = 0.0093). Minimal variation was observed in AIH-2 patients. Most patients presenting with AIH-1 and overlap/ASC post-COVID did not have a personal history of autoimmunity. High viral coinfection rates were observed in post-COVID AIH-1 and AIH-2 presentations.
CONCLUSION: The higher incidence and older presenting age of newly diagnosed AILD patients post-COVID may have resulted from immune dysregulation in susceptible children following the sudden exposure to viral infections after long periods of social isolation, triggering the onset of autoimmunity even in individuals without an autoimmune predisposition.

articles.title: Unequal Starts, Unequal Spaces: Contextual and Individual Influences on Motor Development From Birth to 5 Years in Full-Term and Preterm Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child development is a dynamic process influenced by the interaction between biological risk factors and environmental opportunities.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined individual (gestational age, birth weight, birth length, age and sex) and contextual factors (socioeconomic status, early childhood education attendance and region of residence) associated with motor development in preterm and full-term children during the first 5 years of life.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 539 children aged 0-71 months, including preterm and full-term children, were assessed using the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-Second Edition. Parents completed a sociodemographic questionnaire. Hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses were conducted separately for preterm and full-term groups.
RESULTS: For full-term children, the final model showed that age, sex and socioeconomic status were significant predictors of motor outcomes, with higher motor scores observed among girls and with high socioeconomic status. For preterm children, sex also emerged as a significant predictor, with girls demonstrating higher motor scores. In addition, contextual factors, particularly early childhood education attendance and region of residence, were significantly associated with motor development in preterm children, with higher motor scores observed among children attending early childhood education and residing in urban areas.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight evidence for a combined influence of individual and environmental factors and point out distinct patterns of associations with motor development e in full-term and preterm children.

articles.title: Parents' Experiences of Participation in a Family Camp for Children With ASD: An Inclusive Community in Action.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parents of children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) frequently experience persistent caregiving demands, social isolation and restricted opportunities for family participation. Although family camp programmes have demonstrated positive effects on family well-being, limited evidence explains how parents experience these programmes and construct meaning from participation within inclusive camp environments. This study explored parents' experiences of participating in a residential sport- and arts-based family camp for children with ASD.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted within a constructivist paradigm using reflexive thematic analysis. Twenty-three parents attending a 3-day residential family camp for children with ASD in Türkiye completed open-ended written questionnaires. Data were analysed following Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach, supported by reflexive practices, investigator collaboration, peer debriefing and member reflection to enhance analytical rigour.
FINDINGS: Four interconnected themes were generated: (1) Living Under Continuous Burden: Participation Barriers Extend Beyond the Child; (2) Creating Conditions for Healing Through an Inclusive Community; (3) Participation as the Mechanism of Developmental and Family Transformation; and (4) From Service Recipients to Codesigners of Autism-Friendly Futures. Parents described autism as a family experience characterized by continuous caregiving demands, stigma and participation restrictions. The camp temporarily disrupted these barriers by creating an inclusive environment characterized by psychological safety, peer support and shared participation. Parents perceived participation as the mechanism through which developmental, emotional and relational changes emerged for both children and families, while also strengthening parental confidence, agency and advocacy for more inclusive family-centred services.
CONCLUSIONS: Participation within an inclusive residential sport- and arts-based autism family camp appeared to extend beyond recreation, providing a context in which families reconstructed belonging, well-being and future possibilities. These findings suggest that meaningful participation may represent a key mechanism through which inclusive family camp programmes promote parental well-being, family transformation and more sustainable family-centred autism support.

articles.title: Dietary diversity and allergic diseases among Chinese children and adolescents: Indirect associations via emotional and behavioral problems.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Previous studies have shown that dietary factors are related to the incidence of various allergic diseases. However, emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs) may serve as important roles in this context. This study aims to investigate whether dietary diversity is associated with EBPs in relation to allergic diseases.
METHODS: Follow-up (2019) COHERENCE cohort survey data were analyzed cross-sectionally (n = 102,399; 6-17 years), Guangzhou, China. Dietary diversity scores (DDS) were derived from food intake questionnaires. Allergic diseases were assessed based on physician-confirmed diagnoses, while EBPs were evaluated using the Chinese version of the Parent Report Version of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ-P). Binary logistic regression, forest plots, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and indirect-effect analysis examined links among EBPs, DDS, and allergic diseases.
RESULTS: Mean DDS was 7.70 ± 0.69, the prevalence of allergic diseases was 27.45%, and mean EBPs score was 12.24 ± 4.43. Higher DDS was associated with a lower risk of allergic diseases among children and adolescents. EBPs showed significant statistical indirect associations in the relationship between dietary diversity and allergic diseases. Among them, the statistical indirect association through conduct problems was the greatest (21.99%), and the statistical indirect association through peer relationship problems was the smallest (10.92%). Moreover, in the threshold analysis of allergic diseases, the turning point of EBPs is 18, and the turning point of the DDS is 5.
CONCLUSIONS: EBPs showed a statistical indirect association of DDS and allergic diseases, a nonlinear threshold effect was observed in the relationship between DDS and allergic diseases.

articles.title: From Autoantigens to GlycoRNAs: The Prehistory of RNA at the Cell Surface.
articles.abstract: The discovery of glycoRNAs in 2021 transformed the study of cell-surface biology, but it did not emerge from a vacuum. A substantial, though heterogeneous, body of evidence accumulated over four decades, suggesting that several nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) can access the outer plasma membrane under defined biological conditions. This historical perspective traces that development from the earliest hints in 1981, through the founding observations of 1989-1990 when La/SSB, nucleolin, and Ku70 were independently detected at the cell surface, to the consolidation period of 1990-1995 that connected surface-expressed RNP autoantigens to neonatal lupus and photosensitive cutaneous lupus, and finally to the glycoRNA era beginning in 2021. Throughout, early researchers working with limited tools identified the key phenomenon: surface-expressed nuclear RBPs as potential autoimmune triggers. They articulated the core hypothesis that modern glycoRNA biology is now positioned to test.

articles.title: Human milk short-chain fatty acid concentrations are not associated with early childhood allergic disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are microbial metabolites with immunoregulatory properties. Human milk contains SCFAs which have been proposed as potential modulators of infant immune development. We aimed to examine associations between human milk SCFA concentrations and infant allergic disease outcomes in a high-risk cohort of infants of atopic mothers.
METHODS: SCFAs were measured by targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry in human milk samples collected at 3 and 6 months postpartum from atopic mothers enrolled in the Infant Fish Oil Supplementation (IFOS) Study (n = 147). Associations between milk SCFA concentrations and early childhood allergic disease outcomes (atopic dermatitis, food allergy, allergic rhinitis, and allergen sensitisation at 1 and 2-3 years) were examined using logistic regression.
RESULTS: Human milk SCFA concentrations were broadly stable between 3 and 6 months postpartum, except for acetate which was significantly elevated at 6 months. No significant associations were observed between human milk SCFA concentrations and any allergic disease outcome after correction for multiple comparisons (all p > .05).
CONCLUSIONS: Human milk SCFA concentrations are not associated with allergic disease outcomes up to 4 years of age. These findings suggest that oral SCFA exposure via human milk is insufficient to reduce infant allergy risk, and that gut SCFA production may be a more relevant target for future allergy prevention research.

articles.title: Association of the cerebroplacental ratio with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is frequently complicated by fetal growth compromise. The cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) shows promise for identifying fetuses at risk, but its diagnostic performance specifically in preeclamptic pregnancies remains unclear.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 236 women with singleton preeclamptic pregnancies (January 2020-December 2023). Inclusion criteria: ISSHP-defined preeclampsia, gestational age 28-40 weeks at Doppler examination, and complete UA-PI and MCA-PI data within two weeks before delivery. The primary outcome was antenatal identification of small fetal size (estimated fetal weight <10th percentile). Multivariable logistic regression with prespecified covariates was used to assess independent associations. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis determined optimal cutoffs; bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) corrected for optimism. DeLong test compared AUCs.
RESULTS: CPR demonstrated moderate-to-good diagnostic accuracy for small fetal size (AUC 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.92; optimism-corrected AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91), higher than UA-PI (AUC 0.76, p = 0.018) and MCA-PI alone (AUC 0.75, p = 0.015). The exploratory optimal cutoff was 1.08 (sensitivity 66.0% [95% CI 55.8-75.2%], specificity 80.3%[95% CI 73.0-86.3%]). Abnormal CPR was independently associated with composite adverse outcomes (aOR 3.5, 95% CI 1.8-7.0, adjusting for baseline confounders; aOR 2.4, 95% CI 1.2-4.8, after additional adjustment for birth weight percentile and gestational age at delivery), including emergency cesarean for fetal distress (42.2% vs. 18.5%), 5-minute Apgar <7 (18.9% vs. 5.5%), and NICU admission (48.9% vs. 21.2%). CPR showed higher discrimination in early-onset versus late-onset preeclampsia (AUC 0.87 vs. 0.76), although this difference was attenuated after gestational-age adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In preeclamptic pregnancies, reduced CPR is independently associated with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes, with numerically higher discrimination in early-onset disease, attenuated after gestational-age adjustment. These findings support CPR as a potential adjunctive tool for contemporaneous risk stratification in preeclampsia, particularly early-onset disease, pending prospective validation with serial measurements.

articles.title: A neonatal prediction model for lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheters depth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a robust and generalizable prediction model for PICC depth in neonates undergoing lower-extremity catheterization, with the aim of improving the first-attempt success rate of catheter tip positioning and reducing PICC-related complications.
METHODS: A total of 240 neonates who successfully underwent lower-extremity PICC placement in the neonatal intensive care unit of a maternal and child health hospital were enrolled as study subjects. Variable selection was performed using stepwise regression based on the Akaike information criterion, followed by development of a multiple linear regression model. Internal validation was performed using the random split sample method (8:2). Model performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, coefficient of determination (R2), and Pearson's correlation coefficient.
RESULTS: The final model included two simple and objective variables: body weight on the day of catheterization and puncture site. The prediction equation was established as follows: insertion depth (cm) = 17.3 + body weight at catheterization (kg) × 2.3 - adjustment value for the puncture site (2.7 for small saphenous vein, 4.5 for popliteal vein, 5.1 for popliteal great saphenous vein, and 10.3 for femoral vein, respectively; reference: ankle great saphenous vein). Internal validation showed that the model achieved an R2 of 0.8789, RMSE of 1.0754, MAE of 0.8157, and Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.9375 between the predicted and observed values. Residual diagnostics indicated good predictive accuracy and stability.
CONCLUSIONS: The prediction model for neonatal lower extremity PICC insertion depth based on body weight at the catheterization and puncture sites demonstrated good fit and reliable predictive performance. It can assist in individualizing and precisely determining the catheter insertion depth in clinical practice, thereby reducing repeated adjustments and complications.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and Initial Bolus Dosing of Furosemide in Children on ECMO.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an established technology that provides life-saving mechanical support for critically ill children. In these children, fluid overload is commonly treated with furosemide; however, optimal dosing of furosemide is unknown in children supported with ECMO because ECMO may alter furosemide exposure. In this work, human blood-primed ex vivo experiments quantified red blood cell partitioning and extraction of furosemide by the ECMO circuit. Furosemide partitioned into red blood cells but was not extracted by ECMO circuits. These data then parameterized a pediatric physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of furosemide in children with and without ECMO. Next, plasma furosemide concentrations from 10 critically ill children supported by ECMO were used to evaluate PBPK model performance, with the optimized model achieving average fold error and absolute average fold error of 1.02 and 1.67, respectively. The optimized PBPK model also predicted that ECMO increases apparent volume of distribution by a median of > 30% in neonates and infants. Finally, population PBPK simulations with the optimized PBPK model provided initial bolus doses that most rapidly achieve steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations with and without ECMO. These calibrated initial bolus doses achieved steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations > 3 h faster than continuous infusions without an initial bolus dose, and this improvement was most pronounced in neonates and infants on ECMO. Overall, this work supports comparatively larger initial bolus doses for neonates and infants on ECMO, and provides calibrated initial bolus doses based on plasma exposure for critically ill children.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of antiseizure medication dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States: A retrospective claims-based cohort study, 2004-2021.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe trends and identify factors associated with antiseizure medications (ASMs) dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective claims-based cohort study within AMerican PREGNANcy Mother-Child CohorT (AM-PREGNANT). We identified pregnant persons aged 15-45 years continuously enrolled from 12 months before the last menstrual period (LMP) through pregnancy end, with ≥1 ASM dispensing from 2004 to 2021. Annual prevalence of ASM dispensing was estimated by pregnancy start year. Within a first-ever ASM dispensing cohort, we examined dispensing patterns across pregnancy time windows, ASM-related indications and changes in dispensing during pregnancy. We also assessed factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP among those initiating ASM therapy before pregnancy.
RESULTS: The cohort included 337 449 pregnant persons. Annual ASM dispensing prevalence remained stable (10%-13%). Among those with first-ever ASM dispensing (n = 115 896), 56% had dispensing before pregnancy, of whom 65% had no dispensing during pregnancy. The most common starting ASMs were clonazepam (28%), topiramate (25%) and gabapentin (20%). Dispensing patterns varied by indication: epilepsy was characterized by lamotrigine, levetiracetam and topiramate, generally dispensed for >60 days, whereas psychiatric and pain indications showed more variable patterns, typically with <30 days of dispensing. Factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP included pre-specified indications, comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing; among these, epilepsy/seizure had the strongest association (aOR 2.14; 95% CI 1.78-2.59).
CONCLUSIONS: ASM dispensing varied by indication, with most pre-pregnancy dispensing not continuing during pregnancy. Epilepsy/seizure was most strongly associated with dispensing at LMP, with additional associations observed for comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing.

articles.title: Drug-drug interactions and risk of central nervous system depression in preterm infants: Clinical outcomes from a prospective study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are frequently exposed to central nervous system (CNS) depressant medications, increasing the risk of potential drug-drug interactions (DDIs). However, evidence on the clinical outcomes associated with these interactions remains limited. This study evaluated the association between DDIs with the potential for CNS depression and clinical outcomes in neonates admitted to a NICU.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 600 neonates admitted to a NICU in Brazil. Pharmacotherapy was monitored daily, and DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were identified using the UpToDate® database. Clinical outcomes associated with specific drug combinations were analysed.
RESULTS: A total of 89 neonates (14.8%) were exposed to at least one DDI with the potential for CNS depression. These interactions were associated with a higher occurrence of hypoactivity, reduced peripheral oxygen saturation and mortality. The fentanyl/phenobarbital combination showed the most consistent risk profile, being associated with all evaluated outcomes. Interactions involving magnesium sulphate were associated with reduced oxygen saturation, while fentanyl/fluconazole was associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were associated with clinically relevant adverse outcomes in neonates. The findings highlight fentanyl/phenobarbital as the combination of greatest clinical concern and suggest that oxygen saturation may be a useful marker for monitoring CNS-related DDIs in neonatal intensive care.

articles.title: Pediatric methemoglobinemia in the emergency department: etiology, treatment patterns, and short-term outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize the clinical and etiological features of pediatric methemoglobinemia presenting to a pediatric emergency department, with particular attention to procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, and to explore short-term treatment responses to methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients presenting between November 1, 2022 1 November 2022 1 November 2022, and November 1, 2025 1 November 2025 1 November 2025, with methemoglobin levels ≥ 5% measured by co-oximetry. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, G6PD, genetic, and disposition data were collected. Baseline characteristics and early treatment responses were compared between patients receiving methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.
RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included; the median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-5), and 21 (87.5%) were male. Median initial SpO2 was 88% (IQR, 85%-90%), initial methemoglobin was 25.5% (IQR, 21.4%-30.6%), and post-treatment methemoglobin was 5.8% (IQR, 2.6%-8.3%). Drug exposure accounted for 19 cases (79.2%), most commonly lidocaine (n = 10) and prilocaine (n = 7). Among the five patients without documented oxidant exposure, two had pathogenic CYB5R3 variants and two had likely pathogenic CYB5R3 variants. Eleven patients received methylene blue and 13 received intravenous ascorbic acid. Post-treatment methemoglobin was lower with methylene blue (2.6% vs. 7.8%; p = 0.024), whereas relative reduction did not differ significantly (88.8% vs. 72.8%; p = 0.118).
CONCLUSION: Methemoglobinemia predominantly affected young infants and was most often associated with procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, particularly in the context of circumcision. Topical oropharyngeal anesthetic exposure before intubation should also be recognized as a potential source of oxidant exposure. Treatment comparisons were exploratory, and underlying enzymatic or genetic susceptibility should be considered even when an acquired oxidant exposure is identified.

articles.title: Influenza A(H3N2) Subclade K Activity in Australia in 2025: Epidemiology and Vaccine Effectiveness Results From General Practice Sentinel Surveillance.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, vaccine effectiveness (VE), antiviral prescribing and virological properties for influenza A(H3N2) subclade K detected through Australian general practice sentinel surveillance in 2025.
STUDY TYPE: Retrospective, observational study using routinely collected general practice surveillance data; VE was estimated using a test-negative design.
SETTING, PATIENTS: Data were collected from sentinel general practice sites participating in Australian Sentinel Practices Research Network surveillance across Australia during International Organization for Standardization weeks 1-52 of 2025. Patients presenting with influenza-like illness were systematically selected for virological sampling.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Demographic and clinical characteristics of patients with laboratory-confirmed influenza; VE against general practice-attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza; antiviral prescribing; and sequence-based markers of reduced antiviral susceptibility.
RESULTS: Among 3185 patients with influenza-like illness who were swabbed, 666 (21%) tested positive for influenza. Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K was first detected in week 34 of 2025 and circulated beyond the typical influenza season, peaking in November-December. Of 98 subclade K detections, 36 (37%) were in children aged 5-17 years. Compared with other types, subtypes or subclades of influenza, clinical presentations of subclade K cases were broadly similar, with no consistent clinical pattern distinguishing subclade K. VE against subclade K was 50% overall (95% confidence interval, 8.9-73) and 76% among persons aged 9 months to 17 years (95% confidence interval, 18-93). Among all patients with a recorded antiviral prescription, two-thirds were within the recommended 48-h symptom onset window (76/114). No subclade K viruses had mutations known to reduce susceptibility to the influenza antivirals assessed, including oseltamivir.
CONCLUSION: Among patients attending Australian sentinel general practices in 2025, subclade K prolonged influenza activity into the summer months. General practice sentinel surveillance of influenza can provide timely information on emerging variants and changes in the timing of influenza circulation, raising clinical awareness outside the usual season, informing vaccination strategies and prompting assessment for antiviral treatment.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of FeNO and Alpine Altitude Climate Treatment in Asthma: An EAACI Task Force Report.
articles.abstract: Fractional exhaled NO (FeNO) is a commonly used biomarker for Type 2 airway inflammation. Alpine altitude climate treatment (AACT) often results in reduced airway inflammation. We aimed to systematically review the available evidence and conducted a meta-analysis of studies investigating FeNO reduction after AACT. A systematic literature search in Pubmed, Embase, Scopus, and others was performed to identify original studies in all languages until January 2025 reporting FeNO before and after AACT. Overall, nineteen single-arm interventional studies reporting FeNO at altitudes 970-3100 MASL in 7 countries (Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Kyrgyz Republic), published between 1999 and 2024, were identified. The pooled FeNO reduction from 14 studies by -14.03 (95% confidence interval (CI) -15.53;-12.52) ppb was more pronounced in children (-14.83 (95% CI -16.57;-13.08) ppb) than in adults (-11.67 (95% CI -14.66;-8.67) ppb). The effect was weaker in studies at altitude below 1500 MASL (mean difference (MD) -12.55 (95% CI -14.79;-10.31) versus -15.25 (95% CI -17.28;-13.21) ppb) and with treatment duration more than 6 weeks (MD -11.92 (95% CI -14.25;-9.59) versus -15.55 (95% CI -17.53;-13.57) ppb). AACT results in significant FeNO reduction, likely reflecting decreased airway inflammation after treatment. Given its limited accessibility and resource intensity, future studies are needed to improve the level of evidence.

articles.title: Immediate Postpartum Mental Health and Sleep in Mothers and Fathers with Healthy Newborns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The postpartum period represents a critical window for parental psychological adjustment, but whether this is the case immediately after birth remains understudied. Furthermore, while many aspects of maternal mental health have been widely investigated in high-risk contexts, less is known about critical factors such as sleep-related vulnerability and attachment-related processes in low-risk situations, how these relate to early mental health in fathers, or how these factors may be associated with neonatal behavior.
METHODS: Thirty-two mother-father-newborn triads, comprising 32 mothers, 32 fathers, and their 32 healthy, full-term newborns, were included in the study. Newborn behavioral functioning was evaluated with the NBAS on Day 2. Mothers completed the EPDS, ECR, and STAI on Day 3. Both parents completed the CES-D, PSS, SCI, and FIRST on Day 3. Correlation, paired-comparison, and exploratory regression analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Clinically relevant elevations on at least one psychological or sleep-related measure were observed in 59.4% of mothers and 28.1% of fathers. Mothers showed significantly higher depressive symptoms, poorer sleep quality, and greater sleep reactivity than fathers. Among mothers, depressive symptoms were associated with greater sleep reactivity, with trait anxiety showing the strongest association with depressive symptoms. Maternal and paternal depressive symptoms were also positively associated across partners. Newborn behavioral functioning was broadly within expected ranges, and no association between parental psychological or sleep-related measures and NBAS cluster scores survived FDR correction.
DISCUSSION: Psychological and sleep-related vulnerability was detectable in parents during the immediate postpartum period in this low-risk clinical context, with higher levels observed in mothers. Cross-partner concordance was limited to depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that early screening of both parents may be clinically relevant. Sleep reactivity and anxiety were associated with maternal postpartum distress, but their potential predictive value requires confirmation in longitudinal studies.

articles.title: The Quality of Midwifery Care in Bangladesh: An Integrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ensuring quality midwifery care is imperative for addressing the high rates of maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity in Bangladesh. The quality of midwifery care and its impact on health outcomes are influenced by a variety of factors. The aim of this review was to investigate the quality of midwifery care in Bangladesh, exploring the barriers and facilitators of midwifery using the Quality Maternal and Newborn Care (QMNC) Framework.
METHODS: An integrative review was completed by searching PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science and Scopus databases using combinations of "midwifery" and "Bangladesh." The search ranged from 2010 to August 2024. Abstracts were screened against inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were extracted, assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and categorized into the components of the QMNC Framework.
FINDINGS: A total of 23 articles satisfied the inclusion criteria and were included. The identified research encompassed quantitative (n = 3), qualitative (n = 12) and mixed-method studies (n = 8). Barriers and facilitators to care were identified in each component of the QMNC Framework. Key barriers described included inadequate resources, restricted autonomy and scope of practice, deeply ingrained sociocultural values, limitations in woman-centered care, and disparities in education. Important facilitators to high quality care included the adoption of midwifery-led models of care, integration of telehealth services and improvements in education standards.
CONCLUSION: Applying the QMNC Framework highlights that, while barriers hinder the quality of midwifery care in Bangladesh, leveraging key facilitators is crucial for advancing the profession and improving health outcomes.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial Determinants of Mode of Birth in the United States: A Systematic Review of Maternal Clinical and Contextual Influences.
articles.abstract:
