BACKGROUND: Mode of birth (cesarean or vaginal) is critical to long-term maternal and child health, with cesarean delivery, whether planned or unplanned, linked to child morbidities. However, the rates of cesarean deliveries have accounted for one-third of United States births for more than a decade, with global trends reflecting substantial variation in access and use. A comprehensive synthesis of the factors that condition decisions about the mode of birth within this period is lacking. Understanding the role of contextual and maternal risk factors is essential for designing interventions that support equitable and healthy birth experiences, reduce postnatal complications, and improve child health trajectories.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate evidence examining clinical and contextual factors influencing the mode of birth, including planned and unplanned cesarean deliveries in the United States.
METHODS: The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guided the review report. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CINAHL on February 27th, 2025, for studies published between 2015 and 2025. The quality of evidence was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools and the Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool.
FINDINGS: We included N = 24 studies in this review. Maternal medical conditions were associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery. In contrast, contextual factors such as participation in childbirth education and flexible work schedules were linked to a greater likelihood of vaginal birth. Socioeconomic deprivation and access to healthcare contributed to disparities in the mode of birth. Findings reiterate the multifactorial nature of mode of birth decisions and highlight the need for integrated approaches in maternal care.
CONCLUSION: Mode of birth decisions extend beyond maternal medical conditions. Health workers and future research should integrate contextual, psychosocial, and clinical evidence to design multilevel, equitable interventions.

articles.title: Implementation of the Toronto guidelines for childhood cancer staging: experience from 65 population-based cancer registries participating in the BENCHISTA project.
articles.journal: ESMO Real World Data Digit Oncol
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-based cancer registries (PBCRs) are central to measuring childhood cancer outcomes and informing global health policy. The International Benchmarking of Childhood Cancer Survival by Stage (BENCHISTA) project stimulated participating PBCRs to assign stage at diagnosis according to the international Toronto Stage Guidelines (TGs). This study aims to provide a quantitative assessment of operational findings and structural barriers limiting routine TGs implementation within PBCRs participating in the first phase of BENCHISTA.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Seventy-three PBCRs participating in the first phase of BENCHISTA were invited to complete a semistructured survey assessing operational practices, data collection capacity, and structural and operational barriers to routine implementation of the TGs and associated non-stage-prognostic (NSP) variables across six solid childhood tumours. Sixty-five PBCRs from 23 countries provided valid and complete answers.
RESULTS: Before BENCHISTA, 85% PBCRs reported no routine collection of TGs. Following participation, 51% indicated that they would continue staging all childhood cancers. The principal barriers to TGs assignment were workload (38%), lack of linkage with clinical sources (32%), and time required for data retrieval (29%). Molecular NSP variables-particularly rhabdomyosarcoma fusion markers and medulloblastoma subgroups-were the most difficult to capture due to inconsistent pathology reporting and limited registry access to molecular data. Fewer than half had systematic collection of treatment and recurrence data.
CONCLUSIONS: This multinational survey provides a quantitative assessment of barriers limiting routine TGs implementation in PBCRs. Sustaining consistent data collection will require targeted investment in workforce capacity, improved interoperability between clinical and registry systems, and standardisation of clinical, molecular, and pathology reporting frameworks.

articles.title: Long-term implications of appendectomy in children: reappraising the appendix as a functional organ.
articles.abstract: Appendectomy is among the most frequently performed operations in children, and acute appendicitis remains one of the most common pediatric surgical emergencies worldwide. For more than a century, the appendix was regarded as a vestigial structure whose removal carried no lasting consequence, an assumption that underlies the long-standing default of operative management of appendicitis. Two developments now invite reexamination of that assumption: the growing use of nonoperative management for uncomplicated appendicitis, and an expanding body of evidence arguing the appendix is immunologically active and serves as a reservoir for the gut microbiome. This review synthesizes current data on the long-term implications of appendectomy in the pediatric population. We first examine the appendix as a functional organ-its immunologic role, its function as a microbiome reservoir, and its participation in the gut-brain axis. We review its proposed associations with inflammatory bowel disease, systemic autoimmune disease, and Parkinson disease, followed by its oncologic relevance with respect to appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors and colorectal cancer. Much of the evidence is observational, derived from adults, and contradictory. Appendectomy for appropriate indications remains safe and effective, but increasing understanding of the appendix's biology and consequences of its removal may be helpful with shared decision-making.

articles.title: Advances in appendectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.
articles.abstract: Appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency in children and a leading cause of hospitalization among pediatric patients. Over recent decades, considerable advances have transformed both operative and perioperative management of acute uncomplicated appendicitis. This chapter highlights historical and contemporary literature describing the evolution of acute appendicitis management, with an emphasis on surgical innovation and perioperative care in pediatric patients. Surgical management of appendicitis has evolved dramatically from open procedures performed without anesthesia to the current standard of minimally invasive laparoscopic approaches. Laparoscopic appendectomy has largely replaced open appendectomy and become the standard of care due to reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospital stays, faster recovery, and lower surgical site infection rates. Emerging modifications - including single-incision laparoscopic surgery (SILS), endoscopic, and robotic approaches - further minimize invasiveness and improve cosmetic outcomes, though cost and resource availability remain limiting factors. Parallel to these surgical advances, perioperative care has shifted substantially. Appendicitis, once treated as a surgical emergency, is now commonly managed with antibiotics initially and a less urgent surgical approach. Evidence supports the safety of delayed appendectomy up to 24 h after diagnosis following antibiotic initiation. Preoperative antibiotics have remained standard, whereas postoperative antibiotic use in uncomplicated cases is no longer recommended. Enhanced recovery protocols and outpatient pathways have enabled safe same-day discharge following appendectomy, further reducing healthcare utilization and cost.

articles.title: Changes in posture and balance in children with cerebral palsy assessed using DIERS formetric 4D and clinical scales: An exploratory single-group pre-post observational study.
articles.abstract: Spinopelvic alignment contributes to postural control and balance in children with cerebral palsy. This study aimed to evaluate baseline-to-follow-up changes in DIERS Formetric 4D parameters and explore their associations with changes in clinical measures of balance and trunk control. This exploratory, single-group pre-post observational study included 56 children with cerebral palsy aged 5 to 18 years and classified at Gross Motor Function Classification System levels I to III. Participants received individualized rehabilitation as part of routine care. DIERS parameters and Pediatric Balance Scale, Trunk Control Measurement Scale, and Trunk Impairment Scale scores were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Change was calculated as follow-up minus baseline. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure was applied within defined analysis families. The mean age was 9.86 ± 4.37 years, and 48.2% of participants were female. All 10 clinical total and subscale scores improved significantly after correction. Among 40 DIERS parameters, coronal imbalance, pelvic obliquity, apical deviation root mean square, and apical deviation amplitude changed significantly after correction. Of 400 Spearman correlations between DIERS and clinical change scores, 15 had unadjusted P values below .05, but none remained significant after correction. Selected DIERS parameters and clinical measures changed significantly between baseline and follow-up; however, changes in DIERS parameters were not significantly associated with clinical changes after multiple-testing correction. DIERS Formetric 4D may provide supplementary objective information on spinopelvic alignment but should not replace validated clinical assessments. The clinical relevance of longitudinal changes requires confirmation in controlled prospective studies.

articles.title: Prenatal clinical features and clinical outcomes of fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome: A single-center case series of 22 patients.
articles.abstract: This study analyzes 22 fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome in Eastern China to investigate the prenatal clinical features and postnatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study of 22 fetuses diagnosed with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion (312-855 kilobase) via chromosomal microarray analysis among 2607 prenatal cases from January 2022 to September 2024. Parental origin, ultrasound findings, and postnatal outcomes were evaluated. The 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion prevalence was 0.84% (22/2607). Prenatal ultrasound anomalies were observed in 54.5% (12/22), primarily mild cardiac findings (tricuspid regurgitation), choroid plexus cysts, and thickened nuchal translucency. Parental testing (13 cases) revealed 6 paternal, 6 maternal, and 1 de novo case. Postnatal follow-up of 18 live births (mean 14.7 months) showed normal development in most cases (17/18), with 1 child exhibiting delayed language development. Four pregnancies (18.2%) were terminated despite genetic counseling. Our study underscores that the 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion exhibits incomplete penetrance and variable prenatal phenotypes, complicating outcome prediction. Long-term pediatric follow-up is essential, and early reassurance should be avoided even in cases with normal prenatal findings or favorable short-term outcomes.

articles.title: The effect of physical exercise on sleep quality in Chinese middle school students: A cross-sectional study on the mediating role of positive and negative emotions.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the effect of physical exercise (PE1) on sleep quality (SQ) among Chinese middle school students and to further analyze the mediating roles of positive and negative emotions (NE). A total of 1056 middle school students (aged 11-15 years, M = 13.28, SD = 1.08; 516 males, 540 females) from 6 middle schools in Sichuan Province, China, voluntarily participated in this cross-sectional survey. The Physical Activity Rating Scale, Positive and Negative Affect Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index were used in this study. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. Mediation analyses (model 4) were conducted with the PROCESS 3.5 macro, and the significance of indirect effects was tested using a bias-corrected nonparametric percentile bootstrap method with 5000 resamples, generating 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The total effect of PE1 on SQ was not significant (P > .05). After controlling for positive and NE, the direct effect of PE1 on SQ was also non-significant (P > .05). However, both positive emotions (indirect effect = 0.032, 95% CI [0.015, 0.051]) and NE (indirect effect = 0.037, 95% CI [0.012, 0.064]) played significant mediating roles in the relationship between PE1 and SQ. These findings suggest that PE1 improves SQ in middle school students primarily by enhancing positive emotions and reducing NE, rather than through a direct effect.

articles.title: Associations of personalized prenatal care with delivery and perinatal outcomes in women with high-risk pregnancies.
articles.abstract: This study examines whether the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with delivery and perinatal outcomes among women with high-risk pregnancies in a retrospective observational cohort. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 100 women with high-risk pregnancies who delivered between January 2020 and December 2023. Participants were classified according to documented receipt of personalized prenatal care or routine prenatal care. Propensity scores were estimated using maternal age, gravidity, parity, pre pregnancy or early-pregnancy body mass index, gestational age at registration, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, thyroid dysfunction, uterine scar, and history of adverse pregnancy outcomes. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed using a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. All 100 women were retained after matching. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted independent-group comparisons (50 women per group). Vaginal delivery was more frequent in the personalized-care group than in the routine-care group (62.0% vs 40.0%), corresponding to an absolute difference of +22.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], +2.4- + 39.3) and an odds ratio (OR) of 2.45 (95% CI, 1.10-5.47; P = .028). Cesarean delivery occurred in 28.0% and 48.0% of women, respectively, corresponding to an absolute difference of -20.0 percentage points (95% CI, -37.1-- 1.0) and an OR of 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97). Preterm birth occurred in 10.0% versus 26.0% of women (absolute difference, -16.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -30.7- - 0.8; OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.10-0.97; P = .037). One and 5-minute Apgar scores were higher in the personalized-care group (P = .026 and P = .006, respectively). The composite adverse perinatal outcome, defined as the occurrence of at least one of preterm birth, low birth weight, neonatal asphyxia, or neonatal intensive care unit admission, occurred in 16.0% versus 36.0% of women (absolute difference, -20.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -35.8- - 2.8; OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.13-0.88; P = .023). In this study, the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with differences in delivery patterns, selected neonatal outcomes, nursing-compliance measures, and end-of-care psychological scores. The findings represent associations rather than causal effects and should be interpreted in light of the small sample size, residual confounding, and limited statistical power for several individual outcomes.

articles.title: Global burden of HBV/HCV-related liver diseases, 1990-2021, and projections to 2050: A global burden of disease study 2021.
articles.abstract: Despite the availability of measures to control hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related diseases, achieving elimination remains a substantial challenge. Effective action demands accurate assessment of the present and anticipation of the future. We utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2021 to estimate the global burden of HBV- and HCV-related diseases for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We defined HBV/HCV-related liver disease to include chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and cirrhosis attributable to chronic HBV or HCV. The burden was assessed using the age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), stratified by region, age, sex, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI). GBD estimates were reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs); 1990 to 2021 percentage changes were calculated from point estimates. Forecasting analysis was conducted using the GBD 2021 forecast framework, supplemented by Das Gupta decomposition analysis. From 1990 to 2021, the global ASMRs of HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis declined by 41.51% and 31.47%, respectively, while liver cancer-related ASMR showed divergent changes (HBV: -16.40%; HCV: +2.35%). ASDRs also declined across both cirrhosis and liver cancer (HBV: -42.07%, -22.34%; HCV: -29.34%, -8.24%). Regionally, the highest ASMRs for chronic hepatitis B and C including cirrhosis in 2021 were observed in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa (14.51 per 1,00,000) and Central Sub-Saharan Africa (13.92 per 1,00,000), respectively. The burden of both viruses was generally higher in men. Age-specific mortality rates were highest in older age groups across HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases. By the late 2030s, the mortality burden of chronic hepatitis C is projected to surpass that of chronic hepatitis B, amid a slowing annual decline in the ASMR of chronic hepatitis C (-1.21% to -0.24%). Although the overall burden of HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases may decrease or stabilize, sustained progress hinges on equitable access to vaccination, optimized antiviral therapies, and a renewed global focus on HCV as its relative impact grows. Achieving meaningful reductions across SDI contexts will require not only scientific advances but also strategic efforts to improve affordability and distribution, supported by the political will to implement change.

articles.title: Nonlinear relationship between AST/ALT levels and MASLD: A secondary cross-sectional study in healthy Japanese individuals.
articles.abstract: Fatty liver disease is a prevalent condition worldwide, particularly in developed countries. Previous studies have examined the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and both metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcohol-associated liver disease. However, there is a scarcity of research focusing specifically on the association between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. The objective of this study is to investigate the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD in healthy Japanese individuals. This study was a cross-sectional analysis involving 15,464 participants, comprising 7034 men and 8430 women, aged between 18 and 79 years. Data for this secondary analysis were obtained from the Dryad Digital Repository. A medical professional utilized ultrasound imaging to assess the presence of fatty liver disease and administered a questionnaire to gather information about lifestyle factors, including smoking history, alcohol consumption, and exercise habits. Hematological indicators were evaluated at Murakami Memorial Hospital from 2004 to 2015. By adjusting for sex, age, body mass index, waist circumference, regular exercise, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HbA1c (%), alcohol consumption, smoking status, fasting plasma glucose, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, body weight, gamma-glutamyl transferase, and triglycerides, we identified a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. This relationship exhibited a significant notable threshold at an AST/ALT ratio of 0.95, with odds ratio values of 0.03 (0.02, 0.05) when the ratio was <0.95, and 0.32 (0.22, 0.46) when the ratio was greater than or equal to 0.95. Furthermore, in subgroup analyses, we observed that the relationship between AST/ALT levels and fatty liver varied across different subgroups based on gender, alcohol consumption, and smoking status, with the exception of exercise. There is a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD, with a more pronounced negative correlation observed when the ratio is <0.95. These findings suggest that the AST/ALT ratio may provide supportive information for risk stratification in MASLD, particularly when interpreted in conjunction with sex and lifestyle factors. However, prospective validation of the 0.95 threshold in diverse populations is warranted before any clinical application.

articles.title: Relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia. Blood samples were collected from the median cubital vein, and serum IL-6 concentrations were measured using up-converting phosphor technology. Based on the IL-6 concentration results, parturients were categorized into 2 groups: the normal baseline IL-6 group and the elevated baseline IL-6 group. Demographic and clinical data including maternal age, gestational week, height, weight, body mass index, basal body temperature, intra-labor temperature, number of cervical examinations, duration of the first and second stages of labor, neonatal 1-minute and 5-minute Apgar scores, cesarean section rate, instrumental delivery rate, neonatal transfer, and mechanical ventilation were recorded. The overall incidence of intrapartum fever was higher in the elevated IL-6 group, and mean maternal temperature was also higher at 3 and 9 hours after analgesia (P < .05). No significant differences were observed in other indices (P > .05). Elevated baseline IL-6 was associated with a higher unadjusted incidence of intrapartum fever among women receiving epidural labor analgesia.

articles.title: The trends and hotspots of research on polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents over the past three decades: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women, with increasing research attention directed toward adolescent populations. However, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the research landscape in this subspecialty. This study aimed to evaluate global research trends and hotspots in adolescent PCOS over the past 3 decades using bibliometric methods.
METHODS: Publications on adolescent PCOS from 1995 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer and Citespace were employed for data analysis and visualization, while key bibliometric indicators were computed and presented in tabular form.
RESULTS: A total of 1070 publications were included. Research output steadily increased over time, with the United States (n = 384, 35.89%), Turkey (n = 105, 9.81%), and India (n = 82, 7.66%) being the most productive countries. The most prominent institutions included the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Barcelona, and Monash University. Ibanez, Lourdes (n = 34) was the most prolific author, while the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology (n = 84) and the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (highest citations, n = 6921) were the leading publication platforms. Core research areas encompassed mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, metabolism, and clinical outcomes. Keyword burst detection identified "diagnosis" (strength = 14.12) and "luteinizing hormone" (strength = 13.6) as the most intense hotspots. Notably, "quality of life" (2020-2024) and "depression" (2015-2024) emerged as the most recent and ongoing research frontiers.
CONCLUSION: This first bibliometric analysis of adolescent PCOS reveals growing global interest and active international collaborations in this field. Future research is expected to focus on refining diagnostic approaches and improving long-term quality of life for adolescent PCOS.

articles.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.
METHODS: The data are derived from the Web of Science Core Collection and the PubMed database, covering relevant literature on asthma during pregnancy. The time range is from 2008 to 2024. The search strategy combined asthma-related terms ("asthma" OR "bronchial asthma") with pregnancy-related terms ("pregnancy" OR "gestation" OR "gestational"). After screening, 4088 eligible publications were included in the bibliometric analysis. A separate search of PubMed identified 28 clinical trials for the supplementary analysis of clinical research progress. Bibliometric analyses and visualization were performed using the bibliometrix R package (developed by Massimo Aria and Corrado Cuccurullo, Department of Economics and Statistics, University of Naples Federico II [with an academic spin-off, K-Synth Srl, associated with its dissemination]), CiteSpace (developed by Chaomei Chen, College of Computing and Informatics, Drexel University), and VOSviewer (developed by Nees Jan van Eck and Ludo Waltman, Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University).
RESULTS: This study comprised 4088 publications focusing on asthma during pregnancy. Annual publication counts demonstrated a gradual increase with intermittent fluctuations. The United States dominated both in publication output and international collaboration. Litonjua AA, Bisgaard H, and Weiss ST demonstrated high centrality and citation influence among authors. The core contributing journals included Pediatric Allergy and Immunology and Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Major research focuses encompassed mechanistic exploration, influencing factors, and fetal and child health. Research hotspots were primarily concentrated on "air pollution," "birth cohort," "pregnancy complications," and "maternal diet." In recent years, emerging research frontiers have included "inflammation," "impact," "gut microbiota," "climate change," and "survivors." Clinical trial analysis highlighted nutritional interventions (particularly vitamin D) and precision management using biomarkers like fractional exhaled nitric oxide as current research priorities.
CONCLUSION: This work examined the evolving trends and trajectories within pregnancy asthma research, offering a systematic roadmap for subsequent studies. The article highlighted the main contributors, research hotspots, emerging frontier topics, and key directions for future research. This study can serve as a crucial reference for researchers in this field and relevant stakeholders.

articles.title: High detection rate and genetically diverse porcine sapelovirus in diarrheic Tibetan pigs and isolation of a putative recombinant strain on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
articles.abstract: Porcine sapelovirus (PSV) is an enteric pathogen that can cause acute diarrhea, respiratory distress, reproductive failure, and polioencephalomyelitis in pigs. However, no reports have described on the infection status and genetic characteristics of PSV in Tibetan pigs in China. In this study, 452 diarrheic samples were collected from 32 pig farms on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau across five provinces and autonomous regions of China, including Sichuan, Yunnan, Qinghai, Gansu, and Tibet. The results showed that 226 samples detected positive for PSV using RT-PCR, resulting in a total positivity rate of 50.0% (226/452), with region-specific rates varying from 28.1% in Yunnan to 54.5% in Tibet. Phylogenetic analysis of VP1 sequences indicated extensive genetic diversity among Tibetan pig PSV strains: nine strains were grouped into four clades within the PSV-1 genotype, three belonged to the PSV-2 genotype, and one strain (TPQH-2) formed a distinct VP1 lineage between the PSV-1 and PSV-2 genotypes. Importantly, a novel PSV strain (designated TPKD/China/2025) was successfully isolated from Tibetan pigs in PK-15 cells, and its complete genomic sequence was determined. Comparative analysis of the complete ORF region of PSV revealed that TPKD/China/2025 shared the highest nucleotide (86.7-91.1%) and amino acid (95.4-98.5%) identity with clade II of PSV-1 strains. Recombination analysis suggested that TPKD/China/2025 was likely the result of recombination between two Chinese PSV-1 isolates, HuN8 (clade II) and GS01 (clade I). Furthermore, we tested the pathogenicity of TPKD/China/2025 in 14-day-old Tibetan piglets. TPKD/China/2025-challenged piglets developed severe watery diarrhea and intestinal hemorrhage, resulting in a 40% (2/5) mortality rate. Notably, interstitial pneumonia and meningeal congestion and hemorrhage were also observed in challenged piglets, together with detectable PSV RNA in these tissues, indicating that TPKD/China/2025 can induce severe disease in neonatal piglets under the experimental conditions. Our study provides the first evidence of the high detection rate, pronounced genetic diversity, and emergence of a putative recombinant PSV strain in Tibetan pigs, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance and control of PSV in southwestern China.

articles.title: "Longitudinal Adaptive Functioning and Early Intervention Services in Infants and Toddlers with Single Suture Craniosynostosis".
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early adaptive functioning in children with craniosynostosis (CS) is key to understanding development, yet is understudied.
METHODS: This longitudinal prospective study included the Adaptive Behavioral Assessment System-2 in neurodevelopmental evaluations completed preoperatively (Time 1), 6-months (Time 2) and 18-months (Time 3) postoperatively, and at 36 months (Time 4). Adaptive functioning was compared to norms, over time, and with neurodevelopmental delays (<10 th percentile) for each suture group. Associations between General Adaptive Composites (GAC) and patient characteristics were analyzed with regressions. Caregivers reported on autism concerns and therapies.
RESULTS: Participants (N=268) had sagittal (50%), unicoronal (26%), or metopic (24%) CS with surgery at M=7.9±4.3 months (91% <12 months). Participants were mostly Latino (49%) males (67%) with public insurance (57%). Adaptive functioning was generally stable over time and average clinically except for low Self-Care. GAC delay frequencies were: sagittal CS (12.7%), unicoronal CS (15.7%), and metopic CS (28.1%). GAC was significantly lower than norms for metopic CS at Times 2 through 4 (Cohen's d = -0.34, -0.65. -0.41, respectively). Combined GAC and neurodevelopmental delays were: sagittal CS (11.2%), unicoronal CS (10.0%), and metopic CS (21.9%). Higher GAC was associated with younger test age, females, and higher socioeconomic status. A quarter received therapies and 6% had autism concerns.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, adaptive functioning was average and consistent over time. Delays were highest for the metopic CS group. Autism concerns were comparable to local rate of 6.1% and therapies were indicated. Adaptive functioning screenings along with neurodevelopmental evaluations are recommended as part of CS care.

articles.title: Rehabilitation outcomes in children with physical and intellectual disabilities: a 50-year cohort study in Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Worldwide, an estimated 240-million children live with disabilities ‒ representing one-third of all people with disabilities and 1 in 10 children overall. Children with physical or intellectual disabilities experience diverse functional impairments and health complications that require appropriate rehabilitation. The objective of our study was to analyze rehabilitation outcomes for children with disabilities over 50-years.
METHODS: This cohort is based on medical records of patients aged 0 to 18-years with physical or intellectual disabilities who received outpatient rehabilitation at one outpatient rehabilitation center in Brazil from the 1970s to the 2020s.
RESULTS: Childhood disabilities (physical, intellectual, and multiple) have decreased over time, with boys showing a greater predisposition to all types. The primary cause was congenital, often related to events during the perinatal or neonatal developmental phase. Cerebral palsy with tetraplegia was the most common physical disability, while Down syndrome was the most prevalent intellectual disability. Both Rehabilitation Onset Age and Length of Stay in Rehabilitation have decreased over time. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that the age at which rehabilitation began also decreased.
DISCUSSION: The probability of dying by age five is ten times lower than the probability of living with a disability. Improvements in prenatal and neonatal care have played a significant role in reducing the incidence of childhood disabilities over time and have decreased the coexisting disabilities. The incidence of disabilities has decreased, but at the same time, their prevalence has increased, leading to a greater demand for rehabilitation services.
CONCLUSION: Providing access to rehabilitation and early referral are key to achieving the goals of stakeholders (health professionals, families, and patients), regardless of disability (physical or intellectual).

articles.title: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus NSP14 disrupts STAT2-dependent ISGF3 assembly to suppress IFN-β signaling.
articles.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) is a major enteric pathogen of neonatal piglets and continues to cause serious losses in pig production. Although PEDV has been reported to inhibit host innate immunity through multiple strategies, how it modulates IFN-β-induced JAK-STAT signaling remains incompletely defined. Here, we show that PEDV attenuates IFN-β-induced antiviral signaling by inhibiting ISGF3 complex formation. Mechanistically, NSP14 primarily interacted with STAT2, and this interaction was mediated by the coiled-coil domain (CCD) of STAT2. NSP14 targeting of STAT2 reduced the interaction between STAT2 and IRF9, thereby impairing efficient ISGF3 complex assembly and suppressing IFN-β-induced antiviral transcription. These findings identify the STAT2-IRF9/ISGF3 assembly node as a target of PEDV NSP14 and define a mechanism by which NSP14 antagonizes downstream IFN-β antiviral signaling. IMPORTANCE: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) remains a major cause of severe diarrhea and death in young piglets, creating substantial losses for the swine industry. Although the virus is known to weaken the host interferon response, the mechanisms acting after interferon is produced are not fully understood. Here, we show that the PEDV protein NSP14 targets STAT2, a central component of the antiviral JAK-STAT pathway, and disrupts its association with IRF9. This prevents efficient formation of the ISGF3 transcriptional complex and reduces expression of antiviral genes. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized way in which PEDV suppresses host antiviral defenses and expand the known immune-regulatory functions of NSP14 beyond its established roles in viral RNA metabolism. Defining this virus-host interaction provides a clearer understanding of PEDV immune evasion and identifies the STAT2-IRF9/ISGF3 axis as a potential target for future antiviral strategies.

articles.title: Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines, China (Version 2026).
articles.abstract: In June 2026, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and the National Health Commission issued the Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines (Version 2026). Compared with the 2021 version, the key updates include optimization of the five-dose Diphtheria-Tetanus-acellular Pertussis vaccine schedule (with the first dose advanced to 2 months of age and the fifth dose administered at 6 years of age); inclusion of the bivalent human papillomavirus vaccine in the National Immunization Program as a two-dose series for girls aged 13 years (Table 1); and expanded and refined vaccination guidance for children with medical conditions, including preterm and low-birthweight infants, children with allergies, children born to mothers living with human immunodeficiency virus, children with immune function abnormalities, jaundice, common congenital diseases, or common neurological diseases, and children receiving blood products. This English translation provides a reference for public health professionals.

articles.title: Proteomic Analysis of Plasma Small Extracellular Vesicles and Targeted Metabolomic Analysis of Plasma From Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder with deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and unusual stereotyped interests or activities. With a lack of molecular information on the etiology of ASD, early diagnosis of this disease remains a challenge. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as extracellular vesicles containing various important biomolecules, have been demonstrated to have a functional impact on physiological processes in the central nervous system. Herein, we profiled the proteome of plasma sEVs collected from preschool children with autism and performed targeted metabolic analysis on their plasma samples. Screening of the differentiated proteins between autistic and healthy children revealed potential biomarkers, including those involved in calcium ion binding, such as MACF1 and CALM3. Bioinformatic investigation further identified 10 outlier proteins, such as EHD1 and ERF3A, strongly associated with autism. Targeted metabolic analysis and IPA prediction suggested the potential involvement of the PI3K-AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. The sEV proteomic and plasma metabolomic analyses were performed in parallel, and pathway-level findings from each dataset were compared descriptively. These results provide insight into the biological mechanism of autism and promise in determining biomarkers for the early diagnosis of ASD. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier: ChiCTR1800018616.

articles.title: An Integrated webGIS Platform for Monitoring Global Progress in Soil-Transmitted Helminth Control Programmes Based on Preventive Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infections are among the most common neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). This study aimed to assess changes in preventive chemotherapy (PC) programmes, recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) to control STH prevalence and morbidity mainly among pre-school-aged children (PSAC) and school-aged children (SAC) from 2019 to 2024. Monitoring the implementation and impact of PC programmes is essential to evaluate progress towards the STH-specific targets set by the WHO NTD Road Map 2021-2030.
METHODS: The WHO Collaborating Centre ITA-116 for the Diagnosis of Intestinal Helminths and Protozoa has developed an integrated web Geographical Information System (webGIS) containing data from 2019 to 2024 for 86 endemic countries requiring PC and five countries that are believed to have reached prevalence levels compatible with WHO target. Indicators used to monitor the PC programmes were: (i) implementation progress, (ii) STH prevalence, (iii) STH morbidity and (iv) anthelmintic drug donation and distribution.
RESULTS: Up to 2024, the number of countries that reported having conducted impact assessment and modified the programme implementation was 35/91 (38.5%), compared with only 16/91 (17.6%) in 2019. Of these 35 countries, at baseline, 16/35 (45.7%) had an STH prevalence > 20%. By 2024, 13/16 (81.3%) achieved a substantial reduction in prevalence, with a mean decrease of 33.0% compared with baseline. Similarly, 11/13 (84.6%) countries reported the prevalence of moderate-to-heavy intensity (MHI) STH infections below the public health threshold of 2%. Moreover, during this six-year period, the number of children requiring PC for STH declined, reflecting programme reduction in STH prevalence and morbidity.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight substantial progress in reducing STH prevalence and morbidity, confirming the effectiveness of PC programmes. In this context, the webGIS platform provides a valuable tool for monitoring programme implementation and supporting evidence-based decision-making towards achieving the WHO targets for STH control by 2030.

articles.title: Building Systems Capacity in Paediatric Nutrition: A Descriptive Case Study of a Statewide Network and Feeding Team Model for Children and Youth With Special Health Care Needs.
articles.abstract: The Washington State Nutrition Network, a long-standing collaboration between the Washington State Department of Health (DOH), and the University of Washington's Institute on Human Development and Disability (IHDD), focuses on children and youth with special health care needs (CYSHCN). Established in 1987 following a survey administered by the CYSHCN programme and disseminated to neuromuscular centres as part of a statewide Title V Maternal and Child Health (MCH) needs assessment in 1985, the programme is designed to strengthen the capacity of Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs) to meet the complex nutrition and feeding challenges of CYSHCN. The Network demonstrates how a systems-based practice can address statewide access to care for complex paediatric feeding and nutrition by applying systems thinking methodologies, such as leveraging cross-sector relationships, building and distributing workforce capacity, strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration and promoting equitable access, all by continuously evaluating and adjusting the Network's activities. This descriptive case study describes the Nutrition Network's evolution over four decades and by highlighting its impact on workforce capacity, interdisciplinary collaboration and equitable access to care for CYSHCN. Key elements of this established model may serve as a foundation to inform replication of a systems-based approach to improve access and care coordination for children and youth with chronic and complex nutrition and feeding needs nationwide.

articles.title: A National Poison Data System® description of neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome related to maternal kratom use.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Kratom is a drug derived from the Mitragyna speciosa tree that can exhibit dose-dependent stimulant, analgesic, and sedative effects through mu-opioid agonism and other mechanisms. In the United States, kratom is regulated at the state and local level in some areas but is not federally regulated. As such, it is available for purchase at head shops and gas stations in many markets, as well as through the internet. There are limited data describing Neonatal Opioid Withdrawal Syndrome in children born to mothers using kratom. We seek to further describe neonatal kratom-associated withdrawal using cases reported to United States poison centers.
METHODS: This was a retrospective observational study using the National Poison Data System®. We queried the National Poison Data System® for all exposures of kratom in children < 21 days of age from January 1, 2015 through December 31, 2023. We reviewed de-identified notes, or poison centers completed an online data entry form to provide additional data about the exposure.
RESULTS: There were 20 reported exposures; 14 were included. Median symptom duration was eight days. Symptoms included agitation, tremor, increased tone, tachypnea, decrease oral intake, and weight loss. Nine of 14 received opioid therapy (most commonly morphine and/or methadone), generally starting within 1-3 days after the consult when reported.
DISCUSSION: Neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome may occur in a child exposed to kratom in utero. Our data predate widespread availability of 7-hydroxymitragynine products and exposures were reported only as kratom, limiting the interpretation about current risks.
CONCLUSION: Maternal use of kratom during pregnancy is associated with neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome in neonates immediately or shortly following birth. Women who are pregnant or are planning to become pregnant and use kratom should be counseled on possible risks.

articles.title: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative knee bracing following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains common practice despite growing evidence questioning its clinical benefit. Previous studies demonstrated that brace-free rehabilitation was noninferior to brace-based rehabilitation one year after isolated ACLR using hamstring tendon autograft; however, its long-term effects remain unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term effects five years after surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients enrolled in a prospective randomized controlled trial conducted between 2016 and 2019 were recontacted approximately five years after isolated primary ACLR with hamstring tendon autograft for a long-term follow-up. In the original trial, 139 patients had been randomized to postoperative rehabilitation without a brace (n = 71) or with a functional knee brace (n = 68). Participants completed several patient-reported outcome measures. Furthermore, a standardized telephone interview was performed. Changes between the one-year and five-year follow-up were analyzed.
RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients participated in the long-term follow-up (n = 45 brace-free group, n = 52 brace group). Mean follow-up was 5.2 ± 1.0 years. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding subjective knee function, activity level, quality of life, rerupture rate, revision surgery, or persistent knee-related complaints at final follow-up. However, there was a significant interaction between treatment group and time for the subjective IKDC score. Patients treated without postoperative bracing showed stable or slightly improved subjective knee function, whereas patients treated with a brace demonstrated a significant decline between one and five years.
DISCUSSION: Brace-free rehabilitation after isolated ACL reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft remains safe and effective more than five years after surgery. Postoperative bracing did not reduce rerupture rates, revision surgery, or long-term functional impairment. Instead, brace-free rehabilitation demonstrated a more favorable longitudinal development of subjective knee function. These findings further question the routine postoperative prescription of rehabilitative knee braces following isolated ACL reconstruction.

articles.title: Student perceptions of the School eHealth Education Program Pakistan (eSHEPP): a qualitative study of acceptability, feasibility, and awareness of non-communicable diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noncommunicable diseases are a leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality, and many associated risk behaviors emerge during adolescence. In Pakistan, school health education remains limited and largely lecture-based, leaving adolescents insufficiently equipped to adopt healthy behaviors. To address this gap, the School eHealth Education Program Pakistan, a multimedia and mobile application-supported intervention, was developed. This study explored secondary and higher secondary students' perceptions of the program's acceptability, feasibility, and perceived usefulness in improving awareness of noncommunicable diseases following implementation in school settings.
METHODS: A qualitative explanatory study was conducted in four schools in Karachi (two secondary and two higher secondary; two all-girls and two all-boys schools). The program was delivered over 8 weeks through six classroom sessions. Each 20-30-min session included a short dramatized video, followed by guided discussion and interactive quizzes facilitated by a trained facilitator and teacher representative. Twenty-seven students were purposively sampled to ensure variation by school type and gender. Data were collected through four focus group discussions conducted after the intervention using semi-structured guides in Urdu. Thematic analysis was performed using NVivo through a hybrid deductive-inductive approach.
RESULTS: Students described the program as acceptable and easy to understand, highlighting the engaging dramatized videos, clear language, and supportive subtitles. Participants reported increased awareness of noncommunicable diseases and related risk factors. Some students expressed intentions to make healthier dietary choices, increase physical activity, and discourage smoking among peers. The program was considered feasible within existing school schedules and required minimal technological or personnel resources. Students suggested expanding health topics, slightly extending session duration, and incorporating additional interactive features to enhance engagement.
CONCLUSIONS: The program showed strong acceptability, feasibility, and perceived educational value in under-resourced school settings. With improvements in interactivity and integration into school curricula supported by teachers and parents, it may provide a promising model for adolescent health education in similar contexts.

articles.title: Parent-delivered early language intervention for children with Down syndrome: a feasibility randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with Down syndrome experience significant language difficulties which impact a wide range of outcomes. Parents are well-placed to support their child's language development but evidence-based interventions are limited. The primary objective of this feasibility randomised controlled trial was to evaluate the feasibility (recruitment, retention and adherence to intervention) of a parent delivered language intervention for young children with Down syndrome.
METHODS: Thirty families with a child with Down syndrome (aged 3-6 years) living in North-West and South-East England, UK, were randomly allocated to an intervention (delivering language intervention for 20 min a day, 5 days a week, over 30 weeks) or to a waiting control group. Assessments were completed before intervention (t0), immediately after intervention (t1), and 4 months after intervention (t2). The main outcome measures were descriptions of feasibility regarding recruitment and retention, and intervention completion. Acceptability of the programme and trial procedures were also examined. Exploratory outcomes (including researcher-delivered assessments blind to group allocation) addressed effects on children's skills (language, executive function, early literacy); parents (knowledge, skills and confidence, well-being, quality of life); and the home learning environment.
RESULTS: Expressions of interest were received from 81 families, 31 of whom completed screening. Thirty families met criteria for taking part and were randomised to intervention (n = 15) or waiting control group (n = 15). At post-test (t1) and follow up (t2), 27/30 families (90%) completed assessments. Families in the intervention group completed an average of 25 weeks of the 30-week programme with 10 families delivering > 145/150 sessions. These findings met a priori criteria for recruitment, retention, and adherence success. The intervention and trial procedures were positively evaluated by parents. Effects on exploratory outcomes were highly variable across measures (Hedges' g = - 1.64 to 1.07). There were no adverse events related to study participation.
CONCLUSIONS: The trial was feasible to deliver and findings support progression to a definitive trial to evaluate programme effectiveness. Implications for outcomes and measures for the future definitive trial are discussed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN63251282.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes After Dupilumab Initiation for Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether dupilumab initiation is associated with reduced short-term flare burden, healthcare utilization, and surgical escalation in pediatric patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP).
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: TriNetX United States Collaborative Network.
METHODS: Patients aged ≤18 years with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps were identified between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Dupilumab-treated patients were indexed at treatment initiation and propensity score-matched 1:1 to nondupilumab controls indexed at a systemic corticosteroid burst based on asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and prior endoscopic sinus surgery. Outcomes within 12 months were compared using risk ratios.
RESULTS: In 442 matched patients (221 per cohort), dupilumab-treated patients had lower rates of acute sinusitis (12/221 [5.4%] vs 31/221 [14.0%]; risk ratio [RR] 0.39; 95% CI: 0.20-0.73; P = .002), systemic corticosteroid bursts (80/221 [36.2%] vs 101/221 [45.7%]; RR 0.79; 95% CI: 0.63-0.99; P = .042), and functional endoscopic sinus surgery (19/221 [8.6%] vs 38/221 [17.2%]; RR 0.50; 95% CI: 0.30-0.84; P = .007). Nasal polyp diagnoses were more frequently documented in the dupilumab-treated cohort (148/221 [67.0%] vs 95/221 [43.0%]; P < .0001), while emergency department visits (16/221 [7.2%] vs 27/221 [12.2%]; P = .078) and inpatient admissions (12/221 [5.4%] vs 16/221 [7.2%]; P = .435) were similar between cohorts.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that dupilumab may be a steroid-sparing and surgery-sparing option in pediatric CRSwNP.

articles.title: A Single Institution Case Series: Characterization of Facial Nerve Palsy in CHARGE Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: CHARGE syndrome is associated with facial palsy in an estimated 40% of cases, yet its presentation and management remain poorly characterized. We aimed to describe phenotype, imaging, and interventions in affected patients.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective Case Series.
SETTING: Tertiary care pediatric hospital and facial nerve center of excellence.
METHODS: Retrospective review of CHARGE syndrome cases with facial palsy. Demographics, genetic testing, imaging, management, and clinical features were collected; imaging was independently reviewed by a neuroradiologist.
RESULTS: CHARGE syndrome was identified in 65 patients, of whom 12 had facial palsy (58.3% female); 8/12 had confirmed CHD7 mutations. The most common clinical facial palsy presentation was unilateral (10/12), right sided (7/12), and partial (12/12). The majority had comorbid ear abnormalities (12/12) and heart defects (11/12). Surgical intervention was performed in two patients undergoing facial reanimation procedures, while 7 were managed conservatively with ocular lubrication. Imaging (n = 8) revealed facial nerve hypoplasia/absence in 6 cases and facial muscle atrophy in 7. Zygomaticus major muscle thickness demonstrated concordance between the side of greater muscle atrophy and the clinically affected side of facial palsy in 5 cases. All imaged patients demonstrated semicircular canal abnormalities.
CONCLUSION: The most common presentation of facial palsy in CHARGE syndrome was right-sided palsy with ear abnormalities, heart defects, and growth deficiency. Radiographic findings suggest that facial muscle analysis may provide clinical insight in even subtle cases of facial nerve weakness.

articles.title: Clinical and biochemical profile of c.703G>T p.(Glu235*): A novel pathogenic CYP27A1 variant of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis.
articles.abstract: Cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX) is a rare autosomal recessive inherited disease of cholesterol metabolism caused by variants in the CYP27A1 gene, encoding the enzyme sterol-27-hydroxylase of the cytochrome P450 oxidase system. The resulting deficient conversion of cholesterol to bile acids leads to accumulation of intermediate products such as 5α-cholestane-3-β-ol (cholestanol) in body tissues. Patients exhibit prominent multisystemic involvement with phenotypic variability. Early diagnosis is essential for treatment response. Achilles tendon xanthomas are a hallmark of CTX but may present late in the disease course or, in rare cases, not at all. We report a 24-year-old man who was investigated for progressive gait disorder and profound muscle wasting since adolescence. The patient had a history of neonatal-onset chronic diarrhea, childhood osteoporosis and bone fractures, juvenile bilateral cataracts, recurrent nephrolithiasis, progressive cognitive decline, and major psychiatric disorder. Despite the absence of lipid accumulation in tendons and joints, the sequence of symptom presentation was highly suggestive of CTX. The serum levels of 27-hydroxycholesterol were below the limit of detection, whereas 7α-hydroxycholesterol and cholestanol levels were extremely elevated. We documented homozygous presence of the novel CYP27A1 c.703G>T p.(Glu235*) loss-of-function variant. Chenodeoxycholic acid initiation led to overall clinical improvement, including domains associated with significant resistance to treatment such as cognitive function and fine motor skills, along with normalization of cholestanol and intense suppression of 7α-hydroxycholesterol levels.

articles.title: Perspectives of healthcare workers and policy makers on severe neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia and kernicterus spectrum disorders in Northern Nigeria: A multicenter qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the perspectives of healthcare workers(HCWs) and institutional policymakers regarding severe neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia (SHB) and kernicterus spectrum disorder (KSD).
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a multicenter qualitative descriptive study across five tertiary referral hospitals in Nigeria. We conducted 20 key informant interviews with healthcare workers (HCWs) and institutional policymakers. Semi-structured interviews explored knowledge, clinical practices, barriers and facilitators, health system factors, and policy priorities related to neonatal jaundice/hyperbilirubinaemia and KSD prevention. We used a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis approach and triangulated findings against the World Health Organization (WHO) health system building blocks framework.
RESULTS: Seven major themes were identified: (1) disease burden and recognition of SHB/KSD; (2) delayed presentation largely due to poor awareness and harmful cultural practices; (3) health system limitations in prompt management (staffing shortages, delayed bilirubin testing, blood product shortages, equipment failures); (4) ethical and sociocultural barriers to treatment; (5) hearing impairment as an under-recognized consequence; (6) long-term disability and rehabilitation gaps; and (7) prevention opportunities across the continuum of care. Participants described SHB as a common neonatal emergency and an important cause of neuro-disability, and also identified significant systemic failures and delayed care-seeking perceived to stem from cultural practices, poor referral pathways, inadequate rehabilitation services, and weak policy prioritization for newborn health.
CONCLUSION: Key stakeholders perceived neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia and KSD as preventable causes of neuro-disability in Northern Nigeria, highlighting several end-user and systemic factors perpetuating the high burden. We therefore recommend a coordinated health system strengthening approach, community education, reliable diagnostic/treatment infrastructure, and dedicated leadership engagement across the health system to impact the disease burden.

articles.title: Serum Serotonin and Noninvasive Portal Hypertension Indices in Relation to Esophageal Variceal Severity in Cirrhosis: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal varices are a life-threatening consequence of portal hypertension in liver cirrhosis, and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, the reference standard for detecting them, is invasive and resource-intensive. Serum serotonin, over 90% of which is stored in circulating platelets, has been proposed as a candidate biochemical correlate of portal hypertensive and fibrotic change, but its relationship to variceal severity alongside established noninvasive indices has not been well characterized. This study aimed to determine the association of serum serotonin, Child-Pugh class, portal vein diameter, and platelet count to spleen diameter ratio (PSR) with endoscopically graded esophageal variceal severity in patients with liver cirrhosis, and to explore the diagnostic performance of these markers for identifying high-grade varices.
METHODS: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, 140 participants were enrolled into five prespecified groups of fixed size: non-hepatic controls (n = 40), cirrhosis without varices (n = 40), and grade 1 (n = 20), grade 2 (n = 20), and grade 3 (n = 20) esophageal varices confirmed endoscopically. Serum serotonin was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Group comparisons used one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test according to the normality of model residuals, and the chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test for categorical variables. Spearman correlation and multivariable ordinal logistic regression identified independent predictors of variceal grade among the 60 participants with varices, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed diagnostic performance for grade 2/3 varices among the 99 cirrhotic participants with complete data, with bootstrap correction of cutoff-based estimates for optimism and pairwise DeLong comparison of AUCs; a Firth-penalized model was fitted as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Serum serotonin rose progressively across groups, from 30.0 ± 5.6 ng/mL in controls to 106.5 ± 5.2 ng/mL in grade 3 varices (F = 347.575, P < 0.001), and was, together with portal vein diameter, an independent predictor of variceal grade after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio (OR) of 7.48 per 10 ng/mL, P = 0.0009; portal vein diameter adjusted OR of 1.70 per 0.1 mm, P = 0.0002; exploratory model, n = 59). Apparent areas under the curve (AUCs) for grade 2/3 varices were 0.944 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.895-0.980) for serotonin, 0.923 (0.864-0.974) for portal vein diameter, 0.764 for PSR, and 0.746 for Child-Pugh class; serotonin and portal vein diameter did not differ significantly (DeLong P = 0.553), whereas each exceeded PSR and Child-Pugh class (all P ≤ 0.004). Both associations persisted in the penalized model, and optimism correction changed the accuracy estimates only slightly.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, serum serotonin tracked with esophageal variceal severity and, alongside portal vein diameter, was independently associated with variceal grade, with discrimination comparable to that of portal vein diameter. Because the sample was enriched by design and cutoffs were derived and tested in the same cohort, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in unselected surveillance cohorts before clinical use.

articles.title: Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Across the Age, Autoantibody, Phenotype, Treatment, and Outcome Spectrum: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a severe idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by prominent myofiber necrosis, weakness, and marked creatine kinase elevation. Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) and anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) autoantibodies define clinically relevant subgroups, but uncertainty remains regarding age-related presentation, phenotype, treatment response, and outcomes. The objective of this review was to synthesize published evidence on IMNM using a framework that progresses from IMNM diagnosis to age, autoantibody, phenotype, treatment, and outcomes, emphasizing pediatric and adult disease and antibody-defined heterogeneity. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for literature published from 2015 to 2026. Antibody search terms were optional to ensure seronegative disease was not excluded. From 1,541 initially identified records, 66 reports were retained for qualitative synthesis after rigorous screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and risk-of-bias appraisal. Of the 66 retained reports, 78.8% described adult-only and 12.1% pediatric-only populations. The evidence base relies heavily on case-level data, comprising 24 cohorts/comparative studies, 39 case series or reports, and one phase 2 randomized controlled trial (RCT). The single completed RCT (zilucoplan, a complement C5 inhibitor; n = 27, 8 weeks) did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint. Recent literature highlights emerging cardiac, cutaneous, and metabolic manifestations, alongside exploratory use of targeted treatments like chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors. IMNM exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity by age, autoantibody profile, and phenotype. The dominance of case-level evidence and the negative C5-inhibitor RCT underscore a critical need for adequately powered, mechanistically targeted prospective studies, particularly for pediatric, seronegative, and refractory disease.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Associated Risk Factors of Malaria Infection in Loka Abaya District, Sidama Region, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite continuous efforts to manage malaria, it remains a deadly disease, particularly common in low-lying areas of Ethiopia. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence, trends, and risk factors associated with malaria infection in Loka Abaya district, Sidama region, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out using house-to-house visits from April to June 2023. A total of 186 febrile patients were chosen using systematic random sampling. Those above the age of 18 were included in the study. Five health facilities and one primary hospital in the district provided retrospective data. A systematic questionnaire and microscopic analysis of blood films were used to gather data. The blood samples were evaluated in Hantate primary hospital. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the associated factors of malaria infection. Variables with p value less than 5% were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Of 34,613 suspected patients tested for malaria over the previous 5 years, 26.2% were positive. The lowest rate recorded at 20.3% in 2018, whereas 2020 was the highest rate at 30.1%. Among them, 47.4% and 52.6% were females and males, respectively. Age groups from 5 to 14 covered up 21.6%, adults aged over 15 take up to 57.2%, and children under age 5 were 21.2%. The infection distribution was 58.8% for Plasmodium falciparum, 38.8% for Plasmodium vivax, and 2.4% mixed infections. The highest rate of infection was recorded during September to November. Cross-sectional parasitological survey showed that 18.3% of individuals were infected. The identified risk of contracting malaria was significant for individuals who were closer to mosquito breeding sites (AOR, 13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), did not use a mosquito net while sleeping (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), did not use indoor residual spraying in the previous 12 months (AOR,13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), used a window without a screen (AOR, 2.78.3, 95% CI, 1.03-13.86, p < 0.02), used a thatched roof (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), and did not know how malaria is transmitted (AOR, 4.3, 95% CI, 2.36-22.6, p < 0.04).
CONCLUSION: The study indicated that malaria remains a health issue in the Loko Abaya district. Several factors, including low income, wall openings, proximity to mosquito breeding sites, lack of indoor residual spraying, and lack of bed net use, were important predictors of malaria.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and clinical outcomes of primary congenital glaucoma in Xinjiang, China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) is a rare but sight-threatening disease. However, epidemiological data and long-term outcomes of PCG in Xinjiang are lacking. This study aimed to describe the characteristics, epidemiology, treatment, and outcomes of PCG in Xinjiang, China.
METHODS: The study period spanned from January 2003 to December 2024. The study was conducted in two distinct parts: first, an incidence analysis that compiled case data of all PCG patients treated at designated hospitals in Urumqi, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; second, a retrospective analysis of clinical characteristics focusing on PCG patients admitted to the glaucoma ward of Xinjiang 474 Hospital during the same period.
RESULTS: The incidence of PCG was 1 in 20,160 live births (5.0 cases per 100,000). The incidence rate among males was 5.5 per 100,000 live births, while that among females was 4.4 per 100,000 (male relative risk = 1.2). A total of 244 patients with PCG were analyzed, including 144 males (59.0%) and 100 females (41.0%). The median age at presentation was 38.00 months. The infantile type was the most common; the most frequent signs and symptoms were buphthalmos and photophobia with tearing. Trabeculectomy and Trabeculectomy combined with trabeculotomy were the most common surgical procedures. Age at onset was positively correlated with axial length and negatively correlated with visual acuity; patients with delayed presentation had longer axial lengths and poorer visual acuity. Intraocular pressure (IOP) was well-controlled at the final follow-up, and the reoperation rate was 13.9%.
CONCLUSION: The incidence of PCG in Xinjiang is comparable to international levels, with a high proportion of male and Uyghur patients, and delayed presentation is common. Significant differences were observed across age groups at onset: individuals with earlier onset had higher IOP and more severe visual impairment. Timely diagnosis and combined surgical procedures can effectively control IOP; early screening and standardized intervention are key to improving the prognosis of PCG and reducing blindness.

articles.title: Uveitic glaucoma in a multi-ethnic Malaysian cohort: demography, risk factors and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between uveitis and secondary glaucoma has been established, but the specific factors associated with progression to uveitic glaucoma remain poorly defined. This study aims to identify the prevalence and factors associated with uveitic glaucoma, and their clinical outcomes in a Malaysian cohort.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study reviewing the clinical records of patients who attended the uveitis clinics at tertiary eye centres in Kuala Lumpur and Sarawak, Malaysia.
RESULTS: A total of 257 eyes from 163 patients were included. Mean age at uveitis onset was 37.3 ± 16.2 years with a slight female predominance. The prevalence of uveitic ocular hypertension and uveitic glaucoma was 26.1% and 30.0% respectively. Multiple logistic regression identified age of onset (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.023; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.003-1.044, p = 0.023), male gender (aOR 1.970; 95% CI 1.046-3.709, p = 0.036), presence of posterior synechiae (PS) (aOR 3.326; 95% CI 1.092-10.133, p = 0.034), peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) (aOR 4.606; 95% CI 2.065-10.272, p < 0.001) and intraocular pressure (IOP) at presentation (aOR 1.077; 95% CI 1.039-1.117, p < 0.001) as significant factors for uveitic glaucoma. Steroid responsiveness occurred in 74 (29.2%) corticosteroid-treated eyes. Fifty-three eyes (36.80%) required at least one glaucoma incisional surgery. Chronic uveitis (p = 0.004) and PAS (p < 0.001) were associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Older age of onset, male gender, presence of PS or PAS, and elevated presenting IOP were significant factors associated with uveitic glaucoma. Additionally, chronic uveitis and PAS were factors associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery. Early identification of these factors can prevent onset of uveitic glaucoma, which is a potential blinding complication of uveitis.

articles.title: Increased choriocapillaris non-perfusion in pediatric hypertension assessed by optical coherence tomography angiography(OCTA).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate retinal microvascular changes in pediatric patients with systemic hypertension compared with healthy controls using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 94 pediatric patients (94 eyes; age 6-18 years) with systemic hypertension followed for at least one year and 60 age- and sex-comparable healthy controls. All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmologic examination. OCT was used to measure foveal thickness (FT) and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT). OCTA assessed vascular density (VD) in the superficial and deep capillary plexuses (SCP, DCP), optic nerve head (ONH), foveal avascular zone (FAZ), and choriocapillaris non-perfused area (NPCA) ratio. Body mass index (BMI) and microalbuminuria status were recorded.
RESULTS: FT, SFCT, SCP, DCP, FAZ, and ONH VD did not differ significantly between hypertensive patients and controls (p > 0.05). In contrast, NPCA ratios were significantly higher in the hypertensive group across all measured regions (0.5 mm, 0.5-1.5 mm, and 1.5-3 mm; p < 0.001). Within the hypertensive group, microalbuminuria-negative patients showed higher NPCA ratios in the 0.5 mm and 0.5-1.5 mm regions compared with microalbuminuria-positive patients (p < 0.05), although post hoc power was low. BMI demonstrated a weak negative correlation with DCP vessel density (p < 0.05). In multivariable regression analysis, systemic hypertension remained independently associated with increased NPCA values after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric patients with systemic hypertension without clinical retinopathy show increased choriocapillaris non-perfusion on OCTA, suggesting early subclinical microvascular involvement. OCTA-derived NPCA measurements may reflect early subclinical microvascular alterations associated with pediatric hypertension in children before conventional funduscopic findings become apparent.

articles.title: The influence of suture material selection on maternal and neonatal outcomes in cervical cerclage: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to compare the effects of different suture materials on pregnancy outcome after cervical cerclage, so as to provide basis for better guiding clinical treatment.
METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study, 145 women who underwent history-, ultrasound-, or physical examination-indicated transvaginal cervical cerclage were categorized according to suture materials used for cerclage: a total of 76 received Mersilene tape and 69 received braided suture. The study participants received transvaginal cervical cerclage before 28 weeks and were followed up until delivery to assess pregnancy and neonatal outcomes. The primary outcome of interest is the duration of pregnancy following cervical cerclage surgery. Secondary outcomes encompass the incidence of preterm rupture of membranes (PROM) subsequent to cervical cerclage, placental abruption, cervical lacerations, chorioamnionitis, neonatal survival rates, and neonatal intensive care unit(NICU) admission rates. The study evaluated the effect of two types of suture materials on maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: In this study, compared with the women who used double-stranded braided, the average gestational age of women who used Mersilene cerclage material was prolonged(37.00weeks vs33.00weeks, P = 0.011), the pregnancy time after cerclage was prolonged and the length of cervical closed line after cerclage was longer(92days vs. 72days, P = 0.004), the occurrence of chorioamnionitis among patients utilizing Mersilene tape was markedly lower compared to the braided sutures cohort (5.6% vs. 17.5%, P = 0.030). The neonatal birth weight of patients who utilized the Mersilene tape was markedly greater than that of the braided sutures group (2551.04 ± 945.54 g vs. 2054.68 ± 1116.09 g, P = 0.007), and the neonatal mortality rate was considerably lower (6.9% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.009). But through multivariate logistic regression analyses shown that there are no significant association between cerclage materials and chorioamnionitis was found in this study (OR 0.392(0.022-7.109), P = 0.392).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that the use of Mersilene tape for cervical cerclage offers benefits, including an extension of gestation, a reduction in infection rates, and an enhancement in neonatal outcomes. The retrospective nature of this study precludes definitive causal inferences, and findings should be interpreted with caution. Future research can explore different cerclage materials' effects in larger populations.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of keratoconus in Kilimanjaro region: a population-based evaluation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE STUDY: The study aimed to determine the distribution and determinants of keratoconus (KC) among individuals aged 12-45 years in the Kilimanjaro region, where epidemiological data are currently lacking.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional population-based screening was conducted between July 2024 and January 2025 among secondary schools, college and community members. Screening involved six steps: registration and visual acuity assessment, autokerato-refractometry, the Keratoconus Risk Investigative Survey (KRIS), retinoscopy, corneal topography, and counselling or referral. KC diagnosis and classification was based on a total weighted score ≥ 6-10 (scissor reflex, myopia >-5D, astigmatism ≤ 2.5D, Kmax > 46.5D, I-S > 1.4, steep K > 47D) and KC-suspect if score 2-5 including presence of scissor reflex and/or irregular astigmatism; and no KC if score < 2. Data were analyzed. using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 26 and Stata version 14.
RESULTS: A total of 2,354 participants (49.7% female, 50.3% male), the majority of whom were Black African adolescents, aged 12-19 years, were screened. The prevalence of KC was 1.2% (95% CI: 0.8-1.7), with a mean age of 20.7 ± 7.2 years. Univariate analysis showed associations between KC and male gender (OR = 2.6, p = 0.016), age 12-24 years (OR = 4.0, p = 0.001), eczema (OR = 33.7, p < 0.001), and asthma (OR = 5.5, p = 0.011). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that only eczema is significantly associated with KC.
