Further investigation in large cohort studies is needed to clarify the role of mTOR signaling in SE and to evaluate the effects of mTOR inhibitors and immunotherapies on outcomes in patients with SE/RSE.

articles.title: Employing Implementation Science to Move from Paper to Practice.
articles.abstract: Implementation Science studies evidence practice gap separating innovation from clinical practice and designs interventions to close this gap. Process, determinant and evaluation frameworks provide a systematic way to ensure Implementation Science efforts are planned in a comprehensive and standardized format maintaining core components of the intervention but allowing for context-specific adaptations necessary for sustainment. Logic models provide a blueprint to allow for the operationalization of these models and frameworks. Otherwise, I would add one more sentence. Evaluation is a critical piece of all implementation science work from pre- to post-implementation and can be accomplished through evaluation frameworks. Future efforts are needed to close evidence to practice gaps that exist in the field of allergy-immunology, including crucial technological advancements proven to improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Associations Between Frequency of Smokeless Tobacco and Oral Nicotine Product Use and Suicidality Among High School Students in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited research has examined associations between adolescent smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use and suicidality. Even less is known about how these associations vary by frequency of use.
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use and suicidality among a nationally representative sample of high school students in the United States.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.
METHODS: Data from the 2023 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (n = 17,807) were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use (0 days, 1-5 days, 6-19 days, 20-30 days) and four outcomes: persistent sadness or hopelessness, suicidal ideation, suicide planning, and suicide attempt. Models adjusted for sex, race, ethnicity, grade, and alcohol use. Linear trends across frequency categories were tested. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for other tobacco product use.
RESULTS: Approximately 2% of students reported past 30-day smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use. Compared to no use, heavy use was associated with higher odds of all four outcomes (aORs = 2.11-9.64); moderate use was associated with higher odds of sadness or hopelessness, suicide planning, and suicide attempt (aORs = 2.14-4.91); and light use was associated with higher odds of suicide attempt (aORs = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.74-4.88). Positive linear trends were observed for all four outcomes (p <0.001). Sensitivity analyses showed that compared to no use, heavy use was associated with higher odds of suicide planning (aOR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.23-3.30) and suicide attempt (aOR = 5.63, 95% CI: 2.67-11.88) and light use was associated with higher odds of suicide attempt (aOR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.03-2.77).
CONCLUSION: Frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use was associated with persistent sadness or hopelessness and suicidality. These associations were attenuated after adjusting for other tobacco product use. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal ordering.

articles.title: Association of Parenting Styles and Parental Involvement with the Mental Health of Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize quantitative evidence on associations among parenting styles, parental involvement, and mental health outcomes among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews (ScR) guidelines. Literature published between January 1993 and May 2025 was searched across four databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library). Search terms included Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), title/abstract (ti/ab), and text words (tw). This review included only original quantitative studies examining relationships among parenting styles, parental involvement, mental health outcomes, and glycemic control in adolescents aged 10-19 years with Type 1 diabetes. Qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, and review articles were excluded.
RESULTS: Out of 486 identified studies, 10 met the inclusion criteria, seven focusing on parent-child dyads and three on adolescents only. Across the included studies, supportive and collaborative parenting was consistently linked to fewer depressive symptoms, higher quality of life (QOL), greater self-efficacy, better adherence, and improved HbA1c levels. Conversely, controlling, overinvolved, or uninvolved parenting tended to be associated with increased depressive symptoms, lower QOL, and poorer glycemic control.
CONCLUSIONS: Parenting styles and parental involvement appear to be important factors associated with both psychological adjustment and glycemic control among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes. Although this review did not test a specific theoretical model, the findings can be interpreted through the lens of self-determination theory, underscoring the importance of autonomy support. Future research requires greater conceptual clarity and international standardization of autonomy support measures.

articles.title: Retention Across Developmental Stages: Insights from a Longitudinal Birth Cohort.
articles.abstract: Sustained participant retention is critical to the validity of longitudinal pediatric cohort studies yet remains an operational challenge-particularly in resource-limited settings. We evaluated retention patterns and contributing factors in the Urban Environment and Childhood Asthma (URECA) birth cohort, a multisite study that followed 609 children (49.0% female; 51.0% male) from birth through late adolescence (up to age 17) across four U.S. cities. Overall, 382 (62.7%) of participants completed final assessments at the last planned study visit. Attrition was highest during the first year of life and declined thereafter. Younger maternal age at delivery (<18 years (48% vs 64% for ≥ 18 years) and failure to complete an early-life home visit (44% vs 67% for completed) were significantly associated with lower retention, whereas most other maternal sociodemographic and psychosocial characteristics were not. Adolescent participant factors, including school enrollment, residential stability, anxiety, and depression, were similarly not associated with retention. High retention was sustained through adolescence and during COVID-19-related disruptions, alongside continuity in core study staff, strong and enduring participant-study relationships, flexible communication strategies, participant-centered engagement, and practices designed to reduce logistical barriers. These findings suggest that long-term retention in urban pediatric cohorts is associated with early engagement and the reported/perceived trust and reciprocal relationships over time. Relationship-centered, adaptive, and barrier-reducing approaches may be particularly relevant to supporting sustained participation across developmental transitions and external disruptions.

articles.title: Early Life Interventions in IgE-mediated Food Allergy Prevention and Management.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has become a major public health concern. Over the past decade, advances in understanding early immune development have transformed approaches to both prevention and treatment of IgE-mediated food allergy. Landmark trials demonstrated that early and sustained introduction of allergenic foods, particularly peanut and egg, significantly reduces the risk of food allergy. This lead to a paradigm shift from allergen avoidance to proactive early introduction. For children who develop food allergy, emerging evidence indicates that early intervention may offer unique advantages, possibly due to heightened immune plasticity. Oral, epicutaneous, and sublingual immunotherapy have shown efficacy in increasing allergen tolerance, with studies suggesting improved outcomes and greater likelihood of remission when initiated in early childhood. Mechanistic studies indicate that these therapies modify allergic immune responses through suppression of effector cells, induction of regulatory pathways, and increased production of protective allergen-specific antibodies. In addition, omalizumab has become the first biologic approved in the United States for food allergy in individuals aged ≥1 year. Despite substantial progress, important knowledge gaps remain. Continued integration of mechanistic discoveries, clinical trials, and real-world evidence will be essential to refine precision approaches that maximize prevention, improve treatment outcomes, and reduce the lifelong burden of food allergy.

articles.title: Redefining the Self in Adolescent and Young Adult Survivors of Childhood Cancer: Identity Attributes From a Qualitative Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although survival rates in childhood cancer have improved substantially, survivorship remains a complex and ongoing process marked by identity reconstruction, shaped by developmental transitions, late effects, and the contested meanings of being a "survivor."
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize qualitative evidence on how adolescents and young adults (AYAs) who survived childhood cancer construct their identities and the meanings they attribute to being a "survivor."
METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted using the SPIDER framework. Eligible studies were original qualitative research exploring identity among AYAs diagnosed with cancer during childhood or adolescence who had completed treatment. Publications in English, Portuguese, or Spanish were included. Methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research, and data were analyzed through thematic synthesis.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. Two analytical themes, each supported by 2 descriptive themes, were identified: (1) Identity Configurations and Self-Redefinition, reflecting ambivalence in adopting the "survivor" identity, and (2) The Dual Imprint of Identity, describing the coexistence of personal growth and persistent late effects. Social recognition also shaped identity construction.
CONCLUSION: Identity in childhood cancer survivorship is characterized by ambivalence and a dual imprint of growth and limitation. Survivorship is experienced as an ongoing presence rather than a completed phase.
IMPLICATIONS FOR ONCOLOGY NURSING PRACTICE: Nursing care should incorporate identity-sensitive approaches that support reflection, self-expression, and recognition of individual strengths. Addressing identity in survivorship can promote psychosocial adjustment, autonomy, and long-term well-being among AYAs, reinforcing the need for person-centered oncology nursing care.

articles.title: Earlier and More Criteria-Based Return to Sport After Pediatric Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in North America Compared With the Asia-Pacific Region: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the management and rehabilitation strategies for pediatric anterior cruciate ligament injuries between North America and the Asia-Pacific region.
METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library was performed for studies published between January 2020 and August 2025. Articles were included if they described pediatric anterior cruciate ligament rehabilitation protocols for patients 18 years and younger. Included studies consisted primarily of retrospective studies, cohort studies, case series, technical notes, and cross-sectional studies (Levels II-IV). Data were extracted on bracing use and duration, weight-bearing status, range-of-motion restrictions, sports progression, and return-to-sport criteria.
RESULTS: Forty studies were included (27 North America, 13 Asia-Pacific). Bracing was used frequently in both North America (86%) and Asia-Pacific (72%), with North American protocols often specifying duration (2-6 weeks) or criteria-based discontinuation, whereas Asia-Pacific protocols frequently omitted details. Early range-of-motion restoration was advocated in both regions (North America 85%, Asia-Pacific 91%), although restrictions were applied when meniscal repair was performed. Both regions supported early weight-bearing regardless of surgical technique. Both regions shared similar timelines for running and jogging restrictions; however, North American centers (60%) introduced sport-specific drills earlier between 3 and 6 months. Return-to-sport clearance was delayed beyond 9 months in most protocols (North America 46%, Asia-Pacific 62%). North American center, however, showed more flexibility with 46% allowing return-to-sport clearance before 9 months. North American centers more often incorporated functional criteria (50%) alongside time-based measures, whereas Asia-Pacific centers relied primarily on time-based thresholds.
CONCLUSIONS: Early rehabilitation protocols after pediatric anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction were similar between North America and the Asia-Pacific region with respect to bracing, weight-bearing, and range-of-motion practices. However, return-to-sport progression differed because North American centers more frequently introduced sport-specific activities earlier and more commonly incorporated functional criteria in addition to time-based thresholds, whereas Asia-Pacific centers more often relied on time-based clearance and delayed sport-specific progression.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, systematic review of Level II to IV evidence.

articles.title: Clinical and proteomic features of children with Type 2-low asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biologics for Type 2 (T2) inflammation have advanced asthma care, but T2-low asthma is relatively common in children and remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: This study compared clinical and proteomic features of T2-low and T2-high asthma in difficult-to-treat children age 6-18 years.
METHODS: T2 subgroups were defined with k-means cluster analysis of blood eosinophils, total IgE, and positive aeroallergens. Clinical features were assessed at baseline, after systemic corticosteroids, and at 12 months. Exploratory proteomics analyses for ∼4,000 plasma proteins were performed in a subset and analyzed with CytoMod to identify modules of co-signaling proteins. Pathway analyses were performed with Reactome.
RESULTS: 361 children were enrolled (T2-low, N=65; T2-intermediate, N=141; T2-high, N=155). T2 groupings were biologically and temporally stable. Although all groups had a clinically significant symptom and exacerbation burden, children with T2-low asthma had more infectious comorbidity, lesser exacerbation severity, and higher lung function. CytoMod analyses identified three protein modules. Module 1 was strongly associated with T2-low asthma and contained 80 proteins encompassing 18 biological pathways. Notable proteins in Module 1 included signal transducer and activator of transcription 5A, collagens, and extracellular matrix proteins.
CONCLUSION: Children with T2-low asthma have a different clinical phenotype with more preserved lung function despite symptoms and exacerbations. Exploratory analyses suggest the proteome of children with T2-low asthma also differs, with co-signaling modular analyses implicating extracellular matrix and signaling pathways for future study.

articles.title: Development and validation of a LC-MS/MS method for the quantification of 22 antiepileptic drugs in saliva.
articles.journal: J Chromatogr B Analyt Technol Biomed Life Sci
articles.abstract: Worldwide, 50 million people of all ages are affected by epileptic seizures. Drug therapy is the cornerstone of epilepsy management, but treatments are difficult to equilibrate due to the wide variability in plasma concentrations of antiepileptic drugs (AED), which results in unpredictable dosing. However, target plasma concentrations are known, and therefore therapy monitoring is carried out by measuring drug concentrations to guide dose adjustment. Increasing accessibility to therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is therefore a major issue. Saliva offers an attractive alternative to blood due to its non-invasive collection method, particularly in children and the elderly. However, standardization of saliva collection is mandatory to study the relationship between saliva and plasma concentrations properly, and to explore the feasibility of TDM in saliva. The assay reported here has been validated according to the European Medicine Agency guidelines for 22 AED in saliva collected using the Quantisal® sampling device. The results demonstrate the reliability of the method which offers reproducible saliva collection and ensures analyte stability up to 7 days before sample processing. This assay will be used as part of a clinical study designed to demonstrate its clinical applicability and investigate the relationship between saliva and plasma concentrations of AED, to verify whether saliva could be used as an alternative to blood for monitoring antiepileptic treatment.

articles.title: Advancing neuropsychological and neurodevelopmental outcome measurement in pediatric epilepsy surgery.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy surgery is the most effective treatment for appropriately selected children with drug-resistant epilepsy, however, surgical success continues to be defined primarily by seizure outcomes. Neuropsychological and neurodevelopmental outcomes are inconsistently assessed, and children with substantial developmental or neurological impairment may be systematically underrepresented in postoperative outcome data. We conducted an overview of systematic reviews published from 2015 to 2025 that reported outcomes after pediatric epilepsy surgery, with particular emphasis on cognitive, developmental, adaptive, behavioral, and quality-of-life domains. Among 50 eligible systematic reviews, only 22 (44%) reported neuropsychological or cognitive outcomes. Global cognitive measures predominated, whereas language, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed were substantially less frequently assessed. Only nine reviews quantitatively synthesized neurocognitive or developmental outcomes, and substantial heterogeneity in assessment instruments, baseline testing, and postoperative follow-up limited cross-study comparability. These findings highlight the need to move beyond whether neuropsychological testing is performed toward standardized measurement of meaningful longitudinal change. We propose a framework incorporating common core outcome domains, prespecified assessment intervals, developmentally appropriate and floor-sensitive measures, and inclusion of children unable to complete conventional norm-referenced testing. Prospective integration of harmonized neuropsychological trajectories with structural and functional connectomic measures may further clarify how seizure control, surgical network disruption, and neuroplasticity shape postoperative development. Pediatric epilepsy surgery outcomes should therefore encompass both seizure control and preservation or improvement of cognitive, developmental, adaptive, and functional trajectories.

articles.title: DNA methylation profiling of the RELN gene using MSP in Iraqi pediatric patients with epilepsy: A case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy is one of the most common neurological disorders in children and is influenced by both genetic and epigenetic mechanisms. Altered DNA methylation may contribute to disease susceptibility through changes in gene regulation. The RELN gene is involved in neuronal migration, synaptic plasticity, and brain development, making it a potential target for epigenetic investigation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between RELN methylation levels and pediatric epilepsy and to investigate its potential diagnostic value.
METHODS: A case-control study was conducted involving 47 pediatric epilepsy patients and 39 healthy controls. Genomic DNA was extracted and validated prior to methylation analysis. Quantitative real-time PCR using methylation-specific primers was performed to determine RELN methylation percentage. Statistical analyses included Mann-Whitney testing, logistic regression analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and Spearman correlation analysis.
RESULTS: RELN methylation percentage was significantly higher in patients compared with controls (11.60% [8.88-14.61] vs. 7.77% [6.87-10.73], P < 0.0001). ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory performance with an AUC of 0.811 (95% CI: 0.712-0.887), sensitivity of 80.85%, and specificity of 74.36% at a cutoff value > 8.545%. Logistic regression analysis identified RELN methylation as an independent predictor of epilepsy (adjusted OR=1.537, 95% CI: 1.240-1.906, P < 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between RELN methylation and age, age at first seizure, or days since the last seizure.
CONCLUSION: Increased RELN methylation was significantly associated with pediatric epilepsy and independently predicted disease status, suggesting a potential role for RELN methylation as an epigenetic biomarker in epilepsy.

articles.title: Maternal Substance Use During Pregnancy and Congenital Syphilis Among Hospitalized Neonates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: US congenital syphilis (CS) cases have increased 10-fold in the past decade, exceeding 3700 cases in 2022. This study evaluated the association between maternal substance use during pregnancy and CS among hospitalized neonates by region and year.
METHODS: We analyzed hospitalized neonates (postnatal age ≤28 days) in the Kids' Inpatient Database from 2016, 2019, and 2022. We identified CS using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes and categorized maternal substance use as no substance use, single substance use, or polysubstance use. Using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, we tested effect modification by region and year.
RESULTS: Among 4 531 346 hospitalized neonates, 217 220 (weighted prevalence = 2.5%) had maternal substance use during pregnancy. CS prevalence among substance-exposed neonates increased 467% from 2.5 to 14.5 per 1000 neonates between 2016 and 2022, compared with 0.2 to 0.8 per 1000 neonates among unexposed neonates. After adjusting for demographic charateristics, health insurance status, median household income, housing insecurity, year, and region, single substance use and polysubstance use were associated with higher odds of CS (single substance use: adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 9.68; 95% CI, 8.88-10.55; and polysubstance use: AOR = 17.18; 95% CI, 15.21-19.40). We observed a significant effect modification: the association was much stronger in the West region of the United States (interaction OR = 4.80; 95% CI, 3.10-7.44) than in the Northeast, and the polysubstance use association was significantly elevated in 2022 relative to 2016 (interaction OR = 3.10; 95% CI, 1.81-5.30).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal substance use was strongly associated with CS. These findings underscore the need to address structural barriers to prenatal care through the expansion and integration of syphilis screening within substance use treatment and harm-reduction contexts, especially in regions with a high burden of CS.

articles.title: Non-Typhoidal Salmonellosis Outbreak in Humans Linked to Dry Dog Food, United States, 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Salmonellosis outbreaks affecting humans have infrequently been linked to pet foods or treats, but surveillance of foodborne pathogens in pet foods is important for protecting public health. We describe how surveillance testing of dry dog food resulted in detection of an outbreak of human illnesses caused by Salmonella serotype Kiambu.
METHODS: A state agency isolated Salmonella serotype Kiambu from a bag of Brand A dry dog food purchased at a retail store as part of a US Food and Drug Administration surveillance program. Whole-genome sequencing analysis by core-genome multi-locus sequence typing determined that the isolate detected in pet food was genetically related to Salmonella isolates obtained from ill people. A multistate outbreak investigation was initiated to collect exposure information from patients and to determine measures needed to prevent illnesses.
RESULTS: Seven patients from 7 states were infected with the outbreak strain; 6 of 7 patients were aged ≤1 year. Illness onset dates spanned January 14 to August 19, 2023. Three of 5 patients reported feeding Brand A dry dog food to their dogs. Voluntary recalls were issued for all dog and cat food products produced at the same facility as Brand A. Public communications were issued regarding this outbreak and for the voluntary recalls.
CONCLUSIONS: This outbreak might not have been detected without surveillance testing of pet food products for enteric pathogens. Outbreaks related to dry pet food can be protracted because of the extended shelf life of these products. Enteric pathogens that contaminate pet products can result in infant illness. It is important to educate caregivers about the importance of handwashing after feeding pets and the proper ways to clean and disinfect pet feeding equipment.

articles.title: KRAS Mutations in Ectomesenchymal Chondromyxoid Tumors: A Molecular Analysis of Cases in Tongue and Extra-Glossal Sites.
articles.abstract: Ectomesenchymal chondromyxoid tumor (EMCMT) is a rare mesenchymal indolent neoplasm of the oral cavity, with a marked predilection for the tongue. Extra-glossal tumors are exceedingly rare, and their pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Herein, we retrospectively collected seven extra-glossal and five tongue cases of EMCMT, and examined the molecular features of eleven cases using targeted molecular approaches. EWSR1, PLAG1 and RREB1::MRTFB rearrangements were evaluated, whereas hotspot mutations in EGFR, BRAF, NRAS, KRAS and PIK3CA were screened by pyrosequencing, and detected mutations were subsequently confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The tumors affected seven male and five female patients with an age range of 12 to 57 years (median, 23.0). The cases occurred in the tongue (n = 5), palate (n = 3), alveolar ridge (n = 2), buccal mucosa (n = 1) and gingiva (n = 1). All tumors were treated by local excision; after a median follow-up of 21 months (range, 7-31), three tumors (25.0%) recurred locally and were controlled by re-excision. Morphologically, the tumors were composed of spindle to ovoid-shaped cells arranged in a hyalinized stroma, often demonstrating myxoid and chondroid areas. Cases showed immunoreactivity for podoplanin, S-100 and GFAP and variable (focal or diffuse) reactivity for AE1/AE3 and EMA, and were negative for cytokeratin 7, SMA, calponin and p63. The RREB1::MRTFB fusion was detected in all eleven tumors screened (100.0%), and none of the cases investigated showed EWSR1 or PLAG1 rearrangements. Additionally, 7 of 11 tumors screened (63.6%) harbored KRAS mutations, comprising p.G12D alone (n = 2), KRAS p.G13D (n = 4), or combined KRAS p.G12D and p.G12V variants (n = 1). KRAS hotspot mutations, not previously reported in EMCMT, were frequent in this series (mutant allele frequencies, 29.7-54.9%) and invariably co-occurred with RREB1::MRTFB fusion; their clonal allele frequencies indicate an early event, although their biological significance remains to be determined. Local recurrence occurred irrespective of anatomic site or KRAS status. Detection of RREB1::MRTFB fusion remains the most useful ancillary tool to separate EMCMT from its mimics, particularly myoepithelial neoplasms, whereas the diagnostic utility of KRAS testing requires evaluation in larger, controlled cohorts.

articles.title: Beyond Factor Levels: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Outcome and Bleeding Risk in Congenital Factor VII Deficiency.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCongenital factor VII (FVII) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive bleeding disorder with highly variable clinical expression. Pregnancy management is difficult because FVII activity may rise during gestation in heterozygous women, yet bleeding phenotype and peripartum outcomes correlate poorly with factor level.ObjectiveTo summarize published pregnancies in women with congenital FVII deficiency, clarify how FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, hemostatic prophylaxis, and obstetric factors relate to maternal and neonatal outcomes, and review the reported efficacy and safety of available treatment options.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with descriptive synthesis of published pregnancy cases. PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched from database inception, covering publications available through May 2026. Case reports and case series describing pregnancy outcomes in women with confirmed or presumed congenital FVII deficiency were included. Data were extracted on demographics, genotype or zygosity where reported, FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, anesthesia, prophylaxis, estimated blood loss, thrombotic events, and neonatal outcomes.Bleeding outcomes were standardized using the contemporary ACOG definition of primary PPH, while other clinically significant obstetric bleeding was recorded separately using intervention-based criteria.ResultsForty-five pregnancies from 30 published reports (1992-2026) across 17 countries were identified. Delivery was vaginal in 23 cases and by cesarean section in 20 cases; one case involved medical termination and one did not specify the delivery mode. Severe deficiency (FVII <10%) was present in 27 cases. Among the published cases with evaluable prophylaxis status, hemostatic prophylaxis was administered in 32 of 44 pregnancies (73%). Five of 45 published pregnancies (11%) met contemporary criteria for primary PPH. Five additional cases had other clinically significant primary or peripartum bleeding requiring therapeutic intervention but did not meet contemporary PPH criteria. One source-reported PPH case could not be classified because blood-loss volume and hypovolemia were insufficiently reported. Secondary PPH and clinically significant antepartum hemorrhage occurred in one case each. Most bleeding episodes with a documented etiology were attributable to obstetric or surgical causes, including uterine atony, genital tract laceration, or placental abruption with disseminated intravascular coagulation. However, one recent undiagnosed case developed refractory postpartum hemorrhage after common obstetric causes were excluded, underscoring that coagulopathy may still be contributory.These proportions are descriptive of the published cases and should not be interpreted as population-based estimates of incidence or risk.Four pregnancies were complicated by either confirmed primary PPH or other clinically significant peripartum bleeding despite prophylactic rFVIIa, whereas several pregnancies in women with severe deficiency were managed without prophylaxis and without hemorrhage. These descriptive findings cannot establish prophylactic effectiveness because treatment indications, obstetric risk, and dosing varied across reports.Thrombotic events or thrombotic history were reported in two women. No neonatal hemorrhage was reported among 43 live births.ConclusionsFVII activity alone appears to be an unreliable predictor of peripartum bleeding in the published cases. Management should be individualized according to bleeding phenotype, third-trimester FVII activity, obstetric risk, delivery route, anesthesia requirements, and thrombotic risk. Delivery planning should include timely access to tranexamic acid and appropriate factor replacement when clinically indicated. Postpartum VTE prophylaxis should be individualized according to bleeding stability, thrombotic risk factors, delivery route, and exposure to rFVIIa. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine prophylactic rFVIIa, although it may be considered on a case-by-case basis when the perceived bleeding risk is high. These conclusions are based on heterogeneous case reports and small case series and should be interpreted accordingly.

articles.title: Prenatal Genetics and Investigational in Utero Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease: Clinical, Ethical, and Justice Considerations.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a monogenic hemoglobinopathy with inequities in morbidity and care within and between countries. Prenatal somatic gene therapy is proposed but remains preclinical for SCD. This critical narrative review examines how such an intervention would interact with existing disparities and evaluates it in terms of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. SCD differs from conditions for which fetal intervention is established: fetal hemoglobin is protective, clinical manifestations generally arise after its postnatal decline, and newborn screening permits early preventive care. A prenatal intervention must therefore demonstrate a material advantage over timely postnatal management while exposing neither the pregnant person nor fetus to disproportionate procedural or product risk. Intended somatic treatment is not equivalent to heritable genome editing or embryo selection, although off-target effects, mosaicism and unintended germline exposure require explicit investigation. There is currently no evidence that prenatal somatic gene therapy is cost-effective or would overcome access barriers. Its reliance on fetal medicine, molecular, and manufacturing infrastructure could initially widen disparities. Clinical translation would be ethically defensible only after disease-specific comparative evidence, independent oversight, non-directive consent, lifelong follow-up and a credible equitable-access plan. Strengthening newborn screening and proven care remains the immediate justice priority.

articles.title: Empathic Versus Informational Messaging and Expertise Cues in Search Ads for Suicide Prevention.
articles.abstract: Background: Search-based advertising is used as a digital outreach method to reach users searching for suicide-related terms. However, it remains unclear which ad message elements promote access to support information among users searching for terms related to life issues associated with suicide risk. Aims: We compared empathic and informational headlines and descriptions with and without expertise cues to examine ad message elements that promote access to support information among users searching for life issues. Method: Search-based advertising was displayed in Tokyo, Japan, to users searching for life-issue-related terms across six areas (perinatal women, domestic violence, addiction, depression, sexual minorities, and child abuse). Four ad types were created by combining headline type (empathic vs. informational) and description type (with vs. without an expertise cue). Outcomes were click rate and conversion rates for the three landing page actions (self-check, self-care, and consultation services). We fit mixed-effects binomial logistic regression models. Results: Empathic headlines were associated with higher odds of ad clicks and self-checks, while informational headlines were associated with higher odds of consultation services. Descriptions with expertise cues were associated with lower odds of self-care and consultation services. A headline × description interaction was observed for self-care with higher odds when an expertise cue was paired with an empathic headline. Limitations: As this study examined a limited set of ad elements in Tokyo and used Japanese-language ads and landing pages, conversion outcomes may have been influenced by the structure of the multifunctional landing page. Conclusion: Empathic headlines may promote ad clicks and self-check, whereas informational headlines may support access to consultation services. Expertise cues were not uniformly associated with greater engagement, and their associations varied by outcome and accompanying headline. These findings highlight the importance of tailoring ad messages to the behaviors they are intended to promote.

articles.title: Genetic Diagnoses and Postnatal Outcomes in a Prenatal Cohort of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe genetic diagnoses and characterize postnatal outcomes in a prenatal cohort of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) evaluated at a quaternary fetal center.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of pregnancies referred between 2014 and 2026 for contractures involving ≥ 2 body areas. We categorized cases into three groups using the Hall classification. Demographics, prenatal imaging, genetic results, autopsy findings, and postnatal outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: Ninety-four pregnancies were included: 15 with isolated arthrogryposis, 32 with arthrogryposis and systemic anomalies excluding the central nervous system (CNS), and 47 with arthrogryposis and CNS involvement or fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS). Genetic findings in our cohort included 18 aneuploidies, 3 copy number variants and 25 single gene disorders. Of pregnancies with non-diagnostic cytogenetic findings that underwent next-generation sequencing (NGS), 50% (24/48) had a molecular diagnosis. Neonates with FADS had notably poor outcomes, including high mortality (86%, 6/7) and failed intubation (50%, 3/6) rates. Of neonates with isolated arthrogryposis, 77% (10/13) survived but frequently required respiratory or feeding support, orthopedic surgery, ambulation assistance and had neurodevelopmental delays.
CONCLUSIONS: AMC is genetically heterogeneous with frequent underlying single gene disorders, supporting the use of NGS in prenatal diagnosis. Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain high, particularly with FADS.

articles.title: Long-Term Treatment Outcomes and Remission Durability in Absence Epilepsy: A Nationwide Claims-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Population-level evidence comparing long-term treatment trajectories in childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) and juvenile absence epilepsy (JAE) remains limited. We evaluated claims-defined remission patterns and treatment persistence in a nationwide cohort.
METHODS: Using the South Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database (2011-2025), we identified newly treated probable absence epilepsy and operationally categorized patients as CAE (index age, 0-9 years) or JAE (index age, 10-17 years). Outcomes were claims-defined first remission, antiseizure medication (ASM) reinitiation after claims-defined first remission, claims-defined final remission, and severe post-index outcomes. A multicenter chart review assessed case identification and age-based CAE/JAE concordance.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1,775 patients (1,279 CAE; 496 JAE). Case identification had 78.0% sensitivity, 99.6% specificity, and 94.1% positive predictive value; age-based classification matched clinician-adjudicated CAE/JAE diagnoses in all 32 confirmed cases. In the 2013-2016 cohort with mature follow-up, claims-defined final remission occurred in 67.0% and 34.1% of CAE and JAE cases, respectively, and the median time to claims-defined final remission was 5.89 years in CAE but was not reached in JAE. JAE showed lower claims-defined first remission, more frequent ASM reinitiation after claims-defined first remission, and lower claims-defined final remission than CAE. No significant between-group difference was detected in claims-defined status epilepticus or drug-resistant epilepsy.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides population-level benchmarks for long-term outcomes in absence epilepsy. Notably, durable claims-defined ASM-free remission was not universal or rapid in CAE, and JAE showed lower remission durability and greater treatment persistence.

articles.title: Parent-Child Bonding Strengthens the Influence of Perceived Parental Approval or Disapproval of Adolescent Substance Use: Longitudinal Evidence Across Adolescence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perceived parental approval or disapproval of substance use and parent-child bonding are important family influences on adolescent substance use, yet the developmental mechanisms linking these factors to adolescent behavior remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined whether perceived parental approval or disapproval of substance use influences adolescent substance use through adolescents' substance use attitudes and whether this indirect association is moderated by parent-child bonding. Developmental differences were also examined.
DESIGN: Prospective longitudinal survey data were collected annually between 2004 and 2011 from 4,407 adolescents in 24 U.S. communities followed from Grades 6 to 12.
METHODS: Moderated mediation models with 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals and cluster-robust standard errors examined whether parent-child bonding moderated the indirect association between perceived parental approval or disapproval and adolescent past-month substance use through adolescents' substance use attitudes across early (Grades 6, 7, and 8) and later (Grades 9, 10, and 12) adolescence. Models adjusted for covariates and prior substance use.
RESULTS: Across both developmental periods, perceived parental approval was associated with more favorable adolescent substance use attitudes, which in turn were associated with more frequent subsequent substance use. Conversely, perceived parental disapproval was associated with less favorable attitudes and less frequent subsequent substance use. Closer parent-child bonds strengthened the association between perceived parental approval or disapproval and adolescents' attitudes. This moderating effect was stronger during early adolescence, although the mediated pathway was evident across both developmental periods.
CONCLUSION: Adolescents' substance use attitudes emerged as a key developmental mechanism linking family socialization processes to subsequent substance use across adolescence. Stronger parent-child bonds can amplify both the protective influence of perceived parental disapproval and the risk associated with perceived parental approval of substance use. Effective prevention and intervention efforts should therefore address both parental substance use norms and parent-child relationships.

articles.title: Magnitude and Burden of Substance Use Disorders Among Adolescents in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa: Regional Analysis From Global Burden of Diseases 1990 to 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substance use disorders are chronic conditions characterized by compulsive substance use despite adverse health consequences. However, low-resource settings have limited epidemiological data to inform policies. This study estimated the extent and impact of substance use disorders among adolescents in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African region from 1990 to 2023.
METHODS: The Global Burden of Diseases 2023 estimates, computational techniques, and tools were applied. Disease modelling with a Bayesian meta-regression (DisMod-MR 2.1) was used to estimate non-fatal health outcomes, while the cause of death ensemble model (CODEm) was employed to estimate the fatal health outcomes. Estimates were smoothed by applying the spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression (ST-GPR).
RESULTS: In 2023, there were an estimated 1135 prevalent cases per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 821-1510), 514 incident cases per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 360-697), 100 years lived with disability per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 62-147), 4 years of life lost per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 3-5), and 104 disability-adjusted life years per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 66-150). Males had higher rates than females in most countries. Except for an increase in disability-adjusted life years, the other rates remained stable between 1990 and 2023. Most rates increased in Eritrea and Ethiopia.
CONCLUSION: This study indicated that substance use disorders caused substantial morbidity and disability among adolescents in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African region over the past three decades. Moreover, males consistently experienced a greater health burden than females. Thus, gender-responsive interventions, integration of early detection, treatment, and rehabilitation services into primary healthcare, coordination of region-wide surveillance systems, and cross-border substance control can be recommended.

articles.title: Professional judgement in early childhood: predictors of concern, support needs and referrals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of developmental delays is crucial for timely support. This study examined what factors influence professional concern, perceived support needs, and referral decisions.
METHOD: A vignette study was conducted among 401 professionals evaluating a 2.5-year-old girl with mild eating difficulties, supplemented with manipulated variables about the developmental level of the child, the socioeconomic status, and parental concern. Five outcomes were examined using regression analyses: professional concern, perceived support needs for developmental monitoring and diagnostic assessment and referral for developmental monitoring and diagnostic assessment.
RESULTS: Developmental delay was a predictor of professional concern, perceived support needs and referral behaviour. Parental concern predicted professional concern but not support needs or referral decisions. Organisational sector was associated with support needs and referral decisions.
CONCLUSION: These findings underline the need for targeted training of professionals working with young children in developmental screening and taking parental concerns seriously.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Predictors of Severe Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers is increasingly recognized, yet knowledge on its clinical characteristics and predictors of severe disease remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics of anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months and to identify factors associated with severe anaphylaxis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 68 children aged 0-36 months diagnosed with anaphylaxis at a tertiary pediatric allergy center. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with severe anaphylaxis.
RESULTS: The median age at presentation was 13.0 months (interquartile range [IQR], 7.0-23.0), and 58.8% of patients were male. Food was the leading trigger (80.9%), with tree nuts, hen's egg, and cow's milk being the most common allergens. Skin involvement was the predominant manifestation (94.1%), followed by respiratory and gastrointestinal involvement (both 57.4%). Respiratory involvement was more frequent in females, whereas gastrointestinal manifestations predominated in males. Non-atopic children had significantly higher rates of severe anaphylaxis, cardiovascular involvement, and multisystem reactions than atopic children. Non-food triggers were associated with a more severe clinical course. In univariate analysis, atopy was associated with lower odds of severe anaphylaxis, whereas drug-induced reactions had higher odds of severe disease than food-induced reactions. Neither atopy nor trigger category remained independently associated with severity after multivariable adjustment. All patients received intramuscular epinephrine under protocolized emergency care, and no biphasic reactions or fatalities occurred.
CONCLUSION: Anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months has distinct clinical characteristics. Although food remained the predominant trigger, non-food triggers and the absence of atopy were associated with a more severe clinical phenotype. However, no baseline atopic or trigger-related factor independently predicted severe anaphylaxis after multivariable adjustment, highlighting the challenges of risk stratification in this age group.

articles.title: Quality of Life During Oral Peanut Immunotherapy in the OPIA Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) findings have varied between peanut oral immunotherapy (OIT) trials. The objective of this study was to compare changes in the HRQoL between the OIT and standard (control) treatment groups during the OPIA peanut OIT double-blind randomised controlled trial and at long-term follow-up.
METHODS: OPIA was a single-centre, 3-arm, double-blind placebo-controlled trial of peanut OIT in children aged 10-16 years. Standardised questionnaires (FAQLQ, FAIM, FAQLQ-Parent Burden, PSS) and bespoke surveys were administered at 0, 6, 12 and 13.5 months, with 3-year follow-up. Changes in scores at different time points were analysed descriptively and using 2-tailed T tests. A GEE model investigated the interaction between change in HRQoL score, treatment (OIT vs. standard care) and time. 3 year follow-up surveys were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative analysis.
RESULTS: Sixty-five subjects were randomised and 61 participants completed the study. There was no evidence of difference in HRQoL score changes between the OIT and standard treatment groups from baseline to 12 months or 13.5 months. Furthermore, achieving OPIA's primary efficacy endpoint (tolerance of ≥ 1000 mg of peanut protein (cumulative dose 1449 mg) at month 13.5 double blind placebo-controlled food challenge was not associated with a more favourable change in FAQLQ from baseline to end of study. Changes in global FAQLQ-Parent proxy (FAQLQ-PF) scores from baseline to 12 months were less favourable for carers of children who had experienced treatment-related serious adverse events compared to those without such events (mean change 0.10 vs. -0.97, 0.0063).
CONCLUSIONS: OIT did not confer a HRQoL benefit over standard care in this cohort, based upon the tools used to assess HRQoL. Treatment-related serious adverse effects negatively impacted FAQLQ-Parent proxy scores.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Pregnant Women and Health Care Workers Regarding Antenatal Testing for HIV, Hepatitis B Virus, and Syphilis in Vietnam: Protocol for a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis remains a preventable cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and long-term disability. In Vietnam (Viet Nam), although antenatal care coverage is high, gaps persist in the timing, uptake, and completion of screening and follow-up services for these infections.
OBJECTIVE: This study has 2 parallel population-specific objectives. Among women who recently gave birth, we will estimate completion of antenatal testing for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis and its associated factors with study-defined optimal testing (completion of all 3 tests during the first trimester). Among health care workers (HCWs), we will assess knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices and identify professional factors associated with good practice regarding antenatal screening and MTCT prevention.
METHODS: This multicenter, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2026 in 4 provincial hospitals in northern Vietnam. Women completed an interviewer-administered questionnaire after delivery, once clinically stable and before discharge. Antenatal testing was verified from maternal records, laboratory reports, or electronic records whenever available. HCWs completed a separate anonymous self-administered questionnaire during the same study period. The 2 participant groups were not matched. The primary outcome for women is completion of all 3 antenatal tests during the first trimester (study-defined optimal testing). The primary outcome for HCWs is good practice regarding the prevention of MTCT. The minimum target sample sizes were 601 women and 601 HCWs. Data will be analyzed separately for each group. Descriptive analyses will summarize knowledge, attitudes, and practices indicators and service uptake. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance will be used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: The protocol received ethics approval on February 9, 2026. The study is funded by Thai Binh University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Hung Yen, Vietnam. Recruitment was conducted from June to September 2026. As of manuscript submission, 601 patients and 601 health care workers had been recruited. Data cleaning is planned for October 2026, followed by statistical analysis from November to December 2026. Dissemination of the first study results is planned for the first quarter of 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: The study will provide hospital-based evidence on completion of antenatal triple screening and provider practices. By prespecifying distinct outcomes for women and HCWs, the study is designed to identify actionable gaps while avoiding causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations.

articles.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads.
OBJECTIVE: Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety.
METHODS: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads.
RESULTS: The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection.
CONCLUSIONS: Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research.
INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107879.

articles.title: Examining the Effectiveness of a Dual Executive Function Training Package: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Executive function (EF) refers to the cognitive processes that enable goal-directed regulation of thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. Two interrelated domains are commonly distinguished: "cool" EF, which involves abstract cognitive processes, and "hot" EF, which involves regulation in emotionally or motivationally charged contexts. Children with special educational needs (SEN) frequently show difficulties across both domains, yet most interventions target one in isolation.
OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a dual EF training package for 3 of the most prevalent SEN groups: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), specific learning difficulties (SpLD), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
METHODS: A total of 288 primary school students aged 6 to 12 years with a diagnosis of ADHD, ASD, or SpLD will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention or a waitlist control group, stratified by diagnosis. Each intervention group (n=48) will receive the dual EF training program. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue to receive usual educational and clinical support (standard care) during the study period and will be offered the dual EF program upon completion of the study. Preintervention and postintervention assessments will include neuropsychological tests of EF, teacher- and parent-reported behavioral ratings, and measures of disability impact, school satisfaction, and social participation. Changes in outcome measures will be examined using a mixed-design analysis, with diagnosis (ADHD, ASD, and SpLD) and group (experimental vs waitlist control) as between-participant factors and time (pretest vs posttest) as the within-participant factor. Baseline scores will be included as covariates where appropriate. The analysis will assess overall intervention effects and whether changes over time differ by intervention condition and diagnosis, with significant interactions followed by appropriate post hoc comparisons.
RESULTS: The study was funded by Advance Children Medical and Education Foundation Limited from September 2025 to December 2026 and received ethical approval. Recruitment commenced in early 2026, and 30 participants with ADHD, 30 with ASD, and 45 with SpLD had been enrolled by June 2026. Baseline assessments were completed for all participants. Further data collection and data analysis are scheduled for completion by early 2027, with the results to be submitted for publication thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: This study will evaluate the effectiveness of a theme-based dual EF program that integrates hot and cool EF within a structured curriculum. Findings will provide evidence of the potential of this approach to support EF and related outcomes in children with SEN and may inform future research and inclusive educational practices.

articles.title: 'I Had Been Told I Couldn't [Become a Parent]': Variations of Sex Characteristics and Intersex Family-Building Between Bodily and Reproductive Autonomy.
articles.abstract: Family building is widely understood as a socially meaningful aspiration and a dimension of human rights. For intersex people, or people born with variations of sex characteristics (VSC), pathways to parenthood may be impacted by sociomedical factors that extend beyond those experienced by endosex individuals with infertility. This article explores family-building experiences among adults with VSC by analysing how participants re-imagine reproductive futures in the context of medical power, informational gaps and restrictive reproductive citizenship regimes. Drawing on 64 qualitative interviews with people with VSC, partners and clinicians, alongside a review of reproductive policy frameworks, we examine how biomedical infrastructures, legal regulations and childhood medical experiences overlap with family-building experiences. By foregrounding themes of hermeneutical injustice, embodied agency and reproductive citizenship, this article investigates how participants navigate reproductive futures while mobilising peer expertise and family-building strategies. Ultimately, this paper argues for healthcare and policy frameworks that affirm bodily autonomy and ensure equitable family-building support for people with VSC.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Biologics for Patients with Severe Eosinophilic Asthma: A Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA) remains morbid despite standard care. Lacking head-to-head trials, the comparative efficacy of biologics (mepolizumab, benralizumab, dupilumab, tezepelumab) is unclear. This network meta-analysis (NMA) quantifies their relative efficacy and safety in SEA.
METHODS: Following PRISMA-NMA, we searched databases (inception to July 23, 2025) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of adolescents/adults with SEA comparing these biologics against placebo or each other. Primary outcomes were annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) and change in pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1); secondary outcomes included change in post-bronchodilator FEV1, ACQ/AQLQ scores, and safety. Bayesian random-effects NMA was performed, and treatment rankings were summarized using surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs involving 7,173 participants were included. For AAER, tezepelumab ranked highest (SUCRA: 73.35%), followed by mepolizumab (72.65%), benralizumab (56.23%), and dupilumab (36.20%); the corresponding network estimates versus placebo were mean difference -1.23 (95% credible interval [CrI]: -2.99 to 0.58), -1.16 (95% CrI: -2.76 to 0.49), -0.75 (95% CrI: -1.54 to -0.17), and -0.37 (95% CrI: -2.13 to 1.42), respectively. For ΔPre-BD FEV1, tezepelumab ranked highest (SUCRA: 79.64%), followed by dupilumab (54.42%), benralizumab (52.19%), and mepolizumab (45.71%). Benralizumab ranked highest for ΔPost-BD FEV1 and ΔACQ-5, tezepelumab for ΔACQ-6, dupilumab for ΔAQLQ, and mepolizumab for lower serious adverse event (SAE) risk. For SAEs, network estimates versus placebo were odds ratio (OR) 0.45 for mepolizumab (95% CrI: 0.23 to 0.72) and OR 0.58 for benralizumab (95% CrI: 0.35 to 0.84). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable rankings after exclusion of non-tezepelumab studies, whereas exclusion of Wechsler ME 2022 removed the tezepelumab node. GRADE certainty ranged from very low to high, and potential publication bias was detected for SAEs.
CONCLUSION: This NMA suggests that biologics provide clinically relevant benefits for SEA, particularly in reducing exacerbations. Tezepelumab and mepolizumab had the highest ranking probabilities for AAER. Mepolizumab and benralizumab ranked favorably for lower SAE risk, but these safety estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of potential publication bias. Treatment rankings remain limited by low or very low certainty for many indirect active treatment comparisons, underscoring the need for head-to-head trials.

articles.title: Disseminated histoplasmosis in non-immunocompromised children: A scoping review.
articles.abstract: Reviews describing the occurrence of histoplasmosis in immunocompetent children are lacking in the literature despite case reports documented globally. We conducted a comprehensive literature search following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines to identify individual cases and series on histoplasmosis in immunocompetent children published between January 2001 and October 2025. We identified 30 cases from India (n=10, 33.3%), USA (n=7, 23.3%), Nigeria (=2, 6.7%), Brazil (n=2, 6.7%), China (n=2, 6.7%), Argentina (n=1, 3,3%), Chad Republic (n=1, 3.3%), Georgia (n=1, 3.3%), Mexico (n=1, 3.3%), Costa-Rica (n=1, 3.3%), Paraguay (n=1, 3.3%) and Colombia (n=1, 3.3%). The risk factors were unknown or not reported in most cases. The spectrum of diagnosis was predominantly disseminated histoplasmosis (n=22, 73.3%) followed by pulmonary histoplasmosis (n=2, 6.7%). Outcomes were favourable in 24 (80.0%) cases, three (10.0%) were fatal cases, one (3.3%) was lost to follow-up, and outcomes were not specified in two (n=2, 6.7%). Our findings suggest histoplasmosis can also be encountered in non-immunocompromised children. It should be considered as a differential in children, especially in endemic settings, regardless of their immune status or in the absence of risk factors.

articles.title: Current practice in paediatric occupational therapy in Australia: A descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Australian paediatric occupational therapy has seen significant changes in the last 15 years, yet there have been no published studies in that time that explore current practice. This study aimed to examine and create a profile of current practices of Australian paediatric occupational therapists regarding application of theories and models, goal setting, assessment, intervention, professional development, and use of evidence.
METHODS: In this descriptive study, a purpose-designed online survey was distributed via social media, occupational therapy organisations, and researcher contacts. The survey was open between March and September 2023. The survey was approximately 25 minutes long and included fixed choice and open-ended questions. Descriptive and content analysis were conducted.
CONSUMER AND COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT: An advisory group of paediatric occupational therapists was involved in survey design and testing.
RESULTS: One-hundred and fifty-six surveys were fully completed. Participants predominantly worked in private practice (56.41%) and utilised National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS)/Early Childhood Intervention funding (71.15%). The most common diagnosis seen was autism spectrum disorder (84.62%). The most common theory used was developmental theory (80.00%). The most frequently used model was the Person, Environment, Occupation model (66.67%). The goal setting tool most used was the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (81.15%). The most frequently used assessment was Sensory Profile 2 (71.23%). Participants identified that they most commonly focussed on fine motor training (77.93%), parent/caregiver education (69.66%), and goal directed training (68.28%) for intervention. Less than half (41.67%) reported being 'somewhat satisfied' with their access to professional development, but the majority reported being supported by their workplace in using evidence-based practice (90.38%).
CONCLUSION: Changes in current paediatric occupational therapy practice were identified, which were reflective of the change to funding via the NDIS and evidence supporting top-down interventions. An emphasis on measuring at the level of impairment remains a barrier to supporting and evaluating occupational performance and participation outcomes.

articles.title: History of operative pelvic ring fixation is associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery: A matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic ring injuries requiring surgical fixation are uncommon among women of childbearing age, and evidence to guide delivery in subsequent pregnancies is limited. Cesarean delivery (CD) is vital when indicated, but carries risk of complications, such as pulmonary and infectious complications in the child and an increased risk of infection, hysterectomy, and cardiac arrest in the mother. The purpose of this study was to compare the likelihood of CD in women with a history of pelvic fixation (HPF) and those with no history of pelvic injury (NPI) who were matched on factors related to CD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of live deliveries among military beneficiaries in Birth and Infant Health Research program data between 2002 and 2021. All patients with HPF prior to delivery were selected. A cohort of patients with NPI were randomly selected in a 10:1 ratio, matched on age, year of delivery, number of prior births, and history of CD. The primary outcome of interest was CD. The secondary outcome of interest was indication for CD among the HPF cohort.
RESULTS: There were 79 patients with HPF who had a subsequent pregnancy that resulted in a live birth and 790 controls were selected based on the matching criteria, for a total of 869 patients. The average age at delivery was 26.8 years, 85% had no prior births, and 10% had a prior CD. Patients with HPF had higher prevalence of CD compared to those with NPI (54.4% vs 25.7%; risk ratio: 2.12; 95% confidence interval: 1.52-2.94). History of orthopedic fixation was the most common indication for CD in patients with HPF.
CONCLUSION: HPF increased risk of CD, even when controlling for a history of CD. Women with HPF had approximately twice the prevalence of CD compared with matched women with NPI. Still, nearly half of women with HPF delivered vaginally, suggesting that prior pelvic fixation does not necessarily preclude vaginal delivery. Given that orthopedic fixation itself was frequently documented as an indication for CD, these findings highlight the need for individualized obstetric assessment and further evidence to guide delivery planning after pelvic fixation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.

articles.title: The House That Gendered Racism Built: Gendered Racism, Trauma, Implications for Reimagining Perinatal Health, and Alternative Paths to Health Equity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving health equity requires acknowledging and naming how inequities in the health care system occur, are maintained, and are resisted. Models of self-care indicate that experiencing marginalization and oppression can prompt a variety of coping and resistance strategies that have implications for health and survival. Consistent with a long-standing canon of Black feminist research and a public health critical race praxis approach that recognizes that gendered racism (GR) unfolds across multiple levels, settings, and alongside other complementary systems (e.g., capitalism) impacting life and health outcomes, the current article examines how GR within the health care system leads to trauma and resistance for Black women during the perinatal period.
METHODS: Using data from a U.S. national sample of Black women recruited in 2020, open-ended responses from 73 women who reported having children were coded thematically using an inductive approach.
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Black women reported experiencing subtle and overt medical GR, misogynoir, and trauma in relation to their perinatal care, supporting previous research documenting the legacies and contemporary effects of white supremacist capitalist patriarchy that manifest as obstetric racism. We also find evidence that Black women use resistance strategies in the face of trauma to care for themselves, exercise advocacy, and work to protect and understand their health-both within and outside of the traditional health care system-providing evidence that liberatory futures are possible and are most probable when Black women's voices are centered and leveraged in building those futures.

articles.title: Nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, MRI, and EEG findings.
articles.abstract: To examine the association between gross motor function level and Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (CPM) performance in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy (CP), compare CPM performance with typically developing participants, and explore associations with MRI and EEG findings. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 40 participants with CP and 20 comparison participants aged 10-17 years. CPM totals were converted to center-derived age-referenced scores; the upper available normative age band was applied above age 11.5 years. Gross motor function was classified with the GMFCS. Clinically indicated MRI and EEG findings were categorized using prespecified systems. Median CPM score was 72 (IQR 64-81) in the CP group and 98 (IQR 92-104) in the comparison group (adjusted difference -26.4, 95% CI -31.2 to -21.6). GMFCS level was inversely associated with CPM score (Spearman rho = -.78, 95% CI -.85 to -.68). Predominant white matter injury was associated with lower CPM scores. The adjusted association with epileptiform EEG abnormalities was inconclusive. CPM performance was associated with GMFCS level and MRI pattern, but the cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Gross motor classification must not substitute for accessible neuropsychological assessment.

articles.title: An electrophysiological investigation of inhibitory control in children with dyslexia and the role of comorbid ADHD symptoms: a pilot randomized intervention study.
articles.abstract: Neurobiological research indicates that atypical functioning within left-hemisphere parietal and temporal regions is associated with word-processing difficulties in children with dyslexia. This study used event-related potentials (ERPs) to examine the neural correlates of inhibitory control in children with dyslexia, the effects of computerized inhibition training, and the influence of ADHD symptoms. This pilot study employed a randomized, double-blind, dosage-controlled intervention design. Participants were 62 children aged 10-12 years, including 37 children with dyslexia and 25 typically-developing controls (TDCs). Intervention analyses included 34 children with dyslexia assigned to high (n = 18) or low-dose (n = 16) training. Behavioral performance, electrophysiological responses during a Go/No-Go task, and ADHD symptoms were assessed. Independent samples t-tests showed that children with dyslexia exhibited significantly slower reaction times than TDCs during the picture Go/No-Go task. Children with dyslexia also demonstrated reduced left-lateralized N2 and P3 amplitudes over fronto-central and fronto-temporal regions relative to TDCs at baseline. ADHD inattentive symptoms were significantly associated with slower reaction times at baseline. Mixed-factorial ANOVAs revealed significant reductions in reaction times across both training groups, together with pre- to post-intervention changes in several N2 and P3 indices. These findings suggest that children with dyslexia exhibit altered neural correlates of inhibitory control despite relatively modest behavioral differences and highlight the importance of considering ADHD symptomatology when investigating executive functioning in dyslexia.

articles.title: Learning and memory profile in pediatric craniopharyngioma with and without associated sleep disturbance.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents with craniopharyngioma are at increased risk for visual field cuts, endocrinopathies, associated sleep disturbances, and cognitive challenges. While general intellectual functioning tends to remain intact within this population, the sellar/suprasellar location of craniopharyngiomas can disrupt important neural pathways essential for learning and memory. This study examines rote verbal learning and memory profiles - including nuances in learning approaches and slopes - in a clinical sample of pediatric patients treated for craniopharyngioma. Furthermore, the role of sleep disturbance on these outcomes is also explored. Retrospective data were collected for 17 pediatric patients with craniopharyngioma and associated endocrinopathies who underwent neurosurgical resection and irradiation (for all but one). As hypothesized, specific deficits related to rote verbal learning and memory were noted for the sample despite average estimated intellectual and adaptive functioning, while more pronounced learning and memory deficits were observed in the subset with reported sleep disturbances. Learning slope stagnation and/or decline across trials was observed in 75% of the patients, while post-hoc analyses revealed heightened susceptibility to recency effects (with poorer recall from the middle of the list) and a non-statistically significant trend toward increased intrusion errors, despite preserved semantic clustering. Findings underscore the importance of targeted memory assessment and multidisciplinary sleep management in this population.

articles.title: Academic skills in students with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a genetic neuromuscular disorder increasingly recognized for its neurocognitive phenotype, including cognitive deficits, behavioral disorders, and learning disabilities. Specific distal dystrophin isoforms (e.g., Dp140 and Dp71) play a critical role in central nervous system function, driving individual variability in cognitive impairment. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to define the academic learning profile of reading, spelling, and math skills in children and adolescents with DMD. We systematically searched five databases up to July 8 2025. We included original, peer-reviewed studies that assessed academic performance (reading, spelling, or math) through standardized tests in patients with DMD (confirmed by elevated creatine kinase, gene mutation, or muscle biopsy). We excluded single-case, qualitative, non-controlled, or review articles. Seven Level III non-randomized case-control studies met the inclusion criteria (312 participants: 177 DMD, 135 controls). A random-effects meta-analysis revealed that students with DMD scored significantly lower than controls in reading and math. Math deficits were more pronounced, constrained by domain-general verbal memory bottlenecks. Quantitative data on spelling were limited, though narrative findings showed parallel vulnerabilities. Subgroup analyses with a small number of comparisons (k = 2) were severely underpowered and treated purely as exploratory. Students with DMD face substantial challenges in acquiring core academic skills. Future studies should consider genotypic profiles and distal isoform variations to help explain individual variability and guide personalized educational support. Future longitudinal research with well-matched control cohorts is needed to clarify long-term cognitive and academic trajectories.

articles.title: Does inhibition or attention predict working memory in children with ADHD? Examining age as a moderator.
articles.abstract: Working memory difficulties are among the most consistently reported cognitive impairments in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet it remains unclear whether these difficulties are more closely tied to weaknesses in attentional regulation or in response inhibition. This study examined whether attention and inhibition differentially predict the phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, and central executive components of working memory in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and whether age moderates these relationships.
