A sample of 123 children diagnosed with ADHD (aged 6-13.5 years; 65% male) completed the Integrated Visual and Auditory Continuous Performance Test (IVA-CPT) to assess attention and inhibition, and the Working Memory Test Battery for Children (WMTB-C) to measure the three working memory components. A series of hierarchical regression analyses, corrected for multiple comparisons, was used to test main effects and age interactions. Attention significantly and consistently predicted all three working memory components, accounting for approximately 14% to 20% of the variance, whereas inhibition did not significantly predict any working memory component. Age neither predicted working memory performance nor moderated any of the relationships. These findings were consistent across phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, and central executive components. Attentional regulation, rather than inhibition, emerges as the domain-general mechanism underlying individual differences in working memory among children with ADHD. Interventions targeting attentional stability should therefore be prioritized over inhibition-focused approaches. The absence of age moderation suggests that this cognitive architecture remains stable across middle childhood, although longitudinal replication is warranted.

articles.title: Adult phenotype of genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome: diagnostic challenges and clinical red flags from a multicenter Polish cohort.
articles.abstract:
AIM OF THE STUDY: To characterize the clinical phenotype of adults with clinically diagnosed and genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome (DS), with particular emphasis on seizure evolution, cognitive and motor impairment, and diagnostic delay.
CLINICAL RATIONALE FOR THE STUDY: An increasing number of individuals with DS survive into adulthood and require long-term neurological care. However, the adult phenotype differs from the classical childhood presentation and remains underrecognized in adult neurological practice. Recognition of an age-evolving seizure phenotype, together with intellectual disability, gait and postural abnormalities, and extrapyramidal features, may provide important diagnostic clues and prompt molecular testing in previously undiagnosed adults.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective case series of nine adults (six females and three males) fulfilling clinical diagnostic criteria for DS and carrying a pathogenic or likely pathogenic SCN1A variant. Clinical data were obtained from medical records, neurological examinations, seizure diaries, and psychological assessments performed as part of routine care. Seizure history and evolution, status epilepticus, cognitive and communication impairment, motor phenotype, and treatment history were analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age at evaluation was 27.8 years (range 21-37 years). Seizure onset occurred at a mean age of 6 months, whereas the mean age at molecular diagnosis was 13.2 years, corresponding to a mean diagnostic delay of 12.7 years. Febrile seizures occurred in eight of nine patients and persisted beyond the age of 18 years in three. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures persisted into adulthood in all patients, whereas status epilepticus occurred after the age of 18 years in only one. Intellectual disability was present in all patients and was severe or profound in six; communication impairment was observed in eight. Motor abnormalities were prominent, including gait impairment (9/9), ataxia (8/9), postural abnormalities (8/9), bradykinesia (5/9), hypomimia (5/9), and parkinsonian features (3/9). All patients had been exposed to sodium channel-blocking antiseizure medications before molecular diagnosis, with seizure worsening documented in eight of nine patients.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: The adult phenotype of DS combines persistent drug-resistant epilepsy with intellectual and communication impairment and prominent motor dysfunction. Although generalized tonic-clonic seizures may persist, other features of the epileptic phenotype, particularly status epilepticus, become less prominent with age. Gait, postural, cerebellar, and extrapyramidal abnormalities may provide important diagnostic clues in adults with infantile-onset epilepsy and intellectual disability. Recognition of this age-evolving phenotype may facilitate molecular diagnosis and support syndrome-specific management in adult neurological practice.

articles.title: A Novel SERPINC1 Mutation in a Teenager With Antithrombin Deficiency Leading to Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Vein Thrombosis: Implications for Diagnosis and Management.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is uncommon in adolescents, and hereditary thrombophilia should be considered in unprovoked or progressive cases. We report a 16-year-old Chinese male with pulmonary embolism and extensive deep vein thrombosis that progressed despite anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin followed by unfractionated heparin. Antithrombin (AT) activity was persistently reduced (36%-49%; reference range, 80%-120%), and activated partial thromboplastin time remained subtherapeutic despite heparin dose escalation, suggesting functional heparin resistance. Switching to argatroban achieved clinical stabilization. Whole-exome sequencing identified a previously unreported heterozygous SERPINC1 variant (NM_000488.4: exon5: c.1153 G > T; p.Gly385Cys), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The patient's mother and sister carried the same variant and had reduced AT activity. The patient was subsequently transitioned to rivaroxaban and remained asymptomatic during follow-up. AT activity remained reduced at 1 and 2 years, while follow-up imaging showed a reduction in pulmonary arterial thrombotic burden but persistent lower-extremity venous thrombi. This case highlights the importance of evaluating AT deficiency in young patients with unprovoked or progressive VTE and the need for further evidence to establish the clinical significance of novel SERPINC1 variants.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation for Oral Mucositis Prevention in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: Evidence and Unresolved Supportive-Care Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether protocol-defined photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) for prevention of oral mucositis (OM) in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has demonstrable benefits beyond mucosal endpoints.
METHODS: A critical narrative synthesis prioritizes HSCT trials, guidelines and recent evidence; source identification and unrecorded systematic-search elements are explicitly distinguished.
RESULTS: Mucositis prevention has the strongest direct support. In POMFITT (n = 30), severe OM occurred in 0/15 PBMT-treated and 4/15 control patients (absolute difference -26.7 percentage points), but this sparse comparison is sensitive to the statistical test used. Hospitalization, physical function and quality of life did not differ significantly at discharge. Pediatric controlled and abstract-only findings are indirect or preliminary for several supportive-care endpoints. Associations between OM and infection, opioid use or nutrition cannot establish causal PBMT effects.
CONCLUSION: PBMT should be positioned as a preventive OM intervention in defined HSCT settings, not an established multidimensional supportive-care treatment. Adequately powered endpoint-specific studies with reproducible optical dosimetry are needed.

articles.title: Mid-term outcomes of medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction using suture tape in paediatric and adolescent population: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suture tape medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction avoids tendon graft harvest, but outcomes in children are poorly reported. This study evaluated functional outcomes and complications in children and adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 56 patients (77 knees; 40 female; mean age 14.3 years, range 8.2-17.7) underwent isolated suture tape MPFL reconstruction for recurrent instability at a tertiary centre between 2020 and 2025. Minimum follow-up was 6 months. The primary outcome was the Paediatric International Knee Documentation Committee (Pedi-IKDC) score at ≥6 months (available for 58 knees). Secondary outcomes were recurrent instability, extensor lag and other complications.
RESULTS: The mean Pedi-IKDC score improved from 49.6 (SD 13.9) to 79.6 (SD 16.9), a mean gain of 30.0 points (p < 0.001). Recurrent instability occurred in 5 of 77 knees (6.5%), one following trauma, despite trochlear dysplasia (Dejour B-D) in 79% of knees. An extensor lag was recorded in 17 of 65 knees (26.2%): 16 of these were 5-10° and resolved with physiotherapy within 3-6 months; one of approximately 25° is awaiting revision. Steroid injection for medial patellar pain was required in four knees (5.2%). No physeal complications were observed.
CONCLUSION: Suture tape MPFL reconstruction improved the Pedi-IKDC score by 30.0 points, more than three times the minimal clinically important difference, with recurrent instability (6.5%) comparable to tendon graft reconstruction in children and no physeal complications. Extensor lag (26.2%) was common but resolved with physiotherapy in all but one knee. Suture tape is a reasonable graft-free option; comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Reading Comprehension Strategy Use Among Students With Dyslexia: Evidence From a Transparent and Agglutinative Language.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the use of reading comprehension strategies among middle school students with and without dyslexia in Turkish, a transparent and agglutinative orthography. A total of 484 students (242 with dyslexia, 242 typically developing) participated. Data were collected using the Reading Comprehension Strategies Questionnaire (RCSQ) and Informal Reading Inventory. Multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA) results revealed that students with dyslexia used fewer and less diverse cognitive and metacognitive strategies than their typically developing peers. No developmental increase in strategy use was observed across grade levels in either group. These findings highlight that although transparent orthographies facilitate decoding, Turkish's agglutinative morphology may increase comprehension demands, particularly for students with dyslexia-like profiles. The study provides theoretical insight into how orthographic transparency interacts with morphological complexity to shape strategic reading processes and offers practical implications for designing strategy-based, linguistically responsive intervention programs.

articles.title: Burn Management in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Burn disasters are uncommon but uniquely resource-intensive mass casualty events, requiring prolonged multidisciplinary care that can rapidly exhaust the limited number of verified burn centers and beds. This article reviews the epidemiology and injury patterns of burn disasters, burn-specific triage and transport principles, and system-level planning built on regional burn networks. It examines the American Burn Association's role in center verification, regional response plans, and national burn bed capacity monitoring, alongside federal support mechanisms. Acute resuscitation, damage-control operative strategies, temporary wound coverage, workforce augmentation, and pediatric considerations are addressed, together with ethical decision-making, long-term recovery, and emerging technologies.

articles.title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Screening with the fundal reflex test: a two-year retrospective cohort study of referrals to a tertiary paediatric ophthalmology department and literature review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Fundal Reflex Test (FRT) is widely recommended for infant eye screening, but real-world performance data in non-ophthalmologist hands are limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed referrals to a tertiary paediatric ophthalmology service over a two-year period for an abnormal FRT identified during screening as part of national guidelines in Ireland. Demographics, abnormality type, laterality, referrer type, and guideline-listed risk factors were recorded, and outcomes were statistically analysed.
RESULTS: Of an estimated 30,718 births in the catchment area, 65 infants (0.21%; 1 in 473 births) met the inclusion criteria. Referrals originated from neonatologists (50.8%), general practitioners (46.2%), and paediatricians (3.1%). Abnormalities were most often an absent reflex (70.8%), leukocoria (16.9%), or unspecified abnormality (10.8%); 80% were bilateral. Significant ocular pathology was identified in 4 infants (6.15%): vitreous haemorrhage (n = 2), congenital cataract (n = 1), and strabismus (n = 1). No cases of retinoblastoma were detected. No significant associations were found between pathology and referrer type, laterality, abnormality nature, or listed risk factors.
CONCLUSION: FRT screening produced low referral and detection rates for urgent pathology but identified one congenital cataract per ~ 30,000 births. We discuss the positives and negatives of the FRT test's widespread inclusion in clinical guidelines and the factors which influence its efficient utility in the healthcare service.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of photon radiotherapy versus proton beam therapy for pediatric Ewing sarcoma: Tsukuba Review Project-Ewing sarcoma 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in multimodal treatment strategies and chemotherapy have led to improved outcomes for patients with Ewing sarcoma (EWS). Proton beam therapy (PBT) has increasingly been utilized in pediatric oncology to minimize late toxicities associated with conventional treatments; however, studies addressing the use of PBT in EWS remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a meta-analysis to compare the efficacy of photon radiotherapy (RT) and PBT in pediatric EWS. We analyzed English-language articles published between 1990 and 2022. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and local control (LC).
RESULTS: A total of 38 studies from 36 articles (8 reporting PBT and 30 reporting photon RT) were included in the meta-analysis. PBT showed better 5-year OS and 4- and 3-year LC rates compared to photon RT, while a higher proportion of male patients and a higher rate of concurrent surgery were associated with better OS at selected time points. In a post hoc exploratory analysis restricted to studies published since 2015, only PBT was associated with improved 5-year OS.
DISCUSSION: The observed differences across the entire study period may be attributed to improvements in treatment protocols, including interval-compressed chemotherapy, and recent advancements in supportive care and radiation technology, which could have influenced outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: PBT appears to provide treatment outcomes that are comparable to those of photon RT in pediatric EWS. Further studies are needed to assess long-term outcomes and the treatment-related toxicities of PBT.

articles.title: A diagnostic model for central precocious puberty in girls based on ultrasonic bone age and clinical indicators.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central precocious puberty is a common pediatric endocrine disorder in girls. The diagnostic gold standard, the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test, is invasive, limiting its widespread use. Ultrasound-based bone age assessment is radiation-free, but its diagnostic value within an integrated model remains unvalidated.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a diagnostic model integrating ultrasound bone age advancement (ΔBA_OA) with clinical and biochemical markers for the differential diagnosis of central precocious puberty in girls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 269 girls initially diagnosed with precocious puberty were enrolled. Based on GnRH stimulation test results, they were divided into central precocious puberty (n=66) and non-central precocious puberty (n=203) groups. Clinical data, pelvic ultrasound parameters, hormone levels, and ultrasound bone age parameters were collected. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: ΔBA_OA (odds ratio (OR)=61.05), basal luteinizing hormone (LH) (OR=8.76), and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) (OR=1.02) were independent predictors (all P<0.001). Standardized coefficients confirmed comparable contributions from ΔBA_OA (β=0.675) and LH (β=0.637). The model demonstrated good apparent discriminative ability (AUC=0.972, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.950-0.993). Bootstrap internal validation with 200 resampling iterations yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.968 (95% CI: 0.953-0.992), with a calibration slope of 0.906 and intercept of -0.015, indicating minimal overfitting and satisfactory calibration. The calibration curve showed good agreement (mean absolute error (MAE)=0.016), and DCA indicated positive net benefit. Discrimination remained high across subgroups (AUC 0.959-0.994), though subgroup estimates were exploratory and based on limited event numbers.
CONCLUSION: The proposed model incorporating ultrasound bone age parameter ΔBA_OA with clinical and biochemical markers showed preliminary evidence of apparent discriminative ability. The model is intended as an auxiliary screening tool that may help reduce unnecessary GnRH stimulation testing, but this requires prospective validation. External validation in multicenter, large-sample studies is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications after severe blunt liver trauma in children: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-operative management is standard for hemodynamically stable pediatric blunt liver trauma, but the incidence and optimal surveillance for late intra-hepatic arterial complications remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze late intra-hepatic arterial complications and their management in a cohort of children with severe blunt liver injury, to confirm a clinical protocol.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients younger than 18 years referred to a quaternary liver center for grade ≥3 blunt liver injury (American Pediatric Surgical Association grading). Demographic and clinical data, imaging findings, active arterial bleeding or pseudoaneurysm not suspected at presentation and/or not detected on initial computerized tomography, and surgical and interventional radiology procedures were collected.
RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (median age 14.9 years) with grade III (n=10), IV (n=5), and V (n=17) liver injuries were included. A total of 37 procedures were performed in 19 patients (59%), including peri-hepatic packing, early and delayed surgical explorations, angiography, and 12 embolizations in 11 patients. Overall survival was 100%. In 5 patients (16% of the cohort; all grade IV-V injuries), late intra-hepatic arterial complications were documented on elective follow-up computerized tomography at a median of 10 days after trauma (when patients were asymptomatic), and all were managed successfully by selective interventional radiology, without procedure-related complications. No deaths occurred in this series.
CONCLUSIONS: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications were not rare in children with grade IV-V liver injuries. These findings support considering computerized tomography in children with very severe hepatic trauma, around days 10-15 after trauma, to allow pre-emptive interventional radiology management.

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.
RESULTS: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Imaging of congenital sensorineural hearing loss: a review of syndromic and non-syndromic causes.
articles.abstract: Congenital sensorineural hearing loss (cSNHL) has been increasingly recognized given improvements in prenatal and childhood screening efforts. Etiologies vary widely with a growing body of literature continuing to uncover underlying risk factors and associated syndromes. cSNHL results in significant morbidity with the potential to impair language and social development. Imaging is an integral part of the clinical and potential presurgical assessment for these children. Thus, it is essential for radiologists to be familiar with normal inner ear anatomy, inner ear malformations, and syndromic/genetic etiologies of sensorineural hearing loss.

articles.title: Association between latitude, temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate and the incidence of type 1 diabetes in Hokkaido, Japan: an ecological study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the relationships between latitude, temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate and the incidence of type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Hokkaido, Japan.
RESULTS: We analysed data from the Childhood IDDM Hokkaido Registry, including 458 paediatric T1D cases diagnosed before age 15 between 1959 and 1996. Regional incidence rates were calculated using census data, and meteorological variables were obtained from the Japan Meteorological Agency. Linear regression models examined correlations between T1D incidence and latitude, mean temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate. T1D incidence exhibited regional variation, with the highest rate in Ishikari (1.32 per 100,000 person-years) and the lowest in Hiyama/Oshima (0.53 per 100,000 person-years). A positive association was observed between latitude and T1D incidence. Additionally, mean temperature correlated positively with incidence, suggesting a complex interplay between climatic factors. Lower annual sunshine hours and reduced sunshine rates were associated with increased T1D incidence, supporting the hypothesis that diminished sun exposure contributes to disease risk. Higher latitude and reduced sunshine exposure were associated with increased T1D incidence, highlighting the potential influence of sunlight availability and vitamin D status. Promoting adequate vitamin D levels and safe sun exposure may help mitigate T1D risk in high-latitude populations.

articles.title: Early Life Adversity and Adolescent Sleep: A Longitudinal Study Examining Associations Between Dimensions of Early Adversity and Adolescent Sleep Metrics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A dimensional approach was utilized to examine associations between early environmental adversity (deprivation, unpredictability) and adolescent sleep metrics (average and night-to-night variability in bedtime, wake time, and sleep duration). We predict that greater deprivation and unpredictability are uniquely associated with worse adolescent sleep.
METHODS: In this study (N = 337), preschool unpredictability and deprivation were measured via home observation and parent report; adolescent sleep was measured by actigraphy. Multilevel structural equation modeling examined longitudinal associations between early adversity dimensions and adolescent sleep, controlling for sex, adolescent age, maternal education, preschool family income, and adolescent family income.
RESULTS: In independent models, greater deprivation was associated with more sleep duration variability (β = .18 [.01, .34]), greater bedtime variability (β = .30 [.14, .45]), and shorter average sleep duration (β = -.20 [-.35, -.03]); greater unpredictability was associated with shorter average sleep duration (β = -.21 [-.39, -.02]) and greater bedtime variability (β = .23 [.04, .40]). In the combined model, only greater deprivation (β = .26 [.09, .42]) was associated with greater bedtime variability, controlling for unpredictability.
CONCLUSIONS: While deprivation and unpredictability predict sleep independently, only deprivation played a unique role in adolescents' bedtime variability, beyond other aspects of early childhood adversity. Results inform early intervention and prevention efforts to promote healthy adolescent sleep.

articles.title: The Effect of BST via Telehealth on Caregiver Implementation of Incidental Teaching.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder has increased the need for accessible and scalable behavioral health services. Incidental teaching is an effective naturalistic intervention for increasing communication skills in children with autism, and behavior skills training is an effective method for teaching caregivers to implement evidence-based practices. Although telehealth has emerged as a viable modality for caregiver training, additional replications are needed. This study replicated and extended prior research by evaluating BST delivered via telehealth to train caregivers to implement incidental teaching. Nine caregiver child dyads and three trainers participated. Trainers used synchronous videoconferencing, and researchers evaluated outcomes using three multiple baseline single case designs. Following training, all caregivers improved procedural fidelity and reached 100% accuracy across two consecutive sessions. Caregivers also increased communication opportunities, resulting in increased child mands above baseline levels. Findings support telehealth delivered BST as an effective model for caregiver training.

articles.title: Robust Bayesian Variable Selection and Inference Under Misspecified Nonparametric Mixed Models in Longitudinal Studies.
articles.abstract: In high-dimensional longitudinal interaction studies, it is challenging to perform variable selection and statistical inference when the assumed interaction model is misspecified under heterogeneous disease phenotypes. Partially motivated by analyzing a subset of the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP) data with high-dimensional single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) measurements, we develop a novel sparse robust Bayesian mixed model to capture nonlinear longitudinal interactions. In terms of both parameter estimation and statistical inference, the proposed mixed model is robust not only to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions in the response variable but also to misspecification of nonlinear interaction effects. We have developed a Gibbs sampler incorporating spike-and-slab priors to promote exact sparsity in the identification of appropriate forms of main and interaction effects. Simulation results reveal superior performance of the proposed fully robust Bayesian analysis in identification, estimation, and statistical inference compared with alternative methods. In particular, the proposed analysis enables exact statistical inference in misspecified interaction models by yielding Bayesian credible intervals with nominal coverage probabilities on finite samples. Application of the proposed and alternative methods to the CAMP study sheds novel insight into asthma etiology.

articles.title: Common household foods fail to mitigate button battery esophageal injury in infants: an ex vivo dynamic model study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Button battery (BB) ingestion is a life-threatening pediatric emergency, particularly in infants at high risk of severe esophageal injury. This study evaluated whether readily available household food could mitigate BB-induced esophageal injury in infants.
METHODS: A dynamic ex vivo porcine esophageal model simulating peristalsis, salivary flow, and body temperature was used. After insertion of a CR2032 lithium BB, 5 mL of agave syrup, soy drink, orange juice, ketchup, or honey was administered at 5, 15, and 25 min, then every 30 min for 2, 4, or 6 hours. Outcomes included macroscopic ulcer grade, histologic injury depth, esophageal pH, and residual battery voltage.
RESULTS: In this dynamic model, agave syrup, soy drink, and orange juice did not reduce ulcer severity or histologic injury compared with untreated controls (p>0.05). Ketchup markedly worsened injury, increasing ulcer grades and voltage loss at all time points (p<0.05). Protective effects suggested in static models for agave syrup and soy drink were not reproduced under dynamic conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: Common household foods do not protect against BB-induced esophageal injury in a ex vivo experimental model. Dynamic testing is essential before recommending food-based prehospital therapies.

articles.title: Role of remote ischemic conditioning in necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening inflammatory intestinal disorder predominantly affecting preterm infants, with a high mortality and morbidity rate. The pathophysiology of NEC is intimately linked to immaturity of the intestinal vasculature and derangements in microcirculatory perfusion, rendering the developing bowel susceptible to ischemic injury following enteral feeding. Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) is a non-invasive maneuver involving brief cycles of limb ischemia and reperfusion, which engages endogenous cytoprotective mechanisms that can be transmitted to distant organs, including the intestine. This review examines the scientific basis and clinical trajectory of RIC as a therapeutic strategy in NEC. In preclinical models, RIC administered during the early stages of NEC counteracted characteristic derangements in intestinal microcirculation, mediated through nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide signaling, and thereby led to reduced intestinal injury, attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and prolonged survival. These protective effects occurred only before the onset of irreversible mucosal damage. A non-randomized phase I safety study subsequently confirmed, for the first time in infants with NEC, that RIC was safe and produced no adverse complications. To address the knowledge gaps necessary for an efficacy trial, the RIC-NEC phase II feasibility randomized controlled trial is currently ongoing at 15 international centers across 8 countries. This trial evaluates the feasibility of randomizing and delivering masked RIC to eligible neonates within 24 hours of NEC diagnosis. If successful, a future phase III multicenter randomized controlled trial will assess whether RIC can prevent disease progression and improve clinical outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Patient and Caregiver Education in Inborn Errors of Immunity: Short-Term Changes After a Structured Booklet-Based Intervention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess baseline disease-related knowledge among patients with IEI and caregivers and to explore short-term changes 2 months after the distribution of a structured educational booklet.
METHODS: This exploratory, uncontrolled, single-center, pilot pre-post survey study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric immunology center. Eligible respondents were adult patients with IEI, literate adolescents aged 14-17 years, and caregivers of pediatric patients. Respondents completed a researcher-developed 30-item questionnaire covering general knowledge, warning signs/manifestations, treatment awareness, and protective/preventive measures at baseline and 2 months after booklet distribution. Paired scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
RESULTS: Fifty-one respondents completed both assessments: 33 patients with IEI and 18 caregivers. Mean respondent age was 34.55 ± 12.83 years, and 32 respondents were female. The median total score increased from 23 (interquartile range [IQR]: 19-25) to 25 (IQR: 20-27), with a median paired change of 1 point (IQR: 0-5, P <.001). Treatment awareness increased from 6 (IQR: 4-8) to 8 (IQR: 6-9, P <.001), and protective/preventive measures increased from 8 (IQR: 6-9) to 9 (IQR: 7-9, P = 0.009).
CONCLUSION: Questionnaire scores were higher 2 months after booklet distribution, mainly in treatment and prevention domains. These findings suggest that written educational materials may help identify and address selected knowledge gaps, particularly regarding immunoglobulin replacement therapy, home-based treatment, and preventive measures.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Cytomegalovirus Infection in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, epidemiology, and outcomes of children with active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and to identify risk factors associated with mortality.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of patients admitted to a tertiary-level PICU between January 2015 and January 2023 were reviewed. Patients aged 1 month to 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CMV infection during PICU stay were included. Demographic, clinical, and outcome data were collected. Disease severity was assessed using pediatric risk of mortality (PRISM) and pediatric logistic organ dysfunction (PELOD) scores. Risk factors for mortality were analyzed using regression models, and the predictive value of CMV viral load was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: During the study period, a total of 3320 patients were admitted to the PICU, of whom 79 (2.38%; 95% CI, 1.9-2.9) had laboratory-confirmed CMV infection. Nearly half of the patients (n = 36, 45.6%) were immunocompromised. Overall mortality was 25.3% (n = 20). The main cause of death was septic shock (85%, n = 17). In most non-survivors (80%, n = 16), CMV polymerase chain reaction remained positive prior to death. A PELOD score ≥ 3 independently predicted mortality (crude RR 3.42; 95% CI, 2.98-7.78). Each 1-point increase in PRISM score was independently associated with mortality (crude RR 1.12; 95% CI, 1.05-1.20). Cytomegalovirus viral load demonstrated poor discriminative performance for mortality prediction ( Area Under the Curve-AUC 0.57; 95% CI, 0.47-0.63).
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of CMV infection in critically ill children was low but associated with high mortality. Organ dysfunction severity, particularly elevated PELOD scores, was a significant predictor of mortality. Pediatric risk of mortality score was statistically associated with mortality despite limited discriminative performance, whereas CMV viral load was not associated with mortality. These findings suggest that CMV infection in PICU patients likely reflects disease severity rather than being a direct determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Apparent sporadic Neurofibromatosis type 1 cases with affected yet undiagnosed parents: 6 examples.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: It is broadly accepted that approximately 50% of patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are sporadic, carrying de novo pathogenic variants. However, in routine diagnosis and care, the majority of patients do not report any family history. We hypothesize that a considerable proportion of these sporadic cases are in fact inherited cases with undiagnosed parents due to mild or atypical phenotypes.
METHODS: Sporadic status was assigned according to report and medical record of patients or parents. In six families, a parent coincidently underwent clinical examinations and/or genetic testing for the NF1 gene.
RESULTS: In each of the six cases, one parent was diagnosed for NF1 later. In four cases, the specific familial NF1 variant was confirmed in a parent. In the other two cases, NF1 features were seen in the parents as they accompanied their affected children.
CONCLUSION: Some apparent sporadic NF1 cases may in fact have inherited the disease from affected yet undiagnosed parents. Recognizing these cases ensures adequate medical care for previously undiagnosed parents and alters reproductive risk assessment.

articles.title: Preoperative Laboratory Parameters and Systemic Inflammatory Indices in Surgically Treated Neonatal Necrotizing Enterocolitis and Spontaneous Intestinal Perforation: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare preoperative laboratory parameters and systemic inflammatory indices between neonates with surgically confirmed necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and spontaneous intestinal perforation (SIP) and explore their associations with mortality.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included neonates operated on for intestinal perforation. Preoperative laboratory values were defined as the last sample obtained within 48 hours before the first surgical intervention. Infants treated with peritoneal drainage alone were excluded. Necrotizing enterocolitis and SIP were diagnosed based on operative and histopathologic findings.
RESULTS: Thirty-five neonates were included (NEC, n = 17; SIP, n = 18). Most were preterm (91.4%), and 34/35 (97.1%) had pneumoperitoneum. Serum albumin was lower in NEC than in SIP (2.19 ± 0.60 vs. 2.59 ± 0.52 g/dL, P = .041). No significant differences were observed in hemoglobin, white blood cell count, platelet count, C-reactive protein, pH, lactate, glucose, or inflammatory indices. Overall mortality was 45.7% (16/35), higher in NEC than SIP (58.8% vs 33.3%, P = .181). Non-survivors had lower birth weight (P = .047), lower hemoglobin (P = .047), lower albumin (P = .020), and older postnatal age at surgery (P = .005) than survivors. In SIP, non-survivors had lower hemoglobin (11.5 ± 1.6 vs. 14.6 ± 1.8 g/dL, P = .002), higher white blood cell counts (median 11.4 vs 5.4 ×103/µL, P = .041), and older postnatal age at surgery (20.3 ± 11.4 vs. 7.3 ± 5.2 days, P = .004). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses showed modest area under the curves for albumin in differentiating NEC from SIP (0.68) and for albumin and hemoglobin regarding mortality (0.72 and 0.71).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative laboratory parameters and inflammatory indices did not reliably distinguish NEC from SIP. Albumin, hemoglobin, and surgical timing were associated with mortality in exploratory analyses and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Protective Effect of Dexrazoxane Against Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity in the Treatment of Childhood Cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy is used in 50%-60% of childhood cancers despite well-known cardiotoxicity. The authors evaluated dexrazoxane (DEX) as a cardioprotective agent in children receiving anthracyclines.
METHODS: The authors retrospectively analyzed 142 children aged 0-18 years treated for childhood cancer. The control group comprised 87 patients who received anthracycline alone (2009-2019) and the case group 55 patients who received DEX + anthracycline (2019-2022, after DEX was licensed in Türkiye). Cardiac dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below 50%.
RESULTS: Baseline LVEF was comparable. Mean LVEF fell by 0.71 ± 6.55 points with DEX vs. 6.44 ± 9.76 in controls (Time × Group interaction F(1,140) = 14.77, P < .001), and the difference persisted after adjustment for follow-up duration and treatment covariates (β = +4.60, 95% CI = 1.10-8.10, P = .010). Cardiac dysfunction developed in 11 of 87 controls (12.6%) and in none of the 55 DEX patients (P = .007; log-rank P = .040); this held in a 36-month landmark analysis (0 of 52 vs. 4 of 25, P = .009). Mortality was higher in controls (21.8% vs. 5.5%, P = .009) and in patients with cardiac dysfunction (54.5% vs. 17.1%, P = .012).
CONCLUSION: Dexrazoxane attenuated the early decline in LVEF and reduced the incidence of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity, and this persisted after adjustment for the difference in follow-up duration. With a median DEX follow-up of only 22.8 months, these data support early cardioprotection; longer follow-up is needed to assess protection against late-onset cardiotoxicity.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Surgical and Advanced Interventional Treatments for Pediatric Refractory Constipation: A Systematic Review with Domain-Specific Meta-analyses of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize clinical outcomes and safety of surgical and advanced interventional treatments for pediatric refractory constipation using a phenotype-directed, domain-specific approach.
METHODS: This systematic review with domain-specific meta-analyses of proportions followed PRISMA 2020 and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261378728). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, trial registries, Google Scholar, and reference lists were searched through April 29, 2026. Eligible interventions included antegrade continence enema (ACE) procedures, botulinum toxin injection, transanal irrigation (TAI), diversion, and selected resective or motility-guided procedures. Random-effects single-arm proportions were pooled only within clinically coherent domains; safety outcomes were synthesized structurally when definitions and denominators were not sufficiently comparable for pooling.
RESULTS: Thirty-two primary interventional studies met final eligibility criteria, of which 22 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Descriptive pooled study-defined clinical success or response was 85% (95% CI: 81%-88%) for ACE procedures, 81% (95% CI: 72%-89%) for botulinum toxin injection, 81% (95% CI: 64%-94%) for TAI, and 91% (95% CI: 76%-100%) for resective or advanced surgery. The surgical estimate was exploratory because procedures and indications were heterogeneous. These proportions are not comparative treatment-effect estimates. Certainty of evidence was low or very low, and safety reporting was inconsistent across studies.
CONCLUSION: Advanced interventions may be associated with favorable outcomes in carefully selected children with refractory constipation, but indications and risks are phenotype specific. The evidence does not support direct effectiveness comparisons between therapeutic domains.

articles.title: Behavioral Manifestations and Diagnostic Challenges of Restless Legs Syndrome in Infants and Toddlers.
articles.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a sensory-motor neurological disorder, increasingly recognized in children, yet diagnosis in infants and toddlers remains challenging due to the reliance on verbal symptom reporting. This scoping review aims to synthesize the limited literature on probable RLS in infants and toddlers. A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed and Embase from inception through March 2026. Original studies, case reports, case series, and pediatric cohorts reporting probable RLS with onset or evaluation at ≤3 years were included. Reviews, editorials, and studies focusing exclusively on older populations were excluded. Thirteen studies were identified, of which 7 met inclusion criteria. Of the 7 publications, some focused on infants or toddlers, whereas others provided extractable data for children aged ≤3 years. Across studies, symptom onset was reported as early as 7.5 months in 1 cohort. Probable RLS in infants and toddlers presents as a behavioral sleep disorder characterized by nocturnal motor restlessness, accompanied by sleep fragmentation and distress. A characteristic pattern of awakening after 1-3 hours of sleep with motor agitation was frequently described. Periodic limb movements and low ferritin levels provide supportive evidence. Iron supplementation has been associated with improvement in symptoms in select cohorts. Probable RLS can manifest as early as infancy, presenting as a behavioral phenotype. Increased awareness of early behavioral manifestations and consideration of iron status may facilitate earlier identification and management. Future studies are needed to develop diagnostic frameworks and to better define the natural history of early-onset probable RLS.

articles.title: Flexible Bronchoscopy in Evaluation of Chronic Cough in Children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic cough is a common and challenging cause of pediatric respiratory visits. Differentiating underlying causes, ranging from infection to airway inflammation and aspiration, requires detailed clinical evaluation. Flexible bronchoscopy (FB) can provide additional information regarding lower airway pathology. This study aimed to investigate cough phenotype, radiological and bronchoscopic findings, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cytology, and treatment response in children undergoing FB for chronic cough.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 30 children who underwent FB at a tertiary pediatric center between January 2020 and September 2025. Demographic, clinical, radiological, bronchoscopic, and BALF cytology data were analyzed. Bronchoalveolar lavage samples were classified according to predominant inflammatory cell type.
RESULTS: The median age was 10.2 years (Q1-Q3: 5.7-15.0), and 20/30 (66.7%) patients had wet/productive cough. Chest computed tomography was available in 27 patients, with abnormalities detected in 20 (74.1%); atelectasis was the most common finding (11/27, 40.7%). Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cytology was macrophage-dominant in 21/30 (70.0%) and neutrophil-dominant in 9/30 (30.0%). Lipid-laden macrophages (LLMs) were identified in 7/30 (23.3%). Neutrophil-predominant BALF was more common in patients with bronchoscopic findings suggestive of infection (P = .013). Patients with LLM positivity showed symptomatic improvement following antireflux therapy.
CONCLUSION: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cytology may provide supportive information regarding airway inflammatory patterns in selected children with chronic cough. Interpretation should remain cautious because of the small sample size and retrospective single-center design. Integrating cytologic findings with clinical and bronchoscopic data may support clinical evaluation in children with chronic cough.

articles.title: Fetoplacental Doppler, Amniotic Fluid, and Placental Maturity in Pregnancies at or Beyond 40 Weeks: A Hospital-Based Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancies extending beyond 40 completed weeks are associated with progressive changes in placental function and fetal well-being. Assessment of fetoplacental Doppler parameters, amniotic fluid volume, and placental maturity may provide complementary information for antenatal surveillance. This study evaluated these parameters and their relationship with maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnancies at or beyond 40 weeks.
METHODS: A hospital-based observational study was conducted among 139 women with singleton pregnancies at or beyond 40 completed weeks of gestation. Maternal and obstetric characteristics were recorded, and antenatal assessment included umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler velocimetry, amniotic fluid index (AFI), and placental maturity according to Grannum grading. Labour characteristics, mode of delivery, maternal complications, and neonatal outcomes were documented. Participants were categorized according to gestational age as 40-40+6 weeks, 41-41+6 weeks, and ≥42 weeks.
RESULTS: Of the 139 participants, 110 (79.1%) were at 40-40+6 weeks, 25 (18.0%) at 41-41+6 weeks, and four (2.9%) at ≥42 weeks. Mean UA resistance increased with advancing gestation, with the UA resistance index (RI) increasing from 0.57 to 0.60 and 0.61 and the UA pulsatility index (PI) from 0.84 to 0.88 and 1.12 across the three gestational-age groups, respectively. The derived cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) declined from 1.90 to 1.70 and 1.16. Oligohydramnios (AFI <5 cm) was present in 21 (15.1%) women, while meconium-stained liquor occurred in 40 (28.8%). Labour was induced in 70 (50.4%) women, and lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) was performed in 49 (35.3%), with fetal distress being the leading indication. Eight neonates (5.7%) required neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and no perinatal mortality was recorded.
CONCLUSION: Advancing gestational age beyond 40 weeks was accompanied by increasing umbilical artery Doppler resistance, declining derived CPR, reduced amniotic fluid, and progressive placental maturation. Integrated surveillance using Doppler assessment, AFI, and placental evaluation may assist in monitoring pregnancies extending beyond 40 weeks. The derived CPR findings should be interpreted cautiously because of limitations in directly recorded MCA PI measurements.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Prenatal Screening for Gestational Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder of pregnancy associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Despite its clinical importance, considerable variation remains in approaches to prenatal screening, including the timing, diagnostic strategy, and criteria used to identify affected pregnancies. The expansion of screening also raises concerns regarding unnecessary diagnosis, healthcare utilization, and patient burden. This narrative review of the available literature was conducted to examine different approaches to prenatal GDM screening. The review considered variations in screening timing, screening strategies, diagnostic thresholds, and their associations with maternal and neonatal outcomes. Particular attention was given to the clinical implications of identifying milder degrees of dysglycemia and to the economic and practical consequences of different screening approaches. This review concluded that prenatal GDM screening should aim to achieve clinically meaningful detection while minimizing unnecessary intervention and patient burden. Future research should focus on standardized outcomes, simplified and accessible screening approaches, and context-specific strategies that integrate clinical effectiveness, economic considerations, and healthcare resources.

articles.title: Mortality and Morbidity Pattern of Preterm Neonates: Findings of a Retrospective Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe morbidity and mortality among preterm neonates (<37 weeks' gestation) admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare (JHAH), to evaluate survival by gestational age (GA), and to identify factors associated with mortality.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study reviewed the electronic medical records of all preterm neonates born at JHAH, Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, and admitted to the NICU between January 2019 and December 2023. Maternal, perinatal, and neonatal variables were compared between survivors and non-survivors. Survival to discharge by GA was compared using the log-rank test, and factors associated with mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 587 neonates, 22 (3.7%) died before discharge. Survival was 63.4% at 22-27 weeks, 95.2% at 28-31 weeks, and 99.4% at 32-36 weeks (p < 0.001). The most common complications were bronchopulmonary dysplasia (12.8%), patent ductus arteriosus (9.7%), and intraventricular hemorrhage (3.4%), all more frequent among non-survivors. After adjustment, higher GA was associated with lower mortality (28-31 weeks: adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.11, 95% CI: 0.03-0.33; 32-36 weeks: aOR: 0.015, 95% CI: 0.003-0.046), and small-for-gestational-age status with higher mortality (aOR: 3.82, 95% CI: 1.11-12.61).
CONCLUSION: Mortality among preterm neonates was low overall but concentrated among those born before 28 weeks. GA was the strongest predictor of survival, and growth restriction independently increased mortality risk.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide in Adolescents With Obesity: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background Childhood and adolescent obesity are increasing public health concerns in India and are associated with cardiometabolic complications. However, real-world evidence on the safety and effectiveness of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide among adolescents with overweight or obesity in routine clinical practice remains limited. Objectives This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (r-DNA) among Indian adolescents aged 12-18 years with overweight or obesity. Methods This retrospective, observational study (IAH-BMR/072/06-26) involved 40 adolescents on once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (0.25-2.4 mg) over 32 weeks. Anthropometric measures (body weight (BW), body mass index (BMI), BMI standard deviation score (BMI-SDS), waist circumference (WC), and blood pressure (BP)) were tracked over time. Biochemical outcomes included fasting blood sugar (FBS), postprandial blood sugar (PPBS), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting insulin, lipid profile, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and liver enzymes. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) and paired comparisons were used to assess changes. Results The study population comprised 24 female (60.0%) and 16 male (40.0%) adolescents, with a mean age of 14.82 ± 1.78 years. After 32 weeks, semaglutide demonstrated significant mean reductions in BW (-15.20 kg; 17.2%), BMI (-6.70 kg/m²; 19.4%), BMI-SDS (-1.08), WC (-10.71 cm; 10.82%), systolic BP (-8.30 mmHg), and diastolic BP (-4.50 mmHg) (all p < 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed in FBS, PPBS, HbA1c, fasting insulin, total cholesterol, triglycerides, TSH, serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase, and serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (all p < 0.001). Improvements were consistent across sexes. No adverse events (AEs) were documented. Conclusions Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (r-DNA) was associated with improvements in anthropometric and metabolic parameters among Indian adolescents with overweight or obesity. These real-world findings are broadly consistent with the reductions in BMI and improvements in selected cardiometabolic risk factors reported in the STEP TEENS trial. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to further evaluate its long-term effectiveness and safety.

articles.title: Building Demand for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination in India: A Review of the Behavioural and Social Drivers of Parental and Community Acceptance.
articles.abstract: India launched its National HPV Vaccination Campaign in February 2026, offering free, voluntary, single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls with parental consent. By September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered against an estimated annual cohort of about 1.2 crore girls, with wide variation across states. Because uptake depends on parental decisions, understanding what drives acceptance is now a programme priority rather than an academic question. This narrative review synthesises Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search and organised by the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework, and considers how the shift to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme changes the relevance of earlier findings. Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity. Decisions are shaped by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers. Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts. Before 2026, cost was a dominant practical barrier; with free provision, the remaining practical barriers are mostly access, consent processes, and reaching girls outside school. The national campaign removes the cost barrier but not the belief-based and social barriers. Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy. Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems integrate continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with algorithm-driven insulin delivery and are increasingly used in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D). However, the magnitude and consistency of glycemic benefit across pediatric age groups, together with the safety profile of these systems, warrant focused evaluation. We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials evaluating AID systems in children and adolescents with T1D. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 2026. Eligible studies compared AID with conventional insulin therapy or non-automated pump/CGM-based management and reported glycemic or safety outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Findings were synthesized narratively without quantitative meta-analysis. Of 2,363 records identified, 11 randomized controlled trials met the eligibility criteria. Trials evaluated multiple AID platforms in participants aged 2-18 years, with intervention durations ranging from 12 to 104 weeks. AID consistently improved time in range ([TIR] 70-180 mg/dL). Individual trials reported TIR improvements ranging from approximately 7 to 12 percentage points. In one pediatric trial, TIR increased by 11 percentage points (95% CI, 7-14; P<0.001), while another demonstrated an 8.7-percentage-point increase (95% CI, 7.4-9.9; P<0.001) accompanied by a 0.4-percentage-point reduction in glycated hemoglobin. A six-month trial demonstrated a 6.7-percentage-point increase in TIR (95% CI, 2.7-10.8; P=0.002), with a concurrent 1.9-percentage-point reduction in time below range. Improvements were particularly pronounced during nighttime in several studies. Hyperglycemic exposure generally decreased, whereas hypoglycemia did not consistently increase. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis were uncommon, although the relatively small trial populations limited assessment of rare adverse events. Two trials were judged to have low overall risk of bias, while nine had some concerns; none was judged to have high risk of bias. AID systems consistently improve CGM-derived glycemic outcomes in children and adolescents with T1D, with the most reproducible benefit being increased TIR and reduced hyperglycemic exposure. Improvements in glycated hemoglobin were comparatively modest. Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a consistent increase in hypoglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis, although longer and larger studies are needed to characterize rare safety outcomes. AID should be regarded as an effective strategy for reducing glycemic burden rather than a fully autonomous treatment. Future research should emphasize long-term clinical and psychosocial outcomes, treatment burden, technology-related complications, and representation of diverse pediatric populations.

articles.title: Empowering Birth: An Analysis of Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness Among Pregnant Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-related complications remain a major public health concern, particularly in developing countries. Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness (BPACR) is a key strategy to reduce maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality by encouraging timely utilization of skilled obstetric care. This study aimed to assess the status of BPACR among pregnant women in rural eastern India and identify factors influencing its adoption.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicentric cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,145 pregnant women attending Maternal and Child Health clinics in rural districts of eastern India over a 12-month period. Eligible participants were currently pregnant women who had attended at least one antenatal care (ANC) visit and provided informed consent. Data were collected using a pre-tested, structured questionnaire adapted from the Johns Hopkins Program for International Education in Gynaecology and Obstetrics (JHPIEGO) Safe Motherhood tool. Information regarding socio-demographic characteristics, obstetric history, BPACR practices, and knowledge of obstetric danger signs was obtained. Women practicing at least three key BPACR components were categorized as "well-prepared." Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with BPACR.
RESULTS: Among the participants, 632 (55.2%) had identified a health facility for delivery, 1,129 (98.6%) had arranged transportation, 821 (71.7%) had saved money for delivery-related expenses, and only 142 (12.4%) had identified potential blood donors. Overall, 490 (42.8%) of women were classified as well-prepared. Multivariate analysis revealed that higher socio-economic status (AOR=10.831; 95% CI: 7.384-15.886), joint family living (AOR=3.654; 95% CI: 2.467-5.410), multigravidity (AOR=4.837; 95% CI: 3.099-7.550), and good knowledge of danger signs (AOR=5.344; 95% CI: 3.851-7.416) were significant predictors of better preparedness.
CONCLUSION: Despite satisfactory preparedness regarding transportation and institutional delivery, significant gaps remain in blood donor identification and emergency financial planning. Strengthening maternal education, improving awareness of danger signs, and promoting comprehensive BPACR through community-based interventions are essential to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes in rural settings.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Limitations of Routine Vital Signs and Early Warning Scores in Postpartum Maternal Sepsis: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Maternal sepsis after childbirth can be difficult to recognize because expected postpartum physiological changes and common obstetric complications may resemble early infection. Conversely, sepsis may initially occur without marked physiological abnormalities. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance and limitations of routine vital signs, shock index, and vital sign-based screening systems for the early recognition of postpartum maternal sepsis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar were searched through July 13, 2026, with supplementary citation and manual searching. Eligible studies included postpartum populations and mixed obstetric populations with relevant postpartum data. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using design-appropriate tools. The primary synthesis examined diagnostic and screening performance, while a secondary synthesis considered severity prediction. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis. Nineteen studies were included. Higher-sensitivity screening approaches generally produced more alerts and lower specificity, whereas more specific approaches identified a smaller proportion of cases. In mixed obstetric evidence, systemic inflammatory response syndrome favored sensitivity at the expense of specificity, while quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment showed greater specificity but lower sensitivity. Abnormal temperature was frequently observed without confirmed infection, while sepsis could also occur without fever; other vital signs and composite scores showed similarly context-dependent performance. Shock index was more informative for severity prediction after suspected or confirmed infection than for initial diagnosis. Most studies had important methodological limitations. Current evidence does not support the use of any isolated vital sign or warning score to confirm or exclude postpartum maternal sepsis. Repeated complete observations, assessment of physiological trends, and interpretation within the clinical context may improve recognition.

articles.title: Impact of Congenital Uterovaginal Anomalies on Maternal and Fetal Outcomes at a Tertiary Hospital in Punjab: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital uterovaginal anomalies result from abnormal formation, fusion, or resorption of the Müllerian ducts during embryogenesis. They may remain asymptomatic or present with abnormal uterine bleeding, dyspareunia, subfertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, preterm birth, or fetal malpresentation. This study evaluated maternal and fetal outcomes among pregnant women with congenital uterovaginal anomalies at a tertiary referral hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center prospective observational comparative study was conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Government Medical College and its associated tertiary-care hospital, Amritsar, Punjab, India, from April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2025. Consecutive total-enumeration sampling included all eligible singleton pregnancies with a previously diagnosed anomaly or an anomaly identified during the index pregnancy, delivery, or cesarean section. Multiple pregnancies were excluded. All 32 eligible women were included; therefore, no a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Maternal and fetal outcomes were summarized descriptively and compared with contemporaneous aggregate hospital data for pregnant women without a documented uterovaginal anomaly. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and categorical outcomes were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A two-sided p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Among 5,407 pregnancies/deliveries recorded during the study period, 32 women had a congenital uterovaginal anomaly (hospital-detected prevalence, 0.59%). Most participants (78.13%) were aged 21-35 years. Arcuate uterus was the most frequent anomaly (28.13%), followed by bicornuate and septate uteri (21.88% each). A history of subfertility was present in 40.63% of women, and 43.75% had experienced a previous preterm birth. During the index pregnancy, three spontaneous abortions (9.38%) and two ectopic pregnancies (6.25%) occurred. Among the 27 pregnancies continuing beyond these early outcomes, 12 fetuses (44.44%) had a malpresentation, 15 births (55.56%) were preterm, and 19 neonates (70.37%) had a birth weight <2.5 kg. Aggregate hospital comparisons suggested higher odds of abortion, ectopic pregnancy, malpresentation, preterm birth, and low birth weight among women with anomalies; however, estimates were unadjusted and should be interpreted cautiously because the anomaly group was small and only aggregate comparator data were available.
CONCLUSION: Congenital uterovaginal anomalies should be considered in women with unexplained subfertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, recurrent preterm birth, or fetal malpresentation. Early recognition permits individualized counselling, targeted antenatal surveillance, and delivery planning. Because many anomalies in this cohort were detected only during cesarean delivery, careful documentation and postpartum counselling are essential to guide the management of future pregnancies.

articles.title: Universal Versus Selective Sampling of Umbilical Cord Gases in University-Based, Academic Community-Based, and Private Practice Settings: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background Umbilical cord blood gas analysis provides an objective assessment of fetal metabolic status at delivery and may aid in identifying acute intrapartum hypoxic-ischemic events and newborns at risk for neurologic injury. However, there is no consensus regarding universal versus selective cord gas sampling, and professional society recommendations vary. This study aimed to evaluate differences in umbilical cord gas sampling practices, institutional protocols, and indications for sampling among obstetric providers across university-based, academic community, and private practice settings. Methods An anonymous survey was distributed to independent obstetric providers at hospitals with labor and delivery units throughout the greater Philadelphia region, including New Jersey, from September through December 2023. Eligible respondents included physicians (MD/DO) and certified nurse-midwives who independently managed deliveries. Respondents were categorized as practicing in university-based hospitals with residents, academic community hospitals with residents, or private practices without residents. The survey assessed demographics, knowledge of institutional protocols, individual practice preferences, and indications for cord gas sampling. Pairwise comparisons were performed among practice settings using Fisher's exact test for unordered categorical variables and Wilcoxon tests for ordinal variables. Results Seventy-eight providers responded, of whom 77 met inclusion criteria: 29 (37.7%) practiced in university-based settings, 33 (42.9%) in academic community settings, and 15 (19.5%) in private practice. University-based providers were more likely to report the presence of an institutional cord gas protocol (p<0.01), favor universal cord gas sampling (p<0.05), and obtain cord gases in patients requiring fetal surveillance. Reported frequency of cord gas sampling differed significantly by practice setting, with the highest frequency in university-based hospitals, followed by academic community hospitals and private practices (p<0.05). Across practice settings, providers generally agreed that fetal growth restriction <3rd percentile, Category III fetal heart rate tracings, maternal substance use, and five-minute Apgar scores <7 were indications for cord gas sampling. No significant differences were identified in awareness of protocol specifics, institutional indications for sampling, or methods of cord gas procurement. University-based providers were more likely to report preemptively setting aside a segment of umbilical cord after delivery (p<0.001). Providers across all practice settings supported delayed cord clamping. Conclusions Umbilical cord gas sampling practices and provider preferences vary significantly by practice setting, with university-based providers reporting greater use of cord gas sampling, greater awareness of institutional protocols, and stronger preference for universal sampling compared with academic community and private practice providers. Despite these differences, providers demonstrated agreement on several high-risk clinical indications for cord gas analysis. These findings highlight variability in current practice and identify areas of provider consensus that may help inform standardized criteria for selective cord gas sampling and future prospective studies comparing selective with universal sampling.

articles.title: Transitional Fetal Circulation: A Comprehensive Review of Physiological Adaptation, Failure, and Neonatal Outcomes.
articles.abstract: The change from fetal to neonatal circulation is one of the most rapid and consequential physiological reorganizations in human life, and it is more accurately described as an integrated cardiopulmonary and placental sequence than as simple closure of fetal shunts. Before birth, the placenta is the organ of gas exchange, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is high, and the ductus venosus, foramen ovale, and ductus arteriosus sustain a parallel circulation that preferentially directs relatively oxygenated umbilical venous blood to the myocardium and brain. At birth, lung aeration, clearance of fetal lung liquid, a rise in alveolar and arterial oxygen tension, and mechanical recruitment of the pulmonary microvasculature produce a steep fall in PVR and a several-fold increase in pulmonary blood flow. Pulmonary venous return then replaces umbilical venous return as the dominant source of left ventricular preload, while interruption of the low-resistance placental circuit raises systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and left ventricular afterload. These pressure and flow changes, rather than any intrinsic anatomical event, drive functional closure of the foramen ovale and progressive constriction of the ductus arteriosus. Failure or delay of this coordinated sequence produces a spectrum of hemodynamic disorders: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), myocardial dysfunction, inadequate preload, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the preterm infant, and decompensation of previously unrecognized duct-dependent congenital heart disease. The mechanisms include incomplete alveolar recruitment, hypoxemia, acidosis, inflammation, impaired nitric oxide (NO)-soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signaling, excess endothelin-1 and Rho-kinase activity, oxidative stress, ventricular maladaptation, and adverse ventriculo-ventricular interaction. Because hypoxemia, hypotension, acidosis, and poor perfusion are shared surface features of mechanistically distinct states, assessment based on blood pressure or oxygen saturation alone is inadequate. This review synthesizes fetal circulatory physiology, the molecular and mechanical basis of normal transition, the principal failed-transition phenotypes, and contemporary physiology-guided monitoring and management. It integrates recent evidence on deferred and physiology-based cord clamping, including the 2023 individual participant data meta-analysis of preterm cord management and the 2024 ABC3 randomized trial; the 2024 American Society of Echocardiography update on targeted neonatal echocardiography; the 2025 American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics neonatal resuscitation guidelines; randomized and network meta-analytic evidence on PPHN pharmacotherapy; and the shift from routine early PDA closure to selective, phenotype-based management. A mechanistic understanding of transitional circulation allows earlier recognition of neonatal cardiovascular compromise and discourages the indiscriminate treatment of numerical hypoxemia or hypotension.

articles.title: Caregiver Burden in Highly Complex Pediatric Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Associations With Functional Status and Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Background Caregiver burden is an important consequence of caring for children with highly complex drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Although greater functional impairment may increase caregiving demands, burden may also be influenced by developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) and caregiver characteristics. We aimed to estimate caregiver burden and determine whether child functional status remained associated with burden after accounting for DEE and caregiver characteristics. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analytical study of 59 child-caregiver dyads with highly complex DRE attending a national high-specialty medical center in Mexico City between November 2025 and February 2026. Caregiver burden was assessed using the 22-item Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI), with scores >46 defining overburden. Child functional status was assessed using the Functional Status Scale (FSS). DEE was classified according to an operational definition incorporating frequent seizures and/or epileptiform discharges, developmental slowing or regression, and an underlying etiology contributing to developmental impairment. Logistic regression models evaluated threshold-defined overburden, and a complementary linear model examined continuous ZBI scores. Results Overburden was present in 40/59 caregivers (67.8%; 95% CI, 54.4%-79.4%). Among 54 children with available FSS assessments, FSS scores were higher in dyads with overburden than in those without (median 11 (IQR, 9-20) vs 8 (IQR, 7-11.5); p = 0.021). However, the correlation between FSS and continuous ZBI scores was weak and not significant (rho = 0.165; p = 0.233). FSS was associated with overburden in the univariable model (OR per point, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29), but this association attenuated after inclusion of DEE and caregiver characteristics and was not significant in the combined model (OR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.22). In the combined model, DEE (OR, 8.38; 95% CI, 1.14-61.85) and caregiver age per 10 years (OR, 4.51; 95% CI, 1.26-16.12) were associated with overburden. In the continuous ZBI model, caregiver age was associated with higher burden (B = 6.49 points per 10 years; 95% CI, 1.59-11.39), as was parental caregiver status (B = 13.68; 95% CI, 2.19-25.16), whereas FSS and DEE were not independently associated with continuous ZBI scores. Individual FSS domains showed no consistent association with burden. Conclusions Caregiver overburden was frequent in this Mexican cohort of children with highly complex DRE. Although poorer functional status distinguished caregivers with overburden before adjustment, its association weakened after consideration of DEE and caregiver characteristics and was not observed when burden was analyzed continuously. DEE showed a large but imprecise association with threshold-defined overburden, whereas caregiver age was consistently associated with both categorical and continuous measures of burden.
