These findings suggest that caregiver burden should be understood as a distinct caregiver-level outcome within the broader clinical and family context of highly complex pediatric DRE, rather than solely as a consequence of the child's functional impairment.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Assessment of Gastric Volumes in Paediatric Patients Receiving Five Percent Dextrose Water Versus Plain Water Preoperatively: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative fasting guidelines recommend clear fluids up to two hours before surgery to prevent prolonged fasting times and pulmonary aspiration. Gastric ultrasound is a safe, valid, non-invasive and readily available tool that can be used to look for the residual gastric volumes (GVs) and to confirm the fasting status in case of doubtful fasting period. The aim of this study was to evaluate ultrasound-guided assessment of GVs in children receiving either 5% dextrose water or plain water preoperatively, and to look for the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) and thirst.
METHODS: The study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee and registered with CTRI with trial number CTRI/2023/09/057732. This prospective, randomised, controlled study included 60 American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-II paediatric patients (5-12 years) undergoing elective surgery. Gastric antral cross-sectional area (CSA) and volumes were measured. Patients received 3 mL/kg of either 5% dextrose water (Group A) or plain water (Group B) two hours before surgery. The primary outcome was the measurement of GV at baseline and two hours. Ultrasound assessments were performed at baseline and two hours after fluid intake. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of PONV and thirst in the postoperative period.
RESULTS: The study found no significant differences in antral CSA or volume between the two groups at baseline and two hours. At baseline, CSA: t = -0.900, p=0.372, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.232 (95% CI: -0.580 to 0.220); GV: t= -0.800, p=0.427, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.207 (95% CI: -3.660 to 1.569). After two hours, CSA: t=0.579, p=0.565, effect size (Cohen's d) = 0.149 (95% CI: -0.268 to 0.486); GV: t = -0.561, p=0.577, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.145 (95% CI: -3.396 to 1.910). PONV was absent in both groups, and the prevalence of thirst did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSION: Administering 5% dextrose water or plain water two hours preoperatively has similar effects on residual GVs in paediatric patients. The choice between the two fluids did not influence PONV or thirst significantly.

articles.title: Quality of Life Among Mothers Caring for Children With Cancer at a Tertiary Cancer Hospital in Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background Mothers caring for children with cancer often assume intensive clinical, emotional, and household responsibilities. Evidence on their cancer-related quality of life in Bangladesh remains limited. This study assessed caregiver quality of life and its relationships with maternal, household, and caregiving characteristics. Methods This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 178 mothers at the National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital, Dhaka, from July 2018 to June 2019 using convenience sampling. Face-to-face interviews collected sociodemographic and caregiving data. Quality of life was measured using a 34-item modified Caregiver Quality of Life Index-Cancer (CQOLC)-derived score (range 0-136); under the study-specific coding, higher scores represented poorer quality of life. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and comparisons of mean scores across subgroups were used in this exploratory analysis, and all associations were unadjusted. Results Participants had a mean age of 30.20 years (SD 5.98); 166 (93.3%) were homemakers, and 161 (90.4%) lived in nuclear families. Mean daily caregiving time was 9.38 hours (SD 2.54). The median modified CQOLC-derived total score was 80 (range 51-108). Higher total scores were correlated with more daily caregiving hours (r = 0.366, p < 0.001), longer caregiving duration (r = 0.192, p = 0.010), and older maternal age (r = 0.165, p = 0.027), whereas monthly household income was inversely correlated with the total score (r = -0.183, p = 0.014). Mean total scores also differed by housing type (p = 0.006). Conclusions Within this sample, greater daily caregiving time showed the strongest relationship with poorer study-specific quality-of-life scores; longer caregiving duration, older maternal age, and lower household income were also weakly associated with poorer scores. The findings suggest that caregiver screening and practical and psychosocial support may be useful in pediatric oncology, but they should be interpreted cautiously because of the modified instrument without reliability testing, the cross-sectional design, and single-center sampling.

articles.title: Clinical Insights and Social Vulnerability in Infantile Hemangiomas: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort in Puerto Rico.
articles.abstract: Infantile hemangiomas (IHs) are the most common benign vascular tumors in childhood. While most occurrences regress spontaneously, some require treatment due to ulceration, functional impairment, or cosmetic concerns. In Puerto Rico, social determinants of health potentially affect both access to healthcare and clinical outcomes. The Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), a composite metric encompassing socioeconomic status, household composition, transportation, and other social factors, is commonly used to evaluate community-level vulnerability. This study sought to describe lesion location and treatment modalities, and evaluate whether the SVI is associated with treatment outcomes in IH patients in Puerto Rico as measured by lesion size at presentation, follow-up, and change in lesion size following treatment. Records of pediatric patients diagnosed with hemangiomas between 2015 and 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. A total of 30 patients were identified, and extracted data included patient demographics, treatment modality, lesion location, and lesion size, as measured via a flexible measuring tape, before and after treatment. SVI was calculated and assigned according to patients' residential Zone Improvement Plan (ZIP) code and matched to the corresponding SVI values obtained from the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) database at the time of presentation. Most patients (43.3%) were treated with propranolol, followed by surgical resection or embolization (20%). The most affected areas were the limbs (50%) and the head and neck (30%) region. Using Spearman's rank correlation, the study found that a higher SVI was associated with a larger hemangioma lesion size at presentation (Spearman's rho = 0.681, p = 0.005) and remained correlated with a larger post-treatment lesion size (Spearman's rho = 0.634, p = 0.011). However, the SVI was not associated with the magnitude of size reduction following treatment (Spearman's rho = 0.09, p = 0.742), meaning that the disparities in lesion size are likely due to differences in disease severity at the time of diagnosis rather than differences due to treatment response. Meanwhile, results also suggest that since more than half of patients were managed with pharmacologic therapy, treatment compliance may play an important role in influencing outcomes. Ultimately, SVIs could be used to flag patients who may present later or with larger lesions in order to enable earlier monitoring and management.

articles.title: Minor Salivary Gland Biopsy in Sjögren Disease: From Diagnostic Criterion to Clinical Decision Tool.
articles.abstract: Minor salivary gland biopsy (MSGB) remains an important tool in the evaluation of patients with suspected Sjögren disease (SjD), particularly when the clinical presentation and serologic findings are inconclusive. Although traditionally used to identify focal lymphocytic sialadenitis and determine a focus score, the potential clinical value of MSGB extends beyond a binary positive or negative result. Histopathologic findings may provide additional information about glandular inflammation, lymphoid organization, epithelial injury, fibrosis, and disease phenotype. MSGB may be particularly useful in anti-Sjögren syndrome-related antigen A/Ro (anti-SSA/Ro)-negative disease and may have a role in childhood-onset disease and the assessment of features associated with systemic disease and lymphoma risk. The procedure can generally be performed in an outpatient setting, although sensory complications should be discussed before biopsy. Salivary gland ultrasonography (SGUS) provides a complementary, noninvasive assessment of glandular structure and may help identify patients who require further tissue evaluation. This narrative review discusses the practical indications for MSGB, biopsy technique and safety, histopathologic interpretation, its role in anti-SSA/Ro-negative and childhood-onset disease, prognostic implications, relationship to SGUS, and emerging applications in tissue-based phenotyping and precision medicine.

articles.title: Effects of Intravenous Dexamethasone on IL-6 Levels in Children Undergoing Cardiac Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary bypass provokes a systemic inflammatory response in children, with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels rising rapidly after bypass. Corticosteroids are frequently used to blunt this response, but paediatric evidence remains inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a single intravenous dose of dexamethasone reduces the post-bypass increase in plasma IL-6 and improves early postoperative outcomes in children undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
METHODS: This single-centre quasi-experimental study enrolled 46 children aged one month to 12 years undergoing elective repair of congenital heart disease between January 2025 and August 2025. Participants were purposively recruited and alternately allocated to intravenous dexamethasone (1 mg/kg, maximum 10 mg; n=23, 50.0%) or 2 mL normal saline (n=23, 50.0%) after induction of anaesthesia. Plasma IL-6 was measured before drug administration, two hours after cardiopulmonary bypass, and 24 hours after bypass. Haemodynamic variables, oxygen saturation, extubation time, and intensive care unit stay were recorded.
RESULTS: The median IL-6 increase from baseline to two hours was lower with dexamethasone than with saline (261.90 pg/mL, interquartile range: 195.0-824.0, versus 447.0 pg/mL, interquartile range: 261.70-1,230.20), but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.177). At 24 hours, the median change from baseline was 8.20 pg/mL in the dexamethasone group and 13.0 pg/mL in the saline group (p=0.350). Blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and extubation time were comparable. First-postoperative-day heart rate was higher with dexamethasone (143.63 ± 18.93 versus 117.76 ± 19.57 beats/min; p=0.001), and median intensive care unit stay was longer (120 versus 95.5 hours; p=0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of intravenous dexamethasone at 1 mg/kg, capped at 10 mg, did not significantly attenuate the IL-6 response after paediatric cardiopulmonary bypass. The higher heart rate and longer intensive care stay observed in the dexamethasone group should be treated as exploratory because allocation was nonrandom and perioperative complexity was not adjusted for.

articles.title: From Prevalence to Prediction: A Cross-Sectional Study to Develop a Novel Risk Score for Hearing Loss in High-Risk Neonates in South India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with multiple risk factors are more likely to develop hearing loss. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of hearing loss, identify its predictive factors, and develop a novel clinical risk score for hearing loss among high-risk neonates.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 105 high-risk neonates admitted to the NICU from July 2024 to June 2025. The hearing assessment protocol included transient-evoked otoacoustic emissions at discharge and at six weeks of corrected age, followed by diagnostic brainstem-evoked response audiometry at three months. Associations between risk factors and hearing loss were analyzed using logistic regression. A novel clinical risk score was developed using the factors significantly associated with hearing loss.
RESULTS: The prevalence of hearing loss among high-risk neonates was 4.8% (95% CI, 1.6%-10.8%). Hearing loss was significantly associated with intrauterine toxoplasmosis, perinatal asphyxia, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (NNH) requiring exchange transfusion, stage II or higher hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, neonatal sepsis, neonatal seizures, syndromic or craniofacial anomalies, and ototoxic drug exposure (p < 0.05). The clinical risk prediction model, developed using significant predictive factors and assigning double weight to intrauterine toxoplasmosis and NNH requiring exchange transfusion, achieved a sensitivity of 60% and a specificity of 96% at a cutoff score of ≥3.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of hearing loss among high-risk neonates was 4.8%. The novel clinical risk score developed in this study may help guide targeted screening, timely diagnosis, and early intervention for hearing loss.

articles.title: The Association of Cognitive Behavioral Play Therapy Exposure With Self-Esteem and Self-Efficacy Among School-Age Children With Learning Disabilities: An Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background and objective Learning disabilities in children can affect their emotional and social functioning as well as academic performance and self-perception. Cognitive-behavioral play therapy (CBPT) is a therapeutic approach that may help address psychosocial difficulties in children. However, the evidence on the association between prior CBPT exposure and the self-esteem and self-efficacy of children with learning disabilities remains limited. This study examined the association between prior CBPT exposure and self-esteem and general self-efficacy among school-age children with learning disabilities. Methods This cross-sectional observational study included children aged 10-14 years who had been diagnosed with learning disabilities. Prior exposure to CBPT was determined based on information provided by the participants or their parents, as well as medical records. Participants were classified into three groups according to their previous CBPT exposure: 0 sessions, 1-11 sessions, and ≥ 12 sessions. The levels of self-esteem and general self-efficacy were assessed using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) and the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSE). One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Tukey's post hoc test were used to compare differences among the three groups. Results Among the 125 participants, 50 (40.0%) had no previous CBPT exposure, 40 (32.0%) had completed 1-11 sessions, and 35 (28.0%) had completed ≥ 12 sessions. Mean RSES scores were 24.8 ± 3.8, 27.5 ± 3.8, and 29.8 ± 3.4, respectively, with a significant difference among the groups (p < 0.001). Mean GSE scores were 27.1 ± 4.7, 30.0 ± 4.6, and 32.9 ± 4.0, respectively (p < 0.001). The number of CBPT sessions was positively correlated with RSES scores (r = 0.48, p < 0.001) and GSE scores (r = 0.46, p < 0.001). In multivariable regression analysis, the number of CBPT sessions remained significantly associated with RSES scores (adjusted β = 0.28, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.38; p < 0.001) and GSE scores (adjusted β = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.22-0.45; p < 0.001) after adjustment for relevant demographic and clinical variables. Conclusions Greater previous CBPT exposure was associated with higher self-esteem and general self-efficacy among children with learning disabilities. These findings suggest that children who had received CBPT previously had higher scores on both measures than those with less or no previous exposure. However, this relationship should be interpreted as correlational rather than causal because of the cross-sectional observational design. Further prospective and intervention studies are required to determine whether CBPT leads to improvements in self-esteem and self-efficacy among children in this group.

articles.title: Conventional Therapy in Pediatric Hypophosphatemic Rickets: Growth Outcomes and Nephrocalcinosis Risk.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) is characterized by renal phosphate wasting and impaired skeletal mineralization. Although conventional therapy with oral phosphate and active vitamin D analogues remains widely used, its long-term biochemical, auxological, and renal outcomes are variable. This study aimed to evaluate longitudinal biochemical changes, growth patterns, cumulative phosphate exposure, and nephrocalcinosis (NC) development in children with HR receiving conventional therapy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center case series included 20 children with HR followed for at least 1 year. Clinical, biochemical, and auxological parameters were recorded at baseline and annually. Longitudinal analyses were performed in patients with complete 3-year follow-up (n = 10) using the Friedman test, and cumulative phosphate exposure was compared according to NC status.
RESULTS: Alkaline phosphatase levels decreased significantly during follow-up (P = .021), whereas serum phosphate levels did not show sustained normalization (P = 0.627). Height standard deviation score did not significantly change over 3 years (P = .644). Nephrocalcinosis developed in 25% (n = 5/20) of the overall cohort and in 40% (n = 4/10) of patients with complete follow-up. Patients with NC had significantly higher cumulative phosphate exposure (P = .010), without significant differences in height standard deviation score (SDS) or other biochemical parameters.
CONCLUSION: Conventional therapy was associated with partial biochemical improvement but limited auxological benefit. Higher cumulative phosphate exposure was associated with NC development without evident growth advantage, underscoring the importance of balancing biochemical targets with renal safety in pediatric HR.

articles.title: Clinical Course and Outcomes of Complicated Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Children During a 5-Year Period Including the COVID-19 Pandemic.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a significant cause of morbidity in children. Despite widespread vaccination, the incidence and clinical course of complicated CAP (cCAP) continue to pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical course, management, and outcomes of children with cCAP in pediatric clinical practice.
METHODS: This retrospective-prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary university hospital between December 2019 and December 2024. Children under 18 years of age diagnosed with cCAP were included.
RESULTS: A total of 52 children were included, with a median age of 70.5 months; 48.1% were female. Parapneumonic effusion (PPE) was the most common complication (86.5%), followed by empyema (21.2%) and necrotizing pneumonia (7.6%). Bacterial pathogens were identified in a minority of cases. Among the limited number of culture-positive cases, group A Streptococcus and Streptococcus pneumoniae were the most frequently identified organisms (11.5%, n = 6). Chest tube thoracostomy was required in 60% of patients, and surgical intervention in 9.6%. Patients requiring chest tube placement had significantly higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and longer durations of intravenous (IV) antibiotic therapy. No mortality was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite extensive vaccination in healthy children, cases of cCAP still occur, and the causative agent is isolated only in a very few cases. The findings are consistent with the fact that vaccine breakthrough infections, including those caused by pneumococcal serotypes 3 and 14, may still contribute to severe cCAP, whereas group A Streptococcus was identified in a minority of culture-positive cases. Elevated CRP levels at admission may serve as a useful predictor for invasive interventions.

articles.title: Validity and Reliability of a Thai Version of the Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List (PedHAL) is a self-administered instrument for assessing activity limitations in children with haemophilia, yet no Thai version has previously undergone psychometric evaluation.
AIM: To evaluate the validity and reliability of a Thai version of the PedHAL.
METHODS: Following permission from the original developer, the PedHAL was translated into Thai using forward-backwards translation. Content validity was examined via the content validity index (CVI). Construct validity was determined by correlating PedHAL scores with the Functional Independence Score in Haemophilia (FISH) and the Haemophilia Joint Health Score (HJHS). Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were assessed with Cronbach's alpha and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), respectively. The participants were nineteen children with haemophilia who attended the Departments of Rehabilitation Medicine and Paediatrics, Faculty of Medicine Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, between June 2021 and September 2022.
RESULTS: The Thai PedHAL demonstrated excellent content validity (CVI  =  0.99; threshold  ≥ 0.90) and good construct validity, as evidenced by a strong positive correlation with FISH (r  =  0.703; range 0.70‒0.89) and a moderate negative correlation with HJHS (r  =  -0.475; range 0.40‒0.69). Reliability testing revealed excellent test-retest reliability (ICC  =  0.955; threshold ≥ 0.90) and excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha  =  0.944; threshold ≥ 0.90).
CONCLUSION: The Thai version of the PedHAL has acceptable-to-excellent psychometric properties for measuring activity limitations in Thai children with haemophilia. It may serve as a valuable instrument for both clinical and research applications.

articles.title: Imagery ability in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy and associations with clinical characteristics: a cross-sectional pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Movement Imagery Questionnaire for Children (MIQ-C) assesses children's imagery ability through three subcomponents: internal visual imagery (IVI), external visual imagery (EVI), and kinesthetic imagery (KI).
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the imagery ability and its associations with clinical characteristics in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy (OBPP).
METHODS: Fifteen children with OBPP (mean age 10.67 ± 1.18 years; 8 males and 7 females) and 15 healthy children frequency‑matched for age and sex were included. Motor imagery was assessed using the MIQ-C. Motor and sensory functions in participants with OBPP were evaluated using the Active Movement Scale (AMS) and the Narakas Sensory Grading System (NSG), respectively. Mann-Whitney U tests assessed between-group differences in MIQ-C subscores; intraclass correlation coefficients (95% confidence intervals) evaluated test-retest reliability in both groups; and Spearman rank correlations examined associations with clinical characteristics in the OBPP group.
RESULTS: Children with OBPP had significantly lower scores than the control group across all MIQ-C subscores (after Bonferroni adjustment to 0.0167; p ≤ .005). In the OBPP group, clinical type was strongly negatively correlated with all MIQ-C subscores. Higher imagery scores were observed in children classified as NSG = 3 than in those classified as NSG = 2. Positive correlations also were found between MIQ-C subscores and AMS scores.
CONCLUSION: Compared to controls, children with OBPP demonstrated lower imagery scores, suggesting potential differences in imagery ability between the groups. Exploratory findings also indicated possible relationships between imagery scores and clinical characteristics; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size. Motor imagery assessment may offer complementary information about imagery ability alongside routine motor and sensory evaluations in OBPP rehabilitation.

articles.title: Maternal Caffeine Intake on Fetal and Childhood Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Maternal caffeine consumption during pregnancy may increase fetal exposure due to reduced caffeine metabolism in high-estrogen states. This review aimed to assess the current literature on maternal caffeine intake and its effects on birth outcomes and fetal development.
METHODS: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed and Web of Science were searched using Boolean keyword strategies related to caffeine exposure during pregnancy and fetal outcomes. Eligible designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, observational studies, cross-sectional studies, and case-control studies. Studies that did not assess caffeine exposure during pregnancy, non-original studies, case reports, animal studies, and those outside the 2015-2025 timeframe were excluded. Two independent reviewers evaluated titles, abstracts, and full texts against predefined eligibility criteria, and disagreements were resolved by a third author. Risk of bias was assessed.
RESULTS: We identified 519 records; 17 studies were included after screening. Included cohort and observational designs examined associations between maternal caffeine intake and fetal, neonatal, and childhood outcomes. Several reported dose-dependent associations between higher caffeine intake and reduced fetal growth measures, including lower birth weight and increased risk of small for gestational age, while others found no significant associations after adjusting for confounders.
CONCLUSION AND GLOBAL HEALTH IMPLICATIONS: Prenatal caffeine exposure can alter fetal growth and developmental trajectories, but the impact and reliability of results remain questionable. Discrepancies likely stem from confounding maternal lifestyle factors, variations in caffeine sources, exposure timing, intake quantification, populations, and self-reporting biases, underscoring the need for standardized parameters across prospective studies. From a global health perspective, the overall impact of prenatal caffeine exposure remains unclear due to this inconsistent and confounded evidence base. Ongoing research is essential to better define risks and inform consistent, evidence-based public health recommendations across diverse populations.

articles.title: Two-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging for assessing cardiac dysfunction in liver cirrhosis: correlation with Child-Pugh score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. This study applied 2D-STI to evaluate both ventricular and atrial function in order to identify early myocardial dysfunction in this population.
METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). Thirty healthy individuals served as controls. All 112 participants underwent conventional echocardiography and 2D-STI assessment.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. In contrast, right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly decreased only in Classes B and C (P < 0.05). Left atrial conduit strain (LAScd) was significantly reduced across all LC groups (P < 0.05), whereas left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contractile strain (LASct) demonstrated a biphasic pattern -initially increased, then decreased- compared with controls. Overall, 2D-STI detected cardiac dysfunction earlier than conventional echocardiography. Significant negative correlations were observed between Child-Pugh score and LVGLS, RVFWLS, and RVGLS.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac function is impaired in patients with LC and deteriorates with increasing disease severity. Compared with conventional echocardiography, 2D-STI detects cardiac dysfunction at an earlier stage, providing valuable support for early clinical intervention.

articles.title: Complete Blood Count-Derived Inflammatory Markers in Treatment-Naive Patients With First-Episode Psychosis and First Manic Episode: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence supporting the role of immune-inflammatory mechanisms in psychiatric disorders is increasing. This study compared complete blood count-derived haematological and inflammatory markers in treatment-naive patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP) or a first manic episode (FMEs) and healthy controls (HCs).
METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 74 treatment-naive patients and 91 HC. The primary analysis compared patients with HC, while secondary analyses compared the FEP and FME groups. Selected parameters showing significant between-group differences were further evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and body mass index (BMI).
RESULTS: Patients had higher white blood cell (WBC), neutrophil and platelet counts, plateletcrit, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), derived NLR (dNLR) and neutrophil-to-monocyte ratio (NMR), together with lower platelet distribution width (PDW) and mean platelet volume-to-platelet ratio (MPR). No significant differences in inflammatory markers were found between the FEP and FME groups. WBC and neutrophil counts showed the highest, although moderate, discriminative performance. In adjusted regression models, WBC count, neutrophil count, SII, SIRI and AISI were significantly associated with patient status. However, SII, SIRI and AISI provided no significant incremental explanatory value beyond neutrophil count.
CONCLUSION: Peripheral immune-inflammatory activation may already be evident in the early stages of treatment-naive FEP and FME. The absence of significant differences in inflammatory markers between the FEP and FME groups limits their potential utility as diagnosis-specific biomarkers.

articles.title: Bridging Inpatient and Community Care Following First Episode Psychosis: A Pilot Feasibility and Acceptability Study of a Brief Psychological Intervention.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study evaluated the implementation feasibility and acceptability of a brief CBT-informed psychological intervention designed to bridge inpatient and community care for young adults experiencing a first episode of psychosis (FEP).
METHODS: A six-session individual CBT-informed intervention was delivered to patients experiencing a FEP approaching discharge from a specialist early intervention inpatient unit. The intervention commenced on the ward (the initial session) and continued into the community. Feasibility was assessed from a service implementation perspective, including recruitment, uptake, retention, intervention completion, and outcome measure completion rates. Acceptability was evaluated using satisfaction ratings and qualitative interviews.
RESULTS: During a seven-month period, 43 patients were screened, and 38 were eligible to participate. Twenty-eight (74%) consented, six (15%) disengaged, and 17 (44%) completed all six sessions and study measures. Findings indicated that the intervention could be successfully delivered across inpatient and community settings within routine clinical care. Patients reported high satisfaction with therapy (mean satisfaction score = 4.76/5). Qualitative feedback highlighted the value of psychological continuity across care settings, development of coping strategies, and opportunities to make sense of admission and recovery experiences. Clinical outcome measures were successfully collected; however, the study was not designed to evaluate intervention effectiveness.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that delivering a brief CBT-informed intervention across inpatient and community services is feasible within routine clinical practice and acceptable to young adults experiencing FEP. Further controlled research is required to evaluate clinical effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation for Pediatric Acquired Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVirtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR) rehabilitation shows promise after adult brain injury, but its efficacy in pediatric acquired brain injury remains unclear.ObjectiveTo synthesize within-person changes in cognitive, motor, and functional outcomes following VR/AR rehabilitation in pediatric acquired brain injury and explore moderators.MethodsSix databases were searched through March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Of 373 records, ten studies (nine VR, one AR) were included: four randomized trials and six uncontrolled studies. Standardized mean changes were pooled using three-level random-effects meta-analysis.ResultsAcross 72 effect sizes, VR/AR rehabilitation was associated with significant pre-post improvement (g = 0.62, 95% CI [0.15, 1.09], p = .01). Improvements were significant for motor and functional outcomes, but not cognitive outcomes. Outcome domain, developmental stage, study design, immersion, assessment method, and treatment dose were not significant moderators. Longer pre-post intervals predicted larger changes (β = 0.01, p = .004), potentially reflecting natural recovery. Overall improvements remained significant across assumed correlations and when restricting analyses to VR, excluding mixed diagnostic samples, or clustering by research team. Funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.ConclusionsVR-based rehabilitation was associated with within-person improvement, but comparative efficacy remains uncertain because evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly uncontrolled. Larger controlled studies should evaluate efficacy, safety, mechanisms, durability, and functional transfer.

articles.title: From Training to Practice in Public School Music Therapy: Clients, Service Delivery, and Professional Support.
articles.abstract: Many music therapists work in school settings with children and adolescents with disabilities, yet little is known about how they specifically deliver services. This study describes the results of a questionnaire asking music therapists working in school settings in the United States about their training, current service delivery models, collaboration with other professionals, and thoughts about music therapy in inclusive settings; a total of 360 responses were analyzed. Respondents were neutral about the adequacy of their undergraduate practica and coursework to prepare them to work with children with disabilities but felt that their internship was adequate preparation. During their training and professional work, respondents most often collaborated with special educators and paraprofessionals. Music therapy sessions were most often provided in self-contained groups, followed by individual sessions, and inclusive groups. The most common special education categories served were children with intellectual disability, speech language impairment, and autism. Findings are discussed considering recommendations for educators and suggestions for future research to grow the evidence base about music therapy with children with disabilities.

articles.title: Prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease among obese, overweight, and at-risk children and adolescents in Türkiye: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Among children, the overall prevalence of MASLD is estimated at around 7%, and early manifestation is associated with a more severe prognosis. Despite this growing burden, no systematic analysis of pediatric MASLD prevalence in Türkiye has yet been conducted. Here, we aimed to estimate the pediatric MASLD prevalence among children with specific conditions in Türkiye.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted for studies published in English and/or Turkish between 2005 and 2023 using the databases MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE, and ULAKBIM. The search strategy included the following terms: "Türkiye AND NAFLD AND Pediatric" and "Türkiye AND NAFLD AND Prevalence AND Children AND Adolescent." The studies identified through this literature review were incorporated into the meta-analysis, which included either obese/overweight or at-risk children or adolescents with specific conditions such as increased transaminases.
RESULTS: The pooled overall prevalence of MASLD was estimated as 44.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 39.5-49.7) among at-risk children and adolescents. Heterogeneity among studies was considerable, with an I2 value of 96%, indicating substantial variability. Subgroup analysis showed a pooled prevalence of 54.9% in boys (95% CI: 48.6-61.1) and 41.2% in girls (95% CI: 35.6-46.9). Regionally, the prevalence was 49.0% (95% CI: 41.2-57.1) in the Marmara and Aegean regions, and 42.2% (95% CI: 35.3-49.1) in the Black Sea, Mediterranean, and Central Anatolian regions.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study indicate a markedly high prevalence of MASLD among at-risk children and adolescents. These findings should serve as an alert for policymakers to adapt healthcare strategies aimed at preventing childhood obesity and MASLD.

articles.title: MYCN amplification suppresses PD-L1 and CXCL10 to drive an immunosuppressive microenvironment in neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Qiao et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children, and outcomes for patients with high-risk disease remain poor despite intensive multimodal therapy. MYCN amplification is associated with unfavorable prognosis and an immunologically “cold” tumor microenvironment (TME). This study investigated the impact of MYCN amplification on the expression of PD-L1 and the chemokine CXCL10, two important regulators of antitumor immunity. Analysis of NB patient datasets revealed that MYCN amplification was associated with reduced expression of both PD-L1 and CXCL10. Higher expression of PD-L1 and CXCL10 correlated with significantly improved overall survival. In contrast, PD-1 and PD-L2 showed weaker associations with MYCN status and were not linked to survival outcomes. In MYCN amplified NB cell lines, PD-L1 expression remained inducible by interferon-γ (IFNγ). Silencing MYCN further enhanced IFNγ-induced PD-L1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels, indicating that MYCN suppresses PD-L1 responsiveness. The BET inhibitor JQ1 reduced IFNγ-induced PD-L1 expression regardless of MYCN status, whereas inhibition of CXCL10 secretion was observed only in MYCN non-amplified cells. Retinoic acid (RA), a standard component of NB therapy, increased PD-L1 mRNA expression in all cell lines but increased PD-L1 protein expression primarily in MYCN non-amplified cells. Overall, these findings identify MYCN as a key regulator of immune signaling in NB and suggest that MYCN amplification contributes to an immune-cold tumor phenotype through suppression of PD-L1 and CXCL10 expression. MYCN status may therefore serve as a biomarker for immune stratification and guide the development of combination immunotherapeutic strategies for high-risk NB.

articles.title: Predictors and prognostic stratification of bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
articles.abstract: Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome (BOS) after pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) carries high mortality, partly due to diagnostic delays and static assessments. This brief report evaluates a dynamic monitoring strategy for early warning. This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 201 children who underwent allo-HSCT between January 2015 and December 2024, comprising 29 patients with BOS and 172 non-BOS controls.Independent risk factors for BOS were identified using multivariate Cox regression analysis. Diagnostic performance of a relative FEV1 decline ≥ 10% ("at-risk" signal) was assessed. The longitudinal trajectories of pulmonary function and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) imaging scores were also compared. Cumulative BOS incidence was 6.9%. Multivariate analysis identified grade III-IV aGVHD (HR = 15.12), cGVHD (HR = 6.94), dry cough (HR = 11.77), and an early post-transplant FEV1/FVC decline of ≥ 10% (HR = 8.70) as independent risk factors for BOS development. The "at-risk" signal (BOS stage 0p) advanced diagnosis by a median of 176 days (NPV 85.0%). A significant "radio-functional discordance" (worsening HRCT scores despite stable FEV1) was observed (P < 0.001). Dynamic FEV1 monitoring suggests a sensitive early warning and prognostic signal in pediatric BOS, though its low PPV necessitates integration with comprehensive evaluation. The radio-functional discordance highlights the need for combined functional and imaging surveillance.Given the exploratory nature of this single‑center cohort with limited case numbers, all findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Age-Stratified Sirolimus Trough Concentrations in Pediatric Vascular Malformations: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus is increasingly being used off-label to treat pediatric vascular malformations. In this study, the age-stratified drug exposure, pharmacokinetic variability, and long-term treatment characteristics of sirolimus were evaluated in a real-world pediatric population.
METHODS: In this study, 144 patients (younger than 19 years) with vascular malformations who were treated with sirolimus at a single center (July 2018 and March 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. A total of 2054 therapeutic drug monitoring measurements were obtained. The patients were stratified into 6 age groups (1 month and younger to 12-18 years). The outcomes included trough concentration, interindividual variability (coefficient of variation), target range attainment, treatment duration, and MRI-based response.
RESULTS: The median follow-up was 18.3 months (range, 0.3-74.1 months). Neonates (1 month and younger) showed the highest interindividual variability (coefficient of variation = 61.6%), with lower variability observed in adolescents (40.0%, P < 0.001). Overall, 73.4% of the trough concentrations were within the target range (4-10 ng/mL), and the mean duration within the therapeutic range per patient was 70.9%. Supratherapeutic levels (>15 ng/mL) were most frequent in neonates (6.6%). Prolonged therapy (≥24 months) was observed in 31.9% of patients, with a median duration of 35.1 months. Among the 44 patients who underwent follow-up MRI, 84.1% showed disease improvement or stability.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in this study. Younger patients exhibited greater pharmacokinetic variability, necessitating closer monitoring and cautious dose adjustment. Prospective PK-PD studies incorporating standardized clinical outcomes are needed to define optimal trough targets and individualized dosing strategies.

articles.title: Gamified Self-Care Mobile App for Lifestyle Support in Children With Leukemia: Development and Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with leukemia undergoing chemotherapy may experience difficulties maintaining a healthy lifestyle and self-care behaviors. Mobile health interventions incorporating interactive and gamified educational features may provide an accessible complement to conventional education.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and preliminarily evaluate a gamified self-care mobile app and evaluate the effect of the resulting intervention package on lifestyle scores among children aged 7 to 12 years with leukemia undergoing chemotherapy.
METHODS: This 2-phase study was conducted in Mashhad, Iran. In phase 1, the app was developed using evidence from pediatric oncology guidelines and literature and underwent multidisciplinary expert review, user-based quality assessment using the Mobile App Rating Scale, and technical testing. In phase 2, a total of 60 children undergoing chemotherapy were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to an intervention or control group. Both groups received routine face-to-face education and a pamphlet; the intervention group additionally received the Lukemo app and weekly telephone follow-up for 8 weeks. The prespecified primary outcome was the total score of the Persian version of the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 4.0 (PedsQL 4.0), assessed at baseline and after 8 weeks.
RESULTS: Thirty children were allocated to each group in phase 2, and 59 completed the study (intervention: n=29; control: n=30). At 8 weeks, mean lifestyle scores were 89.79 (SD 10.88) in the intervention group and 81.10 (SD 10.57) in the control group (P=.003). The mean change from baseline was 9.10 (SD 10.36) vs 1.00 (SD 2.39) in each group, respectively, yielding a between-group difference in change of 8.10 points (95% CI 4.08-12.12; P<.001). Within-group improvement was significant in the intervention group (P<.001) but not in the control group (P=.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The intervention package incorporating the Lukemo app and weekly telephone support was associated with greater improvement in lifestyle scores over 8 weeks among children with leukemia undergoing chemotherapy. The independent contributions of the app, gamification, and telephone support could not be determined. Longer-term and multicenter studies are needed to assess sustainability and generalizability.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials IRCT20211007052692N2; https://en.irct.ir/trial/66986.

articles.title: Vaccinated parents are more likely to vaccinate their children.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vaccines are the most effective way to prevent the spread of infectious diseases. Parental vaccination status may influence acceptance of vaccination for their children. The COVID-19 pandemic provided us an opportunity to learn about parental factors that impact the vaccination of children.
METHODS: We conducted a multilingual online survey in rural California to assess parental and child vaccination status.
RESULTS: Our study found that parents who are vaccinated with either the flu or COVID-19 vaccine were likely to report that their child had received a COVID-19 vaccine.
CONCLUSION: Parental vaccination was associated with child vaccination in unadjusted analysis.

articles.title: The natural history of headache in Canadian family practice: a cross-sectional and longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Headache is a common symptom and a cause for frequent visits to family physicians. Most studies involve single visits, failing to address the chronicity of headache.
OBJECTIVES: To estimate the prevalence of headache in family practice and assess the characteristics of patients whose headache becomes enduring versus short-term.
METHODS: Using a de-identified electronic medical record database, two studies were conducted in which each encounter was coded for the patient's reasons for encounter and end of visits (EOV) using the International Classification for Primary Care (ICPC-2-R): (i) a retrospective, cross-sectional (c-s) study of encounters with headache and (ii) a retrospective, longitudinal study of patients with multiple visits for headache. Visits with or without a diagnosis at EOV were tested for associations with patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and healthcare utilization variables. Three patient pathways were identified, one of which represented ongoing visits for a mean of 14 months. The pathways were compared on the same characteristics.
RESULTS: Study 1: 15 149 symptom encounters were made by 1790 patients; headache engendered 254 visits for headache, a rate of 1.7%. Of these, 25.2% did not result in a diagnosis. Study 2: In 41.8% of patients, no diagnosis was made, and a mean of 1.20 visits were required. In 36.4%, a diagnosis was made, but no further encounters were necessary. In 21.8%, a diagnosis was made with continued visits for headache over a mean of 14 months. This group was likely female, had prior psychological conditions, and received more medications than the other two pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: In 41.8% of patients with headache, no diagnosis was made. In one-fifth of patients who continued presenting with headache after a diagnosis was made, special attention and further study are needed.

articles.title: Ovarian function and fertility after childhood cancer: risk assessment in the era of novel treatments.
articles.abstract: Advances in cancer treatment have greatly improved survival in children, adolescents and young adults. Cancer treatments, however, may have important long-term effects on ovarian function and fertility, including an increased risk of premature ovarian insufficiency. Several guidelines recommend fertility preservation counselling for patients exposed to potentially gonadotoxic treatments, although individual risk assessment remains challenging, particularly in children and adolescents. Gonadotoxicity depends on treatment exposure, age and individual susceptibility, and prospective reproductive data remain limited. This review examines the effect of conventional cancer treatments on ovarian function and fertility, as well as the methods currently used to assess ovarian reserve in female childhood cancer survivors and preserve fertility. It also considers how evolving treatment strategies across major cancers affecting adolescents and young adults may influence reproductive outcomes. Particular attention is given to the limited evidence available on the reproductive effects of targeted treatments and immunotherapies. Further prospective studies integrating ovarian reserve markers with long-term reproductive outcomes are needed, particularly for newer anticancer treatments.

articles.title: The burden of diseases, injuries, and risk factors in Canada from 2010 to 2023: an analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Global Burden of Disease Study provides systematic, comparable estimates of health loss from diseases, injuries, and risk factors across place and time. Using the most recent estimates from 2023, we sought to characterize the burden of diseases and injuries in Canada, and compare them to estimates from 2010.
METHODS: From the Global Burden of Disease Study Results tool, we obtained all-age disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates for 2023 and percent changes in all-age and age-standardized DALY rates from 2010 to 2023 for diseases, injuries, and leading risk factors. We also compared Canada to other G7 countries using age-standardized DALY rates and life expectancy.
RESULTS: In 2023, the top 4 causes of all-age DALY rates in both sexes were neoplasms, cardiovascular disease, musculoskeletal disorders, and unintentional injuries, which together accounted for 50% of the total burden of all causes in Canada. From 2010 to 2023, the largest increase in all-age DALY rates was from substance use disorders. All-age DALY rates also increased for respiratory infections and tuberculosis (which included COVID-19). Tobacco continued to be the leading measured risk factor contributing to the attributable all-age DALY rate in 2023, while drug use was the risk factor with the greatest increase in the attributable all-age DALY rate between 2010 and 2023.
INTERPRETATION: The diseases, injuries and risk factors driving the burden of disease in Canada are changing. These shifts suggest a need to orient public and population health interventions, as well as treatment and care, to meet these changes, particularly in areas where burden is increasing.

articles.title: Adjunct Low-Dose Dexmedetomidine for Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Children: An Exploratory Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective sedation in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is complicated by the adverse effects of benzodiazepines and opioids. Dexmedetomidine may provide a benzodiazepine-sparing alternative with distinct pharmacologic properties.
OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that adjunct, fixed low-dose, no-bolus dexmedetomidine would reduce midazolam and fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day in mechanically ventilated children.
METHODS: In a triple-blind randomized controlled trial, 60 mechanically ventilated patients aged 1 month to 12 years were randomized to standard sedation (continuous midazolam and fentanyl) plus low-dose dexmedetomidine (a fixed-rate continuous infusion at 0.2 µg/kg/h without a loading bolus) or matched placebo (0.9% normal saline). In both groups, midazolam and fentanyl were titrated per protocol to achieve the target Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) level.
RESULTS: Among 60 randomized children, adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine did not reduce the prespecified primary outcome of fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Median fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day was 70.0 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the control group and 90.6 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the dexmedetomidine group; median midazolam exposure per ventilator-day was 7.0 mg·kg-1·day-1 and 9.1 mg·kg-1·day-1, respectively. Neither primary comparison remained statistically significant after Holm correction. In an unadjusted secondary analysis, the median time to first successful extubation was 6 days in the dexmedetomidine group and 15 days in the control group. This finding was exploratory and was not confirmed by the prespecified competing-risk or longitudinal ventilation analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine without a loading bolus did not reduce fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Early sedative-analgesic exposure was higher with dexmedetomidine, and the apparent early-extubation signal was exploratory and was not confirmed by competing-risk or longitudinal analyses of ventilation.

articles.title: All-cause mortality among persons with and without diagnosed diabetes in Greenland: a nationwide register-based cohort study.
articles.abstract: Mortality has historically been about twice as high in people with diabetes as in those without, although this gap has narrowed in high-income countries. Whether this pattern also applies in Greenland is unknown. We estimated age- and sex-specific mortality rates and mortality rate ratios by diabetes status in Greenland. In this nationwide register-based cohort study, we included all persons with a registered civil address in Greenland from 2017 to 2023 and used Poisson regression to estimate mortality per 1,000 person-years, mortality rate ratios by diabetes status and sex, and the annual change in mortality. Of 87,652 residents, 2,670 had diagnosed diabetes. During the study period, 3,639 persons died, 388 of whom had diabetes. Age-specific mortality rates were slightly higher among persons with diabetes than among persons without diabetes at most ages in both sexes. However, the differences were not statistically significant. The largest rate ratios were seen at younger ages (death before 50 years). Mortality declined over calendar time in the general population (7% per year in women, 5% in men) but remained unchanged in persons with diabetes. Mortality in Greenland did not differ by diabetes status, which may reflect adequate access to and quality of diabetes care, survivorship bias, or competing risks.

articles.title: Evaluation of collateral circulation in symptomatic Moyamoya disease using artificial intelligence-assisted whole-brain computed tomography perfusion-derived dynamic four-dimensional computed tomography angiography.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of artificial intelligence-assisted dynamic four-dimensional computed tomography angiography (4D-CTA) reconstructed from whole-brain computed tomography perfusion (CTP) source data for assessing collateral circulation in symptomatic Moyamoya disease (MMD).
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 36 patients with digital subtraction angiography (DSA)-confirmed symptomatic MMD who underwent CTP and single-phase CTA (sCTA). Three datasets were derived: group A, conventional sCTA; group B, CTP-derived arterial-phase images; and group C, artificial intelligence-postprocessed 4D-CTA using the Shukun AI algorithm. Image quality was assessed in the arterial phase using objective parameters [CT attenuation, image noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR)] and subjective scores. The diagnostic performance of 4D-CTA was evaluated against DSA for modified Suzuki staging (mSS) and collateral circulation assessment.
RESULTS: Group C showed significantly higher CT attenuation value of the vessel, SNR, CNR, and subjective scores, and significantly lower standard deviation of the vessel and standard deviation of the brain parenchyma than groups A and B (all P < 0.05; most P < 0.001). The 4D-CTA showed excellent agreement with DSA in mSS grading (P < 0.001) and a strong positive correlation (P < 0.001). For collateral circulation grading, good agreement (P < 0.001) and moderate positive correlation (P < 0.001) were observed.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence-assisted 4D-CTA reconstructed from whole-brain CTP enables comprehensive multiphase vascular visualization without additional radiation exposure. It facilitates rapid, reliable, noninvasive evaluation of collateral circulation in symptomatic MMD, offering diagnostic accuracy comparable with DSA with promising potential for routine clinical application.

articles.title: Apolipoprotein ε4-allele as predictor of outcome in radiotherapy-treated childhood brain tumor survivors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) is a polymorphic gene with three main alleles; the ε4-allele is a risk factor for distinct diseases, particularly for Alzheimer's disease. Radiotherapy-treated childhood brain tumor (BT) survivors face an increased risk of developing late-effects, especially cognitive impairment. Despite the similar treatment modality, the outcome varies considerably. Thus, we investigated the influence of ε4-allele on outcome in these survivors.
METHODS: A Finnish national cohort of radiotherapy-treated childhood BT survivors was investigated in a cross-sectional setting (median follow-up of 20 years). Survivors participated in the follow-up visit including neuropsychological and physical examinations, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and laboratory tests. BT and treatment-related information were collected from the patient files. APOE polymorphism was examined, and the results were compared to a previous study on the Finnish population. We also compared the late-effects between ε4-carriers and non-carriers.
RESULTS: Among 58 survivors [median age of 27 (range, 16-43) years], the observed frequencies of APOE genotypes were 78% (N = 45) for ε3ε3, 14% (N = 8) for ε3ε4, 7% (N = 4) for ε2ε3, and 2% (N = 1) for ε2ε4. The presence of ε4-allele was associated with poorer semantic, immediate, and delayed auditory memory. Since all ε4-carriers had ventriculoperitoneal shunt, we compared their results to those of non-carriers with ventriculoperitoneal shunt, which revealed that ε4-carriers had worse immediate and delayed auditory memory. E4-carriers exhibit higher total cholesterol and triglyceride levels than non-carriers.
CONCLUSIONS: APOE ε4-allele may impact the cognitive outcome and cholesterol levels in the radiotherapy-treated childhood BT survivors. E4-carrier survivors may especially benefit from healthy life-style interventions.

articles.title: Return to sports after pediatric brain tumors: Time to move beyond survival.
articles.abstract: Brain tumors are the second most common malignancy in children and adolescents and the leading cause of cancer-related death in this population. While survival rates have improved, survivors are at risk of neurocognitive, motor, and psychosocial sequelae due to both tumor location and treatments used. Participation in sport is increasingly recognized as beneficial for functional recovery, cardiorespiratory fitness, and overall well-being in children and adolescents treated for brain tumors. However, return to play (RTP) may pose some challenges, particularly in the presence of neurosurgical devices, cranial radiotherapy, or residual neurological deficits. This narrative clinical review summarizes current evidence on the risks of sport-related injuries in pediatric brain tumor patients and survivors, highlighting factors influencing vulnerability, including treatment history and specific sport characteristics. We propose a risk-based framework for RTP evaluation emphasizing individualized coordinated assessment by pediatric oncologists, neurosurgeons, and sports medicine specialists. Protective strategies are discussed, although evidence for concussion prevention remains limited. A safe RTP should be enhanced by the here-proposed structured evaluation, balancing safety with the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial benefits of active participation. This framework aims to support clinicians and families in facilitating safe and effective reintegration of pediatric brain tumor survivors into both recreational and competitive sports.

articles.title: Fifteen years of pediatric neuro-oncology trials: Insights from ClinicalTrials.gov to optimize future design.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in children. Despite therapeutic advances, outcomes remain poor, and trial conduct is challenged by disease rarity, limited accrual pools, and complex multimodal regimens. Premature trial termination compounds these challenges, wasting resources and delaying progress. A comprehensive evaluation of the US pediatric neuro-oncology trial landscape and determinants of early discontinuation has not been performed.
METHODS: We queried ClinicalTrials.gov for US-based interventional pediatric neuro-oncology trials initiated between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2024. Trials were categorized by design features, tumor type, sponsor, and consortium involvement. Temporal trends, trial duration, and reasons for discontinuation were analyzed. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed factors associated with trial completion among trials initiated between 2010 and 2019.
RESULTS: Of 819 identified trials, 243 met inclusion criteria. Most trials were early phase (phase 1/1-2, 69.5%) and focused on recurrent/progressive disease (68.3%), with targeted therapy (53.9%) and immunotherapy (26.3%) most common. Trial opening declined significantly over time (Poisson regression, P < .001), although the proportion of closed trials remained stable (χ² P = .97). Mean time to accrual was 4.8 ± 1.2 years, with modest improvement after 2018. Among 52 (21.4%) prematurely closed trials, poor accrual was the leading reason (50%), followed by funding issues (19.2%). Multivariable analysis identified greater site numbers decreasing the risk of premature discontinuation (hazard ratio = 0.55; 95% CI, 0.35-0.83).
CONCLUSIONS: Multisite reach is a key determinant of trial persistence. Strategies to optimize accrual and reduce early termination should prioritize interinstitutional networks and trial platform site networks.

articles.title: Clinical and molecular divergences in diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered: A comparative study of survival outcomes in 1498 adults and children.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered (DMG), is a highly lethal brain tumor that predominantly affects children but is increasingly diagnosed in adults. This study aims to compare the clinical features, molecular profiles, and survival outcomes between these groups.
METHODS: PubMed and EMBASE searches (June 2021) identified 82 studies with 1498 patients (34.7% adults). Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves where necessary. Cox regression analyses were used to compare the overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) between adults and children, with subgroup analyses for age effects on OS.
RESULTS: Adults demonstrated longer median OS than children (16.2 vs 11.4 months, P < .05) and longer PFS (9.17 vs 7.2 months, P < .05). Brainstem involvement was significantly less common in adults than in children (22.6% vs 78.7%). Among patients with brainstem tumors, adults had longer OS, whereas survival was similar between age groups in non-brainstem tumors. Molecular data were limited, available in only 14.2%-37.1% of cases. Adults had higher rates of PPM1D (37.0% vs 12.6%), FGFR1 (17.1% vs 5.6%), and NF1 (35.1% vs 12.3%) mutations and lower rates of ACVR1 mutations (5.0% vs 24.1%). FGFR1, NF1, and TP53 mutations were prognostic in both age groups.
CONCLUSION: Adults with DMG have longer OS compared to children, with the survival advantage confined to brainstem tumors and not observed in non-brainstem tumors. Whether this reflects intrinsic biological differences or tumor location remains uncertain. Prospective studies with comprehensive molecular profiling are needed to better define differences in DMG biology across the age groups.

articles.title: Evaluation of clinical, immunological, genetic characteristics and follow-up results of patients presenting with common variable immunodeficiency phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is an antibody deficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent infections and non-infectious clinical features. Patients presenting with heterogeneous clinical findings lead to delayed diagnosis, various complications, and organ damage.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, immunological, genetic features of CVID cases diagnosed in our clinic over a 20-year period.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 51 patients diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) according to ESID criteria and followed at the Department of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology, Ankara University Faculty of Medicine, between 2002 and 2022.
RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 11.08 years (range: 4-27.91), with a median diagnostic delay of 4.79 years (range: 1-22.91). The most common clinical manifestation was sinopulmonary infections (96%). The most frequent non-infectious clinical manifestation was lymphoproliferation (41.1%). Splenomegaly was significantly more common in patients with autoimmune disease (53.3%). Patients with bronchiectasis had significantly lower proportions of class-switched memory B cells (p = 0.020). CD4+ naive T-cell counts were significantly lower in patients with malignancy compared to those without malignancy (p = 0.006). Genetic analysis performed in 40 patients revealed pathogenic variants in 35%, most frequently involving TACI, followed by ICOS and NFKB2. Following immunoglobulin replacement therapy, infection-related hospitalization rates markedly decreased (from 71.4% to 9.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: CVID patients can present with a wide variety of clinical features. Early diagnosis and treatment can improve quality of life. Identification of genetic defects will enhance understanding of immunopathogenesis opening new avenues for targeted therapies.

articles.title: Peripheral blood CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ T cells as an adjunctive diagnostic biomarker in adult hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: Comparison with an adapted strict Fardet-style HScore.
articles.abstract: Adult hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is diagnostically challenging due to clinical overlap with sepsis, autoimmune disorders, and malignancy-associated hyperinflammation, and existing criteria were developed primarily in pediatric cohorts. We evaluated peripheral blood CD8+ T-cell immunophenotyping as a diagnostic adjunct in adults with suspected HLH, compared against an adapted Fardet-style HScore. This single-center observational cohort study enrolled 106 consecutive adults with cytopenias and hyperferritinemia undergoing bone marrow examination. Patients were classified as HLH (n = 50) or non-HLH (n = 56) by revised HLH-2004 criteria with expert adjudication. Multiparametric flow cytometry quantified single-positive CD8+CD38+ and CD8+HLA-DR+ and dual-positive CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ subsets. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis with Youden-index-derived cut-offs. CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ was the strongest flow-cytometric marker (AUC 0.824). At the Youden-optimal threshold (>16.71% of parent CD8+ T cells), sensitivity was 78% and specificity 81%; at an exploratory 22.69% threshold (same parent CD8+ subset), sensitivity was 64.0% and specificity 87.5%. Single-positive CD8+CD38+ (AUC 0.564) and CD8+HLA-DR+ (AUC 0.427) subsets did not discriminate. The adapted HScore achieved an AUC of 0.970; at a threshold of >196, sensitivity was 94.0% and specificity was 87.5%. The adapted HScore provided the strongest clinicobiochemical framework. CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ was the best-performing flow-cytometric adjunct, offering high specificity for rule-in in gray-zone adult HLH. An integrated strategy combining clinical scoring with immune activation profiling is recommended.

articles.title: Leadership profile of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus services in Brazil: a national cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: National data on the leadership profile of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus services in Brazil are limited, hindering a comprehensive understanding of the characteristics of physicians leading subspecialty training and workforce development.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the leadership profile of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus services in Brazil and evaluate characteristics relevant to subspecialty training and workforce planning.
METHODS: This national cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured online questionnaire administered to physicians leading pediatric ophthalmology and/or strabismus services across Brazil. Potential participants were identified through national professional societies, institutional websites, and professional networks. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Student's t test, and Fisher's exact test, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05, using IBM SPSS Statistics, version 29.0.2.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine leaders from all five geographic regions of Brazil participated (mean age, 46.7 ± 9.4 years), of whom 64.1% were women. Most participants had > 10 years of professional experience (79.5%), and 87.2% had completed fellowship training. Postgraduate degrees were held by 46.2%, and 30.8% had received training internationally. Services were predominantly public (69.2%), located in capital cities (76.9%), and concentrated in the Southeast region (61.5%). Fellowship programs were available in 56.4% of services. No significant differences were identified between male and female leaders. Physicians aged >50 years had longer professional experience (P = 0.042), whereas fellowship training was more frequent among those aged ≤ 50 years (P = 0.025).
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus services in Brazil are led predominantly by women and physicians with substantial subspecialty training. The concentration of services in capital cities and the Southeast region suggests opportunities to expand fellowship training and leadership development across underserved regions, informing future workforce planning in pediatric ophthalmology.

articles.title: Hearing in Noise Test (HINT) in pediatric stuttering: a cross-sectional study of speech perception in noise performance in children who stutter.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stuttering has a multifactorial, dynamic structure and is an involuntary fluency disorder characterized by disruptions in verbal expression. Stuttering is a common speech issue that affects people between the ages of 6 and 12.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare speech perception in noise performance in children with developmental stuttering and their typically developing peers.
DESIGN AND SETTING: A cross-sectional, observational study was conducted at Lokman Hekim University.
METHODS: This study comprised 48 children in total, 24 of whom were 6 to 12 years old and complained of stuttering when they visited the Audiology, Hearing, and Balance Center; the remaining 24 children had no speech disorders. The children who participated in the study were administered the Hearing in Noise Test and underwent an audiological examination.
RESULTS: The mean age of the 24 children with stuttering was 10.87 ± 3.67 years and that of the 24 healthy children was 12 ± 3.84 years. Children with normal hearing who did or did not stutter were included. A comparison of the results of the Hearing in Noise Test for children with fluency disorders and stuttered revealed that the stuttering group's scores were lower, and this difference was identified as statistically significant (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Based on our findings, children who stutter experience greater difficulty with speech perception in noisy environments. This finding is important for the development of children aged 6 to 12 because difficulties in understanding speech in this developmental period negatively affect the social and academic lives of children with stuttering.

articles.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors in the Pediatric Population.
articles.abstract: Pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PPitNETs) are rare but present significant clinical challenges in children. Their diverse presentations necessitate comprehensive endocrinologic and radiographic evaluation. They are most commonly prolactin-secreting or adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting. A genetic mutation can be present, particularly in young patients with aggressive disease. Management is multidisciplinary. Medical therapy is first-line treatment of prolactinomas, and surgery is first-line treatment of most other PPitNETs, with reasonable remission rates when performed in experienced centers. Long-term outcomes are favorable, although hypopituitarism and lifelong hormone replacement remain important concerns. Ongoing surveillance is essential to ensure detect recurrence, and monitor treatment-related complications.

articles.title: Changes in the Number of Patients With Drug Overdose due to Deliberate Self-Harm Transported to the Hospital Emergency Department During the Past 12 Years.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Recently, over-the-counter (OTC) drug overdoses have increased. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics and temporal trends of acute drug overdose and explore effective countermeasures in emergency medical settings.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients admitted to our hospital for acute drug overdose due to deliberate self-harm between January 2012 and December 2023. Data collected from medical records included sex, age, ingested substances, implementation of advanced interventions, and outcomes. Cases were categorized as prescription drugs only or OTC drugs present. Comparisons were made before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Severe cases were defined as those requiring advanced interventions; psychiatric care history was assessed in severe cases.
RESULTS: Of the 1676 included patients (mean age 37.8 years), 74.4% used only prescription drugs, 15.0% used only OTC drugs and 5.1% used both. OTC drug-involved cases increased significantly from 15.7% before to 29.7% after the COVID-19 pandemic (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients aged 10-29 years also increased significantly (p < 0.001), as did their OTC drug use (p < 0.001). Severe cases accounted for 8.2% (n = 137) and 12 deaths (0.7%). The proportion of severe cases did not differ significantly between groups. Among the severe cases, psychiatric care history was more frequent in the prescription-only group (90.9%) compared to the OTC-involved group (54.5%).
CONCLUSION: Since 2019, a marked increase in OTC drug overdoses among younger individuals has been observed. Emergency departments should play a key role in initiating multidisciplinary, community-based support systems to prevent recurrence.

articles.title: Quantitative diagnosis of trigonocephaly from 3D photography using cephalometric and curvature analysis.
articles.abstract: Quantitative analysis of 3D photography has enhanced the diagnosis of non-syndromic trigonocephaly caused by the premature fusion of the metopic suture. However, the assessment of morphological shape traits and the identification of mild-to-moderate trigonocephaly remain challenging. This study aims to present a quantifiable and visually interpretable method to improve diagnostic performance. This retrospective study included 35 normal children (age = 5.9 ± 1.5 years) and 25 patients diagnosed with mild-to-moderate or severe trigonocephaly (age = 1.29 ± 1.04 years). We identified anatomical landmarks and computed cephalometric measurements from 3D photography. Furthermore, we presented a computational method to determine age-independent metrics and employed mean curvature analysis to examine morphological features and enhance diagnostic accuracy. Comparative results of Mann-Whitney U test and one-way ANOVA indicated that the interfrontal angle (IFA), defined by the prominent forehead and lateral frontotemporal points, provides rapid quantitative diagnosis. Curvature analysis suggests that trigonocephaly is characterized by a pronounced mid-forehead, a narrowed lateral forehead, and increased biparietal width. Moreover, the combination of mean curvature with IFA achieved a higher diagnostic accuracy of 95.00%. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method combined with 3D photography provides diagnostic support for trigonocephaly and can complement clinical expertise, especially in mild-to-moderate cases with greater IFA values. Our computational framework also has the potential for application to diagnosis of other craniosynostosis subtypes.

articles.title: Placental abnormalities in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: A systematic review of experimental and clinical studies.
articles.abstract: The placenta is essential for fetal organ development, and its dysfunction is implicated in several congenital anomalies. However, little is known about the status and role of the placenta in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH).
