Herein, we aimed to define the incidence of placental abnormalities in CDH and characterize gross morphology, histology, molecular pathways, and vascular function. Using a predefined search strategy, we performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. Human and animal studies reporting on placental and/or umbilical cord abnormalities in CDH were analyzed. Of 2,820 records identified, 14 articles were included. Human studies reported no consistent macroscopic placental phenotype. Cord abnormalities included hypercoiling, abnormal insertion, and single umbilical artery. Fetal vascular malperfusion, thrombotic lesions, and chronic inflammation were reported at histology. Ex-vivo CDH fetoplacental arteries showed impaired function with excessive constriction and inadequate relaxation. Animal studies reported reduced placental weight, trophoblast injury and apoptosis, and altered retinoid metabolism. Despite extensive literature on CDH, the status of the placenta remains understudied. Available evidence indicates that CDH is associated with abnormalities involving fetal placental vascular pathology. Studies using standardized assessment are needed to define the role of the placenta in CDH and correlate its status with disease severity and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Long-term (≥ 10-year) outcomes after laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To the best of our knowledge, no previous dedicated study has evaluated laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision (LCCE) in a cohort in which all patients had at least 10 years of follow-up. We therefore evaluated long-term outcomes after LCCE in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective two-center cohort study included all 47 consecutive eligible children who underwent LCCE between June 2009 and September 2016. All patients had at least 10 years of confirmed follow-up. The standardized technique included cyst excision with tailored intrapancreatic dissection, intraoperative endoscopy of the common channel and/or intrahepatic ducts, and mucosa-to-mucosa Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy (HJ). The primary endpoint was late biliary event-free survival; overall late event-free survival including intestinal events was a secondary endpoint.
RESULTS: Ten patients (21.3%) had at least 15 years of follow-up. Median follow-up was 12.85 years (IQR 10.89-14.64; range 10.00-17.26). Early and first-year complications occurred in 8 (17.0%) and 4 patients (8.5%), respectively. Two patients (4.3%) developed qualifying late biliary events: one developed cholangitis at 1.02 years and was treated medically, and the other developed an intrahepatic stone at 5.14 years and underwent redo reconstruction. Late biliary event-free survival was 95.7% at both 10 and 15 years. One additional patient underwent surgery for adhesive intestinal obstruction at 13.79 years, resulting in an overall late event-free survival of 90.4% at 15 years. No late pancreatitis, clinically relevant remnant duct pathology, internal hernia, or biliary malignancy occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Standardized LCCE was associated with durable long-term biliary outcomes. However, late biliary and intestinal complications remained possible, supporting continued surveillance into adulthood.

articles.title: Assessing quality of life during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injuries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess quality of life (QOL) outcomes during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI) and to identify factors linked to poorer outcomes. Additionally, the authors aimed to determine the construct validity of the Impact of a Brachial Plexus Injury Questionnaire (Mancuso scale) for use in the birth injury population.
METHODS: This study utilized a cross-sectional, within-subject comparative survey design to assess the QOL outcomes of adolescents and adults with BPBI. Participants older than 13 years of age and with a history of BPBI were identified using the United Brachial Plexus Network Facebook group. QOL was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) in adults, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) in adolescents, and a brachial plexus injury-specific tool (Mancuso scale). To determine construct validity, scores from each Mancuso subscale were compared to the participants' overall WHOQOL-BREF scores.
RESULTS: Adults (n = 59) who completed the WHOQOL-BREF had a mean overall score of 63.1 ± 22.2 (0- to 100-point scale). The scores of the Mancuso scale with regard to the symptoms, limitations, and emotion subscales were 45.8 ± 29.5, 35.2 ± 17.3, and 43.6 ± 25.3, respectively. These findings contrasted with the published values from subjects who had sustained a traumatic brachial plexus injury whose scores were 66 ± 18.7, 48.2 ± 22.3, and 39.5 ± 21.2, respectively. For adolescents (n = 4), the overall score on PedsQL was 63.7 ± 21.3. Adolescent scores on the Mancuso scale were 31.7 ± 26.9, 29.8 ± 20.7, and 39.7 ± 18.8, respectively. In adults, severe functional limitation and limited access to care were associated with poorer QOL (p < 0.05), whereas surgical history and occupational therapy attendance did not. Higher scores on the Mancuso subscales correlated with lower quality of life scores on the WHOQOL-BREF. Adolescent data analysis revealed similar, nonsignificant results.
CONCLUSIONS: BPBI plays a role in long-term QOL, notably by the severity of functional limitation and access to care. The Mancuso scale shows promising construct validity in the adult BPBI population, but a larger sample of adolescents is needed.

articles.title: Cerebrospinal fluid composition and flow dynamics as predictors of shunt performance in neonates with posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH) is the leading neurosurgical complication of preterm intraventricular hemorrhage, yet ventriculoperitoneal shunt failure rates in this population remain disproportionately high and poorly understood. Abnormal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) composition following hemorrhage has been proposed as a key contributor to shunt obstruction, but the clinical relevance of CSF biochemical and flow-related factors has not been systematically evaluated. This review evaluated whether CSF composition or flow dynamics predict shunt performance in neonates with PHH.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420250642742). PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception to June 2025. Studies involving neonates directly evaluating CSF parameters in relation to shunt outcomes were included for outcome synthesis; mechanistic, biomarker, and indirect clinical studies were incorporated separately as contextual evidence to support biological plausibility. A narrative synthesis was performed owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool.
RESULTS: Direct clinical evidence linking CSF composition or flow-related factors to shunt performance in neonatal PHH is critically limited. Thirty-one studies met the inclusion criteria across 4 evidence tiers. Three studies directly related CSF parameters, or a CSF-directed intervention, to shunt outcomes. CSF protein was directly measured in only 1 of these studies and did not predict shunt failure. CSF infection was the strongest clinical predictor of shunt failure. No neonatal study directly measured CSF flow dynamics in relation to shunt outcomes. A broader mechanistic literature has demonstrated that PHH CSF is characterized by markedly elevated inflammatory mediators, growth factors, iron metabolites, and cellular debris, supporting the biological plausibility of CSF-driven shunt obstruction.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite compelling biological rationale, direct clinical evidence linking CSF composition or flow-related factors to shunt performance in neonatal PHH is critically limited. Elevated CSF protein may reflect hemorrhagic burden but does not reliably predict shunt failure as a standalone parameter. These findings do not support the use of CSF biomarker thresholds to guide clinical decision-making at this time. Prospective multicenter studies incorporating serial CSF biomarker profiling and direct flow measurements are needed to determine whether CSF-based predictors can meaningfully inform shunt management.

articles.title: Safety and effectiveness of surgery for medically refractory insular epilepsy in children: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insular epilepsy is an increasingly diagnosed cause of pediatric drug-refractory focal epilepsy. However, adoption of surgical treatments-resective or ablative-has been limited due to concerns about neurological risks. This systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis aimed to identify predictors of seizure freedom and neurological deficits following surgery in children with insular epilepsy.
METHODS: A systematic search of 4 databases up to August 2024 was undertaken to identify studies reporting postsurgical outcomes in patients aged under 18 years with insular epilepsy. Studies with follow-up under 12 months were excluded. Quality assessment was performed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Education (GRADE) framework, and risk of bias was evaluated using Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Published institutional results from 11 patients were included within the analysis. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify predictors of seizure freedom and neurological complications.
RESULTS: Of 154 identified studies, 12 retrospective studies reporting on 97 patients met the inclusion criteria. The median follow-up duration was 37 months. At last follow up, 57% of patients were seizure free, defined as Engel class I or International League Against Epilepsy class 1 and 2. Patients who underwent preoperative stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) had significantly lower odds of seizure recurrence (OR 0.25, CI 0.06-0.95, p = 0.047). Procedure type (resection vs ablation; OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.13-3.27, p = 0.606), age at surgery (OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.94-1.18, p = 0.392), and surgical extent (insular only versus insular "plus" surgery; OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.17-3.59, p = 0.777) were not significant predictors of seizure freedom. Postoperative permanent neurological deficits occurred in 11% of children, with motor deficits being the most common. Younger age at surgery was associated with greater odds of motor deficit (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.78-0.99, p = 0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first and largest systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to report the outcomes of insular epilepsy surgery in a purely pediatric cohort. Both ablative and resective approaches are feasible, with over half of patients achieving seizure freedom and over two-thirds of neurological deficits being transient.

articles.title: Open versus closed wound dressing among children with superficial partial thickness burns: a comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract: Burn injuries disproportionately affect low- and middle-income countries, with children being the most affected group. Although various burn wound care options exist, many are too costly for widespread use in resource-limited settings. This prospective comparative cohort study evaluated outcomes of open versus closed wound dressing in children with superficial partial-thickness burns at Hoima, Kayunga, and Jinja Regional Referral Hospitals. The study was not a clinical trial because treatment allocation was determined by the attending doctor rather than through prospective assignment. Children with burns covering less than 10% or more than 20% of total body surface area were excluded. In the closed dressing group, silver sulfadiazine was applied and covered with dry gauze and crepe bandage, while the open dressing group received silver sulfadiazine without a covering. Wound epithelialization was assessed using the Imito Measure app. A total of 126 children (63 per group) were enrolled, with a mean age of 5.3 ± 2.6 years. Open dressing resulted in significantly greater epithelialization on days 7, 14, and 21, shorter hospital stays, and fewer wound infections than closed dressing (P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in isolated organisms or complications such as anaemia and compartment syndrome. Open dressing was associated with better overall outcomes and should be considered for children with burns involving less than 20% of total body surface area.

articles.title: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents.
articles.abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

articles.title: Functional outcomes in pediatric colorectal surgery: a predictor-based analysis of Hirschsprung disease and anorectal malformation in a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term fecal continence and bowel habit outcomes remain a significant challenge in pediatric colorectal surgery. This study evaluated long-term functional bowel outcomes in patients treated for Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Anorectal Malformations (ARM) using the standardized Rintala Bowel Function Score, identifying key clinical predictors of favorable outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at St. Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, among children who underwent definitive surgical repair for HD and ARM between January 2018 and December 2022. Functional bowel outcomes were evaluated using the Rintala Bowel Function Score (0-20 scale), with a score ≥ 17 defined as a clinically favorable outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to assess predictive factors.
RESULTS: A total of 136 patients were included: 94 with HD and 42 with ARM. In the HD cohort, the presence of associated congenital anomalies and colonic excision proximal to the splenic flexure were major negative predictors of bowel function, reducing the probability of a favorable outcome from 66 to 22% (p = 0.007) and from 75 to 28% (p = 0.008), respectively. In the ARM cohort, 100% of patients with low-severity malformations achieved favorable outcomes compared with 54.5% of those with high/intermediate-severity malformations (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: While anatomical severity appears to be an important factor influencing bowel function outcomes in ARM, associated systemic anomalies and the extent of colonic excision were also associated with poorer bowel function in children with HD. These findings highlight the potential importance of structured, long-term postoperative follow-up, with particular attention to children at higher risk of functional bowel problems.

articles.title: Pediatric total thyroidectomy and lobectomy; an analysis of surgeon specialty and outcomes for same-day discharge.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Our study aimed to evaluate differences in patient outcomes overall and by specialty for same-day discharge (SDD) following pediatric total thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy.
METHODS: Data from the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (NSQIP-P) was used to evaluate thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy patients (2017-2021). For each operation, patients were categorized into SDD and those discharged 1-2 days post-operation (non-SDD). Postoperative outcomes were both analyzed overall and by surgeon specialty (pediatric and adult general surgery, pediatric and adult ENT).
RESULTS: NSQIP-P identified 2,622 patients. Rates of SDD increased from 2017 to 2021 for thyroidectomy (5.2% to 10.9%) and thyroid lobectomy (23.1% to 34.6%). The SDD rate was lower for pediatric general surgeons than for adult general or ENT surgeons for both operations (p < 0.001), without outcome differences. Regression demonstrated steroid use as a risk for readmission (OR 4.42, p = 0.026) and reoperation (OR 5.99, p = 0.047) following thyroidectomy.
CONCLUSION: SDD for pediatric patients undergoing thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy has increased without worsening outcomes. Some surgical specialties have increased rates of SDD without outcome differences. In carefully selected non-steroid using patients meeting specific criteria to optimize communication and minimize complication risks, SDD following pediatric thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy may be a safe option.

articles.title: SiLaC versus PEPSiT for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease: a monocentric retrospective cohort study (PILO-LASER).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence comparing minimally invasive approaches for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is limited. We aimed to compare the effectiveness of Sinus Laser-Assisted Closure (SiLaC) and Pediatric Endoscopic Pilonidal Sinus Treatment (PEPSiT), with particular emphasis on wound healing time and disease recurrence rate.
METHODS: A retrospective monocentric cohort study was conducted including patients aged under 18 years treated for PSD between January 2022 and December 2025. The primary outcome was wound healing time. Secondary outcomes included recurrence rate, postoperative complications and operative time.
RESULTS: Seventy-three patients were included: 21 underwent SiLaC and 52 underwent PEPSiT. Age, sex, height, weight and body mass index did not differ significantly between groups, whereas redo surgery was more frequent in the SiLaC group (6/21 vs. 3/52; p = 0.014). Median wound healing time was significantly shorter following SiLaC than PEPSiT (15 [IQR 15-22] vs. 55.5 [IQR 24.3-113.3] days; p < 0.001; Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift - 38 days, 95% CI - 55 to - 14). Among the 69 patients with available data, recurrence was observed in 3/19 (15.8%) in the SiLaC group and 12/50 (24.0%) in the PEPSiT group (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.534; odds ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.15-2.39). Operative time was slightly shorter with SiLaC (18 vs. 22 min; p = 0.046), although the 95% CI of the location shift reached zero (- 4 min, 95% CI - 8 to 0). No Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complication occurred. Follow-up was shorter in the SiLaC group (2 vs. 5 months; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: SiLaC was associated with significantly shorter time to clinically documented wound healing. Recurrence findings should be interpreted as short-term observations; the study does not investigate long-term recurrence rates. SiLaC's compatibility with lateral positioning and local or locoregional anesthesia may facilitate perioperative and postoperative management. Prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted to assess long-term efficacy, recurrence, recovery, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Dysregulated serotonin reuptake impairs intestinal serotonin availability in human necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal disease in preterm infants associated with impaired gut motility. We previously demonstrated that delayed gastric emptying correlates with intestinal injury severity in experimental NEC. Serotonin (5-HT) from enterochromaffin (EC) cells regulates intestinal motility and gastric emptying. We hypothesized that dysregulated 5-HT signaling contributes to NEC-associated dysmotility.
METHODS: Distal ileal tissues from NEC and non-NEC patients were analyzed by immunofluorescence for EC cells (CHGA), 5-HT, synthesis (TPH1), release (TRPA1), metabolism (MAO-A), and reuptake proteins (SERT, VMAT1). EC cell-enriched human intestinal organoids were generated, and forskolin-induced 5-HT release was assessed following SERT or VMAT1 inhibition.
RESULTS: EC cell number and expression of TPH1, TRPA1, and MAOA were unchanged in NEC ileum. In contrast, SERT and VMAT1 expression were increased in NEC tissues and patient-derived EC cell-enriched organoids. Reduced extracellular 5-HT levels in NEC organoids were restored following SERT or VMAT1 inhibition.
CONCLUSION: NEC is associated with increased 5-HT reuptake despite an unchanged EC cell population, resulting in reduced extracellular 5-HT availability. Dysregulated serotonin signaling may contribute to impaired gastric emptying and gut dysmotility in NEC, identifying serotonin reuptake as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Autotaxin is developmentally expressed in multiple gestation-associated organs and systemically affects parturition in rats.
articles.abstract: Autotaxin (ATX) is a secreted protein with lysophosphatidic acid-generating lysophospholipase D (lysoPLD) activity. Although ATX has been implicated in normal and pathological pregnancies, its gestational role and tissue-specific expression remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed ATX expression and activity in various gestational tissues (ovary, uterus, placenta, and fetal membrane) of normal pregnant rats. Western blot analyses revealed that the relative ATX protein levels increased as pregnancy progressed, except in the uterus, closely aligning with tissue lysoPLD activity. Circulating ATX protein levels also increased toward parturition, with the placenta likely serving as the primary source. Immunohistochemistry localized ATX to steroidogenic cells in the ovarian corpus luteum, vascular endothelial cells and outer smooth muscle in the uterus, and placental trophoblasts. A bolus intravenous injection of an anti-ATX antibody on day 18 of pregnancy induced a trend toward delayed parturition along with >10% neonatal lethality. Thus, ATX is progressively expressed in multiple gestation-related organs, primarily the placenta, and circulating ATX systemically affects parturition and neonatal survival in rats.

articles.title: A multi-level intervention to improve cervical cancer prevention in safety-net settings: The DOSE-CC study protocol for a hybrid type-1 effectiveness-implementation stepped wedge randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is highly preventable, but screening is under-utilized. Approximately 75% of individuals diagnosed with cervical cancer were unscreened, under-screened, or did not receive adequate follow-up after abnormal results. Thus, effective interventions to improve cervical cancer screening and follow-up care are needed. This paper describes the protocol for a multi-level intervention called Development of Systems and Education for Cervical Cancer prevention (DOSE-CC).
METHODS: We will use a hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation, stepped-wedge randomized controlled trial design to assess intervention impact on screening and follow-up. The trial will be conducted in four safety net sites in Florida, Hawaii, and Massachusetts, with guidance from a national advisory board and clinical champions at each site. We will systematically adapt our prior successful intervention, which focused on HPV vaccination of adolescents, to address screening and follow-up. The adapted intervention will involve longitudinal contact with practices and support system changes to improve screening and follow-up processes.
RESULTS: Findings will evaluate the impact of DOSE-CC on (a) screening receipt during medical visits; (b) follow-up care after abnormal results; and (c) population-level up-to-date screening rates at participating sites using data from electronic medical records. We will use the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance Qualitative Evaluation for Systematic Translation (RE-AIM QuEST), a mixed-methods framework to assess implementation outcomes from health care worker, clinical champion, and patient perspectives.
CONCLUSIONS: Results from the randomized controlled trial will assess the impact of the DOSE-CC intervention on cervical cancer screening and follow-up rates, and guide evidence-based future scale-up to other settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07226037, registered on 2025-11-10.

articles.title: Training the Next Generation: How Are We Preparing Pediatric Residents in Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Care?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatricians are expected to provide sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care to adolescents assigned female at birth (AFAB), yet there is variability in the degree of clinical training pediatric residents receive. This study assesses training opportunities and comfort level of pediatric residents providing SRH care to AFAB adolescents.
METHODS: Third-year pediatric residents and their program directors completed a survey assessing resident training and comfort with SRH clinical skills, and perceived importance of topics. Descriptive statistics summarized participant demographics, and χ² or Fisher exact tests assessed associations between experiences and training settings.
RESULTS: Among 111 pediatric residents at 11 residency programs, 99.1% felt it was important to obtain training in SRH. The majority (65.8%) planned to provide SRH services in future practice. Common barriers to addressing SRH needs included insufficient training and lack of comfort of pediatric attendings. All program directors felt it was important to expand opportunities in SRH clinical skills. Conclusions Pediatric residents find value in providing SRH care and most plan to do so after graduation yet may not receive sufficient training. Multiple barriers interfere with provision of SRH care. Standardization of curricula and clinical experiences may increase resident comfort and improve quality of care provided to AFAB youth.

articles.title: Dismissal Policies for Vaccine Delay and Refusal: Experiences among US Primary Care Pediatricians.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As vaccine hesitancy has grown, some pediatric practices implement vaccine dismissal policies in response to families who refuse or delay immunizations. This study aimed to describe the perspectives and practices that underlie dismissal policies by pediatricians.
METHODS: We conducted an exploratory, qualitative study of United States primary care pediatricians. Brief interviews were conducted virtually, with separate semi-structured scripts used for "dismissers" and "non-dismissers." Data were organized into a matrix format for analysis.
RESULTS: Between September 2020 and June 2021, 17 pediatrician interviews were conducted, with 16 included in the data analysis. Of these 16 interviews, 9 were dismissers and 7 were non-dismissers. Both dismissers and non-dismissers felt supported in their policy decisions and were guided in these decisions by a strong support for vaccines. Both groups also differentiated between those who staunchly refused vaccines and those who were vaccine hesitant. Pediatricians with dismissal policies reported frustrations with vaccine refusal and conversations with families about vaccinations that seemed fruitless. Non-dismissers emphasized the value of serving all patients and ensuring that all patients had access to good medical care. Both dismissers and non-dismissers encountered similar reasons for vaccine refusal or delay among vaccine-hesitant families, including concerns about vaccine safety and necessity.
CONCLUSIONS: In this qualitative study of pediatric primary care physicians, we described the themes, many of which are similar between dismissers and non-dismissers, that underlie the decision of whether to dismiss families for vaccine refusal and delay. Future research should investigate the public health impact of these policies.

articles.title: Adverse and Positive Childhood Experiences among US Bereaved Youth (2022-2024).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe associations of adverse and positive childhood experiences (ACEs and PCEs) and social demographic characteristics with exposure to parent or guardian death among a nationally representative sample of US youth (6-17 years).
METHODS: We pooled cross-sectional data from the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health (N=101,617). We estimated stepwise Poisson and Negative Binomial regression models testing the association of parent or guardian death with ACEs and PCEs accumulation in both the full sample and racial and ethnic stratified subsamples.
RESULTS: Approximately 4% of youth experienced parent or guardian death and were disproportionately non-Hispanic Black, Native American/Other Race, or from low-income households. Bereaved youth were more likely to be exposed to all ACEs and less likely to be exposed to the majority of PCEs relative to their non-bereaved counterparts. Youth exposed to parent or guardian death exhibited significantly more ACEs (β = 0.40, IRR = 1.49, SE = 0.03), yet a similar number of PCEs (β = -0.02, IRR = 0.98, SE = 0.01), relative to their non-bereaved peers. The association between parent and guardian death and ACEs was no longer significant among non-Hispanic Black (β = 0.15, IRR = 1.16, SE = 0.08) and Native American/Other Race (β = 0.12, IRR = 1.12, SE = 0.11) youth relative to other racial and ethnic groups.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore the elevated and unequal exposure of adversity among youth exposed to parent and guardian death. Implications for targeted pediatric supports that address heightened adversities and inequities within this population are discussed.

articles.title: Caregiver Perspectives on Health-Related Social Needs Disclosure and Perceived Risk of Child Protective Services Involvement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Health-related social needs (HRSN) screening is frequently implemented in pediatric health care settings. Caregivers may be reluctant to disclose HRSN due to fear of Child Protective Services (CPS) involvement, limiting the effectiveness of these efforts. Our primary objectives were (1) to explore caregiver perspectives regarding HRSN disclosure and perceived risk of CPS involvement, and (2) to identify factors that could alleviate concerns regarding inappropriate CPS involvement and improve caregivers' comfort in disclosing HRSN.
METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with caregivers of pediatric inpatients at an academic quaternary care children's hospital. Caregivers were eligible if they were offered a standardized HRSN screener (Linking Families to Support- LiFTS) during their child's hospitalization. Purposive sampling was used to ensure representation across caregiver sociodemographic characteristics. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by two independent coders using thematic content analysis guided by an adapted health equity implementation framework. Interviews were conducted until thematic saturation was achieved.
RESULTS: We interviewed 25 caregivers who were predominantly Medicaid-insured (60%). Most (64%) disclosed 1+ HRSN. We identified five themes: (1): Balancing benefits of support with perceived risks of HRSN disclosure; (2) potential CPS involvement and fear of family separation; (3) factors and experiences that heighten perceived risks of HRSN disclosure; (4) distinguishing social needs from neglect; (5) trauma-informed practices could facilitate HRSN disclosure.
CONCLUSION: Caregivers valued HRSN screening but described fear of CPS involvement as a barrier to disclosure. Trauma-informed approaches that normalize help-seeking behaviors, emphasize transparency, and distinguish poverty-related need from neglect may improve caregiver engagement with HRSN screening.

articles.title: Investigating Modified Deep Learning Models for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Classification Using Electroencephalography Spectrograms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study developed neurophysiologically informed data augmentation strategies to improve electroencephalogram (EEG)-based deep learning classification of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children with limited labeled EEG data. ADHD affects approximately 8.0% of children and adolescents worldwide, or about 129 million individuals aged 5-19 years. Clinical diagnosis relies largely on behavioral observations; EEG provides objective biomarkers, but conventional image augmentation may not preserve disease-relevant neural oscillation patterns.
METHODS: We introduced band-shuffle augmentation, which exchanges selected spectral content between samples within the same diagnostic class at the level of canonical EEG frequency bands. The method was evaluated through systematic architecture optimization, augmentation experiments, and integration into an adaptive multistrategy training pipeline.
RESULTS: Band-shuffle augmentation achieved 75.05% validation accuracy, 75.76% F1 score, 75.30% sensitivity, and 74.56% specificity, exceeding the 74.32% accuracy of traditional computer vision augmentation. The integrated multistrategy framework achieved 77.47% validation accuracy and 0.8414 AUC, improving accuracy by 27.0% over the 60.99% MobileNetV2 baseline and by 4.2% over conventional augmentation.
CONCLUSION: The results support frequency band-level augmentation as a neurophysiologically informed approach to EEG spectrogram classification. Ablation indicated distinct module contributions, and Grad-CAM highlighted frequency-specific regions consistent with ADHD neurophysiology. This framework may support EEG-based computer-aided screening, although external validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Combined Prenatal Environmental Stressors Induce Suprachiasmatic Degeneration with Unexpected Behavioural Resilience in Long-Evans Rats.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Environmental heat stress and displacement adversity during pregnancy pose significant risks to neurodevelopment, particularly in regions with high maternal mortality and population displacement. The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), the brain's master circadian pacemaker, is vulnerable to prenatal environmental insults, yet the combined impact of thermal and psychosocial stressors on SCN development remains unexplored. We examined the effects of prenatal heat stress and displacement-like conditions on SCN morphology and behaviour across two critical developmental stages.
METHODS: Twenty-five timed-pregnant Long-Evans rats were exposed to heat stress (38-40°C, 2 h daily), displacement conditions (overnight food/water restriction plus overcrowding), combined stressors, or control conditions from gestational days 15-20. Male offspring were assessed at postnatal days 10 (neonatal) and 30 (juvenile).
RESULTS: Heat exposure induced significant maternal hyperthermia (2.5-2.9°C elevation). Histological analysis revealed marked SCN cellular degeneration across stress groups at both developmental stages, characterised by reduced cell counts, pyknotic nuclei, and disrupted tissue architecture. Despite structural damage, juvenile behavioural testing revealed paradoxical outcomes: combined stress exposure reduced anxiety-like behaviour in the elevated plus maze, enhanced sociability in three-chamber testing, while preserving recognition memory. Growth analysis demonstrated preferential brain sparing despite reduced somatic growth, with significantly elevated brain-to-body weight ratios in stress-exposed animals.
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that prenatal environmental stressors cause lasting damage to the SCN but trigger adaptive behavioural responses. The dissociation between structural vulnerability and functional adaptation suggests complex neurodevelopmental programming with implications for populations experiencing heat exposure and displacement adversity.

articles.title: "It Changes Everything, and It Changes Nothing": a Prospective, Mixed-Method Study of the Value of Genomic Sequencing for Parents of Children with Undiagnosed Rare Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While much recent literature has focused on patients' and families' perceptions of the value of genome-wide sequencing (GS, including exome and genome sequencing) for rare disease diagnosis, conceptual and methodological limitations remain. We sought to characterize expectations of, and longitudinal perspectives on, the value of GS and its outcomes for parents of pediatric rare disease patients.
METHODS: From December 2021 through April 2024, we enrolled and followed parents of pediatric patients undergoing GS with pending results. Parents completed three in-depth interviews: at baseline, at return of results, and six months after return. Data were analyzed using both qualitative and quantitative methods.
RESULTS: Thirty-six parents participated. Four key findings emerged: 1) at baseline, parents balanced expansive hope for a range of benefits from GS with tempered expectations; 2) parents of children who received a definitive diagnosis reported achieving many expected outcomes, but the ultimate value of these outcomes was shaped by personal values and contextual factors; 3) parents of children who did not receive a definitive diagnosis nonetheless achieved some of the outcomes they sought from GS through other means; and 4) parents' perceptions of the outcomes of sequencing evolved over time in varying directions.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that the current literature examining the value parents ultimately derive from GS for rare disease diagnosis may fail to address critical nuances in subjective perceptions of value. Better understanding this value requires clarification of theories of value underlying current measures, rigorous, comparative methods, and consideration of families' specific values and preferences.

articles.title: Genetic Counseling When One Partner Carries a CF-Causing Variant and the Other Has the Intronic IVS8-5T Variant.
articles.abstract: Complex genetic counseling situations can arise when whole-gene sequencing is used as part of reproductive genetic carrier screening or newborn screening for cystic fibrosis (CF). One of the most common scenarios is when one reproductive partner carries a CF-causing variant such as c.1521-1523del (or p.F508del) and the other partner carries the c.1210-12T[5] (or IVS8-5T) variant. Questions arise as to what information to provide about the likely outcome if the fetus or newborn has both variants in trans, as well as implications for future pregnancies and other family members. In this paper, we consider an approach to genetic counseling based on knowledge of CFTR biology and available clinical data.

articles.title: Colostrum Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Turkish and Lebanese Mothers Living in Türkiye: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colostrum is biologically important for newborn nutrition and immunity, yet maternal knowledge and feeding practices may vary across health care and social settings.
OBJECTIVE: To compare colostrum-related knowledge items, attitudes, practices, and information sources between Turkish and Lebanese mothers living in Türkiye and assess selected practice-related differences after adjustment.
METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study included a non-probability convenience sample of 305 mothers of children aged 0-3 years (152 Turkish, 153 Lebanese) recruited in Türkiye. Lebanese participants were recruited in Istanbul. Seven researcher-developed knowledge items were analyzed individually with false discovery rate correction; a 9-item attitude score was compared between groups. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression examined breastfeeding within 1 hour and reported advice against colostrum.
RESULTS: Lebanese mothers more often correctly identified early colostrum timing (91.5% versus 79.6%; q = 0.026), greater antibody content (99.3% versus 91.4%; q = 0.003), and that colostrum should not be considered "dirty milk" (92.8% versus 66.4%; q < 0.001). Attitude scores were similar (40.17 ± 3.58 versus 39.43 ± 4.95; p = 0.139). Colostrum administration exceeded 90% in both groups. Early breastfeeding was reported by 94.1% of Lebanese and 82.2% of Turkish mothers. Turkish nationality was associated with lower adjusted odds of early initiation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.386, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.165-0.903) and higher odds of reported advice against colostrum (aOR = 4.515, 95% CI: 1.890-10.784).
CONCLUSIONS: Specific knowledge and practice differences were observed, but nationality should not be interpreted as a proxy for culture. Recruitment geography and retrospective reporting limit broader inference. Context-sensitive counseling may help address specific misconceptions and information needs.

articles.title: The effect of aerobic and core stabilization exercises on primary dysmenorrhea in high school girls: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPrimary dysmenorrhea is common in adolescents and is associated with menstrual pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life. Evidence regarding structured combined exercise programs implemented in school settings remains limited. This study examined the effects of a 12-week combined aerobic and core stabilization exercise program on pain, symptom severity, functional impairment, and quality of life in high school students with primary dysmenorrhea.MethodsA randomized controlled, assessor-blinded trial was conducted in which thirty high school girls were allocated to either an exercise group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The intervention group completed a 12-week aerobic and core stabilization program, whereas the control group maintained usual activities. The primary outcome was menstrual pain intensity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included the Premenstrual Syndrome Scale (PMSS), Menstrual Symptom Questionnaire (MSQ), Functional and Emotional Measure of Dysmenorrhea (FEMD), Dysmenorrhea Impact Scale (DIS), and Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36).ResultsThe exercise group demonstrated reductions in pain intensity, menstrual symptom severity, and functional impairment (p < 0.001). Quality-of-life scores improved across all domains (p < 0.001). No meaningful changes were observed in the control group (p > 0.05). Between-group analyses favored the exercise intervention across all outcomes (p < 0.001).ConclusionA combined aerobic and core-stabilization exercise program may be a feasible and effective adjunctive strategy for managing primary dysmenorrhea in adolescents. However, the restrictive BMI eligibility range (19.0-24.9 kg/m2) limits the generalizability of these findings to adolescents outside this range.

articles.title: From miscuing to misuse: why restraint and seclusion have no place in rights-based education.
articles.abstract: Children with disability are disproportionately subjected to restrictive practices in Australian schools, including physical restraint and seclusion. Often justified as necessary for safety or duty of care, these practices are routinely misapplied as behavioural control measures rather than genuine last-resort interventions. This paper presents a clear and evidence-based argument for the prohibition of physical restraint and seclusion in educational settings. It examines their ethical, legal, and developmental consequences, demonstrating that such practices violate children's rights and undermine their safety, dignity, and long-term wellbeing. Drawing on the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) and research in neurodevelopment and trauma, the paper shows how distress and protest are frequently misinterpreted as aggression, particularly for neurodivergent students. It concludes with a call for coordinated national reform grounded in Positive Behaviour Support (PBS), trauma-informed care, and Low Arousal Approaches to build truly inclusive, rights-based education systems.

articles.title: Childhood Maltreatment and Patterns of Lifetime Traumatic Brain Injury: A Latent Profile Analysis.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major public health concern associated with long-term cognitive, behavioral, and emotional consequences. Although prior research has examined links between childhood maltreatment and TBI, findings have been inconsistent, and binary indicators may not capture heterogeneity in injury severity and frequency. The current study has three research questions: (1) Does childhood maltreatment increase risk for TBI? (2) Are there distinct profiles of lifetime TBI exposure among individuals with TBI? and (3) Do childhood maltreatment and other risk factors predict membership in specific TBI profiles compared to individuals without TBI? In a prospective cohort design study, individuals with documented childhood maltreatment (ages 0-11 years) and a matched control group were interviewed during 1989-1995 (N = 1196, M age = 29), 2000-2002 (N = 896, M age = 40), and 2022-2023 (N = 447, M age = 59). Participants completed the Ohio State University TBI Identification Method at the last interview. Latent profile analysis revealed four distinct profiles among individuals with TBI (N = 220): Mild TBI without Loss of Consciousness (LOC) (n = 114, 51.8%), High-Frequency Mild TBI (n = 19, 8.6%), Mild-to-Moderate TBI with LOC (n = 71, 32.3%), and Severe TBI with LOC (n = 16, 7.3%). Multinomial logistic regressions compared each TBI profile to the no-TBI group and examined predictors of profile membership. Childhood maltreatment was associated with increased likelihood of membership in the High-Frequency Mild TBI profile. Alcohol and drug use symptoms, antisocial personality, psychopathy, and lifetime traumas and victimizations experiences predicted profile membership relative to the no-TBI group. Findings revealed subgroups often obscured by single event classifications and suggest that childhood maltreatment may be associated with repeated mild injuries rather than isolated or severe injuries alone.

articles.title: Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury Across Resource Settings: A Comparative Analysis of Presentation and Outcomes at Two Centers in the United States and Uganda.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) affects thousands of children worldwide and remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality. Pediatric TBI (pTBI) outcomes are disproportionately worse in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) compared with high-income countries (HICs). This retrospective dual-cohort study provides a direct comparative analysis of pTBI presentation, management, and outcomes in LMIC and HIC settings. We analyzed data from the National Trauma Data Bank at a tertiary academic hospital in the United States and a regional referral hospital in Uganda. Patient demographics, injury characteristics, treatment modalities, and in-hospital mortality were compared. Logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with mortality. A total of 1,164 patients (LMIC: n = 333; HIC: n = 831) were included. Road traffic accidents were the leading cause of injury in LMICs (67.9% vs. 44.0%, p < 0.001), while falls were more common in HICs. Moderate-to-severe TBI was significantly more prevalent in the LMIC cohort (42.9% vs. 15.0%, p < 0.001). Intensive care unit (ICU) utilization was lower in LMICs (10.2% vs. 31.9%, p < 0.001). The rate of surgical intervention was lower in the LMIC setting, although the difference was not significant (10.8% vs. 16.7%, p = 0.01). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in LMICs (8.7% vs. 2.3%, p < 0.001). Notably, ICU admission in LMICs was associated with increased mortality risk (Log Odds Coefficient = 1.27, p = 0.02), whereas this association was not observed in HICs. pTBI outcomes differ between settings. This disparity may result from higher burden of severe injuries, lower ICU availability, and differences in critical care efficacy in the LMIC setting. ICU admission in LMICs is paradoxically associated with increased mortality, underscoring the need for targeted improvements in neurocritical care resources and triage strategies. These findings highlight critical disparities and provide a foundation for future interventions to improve pTBI care in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Unique Phenotypic Features in Atelís Syndrome due to a Novel Biallelic SLF2 Variant.
articles.abstract: Atelís syndrome (ATELS) is a chromosomal instability disorder caused by biallelic variants in the SLF2 and SMC5 genes, termed ATELS1 and ATELS2, respectively. Thus far, only one report (seven patients) describes the phenotypic and genotypic characteristics of ATELS1. Herein, we report a novel homozygous SLF2 variant (c.449_450dup, p.V151Mfs*12) in a Kashmiri adolescent with ATELS, who also exhibited distinctive phenotypic features. Severe chronic lung disease (including Rhodotorula mucilaginosa and Serratia marcescens infections) and anorectal malformation were noted. Additionally, immunophenotypic evaluation revealed CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell lymphocytosis, particularly of terminally differentiated effector memory CD8+ T-cells, and a reduction in CD27+ memory B-cell proportions. Marginally and severely elevated levels of serum IgA and IgE, respectively, were also observed. Our patient also presented with manifestations of ATELS2 that have not been reported in ATELS1 to date (persistent eosinophilia, borderline/low lymphocyte counts), thereby further harmonizing the phenotypic features associated with the two genetic etiologies of ATELS.

articles.title: Identity-based bullying and maladaptive weight control behaviors among sexual and gender minority youth: Does bullying subtype and format matter?
articles.abstract: Little is known about how bullying an individual because of their weight may be differentially associated with eating disorder risk compared to bullying for other identity components (e.g., gender, sexual orientation) among sexual and gender minority (SGM) youth. It is also unclear how bullying that occurs in-person versus online may impact maladaptive weight control behaviors. The present study quantified experiences of identity-based bullying and examined their differential associations with maladaptive weight control behaviors by subtype and setting (i.e., in school or online) of bullying. 12,868 adolescent participants who identified as SGM completed measures that assessed engagement in maladaptive weight control behaviors, and experiences of bullying in-school and online across domains of identity including weight, gender, race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, disability, immigration status, and gender expression. High rates of bullying were documented across settings with it occurring more often in-person than online, t(12,152)=19.60, p<.001, d=.18. Experiencing bullying in either setting was associated with maladaptive weight control behaviors: bullying experiences in school, F(29, 10,240)=59.09, p<.001, R 2=.14 and bullying experiences online, F(29, 10,150)=50.25, p<.001, R 2=.13. There were slightly stronger associations between being bullied for visible components of identity (weight, gender expression, gender identity) and maladaptive weight control behaviors (βs=.23-.31 versus βs=.10-.25), though all types of bullying victimization across both settings were associated with greater engagement in these behaviors (p<.001 for all). These findings suggest that more resources are needed to combat bullying across locations and to facilitate coping for adolescents at increased risk of identity-based bullying.

articles.title: TIMES Syndrome in an Indian Child With a Novel LRRC8C Frameshift Variant: The Third Molecularly Confirmed Patient Expanding the Genotypic and Phenotypic Spectrum.
articles.abstract: TIMES syndrome is a recently described multisystem disorder caused by de novo heterozygous gain-of-function variants in LRRC8C, the gene encoding a subunit of the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC). We report an 11-year-old Indian boy with a novel de novo heterozygous LRRC8C frameshift variant (c.1277delT), identified following a diagnostic odyssey lasting 7 years. The proband exhibited the core features of TIMES syndrome, including microcephaly, proportionate short stature, telangiectasia with livedo reticularis and progressive skeletal dysplasia. Notably, the patient also presented with previously unreported chronic, poorly healing, "punched-out" skin ulcerations. In contrast to prior reports, the patient's cognitive development was preserved. Serial radiographs demonstrated a progressive skeletal dysplasia that evolved from early metaphyseal abnormalities to generalized epiphyseal-metaphyseal and axial involvement. Structural modelling suggested truncation of the cytoplasmic leucine-rich repeat domain, which is consistent with dysregulated VRAC gating. This report represents the third molecularly confirmed case of TIMES syndrome and expands the phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of LRRC8C-related disease.

articles.title: Indicators of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder in Adults: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disability associated with challenges in neurocognitive, emotional, and behavioral functioning and, for some individuals, distinct physical features. Although most diagnostic guidelines are applicable across the lifespan, identification and support pathways for FASD are more established in childhood health and social care systems, leaving many adults overlooked. Developing a greater understanding of how FASD may present in adults is essential for recognizing individual needs and ensuring that appropriate, responsive supports are provided. The aim of this scoping review was to examine the extent, range, and nature of research on FASD in adults and identify and describe indicators of FASD in adults. ProQuest, PsycINFO, Medline, and CINAHL databases were searched in Sept 2022, with updates conducted in November 2024 and November 2025 for peer-reviewed studies involving FASD and adults. A total of 88 studies met inclusion criteria. Data capturing study characteristics and indicators or characteristics of adults with FASD were extracted for analysis. Qualitative descriptive and analytical coding processes were applied to data relating to potential indicators, and frequency of papers reporting each indicator was calculated. Publication years of included studies ranged from 1978 to 2025. Most studies were conducted in Canada (n = 36) and the United States (n = 29) and had a neurocognitive and neuroanatomical research focus (n = 21). Ten categories were identified as potential FASD indicators: neurocognitive functioning; physical characteristics and health; behavior; mental health, well-being, and trauma; independent living and life skills; education and employment; co-occurring conditions; social relationships; interactions with statutory systems; and strengths and interests. The findings showed that the indicators were rarely discrete, were not necessarily specific to FASD, and reflected complex interactions between neurodevelopmental differences and environmental context. Indicators are therefore understood in this review as features, characteristics, experiences, patterns, or outcomes that may prompt consideration of FASD alongside other possible neurodevelopmental and psychosocial explanations, rather than as diagnostic markers or features specific to FASD. The indicators identified through this scoping review provide an evidence-based foundation for researchers, clinicians, and individuals with living/lived experience to inform future efforts toward recognizing FASD in adults.

articles.title: Regional Left Ventricular Myocardial Strain Alterations in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and Correlation with Electrocardiographic and Motor Function Alterations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is characterized by progressive degradation of muscle function. Myocardial dysfunction is a major cause of mortality; however, its correlation with skeletal motor function remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess myocardial function and to correlate it with motor function in patients with DMD.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional observational study of patients with DMD. Evaluations included the Motor Function Measurement (MFM) scale, electrocardiogram (ECG), and echocardiography (Echo) with speckle-tracking (STE) imaging of the left ventricle (LV). The level of significance adopted in the statistical analysis was 5%.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients with a mean age of 14.30 ± 4.09 years. The average MFM score was 52.30 ± 16.32%. Electrocardiographic abnormalities were observed in 75% of patients. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was preserved (57.80 ± 9.62%). Global longitudinal strain (GLS) was reduced in 70% of the patients (-15.06 ± 2.46%; normal ≤ -18%), global circumferential strain (GCS) was decreased in 76% (-12.99 ± 2.89; normal ≤ -18%), and global radial strain (GRS) was reduced in 80% (20.52 ± 15.72; normal ≥ 40%). Hypokinesia and a significant reduction in regional myocardial strain (REGLSi) were also observed in the inferior and inferolateral segments of the LV. No significant correlation was found between MFM and ECHO variables.
CONCLUSION: Patients with DMD exhibit early compromise in STE parameters (GLS, GRS and GCS) and in REGLSi, particularly in the inferior and inferolateral LV regions, even with preserved LVEF (Central Figure). No significant correlation was observed between motor and cardiac function parameters.

articles.title: Efficacy of estrogen therapy for postpartum depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum depression (PPD) is one of the most prevalent mental health complications of the perinatal period and is associated with maternal impairment, disruption of the mother-infant bond, and adverse effects on child cognitive and emotional development. The most widely accepted pathophysiological hypothesis involves the abrupt decline in estrogen concentrations following childbirth, leading to interest in estrogen replacement as a potential therapeutic strategy for PPD.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Searches were performed in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL and Scopus using the terms "postpartum depression," "estrogen," "estrogen replacement therapy," and related synonyms. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing estrogen with placebo for PPD treatment were included.
RESULTS: Four RCTs involving 154 women with PPD met the eligibility criteria. The pooled analysis showed a standardized mean difference (SMD) of -0.16 (95% confidence interval (CI) -0.58-0.25; I² = 35%), favoring estrogen but without a statistically significant effect. The certainty of evidence was rated as low according to the GRADE approach, with a two-level downgrade for very serious imprecision due to the limited sample size and wide confidence interval encompassing potentially clinically important benefit, little or no effect, and possible harm.
CONCLUSIONS: Although estrogen therapy has a biological rationale for PPD treatment, the currently available evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Further well-designed RCTs with larger sample sizes, standardized methodologies, and adequate pharmacokinetic monitoring are required to clarify the efficacy and safety of estrogen therapy in this population.

articles.title: Parasitological and entomological assessment of onchocerciasis in ivermectin-naïve, hypo-endemic communities of Ogun State, Nigeria: evidence of ongoing transmission.
articles.journal: Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg
articles.abstract: Onchocerciasis remains a significant public health concern in Africa, particularly in ivermectin-naïve, hypo-endemic communities where transmission may persist undetected. Such areas are highly relevant to the WHO 2030 elimination goals. Ogun State is co-endemic for onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis (LF), and Loa loa, creating complex programmatic challenges for mass drug administration (MDA). This study aimed to provide an integrated parasitological and entomological assessment of Onchocerca volvulus prevalence and vector infectivity in three hypo-endemic communities in Ijebu Northeast Local Government Area (LGA), Ogun State, Nigeria. A preliminary longitudinal entomological study was conducted at the Ebute River breeding site serving Idode, Igede, and Orunwa communities in Ijebu Northeast LGA, Ogun State, Nigeria, from February 2023 to January 2024. Human skin snips (n=209) were examined by microscopy and O-150 PCR to determine infection prevalence by community, sex, and age group. Blackflies were collected monthly (7 a.m.-7 p.m.) using Human Landing Collection (HLC); specimens were dissected for parity assessment and screened for O. volvulus infectivity using O-150 PCR. Human PCR prevalence was 14.8% (31/209) compared with 10.0% (21/209) by microscopy. Orunwa had the highest prevalence (23.8% by PCR), followed by Idode (7.1%) and Igede (5.8%). Based on PCR results, Idode and Igede are classified as hypo-endemic, while Orunwa is classified as meso-endemic. Females had higher prevalence than males (24.3% vs 4.1%; P < .001). Age-specific analysis showed elevated PCR prevalence in the 5-20 years age group (17.7%) and the 50+ years age group (42.3%). Entomologically, 418 Simulium damnosum complex flies were collected, with monthly biting rate peaks of 1260 and 1890 bites/person/month during rainy and late rainy seasons, respectively. Parity rates ranged from 52% to 78%. No infective flies were detected, and annual transmission potential for this study is zero. The 14.8% human PCR prevalence provides direct evidence of ongoing onchocerciasis transmission in these ivermectin-naïve communities. The presence of infection across all age groups, including children, confirms active transmission. Although no infective.

articles.title: Clinician Perspectives on Having Family Building Discussions With People With Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe potential impacts of sickle cell disease (SCD) and its treatments on multiple aspects of family building are emerging. Literature shows individuals with SCD desire biologic parenthood, yet few receive reproductive health counseling. This study aimed to explore SCD clinicians' perspectives on family building discussions with men and women with SCD.MethodParticipants were clinicians from across the United States, recruited via online SCD clinician listservs. Participants completed a survey capturing their demographics, clinical characteristics, and attitudes, practice patterns, challenges, and needs regarding family building discussions. Descriptive statistics summarized the quantitative data, and qualitative responses were categorized into challenges, needs, and resources needed to have these conversations.ResultsOf the 38 participants, 74% were pediatric SCD clinicians and 97% practiced at an academic medical center. Forty-two percent and 30% of clinicians reported not feeling comfortable initiating family building discussions with men and women with SCD, respectively. Reported challenges included lack of time during visits and these discussions not being within the perceived scope of the clinician (e.g., patients being too young, clinicians only practicing inpatient hematology). Needs included culturally informed resources for patients, additional training for clinicians, and clear referral options to specialists.DiscussionSCD clinicians experience multiple barriers that may prevent them from having family building discussions with people with SCD. Future studies investigating the best ways to incorporate family building discussions into SCD care are needed to ensure that people with SCD are able to achieve their family building goals.

articles.title: Pregnancy Surveillance in the Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance Network: Findings from a Multisite Open Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) investigates causes of stillbirth and deaths in children <5 years of age in high-mortality settings. Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance established pregnancy surveillance to prospectively monitor pregnancies and their outcomes and better understand maternal care in these settings. Pregnant women were enrolled during home visits or antenatal care from catchment populations in eight countries (Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and South Africa). At enrollment, data on maternal sociodemographic characteristics, obstetric history, and medical conditions were collected. Data on maternal and infant healthcare and outcomes were collected at delivery and 42 days postpartum. A total of 84,413 pregnant women were enrolled from June 2021 to July 2025; the median gestational age at enrollment was 21.3 weeks. Most (64,820/84,413; 76.8%) participants were <30 years of age (range: 12-55 years), and 70.6% of participants had previous pregnancies. Across sites, the median number of antenatal care contacts was three; 21.6% (15,302/70,940) of women experienced unsupervised or unassisted home deliveries, and 12.0% of newborns were low birthweight. Overall, a high stillbirth rate (22.9/1,000 births; range 4.3-26.5/1,000 among sites), neonatal mortality rate (17.6/1,000 live births; range 4.6-25.2/1,000 among sites), and risk of perinatal death (36.7/1,000 births; range 16.9-43.9/1,000 among sites) were found, with heterogeneity in all mortalities by site (P <0.001). The maternal mortality ratio was 177.5 per 100,000 live births. In the CHAMPS Pregnancy Surveillance catchment areas, women presented late for antenatal care, had too few antenatal contacts (<8), and experienced a high burden of adverse pregnancy outcomes. The findings highlight the need for better pregnancy care in similar areas with high child mortality.

articles.title: Miscarriages and Perinatal Deaths in Sierra Leone: Data From A Nationwide Household Survey.
articles.abstract: Demographic data on adverse pregnancy outcomes in Sierra Leone are scarce. This study examined the prevalence of miscarriages and perinatal deaths from a community perspective by use of a population-based, cross-sectional household survey on surgical conditions conducted in Sierra Leone in 2019-2020. A weighted random cluster design was used to select the enumerator areas with a probability proportional to the population size. Seventy-five clusters were selected, with 25 households per cluster and two random participants per household. Women between 12 and 50 years of age were interviewed about family planning methods and their obstetrical history. A total of 3,745 participants were included; 914 were women of reproductive age. Family planning methods were used by 216/914 women (28.5%). In total, 2,160 lifetime pregnancies were recalled, of which 104/2,160 (4.8%) resulted in early pregnancy loss. Eighty-three (83/104; 79.8%) were reported as spontaneous abortion, 18/104 (17.3%) were intentional abortions. There were 55/2, 160 stillbirths reported (2.5%). The stillbirth rate was 18.4 per 1,000 births (95% CI: 11.2-31.0). The perinatal mortality rate, defined as stillbirth after a gestational age of 28 weeks or neonatal death within the first 7 days after birth per 1,000 births calculated over a 5-year period, was 38.4 per 1,000 births (95% CI: 26.7-55.0). This population-based survey demonstrates a high perinatal mortality rate and low use of family planning methods in Sierra Leone. Miscarriages were likely to be underreported. Improved access to affordable contraception and appropriate medical evaluation of pregnancy loss may help reduce the burden of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Community-Partnered Research to Improve Newborn Screening Awareness and Follow-up in a High-Infant-Mortality Setting.
articles.abstract: Newborn screening (NBS) is a public health program that tests infants for rare but treatable congenital, metabolic, and genetic disorders shortly after birth, creating an opportunity for early intervention that can prevent death and reduce long-term morbidity. Although NBS is often framed as a health equity success, research has shown persistent disparities in the timeliness of diagnosis and treatment following abnormal results. This concern is especially urgent in Cleveland, Ohio, where infant mortality rates exceed state and national benchmarks. In partnership with First Year Cleveland, an organization dedicated to lowering infant mortality rates, we launched a community-partnered pilot. Our goal is to identify actionable, systems-level opportunities to strengthen NBS follow-up by engaging home-visiting perinatal professionals as trusted messengers and implementation partners. We convened stakeholder meetings to build shared understandings of NBS and to elicit frontline perspectives; insights from the initial session were used to co-develop a survey distributed via snowball sampling to home-visiting professionals serving pregnant people and newborns across Cuyahoga County (January 22-March 17, 2025; N=80). Findings showed strong endorsement for family education about NBS (89%), ideally by the third trimester (71%), alongside substantial workforce knowledge gaps, with most respondents reporting no formal training about NBS (71%). Stakeholders emphasized the need for clearer role delineation, generally viewing physicians as the primary source of NBS education while positioning home-visiting professionals as a complementary, secondary source who can reinforce messages and support care navigation. These preliminary findings are shaping a roadmap for meaningful change that combines continued research expansion into additional communities with immediate capacity-building for the home-visitation workforce.

articles.title: Clinical efficacy of intermittent phototherapy combined with triple therapy and pediatric Tuina massage in the treatment of neonatal jaundice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical efficacy of intermittent phototherapy combined with triple therapy and pediatric Tuina massage in the treatment of neonatal jaundice.
METHODOLOGY: This was a retrospective study. A total of 82 jaundiced neonates, admitted to Hebei Reproductive Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital between December 2024 to December 2025, were enrolled to assess the clinical efficacy of the treatment regimen and investigate its impact on total bilirubin(TBIL), carbohydrate antigen 199(CA199), C-reactive protein(CRP), and apolipoprotein M(ApoM).
RESULTS: The overall response rate in the treatment group was 92.68%, significantly higher than the 75.61% of the control group(P< 0.05). After treatment, the levels of TBIL, CA199, CRP, and ApoM in both groups were significantly lower than pre-treatment levels(P< 0.05, respectively). Notably, the treatment group showed more pronounced reductions in all biomarkers compared with the control group, and the differences were statistically significant(all P< 0.05). The duration of jaundice(DoJ) and length of hospital stay(LoHS) in the treatment group were significantly shorter than in the control group(both P< 0.05). The adverse reaction rate in the treatment group was 9.76%, significantly lower than the 26.83% in the control group(P< 0.05). Furthermore, the family satisfaction rate in the treatment group was 95.12%, significantly higher than the 80.49% in the control group(P< 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Intermittent phototherapy combined with triple therapy and pediatric Tuina massage appears to be an effective treatment for neonatal jaundice, significantly improving clinical outcomes. This approach offers a more scientifically grounded and effective treatment protocol for neonatal jaundice management.

articles.title: Effects of adjunctive fusidic acid cream in the intra-incisional dressing on surgical outcomes and satisfaction in children after concealed penis surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the feasibility and efficacy of fusidic acid (FA) cream as an adjunct in intra-incisional dressings for postoperative care of children with concealed penis, by analyzing its effects on incision recovery and caregiver satisfaction.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 186 children who underwent modified Devine procedure for concealed penis at The Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University (July 2023-November 2025). Patients were divided into FA group (n=84, FA cream added to intra-incisional dressing) and Vaseline gauze group (n=102, conventional dressing). Clinical data (age, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative bleeding/infection) and caregiver satisfaction (Likert scale) were collected and compared between groups.
RESULTS: No significant intergroup differences were found in age, operative time, or intraoperative blood loss(P>0.05). The FA group had fewer cases of postoperative bleeding and infection, lower dressing change frequency, and shorter dressing change time (all P<0.05). Satisfaction scores in the FA group were significantly higher than the control group for all dimensions except doctor communication(P>0.05), with a higher overall satisfaction score.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive FA cream in intra-incisional dressings effectively controls peri-incisional infection, accelerates incision healing, reduces complications and dressing change burden, and improves caregiver satisfaction in children with concealed penis, making it worthy of clinical promotion.

articles.title: Clinical profile, genomic insights, and novel variants in Pakistani pediatric B-ALL patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the genomic and molecular alterations in a sample set of Pakistani pediatric B- Acute Lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) patients.
METHODOLOGY: This descriptive analytical study was conducted at the University of Health Sciences, Lahore, Pakistan, from November 2021 to June 2022. Newly diagnosed treatment-naïve pediatric B-ALL patients were enrolled. Following DNA isolation, whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed and genomic variants were analyzed using the Genome Analysis Tool Kit (GATK).
RESULTS: Of the 19 enrolled B-ALL patients, whole genome sequencing data of sufficient quality for variant analysis were available for 12 patients. Single nucleotide variations (SNVs) and INDELs were identified in all 12 of these patients, each carrying a variant in one of four genes: SLC6A4 (n=7, 58%), ZFHX3 (n=3, 25%), SLC26A9 (n=1, 8%), and BRCA2 (n=1, 8%).
CONCLUSION: Immunophenotypic variations and genomic alterations including SNVs and indels were evident in the enrolled B-ALL patients. Extensive efforts are warranted to understand the impact of these genomic and molecular changes in B-ALL for better risk assessment and prediction of prognosis and disease management.

articles.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy: A retrospective observational study at a tertiary care hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and predictors of drug-resistant epilepsy among patients with epilepsy.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective observational study was conducted at the Neurology Department of Liaquat National Hospital, Karachi, for the period from November, 2024 to October, 2025. Patients with epilepsy were enrolled, excluding neonates and those with psychiatric comorbidities or active substance abuse. Participants were recruited consecutively. Descriptive statistics summarized patient characteristics, while chi-square tests evaluated associations between variables such as drug adherence, epilepsy type, and antiepileptic drug (ASM) selection. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated to quantify the strength of these associations.
RESULTS: A total of 382 participants were included (49.5% male, 50.5% female), with a mean age of 31.73 +/- 16.82 years and a mean seizure onset age of 25.3 years. The majority were urban residents with higher educational levels and 19.4% had refractory epilepsy. On multivariate logistic regression analysis, normal MRI brain findings (a OR = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.142-0.570; p < 0.001), normal EEG findings (a OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.256-0.974; p = 0.042) and adherence to the given treatment (a OR= 0.516, 95% CI: 0.234-1.138; p=0.101) have lower odds of having drug resistance. Lower level of education (a OR = 3.496, 95% CI: 1.687-7.245; p < 0.001), and a history of status epilepticus (a OR = 8.029, 95% CI: 4.186-15.400: p <0.001) have higher odds of refractory epilepsy.
CONCLUSION: By identifying key predictors of drug-resistant epilepsy, our study contributes to a better understanding of factors associated with treatment resistance and may inform future interventions.

articles.title: Agreement between digital ocular alignment measurement devices and the prism alternate cover test in horizontal strabismus.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the agreement between digital ocular alignment devices and the prism alternate cover test (PACT) in patients with horizontal strabismus.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 63 patients (31 esotropia, 32 exotropia). Ocular deviation was measured using the prism alternate cover test (PACT) at near (CTN) and distance (CTD) and compared with measurements obtained using the Welch Allyn Spot Vision Screener and the BCN Innova Sensor. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to deviation magnitude (10-30 PD and >30 PD).
RESULTS: The estimated ICC values indicated moderate agreement between the digital devices and PACT measurements. Agreement was generally stronger in exotropia than in esotropia.
