Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated small mean biases but wide limits of agreement. Agreement was more consistent within the 10-30 PD range and decreased in larger deviations.
CONCLUSIONS: Digital ocular alignment devices demonstrated moderate agreement with PACT, particularly in patients with moderate-angle deviations. However, agreement decreased in larger deviations, and the wide limits of agreement indicate that individual measurements should be interpreted with caution. Therefore, PACT remains the clinical reference method for accurate deviation measurement, particularly in surgical planning.

articles.title: RSV and all-cause lower respiratory infection burden among infants residing in remote British Columbia: Retrospective population-based birth cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the population-based incidence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection-related hospitalization in infancy by community remoteness.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of live births within an integrated health jurisdiction in British Columbia (BC, Canada) from April 2013 to March 2024, followed for 1 year, using routinely collected health administrative data. Main outcomes were hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Secondary outcomes were tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Main exposures were community remoteness and social determinants of health. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated with Poisson generalized estimating equations accounting for clustering by community, with and without additional adjustment for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions.
RESULTS: Among 472,623 infants, those living in remote communities (n = 3636) had higher hospitalization risk for all-cause (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to metropolitan areas. Length of stay and PICU admission rates were similar by region. Almost half (48.8%) of children from remote areas hospitalized for RSV-LRTIs required air evacuation. Infants from remote communities remained at higher risk for all-cause (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTI (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12) hospitalizations after adjusting for covariates.
CONCLUSION: Infants in remote communities experienced a disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalization that is not fully explained by measured clinical or social determinants of health. These findings underscore the need for region-specific approaches and equitable implementation of prevention programs as jurisdictions move toward universal RSV immunization.

articles.title: Mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Introduction This systematic review aimed to assess prevalence and characteristics of mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with seven neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions, to compare these to normative populations, and identify associated factors. Material and Methods Using a PRISMA compliant protocol (PROSPERO CRD42023443731), studies on congenital diaphragmatic hernia(CDH), esophageal atresia(EA), abdominal wall defects (AWD: gastroschisis/omphalocele), anorectal malformations (ARM), Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) and surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) were identified through searches in MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library (inception-November 2025) A random-effects meta-analysis of prevalence was conducted, with heterogeneity assessed using I². Significance level was p<0.05. Results Forty-seven studies (published 1991-2025) with 1786 children (median sample size 28, range 10-157) were included: CDH (n=10), EA (n=11), AWD (n=9), NEC (n=2), ARM (n=17), and HSCR (n=5). Most studies originated from Europe (n=31). Mental health and behavioral difficulties were more frequently reported than in norms, in CDH (7/8 studies), EA (6/7 studies), and ARM (4/6 studies). Meta-analysis showed elevated difficulties in 25,7% (Child Behavior Check List; I²=59.6) and 17.8% (Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire; I²=65.3). The prevalence of autism ranged from 10-23% (CDH, AWD) and ADHD from 0-20% (CDH, AWD, NEC, ARM, HSCR). Across studies, methodological quality was generally 'fair' to 'poor'. Clinical and family-related factors were significantly associated with outcomes (p<0.05). Conclusions Children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions risk mental health and behavioral difficulties. Current research leaves room for improvement of study quality. Multidisciplinary follow-up care is warranted, and its effects should be evaluated.

articles.title: Esophageal atresia and co-occurring major anomalies in Denmark 1994-2021: A nationwide register-based study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal atresia (EA) frequently co-occurs with additional major congenital anomalies. Long-term national trends and the influence of anomaly definitions on registry estimates remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, register-based cohort study of infants born in Den-mark during 1994-2021, who participated in the neonatal screening program, which has near-complete coverage. Infants were identified using ICD-10-DK codes in linked national registries. Associated major congenital anomalies were classified with reference to EURO-CAT guidance. Temporal trends were assessed using Poisson regression models. Pheno-types were classified as syndromic or non-syndromic; non-syndromic cases were further classified as isolated or with co-occurring major anomalies.
RESULTS: Among 1,696,357 screened infants, 442 were diagnosed with EA, corresponding to a birth prevalence of 2.61 per 10,000 screened live births (95% CI 2.37 - 2.86). EA preva-lence increased by an estimated 1.6% annually (95% CI 0.4-2.9%; p=0.0073). Syndromic EA accounted for 18.3% of cases, with relatively stable proportions over time. Among non-syndromic cases, 47.6% had at least one co-occurring major anomaly, most commonly car-diovascular anomalies. After excluding atrial and ventricular septal defects, cardiac anoma-lies were recorded in 8.8% overall (28.4% of syndromic and 4.4% of non-syndromic cases).
CONCLUSIONS: EA prevalence among screened live-born infants was consistent with international estimates and showed a modest model-based increase over time. Nearly half of non-syndromic infants had an additional major anomaly, supporting systematic multisystem assessment. Cardiac-anomaly estimates were strongly influenced by inclusion of atrial and ventricular septal de-fects, which should be considered when comparing registry studies.

articles.title: Configurations and Temporal Patterns of Motivational Drivers and Factors Associated With Participation in The Com.
articles.abstract: The Com has been linked to a range of harmful behaviours, such as offline violence, cyber offending, and sextortion. Despite increasing concern from law enforcement and policymakers, little empirical research exists. We analysed information about 29 individuals charged with or convicted of offences associated with The Com from the NOVEL database. Pairwise configurational analysis was used to identify combinations of motivational drivers and factors associated with four behavioural outcomes: offline violence, cyber offending, sextortion, and taking a leadership role. Proximity coefficient analysis examined the temporal sequencing of these factors. Ideological indicators were present in several configurations associated with offline violence, but sequence analysis suggested that these tended to emerge after indicators of violent propensity, questioning any interpretation of ideology as an initial driver. Sextortion demonstrated the most coherent pathways and was associated with social isolation, belonging-, status-, and notoriety-seeking, violence fascination, and mental ill health. Cyber offending pathways were more heterogeneous, tentatively related to notoriety-seeking, status-seeking, and neurodevelopmental conditions; violence fascination occupied a comparatively peripheral role. Leadership pathways combined violent propensity with social isolation and status-seeking. Across outcomes, many of the same vulnerabilities and motivations appeared, but they demonstrated different functional roles.

articles.title: The Clinical and Neuro-Informed Benefits of Utilizing a Grief-Focused Camp for Supporting Childhood Bereavement.
articles.abstract: Grief-focused camps offer clinical and neuro-informed benefits for grieving children. This conceptual article highlights both design and implementation of a bereavement camp, exploring how structured, experiential, and expressive activities engage developing neural networks involved in emotion regulation, attachment, and stress response. Drawing on the Dual-Processing Model of Grief and the Window of Tolerance, the camp model emphasizes relational safety, peer normalization, and multisensory engagement to promote adaptive coping and support the grieving processes. Rotating small-group sessions, large-group activities, and ending with guardian-inclusive activities provides repeated corrective emotional experiences supporting neuroplasticity and resilience. The design intentionally balances opportunities for processing loss with restorative, play-based experiences fostering emotional growth and co-regulation. Clinical implications for counselors include program and staff structures and supervision, grounded in neuro-informed principles. By applying a neuroscience lens to grief-focused camp design, this model demonstrates potential to enhance coping, emotional development, and long-term adaptive functioning in bereaved children.

articles.title: Nationwide trends in pediatric cancer incidence in Saudi Arabia: a comprehensive 20-year study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups. Although childhood cancers represent a significant health challenge, available resources for evaluating their impact remain relatively scarce in the Kingdom. This study provides a detailed analysis of incidence trends over two decades among the Saudi pediatric population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Data on various incidence metrics for pediatric cancer cases (ages 0-14) were obtained from the Saudi Cancer Registry (SCR) for the period of 2001 to 2020. Joinpoint regression analysis was further employed to evaluate temporal trends alongside comparisons with global data.
RESULTS: A total increase of 53.8% in childhood cancer cases was observed, with cases rising from 498 in 2001 to 766 in 2020. Males consistently accounted for more cases and exhibited higher rates of increase (60.5%) compared to females (45.16%). The overall age-specific incidence rate (AIR) increased by 72.07%, with an 80.21% rise in males and 61.77% in females. The most common cancer types were leukemia, brain and central nervous system (CNS) tumors and Hodgkin's lymphoma. The regression analysis revealed a significant upward trend in incidence, with an average annual percentage change (APC) of 2.74% (95% CI: 2.09-3.4) overall, 2.7% (95% CI: 1.99-3.41) in males and 2.81% (95% CI: 2.16-3.47) in females (p < 0.05 for all).
CONCLUSION: Childhood cancer incidence in Saudi Arabia has risen significantly over the past two decades, especially among males. These findings highlight the need for improved surveillance, etiologic research and strategic resource planning.

articles.title: Dermatological conditions in endurance athletes: prevalence and associated factors in a cross-sectional online survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of dermatological conditions among endurance athletes and investigate associations with demographic and sports-related variables.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 400 Brazilian adult endurance athletes, defined as individuals regularly training ≥10 h/week and/or participating in long-distance endurance events. Participants completed a structured questionnaire including demographic data, sports-related variables, sun exposure, photoprotection habits, and self-reported dermatological conditions. Associations between sports modalities and dermatological outcomes were assessed using logistic regression, with effect sizes expressed as odds ratios and 95%CIs.
RESULTS: Dermatological conditions were highly prevalent, with mechanically induced lesions representing the most frequent group. The most common conditions were foot blisters (73.8%), excoriations (59.0%), calluses (56.3%), abrasions (54.8%), and traumatic onycholysis (53.8%). First-degree sunburn (40.8%) and insect stings (36.3%) were the most frequent inflammatory/environmental conditions. Running was independently associated with foot blisters (OR 5.0; 95%CI 2.2-11.7) and traumatic onycholysis (OR 3.2; 95%CI 1.4-7.6), whereas cycling was associated with bacterial folliculitis (OR 2.7; 95%CI 1.0-7.5). Most athletes reported sun exposure exceeding 1 h per training session, while regular sunscreen use remained incomplete (56.4%). Self-reported skin neoplasms were uncommon but included seven melanoma cases, all among runners.
CONCLUSION: Endurance athletes exhibit a substantial burden of dermatological conditions related to repetitive mechanical stress, ultraviolet exposure, and sport-specific practices. Educational and preventive strategies focused on friction reduction, photoprotection, and early recognition of suspicious skin lesions may reduce short- and long-term morbidity.

articles.title: Child Opportunity Index 3.0 and Health Care Use in Children With Complex Chronic Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Children with complex chronic disease (C-CD) disproportionately use health care. We evaluated the association between neighborhood opportunity, measured by Child Opportunity Index (COI) 3.0, and health care use among children with C-CD and, secondarily, between insurance type and use. We hypothesized that children in lower COI neighborhoods would have higher use.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study spanned 2019 to 2025. Children aged at most 21 years with C-CD, identified using the Pediatric Medical Complexity Algorithm, with an index encounter in 2019 were included. The primary exposure was census tract-level COI 3.0; quintiles were collapsed into 3 groups because of small subgroup sizes. Primary outcomes were mean annual inpatient admissions and hospital length of stay (LOS). Secondary outcomes were mean annual emergency department visits, outpatient clinic visits, and missed appointment rate. Multivariable regression models assessed associations of COI group and insurance status with use, adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, and number of body systems affected.
RESULTS: Of 3535 children with C-CD, 2419 (68%) lived in very low/low COI tracts, 633 (18%) in moderate, and 483 (14%) in high/very high. Compared with children in high/very high COI neighborhoods, those in very low/low COI neighborhoods had longer LOS (14.1 vs 10.0 days; P = .007) and more outpatient clinic visits (30.8 vs 25.7; P = .02).
CONCLUSION: Neighborhood-level factors may substantially influence health care use among children with C-CD. Targeted interventions and advocacy addressing social and structural barriers are likely needed. Better understanding these factors may help health systems improve care delivery, allocate resources, and reduce disparities.

articles.title: Standards to Support Healthy Sleep for Pediatric Inpatients and Their Families: A Delphi Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sleep is essential for physical and mental health. However, its importance is often overlooked in hospitals, negatively impacting children's well-being and recovery as well as their caregivers' ability to provide support. The aim of this study was to achieve consensus on internationally relevant standards to promote healthy sleep in hospitals providing pediatric in-patient care.
METHODS: An expert steering group developed 32 potential standards for supporting child and caregiver sleep in hospitals based on research, clinical experience, and surveys of pediatric sleep groups. A panel formed from the International Pediatric Sleep Association (IPSA) membership completed a 3-round Delphi study to guide the development of 5 to 15 final standards. Consensus was defined as at least 80% agreement using a 4-point Likert scale. Narrative comments were incorporated.
RESULTS: Seventy-six multiprofessional participants from 23 countries/regions consented to participate. A panel of 49 were selected, maximizing geographical and professional representation, to complete rounds 2 and 3, with 35 (71%) from 20 countries/regions and 23 (47%) from 13 countries/regions participating, respectively. Consensus was high throughout. The final round organized the information into 5 overarching standards encompassing sleep included in the health care plan, commitment from senior management, promotion of circadian rhythms, family support, and environmental modifications. Each standard had 5 or 6 associated criteria. The standards achieved 96% agreement.
CONCLUSIONS: Consensus was achieved on 5 overarching standards with their associated criteria designed to facilitate stepwise change, be adaptable to local contexts, and provide measurable outcomes to support healthy sleep for hospitalized children and families globally.

articles.title: Gender Representation in Leadership of Pediatric Hospital Subspecialty Organizations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equity in leadership of hospital-based pediatric organizations at the national level is essential to supporting a diverse workforce and patient population.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the gender representation of women on leadership committees and boards of external organizations compared with their representation in the workforce of neonatal-perinatal medicine, pediatric critical care medicine, pediatric hospital medicine, and pediatric cardiac critical care.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study of publicly available data in 2024.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was representation of women in external leadership of selected subspecialties. Measures included demographic and institutional variables of American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) and external leadership organizations.
RESULTS: A total of 771 individuals across 41 external organizations were included. Women constituted 54% of these ABP-certified hospital-based subspecialists and 47.7% of identified leaders (P < .05). The representation of women was 45.5% after excluding nonphysician leaders. Women represented 35% of those holding "top seats," including president, chair, editor-in-chief, or equivalent titles. Of the categories of external organizations, women were least likely to be represented as leaders of research-oriented organizations at 42.8%. We were unable to determine the candidacy or selection process for leadership for more than 70% of the organizations. Among this subset, only 42.7% of leaders were women.
CONCLUSION: Women pediatric physicians were significantly underrepresented in external leadership positions compared with the workforce in an aggregate of hospital-based subspecialties. A lack of transparency in leadership selection may contribute to gender inequities in leadership. Opportunities exist for promoting leadership that is representative of the workforce.

articles.title: Hospitalized and Population Prevalence Over Time of Children With Medical Complexity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Children with medical complexity (CMC) experience disproportionately higher adverse health outcomes. Studies have reported their point prevalence and smaller-scale outpatient trends; however, hospitalized prevalence trends and larger-scale population prevalence trend estimates have not been done. As such, our objective was to report the prevalence trends of hospitalized CMC from 2006 to 2024 in the hospitalized and provincial population of Alberta, Canada.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, repeated, cross-sectional study of CMC prevalence, aged 0 to 18 years, in 2-year intervals from 2006 to 2024 using data from all residents of Alberta, Canada. We identified all children with at least 1 inpatient hospitalization associated with a complex chronic condition (CCC). We calculated prevalence both by dividing the absolute count of children hospitalized with a CCC in a time interval by the age-matched hospitalized population and the age-matched Alberta population for the same time interval.
RESULTS: The most recent adjusted overall hospitalized prevalence, from the 2022-2024 time interval, was 6301 per 100 000, and the adjusted provincial prevalence of hospitalized CMC was 784 per 100 000 population. The adjusted hospitalized prevalence increased by 3.9% per 2-year time interval from 2006 to 2018, followed by a decline of 3.1% per time interval in 2019-2024. The adjusted provincial prevalence of hospitalized CMC increased by 2.6% per time interval from 2006 to 2014, followed by a decline of 3.4% per time interval from 2015 until 2024.
CONCLUSIONS: A peak followed by a decline was seen in hospitalized CMC prevalence between 2014 and 2018 in the provincial and hospitalized population, which may be aligning with preliminary evidence from the literature.

articles.title: Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies: Principles, Challenges, and Recommendations.
articles.abstract: Observational studies play a crucial role in pediatric research by assessing disease burden, real-world effectiveness and safety, risk factors, and rare outcomes. They are particularly important for questions for which randomized controlled trials would be unethical, impractical, or not well aligned with the clinical question. The incorporation of observational studies into meta-analyses allows for greater synthesis of observational data; however, conducting these evidence syntheses introduces unique methodological challenges. These include increased heterogeneity, residual confounding, and a higher risk of within- and between-study biases, which can compromise the validity of pooled estimates. This article outlines key considerations for conducting meta-analyses of observational studies. Guidance is provided on protocol development, defining inclusion criteria, selecting appropriate study designs, extracting effect estimates, and managing confounding and heterogeneity. Using a published meta-analysis on the association between particulate matter exposure and childhood asthma, we illustrate practical challenges and strategies for interpretation.

articles.title: Socioecological Influences on Food and Nutrition Security Among Publicly Insured Families.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding of the factors influencing food and nutrition security among households with children remains limited, particularly during pediatric hospitalization, a vulnerable period for food access. Caregivers' perspectives offer critical insights into the determinants of food-related decision-making and the strategies households use to obtain preferred, nutritious foods.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using semistructured interviews with caregivers of publicly insured hospitalized children from an existing study cohort. We purposively sampled participants using maximal variation sampling to reflect a range of food and nutrition security statuses. Guided by a socioecological framework, interviews explored caregivers' perspectives on nutrition, food access and benefits, and community resources. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis with both inductive and deductive coding, informed by the same framework.
RESULTS: We interviewed 23 caregivers, predominantly from food-secure and nutrition-secure households. Six themes were identified, including (1) balancing nutritional ideals with everyday realities; (2) dynamics of food access across cycles of resource fluctuation and strain; (3) dignity, choice, and a hierarchy with food assistance programs; (4) food scarcity-driven sacrifice, emotional burden, and adaptive measures; (5) technology-enabled strategies to mitigate barriers to food access and nutrition information; and (6) skepticism toward the food system and a preference for natural foods.
CONCLUSION: Constrained choices, fluctuating resources, and system-level factors shaped perceptions of food and nutrition, influencing caregivers' sense of dignity, control, and adaptive strategies, such as using grocery-delivery services and online sources. These findings highlight the importance of autonomy and stability in supporting vulnerable families' access to preferred foods.

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.
CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

articles.title: Pharmacologic Management of Pediatric Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity in North America.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe pharmacological management approaches to pediatric paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) among North American pediatric attending physicians.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional web-based survey of pediatric attending physicians conducted from March to August 2023. The questionnaire examined PSH medication utilization and preferences, subspecialty responsibilities for managing PSH, and the influence of patient age on medication selection. Descriptive statistics summarize PSH medication utilization and rank-order preferences. Chi-square analyses examined relationships between physician specialty and medication selection.
RESULTS: Among 295 respondents (33% palliative care, 23% neurology, 18% complex care, 17% physiatry), considerable heterogeneity in PSH pharmacotherapy approaches was observed. The most used abortive PSH medications were gamma-aminobutyric acid A (GABA-A) agonists (86%), alpha-2 agonists (79%), and opioids (49%). Leading preventive PSH medications included alpha-2 agonists (90%), gabapentinoids (89%), and beta-blockers (66%). Top-ranked medications for abortive management were alpha-2 agonists, GABA-A agonists, and non-opioid analgesics; and gabapentinoids, alpha-2 agonists, and beta-blockers for preventive management. While physiatrists and neurologists were most frequently identified as primary managers of PSH at participants' home institutions, several other specialties (including multidisciplinary models) were reported as well. We observed significant differences in utilization of alpha-2 agonists, opioids, dopamine agonists, and beta-blockers across subspecialties (all P < .05). Patient age influenced medication selection among 41% of our sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic management of pediatric PSH currently lacks clinical consensus and varies significantly based on physician subspecialty. Our findings underscore the need for focused research efforts to identify optimal treatment strategies and develop standardized and evidence-based management guidelines.

articles.title: Adult Care in a Pediatric Hospital: Patterns and Implications of an Internal Medicine Consult Service at a Children's Hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children's hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023.
RESULTS: Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14-71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1-22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0-21) each. The most common comorbidities were technology dependence (47%), solid tumor malignancy (22.5%), genetic conditions (20.2%), epilepsy (19.7%), congenital heart disease (17.4%), and cerebral palsy (15.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: Adult consult services in children's hospitals support a medically complex population with diverse childhood-onset and adult conditions and function as longitudinal clinical partners. These findings support the role of adult medicine expertise in children's hospitals to help recognize and manage adult-specific care needs and transitions.

articles.title: Practical Guidance for Promoting Language Equity in Pediatric Hospital Medicine Research.
articles.abstract: Children whose caregivers use languages other than English (LOE) experience persistent inequities in pediatric health care yet remain systematically underrepresented in research. Inpatient pediatric studies present distinct challenges to achieving language-equitable research, including complex clinical workflows and variable regulatory requirements. Prior literature highlights the importance of including participants who use LOE in pediatric research, but practical methodological guidance tailored to inpatient settings remains limited. We outline a framework to support pediatric hospitalists in designing rigorous studies that more fully include families who use LOE as participants and partners. We provide actionable strategies to promote language equity across the full research lifecycle, including study design, budgeting, recruitment, consent, data collection, analysis, reporting, and dissemination. These strategies address common inpatient challenges such as interpreter logistics, institutional review board variability, and minimizing participant burden during hospitalization. By anticipating language needs and incorporating inclusive design principles throughout the research process, hospitalists can generate more representative evidence to inform equitable care for all children and families, regardless of language.

articles.title: Social Media Asthma Education to Reduce Pediatric Health Care Use: A Bayesian Randomized Control Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Traditional pediatric asthma education is often fragmented and time limited. Social media may provide a more sustained platform for education. We hypothesized that social media-based education (SME) about asthma would reduce health care use the year after asthma hospitalization.
METHODS: In a 2-center Bayesian randomized trial, caregivers of patients aged 3 to 17 years hospitalized for asthma were randomly assigned to social media plus usual care or usual care alone, stratified by age (3-11 vs 12-17 years) and center. The SME group received at least weekly educational post via Facebook and Instagram. The primary outcome was total number of treatment days in a medical setting within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included treatment days across different settings, time to emergency department (ED) revisit or hospital readmission, missed school days, and patient satisfaction. Analyses were conducted using Bayesian generalized linear models with a neutral prior.
RESULTS: Two hundred participants were enrolled. Compared with usual care, SME had a 93% probability of reduced total treatment days (relative risk [RR] 0.80; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.59-1.07) and a 96% probability of decreased unplanned treatment days (RR 0.67; 95% CrI, 0.43-1.05). Mean time to ED revisit was 186 days in controls vs 225 days in the SME arm, with a 92% probability of reduction. Social media participants had longer time to readmission (293 vs 218 days; 81% probability of reduction) and greater satisfaction with education (73% vs 36%) than controls.
CONCLUSIONS: SME was well accepted and likely reduced health care use and delayed posthospitalization ED visits and readmissions compared with usual care.

articles.title: Childhood abuse is linked to poor sleep in adult women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women are disproportionately affected by poor sleep, both in terms of quantity and quality. One relatively unexplored association with poor sleep is adverse childhood experiences, which also disproportionately affect women. Prior research treats all adverse experiences as equivalent, focusing on the number of adverse events rather than the types of adversity experienced. This cumulative focus, while valuable for identifying dose-dependent responses, overlooks how different adversities are detrimental for women's health.
METHODS: We investigated how adversity contributed to sleep issues in a sample of treatment-seeking women (N=350). Survey measures collected participants' demographic information, adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), and sleep quantity and quality. We used cumulative and dimensional person-centered analytic approaches, the latter of which revealed four distinct adversity subgroups and two distinct sleep subgroups.
RESULTS: Women having experienced abuse-related adversity (emotional and/or physical) as well as multiple forms of adversity (high cumulative scores) were more likely to experience worse sleep. Those experiencing abuse experienced sleep issues even when their cumulative adversity scores did not reach clinical thresholds. Women classified within household dysfunction and low cumulative scores did not report deleterious sleep.
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that specific patterns of childhood adversity uniquely contribute to adult sleep issues among women. These women are not captured in cumulative scoring methods, potentially leading to their abuse histories being overlooked in clinical settings. This study underscores the importance of using dimensional approaches to ACE research and highlights the enduring impact of childhood adversity on women's sleep health.

articles.title: Age-stratified sex differences in outcomes after lower extremity fracture fixation: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundOutcomes of open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) of lower extremity fractures vary based on patient sex and age.MethodsWe performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX national research database. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent ORIF of lower extremity fractures, including pelvis and acetabulum, between 2003 and 2023 were identified. We conducted 1:1 propensity score matching (male vs. female) to balance comorbidities, including age, race, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, BMI, osteoporosis, and smoking status. Patients were stratified into age groups (18-39, 40-64, ≥ 65 years). Postoperative outcomes at 90 days and two years were compared using risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals.ResultsOf 204,152 patients, 147,518 remained after matching. Males had significantly higher complication rates than females: deep vein thrombosis, 2.1% vs. 1.5%; pneumonia, 1.5% vs. 1.0%; nonunion requiring surgical treatment, 4.8% vs. 3.5%; and amputation, 1.1% vs. 0.5% (all p<0.001). Males also had higher rates of 90-day emergency department visits (4.6% vs. 3.8%) and readmissions (6.7% vs. 4.6%, p<0.001). These sex disparities were most pronounced in midlife (40-64 years). Conversely, females had higher rates of complex regional pain syndrome across all ages.ConclusionBoth sex and age are predictors of postoperative outcomes following lower extremity ORIF, with the largest sex disparities in patients aged 40-64 and higher CRPS rates in females across all age groups.

articles.title: Designing a culturally responsive digital mental health E-clinic for women and adolescent girls in Jordan: A qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Psychological distress among women and adolescent girls is a public health concern in low- and middle-income settings, where social adversity, stigma, displacement, and health-system constraints can hinder recognition and care. In Jordan, little is known about how healthcare providers recognize and respond to psychological distress within maternal, reproductive, and adolescent health services, or how they perceive culturally responsive digital mental health support. This study explored providers' perspectives, barriers to recognition and response, and the potential role of a digital mental health e-clinic.
METHODS: An interpretivist qualitative design using focus group discussions and in-depth interviews was adopted. A semi-structured guide explored clinical recognition of distress, service constraints, referral pathways, training and role-related challenges, and requirements for digital support. Audio-recorded Arabic data were transcribed verbatim, anonymized, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: The dataset comprised eight focus group discussions and four in-depth interviews. Providers recognized psychological distress through clinical observation, interpersonal cues, and professional experience, particularly during perinatal care. However, limited mental health training, heavy workloads, unclear professional authority, uneven institutional capacity, and fragmented referral pathways constrained assessment, documentation, and action. Participants viewed structured screening as an adjunct to clinical judgement for identifying individuals who may require further assessment and referral, but not as a diagnostic tool. They support digital tools when embedded within functioning care pathways and accompanied by professional training, supportive supervision, clear escalation procedures, confidentiality safeguards, and access to services.
CONCLUSIONS: A culturally responsive digital mental health e-clinic may strengthen recognition, documentation, triage, referral, and continuity of care when integrated with clinical judgement and existing services. Digital tools should complement, not replace, professional assessment or specialist care. Improving mental health care for women and adolescent girls requires coordinated clinical, educational, service-level, and structural responses that address individual needs and wider social conditions contributing to psychological distress.

articles.title: Vaping-Related Pneumomediastinum in Adolescents: Characterizing Work Up and Management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent vaping, including nicotine and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) products, carries numerous adverse effects. Case reports, primarily in young adults, describe an association between inhaled substance use and pneumomediastinum, but management of affected adolescents remains unclear. This study sought to characterize this population and identify variations in practice patterns to improve future care.
METHODS: A single center, retrospective descriptive study with 60-day follow-up was conducted. The hospital's radiology database was searched for imaging studies noting "pneumomediastinum" in patients >10 and 18 years from January 2014-May 2025. Patients with pneumomediastinum secondary to another etiology (ex: trauma, recent surgery) were excluded. Those reporting recent inhaled substance use were included.
RESULTS: Forty-one adolescents met inclusion criteria. Median age at symptom onset was 16 years (range 14-18 years). Nicotine and THC vaping were reported in 73.2% and 78.0% of patients, respectively, with >50% using daily. Hospital admission occurred in 68.3% of cases with median length of stay of 2 days (IQR 1, 3). Three patients required intensive care unit admission, one of whom was hypoxic and obtunded at presentation necessitating intubation. Admitted patients underwent more chest radiographs than those discharged from the emergency department (median 2 vs 1, p=0.027). Nineteen patients underwent esophagram, none demonstrating injury. No interventions were required and no patient experienced recurrence during follow up.
CONCLUSION: Management of vaping-related pneumomediastinum in adolescents, notably the use of imaging, varies considerably. Most patients may not require admission or transfer to a specialized pediatric facility unless presenting with hypoxia or respiratory distress.

articles.title: Prognostic Utility of the Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis in Infants: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score was developed in adults, but its prognostic utility in children remains uncertain. This study evaluated the conventional admission LRINEC threshold of ≥6 for predicting adverse clinical outcomes in infants with necrotizing fasciitis.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 93 infants with clinically diagnosed necrotizing fasciitis at a tertiary pediatric surgical center between February 2021 and August 2023. Admission LRINEC scores were categorized as <6 or ≥6. The primary endpoint was a composite of unplanned repeat surgical debridement for persistent or progressive infection, hospitalization exceeding 21 days, worsening sepsis, or in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: The mean age was 187.9 ± 96.6 days. Composite adverse outcomes occurred in 77 infants (82.8%), and seven (7.5%) died. Unplanned repeat debridement was required in 43 patients (46.2%). Among infants with LRINEC ≥6, 19/20 (95.0%) experienced an adverse outcome, compared with 58/73 (79.5%) with LRINEC <6. Sensitivity was 24.7% (95% CI, 16.4%-35.4%) and specificity was 93.8% (95% CI, 71.7%-98.9%). Positive and negative predictive values were 95.0% and 20.5%, respectively. The association was not statistically significant (risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.95-1.40; P = 0.178). Overall, 75.3% of adverse outcomes occurred among infants with LRINEC <6.
CONCLUSIONS: The conventional LRINEC threshold demonstrated poor sensitivity for adverse clinical outcomes in infants with necrotizing fasciitis. A low score should not provide prognostic reassurance or replace clinical assessment. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate pediatric-specific prognostic tools.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III - Prospective observational cohort study.

articles.title: Patient-Specific Auricular Prosthetic Rehabilitation in Bilateral Microtia Using a Hybrid Digital Workflow: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: There are several types of congenital auricular deformities that can cause facial asymmetry and cosmetic concerns as well as psychological concerns as children and adolescents grow. One of the many options for treatment of congenital auricular defects is surgical reconstruction of the auricle. However, many patients with auricular defects are presented with the option of surgical reconstruction and decline and opt for non-surgical auricular prostheses instead. This report describes a 10-year-old girl with bilateral microtia but a more severe right auricular defect. The right ear was smaller and more severely deformed, whereas the left ear was less deformed and larger than its counterpart. The comparatively better-developed but hypoplastic left auricle served as the patient-specific reference for rehabilitation of the more severely affected right side. The defect and contralateral ear were digitized using a desktop scanner, followed by digital mirroring, model refinement, and stereolithographic 3D printing. The printed auricular template was used to fabricate a wax pattern, which was clinically adjusted before processing the definitive prosthesis in room-temperature vulcanizing silicone. The prosthesis engaged the existing loop deformity of the posterior helix, with supplemental retention provided by a medical adhesive. At the 3-month follow-up, the prosthesis showed satisfactory retention and acceptable marginal adaptation, with no clinically apparent color change or peri-auricular tissue reaction during this short-term observation period. The present case illustrates the short-term clinical feasibility of a hybrid digital-conventional workflow for fabricating a patient-specific auricular prosthesis in a pediatric patient who declined surgical reconstruction.

articles.title: Severe Fetal Anemia and Pancytopenia in Maternal Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Treated with Serial Intrauterine Transfusions and Intravenous Immunoglobulin: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Severe fetal anemia with hydrops and multilineage cytopenia is rarely reported in pregnancies complicated by maternal systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We report a 33-year-old woman with SLE and maternal thrombocytopenia whose fetus developed hydrops and an MCA-PSV of 1.823 MoM at 24+6 weeks. Fetal sampling before the first intrauterine transfusion (IUT) showed hemoglobin 3.3 g/dL, hematocrit 10.5%, WBC 0.28 × 10³/µL and platelets 17 × 10³/µL. The first IUT at 25+6 weeks corrected the anemia, although profound leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were documented immediately afterward. Repeat sampling immediately before a second IUT at 28+1 weeks showed hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 0.14 × 10³/µL and platelets 26 × 10³/µL. Serial IUTs corrected fetal anemia; maternal IVIG was given empirically because of concern for an additional immune contribution, without proof of immune-mediated cell destruction or an independent IVIG effect. Fetal growth restriction and abnormal Dopplers contributed to delivery at 33+6 weeks. The neonate had normal blood counts without postnatal transfusion. This case highlights the importance of targeted evaluation for fetal anemia when concerning sonographic findings arise in SLE pregnancies.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Bumetanide (NKCC1 Inhibitor) for Core Symptoms in Childrenwith Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis(2020-2026).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bumetanide, a selective inhibitor of the Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻ co-transporter 1 (NKCC1), is hypothesised to restore hyperpolarising γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated inhibition and has been investigated as a disease-modifying therapy for the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Early small randomised controlled trials (RCTs) reported benefits on the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS); however, two large Phase III trials (SIGN-1 and SIGN-2; Fuentes et al., 2023) failed on their primary endpoints. An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, with the search extended from January 2020 to May 2026, was conducted to clarify the efficacy, safety and moderators of effect of bumetanide for core ASD symptoms in children.
METHODS: Seven databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, PsycINFO, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP) were searched from January 2020 to 9 May 2026. A single investigator screened records, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, each step being carried out twice at a separation of several weeks with the second pass made blind to the first. The primary outcome was change in CARS total score. Secondary outcomes included the Social Responsiveness Scale, second edition (SRS-2), the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS), Clinical Global Impression scales and pre-specified safety endpoints. Mean differences (MD) and standardised mean differences (SMD; Hedges' g) were pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, and absolute effects and numbers needed to harm (NNH) were derived for safety outcomes. All numerical data were verified against the primary reports and trial registries. Post hoc analyses examined trial design features, mean change within each arm, and how the trials reported co-occurring conditions and excitation/inhibition-relevant behavioural phenotypes. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to assess certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Ten RCTs (about 1,020 children) were included, of which six (710 children analysed) provided arm-level CARS data. The pooled MD favoured bumetanide (MD -1.27; 95% CI -2.05 to -0.49; I² = 63%; SMD -0.47, 95% CI -0.80 to -0.14) but was well below the minimal clinically important difference of approximately 4.5 points. The four earlier trials gave MD -1.83 (95% CI -2.85 to -0.82; SMD -0.74), whereas the two Phase III trials, whose primary endpoint was the CARS2, gave MD -0.19 (95% CI -1.12 to +0.73; SMD -0.04). Children receiving bumetanide improved by a similar amount in both trial generations (3.43 and 3.57 points); children in the control arms improved by 1.28 points in the earlier trials and 3.38 points in the Phase III trials. Larger trials found smaller mean differences, and age did not significantly modify the effect (p = 0.11). No trial pre-specified attention-deficit/hyperactivity symptoms, impulsivity or seizure frequency as an outcome. Bumetanide increased hypokalaemia (RR 7.77; 95% CI 3.59 to 16.83; NNH 7), polyuria (RR 3.31; 1.47 to 7.43; NNH 4) and serious adverse events (RR 2.25; 1.03 to 4.91; NNH 24). Certainty of evidence was Low for CARS and ranged from Low to High for safety outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Bumetanide produces, at most, a small CARS reduction that falls below clinical meaningfulness in unselected children, is absent in the Phase III trials, and is accompanied by an unfavourable tolerability profile. The difference between trial generations lies in how much the control arms improved rather than in the response to bumetanide, so the earlier positive estimates are not a reliable guide to efficacy. The available data do not, however, allow a clean separation of 'the drug does not work' from 'the trials were not built to detect what the drug does': the endpoint used across the programme is a diagnostic severity instrument with limited sensitivity to the excitation/inhibition-linked behaviours that the mechanism should most plausibly modify, and a machine-learning reanalysis of the Phase III data has since identified cross-validated responder subgroups comprising up to 40% of participants. Current evidence does not support routine clinical use. Future trials should prioritise biomarker-stratified designs with blinded or objective outcome assessment, pre-defined responder criteria and endpoints matched to the proposed mechanism.

articles.title: Primary Treatment of Congenital Aortic Stenosis in Infants: A Comparative Analysis of Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty and Surgical Aortic Commissurotomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) and surgical aortic commissurotomy (SAC) as primary treatment strategies for congenital aortic stenosis in infants during the first year of life.
METHODS: This retrospective two-center cohort study included 89 infants with congenital aortic stenosis treated between April 2015 and June 2025 at two tertiary centers. Patients were divided according to the initial intervention: BAV (n = 39) and SAC (n = 50). The primary endpoint was any repeat intervention on the aortic valve. Secondary endpoints included hospital and late mortality, recurrent hemodynamically significant aortic stenosis, and clinically significant aortic regurgitation. To reduce treatment-selection bias, propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using age, sex, body weight, body surface area, and distal aortic arch Z-score, yielding 33 matched pairs. Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared with the log-rank test. Cox regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for reintervention.
RESULTS: In the matched cohort, both strategies achieved initial technical success with no in-hospital deaths in either group. SAC provided superior early hemodynamic relief, with lower intraoperative peak gradient (21.0 [13.0-31.0] vs 30.0 [20.0-41.0] mm Hg; p = 0.048), lower intraoperative mean gradient (10.5 [8.0-14.0] vs 20.0 [12.0-25.0] mm Hg; p = 0.005), and lower discharge peak and mean gradients (25.0 [18.0-35.0] vs 39.0 [32.0-50.0] mm Hg, p < 0.001; and 15.0 [11.0-22.0] vs 24.0 [15.0-27.0] mm Hg, p = 0.023, respectively). However, SAC was associated with longer procedural duration, longer mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care and hospital stay, and greater need for inotropic support. During follow-up, severe aortic regurgitation developed significantly more often after BAV than after SAC (18.7% vs 0%; p = 0.012). Although the rates of reintervention and restenosis did not differ significantly in the matched cohort, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed superior freedom from reintervention after SAC at 45 months (30.5% [95% CI, 15.6%-46.9%] vs 12.3% [95% CI, 2.8%-29.3%]; log-rank p < 0.001). Freedom from restenosis was also higher after SAC (30.5% [95% CI, 15.6%-46.9%] vs 15.4% [95% CI, 3.4%-35.4%]; log-rank p = 0.039). Low body weight at the time of the initial procedure was the only independent predictor of reintervention.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective matched cohort of infants with congenital aortic stenosis, SAC was associated with lower early residual transvalvular gradients and fewer observed cases of severe AR, but required a more invasive procedure and longer postoperative recovery. BAV provided faster recovery and remains an important option, particularly in critically ill or low-weight infants.

articles.title: The impact of childhood obesity on the developing skeleton.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is an increasingly prevalent global health concern associated with significant metabolic, endocrine, and skeletal consequences. During critical periods of growth and peak bone mineralisation, excessive adiposity may impair skeletal development by disrupting bone formation and remodeling. The effects of obesity on bone metabolism are complex and multifactorial, involving altered mechanical loading, hormonal dysregulation, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Key mediators, including insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and disturbances in calcium-phosphate-magnesium-vitamin D homeostasis, contribute to impaired osteoblastic and osteoclastic activity. Additionally, gut microbiome dysbiosis and reduced nutrient absorption may exacerbate skeletal fragility and abnormal mineralisation. This review provides an integrative overview of current evidence regarding the impact of obesity on the developing skeleton. It discusses (I) methods of bone assessment in children with excess body weight and associated diagnostic challenges, (II) biomarkers relevant to bone metabolism and obesity-related skeletal alterations, (III) the role of dietary factors, nutrient intake, and physical activity in bone development, and (IV) future research directions aimed at reducing fracture risk and improving skeletal health outcomes in paediatric populations.

articles.title: Spatial disparity in zero-dose children in India: A multilevel geostatistical analysis using national sample data.
articles.abstract: Children who have not received the first dose of the DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis) vaccine are primarily referred to as zero-dose children and are concentrated in socioeconomically and geographically disadvantaged areas. Most studies have treated these factors as uniform across space, often overlooking the inherent geographical variability in their association. The study aims to explore the spatial distribution, heterogeneity and district-level determinants of zero-dose children across India. We analyzed data from 40,683 children included in the National Family Health Survey (2019-21), spanning 707 districts, considering spatial autocorrelation, hotspot clustering, ordinary least squares (OLS), spatial lag model (SLM), spatial error model (SEM), and geographically weighted regression (GWR), for statistical modeling. The national prevalence of zero-dose children was 6.68%, and hotspots were identified primarily in northeastern and central India. The spatial regression model shows that place of delivery, antenatal care (ANC) visits, maternal media exposure, religious affiliation, and rural residency are key factors significantly associated with zero-dose children, as demonstrated by GWR, which showed the best model fit. These findings urge that India needs multi-dimensional interventions and strategies to tackle zero-dose children. Strengthening maternal healthcare education, improving ANC coverage, enhancing service delivery, and outreach in underserved areas are crucial steps toward equitable immunization coverage. The spatial disparities are also a crucial component in understanding and addressing immunization gaps in India. Tailored, region-specific strategies are essential to reduce the burden of zero-dose children and meet the Immunization Agenda 2030 targets.

articles.title: Leucine exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in maple syrup urine disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic, longitudinal, and treatment-related evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurodevelopmental impairment remains a major long-term complication of maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). Although leucine is a principal neurotoxic metabolite, studies have characterized exposure using clinically distinct measures, including diagnostic or acute peak concentrations and longitudinal indices of metabolic control. We therefore evaluated these exposure patterns separately and examined neurodevelopmental outcomes in the context of early diagnosis and liver transplantation.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to July 26, 2026. A total of 203 records were identified through database searching (63 PubMed/MEDLINE, 58 Scopus, and 82 Web of Science); 46 unique studies were included after deduplication, screening, full-text assessment, and supplementary reference-list searching. Leucine exposure was classified as diagnostic/peak or long-term/mean exposure. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to studies with sufficiently comparable populations, exposure definitions, outcomes, and effect measures. Correlations between long-term/mean leucine and IQ were transformed to Fisher's z, pooled using inverse-variance random-effects weighting with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator of between-study variance, and back-transformed to Pearson's r. Heterogeneous outcomes were synthesized narratively. Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised with JBI tools appropriate to study design.
RESULTS: Four studies (total N = 61) contributed to the long-term/mean leucine-IQ meta-analysis. Higher long-term/mean leucine exposure was associated with lower IQ (pooled r = -0.40, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.05; I2 = 39%; tau2 = 0.056). The 95% prediction interval was -0.77 to 0.17. Leave-one-out analyses identified the small le Roux study as influential; its exclusion yielded r = -0.52 (95% CI -0.70 to -0.27; I2 = 0%). Diagnostic/peak leucine showed a less consistent relationship with later neurodevelopment and was not combined in a single pool. The approximately 200 μmol/L value reported in longitudinal evidence is best interpreted as a study-level treatment-associated target in young children, not a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Newborn screening and early diagnosis were generally associated with more favorable clinical and neurological outcomes. Liver transplantation consistently improved metabolic stability, whereas neurocognitive improvement was variable.
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal leucine exposure appears more consistently associated with neurodevelopmental outcome in MSUD than a single concentration measured at diagnosis or during an acute episode. The findings support early diagnosis and sustained metabolic control while cautioning against interpreting any single leucine value as a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Liver transplantation provides robust metabolic stabilization but may not reverse established cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Does fetal head station affect maternal and neonatal outcomes in second-stage cesarean delivery?
articles.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between digitally assessed fetal head station (FHS) and outcomes of second-stage cesarean delivery (CD).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 418 term singleton second-stage CDs at a tertiary center (2012-2023). FHS was categorized as ≤ 0 or ≥+1 and was assessed before vacuum extraction when attempted. The maternal composite comprised vaginal push assistance, uterine incision extension, hemoglobin decrease > 3 g/dL, transfusion, endometritis, postpartum fever, or rehospitalization; the neonatal composite comprised 5-minute Apgar score < 7 or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Complete-case models adjusted for maternal age, second-stage duration, and fetal head position, with and without failed vacuum.
RESULTS: FHS was ≤ 0 in 276 women and ≥+1 in 142; failed vacuum rates were 13.0 % and 50.7 %, respectively. Maternal composite rates were 71.0 % and 73.2 %; neonatal composite rates were 9.8 % and 16.9 %. With failed vacuum adjustment, adjusted odds ratios (95 % confidence intervals) for FHS ≥+1 were 1.15 (0.62-2.12) for the maternal composite and 1.21 (0.55-2.68) for the neonatal composite. Without failed vacuum adjustment, associations were observed for transfusion (2.46, 1.18-5.12) and cord pH < 7.2 (2.39, 1.19-4.82).
CONCLUSION: Digitally assessed FHS was not significantly associated with the assessed outcomes in full-cohort models including failed vacuum extraction. These findings suggest that the complexity and outcomes of second-stage CD may be influenced by multiple intrapartum factors beyond clinical assessment of FHS alone.

articles.title: Autistic traits and behavioral problems at age 8 after assisted reproductive technology: A Japanese multicenter cohort study of singleton term children born to infertile couples.
articles.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared autism-related traits and behavioral/emotional problems at age 8 among singleton term children born to infertile couples who conceived without IVF or embryo transfer (no-IVF/ET), or by fresh (FreET) or frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET).
METHODS: In a multicenter JISART cohort, 854 children were analyzed (no-IVF/ET, n = 100; FreET, n = 340; FET, n = 414). The main model (Model 2) included 617 children, of whom only 74 were no-IVF/ET comparators. Autism-related traits were assessed using the Autism Spectrum Quotient Children's Version (AQ), and behavioral/emotional problems were assessed using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). Group differences were examined using sex-stratified adjusted analyses, and exploratory threshold analyses used Firth's logistic regression pooling boys and girls.
RESULTS: Among girls, AQ and CBCL scores did not differ significantly between the groups. Among boys, the FreET-no-IVF/ET AQ difference was 3.30 points in Model 1 (Dunnett-adjusted 95 % CI, 0.31-6.29; P = 0.028) and 3.22 points in Model 2 (-0.16 to 6.60; P = 0.063). The AQ scores after FET and CBCL scores in both ART groups did not differ significantly from those in the no-IVF/ET group. The unadjusted threshold proportions did not differ significantly among the groups. In exploratory Firth regression pooling boys and girls, FreET was associated with higher odds of AQ ≥ 25 (OR, 4.18; 95 % CI, 1.22 to 21.79; Holm-adjusted P = 0.041).
CONCLUSIONS: Among term singleton children with available age-8 outcomes, Model 2 showed no significant differences in continuous AQ or CBCL scores between the ART and no-IVF/ET groups. The association between FreET and AQ ≥ 25 is exploratory and requires confirmation.

articles.title: Implementation of the PaliEnf Digital Technology Based on Standardized Nursing Languages to Improve Nursing Documentation in Pediatric Oncology Palliative Care.
articles.abstract: AimTo evaluate the effect of the PaliEnf application on the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care.MethodsThis quasi-experimental study compared pre- and post-intervention periods and was conducted in accordance with the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs (TREND) guidelines in a Pediatric Oncology Intensive Care Unit at a Brazilian national cancer referral center. The intervention consisted of implementing the PaliEnf application, a digital technology structured according to the NANDA International (NANDA-I), Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC), and Nursing Outcomes Classification (NOC) systems. Ten nurses were trained to use the application. The quality of nursing process documentation was assessed before and after the intervention using the Quality of Diagnoses, Interventions and Outcomes (Q-DIO) instrument. Comparisons between periods were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, adopting a significance level of 5%.ResultsA total of 40 medical records were analyzed, including 20 from the pre-intervention period and 20 from the post-intervention period. Significant improvement in nursing process documentation was observed following implementation of the PaliEnf application, with increased scores across all Q-DIO dimensions (p < 0.001). The overall Q-DIO score increased from a median of 16.5 (IQR: 15.75-19.75) to 43.5 (IQR: 41.00-44.25). The greatest improvements were identified in items related to diagnostic structuring, coherence among nursing diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes, and documentation of patients' clinical progress.ConclusionImplementation of the PaliEnf application was associated with significant improvement in the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care. The findings suggest that digital technologies grounded in standardized nursing languages may support structured documentation and improve the internal coherence of the nursing process in complex clinical settings. Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (REBEC): UTN U1111-1297-9546.

articles.title: Enzyme Therapy Discontinuation After Pancreatic Function Recovery in Children With Cystic Fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT) improves outcomes in children with CF (CwCF). We hypothesized that HEMT may restore pancreatic function in children with pancreatic insufficiency (PI) and reduce the need for pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) and reduce treatment burden.
METHODS: In this single-center cohort, CwCF and PI receiving HEMT for > 6 months were offered FE-1 testing as routine care. Post-HEMT FE-1 levels were compared to PI diagnosis values. Demographic and clinical data, including CFTR genotype and sweat chloride, were collected. PERT was discontinued if post-HEMT FE-1 levels were ≥ 200 µg/g. Patients were followed with repeat FE-1 testing, growth assessments, fat-soluble vitamin (FSV) levels, and gastrointestinal (GI) symptom assessment.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients (age 0.4-14.0 years at HEMT start) were included; 62% homozygous for delF508. Ten patients (34%) converted from PI to pancreatic sufficient (PS) after HEMT initiation (mean age 5.5 ± 3.4 y). Nine (90%) discontinued PERT and maintained FE-1 ≥ 200 µg/g over a mean follow-up time 1.5 ± 0.8 y. One patient experienced a transient decline in FE-1, with increased GI symptoms, then recovery of PS. No changes in anthropometric measurements or FSV levels were observed after PERT discontinuation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of CwCF and PI, one-third converted to PS after initiation of HEMT. All patients who discontinued PERT went without adverse nutritional effects. Given fluctuations in FE-1, these findings support reassessment of pancreatic function in children receiving HEMT and continued monitoring after PERT withdrawal to confirm sustained PS and nutritional status.

articles.title: Exploring the Relationship Between CFTR Modulator Therapy, Body Image, and Eating Attitudes in Adolescents With Cystic Fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a vulnerable period for people with cystic fibrosis (CF), marked by nutritional challenges and increased risk of anxiety, depression, disordered eating, and body dissatisfaction. With the widespread use of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapies, adolescents with CF (AwCF) are increasingly achieving healthy weight targets. However, the psychosocial implications of modulator-associated weight gain, particularly regarding body image and emotional well-being, remain poorly understood. This study compared body image, eating-related, and psychological outcomes among AwCF with and without modulator therapy and matched healthy peers.
METHODS: In this prospective case-control study, 84 AwCF (41 CFTR modulator-receiving [MOD-R] and 43 CFTR modulator-non-receiving [MOD-NR]), and 53 healthy controls (HC), completed validated self-report measures assessing body image (BFPP), body esteem (BESAA), eating disorder symptoms (EDE-Q), muscle dysmorphia (MDDI), depression (PHQ-9), and anxiety (STAI).
RESULTS: Body satisfaction was most frequently reported in the MOD-R group, a desire to be larger in the MOD-NR group, and a desire to be thinner in the HC group (p = 0.041). Body image dissatisfaction was significantly lower in AwCF than in healthy peers (p = 0.016), with no differences in body esteem. Both CF groups had significantly lower eating disorder symptom scores and lower depression and trait anxiety (STAI-T) scores than healthy controls (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that AwCF may develop a health-oriented body perception that buffers against sociocultural appearance pressures, regardless of modulator use, potentially reflecting adaptive coping processes and the effects of regular multidisciplinary care.

articles.title: Patterns and Trends in Bronchiolitis and RSV-Associated Hospitalizations in Infants in Israel Prior to Nirsevimab Introduction (2018-2023).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of bronchiolitis and lower respiratory tract infection requiring hospitalization in infancy. We aimed to characterize the epidemiology of bronchiolitis and RSV-associated hospitalizations among infants in Israel before the introduction of universal nirsevimab immunization.
METHODS: Using the Israeli Ministry of Health National Hospital Discharges Database, we retrospectively analyzed bronchiolitis/RSV-associated hospitalizations in infants under 1 year of age nationwide (2018-2023), including rates, age, seasonality, PICU admissions, length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Not all cases were laboratory-confirmed, because testing was incomplete and results available after discharge were not added to the records.
RESULTS: A total of 28,138 bronchiolitis and RSV-associated hospitalizations were identified. Annual hospitalization rates ranged from 25 to 33 per 1000 infants, falling to 12 per 1000 in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Infants aged 1 month accounted for the highest proportion of hospitalizations (21.1%), followed by 2 months (14.4%) and < 1 month (11.4%); 58.7% were male. RSV seasonality was disrupted during the pandemic, with a summer resurgence in 2021, before returning to the typical winter pattern by 2022-2023. Mean hospital stay was 3.7 days, 7%-10% required PICU admission, and in-hospital mortality due to bronchiolitis or RSV-associated disease remained low (0.57 per 1000 hospitalizations).
CONCLUSIONS: Bronchiolitis and RSV-associated disease remained a major cause of infant hospitalization in Israel, particularly during the first months of life. These nationwide data provide a baseline for evaluating the impact of Israel's universal Nirsevimab program, introduced in September 2025, on RSV-related hospitalizations and severity.

articles.title: Biological Proximity Shapes Ecological Correlation Patterns in Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Nationwide Population-Based Administrative Data Study From Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal risk factors for bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) are well characterized in individual-level neonatal cohorts, but whether the population-level administrative burden of BPD co-varies with these determinants over time in a low- or middle-income country remains unclear. Ecological analyses cannot establish individual causation, but they can generate policy-relevant hypotheses when maternal-neonatal linkage is unavailable.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide ecological time-series study using Colombian administrative healthcare data (RIPS/SISPRO) and vital statistics, 2015-2024. Annual administrative prevalence rates were computed for BPD (ICD-10 P27.1) and 18 perinatal conditions using official DANE denominators: population < 1 year for BPD and neonatal conditions, and live births for maternal conditions. Conditions were assigned a priori to three biological-proximity levels: upstream maternal determinants, direct neonatal pathophysiology, and downstream/developmental outcomes.
RESULTS: BPD administrative prevalence rose from 60.3 to 127.6 per 100,000 infants, peaking at 169.9 in 2019 (APC + 6.1%/year; 95% CI + 5.3 to +6.9). Correlation strength followed the hypothesized proximity gradient: direct neonatal pathophysiology (mean ρ = 0.804) > upstream maternal determinants (mean ρ = 0.709) > downstream/developmental outcomes (mean ρ = 0.391). This hierarchy was directionally preserved across Kendall, leave-1-year-out, COVID-exclusion, and detrended analyses, although detrending attenuated several associations, as expected for ecological time-series data. BPD mortality was uncorrelated with administrative prevalence (ρ = 0.21), while the ecological case-fatality ratio fell from 15.6% to 4.3% (p = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: In Colombia, the administrative burden of BPD co-varied with perinatal morbidity in a biologically coherent hierarchy. These findings do not prove individual-level causation, but support integrated perinatal surveillance and the development of linked maternal-neonatal data sets in similar settings.

articles.title: Usability of Hand-Held Devices With an Electrochemical Sensor to Determine Nasal Nitric Oxide in Clinical Routine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasal nitric oxide (nNO) is an established screening tool for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD). Customary chemoluminescence-based analyzers preclude widespread screening for PCD. Portable devices with electrochemical sensors have not been clinically validated.
OBJECTIVE: To compare test success and nNO levels between a chemoluminescence analyzer (CLD88 sp) and a portable device (NIOX MINO) in clinical routine, and to assess whether a tidal breathing velum-closure (TBVC) method increases test success.
METHODS: Measurements were performed in children ≥ 3 years using a conventional single-breath maneuver against an expiratory resistance (ER) for CLD88, and a breath-hold (BH) method for NIOX. TBVC was evaluated for both devices.
RESULTS: One hundred and twenty children referred for investigation of respiratory symptoms were included (median age 9.9 years, range 3.1-18.5). For conventional breathing methods, test success increased from preschool age (CLD88 10% and NIOX 3.3%) to adolescence (87.5% and 65%). TBVC increased test success for both devices (preschoolers 80% and 70% vs. adolescents 97.5% and 97.5%; p < 0.001 for all age groups). Median nNO was higher for CLD88 with 263.3 nL/min (ER) and 283.7 nL/min (TBVC) compared to NIOX with 214.5 nL/min (BH) and 208.1 nL/min (TBVC) (p = 0.013 and p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Test success is low when conventional breathing methods are applied, especially in younger ages, but can be increased by TBVC. Nasal NO levels are lower for electrochemical sensor devices compared to chemoluminescence analyzers with no difference between conventional and TBVC methods. These findings support using portable analyzers with TBVC as a promising tool to screen-out PCD.

articles.title: Telerehabilitation-Based Group and Individual Exercise in People With Cystic Fibrosis: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare the effects of telerehabilitation-based individual and group exercise, against routine treatment on exercise capacity, lung function, muscle strength, anaerobic power, balance, quality of life (QoL), and change in clinical status in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF).
METHODS: Forty-five pwCF (8-18 years) were randomly allocated into three groups: (1) telerehabilitation-based group or (2) telerehabilitation-based individual exercise, and (3) control arm. Telerehabilitation-based groups underwent supervised exercise programmes 3 days/week via an online platform, and the control arm continued their routine care during an 8-week period. Exercise capacity of PwCF was assessed with 6-min walk test and incremental shuttle walk test. Spirometry measurements, muscle, and handgrip strength were recorded and evaluated. Anaerobic power via vertical jump test, balance via TimedUp and GoTest, and quality of life via Pediatric QoL Inventory were assessed as well. Adherence rates to exercise programmes were calculated.
