Change in clinical status for all groups, and motivation and enjoyment in the intervention groups were assessed.
RESULTS: Forty-one participants completed the study. Both exercise groups showed greater improvements than the control group in the 6-min walk distance, incremental shuttle walk test distance, the Timed Up and Go test, vertical jump performance, participant-reported QoL, and most upper- and lower-extremity muscle strength outcomes (all p < 0.05), with no significant differences between the two exercise groups. Significant group × time interactions were also observed for FEV1 and FEV1/FVC. Handgrip strength and parent-reported QoL did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSION: The current study demonstrates similar effects between tele-exercise sessions, with better outcomes than control group. Clinical teams can integrate telerehabilitation-based group exercise into CF centres.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT05590169.

articles.title: Structural Airway Findings and Bronchoalveolar Lavage Microbiology in Children With Bronchiectasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric data integrating bronchoscopic airway findings, computed tomography (CT) morphology, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) microbiology in bronchiectasis remain limited. We aimed to describe these findings and examine their associations.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study with cross-sectional analyses included 86 children with CT-confirmed bronchiectasis unrelated to cystic fibrosis. Flexible bronchoscopy was performed for clinical indications in 43 children, of whom 41 underwent BAL. Bronchoscopic findings, CT morphology, and quantitative BAL cultures were evaluated. Exploratory analyses examined factors associated with purulent secretions and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation.
RESULTS: Mucoid secretions (34/43, 79.1%) and bronchomalacia (13/43, 30.2%) were the most frequent bronchoscopic findings. Annular mucosal folds were documented in seven children (16.3%). Purulent secretions were more frequent in saccular-cystic than in tubular or varicose bronchiectasis (odds ratio, 21.43; 95% confidence interval, 2.15-213.58; p = 0.004). Clinically significant bacterial growth was detected in 31/41 BAL samples (75.6%). Among culture-positive samples, the predominant organisms were Haemophilus influenzae (11/31, 35.5%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (7/31, 22.6%), and Streptococcus pneumoniae (6/31, 19.4%). Neurological disease was more frequent in the Pseudomonas aeruginosa group than in the other culture-positive group (42.9% vs 4.2%; p = 0.027).
CONCLUSION: In this clinically selected subgroup, bronchoscopy and BAL provided additional structural and microbiological information. The association of purulent secretions with saccular-cystic morphology was imprecisely estimated, annular mucosal folds require prospective validation, and the P. aeruginosa finding should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Improving Inhaled Corticosteroid Prescribing Practices for Children Admitted With an Asthma Exacerbation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Asthma management guidelines recommend inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), including as-needed use, to treat airway inflammation, reduce bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and thereby lower the risk of severe exacerbations. Our objective was to achieve a 90% inpatient ICS initiation rate for children hospitalized with an acute asthma exacerbation over a 12-month period. We focused our initiative on hospitalized children to target those at greatest risk of asthma-related morbidity.
METHODS: The Model for Improvement was used to define study aims/measures and create a key driver diagram to guide intervention design. Interventions focused on enhancing ICS access, standardizing workflow, healthcare provider asthma education, and integrating clinical decision support into the electronic health record. We performed serial planned experimentation to test interventions using Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles. Shewhart P-charts and established rules for detecting special cause variation were used to analyze data. Our outcome measure was ICS initiation rate during inpatient hospitalization among children discharged on ICS therapy. Process measures were the percentage of children for whom asthma severity was assessed on admission, and the percentage of children continued on home ICS therapy during admission. The balancing measure was length of stay.
RESULTS: The percentage of children initiated on ICS therapy during admission increased from 16% to 80% over a 12-month period with further improvement reaching 94% 1-year post-intervention. There was no change in length of stay.
CONCLUSION: The availability of a pediatric-appropriate ICS on hospital medication formulary and the initiation of an asthma clinical management pathway were the most impactful interventions to improve ICS prescription for children admitted with an asthma exacerbation.

articles.title: Delayed Liver Test Elevations During Long-Term Elexacaftor/Tezacaftor/Ivacaftor Therapy in Adults With Cystic Fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a labeled risk of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) that most often arises within the first year of therapy; elevations beyond that window are incompletely characterized. We hypothesized that new liver test elevations occur after the first year and are associated with identifiable host- and exposure-related risk factors.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort study of 124 adults with cystic fibrosis (CF) who received ETI for at least 12 months. Delayed liver test (dLT) elevations were defined as elevations occurring more than 12 months after initiation.
RESULTS: Thirty-six patients (29%) developed new alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevations beyond 12 months, of whom 6 (16.7%) had no identifiable alternative contributor and were attributed to ETI. Delayed elevations were associated with male sex (p = 0.04), F508del homozygosity (p = 0.05), prior CF liver disease (p < 0.001), acetaminophen exposure (p = 0.007), and concurrent infection or inflammation (p = 0.002). Six patients had clinically significant elevations exceeding 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN); in these, total bilirubin remained normal and hepatic imaging and elastography identified no alternative etiology, and Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method scoring classified five as "possible" and one as "probable" DILI. ETI dose reduction normalized or stabilized ALT in most, with only modest spirometric change.
CONCLUSIONS: New liver test elevations occurred after the first year of ETI in a substantial minority of adults with CF, and in 16.7% no alternative cause was identified. These findings support continued, risk-informed liver test monitoring beyond the first year.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of older adults who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery for symptomatic Rathke cleft cysts.
articles.abstract: Rathke cleft cysts (RCCs) are benign cystic lesions in the sellar and suprasellar regions that are often asymptomatic but may cause symptoms due to the compression of adjacent structures. With the aging of population, the incidence of symptomatic RCCs in older adults is increasing. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, and follow-up between older and younger adult patients systematically. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for RCCs at a single center from 2011 to 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: nonelderly (18-59 years) and elderly (≥ 60 years). A total of 153 patients were analyzed, with 120 younger and 33 older adult patients. Older adults presented more frequently with dizziness and fatigue. The elderly group had a shorter operation time, whereas the other surgical outcomes were similar between the two groups. The incidences of perioperative diabetes insipidus and mortality during follow-up were significantly higher in the elderly group. The recurrence rate was also higher, but no significant difference was observed. In multivariable Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, older age (adjusted SHR: 3.99, 95% CI: 1.45-11.00, p = 0.007) and cyst location, including both suprasellar (adjusted SHR: 12.70, 95% CI: 1.39-115.00, p = 0.024) and sellar-suprasellar extension (adjusted SHR: 8.67, 95% CI: 1.09-68.70, p = 0.041; vs. sellar), were associated with recurrence, whereas preoperative hypopituitarism was not (adjusted SHR: 2.20, 95% CI: 0.76-6.36, p = 0.200). EES is safe and effective for elderly patients with symptomatic RCCs. Elderly patients often present with atypical symptoms, leading to a delayed diagnosis. RCCs seem to be more likely to recur in older patients than in younger adults; thus, more careful monitoring and longer follow-up period is needed on the older adults.

articles.title: Subclinical Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Among Emergency Department Patients With Elevated Blood Pressure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet early detection of target organ damage is often missed, particularly in patients with limited access to care. The Emergency Department (ED), a key site of care for underserved populations, may offer an opportunity for risk stratification; we sought to determine the prevalence of LVH-a marker of subclinical disease and increased cardiovascular risk-among ED patients with asymptomatic elevated blood pressure and assess differences by sex, race, and insurance status.
METHODS: We enrolled a convenience sample of adults aged 18-65 years presenting to an academic ED with blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg systolic or ≥ 90 mmHg diastolic on two measurements. Subjects with prior LVH, active cardiac disease, hypertensive emergency, dialysis dependence, or pregnancy were excluded. LVH was identified using left ventricular mass indexed to height2.7 or body surface area via focused (point-of-care) cardiac ultrasound (parasternal long-axis view). Multivariate logistic regression assessed associations with LVH.
RESULTS: Among 155 subjects, 46 (29.7%, 95% CI 22.5%-36.9%) had LVH. Mean age was 46.9 ± 12.1 years; 53.6% were women. LVH was more prevalent in women (38.6% vs. 19.4%; p = 0.009) and remained independently associated with female sex (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.14-5.22, p = 0.021) and prior hypertension (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.14-5.39, p = 0.023). Notably, 18.3% of patients without a prior hypertension diagnosis demonstrated LVH (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: Nearly one-third of ED patients with elevated blood pressure had LVH, including many without known hypertension, with a higher prevalence among women.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05730309.

articles.title: Factors associated with post-tonsillectomy secondary hemorrhage: A retrospective study of 3289 patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To determine the epidemiological characteristics of post-tonsillectomy secondary hemorrhage (PTSH) across different age groups and to explore factors associated with PTSH in a large Asian cohort.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted on 3289 consecutive patients who underwent tonsillectomy from March 2015 to March 2025. PTSH was defined as bleeding occurring ≥24 h postoperatively requiring medical intervention. Only univariable analyses (chi-square or Fisher's exact test) were performed; therefore, all findings are reported as associations rather than independent effects.
RESULTS: The overall PTSH incidence was 1.73% (57/3289). Age was associated with PTSH (P < 0.001), with the highest bleeding rates in adolescents (13-17 years, 3.82%) and young adults (18-44 years, 3.38%). Surgeon volume was associated with PTSH (P < 0.001): the low-volume group (≤50 cases) had a 3.18% bleeding rate versus 0.83% in the high-volume group (>200 cases). Infectious-hypertrophic lesions had the highest bleeding rate (3.73%, P = 0.007). In adults (≥18 years, n = 1067), high BMI, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes were each associated with higher bleeding rates (all P < 0.05). Two cases of pseudoaneurysm were successfully managed via interventional embolization.
CONCLUSION: Low surgeon volume, infectious-hypertrophic lesions, high BMI, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus were factors associated with PTSH in univariable analysis. Adolescent and young adult males may warrant closer perioperative attention; this subgroup analysis was exploratory. Clinically, perioperative risk assessment should be strengthened, surgical training standardized, and vigilance maintained for serious complications such as pseudoaneurysm.

articles.title: Distinct predictors of sleep timing and sleep problems in infants and young toddlers: The role of parental chronotype, sleep quality, and psychological distress.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child sleep timing and perceived sleep problems may have different family-level correlates. We examined associations of maternal and paternal chronotype, sleep quality, psychological distress, maternal sleep-related cognitions, and paternal involvement in infant care with infant and young toddler sleep timing and perceived sleep-problem severity.
METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study included 107 mother-father-child triads aged 6-18 months. Child sleep was evaluated using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised. Sleep midpoint was calculated as a measure of child sleep timing, and perceived sleep-problem severity was assessed on a 1-5 ordinal scale. Both parents completed measures of chronotype, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), anxiety, and depressive symptoms; maternal sleep-related cognitions and paternal involvement were also assessed. Multiple linear and ordinal logistic regression models evaluated associations with the two outcomes.
RESULTS: Greater maternal morningness was independently associated with an earlier child sleep midpoint, including after adjustment for child age (B = -0.051, 95% CI -0.075 to -0.026; p < 0.001). In the combined ordinal model, poorer maternal sleep quality was the only factor independently associated with greater perceived sleep-problem severity (aOR = 1.28 per PSQI point, 95% CI 1.12-1.46; p < 0.001). No paternal variable was independently associated with either outcome in the adjusted models. Child sleep midpoint was not associated with sleep-problem severity (Spearman's ρ = -0.088, p = 0.369).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal chronotype was associated with infant and young child sleep timing, whereas maternal sleep quality was associated with perceived child sleep-problem severity. These findings suggest that child sleep timing and sleep problems may represent distinct dimensions of sleep in infants and young toddlers.

articles.title: Through tired eyes: Self-reported sleepiness and sleep patterns of children with and without ADHD.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIM: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is common among children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) but is frequently under-recognised, with most paediatric sleep research relying on parent-report or objective measures that cannot capture the child's subjective experience of sleepiness. This study examined self-reported EDS and sleep patterns in Australian primary school-aged children with and without ADHD and examined whether the inattentive (ADHD-I) and combined (ADHD-C) presentations show distinct sleep profiles.
METHODS: Two hundred and seventy-three children aged 7-12 years (typically developing [TD], n = 131; ADHD-I, n = 57; ADHD-C, n = 85) completed the Children's Report of Sleep Patterns-Sleepiness Scale and a modified Children's Report of Sleep Patterns self-reported deriving measures of daytime sleepiness and sleep habits, with group differences examined.
RESULTS: Children with ADHD-C took significantly longer to fall asleep and were more likely to use nighttime medication than TD children and woke more frequently overnight than children with ADHD-I. Children with ADHD-C also reported increased amount of sleepiness than TD children, an effect that approached significance. Children with ADHD-I reported significantly higher sleepiness at school than TD children and rated themselves less positively as sleepers than TD children, despite no significant differences in other self-reported sleep variables.
CONCLUSION: Children with ADHD-C and ADHD-I did not differ significantly in overall sleepiness, but differences emerged in specific domains, including longer sleep onset latency and increased nighttime medication use in ADHD-C as well as increased sleepiness at school for children with ADHD-I. A trend also emerged toward poorer self-rated sleeper status in children with ADHD-I without corresponding differences in other self-reported sleep variables. These findings support routine sleep screening in ADHD and the clinical value of asking children directly about their own sleep experience.

articles.title: Disease severity and treatment associations in narcolepsy type 1: a real-world long-term prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The long-term disease severity of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) under routine treatment is insufficiently characterised. In a real-world setting, we examined disease severity changes from unmedicated baseline to medicated follow-up in a large NT1 cohort.
METHODS: We assessed 130 children and adults with NT1 twice (unmedicated baseline; follow-up under routine treatment (92.3% medicated); mean 5.5 years apart). Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Stanford Sleep Questionnaire, polysomnography, multiple sleep latency test (MSLT), and BMI were assessed. Baseline and follow-up were compared, stratified by ± sodium oxybate use. Additionally, adjusted regression models examined associations between disease severity and age, sex, disease duration, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) hypocretin-1, and medication categories (wake-promoting, antidepressants, sodium oxybate), including sex/age-by-medication interactions.
RESULTS: From baseline to follow-up, ESS, REM-related symptom frequency and number of sleep-onset REM periods (SOREMPs) decreased; MSLT mean sleep latency (MSL) increased (all p < 0.01). Nocturnal sleep fragmentation and adult BMI increased only in sodium oxybate non-users. In regression models, baseline severity significantly predicted follow-up severity for nearly all corresponding outcomes and at both timepoints, female sex was persistently associated with higher ESS and more frequent cataplexy, younger age with more MSLT SOREMPs, and undetectable hypocretin-1 (<40 pg/ml) with shorter MSL. Further, the association between sodium oxybate and MSL differed by sex.
CONCLUSION: In a real-world setting, overall NT1 disease severity improved from unmedicated baseline to medicated follow-up, with most favourable trajectories in sodium oxybate users. Despite medication, baseline severity predicted follow-up severity, and female sex, younger age, and undetectable CSF hypocretin-1 deficiency were associated with greater severity at both timepoints. Our findings highlight that substantial improvements under routine treatment coexist with long-term persistent differences in disease severity. This underlines heterogeneity of NT1 trajectories and the importance of considering treatment as well as sex, age, and hypocretin deficiency in the long-term clinical management of NT1.

articles.title: Longitudinal associations between infant parenting and toddler sleep: Examining the moderating role of infant regulation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early-life sleep has lasting health effects, with caregivers playing a central role in its development. Parenting is associated with sleep duration and quality during both infancy and toddlerhood. Less is known about longitudinal associations from infancy into toddlerhood.
METHODS: The current analysis evaluated parenting routine, nurturance, and anxiety at age seven months as predictors of child sleep duration and sleep problems at ages 18-24 months, along with moderation by infant regulation at seven months. Participants were 66 first-time parents (Mage = 30.8 years, 60.9% White, 97% mothers).
RESULTS: Tests of associations between infant parenting and toddler sleep were non-significant. However, the interaction between infant parenting routine and infant regulation in the prediction of toddler sleep duration was significant (p = .00405). At low levels of infant regulation, lower levels of routine predicted shorter sleep, while higher levels of routine predicted longer sleep. The opposite relation was observed at high levels of infant regulation.
CONCLUSIONS: At low levels of infant regulation, parents who reported using more routines in infancy had toddlers with longer sleep duration. At high levels of infant regulation, parents who reported using more routines in infancy had toddlers with shorter sleep duration. This finding is novel but will need to be replicated in larger, more diverse samples. Further exploration of infant temperament and parent-infant interactive effects are warranted to better understand implications for early life sleep.

articles.title: Ryan House: Sharing 15 Years of Inpatient Pediatric Respite and Hospice Experience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundA 2021 UNICEF report estimates that nearly 240 million children live with disabilities globally, including children with medical complexity (CMC). In the United States, over 2 million children have complex medical needs requiring around-the-clock care, creating significant physical, emotional, and financial burdens for their families.ObjectiveTo describe the organizational structure, financial support, medical staffing model, and patient demographics of Ryan House, aiming to establish its framework as a global standard that can be adapted to support communities worldwide.Setting & InterventionRyan House is one of only 3 inpatient pediatric facilities in the United States offering dedicated respite and palliative hospice services for CMC. The facility provides a flexible, community-based care model designed to extend support from clinical settings into the home life of families.ResultsDuring its 15 years of operation, Ryan House has served over 1100 patients and families, delivering more than 24 000 days of care. The manuscript details the specific operational, staffing, and funding structures that enabled this level of service delivery.ConclusionRyan House represents a unique and critical resource for families caring for CMC. Its operational model offers a scalable and adaptable framework that can be implemented globally to alleviate caregiving burdens and improve quality of life for complex pediatric populations.

articles.title: The Effect of Care Team Composition on Healthcare Resource Use Among Rural Children Enrolled in Hospice.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the effect of care team composition on healthcare resource use among rural children enrolled in hospice during the last year of life.MethodsThe sample included 3131 children aged 20 years or younger who received concurrent hospice care, resided in rural communities in 28 Midwestern and Southern states, and were enrolled in Medicaid between 2011 and 2022. Analyses used multivariable logistic and Poisson regression models adjusted for demographic, health, and community characteristics and year of data collection.ResultsChildren had a mean age of 10.1 years (SD = 7.1); 42.1% received care from a medical subspecialist, 52.5% from a primary care provider, and the mean care team size was 9.1 providers (SD = 17.0). Multiple hospital admissions occurred in 80.3% of children, multiple ED visits in 40.4%, and children averaged 1.2 duplicate medications (SD = 0.90). Subspecialist involvement was associated with lower resource use: 69% lower odds of multiple admissions, 83% lower odds of multiple ED visits, and a 37% lower rate of duplicate medications. In contrast, primary care involvement and larger care team size were associated with significantly greater resource use, particularly ED visits and medication utilization.ConclusionCare team composition was significantly associated with healthcare use among rural children enrolled in hospice. Future research should examine the specific mechanisms through which care team composition influences healthcare use.

articles.title: Cigarette smoking in Canadian adolescents: A cross-sectional examination of psychosocial determinants.
articles.abstract: Tobacco cigarette smoking is often initiated during adolescence. Although rates of cigarette smoking have declined in the past decades, some Canadian adolescents still engage in this behaviour despite its widely known health risks. It is important to understand the predictors of cigarette smoking in a contemporary context. Psychosocial factors associated with cigarette smoking behaviours among Canadian adolescents are examined. # Methods This study used a population-based dataset of 23,732 Canadian adolescents in grades 6-10 who completed the 2022 cycle of the Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) Survey. Bivariate analysis and sequential multiple logistic regression models were utilized to assess adolescents' odds of having ever smoked cigarettes in relation to a range of psychosocial predictor variables. # Results Among the participants, 7.5% reported having ever smoked cigarettes. The fully specified models showed significant associations between cigarette smoking and other substance use (vaping: Odds Ratio=26.3, alcohol: Odds Ratio = 4.7) and higher friend support (Odds Ratio = 1.1), indicating that these were predictors of cigarette smoking, when holding other factors constant. Higher relative family affluence (Odds Ratio = 0.6), having higher family support (Odds Ratio=0.9), and higher teacher support (Odds Ratio = 0.8) were significantly associated with reduced odds of cigarette smoking. # Conclusion Other substance use was a significant predictor for increased odds of smoking. Some factors that were associated with reduced odds were identified, including family and teacher support. These findings can inform future research that seeks to examine the mechanisms underlying these associations.

articles.title: Adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health services in Asia-Pacific settings: a systematic scoping review.
articles.abstract: In the Asia-Pacific region, adolescents face significant impacts from unintended pregnancy and are disproportionately affected by the growing HIV epidemic. Despite decades of policy commitments, adolescents have high unmet need for sexual and reproductive health services. The World Health Organization's 2015 global standards for quality adolescent health services provide a framework, but evidence of their implementation in the region remains limited. This systematic scoping review mapped approaches to adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health service delivery in Asia-Pacific low- and middle-income countries and factors influencing implementation. On 6 January 2026, three databases (Medline, Embase and Scopus) were searched for peer-reviewed literature published between January 2019 and December 2025. In line with scoping review methodology, methodological quality was not assessed. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning nine South and Southeast Asian countries; none were from Pacific Island countries. The most evidence was available for Standards 1, 3 and 5. Where studies reported on equity and non-discrimination (Standard 6), and providers' competencies (Standard 4), they described shortfalls, although evidence on competencies was mixed. Few studies reported on community support, data and quality improvement, or adolescents' participation (Standards 2, 7 and 8), reflecting limited available evidence. These findings underscore priorities for investment in adolescent health. More comprehensive, adolescent-centred sexual and reproductive health services and action on stigma are needed, with adolescent engagement and co-leadership central to this shift. Self-care may complement formal health systems, although evidence of its effectiveness in the region remains limited.

articles.title: The impact of a co-designed PrEP referral directory on PrEP continuation among migrant female sex workers in Kisii County, Kenya.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Kenya, female sex workers (FSWs) are disproportionately burdened with HIV compared with the general population. Low continuation of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among FSWs, driven by temporary or permanent migration from safe spaces, heightens their risk of HIV acquisition and transmission, as many do not know where to access PrEP in new locations. We evaluated the impact of a PrEP referral directory in enhancing PrEP continuation among young migrant FSWs.
METHODS: We adopted a pre-post study design, with PrEP continuation as the primary outcome. Health facilities offering PrEP in common migration destinations were mapped. FSWs aged 18-24 years were randomly selected from a safe space register, enrolled, and provided with a co-designed PrEP referral directory listing PrEP-offering facilities. Participants were encouraged to call, or text prior to migrating to facilitate early linkage to services. Phone-based follow-up interviews and facility records were used to assess continuation, comparing pre- and post-intervention periods.
RESULTS: We enrolled 299 participants: mean age was 22 years; 12 out of 299 had no formal education, 163 out of 299 had primary education and 239 out of 299 were single. Migration was the main barrier to continuation (48.1%), with 28.4% migrating twice and 23.7% three times monthly. Post-intervention, 68.2% obtained PrEP refills at linked facilities, with 96.0% citing the directory as the main facilitator. PrEP continuation increased from 17.6% pre-intervention to 41.3% post-intervention (P < 0.001). Monthly continuation rose significantly: 11% versus 40% (OR 5.1, 95% CI: 2.47-11.89) in Month 1; 20% versus 38% (OR 2.5, 95% CI: 1.36-4.96) in Month 2; 22% versus 43% (OR 2.4, 95% CI: 1.38-4.49) in Month 3; 19% versus 47% in Month 4 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 2.04-8.11); 17% versus 43% in Month 5 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 1.98-8.41); and 17% versus 37% in Month 6 (OR 2.8, 95% CI: 1.48-5.55). All comparisons were statistically significant (P < 0.001 for Months 1, 4 and 5; P = 0.002 for Month 2, P = 0.0013 for Month 3 and P = 0.0008 for Month 6).
CONCLUSION: The PrEP referral directory significantly improved PrEP continuation among migrating FSWs. Integrating such mobility-responsive tools into PrEP programming could strengthen PrEP continuation among mobile key populations.

articles.title: Non-invasive physiotherapy interventions for autistic children and adolescents using the F-words Lens Tool: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To map non-invasive physiotherapy interventions for individuals with autism spectrum disorder, using the F-words Lens Tool to summarize the main components of these interventions.
METHOD: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PEDro, Embase, the Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus for studies published between 2001 and 2026 involving autistic children and adolescents. Intervention components were analysed using the Rehabilitation Treatment Specification System and linked to the F-words through the F-words Lens Tool framework. The review was co-developed with patient and public involvement.
RESULTS: Forty-eight studies were included. Most interventions were delivered by physiotherapists (71%), whereas 29% were interdisciplinary. Twenty-eight distinct interventions were identified, with ingredients covering five F-words domains: Functioning (e.g. structured and repetitive motor task practice; 67.96%); Fitness (e.g. aerobic and resistance exercises; 60.7%); Friends (e.g. group activities and facilitation of social interaction; 35.71%), Family (e.g. parent training and adaptation of routines; 20.8%); and Fun (e.g. meaningful and motivating activities; 14.3%). No components related to the Future domain were identified.
INTERPRETATION: Interventions mainly focused on functioning and fitness, with limited attention to the Future domain. The F-words Lens Tool helped identify important gaps and support more comprehensive, person-centred approaches.

articles.title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
articles.abstract: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

articles.title: Epidemiologic profile of self-reported drug allergy in a sample of adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported drug allergy (SRDA) continues to be a major global public health problem, particularly among adult females.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the epidemiologic profile of SRDA in adolescent females aged 13-19 years with dysmenorrhea.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: In this cross-sectional study, data of 821 participants were analyzed. The data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire. The diagnosis of allergic disease was established with self-reported information provided by participants, without performing laboratory tests or physical examination.
RESULTS: The mean age of adolescent females was 17.8 ± 0.7 years. The mean age at the onset of menarche was approximately 11.8 ± 1.4 years; moreover, 59.3% of the participants experienced regular menstruations, but 72.0% suffered from dysmenorrhea. A total of 83 (10.1%) adolescent females reported having SRDA; of these, 23 participants (27.7%) reported being allergic to more than two medications; moreover, the age at the onset of SRDA was 10.7 ± 6.6 years. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that allergic rhinitis, consumption of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and recommended use of NSAIDs by mothers were associated with SRDA. Allergic rhinitis and consumption of NSAIDs without prescription were associated with SRDA in adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
CONCLUSION: It is important that parents understand the adverse effects that these medications generate if used without professional supervision. Healthcare professionals should be better trained to identify adolescent females with greater susceptibility to reporting SRDA.

articles.title: Laryngeal involvement in chronic spontaneous urticaria-associated angioedema: Is there a genuine risk?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) affects up to 1% of the population, and 40% of patients develop concomitant angioedema (CSU-AE). While clinically significant laryngeal involvement in mast cell-mediated CSU-AE is considered rare, and large cohorts report no fatal airway compromise, patients frequently present to emergency departments with symptoms perceived as potentially airway affecting.
OBJECTIVE: To describe retrospective clinical observations of CSU-AE patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of upper airway involvement and to contextualize these findings within the existing literature.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective descriptive review of consecutive CSU patients evaluated between October 2017 and July 2018 at two tertiary referral centers (Milan, Italy and Sofia, Bulgaria). Medical records were screened for angioedema localization, history of physician-documented laryngeal involvement during emergency evaluations, history of airway interventions, medication exposure, and acute treatment response.
RESULTS: Among 1,098 patients, 530 (48%) experienced angioedema and wheals in the context of CSU-AE. Thirteen patients (2%) had objectively documented laryngeal involvement prompting emergency assessment; three patients (all female) underwent endotracheal intubation. No fatalities or loss of consciousness occurred. None had concurrent wheals during the reported laryngeal episodes. History of NSAID exposure preceded some laryngeal exacerbations, though not in intubated cases. None of the patients was receiving ACE inhibitor treatment, all had normal C1 inhibitor (antigen and function) and normal C4. Laryngeal symptoms resolved within hours following standard acute therapy with corticosteroids and/or antihistamines (AHs). Due to the retrospective design, diagnostic work-up for alternative angioedema mechanisms (genetic testing) was incomplete.
CONCLUSIONS: These observations do not indicate an increased intrinsic airway risk in CSU-AE. Rather, they illustrate diagnostic and management challenges in emergency settings and highlight the importance of mechanism-aware clinical assessment to avoid unnecessary invasive airway interventions. Laryngeal angioedema in CSU-AE is rare and presents with a mild clinical phenotype that does not typically require airway intervention.

articles.title: Antibiotic allergy labels in children attending a tertiary paediatric allergy clinic: prevalence, clinical phenotypes and delabelling outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic allergy labels are common in children, although many are assigned on the basis of clinical history and are not confirmed following specialist evaluation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of suspected antibiotic allergy labels and to describe implicated antibiotics, reaction phenotypes, temporal trends, atopic comorbidities and oral drug provocation (ODP) outcomes among children attending a tertiary paediatric allergy clinic.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational study of children aged 0-17 years attending a tertiary paediatric allergy outpatient clinic in Athens, Greece, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data on reported antibiotic allergy, implicated agents, reaction phenotypes, atopic comorbidities and ODP outcomes were extracted from specialist clinical records.
RESULTS: Among 742 outpatient visits representing 569 unique children, 57 visits (7.7%; 95% CI 6.0-9.8) and 55 children (9.7%) carried a suspected antibiotic allergy label. Label prevalence declined from 10.7% in 2023 to 4.7% in 2025. Aminopenicillins accounted for 77.4% of implicated antibiotic entries, with amoxicillin-clavulanate being the most frequently implicated agent. Delayed cutaneous reactions predominated (81.0%), whereas immediate reactions were uncommon (10.3%). Among 56 completed ODP assessments, 52 (92.9%) demonstrated tolerance, including 44/47 delayed cutaneous reactions, 5/6 immediate reactions and all three challenged serum sickness-like reactions.
CONCLUSION: In this tertiary paediatric allergy cohort, reported antibiotic allergy predominantly reflected histories of non-severe beta-lactam reactions and was infrequently confirmed following specialist evaluation. These findings support careful clinical assessment and structured risk stratification, with ODP performed by experienced specialists in appropriately selected children as part of antibiotic allergy delabelling pathways.

articles.title: Association of sleep disturbances with poor asthma control in children: Unveiling a hidden burden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a prevalent chronic condition in children and has been associated with sleep disturbances. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of sleep disturbances in children with asthma and to identify the clinical predictors of impaired sleep quality.
METHODS: The study included children aged 6-16 years with asthma who were followed at the Pediatric Allergy and Immunology Department of Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. A control group of participants with comparable age and demographic characteristics and without any history of chronic, allergic, or psychiatric conditions was also recruited. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC), while asthma control was evaluated using the Childhood Asthma Control Test (C-ACT) or ACT. Asthma severity and treatment steps were categorized according to the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA).
RESULTS: A total of 210 children diagnosed with asthma (mean age: 11.2 ± 3.4 years; 54.3% male) were included in the study. According to the SDSC, 45.2% of children with asthma had clinically significant sleep disturbances. Compared to healthy controls (n = 199), asthmatic children had significantly higher total SDSC scores [63 (IQR: 50-74) vs. 53 (46-61); p < 0.001] and all subscale scores (p < 0.001). Among asthmatic children, poor asthma control, GINA Step ≥3 treatment, and asthma exacerbations within the last six months were significantly associated with sleep disturbances. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, ACT/C-ACT scores were identified as independent predictors of sleep disturbance, with higher scores associated with lower odds of sleep disturbance (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.35; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Poor asthma control was strongly associated with sleep impairment. Routine assessment of sleep quality could support asthma management in pediatric populations.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and treatment response of Eosinophilic Esophagitis in pediatric patients: A descriptive study in a tertiary care institution in Cali, Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic immune-mediated esophageal disease with increasing incidence worldwide, although pediatric data from Latin America remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal descriptive study including patients aged 0-18 years diagnosed with EoE between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary referral center in Colombia. Diagnosis was based on compatible clinical manifestations and histologic confirmation on esophageal biopsy. Demographic, clinical, histologic, and allergen sensitization profiles, as well as treatment response and endoscopic follow-up, were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Seventy-five patients were included, with a median age of 10 years, and 65% were male. The most frequent symptoms were persistent gastroesophageal reflux (53%), recurrent abdominal pain (51%), and vomiting (32%). Allergic comorbidities were frequent, predominantly allergic rhinitis and asthma. Among patients who underwent follow-up endoscopy (68%), clinical and histologic remission were observed in 59% and 39%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: This pediatric cohort demonstrated a substantial atopic burden and a heterogeneous therapeutic response. The discordance between clinical and histologic remission underscores the importance of structured endoscopic follow-up. These findings provide region-specific data that may inform multidisciplinary management strategies in pediatric EoE.

articles.title: High prevalence of hypovitaminosis D in Mexican children with atopic dermatitis: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D has been implicated in epidermal barrier function and immune regulation, but its clinical relevance in pediatric atopic dermatitis (AD) remains uncertain. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency in Mexican children with AD and to explore its association with disease severity in a tertiary-care setting. Patients aged 6 months to 17 years evaluated between January 2022 and January 2023 were included if they had a diagnosis of AD and an available serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D measurement. Disease severity was assessed using the SCORing Atopic Dermatitis index. A total of 423 patients were analyzed; 223 (52.7%) had mild disease, 178 (42.1%) had moderate disease, and 22 (5.2%) had severe disease. Only 23 patients (5.4%) had sufficient vitamin D levels, whereas 273 (64.5%) had insufficiency and 127 (30.0%) had deficiency. The distribution of categorical vitamin D status did not differ significantly across severity strata. Serum vitamin D levels differed modestly across severity groups, with the lowest mean concentration observed in severe disease. In the full cohort, serum vitamin D levels were not independently associated with SCORAD after age adjustment. In an exploratory analysis restricted to moderate-to-severe disease, lower vitamin D levels were associated with higher SCORAD values. Hypovitaminosis D was highly prevalent in this Mexican pediatric cohort with AD. Its relationship with disease severity appears nonuniform and should be interpreted cautiously in light of the cross-sectional design.

articles.title: Barriers to Implementing Sleep Interventions for Children With Autism: Malaysian Occupational Therapists' Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Implementing sleep interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder remains challenging. This study identified barriers faced by Malaysian pediatric occupational therapists. A convergent mixed-methods design integrated quantitative survey data from 112 occupational therapists with qualitative data from two focus group discussions (N = 10). Two major barriers emerged: (a) inadequate formal training and knowledge gaps regarding evidence-based sleep management, reported by 76.8% and 67.0% of survey respondents, respectively, leading to reliance on informal practices; and (b) a lack of standardized resources (59.8%) and clinical time constraints, which limited intervention consistency. Malaysian occupational therapists face critical educational, resource, and operational gaps in pediatric sleep practice. Overcoming these barriers requires structured curriculum integration, continuing professional development, standardized clinical toolkits, and multidisciplinary practice frameworks.

articles.title: Development and Initial Psychometric Evaluation of the Family Life Impact Questionnaire.
articles.abstract: Occupation and co-occupation are central to occupational therapy, yet no standardized instrument exists to measure ease of participation in co-occupations for families with a child with sensory integration challenges. This study describes the initial development and psychometric evaluation of data gathered with the Family Life Impact Questionnaire (FLIQ), a parent-report measure assessing perceived ease of family participation. Using Rasch measurement methods, we iteratively evaluated the 43-item FLIQ with a sample of 62 parents of children with sensory integration challenges (n = 25) and typically developing children (n = 37). Analyses supported a two-subscale structure: Social Participation (nine items) and Daily Life Management (25 items), rated on a 4-point scale. Both demonstrated strong reliability (person separation reliability = .88-.95), good item fit, and large between-group effect sizes. FLIQ shows promise as a clinically meaningful, occupation-centered instrument for assessing and monitoring family participation outcomes.

articles.title: Association of genotype-predicted thiopurine S-methyltransferase/nudix hydrolase 15 phenotypes with 6-mercaptopurine tolerability and hospitalization-related outcomes in Chinese pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia patients: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This multicenter retrospective study aimed to investigate the association of genotype-predicted thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) and nudix hydrolase 15 (NUDT15) phenotypes with 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP) treatment tolerance and hospitalization-related outcomes during high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) consolidation block in Chinese pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) patients.
METHODS: This study included 103 Chinese pediatric ALL patients. Genotypes were translated into Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline-defined predicted metabolizer phenotypes, and patients were classified as predicted normal metabolizers (n = 80) or predicted intermediate metabolizers (n = 23). Data on 6-MP treatment tolerance and hospitalization-related outcomes were collected across four cycles of HD-MTX treatment. Longitudinal data were analyzed using linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models. To control the false discovery rate across the five prespecified primary outcomes in the mixed-effects modeling, multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P values (Padj) < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the predicted normal metabolizers and intermediate metabolizer groups. The body surface area-adjusted 6-MP total dose was consistently lower in the intermediate metabolizer group across all four cycles. Longitudinal analysis confirmed that intermediate metabolizer patients experienced significantly longer inpatient stays (β = 0.98 days, Padj = 0.033), a higher risk of chemotherapy delay [odds ratio (OR) = 2.86, Padj = 0.02], and an increased likelihood of unplanned readmission (OR = 3.75, Padj = 0.018). Intermediate metabolizer status was not significantly associated with infection risk.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, genotype-predicted TPMT/NUDT15 intermediate metabolizer status was associated with lower prescribed 6-MP dose intensity and worse hospitalization-related outcomes during HD-MTX consolidation.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomics of stimulant treatment response: protocol for an open-label clinical trial to identify genomic predictors of methylphenidate response in youth with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methylphenidate is a first-line pharmacological treatment for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents. However, approximately one-third of patients experience inadequate symptom improvement or intolerable adverse effects, and clinicians currently lack biomarkers to guide prescribing decisions.
METHODS: The pharmacogenomics of stimulant treatment response study is an open-label clinical trial designed to identify genomic profiles associated with methylphenidate treatment response and tolerability in youth with ADHD. A total of 400 Canadian youth aged 6-24 years who are initiating long-acting methylphenidate treatment are eligible. Participants will provide saliva samples for genome-wide genotyping and complete weekly clinical assessments over 4 weeks, including the Strengths and Weaknesses of ADHD Symptoms and Normal Behaviors Rating Scale, Canadian ADHD Resource Alliance Side Effect Form, neurocognitive tasks, and quality-of-life measures. Blood microsamples will be collected at week 4 for methylphenidate and ritalinic acid concentration determination. Primary analyses will examine associations between genomic profiles, including candidate gene variants, genome-wide significant loci, and polygenic scores for psychiatric disorders and treatment outcomes. Secondary analyses will explore pharmacokinetic correlates of response.
DISCUSSION: At the time of writing, 126 participants have been enrolled, of whom 110 have completed the trial protocol. This trial will establish a comprehensive pharmacogenomics research platform to advance precision prescribing of methylphenidate.

articles.title: Olfactory Reference Symptoms in Adolescents: Functional Impact, Odor-Related/Hygiene Behaviors, and Associations with Anxiety, Depression, and Prodromal-Like Experiences.
articles.abstract: Background: Olfactory reference symptoms involve persistent concerns about emitting an unpleasant body odor and may be accompanied by social avoidance, repetitive behaviors, and functional difficulties. This study examined symptom severity, self-reported functional impact, odor-related/hygiene behaviors, and associated psychopathological dimensions in adolescents. Methods: This cross-sectional online survey included 105 adolescents. Participants completed the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Modified for Olfactory Reference Syndrome (ORS-YBOCS), Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS), Prodromal Questionnaire-Brief (PQ-B), and Somatosensory Amplification Scale (SSAS), together with sociodemographic questions and items assessing functional impact and odor-related/hygiene behaviors. Primary associations were examined using Spearman correlations and hierarchical multiple linear regression controlling for age and sex. Results: The mean ORS-YBOCS total score was 10.68 ± 8.04. Participants most commonly reported body-odor-related difficulties in social activities, school attendance, friendships, and romantic interactions. Common behaviors included excessive washing, odor masking, checking, airing out the environment, and sniffing the perceived odor source. ORS-YBOCS scores were positively correlated with RCADS, SSAS, and PQ-B total scores. Social anxiety/social phobia showed the largest correlation among RCADS subscales. In the final regression model, RCADS and PQ-B total scores remained independently associated with higher ORS-YBOCS scores, whereas SSAS was not independently significant. Conclusion: Olfactory reference symptoms in adolescents were associated with functional impact, odor-related/hygiene behaviors, anxiety-depression symptoms, somatosensory amplification, and prodromal-like experiences. Anxiety-depression symptom burden and prodromal-like experiences remained independently associated with symptom severity, supporting the clinical relevance of body-odor concerns as a multidimensional symptom domain.

articles.title: Sleep Characteristics in Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder: Associations with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury and Suicidality.
articles.abstract: Background: Sleep disturbances impact outcomes in major depressive disorder (MDD). This cross-sectional study evaluated subjective sleep quality and habits in adolescents with MDD and their associations with suicide attempt (SA) and non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI). Methods: Sixty-eight adolescents aged 13-18 years with MDD were classified as NSSI-only, SA-only, and combined. Clinical severity and depressive symptoms were measured with Clinical Global Impression-Severity scale and Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R). Self-harm and suicidality were evaluated using Inventory of Statements About Self-Injury and Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale. Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) assessed past-month sleep quality and past-week sleep habits. Results: Participants had poor sleep quality (89.7%) and disturbed sleep habits (83.8%), without group differences. CSHQ scores correlated moderately with lifetime NSSI frequency (r = .36, P = .003), whereas PSQI scores correlated weakly (r = .28, P = .023). PSQI scores were modestly related to past-month suicidal ideation severity (r = .28, P = .022). In hierarchical regressions controlling for sedative medications and CDRS-R scores, CSHQ (β = 0.299, P = .022) and PSQI (β = 0.248, P = .047) accounted for incremental variance in lifetime NSSI frequency. Conclusion: Sleep problems are common among adolescents with MDD, suggesting a clinical feature rather than a subgroup-specific trait. Sleep disturbance was associated with lifetime NSSI burden beyond depression severity, indicating a clinically relevant assessment domain. Prospective longitudinal studies should clarify temporal and bidirectional relationships with self-harm outcomes.

articles.title: National Trends and Demographic Disparities in Self-Reported Cognitive Difficulty Among U.S. High School Students, 2015-2023.
articles.abstract: The National Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) asks students whether, because of a physical, mental, or emotional problem, they have serious difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions. We analyzed nationally representative 2015-2023 YRBS data from 50,222 U.S. high school students using survey-weighted prevalence estimates and logistic regression. The prevalence of this self-reported cognitive difficulty increased from 29.9% (95% CI, 27.7%-32.1%) in 2015 to 45.0% (95% CI, 43.1%-47.0%) in 2023-approximately 3 in 10 students to nearly 1 in 2 (adjusted odds ratio per 2-year cycle, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.25)-while 2021 and 2023 estimates were similar. The increase was steeper among female than male students. In secondary models, insufficient sleep, excessive recreational screen use, frequent poor mental health, household basic needs not consistently met, and unstable housing were associated with cognitive difficulty. These findings identify a growing functional signal requiring surveillance, school-health assessment, referral pathways, and further study.

articles.title: Brief Report: Short-Term Outcomes of Child-Child Sexual Interactions.
articles.abstract: There is much controversy over the potential effects of sexual interactions between similar-aged children, although little empirical data relevant to the question has been offered. Exploratory, non-violent, and non-coercive play is at times conflated with abusive interactions, with both lay and professional authors fearing that sexual exploration of any kind may lead to adverse outcomes. Problems with conflation of these two experiences emerge frequently in legal contexts, where experts are requested to comment on the potential consequences of child-child sexual encounters based on very little empirical information. To investigate such interactions, 25 children seen in forensic or clinical settings were examined utilizing the Trauma Symptom Checklist for Children (TSCC). Results showed limited potential negative outcomes, with no child meeting criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). One child did receive a borderline positive result and several were elevated on specific subscales, most commonly Sexual Concerns and Anxiety. In general, results suggest that child-child sexual interactions are not universally harmful, although specific reactions will vary due to family and cultural context.

articles.title: Early Developmental Interventions for Infants Born Very Preterm: A Survey of Australian Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy Practice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To describe clinical practices of Australian physiotherapists and occupational therapists providing early developmental interventions for infants born very preterm (VPT; <32 weeks' gestation) during the first year of life.
METHODS: A national survey was conducted with physiotherapists and occupational therapists who had cared for infants born VPT, under 12 months' corrected age. Clinician demographics and practice characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. Intervention descriptions (guided by the Template for Intervention Description and Replication for Rehabilitation checklist), and perceived barriers and facilitators, were analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Of 114 responses analyzed (74.6% physiotherapists), representing all Australian states, territories and care sectors, most reported more than 10 years of clinical experience (65.8%), provided care during neonatal hospital admissions (65.8%), and worked within multidisciplinary teams (93.9%). Interventions encompassed multiple interacting components, described using varied terminology. Three categories of barriers and facilitators included: systems and structures, infant and family characteristics, and clinician capabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Physiotherapists and occupational therapists in Australia provide early developmental interventions across multiple sectors within collaborative practice settings. Variability in terminology and systems-level barriers highlight the need for greater consistency in clinical practice. Standardization of terminology and strengthening clinician capabilities are key priorities for the field.

articles.title: A novel workflow for three-dimensional and longitudinal analysis of craniofacial morphology and its application to syndromic bilateral coronal synostosis after endoscope-assisted suturectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative evaluation of craniofacial morphology continues to be challenging because the orbital and frontal regions are complex three-dimensionally. These regions are severely affected in syndromic patients with bilateral coronal synostosis. The aim of this study was to establish a workflow for three-dimensional and longitudinal evaluation of craniofacial morphology using average craniofacial models of healthy Japanese infants and apply this workflow to syndromic patients with bilateral coronal synostosis after endoscope-assisted suturectomy.
METHODS: Seven syndromic patients with bilateral coronal synostosis, including those with involvement of additional cranial sutures, who underwent endoscope-assisted suturectomy between 2017 and 2023 at the National Center for Child Health and Development (Tokyo, Japan) were included. Three-dimensional craniofacial morphology was quantitatively compared between patients and age-matched average models at pre- and postoperative time points using image processing and evaluation software. Furthermore, craniofacial growth patterns were compared three-dimensionally between patients and average models to evaluate longitudinal changes in relation to physiological growth.
RESULTS: Patient's craniofacial morphology was closer to the average model approximately 1 year after surgery. Compared with physiological changes in age-matched average models, forehead protrusion was suppressed and forward growth of the nasal-supraorbital region was enhanced.
CONCLUSIONS: Our workflow enabled quantitative, three-dimensional, and longitudinal evaluation of craniofacial morphology in relation to age-matched average models. Application of this workflow to syndromic patients with bilateral coronal synostosis elucidated postoperative changes in the forehead and nasal-supraorbital morphology.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacteria on Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Surfaces at a Tertiary Hospital in Kampala, Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: About 60% of neonatal sepsis cases are hospital-acquired and are often caused by Gram-negative bacteria, with a high rate of antimicrobial resistance. Outbreaks of multidrug-resistant bacteria in neonatal units occur at rates 20 times higher in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income settings. We conducted 4 rounds (R1-4) of environmental sampling in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in Kampala, Uganda, to inform an infection prevention and control (IPC) program tailored to a resource-limited setting.
METHODS: Eighty-two swabs were taken over 12 months (2021-2022) from n = 13 high-touch surfaces, n = 10 low-touch surfaces (R1-3) and n = 6 staff items (R4). Potential pathogens were identified using standard biochemical methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion. Hand hygiene audits were conducted throughout the study period. A collaborative working group of NICU, IPC and research staff co-developed IPC interventions.
RESULTS: Of 146 organisms isolated, 127 (82%) were potential pathogens, predominantly Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp. and Citrobacter spp. High-touch sites such as sinks, cots and drug trolleys showed persistent contamination. Resistance to first-line antibiotics was high: gentamicin (48/91, 52%), ampicillin (25/25, 100%) and ceftazidime (30/91, 33%). After color-coded feedback, a unit-wide deep clean reduced potential pathogens by 60% from R1 (n = 63) to R2 (n = 25). However, levels rebounded in R3 (n = 32), representing a 21% increase compared with R2 (n = 25), highlighting inconsistencies in cleaning.
CONCLUSIONS: Targeted environmental cleaning can reduce NICU contamination by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens. Sinks were persistent reservoirs, underscoring the need for consistent daily cleaning and staff engagement. In low- and middle-income country settings, simple, low-cost IPC measures informed by environmental surveillance may support sustainable hospital-acquired infection reduction.

articles.title: Human Metapneumovirus-associated Infections Among American Indian and Alaska Native Children, 2019-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications.
METHODS: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta). Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors.
RESULTS: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In 2023-2024, incidence rates of HMPV-associated ARI hospitalization per 1000 children <5 years old were 11.3 (95% confidence interval: 8.6-14.8) in the Southwest, 10.3 (7.4-14.4) in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, and 0 (0-1.1) in Anchorage. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits.
CONCLUSIONS: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.

articles.title: Epidemiologic Variability and Clinical Severity Across 11 Influenza Seasons in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza is a major cause of respiratory illness, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in children. Seasonal influenza epidemics were profoundly disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Whether the clinical presentation and disease severity differ according to influenza virus type and subtype remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to describe temporal changes in epidemiology, clinical characteristics, outcomes and healthcare utilization among laboratory-confirmed pediatric influenza cases over 11 seasons and to explore associations between virus type/subtype and clinically important outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at a tertiary pediatric hospital, including all laboratory-confirmed influenza cases identified in children presenting with acute respiratory infection between July 2015 and June 2026, and analyzed the distribution of cases and their demographic and clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: Influenza was detected in 3105 children (median age, 4 years), the majority of whom were previously healthy (82.4%). Within this cohort, hospitalization was required in 17.9% of cases, with 1.1% requiring intensive care admission, and 22.8% developing complications, including encephalitis and sepsis. Influenza circulation patterns, including the timing of peak activity and the duration of annual epidemics, varied over time. After an 18-month absence of reported cases during the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021-2022 season was marked by a substantial resurgence, followed by 2 years of atypical year-round circulation before returning to the usual seasonal pattern. Influenza A accounted for 72.3% of cases, with alternating predominance of virus types and subtypes without a consistent epidemiologic pattern. In a restricted type/subtype analysis, influenza A(H1N1) cases had a higher frequency of hospitalization and recorded moderate-to-severe complications, and this association remained statistically significant after multivariable analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Influenza was associated with clinically important illness and healthcare use among children in this hospital-based cohort, most commonly among otherwise healthy children, highlighting the importance of influenza prevention strategies. During and after the COVID-19 pandemic, influenza epidemiology changed markedly, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.

articles.title: Mental Health Treatment Gaps in Autistic Boys and Girls Across Childhood and Adolescence: Implications for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing.
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: Many autistic children have co-occurring psychiatric conditions, yet some do not receive mental-health services their caregivers say they need. We examined unmet care by age and sex, with a closer examination of adolescent girls.
METHODS: We pooled 2020-2024 National Survey of Children's Health data. The analytic cohort included 45,721 children ages 3-17 with current anxiety, depression, ADHD, or behavioral/conduct problems (6470 autistic; 39,251 non-autistic). Survey-weighted models adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, public insurance, and poverty.
FINDINGS: Across ages 3-17, autism was associated with unmet care in boys (aOR, 1.57; 95% CI 1.22-2.02; p < 0.001) and girls (aOR, 1.63; 95% CI 1.09-2.42; p = 0.016). Age-stratified associations were significant in younger boys (aOR, 1.79) and adolescent girls (aOR, 2.34), but not younger girls or adolescent boys. Among autistic adolescents, girls had higher adjusted odds than boys (aOR, 1.79; p = 0.011). Nearly one in eight autistic adolescent girls (12.4%) reported unmet care.
CONCLUSIONS: Unmet mental-health care was especially common among autistic adolescent girls, although younger autistic boys also showed an important disparity. Nurses should ask whether needed services were obtained, follow up on unsuccessful referrals, and help families establish care.

articles.title: Inpatient Faecal Disimpaction in Children: A Multicentre Audit of Management Practices and Short-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Faecal impaction is a common complication of paediatric functional constipation and frequently necessitates inpatient disimpaction. Despite this, there is no universally accepted protocol for inpatient management, and endpoints defining successful disimpaction remain unclear. This study aimed to audit inpatient management strategies for paediatric faecal impaction and assess whether stool output characteristics at discharge are associated with short-term clinical improvement.
METHODS: This multicentre retrospective audit included children aged 4-17 years admitted for inpatient faecal disimpaction across eight Queensland hospitals between January and December 2021. Data collected included demographics, disimpaction regimens, route of administration, adjunct enema use, length of stay (LOS), Bristol Stool Scale scores at admission and discharge, and Bowel Management Tool Scores (BMST) at admission and first follow-up.
RESULTS: Seventy-five inpatient episodes were included. Median LOS was 4 days (interquartile range, 3-5). BMST improved by a median of 3.5 points, with 73% of patients demonstrating categorical improvement at follow-up. Adjunct enemas were used in 24% of admissions and were not associated with reduced LOS compared with admissions without enemas (median 5.2 vs. 4.3 days; p=0.60). Nasogastric/gastrostomy administration was used in 71% of cases and oral administration in 29%, with no significant difference in LOS (p=0.44). Approximately 84% of patients were discharged with Bristol Stool Types 7-7+. Achieving Type 7+ stool output (clear and watery) did not confer greater improvement in BMST compared with Type 7 output [3 (1.5-7) vs. 4 (2-6.2), p=0.7].
CONCLUSION: Inpatient faecal disimpaction is associated with meaningful short-term symptom improvement in children. Treating to clear outputs does not appear to confer additional clinical benefit. These findings support a pragmatic approach to inpatient disimpaction and highlight the need for standardised, evidence-based protocols.

articles.title: Clinical Benefits and Safety of Triple-Strain Bifidobacterium Supplementation for Preterm Infants in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Setting: A Hospital-Based Clinical Study in Indonesia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study investigated the clinical outcomes and safety profile of triple-strain Bifidobacterium supplementation in preterm infants treated in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial included preterm infants born at 28 to <34 weeks of gestation with birth weights of 1,000 to <2,500 g. A total of 66 infants were randomly assigned to probiotic or control groups. Infants in the probiotic group received triple-strain Bifidobacterium supplementation once their enteral intake reached 10 mL/kg/day, which was continued until discharge. The probiotic formulation included Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis M-63, Bifidobacterium breve M-16V, and Bifidobacterium longum subsp. longum BB-536. The clinical outcomes were evaluated from admission to discharge.
RESULTS: Infants in the probiotic group reached full enteral feeding more rapidly than those in the control group (p=0.005). Feeding intolerance, including vomiting, abdominal distention, and brownish gastric residue, was significantly lower in the probiotic group (relative risk [RR], 0.538; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.351-0.825; p=0.002), with lower incidences of vomiting, abdominal distension, and brownish gastric residue. No significant differences were observed in weight gain, necrotizing enterocolitis, late-onset sepsis, duration of antibiotic therapy, duration of parenteral nutrition, or length of hospital stay. No major probiotic-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: Triple-strain Bifidobacterium supplementation accelerated the achievement of full enteral feeding and reduced feeding intolerance in preterm infants treated in the NICU. No significant reduction in the antibiotic duration or length of hospital stay was observed. No major safety concerns were identified, but the safety findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Comparison of Outcomes of Neonates with and without Necrotizing Enterocolitis Based on Oxidant/Antioxidant Ratio.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) affects 2-5% of all preterm infants and is responsible for approximately 8% of all admissions to the neonatal intensive care unit. Given the role of oxidative disturbances in NEC, the present study compared neonates with and without NEC based on the oxidant/antioxidant ratio.
METHODS: This cohort study compared 180 neonates, including 126 (70.0%) without NEC and 54 (30.0%) with NEC. This study was conducted at Ghaem Hospital in Mashhad, Iran, from January 2020 to January 2026 using a convenience sampling method. Each participant was followed up for 2 years. Data were collected using a researcher-developed checklist comprising three parts: maternal characteristics, neonatal characteristics, and laboratory information. We compared umbilical cord pH, pro-oxidant-antioxidant balance (PAB; ratio of prooxidants to antioxidants expressed in hydrogen peroxide equivalents) levels, and short- and long-term neonatal outcomes (at two years of age). Chi-square, regression, and t-tests were used for the data analysis.
RESULTS: In patients with fatal NEC, PAB levels (38.44±37.08) were nearly 1.5 times as high as those in NEC patients who were discharged alive (27.14±30.72; p=0.103). NEC patients with abnormal long-term outcomes had significantly elevated PAB levels (34.72±33.49), nearly double those with normal outcomes (19.54±14.38; p=0.006).
CONCLUSION: Measuring PAB in the umbilical cord can help predict NEC incidence and associated two-year prognosis.

articles.title: Gallstones and Biliary Sludge in Children: Age-Related Etiologies, Clinical Patterns, and Outcomes of Ursodeoxycholic Acid Therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pediatric gallstone disease is increasingly becoming recognized, primarily due to the growing use of ultrasonography and rising rates of obesity. However, data comparing age-related etiologies, symptom patterns, and medical treatment outcomes remain limited.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 308 children (0-18 years) diagnosed with gallstones or biliary sludge between 2016 and 2022. Patients were stratified into five age groups: neonatal (0-1 month), infant (1-12 months), preschool (1-5 years), school-age (5-12 years), and adolescent (12-18 years). Demographic, clinical, biochemical, and ultrasonographic data were analyzed. The effectiveness of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) therapy and the need for surgical intervention were evaluated by age group.
RESULTS: Among 308 patients (57.1% female; mean age 8.2±4.7 years), 235 (76.3%) had gallstones and 73 (23.7%) had biliary sludge. The leading etiologies were idiopathic (40.8%), ceftriaxone-associated (13.1%), and obesity-related (9.2%). While most infants were asymptomatic, the symptoms frequency increased with age. UDCA was administered to 275 (89.3%) patients. Complete or partial resolution occurred in 35.3% and 91.8% of gallstone and sludge cases, respectively, with no significant difference between treated and untreated groups. No infants required surgery, whereas surgical intervention increased to 39.3% in adolescents and was significantly higher among patients, who did not receive UDCA (p=0.001).
CONCLUSION: Pediatric gallstones and sludge diseases displayed distinct age-dependent patterns. UDCA therapy showed limited efficacy in true gallstones; however, it reduced the surgical need in older children. Therefore, conservative management is appropriate for infants, as most cases resolved spontaneously without further intervention.

articles.title: Effects of Adjunctive Physiotherapy on Clinical Outcomes in Children with Functional Constipation: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
