PURPOSE: Functional constipation (FC) is a common pediatric gastrointestinal disorder that has a substantial impact on affected children and their families. This study aimed to evaluate whether the addition of physiotherapy (PT) to standard medical treatment improves clinical outcomes in children with FC.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled study, 65 children aged 4-18 years diagnosed with FC according to the Rome IV criteria were allocated to receive standard medical treatment alone (n=35) or standard medical treatment plus PT (n=30). All patients received lactulose, toilet training, and dietary counseling. The PT program included abdominal isometric exercises, abdominal massage, pelvic floor exercises, and diaphragmatic breathing and was conducted for 3 months. The primary outcome was within-group improvement in constipation-related symptoms, and the secondary outcome was overall treatment success, defined as the absence of FC according to the Rome IV criteria at the end of follow-up.
RESULTS: All constipation-related symptoms significantly improved over time in both groups. A significant between-group difference was observed only for stool-withholding behavior, which improved more frequently in the PT group (adjusted odds ratio, 3.680; 95% confidence interval, 1.410-9.610; p=0.008). No significant intergroup differences were found in other symptoms. The overall treatment success rate was higher in the PT group than in the standard medical treatment group (100.0% vs. 85.7%, p=0.031).
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive PT may improve short-term overall treatment success in children with FC, particularly by reducing stool-withholding behavior. Larger studies with longer follow-up periods are required to confirm these findings.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Decision Analysis of the Accuracy of Intestinal Lymphogram for Celiac Disease in Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Celiac disease (CD) is characterized by an increased proportion of CD3+ T-cell receptor gamma/delta-positive (TCRγδ+) intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) and a reduced number of CD3-IELs. We aimed to summarize available evidence on the accuracy of intestinal flow cytometry for diagnosing CD in children.
METHODS: Electronic and manual searches were performed using keywords related to diagnostic validity. Two researchers independently extracted data from the selected studies. Pooled estimates of the accuracy measures were calculated using a random-effects model, and the risk of bias and threshold effect were further assessed. The clinical utility of intestinal lymphogram in diagnosing several serological and histological phenotypes (conventional, seronegative, and potential CD) was simulated using a Bayesian approach. Accordingly, the meta-analyzed indicators and several assumptions regarding CD prevalence were considered.
RESULTS: The search yielded 656 citations, of which seven were finally included, providing a population of 1,248 patients with CD. Pooled sensitivity and specificity of combined high TCRγδ+ and low CD3-IELs were 90% and 99%, respectively. Only two high-quality studies provided sensitivity data for children initially diagnosed with potential CD. Across both cohorts, 38% of children with potential CD progressed to CD, based on heterogeneous diagnostic criteria. Using pooled diagnostic accuracy measures for this pre-test probability, the resulting positive and negative predictive values were 98% and 95%, respectively. No specific data on seronegative CD were retrieved.
CONCLUSION: The intraepithelial lymphogram acts as a potentially useful adjunctive marker in children, though its prognostic value in potential CD remains uncertain.

articles.title: Clinical, Laboratory, and Genetic Evaluations of Cystic Fibrosis Patients with Gastrointestinal System Involvement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive genetic disease caused by a mutation in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene. This study provides a detailed evaluation of patients with CF and gastrointestinal (GI) involvement at our university, a reference center in southern Turkey, with respect to genetic, clinical, radiological, and anthropometric characteristics.
METHODS: The clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings, genetic results, and prognoses of 97 patients diagnosed with CF and followed at the Cukurova University Medical Faculty, Department of Pediatric Gastroenterology, between 2011 and 2022 were retrospectively reviewed.
RESULTS: Pancreatic insufficiency was detected in 75.3% of patients and was the most common GI manifestation. It was followed by growth retardation (64.9%; defined as a weight below the 5th percentile at any time during follow-up), constipation (30.9%), gastroesophageal reflux (GER; 14.4%), hepatic steatosis (4.1%), pancreatitis (4.1%), rectal prolapse (1.0%), and meconium ileus (1.0%). Genetic analysis showed that F508del was the most common mutation (14.4%). According to the Gomez and Waterlow classifications, malnutrition improved significantly over time (p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: In recent years, the inclusion of CF in newborn screening programs in many countries has enabled earlier diagnosis. Along with a better understanding of its pathophysiology, improved care, and advances in treatment, this has increased the number of patients followed into adulthood. Because CF is a multisystem disease, a multidisciplinary approach is required.

articles.title: Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Children Undergoing Major Non-Cardiac Surgery: Protocol for a Multicentre Study (POAKIDS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with increased mortality and adverse long-term outcomes. Postoperative AKI is a common and recognised complication after surgery in adults. In children, AKI following paediatric cardiac surgery has been extensively studied. However, the incidence and characteristics of postoperative AKI after non-cardiac surgery in children remain poorly defined, with existing evidence largely derived from retrospective and single-centre studies.
METHODS: POAKIDS is an international, multicentre, prospective observational study including hospitalised children aged 0-16 years undergoing major non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Postoperative AKI will be defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative AKI. Secondary objectives include evaluation of established and novel urinary biomarkers as predictors of postoperative AKI and exploration of perioperative potential predictors of renal injury. The maximal follow-up is seven postoperative days. Sample size is based on the incidence estimate, with a planned inclusion of 2000 patients. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, agreement analyses, and exploratory regression models.
DISCUSSION: This study aims to provide robust prospective data on the incidence of postoperative AKI in children undergoing major non-cardiac surgery and to improve understanding of perioperative renal injury in this population. By combining standardised AKI definitions with systematic biomarker assessment, the results are expected to inform future preventive strategies and guide the design of interventional studies targeting postoperative renal injury in paediatric perioperative care.

articles.title: Early Complications of Epicardial Permanent Pacemaker Implantation in Neonates and Infants Weighing 5 kg or Less.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the incidence and predictors of early complications following epicardial permanent pacemaker (ePPM) implantation in neonates and infants weighing 5 kg or less.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 40 patients weighing 5 kg or less who underwent ePPM implantation between 1999 and 2025. Early complications were defined as ePPM-related adverse events requiring medical or surgical intervention within 6 months post-implantation. Firth's penalized logistic regression was performed to identify predictors for early complications. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) determined the optimal cutoff value.
RESULTS: The median age and body weight at implantation were 58 days (interquartile range [IQR], 21.8-118.3 days) and 3.7 kg (IQR, 3.2-4.3 kg), respectively. Early complications occurred in 9 patients (22.5%), including wound dehiscence (n=5), pocket infection (n=3), and pericardial effusion (n=1). On multivariable analysis, body weight at implantation was an independent predictor of complications (odds ratio [OR], 0.77 per 100-g increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98; p=0.031). ROC analysis identified 3.5 kg as the optimal cutoff value for predicting early complications (area under the curve, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.87-1.00; p<0.001), with 100% sensitivity and 84% specificity. A staged ePPM implantation strategy using initial temporary epicardial pacing was performed without early complications in four high-risk patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Early complications remain a significant concern after ePPM implantation in neonates and infants weighing 5kg or less, with body weight identified as an independent predictor. Patients weighing below 3.5 kg represent a high-risk subgroup requiring tailored surgical strategies and vigilant postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations.
RESULTS: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants.
CONCLUSION: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric forensic cases during the COVID 19 lockdown and reopening periods: a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary care pediatric emergency department.
articles.abstract: The COVID‑19 lockdown disrupted daily life, altering children's exposure to risks and reshaping emergency department utilisation. Understanding how these changes influenced pediatric forensic epidemiology is essential for prevention and policy development. All forensic cases involving children aged 1 month-18 years were included. Two periods were analysed: the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020-June 2021) and the post-lockdown period (June 2021-March 2024). Data on demographics, causes, outcomes and costs were extracted from medical and forensic records. During the COVID‑19 lockdown period, the incidence of forensic cases was 25.8 per 1000 PED visits per month, whereas during the reopening period this rate decreased to 12.7 per 1000 PED visits per month (p < 0.001). Exposure to chemical substances and assault were more frequent during the lockdown period (p = 0.01 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas food poisoning was more common during the reopening period (p = 0.004). Forensic cases were predominant among female adolescents (p = 0.004). Male sex was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of forensic cases (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.49, p = 0.011). Furthermore, the COVID-19 lockdown period was independently associated with an increased odds of forensic cases (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.65-2.56, p < 0.001). The median outpatient and total bills per PED visit were lower in forensic cases (48.7 vs. 68.1 TRY, p < 0.001 and 57.8 vs. 90.2 TRY, p < 0.001, respectively). Different COVID‑19 periods were associated with significant differences in the incidence, causes, and patterns of pediatric forensic cases. Male sex and the lockdown period were identified as independent risk factors for forensic presentations, highlighting the complex interaction between demographic and temporal factors in forensic epidemiology.

articles.title: Trends in United States Pediatric In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence and Mortality in a Nationally Representative Sample, 2009-2022.
articles.abstract:
AIM: National estimates of pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) incidence in the United States rely on a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative datasets offer a nationally representative alternative. We estimated nationally representative pediatric IHCA incidence and mortality trends from 2009 through 2022.
METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of five triennial editions of the Kids' Inpatient Database (2009-2022), identifying IHCA in children <18 years by ICD-9 (99.60, 99.63) and ICD-10 (5A12012) cardiopulmonary resuscitation procedure codes. Two hospitals with implausible CPR rates were excluded. Survey-weighted incidence per 1,000 hospitalizations and in-hospital mortality among resuscitated children were estimated overall and by neonatal status, complex chronic condition (CCC) status, ZIP-code income quartile, and US Census region. Trends were tested with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression across the full period and, as exploratory analyses, within the ICD-10 era (2016-2022).
RESULTS: Observed IHCA incidence was 1.11/1,000 in 2009 and 1.22/1,000 in 2012, decreased to 1.11/1,000 at the ICD-10 transition and increased to 1.35/1,000 by 2022. IHCA incidence in children hospitalized with a CCC rose from 3.26 to 6.60/1,000 (6.2%/year, p<0.001), while incidence without CCC remained low. Incidence varied by socioeconomic status (lowest vs highest income quartile 1.78 vs 1.04/1,000 in 2022). In-hospital mortality ranged from 34.1% (2012) to 40.4% (2019), whereas IHCA deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased 1.7%/year (p<0.001), concentrated among children with a CCC.
CONCLUSION: The incidence of pediatric IHCA increased among hospitalizations involving children with CCC and was higher among children who live in lower income areas. In-hospital mortality after CPR was largely stable, whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased among children with CCC. A single hospital's coding practices can materially distort national administrative estimates. What is already known Pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest affects approximately 15,200 children annually in the United States, with this national estimate derived primarily from a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative databases offer nationally representative coverage but rely on procedure codes that are susceptible to misclassification. What this study adds In this nationally representative administrative database sample spanning 2009-2022, this study demonstrated that: 1) the incidence of IHCA among children with complex chronic conditions (CCC) rose steadily and accounted for the substantial majority of events, 2) the overall IHCA incidence was higher among children who live in lower income areas with the gradient worsening over the period evaluated, and 3) in-hospital mortality after CPR increased only slightly (34-40%), whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased more, driven mainly by rising incidence among children with CCC, and 4) CPR coding at a single hospital can substantially distort national administrative estimates.

articles.title: Investigating the Therapeutic Potential of MSC-EVs in Neonatal HIE.
articles.abstract: Perinatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a severe brain injury in newborns and could cause long-term neurological developmental disorders. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) are increasingly regarded as an effective cell-free therapeutic approach due to their low immunogenicity, natural ability to cross the blood-brain barrier, and engineerable properties. This review indicates that MSC-EVs can achieve better therapeutic effects by specifically regulating the immune response and promoting repair at different stages of neuroinflammation. It systematically summarizes engineering optimization strategies to enhance the therapeutic effect of MSC-EVs, including reprogramming EV components via hypoxia or drug pretreatment and improving EV biological activity and tissue bioavailability through 3D culture combined with biomaterial delivery systems. Additionally, it analyzes the efficacy, advantages, and limitations of different administration routes for the treatment of cerebral ischemia-hypoxia diseases. Finally, it discusses the limitations of MSC-EVs in the treatment of HIE and future research directions, providing a comprehensive theoretical basis for the clinical translation of MSC-EVs as a targeted treatment for neonatal HIE.

articles.title: Health service delivery for children with congenital limb differences: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health service delivery pathways for children with congenital hand and upper limb differences (CLD) are heterogeneous, with access to specialized pediatric hand therapy influenced by geographic location, resource availability, and broader healthcare system structures.
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to describe and evaluate health service delivery for children with CLD, illustrated through the service pathway for camptodactyly from diagnosis through specialized clinics and hand therapy follow-up for contracture management.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort design.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of children with camptodactyly (0-18 years) and were assessed by specialists at the [de-identified] clinic, over a 11-year period. Demographic, follow-up and no-show history, and location of primary residence data were extracted. Geographical distance between primary residence, specialist upper limb clinic, and community rehabilitation centres were mapped. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's Exact Test were conducted to describe the population and evaluate impacts of geographical distance and health services outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 110 children with camptodactyly were included (50.9% female), 72 (65.5%) had isolated camptodactyly and 38 (34.5%) had arthrogryposis. The average travel distance to the specialist clinic was 34.5 ± 22.7 km for participants living in the Greater Toronto Area and 324.7 ± 370.9 km for those outside the catchment area. Loss to follow-up was significantly higher among participants outside the catchment area (p=.03). Mapping of referrals indicate that children rehabilitation centres are geographically strategic, suggesting potential partnerships.
CONCLUSION: Children with CLD from outside the hand specialist catchment area travelled substantially greater distances and had higher odds of being lost to follow-up, highlighting geographic disparities in care continuity. Strengthening partnerships between tertiary centers and community pediatric rehabilitation centres, developing and expanding pediatric hand therapy resources, and leveraging virtual care models may help reduce travel burden and improve equitable access to health services for children with CLD.

articles.title: Exploring Australian child and youth mental health occupational therapists' perception and utilisation of creative activities: A survey snapshot.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Creative activities have traditionally been an important therapeutic medium in occupational therapy; however, research suggests a decline in their perceived efficacy, utilisation, and teaching. This study explored Australian child and youth mental health (CYMH) occupational therapists' perceptions and use of creative activities.
METHOD: A 31-item web-based survey, comprising quantitative and qualitative questions, was disseminated via convenience sampling to collect data from Australian CYMH occupational therapists. Descriptive statistics and non-parametric Mann-Whitney U tests were used for quantitative data, with inductive content analysis used for qualitative data.
RESULTS: Analysis of 33 completed surveys revealed creative activities were perceived as a highly efficacious therapeutic medium (78%), utilised most frequently multiple times a week (66%). All respondents utilised creative activities, although 64% were not content with their current use. Although 67% rated confidence using creative activities highly, 97% identified additional training needs to feel more confident. Three main categories central to use of creative activities arose: 'creative activities as a therapeutic medium', 'legitimacy of creative activities within occupational therapy' and 'initial and ongoing professional development'.
CONCLUSION: Australian CYMH occupational therapists perceived and utilised creative activities positively. Lack of discipline-specific evidence and unmet training needs impacted confidence in their use.

articles.title: Comparison of occupational balance in high school students with different nomophobia levels: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The study investigates the relationship between nomophobia and occupational balance among high school students. Nomophobia, or the fear of being without a mobile phone, is increasingly prevalent among adolescents, potentially impacting their daily routines and well-being. This study aimed to examine the relationship between nomophobia levels and occupational balance among high school students.
METHODS: Sociodemographic data were obtained with a sociodemographic form. The Adolescent Occupational Balance Scale was used to measure occupational balance. The Nomophobia Questionnaire was used to determine nomophobia levels. A total of 258 students participated in the study.
RESULTS: Findings reveal that as nomophobia levels increase, students' ability to manage time and participate in various activities significantly decreases. This study found that students with severe nomophobia showed lower scores in occupational diversity and harmony, indicating that excessive reliance on digital platforms may reduce participation in social and academic activities.
CONCLUSIONS: The study suggests that high levels of nomophobia may limit individuals' ability to engage in a variety of meaningful activities, thereby disrupting their occupational balance. Considering occupational balance in future research and intervention strategies is crucial for promoting healthier technology use and improving the overall well-being of high school students.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial number: not applicable.

articles.title: Opioid Prescribing Calibration, Consumption, and Disposal After Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A 7-year Institutional Stewardship Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathways have reduced inpatient opioid exposure after posterior spinal fusion (PSF) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), yet the discharge prescription has received far less scrutiny. Temporal trends in prescription size, caregiver-reported consumption, and household disposal of unused medication remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 321 patients aged 10 to 20 years undergoing primary PSF for AIS from 2018 to 19 through 2024 to 25 at a single tertiary pediatric hospital. Prescribing among 275 patients discharged with tablets was modeled with multivariable linear regression. Caregiver-reported pill counts from a postoperative survey (consumption cohort, n=79; telephone era, n=36; text-message era, n=43) informed consumption and waste analyses; disposal and home pain-management items came from all respondents (n=91 to 115 per item). Sensitivity analyses addressed pathway timing, survey modality, response bias, and missing pill counts among families still taking opioids.
RESULTS: Median tablets prescribed declined 67%, from 55 to 18 (adjusted β=-4.91 tablets/year; 95% CI, -5.53 to -4.29; P<0.001), beginning before the most recent ERAS pathway. Reported consumption declined from a median of 30 to 7 tablets, but this decline could not be separated from the survey modality change (telephone era only, P=0.69). The median unused proportion rose from 10% to 40% (unadjusted β=+4.6 percentage points/year; P=0.004) but not significantly after adjustment (P=0.056) or when families still taking opioids were assumed to use their full prescription. Among families with leftover opioids, 22% reported disposal. Requests for additional pain medication (18%) and satisfaction (93%) did not differ between survey eras.
CONCLUSIONS: Discharge opioid prescribing after PSF for AIS declined substantially over 7 years without an apparent change in home pain-management outcomes. Consumption and waste estimates are less certain because they rest on a small, survey-dependent cohort. A default prescription near 15 tablets is a hypothesis for prospective testing, and routine disposal kits at discharge warrant evaluation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV-therapeutic study.

articles.title: Using Information Theory to Evaluate the Predictive Capability of Subadult Age Indicators Throughout Ontogeny.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Relationships between chronological age and skeletal and dental indicators of growth and development have largely contributed to shaping our approaches to subadult age estimation in biological anthropology. Dental development has historically been considered the most accurate age indicator. This somewhat suppositional appreciation of the predictive capability of age indicators conflates genetic potential (a biological phenomenon) with predictive power (a statistical phenomenon). Further, indicators of growth and development are scored or assessed differently (i.e., continuous vs. ordinal data). This data complexity further convolutes the relationship between indicator and estimates. The current study uses information theory to better understand the relationships of skeletal and dental growth and development indicators with age across postnatal ontogeny and evaluate their respective predictive power.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty-two indicators including long bone measurements, epiphyseal fusion stages, and dental development stages were recorded for 1317 contemporary male and female US individuals aged between birth and 21 years. Information gain of each indicator on age was assessed using 62 univariate mixed cumulative probit (MCP) models.
RESULTS: Each variable provides varying levels of information to age throughout the subadult period. Patterns of information gain mirror developmental trajectories (i.e., growth velocity, fusion/mineralization activity), are sexually dimorphic, and are affected by the data type and precision in data collection.
DISCUSSION: These findings challenge the idea of a best indicator or variable for subadult age estimation, elucidate the complex patterns of age-related relationships during ontogeny, and corroborate multivariate and multi-indicator age estimation models.

articles.title: A Narrative Review of Myths and Misconceptions About Methylphenidate in the Treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Methylphenidate (MPH) has been a cornerstone of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) pharmacotherapy for more than 70 years, with robust evidence supporting its efficacy and tolerability across the patient lifespan. Despite this extensive evidence base, persistent myths and misconceptions among clinicians, patients, and caregivers continue to drive treatment hesitancy, premature discontinuation, and suboptimal prescribing practices. Our objective was to identify and critically appraise prevalent myths surrounding MPH use in ADHD that may adversely influence treatment decisions.
METHODS: Myths were identified based on clinical experience, discussions with prominent ADHD experts, and a literature search for relevant articles and guidelines. Evidence from the literature was reviewed and supplemented with clinical recommendations.
RESULTS: Twelve common misconceptions about MPH were identified. These include misconceptions about interchangeability and dose equivalence between MPH formulations, treatment timing for continuous symptom control, endurance of drug onset- and offset-related side effects, and patient feelings as an indicator of drug effectiveness. Myths that MPH will always cause insomnia, increase anxiety and depression, stunt growth, have similar levels of abuse potential and side effects as other drugs, or worsen behavior in patients with autism spectrum disorder were also identified, as well as a common misconception that MPH is only effective in child and adolescent populations. Evidence gathered from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, pharmacokinetic studies, and clinical practice guidelines provided counterarguments to these concerns.
CONCLUSIONS: MPH remains a well-studied, effective, and generally well-tolerated treatment for ADHD in children, adolescents, and adults. The diversity of available formulations, including novel delivery systems such as delayed-release/extended-release MPH and serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate, allows for individualized treatment matched to patient needs and daily functional demands. Clinicians who understand evidence-based rebuttals to myths about MPH can improve prescribing decisions and patient/family counseling while reducing the burden of misinformation that contributes to the undertreatment of this highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder.

articles.title: Gestational Age and Birthweight in Risk Analyses of Retinopathy of Prematurity.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Low gestational age (GA) and birthweight (BW), the strongest risk factors for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), are routinely adjusted for without consideration of variable structure. We explored how to model them, using sepsis, oxygen exposure, and small for gestational age (SGA) as illustrative exposures.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the prospective ELGAN cohort (23-27 weeks' gestation; 14 US hospitals, 2002-2004), excluding infants without eye examination or missing data, leaving 1,259 of 1,506 infants. Any ROP was modeled by logistic regression, with GA and BW as continuous, categorical, or indicator variables. Parameterizations were compared by likelihood ratio test and Akaike information criterion; effect modification was assessed by interaction terms.
RESULTS: ROP prevalence was 67%, declining from 91% at 23 to 47% at 27 weeks. A linear GA term fitted less well than week-specific indicators (p = 0.03). The crude oxygen OR, 4.3 (3.1-6.0), decreased to 2.2 (1.4-3.5) after GA adjustment, but exposure was confined to the lower GA group (331/638 vs 10/621). Sepsis estimates were stable (1.6 to 1.5; interaction p = 0.2). SGA was associated with ROP (1.8, 1.3-2.7), but only in the more mature half (3.0, 1.9-4.7 vs 1.1, 0.6-2.0; interaction p = 0.01).
CONCLUSION: GA and BW are not interchangeable proxies for immaturity; uncritical adjustment can attenuate, mask or reverse associations. As screening and prevention rely on such estimates, studies should state the assumed role of GA and BW, justify their functional form and report GA-specific estimates.

articles.title: Navigating discharge information during early oral antibiotic switch in children: a qualitative comparison of caregiver and clinician experiences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early switch from intravenous (IV) to oral antibiotic therapy is clinically safe for hospitalized children and supports earlier discharge. Responsibility for ongoing care then shifts to caregivers, increasing reliance on effective communication during the hospital-to-home transition.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the information needs and preferences of caregivers during children's transition home on oral antibiotic therapy and examine clinician perceptions of these needs.
METHODS: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children discharged home on oral antibiotics following IV therapy and clinicians involved in their care. Participants were recruited through a hospital participating in the HOMEFREE program and consumer networks. Interviews explored information needs, timing, delivery, understanding, and discharge readiness. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, followed by interpretation through Longo's Extended Model of Health Information Seeking Behaviour.
RESULTS: Fifteen caregivers and eight clinicians participated. Four interrelated themes were identified. Information was frequently delivered at clinically appropriate but challenging time points, limiting families' ability to absorb key messages. Clinicians relied primarily on verbal communication, whereas caregivers preferred written information that could be revisited after discharge. Confidence in oral antibiotic therapy developed through observing recovery at home rather than clinical explanation alone. Caregivers often compensated for information gaps through vigilance and self-advocacy, and clinicians recognised that this dynamic could advantage more confident families.
CONCLUSIONS: Although oral antibiotic switch is clinically safe, family confidence and preparedness may be influenced by how information is delivered and used. Timely, multimodal communication may support safer and more equitable discharge.

articles.title: The New Kid on the Block: A Retrospective Multicenter Real-World Experience with Maribavir for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Pediatric Transplant and Cellular Therapy Recipients.
articles.abstract: This multicenter retrospective case series characterizes maribavir (MBV) use for cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in 62 immunocompromised children treated at 18 United States centers from 2015 through 2024. The most common indications for use were suspected antiviral resistance (45.2%), documented resistance (19.4%), and lack of appropriate alternative agents (11.3%). Among 59 participants with detectable CMV DNAemia when their first course began, 66.1% had complete response, 5.1% had partial response, 27.1% had no response, and one relapsed before treatment cessation. CMV DNAemia ≥50,000 IU/mL was associated with a lower response rate, and MBV resistance was identified in four participants. Across 70 total treatment episodes, 21.4% reported adverse events and discontinuation attributed to MBV occurred in 5.7%. Concomitant use of MBV and other anti-CMV directed medications occurred frequently. Although efficacy results are limited by the observational design, these results highlight real-world pediatric experience and safety.

articles.title: Natural History of Glucose Homeostasis and β-Cell Function from Childhood to Early Adulthood in Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia Patients with Early Iron Chelation: A Ten-Year Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron overload from chronic transfusion therapy progressively impairs pancreatic β-cell function and insulin action in transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (β-TDT), but longitudinal data from childhood through early adulthood are scarce.
OBJECTIVES: To describe, in a single retrospective cohort of patients with β-TDT followed for tenyear, (i) the annual evolution of oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)-derived glycemic values and (ii) insulin resistance and β-cell function indices from late childhood to early adulthood.
METHODS: Twenty-three patients with TDT (12 males, 11 females) were followed from mean age of 10.2 ± 0.9 years (baseline) to 20.8 ± 0.85 years (ten-year follow-up). All patients received subcutaneous iron chelation with deferoxamine (DFO) monotherapy throughout. A standardized OGTT was done yearly. Plasma glucose and serum insulin were measured at 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes after glucose load to evaluate glucose homeostasis and indices of insulin secretion and sensitivity. Results were compared with contemporaneous healthy controls (two separate, non-overlapping cross-sectional control groups at baseline and at ten years). Pearson and Spearman correlations examined bivariate relationships between glycemic and insulin parameters using one observation per patient (n = 23); the 230 annual OGTTs were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models, generalized estimating equations (GEE) and Kaplan-Meier estimates.
RESULTS: In the whole cohort, fasting glucose rose from 91.6 ± 11.6 to 94.6 ± 10.7 mg/dL, 30-minute post-load glucose from 137.6 ± 26.8 to 147.6 ± 20.1 mg/dL, 60-minute and 120-minute post-load glucose (113.5 ± 23.5 to 147.6 ± 31.4 mg/dL and 101.6 ±16.9 to 132.4 ± 15.3 mg/dL, respectively). HOMA1-%β fell from 119.8 ± 72.1 to 62.6 ± 24.9, while HOMA1-IR declined from 1.81 ± 0.78 to 1.26 ± 0.59, and ISSI-2 showed no linear trend, declining until about year 5 before partly recovering (1.82 ± 0.58 to 1.87 ± 0.57). At baseline, fasting glucose correlated positively with HOMA-IR (r: 0.46, P =0.027) and inversely with HOMA1-%β (r: -0.69, P < 0.001) and ISSI-2 (r: -0.72, P < 0.001); 30-minute post-load glucose at baseline was associated with 1-hour post-load glucose at ten year (r: 0.6545, P < 0.001; n = 23). At 10 years of follow-up, dysglycemia was present in 11/23 patients (47.8%; 3 isolated impaired fasting glucose [IFG], 5 isolated impaired glucose tolerance [IGT], 3 combined IFG plus IGT), more frequently in males than in females (8/12 vs. 3/11; Fisher's exact test, P = 0.10). Notably, HOMA1-%β was significantly lower than in controls at ten years (P < 0.0001), whereas ISSI-2 was significantly lower than in controls at baseline and after 10 years of follow-up (P < 0.0001 and 0.0042, respectively). No significant difference in the prevalence of dysglycemia between patients with good (mean serum ferritin: 607.4 ± 180.3 μg/L) and poor compliance (mean serum ferritin: 1998.6 ± 886.3 μg/L) with iron chelation therapy with DFO was documented (5/11 vs. 6/12; χ2: 0.0475, P= 0.82). In mixed-effects models of the annual OGTTs, 1-h and 2-h PG rose by 4.5 and 3.4 mg/dL per year (both P < 0.001), and 21 of 22 initially normoglycemic patients had a 1-h PG ≥155 mg/dL at least once (median 6 years). After adjusting for follow-up time, serum ferritin was not associated with glycemic status or the β-cell index.
CONCLUSIONS: Deterioration in glucose tolerance over the study period appeared to be associated mainly with a decline in surrogate indices of insulin secretory capacity rather than with a progressive increase in insulin resistance (IR), although HOMA- and OGTT-derived indices do not measure β-cell function directly. Reduced surrogate indices of β-cell function were already evident in childhood and were associated with an earlier, higher elevation of plasma glucose at 30 minutes after glucose load compared with controls. OGTT-derived indices of insulin secretion and sensitivity could help tailor screening intensity.

articles.title: Maternal Exposure to Stress and Child Risk of Obesity: A Cross-Sectional Study of Women and Their Children Aged 5-15 Years Living in a Deprived Urban Peruvian Community.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Maternal stress during childhood may contribute to childhood obesity through effects on parenting, parent-child relationships, or children's stress responses. However, evidence is largely based on maternal self-reported stress, while studies using physiological measures like cortisol have found inconsistent associations. Most studies have been conducted in high-income settings, limiting generalisability. Using psychological and physiological stress markers, this cross-sectional study evaluates maternal stress exposures and child risk of obesity in 475 pairs of Peruvian women and their children, age 5-15 years, in a disadvantaged urban area.
METHODS: Maternal stress exposures included psychological distress (12-item General Health Questionnaire categorizing moderate/high vs. no/low distress) and allostatic load (AL; lower/moderate/higher AL assessed from latent profile analysis of hair cortisol, BMI, waist circumference and blood pressure). Child outcomes included BMI and waist circumference-for-age z scores (BAZ and WCAZ). Linear regression analyses were conducted, adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: Versus mothers with no/low distress, those with moderate/high distress had children with 0.40 (95% CI: -0.66, -0.13) and 0.32 lower (-0.53, -0.11) BAZ and WCAZ respectively. Versus lower AL mothers, moderate AL mothers had children with 1.15 (0.41, 1.88) and 0.74 (0.20, 1.28) greater BAZ and WCAZ while higher AL mothers had children with 1.43 (0.95, 1.92) and 0.91 (0.50, 1.32) greater BAZ and WCAZ respectively. Higher maternal cortisol likely independently predicted child adiposity.
CONCLUSIONS: Children of mothers with higher AL were at greater risk of overweight or obesity, which may add to the rising burdens of non-communicable diseases in resource-constrained settings as well as related social, economic, and public health costs.

articles.title: SH3TC2-Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4 C: an Italian multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4 C (CMT4C), caused by biallelic variants in SH3TC2, is the most common autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathy. Italian multicentre data with detailed genotype-phenotype characterisation are lacking. Yet knowledge of the natural history is urgently needed as SH3TC2 gene replacement therapy approaches clinical trials following a successful Pre-Investigational New Drug meeting with the FDA in November 2024.
METHODS: We screened 684 patients with genetically unresolved CMT using a combination of exome analysis and a multigene next-generation sequencing panel and identified nine (from five Italian neurology centres) with biallelic SH3TC2 variants. All patients underwent standardised neurological examination, nerve conduction studies, and assessment using the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Examination Score version 2 (CMTESv2). Variant pathogenicity was assessed according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) criteria incorporating REVEL (Rare Exome Variant Ensemble Learner) and CADD (Combined Annotation-Dependent Depletion) scores.
RESULTS: Nine patients (5 males, 4 females; age 3.5-66 years) were studied. Twelve distinct SH3TC2 variants were identified, including four not previously reported: p.Glu794* (likely pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP guidelines), p.Gly18Ser (variant of unknown significance, VUS), p.Ala526Thr (VUS), and p.Thr1098Ile (VUS). Scoliosis was present in 6/9 patients (66.7%), foot deformities in 7/9 (77.8%), and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/9 (22.2%). Genotype-phenotype analysis revealed marked intra-class variability, including a 59-year-old with homozygous frameshift variants and near-normal function (CMTESv2 total score of 3). One patient was diagnosed presymptomatically at age 3.5 years through cascade genetic testing prompted by comorbid features of Angelman syndrome. All seven symptomatic patients showed motor nerve conduction velocities below 35 m/s. Novel variants p.Gly18Ser and p.Ala526Thr are of uncertain significance and require functional validation: p.Ala526Thr lies immediately adjacent to the functionally characterised pathogenic residue Arg529, whereas p.Gly18Ser lies 16 residues from the myristoylation site at Gly2, within a segment of very low predicted model confidence.
CONCLUSIONS: This Italian multicentre cohort expands the SH3TC2 mutational spectrum highlighting the marked phenotypic variability of CMT4C, and the possibility of presymptomatic identification through multigene NGS panels. Our data contribute to the evidence base required for the design of forthcoming gene therapy clinical trials.

articles.title: Feasibility of Simulated Low-Count [18F]FDG PET/MR for Patients with Pediatric Epilepsy.
articles.abstract: To minimize radiation risks in pediatric PET imaging, injected dose should be kept as low as reasonably achievable. The aim of this study was to explore whether simulated low-count [18F]FDG PET/MR could preserve diagnostic quality in pediatric epilepsy, thereby supporting the design of future lower-activity validation studies. Methods: Twenty-seven pediatric patients with epilepsy were enrolled. List-mode PET data acquired over 20 min were truncated to 10, 7, and 4 min to simulate count reductions of 50%, 65%, and 80%, respectively. Image quality of the PET images was assessed visually using a 5-point Likert scale and quantitatively using contrast-to-noise ratio and coefficient of variation. The intraclass correlation coefficient was used to evaluate SUV ratio (SUVR) consistency across the simulated count reduction levels in different brain regions. Two computer-assisted methods, region of interest (ROI)-based methods and voxel-based methods, were used for epileptogenic zone (EZ) lateralization. For the ROI-based method, a machine learning model using regional SUVRs as features was applied, and performance was evaluated via receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis and the area under the curve, with statistical significance assessed by the DeLong test. For the voxel-based method, EZ lateralization was determined on the basis of the hemisphere of hypometabolic clusters identified through asymmetry analysis. Lateralization agreement with the clinical consensus was compared across simulated levels of count reduction. Results: Quantitative analysis showed that the contrast-to-noise ratio decreased and the coefficient of variation increased significantly with simulated count reduction. Visual assessment indicated that, although overall image quality declined, count reduction up to 65% remained clinically acceptable under these simulated conditions. High consistency in mean SUVRs was observed between full-count and simulated low-count PET images across brain regions. Both ROI-based and voxel-based methods demonstrated that EZ lateralization agreement with the clinical consensus did not decline with simulated count reduction. Conclusion: Our study in pediatric epilepsy suggests that a 65% simulated count reduction preserved clinically acceptable [18F]FDG PET image quality, stable SUVR quantification, and concordance of EZ lateralization with the clinical consensus. These findings support the need for prospective validation of a low-activity protocol in pediatric epilepsy.

articles.title: Evaluating Urinary Volatile Organic Compounds as a Novel Metabolomic Biomarker to Differentiate Between Acute Tubular Necrosis and Acute Graft Rejection Following Kidney Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Distinguishing between acute tubular necrosis (ATN) and acute rejection following kidney transplantation currently relies on transplant biopsy findings. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are gaseous products of metabolic processes in organisms which are typically released with greater abundance in disease when there is metabolic dysregulation. Our study aimed to evaluate the extent in which urinary VOCs can differentiate between ATN and acute rejection in patients with a kidney transplant.
METHODS: Kidney transplant recipients age 18-75 years, diagnosed with ATN or acute rejection following transplant biopsy, were included. Urine samples collected from study patients prior to biopsy were processed. Urine samples were centrifuged and the supernatant was collected, stored at -80°C, and defrosted overnight at 4°C before sampling for stir bar sorptive extraction (SBSE). The sample was then analyzed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Post-processing of GC-MS data separated complex mixtures of VOCs based on their volatility and polarity. Mass-to-charge ratios and fragment patterns were measured for individual VOCs identification and quantification.
RESULTS: 47 patients (26 ATN, 21 acute rejection) were included. Linear discriminant analysis demonstrated distinct separation between the ATN and acute rejection groups based on urinary VOCs profiling of 23 VOCs (p < 0.001). Multivariate linear regression analysis reported 7 VOCs that were significantly upregulated in the ATN compared to the acute rejection group (p < 0.001), and 2 VOCs significantly downregulated in the ATN compared to the acute rejection group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Our novel data suggests potential clinical utility of urinary VOCs as a non-invasive metabolomic biomarker to differentiate between ATN and acute rejection.

articles.title: In Vivo Efficacy of Replication Stress Targeted Therapy in Ewing Sarcoma.
articles.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a rare pediatric cancer of the bone and soft tissue. Although the five-year survival rate of localized disease is relatively high, outcomes for patients with metastatic or recurrent disease are poor. Additionally, aggressive chemotherapy use in pediatric populations increases the risk of secondary complications. We have previously demonstrated the success of in vitro targeting of replication stress in EwS. Here, we evaluate this combination in vivo. Cell division cycle 7 (CDC7), also known as DBF4-dependent kinase (DDK), and WEE1 kinase inhibition was compared to EwS standard-of-care regimens. NSG mice received subcutaneous injections of the cell lines TC-32, A673, or RD-ES, or engraftments of SJEWS001321_X1 patient derived xenograft tissue, followed by three cycles of treatment. Arms with DDK inhibition (DDKi) + WEE1 inhibition + irinotecan (triplet arm) delivered with an optimized schedule were significantly more effective in acute reduction of tumor volume with durable reduction of volume compared to all other groups in TC-32 cell line derived xenografts (p < 0.01). Triplet arms with full dose or half dose irinotecan were equally effective (p > 0.05), suggesting that this strategy allows chemotherapeutic de-escalation. In an EwS patient derived xenograft, arms with DDKi + irinotecan were as effective as the triplet arm (p > 0.05). Replication stress targeted therapy with a chemotherapy backbone is more efficacious than comparable standard-of-care therapies and allows dose de-escalation of chemotherapy. Thus, this strategy is a promising potential therapeutic combination in Ewing sarcoma and should be considered for advancement to the clinic.

articles.title: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) is an effective targeted therapy for RAS-mutant neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children. Patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) high-risk (HR) NB exhibit poor outcomes despite intensive multimodal therapy. Although MAPK pathway activation is prominent in HRNB, FDA-approved MEK inhibitors and KRAS G12C inhibitors have shown limited preclinical single-agent activity in HRNB. Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), a potent and selective RAS(ON) inhibitor, has demonstrated activity in preclinical models and early-phase clinical trials of RAS-mutant adult cancers. A subset of R/R HRNB tumors harbors diverse RAS mutations, providing a rationale for investigating RMC-6236 in this setting. Here, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy and effects of oncogenic signaling modulation of RMC-6236 across NB models with RAS pathway activation. As a single agent, RMC-6236 significantly reduced cell viability, suppressed downstream MAPK signaling, increased expression of the MAPK pathway effector BIM, and induced cell death in RAS-mutant NB models as well as in NF1-mutant NB models. In vivo, RMC-6236 demonstrated on-target activity, significantly inhibited tumor growth, and extended survival in RAS-mutant HRNB mouse models. Furthermore, RMC-6236 induced BIM upregulation and promoted BIM:BCL-2 complexes in RAS-mutant NB. As such, the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax further potentiated RMC-6236-mediated killing by disrupting these complexes. Together, these findings identify RMC-6236 as a promising targeted therapy for RAS-mutant NB and support its clinical investigation, both as a single agent and in combination with venetoclax, in this patient population.

articles.title: Increasing Emergency Department Burden of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Injuries: A National 10-Year Analysis of Mechanisms and Severity Predictors, 2015-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) is a rapidly growing grappling-based combat sport, but emergency department (ED) surveillance and sport-specific mechanism classification are limited.
HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that BJJ-related ED visits have grown disproportionately compared with overall martial arts ED presentations and that sport-specific mechanisms predict nonroutine disposition.
STUDY DESIGN: Descriptive epidemiology study.
METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), 2015-2024. BJJ cases were identified from product code 3257, which corresponds to martial arts equipment and activity-related injuries, followed by a 2-reviewer narrative review. Trends were analyzed using survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression. An 11-category force vector mechanism taxonomy was developed from narratives. Pre- versus post-COVID eras were compared with false discovery rate correction. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of nonroutine disposition.
RESULTS: Of 7618 martial arts ED visits, 1448 (19.0%) were BJJ related (58,170 weighted national cases). Annual BJJ volume rose nearly 5-fold (incidence rate ratio, 1.148/year; 95% CI, 1.090-1.209; P < .001) while total martial arts volume remained stable; BJJ's share climbed from 7.3% to 27.7%. The cohort was 78.0% male (mean age 25.7 ± 12.3 years); pediatric patients (≤17 years) comprised 29.5%. Strain/sprain (23.2%), fracture (15.5%), and contusion/abrasion (9.3%) predominated. The taxonomy classified 69.8% of cases into 8 defined categories, led by direct impact (21.8%), joint torque (16.4%), and fall (11.2%), with the remaining 30.2% indeterminate; the era profile was stable after multiplicity correction. Four independent predictors of nonroutine disposition emerged: internal injury (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 20.62; 95% CI, 7.55-56.26), neck compression (aOR, 5.26; 95% CI, 1.84-14.98), fracture (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 1.30-10.90), and age (aOR, 1.50 per decade; 95% CI, 1.18-1.90); optimism-corrected C-statistic = 0.748.
CONCLUSION: Our study showed that BJJ-related ED presentations are rising rapidly while the injury profile remains stable; because denominators are unavailable, these are presentation counts rather than a measured change in per-capita injury risk. The injury taxonomy and disposition model further identified predictors of injury patterns and ED disposition. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective, exposure-denominated validation.

articles.title: Effects of enoxaparin sodium combined with magnesium sulfate on coagulation and pregnancy outcomes in early-onset preeclampsia with severe features: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine whether adding prophylactic-dose enoxaparin to magnesium sulfate is associated with coagulation and pregnancy outcomes in early-onset preeclampsia with severe features (EO-PE-SF) managed expectantly.
METHODS: Consecutive EO-PE-SF patients hospitalized from January 2021 to December 2023 who were eligible for expectant management with ≥5 days of observation and complete coagulation data were analyzed (n=200; 100 magnesium sulfate monotherapy, 100 combined therapy). Coagulation markers, angiogenic biomarkers, blood pressure, proteinuria, maternal and neonatal outcomes, and adverse events were compared using t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, analysis of covariance, multivariable regression, and propensity score matching.
RESULTS: Combined therapy was associated with lower post-treatment D-dimer (276.25±91.65 vs. 347.89±80.20 µg/L fibrinogen-equivalent units, P<0.001), more favorable soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1/placental growth factor profiles, lower blood pressure and proteinuria, and longer gestation at delivery (33.47±2.36 vs. 32.28±2.25 weeks, P<0.001). Unadjusted neonatal intensive care unit admission was lower in the combined group (51.0% vs. 76.0%, P<0.001) but not after adjustment (odds ratio 1.15, 95% confidence interval 0.45-2.90, P=0.775). Magnesium-related adverse effects did not differ significantly (13.0% vs. 9.0%, P=0.499).
CONCLUSIONS: In selected EO-PE-SF patients eligible for expectant management, combined prophylactic-dose enoxaparin and magnesium sulfate was associated with more favorable coagulation and angiogenic profiles and longer pregnancy prolongation. Randomized trials are needed before clinical practice changes.

articles.title: Construction of a management model based on traditional Chinese medicine comprehensive health management for a high-risk gestational diabetes mellitus population and its impact on postpartum diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) comprehensive health management program for high-risk pregnant women with gestational diabetes and evaluate its impact on postpartum diabetes.
METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 248 pregnant women from August 2024 to July 2025 (registration: ITMCTR2026000970). Participants were assigned to a control group (routine management, n=123) or an experimental group (TCM comprehensive health management, n=123). Glycemic parameters, islet function indicators, and lipid parameters, psychological scores, maternal-infant outcomes, and risk factors for postpartum diabetes were compared.
RESULTS: At baseline, no significant differences were observed between the groups in any indicator (P > 0.05). Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant main effects of time and group and significant time × group interaction effects (P < 0.05). After the intervention, FPG, 2hPG, and HbA1c significantly decreased in both groups (P < 0.05), with greater reductions in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Islet function indicators (FINS, C-P, and HOMA-IR) also declined significantly, with larger decrements observed in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Concurrently, TC, TG, and LDL-C decreased while HDL-C increased in both groups, all favoring the experimental group (P < 0.05). SAS and SDS scores decreased significantly, with more pronounced improvements in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses revealed a significant treatment-by-age interaction (P=0.034), with participants aged ≥ 35 years showing more pronounced glycemic improvements than those < 35 years. Among TCM constitution types, the Yin-deficiency subgroup exhibited significant between-group differences in glycemic benefits (P < 0.001), although the overall interaction across constitution types did not reach statistical significance (P=0.416). The experimental group further exhibited lower rates of cesarean section, pregnancy complications, and perinatal adverse outcomes (P < 0.05). At 6-month postpartum follow-up, FPG and 2hPG remained significantly lower in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified TCM management as an independent protective factor and family history of diabetes, pre-pregnancy BMI, and prenatal FPG and 2hPG as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSION: TCM comprehensive health management effectively improves glucose and lipid metabolism, enhances islet function, alleviates anxiety and depression, reduces maternal-infant complications, and lowers the risk of postpartum diabetes, with potential greater benefits observed in older pregnant women and those with Yin-deficiency constitution, although the age-related finding requires confirmation in future studies.

articles.title: Biologics for moderate-to-severe eosinophilic asthma in children: a network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric moderate-to-severe eosinophilic asthma (EA) is a severe refractory condition with limited response to conventional therapy. Although biologic agents offer new treatment options, comparative data on their efficacy and safety remains insufficient. This network meta-analysis evaluated Omalizumab, Mepolizumab, Benralizumab, Lebrikizumab, and Dupilumab in children with moderate-to-severe EA. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP databases was conducted up to March 31, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing these biologics with placebo or active control/standard care were included. The primary outcome was annual asthma exacerbation rate; secondary outcomes included FEV1 changes, adverse events (AEs), and serious adverse events (SAEs). Network meta-analyses were performed using a consistency model in Stata 16.0. Effect sizes are reported as risk ratios (RR) or standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals. Treatment rankings were based on SUCRA values. Thirteen RCTs (n = 3,269) were included. Dupilumab (RR = 0.34), Omalizumab (RR = 0.59), and Mepolizumab (RR = 0.73) significantly reduced exacerbations versus placebo. Dupilumab was associated with a lower exacerbation rate than Omalizumab (RR = 0.58) and Mepolizumab (RR = 0.47). SUCRA rankings favored Dupilumab (94.1%) for exacerbation reduction; however, as Dupilumab's ranking is based on a single trial, this probability carries high uncertainty and should not be equated with proven clinical superiority. Only Omalizumab significantly improved FEV1 (SMD = 1.00). Mepolizumab showed the highest AE risk, while Omalizumab had the best safety profile (SUCRA = 87.8%). SAE frequencies were comparable across treatments; however, due to extreme event sparsity across trials, these network estimates carry substantial statistical uncertainty and should be interpreted with caution. These comparative findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating given the limited study count, heterogeneity in control group background therapies, and lack of direct head-to-head trials. Preliminary indirect evidence suggests Dupilumab may hold potential advantages for exacerbation reduction, while Omalizumab shows tentative benefits for lung function and safety. Future head-to-head trials are required to confirm these tentative observations. Treatment selection must remain individualized.

articles.title: The predictive value of recurrent respiratory tract infection and serum ASO, D-D, IgA, β2-MG for renal injury in children with Henoch-Schonlein purpura.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the predictive value of recurrent respiratory tract infection (RRTI) and serum antistreptolysin O (ASO), D-dimer (D-D), immunoglobulin A (IgA) and β2-microglobulin (β2-MG) in renal injury in children with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (HSP).
METHODS: Clinical data of 252 children with HSP were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into renal injury and non-renal injury groups based on whether renal injury occurred. RRTI incidence and serum levels of ASO, D-D, IgA and β2-MG were compared between the groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to screen independent predictors. Internal validation was performed using Bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to evaluate model performance and clinical net benefit.
RESULTS: The incidence of RRTI and levels of serum ASO, D-D, IgA and β2-MG in the renal injury group were significantly higher than those in the non-renal injury group (P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis identified RRTI and elevated ASO, D-D, IgA, and β2-MG as independent predictors (P < 0.05). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.772, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.745 after bootstrap validation, significantly outperforming each single indicator. DCA confirmed that the combined model had the highest clinical net benefit within the risk threshold range of 0.1-0.9.
CONCLUSIONS: The five-indicator combined model demonstrates preliminary predictive potential as an early screening tool of HSP renal injury. However, further multi-center external validation is required to confirm its generalizability before routine clinical application.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of ultrasound elastography for assessing liver stiffness in children with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and biliary atresia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) in assessing liver stiffness in pediatric patients with NAFLD and in infants with biliary atresia (BA).
METHODS: In this retrospective study with case-control sampling, 129 children with NAFLD and 129 healthy controls, as well as 83 infants with BA and 83 age-matched infants with non-BA cholestasis, were enrolled. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was performed using 2D-SWE. Demographic, anthropometric, biochemical, and conventional ultrasound data were collected at enrollment.
RESULTS: In the NAFLD cohort, LSM was significantly higher in the NAFLD group than in healthy controls (4.42 ± 0.92 vs. 3.74 ± 0.28 kPa; P < 0.001), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.865 (95% CI: 0.820-0.910). All other metabolic, inflammatory, and ultrasound measurements also showed significant differences between the two groups (all P < 0.05), except for age, sex, total bilirubin, and direct bilirubin (P > 0.05). In the BA cohort, LSM was significantly higher in BA infants than in non-BA cholestasis infants (13.58 ± 8.46 vs. 6.31 ± 1.02 kPa; P < 0.001; AUC = 0.890, 95% CI: 0.865-0.935). BA infants also showed significantly elevated liver enzymes, bilirubin, inflammatory markers, and rates of gallbladder abnormality, splenomegaly, and ascites, as well as lower lipid levels (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: 2D-SWE provides good diagnostic accuracy for detecting liver stiffness in pediatric NAFLD and BA, supporting its use as a non-invasive assessment tool for group discrimination in these two distinct pediatric liver diseases.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of enuresis among primary school-aged children in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal enuresis (NE) is a common childhood condition that can cause psychological distress, social isolation, and impaired quality of life for affected children and their families. However, most previous studies have focused on children and adolescents as a whole, with limited evidence specifically for primary school-aged pupils.
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence and associated factors of NE among primary school students (5-12 years) in China.
METHODS: We searched the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, the China Science and Technology Journal Database, PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for cross-sectional studies on the prevalence and associated factors of NE in Chinese primary school children from inception to May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool prevalence estimates and odds ratios (ORs). Descriptive subgroup analyses and random-effects meta-regression were performed to explore heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 161,662 participants (11,091 NE cases) were included. The pooled prevalence of NE was 10% (95% CI: 9%-11%), which should be interpreted as a descriptive summary of the available data rather than a precise population estimate, given the substantial heterogeneity across studies (I2 = 100%). Descriptively, the prevalence was higher in males (9%) than in females (6%) and showed a downward trend with age, decreasing from 16% at age 5 to 2% at age 12. Meta-regression analysis indicated that diagnostic criteria alone did not account for the observed between-study heterogeneity (R2 = 0%, I2 res = 99.16%). Significant associated factors included male sex (OR = 1.48), family history of NE (OR = 2.60), constipation (OR = 1.85), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (OR = 2.63), arousal dysfunction (OR = 2.76), bedtime fluid intake (OR = 1.95), daytime symptoms (OR = 1.88), and living in households with three or more children (OR = 2.32), while older age was associated with lower odds of NE (OR = 0.76).
CONCLUSION: NE prevalence among Chinese primary school children is relatively high and influenced by multiple demographic, genetic, physiological, and environmental factors. Enhanced screening and comprehensive management for this population are warranted. However, given the persistent, massive heterogeneity (I2 = 100%) that remains unexplained by diagnostic criteria, this pooled prevalence should be interpreted with caution as a contextual descriptive summary rather than a single standardized parameter.

articles.title: Pain Pathophysiology and Assessment in Pediatric Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Pain is pervasive and affects upwards of 59% of critically ill children. Consequences of severe pain include worsened health related quality of life and longer lengths of stay. Evaluating pain in non-verbal critically ill children is a unique challenge due to difficulties with communication and the wide variety of developmental stages. The purpose of our review is to examine the underlying pathophysiology of pain, the current landscape in pain assessment of non-verbal critically ill children and pain assessment tools for non-verbal critically ill children. We performed literature searches from April 25, 2023 to November 20, 2025; we performed literature searches using PubMed and EMBASE with a combination of keywords that included "pain", "pathophysiology", "pediatric", "comfort-behavioral", "FLACC", "P-CPOT", "ventilated", "PICU". The pathophysiology of pain starts with inflammatory reactions at the site of injury, which are transmitted via the dorsal horn to the ascending spinothalamic tract and converge onto the brain using two separate pathways. There are three behavioral pain scales that have been validated in both ventilated and non-ventilated critically ill children: the faces, legs, activity, crying, and consolability scale; the COMFORT-Behavior scale; and the pediatric critical care pain observation tool. While pain assessments are regularly performed in PICUs worldwide, there still exist sites in which validated scales are not used, or no scales are used to evaluate pain. Pain is frequent among critically ill children, and its prompt identification can be challenging. Understanding the pathophysiology of pain and the barriers that clinicians face in identifying pain, particularly in non-verbal critically ill children, will improve the care of these patients.

articles.title: Seroepidemiological survey of Neospora caninum infection in dairy goats from Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil.
articles.abstract: Neosporosis is a significant veterinary parasitosis caused by coccidian species Neospora caninum. Parasitism by N. caninum can lead to important reproductive changes, such as abortion, stillbirth, and neonatal death in domestic ruminants like goats. Considering the foregoing, the aims of the current study are to determine the seroprevalence of N. caninum infection in dairy goats bred in farms in Rio de Janeiro State, and to identify possible risk factors for these animals. Blood samples were collected from 460 dairy goats bred in dairy farms in Niterói, Nova Friburgo, Sapucaia, Tanguá, Valença and Vassouras cities, Rio de Janeiro State, between October 2020 and December 2022. Serum samples were subjected to enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to investigate anti-N. caninum IgG antibodies based on using this protozoan's total soluble antigen. Producers answered a semi-structured questionnaire comprising data about epidemiological variables associated with the geographic features of their farm and with the zootechnical features of their herd, as well as with reproductive, nutritional and health management processes, and with milk production and offspring suckling, to assess risk factors for N. caninum infection. In total, 28% (129/460) of all assessed samples were seroreactive to IgG against N. caninum in ELISA test. Seropositivity frequency recorded for N. caninum ranged from 12.5% (25/200) to 81.1% (30/37) among the analyzed farms. The final logistic regression models have evidenced association between N. caninum seropositivity and sex, type of sheepfold floor, underweight offspring birth, veterinary care frequency and time spent suckling (p-value ≤ 0.05). Overall, high N. caninum infection seroprevalence in dairy goats bred in Rio de Janeiro State appears to be mainly determined by management practices. More specific prevention and control measures aimed at interrupting neosporosis epidemiological chain are extremely important to help reducing both economic and animal health impacts. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to report N. caninum infection seroprevalence in goats bred in Rio de Janeiro State.

articles.title: Molecular epidemiology, virulence gene profiles, and clinical outcomes of bovine Cryptosporidium in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. are major causes of neonatal calf diarrhea and represent a zoonotic concern. This study investigated Cryptosporidium occurrence, GP60 subtype distribution, and selected virulence-associated gene targets in bovine field samples from Türkiye. Fecal samples were collected from 83 diarrheic calves aged 5-30 days from 20 farms; after 16 of the sampled calves subsequently died, their respective asymptomatic dams were additionally sampled as an outcome-dependent, calf-associated group rather than as an independent control group. All 99 samples were screened by Kinyoun acid-fast staining, and the 76 microscopy-positive samples were subsequently subjected to SSU 18S rRNA nested PCR. Ten virulence-associated gene targets were screened by PCR, and GP60 subtyping was performed for all PCR-confirmed samples. Oocyst-like structures were detected in 76/99 samples (76.8%), and 74/76 (97.4%) microscopy-positive samples were confirmed by PCR. GP60 sequence analysis identified two C. parvum IIa subtype patterns: IIaA13G2R1 (58/74, 78.4%) and IIaA14G1R1 (16/74, 21.6%). In this dataset, IIaA13G2R1 was detected in all fatal calf cases and their asymptomatic dams, whereas IIaA14G1R1 was observed only among non-fatal diarrheic calves. GP60, COWP, Cp15, TRAP-C1, HSP70, HSP90, and aminopeptidase-like metalloprotease were detected in all 74 PCR-confirmed samples; cryptopain and cryptostatin were each detected in 65/74 samples (87.8%), and CDPK in 58/74 samples (78.4%). Among the variably detected targets, CDPK showed an exploratory association with calf outcome; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Apart from previous PCR-based work targeting COWP and Cp15, this study provides the first broader PCR-based profile of selected virulence-associated gene targets in bovine Cryptosporidium field samples from Türkiye. These findings represent preliminary molecular associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of gene expression, functional virulence, or causality.

articles.title: Maternal morphine exposure during lactation alters hippocampal morphology and Oprm1 expression in rat offspring: An experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal morphine use during lactation may affect neonatal brain development through drug transfer into breast milk.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of short-term maternal morphine exposure during lactation on hippocampal morphology and neurodevelopment-related gene expression in rat offspring.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This experimental study was conducted at Mazandaran University of Medical Sciences, Ramsar Campus, Ramsar, Iran in 2025. Adult lactating Sprague-Dawley rats (210-240 gr, 2-4 months) were randomly assigned to either the control or morphine-treated group. Lactating female rats in the treatment group received morphine sulfate (10 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) on postnatal days 4 and 5, whereas control animals received normal saline. On postnatal day 12, hippocampal tissues from their offspring (n = 6/group) were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction analyses. Immunohistochemical assessment included glial fibrillary acidic protein, S100 calcium-binding protein, and synaptophysin. Gene expression levels ofneuronal differentiation-1, synaptophysin, neurexin-1, and opioid receptor Mu 1 were quantified using the Δ Δ  Ct-2 method.
RESULTS: Histological examination revealed qualitative evidence of neuronal degeneration and inflammatory cell accumulation in the hippocampus of morphine-exposed offspring. Analysis demonstrated reduced immunoreactivity for glial fibrillary acidic protein, S100, andsynaptophysin immunoreactivity compared with controls. Gene expression analysis showed a significant reduction in Oprm1 expression (p = 0.0176). Although other genes examinedexhibited lower mean expression levels in the morphine-exposed group, these differences did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Short-term maternal morphine exposure during lactation was associated with hippocampal histopathological alterations and reduced Oprm1 expression in rat offspring. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health applications are increasingly integrated into antenatal care as supportive tools to enhance maternal knowledge, promote healthy behaviors, and improve clinical and psychosocial outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise evidence on the effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Web of Science, without language restrictions. Search terms included "mobile applications" and "pregnancy". This umbrella review synthesized evidence from 21 systematic reviews and meta-analyses published up to May 17, 2025, covering 180 randomized controlled trials with sample sizes ranging from 456-10,348 participants. The methodological quality of eligible articles was assessed using AMSTAR 2.
RESULTS: Findings consistently showed that mobile applications can improve maternal knowledge, self-management, physical activity, diet, weight control, and adherence to prenatal care recommendations.
