Positive effects were also reported for mental health, including reductions in stress and depressive symptoms, while evidence suggested decreased cesarean section rates, neonatal intensive care admissions, and adverse maternal-fetal outcomes. Despite encouraging results, the overall evidence is constrained by methodological limitations, heterogeneous app designs, small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and incomplete reporting, reducing the strength and generalizability of conclusions.
CONCLUSION: Mobile health interventions demonstrate considerable potential as complementary strategies in prenatal care. Future research should focus on high-quality, large-scale, long-term trials with culturally sensitive, personalized approaches. Strong collaboration among researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers is essential to fully harness the impact of mobile applications on maternal and neonatal health.

articles.title: Local Treatment for Perineal and Perianal Rhabdomyosarcoma: Clinical Practice Guidelines and Consensus Statement From the Children's Oncology Group, European Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma Study Group, the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe, and the International Soft Tissue Sarcoma Consortium.
articles.abstract: Local control of rhabdomyosarcoma in the perianal and perineal region (PRMS) is challenging due to the unfavorable tumor location, the often advanced stage of disease, the prevalence of alveolar histology with PAX3/FOXO1 fusion, and frequent regional lymph node (LN) involvement at presentation. Distant metastases are present at diagnosis in up to 49% of patients. Given the high risk of recurrence, the prognosis of patients with PRMS treated with multimodal treatment is poor, with a reported 5-year overall survival (OS) rate of 39%-52%. Due to the rarity of PRMS along with variations in treatment protocols over time and across different cooperative groups, we have developed consensus local treatment guidelines. This guideline is based on a comprehensive literature review and expert opinion and is endorsed by the International Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Consortium (INSTRuCT). It integrates insights from three leading pediatric oncology cooperative groups: the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe (CWS; since December 2024 part of European pediatric Soft-tissue sarcoma Study Group [EpSSG]), Children's Oncology Group (COG), and EpSSG. This document addresses surgical therapy options, including biopsy, nodal staging, and various resection modalities, as well as options for radiotherapy, such as intensity-modulated radiation therapy, proton beam therapy, and brachytherapy.

articles.title: Indocyanine Green Assists in Identification of Solid Tumor Pulmonary Metastases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The presence of pulmonary metastases reduces overall survival in patients with certain solid tumors; therefore, surgical clearance is crucial to cure for some types. This multi-institutional prospective study sought to determine the utility and diagnostic accuracy of indocyanine green (ICG) for delineating pulmonary metastases in diverse pediatric, adolescent, and young adult solid cancers.
PROCEDURE: Thirteen member institutions of the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative administered preoperative ICG to patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy for primary or recurrent solid tumor malignancy (2019-2023). Surgeons reported their perspective on ICG utility for pulmonary metastasectomy following each operation. The diagnostic accuracy of ICG fluorescence to identify a pathologically confirmed tumor-containing specimen was determined.
RESULTS: Of 829 specimens resected during 134 pulmonary metastasectomies (30.6% hepatic, 47.0% osteosarcoma, 17.2% non-osteosarcoma-type sarcomas ["other sarcomas"], 5.2% other non-hepatic and non-sarcoma tumor types ["other tumor types"]). Surgeons reported ICG as helpful in 77.6% of procedures. In 11.9% of cases, ICG identified viable metastases not visualized on preoperative imaging. Adjusted diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI]) for metastases from all tumor types was 80.7% (77.9%-83.3%) and 82.5% (78.9%-85.8%), respectively. By primary tumor histology, adjusted accuracy and sensitivity (95% CI) were 83.2% (74.4%-89.9%), 46.7% (28.3%-65.7%) for metastases from other sarcomas, 80.6% (75.3%-85.2%), 95.6% (91.8%-98.0%) for hepatic tumors, 80.6% (76.6%-84.2%), 77.1% (71.4%-82.2%) for osteosarcoma, and 72.7% (49.8%-89.3%), 60.0% (26.2%-87.8%) for other tumor types.
CONCLUSIONS: During pulmonary metastasectomy, adjusted diagnostic accuracy of ICG was 80.7%, and, importantly, 11.9% of metastasectomies contained viable tumors identified by ICG but not by preoperative imaging.

articles.title: Return to School and Readmission Risk After Pain-Related Hospitalizations in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain is the primary cause of inpatient admissions in sickle cell disease (SCD) and readmission is common. For school-aged youth, successful transition from the hospital necessitates school reentry. This study assessed rates of school return following a pain-related admission and the relationship between school return and readmission.
METHODS: Sixteen youth (7-17 years) admitted for SCD-related pain and caregivers completed daily surveys about school attendance and pain severity for 10 consecutive school days after discharge. Descriptive, independent samples t-test, and chi-square analyses were used to assess differences in pain, school attendance, and readmission.
RESULTS: On average, participants (age M = 13.75; 69% female; 75% HbSS) attended 6.13 out of 10 school days, with 25% returning the next school day after discharge and 13% attending all 10 days. Almost all (94%) reported ongoing pain throughout the monitoring period. Most youth (63%) exhibited variable school attendance after initial school return. Those with variable attendance attended fewer school days (M = 4.40, SD = 2.46) compared to "consistent school attenders" (M = 9, SD = 0.89), p < 0.001, and reported higher daily pain (MVariableAttenders = 3.78, SDVariableAttenders = 1.68; MConsistentAttenders = 1.47, SDConsistentAttenders = 0.81), p = 0.007. Half of "variable school attenders" were readmitted, compared to none of the consistent attenders, χ2 (df = 1) = 4.36, p = 0.037.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that school reentry after a pain-related hospitalization is difficult for many patients and essential to consider in discharge planning. Youth continue reporting pain following discharge, with some experiencing variable school attendance and readmission for pain. Promoting school attendance should be a core component of comprehensive SCD management plans, with implications for pain management and healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Multimodality Care and Survival in Adolescents and Young Adults With Metastatic Non-Rhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma in California.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 20% of adolescents and young adults (AYA: ages 15-39) with non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma (NRSTS) are diagnosed with metastatic disease, which has a dismal prognosis. Optimal care is critical to improve outcomes, but there is no consensus on the best management approach. We sought to evaluate multimodality care (MMC) and survival among AYAs with metastatic NRSTS.
METHODS: We identified AYAs diagnosed during 2004-2022 with metastatic NRSTS in the California Cancer Registry. We defined MMC as first-line treatment receipt of surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation per the Children's Oncology Group ARST0332 protocol. We used multivariable logistic regression to evaluate associations of sociodemographic and clinical factors with receipt of MMC, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression to examine the impact of MMC on overall survival.
RESULTS: Of the 726 AYAs with metastatic NRSTS, 14% received MMC. A larger proportion of patients 15-25 years old who were treated by pediatric (vs. medical) oncologists received chemotherapy (96% vs. 75%), radiation (53% vs. 34%), and chemoradiation (51% vs. 25%). Older age (>21 years) was associated with decreased odds of receiving MMC. In patients ages 15-25, treatment by a pediatric (vs. medical) oncologist was associated with higher odds of receiving MMC (odds ratio [OR] = 3.4, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.33-8.72). Median overall survival was longer for patients receiving MMC (2.1 vs. 1.1 years), although associations did not remain statistically significant in the multivariable-adjusted model (HR = 0.89, CI = 0.68-1.16). Receiving all care at a specialized cancer center was associated with improved overall survival (HR = 0.63, CI = 0.49-0.81).
CONCLUSION: We found that only 14% of AYAs with metastatic NRSTS received MMC, which was impacted by age at diagnosis and physician specialty. Future research should investigate decision-making in patients with metastatic NRSTS and their providers, and its impact on outcomes.

articles.title: First Report of Gene Therapy in a Patient With Hemoglobin SC Disease.
articles.abstract: Gene therapy in patients with severe sickle cell disease has been recently approved for commercial use, even in children. Clinical trials leading to approval were limited to patients with hemoglobin SS and Sβ0, due to the severity of disease in these patients. The efficacy of gene therapy in patients with hemoglobin SC disease is unknown. We provide details on treatment and clinical course of the first hemoglobin SC patient treated with gene therapy due to the severity of symptoms and the absence of any viable treatment options that could provide relief from the ravages of the disease.

articles.title: A Phase IB Study to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of Nivolumab or Nivolumab With Azacitidine in Patients With Recurrent, Resectable Osteosarcoma: A Report From the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relapse rates following complete surgical resection (CSR) of pulmonary osteosarcoma recurrence remain high. We hypothesized that PD-1 inhibition with nivolumab (Nivo) combined with epigenetic priming using azacitidine (5-Aza) would be safe and augment systemic immune activation in patients with resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse.
METHODS: This Phase I trial sought to establish the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of perioperative Nivo/5-Aza in patients ≤39 years old with isolated, resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse. Three dose levels (DLs) were studied using a modified 3 + 3 design with dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) assessed from Day 1 of therapy to CSR. Patients received biweekly Nivo 3 mg/kg alone (DL1) or with 5-Aza at 60 or 75 mg/m2/day (DL2 and DL3) in 28-day cycles.
RESULTS: Twenty patients received therapy; 18 were evaluable for DLTs. DL3 exceeded the maximum tolerated dose (Grade 3 vomiting, prolonged Grade 4 neutropenia). Common adverse events included anemia, neutropenia, and nausea. Seventeen patients (85%) reached CSR after neoadjuvant therapy. Median event-free survival (EFS) was 3.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7-7.7 months), and median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% CI: 10.1-42.6 months). Combination therapy was associated with evidence of systemic immune activation, including increases in IFN-γ, IL-1α, IL-1β, and CCL5.
CONCLUSION: The RP2D was Nivo 3 mg/kg and 5-Aza 60 mg/m2/day on Days 1-5 and 8-9. The combination was feasible and tolerable. EFS was limited in the context of a Phase I trial. These findings provide safety, feasibility, and exploratory immunologic data to inform future immunotherapy trials in osteosarcoma.

articles.title: Timing of Eltrombopag Initiation and Treatment-Free Remission in Children With Persistent and Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Retrospective Tertiary-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eltrombopag is an established second-line therapy for children with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), but treatment-free remission after discontinuation and its relationship with treatment timing remain insufficiently defined. We evaluated eltrombopag outcomes, focusing on initiation timing and time to treatment-free remission.
PROCEDURE: This retrospective tertiary-center cohort included children with persistent or chronic ITP followed from December 2014 to December 2024. Of 81 patients, 41 received eltrombopag. Treatment-free remission was defined as maintaining a platelet count ≥50 × 109/L for at least six consecutive months without ITP-directed treatment and without bleeding or other clinical symptoms. Persistent- versus chronic-phase initiation was compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and the log-rank test.
RESULTS: Overall, platelet response was achieved in 36/41 patients (88%), sustained platelet response in 23/41 (56%), and treatment-free remission in 14/41 (34%). In the 40-patient timing cohort, time to treatment-free remission was shorter with persistent-phase initiation than with chronic-phase initiation (log-rank p = 0.027); Kaplan-Meier estimated median times were 28 and 78 months, respectively. Among patients achieving treatment-free remission, a longer diagnosis-to-eltrombopag interval was associated with a longer eltrombopag-to-remission interval (rho = 0.543, p = 0.045, n = 14). Adverse events occurred in 8/41 patients (20%), with no permanent discontinuations.
CONCLUSIONS: Eltrombopag was associated with high platelet response rates and treatment-free remission in approximately one-third of treated children. Persistent-phase initiation was associated with shorter time to treatment-free remission than chronic-phase initiation. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine whether earlier eltrombopag initiation is associated with a higher likelihood of, or shorter time to, treatment-free remission.

articles.title: Late Effects of 131I-MIBG in Survivors of High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Meta-iodobenzylguanidine radiolabeled with iodine-131 (131I-MIBG) is used to treat high-risk neuroblastoma (HRNBL). Late toxicities of 131I-MIBG have not been well studied due to limited survival of patients receiving this therapy for relapsed disease.
METHODS: The Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN study evaluated HRNBL survivors diagnosed after 2000 and alive at least 5 years from diagnosis. Clinical history and the prevalence of late effects were summarized for participants treated with 131I-MIBG (cases). Participants who did not receive 131I-MIBG were randomly selected and matched by age at diagnosis and relapse history (controls) in a 1:2 case-control study design. Chi-squared analysis was used to evaluate the association between 131I-MIBG and late toxicities.
RESULTS: Of 375 participants in the LEAHRN analytic cohort, 32 (8.5%) received 131I-MIBG. Differences in the proportion with thyroid toxicity and growth failure were observed but not statistically significant. The proportions of other major organ toxicities were not different between cases and controls, including subsequent malignancy.
DISCUSSION: No statistically significant differences were identified in the burden of late toxicities for HRNBL survivors treated with and without 131I-MIBG. A small sample size likely limited the ability to detect statistically significant differences. Our data provide information for follow-up care of 131I-MIBG-treated survivors and clinical trial design.

articles.title: Total Serum IgG Is a Poor Surrogate for Pneumococcal Protection Following Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with sickle cell disease (SCD) have functional asplenia and a higher risk of invasive pneumococcal disease. While allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative, post-transplant immune reconstitution is heterogeneous. Total serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) is widely used to gauge humoral recovery yet may not reflect pneumococcal serotype-specific seroprotection.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with SCD who underwent myeloablative matched sibling donor HSCT at Texas Children's Hospital between 2005 and 2024 and obtained pneumococcal serotype-specific antibody titers at approximately 1 year. Seroprotection was defined as an antibody concentration ≥1.3 µg/mL in ≥70% of 14 tested serotypes. Longitudinal total IgG, IgA, IgM, tetanus titers, and lymphocyte subsets (CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, CD19+) were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and penalized multivariable logistic regression were performed (n = 51).
RESULTS: Of 51 patients, 32 (62.7%) achieved pneumococcal serotype-specific protection at approximately 1 year. Total IgG correlated weakly with protection at all time points (r = 0.28-0.38). Day +365 total IgG did not differ between protected and unprotected patients (p = 0.134); at commonly used thresholds between 400 and 600 mg/dL, sensitivity was 97%, but specificity was 0%, and all unprotected patients exceeded 600 mg/dL. Day +365 IgG showed limited discrimination (AUC 0.63). Broad quantitative lymphocyte subsets were also not significantly correlated with the proportion of protective pneumococcal serotypes. No invasive pneumococcal disease occurred during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Normal total serum IgG does not reliably identify pneumococcal serotype-specific seroprotection after HSCT in pediatric SCD. Serotype-specific antibody assessment provides information not captured by total IgG alone.

articles.title: Caregiver Primary Language and Barriers to Care at Diagnosis of Pediatric Acute Leukemia.
articles.abstract: Timely diagnosis is critical in pediatric acute leukemia. This study evaluated the relationship between caregiver primary language, access to care, and disease acuity among 62 children with acute myeloid leukemia or acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated at two children's hospitals. The languages evaluated were primarily English and Spanish. The validated Barriers to Care Questionnaire measured access to care across five domains: pragmatics, skills, expectations, marginalization, and knowledge-and-beliefs. Leukemia disease acuity was assessed using laboratory markers. Caregivers with a primary language other than English reported greater skills-related barriers and their children presented more frequently with hyperuricemia, potentially indicating higher leukemia burden and acuity. These findings highlight language-related navigation barriers as potential contributors to healthcare access.

articles.title: Real-world safety profiles of newer antiseizure medications: A pharmacovigilance study based on FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the post-marketing safety of four newer antiseizure medications (ASMs)-brivaracetam (BRV), cannabidiol (CBD), cenobamate (CNB), and fenfluramine (FFA).
METHODS: A pharmacovigilance study was conducted using data from the FAERS database (Q1 2016-Q4 2024). Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect adverse event (AE) signals using three algorithms. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, reporter, and treatment strategy. We employed multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for covariates including age, sex, weight, dose, and concomitant medications, to validate associations between ASMs and specific AEs and to identify potential influencing factors. Bayesian network analysis was conducted to explore conditional dependencies among variables. Hospitalization risk was evaluated based on system organ classes.
RESULTS: After data cleaning, 13 763 reports were included. We identified 308 positive preferred term (PT) signals. Seizure-related AEs were frequently reported. All four ASMs had the PT of seizure cluster, with each exhibiting distinct AE profiles: BRV with psychiatric disorders, CBD with gastrointestinal events, CNB with visual dysfunction, and FFA with valvular heart disease (VHD). Children had higher reporting odds of seizure with BRV and CBD, while reporting odds of FFA-related VHD were lower in children; polytherapy was associated with higher reporting odds of somnolence, and AE reporting patterns varied by reporter source. Both CBD-related gastrointestinal events and FFA-related cardiac events exhibited dose-dependent effects. Infection-related AEs were associated with higher odds of hospitalization for multiple ASMs.
SIGNIFICANCE: This study comprehensively characterizes the safety profiles of newer ASMs and highlights the importance of tailored AE monitoring based on specific ASM and patient characteristics.

articles.title: Preserved Right Ventricular Function With Early Remodeling in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease: Comprehensive Echocardiographic Assessment and Longitudinal Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity in sickle cell disease (SCD), but right ventricular (RV) involvement in children remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to assess RV structure and function in pediatric SCD using conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography, and to examine associations with clinical features, hydroxyurea use, hemolysis markers, and longitudinal changes.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of children with SCD followed at a single tertiary center from 2015 to 2023. Clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected, and age- and sex-matched healthy children served as controls. Echocardiographic assessment included RV dimensions, systolic indices, tricuspid regurgitant velocity (TRv), and RV free-wall strain.
RESULTS: A total of 185 children were included (118 with SCD and 67 controls; mean age, 11.7 ± 5.3 years). Compared with controls, children with SCD had larger RV dimensions, slightly lower RV fractional area change, and higher TRv, whereas RV free-wall strain remained largely preserved. RV strain correlated with age, RV size, fractional area change, and TRv, but not with hydroxyurea use, anemia, hemolysis markers, or most clinical complications. RV indices were similar across genotypes. Elevated TRv (≥2.5 m/s) was present in 12.9% of patients. Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated stable RV function over time.
CONCLUSIONS: Children with SCD exhibit subtle RV remodeling and mildly increased pulmonary pressure despite preserved RV systolic function. These findings suggest that early right-heart changes in pediatric SCD are predominantly structural and hemodynamic rather than functional.

articles.title: How well does spirometry capture the symptom range in primary ciliary dyskinesia? A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) present a variety of respiratory symptoms. Spirometry, particularly forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), is the most commonly used outcome measure in clinical follow-up; however, it is not known how well it captures the range of respiratory symptoms experienced by patients.
METHODS: We sent the FOLLOW-PCD questionnaire to all patients registered in the Swiss PCD Registry (to the parents of those aged <14 years) asking about upper and lower respiratory symptoms. In patients who had had a routine lung function done within a year of survey completion, we extracted data from clinical records and calculated spirometric indices z-scores based on the Global Lung Function Initiative references. We used linear regression to study associations between FEV1, forced vital capacity (FVC), FEV1/FVC and frequency of respiratory symptoms, adjusted for age, sex and regular physiotherapy.
RESULTS: Of 99 patients invited, 64 (67%) completed the survey; for 54 of them (median age: 24 years, IQR: 15-47; 50% females) we also had an FEV1 measurement (mean z-score -2.29 [-3.37 to -1.03]), with 2.2 month median time between survey and lung function test. Patients reporting wheezing (76%) had lower FEV1 and FEV1/FVC z-scores (FEV1 z-score for infrequent and frequent wheezing compared to no wheezing: -1.13 [95% CI: -2.13 to -0.12] and -1.11 [-2.20 to -0.20], respectively). Similarly patients reporting frequent shortness of breath (29.5%) also had lower FEV1 and FEV1/FVC z-scores (FEV1 z-score for frequent shortness of breath compared to no shortness of breath: -1.27 [-2.50 to -0.04]). We found no signs of an association between reported nasal symptoms, snoring, coughing, sputum production and chest pain with FEV1, FVC or FEV1/FVC.
CONCLUSION: In our study, self-reported wheezing and frequent shortness of breath were associated with lower FEV1 and FEV1/FVC, commonly used for patient follow-up. However, we need additional outcome measures, e.g. lung clearance index, imaging outcomes or upper airway assessments, together with regular and standardised assessment of patient-reported symptoms, to capture the range of respiratory morbidity patients with PCD experience in daily life and guide management successfully.

articles.title: Transfer to adult care - experiences of young adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Jamaica.
articles.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has improved health outcomes for adolescents living with the human Immunodeficiency Virus (ALHIV). Long-term survival necessitates effective interventions for optimal continuity of care as they transition to adult healthcare. No National Transition Policy for adolescents with chronic illnesses exists in Jamaica, despite anecdotal reports of informal, site-specific processes for their transfer from pediatric to adult care settings. We present qualitative evaluative feedback from eleven young adults living with HIV (YALHIV) (18-34 years old) post-transfer from pediatric to adult care. Identified themes included: (1) perceptions of transfer - apprehension and uncertainty, (2) barriers to transfer - remorse about moving to adult clinics, stigma, loss of bond with providers, lack of communication, (3) facilitators - greater personal responsibility, shorter wait times with flexible scheduling at the adult clinic, (4) self-management (adherence to clinic visits and antiretroviral medication) and (5) recommendations - enhanced collaboration between pediatric and adult healthcare providers (HCP), pre-transfer exposure to the adult clinic, and increased psychoeducation pre- and post-transfer. These qualitative findings inform the transition process for YALHIV, which should be optimized through early, continual disclosure of diagnosis and enhanced psychoeducation for clients, while fostering a collaborative approach between pediatric and adult healthcare providers.

articles.title: Feasibility of implementing a digital peer-support intervention aimed at reducing HIV-related stigma among adolescents and young adults living with HIV in south Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Adolescents and young adults living with HIV (AYLHIV) experience a high burden of HIV-related stigma, but there are limited data on the interventions needed to reduce stigma. We assessed the feasibility of a planned Telegram-based peer-support intervention to reduce HIV-related stigma among AYLHIV in south Ethiopia. Eighteen AYLHIV (15-22 years old) were recruited from three public hospitals. The nine-week intervention was delivered via Telegram Messenger following an initial digital skill orientation, irrespective of prior experience of using the mobile application. In a mixed-methods design, we collected data using semi-structured face-to-face interviews and focus group discussions and reported feasibility outcomes using Bowen et al.'s framework. Participants described the discussion platform as private, safe, and supportive, with a family-like atmosphere. Retention was high (94.4%) and the overall scheduled-session attendance rate was 67.6%. Participants exchanged 4,033 messages, with an average of 13 messages per participant per session. Contextual, operational, and technical barriers may have reduced engagement; participants also provided recommendations to improve future intervention. Overall, the Telegram Messenger-based digital peer-support intervention appears feasible and acceptable across key feasibility domains, supporting progression to an evaluation of intervention effectiveness.Abbreviations: AYLHIV: adolescents and young adults living with HIV; ART: antiretroviral therapy; ARV: antiretroviral; EAT: East Africa Time; GB: gigabyte(s); HIV: human immunodeficiency virus; IT: information technology; mHealth: mobile health; MRC: Medical Research Council; SD: standard deviation.

articles.title: Olfactory Disorders in Children: A Clinical Approach to Aetiologies, Psychophysical Testing and Therapeutics.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Olfaction is a critical physiological function, yet paediatric olfactory dysfunction remains poorly characterized compared to adult populations. This narrative review aims to synthesize current knowledge regarding the aetiology, diagnosis and management of olfactory disorders in children to provide a practical guide for general paediatricians and otolaryngologists.
METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/Medline, Scopus and Embase. A total of 425 peer-reviewed clinical trials, observational studies and guidelines focusing on paediatric olfaction were evaluated and 41 highly relevant articles were included.
RESULTS: The exact prevalence of paediatric olfactory disorders remains unclear, though it is highly underdiagnosed. Unlike adult presentations, paediatric aetiologies are predominantly congenital (accounting for roughly two-thirds of cases, such as Kallmann syndrome), while acquired causes (traumatic brain injury, post-viral) account for one-third. Diagnostic modalities must be age-appropriately tailored; tools like the 'U-Sniff' or 'Smell Wheel' are required for younger children, alongside high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to evaluate olfactory bulb aplasia. Therapies range from surgical correction for conductive losses to targeted olfactory training for sensorineural deficits.
CONCLUSION: Olfactory disorders in children carry potential safety and developmental consequences. Implementing age-adapted testing and systematic clinical pathways is essential for improving diagnosis and patient outcomes in paediatric practice.

articles.title: Early-Life Movement Behaviour Patterns and Later Clinically Diagnosed Obesity: A Longitudinal Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the longitudinal association between early-life movement behaviour patterns and later clinically diagnosed obesity.
METHOD: In the population-based All Babies in Southeast Sweden (ABIS) cohort, 16 415 children were included after consent. A total of 542 participants had an obesity diagnosis recorded in the Swedish National Patient Register through 2023. Questionnaire-based movement behaviour data were collected at ages 3, 5, 8, 10-12 and 17-23 years. A Total Activity Score (TAS) combining physical activity and sedentary behaviours was used to classify participants as less active or highly active. Cox proportional hazards regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for maternal education and parental body mass index.
RESULTS: Higher TAS was associated with a lower hazard of clinically diagnosed obesity from age 5 onwards. Adjusted HRs for highly active versus less active participants were 0.85 (0.62-0.97, p = 0.003) at age 5, 0.66 (0.43-0.78, p = 0.002) at age 8, 0.54 (0.38-0.67, p = 0.001) at age 10-12 and 0.49 (0.23-0.59, p = 0.001) at age 17-23. Associations were observed in both sexes, without formal interaction testing.
CONCLUSION: Favourable childhood movement behaviour patterns were associated with a lower hazard of clinically diagnosed obesity.

articles.title: Adolescent Growth Spurt in Boys Analysed by the Infancy-Childhood-Puberty Growth Model.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the effects of growth hormone and sex steroids on height gain during puberty by applying the infancy-childhood-puberty growth model.
METHODS: To isolate the effects of both growth hormones and sex steroids, we analysed data from the Solna growth study. This cohort study was performed in Solna, Sweden from 1954 to 1983.
RESULTS: The results showed that the pubertal growth spurt represents two isolated endocrine elements: growth hormone and sex steroids. The two elements exhibited an additive effect. The pre-pubertal growth, related to the effect of growth hormone, continues in a decelerating manner during adolescence. Additional growth related to sex steroids is independent of the timing of puberty.
CONCLUSION: The infancy-childhood-puberty growth model is currently the only model that can dissect the growth curve from birth to adulthood into biological elements representing different endocrine stages.

articles.title: A Pilot Study of Peer-Delivered Sun Safety Education: Impact on Elementary Students' Dermatologic Knowledge and Melanoma Identification Skills.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Skin cancer is the most common cancer affecting Americans, with sun exposure during childhood playing a major role in skin cancer development. Traditional adult-delivered sun safety programs face engagement limitations, while peer-delivered education may enhance learning through social modeling and relatability.
OBJECTIVES: To present the results of a pilot study evaluating the preliminary effectiveness of a peer-delivered sun safety education program in improving elementary students' comprehensive dermatologic knowledge, including skin anatomy, melanoma identification skills, and sun protection knowledge.
METHODS: In this single-site pilot study, forty-six elementary students (22 third-graders, 24 fifth-graders) completed a comprehensive 9-item knowledge assessment immediately before and after a peer-delivered skin and sun education presentation. Two trained student presenters delivered content covering skin anatomy, ultraviolet radiation, physical versus chemical sunscreens, sun protection strategies, and melanoma ABCs with visual examples. The assessment evaluated anatomical knowledge, sunscreen science, melanoma identification skills, and sun safety knowledge; two additional unscored behavioral questions (sunburn history and intention to protect the skin) were also asked.
RESULTS: In this pilot sample, both grades demonstrated statistically significant improvements with very large effect sizes. Third-graders improved from 5.73 to 8.41 out of 9 points (p<0.001, Cohen's dz=2.29). Fifth-graders improved from 6.42 to 8.75 points (p<0.001, dz=2.08). Overall, 93.5% of students showed improved knowledge.
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary pilot study, peer-to-peer education was associated with significant immediate improvements in sun safety knowledge among elementary students. However, given the small sample size (n = 46) and single-site, uncontrolled design, these findings are hypothesis-generating. Further evaluation in larger, multi-site, controlled studies is needed before broader conclusions about the generalizability or superiority of this peer education model can be drawn. This pilot may inform the design of future school-based melanoma prevention research.

articles.title: Hyperkeratotic Halo Nevus in Childhood: Three Cases with Standard and UV Dermoscopic Documentation and Narrative Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Halo nevus (HN) is a benign melanocytic lesion with a peripheral depigmented halo due to immune-mediated regression. A rare hyperkeratotic pediatric variant may precede halo development, posing a diagnostic challenge.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical and dermoscopic features of hyperkeratotic halo nevus (HHN) in children.
METHODS: We performed a narrative literature review and reported a case series of three children evaluated with clinical examination, dermoscopy, and UV dermoscopy. Screening for autoimmune diseases included thyroid function, anti-thyroid antibodies, and celiac serology.
RESULTS: Three Caucasian children (mean age 9 years) presented with multiple asymptomatic hyperkeratotic halo nevi, mainly on the trunk (Fitzpatrick II). Diagnosis was based on clinical and dermoscopic findings; biopsy was not required. Thyroid function and celiac serology were unremarkable in all patients, while one patient showed positive anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies despite normal thyroid function. UV dermoscopy enhanced visualization of perilesional depigmentation and showed increased central reflectance, which we interpreted as a possible keratin-related optical phenomenon.
CONCLUSIONS: HHN is a rare but benign variant of HN that can be diagnosed clinically when dermoscopic features are reassuring. UV dermoscopy may provide complementary information by enhancing visualization of perilesional depigmentation; the observed increased central reflectance may represent a keratin-related optical phenomenon, although this interpretation requires further validation.

articles.title: Eruptive Melanocytic Nevi in a 11-Year-Old Girl Following Stevens-Johnson Syndrome: Case Report and Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Eruptive melanocytic nevi (EMN) are melanocytic nevi occurring in a short time interval. EMN may be idiopathic or triggered by dermatological conditions and/or systemic treatments.
OBJECTIVES: We report the case of an 11-year-old female patient developing EMN after a bullous eruption, and performed a systematic review of current literature, focusing on pediatric EMN both idiopathic and dermatologically triggered.
METHODS: A literature search, using PubMed database and following PRISMA guidelines, was carried out, including all records up to the 6th of June 2025. Inclusion criteria were: English language, human subjects, age </= 18 years, idiopathic or dermatologically triggered EMN, detailed clinical data.
RESULTS: 30 pediatric patients with EMN were included in the review. Idiopathic cases accounted for 7 patients, while a clear dermatological cause was reported in 22/30 patients. Of note one patient developed EMN after Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) without previous skin involvement. A complete clinical correspondence between previous lesions and EMN has been found in 6/11 patients with a history of previous bullous eruption, and only in 2/7 patients with LCH displaying skin involvement. Histological examination in 25/30 patients revealed compound or junctional nevi, with no cases of melanoma.
CONCLUSIONS: Even if patients undergoing severe bullous eruptions frequently receive systemic immunosuppressive treatments, the high level of anatomic correspondence between bullous lesions and subsequent EMN seems to suggest an etiological link between the disruption of the cutaneous basement membrane and the melanocytic proliferation. Conversely, in LCH, EMN may be triggered by both cutaneous lesions and systemic treatments. Melanoma occurs rarely among EMN, although follow-up is recommended.

articles.title: Pediatric Head and Neck Abscesses: Trends in Bacteriology and Susceptibility.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate changes in bacterial organisms and susceptibility patterns in head and neck abscesses in pediatric patients at the University of Chicago.
STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional retrospective chart review from January 2016 to December 2024.
SETTING: Chart review conducted among patients in a single, urban, academic institution.
METHODS: 153 pediatric patients under the age of 18 who underwent incision and drainage of head and neck abscesses at the University of Chicago were identified. The following demographic information was collected from each chart: age, sex, race, location of abscess, antimicrobial treatment prior to surgery, as well as the organisms that grew from each culture. We compared the data obtained from our current review to that published in a prior study from our institution in 2006. A chi-square test was used, and significance for the confidence intervals was set at P < .05.
RESULTS: There were no significant changes in the number of abscesses in which organisms were detected or in the patterns of growth, including the proportions of Staphylococcus aureus and non-S. aureus growth.
CONCLUSION: Our study shows a similar proportion of MRSA organisms isolated from pediatric head and neck abscesses compared to our earlier study from 2006. Ninety-one percent of MRSA cases at our institution were still susceptible to clindamycin, reaffirming the fact that this antibiotic is still a dependable choice for empiric treatment. However, the results suggest a tendency towards increasing clindamycin resistance in both MRSA and MSSA organisms which should be monitored carefully.

articles.title: Pediatric Musculoskeletal Emergencies: A Primer for Practicing Radiologists.
articles.abstract: Acute musculoskeletal conditions are a frequent cause of pediatric emergency imaging. In children, skeletal immaturity and open physes influence injury patterns, predisposing to unique fracture types. Incomplete ossification and growth plate anatomy may obscure or mimic pathology, complicating interpretation. Beyond trauma, musculoskeletal infections are also common reasons for pediatric emergency visits. Radiographs remain the first-line imaging modality, while ultrasound, CT, and MR imaging are important problem solving modalities. Clear understanding of age-related patterns of musculoskeletal injury and infection, normal anatomic variants, and imaging pitfalls allows accurate assessment of various acute musculoskeletal conditions in the pediatric population.

articles.title: Abdominopelvic Imaging Emergency in Children: A Comprehensive Update and Review.
articles.abstract: Abdominopelvic emergencies are one of the most common causes of pediatric emergency department visits, frequently resulting in urgent surgical management. Because conditions such as midgut, volvulus and torsion are time-sensitive, accurate and timely diagnosis is essential and imaging evaluation plays a crucial role. Following abdominal radiograph, ultrasound remains the preferred next imaging modality in most conditions to avoid radiation, even more so with the introduction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Advancements in computed tomography and MRI continue to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient safety. This article provides an up-to-date review of current imaging protocols and imaging characteristics of pediatric abdominopelvic emergency conditions.

articles.title: Pediatric Thoracic Imaging Emergency: Practical Approach for Daily Practice.
articles.abstract: Imaging of thoracic emergencies in children is crucial for early diagnosis, guiding treatment, and avoiding severe complications. Radiography, ultrasound, and computed tomography are the most common modalities in emergency imaging. Radiologists should be familiar with the appropriate choice of imaging modality and the radiologic characteristics of serious conditions that can present acutely in the pediatric emergency room. This article discusses a practical overview of the major pediatric thoracic emergencies, including pulmonary infections, airway abnormalities, neoplasms, air leaks, traumatic injuries, and foreign bodies. An up-to-date review of key imaging findings is provided, with emphasis on features that are unique to children.

articles.title: Neonatal Imaging Emergencies: Essential Considerations for General Radiologists.
articles.abstract: Neonatal emergencies comprise a diverse group of congenital and acquired conditions that require prompt diagnosis and intervention to minimize morbidity and mortality. Imaging plays a critical role in the evaluation of these disorders, with radiography remaining the cornerstone of initial assessment in the neonatal intensive care unit. Familiarity with the imaging appearances of emergent neonatal conditions is essential for radiologists. This article reviews the key imaging findings of neonatal emergencies, which can be categorized into pulmonary, cardiomediastinal, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, diaphragmatic, and catheter-related emergencies.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Emergency Radiology: Where Do We Stand Now?
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in pediatric emergency radiology, where timely and accurate image interpretation is critical. Current evidence highlights its strongest role in detection and localization tasks across neuroimaging, thoracic, abdominopelvic, and musculoskeletal studies. AI also shows promise for classification, severity assessment, and workflow prioritization, improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in some settings. However, existing research is limited by retrospective designs, small datasets, insufficient external validation, and poor transferability of adult-trained models. Pediatric-specific models, multicenter validation, prospective studies, and thoughtful clinical integration are needed before wider adoption beyond assistive use in routine pediatric emergency imaging practice today.

articles.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock.
SETTING: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025.
PATIENTS: Patients 0-18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1-3 on days 1-2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0-6] vs. 5 [1-7] T2 vs. 5 [2-7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = -0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

articles.title: Residents' Ventilator Management Performance in an Online Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Case Scenario: Secondary Analysis of the Game-Based Education in Residency Study, 2015-2017.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate resident performance in an online pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) case scenario of mild/moderate severity, with the provision of individualized feedback.
DESIGN: A secondary analysis of the Game-based Education in Residency study.
SETTING: The dataset comprised residents in their first clinical rotation in any of 28 international PICUs, recruited between October 2015 and December 2017.
SUBJECTS: Residents who used the online mechanical ventilation (MV) simulator and completed PARDS tasks were included in the analysis.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The simulated MV parameters analyzed among 125 residents were positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), Fio2, tidal volume (Vt), peak inspiratory pressure (PIP), Pao2, and pH. Residents' MV selections in relation to recommended scoring goals were: median (interquartile range [IQR]) PEEP, below or in the lower range (8 cm H2O [IQR, 7-8 cm H2O]); median Fio2, above or in the higher range (60% [IQR, 51-60%]); and median Vt, within range (5.36 mL/kg [IQR, 4.98-5.73 mL/kg]). Residents had higher than recommended median Pao2 (93 mm Hg [IQR, 83-99 mm Hg]), pH (7.37 [IQR, 7.33-7.40]), and median PIP (30 cm H2O [IQR, 28-31 cm H2O]). Progress through the case scenario was associated with greater odds (odds ratio [OR] and 95% CI) of adherence to goals in PEEP, Fio2, and Vt: PEEP (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.65-4.34; p < 0.001); Fio2 (OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.29-4.76; p = 0.007); and Vt (OR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.11-6.38; p = 0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: In an international PICU residents' educational dataset from 2015 to 2017, we found that progression through the simulated PARDS case was associated with greater odds of adherence to PEEP, Fio2, and Vt goals, which suggests that repeated practice and individualized feedback were of benefit. However, residents did not wean Fio2 or MV parameters when Pao2 and pH were above goal. These results may help educators design contemporary MV teaching.

articles.title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system.
DESIGN: Retrospective, population-based cohort study.
SETTING: South Korea's National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population.
PATIENTS: Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000-37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Physical Restraint Use in Critically Ill Children: A Secondary Analysis of the PICU Up! Pilot Trial, 2019-2020.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify clinical factors associated with physical restraint use in critically ill children.
DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected observational daily data from the baseline (preintervention) phase of the PICU Up! multicenter stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial (NCT03860168). The analytic dataset represents a shared subset of the larger parent study population.
SETTING: Six PICUs in the United States, from May 2019 to March 2020.
PATIENTS: A total of 1153 patients younger than 18 years admitted to a PICU for 3 or more days.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Children younger than 18 years old admitted for 3 or more consecutive PICU days were included. Daily data on sedation level, medication exposure, device use, and restraint status were collected, and multivariable generalized estimating equation models were used to evaluate associated factors. Physical restraints were used in 216 patients (18.7%) and 1,043 of 11,491 patient-days (9.07%), with a median duration of 3 days (interquartile range, 2-5). In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72-31.07). Other significant factors included age 3-17 years vs. 0-2 years (aOR, 2.46-2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39-6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05-2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42-2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] -1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24-2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52-1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47-2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use (p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge.
CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS -1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

articles.title: Utility of Renal Replacement Therapy for Infants With Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and survival outcomes in infants with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) receiving extracorporeal life support (ECLS).
DESIGN: Multicenter retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization database (2011-2020). Propensity score (PS) matching was used to account for pre-ECLS disease severity.
SETTING: International multicenter ECLS centers.
PATIENTS: Infants with CDH requiring ECLS.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 2815 infants, 749 infants (26.6%) received RRT. Before matching, +RRT patients had significantly lower survival to discharge (35.5% vs. 60.2%; p < 0.0001). PS matching generated 413 pairs with balanced pre-ECLS characteristics. After matching, +RRT remained associated with significantly lower survival to discharge (36.3% vs. 57.4%; survival odds ratio, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32-0.56; p < 0.0001). +RRT patients also experienced longer median ECLS durations (15 vs. 9.4 d; p < 0.0001) and higher rates of severe on-ECLS AKI (10.9% vs. 3.6%; p < 0.0001). Stratified analysis showed that RRT was associated with significantly worse survival only in patients undergoing on-ECLS CDH repair.
CONCLUSIONS: In infants with CDH on ECLS, RRT use is strongly associated with increased ECLS duration and decreased survival to discharge. Although PS matching suggests this association persists regardless of baseline severity, RRT likely serves as a marker for significant clinical deterioration during the ECLS course.

articles.title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics.
DESIGN: Prospective single-center physiologic study.
SETTING: Cardiac PICU.
PATIENTS: Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease.
INTERVENTIONS: Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O and low tidal volume (Vt; 6-7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high Vt (9-10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low Vt; and 4) PEEP 8, low Vt. Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (PL), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H2O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory PL 0-2 cm H2O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18-50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0-3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low Vt. Chest closure reduced expiratory PL in all conditions, at baseline from -0.5 cm H2O (-1.2 to -0.1 cm H2O) to -2.5 cm H2O (-3.1 to -1.8 cm H2O). Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory PL differently depending on the ventilator settings. High Vt was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high Vt was more frequently associated with high nondependent PL, suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory PL more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and Vt adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory PL and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

articles.title: The Current State of Ventilator Liberation Practices and Outcomes in the United States-A Report From the Ventilator Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Describe and explore interunit baseline ventilator liberation practices and outcomes related to the 2023 Pediatric Ventilator Liberation Guidelines within the original cohort of Ventilation Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative units.
DESIGN: Observational cohort study.
SETTING: Nineteen VentLib4Kids ICUs in the United States (13 general medical/surgical, five cardiovascular, and one mixed).
PATIENTS: First planned extubation attempt where code status allowed reintubation in patients younger than 19 years old, endotracheally intubated for any indication between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 2315 ventilator courses were included. Most were 28 days to younger than 6 years old (65.5%) and had a lower respiratory infection diagnosis (23.8%). Prematurity (13.2%) was the most common comorbidity. Spontaneous breathing trial exposure demonstrated the highest guideline concordance at 74.6% (median; interunit range [IUR], 49.6-100%), whereas maximal inspiratory pressure testing was lowest (3.7%; IUR, 0-62.4%). Most courses (55.5%; IUR, 19.8-99%) included an air leak test. Among those without an air leak noted or greater than 25 cmH2O, 70.1% were exposed to dexamethasone in concordance with the guidelines. Initiation of dexamethasone greater than or equal to 6 hours before extubation predominated (81.1%) at a median dose of 0.5 mg/kg/dose in exposed groups. Planned postextubation high-flow nasal cannula (44.3%) and bilevel positive airway pressure (18.6%) were most common. Unit-level use of any planned postextubation noninvasive respiratory support ranged from 20.6% to 100%. Among infants, planned continuous positive airway pressure was used in 6.7% of subjects. Among all courses, 10.4% (IUR, 4.5-19.2%) ended with extubation failure (reintubation within 48 hr).
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline VentLib4Kids practices demonstrate varying degrees of concordance with guideline recommendations along with significant interunit variation. These results align with prior international survey data and support the need for structured, multicenter quality improvement and guideline implementation strategies.

articles.title: Early-life viral immune challenge alters behavior and growth trajectories in zebra finches (Taeniopygia guttata).
articles.abstract: Early-life immune challenge (ELIC) is particularly costly as neonates are limited to an innate immune response when exposed to pathogens outside the maternal repertoire. As the post-natal period requires extensive energy, reallocation of resources toward pathogen clearance may alter developmental trajectories. Our objective was to evaluate the effects of an ELIC on nestling behavior and growth trajectories in zebra finches (Taeniopygia guttata) using polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid (poly I:C), a viral mimetic. Nestlings were challenged with poly I:C, saline, or simply handled (no injection) on post-hatch day (PHD) 5. Behaviors associated with sickness responses were quantified from videos recorded over the following 10 days. Growth was monitored through PHD 60 using repeated measures of mass, wing chord, and tarsus length. Poly I:C-challenged nestlings exhibited classic sickness behaviors, including reduced begging 1-day post-injection (DPI) and reduced parent-directed begging and feeding 4 DPI. Both poly I:C and saline-challenged birds exhibited persistently lower body mass and condition than non-injected controls. Structural measures of body size and fledging age were unaffected by treatment, suggesting that nestlings prioritized development of traits critical for fledging despite reduced overall body mass. These findings show that early-life immune activation can alter nestling behavior and produce lasting effects on growth trajectories.

articles.title: A comparison of UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications DESIGN: National population-based study SETTING: All births in France over 1 week in 2021 POPULATION: 11,845 women with a live-born singleton, with data abstracted from medical records and maternal interviews MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Prevalence of low-risk women and discrepancies in low-risk exclusion criteria between UK and French guidelines RESULTS: The prevalence of women at low-risk was 64.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 63.3-65.0) and 71.2% (70.4-72.0) according to UK and French guidelines, respectively. Overall, 58.9% (58.0-59.8) of women were at low-risk according to both guidelines, 5.2% (4.8-5.6) according to UK guidelines only and 12.3% (11.7-12.9) for French guidelines only. Risk level is assessed at the beginning of pregnancy in French guidelines but at the end of pregnancy in UK guidelines. Uterine scar and insulin-treated gestational diabetes were the main low-risk exclusion criteria in UK but not French guidelines. A history of a small-for-gestational age (SGA) newborn or preterm birth and antenatal suspicion of SGA for the current pregnancy were the main low-risk exclusion criteria in French but not UK guidelines.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of pregnant women at low-risk of complications differed between UK and French guidelines because of discrepancies in the timing of risk assessment and low-risk exclusion criteria. This suggests the need for complementary guidelines including criteria derived from validation studies to orient low-risk women toward both the appropriate practitioner for prenatal follow-up and the suitable place of birth.

articles.title: From pattern recognition to pathophysiology: should intrapartum cardiotocography interpretation in France move beyond the 2007 CNGOF classification? A narrative review and position paper.
articles.abstract: Intrapartum cardiotocography (CTG) is the main method of fetal surveillance in France, where interpretation relies on the five-tier classification derived from the 2007 guidelines of the French College of Gynaecologists and Obstetricians (CNGOF). Like other pattern-based systems, its accuracy and reproducibility are limited. Physiological CTG interpretation, formalised in an international expert consensus statement in 2018 and revised in 2024, proposes to replace category-based grading by recognition of the type of hypoxic stress, of fetal compensation and decompensation, and of non-hypoxic mechanisms such as intra-amniotic inflammation or pre-existing hypoxia. As growing numbers of French teams adopt this approach, the question has become pressing to maintain homogeneous CTG interpretation nationwide. We appraise the evidence on both sides. Supporting arguments include a consistent experimental basis, clinically relevant features ignored by current classifications, higher sensitivity in one comparative study and a single-centre before-after study reporting lower neonatal morbidity. Arguments for caution include the absence of randomised trials, before-after designs exposed to secular trends and to co-interventions such as more frequent tocolysis and more caesarean births, inter-observer agreement that is no better - and in one study worse - than with conventional classifications, the concentration of the supporting evidence within the group that developed the method, and the limited clinical benefit of earlier physiologically based technologies. As a hypothesis for evaluation rather than a recommendation, we outline a hybrid model aligning terminology with FIGO definitions and adding a structured physiological layer, to be coordinated nationally and tested in a pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial.

articles.title: Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia Treatment Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study on Prognostic Factors and Survival in a Low- to Middle-Income Country.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) outcomes remain substantially lower in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where treatment-related mortality (TRM), treatment abandonment, and limited access to risk-adapted therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remain important challenges. We evaluated contemporary outcomes and factors influencing survival in children with AML treated at a tertiary center in Pakistan.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients aged <18 years diagnosed with AML between 2011 and 2023. Patients in main AML cohort were compared between an early era (2011-2016) and a later era (2017-2023), following institutional availability of HSCT. Overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), and relapse-free survival (RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were estimated using competing-risk analysis. Acute myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome (AML-DS) and Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) were analyzed separately.
RESULTS: Among 143 patients in the main AML cohort, 114 (80%) initiated therapy and 69 (60%) achieved complete remission. Induction mortality was 16%, while TRM occurred in 27% of treated patients, predominantly due to sepsis. Three-year OS, EFS, and RFS were 35%, 17%, and 38%, respectively. Survival did not differ significantly between the early and later eras (3-year OS, 37% vs. 32%, p=0.70; EFS, 20% vs. 15%, p=0.35). The 3-year cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were 51% and 26%, respectively, with no significant differences between eras. Thirty patients relapsed; 12 received salvage therapy, of whom nine achieved a second remission. Treatment abandonment occurred throughout the treatment course, including in 16% before therapy initiation. Intermediate- and high-risk disease and higher presenting white blood cell count were associated with increased mortality on multivariable analysis. Twelve patients underwent HSCT, all in the later era. Three-year OS was 78% in AML-DS and 75% in APL.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric AML outcomes remained limited by the combined effects of TRM, relapse, and treatment abandonment. Institutional availability of HSCT in the later era was not associated with improved population-level survival, although the small number of transplanted patients precludes conclusions regarding HSCT effectiveness. Strengthening supportive care, molecular risk stratification, treatment continuity, and timely access to salvage therapy and HSCT may improve outcomes in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Task-specific Humeral Head Translation Is Associated With Neuromuscular Recruitment Deficits in Multidirectional Shoulder Instability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidirectional shoulder instability is a common clinical challenge, particularly in adolescents and young adult females. It can impact daily function and athletic performance. However, evidence regarding the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle recruitment patterns in this population remains unclear.
QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: This study aimed to (1) compare humeral head translation between patients with multidirectional instability and controls, as well as among clinical subgroups characterized by anterior, inferior, and posterior instability; (2) examine shoulder muscle activity across groups, including variations within clinical subgroups; and (3) investigate the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle activation levels during three standardized isometric tasks.
METHODS: From an initial screening of 37 patients and 35 controls, 19% (7) of patients and 14% (5) of controls were excluded based on predefined criteria (shoulder pain < 3 months, prior shoulder surgery, or adhesive capsulitis), leaving 30 eligible participants with multidirectional instability (25 female, mean ± SD age 24 ± 1 years) and 30 control participants (23 female, age 25 ± 4 years) who successfully completed all testing without data loss. To address our three study questions, the methodology was structured as follows: first, ultrasonography was used to calculate humeral head translation via changes in acromiohumeral and glenohumeral distances. Based on clinical relevance and patient perception thresholds, a difference of ≥ 1.4 mm in humeral head translation was defined as the minimal detectable change (MDC). Second, surface electromyography recorded muscle activities (biceps long head, infraspinatus, middle deltoid, serratus anterior, upper trapezius, and lower trapezius) across groups and clinical subgroups during three isometric tasks, including (1) isometric shoulder flexion, (2) isometric horizontal adduction, and (3) extension while holding weight. For extension while holding weight, participants lifted a standardized dumbbell (5 kg for participants with BMI ≥ 21 kg/m2 and 4 kg for those with a BMI of < 21 kg/m2). All data on muscle activity are reported as percentages of maximum voluntary isometric contraction rather than absolute values, with 20% representing the MDC. Participants were further stratified into subgroups based on predominant instability patterns, and comparative analyses were conducted to evaluate differences in humeral translation and muscle activities across these specific groups. Third, the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle activation levels was investigated using Pearson correlation coefficients, interpreted as weak for r < 0.30, moderate for r = 0.30 to 0.50, and strong for r > 0.50.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with multidirectional instability demonstrated greater humeral head translation across all tasks, exceeding the MDC threshold in controls versus patients for anterior translation (mean ± SD 0.4 ± 0.3 mm versus 2.6 ± 1.1 mm, mean difference 2.2 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.8 to 2.6]; p < 0.001), posterior translation (0.4 ± 0.2 mm versus 2.2 ± 1.2 mm, mean difference 1.8 [95% CI 1.3 to 2.2]; p < 0.001), and inferior translation (0.3 ± 0.2 mm versus 3.0 ± 1.8 mm, mean difference 2.8 [95% CI 2.1 to 3.4]; p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis showed that patients with a predominant direction of instability experienced the greatest translation during corresponding specific tasks (mean difference 1.5 to 2.4 mm [95% CI 0.2 to 4.1]; p < 0.02). We found no clinically important difference between controls and patients in terms of infraspinatus activity during horizontal adduction (23% ± 11% versus 15% ± 6%, mean difference 8% [95% CI 2% to 13%]; p = 0.001). Similarly, no clinically important difference was observed in upper trapezius activity during weighted extension (32% ± 19% versus 17% ± 13%, mean difference 14% [95% CI 4% to 22%]; p = 0.001), nor in middle deltoid activity during weighted extension (11% ± 6% versus 7% ± 4%, mean difference 3% [95% CI 1% to 6%]; p = 0.009). Only the reduction in biceps long head during flexion in controls versus patients (64% ± 38% versus 36% ± 12%, mean difference 29% [95% CI 14% to 44%]; p < 0.001) exceeded the MDC threshold. Correlations between translation and muscle activity occurred during specific tasks, showing moderate positive associations with serratus anterior (r = 0.38; p = 0.04) and lower trapezius activity (r = 0.40; p = 0.03) during flexion and a strong positive association with middle deltoid activity during horizontal adduction (r = 0.59; p = 0.001), whereas no correlations were found during weighted extension.
CONCLUSION: Patients with multidirectional instability exhibit task-specific increases in humeral head translation exceeding the MDC, driven by distinct neuromuscular deficits. Subgroup analyses show that patients experience the greatest translation during tasks corresponding to their predominant direction of instability. Future studies should evaluate the longitudinal efficacy of rehabilitation protocols in modifying abnormal translation patterns and improving clinical outcomes across different subgroups.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: From a foundational science perspective, our findings indicate that traditional, generalized shoulder strengthening is insufficient for multidirectional instability. Instead, rehabilitation should utilize direction-specific interventions tailored to each patient's predominant instability pattern, targeting underperforming muscles to mitigate abnormal joint translation and restore dynamic glenohumeral stability.

articles.title: Association Between Timing of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Diagnosis and Perinatal Outcomes: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the association between the timing of gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosis and perinatal outcomes, including large-for-gestational-age birth, neonatal hypoglycemia, and postpartum dysglycemia.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included women with gestational diabetes mellitus who delivered at Saitama Medical Center between April 2020 and March 2023. Women were classified according to the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus before or at or after 24 gestational weeks. The primary outcome was large-for-gestational-age birth. Associations were evaluated in the overall cohort and after propensity score matching using infertility treatment, family history of diabetes, nulliparity, and pre-pregnancy body mass index.
RESULTS: Among 228 women, 97 were classified into the early diagnosis group and 131 into the late diagnosis group. The incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth was significantly lower in the early diagnosis group than in the late diagnosis group (13.4% [13/97] vs. 29.0% [38/131], p = 0.008). In the propensity score-matched cohort (92 pairs), this association remained significant (10.9% [10/92] vs. 28.3% [26/92], p = 0.005). Neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ significantly between the groups after matching (p = 0.730 and p = 0.711, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed at or after 24 gestational weeks was associated with a higher incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth, whereas neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ according to the timing of diagnosis.

articles.title: Aglepristone Use in Planned Caesarean Sections: Insights Into Neonatal Viability and Uterine Receptor Expression in Bitches.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated clinical and uterine effects of aglepristone before planned caesarean section (CS) in bitches. Twelve bitches received aglepristone (n = 7) or served as controls (n = 5). Aglepristone (Alizine) at 15 mg/kg SC was administered on Days 60-61 after ovulation, followed by planned CS 20-24 h later. Maternal milk production and vaginal discharge, neonatal survival and Apgar scores, serum progesterone and estradiol, and uterine progesterone receptor (PR) and oestrogen receptor alpha (ERα) expression were evaluated. PR and ERα mRNA were measured by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), and protein expression at placental and inter-placental sites was investigated by immunohistochemistry using H-scores. Aglepristone did not significantly affect maternal outcomes, neonatal survival, or circulating steroids. Immediate neonatal Apgar scores were significantly higher in treated puppies, although the mean difference was small and all puppies were clinically vital. PR and ERα mRNA did not differ between groups or sites. Myometrial PR was higher at placental than inter-placental sites within treated bitches, while myometrial ERα was higher in treated than control bitches at both sites. Thus, aglepristone may modulate uterine receptors, particularly myometrial ERα, without generalized transcriptional changes; the small Apgar difference should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Ferroptosis and Oxidative Stress in Sickle Cell Anemia.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death, plays a key role in the pathophysiology of sickle cell disease (SCD). This study is a narrative review on oxidative stress and ferroptosis in children with SCD in Africa and Colombia, through literature searches to select articles published between 2019 and 2024. The search included terms such as "sickle cell," "oxidative stress," "ferroptosis," "Africa," and "Colombia," consulting databases like PubMed, Springer, Google Scholar and ScienceDirect, and selecting 11 relevant studies. The results show that ferroptosis, induced by the accumulation of free iron, lipid peroxidation, and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS), worsens complications such as kidney damage, vase-occlusive crises, and chronic inflammation. In Africa, factors like low hepcidin levels and genetic mutations, such as Q248H in ferroportin, increase oxidative stress and susceptibility to ferroptosis.
