In Colombia, the high prevalence of hemoglobin S in the Caribbean and Pacific regions is associated with severe crises and significant tissue damage. Clinical cases suggest that hydroxyurea reduces vaso-occlusive crises by raising fetal hemoglobin (HbF) levels and chelating free iron. Although ferroptosis is a secondary mechanism in the pathophysiology of SCD, it significantly amplifies complications, making it essential to implement therapeutic strategies that regulate iron homeostasis and reduce oxidative stress using antioxidants and lipid peroxidation inhibitors.

articles.title: Genomic Landscape of Neuroblastoma and Neuroblastic Tumors: An Integrated Network Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neuroblastoma (NBL) is the most frequently occurring solid tumor outside the brain in children, while ganglioneuroblastoma is a distinct entity within the spectrum of peripheral neuroblastic tumors. This pediatric cancer is highly varied, displaying a range of clinical and genomic characteristics that significantly affect prognosis and treatment strategies.
METHODS: In this study, we systematically analyzed clinically annotated and genomically profiled multiomics data from 1472 samples representing NBL and other peripheral neuroblastic tumors across four international cohorts using the cBioPortal platform.
RESULTS: Comprehensive genomic profiling revealed that ALK was the most frequently altered gene among the analyzed cohorts, while TTN, MUC16, ATRX, PTPN11, and MYCN showed less common recurrent alterations. Most of the identified alterations were missense mutations, whereas copy number alterations and structural variants were found in only a small number of samples. Correlation analysis demonstrated a positive association between diagnosis age and fraction genome altered, with amplifications and gains in ALK and MYCN being associated with higher levels of genomic instability. Kaplan-Meier analyses demonstrated no statistically significant association between the combined genomic alteration status of the selected candidate genes and overall survival, progression-free survival, or disease-free survival. In addition, gene ontology enrichment and protein-protein interaction network analyses indicated results that suggested the involvement of these genes in transcriptional regulation, chromatin structure, and oncogenic signaling, with ALK identified as a key network hub.
CONCLUSIONS: The clinical and biological significance of recurrent genomic alterations in NBL and ganglioneuroblastoma may help improve the current risk stratifications and have a bearing on potential targeted therapies.

articles.title: Antimicrobial Management of Surgical Necrotizing Enterocolitis: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence-based antimicrobial regimens are lacking for surgical necrotizing enterocolitis. We evaluated the association between antimicrobial practices and outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of infants with surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (2010-2019) at ten children's hospitals. Demographics, antimicrobial choice, and postoperative outcomes were assessed using multivariable regression.
RESULTS: Among 306 neonates (median gestational age 26 wk [interquartile range 25-29], birth weight 850 g [680-1100], age at diagnosis 8.5 wk [3-21]), 15 antimicrobials were used in 94 initial regimens. Postoperatively, 15 were administered in 107 regimens. Pre- and postoperative regimens differed in 67%. The most frequently used antibiotics were ampicillin, clindamycin, gentamicin, and vancomycin. Antifungals were often given to those with lower weight at diagnosis. 34% died during the index admission. No initial antimicrobial agent was associated with mortality. Excluding early deaths, patients received a median of 14 d of postoperative antibiotics. The duration of postoperative antibiotics (>7 d versus < 7 d) was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (odds ratio 0.86, P = 0.93). Adjusted regression analyses demonstrated no associations between postoperative antimicrobial choice and enteral autonomy, stoma complications, neurodevelopmental impairment, or cholestasis. Antifungal use was associated with higher odds of late mortality (odds ratio 5.22, P = 0.023), likely secondary to underlying illness severity.
CONCLUSIONS: Antimicrobial management varied widely. No individual antimicrobial agent improved survival; however, binary analysis of antimicrobial exposure limited conclusions. Longer antimicrobial duration was not associated with improved survival. Prospective randomized studies may help define optimal antibiotic management.

articles.title: Is all gross hematuria high risk? Age-stratified outcomes after anticoagulation initiation using a large claims database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Anticoagulation (AC) worsens underlying hematuria, though its impact on the incidence and subsequent guideline-based workup of gross hematuria (GH) is unknown. Using a large claims database, we characterized GH evaluation patterns after AC initiation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX Network, adults initiating anticoagulation were age- and sex-stratified by 2025 American Urological Association (AUA) microhematuria risk groups. Primary outcomes included 1-year sequential rates of GH, cystoscopy, transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT), and bladder cancer diagnosis. Cox proportional hazards models with 1:1 matching for age, race, body mass index, smoking, hypertension, and urolithiasis were performed to estimate hazard ratios for primary outcomes in individuals following AC initiation compared to non-AC controls.
RESULTS: Among 891,273 males and 930,311 females initiating AC, GH occurred in 0.8% of individuals. The combined bladder cancer diagnosis rate for low-risk aged males (18-39 years old) and females (18-59 years old) was ≤0.46% (n ≤ 15). Among 1.0% (n = 5,563) of high-risk males (≥60 years old) diagnosed with GH, bladder cancer diagnosis rate was 1.1% (62/5,563), whereas for intermediate-risk women (≥60 years old), it was 0.59% (28/4,762). AC initiation was associated with significantly higher risks of GH, cystoscopy or TURBT, and diagnosis of bladder cancer compared to controls across all sexes and age groups.
CONCLUSIONS: AC initiation is associated with higher rates of GH and subsequent urologic evaluation, possibly reflecting enhanced detection rather than increased cancer risk. Given the low malignancy yield in younger cohorts, age-based risk stratification for GH after AC initiation may improve diagnostic efficiency and reduce unnecessary evaluations.

articles.title: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh in 2026: national surveillance trends, cumulative divisional burden, and historical vaccination context.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bangladesh experienced a major measles resurgence in 2026. We reassessed early outbreak indicators while distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden and historical vaccination measures.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) bulletins dated 2-30 April 2026, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. We reconstructed cumulative division-level counts from the 22 April bulletin and calculated population-standardized notification rates using the 2022 census. Official national measles-containing vaccine coverage for 2019, 2023 and 2024 provided historical context.
RESULTS: By 30 April, DGHS reported 37,131 suspected and 5028 confirmed cases, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. On 22 April, cumulative division-level totals were 27,164 suspected and 3934 confirmed cases. Dhaka recorded 2634 confirmed cases, or 5.957 per 100,000 population. Official national MCV1 and MCV2 coverage in 2024 was 86.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Earlier childhood MR1 division-level measurements were not contemporaneous with the outbreak and were not used for correlation testing.
CONCLUSIONS: The early outbreak showed substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity. Accurate interpretation requires matching reporting windows, strengthening age- and vaccination-status surveillance and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage.

articles.title: Position of the Polish Society for Inborn Errors of Metabolism on the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of patients with Gaucher disease.
articles.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the GBA1 gene, resulting in deficient glucocerebrosidase activity and accumulation of glucosylceramide within macrophages. Three main clinical forms are distinguished according to the presence and extent of central nervous system involvement: non-neuronopathic type 1 (GD1), acute neuronopathic type 2, and chronic neuronopathic type 3. The disease presents with a broad spectrum of manifestations, including hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, skeletal complications, pulmonary involvement, and neurological symptoms in neuronopathic forms. This position statement of the Polish Society for Inborn Errors of Metabolism summarizes current recommendations for the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of patients with GD. The document discusses the molecular background, epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic algorithms, biomarkers, imaging modalities, and severity assessment tools. Particular attention is given to enzyme replacement therapy, which remains the standard of care for GD1 and type 3 GD, and to substrate reduction therapy with eliglustat in selected adults with GD1. The role of supportive treatment, management during pregnancy, monitoring of therapeutic efficacy, multidisciplinary care, and transition from pediatric to adult services is also addressed. Emerging therapeutic approaches, including pharmacological chaperones and gene therapy, are reviewed. The recommendations emphasize early diagnosis, individualized treatment, and long-term follow-up in specialized reference centers.

articles.title: Maternal-fetal considerations of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in cystic fibrosis (CF) treatment, particularly the development of CFTR modulators (CFTRm), have transformed disease management and substantially improved survival, health status, and reproductive outcomes in people with CF. In addition to lung symptoms, CF is characterised by pancreatic insufficiency, meconium ileus, and reduced fertility, leading to a shorter life expectancy. CFTRm, e.g. elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor partially restore CFTR function. Together, these treatments have markedly improved survival and quality of life for individuals with CF. As increasing numbers of women with CF conceive while taking CFTRm, understanding maternal-fetal drug exposure has become a clinical priority. Emerging evidence demonstrates that CFTRm cross the placenta and can be detected in cord blood, neonatal plasma, and infant tissues. However, the extent of fetal exposure, tissue accumulation and potential developmental implications remain incompletely understood. Herein, we emphasise the mechanistic and pharmacological evidence underlying fetal exposure to CFTRm . This review synthesises current evidence regarding the transplacental transfer, fetal exposure and developmental implications of CFTRm during pregnancy. We discuss emerging pharmacokinetic data, reported maternal and infant outcomes and key knowledge gaps that remain regarding the safety of in utero CFTRm exposure.

articles.title: Imaging in young ischemic stroke: a pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Young ischemic stroke encompasses a group of cerebrovascular disorders occurring in patients younger than 45 years, with pediatric stroke generally defined as stroke occurring between 28 days and 18 years of age. The incidence of stroke in the pediatric and young adult population is increasing and is emerging as a major public health issue. Diagnosis of young stroke is often challenging because of non-specific clinical presentations, etiologies that differ from those in older adults, and the wide range of stroke mimics. Imaging plays a critical role in the prompt and accurate diagnosis of young stroke by characterizing stroke subtypes, identifying underlying causes, assessing vascular abnormalities, and guiding management decisions. This pictorial review highlights the current imaging workup for diagnosing young stroke describing the advantages and limitations of various imaging modalities. We present a pictorial review of stroke in the young based on their imaging features, differentiating them from common stroke mimics. Using a multimodality case-based approach, we illustrate the characteristic imaging findings and classic signs of a broad spectrum of young ischemic stroke etiologies. They range from common causes like cardioembolism and dissection to less common infectious, metabolic and genetic causes like Borrelia vasculitis, Fabry disease and Adenosine deaminase 2 deficiency (DADA2). This review aims to equip radiologists and trainees with a structured and practical approach to the diagnosis and management of young stroke through classic imaging patterns and illustrative cases, ultimately facilitating improved patient outcome.

articles.title: Taiwanese Dermatological Association consensus for the management of atopic dermatitis: A 2024 update.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense itching. AD commonly arises in children, in some of whom the condition may persist into adulthood; and a significant proportion of patients experience adult-onset disease as well. Although the prevalence of AD in Taiwan has risen over the past decades, recent therapeutic advances have contributed greatly to disease management. The Taiwanese Dermatological Association (TDA) has therefore developed an evidence-based consensus for the management of AD in Taiwan, and established a consensus committee to provide regular updates. This paper presents the 2024 update, for which a literature search was conducted to include relevant papers published between January 2020- March 2023. Supplementary searches targeted to approvals of new AD medications were subsequently conducted, and information was updated to August 2026. The consensus committee included 17 dermatology experts, and a modified Delphi method was used to evaluate the recommendations, with an approval threshold of ≥ 75%. A total of 21 new recommendations were added, 4 recommendations were revised, and the treatment algorithm was updated. Special considerations for pregnant, lactating, pediatric, and geriatric patients, as well as patients with active infections or undergoing vaccination, were included. This update incorporates the latest evidence and approved therapies, and may help to enhance treatment outcomes for AD patients in Taiwan.

articles.title: FGF23 and Cardiac Remodeling in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Rapid Review and Exploratory Quantitative Synthesis.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), elevated left ventricular mass index (LVMI), diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and cardiovascular mortality are common in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises early in CKD and is linked to cardiac remodeling, but consistency across studies is unclear. We conducted a rapid review of FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD, incorporating a reanalyzed unpublished single-center cohort, and pooled effect estimates where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics. A structured web-based search (August 2026) identified 11 candidate studies on FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD; 9 met eligibility, including 1 unpublished investigator-held cohort (n = 80) reanalyzed for this review. Pooling (inverse variance) was performed only where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics; all pooled estimates are exploratory, below the prespecified 3-study minimum. For FGF23 and LVH, using a derived LVH variable from the present cohort, a pooled log-FGF23 odds ratio (OR) across 2 adult-CKD studies (n = 242) was 1.33 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.92-1.93), I2 = 78%; a pediatric study (OR 2.53, n = 587) was consistent in direction but unpooled. For LVMI, correlations were not pooled; a Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort cohort showed higher LVMI only in the top quartile. For heart failure/cardiovascular mortality, a pooled hazard ratio across 2 studies (n = 374) was 2.37 (95% CI 1.47-3.84), I2 = 0%, with LVMI mediating only 7-22% in Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort. FGF23 was not significantly associated with diastolic dysfunction after adjustment (OR 1.51/standard deviation, 95% CI 0.92-2.47). The available evidence, though sparse and heterogeneous, is directionally consistent with a positive FGF23-cardiac remodeling association in CKD. Certainty is very low throughout; a full multi-database search is needed before a definitive conclusion.

articles.title: Natural History of Prenatally Identified Children With 48,XXYY Syndrome in Infancy and Early Childhood.
articles.abstract: 48,XXYY syndrome is a rare sex chromosome aneuploidy (SCA) associated with a variable profile of neurodevelopmental and medical. The limited information available in the literature is almost exclusively limited to postnatally diagnosed cases. This study aims to describe the early medical and developmental features of prenatally identified 48,XXYY infants, The eXtraordinarY Babies Study prospectively follows children prenatally identified to be at high risk for SCA with annual medical and neurodevelopmental evaluations. Data presented herein include the prevalence of medical conditions, developmental milestones, developmental and adaptive functioning assessment scores, and therapy utilization in 15 participants confirmed to have 48,XXYY. Comparisons were made with 47,XYY and 47,XXY males also enrolled in the eXtraordinarY Babies Study, the general population and a 2008 cohort of individuals postnatally identified 48,XXYY. Infants and young chlidren with 48,XXYY exhibited a range of early medical features, including elevated rates of feeding and GI disorders (breastfeeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux, and eosinophilic esophagitis), allergic disorders (food allergies and environmental allergies), and hypotonia. Developmental and adaptive functioning scores identified variable delays in motor, communication, and social domains, with nearly all infants receiving speech therapy, physical and/or occupational therapy due to delays or proactive developmental care. Medical and developmental findings were more prevalent in 48,XXYY compared to the 47,XYY and 47,XXY cohorts, although considerable individual variability and overlap in developmental functioning were observed across groups. Compared to the 2008 postnatally identified 48,XXYY cohort, infants identified prenatally received earlier intervention services, and developmental outcomes in the first years of life were similar between the two groups. Prenatal identification of 48,XXYY provides opportunity for early developmental monitoring, anticipatory guidance, and proactive referrals for medical evaluations and intervention. These findings provide valuable insights for genetic counselors and healthcare providers, emphasizing the spectrum of medical and developmental findings and the importance of early and proactive care to support individual outcomes. Prospective study of this prenatally identified cohort will provide important data about the natural history and phenotypic variability in XXYY, as well as identification of predictors of health and developmental outcomes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03396562.

articles.title: Altered quadriceps forces and patellofemoral joint loading during walking in adolescents with patellar instability.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Patellofemoral instability is a common and clinically important knee disorder in children and adolescents, but its functional biomechanics during walking remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare gait kinematics, quadriceps muscle forces, and patellofemoral joint contact forces during walking between adolescents with recurrent patellar instability (PFP) and typically developing (TD) controls. We hypothesized that the PFP group would exhibit altered gait kinematics together with reduced or redistributed quadriceps-force and patellofemoral contact-force patterns during gait.
METHODS: This study used an electromyography (EMG)-informed neuromusculoskeletal modeling framework to compare gait kinematics, quadriceps muscle forces, and patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms during walking between adolescent participants with PFP and TD controls. Forty-eight adolescents were included, comprising 24 participants with PFP and 24 controls. Three-dimensional gait analysis, ground reaction forces, and surface EMG were collected during level walking. Between-group differences were evaluated using peak comparisons, statistical parametric mapping (SPM), and principal component analysis (PCA).
RESULTS: No significant between-group differences were detected in kinematic waveforms using SPM (all p > 0.05). In contrast, significant differences were identified in patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms in the mediolateral (cluster-level p = 0.0497 and p < 0.001) and proximodistal (both cluster-level p < 0.001) directions. Peak comparisons further showed larger relative differences in quadriceps muscle forces and patellofemoral joint contact-force components than in most kinematic variables. The PCA identified additional between-group differences in selected frontal- and transverse-plane kinematic waveforms, patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms, and quadriceps force waveforms, particularly for vastus lateralis and rectus femoris. The PFP group also showed broader dispersion of principal component scores, indicating greater between-subject variability.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that adolescent PFP during walking is characterized less by large overt differences in gross gait kinematics and more by altered quadriceps force and patellofemoral joint loading patterns. EMG-informed neuromusculoskeletal modeling may therefore provide clinically relevant biomechanical information that could support future patient-specific assessment and rehabilitation research beyond conventional gait analysis alone.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Prevalence of Japanese Encephalitis in Pediatric Patients with Positive Vaccination History among Acute Encephalitis Syndrome Cases at a Tertiary Care Center in Ranchi, Jharkhand: A Retrospective Observational Cross sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) remains a leading cause of pediatric neuro-morbidity in India. Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is a major viral contributor. Despite mass immunization, breakthrough infections present an emerging public health challenge.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of JE among vaccinated pediatric AES patients, evaluate real-world vaccine effectiveness, and identify risk factors for breakthrough infections.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational cross-sectional study at Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences, Ranchi, analyzing 267 pediatric patients (aged 3-18 years) admitted with AES over 12 months. Diagnosis was confirmed using cerebrospinal fluid MAC-ELISA or serum MAC-ELISA for JE-specific IgM antibodies and brain magnetic resonance imaging.
RESULTS: Among 267 enrolled cases, 189 (70.8%) had documented JE vaccination. JE positivity was significantly lower among vaccinated than unvaccinated children (24.3% vs. 46.2%; P < 0.001), representing a 47.4% relative reduction in JE prevalence among AES admissions. JE prevalence significantly increased with time elapsed since vaccination (14.3% at <1 year vs. 40.0% at >5 years; P = 0.012). In multivariable logistic regression, time since vaccination ≥3 years (adjusted odds ratios [aOR] = 2.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.24-6.51; P = 0.014), proximity to rice fields (<500 m) (aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.02-6.42; P = 0.045), and monsoon season admission (aOR = 3.18, 95% CI: 1.35-7.48; P = 0.008) were independent risk factors for breakthrough infections. Vaccinated JE-positive cases had higher mortality (21.7% vs. 10.5%; P = 0.045) and neurological sequelae rates (52.2% vs. 33.6%; P = 0.026) than vaccinated JE-negative controls.
CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized pediatric AES admissions, a notable hospital-based breakthrough prevalence of 24.3% was observed, driven primarily by waning immunity over time and intense environmental exposure. Implementing booster schedules at -year intervals and integrated vector control are urgently needed.

articles.title: Chicken Bone-induced Esophageal Perforation in a Child Presenting with Extensive Cervico-Thoracic Prevertebral Abscess and Sepsis: A Rare Case Report.
articles.abstract: Esophageal perforation following foreign body ingestion is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening condition in children, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. Sharp foreign bodies such as chicken bones may result in deep tissue injury, abscess formation, mediastinitis, and sepsis. We report the case of an 8-year-old boy who presented with throat pain, cough, vomiting, and epigastric pain following accidental ingestion of a chicken bone. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed an extensive cervico-thoracic prevertebral abscess extending from C2 to T6 with multiple air pockets and a retained foreign body at the T5-T6 level, suggestive of esophageal perforation. The patient underwent emergency right posterolateral thoracotomy with drainage of the abscess and removal of the impacted chicken bone. Intraoperative flexible esophagoscopy demonstrated a 1 cm perforation at the cricopharyngeal level. Definitive repair of the posterior esophageal rent was subsequently performed through a left cervical approach with reinforcement using a sternohyoid muscle flap. The postoperative course was complicated by anastomotic leak, high-output esophageal fistula, right vocal cord dysfunction, and Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis. Conservative management with feeding gastrostomy and nutritional support resulted in gradual recovery, and follow-up contrast studies showed complete healing without residual leak or stricture formation. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion in children with persistent symptoms following foreign body ingestion. Early imaging, prompt diagnosis, and multidisciplinary individualized management are essential to prevent severe complications and improve outcomes in pediatric esophageal perforation.

articles.title: Neuroimmune, neurochemical and behavioral studies in humanized heterozygous-IL-34 and wild-type NOG mice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Humanized NOG mice are increasingly used to investigate neuroimmune disorders, but their baseline behavioral, neurochemical, and immunological characteristics remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We evaluated the effect of IL-34 mediated human microglial engraftment on peripheral immune T-cell reconstitution, brain metabolites, and behavior in humanized heterozygous HSC-NOG-IL-34 (HET) and wild-type HSC-NOG (WT) mice. Neonatal mice were engrafted with human CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and assessed using flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS), and behavioral testing. Multivariable linear regression analysis was used to evaluate the effect of genotype, sex, age and their interactions.
RESULTS: Peripheral human CD45+, CD3+, and CD4+ T-cell populations increased with age but did not differ by genotype. HET mice showed higher number of IBA1+ and HuNu+ cells in the brain than WT mice, indicating enhanced human microglial engraftment. 1H-MRS metabolites did not differ by genotype, sex or age. Locomotor activity declined with age in both the groups. HET mice showed age-related reductions in exploration of novel and familiar objects, whereas WT mice showed increased exploration of familiar objects. The discrimination index remained unchanged in both the groups. HET mice also spent more time in the stranger zone and showed reduced investigation of the empty cup with age. In contrast, WT mice showed reduced time in the stranger zone.
CONCLUSIONS: HET mice showed greater human microglial engraftment and more pronounced age-related declines in exploratory behavior than WT mice. These findings support the utility of HSC-NOG-IL-34 mouse model for investigating neuroimmune disorders underlying behavioral dysfunction.

articles.title: Characteristics and co-morbidities of pediatric patients requiring cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract: Cholelithiasis in children is an increasingly recognized condition, due to the rising prevalence of risk factors and advances in diagnostic techniques. This retrospective descriptive cohort analyzed the characteristics of patients who underwent surgery for cholelithiasis in two Italian centers. From 2013 to 2023, 53 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Data collected included surgical indications, predisposing factors, and perioperative management. When preoperative ultrasound detected stones in the common bile duct, Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) was performed, followed by Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (LC) after two months. Postoperative clinical and ultrasonographic follow-up was conducted at 6 months and 1 year. The primary indication for surgery was symptomatic cholelithiasis in 38 patients (71.7%), followed by acute cholecystitis in 11 (20.7%) and persistent cholelithiasis in 4 (7.6%). Predisposing factors included hematological disorders in 14 cases (26.4%), a positive family history in 25 (47.2%), exposure to lithogenic substances in 9 (17.0%), and obesity in 9 (17.0%). ERCP was performed in 7 patients. Postoperative complications included one case of biliary fistula and one case of post-cholecystectomy syndrome. At follow-up, all patients were asymptomatic except for two who reported nonspecific abdominal pain. The most common risk factors for pediatric cholelithiasis in our cohort were a positive family history, hematological disorders, and obesity. LC remains the standard surgical treatment in children, with the primary aim of preventing complications.

articles.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for stuttering and other speech disorders.
articles.abstract: Speech and communication disorders have historically been framed as behavioral habits or peripheral motor problems, an interpretation that obscures their neurobiological complexity, contributes to stigma, and may discourage people from seeking treatment. This chapter applies the framework of Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation (NIPE) to speech disorders, focusing on developmental stuttering as the primary exemplar, childhood apraxia of speech as a second speech disorder, and Tourette syndrome with vocal tics as a neurodevelopmental condition with prominent vocal manifestations, while drawing on obsessive-compulsive disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorder as mechanistically informative comparators. We integrate evidence suggesting that speech symptoms emerge from interactions among distributed cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical loops, cerebellar timing and prediction networks, auditory-motor integration pathways, executive and limbic systems, and, as a working hypothesis, glial mechanisms that may regulate circuit stability. Within this framework, symptom variability and heterogeneous treatment response are reframed as expected features of state-dependent neural systems rather than failures of effort, motivation, or character. We describe how NIPE can translate these mechanisms into accessible, non-reductionist explanations that complement speech therapy, pharmacotherapy, neuromodulation, and multidisciplinary care by aligning expectations, reducing stigma, and supporting engagement during the gradual process of neuroplastic change, which we frame as support for adaptation, participation, and self-efficacy rather than as normalization of brain circuitry. We also consider precision NIPE tailored to dominant mechanism profiles, the promise and ethical risks of digital delivery, and key limitations, including neurobiological oversimplification and limited direct trial evidence, that define priorities for establishing NIPE as a rigorously tested, person-centered component of care.

articles.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for tic disorders.
articles.abstract: Tic disorders are neurodevelopmental conditions that begin in childhood and are marked by the presence of tics, or involuntary movements or sounds. Tics are neurobehavioral in nature-they are biologically based and influenced by a person's environment and experiences. Psychoeducation for tic disorders is important because these disorders are often misunderstood, and psychoeducation can provide patients and their families with accurate knowledge about the biological basis of tics, available treatment options, and guidance about supportive and empowering ways to navigate a tic disorder diagnosis. In this chapter we describe core elements of neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) and provide strategies for delivering these elements. Delivery of NIPE in this chapter has been tailored to children and caregivers because tics begin and are most often diagnosed in childhood and adolescence.

articles.title: MEK inhibitors in the management of NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas in children: experience from a reference center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is characterized by hyperactivation of the RAS pathway. MEKi, which inhibit downstream targets, have been shown to be effective in the treatment of symptomatic, unresectable plexiform neurofibromas (PN). We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study in the NF1 reference center of Marseille. Seven patients with NF1 treated with MEKi (MEK inhibitor), mainly selumetinib, were included. Pre-treatment evaluations, clinical presentation, treatment duration, and clinical and radiological efficacy and safety outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: The mean age at NF1 diagnosis was 3.5 years. PN most commonly manifested as pain (85.7%), signs of spinal cord compression (28.6%) were observed, presenting with gait disturbances, neurogenic pain, and/or radiological evidence of spinal cord involvement, respiratory disease (14.3%), and abdominal mass syndrome (14.3%). The mean delay before MEKi initiation was 6.4 years. Selumetinib was administered to all patients (five first-line, two after trametinib). All patients who initially reported pain experienced clinical pain relief by the first month, and in four, tumor bulk decreased palpably. On imaging, treatment with selumetinib resulted in tumor reduction in two patients and disease stabilization in five. Side effects were mostly cutaneous, gastrointestinal, and muscular. Mean follow-up on selumetinib was 18 months (8-24).
CONCLUSION: Selumetinib was effective clinically and radiologically with an overall acceptable safety profile. However, longer-term prospective studies are needed to confirm sustained response, establish therapeutic indications, and optimize management of complex NF1 cases.

articles.title: Longitudinal pulmonary function in children with sickle cell disease after acute chest syndrome: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute chest syndrome (ACS) is one of the most severe complications of sickle cell disease (SCD) and may contribute to long-term pulmonary morbidity. However, its impact on pulmonary function evolution in children remains insufficiently documented.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between ACS and longitudinal changes in pulmonary function parameters in pediatric patients with SCD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective monocentric study at Reims University Hospital including children with SCD who underwent pulmonary function testing between 2017 and 2025. Patients with a history of ACS were compared with those without ACS. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), FEV₁/FVC ratio, and carbon monoxide transfer coefficient (KCO) were analyzed at baseline and after two years of follow-up. Within-group longitudinal analyses were performed. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients with asthma was also conducted.
RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in baseline FEV₁ or at two-year follow-up between ACS and non-ACS groups (p = 0.44 and p = 0.40, respectively). In contrast, the FEV₁/FVC ratio was significantly lower in the ACS group both at baseline and at two years (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). Baseline KCO values were higher in patients with ACS (p = 0.01), but no significant difference persisted at follow-up (p = 0.07). Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with asthma yielded similar findings.
CONCLUSION: ACS was not associated with a decline in FEV₁ but was consistently associated with lower FEV₁/FVC ratios, suggesting early airflow limitation. These findings support systematic pulmonary function monitoring in children with SCD, particularly following ACS episodes, to enable early detection of respiratory involvement.

articles.title: Evidence-Based Vaccination Toolkit to Improve Competence and Confidence in Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite proven effectiveness of childhood immunizations, vaccine hesitancy remains a significant barrier to vaccine uptake, highlighting the need for educational interventions to prepare student clinicians for this practice reality.
AIM STATEMENT: This project aimed to create and implement a vaccination toolkit for Doctor of Nursing Practice-Pediatric Nurse Practitioner (DNP-PNP) students at a large university and evaluate the effect on confidence and anxiety around pediatric vaccination education and delivery.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest design was used to evaluate effect of a vaccine education intervention, guided by the Plan-Do-Study (PDSA) quality improvement framework and reported in accordance with the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines.
RESULTS: Overall, there was no statistical difference between pre- and post-toolkit scores for anxiety or self-confidence, with p = .126 (variances assumed) and p = .797, respectively. However, itemized analysis of the NASC-CDM scale yielded significant improvements in several individual measures.
CONCLUSION: Although changes in NASC-CDM scores were not statistically significant, item-level findings suggest the intervention may improve student confidence in vaccine counseling. Larger quasi-experimental studies are needed to evaluate educational intervention impacts on vaccine communication self-efficacy.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Family Maltreatment After Military Parental Injury in a Matched Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric nurse practitioners may provide care for military families experiencing parental health conditions associated with injury. Parental injury or illness may contribute to stress, leading to increased risks of child maltreatment or family violence.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6,253 spouses and 13,298 children of 9,157 injured service members who returned to duty. Records were followed for two years for child maltreatment, family violence, and well-child care. Chi-square, Wilcoxon rank sum tests, and logistic regression compared and calculated odds of outcomes.
RESULTS: Families with parents who experienced co-occurring mental health and physical injury were at significantly increased risk of child maltreatment, family violence, and decreased well-child care. Having a non-injured parent with a mental health diagnosis was associated with significantly higher odds of maltreatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric nurse practitioners should be aware of risk factors for maltreatment during periods of parental injury and provide avenues for early identification.

articles.title: Association of epilepsy subtypes with elevated depressive symptoms in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the coexistence of elevated depressive symptoms and epilepsy in children and adolescents and to ascertain if the symptoms are related to a specific localization.
METHODS: Patients between ages 9-14 with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), extratemporal lobe epilepsy (ETLE), and generalized epilepsy were followed up, and healthy siblings of these patients in the same age group as the control group were included in the study. The study included 89 epilepsy patients and 89 control subjects. Children's Depression Inventory (CDI) was used to determine the rate of elevated depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: The average age of the patients was 12.2 ± 1.8, 50.6% of them were female. Fifty (56.2%) of the patients were being followed up for generalized epilepsy, 14 (15.7%) for ETLE, and 25 (28.1%) for TLE. Elevated depressive symptoms (CDI ≥19) were found to be significantly higher in the TLE and ETLE epilepsy groups compared to the control group (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004, respectively). The rate of elevated depressive symptoms (CDI ≥19) was significantly higher in the TLE group compared to the generalized epilepsy group (52.0%vs. 12.0%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between TLE and ETLE, or between ETLE and the generalized epilepsy group (both p > 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that TLE remained independently associated with elevated depressive symptoms (adjusted OR 7.87, 95% CI 2.42-25.64; p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated depressive symptoms in children and adolescent patients were more frequently detected in the TLE group. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to clarify the relationship between epileptic focus localization and elevated depressive symptoms.

articles.title: Assessment of conversational pragmatics (ACP): Validation of a screening tool for pragmatic difficulties in children aged 6-11 with spoken language difficulties.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVE: Pragmatics-the ability to use language appropriately in social contexts-is a multidimensional skill involving verbal and non-verbal communication, social cognition, and executive functions. While pragmatic difficulties are recognized across neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), their assessment remains challenging due to terminological heterogeneity and a lack of standardized tools. This study aimed to validate the Assessment of Conversational Pragmatics (ACP), a 26-item parental questionnaire designed to identify pragmatic difficulties in French children aged 6-11.
MATERIALS AND METHODOLOGY: The study included 947 children: 549 typically developing (control), 299 with Language Difficulties (LgD) of whom 229 were identified as having a Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), and 99 verbal persons with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Principal component analysis confirmed the ACP's unidimensional structure, with excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α, 0.90; 95% CI, [0.87;0.91]). Test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.78; 95% CI, [0.66;0.86]), and external validity was supported by strong correlations with the CELF-5 Pragmatic Profile (rs = 0.81).
RESULTS: The ACP effectively discriminated between the three groups, with median scores of 68 [IQR, 62-74] (control), 55 [IQR, 47-64] (LgD), and 44 [IQR, 37-64] (ASD) (p < 0.001). Optimal cut-off scores were identified: ≤58 indicated a 60% risk of language difficulties, and ≤46 a 58% risk of ASD. However, the ACP did not differentiate between children with LgD and specific developmental language disorder (DLD), likely due to recruitment bias in specialized centres.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the ACP's robustness as a screening tool for pragmatic difficulties, offering a quick, reliable, and free resource for healthcare professionals. Its use of parent-reported data addresses the challenge of assessing pragmatic skills in clinical settings, where one-on-one interactions may not reveal a child's full communicative profile. The ACP's standardization across distinct populations provides a valuable clinical aid for early identification and referral, supporting timely intervention for children at risk of pragmatic impairments.

articles.title: Maternal prepartum intravenous fluid administration is associated with neonatal weight loss at day 2 of life.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal intravenous fluid administration during labor is widely used for treatment administration and to ensure adequate uteroplacental perfusion. Its potential effects on neonatal outcomes, particularly early weight loss, are not fully understood, with data mainly derived from breastfed infants. Evidence in formula-fed infants remains lacking.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the impact of prepartum maternal fluid administration on 48-h weight loss in exclusively formula-fed newborns. Blood cord hematocrit was also studied as a reflection of neonatal potential blood dilution.
METHODS AND SETTING: This retrospective, observational study was conducted at Amiens-Picardie University Hospital between September and December 2024. Term singleton infants exclusively formula-fed during the first two days of life were included. Maternal intravenous fluid volumes during the 12 h preceding delivery were recorded. The primary outcome was neonatal weight loss at day 2. The secondary outcome was blood cord hematocrit.
RESULTS: Among 200 mother-infant dyads, maternal fluid loading >4 mL/kg and > 6 mL/kg in the 4-6 h before delivery was significantly associated with greater neonatal weight loss at 48 h (p = 0.0168 and p = 0.027, respectively). Oxytocin exposure was also associated with increased weight loss (p = 0.036). Higher fluid intake >2 mL/kg in the 2 h before delivery correlated with lower cord hematocrit (p = 0.024).
CONCLUSION: Higher maternal intrapartum fluid administration was associated with increased neonatal weight loss and lower cord blood hematocrit in formula-fed infants. These findings support the hypothesis of transient neonatal fluid overload followed by diuresis, and underline the need to account for maternal fluid balance when interpreting early neonatal weight changes.

articles.title: Prevalence of overweight and obesity among preschool children in the Alpes-Maritimes department (South-Eastern France).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood overweight and obesity are major public health concerns, with increasing prevalence from an early age. Early onset is associated with persistence into adulthood and long-term complications.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of overweight and obesity in preschool children and to assess their distribution according to social context.
METHODS AND SETTING: This study covered the 2021-2022 school year. Weight and height recorded during routine health assessments of children aged 3-4 years attending the first year of preschool were collected in the Alpes-Maritimes department, with 88.1% coverage. Overweight and obesity, defined by the International Obesity Task Force (IOTF) reference curves, were compared according to whether the school belonged to an Education Priority Network (REP) or a reinforced Education Priority Network (REP+) and area-based socioeconomic deprivation measured using the French Deprivation Index (FDep).
RESULTS: Among 9,443 included children, 9.2% were overweight, and 2.2% had obesity. In non-REP areas, 8.6% of children were overweight, and 1.9% had obesity. In REP/REP+ areas, 14.1% were overweight, and 5.0% had obesity. The combined prevalence of overweight and obesity increased from 9.4% in the least deprived areas (FDep Q1) to 16.8% in the most deprived areas (FDep Q5).
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the association between social disadvantage and early childhood obesity. Targeted public health interventions tailored to the most vulnerable areas are needed to curb this trend.

articles.title: Hippotherapy for the social communication of children with ASD: An exploratory randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hippotherapy has emerged as a promising complementary approach, offering rich sensorimotor and social experiences that may enhance communication outcomes in children with ASD. However, despite growing interest in equine-assisted interventions, there is a scarcity of robust randomized clinical trials examining structured speech-language programs focused on social communication within hippotherapy settings. This study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the Step-by-Step in Communication program (a standardized speech-language intervention used in hippotherapy) in improving communicative and linguistic skills in children with ASD.
METHODS: Randomized clinical trial with 49 children aged 2 to 6 years diagnosed with ASD. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: G1 (one session per week for 24 weeks) and G2 (two sessions per week for 12 weeks), both totaling 24 sessions. The intervention followed the Step-by-Step in Communication program. Outcomes were assessed using the Behavioral Observation Protocol (PROC) and the Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC).
RESULTS: Both groups' language skills improved significantly intragroup, as measured by PROC, and reduced significantly three ATEC domains, whereas no significant changes were observed in the Health/Physical/Behavior domain. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline scores, revealed no significant differences between groups and their intervention conditions.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that hippotherapy may be an effective complementary intervention for improving language and autism-related outcomes in children with ASD. Different weekly intervention frequencies with the same total number of sessions did not appear to influence final outcomes; hence, the program may be implemented with different weekly schedules without compromising its effectiveness.

articles.title: Study Design and Baseline Characteristics of APOLLO: A Phase 3 Study of Bitopertin in Erythropoietic Protoporphyria and X-Linked Protoporphyria.
articles.abstract: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) and X-linked protoporphyria (XLP) are characterized by protoporphyrin IX (PPIX) accumulation, causing debilitating cutaneous phototoxic reactions and, in some cases, protoporphyric hepatopathy. Glycine transporter 1 (GlyT1) supplies extracellular glycine for erythroid heme biosynthesis. Bitopertin is an investigational oral GlyT1 inhibitor shown to significantly reduce PPIX and improve light tolerance and quality of life in patients with EPP or XLP. APOLLO is a global randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study designed to confirm the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bitopertin in adults and adolescents with EPP or XLP. Eligible participants were ≥ 12 years of age with diagnosis by biochemical and/or genetic testing and randomized 1:1 to receive once-daily oral bitopertin 60 mg or placebo over 24 weeks. Co-primary endpoints are percent change in whole blood metal-free PPIX and average monthly total time in sunlight on days without pain from a phototoxic reaction between 10:00 and 18:00 after 24 weeks. The general design and participants' baseline characteristics are described herein. Between April 2025 and March 2026, 199 patients were screened at 28 study sites in the United States, Canada, Europe, United Kingdom, and Australia; 183 participants were randomized. Mean (SD) age was 37.1 ± 17.1 years; 59% were female and 91% were White. Most participants (93%) had EPP, whereas 7% had XLP. Overall, 60% had not received prior treatment for EPP; 28% and 18% previously received afamelanotide or dersimelagon, respectively. Adolescents (12 to < 18 years) represented 19% of enrolled participants, and most adolescents (85%) had not previously received afamelanotide or dersimelagon. APOLLO is designed to evaluate bitopertin as a potential disease-modifying therapy for EPP and XLP. Baseline demographic and disease characteristics were consistent with prior EPP/XLP and generally support the relevance of the study's safety and efficacy findings to the broader EPP/XLP population.

articles.title: Prediction of severe neonatal morbidity using maternal, fetal, social, and delivery factors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate prediction models for severe neonatal morbidity (SNM) at admission for delivery and at delivery while evaluating the incremental contribution of maternal, fetal, social, intrapartum, and immediate post-delivery factors.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of singleton deliveries ≥32 weeks' gestation at two tertiary hospitals (2019-2023). SNM was defined using a composite of severe neonatal diagnoses and procedures. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70 %) and testing (30 %) cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression models were developed iteratively to predict SNM at admission for delivery and at delivery. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), compared using the DeLong test, and overall accuracy using Brier scores.
RESULTS: Among 53,872 singleton deliveries, 3,775 newborns (7.0 %) experienced SNM. Maternal factors alone demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.721, 95 % CI 0.704-0.738); adding fetal and social factors produced a modest increase (AUC 0.738, 95 % CI 0.721-0.755; difference 0.017, 95 % CI 0.005-0.029; p=0.0051). Gestational age was the strongest predictor; others included major structural anomalies, polyhydramnios, abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers, hypertensive disorders, and substance use disorder. Adding intrapartum factors and newborn sex increased the AUC to 0.776 (95 % CI 0.761-0.791); birthweight relative to gestational age added minimal improvement (AUC 0.780, 95 % CI 0.765-0.795).
CONCLUSIONS: SNM can be predicted with moderate accuracy using routinely available clinical information. Fetal and social factors modestly improved discrimination, and intrapartum information further improved it, supporting staged neonatal risk assessment during the delivery hospitalization.

articles.title: Bolus Volume and Mortality in Extremely Low Gestational Age Infants with Shock.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between clinical outcomes and the volume of fluid boluses administered during the first 24 hours of a shock episode in extremely low gestational age newborns (ELGANs) requiring vasoactive support.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included ELGANs (≤28 weeks) at a single Level IV NICU between 2013 and 2021 who received vasoactive medications for shock within the first seven days of life. The primary predictor was total fluid volume (cc/kg) administered in the first 24 hours of shock. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, 5-minute Apgar score, systemic corticosteroid use, and highest vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS).
RESULTS: Of 97 infants, 26 (27%) died within 14 days of the shock episode. Non-survivors received a higher median bolus volume compared to survivors (40 cc/kg vs. 20 cc/kg, p<0.001). Greater bolus volume was independently associated with increased odds of 14-day mortality (aOR 1.026, 95% CI 1.004-1.048, p=0.019). Each additional 10 cc/kg was associated with an approximately 29% increase in mortality odds. No significant associations were found between bolus volume and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or bronchopulmonary dysplasia after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Greater cumulative fluid bolus volume was independently associated with higher 14-day mortality in ELGANs with shock requiring vasoactive support. Although residual confounding illness severity cannot be excluded, these findings support cautious, individualized use of volume expansion and highlight the need for prospective studies of hemodynamically targeted resuscitation in this population.

articles.title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.
RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

articles.title: Healthcare Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among healthcare providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed healthcare team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations.
STUDY DESIGN: A cross‑sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary NICU team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple‑choice questions, Likert‑scale statements, and open‑ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open‑ended responses.
RESULTS: A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety.
CONCLUSIONS: Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

articles.title: Early Feeding Characteristics from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Through the First Year of Life and Neurodevelopment at 24 Months in Preterm Infants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) oral feeding progression and feeding development during the first year of life are associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months corrected age in preterm infants.
STUDY DESIGN: This longitudinal cohort study included 94 preterm infants born at < 37 weeks' gestation in a single level III NICU. NICU feeding progression was operationalized using gestational age-adjusted z-scores for time to full oral feeding. Parent-reported feeding symptoms and feeding skills were assessed during early (1-2 months), mid (4-8 months), and late (10-12 months) infancy. Neurodevelopment was assessed at 24 months corrected age using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-IV). Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine associations between early feeding characteristics and 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes, adjusting for gestational age, infant sex, parent education, and parent race.
RESULTS: Delayed NICU feeding progression showed a trend toward lower motor scores at 24 months (β = -5.12, p = 0.06). Parent-reported feeding symptoms during late infancy were associated with lower motor scores (β = -0.10, p = 0.03) and a similar trend for language score (β = -0.17, p = 0.06). Higher feeding skill proficiency during mid and late infancy was consistently associated with higher motor, language, and cognitive scores (mid infancy: β = 0.19-0.37, p < 0.01; late infancy: β = 0.23-0.38, p < 0.001). The Oral-Motor Coordination, Basic Movement Patterns, and Fundamental Oral-Motor subscales also demonstrated significant positive associations across all neurodevelopmental domains in both mid and late infancy.
CONCLUSION: Feeding characteristics from NICU hospitalization through infancy, including oral feeding progression, feeding symptoms, and feeding skill development, were associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months in preterm infants. These early feeding characteristics may provide clinically accessible measures to inform developmental surveillance and follow-up care.
KEY POINTS: · Delayed NICU oral feeding progression trended toward lower 24-month motor scores in preterm infants.. · More late infancy feeding symptoms were associated with lower 24-month motor scores.. · Higher infant feeding skill proficiency was associated with higher 24-month Bayley-IV scores.. · Early feeding monitoring helps identify preterm infants needing targeted developmental support..

articles.title: Association of Excess Gestational Weight Gain with Neonatal Hypoglycemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neonatal hypoglycemia is a significant contributor to neonatal morbidity. Diabetes, preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, growth restriction, and maternal obesity have been shown to increase the risk. We hypothesized that excess gestational weight gain is associated with increased rates of neonatal hypoglycemia.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of singleton, term deliveries in a single center between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2021, excluding patients with preexisting or gestational diabetes. The primary outcome was incidence of neonatal hypoglycemia. Institute of Medicine guidelines were used to determine category of gestational weight gain based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. Secondary outcomes included rates of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit admission by gestational weight gain category. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for potential confounders (macrosomia and pre-pregnancy obesity).
RESULTS: There were 23,902 term, singleton deliveries. Patients with excess gestational weight gain were more likely to be non-white, have undergone a cesarean delivery (CD) (29 vs. 22%, p < 0.001), have higher birthweight (3,522 vs. 3,333 g, p < 0.001), and have a higher pre-pregnancy body mass index (27 vs. 26, p < 0.001) compared with patients with appropriate gestational weight gain. The odds of neonatal hypoglycemia were significantly higher for women with excess gestational weight gain (adjusted odds ratio 1.28, 95% CI: 1.12-1.47). Odds of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions were also increased. Conversely, appropriate weight gain was protective against neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted odds ratio 0.73, 95 %: 0.63-0.85).
CONCLUSION: These data suggest that independent of maternal body mass index, macrosomia, or diabetes status, excess gestational weight gain is associated with an increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia. Although more research is needed to elucidate the pathophysiology and confirm these findings, these data suggest that counseling on gestational weight gain should address a potential increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia at birth with excess gestational weight gain.

articles.title: International Nosocomial Infection Control Consortium (INICC) report of healthcare-associated infections, data summary of 44 countries for 2017-2022, Adult and Pediatric Units, Device-associated Module.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report International Nosocomial Infection Control Consortium (INICC) data from 2017 to 2022 on 499 intensive care units (ICUs) in 44 countries across Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East.
METHODS: Prospective ICU patient data were collected via the INICC Surveillance Online System. CDC/NHSN definitions were applied to device-associated healthcare-associated infections (DA-HAIs).
RESULTS: We collected data on 274,653 patients, 1,685,152 patient-days, 794,473 central line (CL)-days, 576,956 mechanical ventilator (MV)-days, and 1,024,993 urinary catheter (UC)-days. We identified 3,001 CL-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI), 4,623 ventilator-associated pneumonias (VAP), and 2,829 UC-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI). Combined DA-HAI rates were 3.81 per 100 patients and 6.20 per 1,000 patient-days. CLABSI occurred at 3.78 per 1,000 CL-days, VAP at 8.01 per 1,000 MV-days, and CAUTI at 2.76 per 1,000 UC-days. Resistance reached 72.9% to ceftriaxone and 58.6% to imipenem in Klebsiella pneumoniae; 75.8% to cefotaxime in Escherichia coli; 42.9% to ceftazidime and 55.1% to imipenem in Pseudomonas aeruginosa; and 88.3% to piperacillin-tazobactam and 88.5% to imipenem in Acinetobacter spp. Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus was 45.3% and vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis 8.0%.
CONCLUSIONS: DA-HAI rates were 2.1 to 7.3 times CDC/NHSN pooled means, and bacterial resistance was high, supporting continued prevention.

articles.title: The Role of Droperidol in the Management of Acute Agitation: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute behavioral disturbance accounts for ~1.7 million emergency department visits in the USA annually, with 83% involving an underlying serious mental illness. A 2001 FDA black box warning regarding QT prolongation reduced use of droperidol, a butyrophenone antipsychotic, but recent data challenge these concerns.
METHODS: We reviewed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies from 2000 to 2025 assessing droperidol's efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: Droperidol provides rapid, effective sedation, with onset within 3 to 10 minutes and median time to adequate sedation of 14 to 25 minutes. Sixty-four percent of patients achieved adequate sedation at 15 minutes with droperidol versus 25% to 35% with ziprasidone and 29% with lorazepam. QT prolongation occurred in 1.3% of 1009 patients, mostly those with pre-existing risk factors. Respiratory depression was less common with droperidol (12%) than with ziprasidone (36% to 39%) or lorazepam (48%). Droperidol-midazolam combinations achieved faster sedation and reduced need for rescue medications (41% vs. 62%). Droperidol-treated patients had shorter hospital stays. Large studies found negligible rates of torsades de pointes or extracardiac arrhythmias. Elderly and pediatric patients responded favorably to low-dose droperidol. The American College of Emergency Physicians now recommends droperidol as first-line treatment for severe agitation. Combined with benzodiazepines, droperidol shows synergistic effects and allows lower doses of both with fewer adverse effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Recent evidence contradicts earlier FDA concerns, supporting droperidol as a safe, effective treatment for acute agitation. Its rapid onset, efficacy, safety profile, and operational benefits, including shorter ED stay, support its return to routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Impact to Healthcare-Associated Viral Gastroenteritis Infection Rate Using Different Visitation Models in a Pediatric Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric healthcare-associated viral gastroenteritis infections (HA-VGI) contribute to morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and outbreaks. Visitor-related transmission is a recognized risk factor; associations between visitation models and HA-VGI incidence remain understudied.
METHODS: HA-VGI rates were compared across four visitation models: (Period 1) seasonal visitation, visitors <13 years restricted December 1-April 30; (Period 2) two legally authorized representatives (LAR) permitted, mandatory masking; (Period 3) masking with an LAR-approved 10-person visitor list, including siblings; (Period 4) identical visitation model without masking (December 2017-June 2025). HA-VGI was defined as gastroenteritis on or after hospital day 3. Changepoint analysis, interrupted time series modeling, nonparametric comparisons, and multivariable linear regression assessed differences across periods. Regression models adjusted for community GI viral activity and calendar month. Rates were compared by unit and pathogen.
RESULTS: Median HA-VGI rates declined significantly during Period 2 compared with Period 1 (0.93 vs. 5.14 per 10,000 patient days; p<0.001). Although rates increased in Period 3, they remained below Period 1. Adjusted regression demonstrated lower rates during Periods 2 and 3 than during Period 1 (β=-3.01 and -3.07, respectively; both p<0.001). Period 4 did not significantly differ from Period 1. Community GI viral activity was independently associated with HA-VGI rates (β=5.94; p=0.002). ICU rates were lower than non-ICU rates; norovirus predominated.
CONCLUSIONS: Year-round sibling visitation with visitor limits was not associated with increased HA-VGI incidence compared to seasonal visitation. Mandatory masking was associated with lower HA-VGI rates independent of community viral activity and seasonality and may provide protection during increased GI viral circulation.

articles.title: Reading Abilities and Visual Evoked Potentials in Hearing-Impaired Children: A Comparative Study of Cochlear Implant and Hearing Aid Users.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate reading comprehension skills, visual evoked potentials (VEP), and saccadic eye movements in hearing aid (HA) users, cochlear implant (CI) users, and individuals with normal hearing (NH), to investigate the relationship between sensory processing and reading ability.
METHODS: The study included 45 participants, 15 HA users, 15 CI users, and 15 NH. VEP, a saccadic test, and a reading comprehension test were performed. VEP recordings were conducted with and without the hearing device for HA and CI users.
RESULTS: Reading comprehension scores in the CI group were significantly lower than those in the NH and HA groups (p < 0.001). Rightward saccade velocity was consistently lower than leftward velocity across all groups. Notably, VEP amplitudes in HA users (N1-P1: p = 0.048) and CI users (N1-P1: p = 0.005, 0.019, 0.001; P1-N2: p = 0.010, 0.008, 0.022) were significantly larger in the unaided condition (without device) compared to the aided condition. Correlation analyses did not reveal a consistent pattern of association between reading comprehension scores and VEP parameters.
CONCLUSION: While reading skills were found to be weaker in the CI group, the absence of a direct correlation between VEP/saccadic parameters and reading scores suggests that lower level sensory processing and higher order reading comprehension may operate through distinct mechanisms. The increased VEP amplitudes observed without hearing devices suggest a cross-modal neuroplastic compensation in the visual cortex during auditory deprivation.

articles.title: Sleeper Growth Plate Modulation for the Treatment of Mechanical Axis Deviation: A Review Article.
articles.abstract: This article aims to review the use of sleeper growth plates (SGPs) in the management of mechanical axis deviation in pediatric patients. Growth modulation using staples or the 8 plate have offered effective treatment options, but overcorrection and rebound remain prevalent issues. The SGP offers a potential solution involving metaphyseal screw removal only from the 8 plate construct. This potentially facilitates simple reapplication of the metaphyseal screw to resume growth modulation if deformity recurs. Using the available literature, this article reviews the history, indications, technique, and potential complications associated with SGP use.

articles.title: Latent Profile Analysis of Reproductive Concerns in Thyroid Cancer Survivors: Implications for Stratified Fertility Preservation Interventions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study applied latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify distinct phenotypes of reproductive concerns (RCs) and their influencing factors among young adult thyroid cancer (TC) patients in a Chinese tertiary hospital setting, providing preliminary evidence for stratified fertility preservation interventions.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 313 TC patients (aged 18-45 years) recruited from a tertiary hospital in China. RCs were assessed using the Reproductive Concerns After Cancer scale. LPA was employed to identify distinct subgroups, and multivariate logistic regression was performed to determine factors associated with profile membership.
RESULTS: Three latent profiles were identified: (1) Low Concern-Traditional (28.7%), characterized by minimal distress and family-oriented priorities; (2) Moderate Concern-Balanced (44.4%), characterized by intermediate distress and conflicted family and reproductive goals; and (3) High Concern-Comprehensive (26.8%), characterized by severe distress, particularly in partner disclosure and child's health. Multivariate logistic regression (with the 40-45 years age group as reference) indicated that patients aged 18-29 years (odds ratio [OR] = 0.184, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.055-0.609, p = 0.006) and 30-34 years (OR = 0.213, 95% CI: 0.073-0.624, p = 0.005) had significantly lower odds of high RC compared with those aged 40-45 years, suggesting that older age is independently associated with higher concern after adjustment for treatment-related covariates. Patients who underwent thyroidectomy (OR = 8.944, p = 0.016) or radioactive iodine therapy (OR = 2.131, p < 0.001) exhibited significantly elevated RCs compared to untreated patients. Sensitivity analyses restricted to female participants (n = 259) yielded class structures, proportions, and covariate effects virtually identical to the primary combined-sample analysis, supporting the robustness of our findings.
CONCLUSION: This study delineates three distinct RC profiles among young Chinese TC patients. Key correlates of greater RC include older age (40-45 years, independently associated after multivariate adjustment), radioactive iodine therapy (I131), and surgical treatment, while younger age was associated with greater concern at the univariate level. Tailored interventions are recommended to address the specific needs of each subgroup. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to validate these phenotypes and translate findings into clinical practice.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This is a cross-sectional observational study, which is not subject to clinical trial registration requirements.

articles.title: Sexual, Pharmaceutical, and Lifestyle Variables in a Cohort of Pregnant Western Australian Women, and Their Association With Detection of Vaginal Microorganisms and Preterm Birth.
articles.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The vaginal microbiome is shaped by factors such as sexual behaviour, smoking, and feminine hygiene practices. Although these associations are well documented in non-pregnant women, less is known in pregnancy, particularly in Australia, despite links between the vaginal microbiome and complications like preterm birth (PTB).
AIM: To document sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle variables in pregnant Australian women and examine their associations with vaginal microorganisms and, secondarily, PTB risk.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Mid-pregnancy (12-23 weeks' gestation) vaginal swabs from 936 women in the Predict1000 study were analysed for key microorganisms using qPCR. Participants completed a recruitment survey on medication use, urinary/vaginal infections, smoking, alcohol use, sexual practices, and vaginal douching. Associations between these factors, PTB (spontaneous and indicated), and specific microorganisms were assessed using Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests.
RESULTS: Thirteen percent of women reported smoking during pregnancy. Over half reported vaginal intercourse 1-2 times per week, although one quarter reported none. Thirty-two percent engaged in other sexual activities, most commonly oral sex (25%), followed by use of sex toys (11%). Vaginal douching was uncommon (3%). Sexual behaviour and douching were not associated with PTB risk. Smoking was associated with increased rates of non-optimal microbes, an association that persisted after correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between reduced frequency of vaginal intercourse (< 2 times/week) and lower prevalence of non-optimal vaginal microbes, and between douching and higher detection of Gardnerella vaginalis and Ureaplasma parvum, were also observed but did not remain significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: Sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle factors influenced the vaginal microbiota in pregnancy, but none were associated with PTB risk.

articles.title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
articles.abstract: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m2, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m2). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3).
