One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

articles.title: Why the Geometric Mean Is Better Than the Arithmetic Mean for Composite Index of Fitness Scores: A Case Study Using the Motor Competence-Neuromuscular Fitness Relationship in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the associations between neuromuscular fitness (NF) and body shape (stature, body mass, and waist circumference), fundamental movement skills (FMS), and perceived competence in children. We considered 2 methods for combining NF scores: the arithmetic mean (AM) of z-scores and the geometric mean (GM).
METHODS: Seven hundred and fifteen children (7-10 y old, 359 boys and 356 girls) underwent assessment of PF (10-m speed, standing long jump and seated medicine ball throw), FMS (Test of Gross Motor Development 3), perceived competence, stature, body mass, and waist circumference.
RESULTS: Principal components analysis confirmed that the 3 NF variables comprised 1 latent construct. Analysis of covariance was used to examine the amount of variance in PF that could be explained by anthropometric variables, FMS, perceived competence, and sex for both the AM and the GM. Results from this analysis show that by adopting a GM rather than an AM, the resulting composite index was more effective at detecting body size and locomotor behaviors associated with NF.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that a composite measure of NF using the GM is more robust and also superior to using a composite of the AM in explaining associations between FMS, perceived competence, and body-size variables and NF.

articles.title: From Competence to Expertise in Congenital Cardiology: The LENS Model for Learning to See Problems Differently.
articles.abstract: Competency-based medical education has improved how paediatric and congenital cardiology defines readiness for independent practice. Competencies and entrustable professional activities describe what trainees should be able to do, and the degree of supervision they require. Competence is an essential threshold rather than the endpoint of professional development. The mechanisms through which a competent congenital cardiologist subsequently develops expertise remain incompletely understood. Research in medical education and cognitive psychology suggests that experts do not simply accumulate more knowledge or more clinical experience. Expertise involves changes in knowledge organisation, clinical problem representation, information selection, recognition of discordance, management of uncertainty, decision-making and adaptation when familiar solutions are insufficient. These concepts are particularly relevant to congenital cardiology, where clinicians integrate complex anatomy, physiology, imaging, haemodynamics, previous interventions and longitudinal trajectories while frequently making decisions despite incomplete evidence. We propose that the expert congenital cardiologist may be distinguished not simply by knowing more answers, but by seeing problems differently. We introduce the LENS model as a conceptual framework for this process: Link information into a coherent clinical representation; Extract the discriminating signal from noise; Notice discordance, uncertainty and possible failure of the initial pattern; and Shift reasoning strategy, seek distributed expertise or learn when the existing model is insufficient. The framework integrates literature on medical expertise, deliberate practice, adaptive expertise, uncertainty and congenital cardiac decision-making. It offers a vocabulary for teaching, faculty development and future empirical study while deliberately preserving the distinction between career stage, reputation and demonstrated expertise.

articles.title: Patients with Congenital Heart Disease have Inferior Intent-to-Treat Outcomes When Listed for Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: While the impact of patient characteristics on waitlist and post-transplant mortality in pediatric heart transplantation has been widely studied, these metrics are limited in their ability to provide a complete picture for patients and their families. In contrast, less prevalent in the literature is an intent-to-treat analysis approach, which provides a single data point that encompasses both of these measures. This retrospective study examines pediatric patients listed for heart transplantation in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database between 2016 and 2025, evaluating the impact of transplant indication on intent-to-treat outcomes following the implementation of the 2016 allocation policy, which prioritizes children with congenital heart disease (CHD) on inotropic support. Kaplan-Meier analysis by transplant indication was performed across all pediatric patients listed during the study period, followed by Cox regression analyses using clinical and demographic covariates. In this initial analysis, CHD patients had poorer intent-to-treat outcomes. Risk and protective factors in this particularly high-risk population were then identified using univariable Cox regression. Significant factors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable Cox regression, which was used to generate a predictive score for one-year intent-to-treat mortality (c-statistic = 0.74). Risk factors significant in the multivariable analysis were age 0-1 years, geographic region, public (rather than private) insurance, need for life support and/or hemodialysis, and low serum albumin level. Following external validation and study of transplant timing on outcomes, these findings may serve as an additional tool to identify and prioritize high-risk patients and target modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Short-Term Thromboprophylaxis with Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Children After Surgical Bioprosthetic Pulmonary Valve Replacement: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: The impact of short-term thromboprophylaxis on short and mid-term outcomes in children undergoing surgical pulmonary valve placement (SPVR) is not well defined. Furthermore, the use of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in this population is not well studied. In this single-center, retrospective study, aspirin (ASA) monotherapy was compared to short-term (3 months) ASA + DOAC in children ≤ 18 years of age undergoing SPVR. We aimed to evaluate pulmonary valve (PV) mean gradient, PV peak gradient, and PV dysfunction (defined as moderate or greater regurgitation or stenosis) on echocardiogram at three time points: post-operative discharge (T1), one-year follow-up (T2), and most recent follow-up (T3). Sixty-six patients were included, of whom 32 received ASA monotherapy and 34 received ASA + DOAC for 90 days, with a total median follow-up time of 851 days. Baseline demographics were similar between the groups. There was no difference between groups regarding PV mean and peak gradient, or PV dysfunction at T1, T2, or T3. There were 16 bleeding events with no difference between the ASA and ASA + DOAC groups (6 (19%) vs. 10 (29%); p = 0.31, respectively). There were no differences regarding clinically relevant non-major bleeding, readmission within 30-days for bleeding, or hospital length of stay. In children undergoing SPVR, short-term thromboprophylaxis with ASA + DOAC had a similar safety profile to ASA monotherapy. DOAC use did not show significant benefit in PV function in the short-term. The benefits of DOAC thromboprophylaxis in SPVR should be evaluated with long-term, prospective studies.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatrics.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pediatric practice, particularly for triage, early detection, documentation, and point-of-care decision support. Some currently available tools perform at an expert level, including bone age estimation and fracture detection. Ambient documentation is easing a persistent burden, and language models effectively draft notes and messages. However, the evidence for the technology in pediatrics lags behind adult medicine. Of the 876 AI and machine learning (ML) enabled devices currently authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), only 149 carry labeling for patients younger than 18 years, and only 19% of those report validation in children. This review article examines where AI already exists in, or is approaching, everyday pediatric use. In each domain, the discussion pairs the strength of the technology with its present limitations. Notably, strong test set statistics do not always translate into better outcomes, and few pediatric tools have been validated externally or prospectively. The reasons for that gap are examined in depth: pediatric datasets are smaller and less representative, which leaves them more prone to bias, and a child's consent binds their data for longer than an adult's. In general, the argument is neither for swift adoption nor for resistance. Instead, it is for holding the technology to a high standard, which means keeping a human in the loop and training clinicians to be exacting judges of the currently available tools.

articles.title: The current state of artificial intelligence and adolescent mental health: the promise and perils of a new frontier.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care
articles.abstract: Adolescent mental health remains a topic of concern in the United States and worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the youth mental health crisis, which began nearly a decade earlier. The ongoing shortage of mental health professionals, including therapists and child and adolescent psychiatrists, means many adolescents who require mental health treatment do not receive it. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated promise in the field of adolescent mental health, including in screening, detection and risk prediction, intervention and treatment, clinical decision support and workflow augmentation, and in the training of future mental health professionals. However, the study of AI tools in the mental health space remains in its infancy, and most are not yet ready for routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, the potential risks of AI and its use in adolescent mental health treatment are significant and must be addressed prior to widespread use. Health care professionals, adolescents, and their caregivers need to develop AI literacy to use the technology safely and responsibly. Additionally, AI governance and legal frameworks are necessary to ensure that AI technology use is safe, equitable and ethical for all users. At the present time, AI technology should serve a supportive and complementary role to human-delivered adolescent mental health care.

articles.title: Neurosurgical outcome in infants with low-grade glioma - systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low-grade gliomas (LGGs) in infants pose significant clinical challenges due to their biologically distinct behavior and frequent location in surgically complex regions. While resection remains the preferred initial treatment, its feasibility is frequently limited by age-specific clinical and tumor-related factors. This review explores the role of tumor resection in infants and its association with survival, disease progression, and neurological outcome.
METHODS: A systematic literature search identified studies published within the last decade reporting surgical outcomes in infants with LGGs. Retrospective and prospective cohort studies and relevant case reports were included. Methodological quality was assessed, and relevant data were extracted and analyzed.
RESULTS: Complete resection was less commonly achieved in infants (20.1% vs. 30.9% in total), who demonstrate higher rates of tumor progression and more frequently require multimodal treatment strategies. Resectability was influenced by tumor location, growth pattern, and patient age. Although infants appear to experience lower overall survival rates and greater need for adjuvant, non-surgical therapies, a greater extent of resection is consistently associated with improved survival outcomes, reduced rates of reoperation, and decreased reliance on additional therapeutic modalities.
CONCLUSION: In infants with LGG, the maximal safe extent of resection should be pursued where anatomically feasible. However, particularly for midline tumors, where extensive resection is often not possible, comprehensive assessment of tumor biology and further investigation of non-surgical treatment options are essential to optimize therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Molecular diagnostics and liquid biopsy approaches in diffuse midline glioma: an update and literature review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs), H3 K27-altered, are aggressive childhood central nervous system tumors that remain almost uniformly fatal. Historically diagnosed radiographically as diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), these tumors are now defined by integrated anatomic and molecular criteria encompassing H3 K27-mutant, EZHIP-overexpressing, and EGFR-altered subtypes. Advances in tissue sampling have transformed understanding of their molecular landscape, but their eloquent location, the sampling bias inherent to stereotactic biopsy, and the impracticality of repeated tissue sampling have motivated interest in biofluid-based approaches. Liquid biopsy is being investigated as a complementary modality for molecular characterization, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of progression and resistance.
METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE for articles published through 31 July 2026, supplemented by a ClinicalTrials.gov search performed on the same date. Eligible articles described liquid biopsy methodologies, biomarker substrates, or clinical applications in DMG or DIPG; a separate, explicitly labeled category of enabling or methodologically relevant studies performed on tissue or in other tumor types was retained.
RESULTS: We summarize the WHO CNS5 molecular definition of DMG, the role and limitations of tissue-based diagnosis, the spectrum of liquid biopsy substrates and platforms with study-level performance data, and the incorporation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sampling into interventional DMG trials. We distinguish exploratory biomarker collection from analytically or clinically validated testing, and we address CSF access, safety, selection bias, and turnaround time.
CONCLUSIONS: Liquid biopsy in DMG remains investigational. No application, whether molecular diagnosis, response monitoring, pseudoprogression adjudication, or treatment adaptation, is currently prospectively validated for clinical decision-making. Standardized, prospective, multi-institutional studies with predefined thresholds are required.

articles.title: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children (≤ 3 years): A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children presents unique challenges related to cranial development, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disturbances, and subsequent reconstruction. This systematic review evaluated the indications, operative techniques, postoperative complications, and outcomes of conventional decompressive craniectomy and bone-preserving expansile procedures in children aged ≤ 3 years.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for English-language clinical studies involving age-eligible children. Study characteristics, operative details, complications, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Of the 1970 identified records, 46 publications were included, predominantly case reports and small case series. Indications included traumatic brain injury, cerebrovascular events, hemorrhage, and other causes of severe cerebral swelling. Procedures comprised conventional bone-out decompression and various bone-preserving techniques. Hydrocephalus, subdural and extracranial fluid collections, CSF leakage, wound complications, and bone-related morbidity were reported. Conventional decompression introduced subsequent reconstruction requirements and potential bone-resorption complications. Bone-preserving approaches maintained native cranial bone but were not free of CSF-related complications, altered bone fusion, or later reconstructive procedures. Inconsistent outcome definitions, age-specific denominators, and follow-up prevented reliable comparative estimates.
CONCLUSION: Evidence on decompressive surgery in children aged ≤ 3 years remains limited by small, heterogeneous studies and inconsistent outcome reporting. Although both conventional and bone-preserving techniques are feasible, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. CSF-related complications and reconstructive morbidity warrant particular attention. Standardized complication reporting and long-term assessment of cranial growth and neurodevelopment are essential to guide surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Vacuum-assisted elevation as a minimally invasive strategy for ping-pong skull fractures: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ping-pong skull fractures, although rare, represent a distinctive form of depressed skull fracture that primarily affects newborns and infants following traumatic brain injury, birth-related trauma, or compression during delivery. Due to the high malleability of the cranial vault at this age, the application of negative pressure over the depressed area has emerged as a minimally invasive therapeutic alternative capable of promoting bone elevation through local suction. The present study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this technique in the treatment of ping-pong skull fractures.
METHODS: A systematic search of publications was conducted in databases including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, covering studies published up to April 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series. Data analysis was performed using RStudio (version 2026.01.1).
RESULTS: Among the included studies, comprising a total of 81 patients, complete elevation of the ping-pong skull fracture was achieved in 86.52% of cases (95% CI 71.81-94.17; I2 = 25.0%). General complications were reported in 9.82% of patients (95% CI 4.84-18.90; I2 = 0%). The pooled rate of patients requiring a subsequent surgical approach after vacuum-assisted treatment was 10.58% (95% CI 3.95-25.40; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSION: The vacuum-assisted elevation represents a therapeutic option for PPF, showing encouraging results across clinical, radiological and safety outcomes. However, more and larger studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Magnetic interference and programmable valves: navigating hidden risks in everyday life and clinical settings.
articles.abstract: Programmable shunt valves, widely used in hydrocephalus, especially in children, allow non-invasive pressure adjustment, but their magnetic rotors make them vulnerable to unintended setting changes. We mapped evidence on magnetic interference from medical and everyday sources. We conducted a scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of PubMed, Embase and Scopus (to 20 September 2026), extracting design, valve, magnetic source, effect and reversibility, with descriptive quality appraisal. Of 674 records, 51 studies were included: 31 ex vivo or in vitro, 10 clinical series, 9 case reports and 1 of unstated design. Sources included magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), other medical and hearing devices, and everyday objects (magnetic toys, smartphones, headphones, tablets). Quality, appraised in 47 full texts, was variable. In two large clinical series, settings changed after 26.7% and 56.7% of MRI examinations, mainly in Strata but also in Polaris (31%), Certas Plus (12%) and proGAV (10%), never in the few Strata MR or proGAV 2.0; a randomized trial found none in Certas Plus. Ex vivo, locking valves resisted 3 T; at 7 T, outside their labeling, Certas Plus and proGAV 2.0 lost reprogrammability. Everyday devices altered most valves, mainly at contact, except proGAV models and M.blue Plus; several bench studies found no change. Susceptibility varies by model and appears highest in valves without a mechanical lock. MRI is the best-documented clinically relevant source of setting changes; settings should be verified afterwards in all valves. Given limited evidence, distance from magnets and caregiver education, particularly for children, are precautions rather than proven safety limits.

articles.title: Pediatric brainstem incidentalomas: an international retrospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatric incidental brain tumors have become an increasing clinical challenge due to the widespread use of neuroimaging. These incidentalomas encompass a broad spectrum of pathologies, ranging from low-grade to high-grade lesions. The brainstem represents one of the most complex and surgically risky anatomical regions. Incidentalomas of the brainstem are a poorly understood entity, and standardized management protocols are lacking.
METHODS: A retrospective, international, multicenter study was conducted across nine tertiary centers in six countries. Patients younger than 20 years with incidentally discovered brainstem lesions demonstrating radiological characteristics of a tumor were included. Management strategies, timing of intervention, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 32 patients were identified, including 16 females. Age at diagnosis ranged from 1 to 17.3 years (mean 7.5 ± 4.8 years). The most common indications for imaging were unrelated conditions such as macrocephaly, transient strabismus, and growth delay. Seventeen patients (53%) were managed conservatively without surgery during a mean follow-up of 84.2 ± 53.2 months. Thirteen patients (41%) underwent immediate intervention including three with presumed diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, while two (6%) required delayed intervention 67.8 and 72.1 months after diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Similar to incidental lesions in other brain locations, brainstem incidentalomas represent a wide spectrum of neoplastic pathologies, including both low-grade and high-grade tumors. While many lesions remain stable under observation, a subset may demonstrate progression and ultimately require surgical intervention.

articles.title: Pediatric nondysraphic intramedullary spinal cord lipomas: surgical burden, reoperations, and long-term outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Spinal cord lipomas without spinal dysraphism are rare tumors but can cause substantial neurological deficits. Resection is particularly challenging owing to tight tumor-cord interface and there is no clear consensus regarding the management in the pediatric population. Therefore, we review our experience treating a cohort of pediatric patients with intramedullary lipomas.
METHODS: A database of pediatric patients surgically treated for intramedullary spinal cord tumors at a large comprehensive cancer center and affiliated children's hospital was reviewed between 2012 and 2025. Cases with a confirmed histology of lipoma were included. Demographic, surgical, and outcome data were collected.
RESULTS: Seven patients were identified with spinal cord lipomas, with a median age of 9 years. All tumors spanned the cervical cord. Symptoms included pain, paresthesias, numbness, weakness, and bowel/bladder dysfunction. Five patients required repeat surgeries for hardware failure, repeat debulking, cerebrospinal fluid leak, and scoliosis repair. Two patients had long-term tumor progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical decision-making in pediatric intramedullary lipomas needs to balance maximal safe resection with the risk of iatrogenic deficits. Patients should be counseled about the significant risks and need for lifelong monitoring. In our series, reoperations were frequent and included both disease-related (repeat debulking/detethering) and treatment-related (CSF leak, deformity, and hardware complications). Early intervention before patients develop debilitating symptoms may help maximize long-term neurological outcomes.

articles.title: Does timing of decompressive craniectomy influence outcomes in pediatric traumatic brain injury? A scoping review of institutional series and cohort studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) is a leading cause of disability and death in the pediatric population, frequently complicated by refractory intracranial hypertension. While decompressive craniectomy (DC) is utilized to relieve elevated intracranial pressure (ICP), the optimal timing for surgical intervention remains undetermined.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed to identify studies evaluating the timing of DC in pediatric patients (< 18 years) with sTBI.
RESULTS: Eleven retrospective studies (ten independent cohorts) met the inclusion criteria. The mean or median admission GCS ranged from 3.5 to 6, and the mean preoperative ICP ranged from 27.2 to 49.8 mmHg. The definition of "early" DC varied substantially, ranging from under one hour to 24 h post-injury. A large database study observed higher in-hospital mortality after DC within 2 h of admission, most likely reflecting confounding by indication, as these patients had greater injury severity. Smaller cohorts found no association between timing and mortality. Overall, the synthesized evidence demonstrated no statistically significant correlation between time to surgery and long-term favorable neurological outcomes, except for one study that observed a correlation between favorable outcomes and DC within 4 h.
CONCLUSION: Current clinical evidence is limited and methodologically heterogeneous, precluding the establishment of definitive timing thresholds for DC in pediatric sTBI. No consistent association between surgical timing and long-term functional outcomes has been demonstrated, and the higher mortality after very early DC likely reflects baseline injury severity.

articles.title: Prognosis and Determinants of Mortality of Infective Endocarditis in Liver Cirrhosis: a Multicenter Case-matched Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) in patients with liver cirrhosis is poorly characterized, and the impact of cirrhosis severity on management and outcomes remains unclear. We aimed to describe the epidemiological, clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and prognostic features of IE in patients with cirrhosis compared to controls without cirrhosis.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective bicentric cohort study including consecutive patients with definite or possible IE. Patients with cirrhosis were matched 1:4 with controls without cirrhosis on age, sex, center, comorbidities, prosthetic valve status, and causative microorganism. Cirrhosis severity was assessed using the Child-Pugh classification. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with mortality.
RESULTS: Among 1550 screened IE episodes, 79 patients (5.1%) had cirrhosis and were matched to 316 controls. Baseline characteristics and IE predisposing conditions were similar between groups including microbiology. Cardiac surgery was performed less often in patients with cirrhosis than in controls (19/79 [24.1%] versus 146/316 [46.2%], P = .001). Cirrhosis-related complications were frequent and increased with disease severity, including acute kidney injury (P = .033). Ninety-day mortality was higher in patients with cirrhosis than in controls (28/79 [35.4%] vs 42/316 [13.3%], P < .001). In multivariable analysis, absence of cardiac surgery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.2; 95% CI [1.0-4.9]), Child-Pugh B (aOR 2.9; 95% CI, 1.1-7.5) and Child-Pugh C cirrhosis (aOR 6.9; 95% CI, 2.3-20.6), but not Child-Pugh A (aOR 1.6; 95% CI, .3-8.9), were independently associated with 90-day mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: IE prognosis in patients with cirrhosis is driven primarily by liver disease severity and associated organ dysfunction.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Bipolar Disorder.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Pediatric (bipolar disorder) BD carries substantial morbidity, including prolonged symptom burden, high rates of suicide attempts and substance use, and psychosocial impairment. Accurate diagnosis requires careful longitudinal assessment, as presentations in youth often differ from adults, with more rapid cycling, mixed features, and irritability over classic euphoric mania. Early diagnosis and treatment are critical to reduce potential impairment and to support early recovery of youth with BD. The purpose of this article is to discuss the use of antipsychotics in the treatment of pediatric BD.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Pediatric Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Trauma-Related Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Childhood trauma is associated with a broad spectrum of psychiatric symptoms beyond core posttraumatic stress disorder criteria, including emotional dysregulation, aggression, sleep disturbance, and behavioral instability that impair functioning and safety. The pediatric evidence base is limited to case reports and small observational studies, with no randomized controlled trials. Adult data show modest and inconsistent benefits with notable adverse effects. Antipsychotics should be embedded within trauma-informed care, applied in a time-limited, symptom-specific manner, and closely monitored for metabolic, neurologic, and potential neurodevelopmental effects. Their role remains narrow and adjunctive, with psychotherapy, diagnostic precision, and risk minimization as primary priorities.

articles.title: Clozapine in Children and Adolescents: Indications, Efficacy, and Safety.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic but it remains underutilized. This review synthesizes evidence for clozapine use in children and adolescents, including additional indications such as suicidality, aggression, autism, and catatonia. Children have differences in pharmacokinetics, dosing, and side effect profiles. Although side effects can include agranulocytosis, myocarditis, and metabolic effects, regular laboratory and vital sign monitoring and adjunctive treatments can mitigate these risks. Persistent barriers often delay initiation, but increased education and systems-level changes can reduce barriers to clozapine use. Recent regulatory changes and emerging evidence support earlier and more widespread use of clozapine in appropriately selected pediatric populations.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Adolescents with Substance Use and Substance Use Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Antipsychotic medications are frequently prescribed off label in adolescents, particularly to manage agitation, behavioral dysregulation, and sleep disturbances, often in the context of substance use. However, their use is not consistently supported by a strong evidence base and carries meaningful risks, including metabolic, neurologic, and long-term health consequences. This article examines the clinical complexity of adolescents with substance use and co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, highlighting the risk of diagnostic ambiguity during acute intoxication or withdrawal. We provide a practical, developmentally informed framework to guide clinicians in the thoughtful, time-limited, and indication-specific use of antipsychotics in this population.

articles.title: Psychosis in medically ill Children and Adolescents.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Psychosis in children and adolescents caused by medical illnesses/conditions is rare. Visual hallucinations, confusion, and change of baseline mentation support this diagnosis. Certain physical examination findings also suggest a secondary etiology of psychosis. Specific laboratory, imaging, and other tests are then utilized. Numerous medical etiologies have been identified to cause psychosis in children and adolescents, specifically delirium, inborn errors of metabolism, genetic syndromes, encephalitides, other systemic infections, space occupying lesions, seizures, trauma, and endocrine and nutritional disorders. Treatment is mainly extrapolated from the delirium literature, and there are conflicting data showing the utility of antipsychotic use for secondary psychosis.

articles.title: Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder and Atypical Antipsychotics.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD) was introduced to classify children with impairing, chronic irritability and outbursts. Approaching treatment starts with evidence-informed assessment including using standardized rating scales to support diagnostic decision making and track symptom response. DMDD has no Food and Drug Administration-approved medications and few randomized clinical trials demonstrating efficacy. It is recommended to start with treating co-occurring disorders, often attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and then to treat residual symptoms. Atypical antipsychotics have evidence of efficacy in treating irritability and reactive aggression and come with adverse effects, including metabolic side effects. Therefore, benefit versus risk analysis of atypical antipsychotics is needed.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Antipsychotic medications may be effective for the management of irritability, aggression, and other mental health disorders in youth with autism spectrum disorder and other neurodevelopmental disorders including intellectual disability. While these medications may significantly improve safety outcomes and quality of life, autistic youth may be at greater risk of overprescribing, side effects, and insufficient monitoring. Best practice includes clarifying target symptoms/behaviors, using lowest effective doses, ensuring first-line behavioral and environmental interventions, collaboratively working with parents/guardians and other care team members, utilizing creative strategies to follow gold-standard monitoring guidelines, and deprescribing when able.

articles.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and Disruptive Behavior Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Disruptive behavior disorders (DBDs; oppositional defiant disorders, and conduct disorders) frequently co-occur with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and can be commonly associated with aggression, a major driver of clinical presentation and service utilization. Despite no US Food and Drug Administration -approved medications for DBDs in this population, antipsychotics, specifically second-generation agents, are used in clinical practice for this purpose. Evidence supports behavioral interventions as a first-line treatment of DBDs. In youth with comorbid ADHD, optimized stimulant and non-stimulant treatments of ADHD are indicated. Among antipsychotics, risperidone has the strongest evidence for reducing aggression, particularly as adjunctive therapy to stimulant medications.

articles.title: Curative Therapy for Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Model Disease for Multidisciplinary Sarcoma Care.
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is an aggressive soft tissue sarcoma affecting children and adolescents. Treatment involves a multidisciplinary approach, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. This review focuses on newly diagnosed RMS and discusses the role of surgery in RMS evaluation and treatment, highlighting the importance of achieving local control. We also discuss chemotherapy and radiation therapy, as well as ongoing controversies and novel strategies under investigation, including targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and novel biomarkers. Efforts are ongoing to improve outcomes for patients with RMS, particularly those with high-risk disease.

articles.title: Classification of transmission routes in neonatal scrub typhus: a three-rule biologically anchored framework derived from systematic review data.
articles.abstract: Neonatal scrub typhus (NST) may be acquired vertically or horizontally, with important implications for clinical and public health management. No existing framework systematically classifies the transmission route in NST. A systematic review of published NST cases identified a critical reporting gap: 70.3% (26/37) had no author-reported transmission classification, with inconsistent terminology and limited biological justification. We developed a biologically anchored framework to address this gap. A three-rule hierarchical classification framework was developed through systematic retrospective application to 37 individual patient cases from 21 studies published between 2000 and 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420251054293). Four independent, blinded investigators applied the framework. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Fleiss' kappa (κ), and majority agreement was defined as concordance among at least three of four investigators. The framework was anchored by three biologically grounded principles: mechanistic evidence (neonatal eschar), temporal plausibility based on incubation-period boundaries, and probabilistic maternal diagnostic evidence. Framework classification yielded Proven Horizontal (n = 9), Probable Horizontal (n = 11), Definitive Vertical (n = 2), Probable Vertical (n = 6), and Indeterminate (n = 9). Among the 28 cases with an assignable transmission route, 20 (71.4%) were classified as horizontal and 8 (28.6%) as vertical. Inter-rater agreement was near-perfect (Fleiss κ = 0.82; 95% confidence interval 0.71-0.93), with majority agreement (≥3 of 4 investigators) in 91.89% of cases (34/37). Disagreement occurred predominantly within the day of life 8-20 contested window, particularly when maternal testing was incomplete or noncontributory. The proposed three-rule framework provides a reproducible approach to transmission-route classification in NST and warrants prospective external validation. Three data elements, namely, neonatal eschar, precise day of life at onset of illness, and maternal diagnostic evidence (clinical and laboratory), should be reported in future NST cases.

articles.title: A quality improvement initiative to increase kangaroo mother care duration in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit in Northern India.
articles.abstract: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) reduces mortality and morbidity in preterm and low-birth-weight infants, but daily duration in Indian neonatal units often falls short of the World Health Organization minimum of 8 hours. In our Level III neonatal unit, a baseline audit found a mean KMC duration of 4 hours/day, and infants on non-invasive respiratory support rarely received KMC. Using the Point-of-Care Quality Improvement framework, three Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles over 12 weeks (December 2024-February 2025) addressed staff training for KMC during continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), family engagement and workflow, and behavioural reinforcement. A 12-week sustenance phase followed. Eligible infants weighed <2000 g, were haemodynamically stable, and were not on invasive ventilation or phototherapy. KMC hours were taken from shift-wise nursing records. The outcome was mean daily KMC duration per infant, analysed on a run chart. All 20 eligible infants received KMC, 12 (60%) while on CPAP or HFNC. Median per-infant KMC duration was 9.75 hours/day (interquartile range 8.8-10.6), compared with 4 hours/day at baseline; 17 infants (85%) averaged at least 8 hours/day. Duration was lower among infants who started KMC during the second and third cycles and returned to the median during the sustenance phase. No hypothermia or device dislodgement occurred; one infant had an apnoeic episode. A people-centred quality improvement initiative using existing unit resources was associated with longer daily KMC, including in infants on non-invasive respiratory support, and the gain was maintained over 12 weeks. The 12-hour target could not be reached.

articles.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).
CONCLUSION: Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

articles.title: Exploring outcomes and insights from joint agency response investigations for children with learning disabilities who die unexpectedly: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In England, sudden unexpected child deaths are investigated through a joint agency response (JAR). There is wide variation in practice concerning JAR, particularly for children with underlying health conditions, many of whom have learning disability (LD); potentially limiting identification of causes and contributory factors for deaths.
METHODS: All child deaths with LD (including those who died suddenly and unexpectedly), aged 4–17 years, dying between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022 were identified retrospectively by the National Child Mortality Database (NCMD). Data were extracted from NCMD records and information on life-limiting conditions (LLCs) obtained from Hospital Episode Statistics. Unexpected deaths investigated through a JAR were compared with those without for demographics, underlying conditions, causes of death and process of investigations.
RESULTS: There were 738 deaths of children with LD of which 309 (41.8%) were unexpected; 257/309 (83%) had LLCs; 215/309 (69.5%) were subject to JAR. Chromosomal, genetic and congenital anomalies were the most common cause of death accounting for 95/215 (44.2%) JAR cases and 49/94 (52.1%) non-JAR cases. Compliance with JAR processes overall was low. Postmortem examination (PM) took place for 166/215 (77.2%) JAR cases and 21/94 (22.3%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). A new condition was identified as the cause of death rather than a pre-existing condition as cause of death in 112/215 (52.3%) JAR cases compared with 13/94 (13.8%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). After adjustment for JAR components, only PM remained associated, with an increase in chance of identifying a new cause of death (72.1% (95% CI 61.6% to 72.7%)). JAR home visits provided little new information relevant to the cause of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Clearer guidance is required on when and how to undertake JAR investigations following sudden deaths of children with LD. Current guidance is largely based on deaths of previously healthy children.

articles.title: Predictors of refractory CMV infection in children with haematological malignancies after allogeneic HSCT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) remains a major complication of allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), yet predictors and immunological consequences of refractory infection are poorly characterised in children.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 144 children undergoing allo-HSCT for haematological malignancy, assessing predictors of clinically significant CMV infection (csCMVi) and refractory infection, and lymphocyte reconstitution in 107 patients with serial immunophenotyping.
RESULTS: Reactivation occurred in 30% of patients, csCMVi in 27%, of whom 67% met refractory criteria (26/144, 18% of the full cohort). Recipient seropositivity strongly predicted csCMVi (odds ratio [OR] 10.84, 95% CI 4.33-32.14) but was not significantly associated with refractory infection, a comparison limited by the csCMVi cohort being almost uniformly recipient seropositive. Among csCMVi patients, refractory infection was predicted by matched unrelated donor (MUD) (OR 13.00, 95% CI 2.28-101.64) and anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) use (OR 4.59, 95% CI 1.20-19.96). An ordinal donor/ATG gradient showed stepwise increases in refractory risk, from 25% (matched sibling donors) to 88% (MUD with ATG, OR 2.69 per level). Refractory infection was associated with longer viraemia (111.5 vs 14.0 days), higher cumulative viral load, and impaired T-cell reconstitution with lower CD3⁺, CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ counts at day +90 and five-fold lower TEMRA CD8⁺ counts at day +180.
CONCLUSIONS: The transplant factors associated with refractory infection differed from those associated with reactivation, and refractory infection carried a distinct immunological signature, T-cell reconstitution is an accessible biomarker, and TEMRA CD8⁺ expansion warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Prospective Multi-Institutional Validation of a Practical Eculizumab Dosing Regimen for Transplant-Associated Thrombotic Microangiopathy in Children and Young Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA) is a life-threatening complication following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Terminal complement blocker eculizumab improves outcomes in high-risk complement-mediated TA-TMA, but HSCT recipients exhibit accelerated and highly variable drug clearance, particularly in the presence of gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding, making dosing regimens developed for other complement-mediated diseases inadequate. Although individualized dosing using real-time complement biomarker monitoring is effective, these resources are unavailable at most transplant centers, limiting optimized implementation of eculizumab therapy.
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to translate extensive real-time PK/PD-guided eculizumab dosing experience into practical, fixed dosing regimens presented in an easy-to-use table format for HSCT recipients with high-risk TA-TMA, enabling implementation at centers without access to real-time complement biomarker and drug pharmacokinetic (PK) monitoring. We sought to derive weight- and bleeding status-based dosing recommendations for the loading, induction, and maintenance phases of therapy, determine the treatment duration required for most patients, identify dosing schedules with the lowest drug utilization, and prospectively validate this dosing framework in an independent multi-institutional clinical study.
STUDY DESIGN: Eculizumab dosing requirements were derived using PK/PD model-informed simulations integrated with real-time drug concentration, complement biomarker, and clinical outcome data from 64 consecutively treated patients with high-risk TA-TMA (PK64 cohort). Weight- and bleeding status-based fixed dosing regimens were developed for the loading, induction, and maintenance phases of therapy and prospectively validated in an independent multi-institutional interventional study of 23 patients receiving early eculizumab therapy for high-risk TA-TMA with multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (PK23 cohort).
RESULTS: A total of 87 HSCT recipients with high-risk complement-mediated TA-TMA were included. PK/PD modeling identified distinct dosing requirements according to body weight and gastrointestinal bleeding status, established more granular weight categories than currently approved eculizumab dosing, defined phase-specific loading, induction, and maintenance regimens, and identified drug-utilization-optimized dosing schedules with equivalent predicted clinical outcomes. The final product was a set of fixed eculizumab dosing regimens summarized in practical table format for routine clinical use without real-time complement biomarker monitoring. The derived dosing framework was then prospectively validated in an independent, multi-institutional interventional study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03518203; IND 136738; NIH R01 HD093773). Validation confirmed that the derived dosing framework accurately predicted phase-specific dosing requirements, pharmacokinetic behavior, and complement control across independent patient populations, supporting the reproducibility and clinical applicability of the proposed dosing tables.
CONCLUSIONS: This study translates extensive real-time PK/PD experience into practical model-informed fixed eculizumab dosing regimens presented in an easy-to-use table format for HSCT-associated TA-TMA. The framework provides weight-, bleeding status-, and treatment phase-specific guidance that can be implemented at centers without real-time complement biomarker monitoring. It is applicable to eculizumab and eculizumab biosimilars and supports biologically informed treatment discontinuation once complement-mediated disease activity has resolved, helping avoid unnecessarily prolonged therapy.

articles.title: Prenatal paracetamol (acetaminophen) exposure and autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects approximately 1% of children worldwide. Paracetamol is the most widely used analgesic during pregnancy, yet whether prenatal exposure increases offspring risk of ASD remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the association between prenatal paracetamol exposure and ASD in offspring.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and CINAHL were searched to 17 September 2026. We identified observational studies evaluating prenatal paracetamol exposure and clinically diagnosed ASD in offspring. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. We pooled adjusted effect estimates using random-effects meta-analysis. Bayesian random-effects models estimated posterior probabilities of clinically important risk (relative risk (RR) >1.10) thresholds. We rated the certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: Nine cohort studies met eligibility criteria; seven (n=5 817 129 offspring) contributed to the primary meta-analysis. The effect of paracetamol on ASD risk was very uncertain (RR 1.10; 95% CI 1.05 to 1.15; very low certainty). Bayesian analyses showed posterior probabilities of a clinically important increase ranging from 26% to 61% across prior assumptions. Pooled estimate across five sibling-controlled analyses showed little to no difference in ASD risk (HR of 0.99; 95% CI 0.95 to 1.03; low certainty), with posterior probabilities of a clinically important increase of ≤1.3% across all priors.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence on the effect of prenatal paracetamol exposure on ASD risk is very uncertain. Furthermore, sibling-controlled analyses, accounting for familial confounding, suggest little to no difference in ASD risk. These findings do not support a causal relationship.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261306129.

articles.title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.
SETTING: A tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India.
PARTICIPANTS: 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity, including duration of hospitalisation, intensive care stay, oxygen requirement, inotropic support and ventilator support.
RESULTS: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. Mucocutaneous manifestations varied significantly across waves (p=0.02). The duration of hospital stay (p=0.004), duration of fever (p=0.009) and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p=0.003) decreased significantly over successive waves, suggesting reduced overall disease severity. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly (p=0.002), while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave (p<0.0001). Oxygen requirement declined significantly in the third wave (p=0.02), whereas intensive care stay, inotropic support and ventilator support did not differ significantly between waves.
CONCLUSIONS: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement. The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.

articles.title: Role of hyponatraemia in risk stratification of well-appearing febrile infants aged 28-90 days: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Distinguishing invasive and serious bacterial infections (IBI and SBI) remains challenging. We aimed to evaluate the role of hyponatraemia in identifying IBI and SBI and to assess its contribution to the Step-by-Step Approach in well-appearing febrile infants aged 28–90 days.
METHODS: This single-centre, 10-year retrospective study included well-appearing febrile infants aged 28–90 days without an apparent source of infection. Clinical characteristics were compared between infants with and without hyponatremia. In patients meeting the laboratory criteria of the Step-by-Step Approach, serum sodium was integrated into the final step and diagnostic performance was compared with the original algorithm.
RESULTS: Among 381 patients, 69 (18.1%) had hyponatremia. IBI was more frequent in the hyponatraemia group than in the normonatraemia group (11.6% vs 1.3%, p<0.001). Hyponatraemia was also associated with higher SBI rates, hospitalisation and longer length of stay (p<0.001). Of the 291 patients with procalcitonin measurements, 9 (3.1%) had IBI and 74 (25.4%) had SBI. Among 164 (56.3%) classified as low-risk, 1 (0.6%) had IBI and 18 (10.9%) had SBI. Integrating serum sodium into the algorithm identified 1 additional IBI and 6 additional SBI cases among low-risk infants and improved the negative predictive value for IBI (100% vs 99.4%). The sodium-integrated approach also showed a lower negative likelihood ratio (<0.01 vs 0.19) and lower post-test probability of IBI (<0.01% vs 0.6%); as this reflects a single reclassified IBI case, this estimate warrants cautious interpretation pending validation in larger cohorts. The SBI reclassification, based on a larger number of events, showed a more robust improvement in sensitivity (75.7% vs 83.8%).
CONCLUSION: Hyponatremia is associated with increased IBI and SBI rates in well-appearing febrile infants. Integrating serum sodium into the Step-by-Step Approach modestly improved risk stratification and may enhance identification of low-risk patients.

articles.title: Paediatric clinicians' knowledge and experiences of e-bike and e-scooter harms in children and young people: a UK national service evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: E-bike and e-scooter use is increasing, with growing concern about harms in children and young people (CYP). We assessed paediatric clinicians’ legislative knowledge, clinical experiences and prevention opportunities.
METHODS: This UK national service evaluation comprised a narrative literature review, clinician survey, structured local needs-assessment discussions and contextual mortality data from England. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; free-text responses and discussion notes underwent descriptive thematic synthesis.
RESULTS: 484 clinicians contributed: 353 completed the survey, 217 participated in structured local discussions and 86 contributed to both components. Legislative knowledge was limited: 11% correctly identified the minimum age for rental e-bike use, 22% for private e-bike use and 25% knew that a driving licence is required for rental e-scooter use. Of 303 clinicians, 142 (47%) reported encountering e-bike or e-scooter-related injuries or discussing micromobility use with CYP in the past year. Reported harms included head injury, fractures and polytrauma, with dual riding, lack of helmet use and motor-vehicle collisions commonly reported. National mortality data identified 17 child deaths in England between April 2019 and December 2025 related to e-bike or e-scooter use; numbers were small, and 2025 data were incomplete, but the distribution over time raises concern that deaths may be increasing. Clinicians reported inconsistent advice provision, barriers to discussion and support for coordinated prevention strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: E-bike and e-scooter-related harm is an emerging paediatric public health concern. Improved education about additional risks, integration into routine risk assessment, improved injury surveillance and coordinated policy responses, including legislative review, are needed to reduce preventable harm.

articles.title: Opioid prescribing practices at discharge across common pediatric urologic surgery procedures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In 2020, the American Pediatric Surgical Association released evidence-based guidelines for opioid prescribing after common urologic surgeries. Procedures were grouped into recommended opioid free recovery (OFR) and opioid free recovery possible (OFRP). The purpose of this study was to evaluate opioids prescribed at discharge across common procedures in pediatric urologic surgery.
METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (2023) was queried for patients ≤18 years undergoing elective procedures, including one OFR procedure (hypospadias repair) and two OFRP procedures (orchiopexy and pyeloplasty). The primary outcome was the proportion of opioid prescriptions at discharge for OFR and OFRP procedures. Secondary outcomes were demographic and clinical variables associated with an opioid prescription at discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 4149 patients underwent hypospadias repair (OFR), while 2916 patients underwent OFRP procedures (1220 orchiopexy; 1696 pyeloplasty). For hypospadias repair, 28.2% were given an opioid prescription at discharge with associations of opioid prescriptions with age, race, ethnicity, postoperative length of stay and operation time. Within ORFP procedures, 21.1% of patients were prescribed an opioid at discharge. Factors associated with opioid prescriptions after orchiopexy were age, ethnicity, history of asthma and operative time, while after pyeloplasty, associated factors were age, ethnicity, procedure approach, and postoperative length of stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite published guidelines, hypospadias repair, orchiopexy and pyeloplasty procedures had >20% of patients prescribed opioid at discharge. Further research and quality improvement efforts on postoperative pain management protocols to improve opioid stewardship in pediatric urology are warranted.

articles.title: Chasing VUR in infants after UTI: A national survey of clinical practice and concordance with recommendations among polish paediatricians, paediatric nephrologists, and urologists.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the availability of recommendations regarding post-urinary tract infection (UTI) diagnostics in infants, clinical practice remains heterogeneous. Observations suggest that vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is diagnosed in a relatively small proportion of voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) examinations, which may reflect either limited precision of the guidelines or suboptimal concordance with them.
AIM: The aim of the study was to assess familiarity and concordance with current diagnostic recommendations regarding the use of VCUG after UTI in infants among Polish clinicians.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A nationwide anonymous online survey was conducted among physicians working in centres performing VCUG. A total of 86 responses were obtained; 21% of respondents were paediatric urologists, and 79% were paediatricians and nephrologists/paediatric nephrologists. The participants were asked to comment on different clinical scenarios and to complete a structured questionnaire.
RESULTS: Knowledge of indications for VCUG was declared by 92% of respondents. Concordance varied substantially between individual clinical scenarios (39.5-98.8%): it was nearly complete (98.8%) in cases with a clear clinical picture (impaired renal function, hydronephrosis with ureteric dilatation), but only 48.8% of respondents referred an infant with recurrent febrile UTIs and normal US findings for VCUG. VCUG was most commonly postponed for ≥2 weeks after resolution of infection (90%). Across the clinical scenarios, physicians in training most consistently selected guideline-concordant responses (64.7-100%). Routine antibiotic prophylaxis prior to VCUG was used by 68.6% of physicians. Ultrasound was most commonly recommended twice-during the acute phase of UTI and after its resolution (43%). Renal pelvic dilatation with anteroposterior (AP) diameter of ≥10 to <15 mm was most commonly considered an indication for VCUG, regardless of UTI history. Multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a history of UTI was considered an indication for VCUG by 50% of respondents, with urologists being the least likely to recommend the procedure in such cases. Isolated ureteric dilatation and a hypodysplastic kidney with urinary tract dilatation were considered the most suggestive US findings for VUR (56% and 77%, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite good awareness of current recommendations, responses varied substantially across clinical scenarios, particularly in areas where recommendations were less specific or differed between societies. The greatest uncertainty concerns US findings suggestive of VUR, timing of VCUG and antimicrobial prophylaxis. More unified, explicit and clinically applicable recommendations are needed.

articles.title: Mauriac Syndrome in the Era of Advanced Diabetes Care: A Narrative Mini-Review.
articles.abstract: Mauriac syndrome is a rare but clinically significant complication of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes mellitus, characterized by growth failure, delayed puberty, and hepatomegaly due to excessive hepatic glycogen accumulation. Although once considered a historical entity of the pre-intensive insulin era, it continues to be reported sporadically in children, adolescents, and adults, largely through case reports and small series, with no robust estimates of true prevalence available. Recurrent cycles of hyperglycemia and supraphysiologic insulin exposure drive hepatic glycogen deposition, while limited evidence, primarily from small observational studies, suggests that genetic susceptibility may modulate individual risk. Recent work has identified heterozygous variants in genes involved in hepatic glycogen metabolism, particularly those encoding components of phosphorylase kinase (e.g., PHKG2), although their causal role remains incompletely defined. In many patients, hepatic glycogenosis is the sole manifestation and can mimic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, leading to diagnostic delay. The condition is largely reversible with sustained improvement in glycemic control; however, overly rapid correction may precipitate microvascular complications. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on the epidemiology, clinical features, pathophysiology, diagnostic considerations, and management of Mauriac syndrome, highlighting its ongoing relevance in contemporary diabetes practice.

articles.title: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy type 1 associated with a novel RANBPe2 variant: Clinical, radiological, molecular, and computational analysis.
articles.abstract: RANBP2/Nup358 is the largest human nucleoporin and a major structural and functional component of the cytoplasmic filaments of the nuclear pore complex. Heterozygous missense variants in RANBP2 are associated with Acute Necrotizing Encephalopathy type 1 (ANE1), a rare autosomal dominant pediatric encephalopathy often triggered by viral infection and characterized by rapid neurological deterioration and symmetric thalamic lesions. In this study, we report a 5-year-old girl who presented with status epilepticus following fever and viral nasopharyngitis. Brain MRI revealed bilateral thalamic and brainstem lesions consistent with acute necrotizing encephalopathy initially suggestive of Leigh syndrome. Full mitochondrial DNA sequencing, long-range PCR, and quantification of mitochondrial DNA copy number revealed no pathogenic mtDNA variants, no detectable large-scale mtDNA rearrangement, and no mtDNA depletion. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in RANBP2, c.3163C > T (p.Pro1055Ser), affecting a highly conserved proline residue located in the FG repeat region in the inter-domain linker between the N-terminal domain and the first Ran-binding domain (RanBD1). The variant was not detected in either tested parent. "Residue 1055 was predicted to lie within a low-confidence, intrinsically disordered region. Therefore, the structural models were considered descriptive and were not interpreted as evidence of mutation-induced structural or interaction changes. The clinicoradiological phenotype and genetic findings support p.Pro1055Ser as a candidate ANE1-associated variant, although its pathogenic role remains unproven due to the absence of variant-specific functional validation. This report expands the spectrum of RANBP2 variants observed in ANE-compatible phenotypes.

articles.title: Cochlear implantation in children with cerebral palsy: a retrospective cohort study of auditory and speech outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cochlear implantation (CI) is standard for severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss, but outcomes in children with cerebral palsy (CP) remain unclear.
AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To compare auditory and speech outcomes after CI in children with and without CP.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 85 children (40 with CP, 45 without comorbidities). Improvement was defined as change between 6- and 12-month post-implantation assessments; preoperative CAP/SIR were unavailable, so 6-month scores reflected early implant use rather than baseline. Responders were identified using distribution-based thresholds (ΔCAP < 3; ΔSIR < 2), adjusted for age and sex.
RESULTS: Both groups improved significantly from 6 to 12 months (p < 0.001), but children without CP had higher CAP and SIR scores at both follow-ups. CP was associated with suboptimal SIR improvement (adjusted OR 2.29; 95% CI 1.23-4.26) and CAP improvement (adjusted OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.83-7.58).
CONCLUSION: CI produced sustained 6- to 12-month improvements, although absolute scores remained lower in children with CP. Unvalidated thresholds and lack of CP subtype/GMFCS stratification limit generalization.
SIGNIFICANCE: These findings can guide realistic family counseling and highlight the need for validated thresholds and CP-specific stratification in future research.

articles.title: Using placental biomarkers to guide delivery in late preterm preeclampsia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In women with late preterm preeclampsia without severe features, the optimal timing of delivery remains uncertain. Earlier delivery may reduce progression to severe maternal disease, whereas expectant management may limit neonatal morbidity related to late preterm birth. Because conventional clinical criteria have limited ability to predict short-term deterioration, angiogenic biomarkers may provide additional risk stratification. A randomized clinical trial showed that biomarker-guided timing of delivery reduced progression to preeclampsia with severe features; however, its effectiveness in routine clinical practice has not been established.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether angiogenic biomarker-guided timing of delivery, when implemented in routine clinical practice, was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features and to compare short-term neonatal outcomes between study periods.
STUDY DESIGN: Before-after cohort study at the two principal recruiting centers of the previous trial, including singleton pregnancies with preeclampsia without severe features between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks. Women managed expectantly from 2014 to 2017 were compared with women managed according to angiogenic biomarkers from 2022 to 2025. Delivery was recommended for an abnormal angiogenic profile, defined according to the center-specific protocol as PlGF <60 pg/mL in Center 1 or an sFlt-1/PlGF ratio >110 in Center 2. The primary maternal outcome was progression to preeclampsia with severe features. The coprimary neonatal outcome was composite neonatal morbidity, including respiratory distress, hypoglycemia, jaundice, 5-minute Apgar score <7, umbilical arterial pH <7.00, or neonatal admission. Confounding was addressed with propensity-score weighting and multivariable regression.
RESULTS: Progression to preeclampsia with severe features decreased from 52.1% to 19.6%, an observed unadjusted absolute difference of 32.5 percentage points (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.22; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.13-0.38). Composite neonatal morbidity decreased from 57.0% to 45.6% (aOR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30-0.81); this difference was driven by fewer neonatal admissions, whereas neonatal morbidity excluding admission was nearly identical between periods (35.2% vs 35.6%). Gestational age at delivery did not differ significantly between the biomarker-guided and standard-care periods (36.7 vs 36.6 weeks; adjusted mean difference, 0.09 weeks; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.28).
CONCLUSION: Angiogenic biomarker-guided delivery timing was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features, without earlier delivery at the cohort level. No between-period difference was observed in short-term neonatal morbidity excluding neonatal admission; because the study was not designed or powered to establish neonatal noninferiority, clinically important differences in neonatal morbidity could not be excluded. By supporting earlier delivery in women with an abnormal biomarker profile and continued surveillance in those with a reassuring profile, angiogenic testing may help individualize delivery-timing decisions in late preterm preeclampsia without severe features.

articles.title: State of The Art of The da Silva's Cone Operation for Treatment of Ebstein's Anomaly.
articles.abstract: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a complex congenital heart disease caused by embryological failure of the tricuspid valve (TV) leaflet delamination, leading to displacement of the leaflets and right ventricular myopathy. In 1958, Hunter and Lillehei began developing surgical techniques for the repair of EA. Their technique was followed by many others. However, those techniques presented significant limitations due to the wide range of anatomical variations in the disease. The Da Silva Cone repair (CR) for EA emerged as the most anatomical repair technique for all forms of the disease, yielding the best results for most patients. Since CR can be performed with low mortality and morbidity, is effective and durable, and rarely requires TV replacement, it has been widely adopted. It allowed that surgical intervention can be indicated before the development of significant right ventricular dilatation or dysfunction. CR can be applied to any age, but it carries more risk in the neonate with critical EA. Therefore, neonates with critical EA may benefit from a staged approach, performing the Starnes procedure in the neonatal period and the CR later. The 2025 American Association for Thoracic Surgery expert consensus on managing EA covered preoperative evaluation, surgical indications, and contraindications in neonates, children, and adults. Additionally, the expert consensus discussed the approach to cardiac arrhythmias associated with EA and alternative procedures for select cases, including TV replacement and a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, depending on patient characteristics. They also agreed that the CR repair of the TV is beneficial when surgery is indicated.

articles.title: Understanding parental perspectives on chemotherapy side effects in children with cancer at Bugando medical centre, Mwanza, Tanzania: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: IntroductionChildhood cancer treatment often involves chemotherapy, which is associated with adverse drug reactions/side effects that require close monitoring. Parents and guardians play a critical role in identifying and managing these reactions in children. This study assessed the awareness, attitudes, and proactive monitoring practices of parents/guardians regarding chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions among children with cancer at a tertiary referral hospital in Tanzania.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 parents/guardians of paediatric cancer patients receiving chemotherapy at Bugando Medical Centre, Mwanza, Tanzania. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using Stata version 16. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression analyses were performed.ResultsMost participants demonstrated low awareness of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions (80.5%). However, positive attitudes (58.5%) and proactive monitoring practices (69.0%) were observed. Female caregivers were more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices than male caregivers (AOR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.05-3.68, p = 0.03).
