Participants who were aware of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions were also more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices (AOR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.22-8.35, p = 0.02).ConclusionsDespite limited awareness, parents and guardians demonstrated positive attitudes and self-reported proactive monitoring of their children for chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions. Strengthening caregiver education and communication during cancer treatment may improve awareness, facilitate early recognition, reporting and appropriate management of adverse reactions.Clinical trial NumberNA.

articles.title: Focal Digital Clubbing as an Initial Symptom of Adolescent-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Digital clubbing is typically linked to pulmonary or cardiovascular diseases. There have been no reported cases of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) where the initial complaint was solely foca digital clubbing and a chilblain-like rash on the ngers. A 13-year-old girl experienced digital clubbing for 3 months. Physical examination revealed focal digital clubbing of the thumb, index nger, and middle nger on her right hand, along with slight blotchy erythema assessed as a chilblain-like rash. Laboratory data showed hypocomplementemia and a high anti-double-stranded DNA antibody titer. She was also positive for antiphospholipid antibodies, had prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time, and elevated anti-prothrombin antibody levels. She was diagnosed with SLE complicated by hypoprothrombinemia associated with lupus anticoagulant. Prednisolone treat ment resolved the digital clubbing and laboratory abnormalities. Digital clubbing may be an initial symptom of SLE. Screening for autoimmune diseases should be considered when a patient presents with digital clubbing not associated with pulmonary or cardiovascular diseases or malignant tumors.   Cite this article as: Sato M, Nagamori T, Kurisawa MJ, Tsuda J, Ishibazawa E, Takahashi S. Focal digital clubbing as an initial symptom of adolescent-onset systemic lupus erythematosus: a case report. Eur J Rheumatol. 2025, 12(4), 0075, doi:10.5152/eurjrheum.2025.24075.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of genetic testing in heart transplant recipients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: A single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy genetic testing is recommended for patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) but is inconsistently applied once a patient has reached end-stage disease and undergone heart transplantation. Whether a transplant program can systematically test its existing NICM cohort and what completion rate is achievable when testing is operationalized in the clinic rather than offered ad hoc is not well characterized.
METHODS: We studied all 73 adults followed in the Southern Alberta Transplant Program after transplantation for NICM: dilated (DCM), non-dilated left ventricular (NDLVC), restrictive, or hypertrophic (HCM). Cardiomyopathy genetic testing was offered as a program-wide initiative and performed in adulthood using clinically validated multigene panels. Variants were classified by ACMG/AMP criteria; pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants interpreted as explanatory for the recipient's cardiomyopathy were counted as diagnostic. Single heterozygous P/LP variants in autosomal recessive genes were interpreted as carrier findings and not counted toward yield. Yields are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); the childhood- versus adult-transplant comparison was tested with Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: Of 71 eligible patients, 27 (38.0%) had a genetic-testing result before the 12-month operational window; of the 44 offered testing during the window, 37 completed it (84.1%), raising cohort testing coverage to 90.1% (64/71). A diagnostic pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant was identified in 28 of 64 tested patients (43.8%; 95% CI 32.3%-55.9%); a sensitivity analysis restricted to the 36 patients tested with the comprehensive Invitae 121-gene panel yielded an indistinguishable 38.9% (14/36; 95% CI 24.8%-55.1%), with no evidence that variation in panel breadth materially biased the overall estimate. Two additional patients carried a single heterozygous P/LP variant in an autosomal recessive gene (carrier findings, not counted). Yield was higher in patients transplanted in childhood (10/14, 71.4%) than in adulthood (18/50, 36.0%; Fisher's exact P = 0.031). TTN was the most frequent gene (7 P/LP), followed by LMNA, PKP2, and MYH7 (3 each).
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-month program-wide initiative raised cardiomyopathy genetic testing coverage in an existing NICM heart transplant cohort from 38% to 90% by embedding testing in routine transplant clinic visits. The diagnostic yield among tested patients (43.8%) was consistent with published estimates and similar when restricted to the most comprehensive panel, with markedly higher yield in patients transplanted in childhood. These findings provide a reproducible operational template for transplant programs seeking to close the implementation gap in cardiomyopathy genetic evaluation and to enable cascade testing of at-risk relatives.

articles.title: Phase resolved functional lung (PREFUL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) detects perfusion deficits in pediatric lung transplant recipients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a radiation-free technique that detects regional ventilation and perfusion abnormalities and has shown promise for identifying chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) in adult lung transplant (LTx) recipients. Its utility in pediatric LTx has not been investigated. We evaluated the feasibility of PREFUL MRI in pediatric LTx recipients and its association with pulmonary function.
METHODS: In this single-center cross-sectional study, pediatric LTx recipients and healthy controls underwent contrast-free PREFUL MRI at 1.5 T to quantify regional ventilation and perfusion defects. Spirometry and nitrogen multiple-breath washout were performed to determine forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁) and lung clearance index (LCI). Group differences were assessed using the rank-sum test, and associations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation.
RESULTS: Twenty-two of 24 eligible pediatric LTx recipients (feasibility 92%; median age 13.6 years [range 6-17]; median time since LTx 3.9 years [range 0.6-16.3]) and 11 healthy controls (median age 10.7 years [range 6-15]) completed the study. Perfusion defect extent was significantly greater in pediatric LTx recipients than in controls (p = 0.001), whereas ventilation defects did not differ (p = 0.359). No participant met spirometric criteria for CLAD. FEV₁ %predicted, but not FEV₁ % of baseline, correlated inversely with perfusion defect extent (ρ = -0.487, p = 0.022). No correlations were observed between LCI and MRI-derived ventilation or perfusion parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: PREFUL MRI is feasible in pediatric LTx recipients and detects regional perfusion abnormalities despite stable spirometry. It may provide a sensitive, radiation-free imaging biomarker for monitoring the pediatric lung allograft.

articles.title: Foramen Magnum Stenosis in Achondroplasia: Imaging-Based Surgical Indications, Synchondrosis Fusion, and the Role of Ventriculomegaly.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Foramen magnum stenosis (FMS) and ventriculomegaly are frequent in achondroplasia due to cranial base hypoplasia. While FMS can cause spinal cord compression, the optimal treatment strategy remains debated. We reviewed our single-center experience and explored factors influencing surgical decisions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 18 children with achondroplasia evaluated between 2008 and 2024. MRI was used to assess FMS by anterior-posterior diameter and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) area at the foramen magnum level. Ventriculomegaly was defined as an Evans Index ≥0.30. CT was used to evaluate foramen magnum morphology and synchondrosis fusion. Surgical indications were based on imaging findings of compression and intramedullary changes.
RESULTS: The median age at initial imaging was 9.5 months. Thirteen patients underwent foramen magnum decompression (FMD) and 5 were managed conservatively. The surgical group showed significantly smaller craniocervical junction CSF spaces compared with nonsurgical cases (p < 0.05). Synchondrosis fusion occurred earlier in achondroplasia than in controls. Ventriculomegaly was present in 66%, but its severity did not correlate with FMD. All surgical cases achieved decompression without major complications. Of the 13 surgical patients, 9 were followed for more than 1 year (median follow-up: 122 months). Within this subgroup, 4 developed radiological bone regrowth with re-stenosis, but all remained asymptomatic and none required reoperation.
CONCLUSIONS: FMS in achondroplasia poses major risks, yet its natural history and management remain unclear. Our findings support early imaging-based screening and timely intervention in cases with cord compression. While FMD effectively relieves compression, it does not address underlying ossification abnormalities, requiring continued surveillance. Premature synchondrosis fusion may play a key role, and future studies should consider combined surgical and medical approaches to improve outcomes.

articles.title: Cranial Injuries due to Misuse of Infant Carriers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infant carriers (car seats, bouncy chairs) can cause injuries when used for other than their intended purpose.
METHODS: We studied children aged 0-24 months with carrier related injuries reported to the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study (PTOS) dataset (2001-2022 inclusive).
RESULTS: There were 562 injured children, averaging 23 injuries per year. Mean age was 3.3 months; 54.3% were male. Most (82.7%) fell from an elevated surface; 88.7% fell an estimated 2-5 feet. Head injuries (intracranial injury/hemorrhage and/or skull fracture) were present in 85.6%. Admission Glasgow Coma Scores were most commonly 15 (79.1%); 7 had GCS <12. Average Injury Severity Score was 9.3 (range 1-30). Average length of stay was 1.4 days; 30% spent >1 day in the intensive care unit. Two children underwent cranial operations. There were no deaths, and 82.9% were discharged home.
CONCLUSION: Falls in, or from, infant carriers are a significant public health concern. Education, advocacy, and changes in carrier design may help reduce the frequency of these injuries.

articles.title: Gamma Knife Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Pediatric Meningiomas.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the generally benign and slow-growing nature of many adult meningiomas, meningiomas in pediatric patients often exhibit more aggressive behavior. Gamma Knife stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is a non-invasive modality that is widely used as either an initial upfront or adjuvant management for meningiomas. We reviewed our 35-year meningioma experience to assess its role in pediatric patients.
METHODS: The authors reviewed the clinical and imaging data of 2,030 meningioma patients who underwent SRS between 1987 and 2022 at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC). We identified 9 patients <18 years (2 female; median age, 14.5 years). None of the patients had neurofibromatosis type 2. The neurological outcomes, overall survival, local tumor control, and development of adverse radiation effects were evaluated. Three patients received prior therapeutic radiation: one underwent prophylactic cranial irradiation for lymphoblastic leukemia, one received focal cranial irradiation for craniopharyngioma, and one underwent craniospinal irradiation for medulloblastoma. Seven patients had prior tumor resection, while two asymptomatic patients were diagnosed incidentally (one during craniopharyngioma surveillance imaging and the other after head trauma). The median cumulative tumor volume at SRS was 6.0 cc (range, 0.5-11.8 cc). The median margin dose prescribed was 14 Gy (range, 11-25 Gy).
RESULTS: At last follow-up, 5 patients were alive. Four patients had died, two from progressive intracranial disease and two from unrelated medical causes. The median overall survival was 8.9 years (range 2.0-16.2 years). The median progression free survival was 8.2 years (range 1.1-13.4 years). Five patients experienced tumor progression at a median of 2.1 years (range, 1.1-13.4 years) after SRS. After local tumor progression, 2 patients received repeat SRS, and the remaining patients required additional surgery, fractionated external beam radiotherapy, or chemotherapy. No patient developed adverse radiation effects, had malignant tumor transformation, or developed other types of CNS malignancies.
CONCLUSION: Meningiomas are rare tumors in the pediatric age group and can exhibit aggressive behavior. Tumor control was achieved in 6 of 9 patients after one or more SRS procedures. SRS presents as a reasonable primary option or should be considered for early intervention after surgery. Patients and families should be counseled that multiple SRS sessions might be needed to achieve eventual tumor control.

articles.title: Complex Type Split Cord Malformation: A Two-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complex spinal dysraphism is the condition where multiple dysraphic pathologies are observed in the same patient. Complex type split cord malformation (SCM) is a compound dysraphic phenotype involving disruptions at multiple developmental stages, characterized by the co-occurrence of SCM and spina bifida aperta. This study aimed to understand the differences between complex SCMs from classical SCM cases in terms of embryological aspects, perioperative management, and follow-up.
METHODS: Patients with SCM associated with spina bifida aperta who were treated at Dicle University and Kocaeli University, Departments of Neurosurgery, between 2011 and 2025 were included in the study. Patient age (months), gender, presenting clinic, lesion localization, SCM type, number of affected vertebrae, neurological status, presence of tethered cord, presence of kyphoscoliosis, spina bifida aperta type, Chiari malformation, syringomyelia, presence of posterior fusion defect number of vertebrae with defect, hydrocephalus, accompanying intracranial pathologies, and additional anomalies were included in the study.
RESULTS: The study included 44 patients who underwent surgery for complex SCM. Of the patients, 81.8% were operated on during the neonatal period in the same session with spina bifida aperta surgery. Surgery was planned for 11.4% of patients for follow-up purposes and for 6.8% following detection of SCM on MRI performed due to gait disturbances. It was observed that 68.2% of patients were plegic/severely paretic, 22.7% had moderate paresis, and 9.1% had mild paresis/normally. Regarding the type of spina bifida aperta, 72.7% of patients had myelomeningocele, and 27.3% had myeloschisis. Type 1 SCM was detected in 79.5% of patients, type 2 SCM in 13.6%, and type 1.5 SCM in 6.8%. Additionally, 93.2% had tethered cord/thickened-fatty filum terminale, 90.9% had posterior fusion defects, 77.3% had hydrocephalus, 68.2% had kyphoscoliosis, 65.9% had Chiari malformation, 54.5% had syringomyelia, 45.5% had intracranial pathologies other than hydrocephalus, and 4.6% had lipoma.
CONCLUSION: Complex SCMs should not be viewed solely as a spinal pathology; they should be evaluated multidisciplinarily in the perioperative period in terms of anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta. In these cases that are diagnosed at a younger age, the incidence of type 1 SCM increases, while the frequency of occurrence in the lumbar region decreases and increases in the thoracic region. Furthermore, it has been determined that additional anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta occur more frequently with complex SCMs.

articles.title: Transfusion practices among children admitted to a South African PICU following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood products may be required in patients undergoing cardiac surgery; however, there is a paucity of data on blood transfusion guidelines in the perioperative and postoperative cardiac surgery period.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prevalence of blood product transfusion, factors associated with transfusion and outcomes in patients who received blood products following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-centre observational study that consecutively recruited 126 children aged <18 years admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) following cardiac surgery between July 2017 and January 2018. Demographic, intraoperative and postoperative blood product transfusion data were extracted from patient records, entered into a standardised case record form and analysed using Statistica version 13 (StatSoft Inc, USA). Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: Of the recruited children, 53% received blood products, with 30.9% receiving cryoprecipitate, 22.2% receiving packed red blood cells, 18.3% receiving albumin, 15.9% receiving fresh frozen plasma and 15.1% receiving platelet concentrates. Factors associated with the use of blood products included previous cardiac surgery, younger age, lower weight and prolonged coagulation parameters (p<0.05). Receiving blood products was associated with worse outcomes: a standardised mortality ratio of 3.1 v. 0 (p<0.0001), median (IQR) PICU length of stay of 5 (3 - 11) v. 2 (2 - 5) days (p<0.0001), and duration of mechanical ventilation of 47 (22 - 132) v. 20 (6 - 27) hours (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a high prevalence of blood product use in children in the PICU following cardiac surgery, and this is associated with worse outcomes.
CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This is the first South African study to describe the use of all major blood product types, not only red blood cells, and their indications in children following paediatric cardiac surgery. It demonstrates a markedly different transfusion pattern from that reported in North American PICUs, with cryoprecipitate, rather than red blood cells, being the most frequently used product. Blood product use was common and was independently associated with worse outcomes, including longer PICU stays, prolonged ventilation and higher standardised mortality. These findings highlight the need for locally developed, evidence-based transfusion protocols to support blood product stewardship, particularly in resource-constrained settings that depend on voluntary blood donation.

articles.title: Risk of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension Following Anemia in Young Adults: A Retrospective Cohort TriNetX Database Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Anemia has been associated with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) in small studies, but whether severity modulates IIH risk remains unclear. This study evaluated the hazard of incident IIH after mild, moderate, and severe anemia in young adults.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX Research Network (111) health care organizations), adults aged 18-50 years with persistent anemia (≥2 hemoglobin values) were stratified as mild (11.0-12.9 g/dL), moderate (8.0-10.9 g/dL), or severe (<8.0 g/dL) and matched 1:1 to controls (Hb ≥ 13.0 g/dL) by propensity score matching on demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, and socioeconomic factors. The primary outcome was incident IIH; Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) at 6 months, 1 year, and 3 years. Sensitivity analyses applied the World Health Organization (WHO) women's mild threshold and compared patients with vs without iron supplementation.
RESULTS: After matching, 1,240,670 mild anemia patients (mean age 29.0 ± 8.7 years, 83.4% female), 666,515 moderate (29.7 ± 8.1, 86.3% female), and 114,785 severe (31.0 ± 8.9, 75.4% female) were compared with equal-sized control cohorts. Hazard of incident IIH was elevated at every severity and time interval. At 6 months, HRs were 1.45 (95% CI 1.29-1.63), 1.61 (1.39-1.86), and 2.53 (1.82-3.52) for mild, moderate, and severe anemia. At 1 year, HRs were 1.35 (1.22-1.49), 1.33 (1.17-1.51), and 1.94 (1.46-2.58). At 3 years, HRs were 1.17 (1.08-1.26), 1.15 (1.04-1.27), and 1.40 (1.11-1.76); all estimates remained significantly elevated, although CIs overlapped across severity bands. The WHO women's threshold sensitivity yielded concordant, modestly stronger estimates (6 months: HR 1.99 [1.73-2.30]; 3 years: 1.43 [1.31-1.58]). Iron supplementation was associated with reduced IIH hazard (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.93; n = 340,660 per group).
DISCUSSION: Anemia is associated with elevated hazard of incident IIH in young adults across all severity bands. Point estimates were higher with greater anemia severity and at earlier follow-up, but CIs overlapped across severity bands, so a severity gradient could not be established. Iron supplementation was associated with reduced hazard. Findings are limited by observational design, administrative case identification, and low absolute incidence; anemia represents a potentially modifiable factor warranting evaluation in patients with papilledema.

articles.title: The Combined Effect of Migraine and Smoking on Premature Stroke and All-Cause Mortality in Parous Women: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Migraine and smoking are established stroke risk factors. We examined the individual and combined effects of migraine and smoking on risk of premature stroke (age 60 years or younger) and all-cause mortality in women and evaluated additive interaction.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based cohort study using nationwide Danish health registries (1996-2022). Women aged 15-60 years giving birth during 1996-2022 were identified through the Danish Medical Birth Registry and categorized as having migraine, smoking, both exposures, or neither (reference). Participants were followed until stroke, death, emigration, 61st birthday, or December 31, 2022. Outcomes were ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Absolute risks (ARs), adjusted hazard ratios (HRs), and relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 1,677,707 women (median age 29-32 years across exposure groups), the 20-year AR of premature ischemic stroke was 0.8% in the reference cohort (n = 1,389,361), 1.3% with migraine (n = 65,422), 1.5% with smoking (n = 214,277), and 2.8% with both exposures (n = 8,647). ARs of premature hemorrhagic stroke were 0.3%, 0.5%, 0.6%, and 0.9%. All-cause mortality ARs were 1.0%, 1.2%, 2.3%, and 3.4%. Compared with the reference cohort, adjusted HRs for premature ischemic stroke were 1.85 (95% CI 1.66-2.05) for migraine, 2.10 (95% CI 1.99-2.20) for smoking, and 3.61 (95% CI 3.03-4.31) for both exposures. HRs for premature hemorrhagic stroke were 1.46 (95% CI 1.23-1.74), 2.02 (95% CI 1.87-2.18), and 2.60 (95% CI 1.91-3.54). For all-cause mortality, HRs were 1.08 (95% CI 0.96-1.22), 2.44 (95% CI 2.34-2.54), and 3.30 (95% CI 2.80-3.88). The 20-year RERI was 0.67 (95% CI 0.22-1.13) for ischemic stroke, 0.11 (95% CI -0.59-0.82) for hemorrhagic stroke, and 0.78 (95% CI 0.34-1.22) for mortality.
DISCUSSION: Migraine and smoking were associated with elevated risk of premature stroke, and mortality risk was increased among women who smoked regardless of migraine status. Additive interaction indicated excess risk of ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality among women with migraine who smoked. These findings support targeted cessation strategies to reduce premature vascular events and mortality.

articles.title: Validation of the BASED Score as a Prognostic Biomarker for Refractory Epilepsy Following Treatment of Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Refractory epilepsy is common among children with a history of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS), yet no validated prognostic biomarkers exist to guide early risk stratification. The Burden of Amplitudes and Epileptiform Discharges (BASED) score is an interictal EEG rating scale for children with IESS, with scores of 4 or 5 suggesting epileptic encephalopathy. The objective of this study was to determine whether a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 is a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.
METHODS: This retrospective validation study of children with IESS was conducted at a Level 4 pediatric epilepsy center. Children with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) were excluded. Three blinded reviewers assigned 2021 BASED scores to full-length post-treatment EEGs. Refractory epilepsy was defined as persistent seizures despite treatment with at least 2 antiseizure medications or completion of epilepsy surgery. Prespecified performance benchmarks for BASED 4/5 as a rule-in test required ≥80% specificity and a positive likelihood ratio of ≥4.
RESULTS: The cohort included 123 children (42.3% female), with a median first treatment age of 8.0 months (IQR 5.9-10.3) and follow-up duration after first treatment of 58.8 months (IQR 42.2-80.7). Only 11.4% had a favorable etiology. EEGs (median 19 hours) were completed at a median of 47 days (32-72) after starting treatment. The inter-rater agreement for epileptic encephalopathy was excellent (κfree = 0.78). Half (52%) of the children had refractory epilepsy. BASED 4/5 demonstrated high specificity (88.1%, 95% CI 77.1-95.1) for refractory epilepsy, with a positive likelihood ratio of 4.4 (2.1-9.1). The sensitivity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 51.6% (38.7-64.3), 82.5% (69.3-90.8), and 62.7% (56.1-68.7), respectively. An exploratory composite indicator comprising BASED 4/5, persistent epileptic spasms, and/or epileptic spasms relapse demonstrated higher sensitivity (79.7%, 67.8-88.7) with modestly reduced specificity (81.4%, 69.1-90.3).
DISCUSSION: Study limitations include the single-center design, exclusion of children with TSC, variable EEG timing, and shorter follow-up in some children. Nevertheless, in this independent validation cohort, a post-treatment BASED 4/5 demonstrated favorable prognostic performance consistent with its proposed use as a rule-in test for refractory epilepsy. These findings support a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 as a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.

articles.title: Frequency-Specific Thalamocortical Network Dynamics During Focal Seizures in Humans.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The thalamus is an emerging neuromodulation target in drug-resistant focal epilepsy because of its frequent ictal involvement. However, frequency-specific and directional thalamocortical dynamics remain poorly understood. We sought to characterize thalamocortical network dynamics across seizure evolution using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed SEEG recordings from patients with pediatric-onset drug-resistant focal epilepsy with simultaneous cortical and thalamic sampling focusing on the anterior nucleus (AN) and centromedian nucleus (CM). We applied visual analysis with quantitative measures of spectral power, imaginary coherence, and spectral Granger causality across slow (1-12 Hz), β (13-30 Hz), and γ (30-70 Hz) bands to quantify thalamocortical and cortico-cortical interactions from seizure onset to termination. Random forest models were trained to classify seizure state using thalamic EEG features as an exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 19 patients (median age, 16.9 years; 31.6% female), with 66 focal seizures analyzed. Thalamic ictal activity was present at seizure onset in 81% of sampled thalamic contacts and became nearly universal by seizure termination. Both the thalamus and seizure onset zone showed increased spectral power during seizures, with prominent slow-band augmentation at seizure termination in the thalamus. Similarly, thalamocortical imaginary coherence increased during seizures, with the largest changes near seizure termination in the slow band (AN-SOZ: 11% [IQR, 2 to 20], rank-biserial correlations (rrb) = 0.84; CM-SOZ: 12% [IQR, 3 to 23], rrb = 0.84) and β band (AN-SOZ: 5% [IQR, 0 to 12], rrb = 0.74; CM-SOZ: 8% [IQR, 2 to 15], rrb = 0.86). Directed connectivity analyses demonstrated bidirectional thalamocortical interactions, with large slow-frequency thalamus-to-SOZ outflow near seizure termination from both AN and CM, exceeding propagation-zone-to-SOZ cortico-cortical flow (both p < 0.01). Seizure state was classified using thalamic EEG features, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.825 for AN and 0.839 for CM.
DISCUSSION: Human focal seizures engage frequency-specific and bidirectional thalamocortical interactions that evolve from onset to termination. These findings support the thalamus as a source of clinically relevant seizure-state information and may inform thalamic biomarker development for neuromodulation in drug-resistant epilepsy.

articles.title: Overweight and Rapid Weight Gain Following Pediatric Kidney Transplantation in Chinese Children.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to descriptively characterize posttransplant weight gain trajectories, obesity prevalence, and explore factors associated with weight gain in Chinese pediatric kidney transplant recipients, a population for whom such data remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all Chinese children who received kidney transplants in Hong Kong from 2013 to 2023. Primary outcome was BMI Z scores, assessed at baseline and serially posttransplant using local reference data. Rapid weight gain was defined by ≥ 0.5 increase in BMI Z score or ≥ 10% increase in body weight during the first-year posttransplant.
RESULTS: Fifty-three Chinese children (59% male; median age at transplant 13.3 years, IQR, 7.9-17.8) were analyzed and followed for 6.1 years (IQR, 2.8-8.1). Mean BMI Z score increased significantly from baseline to 1-year posttransplant (Δ = +0.47 SD, p = 0.0001). The prevalence of overweight/obesity significantly increased from 13.2% at baseline to 30.2% at 1 year (p = 0.05). Rapid weight gain occurred in 64.2% of patients. In exploratory analyses, family history of obesity (46.7% vs. 13.5%; p = 0.03) and overweight/obesity prior to transplant (31.3% vs. 5.4%; p = 0.02) were associated with 1-year overweight/obesity. Cardiometabolic outcomes and kidney function were comparable between patients with or without rapid weight gain.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant weight gain is common following pediatric kidney transplant. Early screening, identification, and timely intervention are keys to halt disease progression.

articles.title: Bladder Management in Pediatric Kidney Transplantation: A Narrative Systematic Review With a Hypothesis-Generating Phenotype Framework.
articles.abstract: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract cause 30%-50% of pediatric end-stage renal disease, and roughly one-third of affected children have clinically significant lower urinary tract dysfunction (LUTD). Transplanting into a dysfunctional bladder increases the risks of infection, graft pyelonephritis, and graft loss; however, there is no consensus on clinical objectives, catheterization and augmentation practices vary across centers, and no validated bladder-specific risk score has been established. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library (2000-2025) for studies of pediatric kidney transplant recipients (≤ 18 years) that reported graft, urologic, or infectious outcomes related to bladder function. Two reviewers screened studies and extracted data, and risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Fifty-two studies met the inclusion criteria, including 10 retrospective cohort studies with 428 children. Because comparable cohorts were few and outcome definitions were heterogeneous, the evidence was synthesized narratively, with quantitative pooling limited to graft survival in five cohorts. Pooled graft survival in recipients with LUTD was 83.8% (95% CI 75.6%-89.7%; I2 = 28%; moderate certainty), and the available comparisons showed no significant difference in graft survival between recipients with LUTD and those with normal bladders. Urologic complication and urinary tract infection (UTI) rates varied primarily with follow-up duration rather than with underlying pathology alone. Seven risk factors were associated with adverse outcomes; children with three or more factors had higher UTI rates and lower 5-year graft survival than those with fewer factors. Clean intermittent catheterization and Mitrofanoff procedures were associated with better long-term graft survival despite higher UTI rates. We propose classifying LUTD into four phenotypes according to the dominant injury mechanism: low compliance with high pressure, poor emptying, isolated detrusor overactivity, and mixed dysfunction. This framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Overall certainty of evidence is low to moderate; consensus definitions, registry harmonization, and prospective validation of phenotype-based algorithms should take priority over the publication of further unvalidated risk scores. Trial Registration: PROSPERO: CRD420261416509.

articles.title: Reconsidering Age Boundaries in Kidney Transplant Allocation: Advantages and Limitations of a Strict Age Cutoff Versus Continuous Prioritization Models for Childhood-Onset Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: In the United States, there is a recognized legal and ethical obligation to prioritize pediatric transplant candidates. However, the implementation of pediatric priority can create new ethical challenges. This manuscript discusses the ethical implications of the existing, "strict" age threshold for pediatric priority compared to the impacts of a hypothetical, "continuous" approach to age in allocation, with attention to the practical implications of such policies. The existing "strict" age threshold is transparent, consistent, and feasible. By addressing the increased harm faced by young children with kidney disease and improved graft survival among pediatric recipients, it meets the ethical principles of beneficence and utility. Conversely, a "continuous" age prioritization would not only address the disproportionate risks of dialysis and benefits of transplant in the youngest children, but also improve access for vulnerable young adult candidates with childhood onset kidney disease. Both prioritization strategies would serve to benefit children, but their implementation can result in inequities that require additional, mitigating policies. Special attention should be paid to the potential impacts on allocation priority for children under 5 years of age, young adults, and the potential, unintended inequities that may result from transplant center-specific listing practices.

articles.title: Patient- and family-reported satisfaction in child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care: An exploratory descriptive survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe and compare patient- and family-reported satisfaction with child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care in a Japanese inpatient unit.
METHODS: Patients aged 8-15 years discharged from a single Japanese inpatient unit and their families completed an anonymous web questionnaire with separate patient and family versions. Overall satisfaction was rated on a 10-point scale, and respondents who reported interaction rated the usefulness of five professional groups. Because responses were unlinked, 10 probable patient-family pairs identified from submission times were used in sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Invitations were handed to 61 patients and their families at discharge; 52 family members (85.2%) and 26 patients (42.6%) responded. Family members reported higher satisfaction than patients (mean 8.14 [SD 1.83] vs. 6.27 [SD 2.15]; medians 8 vs. 7; mean difference 1.87, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-2.86), and the lower 95% CI limit was at least 0.73 in all sensitivity analyses addressing dependence between the groups. The maximum score was given by 25.5% of family members and 3.8% of patients. Among respondents who rated each professional group, a higher proportion of family members than patients rated child and adolescent psychiatrists (98.1% vs. 69.2%) and nurses (92.3% vs. 73.1%) as useful, whereas proportions for psychiatric social workers, clinical psychologists, and teachers were similar or higher among patients. These profession-specific comparisons were descriptive only.
CONCLUSION: Patients rated inpatient care less favorably than family members. Family reports should complement, not replace, patients' own evaluations, and future multicenter studies should use matched patient-family dyads.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a LASSO-Based Prediction Model for Postoperative Bleeding Following Pediatric Tonsillectomy and Adenoidectomy.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Despite technological advancements, children undergoing adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation remain at risk for postoperative bleeding. This study aimed to construct a precise machine learning-based model to predict the risk of postoperative bleeding in this population.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study involving 306 pediatric patients who underwent the procedure between January 2023 and January 2025 was conducted. Clinical data, including demographic characteristics, preoperative laboratory findings, and surgical details, were collected and cleaned. The dataset was randomly divided into a training set (n = 244) and a validation set (n = 62) at an 8:2 ratio. A predictive model was developed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) cross-validation algorithm, and its performance was assessed in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: Among 306 children, 24 (7.8%) experienced postoperative bleeding. Univariate comparisons identified significant differences in 11 variables: age, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), disease duration, postoperative infection, dietary compliance, postoperative pain, lymphocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) (all p < 0.05). At lambda.1se = 0.022, LASSO logistic regression retained four predictors: postoperative infection, dietary compliance, age, and postoperative pain. After 1000 bootstrap resamples, the out-of-bag area under the curve (AUC) was 0.935 (95% CI: 0.875-0.995), with a Brier score of 0.035, calibration intercept of 0.045, and calibration slope of 1.418. At the optimal probability cutoff of 0.114, sensitivity was 0.875, specificity was 0.936, and the Youden index was 0.811.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative infection, dietary adherence, postoperative pain, and age are significant predictors of bleeding following pediatric adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation. The LASSO-based model provides a reliable tool for identifying high-risk patients and optimizing perioperative management.

articles.title: Intensive communicative and linguistic intervention in Noonan syndrome: A case study.
articles.abstract: Noonan syndrome (NS) is a genetic developmental disorder within the RASopathies and is frequently associated with language and communication impairments affecting multiple linguistic domains. Evidence regarding the effectiveness of intensive speech-language intervention in this population remains limited. This case study evaluated the effectiveness of an intensive, individualised, and multimodal communicative and linguistic intervention in a school-aged girl with NS. An 8-year-old girl with NS received an intensive speech-language intervention (20 hours/week for four weeks). The program targeted speech intelligibility, phonological skills, morphosyntax, lexical-semantic development, and pragmatic communication, using play-based strategies in clinical and natural contexts. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included standardised and criterion-referenced measures of language and communication. Post-intervention outcomes showed clinically meaningful improvements in communicative intentionality, pragmatic skills, receptive vocabulary, and speech intelligibility. Standardised language scores showed limited quantitative change, but functional communication and social participation improved substantially. Intensive and individualised intervention may promote significant gains in functional communication in children with Noonan syndrome.

articles.title: Recompensation in autoimmune hepatitis.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an immune-mediated liver disease in which persistent necroinflammation drives progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, and ultimately portal hypertension-related decompensation. Effective immunosuppression may halt hepatic inflammation, thereby inducing biochemical (and histological) remission, facilitating regeneration of hepatic function, clinical recompensation, and fibrosis regression. Studies indicate that approximately 19-54% of immunosuppressed patients achieve recompensation. Lower Child-Pugh score, lower immunoglobulin G levels, and a complete biochemical response are associated with higher recompensation rates, whereas advanced-grade hepatic encephalopathy and a higher Model for End-stage Liver Disease score are associated with lower recompensation rates. Recompensation improves prognosis and transplant-free survival compared with non-recompensated AIH patients. However, recompensation should not be equated with resolution of portal hypertension or a reduced risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, which may persist and continue to require surveillance and treatment. CONCLUSION: Recompensation in AIH is possible and confers better clinical outcomes. However, with the definition of aetiological control less well defined, data remain heterogeneous.

articles.title: Early histological remission and prognosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Early remission in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is increasingly recognized for providing long-term prognostic benefits, despite limited supporting data. We examined the prognostic value of histological remission within 12 months of diagnosis.
METHODS: A nationwide cohort study of 14 019 Swedish IBD patients diagnosed in 1990-2022. These patients underwent ileo-colorectal biopsies showing histological remission or inflammation within 1-<12 months post-diagnosis. We estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for treatment failure (IBD-related surgery, hospitalization, third corticosteroid dispensation, or second-line advanced therapies), colorectal cancer (CRC), and death until 2023. We adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, IBD phenotype, and medication history.
RESULTS: Early histological remission was more prevalent in patients with higher educational attainment or those diagnosed since 2000, but less common in childhood-onset (<18 years) and elderly-onset (≥60 years) IBD. Average follow-up extended to 13.7 years. Compared to early remission, histological inflammation within 12 months was linked to an increased risk of treatment failure (aHR = 1.47, 95% CI = 1.39-1.54), particularly hospitalization (aHR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.39-1.54) and second-line advanced therapy (aHR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.34-1.91). Histological inflammation (vs early remission) was also linked to a heightened CRC risk (aHR = 1.65, 95% CI = 1.21-2.24), with similar risks in Crohn's disease (CD: aHR = 1.66, 95% CI = 0.94-2.93) and ulcerative colitis (UC: aHR = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.20-2.60). Mortality risk was elevated in CD (aHR = 1.21, 95% CI = 1.01-1.45) but not UC (aHR = 0.96, 95% CI = 0.85-1.08). Associations were similar for corticosteroid-free histological remission within 6 and 12 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained histological inflammation (vs remission) 12 months after IBD diagnosis predicted a higher risk of treatment failure and CRC, indicating that early histological remission may improve long-term disease prognosis.

articles.title: REACH: A multidimensional index for measuring community concordance in US children's hospitals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equitable access to pediatric healthcare is essential for improving health outcomes and assessing health system accountability. Existing metrics for measuring hospital concordance with surrounding communities are adult-centric or sensitive to hospital catchment area definition.
OBJECTIVE: Through REACH (Representation and Equity in Area-based Child Hospitalizations) index, we aimed to develop a multidimensional, robust, and standardized concordance measure that combines four sociodemographic dimensions, ethnicity, payor, race, and sex, into a composite score that is comparable across hospitals.
METHODS: Using 695,046 inpatient and observation encounters from 48 U.S. children's hospitals in the Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) for 2023 and 2023 American Community Survey (ACS) five-year estimate, we defined hospital catchment areas and calculated dimension-specific concordance indexes using weighted Chi-square divergence between observed hospitalizations and expected pediatric population. The four indexes were aggregated into a composite REACH score with 95% confidence intervals. Robustness of REACH was assessed using Spearman correlation between unrestricted and two conservative catchment definitions across 48 hospitals.
RESULTS: REACH scores ranged from 0.89 to 0.98. All hospitals demonstrated high (≥0.80) to very high (≥0.90) concordance, with 60% of hospitals scoring ≥0.95. REACH was stable across catchment definitions, with strong correlations (ρ ≥ 0.7); all hospitals stayed in the high-to-very high range. Overall, 87.5% of hospitals retained their concordance category, while six showed modest downward shifts (from very high to high) under the most conservative definition.
CONCLUSION: REACH offers an effective framework to measure community concordance in pediatric hospitals, with potential future applications for benchmarking, quality improvement, and policy development to advance equitable healthcare access.

articles.title: Caregiving networks and children with neurologic impairment: A multicenter social network analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with neurologic impairment (NI) often require care from multiple paid and unpaid caregivers-a "caregiving network"-yet little is known about how caregiving networks influence child health. Understanding how networks influence health could support innovative intervention designs targeting groups of caregivers.
OBJECTIVES: This multicenter prospective cohort study will evaluate whether caregiving network characteristics are associated with serious health events and quality of life among children with NI.
METHODS: THRIvE (Teamwork and Healthy Relationships Improving Engagement in Caregiving) is a multicenter prospective cohort study enrolling children ages 2-16 years with NI and at least one hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visit in the prior 12 months, along with primary caregivers (PCGs) and secondary caregivers (SCGs), at five academic medical centers. Caregiving networks will be assessed at enrollment using egocentric social network analysis administered to PCGs and validated with SCG surveys. Exposures include network density, centralization, triadic closure, network size, and composition. Primary outcomes at 12 months are serious health events (death or hospitalization) and child quality of life. Secondary outcomes include clinical symptoms, missed school days, and ED visits. Associations will be examined using mixed-effects regression models accounting for site clustering, confounding, and multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: This study will provide novel prospective evidence about how caregiving network configurations are associated with health outcomes in children with NI.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings may identify modifiable social network features that can inform future family-centered, network-based interventions to improve child health and quality of life.

articles.title: Design Thinking in Advance Care Planning for Emerging Adults: Enhancing Control and Customization to Support Engagement.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study examined how emerging adults with serious illness engage with advance care planning (ACP) through a design-informed lens.Background:ACP enables individuals to communicate their preferences and goals for medical care if they are unable to make decisions for themselves. Although ACP is widely recognized as critical for individuals with serious illness, engagement remains low among emerging adults (ages 18-29), a distinct developmental subgroup within the adolescent and young adult population. Traditional ACP approaches emphasize documentation and legal requirements, which may limit engagement among individuals navigating identity development, autonomy, and future-oriented life transitions.Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 39 emerging adults with oncology or hematology diagnoses who reviewed the ACP communication guide, Voicing My CHOiCES (VMC). Structured interviews assessed participant perspectives on usability, preferences, and emotional responses. Data were explored using thematic content analysis.Results:Two central themes emerged: (1) affording choice and control and (2) designing for customization and usability. Participants valued opportunities for personalization, structured guidance, and revisable formats. Design elements that supported autonomy, reduced cognitive burden, and facilitated reflection were associated with more positive experiences of engagement, while overly rigid features constrained expression.Discussion: Across themes, ACP engagement with emerging adults was closely tied to how the VMC tool structured interaction. Design features that enabled choice, reduced complexity, and allowed for iterative engagement were associated with more positive experiences. This suggests that designing ACP as a flexible, user-centered, developmentally tailored process may better support meaningful participation.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in the Organ Donation Process Among Pediatric Brain-Dead Donors: A Nationwide Study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the pediatric organ donation process and age-related differences among brain-dead donors in Japan and evaluate organ-specific transplantation rates and graft survival across age groups.
DESIGN: Nationwide retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: National donor records maintained by the Japan Organ Transplant Network.
PATIENTS: All pediatric (≤ 17 yr old) brain-dead organ donors in Japan between July 17, 2010, and March 31, 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 100 pediatric brain-dead organ donors were included. Donors were categorized into three age groups: younger than 6 years (n = 32), 6-14 years (n = 48), and 15-17 years (n = 20). The time intervals from hospital admission to organ procurement showed marked age-dependent prolongation, with median durations of 28, 19.5, and 13.5 days, respectively (p < 0.01). Younger donors were more frequently managed in children's hospitals and pediatric departments, whereas older donors were increasingly managed in emergency and critical care settings. Organ transplantation was achieved in 99% of donors. Organ-specific transplantation rates were consistently high for the heart, liver, and kidneys across all age groups, whereas lung and pancreas transplantation rates increased with donor age. During donor management, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic function were generally maintained or improved until procurement. No significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed for any organ type.
CONCLUSIONS: The pediatric organ donation process in Japan was substantially prolonged in an age-dependent manner, particularly among donors younger than 6 years. Despite prolonged donor management, transplantation rates remained high, and no significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed. These findings highlight the importance of sustained multidisciplinary and family support throughout the donation process and may provide insights for pediatric donation systems in low-volume settings.

articles.title: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Multicenter PICUs.
PATIENTS: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.
CONCLUSIONS: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

articles.title: Chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment attenuates auditory fear conditioning in adult male rats.
articles.abstract: Noncompetitive-777-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms, supporting the NMDA receptor hypofunction hypothesis. Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade with MK-801 is widely used to model neurodevelopmental aspects of schizophrenia; however, its impact on cue-specific fear learning remains incompletely characterized. Male Sprague-Dawley pups received subcutaneous injections of MK-801 (0.4 mg/kg) or saline twice daily from postnatal day 7-20. In adulthood, rats underwent auditory fear conditioning (five tone-shock pairings), 4 days of extinction (45 tone-alone trials/session), a retrieval test, and a remote retrieval test. Across acquisition and all test sessions, MK-801-treated rats showed consistently lower freezing than controls. These findings suggest that chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment disrupts acquisition or expression of cue-shock associations, or both. Given the small sample size and the potential contribution of altered locomotion or shock reactivity, future work should incorporate locomotor and sensory controls.

articles.title: The relationship of physical activity and exercise to the initiation and use of nicotine and cocaine.
articles.abstract: Each year, the USA federal government spends hundreds of billions of dollars addressing the ramifications of substance use; however, limited and ineffective treatment strategies exist to mitigate these challenges. Continued targeting of the adolescent population contributes to the growing number of substance-dependent individuals because of an enhanced susceptibility to substance use. Many studies have suggested that exercise may be a suitable adjunct or nonpharmacological therapy because of its rewarding potential and ability to reduce stress and other drug-related risk factors. This review aims to assess the clinical associations of physical activity and preclinical evidence of exercise as protection against the development of nicotine and cocaine use disorders. This will build on previous work by using a substance-use-cycle-specific lens, focusing on substance initiation and use, while clarifying and addressing concerns about the timing of exercise exposure relative to the substance-use experience and its impact on exercise intervention efficacy. Together, this work identifies clinical observations associated with lower instances of nicotine initiation and use, in addition to preclinical behavioral and molecular interventions associated with reductions in cocaine initiation and use, providing support for the protective effect of physical activity and exercise.

articles.title: The impact of parity on postpartum recovery and perinatal outcomes among obese women.
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and may affect postpartum recovery; however, the role of parity remains unclear. This study evaluated the relationship between maternal and neonatal outcomes and postpartum recovery quality by parity in obese women. This descriptive and correlational study included 128 women (64 primiparous, 64 multiparous) with body mass index ≥30 kg/m². Data were collected using standardized forms and the Obstetric Quality of Recovery Scale. No significant difference was found between groups in total recovery scores (p>0.05), although multiparous women had higher scores in current recovery perception (p<0.05). Mode of delivery, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and oxygen requirement were associated with recovery outcomes. Regular antenatal care was identified as a significant predictor, although the regression model explained only a limited proportion of the variance. Parity was not an independent determinant of overall recovery; maternal and neonatal factors appear to play a more important role. L'obésité maternelle est associée à des issues maternelles et néonatales défavorables et peut affecter la récupération post-partum ; toutefois, le rôle de la parité reste incertain. Cette étude a évalué la relation entre les issues maternelles et néonatales et la qualité de la récupération post-partum en fonction de la parité chez les femmes obèses. Cette étude descriptive et corrélationnelle a inclus 128 femmes (64 primipares, 64 multipares) présentant un indice de masse corporelle ≥ 30 kg/m². Les données ont été recueillies à l'aide de formulaires standardisés et de l'échelle de qualité de la récupération obstétricale. Aucune différence significative n'a été observée entre les groupes concernant les scores totaux de récupération (p > 0,05), bien que les femmes multipares aient obtenu des scores plus élevés concernant leur perception de la récupération actuelle (p < 0,05). Le mode d'accouchement, l'admission en unité de soins intensifs néonatals et les besoins en oxygène étaient associés aux issues de récupération. Un suivi prénatal régulier a été identifié comme un facteur prédictif significatif, bien que le modèle de régression n'explique qu'une faible proportion de la variance. La parité n'était pas un déterminant indépendant de la récupération globale; les facteurs maternels et néonataux semblent jouer un rôle plus important.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of underweight among children under five years in Southern African countries: A comparative study.
articles.abstract: Underweight is a public health issue that affects children in low-middle income countries. It is defined as low weight for age. The study aimed to examine factors associated with underweight among children under five years in SADC. The study used Demographic and Health Surveys conducted in Lesotho (2014), Malawi (2015-16), South Africa (2016) and Zambia (2018). The study population consisted of children under the age of five years: 1869 in Lesotho, 5786 in Malawi, 1416 in South Africa and 9689 in Zambia. Chi-square test and logistic regression were used to establish social and demographic factors associated with underweight. The study results show that Malawi and Zambia had high prevalence (11.7% and 11.8%) of underweight as compared to Lesotho and South Africa (10.3% and 5.9%) respectively. It is therefore suggested by this study that the predominant factors such as child's age, child's sex, birth weight, mother's education, and household income to be considered by policymakers and stakeholders when implementing programmes and policies to reduce underweight. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the importance of multisectoral interventions that address the basic, underlying, and immediate causes of malnutrition to reduce the prevalence of underweight among children under five years.

articles.title: A Gap on Judgment of Fertility and the Need for Contraception Between Physicians and Patients With Rheumatic Diseases: A Multicenter Questionnaire Survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Effective contraception is essential for women of reproductive age with rheumatic disease (RD), specifically those receiving teratogenic drugs, and physicians should recognize that these women may wish to conceive or control their fertility. This study aimed to evaluate the status of preconception care and contraception use, awareness, and counseling among women with RD in Japan.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire survey included Japanese women with RD (age: 18-45 years) and their attending physicians, conducted between September 2023 and May 2024 at 14 medical institutions. Patient and physician responses were linked and analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 157 patients completed the survey. Of these, 35% of patients wished to conceive in the future and 38% were aware of their current need for contraception. The results revealed a gap between physicians' and patients' judgment of fertility and the need for contraception. Most patients used less effective contraceptive methods (condoms: 67.1%; withdrawal: 20.5%). Although patients were aware of the need for contraception, only 12% had received specific contraception instructions from their healthcare providers, whereas 39% had never received contraception counseling. Most of the patients decided on contraceptive methods themselves or together with their partners. One patient who tested positive for antiphospholipid antibodies used contraindicated estrogen-containing contraceptives.
CONCLUSION: Significant deficiencies exist in contraception counseling and awareness among women with RD. Proactive and system-building approaches are urgently required to improve preconception care and reproductive safety in this population.

articles.title: Upper Eyelid Lipofilling for Improving Ocular Comfort in Facial Palsy: A 12-Year Experience in 350 Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The eyelid implantable weight is the most commonly used remedy for the correction of lagophthalmos. However, this approach has several limitations (migration, extrusion, poor esthetics, infection, astigmatism). It targets the restoration of eyelid closure, which is not the correct goal. The main goal should be to improve blinking, as it plays a crucial role in ocular surface protection and overall function. This objective can be achieved much more effectively through eyelid lipofilling. Lipofilling provides a more physiological restoration of blinking and enhances functional and esthetic outcomes compared with traditional eyelid weight implantation.
METHODS: Between 2012 and 2025, 432 upper eyelid lipofillings were performed in 350 patients, including 206 treated with the original technique and 144 with the modified technique. Of these, 318 patients had adequate follow-up and were included in the clinical outcome analysis.
RESULTS: All patients reported immediate improvement of corneal comfort. The need for artificial tears significantly decreased. The immediate improvements were partially reduced 2 months after surgery due to the initial resorption of the grafted fat, after which they remained stable. In 62 cases, a second lipofilling procedure was necessary. In 10 cases, a third lipofilling procedure was necessary.
CONCLUSIONS: Lipofilling of the upper eyelid sulcus has demonstrated a strong ability to reduce symptoms and improve corneal comfort in a large number of patients. The esthetic outcome is significantly superior compared with the application of a traditional eyelid weight.

articles.title: Cytopathologic Diagnosis of Non-Neoplastic Inflammatory Disorders of Lymphoid Organs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) is a minimally invasive, cost-effective, and accurate method for evaluating enlarged lymph nodes, especially useful in pediatric cases where most aspirates are benign. It can be performed by palpation or under ultrasound guidance for deeper lesions. Rapid onsite evaluation enhances specimen adequacy and guides ancillary testing. FNAB, often combined with flow cytometry, can reduce the need for surgical biopsies by up to 86%, with reported sensitivity and specificity of 85-95% and 98-100%, respectively.
SUMMARY: Despite its advantages, FNAB is sometimes undervalued due to misconceptions about its diagnostic capabilities. The recently introduced WHO Reporting System for Lymph Node, Spleen, and Thymus Cytopathology, based on the Sydney System, aims to standardize reporting. It categorizes aspirates into five diagnostic groups, each with an associated risk of malignancy (ROM) and management recommendations. The "benign" category is the most common and includes non-neoplastic inflammatory conditions. Cytopathologists assess cellularity and cytologic features to distinguish benign from atypical or malignant processes. Low-power evaluation of smear patterns helps differentiate infectious from reactive causes. Flow cytometry is crucial for identifying lymphoproliferative disorders and leukemic infiltrates. The ROM for benign FNABs ranges from 2 to 16%, with a pooled estimate of 5%. Management typically involves clinical follow-up, with repeat FNAB or biopsy reserved for persistent or suspicious cases. Familiarity with lymph node cytology and integrated diagnostic approaches is essential for accurate patient care.
KEY MESSAGES: Familiarity with lymph node cytology and integrated diagnostic approaches is essential for accurate patient care.

articles.title: Cytopathologic Diagnosis of Lymphomas in Serous Effusions, Cerebrospinal and Vitreous Fluid.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haematolymphoid lesions in serous effusion, cerebrospinal, and vitreous fluid are encountered regularly. In the paediatric clinical setting, haematolymphoid lesions are the most common cause of malignant serous effusions. Cytologists and cytopathologists should be prepared to evaluate such samples as part of routine diagnostic practice. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the cytomorphological features and diagnostic considerations of lymphomas involving serous fluids, cerebrospinal, and vitreous fluids.
SUMMARY: B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas are most often encountered in fluid cytology specimens. A practical method for triaging lymphocyte-predominant effusions involves assessing lymphoid cell size, specifically distinguishing between small-to-medium and large lymphoid cells. A significant differential diagnosis of small-medium lymphoid cells in fluid specimens is reactive lymphocytosis while that for large cells is metastatic malignant, and atypical or malignant mesothelial cells.
KEY POINTS: Cytologic evaluation of fluids containing lymphocytes provides valuable information regarding the nature of these lesions. Accurate cytologic diagnosis, with clinicopathologic correlation and judicious use of ancillary testing where possible, is essential for identifying the underlying cause of effusion, guiding therapy, monitoring disease progression or relapse, and informing prognosis. To optimize diagnostic outcomes, proper collection, transport, and preparation of fluid specimens is required. Collaboration with haematopathologists and use of standardized cytologic reporting systems further contribute to diagnostic accuracy and consistency. Emerging technologies, including molecular profiling, liquid biopsy, single-cell multi-omics and artificial intelligence, offer promising avenues for advancing the diagnosis and prognostication of haematolymphoid malignancies in fluid-based samples. Further research will determine their clinical utility.

articles.title: Regenerative Stress Contributes to Higher Clonal Hematopoiesis with Myelodysplastic Features in Sickle Cell Disease Mice.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects millions globally, causing significant lifelong morbidity and early death. As childhood mortality is reduced and SCD patients are surviving to adulthood, increased risk of hematological malignancy (HM) is becoming evident. Risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)/acute myeloid leukemia, following gene therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) is also higher in SCD. The specific pathobiology that predisposes to HM is necessary to address, since survival has improved and gene therapy and HSCT are being increasingly used. We modelled the increased risk of HM in humanized SCD mice, compared to age-, sex- and strain-matched normal counterparts. We serially monitored hematopoiesis in blood and bone marrow up to 1-year-of-age and performed highly sensitive, error-corrected deep sequencing of 450 MDS/HM-associated genes. Unlike controls, SCD mice showed an 'ageing-like' phenotype with premature development of myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) mutational profile characteristic of aged mice/humans. Furthermore, a high proportion of SCD mice developed hematopoiesis with dysplastic features reminiscent of MDS morphology and higher clonal hematopoiesis burden. Imposition of regenerative stress by serial HSCT further increased HSPC mutational burden, resulting in evolution/expansion of clones harboring oncogenic driver mutations. Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.

articles.title: Fertility, pregnancy, and parenthood: Risks and impacts among urologists.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The feminization of urology highlights challenges regarding pregnancy and parenthood. We surveyed French urologists to evaluate the impact of parental leave on service organization, surgical activity, and gestational risks.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from April to August 2023 among members of AFU and AFUF. A total of 325 urologists responded (31% women, 69% men; mean age: 46 years). Data were analyzed using Sphinxdeclic.
RESULTS: Male urologists had more children than females (3 vs. 2, P<0.01). Overall, 37% delayed childbearing due to career (68% of women). Infertility rate was 16%. Parental leave was perceived as having a negative impact for 32% of colleagues. Only 13% of women had coverage replacement, 31% ceased night shifts, and 15% worked t until the end of their pregnancy. Ionizing radiation exposure continued in 64% of cases. High complication rates occurred during pregnancy (48%), including miscarriages (21%) and preterm births (24%). Only 30% continued breastfeeding upon returning. 41% of private practitioners experienced a negative financial impact. Only 31% of men took paternity leave.
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy among female urologists carries high complication rates. Despite growing gender parity in French urology, structural adaptations during pregnancy, lactation support, and paternity leave adoption remain inadequate. Institutional reforms are required to safeguard reproductive health and ensure equity.

articles.title: Emerging Drugs.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic development in Sjögren's disease has accelerated after decades of largely negative clinical trials. Improved patient selection, refined outcome measures, and targeted modulation of key immune pathways have produced positive late-stage studies and the prospect of disease-modifying treatment. This article examines emerging B-cell-directed therapies, neonatal Fc receptor inhibitors, costimulatory blockade, intracellular signaling inhibitors, immune-restorative approaches, repurposed therapies, and cellular treatments. It also considers lessons from contemporary trials, including phenotype-based enrollment, multidimensional endpoints, and organ-specific responses, and discusses how these advances may enable increasingly precise therapeutic selection.

articles.title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatologic conditions occur in reproductive aged women, requiring a multidisciplinary approach to care. Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

articles.title: Long-Term Postpartum Dyspareunia and Sexual Dysfunction After Childbirth.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postpartum sexual dysfunction is common, but long-term outcomes beyond the early puerperium remain insufficiently integrated into routine postpartum and gynecologic care.
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to systematically review dyspareunia and sexual dysfunction beyond 6 months postpartum, including associated factors and rehabilitation interventions.
STUDY DESIGN: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL from inception to January 31, 2026. Eligible primary studies included postpartum women with at least 1 relevant sexual outcome assessed at or beyond 6 months after childbirth. Prevalence and associated-factor findings were synthesized descriptively. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to randomized rehabilitation trials reporting validated sexual-function outcomes at eligible postpartum time points with extractable numerical data.
RESULTS: Twenty-two eligible reports representing 21 unique studies or cohorts were included; 2 randomized rehabilitation studies contributed to quantitative synthesis. Dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remained clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum, with incomplete recovery persisting in a substantial subset of women. Persistent morbidity was most consistently associated with severe perineal trauma, including obstetric anal sphincter injury; associations with operative delivery were less consistent. Breastfeeding-related symptoms, depressive symptoms, pelvic floor morbidity, and genital or body image concerns were also reported. The pooled rehabilitation estimate favored intervention but was imprecise and highly heterogeneous (standardized mean difference: 1.19; 95% CI, -0.18 to 2.57; I²=91.7%), with very-low-certainty evidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remain clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum and warrant proactive assessment within routine postpartum and gynecologic follow-up, with multidisciplinary management and referral for pelvic floor rehabilitation or urogynecologic evaluation when indicated.

articles.title: Acute adverse events associated with commercially available chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell infusions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy is increasingly used to treat a variety of diseases, but limited data exist on acute adverse events (AEs) associated with these infusions. We aimed to evaluate AEs associated with Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved CAR-T cell infusions in adult and pediatric patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a 5-year retrospective study carried out at a multi-hospital center. Demographic information, disease state, infusion data, medical history, and pre-infusion vitals were extracted from the electronic health record system. Acute AEs were graded per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) criteria. Associations between AEs and collected variables were analyzed using binary logistic regression and machine learning (random forest classifier) methods.
RESULTS: Among 339 adult infusions, 37 AEs were identified (11%): idecabtagene vicleucel 7/40 infusions, lisocabtagene maraleucel 1/39, ciltacabtagene autoleucel 12/104, tisagenlecleucel 5/24, brexucabtagene autoleucel 3/26, and axicabtagene ciloleucel 9/106. Most AEs were grade 1 (54%). Eleven reactions were grade 2, four reactions were grade 3, and two reactions (hypotension, bronchospasm/shortness of breath) were grade 4. No grade 5 AEs occurred. In adults, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) exposure normalized to body weight was associated with a higher acute AE risk (p = 0.007 [binary logistic regression]), supported by machine learning analysis. Among 30 pediatric infusions, one grade 1 hypotensive reaction occurred (~3%). No further statistical analyses were performed in the pediatric cohort because of the limited number of events.
CONCLUSION: FDA-approved CAR-T cell infusions demonstrated a low rate of acute AEs, supporting the safety of current products. The association between increased DMSO exposure and acute AE risk identifies a potential, actionable target for further risk reduction.

articles.title: Nasal Dermoid Cysts Mimicking Lacrimal and Periorbital Infections in Children: A Clinicoradiologic Case Series.
articles.abstract: Nasal dermoids, also referred to as nasal dermoid sinus cysts, and the more cranially located nasofrontal dermoid cysts may present with pediatric periorbital inflammation or masquerade as lacrimal excretory system infections, delaying definitive diagnosis and proper management. We describe 6 children (5 boys, 1 girl; age range, 12 months-48 months) who presented with upper eyelid abscesses, draining periocular sinuses, or dacryocystitis-like swelling secondary to nasal dermoid sinus cyst or nasofrontal dermoid cyst.
