All had received repeated courses of systemic antibiotics before formal diagnosis; 4 had undergone incision and drainage, and 1 had undergone prior nasolacrimal probing before the definitive diagnosis was established. A midline nasal pit or sinus was identified in all patients. CT demonstrated characteristic osseous abnormalities, and MRI better delineated tract extent and assessed intracranial involvement in 4 patients. Four patients underwent complete surgical excision, with no recurrence of infection over a follow-up period ranging from 1 to 4 years. Nasal dermoids should be considered in young children with recurrent or atypical periorbital inflammation. Careful nasal midline examination and cross-sectional imaging can prevent misdiagnosis and facilitate timely definitive management.

articles.title: Demographic, clinical and echocardiographic profile of adult patients with congenital heart disease at a leading cardiovascular healthcare facility of Pakistan: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic characteristics of adults with congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was performed at the department of pediatric cardiology, National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD), Karachi, Pakistan, from November 2022 to October 2023. Inclusion criteria were adult patients (≥18 years of age) diagnosed with CHDs (both already diagnosed and newly diagnosed).
RESULTS: Of 184 patients, 100 (54.3%) were male. Mean age and BMI were 25.66 ± 9.19 years and 17.75 ± 4.32 kg/m2. Seventeen (9.2%) adult CHD patients were newly diagnosed. Shortness of breath, cyanosis, palpitation, and chest pain, were reported in 158 (85.9%), 65 (35.3%), 52 (28.3%), and 51 (27.7%) patients. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) were the most common CHD types, noted in 46 (25.0%), 35 (19.0%), 32 (17.4%), and 12 (6.5%) patients respectively. ASD was significantly more prevalent in females than in males (82.9% vs. 17.1%, p < .001), and it was significantly more frequent in 18-30 age group (p < .001). TOF was more common in 18-30 age group (p = .013). VSD was significantly more prevalent in males (p = .028).
CONCLUSIONS: TOF, ASD, VSD, and PDA were the most frequent types of adult CHDs. Notably, 9.2% of patients were newly diagnosed, suggesting potential underdiagnosis or late detection. With a substantial portion of the population experiencing CHD-related symptoms with some diagnosed only in adulthood, demand for dedicated centers equipped with expertise in managing adult CHD becomes evident.

articles.title: Hepatocellular Tumors in Patients With Ornithine Transcarbamylase Deficiency Include Focal Nodular Hyperplasia, Hepatocellular Adenoma, and Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (OTCD) is the most common urea cycle disorder and can cause potentially life-threatening hyperammonemia. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and hepatocellular adenoma (HCA) have been reported in OTCD, usually in adults. Non-neoplastic histologic findings include non-specific glycogenosis, steatosis, and fibrosis.
DESIGN: A retrospective pathology database search between 2000 and 2024 was performed to identify patients with a clinical history of OTCD. Electronic medical records were reviewed for clinical, laboratory, genetic, and imaging findings. Available native liver specimens underwent histologic review, with additional studies performed in select cases.
RESULTS: We identified 11 patients with OTCD. All patients were diagnosed biochemically; pathogenic OTC mutations were detected in all 8 tested patients. Three patients had hepatocellular lesions. One patient with Li-Fraumeni syndrome developed focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) at age 6 and conventional HCC at age 10, when OTCD was also diagnosed. RNA sequencing revealed biased allelic expression toward the mutant OTC allele in the FNH (100% mutant), HCC (94% mutant), and background liver (87% mutant). Two additional pediatric patients had incidental HCAs identified on explant examination at 9 and 17 years of age. The remaining 8 patients (72%) had no focal hepatic lesions. Glycogenosis was the most common histologic finding (10/11, 91%). Only 1 patient had significant steatosis (grade 2) or fibrosis (stage 1).
CONCLUSION: Hepatocellular tumors in OTCD included HCC, HCA, and FNH in pediatric patients. Glycogenosis was the predominant non-neoplastic histologic finding. These findings expand the spectrum of hepatic lesions and non-neoplastic liver pathology reported in OTCD.

articles.title: Documenting Psychosocial Needs at the End of Life: Implementation of an Interdisciplinary Huddle to Foster Communication in Pediatric Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: - Psychosocial support is a core component of pediatric oncology palliative care (PPC), yet structured approaches for documenting and communicating psychosocial information across interdisciplinary teams remain inconsistent in pediatric cancer.
OBJECTIVE: - To describe the content documented within a structured interdisciplinary psychosocial huddle note and summarize lessons learned from its implementation within a hospital-based pediatric palliative care program for children with cancer.
METHODS: - This single-site retrospective decedent study included patients at a large pediatric cancer center with at least one documented end-of-life psychosocial huddle note between October 2023 and October 2025. The first huddle note for each patient was reviewed for documentation across nine psychosocial domains. Demographic, clinical, temporal, and interdisciplinary participation data were collected. For patients with multiple notes, changes in documentation over time were assessed.
RESULTS: - Forty-six patients with malignancy met inclusion criteria. The most frequently documented domains were social/spiritual support (84.8%), family/caregiver support (82.6%), and anticipatory grief (76.1%). Emotional distress (45.7%) and goals of care/decision-making (43.5%) were documented in nearly half. Notes reflected broad interdisciplinary participation, particularly from social work, child life, and spiritual care. Documentation patterns varied across demographic and clinical subgroups. Among 14 patients with multiple notes, all demonstrated changes in at least one psychosocial domain over time.
CONCLUSIONS: - Structured psychosocial huddle notes facilitated interdisciplinary communication and documentation of supportive care needs and revealed variability in documentation of decision-making processes. Standardized longitudinal documentation may strengthen communication, continuity, and goal-concordant end-of-life care in PPC for children with cancer.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinician Success, Quality, and Resilience in Outpatient Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Many inpatient PPC programs are growing into the outpatient setting, heeding the call of national organizations to offer pediatric palliative care (PPC) across the care continuum. In this context, expanding PPC programs face high volumes with limited resources.
OBJECTIVES: To improve sustainability, we aimed to assess associations between outpatient pediatric palliative care (OPPC) clinic operationalization and clinician perception of programmatic success, quality of care and team resilience.
METHODS: In a national cross-sectional study, 48 freestanding children's hospitals with established inpatient PPC programs were surveyed about their OPPC program's success, quality of care, and team resilience in Spring 2021; participants were asked to base responses on pre- March 2020 experiences.
RESULTS: Of the 28 programs with OPPC, 89% (25/28) responded to items on programmatic success, quality of care, and team resilience. Most reported that OPPC program design and workflow allowed for high-quality care (76%). Half felt their design and workflow were successful (52%) and promoted team resilience (48%). Across different clinical care models, OPPC programs with a dedicated clinic space reported increased programmatic success. Use of a free-standing clinic model was significantly associated with increased perception of success and high-quality care compared to floating and embedded clinic models. Perception that OPPC design and workflow promoted team resilience was associated with perception of high-quality care.
CONCLUSION: OPPC program design and workflow impacts clinician perception of success, provision of high-quality care, and team resilience. Quality metrics specific to OPPC models are needed to guide programs in successful expansion of PPC into the outpatient clinic setting.

articles.title: Perceived Clinical Utility of a Routine Family Experience Feedback Loop in Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Home is typically the preferred setting of care for children living with serious illness, yet children and families frequently experience unmet needs in the home. Pediatric palliative care (PPC) teams provide longitudinal support for these children and families but have limited insight into families' day-to-day experiences and needs while at home. Routinely collecting family-reported data about care experiences in the home and sharing these data with PPC teams may enable more timely, responsive, and family-centered care.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the perceived clinical utility of sharing routinely collected, digitally enabled, family-reported data between families and PPC teams.
METHODS: We used a modified experience-based co-design approach to evaluate acceptability, perceived feasibility, and perceived clinical actionability through 1) individual interviews with family participants, (2) "clinical action check-in" meetings with outpatient PPC clinicians, and (3) co-design sessions with PPC and hospice clinicians. We used a content analytic approach to identify codes, categories, and themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-four parents of children with serious illness and 11 PPC and hospice clinicians participated in this project. Sharing routinely collected care experience data was perceived as: (1) acceptable or valuable, although comfort and willingness varied for families, (2) feasible with attention to timing, frequency, recipients, and implementation, and (3) clinically actionable along a spectrum.
CONCLUSION: A routinely collected, digitally enabled feedback loop between home and hospital is perceived by families and clinicians as holding promise for helping teams identify unmet needs and tailor care. Facilitating routine, bidirectional communication between families and teams may improve alignment between the care provided and families' needs at home.

articles.title: ACCOMPANI: A Psychosocial Nurse Intervention for African American Families in Pediatric Oncology.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: African American parents of children with cancer face magnified existential crisis, defined as emotional distress related to the child's illness and intensified by disconnected and discordant health care interactions and economic worries. Nurses providing direct care are positioned to elicit parents' psychosocial needs and facilitate psychosocial care but have identified barriers to intervention.
OBJECTIVES: To co-develop components of a nurse-targeted intervention, ACCOMPANI, African American Childhood Cancer Multiprong Psychosocial Nurse Intervention through thought partner engagement.
METHODS: We conducted a deductive-inductive thematic qualitative study involving seven thought partners who participated in six-remote focus groups and supplemental individual interviews (n=5). Thought partners included African American parents of children with cancer (n=2), pediatric oncology nurses (n=2), pediatric oncology social worker (n=1), an African American community partner (n=1), and an African American disparity scholar (n=1). Thought partners were presented with a raw intervention prototype and provided iterative feedback on intervention components and delivery.
RESULTS: Thought partners endorsed ACCOMPANI's three targeted domains (attitude, knowledge, and skills) and contributed to developing the intervention components and delivery characteristics. Three themes shaped revisions: (1) cultural relevance, emphasizing avoidance of monolithic assumptions and centering lived experiences; (2) participant engagement, highlighting brief, modular, and flexible learning; and (3) interactive learning, using digital storytelling, web-based modules, and realistic animated simulations. Feedback led to a four-session intervention to be delivered digitally over four consecutive weeks.
CONCLUSION: ACCOMPANI, the first nurse-targeted intervention for African American families with childhood cancer, aims to facilitate psychosocial care. Findings will inform future refinement and pilot testing.
FUNDING: This work was conducted with the support from 2023 Pedals for Pediatrics (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute) as well as 2023 K12TR004381 award through Harvard Catalyst | The Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center (National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health). The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of Harvard Catalyst, Harvard University and its affiliated academic healthcare centers, or the National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Altitude and disease persistence in childhood immune thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: Yin and colleagues reported childhood immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) lasting at least three months in 8.8% of children hospitalized in Xining and 27.3% in Ningbo. In Ningbo, 79 of 88 children achieved complete response within the first seven days, while only 64 recovered before three months. At least 15 of the 24 children with prolonged disease must therefore have achieved early complete response. Linking their platelet counts to intervening treatment would clarify how long those responses lasted. Because each altitude was represented by one hospital, referral practices and opportunities to detect secondary immune disease may also contribute to the observed difference. Parental consanguinity, family histories of immunodeficiency or autoimmunity, immunoglobulin levels before intravenous immunoglobulin, and diagnoses emerging during follow-up merit systematic documentation. Our clinical impression of more frequent persistence in Van than in Adana raises this question in Türkiye. Published series from Van, Adana, and Istanbul used different definitions of disease duration, limiting geographic comparisons. At three months, a child's platelet trajectory and the appearance of another cytopenia or lymphoproliferation can guide reassessment of presumed primary ITP. Prospective comparisons across residential altitudes should document bleeding, rescue treatment, sustained platelet recovery off therapy, and the timing and basis of any subsequent diagnosis.

articles.title: Early-Life Farm Exposure and Food Allergy.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has increased substantially, increasing interest in environmental exposures that may promote immune tolerance. The "farm effect," in which children raised in traditional farming environments have lower rates of allergic disease, may also extend to food allergy. This review summarizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking prenatal and early-life farm exposures with food allergy and related atopic outcomes. Protective associations likely reflect combined exposures to livestock, farm dust, environmental microbes, diet, and farm milk during critical developmental windows. Proposed mechanisms include altered gut microbiome maturation, microbial metabolites, reduced epithelial inflammation, innate immune programming, and enhanced regulatory T-cell responses. However, direct evidence for clinically confirmed food allergy remains limited compared with evidence for asthma and allergic sensitization. Future studies should identify specific microbial, metabolic, and immune pathways that mediate protection and determine whether safe, defined surrogates of farm exposure can be translated into food allergy prevention strategies.

articles.title: Laparoscopic per-operative cholangiogram in infants with neonatal cholestasis: Diagnostic and therapeutic utility.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the diagnostic and therapeutic utility of laparoscopic per-operative cholangiography (POC) in infants with neonatal cholestasis and inconclusive pre-operative investigations.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted of infants who underwent laparoscopic POC for evaluation of neonatal cholestasis between November 2023 and October 2025. Laparoscopic POC was performed in infants with neonatal cholestasis and equivocal clinical, laboratory, imaging or histopathological findings. Infants with a diagnosis of biliary atresia (BA) or choledochal cyst (CDC) who proceeded directly to surgery without POC and those undergoing primary open exploration were excluded. Demographic data, pre-operative investigations, operative findings, final diagnosis, management and outcomes were analysed.
RESULTS: Eleven infants (7 males and 4 females) underwent laparoscopic POC at a median age of 3 months (range: 1.5-8 months). Cholangiography was successfully completed in eight patients (72.7%), while 3 infants had an atretic gallbladder precluding cannulation. Six infants were diagnosed with BA and subsequently underwent Kasai portoenterostomy. Alternative diagnoses were established in five infants, including CDC ( n = 2), spontaneous common bile duct (CBD) perforation ( n = 1), inspissated bile syndrome ( n = 1) and Caroli's disease ( n = 1). Laparoscopic POC accurately delineated biliary anatomy and directly guided definitive management in all cases. One infant with spontaneous CBD perforation underwent cholecystostomy and intraperitoneal drainage with complete recovery. Both CDC patients underwent laparoscopic cyst excision with Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy. There were no procedure-related complications, bile leaks or intra-operative mortality. During a median follow-up of 12.2 months, one infant with BA died from sepsis-related complications and another was referred for liver transplantation because of progressive liver disease.
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic POC is a safe, minimally invasive and highly effective diagnostic modality for infants with neonatal cholestasis when pre-operative evaluation is inconclusive. Beyond reliably differentiating BA from other causes of cholestasis, it provides real-time assessment of biliary anatomy and facilitates individualised therapeutic decision-making while avoiding unnecessary exploratory laparotomy.

articles.title: Genetic Risk Stratification for Pediatric Fever-Associated Seizures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract: Fever-associated seizures are a common pediatric emergency. Complex febrile seizures and fever-sensitive epilepsy show marked genetic heterogeneity, but real-world evidence linking genetic information to the prediction of short-term recurrence and readmission remains insufficient. This single-center real-world retrospective cohort included children with their first qualifying fever-associated seizure presentation at the center from 2019 to 2023 and at least 12 months of follow-up. Genetic variants were classified according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria, and pathway-based genetic risk tiers were constructed. Multivariable Cox models were used to evaluate associations between pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and 12-month recurrence and readmission. Prediction models based on clinical variables alone and models additionally incorporating genetic risk tiers were compared using the C-index, 12-month area under the curve, Brier score, net reclassification improvement, integrated discrimination improvement, bootstrap correction, and decision curve analysis. The overall pathogenic or likely pathogenic detection rate was 13.64%, with a higher rate in fever-sensitive epilepsy than in complex febrile seizures. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were independently associated with recurrence and readmission, and high-risk pathways showed stronger effects. Adding genetic risk tiers modestly improved internally validated predictive performance and showed greater decision-curve net benefit. These findings suggest that genetic information may have potential value for short-term risk stratification and post-discharge management in children with fever-associated seizures; however, independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Reduces Hypoxic-Ischemic Brain Damage in Neonatal Rats by Suppressing Ferroptosis and Apoptosis via Regulating the Nrf2/GPX4 Pathway.
articles.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic brain damage (HIBD) is an important cause of neonatal nervous system damage, and ferroptosis is the key cell death mode mediating HIBD. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) has been shown to have neuroprotective effects, but whether it can alleviate HIBD by regulating ferroptosis is still unclear. The neonatal rat HIBD model was established, and behavioral and neurological functions were evaluated by the grip test, rotarod test, and Zea-Longa score. Pathological staining was used to evaluate the impact of DEX on cortical pathological damage, hippocampal neuronal loss, and apoptosis. An oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) model was established using PC12 cells. A Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, a lactate dehydrogenase assay, Nissl staining, and flow cytometry were used to assess cell damage. Dihydroethidium staining, Prussian blue staining, and biochemical assay kits were employed to detect oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related indicators. Meanwhile, Western blotting was performed to measure the expression of proteins related to ferroptosis, apoptosis, and the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) signaling pathway. DEX dose-dependently reduced cerebral infarction volume and neurological deficit scores, ameliorated pathological damage in brain tissue, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis in HIBD rats. At the same time, DEX treatment effectively promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation, upregulated GPX4, and ameliorated oxidative stress and iron metabolism disorders in HIBD rats. Nfe2l2 knockdown significantly attenuated the neuroprotective and ferroptosis-inhibitory effects of DEX in HIBD rats. In vitro, DEX intervention ameliorated the PC12 cell damage caused by OGD, activated the Nrf2/GPX4 axis, and inhibited ferroptosis. Nfe2l2 knockdown attenuated the protective effect of DEX on PC12 cells. Intervention with the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 attenuated the promoting effect of Nfe2l2 knockdown on oxidative stress and ferroptosis. In conclusion, DEX inhibits ferroptosis by regulating the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway, reduces pathological damage to brain tissue in HIBD rats, and inhibits oxidative stress and neuronal apoptosis.

articles.title: Pediatric Seropositive Autoimmune Encephalitis: A Health Outcome Study.
articles.abstract: The autoimmune encephalitides (AE) are immune-mediated diseases of the central nervous system affecting children. This study from Lebanon describes the clinical presentations, treatments, and outcomes of antibody-positive autoimmune encephalitis in children. This is a retrospective study of children ≤ 18 years old with antibody-positive AE that presented to the American University of Beirut Medical Center (AUBMC) from January 2010 to October 2024. The Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) was used to assess outcomes, with scores of 0-2 indicating a good outcome and 3-5 indicating a poor outcome. Fisher's exact test was used to correlate outcome with categorical variables, including sex, geographic region, clinical presentation, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cell counts, brain imaging findings, antibody titers, time to treatment, first line treatment, second line treatment, and outcomes at 6 months follow-up, and Mann Whitney U test categorizing age as a continuous variable. Results: Seventeen patients were included. Detected antibodies were anti-myelin oligodendrocyte protein (MOG) (58.8%), N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) receptor antibody (17.6%), neuromyelitis optica (NMO) aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibodies (17.6%), and anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibody (6%). Immunotherapy consisted of high-dose methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and/or plasma exchange. Of patients with myelin oligodendrocyte antibody disease (MOGAD), 90% had a good outcome. Outcome was poor in 4/17 patients (23.5%). No variables were significantly correlated with the final outcome. Autoimmune encephalitis affects quality of life. These findings may increase awareness of pediatric AE and MOGAD in Lebanon and inform clinical recognition and management.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Management of Acute Appendicitis During Pregnancy-Does Appendicitis Severity Affect Neonatal and Maternal Outcomes?
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate whether the severity of acute appendicitis affects maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnant patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy.MethodA single center retrospective study was conducted between 1/2004 and 8/2023. Pregnant patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy for presumed appendicitis were identified and included according to inclusion criteria. Patients were stratified by disease severity into uncomplicated acute appendicitis (UAA), complicated acute appendicitis (CAA), and normal appendix (NA). Clinicopathological, maternal, and neonatal outcomes were compared using univariate analysis, followed by multivariate analysis for variables found significant.ResultsOf the 284 patients identified, 182 (64.1%) were included in the analysis of whom 145 (79.7%) had UAA, 21 (11.5%) had CAA and 16 (8.8%) had NA. Compared to patients with UAA and NA, those with CAA had longer operative times (51 minutes vs 30 and 41.5, p = <0.001, respectively), longer lengths of stay (4 days vs 2 and 1.5, p = <0.001) and their neonates had higher birth weights (3.33 vs 3.30 and 2.92, P = 0.011). There were no differences in the delivery mode, gestational age at delivery, preterm birth rates, incidence of small-for-gestational-age neonates, or postoperative complications. One fetal death was recorded. An exploratory analysis found that CAA was independently associated with increased birth weight.ConclusionIn pregnant patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy, the severity of acute appendicitis was not associated with adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes. These results suggest that laparoscopic management may be safe across the spectrum of appendicitis during pregnancy, warranting confirmation in larger multicenter studies.

articles.title: Asthma Blitz Days: An Innovative Approach to Asthma Management in Schools.
articles.abstract: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic condition among school-aged children in the United States, contributing to emergency department visits, school absences, and diminished well-being. Inadequate asthma control is driven by medication nonadherence, psychosocial stressors, and social determinants of health. School nurses are pivotal in coordinating care, supporting medication management, and fostering asthma-friendly environments. In Pitt County, North Carolina, Asthma Blitz Days were developed as a collaborative, school-based intervention between Pitt County School Health Program and ECU Health (formerly Vidant) Maynard Children's Hospital Pediatric Asthma Program. Targeting Pre-K to 5th grade students with documented asthma, this program assessed symptoms, delivered age-appropriate education using the teach-back method, and improved medication and documentation compliance. School nurse-led, multidisciplinary interventions like Asthma Blitz Days offer a scalable approach to improving asthma control and promoting health equity in school communities.

articles.title: Autistic Adolescents and Associate Medical Conditions.
articles.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder is a neurological and developmental condition impacting 1 in 31 children. Children, identified on the autism spectrum, are typically diagnosed by the age of 8; however, research indicates that there could be as many as 25% of undiagnosed adolescents. Autistic adolescents have a significantly higher prevalence of mental-health and medical conditions than their neurotypical peers including gastrointestinal disorders (e.g., chronic constipation), seizure disorders, sleep disturbances, and nutritional disorders (e.g., overeating). Part-1, "Interventions for Adolescent Students with Autism and Co-Occurring Mental Health Disorders," of this three-part series discussed interventions for the mental health comorbidities often experienced by autistic adolescents. This second article will address common medical conditions experienced by autistic adolescents and how school nurses can help manage these conditions in school settings.

articles.title: Anti-ZIKV IgG Subclass Profiles and Anti-DENV IgG Are Associated With Neonatal Outcomes Following ZIKV Infection During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Most infected individuals present mild symptoms; however, vertical transmission of ZIKV can lead to Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS), which includes microcephaly, neurological, hearing, ophthalmological, and morphological abnormalities. Given the high prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) exposure and antibody cross-reactivity among flaviviruses, understanding how maternal humoral antibody profiles relate to neonatal outcomes after ZIKV infection is important. In this exploratory study, we evaluated maternal and neonatal anti-ZIKV total IgG, anti-ZIKV IgG1 and anti-ZIKV IgG3, and anti-DENV IgG reactivity in relation to maternal-neonatal antibody patterns and neonatal outcomes. Samples from pregnant women and their newborns were collected in Brazil, including pregnancies with microcephaly and other clinical or imaging abnormalities. Anti-ZIKV and anti-DENV IgG reactivity was measured by ELISA. Lower neonatal anti-ZIKV IgG3 reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities in the individual comparison, although this association did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Lower neonatal anti-DENV IgG reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities and with any clinical or imaging abnormality, and both associations remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. These exploratory associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish functional protection or a causal role for the measured antibody profiles.

articles.title: Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
articles.abstract: The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials. In precision oncology, MDTs can simulate disease progression and therapeutic responses, allowing treatment regimens to be tested virtually before administration and thereby supporting personalized treatment decisions. In virtual clinical trials, MDTs can enhance randomized trials through the PROCOVA™ methodology, provide synthetic control arms for single-arm studies, and support the identification of optimal dosing regimens in early-phase trials. However, MDTs also face challenges related to computational complexity, generalizability across diverse populations, AI-related model validation and regulatory compliance, and underdeveloped ethical frameworks for continuous-learning systems. Despite these challenges, MDTs hold considerable potential to reshape cancer care, optimize individualized therapies, and accelerate oncology drug development.

articles.title: Preparation of Mouse Primary Microglia Cultures for α-Synuclein Propagation.
articles.abstract: Hyperstimulation of microglia affects the regulation of α-synuclein (α-syn) spreading in the brain. Isolation and purification of primary microglia from animal brains will be a useful tool for investigating the pathological α-synuclein propagation in vitro. In this chapter, we describe a general operational procedure that involves culturing mixed neuroglial cells from the cerebral cortex and hippocampus of neonatal mice and obtaining primary microglia through mechanical oscillation. The primary cells are suitable for establishing microglial activation induced by α-synuclein preformed fibrils (α-syn PFFs). Conditioned medium produced by these microglial cells to further culture neuronal cells recapitulates the transmission of amyloid α-syn to neurons. This protocol may provide an effective ex vivo model for studying microglia-related neuroinflammation in amyloid α-syn cell-to-cell transmission.

articles.title: Preparation of Rat Primary Cortical Astrocyte Culture.
articles.abstract: Astrocytes and neurons originate from common neural stem cells, with astrocytes playing essential roles in neuronal survival. By forming the blood-brain barrier, astrocytes create a specialized metabolic environment that supports neuronal function. Traditionally, astrocytes have been classified as neurotoxic or neuroprotective subtypes based on gene expression and phenotypes, but their diversity across brain regions and functions renders this binary categorization insufficient. Increasing evidence also highlights astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles as protective mediators against neuronal injury and degeneration. Understanding astrocytic functions is therefore critical for elucidating the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases, and diverse co-culture and organoid models have been developed for this purpose. Primary astrocyte cultures, which are thought to retain characteristics of the in vivo environment, remain a robust and versatile system. In this chapter, we describe a fundamental protocol for isolating and culturing astrocytes from neonatal rat brains. This method is an isolation and culture method that takes advantage of the difference in adhesiveness between astrocytes and other brain cells, which allows the generation of large cell populations, making it particularly suitable for biochemical analyses and for isolating scarce materials such as extracellular vesicles and microRNAs.

articles.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values.
RESULTS: Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Propofol Induction for Sedated Radiologic Procedures in Patients With Trisomy 21.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with Trisomy 21 (T21) are more susceptible to sedation-related adverse events (AEs). Few studies address the risk of propofol or compare natural airway sedation regimens in this population. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is less likely than propofol to result in AEs as it promotes a more natural sleep and less airway muscle relaxation.
METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data. We queried the Pediatric Sedation Research Consortium (PSRC) Database from the years 2020 to 2025. The demographic characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. The incidence of sedation-related AEs and sedation failures were described by induction drug (DEX vs. propofol). Any medication used other than DEX or propofol were excluded. We performed a propensity score analysis comparing the DEX cohort to the propofol cohort. All the statistical work was performed using SAS 9.4.
RESULTS: A total of 337 patients met inclusion criteria. The average age was 7 years. Forty-four percent of AEs were partial airway obstruction. For the bivariate analyses, the AE outcome variable is statistically significant with the medication variable (χ2df=1=33.249, P<0.001). Induction with propofol had a 5 times higher odds of an AE (OR=5.069, 95% CI: 2.829-9.082). After propensity score matching, there are a total of 216 matched observations.
CONCLUSION: In patients with T21 undergoing radiologic procedures, the odds of having any AE are higher with induction using propofol compared with DEX. Greater consideration should be given for use of DEX induction for patients with T21 undergoing sedated radiologic procedures.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.
OBJECTIVE: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.
STUDY SELECTION: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.
RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.
RESULTS: Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).
CONCLUSION: After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children.
METHODS: In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences.
CONCLUSION: Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

articles.title: Phototherapy Irradiance Exposure in Near-Term Infants Treated for Indirect Hyperbilirubinemia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate phototherapy irradiance in near-term infants with indirect hyperbilirubinemia and compare it with American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) intensive phototherapy thresholds.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective observational study conducted at level III and level IV neonatal intensive care units within a single health system. Neonates born at ≥35 weeks' gestation with indirect hyperbilirubinemia requiring overhead phototherapy were enrolled, and irradiance was measured with a single calibrated light meter at the infant's trunk beneath the light source. Clinical and treatment data, including gestational age, birth weight, bilirubin concentrations, irradiance levels, number of phototherapy devices, phototherapy duration, and phototherapy-associated adverse effects, were collected.
RESULTS: Seventy infants were enrolled. The median gestational age was 38.0 weeks, and the median birth weight was 3135 g. The median irradiance was 60.8 μW/cm2/nm (IQR, 43.0-71.1; range, 19.1-106.0), approximately 2-fold the AAP minimum threshold for intensive phototherapy. Intensive irradiance (≥30 μW/cm2/nm) was achieved in 94.3% of infants. Hyperthermia occurred in 6 infants (8.6%), rash occurred in 4 infants (5.7%), and diarrhea occurred in 1 infant (1.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary neonatal intensive care unit practice, phototherapy irradiance is frequently and substantially above the AAP-recommended minimum thresholds, with a median dose approximately twice the guideline minimum. These findings highlight variability in phototherapy dosing and may inform quality improvement efforts to optimize irradiance delivery. Further studies should evaluate efficacy and long-term safety of high irradiance exposure.

articles.title: Neonatal pancreatitis as the initial presentation of familial chylomicronemia syndrome: A case report of a homozygous lipoprotein lipase variant (p.Ser286Arg) in a Tunisian patient.
articles.abstract: Familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder, most commonly caused by lipoprotein lipase (LPL) deficiency. We report the case of a 24-day-old female neonate admitted for fever and abdominal distension. Laboratory investigations revealed elevated serum lipase and inflammatory markers. Abdominal computed tomography demonstrated features of necrotizing acute pancreatitis with intraperitoneal effusion. The milky appearance of the serum prompted lipid profiling, which revealed extreme hypertriglyceridemia (50.8 mmol/L). LPL activity was reduced, and genetic testing confirmed a homozygous pathogenic variant in the LPL gene, LPL:c.858T > A;p.(Ser286Arg) located within the LPL catalytic triad. Initial management included bowel rest, supportive care, and antibiotics, followed by gradual reintroduction of enteral feeding with medium-chain triglyceride-based formulas. This case highlights neonatal pancreatitis as a life-threatening complication of FCS.

articles.title: Quality of life in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease over the past decade: A repeated cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Children with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), experience a significantly lower health-related quality of life (HRQoL) compared to healthy children. Over the past decade, advancements in IBD care may have influenced HRQoL. The aim of this study was to compare HRQoL between two independent pediatric IBD cohorts from distinct time periods.
METHODS: Two pediatric IBD cohorts, T1 cohort (2014-2015) and T2 cohort (2022-2024), completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 4.0 (PedsQL) and the IBD-specific IMPACT-III questionnaire. Total and scale scores of both questionnaires were compared between the two cohorts. Moreover, the HRQoL of T2 was compared to the general population (GP).
RESULTS: In total, 117 (T1: 72, T2: 45) patients completed both questionnaires. The PedsQL total and scale scores did not differ between T1 and T2 for both patients with CD and UC. IMPACT-III total and subscale scores showed no differences for patients with CD and the total IBD-cohort. In UC, the IMPACT-III total score and its subdomain social functioning were higher in T2 (p = 0.049 and p = 0.013, respectively). Children with IBD in the T2 cohort scored lower in the physical (p = 0.001) and school (p = 0.001) functioning subscales when compared to the GP cohort.
CONCLUSION: This study shows no overall difference in HRQoL for pediatric patients with IBD over the past decade but indicates an improvement in HRQoL for children with UC.

articles.title: Candidemia in patients with intestinal failure: Diagnostic utility of fungal blood cultures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatric patients with intestinal failure (IF) receiving parenteral nutrition are at increased risk for candidemia. Evaluation of central line-associated bloodstream infection often includes aerobic, anaerobic, and fungal blood cultures, but the diagnostic yield of dedicated fungal cultures is uncertain. We evaluated fungal blood cultures compared with aerobic cultures for detecting candidemia.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with IF and central venous catheters admitted to Children's National Hospital from 2010 through 2020 was conducted. Candidemia episodes were identified through microbiology records. Primary analysis included episodes with both aerobic and fungal blood cultures obtained on the first day of fungemia. Time to positivity (TTP) was compared between paired cultures.
RESULTS: Among 121 hospitalizations, 20 candidemia episodes occurred in 17 patients; 14 had paired aerobic and fungal cultures and were included in the primary analysis. Median age was 3.3 years (interquartile range [IQR] 1.0-8.7), and median length of stay was 25.5 days (IQR 17.0-36.3). Candida parapsilosis and Candida guilliermondii were most common (13/20 episodes). Ninety percent were receiving parenteral nutrition, and 90% had antimicrobial exposure within 6 months. In all paired cases, Candida grew in both cultures. Aerobic cultures had faster TTP than fungal cultures (23.8 ± 8.5 vs. 67.2 ± 18.0 h; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Aerobic cultures detected all candidemia identified by fungal cultures and had faster TTP. Dedicated fungal cultures provided no observed incremental diagnostic yield, although sample size limits precision. Larger studies should determine whether selective rather than routine fungal cultures are appropriate in pediatric IF.

articles.title: Improving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in hospitalized pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Youth hospitalized with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. Using quality improvement methods, we aimed to increase the rate of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst select hospitalized patients with IBD by reaching 90% algorithm adherence by June 2023 and sustaining.
METHODS: Current evidence, external institutional algorithms, and multidisciplinary collaboration (hematology, pharmacy, surgery) were used to create an algorithm for providing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin. The algorithm was implemented in February 2023 for all patients admitted with active IBD to a large, tertiary care children's hospital. Rates of algorithm adherence and rates of enoxaparin receipt during the project period were compared to baseline rates. Patient and provider education, electronic data tracking, and regular data auditing and review with providers were used to improve algorithm adherence. Reasons for non-adherence to the algorithm and rates of VTE, bleeding complications, and medication side effects during hospitalization were tracked.
RESULTS: The proportion of patients who appropriately followed the algorithm reached 94%, increased from 50% when the algorithm was retrospectively applied to the pre-project period (p < 0.001). The total proportion of hospitalized patients who received pharmacologic prophylaxis increased from 1% to 31% (p < 0.001). Following algorithm introduction, there were no VTEs or reported complications from enoxaparin during hospitalization.
CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of a standardized algorithm was associated with significantly increased rates of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst children hospitalized with IBD with no recorded adverse in-hospital events.

articles.title: Novel pathogenic variant in haploinsufficiency of A20 with severe gastrointestinal effects and fulminant hepatic failure: A pediatric case series.
articles.abstract: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a rare autoinflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3), encoding a negative regulator of nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NFκB) signaling. We report two pediatric patients with a previously unreported novel pathogenic variant (p. Glu409*) in the zinc finger (ZnF) 1 domain, exhibiting markedly divergent phenotypes. Case 1 presented with very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD) and autoimmune thyroiditis, requiring aggressive infliximab dose escalation. Case 2 developed fulminant hepatic failure requiring liver transplantation, followed by post-transplant complications including refractory rejection, recurrent infections, and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. This represents the first known case of HA20 in solid organ transplantation. These cases underscore the importance of early genetic diagnosis in unexplained pediatric inflammatory disease and transplant rejection, as HA20 recognition may alter immunosuppressive strategies and guide therapies including cytokine blockade or Janus kinase (JAK) inhibition.

articles.title: Eosinophilic esophagitis and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome: A case series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RTS) is a rare disorder characterized by intellectual disability, poor growth, distinctive facial features, and gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. While dysphagia and feeding difficulties are well recognized in RTS, the prevalence and clinical significance of eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in this population remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series at a single pediatric tertiary care center (2012-2022) collecting demographic, genetic, clinical, endoscopic, and histopathological data.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients with RTS were identified; 15 (56%) had an identifiable genetic variant (12 with CREBBP and 3 with EP300). Seventeen patients (63%) had GI symptoms and 8 (30%) underwent endoscopy. Four patients (15%) were diagnosed with EoE, with one patient also having eosinophilic gastritis and eosinophilic duodenitis. Age at diagnosis ranged from 8 months to 23 years. Presenting symptoms included food impaction, vomiting, dysphagia, and poor weight gain. Three of the 4 patients had RTS type 1 (CREBBP variant gene). Treatments included proton pump inhibitors, swallowed steroids, and dietary elimination with variable responses. Compared with the general population, the odds of EoE in our RTS cohort were 121-fold higher (odds ratio = 121.6, 95% confidence interval: 13.1-1131.0, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a markedly increased prevalence of EoE in patients with RTS. Early recognition and evaluation of GI symptoms with endoscopic assessment is important to enable timely diagnosis, optimize management, and reduce the risk of EoE-related complications. Further research is needed to understand the underlying genetic and immunologic mechanisms linking RTS and EoE.

articles.title: Parent perceptions of disease monitoring in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: The influence of intestinal ultrasound exposure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Monitoring pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) typically requires invasive or resource-intensive testing. Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is a noninvasive, radiation-free, point-of-care modality increasingly used in pediatric IBD. Whether IUS exposure influences parent preferences for disease-monitoring strategies remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of parents of children with IBD at a tertiary center. Parents, recruited from a prospective IBD biobank with linked clinical data, were stratified by prior IUS exposure based on clinical records/imaging history. The survey assessed parent preferences, perceived discomfort, and perceived usefulness for five monitoring modalities (IUS, colonoscopy, cross-sectional imaging [magnetic resonance imaging/computed tomography], blood tests, and stool studies), as well as parent activation (parent-patient activation measure), medication adherence (parent-adapted Morisky Medication Adherence Scale), and visit impact.
RESULTS: Sixty-two parents completed the survey (31 IUS-experienced, 31 IUS-naïve). Compared with IUS-naïve parents, IUS-experienced parents were more likely to report definite preference for IUS (83% vs. 36%, p = 0.003), rate IUS as completely useful (67% vs. 27%, p = 0.002), and report no perceived discomfort with IUS (90% vs. 68%, p = 0.01); conversely, they were more likely to report great discomfort with cross-sectional imaging (37% vs. 12%, p = 0.04). Trends toward greater perceived visit benefit included higher trust in physician recommendations (97% vs. 81%, p = 0.07) and greater sense of control over their child's IBD (90% vs. 71%, p = 0.08). Parent activation and adherence were high across groups. Qualitative responses highlighted reassurance, speed, and noninvasiveness of IUS.
CONCLUSIONS: Parents report strong acceptance of IUS, with prior exposure associated with greater preference, perceived usefulness, and lower perceived burden.

articles.title: Social Determinants of Health in Infantile Hemangioma Care: A 10-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective of this study was to determine how measures of social vulnerability correlate with timing and modality of treatment for infantile hemangioma (IH).
METHODS: Clinical informatics techniques were used to identify patients diagnosed with IH before 24 months of age over a 10-year period at a single academic institution. Outcomes included age at diagnosis, treatment received, and age at treatment initiation. Multivariable regression models were used to measure associations with race, home language, insurance payor, and neighborhood Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Changes in these outcomes after the 2019 publication of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) IH Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG) were also assessed.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1633 patients. Black infants received propranolol later than White infants (β = +4.82 months, p = 0.0224). Asian patients were diagnosed earlier than other races/ethnicities (β = -1.03 months, p = 0.0385) and had lower odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 0.61, p = 0.0339). Infants from non-English-speaking families had lower odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 0.37, p = 0.0005) and initiated timolol earlier than patients from English-speaking families. Government-insured patients had higher odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 1.66, p = 0.0097), lower odds of receiving timolol (OR = 0.65, p = 0.0093), and later timolol initiation (β = +3.23 months, p = 0.0079) than privately insured patients. Patients in the most disadvantaged quartile (Q4) started timolol later than other groups (p = 0.0055). Following publication of the 2019 CPG, age at diagnosis decreased from 6.30 to 5.04 months (p = 0.001) and timolol was started earlier (6.84-4.32 months, p = 0.0006).
CONCLUSIONS: Race, preferred language, insurance status, and neighborhood-level social vulnerability were associated with differences in the timing and modality of IH care. These findings underscore the need for focused study and intervention to ensure that all infants with IH receive timely and effective IH care, regardless of social circumstance.

articles.title: Hydroxychloroquine as adjunctive therapy in steroid-dependent pediatric Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease with liver dysfunction: A case report.
articles.abstract: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease is usually self-limiting, but treatment of steroid-dependent disease in children remains uncertain. We report a 7-year-old girl with biopsy-confirmed Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease and severe liver dysfunction. She presented with intermittent fever and cervical lymphadenopathy, followed by rash and worsening liver dysfunction. Cervical lymph node biopsy revealed necrotizing lymphadenitis without evidence of malignancy. Antinuclear and U1 ribonucleoprotein antibodies were positive; liver-kidney microsomal type 1 antibodies were subsequently detected. Serologic tests for the viruses examined were negative, although hepatitis A testing was not performed. Retrospective assessment using the revised International Autoimmune Hepatitis Group scoring system did not reach the threshold for probable autoimmune hepatitis. Nevertheless, autoimmune hepatitis could not be excluded because liver histology was unavailable and the viral evaluation was incomplete. After relapse during prednisolone tapering, she received methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine. Remission was achieved, allowing gradual corticosteroid tapering. Prednisolone was discontinued at month 39 and hydroxychloroquine at month 50 after disease onset. No relapse occurred during the subsequent 8-month follow-up. No hydroxychloroquine-related adverse events, including retinopathy, were observed during 44 months of treatment or the subsequent follow-up. This case adds to the limited experience with prolonged hydroxychloroquine use in younger children with steroid-dependent Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. Hydroxychloroquine may have contributed to corticosteroid tapering, although its independent efficacy cannot be established because it was initiated alongside intensified corticosteroid therapy.

articles.title: Enhancing Rural and Indigenous Pediatric Dermatology: A Scoping Review and Practical Algorithm for Primary Care.
articles.abstract: Children living in rural and remote Canadian communities, including many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities, face substantial barriers to timely dermatologic care. We conducted a scoping review of common pediatric skin conditions in these settings and used the findings, supplemented by established clinical guidance and expert input, to develop a practical diagnostic and management algorithm for front-line clinicians. The review focuses on inflammatory, infectious, and environmental conditions commonly encountered in primary care and highlights contextual factors that may influence presentation, treatment, and outcomes, including geographic isolation, limited specialist access, crowded housing, water insecurity, and extreme weather exposure. The proposed algorithm is intended to support initial assessment, treatment, and referral while identifying persistent evidence gaps and the need for culturally safe, community-informed models of care.

articles.title: Conceptualizing a Revised Self-Regulation Framework for Medication Adherence in Children and Adolescents With Sickle Cell Disease Undergoing Stem Cell Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background: Children and adolescents with sickle cell disease (SCD) undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) require complex medication regimens, placing them at increased risk for nonadherence. While many adherence-related determinants have been described, theoretical frameworks to integrate these influences remain limited. Self-regulation theory (SRT) offers a framework for examining the cognitive, emotional, and behavioral processes underlying adherence. Purpose: This article conceptualizes a revised self-regulation framework to better understand and address medication adherence among children and adolescents with SCD undergoing HSCT. This modified framework will be used in future research to identify adherence barriers, develop tailored interventions, and improve clinical care. Methods: A theory-driven conceptual analysis was conducted using foundational SRT literature and empirical evidence related to medication adherence in SCD and pediatric transplantation. SRT constructs were examined and adapted to address the unique characteristics of children and adolescents with SCD undergoing transplantation. Results: The revised framework exemplifies how personal, behavioral, and environmental factors, mediated by self-regulation processes, influence medication adherence behaviors and outcomes in this population. It underscores the importance of strengthening self-efficacy and tailoring interventions to individual and contextual needs. Implications for Practice: Applying this revised SRT framework can guide the development of personalized, theory-driven interventions to improve medication adherence and health outcomes of children and adolescents with SCD undergoing HSCT.

articles.title: Predictors of Parental Strain in Pediatric Atopic Dermatitis: Findings From the US National Survey of Children's Health.
articles.abstract: Caring for a child with atopic dermatitis (AD) places strain on parents, but it remains unclear whether additional atopic comorbidities or psychosocial context compounds this burden. Data from the 2007-2008 National Survey of Children's Health among 6913 children aged 6-17 years was analyzed using survey-weighted multivariable regression to examine associations between a 5-item parental strain scale and parent-reported AD severity, comorbid asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy, along with family, social, and healthcare access factors. Increased parental strain was associated with AD severity and with delayed or forgone care. Decreased parental strain was associated with better maternal mental health and with the female sex of the child. Atopic comorbidities were not associated with strain. Parental strain was more strongly associated with psychosocial factors and the severity of AD than the presence of additional atopic comorbidities.

articles.title: The seroprevalence of celiac disease in Syrian refugee children with malnutrition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Malnutrition in children is a significant public health issue. Various factors that can cause malnutrition include inadequate intake, inadequate digestion, inadequate absorption, increased demand, and increased catabolism. Celiac disease (CD) also causes malnutrition as a result of inadequate digestion. The number of studies investigating seroprevalence of CD in children with malnutrition is limited. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the seroprevalence of CD among Syrian refugee children with malnutrition.
METHODS: The current study was conducted between January and December 2023. All children with malnutrition, who receiving enteral nutrition were included. The children's age and sex, body weight, height upon admission were recorded. Tissue transglutaminase antibody IgA test (tTG IgA) and total IgA test were used to diagnose CD in all patients. Gastroduodenoscopy was planned to be performed in all seropositive children to diagnose CD.
RESULTS: Of the 329 patients, 179 (54.4%) were female. The mean age of patients was 5.82 ± 4.17 years. The median tTG IgA value was 2 IU/L (0.4-200.0). The seroprevalence of CD was found to be 3.34% (11/329), 9 of them had been receiving enteral feeding for at least 6 months. Gastroduodenoscopy was not performed on most of the patients because they could not be reached due to communication problems (the phone number was wrong or not in the system, etc.). But 2 of them was diagnosed without biopsy according to the ESPGHAN 2020 guidelines for diagnosing CD.
CONCLUSIONS: We detected higher seroprevalence of CD in children with malnutrition compared to general population. Beacuse celiac disease is a chronic multi-systemic illness, early detection of CD is critical to avoiding long-term consequences. Therefore, screening for CD should be an essential part of work-up in all Syrian refugee children with malnutrition. We hereby recommend verifying the contact information of refugee patients at the time of application.

articles.title: Ketamine versus Diazepam for Pediatric MRI Sedation in Northern Malawi: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in children requires adequate sedation to ensure procedural success. In resource-limited settings, sedative options are often restricted, and comparative data on ketamine and diazepam are scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and MRI completion rates of ketamine versus diazepam for pediatric sedation at a low-resource hospital in northern Malawi.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study including children aged 0-14 years who underwent MRI with ketamine (n = 20) or diazepam (n = 36) at Mzuzu Central Hospital between August 2025 and March 2026. Sedation success was defined as Ramsay Sedation Score 4-5 with stable vital signs and absence of movement during MRI. Primary outcomes were sedation onset time, sedation success rate, recovery time, adverse events, and MRI completion rates.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Ketamine was associated with a shorter sedation onset (mean 1.55±0.39 min vs 3.43±0.45 min, P < 0.01), higher sedation success rate(19 (95%)vs 24 (67%), P < 0.05), and longer recovery time (mean 58.64±7.14 min vs 43.10±5.04 min, P < 0.01) compared with diazepam. The incidence of adverse events was similar between the two groups, with no severe complications observed. First-pass MRI completion (19 (95%)vs 21 (58%), P < 0.01) and overall scan success rates (20(100%)vs 25(69%), P < 0.05) were higher in the ketamine group.
CONCLUSIONS: In this low-resource setting, ketamine provided faster, more reliable pediatric MRI sedation than diazepam, with higher procedural success and a favorable safety profile. Ketamine may be considered the preferred sedative for pediatric MRI in similar resource-limited hospitals, provided continuous monitoring and anesthetic oversight.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Integrating a Peer Education Program to Improve HIV Service Uptake Among University Students: Evidence from Malawi University of Business and Applied Sciences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although peer education programs are crucial in Malawi, there is paucity of data on their effect on uptake of HIV services among students in colleges. This study assessed the effectiveness of integrating a peer educators' program in enhancing HIV services uptake among students at Malawi University of Business and Applied Sciences.
METHODS: This was a complementary mixed-methods study. The quantitative component employed a retrospective comparative pre-post design to assess changes in HIV service utilization before and after integration of the peer educator programme. Quantitative data on HIV service utilization provided by the MUBAS campus clinic were obtained for 12-month period before integration of the peer educator programme and 12-month period following its integration. Comparative analysis and Z-test were performed to compare the proportions of students accessing HIV service before and after integration of the program. An exploratory qualitative study used 12 key informant interviews [KIIs] to explore barriers and facilitators in the implementation of the program. Data were analysed using a framework method of analysis.
RESULTS: The study findings showed that in 2023, before the integration of the peer educator program, a total number of 1,875 clients accessed HIV services compared to 2,579 clients who accessed the services in 2024. This indicates a 37.55% percentage increase [Z-value of +12.418 and p = 2.09 × 10-35]. HIV self-test kit distribution increased by 241% following the integration of peer educators, with a Z-value of +20.544 and p = 8.68 × 10-94. Participants regarded the peer educator program as effective in improving students' knowledge, related to HIV and SRHR, facilitating access to sexual and reproductive health services and promoting health seeking behaviour among students at MUBAS.
CONCLUSIONS: The integration of peer educator programs in services distribution, demonstrated to be an effective model to improve access to HIV services among young people in higher education institutions.

articles.title: Clinical Research on the Treatment of Post-Appendectomy Incision Infection with Traditional Chinese Medicine Patch Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an external Traditional Chinese Medicine patch containing Mirabilite and Borneol for improving incision healing and preventing postoperative infection after appendectomy.
METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial included 120 patients undergoing appendectomy for acute suppurative appendicitis were randomly assigned to an intervention group and a control group. Both groups received routine postoperative intravenous antibiotics and sterile gauze dressing. The intervention group additionally received an external Traditional Chinese Medicine patch composed of Mirabilite (500 g) and Borneol (10 g), applied over the surgical incision once daily for 5-7 days. Primary outcome was surgical incision healing grade. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, time to suture removal, swelling area relative to incision length, dressing change frequency, length of hospital stay, postoperative complications, and serum inflammatory cytokine levels including TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-1β and IL-8.
RESULTS: The intervention group showed a significantly higher rate of Grade A healing (P < 0.001), and a higher rate of Grade B healing (P = 0.002). Postoperative VAS pain scores were significantly lower in the intervention group (P < 0.001). Time to suture removal, swelling-to-incision length ratio, dressing change frequency, and hospital stay were all significantly reduced in the intervention group (P < 0.001). The incidences of incision infection and abdominal abscess were significantly lower in the intervention group (P = 0.019 and P = 0.036, respectively). Although serum levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-1β and IL-8 increased postoperatively in both groups, the magnitudes of increase were significantly smaller in the intervention group (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: External application of a Traditional Chinese Medicine patch containing Mirabilite and Borneol significantly improves postoperative wound healing and reduces infection-related complications following appendectomy for acute suppurative appendicitis. The therapeutic effects may be associated with modulation of the postoperative inflammatory response.

articles.title: Improving Rates of Screening for Health-related Social Needs in a Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In September 2024, our hospital implemented health-related social needs (HRSN) screening in the pediatric emergency department (PED). We aimed to increase rates of completed HRSN screens from a baseline of 18% in October 2024 to greater than 50% by December 2025.
METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, we implemented a new workflow that shifted from verbal to paper screening, posted screening posters in the PED, and provided stakeholders with education and weekly updates on screening rates. The primary outcome measure was the percentage of eligible patient encounters with a completed HRSN screen. The secondary outcome measure was the percentage of patients with a completed HRSN screen who requested to be connected with resources.
