We created statistical process control charts and performed chi-square tests or Fisher's exact tests to assess the associations between demographics and HRSN screen completion status.
RESULTS: The mean screening rate increased from 18% to 40% during the course of 14 months. The mean rate of patients/caregivers requesting connection to resources on HRSN screens increased from 16% to 29%. Patients aged younger than 18 years, Black non-Hispanic patients, Hispanic patients, patients with public insurance, and patients who preferred the Haitian Creole language were less likely to have a completed HRSN screen.
CONCLUSIONS: Through our quality improvement initiative, we improved HRSN screening rates in our PED. We observed an increase in the rate of patients/caregivers requesting connections to resources. We could increase these rates in future studies through targeted interventions to engage patient groups that were less likely to complete screening and by improving stakeholder buy-in.

articles.title: Increasing Resident Involvement in Medical Resuscitations in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary care and general emergency providers must recognize critically ill children and initiate life-sustaining interventions, yet trainees report limited experience and low confidence in this domain. The pediatric emergency department (PED) offers an optimal setting to improve resident exposure to pediatric medical resuscitations (MRs). We aimed to increase resident involvement in PED MRs from 45% to 70% during a 6-month period and evaluate the effect on resident confidence in managing critically ill children.
METHODS: We implemented a disruptive alarm-based alert system and assigned 1 resident per shift to a defined MR-response role. The process measure was alert-system use per 25 MRs; the outcome measure was the percentage of MRs with resident involvement, defined by resident completion of the encounter note per 25 MRs. We assessed change over time using standard rules for special-cause variation. Residents voluntarily completed pre- and postintervention surveys.
RESULTS: Resident involvement in MRs in the PED increased from 45% to 64%. Use of the disruptive alarm increased from 0% to 33%. Residents initially indicated increased confidence in responding to MRs, but this confidence waned over time.
CONCLUSIONS: A standardized disruptive alert system paired with designated MR roles increased resident involvement in MRs in the PED and may influence resident confidence in managing critically ill children.

articles.title: An Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating the Effect of Oil Massage on Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia in Stable Preterm Babies Admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To study the effect of oil massage on duration of phototherapy in preterm neonates with hyperbilirubinemia.
METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial, the authors included hemodynamically stable preterm neonates born at less than 37 wk of gestation. They were randomized to either of the two groups: One group received phototherapy alone, while the other received phototherapy plus oil massage. In the latter group, massage was administered twice daily for 15 min. The primary outcome (phototherapy duration) was compared between groups using an independent t-test. Secondary outcomes, including daily and cumulative stool frequency, were analysed using independent t-tests for each time point. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen's d. All tests were two-tailed, and p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The intervention group (oil massage + phototherapy) required an average of 7.73 h (approximately 7.6%) less phototherapy compared to the control group, which is statistically significant (p-value 0.0118).
CONCLUSIONS: Oil massage, as an additive regimen to phototherapy, helps in reducing the duration of phototherapy in preterm infants with hyperbilirubinemia.

articles.title: Utility of the Acute Illness Observation Scale in Assessing Severity of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Children Aged 2-60 Months: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Early identification of severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children is difficult in resource-limited settings. The Acute Illness Observation Scale (AIOS) is a bedside score based on observable behavioural and physiological parameters. The authors evaluated its utility for severity assessment in children aged 2-60 mo with CAP.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 144 children aged 2-60 mo with CAP admitted to a tertiary-care teaching hospital in Central India (June 2023-November 2024) were classified using IMNCI criteria. AIOS was assessed at admission. ROC analysis used IMNCI-defined severe pneumonia as the outcome; the optimal cut-off was selected by the Youden Index.
RESULTS: Severe pneumonia was present in 79.9% of participants. Higher AIOS scores were associated with grunting, inability to drink/feed, lethargy, crepitations, bronchial breathing, hypoxaemia, leukocytosis, abnormal chest radiographs, intravenous fluid and antibiotic requirements, and longer oxygen therapy. AIOS ≥12 had sensitivity 73.9%, specificity 89.7%, PPV 96.6%, NPV 46.4%, accuracy 77.1%, and AUC 0.89.
CONCLUSIONS: AIOS may complement IMNCI-based severity assessment in tertiary emergency and resource-limited settings. Diagnostic performance should be interpreted cautiously because AIOS and IMNCI contain overlapping clinical features and IMNCI is not an independent gold standard.

articles.title: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis and Evans Syndrome Presenting as Transfusion Refractory Anaemia.
articles.abstract: Evans syndrome is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and immune thrombocytopenia. When associated with other autoimmune diseases, it is classified as secondary Evans syndrome. Its association with Hashimoto's thyroiditis is extremely rare, suggesting a possible shared immunopathogenic mechanism. The authors report a case of an adolescent girl presenting with fatigue, pallor, and menorrhagia for two months. Despite multiple blood transfusions, she remained severely anaemic, indicating ongoing haemolysis. Evaluation revealed autoimmune haemolytic anaemia with a positive direct antiglobulin test and thrombocytopenia. Further work-up confirmed Hashimoto's thyroiditis, establishing a diagnosis of secondary Evans syndrome. This represents the first reported paediatric case from India, highlighting the diagnostic approach and management considerations.

articles.title: Kidney-Alone Transplantation With siRNA Therapy in Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) is a rare genetic disease causing severe hyperoxaluria, kidney stones, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney failure (KF) followed by systemic oxalosis. Expert guidelines traditionally recommended liver-kidney transplantation (LKTx) for patients with vitamin B6-unresponsive PH1 and KF, with 1-year mortality of 5% to 15%. Small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) therapies targeting hepatic oxalate production have shifted the treatment landscape. Eighteen patients on siRNA therapy with successful kidney-alone transplantion (KATx) have been reported.
METHODS: A multicenter, international, retrospective case series from 11 countries included patients with: (1) confirmed PH1 diagnosis; (2) KATx as definitive kidney replacement therapy; and (3) concurrent lumasiran and/or nedosiran treatment beyond the induction phase before and/or after transplantion.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight patients were analyzed: at transplantion, 27 received lumasiran, 6 received nedosiran, and 1 received both; 60.5% carried a priori vitamin B6-responsive variants. All 25 AGXT alleles identified were pathogenic or likely pathogenic, including 3 not previously reported in PH1 and 1 requiring haplotype-level resolution. Median pretransplant plasma oxalate was 59 μmol/l (interquartile range [IQR], 30; range, 5-100). Donors were deceased in 57.9%; 39.5% of recipients were pediatric. Median follow-up was 25 months (range, 2-60). Peritransplant or posttransplant dialysis was used in 60.5%. Four patients diagnosed after KATx were included; 3 were successfully treated with lumasiran. One-year graft survival was 95%; patient survival was 100%.
CONCLUSION: This international series supports KATx as standard of care for carefully selected patients with PH1 with assured long-term siRNA therapy and expert follow-up. Practical recommendations, including a peritransplant checklist emphasizing expert-centered care and vigilance for emerging complications, are provided.

articles.title: Surgical and Cosmetic Outcomes After Fronto-Orbital Advancement With Hybrid Fixation for Unilateral Coronal Craniosynostosis: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fronto-orbital advancement (FOA) remains the standard surgical treatment for unilateral coronal craniosynostosis, particularly in patients presenting beyond the age window for endoscopic treatment and in those with significant frontal and orbital deformity. However, postoperative relapse, residual asymmetry, and fixation-related limitations remain important clinical concerns. Fixation strategies aim to provide immediate structural stability while minimizing potential interference with subsequent cranial growth.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate surgical, morphometric, cosmetic, and perioperative outcomes after FOA using a hybrid fixation strategy in patients with nonsyndromic unilateral coronal craniosynostosis.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 14 patients treated between January 2023 and December 2024 at the JSC National Center for Neurosurgery, Astana, Kazakhstan. All patients had CT-confirmed unilateral nonsyndromic coronal craniosynostosis and underwent primary FOA with combined fixation using biodegradable plates in key structural regions and absorbable sutures between individual remodeled bone fragments. Cosmetic outcomes were assessed using the Whitaker classification and clinician-rated Visual Analog Cosmetic Score (VACS), with each patient's VACS calculated as the mean of independent ratings from 10 assessors. Morphometric evaluation combined cephalic index (CI), as a measure of overall cranial width-to-length proportions, with frontal asymmetry index (FAI), orbital assessment, and nasal deviation angle (NDA). Perioperative safety outcomes and follow-up data were also analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age at surgery was 16.7±12.9 months, and mean follow-up was 16 months (range 12-24). Favorable cosmetic outcomes were achieved in all patients: 92.9% were classified as Whitaker class I and 7.1% as class II, with no class III or IV outcomes or revision surgeries. Median postoperative VACS was 9.5 (range 6-10). FAI categories decreased in 10 of 14 patients (exact sign test, P=0.002; Holm-adjusted P=0.006). CI categories decreased in 6 patients (P=0.031; Holm-adjusted P=0.063), without establishing normalization of cranial shape. NDA categories showed no evidence of a directional change (P=0.625). All 14 patients received intraoperative autologous blood reinfusion and additional allogeneic blood transfusion. Mean total hospital stay was 18.9±3.5 days, including both preoperative and postoperative inpatient care. No major postoperative complications, cerebrospinal fluid leakage, surgical-site infection, relapse, or reoperation were observed.
CONCLUSION: Extended FOA with hybrid fixation was associated with favorable early cosmetic outcomes in this retrospective cohort. These findings describe the combined reconstructive procedure and do not establish the independent contribution of fixation, preservation of physiological cranial growth, or superiority over alternative fixation methods. Larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Pediatric Le Fort Fractures: Does Surgical Timing Predict Complications and Length of Stay?
articles.abstract: Operative timing, complications, and length of stay (LOS) across pediatric Le Fort fracture types remain poorly characterized. Using Pediatric Health Information System data from 2015 to 2025, the authors identified patients with isolated Le Fort type I, II, or III fractures undergoing repair and compared time to procedure, complications, hospital LOS, as well as rates of concomitant traumatic brain injury (TBI) and cervical spine injury (CSI). Among 350 patients (I, 150; II, 114; III, 86), time to first procedure did not differ by type, but time to repair increased with fracture type (2.9, 5.1, 6.7 d; P < 0.001). Respiratory, neurologic, ophthalmologic, hematologic, and metabolic complications increased stepwise across fracture types, whereas dental and occlusal complications predominated in type I. Likewise, concomitant TBI and CSI increased with fracture type. In multivariable analysis, Le Fort type was not an independent predictor of LOS (P = 0.2). Presence of any complication (incidence rate ratio: 2.60), intensive care unit admission (1.46), concomitant TBI (1.43), high-acuity CSI (1.44), and longer time to repair (1.48 per log-day) independently predicted longer hospital LOS (all P < 0.01). Higher grade Le Fort fracture type aligned with delayed repair, greater complication burden, and longer stay, but appeared to mark injury severity rather than independently determine LOS.

articles.title: Montelukast sodium in preventing oxygen requirements at day 28 in preterm infants: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: BackgroundEvaluating the efficacy and safety of oral montelukast in preventing oxygen requirement at day 28 of birth in preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit through a randomized trial with open-label treatment administration and blinded outcome assessment.MethodsTarget Population: 92 preterm infants admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Units of four hospitals.
INTERVENTION: Daily oral administration of 1 mg/kg montelukast.
PRIMARY OUTCOME: Incidence of Oxygen requirement on days 14 and 28 of life.ResultsReduction in Oxygen requirement: Significantly lower in the intervention group (31.7%) compared to the control group (55%). Lung Disease Severity: Pulmonary Severity Score was significantly lower in the montelukast group on days 14 and 28. Safety Profile: No serious drug-related adverse effects were reported.
SECONDARY OUTCOMES: No statistically significant differences were observed regarding mortality or length of hospital stay between the two groups.ConclusionPreventive administration of montelukast in high-risk preterm infants appears to be safe and effective in reducing the incidence of oxygen requirement at day 28/discharge.

articles.title: Alkaline phosphatase recovery patterns and in-hospital mortality in very low birth weight infants: A single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundLow alkaline phosphatase (ALP) values in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants have received little attention, and the clinical significance of serial ALP changes after an initial low value is unclear. We examined whether ALP trajectory patterns were associated with in-hospital death in VLBW infants.Materials and MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included VLBW infants admitted from 2013 to 2024 with a serum ALP ≤100 U/L after postnatal day 2. Infants were classified by their subsequent ALP course. Non-recovery was defined as fluctuation or persistent suppression. The primary outcome was in-hospital death. Unadjusted comparisons were supplemented by landmark and time-dependent Cox analyses.ResultsOf 1,652 VLBW infants, 55 were included: sustained recovery in 23, fluctuation in 5, persistent suppression in 9, and no follow-up in 18. Mortality was 92.9% (13/14) in the non-recovery group versus 21.7% (5/23) in the sustained recovery group (risk ratio [RR] 4.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.11-9.81). All 18 infants without follow-up died and were not included in this comparison. At a 7-day landmark, subsequent mortality was 77.8% (7/9) with a most recent ALP ≤100 U/L versus 33.3% (7/21) with ALP >100 U/L (RR 2.33, 95% CI 1.10-4.84; gestational age-adjusted odds ratio 6.07, 95% CI 1.09-50.29).ConclusionAmong VLBW infants with ALP ≤100 U/L, absence of sustained ALP recovery above 100 U/L was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, and the association persisted, although attenuated, in landmark analyses that accounted for early deaths. Whether ALP trajectory provides prognostic information beyond illness severity requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Application of the ICF in the functioning assessment of children with suspected developmental coordination difficulties.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) is based on a biopsychosocial model that promotes a multidimensional approach in rehabilitation. The ICF has been recommended as a framework for clinical reasoning in several health conditions, including those characterized by motor difficulties such as Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD). We compared the functioning profile of children with motor challenges (at risk [r-DCD] and probable DCD [p-DCD]) with those with typical neurodevelopment (TND) using the ICF framework.
METHODS: Cross-sectional study involving children from Southern Brazil. ICF-informed instruments included: body functions (MABC-2, 6MWT, SDQ-Por); activities (DCDQ-Br, IPAQ-SF, SDQ-Por); participation (PEM-CY) and contextual factors (sex and age). Statistics included the chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, and the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's post hoc test with p < 0.05.
RESULTS: 208 children (mean age 8.2 [1.3] years) classified as TND (n = 158), r-DCD (n = 25) and p-DCD (n = 25) were included. In the activities domain, except for the expected lower motor skills in the p-DCD group, no differences were found across groups. In participation, there were significant differences only for lower involvement in the community for p-DCD (p = 0.016).
CONCLUSION: The impact of motor challenges was found in activities and in participation. These findings underscore the role for physical therapy interventions targeting improved coordination and balance while encouraging social interactions. The study serves as an example of how to select and combine assessment instruments aligned with ICF domains to evaluate children with motor difficulties.

articles.title: Early TSH-FT4 discordance and subsequent biochemical TSH elevation in NICU-admitted neonates: An exploratory retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether relative thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-free thyroxine (FT4) imbalance on postnatal day 2 was associated with subsequent TSH elevation in neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).Study DesignThis single-center retrospective cohort included 154 NICU-admitted neonates with simultaneous serum TSH, free triiodothyronine, and FT4 measurements on postnatal day 2 and at least one subsequent serum TSH measurement. The primary predictor was the TSH-FT4 Δ score, defined as cohort-standardized TSH minus cohort-standardized FT4. The primary outcome was new threshold crossing or a further TSH increase after day 2 using an operational threshold of >15 mIU/L. Associations were evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for gestational age.ResultsEight infants met the primary outcome. Each 1-standard-deviation increase in the day-2 TSH-FT4 Δ score was associated with higher odds of subsequent TSH elevation (adjusted odds ratio, 2.47; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-5.91; p = 0.024). Day-2 TSH, day-2 FT4, and the TSH-FT4 average score showed no clear associations. A three-analyte score incorporating free triiodothyronine showed a similar association.ConclusionRelative TSH-FT4 discordance during early neonatal thyroid testing was associated with subsequent biochemical TSH elevation. These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as establishing a clinical predictive tool and require prospective external validation using standardized follow-up and clinically meaningful thyroid outcomes.

articles.title: Association of growth following laparotomy with white matter and cerebellar injury in preterm infants with surgical NEC.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the impact of perioperative growth measurements following laparotomy on white matter abnormalities (WMA) and cerebellar injury from MRIs performed at term-equivalent in preterm infants with surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC).MethodsIn this retrospective cohort, growth parameters were assessed at birth, before NEC diagnosis and exploratory laparotomy, 28 days after bowel resection, before reanastomosis, at 36 weeks corrected gestational age, and at discharge. Term-equivalent MRI was evaluated for WMA, gray matter abnormality (GMA), and cerebellar injury. WMA associations were examined using separate unadjusted logistic models and models adjusted for gestational age. Within-infant and between-group z-score changes across intervals were assessed with Holm adjustment.ResultsAmong 51 infants, 26 (51.0%) had WMA. Any WMA was associated with lower head circumference (HC) at 36 weeks corrected gestational age (p = 0.04), lower discharge length z-score (p = 0.05), and lower HC z-scores at 36 weeks (p = 0.05) and discharge (p = 0.02). Moderate/severe WMA was associated with lower weight (p = 0.04), length (p = 0.03), and HC (p = 0.01) before reanastomosis and lower HC at discharge (p = 0.04). Higher length z-score (p = 0.04) and HC z-score (p = 0.05) at discharge, and greater length (p = 0.04) and HC (p = 0.05) before reanastomosis, were associated with lower odds of moderate/severe WMA after adjustment for gestational age. Cerebellar injury occurred in 8 infants (15.7%) and was associated with lower weight, length, and HC before NEC diagnosis (p = 0.01, p < 0.01, p = 0.01) and 28 days after resection (p = 0.01, p = 0.01, p = 0.01).ConclusionsBetter linear and head growth before reanastomosis and at discharge were associated with lower WMA severity. Our findings are hypothesis-generating and support the possibility that serial linear and head growth measurements may help identify infants at greater neurological risk following the surgical NEC.

articles.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials.
AIMS: To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence.
CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

articles.title: Neurofilament levels in cord blood of fetal growth restricted newborns.
articles.abstract: BackgroundStructural and functional brain deficits in fetal growth restriction (FGR) are well documented. The aim of this study was to determine whether there is a correlation between Neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels in umbilical cord blood and FGR at birth.MethodsThis prospective observational pilot study enrolled 85 pregnant women (control group (N = 58) and FGR group (N = 27)). No a priori sample size calculation was performed and all analyses are exploratory.ResultsThe median levels of NfL were significantly higher in FGR (14.3 (9.7-25.1 IQR)) compared to the controls (11.9 (8.2-15.9 IQR) (p = 0.014)). Median levels of NfL were significantly higher in "early onset" FGR group (29.8 (24.5-34.8 IQR)) compared to the controls (11.9 (8.2-15.9 IQR) (p < 0.001)). There was no significant difference in median NfL levels between "late onset" FGR group (11.6 (9.2-14.3 IQR)) and controls (11.9 (8.2-15.9 IQR) (p = 1)).ConclusionHigher cord blood NfL concentrations were observed mainly in early-onset FGR. However, because early-onset FGR was strongly confounded with prematurity, clinical severity, cesarean delivery, NICU admission, and lower cord pH, and because no preterm non-FGR control group was available, an FGR-specific neuronal injury cannot be established from this study. These findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Association and limited predictive performance of first-trimester PAPP-A, free β-hCG, and nuchal translucency for adverse neonatal outcomes: Prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEarly prediction of adverse neonatal outcomes remains challenging. This study evaluated the associations and predictive performance of first-trimester pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A), free β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), nuchal translucency (NT), and maternal age.MethodsThis prospective cohort enrolled 1244 singleton pregnancies at 11-13 + 6 weeks, with 1229 analyzed after 15 were lost to follow-up. Primary outcome comprised preterm birth, low birth weight, or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. Models underwent held-out validation (30%), with additional bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) of the combined model.ResultsComposite adverse neonatal outcomes occurred in 469 pregnancies (38.2%). Lower PAPP-A MoM was independently associated with composite outcome (adjusted OR 0.274, 95% CI 0.188-0.399; p < 0.001), particularly low birth weight and NICU admission. In an exploratory model incorporating HDP and SGA, the PAPP-A point estimate reversed direction and became statistically nonsignificant (adjusted OR 1.510, 95% CI 0.942-2.420; p = 0.087), warranting cautious interpretation because of potential downstream adjustment bias. Discrimination for the composite adverse neonatal outcome was limited for PAPP-A alone (AUC 0.620, 95% CI 0.563-0.673) and the combined model (AUC 0.610, 95% CI 0.553-0.665), with no significant improvement following combination (paired DeLong p = 0.315). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected development-sample AUC of 0.642, whereas the held-out validation AUC was 0.610. Decision-curve findings were exploratory and did not establish clinical benefit. Neither model demonstrated sufficient discrimination for individual-level risk stratification.ConclusionAlthough lower PAPP-A was independently associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, neither PAPP-A alone nor the combined model provided reliable individual-level prediction. Further development and external validation of integrated models are warranted.

articles.title: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes Up to 5 Years of Age in Very Preterm Infants: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The advances in neonatal care have led to a substantial increase in the survival rate of premature infants and, consequently, to a progressive attention to morbidity and neurodevelopmental outcomes in this population. The aim of this study was to evaluate very preterm children's neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 and 5 years of age, to examine the stability of developmental performance, and to identify neurodevelopment determinants at age 5.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 85 very preterm infants (gestational age < 30 weeks or very low birth weight) born and followed at a Portuguese tertiary neonatal center. Neurodevelopment was assessed at ages 2 and 5 using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales (GMDS). Neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI) was classified as the combined outcome of GQ < 70, cerebral palsy, severe visual impairment or severe hearing impairment. The stability of GMDS quotients was assessed using Pearson correlation coefficients.
RESULTS: At age 2, 18.5% of children had developmental delay (GQ < 85) and 11.1% met criteria for NDI. By age 5, both rates decreased to 9.1%. Developmental quotients demonstrated strong longitudinal stability (r 0.67 - 0.92, all p < 0.001). While locomotor scores improved, ophthalmological abnormalities and the need for speech therapy were more frequent at preschool age. School assistance was required in 23.6%, and 48% needed at least one form of therapy by age 5. Griffiths Mental Development Scales scores at age 2, duration of oxygen therapy, and length of hospital stay were identified as predictors of neurodevelopment at age 5. Severe intraventricular hemorrhage (aOR = 18.0; CI 95%: 1.7 - 190.6) and prolonged hospitalization (aOR = 1.06; CI 95%: 1.01 - 1.11) were independent predictors of NDI.
CONCLUSIONS: Early developmental assessment provides valuable prognostic information in very preterm children. Nevertheless, follow-up assessments beyond age 2 remain important for accurately identifying developmental needs.

articles.title: Evaluation of Working Memory Ability and Listening Effort in Individuals with and without Misophonia: Comparative Investigation without Trigger Exposure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Misophonia is characterized by a negative reaction to triggering stimuli. Although it can be hypothesized that attentional shifts toward triggering stimuli can influence cognitive performance in individuals with misophonia, the present study focused on evaluating the baseline working memory ability and listening effort of individuals with typical hearing with and without misophonia in the absence of such triggers.
RESEARCH DESIGN: Data were collected using a standard group comparison design and nonprobability purposive sampling method.
STUDY SAMPLE: The current study comprised 30 participants 18-30 years of age who were divided into two groups of 15 each.
DATA COLLECTION: Working memory was assessed using the forward digit span, backward digit span, ascending digit span, and descending digit span. Listening effort was measured using the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Task Load Index (TLX) after completion of each task. These tests were conducted in the absence of triggers.
RESULTS: It was found that the working memory ability measured using digit span tests was comparable (p > 0.05) between groups with and without misophonia. No statistically significant difference (p > 0.05) in NASA TLX scores was observed between these groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with and without misophonia have comparable working memory ability and listening effort while performing simple working memory tasks, which could be attributed to the noncontinuous nature of misophonia. To generalize these findings, further research of a wider population is required.

articles.title: Leisure Noise Effects on Tinnitus Occurrence in Adolescents and Young Adults: Influence of Exposure Duration and Exposure Environment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reports of tinnitus in adolescents have revealed effects of noise exposure and secondhand smoke (SHS), but information is limited about the intersection of risk factors for auditory health and quantification of noise exposure among young adults.
PURPOSE: This study examined effects of leisure noise exposure duration, noise environment, and SHS exposure duration on tinnitus presence, tinnitus manifestation, and tinnitus duration in adolescents and young adults. A secondary purpose was related to tinnitus examination through a total leisure noise (TLN) quantification that facilitated exploring possible U.S. guidelines for hazardous leisure noise levels.
DESIGN: This nonexperimental, cross-sectional design with a convenience sample examined retrospective survey data.
SAMPLE: Participants (n = 261; 70 percent female) were nonsmokers including adolescents (n = 102; mean age = 15.7 years) and college students (n = 159; mean age = 19.7 years).
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Survey responses to 11 questions were collated for statistical analysis, including logistic regression and an exploratory TLN mathematical calculation.
RESULTS: Tinnitus presence was 41 percent overall; 72 percent reported occasional tinnitus manifestation and 89.7 percent had intermittent tinnitus duration. Reported noise exposure was 44 percent and SHS exposure was 94.6 percent, overall. Multinomial regression analyses for tinnitus manifestation revealed that occasional/daily tinnitus was 1.96 times more likely in females than in males (a sex effect), and it was 3.46 times less likely in individuals who reported noise exposure in bars/clubs than in those who did not report such noise exposure. Binary regression analyses for tinnitus presence revealed a spurious finding and no significant results for tinnitus duration and SHS exposure. Secondary TLN and TLN hazard cutoff analyses for tinnitus presence, tinnitus manifestation, and tinnitus duration were not significant.
CONCLUSIONS: In this sample of adolescents and young adults, leisure noise exposure was more influential for reported tinnitus than secondhand smoke exposure. Females were almost twice as likely as males to experience occasional tinnitus, and noise exposure in bars/clubs was less likely to yield occasional tinnitus. TLN analyses provided first reports of statistical trends in U.S. adolescents that may guide future studies addressing leisure noise limits.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Case history for adolescents and young adults should prioritize identifying any leisure noise exposure and its source(s) and duration. Assessment in this population should evaluate tinnitus occurrence and duration, and females reporting ear noises without external stimuli should receive dedicated care given their higher risk for occasional tinnitus.

articles.title: Chirp-Evoked Auditory Brainstem Responses and Extended High-Frequency Hearing: Preliminary Observations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extended high-frequency (EHF; 9-20 kHz) hearing loss can emerge despite audiometric thresholds within normal limits (i.e., ≤20 dB HL for 0.25-8 kHz) and may signal early auditory decline. Auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) are candidate objective markers, but standard broadband click ABRs may be insensitive to subtle, frequency-specific neural changes.
PURPOSE: We tested whether a 4-kHz centered chirp-evoked ABR differentiates young adults by EHF sensitivity better than traditional click-evoked ABR.
RESEARCH DESIGN: This was a cross-sectional, between-groups comparison of ABR metrics (Wave I, Wave V, and Wave I/V amplitude ratio) elicited by clicks versus a 4-kHz narrowband chirp.
STUDY SAMPLE: The study included 30 young adults (27 females, 3 males; 18-28 years of age; mean age = 20.06 years, standard deviation = 2.16). Participants were grouped by EHF pure-tone average (10, 12.5, 16, and 20 kHz): Better EHF (≤0 dB HL; n = 18) and Worse EHF (>0 dB HL; n = 12). Standard audiometric thresholds (0.25-8 kHz) were within normal limits in both groups; groups differed at 10-20 kHz.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Right-ear stimulation was achieved via insert earphones with the following characteristics: click: 100-µs pulse (10 Hz-10 kHz); chirp: 2,000 µs upward iChirp centered at 4 kHz (-6 dB ≈ 3.97-5.03 kHz); 1,600 alternating-polarity sweeps/stimulus at 70 dB nHL; 11.1/s; Cz-to-mastoid montage; 100- to 3000-Hz bandpass. Two blinded raters marked Wave I (1-2 ms) and Wave V (5-7 ms); amplitudes were quantified peak-to-trough. Group comparisons used Welch's t tests with within-family Bonferroni correction.
RESULTS: Click-evoked ABRs did not differ between groups (Wave I: Better = 0.191 µV, Worse = 0.196 µV, p = 0.894; Wave V: Better = 0.369 µV, Worse = 0.400 µV, p = 0.479; I/V ratio: p = 0.847). Chirp-evoked ABRs showed (1) a trend toward smaller Wave I in the Worse EHF group (Better = 0.386 µV, Worse = 0.307 µV, p = 0.150); (2) significantly larger Wave V in the Worse group (Better = 0.319 µV, Worse = 0.425 µV, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.033); and (3) a significantly lower Wave I/V ratio in the Worse group (Better = 1.40, Worse = 0.751; Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.0214).
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary sample, 4-kHz chirp-evoked ABRs, but not clicks, differentiated young adults by EHF sensitivity, suggesting high-frequency-specific ABR paradigms can reveal subtle neural differences associated with EHF loss.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: Chirp-based ABR measures that target ∼4 kHz may complement EHF audiometry by capturing subtle neural differences before overt perceptual deficits emerge. Such objective markers could help clinicians identify at-risk listeners earlier and refine monitoring protocols in noise-exposed or otherwise vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Nutritional and metabolic profile of children with type 1 and 2 spinal muscular atrophy managed at a referral center.
articles.abstract: Introduction. Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a degenerative genetic disorder that primarily affects motor neurons. Disease-modifying therapies have altered the disease's natural course and led to new clinical phenotypes. Recent evidence suggests a systemic impact, including metabolic abnormalities. Objective. To describe the anthropometric, nutritional, and metabolic profiles of children with SMA types 1 and 2 treated at a referral center. Population and methods. We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study at a tertiary care hospital between 2020 and 2023. We analyzed anthropometric measurements, lipid profile, glucose profile, and nutritional status in 17 children under 12 years of age with type 1 and 2 SMA during their first visit. Results. A high prevalence of overweight, as well as abnormalities in lipid and glucose metabolism-including insulin resistance-was observed in a significant proportion of patients. An exploratory comparison between type 1 and type 2 SMA revealed a heterogeneous profile: some parameters, such as low HDL and high BMI, were more common in type 1 SMA, while elevated insulin levels were more common in type 2 SMA. These findings do not allow for definitive conclusions regarding differences between subtypes. The only patient treated during the presymptomatic stage had a nutritional and metabolic profile within expected parameters. Conclusion. This study highlights the need for a multidisciplinary approach that includes nutritional and metabolic assessment in the follow-up of patients with SMA, tailored to their new phenotypes and increased life expectancy.

articles.title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia Diagnosed in Adolescence Complicated by Invasive Aspergillosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is a primary humoral immunodeficiency that is typically recognized in early childhood. We report a 16-year-old male with recurrent respiratory tract infections (RTIs) since childhood who presented with severe pulmonary infection and focal neurological deficits. Immunologic evaluation showed profound hypogammaglobulinemia, with serum IgG of 0.24 g/L and both IgA and IgM < 0.10 g/L, together with virtually absent peripheral CD19+ B cells (0.00%). Genetic testing identified a hemizygous Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) c.1039G > C (p.Ala347Pro) variant. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) detected the Aspergillus flavus/oryzae complex. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) galactomannan (GM) tests were positive, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions. Taken together, these findings supported invasive pulmonary aspergillosis with possible central nervous system (CNS) Aspergillus involvement. This case illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of XLA, including delayed recognition until adolescence, and underscores the importance of integrating immunologic, microbiological, mycological, imaging, and longitudinal clinical evidence when interpreting multiple pathogen-detection results in complex infections.

articles.title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and management in nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Asthma is one of the most common chronic respiratory conditions in the UK, affecting both children and adults. It is characterised by airway inflammation, variable symptoms, and reversible airflow limitation. This article provides a nursing-focused overview of asthma, exploring the definition, altered pathophysiology, diagnosis, and both pharmacological and non-pharmacological management. It highlights the importance of accurate assessment, early differentiation from other respiratory conditions, and the use of structured diagnostic tools within national guidance. Education, adherence support, and awareness of excessive reliever use are identified as key nursing priorities. By following national and local guidelines, promoting the use of combination and anti-inflammatory therapies, and providing holistic, person-centred education, nurses can improve symptom control, reduce preventable hospital admissions, and enhance quality of life for individuals and families living with asthma.

articles.title: Functional Somatic Symptoms in Paediatric Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Aberrant stress-system activation or dysregulation affects the cardiovascular system through various pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, neuro-endocrine system, and a range of neurophysiological intermediaries. In children with congenital heart disease-who have high rates of adverse childhood experiences, comorbid medical conditions, and neurodevelopmental issues-this activation/dysregulation commonly results in functional cardiac symptoms such as orthostatic intolerance, (functional) chest pain, and syncope-like presentations. Despite the obvious need, research into stress-system responses in children with congenital heart disease is limited. This article reviews commonly encountered clinical scenarios with the goal of encouraging practitioners to recognise the interconnections between structural cardiac lesions in children, stress-system activation/dysregulation, and functional somatic symptoms. Children with congenital heart disease and comorbid functional symptoms require comprehensive management strategies. We propose a framework to help clinicians facilitate appropriate treatment.

articles.title: All About the Meds: Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-aged Female Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract: The number of reproductive-aged solid organ transplant recipients continues to rise, underscoring the need for comprehensive reproductive health counseling that spans throughout the transplant continuum. Fertility is often impaired in end-stage organ disease but often resumes within months after transplantation, which may cause unintended pregnancy during a period of heightened maternal, fetal, and allograft vulnerability. This review synthesizes the evidence and expert consensus from the American Society of Transplantation Women's Health Community of Practice Controversies Conference on contraception, infertility, and immunosuppression in reproductive-aged female transplant recipients. Recommendations are largely US-based, although reference to international variability is noted, where relevant. We outline contraceptive options with attention to efficacy and safety in transplant recipients. Data on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies in solid organ transplant recipients remain limited, although emerging evidence supports the feasibility and safety of ovulation induction, in vitro fertilization, and single-embryo transfer with careful monitoring for complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Immunosuppressive regimens require individualized adjustment before, during, and after pregnancy: calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids, and azathioprine are generally considered safe, whereas mycophenolate is strictly contraindicated due to teratogenicity; the safety of mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors and belatacept remains incompletely defined. Lactation is supported with most immunosuppressants, although caution is warranted with mycophenolate and mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors. Ultimately, preconception counseling, shared decision-making, and coordination amongst transplant, maternal-fetal medicine, and reproductive endocrinology specialists are essential to optimize outcomes for recipients, grafts, and infants. Closing persistent knowledge gaps and enhancing access to reproductive care should remain a research and policy priority in transplant medicine.

articles.title: Anti-HLA Alloantibody Responses in Living Donor Uterus Transplantation: A Single-center Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Until 1 decade ago, absolute uterine infertility invariably prevented women from bearing their own biological child. A major causative factor is Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. However, uterus transplantation (UTx) has recently emerged as a successful treatment strategy, with >70 children being born to UTx recipients. This clinical situation represents a unique immunological scenario-namely the combined sensitization risk from solid organ transplantation and exposure to paternal alloantigens of the fetus.
METHODS: Given the rarity of such cases, we assessed HLA sensitization in this context using a microbead-based assay (Luminex) with HLA screening as well as single-antigen beads in 7 UTx patients.
RESULTS: We observed broad, strong IgG alloimmune responses in 3 UTx recipients, directed against both donor and paternal alloantigens. These responses primarily emerged and amplified after graft hysterectomy and withdrawal of immunosuppression, while intermittently also being evidenced before hysterectomy in 1 case. This contrasts with 4 women with transplants remaining in situ and on immunosuppressive treatment, who lack sensitization signs so far.
CONCLUSIONS: These scarce preliminary data already suggest a relevant risk of broad sensitization in this unusual setting. UTx may therefore (1) represent a unique model for studying HLA sensitization under combined physiological and nonphysiological conditions, (2) warrant informing recipients about the risk of HLA alloimmunization, and (3) require further investigation to understand the implications and long-term consequences, demanding the generation of larger datasets.

articles.title: Very Early-Onset Schizophrenia in a 9-Year-Old With X-Linked Ichthyosis: Case Report.
articles.abstract: Very early-onset schizophrenia (VEOS) is a rare childhood psychiatric disorder with a poor prognosis that is characterized by varying degrees of positive and negative symptoms. The disorder is challenging to diagnose at a young age due to overlap with other developmental and behavioral disorders. Treatment and management are complicated by the rarity of VEOS and the poor prognosis seen in prior patients. This case follows BB, a 9-year-old boy who has VEOS with a multifactorial etiology from biological, psychological, and social influences. BB's case demonstrates the complexities of evaluation along the developmental trajectory as symptom presentation and environmental influences evolve over time. A unique point of interest is the co-occurrence of X-linked Ichthyosis, which has been documented in a prior case report of childhood schizophrenia and severe attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This piece contributes to the limited literature on VEOS, especially in the setting of other developmental issues such as comorbid medical illness and attachment disorders.

articles.title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
articles.abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

articles.title: Variants of mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a heterogeneous group of conditions in which neuroinflammation, systemic inflammation, and impaired mitochondrial energy function (mitochondrial dysfunction) serve as interconnected pathogenetic factors. Using organic acids profiling in urine it is possible to assess metabolic alterations related to glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, fatty acid β-oxidation, ketogenesis, branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) catabolism, and coenzyme Q10 metabolism. In this study we have analyzed 26 such metabolites in children with ASD and a control group of neurotypical children. The objective was to identify and characterize metabolic variants of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD children and to evaluate the impact of the microbiota to the urinary organic acid profile. This single-center, observational, cross-sectional study included 105 ASD children (aged 3-9 years) and 95 conditionally healthy, neurotypical children, matched for age and sex. Urinary organic acids were measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Children with ASD exhibited diverse, bidirectional alterations in metabolites associated with energy metabolism. In the overall clinical group, there were elevated levels of pyruvic, cis-aconitic, isocitric, fumaric, and sebacic acids, as well as several intermediates of BCAA catabolism, and decreased levels of 2-ketoglutaric and succinic acids. Cluster analysis resulted in the identification of two distinct metabolic variants. The first cluster included 58 children and was characterized by the hyperexcretion of most organic acids, a pronounced alteration in TCA cycle markers, elevated meglutol levels, and a higher density within the metabolic correlation network. The second cluster, comprising 47 children, showed a metabolic profile similar to that of the control group, with reduced excretion of several key metabolites - primarily those associated with the TCA cycle and coenzyme Q10 metabolism. The primary contributors to the separation between these clusters were cis-aconitic, isocitric, citric, 2-ketoglutaric, malic, and fumaric acids, as well as meglutol. Urinary organic acids profiling enabled the identification of two patterns of metabolic dysregulation: hyperexcretory and hypoexcretory. These patterns reflect varying states of mitochondrial dysfunction, ranging from compensatory to subcompensated or decompensated. Subsequent comparison of the identified patterns of metabolic dysregulation with the functional status of mitochondria requires longitudinal monitoring of clinical condition of patients and also the assessment of inflammatory markers, such as pro-inflammatory cytokines, quinolinic acid, and kynurenic acid.

articles.title: The myokine irisin: role in the regulation of adipose tissue homeostasis and potential in the treatment of obesity.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a global health issue that, in the modern world, affects children and adolescents as well. It is a chronic disease accompanied by metabolic disturbances such as insulin resistance and dyslipidemia. Obesity is characterized by low-grade chronic inflammation of adipose tissue, with the blood showing elevated levels of pro-inflammatory factors and reduced levels of anti-inflammatory factors - collectively known as adipokines - secreted by this tissue. Obesity contributes to the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus and increases the risk of atherosclerosis, hypertension, and other cardiovascular diseases. Skeletal muscles play a vital role in regulating systemic metabolism, partly through the secretion of biologically active factors called myokines. One such myokine, currently the subject of active research, is irisin, which is involved in the homeostasis of adipose tissue. Irisin is a peptide derived from the precursor protein FNDC5, produced primarily in striated muscle in response to physical exercise. Irisin participates in the regulation of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, influences metabolic processes in the liver and skeletal muscle, stimulates thermogenesis, and is capable of modulating the remodeling of the immuno-metabolic microenvironment within adipose tissue. Increasing blood irisin levels through the administration of exogenous irisin is currently being explored as a potential therapeutic approach for obesity and associated cardiometabolic disorders.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers.
RESULTS: 161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

articles.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR).
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR < 5th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI (< 5th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P < 0.01), neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR, 2.33 (95% CI, 1.24-4.37); P = 0.01) and composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01) compared with Group 1. Furthermore, Group 2 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (OR, 2.06 (95% CI, 1.12-3.79); P = 0.02) and birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models.
CONCLUSIONS: In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight < 3rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Association of single intrauterine fetal demise with severe brain injury and death in liveborn cotwins delivered before 32 weeks: large single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent association in twin pregnancy between single intrauterine fetal demise (sIUFD) and major short-term adverse outcomes, particularly severe brain injury (SBI) or death, in extremely and very preterm liveborn cotwins (delivered < 32 weeks), to examine whether this association extends beyond chorionicity and to identify critical gestational windows of vulnerability and potential mediating pathways.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included twin pregnancies, with or without sIUFD, delivered < 32 weeks at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, between January 2014 and December 2024, with neonates admitted immediately after birth to the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sIUFD and the primary outcome, a composite of SBI or death of the liveborn cotwin prior to hospital discharge. Subgroup analyses stratified by chorionicity and gestational age at sIUFD were performed to identify risk patterns and critical gestational windows of vulnerability. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore whether the association between sIUFD and SBI or death was mediated by early-onset sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth or the 5-min Apgar score, and sensitivity analyses incorporating propensity-score matching to balance baseline confounders were performed to assess the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: In total, 1069 twin pregnancies delivered < 32 weeks were included (113 with and 956 without sIUFD). sIUFD was independently associated with significantly increased odds of SBI or death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 2.85 (95% CI, 1.61-4.97)). This association was consistent across monochorionic and dichorionic subgroups. The highest point estimate was observed when sIUFD occurred at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks' gestation (aOR, 3.72 (95% CI, 1.64-8.06)). Mediation analysis identified a 5-min Apgar score < 7, suggestive of perinatal asphyxia, as the primary mediator of SBI or death (proportion mediated: 24.30%), while disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth and early-onset sepsis acted as significant secondary mediators (proportions mediated: 6.60% and 4.30%, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: sIUFD is independently associated with an increased risk of SBI or death in liveborn cotwins delivered < 32 weeks, regardless of chorionicity, particularly when demise occurs at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks. Perinatal asphyxia is the primary mediator of this association. These findings support intensified monitoring of all surviving cotwins, with surveillance guided by the gestational age at sIUFD. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.

articles.title: Lichen sclerosus amongst Prepubertal Nepalese Boys with Phimosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lichen sclerosus (Ls), a chronic lymphocyte-mediated scarring dermatosis of possibly autoimmune origin typically affects the foreskin and glans penis in boys. With an elusive etiology and multifactorial causation, it has an incidence that is globally variable. Nevertheless, a resultant genital discoloration and recurrent balanoposthitis can seriously impact urinary functions in boys in addition to the risks of malignancy. Early identification is imperative for successful control and prevention of complications.
OBJECTIVE: To study the profile of Nepalese boys with phimosis, determine the prevalence of Lichen sclerosus and assess the outcomes of treatment modalities.
METHOD: A prospective observational study was performed in boys who underwent treatment for phimosis between 1st September 2024 to 28th February 2026. Demographical profile, clinical findings, surgical details and outcomes were studied.
RESULT: A total of 200 boys were evaluated for symptomatic non-retractable foreskins at a mean age of 8 years (range: 4-16 years) and a mean symptom duration of 17 months. Of them, 139 were clinically diagnosed to have Physiological Phimosis (PhP) with most of them categorized as Kikiro's Grade I-II. They underwent Foreskin Adhesiolysis (FA) as a conservative treatment along with local application of ultra potent steroid cream for 2 months and foreskin hygiene maintenance thereafter. At the end of 3 months, they all had complete resolution of symptoms and no recurrence. The remaining 61 were diagnosed to have Pathological Phimosis (PaP) with most of them categorized as Kikiro's Grade III-IV and underwent Sleeve circumcision. Of them, 33 had histological evidence of lichen sclerosus while the rest 28 had non-specific chronic inflammation (non-Ls). The overall prevalence of lichen sclerosus was found to be 16.5% (33/200). Boys with lichen sclerosus were also treated with steroid cream as an adjuvant therapy for 2 months and followed up for a median period of 10 months while the rest (non-Ls) were followed up without adjuvant treatment. No serious complications were noted.
CONCLUSION: A vast majority of Nepalese boys (69.5%) with symptomatic phimosis were responsive to conservative measures with only a third needing operative management. Of these, lichen sclerosus was the underlying pathological cause in 16.5%.

articles.title: Dermoscopic Findings in Alopecia Areata: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition characterized by non-scarring hair loss affecting the scalp and other hair-bearing regions. Dermoscopy, a non-invasive diagnostic method, significantly improves the ability to confirm diagnosis, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and dermoscopic patterns of alopecia areata among patients attending a tertiary dermatology centre in Nepal.
METHOD: A descriptive cross-sectional study was carried out over one year at Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital's Dermatology Outpatient Department including 60 patients clinically diagnosed with alopecia areata. Scalp and affected areas were examined using a Heine Delta 20 contact dermoscope with 10-16× magnification. Demographic, clinical features, and dermoscopic findings were collected and analyzed.
RESULT: Sixty patients were evaluated. Male patients predominated (41/60), and the largest age group was 21-30 years (35/60). Disease duration was less than six months in 48/60 patients. Localized patchy alopecia was the predominant presentation (49/60), with the occipital scalp being the most frequently involved site (27/60). Dermoscopy most frequently demonstrated yellow dots (58/60), followed by short vellus hairs (42/60), black dots (37/60), broken hairs (35/60), exclamation mark hairs (32/60), and white regrowing hairs (14/60).
CONCLUSION: Dermoscopy is a rapid and non-invasive modality that demonstrates characteristic findings in alopecia areata. In this cohort, yellow dots, short vellus hairs, black dots, broken hairs, and exclamation mark hairs were frequently observed. Further analytical studies are required to determine their associations with disease duration and SALT severity. Dermoscopy also offers economic value by reducing the need for unnecessary laboratory investigations in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Hemoglobinopathies in Children with Anemia Presenting to Nepalgunj Medical College.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia refers to reduced number of red blood cells or haemoglobin level lower than the standard range for age and sex. It is a major global health issue and is an indicator of poor nutrition, health as well as the social and economic development of a population. Symptoms are lethargy, fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. Causes include iron deficiency, vitamin deficiencies, malaria, intestinal helminthes, viral infections, chronic diseases, hemoglobinopathies, hemolysis etc. Hemoglobinopathies are the most prevalent single-gene autosomal recessive disorders which involve disorders in globin chain synthesis, that may either be quantitative (thalassaemias) or qualitative (sickle cell). These disorders can be prevented by proper genetic counselling and screening.
OBJECTIVE: To find the prevalence and distribution of hemoglobinopathies among anemic children attending Nepalgunj Medical College.
METHOD: The cross-sectional study was carried out in the department of Pediatrics, on 86 children, aged 12 months - 15 years, in whom anemia was detected, either on examination or on investigation. Complete blood counts, peripheral blood smear, and Hb-electrophoresis were done.
RESULT: Among 86 children, majority were of age group 1 - 5 years (40.7%), making male : female ratio 1.2:1. The youngest child was of 12 months with average age 8.0 ± 4.8. Commonest morphology was microcytic hypochromic anemia (81.4%). Hemoglobinopathies was seen in 31.39% children, sickle cell disease being most common (16.3%), followed by Beta Thalassemia trait (4.7%), 73.3% children were from tharu family. There was no statistically significant association between ethnicity and hemoglobinopathies as well as sickle cell disease.
CONCLUSION: Hemoglobin disorders are also common causes of anemia in children. These were seen in various ethnic groups and were not limited to tharus with consanguineous marriages. Thus, hemoglobinopathies should also be thought-of in non-tharu people with microcytic hypochromic anemia. However, further studies on larger population are needed to determine significant relation between ethnicity and hemoglobinopathies.

articles.title: Clinico-demographic Profile and Associated Factors of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autism Spectrum Disorder is a neurodevelopmental disorder with symptoms manifesting in early childhood.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the clinical and sociodemographic profile of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and identify associated factors.
METHOD: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Children were recruited consecutively at the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Unit, Kanti Children's Hospital, Nepal. The study duration was from 1st August 2023 to 31st January 2024. The study was approved by Institutional Review Board of Kanti Children's Hospital. A semi-structured proforma and Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition were used to assess the children. Data were entered and analysed using IBM SPSS version 16.0.
RESULT: The sample included 145 children. Mean age of diagnosis was 44.1 months (SD ± 18.7). Majority of them were 119 (82.1%) male, 85 (58.6%) belonged to nuclear family, and 69 (47.5%) were single child. Male to female ratio was 4.5:1. The mean paternal and maternal ages at the time of conception were 32.1 years (SD ± 6.5) and 27.7 years (SD ± 5.2), respectively. Most common source of referral was doctors/ health workers 66 (45.5%), parents themselves 45 (31%) and relatives 15 (10.3%). The main reason for visit was speech delay 135 (93.1%) and poor socio emotional reciprocity 76 (52.4%). Mean childhood autism rating score was 34.9 (SD ± 4.3), with 108 (74.4%) having mild-to-moderate autism severity. Sibling status was significantly associated with autism severity (p= 0.042) as children without siblings were more likely to exhibit mild to moderate symptoms compared to those with one or more siblings.
CONCLUSION: The study shows higher rate of Autism Spectrum Disorder among males and diagnosis at an early age. Presence of a sibling may affect autism severity.

articles.title: Intensity-controlled Raster Scanning Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy With a Heavy-ion Gantry: Clinical Experience at Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center.
articles.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0.
RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes following balloon aortic valvuloplasty for congenital aortic stenosis in children: a 29-year single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Initial treatment of critical aortic stenosis in children, balloon or surgical aortic valvuloplasty, remains debated. Our centre used the balloon procedure first in almost all patients for over 29 years, a predominantly balloon-first cohort.
OBJECTIVE: To characterise long-term outcomes of balloon aortic valvuloplasty as first-line treatment for critical aortic stenosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 201 patients treated between June 1996 and December 2025, grouped as neonates (0-28 days), infants (29-365 days), and children (>365 days). Freedom from surgery and reintervention were analysed with the Kaplan-Meier method; categorical comparisons used chi-square tests.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 9 years. Aortic valve surgery was required in 78 patients (38.8%), most commonly a Ross or Ross-Konno procedure (49, 62.8%). Neonates required surgery more often than infants and children (36/74, 48.6% versus 42/127, 33.1%; p = 0.042); median time to surgery in neonates was 6 months. One-year Kaplan-Meier freedom from surgery was 63% in neonates, 91% in infants, and 96% in children. Moderate-to-severe post-procedural valve dysfunction was associated with more surgery than mild dysfunction (49.3% versus 33.3%; p = 0.041). Kaplan-Meier freedom from any reintervention was 47% at 10 years and 31% at 15 years. Mortality was 3.5% overall and 8.1% in neonates, mostly in the early era.
CONCLUSIONS: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty is an effective first-line treatment for infants and children with critical aortic stenosis. However, many neonates need surgery within the first year, usually a Ross procedure. In centres with experienced cardiac surgeons, surgical aortic valvuloplasty could be considered a reasonable alternative initial approach for neonates.
