articles.title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed.
AIM: To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability.
METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively.
RESULTS: Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain.
CONCLUSION: Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.
METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.
CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Fulminant Guillain-Barre Syndrome as the Cardinal Presenting Feature of New Onset Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Here we present a complex case of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting initially as fulminant Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS). This particular manifestation of neuropsychiatric lupus is uncommon but can be severe and even life threatening. Increasing providers' awareness of the overlap between lupus and GBS will improve diagnostic accuracy and timing as well as expedite appropriate therapies, which may differ from typical GBS treatment.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 12-year-old previously healthy Hispanic female presented with subacute onset vision changes and imbalance with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and hyporeflexia. Given her classic clinical triad and suspicion for GBS variant Miller Fischer syndrome (MFS), neuroaxis imaging was obtained. MRI showed cranial nerve and ventral nerve root enhancement, and cytoalbuminologic dissociation seen on cerebrospinal fluid analysis also supported this diagnosis. Weakness including the facial and bulbar muscles and the extremities progressed rapidly and threatened respiratory functions, so the patient was intubated. Typical treatments for GBS including intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and plasma exchange (PLEX) were insufficient to manage symptoms, and additional evaluations supported a diagnosis of SLE with nephritis. Coordinated care between neuroimmunology and rheumatology enabled rapid escalation of therapy to include high-dose intravenous steroid pulses, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab. Together, these therapies eventually stabilized the patient, and with support from neuropsychology, psychiatry, and rehabilitation medicine, she was able to discharge from the hospital after 115 days of admission. She has remained in remission on maintenance immunosuppression including mycophenolate mofetil as well as hydroxychloroquine.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuropsychiatric lupus can be difficult to diagnose and manage, but its severity necessitates vigilance and aggressive management. In the current case, the isolated neurological symptoms at presentation consistent with GBS could have delayed diagnosis, but neuroimmunology and rheumatology were consulted early, and appropriate diagnostic testing was performed. The patient's multidisciplinary team worked closely together to appropriately escalate her treatment beyond what is typical for GBS, ultimately leading to remission of her neuropsychiatric symptoms and recovery of her baseline neurological status. This case highlights the complex nature of neuropsychiatric lupus, suggests that SLE should be on the differential in atypical or difficult-to-treat cases of GBS, and underscores the need for coordinated interdisciplinary care to achieve best outcomes for these patients.

articles.title: Exploring the COSA-t and Other Occupation-Based Assessments in Pediatric Occupational Therapy for Tic Disorders.
articles.abstract: ImportanceThere is a paucity of research describing the occupational therapy assessment process for children with tic disorders (TD) and the priority areas of occupational performance that should be considered during assessment.ObjectiveThis study aimed to (1) explore the content validity of the COSA-t items, as indicated by clinical importance and (2) understand how occupational therapists use the COSA-t and other occupation-based assessments to inform their Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT) practice.DesignCross-sectional, qualitative study.SettingVirtual focus groups (Zoom) and asynchronous surveys.ParticipantsOccupational therapists were recruited through closed, professional networks. All participants were CBIT trained, had experience providing occupational therapy to at least one child with TD, and had training or experience administering the COSA-t or other occupation-based assessments with children with TD.Outcomes and MeasuresParticipants rated the clinical importance of each COSA-t item using a 0 to 10 visual analog scale. Five virtual focus groups explored participants' use of occupation-based assessments with children with TD.ResultsNineteen occupational therapists completed the survey of clinical importance and 18 participated in focus groups (17 female, 1 male, 2-20 years of experience). COSA-t importance ratings ranged from 5.95 to 8.95. Occupation-based assessments were a starting point, revealed the daily impact of tics, provided clinical discernment, and fostered motivation and insight.Conclusions and RelevanceThe occupational therapists found value in administering occupation-based assessments, such as the COSA-t. Therefore, there is a pressing need for further evidence to support the incorporation of self-reported, occupation-based assessments into interventions with children with TD.

articles.title: Development of the Children's Occupational Justice Scale Across Metropolitan and Non-Metropolitan Contexts.
articles.abstract: ImportanceOccupational justice is a core concept in occupational therapy; however, no standardized self-report measure exists for school-aged children, limiting the identification of occupational inequities and evaluation of participation-focused interventions.ObjectiveTo develop and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Children's Occupational Justice Scale (COJS) and examine its ability to distinguish between children from metropolitan and non-metropolitan contexts.DesignCross-sectional scale development and psychometric validation study.SettingSchools located in metropolitan and non-metropolitan regions of Türkiye.ParticipantsA total of 873 children ages 11 to 14 years participated. Independent samples were used for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 428) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 445). Test-retest reliability was assessed in 94 participants.Outcomes and MeasuresThe preliminary COJS was developed through literature review, expert evaluation, and pilot testing. Construct validity, reliability, and known-groups validity were examined.ResultsEFA supported a 23-item, four-factor structure explaining 68.47% of the variance. CFA demonstrated good model fit (Comparative Fit Index = .957, Tucker-Lewis Index = .949, Goodness-of-Fit Index = .918, Root Mean Square Error of Approximation = .054, Standardized Root Mean Square Residual = .047). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach's α = .94; McDonald's ω = .95), and test-retest reliability was strong (intraclass correlation coefficient = .91, 95% confidence interval [.87, .94]). Children in metropolitan regions reported significantly higher occupational justice scores than children in non-metropolitan regions (p < .001).Conclusions and RelevanceThe COJS demonstrated strong validity and reliability for assessing occupational justice among school-aged children. The scale may provide occupational therapy practitioners and researchers with a novel tool for identifying occupational inequities and evaluating children's perceptions of participation opportunities, inclusion, choice, and environmental support.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Drive-Fun Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial to Reduce Driving Risks Among Adolescents With ADHD.
articles.abstract: ImportanceAdolescents with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are more likely to be involved in motor vehicle accidents, highlighting the need for early intervention. However, there is a lack of evidence-based interventions addressing driving safety in this population.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of the Drive-Fun cognitive-functional intervention on simulated driving performance, attentional control, and visual scanning in adolescents with ADHD.DesignRandomized controlled trial with three parallel groups: Drive-Fun, an educational intervention, and a control group.SettingA university research laboratory.ParticipantsNinety-three adolescents (M age = 16.8 years, SD = 0.52) diagnosed with ADHD.Outcomes and MeasuresPrimary outcomes were simulated driving errors; secondary outcomes included the percentage of time spent within the optimal Cognitive Effort Index (CEI) range and eye-tracking metrics.ResultsThe Drive-Fun group demonstrated significant time-by-group interactions: reduced driving errors, F(2, 89) = 82.65, p < .001; increased percentage of time spent within the optimal CEI range, F(2, 89) = 15.56, p < .001; fewer dashboard fixations, F(2, 89) = 27.65, p < .001; and more fixations on traffic lights, F(2, 89) = 7.61, p = .001, and pedestrians, F(2, 89) = 10.15, p < .001. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated greater improvements in driving performance among adolescents with lower Conners Hyperactive Scores and no regular sports participation within the Drive-Fun group.Conclusions and RelevanceThe Drive-Fun intervention improved simulated driving performance, cognitive engagement, and visual scanning, indicating its potential to reduce driving-related risks among adolescents with ADHD. Improvements were maintained at follow up, indicating sustained benefits. These findings support integrating cognitive-functional strategies and simulation-based training into occupational therapy to enhance adolescents' driving readiness and safety.

articles.title: Training Community Health Workers in Administering the ASQ-3 for Infants at Risk for Developmental Delay.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The primary aim was to determine the performance of Community Health Workers (CHWs) in administering the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ-3) to identify infants with DD. The second aim was to determine the predictive validity of the CHW-administered ASQ-3.
METHODS: The performance of 12 CHWs was determined via a posttraining evaluation and interrater reliability. Predictive validity of the 6- and 12-month ASQ-3 with the Bayley-4 was assessed.
RESULTS: CHWs' posttraining scores, intraclass correlation coefficients, and percent agreement determined the performance of the CHWs. Intraclass correlation coefficient values ranged from moderate to excellent, with additional training for the 12-month ASQ-3. The measure demonstrated high negative predictive values.
CONCLUSION: CHWs demonstrated excellent reliability using the 6-month ASQ-3 assessment. This suggests a viable approach for screening in lower middle-income countries. The predictive validity of the CHW-administered ASQ-3 against the Bayley-4 was limited, necessitating further investigation.

articles.title: Two-Wheel Cycling Interventions for Children With Disabilities: A Practice Survey in the United States.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Describe current practices and influential factors of 2-wheel cycling interventions for children with disabilities in the United States (US).
METHODS: An electronic survey was developed, validated, and distributed to individuals in the US who teach 2-wheel cycling. Closed-ended responses of participant demographics, interventions, and influential factors were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Open-ended responses of influential factors were analyzed inductively to identify common themes.
RESULTS: Fifty-two participants completed the survey, a 34% response rate, primarily physical (28, 54%) and occupational therapists (13, 25%) from across the US. Respondents taught mostly novice riders with a variety of health conditions. Interventions commonly involved one instructor per rider (40, 77%) using whole-task practice (48, 92%) and standard 2-wheel bicycles (51, 98%). Influential factors included rider's and family's motivation, individualized teaching, access to proper equipment, and safe practice environments.
CONCLUSIONS: Current practices appear variable. Findings highlight the importance of family involvement, individualized teaching, and proper equipment in safe environments (Supplemental Digital Content 1, Video Abstract, available at: https://youtu.be/FLT62XIME2M).

articles.title: Paediatric respiratory syncytial virus healthcare associated infection (RSV-HAI) surveillance: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infection in young children and an important healthcare-associated infection (HAI) in paediatric settings. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology and clinical impact of RSV-HAI and assess the potential feasibility of prospective surveillance.
METHODS: Single-centre surveillance study using retrospective and prospective weekly case ascertainment over four years (2018-2020, and 2024). RSV positive children with symptom onset greater than 72 h post presentation were eligible and followed for two weeks. Surveillance by a specialist IPC nurse was supported through a digital report in the electronic medical record system. Data were reported on RSV-HAI per 1000 occupied bed days, child characteristics, and clinical outcomes. Surveillance feasibility indicators included surveillance workload and screening yield.
RESULTS: A total of 79 children with RSV-HAI were identified with an overall rate of 0.22 cases per 1000 occupied bed days. The median age of children was 2.1 years (interquartile range 0.4-6.8) and most had a medical comorbidity (65/76, 85.5%). One third of children received antibiotics to treat acute lower respiratory infection (26/79, 32.9%) and 11.4% (9/79) were new admissions to the intensive care unit. The overall screening yield was 42.9% (79/184 screened records), and surveillance screening was completed within 15 min in most surveillance weeks (175/199 weeks, 87.9%).
CONCLUSION: RSV is an important and potentially preventable HAI which is highly relevant to paediatric hospital care. This pilot study demonstrates a potentially feasible surveillance approach which could support IPC program implementation.

articles.title: Acute Hemolysis Due to Metformin in a Young Adult Treated for T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) are at risk for hyperglycemia due to asparaginase, glucocorticoids, and possible underlying predisposition for glucose intolerance. The use of metformin in pediatric oncology patients is not yet widespread; however, it may be used to control blood glucose levels.
OBSERVATION: We report a young adult with T-cell ALL in maintenance chemotherapy who developed hemolysis 2 weeks after starting metformin, with resolution upon cessation of metformin.
CONCLUSIONS: We present this case to increase awareness of metformin-related hemolysis, review the literature, and discuss possible mechanisms for this adverse event.

articles.title: Early Initiation of Emicizumab Prophylaxis in Infants With Severe Hemophilia A, a Real-World Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is common in infants with hemophilia. We evaluated 15 children with severe hemophilia A who were initiated on emicizumab prophylaxis in infancy at the Pediatric Coagulation Center in Dublin, Ireland.
OBSERVATIONS: The median age at emicizumab initiation was 13 weeks (range, 1 to 38  wk), and in 9 children diagnosed in the first week of life, it was 5 weeks (range, 1 to 16 wk). After a median follow-up of 36.3 months (15.6 to 55.75), no child developed ICH or spontaneous bleeding.
CONCLUSIONS: Emicizumab prophylaxis in early infancy is safe and effective in the prevention of ICH and spontaneous bleeding in children with severe hemophilia A.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Bloodstream Infections and Impact of Antibiotic Prophylaxis: A 10-Year Experience at a Tertiary Care Pediatric Oncology-Hematology Center in Italy.
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in pediatric oncology-hematology patients. The local epidemiological landscape varies across centers, requiring continuous institutional surveillance. BSI episodes at a tertiary pediatric oncology-hematology center (Bari, Italy) were retrospectively reviewed over 10 years (2014 to 2024), analyzing microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial susceptibility, and the impact of 2 prophylactic policies: amoxicillin-clavulanate prophylaxis (2014 to 2019) versus its discontinuation (2019 to 2024). Among 568 newly diagnosed patients, 208 BSIs were documented in 144 (25.4%), with 93.8% monomicrobial. Gram-positive organisms predominated (61.6%), with coagulase-negative staphylococci as the most frequent isolates. Escherichia coli was the leading Gram-negative pathogen (9.5%). Eight fungal BSIs occurred exclusively in hematologic malignancies, half caused by Candida parapsilosis; 2 were polymicrobial. Peak C-reactive protein independently predicted Gram-negative BSI in multivariable analysis (OR: 1.005; 95% CI: 1.001-1.010; P<0.05), with limited discriminatory performance (AUC: 0.62). Blood culture positivity was significantly higher during prophylaxis (5.75% vs. 3.65%; P<0.001). Multidrug-resistant organisms remained rare (3.8%), with no methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus or vancomycin-resistant enterococci detected. BSI-related mortality was 1.4%, confined to Gram-negative and fungal episodes. Prophylaxis discontinuation was associated with lower positivity rates. An empirical escalation strategy ensured adequate coverage while minimizing antibiotic exposure, supporting its use in this setting.

articles.title: Acute Mastoiditis in Children in the Era of Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines.
articles.abstract: This retrospective study assessed changes in acute mastoiditis (AM) incidence, bacteriology, and complications after pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV)-7 and PCV-13 introduction at Children's Hospital of Michigan, Detroit, from 2000 to 2018. In this review of 242 children with AM, 138 cases occurred during PCV-7 use (2000-2010) and 104 during PCV-13 use (2011-2018). Incidence did not change after PCV-13 introduction (P = .31). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the predominant pathogen in both periods (P = .375), while Streptococcus pyogenes infections increased during PCV-13 era, affecting older children (median age, 87.5 vs 30.0 months for S pneumoniae). Complications occurred throughout including subperiosteal abscess (n = 39), venous sinus thrombosis (n = 10), and intracranial extension (n = 7). Partial or complete PCV vaccination was documented in 13 with S pneumoniae AM. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine-13 use was not associated with a reduction in occurrence of AM compared with PCV-7. Research is needed to evaluate the effect of pneumococcal vaccines on AM incidence and complications.

articles.title: Reversible Xerophthalmia in an Autistic Child With Selective Eating.
articles.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) is a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness. Increasingly, severe nutritional deficiencies are recognized in urban settings among children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) due to extreme dietary selectivity. A 9-year-old girl with ASD and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder presented with a 2-month history of bilateral ocular redness and photophobia refractory to topical therapies. Examination revealed a Bitot's spot, conjunctival keratinization and a corneal epithelial defect in the right eye and left inferior conjunctival xerosis. Diagnosed with xerophthalmia secondary to VAD, she also had multiple micronutrient deficiencies and nutritional rickets. Management included intravenous vitamins A and D, oral multivitamins, and electrolyte correction. Within 1 month, ocular changes fully resolved, leaving a superficial right corneal scar. Chronic, treatment-resistant ocular symptoms in children with ASD should prompt suspicion of VAD. Early multidisciplinary intervention and prompt supplementation are vital to prevent permanent blindness.

articles.title: Bronchiectasis and Chronic Bronchitis after a Delayed Diagnosis of Childhood-onset XLA with a Novel BTK Frameshift Variant: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is usually diagnosed in childhood, and a delayed diagnosis may allow irreversible lung damage. A 27-year-old man had recurrent respiratory infections since childhood and suspected inborn error of immunity, but was never genetically confirmed or treated. He presented with chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, profound hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent peripheral B cells. A novel hemizygous BTK frameshift variant, c.90del, was identified, and BTK deficiency was confirmed. After immunoglobulin replacement, follow-up CT showed resolution of pneumonia, but persistent bronchiectasis, indicating irreversible airway damage. Internists should consider XLA in such adults to enable a timely diagnosis and treatment to prevent lung damage.

articles.title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Coronary Artery Involvement in Kawasaki Disease: Experience From Southern Tunisia.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis associated with coronary complications. We aimed to describe clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and factors associated with coronary involvement. This retrospective, single-centre study included 70 children over 18 years (2007-2024). Univariate analyses assessed clinical and laboratory associations. The mean age was 55.4 ± 32.8 months; 61.7% were younger than 5 years. Coronary involvement occurred in 32/70 (45.7%), including dilation in 25 (35.7%), wall thickening in 7 (10.0%) and aneurysms in 3 (4.3%). Lesions regressed in 27/32 (84.4%). Significant associations included cheilitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, cough, rhinorrhoea, leucocytosis, lymphocytosis, lower mean corpuscular volume, higher mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration, thrombocytosis and elevated alanine aminotransferase. These unadjusted associations do not establish independent predictors. Early diagnosis, intravenous immunoglobulin and aspirin remain essential. Systematic echocardiographic assessment, structured follow-up and larger multicentre studies are needed to improve coronary risk stratification and long-term outcomes in children with KD.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Early Clinical Prediction Model for Post-Encephalitic Epilepsy in Children With Viral Encephalitis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Post-encephalitic epilepsy (PEE) is a serious long-term sequela of pediatric viral encephalitis, yet early risk stratification tools are lacking. In this single-center retrospective cohort study of 206 children with viral encephalitis, 43 (20.87%) developed PEE during follow-up. A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating 4 early clinical predictors-acute seizure count, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) white blood cell count, consciousness disturbance, and cortical involvement-demonstrated good discrimination and acceptable calibration. Decision curve analysis showed higher net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.06 to 0.99. Sensitivity analyses, including false-discovery rate correction, adjustment for follow-up duration, pathogen-stratified analyses, and a time-to-event (Cox) model, did not materially alter the principal findings. This model, built from routinely available variables, showed promise for early identification of children at elevated risk for PEE in internal validation. External validation in independent multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics of Pneumococcal Pneumonia in Children: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Given the decline in pneumococcal infections related to widespread childhood vaccinations in the United States, we evaluate the rate of Streptococcus pneumoniae and also report the demographic and radiographic characteristics of children with pneumococcal pneumonia in the post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era. We studied the prevalence of medical comorbidities, clinical presentations and outcomes, antibiotic susceptibility results, and radiographic findings among children aged less than 18 years presenting to a pediatric Emergency Department between 2010 and 2023 with a diagnosis of pneumonia and detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae in blood and/or pleural fluid. Of the 31 cases of pneumococcal pneumonia, over 50% occurred among children less than 5 years of age, and 71% of children had medical comorbidities. Eighty percent of children had radiographic pneumonia; the most common radiographic findings included opacities (71.0%), consolidation (29.0%), and pleural effusion (25.8%). Given high rates of antibiotic overtreatment, these findings may help clinicians to judiciously use antibiotics for children with pneumonia.

articles.title: Treatment of vitiligo with narrowband ultraviolet B phototherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitiligo is an acquired immune depigmenting disorder. Narrowband 311 nm ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is an important component of the standard treatment. Many questions arise about its safe use. The aim of the study was to clarify the use of NB-UVB in the management of vitiligo.
METHODS: A comprehensive review was coordinated by the French Society of Photodermatology, French vitiligo experts and the Centre of Evidence of the French Society of Dermatology to ascertain the efficacy and safety of NB-UVB used for vitiligo to draw up consensus guidelines.
RESULTS: The consulted experts defined NB-UVB phototherapy as a cornerstone treatment of vitiligo. They ensure its safety by establishing a dose protocol regarding treatment duration and subsequent monitoring. Given that most studies show that NB-UVB is not associated with an increased incidence of skin cancers, there is no ceiling on the maximum number of sessions allowed in adults with dark Fitzpatrick skin phototypes. In children and fair-skinned patients, additional data on the maximum number of sessions are needed before a recommendation can be made, even if the risk of cutaneous malignancy seems reduced in the population with vitiligo. For increased efficacy, NB-UVB combined with topical agents (calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids and ruxolitinib) and oral corticosteroids should be considered in localized vitiligo and active disease, respectively. A combination of NB-UVB with oral Janus kinase inhibitors seems promising.
CONCLUSION: There are now guidelines available to French dermatologists and practitioners for treating vitiligo with NB-UVB phototherapy.

articles.title: On the value of extending propranolol treatment for more than 6 months for infantile hemangioma: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infantile hemangiomas (IH) occur in approximately 4.5% of children, of whom 10% require treatment. The French and European guidelines recommend propranolol treatment for a minimum of 6 months; however, observational studies indicate that treatment is often extended beyond this duration in clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the clinical relevance of continuing propranolol beyond 6 months.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at Nancy Hospital, including infants treated with propranolol for ≥6 months between 2014 and April 2025. Patients were divided into a 6-month treatment group (6M group) and a prolonged treatment group (PT group, >6 months). IH regression was assessed by two blinded evaluators, with complete or near-complete regression defined as ≥80% reduction in IH volume.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included: 42 in the 6M group and 26 in the PT group (mean duration 9.7 ± 2.4 months). Deep or mixed IH were more frequent in the PT group (73% vs 43%). Complete or near-complete regression was observed in 34 patients (81%) in the 6M group and 20 patients (77%) in the PT group (p = 0.69). Severe adverse events were rare; one severe case of hypoglycemia occurred in the PT group. The relapse and re-treatment rates were not significantly different.
CONCLUSION: Extending propranolol beyond 6 months did not significantly improve IH regression, even in deeper lesions. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective design, small sample size, heterogeneous photographic assessment, and difficulty distinguishing treatment effects from natural involution. Prospective studies with larger cohorts are needed to identify IH subtypes that might benefit from longer therapy.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals the neurogenetic spectrum of pediatric epilepsy in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder, and diagnostic yield from next-generation sequencing varies substantially across cohorts and health-care settings. Population-specific data remain particularly limited for pediatric patients from underrepresented regions. In this retrospective two-center study, we evaluated 690 individuals with epilepsy onset at 18 years of age or younger who underwent whole-exome sequencing between January 2020 and April 2025. Patients with congenital infection, brain trauma, stroke, or perinatal asphyxia as the primary cause of epilepsy were excluded. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic findings were identified in 205 of 690 patients (29.7%). Single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and insertions/deletions (indels) accounted for 195 patients (28.2%), whereas clinically relevant copy number variants accounted for 10 patients (1.4%). The cohort included 370 males (53.6%) and 320 females (46.4%). We identified 68 rare SNVs and indels, of which 48 were classified as novel because they were absent from ClinVar, gnomAD, and dbSNP and had not been reported in the published literature at the time of analysis. In addition, four variants with rs identifiers lacked ClinVar records and prior case-based publications, and 15 variants had previously been reported only once. Eleven copy number variants were detected in 10 patients; all but one were confirmed by orthogonal testing. Several findings were considered of particular neurogenetic interest, including variants in genes with synaptic or ion-channel relevance and rare recurrent findings that may broaden the recognized phenotypic spectrum of pediatric epilepsy. Overall, this study supports the clinical utility of whole-exome sequencing in pediatric epilepsy and provides population-specific neurogenetic data from Türkiye, while also highlighting a subset of rare findings that require replication and functional validation.

articles.title: COL4A1 mutation underlying recurrent spontaneous intraparenchymal hemorrhage in an adolescent: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COL4A1-associated vasculopathy is a rare genetic small-vessel disorder characterized by structural fragility of the cerebral vasculature and an increased risk of ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and leukoaraiosis. Its implications for acute neurocritical care management remain incompletely defined.
OBSERVATIONS: An 18-year-old male with a prior history of unexplained intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse cerebral microhemorrhages presented 1 year later with acute neurological deterioration due to a large cerebellar hemorrhage, requiring emergency external ventricular drain placement and suboccipital decompressive craniectomy. Extensive imaging, vascular, infectious, and inflammatory evaluations were unrevealing. During hospitalization, he experienced recurrent intracranial hemorrhages, including a pontine hemorrhage, out of proportion with underlying coagulopathy. Following initiation of pharmacological deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis, an additional hemorrhagic event occurred. Genetic testing ultimately revealed a pathogenic heterozygous COL4A1 mutation.
LESSONS: COL4A1-associated disease should be considered in young patients with recurrent or unexplained intracranial hemorrhage and extensive cerebral microbleeds. Early recognition is critical, as standard neurocritical care algorithms including pharmacological thromboprophylaxis may confer increased hemorrhagic risk in the setting of diffuse structural vessel fragility. When identified early, genetic diagnosis should prompt proactive awareness of rebleeding risk and prospective modification of DVT prophylaxis timing and blood pressure targets rather than rigid application of standard ICH guidelines. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26379.

articles.title: The Ross procedure: Technical principles, operative strategy, and pitfalls for long-term success.
articles.abstract: The Ross procedure remains an attractive aortic valve replacement strategy for children, adolescents, and selected young adults. Pulmonary autograft replacement provides excellent hemodynamics, freedom from anticoagulation, growth potential in children, and favorable long-term survival in appropriately selected patients. These advantages, however, come at the cost of substantial technical complexity. Small imperfections during autograft harvest, implantation, coronary transfer, or root reconstruction can result in early dysfunction, coronary complications, or late autograft dilatation and failure. The purpose of this review is to summarize a practical and reproducible approach to the Ross procedure with emphasis on operative strategy, technical details, Ross-Konno modifications, autograft stabilization techniques, and avoidance of common pitfalls. Rather than advocating a single technique, we emphasize fundamental principles that permit adaptation to patient anatomy while maintaining the geometric integrity of the left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, and pulmonary root.

articles.title: Aortic Root Remodeling Patterns and Outcomes Five Years Following Contemporary Root Replacement Strategies in Young Patients: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Background: Long-term dimensional remodeling patterns after contemporary aortic root operations in young patients have historically not been well characterized and this may inform surgical decision-making.Methods: We evaluated longitudinal aortic root and annular remodeling patterns and clinical outcomes after the Bentall, Ross, or Valve-Sparing Root procedures from January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2024.Results: Sixty patients underwent aortic root replacement. Of these, 17 had the Bentall procedure (BP), 20 had the Ross procedure, and 23 had Valve Sparing Aortic Root Replacement (VSARR). On average Ross patients (4 years) were younger than BP (16 years) and VSARR (16 years) (p = .0001). Marfans (20%, 12/60), Down Syndrome (3%, 2/60) and Loeys-Dietz (3%, 2/60) were prevalent. All Marfan patients (n = 12) underwent VSARR (p = .006). The leading surgical indications were aortic regurgitation (78%, 47/60), aortic stenosis (58%, 35/60), and aortic aneurysm (46%, 28/60). Mortality rate was 7% (n = 4/60) and no statistically significant difference in survival was observed (p = .94). Reoperation occurred in 3 of 60 patients (5%). Four of 60 patients (7%) had endocarditis. At 5 years, the change in aortic root size was significantly different across operation types (p = .041), with significant dilation noted in the Ross cohort.Conclusions: Ross patients demonstrated greater neoaortic root enlargement at 5 years, although valve competence was generally preserved. Given the differences in age, underlying pathology, and surgical selection among the groups, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive remodeling patterns rather than evidence of the superiority of one operative strategy.

articles.title: Glenn Takedown Reconstruction Technique During Biventricular Conversion: A Contemporary Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: BackgroundGlenn takedown is an important component of staged biventricular conversion after superior cavopulmonary connection. We evaluated contemporary superior vena cava (SVC) reconstruction strategies, their evolution, and outcomes.MethodsWe reviewed consecutive patients undergoing Glenn takedown during biventricular conversion at Boston Children's Hospital from 2014 through 2024. Rescue takedowns returning patients to a systemic-to-pulmonary artery (PA) shunt or continued single-ventricle palliation were excluded. Reconstruction was classified as direct SVC-right atrial anastomosis, anterior patch/right atrial flap, interposition conduit, or mixed/asymmetric reconstruction.ResultsAmong 162 patients, reconstruction techniques used were anterior patch/right atrial flap in 120 (74.1%), interposition conduit in 33 (20.4%), direct anastomosis in 3 (1.9%), and mixed/asymmetric reconstruction in 6 (3.7%). Median age was 3.9 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-5.6). Interposition use increased from 2 of 66 (3.0%) from 2014 to 2018 to 31 of 96 (32.3%) from 2019 to 2024 (P < .001). SVC reintervention occurred in two of 162 patients (1.2%) and pulmonary artery reintervention in 4/162 (2.5%) patients during a median follow-up of 1.52 years (IQR, 1.08-4.42). Temporary junctional rhythm occurred in 8/162 (4.9%); 7/162 (4.3%) received permanent pacemakers for atrioventricular block. All-cause mortality was 9.3% (15/162).ConclusionsGlenn takedown during biventricular conversion can be achieved using several reconstruction techniques selected according to individual anatomy. Our current practice favors interposition grafting when a tension-free native-tissue connection cannot be achieved, or additional space is required. SVC- and PA-related reinterventions were uncommon during available follow-up; longer surveillance is needed to assess late conduit-related outcomes.

articles.title: Delayed Diagnosis of Coronary Sinus Ostial Atresia in a Single-Ventricle Patient.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Coronary sinus ostial atresia is a rare congenital anomaly that is often clinically silent; however, hemodynamic compromise can occur if venous drainage is interrupted. We present a 4-month old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who previously underwent palliation with a Norwood procedure. During bidirectional Glenn palliation, ligation of a 2-mm left superior vena cava resulted in coronary sinus dilation and myocardial edema, raising suspicion for coronary sinus ostial atresia. The coronary sinus was unroofed, and the child recovered well.

articles.title: Pediatric Frostbite and Cold-Weather Injuries in the United States: A Multi-Database Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric cold-weather injuries (frostbite and hypothermia) are uncommon but can lead to substantial morbidity, including amputation and long-term functional loss. National data on incidence, management, and outcomes are limited, particularly for fatalities outside healthcare settings. We conducted a retrospective analysis using three complementary data sources: an institutional registry at an American Burn Association-verified burn center (2018-2026), the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Readmission Database (NRD 2016-2021), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Storm Events Database (NOAA 2016-2023). Our institutional cohort included 16 patients (ages 1-17 years; 68.8% >13 years); treatments included rapid rewarming (43.8%), perfusion imaging (56.3%), thrombolytic therapy (18.8%), and hyperbaric oxygen therapy (31.3%). Two patients required amputation; both presented with hemorrhagic blisters, had delayed care, and did not receive thrombolytics. No thrombolytic-related complications were observed. Nationally, 2,155 pediatric cold weather injuries occurred; a national estimated hospitalization rate of 1.62 per 100,000. 79 pediatric frostbite admissions were identified, including 15 admissions designated as severe injury. NOAA data captured 16 pediatric deaths and 49 injuries across 30 states. Pediatric cold-weather injuries result in morbidity and mortality across diverse U.S. regions. Early aggressive management may reduce amputation and broader adoption of standardized protocols and public health prevention strategies are needed. Limitations of public health data emphasize the need for integrating diverse data sources to better understand the full impact of cold-weather injuries in the U.S.

articles.title: Relationship between pulse wave velocity and estimated glomerular filtration rate in children and adolescents at increased cardiovascular risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between renal function and arterial stiffness in pediatric populations is unclear. No studies examined the association between estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and arterial stiffness in children with normal kidney function.
METHODS: This study aims to assess the association between eGFR and pulse wave velocity (PWV), an acknowledged index of arterial stiffness, in different vascular beds, as measured by the carotid-femoral (cf) and the carotid-radial (cr) PWV, in a cohort of children and adolescents with normal kidney function, referred to a Pediatric Unit for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment due to excess weight and/or high blood pressure (BP).
RESULTS: We studied a cohort of 565 children and adolescents (median age: 10.9 years, SD 2.6; 46.2% female). Of these, 82.5% were overweight or obese, and 27.6% had high normal BP or were hypertensive. The median eGFR was 147.6 ml/min/1.73 m2 (IQR:132.0-165.0). The median cf-PWV and cr-PWV were 4.9 m/s and 5.7 m/s, respectively. 17.2% (n = 93) of the study sample had cf-PWV values equal or greater than 95th percentile, according to sex and age. After adjustment for age, pubertal stage, systolic and diastolic BP z scores or presence of hypertension, BMI z-score or weight class and heart rate, a significant inverse correlation was shown between eGFR and cf-PWV (P = 0.001), while the relation between eGFR and cr-PWV was weaker. Children and adolescents in the third eGFR tertile had significantly lower cf-PWV values than those in the first tertile (-0.34 m/s, P = 0.01). The factors that were significantly associated with cf-PWV values above the 95th percentile were systolic and diastolic BP z scores, the presence of hypertension and heart rate (P < 0.01 for all).
CONCLUSIONS: eGFR values are significantly and inversely correlated with cf-PWV in children and adolescents at increased cardiovascular risk with normal kidney function. This relationship is independent from BP and BMI.

articles.title: Physical Intimate Partner Violence Before and During Pregnancy and Adverse Birth Outcomes Using PRAMS 2016-2020 Data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the prevalence of physical intimate partner violence (IPV) in the 12 months before and during pregnancy and its association with adverse birth outcomes using 2016-2020 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) data.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of PRAMS data.
SETTING: PRAMS Phase 8 surveillance data were collected by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention from 2016 to 2020 across multiple states.
PARTICIPANTS: Annual sample sizes per state range from about 1,000 to 3,000 women.
METHODS: Analysis of deidentified PRAMS Phase 8 data and weighted logistic regression to examine adjusted odds ratios (aOR) of each outcome.
RESULTS: The prevalence of physical IPV was 2.8% before pregnancy and 1.96% during pregnancy. Physical IPV, in both periods, was consistently associated with increased odds of adverse birth outcomes. Those who experienced physical IPV before pregnancy had increased odds of low birth weight (LBW; aOR = 1.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.2, 1.5]), preterm birth (PTB; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]), and small for gestational age (SGA; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]). Similarly, those who experienced physical IPV during pregnancy had increased odds of LBW (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.3]), PTB (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]), and SGA (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]).
CONCLUSION: Physical IPV before and during pregnancy are distinct yet related exposures, each associated with increased odds of LBW, PTB, and SGA. These findings support the importance of identifying women experiencing IPV during the preconception and prenatal periods. Consistent with existing clinical recommendations, health care professionals should provide IPV screening and use a trauma-informed approach to care for women who are at risk for experiencing IPV. Preventing and reducing IPV among women has significant implications for improving maternal and fetal health. Providing access to comprehensive services that meet the physical, health care, emotional, social, legal, and economic needs of women and children is crucial.

articles.title: Transglutaminase 2 contributes to bacterial control and inflammatory pathology in Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
articles.abstract: The host response to Mycoplasma pneumoniae not only contributes to bacterial control, but can also cause acute lung pathology. The molecular drivers of this response remain incompletely defined. In this study, we identify transglutaminase 2 (TG2) as a contributor to bacterial control and acute inflammatory pathology in host defense. We observed that serum TG2 concentrations were significantly increased in pediatric patients with M. pneumoniae pneumonia. Mechanistically, in human bronchial epithelial cells, M. pneumoniae increased TG2 expression and transglutaminase activity through a TLR2-dependent pathway that engages a TG2/NF-κB/HIF-1α positive feedback loop. This feedback loop was associated with increased expression of matrix metalloproteinases and fibronectin. Infection of TG2-deficient mice with M. pneumoniae resulted in significantly attenuated lung inflammation, cytokine production, and expression of extracellular matrix remodeling proteins, but was associated with impaired bacterial control and substantially higher pulmonary pathogen loads. Bone marrow chimeras in which TG2 was absent from the recipient compartment showed the same pattern, with higher bacterial burdens and reduced inflammation relative to control chimeras. These findings identify TG2 as a mediator that couples effective bacterial control to inflammatory lung injury.

articles.title: Clinical and laboratory-based prognostic factors for pediatric postthrombotic syndrome: findings from the Kids-Duration of Therapy for Thrombosis in Children trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Knowledge on risk factors for the development of pediatric postthrombotic syndrome (PTS) is scarce. We previously identified low plasma fibrinolytic capacity and persistent complete veno-occlusion as candidate risk factors for pediatric PTS. This study aims to substantiate and expand on these findings through a prespecified secondary analysis of the Kids-DOTT trial.
OBJECTIVE: To identify additional clinical and molecular prognostic factors for the development of PTS in children presenting with first time provoked deep venous thrombosis (DVT).
METHODS: We analyzed clinical data and plasma specimens from children with an extremity DVT in the Kids-DOTT trial. PTS was assessed at 1 year post DVT. Plasma fibrinolytic capacity and biomarkers of fibrinolysis were measured in plasma collected at 6 weeks post DVT. Risk factors, identified in our prior work or substantiated in the literature, were evaluated via univariable logistic regression, and variables with P < .05 were included in a multivariable model.
RESULTS: A total of 399 patients were included; 37% developed PTS. In the multivariable clinical model, adolescent age (13 to <21 years) and complete veno-occlusion at 6 weeks were associated with PTS (odds ratio [OR] = 1.69, 95% CI = 1.11-2.57, P = .015 and OR = 2.19, 95% CI = 1.2-3.99, P = .01, respectively). In a biomarker-enhanced model, complete veno-occlusion, reduced plasma fibrinolytic capacity, and increased levels of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 antigen at 6 weeks were independent prognostic factors for PTS (OR = 2.76, 95% CI = 1.13-6.71, P = .025; OR = 1.83, 95% CI = 1.02-3.30, P = .044; and OR = 1.99, 95% CI = 1.1-3.59, P = .025, respectively).
CONCLUSION: We identified complete veno-occlusion, reduced plasma fibrinolytic capacity, and increased plasma levels of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 at 6 weeks post DVT as independent prognostic factors for the development of PTS in children with provoked DVT.

articles.title: Modeling 1-deamino-8-D-arginine vasopressin response from endothelial storage to individualized dosing in mild hemophilia A and symptomatic carriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Desmopressin (1-deamino-8-D-arginine vasopressin, DDAVP) is the first-line treatment for patients with mild hemophilia A (HA) and symptomatic carriers, but the hemostatic response varies widely. Despite over 4 decades of clinical use, DDAVP plasma concentrations had never been measured in HA, and no mechanism-based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of its hemostatic effects had been developed.
OBJECTIVES: To quantify DDAVP plasma concentrations in mild HA and symptomatic carriers and develop a mechanism-based population PK/PD model linking drug exposure to von Willebrand factor (VWF) and factor VIII (FVIII) responses in order to characterize the sources of variability in DDAVP response.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 72 patients (48 males with mild HA, 24 symptomatic carriers) received a single intravenous DDAVP infusion. Plasma DDAVP concentrations were quantified for the first time using a validated liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry method, alongside VWF antigen and factor VIII (FVIII) activity measurements. A mechanism-based population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling.
RESULTS: DDAVP pharmacokinetics followed a 2-compartment model. The pharmacodynamic model incorporated an explicit endothelial storage pool representing Weibel-Palade bodies, from which VWF and FVIII are released upon DDAVP stimulation. FVIII disposition was modeled as a function of VWF-FVIII binding, with distinct elimination rates for free and VWF-bound FVIII. Body weight was the main determinant of DDAVP exposure. Sex, ABO blood group, and age influenced VWF and FVIII baseline levels and disposition. VWF binding doubled FVIII half-life (4.6 vs 2 hours). Female carriers had 54% higher FVIII exposure than males, driven by higher baseline VWF and a longer effective FVIII half-life, resulting in prolonged hemostatic coverage. Simulations reproduced tachyphylaxis through endothelial pool depletion and identified patient profiles at risk of insufficient coverage.
CONCLUSION: This mechanism-based population PK/PD model provides a framework for individualized DDAVP dosing in mild HA and symptomatic carriers.

articles.title: Development of the PedsADAPSS Caregiver Report: A Measure of Caregiving Appraisals in Pediatric Spinal Cord Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and gather evidence supporting content validity for the Pediatric Appraisals of Disability Primary and Secondary Scale (PedsADAPSS) Caregiver Report, a condition-specific measure designed to assess SCI-related caregiving appraisals in pediatric populations.
METHODS: This was an iterative mixed-methods instrument development study. Item generation was informed by the Stress-Appraisal-Coping framework and existing appraisal measures, including the Appraisals of Disability: Primary and Secondary Scale (ADAPSS). An initial item pool was refined through binning and winnowing conducted by a multidisciplinary advisory board and research team. A modified Delphi survey with pediatric SCI professionals evaluated domain alignment and item retention. Cognitive interviews were conducted with caregivers of youth with SCI across 3 iterative rounds to assess item clarity, relevance, and response processes.
RESULTS: Initial item development yielded an item bank reflecting 4 appraisal domains: Harm/Loss, Threat, Challenge, and Coping Potential. Following advisory board review and Delphi consensus procedures, items were revised, removed, or added to improve conceptual precision and SCI specificity. Twelve cognitive interviews with caregivers further informed item refinement, resulting in a 41-item measure with evidence supporting content validity and response process validity. Caregivers reported that items were relevant to their lived experience and reflected key SCI-specific caregiving demands.
CONCLUSION: The PedsADAPSS Caregiver Report is a theory-based, condition-specific instrument designed to assess SCI-related caregiving appraisals. By operationalizing primary and secondary appraisal processes within a relational framework, the measure examines how caregivers interpret and respond to SCI-related demands in pediatric SCI. Ongoing field testing will evaluate its psychometric properties and potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Monitoring Fertility in Men with Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Europe, each year, ∼25,000 individuals, mostly young men, have a spinal cord injury (SCI). As in men living with SCI, infertility is a frequent issue due to ejaculatory dysfunction and poor sperm quality, fertility preservation (FP) is essential.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review explores the optimal timing for proposing or implementing FP procedures and the appropriate fertility monitoring methods for male patients with SCI.
METHOD: This systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines. French and English studies on FP in <60-year-old men with SCI from January 1990 to July 2025 were included. The review addressed 2 questions: (1) the best timing for proposing and carrying out FP procedures, and (2) suitable fertility monitoring strategies in patients with SCI who have or have not undergone FP.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies were analyzed, including 1 meta-analysis and 2 prospective trials. The mean patient age was 30 years. Cryopreservation negatively affected sperm motility and DNA integrity similarly in patients with SCI and in non-SCI patients with infertility. Conversely, sperm DNA fragmentation and mitochondrial dysfunction were significantly higher in SCI men. Biological markers, such as zinc and somatostatin, correlated with sperm parameters. Testicular biopsies and Sertoli/spermatid ratio predicted the ejaculate quality. Adolescents face unique challenges due to their ongoing psychological maturation and the risk of infection from long-term catheter use.
CONCLUSION: In all <60-year-old patients with SCI, FP could be proposed as early as possible during the rehabilitation process and reiterated as patients progress, particularly when adolescent patients reach the age of majority.

articles.title: Comparing 70 kV and 120 kV photon-counting CT protocols for pediatric cardiac imaging in children weighing 10-30 kg: Radiation dose and image quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.
CONCLUSION: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

articles.title: Precannulation Risk Factors Associated With Hemorrhagic Events During Respiratory Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Children: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic complications are frequent and clinically significant during pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet associated precannulation factors remain poorly defined. We evaluated these factors in a multicenter retrospective cohort of children receiving respiratory ECMO at four Colombian centers during 2018-2022. A total of 106 children were included; 53 (50.0%) developed at least one hemorrhagic complication during ECMO support, and 83% of events occurred within the first 7 days after cannulation. Cannulation-site bleeding was most frequent (41.5%), followed by intracranial hemorrhage (22.6%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (17.0%). In bias-reduced adjusted analyses, higher precannulation lactate concentrations, lower bicarbonate levels, previous severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, adenovirus infection at admission, and longer mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support before ECMO remained associated with bleeding. Patients who developed hemorrhagic complications had higher 28 day mortality than those without bleeding (39.6% vs. 13.2%; p = 0.002). When bleeding was modeled as a time-dependent exposure, hemorrhagic events were associated with a higher subsequent hazard of 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 4.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.09-11.64). Hemorrhagic complications affected half of children receiving respiratory ECMO, occurred predominantly during the first week, and were associated with increased mortality. Several precannulation characteristics remained associated with bleeding in bias-reduced adjusted analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children's hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The primary outcome was pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) mortality. Among 73 patients (non-ECPR, n = 58; ECPR, n = 15), ECPR was associated with increased mortality in unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR], 5.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.47-18.53; p = 0.010). After adjustment for pre-ECMO physiologic variables, the association between ECPR and mortality was no longer significant (adjusted OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 0.37-8.08; p = 0.483). Lower pre-ECMO arterial pH remained associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR, 1.87 per 0.1 decrease; 95% CI, 1.20-2.92; p = 0.006). In a sensitivity analysis, underlying cardiac disease was associated with lower mortality than noncardiac disease (adjusted OR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.07-0.79; p = 0.020). These findings highlight the associations of pre-ECMO physiologic status and underlying disease category with PICU mortality.

articles.title: Ventricular Assist Devices Effectively Bridge Pediatric Patients to Heart Retransplantation: An ACTION Registry Study.
articles.abstract: The use of ventricular assist devices (VAD) in pediatric patients as a bridge to heart transplantation has increased over the past two decades. However, the use of VAD to bridge pediatric transplant recipients to retransplantation is rare and under-studied. We performed a retrospective study using the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) registry to evaluate patient characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients bridged to retransplant with VAD. A total of 24 patients were identified and supported for a median duration of 64 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 15.0-101.25). Of these, 54% (n = 13) were implanted as a bridge to retransplant candidacy (BTC) and 46% (n = 11) as a bridge to retransplant (BTT). We found a high prevalence of major adverse events, including infection in 75% (n = 18), bleeding in 42% (n = 10), renal dysfunction requiring dialysis in 33% (n = 8), and stroke in 8% (n = 2). Despite this, 71% (n = 17) survived to retransplant, with an 88% 1 year survival following retransplant. Device mortality was higher in BTC compared to BTT (46% vs. 9%; p = 0.046). Our study is the first multicenter study evaluating the use of VAD as a BTT. We exhibit a high prevalence of adverse events on VAD, but a favorable waitlist and post-retransplant survival.

articles.title: Recurrent Pediatric Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans of the Abdominal Wall: A Rare Case Report With Diagnostic and Surgical Challenges.
articles.abstract: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare, locally aggressive sarcoma usually seen in adults. We report a recurrent epigastric DFSP in an 11-year-old boy, initially misdiagnosed on incisional biopsy. Accurate diagnosis and successful treatment required wide excision, careful surgical planning, and multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Clinically Suspected Fulminant Myocarditis Following PCR-Confirmed Pertussis in an Infant: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Cardiac involvement following pertussis infection is uncommon but may be associated with severe clinical deterioration in infants. We report the case of a 3-month-old girl who developed shock, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe biventricular systolic dysfunction approximately 2 weeks after PCR-confirmed Bordetella pertussis infection. Echocardiography demonstrated marked left ventricular dilatation, global hypokinesia, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. Troponin I was markedly elevated. The clinical presentation was consistent with suspected fulminant myocarditis, although definitive myocardial confirmation was unavailable. The infant received intensive supportive care, inotropic treatment, heart failure medications, antiarrhythmic therapy, and intravenous immunoglobulin, with subsequent clinical and echocardiographic improvement. She was discharged in a stable condition but died unexpectedly approximately 2 months later. The immediate cause of death remained undetermined. This case emphasizes the importance of early cardiac assessment and structured post-discharge surveillance in infants with severe cardiac dysfunction following pertussis infection.

articles.title: Vitamin C Use and Severe Haemolysis in Pediatric G6PD Deficiency: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: This case highlights the danger of relying solely on neonatal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) screening, which may yield false negatives and the risk of routine vitamin C use in G6PD-deficient children, which can trigger severe hemolysis. Clinicians must remain vigilant and prioritize public education on safe medication practices in pediatric care.

articles.title: Idiopathic Neonatal Ileocolic Intussusception Without a Pathological Lead Point Presenting as Intestinal Obstruction: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Neonatal intussusception is extremely uncommon, being responsible for 0.3% of all cases of intussusceptions and 3% of all neonatal intestinal obstruction. Due to its nonspecific nature, it may mimic necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and cause a delay in the diagnosis. Idiopathic intussusception in the term neonates is unusual as most have a pathological lead point. A case of a full-term male infant presenting on the third day of life with abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and stools with mixed blood. Examination showed a non-tender mass in the right iliac fossa while the digital rectal examination revealed red currant jelly stool. Ultrasonography showed 23 × 18 × 44 mm target sign suggestive of intussusception. On emergency laparotomy, there was gangrenous ileocolic intussusception that extended from 15 cm proximally to the ileocecal junction to mid-sigmoid colon. Reduction by manual manipulation under general anesthesia through laparotomy was unsuccessful and so the gangrenous bowel was resected and a primary end-to-end ileosigmoid anastomosis done. Histopathology did not reveal a lead point while the gross examination of the specimen confirmed the diagnosis of intussusception. The enteral feeds were started on postoperative day (POD) five and discharged on POD 10. He was asymptomatic and growing well at 1 month follow-up and still asymptomatic, achieving all his milestones at 6 months of follow-up. Idiopathic ileocolic intussusception should always be included in the differential diagnosis of all neonatal intestinal obstructions.

articles.title: Pediatric T-Cell Lymphoblastic Lymphoma Presenting as Rapidly Progressive Tonsillar Hypertrophy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We discuss an 8-year-old male who presented with asymmetric, rapidly progressive tonsillar hypertrophy and cervical lymphadenopathy. He was treated empirically with corticosteroids, antibiotics, and semi-elective tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy. Pathology was consistent with T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. Early recognition of pediatric malignancy and referral to subspecialty care can mitigate perioperative risks and optimize oncologic outcomes.

articles.title: Werner Syndrome With Multisystem Manifestations in a 35-Year-Old Bangladeshi Man: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Werner syndrome, also known as adult progeria, is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by premature aging and multisystem involvement. We report the case of a 35-year-old Bangladeshi man who presented with growth arrest during adolescence resulting in short stature, bilateral posterior subcapsular cataracts, diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, chronic non-healing ulcers, scleroderma-like skin changes, muscle wasting, and ankle ankylosis. Molecular genetic analysis identified a pathogenic WRN gene variant (c.3233 + 2 T >C in intron 26), confirming the diagnosis of Werner syndrome. A younger sister exhibited similar phenotypic features, suggesting possible familial occurrence; however, she was not genetically tested. Laboratory investigations revealed normocytic normochromic anemia, hypertriglyceridemia, elevated gonadotropin levels, markedly reduced serum testosterone, and marked hyperferritinemia. In addition, radiological evaluation demonstrated generalized osteopenia with talocalcaneal and ankle joint ankylosis, while electrocardiography revealed left ventricular hypertrophy. Management focused on long-term control of metabolic and endocrine comorbidities together with comprehensive wound care for chronic ulcers. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, molecular confirmation, multidisciplinary management, and regular surveillance for cardiovascular complications and malignancies in patients with Werner syndrome.

articles.title: Fournier's Gangrene Following Recent Varicella in an Immunocompetent Adult: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Varicella is a common, usually self-limiting viral illness in children; however, adult infection may be associated with severe systemic and secondary bacterial complications. Fournier's gangrene (FG) is a rare, rapidly progressive, and fatal necrotizing fasciitis involving the genital and perineal region, commonly seen in immunocompromised individuals. The occurrence of Fournier's gangrene in temporal association with recent varicella in an immunocompetent adult is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 32-year-old previously healthy male who developed Fournier's gangrene 2 weeks after varicella infection. He presented with high-grade fever, malaise, and rapidly progressive scrotal pain, erythema, swelling, and necrosis. On examination, extensive scrotal edema, sloughed skin, exposed fascial planes, and foul-smelling purulent discharge extending to the perineum and left thigh were noted. Laboratory evaluation revealed marked leukocytosis, elevated inflammatory markers, and a high Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score. Ultrasonography demonstrated fascial thickening with gas within soft tissues, while wound and blood cultures revealed polymicrobial infection. He was managed with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, hemodynamic support, and repeated surgical debridements followed by secondary wound closure, resulting in gradual clinical recovery. This case highlights a rare but life-threatening complication of adult varicella in an immunocompetent individual. The close temporal relationship between recent varicella and the subsequent development of FG suggests a temporal association, although a causal relationship cannot be established from a single case report. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for necrotizing soft tissue infections in patients presenting with perineal pain and swelling following varicella, as early diagnosis and prompt surgical intervention are critical for survival.

articles.title: Thromboembolism, A Rare Presentation of Chronic Pancreatitis in Pediatrics: Diagnostics and Management Challenges in Tanzania.
articles.abstract: Pediatric chronic pancreatitis is uncommon, and vascular thromboembolic complications are rarely reported in children. Diagnosis may be particularly challenging in resource-limited settings where advanced pancreatic investigations are not readily available. We report a 2-year-old boy who presented with progressive abdominal distension, fever, weight loss, lower limb edema, and bulky, foul smelling stools. Laboratory investigations showed markedly elevated serum and ascitic amylase and lipase levels. Abdominal computed tomography demonstrated pancreatic calcifications with irregular pancreatic margins, massive ascites, and extensive inferior vena cava thrombosis. Chest computed tomography demonstrated pulmonary embolism involving the right pulmonary artery and its segmental branches. Pancreatic exocrine function testing and genetic evaluation were unavailable. The patient was managed with repeated therapeutic paracentesis and anticoagulation, initially with unfractionated heparin and subsequently with enoxaparin. Follow-up Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated resolution of the inferior vena cava thrombus. The child was discharged in stable condition but was subsequently lost to follow-up. Managing pediatric pancreatitis in our settings presents major diagnostic and therapeutic hurdles, demanding high clinical vigilance, and may be complicated by multiple thrombotic events. Furthermore, once diagnosed, surgical intervention is often suboptimal in resource-constrained settings due to an elevated risk of postoperative complications.

articles.title: Protein intake scaling and muscle status in children with Spinal Muscular Atrophy: implications for protein prescription.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Protein requirements in children with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) are uncertain, and conventional protein targets expressed per kilogram of body weight may be difficult to interpret because fat-free mass is disproportionately reduced. We examined whether protein intake expressed relative to body weight, fat-free mass (FFM), or energy was associated with muscle status and whether these associations differed by SMA phenotype or disease-modifying therapy (DMT) exposure.
METHODS: This longitudinal observational analysis included 248 assessments from 114 children aged 24-159 months with SMA types 1 and 2. Protein intake was derived from dietitian-reviewed 3-day food records. Arm muscle area (AMA) z score was the primary outcome and fat-free mass index (FFMI) the secondary outcome. Generalised estimating equations accounted for repeated assessments and clinical covariates. Within-person, consecutive-visit, sensitivity, interaction, and paired pre/post-DMT analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Protein intake per kilogram of body weight was not associated with AMA (β = -0.001; 95% CI -0.204 to 0.202; P = 0.99), with no interaction by SMA type or treated status. Protein per kilogram of FFM was associated with concurrent AMA (β = 0.189; 95% CI 0.066 to 0.312; q = 0.018), but this association was not robust longitudinally and was absent after adjustment for dietary energy relative to measured resting energy expenditure, although the original model fitted in the same 226 assessments still showed the association (β = 0.182; 95% CI 0.032 to 0.332). Only 3 of 245 assessments were below the age-specific population reference intake (PRI) for healthy children, whereas 75.5% were at least twice that value; this does not establish protein adequacy in SMA. In 27 paired assessments surrounding DMT initiation, body-weight-normalised protein intake decreased without significant changes in AMA or FFMI.
CONCLUSION: In children with SMA whose protein intake was predominantly at or above the general-population PRI, higher protein intake was not associated with better muscle status, and no phenotype- or DMT-specific protein target was identified. FFM-normalised protein was not supported as a prescription target. Nutritional management should emphasise protein adequacy, energy balance, body composition, growth, and longitudinal response rather than routine protein escalation.

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Based Dietary Advice: A Scoping Review of Nutritional Accuracy, Safety, and Eating-Related Risks.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based dietary advice, with particular attention to nutritional accuracy, safety, weight-management guidance, eating-related harm, and professional safeguards.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, refined by Levac et al., and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase were searched up to 30 June 2026. Original empirical studies evaluating generative AI or large language models for dietary advice, meal planning, nutritional information, weight management, or eating-disorder-related guidance were eligible. Study selection, data charting, and synthesis were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus or third-reviewer assessment.
RESULTS: Nine studies published between 2023 and 2026 were included. In this small and emerging evidence base, one study reported 84.38% accuracy on an objective nutrition-literacy assessment, and another found overall Diet Quality Index-International scores above 70 for chatbot-generated weight-loss plans. However, important limitations were identified in caloric accuracy, portion sizing, macronutrient and micronutrient balance, reproducibility, personalization, and management of food allergies and multimorbidity.
