Potential safety concerns were identified in adolescent and eating-disorder scenarios, where chatbot responses sometimes combined appropriate healthy-eating advice with restrictive or weight-focused recommendations; these studies did not establish resulting clinical or behavioral harm. Although some systems encouraged consultation with healthcare professionals, safety warnings and referral to regulated resources were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: Evidence from the nine included studies remains preliminary, heterogeneous, and largely simulation-based. Generative AI may have a supplementary role in nutrition education and preliminary dietary guidance, but the available evidence is insufficient to support autonomous use in place of dietitians. Current findings indicate potential safety risks in high-risk or clinically complex scenarios rather than demonstrated long-term harm. Longitudinal and real-world studies are needed to establish the clinical and behavioral effects of AI-generated dietary advice.

articles.title: Exploring the potential therapeutic significance of secukinumab for annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
articles.abstract: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis (AEI), also known as KRT1/KRT10-nEDD-annular, is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by recurrent annular erythema on the trunk and proximal extremities. Currently, the treatment of AEI is limited to the use of emollients, keratolytics, and oral retinoids, which remains insufficient. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of secukinumab in patients with AEI. Two patients with AEI were enrolled for secukinumab therapy following a laboratory assessment that excluded contraindications. Disease severity was assessed using the Ichthyosis Area and Severity Index (IASI), the Children's Dermatology Life Quality Index (cDLQI) and the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), and the 5-D itch scale. Immunological profiling was performed by measuring biomarker levels in both serum and lesional skin tissue. Significant differences in treatment efficacy were observed between the paediatric and adult patient receiving secukinumab, with the paediatric patient demonstrating marked outcomes and improvements in both subjective symptoms and skin lesions. Notably, despite showing no pre-treatment elevation in serum IL-17A levels, the paediatric patient exhibited increased IL-17A expression in lesional skin. Limitations: Small sample group. Although our findings are based on a small sample size, they provide novel therapeutic perspectives for the management of AEI and offer preliminary therapeutic clues for future clinical management.

articles.title: Recognition of Emergency Symptoms and Preparedness for Major Health Risks in Elementary Schools in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elementary schools are settings in which children may experience unexpected health emergencies, and school staff play a central role in prevention and early response. While symptom recognition among staff is generally reported to be high, less attention has been paid to how initial responses and medical referrals are understood, shared, and operationalized within schools.
METHODS: We conducted a web-based survey of 505 elementary school staff members across Japan between July and August 2025 to assess recognition of key symptoms and respondents' awareness of school-based preparedness for concussion, heat stroke, food allergy, and choking. Background characteristics and preparedness measures were summarized using descriptive statistics. Associations between preparedness scores and respondent- and school-level factors were explored using multivariable linear regression models.
RESULTS: Recognition of key symptoms was generally high across conditions. In contrast, reported awareness of school-based preparedness measures varied widely, with first-aid procedures reported by 80%-90% of respondents, whereas recurrence prevention and return-to-activity protocols were less frequently reported, particularly for concussion (19.6%). Multivariable analyses showed higher preparedness scores among principals and vice principals across conditions (mean differences [MDs], 0.4-0.7), while lower scores were observed for food allergy in smaller schools (< 100 students, MD -0.49; 95% CI -0.87 to -0.11) and in the Hokkaido/Tohoku region (MD, -0.72; 95% CI -1.26 to -0.18).
CONCLUSIONS: Symptom recognition for major school health emergencies was generally high, whereas respondents' awareness of preparedness measures for recovery and emergency decision-making was less consistent. Awareness varied across staff roles, highlighting potential gaps in dissemination of school preparedness procedures.

articles.title: Association of vitamin therapy with acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus and neurological outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus (AEFCSE) has a poor prognosis, but no definitive treatment. We aimed to evaluate whether early combination vitamin therapy (VT) (vitamin B1, B6, and l-carnitine) could prevent AEFCSE onset and improve neurological outcomes of pediatric febrile status epilepticus (FSE).
METHODS: The present, single-center, retrospective observational study enrolled patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit during 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 with FSE lasting ≥30 min. The patients were categorized into a VT group, who received vitamins within 72 h of the initial seizure onset, and a non-VT group. The primary outcome was the AEFCSE incidence. The secondary outcome was AEFCSE-related, poor neurological prognosis as defined by the Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity scores was used to adjust for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Of 109 included patients with FSE, 40 (37%) and 69 (63%) were in the VT and the non-VT group, respectively. AEFCSE occurred in eight (20%) and 11 (16%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, VT was associated with lower but non-significant odds of AEFCSE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.73). AEFCSE-related, poor neurological outcomes occurred in five (13%) and eight (12%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, the odds were lower but non-significant (OR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.16-1.90).
CONCLUSIONS: Early combination VT demonstrated an exploratory association with lower AEFCSE incidence and improved neurological outcomes in children with FSE albeit the findings were inconclusive.

articles.title: Day-29 Minimal Residual Disease and Candidate Adverse Molecular Alterations for Survival Stratification in a TARGET/cBioPortal Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Cohort.
articles.abstract: Day-29 minimal residual disease (MRD) is central to risk assessment in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but MRD alone may not fully explain outcome heterogeneity. We performed a retrospective patient-level analysis of the public TARGET/cBioPortal cohort to evaluate whether MRD and candidate adverse molecular alterations (CAMA) jointly stratify event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS). The roster contained 1551 patients; MRD was available for 1534, including 1058 below 0.01% and 476 at or above 0.01%. EFS and OS source fields were available for 1535, with 399 coded EFS events and 254 deaths. Their intersection with available MRD contained 1524 patients, 391 EFS events and 246 deaths. Molecular profiles were selectively available: 137 patients had mutation profiles and 682 had copy-number profiles. Source verification did not establish complete CAMA-negative status, a valid Ph-like classifier, diagnostic timing of all molecular samples, or alignment of the exported survival clock with MRD sampling. CAMA rules were outcome-informed, and the original fully adjusted model had coding and estimation problems. Accordingly, historical HRs and C-index differences are disclosed for reproducibility but are not retained as valid prognostic estimates. The clinical-molecular research framework is retained as the study question; joint survival stratification and incremental discrimination are not established by this dataset.

articles.title: Pediatric Dermatologic Conditions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric skin conditions of the lower extremity present a diagnostic and management challenge, and this article offers the practitioner a systematic framework. It opens with practical guidance on performing cutaneous procedures in children-engaging the parent, minimizing pain and anxiety through topical anesthesia and distraction, and setting postoperative limits for optimal scar outcomes. It then surveys environmentally induced disorders, bites and stings, genodermatoses including the palmoplantar keratodermas, and bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. Eczematous conditions, psoriasis, nevi, pediatric melanoma, and nail disorders are each reviewed with attention to lower extremity presentation, common misdiagnoses, and current management strategies.

articles.title: Pediatric Foot and Ankle Infection and Osteomyelitis.
articles.abstract: This article reviews pediatric foot and ankle infections and osteomyelitis, emphasizing how a child's developing vasculature, growth plates, and periosteum predispose to rapid hematogenous spread and unique complications like growth arrest. It covers epidemiology, age-specific and risk-specific patterns, and a classification spanning superficial soft-tissue infection, deep infection, septic arthritis, and acute/subacute/chronic osteomyelitis. Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant S aureus) and Kingella kingae are highlighted as key pathogens. Diagnostic strategy combines inflammatory markers, cultures, and MRI, while management centers on targeted antibiotics with early transition to oral therapy and timely surgical debridement. Four illustrative case studies and emerging diagnostic/therapeutic trends round out the discussion.

articles.title: The Newborn Examination and Pediatric Foot Development.
articles.abstract: Neonatal foot and ankle pathology is underemphasized in most medical training, leaving podiatrists increasingly called upon to assess newborns. This article sets out a systematic approach: a detailed prenatal, maternal, perinatal, and developmental history, followed by examination extending from head, neck, upper extremities, thorax, and spine to hips and knees. It then reviews common lower extremity conditions-hallux nail disorders, curly toe, digiti quinti varus, focal gigantism, brachymetatarsia, syndactyly, polydactyly, hallux varus and valgus, metatarsus adductus, talipes equinovarus, and calcaneus deformities-stressing early serial casting where indicated and delaying most surgical correction until skeletal maturation.

articles.title: Temporal changes in IgM heavy chain gene expression in neonatal foals.
articles.abstract: This study described the postnatal pattern of immunoglobulin heavy constant mu (IGHM) mRNA expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of 10 Polish Pony foals and compared it with plasma IgM concentration. Blood was sampled before first suckling and at 1, 10, 20, 30 and 60 days of age. IGHM was measured by RT-PCR and IgM by ELISA; changes over time were assessed with the Friedman test. Plasma IgM rose sharply from a low birth value (median 5.2 mg/dL) to a peak by day 1 (215 mg/dL), then declined and appeared to plateau at intermediate levels through day 60 (χ²(5) = 23.16, p < 0.001). IGHM expression showed a smaller-magnitude pattern, rising from 11.1 (2^-ΔCt relative to HPRT) at birth to a peak around days 20-30 and declining by day 60 (χ²(5) = 17.19, p < 0.01), though no pairwise comparison remained significant after correction. Findings indicate postnatal maturation of the B-cell/immunoglobulin compartment in foals.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum and morbidity of ocular parasitic infections among rural children in central India.
articles.abstract: Ocular parasitic infections are an under-recognised cause of ocular morbidity in low- and middle-income countries. We found Taenia solium (26.5%) was the most common parasite, followed by Toxocara canis/cati (19.4%), Toxoplasma gondii (17.3%) and Acanthamoeba spp. (11.2%). Reduced visual acuity (66.3%), retinitis/chorioretinitis (38.8%), uveitis (32.7%) and vitreous involvement (28.6%) were the predominant clinical manifestations. Poor nutritional status was significantly associated with infection. Frequent open defaecation, barefoot outdoor play and inadequate handwashing before meals were identified as significant behavioural risk factors for ocular parasitic infection.

articles.title: Flow cytometry-based drug response profiling of primary B-precursor ALL cells in co-culture with bone marrow-derived stromal cells.
articles.abstract: Despite major improvements in the long-term survival of pediatric patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), relapse and resistance to frontline therapy remain major clinical challenges with limited treatment options. To identify effective therapeutic alternatives, ex vivo drug response profiling (DRP) on patient-derived leukemia cells enables systematic and rapid screening of various therapeutic agents, both individually or in combination. However, performing DRP on primary ALL cells in monoculture is often complicated by their high rate of spontaneous cell death ex vivo, which compromises assay reliability, especially over extended periods of drug testing. To overcome this limitation, co-culture systems using feeder cells, such as human or murine bone marrow-derived stromal cells or hTERT-immortalized mesenchymal stem cells (hTERT-MSCs), can provide essential survival support for leukemia cells. Here, we present a flow cytometry-based protocol to profile cell death responses of patient-derived xenograft (PDX) B-precursor ALL cells in co-culture with different bone marrow-derived stromal feeder lines following treatment with different drugs. This robust and scalable assay allows discrimination of leukemic cells from stromal layers, quantification of cell viability/cell death and proliferation, and assessment of drug responses of different ALL samples to chemotherapeutic agents as well as preclinical and early clinical small-molecule inhibitors. This platform can also be used to evaluate drug responses of ALL cells as part of personalized therapeutic strategies, which may be particularly relevant for patients with refractory or relapsed pediatric ALL.

articles.title: Fulminant Early-Onset Sepsis Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Aeromonas hydrophila in a Preterm Neonate: A Case Report and Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is a rare but virulent pathogen in neonates, historically associated with aquatic environments. However, the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains presenting as early-onset sepsis (EOS) poses a severe diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma. We report a fatal case of a preterm neonate (33 weeks gestation) who developed fulminant septic shock at 20 hours of life. Despite the initiation of broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam), the clinical course rapidly progressed to pulmonary hemorrhage and death at 26 hours of life. Blood cultures subsequently confirmed Aeromonas hydrophila septicemia with high-level resistance to carbapenems (Meropenem MIC > 16 μg/mL) and piperacillin-tazobactam (MIC > 128 μg/mL). This case highlights the growing threat of nonfermenting MDR gram-negative organisms in EOS and underscores the limitations of standard empiric regimens against atypical pathogens.

articles.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) affects up to 40% of adolescent and reproductive-age females and is a leading cause of complications such as severe anemia, iron deficiency and hospitalization. In adolescents and young women, it is commonly linked to anovulatory cycles and underlying inherited bleeding disorders, with von Willebrand disease (VWD) being the most prevalent but frequently underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the prevalence of VWD among adolescents and young women aged ≤25 years assessed for HMB within hospital-based settings and evaluates diagnostic setting gradients.
METHODS: This review included six databases - PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, and ProQuest that were searched electronically using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. After the search, the articles were transferred to Rayyan software for further screening. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool. Data extraction was performed, and the findings were presented narratively.
RESULTS: Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting revealed a distinct diagnostic gradient: Specialized Hematology and Hemophilia Treatment Centres (HTCs) demonstrated the highest prevalence at 16.78% (77/459), followed by Inpatient / Acute Emergency Admissions at 10.20% (25/245), General Tertiary Referral Hospital Settings at 10.20% (65/637), and Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) / Multidisciplinary Outpatient HMB Clinics at 8.70% (32/368).
CONCLUSION: von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024563010.

articles.title: Knowledge, Practices, and Training Needs Related to Radiation Protection among Critical Care Staff Exposed to Portable Radiography: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portable radiography is frequently performed in critical care settings, where healthcare workers may be exposed to scattered ionizing radiation. Adequate knowledge and appropriate protective practices are important components of occupational radiation protection.
OBJECTIVE: To assess radiation protection knowledge, practices, and training needs among nurses and physicians working in critical care units during portable radiography in hospitals in Bethlehem and East Jerusalem, Palestine.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among nurses and physicians working in intensive care units, cardiac care units, and neonatal intensive care units in nine hospitals between November 2022 and March 2023. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, objective radiation protection knowledge, reported radiation protection practices during portable radiography, personal protective equipment use, training history and needs, and self-rated knowledge.
RESULTS: A total of 142 critical care staff participated, including 104 nurses and 38 physicians. The mean objective radiation protection knowledge score was 8.30 ± 2.83 out of 14 (59.3%). Although 85.3% of participants rated their radiation protection knowledge as good or very good, objective assessment indicated that 68.3% had poor or fair knowledge. Regarding reported practice behaviors during portable radiography, leaving the unit during image acquisition was the most common response (37.3%), followed by maintaining maximum distance within the unit (23.2%), relocating to a break room (19.0%), remaining at the nursing station (12.0%), and standing behind shielding (8.5%). Use of personal protective equipment was limited, with 48.6% reporting that they never used lead aprons, 62.7% never using thyroid shields, 68.3% never using lead gloves, and 73.9% never using protective eyewear. Most participants (72.5%) had never attended formal radiation protection training, and 85.2% reported a need for additional education.
CONCLUSION: Critical care staff demonstrated a discrepancy between perceived and objectively assessed radiation protection knowledge and reported inconsistent use of protective measures during portable radiography. The findings support structured and continuing radiation protection education and institutional measures to reinforce appropriate occupational protection practices.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis in a Growth Faltering Infant With Acinetobacter Sepsis-A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery thrombosis is a rare finding in infant patients. Contributors to infant hypercoagulability include inherited thrombophilias, immature anticoagulation systems, and systemic insults such as septic shock and liver disease.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 7-week-old girl with perinatal HIV exposure diagnosed with a pulmonary artery thrombus. The patient was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) for sepsis due to Acinetobacter nosocomialis bacteremia. During a workup for growth faltering and an S3 gallop, echocardiogram revealed a mass in the main pulmonary artery. Days later, after failing to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation, infant developed hypoxia and echocardiogram demonstrated worsening luminal obstruction by the thrombus, prompting urgent treatment with thrombectomy. We hypothesize that septic shock, with associated coagulopathy and severe dehydration, predisposed to thrombus formation in this critically ill patient.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the rapid, multidisciplinary approach to diagnosing a pulmonary artery thrombus and the underlying factors contributing to hypercoagulability in an infant. This case is novel for the patient's risk factor of perinatal HIV exposure, which may have predisposed her to opportunistic infection as well as thrombosis. Hypoxia and hemodynamic instability presented later in her course, prompting invasive management. Early recognition and timely intervention are essential for optimizing patient outcomes.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Maternal Peripheral Blood PAF and sFlt-1 Levels for Preterm Birth Secondary to PPROM.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a leading cause of preterm birth, which seriously endangers maternal and neonatal health. Platelet-activating factor (PAF) and soluble FMS-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) play important roles in pregnancy, but their predictive value for preterm birth following PPROM remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of maternal peripheral blood PAF and sFlt-1 levels for spontaneous preterm delivery (SPTD) secondary to PPROM.
METHODS: A total of 85 singleton pregnant women with a gestational age of 23 + 0 to 30 + 6 weeks who were diagnosed with PPROM were enrolled. Based on the occurrence of SPTD within 14 days after sampling, the participants were divided into an imminent SPTD group (iSPTD, n = 45) and a non-imminent SPTD group (non-iSPTD, n = 40). Serum levels of PAF and sFlt-1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariate logistic regression was used to analyze their independent association with SPTD within 14 days post-sampling, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were employed to evaluate their predictive value.
RESULTS: Maternal peripheral blood levels of both PAF and sFlt-1 were significantly higher in the iSPTD group than in the non-iSPTD group (all p < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that PAF (odds ratio [OR] = 1.272, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.094 - 1.480) and sFlt-1 (OR = 1.179, 95% CI: 1.058 - 1.315) were independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling. ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting SPTD within 14 days was 0.762 for PAF and 0.738 for sFlt-1. The combined nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.829, demonstrating good predictive performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated maternal peripheral blood levels of PAF and sFlt-1 are independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling in patients with PPROM. Both biomarkers exhibit predictive value for SPTD, and their combination in a nomogram model can further improve predictive performance, showing potential for clinical application.

articles.title: Cytomegalovirus Seroprevalence Among Pregnant Women in the Region of Rabat, Morocco: a Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital CMV infection can lead to outcomes such as hearing loss and neurodevelopmental disabilities.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated the CMV IgG seropositive rate in 200 pregnant women in the Rabat region to determine mothers' immune status and its distribution pattern. The sera were obtained from a serum bank between January and October, 2021. Questionnaires were administered to obtain information regarding the sociodemographic and clinical data of the enrollee. Maternal CMV serology was determined, using Alinity i chemilumi-nescence microparticle immunoassays for IgG quantitative detection.
RESULTS: The age range was from 17 to 46 years, with a median age of 30 years (IQR 24.8 - 35) and a mean gestation of 20.4 ± 4.1 week. The seroprevalence of CMV IgG antibodies was 198 (99%), while 1% of participants were seronegative.
CONCLUSIONS: We recorded a low risk profile for primary CMV infection during pregnancy due to the large number of seropositive women that were infected at a young age.

articles.title: Serum Vitamin D Combined with Obstetric Parameters to Construct a Nomogram Model for Predicting the Risk of PFD Disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) significantly impacts women's quality of life and mental health. Although existing studies suggest various obstetric factors may contribute to PFD, there is a lack of early prediction tools based on readily available indicators. This study aimed to develop a nomogram model incorporating serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)VitD] levels and routine obstetric parameters to predict the risk of PFD.
METHODS: A total of 300 women who delivered and completed a 6-week postpartum follow-up were enrolled. Data on age, body mass index (BMI), duration of the second stage of labor, neonatal birth weight, and serum 25(OH) VitD levels within 24 hours postpartum were collected. Participants were divided into PFD and non-PFD groups based on follow-up outcomes. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for PFD, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression revealed that age, BMI, duration of the second stage of labor, birth weight, and 25(OH)VitD levels were independent predictors of PFD (p < 0.05). The nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.830 with calibration curves demonstrating good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated substantial clinical net benefit across a wide probability threshold range.
CONCLUSIONS: The developed nomogram model effectively predicts postpartum PFD risk using easily obtainable pre- and post-delivery indicators. This model may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals, guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies and improving early intervention and prevention of PFD.

articles.title: Study of Aichi Virus in Children with Acute Gastroenteritis: a Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Rotavirus and adenovirus are well-established viral etiologies, while Aichi virus (AiV) has emerged as a potential pathogen for AGE.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 134 children ≤ 5 years old presenting with AGE to Mansoura Children's Hospital, Egypt, in 2024. Stool samples were tested for rotavirus and adenovirus antigens by ELISA and for AiV RNA by real-time PCR.
RESULTS: Rotavirus was detected in 37.3% of cases, adenovirus in 25.4%, and AiV in 2.2%. All AiV-positive samples were co-detected with rotavirus (p = 0.05), while no significant association was observed with adenovirus (p = 0.57).
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first report of AiV detection in Egyptian children with AGE. Although prevalence was low, its consistent association with rotavirus suggests possible synergistic or opportunistic infection, warranting further epidemiologic and molecular investigations.

articles.title: Comparison of Testosterone in Umbilical Cord Blood of Preterm Infants Measured by Immunoassay and Mass Spectrometry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testosterone plays an important role in male sexual differentiation. In adult males, electrochemiluminescence immunoassays (ECLIA) are used globally to measure serum testosterone levels because of their efficiency and good correlation with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), despite their cross-reactivity potential. However, the accuracy and clinical significance of these methods in the early neonatal period remain unclear. This study compared umbilical cord testosterone levels measured using ECLIA and LC-MS/MS to discriminate sex differences between two methods in preterm infants with typical external genitalia.
METHODS: Forty-eight preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of the Nihon University Itabashi Hospital between May 2020 and March 2024 were recruited. Umbilical cord serum testosterone levels were measured using ECLIA and LC-MS/MS. Sex differences in testosterone levels between males and females were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test for median values and interquartile ranges (IQRs) (p-value < 0.05). The Spearman's correlation analysis, a non-parametric method, was performed to evaluate the correlations between testosterone levels measured using ECLIA, and testosterone levels measured using LC-MS/MS. Method comparison between ECLIA and LC-MS/MS was performed using Passing-Bablok regression. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to assess the ability of testosterone levels measured using ECLIA and LC-MS/MS to predict sex of preterm infants with typical external genitalia, respectively.
RESULTS: This study included 38 preterm infants with typical external genitalia (16 males and 22 females). Testosterone levels measured using ECLIA were significantly higher and exhibited wider distributions (males: 1.10 ng/mL, IQR 0.90 - 2.69; females: 0.95 ng/mL, IQR 0.71 - 1.18) than those measured using LC-MS/MS (males: 0.210 ng/mL, IQR 0.164 - 0.327; females: 0.026 ng/mL, IQR 0.0112 - 0.0526) (p-value < 0.05). The correlation between testosterone levels measured using ECLIA and those measured using LC-MS/MS was weak (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient ρ(rho) < 0.5). In all infants, the Passing-Bablok regression yielded a slope of 0.082 and an intercept of -0.021 (Figure 3A), indicating limited agreement. Among preterm infants with typical external genitalia, the ROC curve analyses showed that LC-MS/MS had superior diagnostic accuracy than ECLIA, clearly differentiating males from females (area under the curve = 0.96 vs. 0.715, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: In preterm infants at birth, immunoassays (ECLIA) demonstrated limited accuracy in measuring serum testosterone levels. Therefore, we recommend using LC-MS/MS because of its superior precision, clearer sex differentiation, and greater clinical utility.

articles.title: A Comparative Study on Next-Generation Sequencing for the Detection of FLT3 Mutations in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: FLT3 mutations are frequently observed in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and serve as important prognostic markers. Next-generation sequencing (NGS), a recently adopted molecular diagnostic tool, enables comprehensive profiling of genetic alterations. This study investigated FLT3 mutations detected by targeted NGS in patients with AML and compared the findings with those obtained via fragment analysis or direct sequencing.
METHODS: A total of 185 patients were enrolled in the study, including 176 with newly diagnosed AML and 9 with relapsed AML. FLT3 mutations identified by targeted NGS were compared with the results from fragment analysis or direct sequencing.
RESULTS: Among newly diagnosed AML patients, the overall FLT3 mutation positivity rate was 28.4% (50/176), comprising 21.6% (38/176) for FLT3-ITD, 8.5% (15/176) for FLT3-TKD, and 3.4% (6/176) for non-ITD/TKD FLT3 mutations. Most FLT3-ITDs (36/38) were detected by both NGS and fragment analysis, demonstrating high concordance. Out of the four FLT3-ITDs identified by NGS in relapsed AML, two with low allele frequencies (0.1 and 1.0) were not detected by fragment analysis. Among the 15 FLT3-TKD-positive cases identified by NGS, five with low allele frequencies (3.85 - 12.91) were not detected by direct sequencing. In newly diagnosed AML, multiple FLT3-ITD, multiple FLT3-TKD, and dual FLT3-ITD-TKD mutations were observed in 4.0% (7/176), 1.1% (2/176), and 1.1% (2/176) of patients, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: NGS demonstrated high reliability and superior sensitivity compared to fragment analysis or direct sequencing for the detection of FLT3 mutations. Moreover, NGS provided additional genetic insights through its comprehensive mutational analysis.

articles.title: Diagnostic Challenges in Paediatric Pulmonary Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Paediatric lung nodules pose a diagnostic challenge due to a broad differential diagnosis and limited standardized evaluation guidelines. We present the case of a 12-year-old female with an incidentally discovered 27 mm calcified left pulmonary nodule during evaluation for chronic cough. She was asymptomatic at presentation, with an unremarkable examination and an extensive negative infectious, oncologic, and rheumatologic workup. Procedural challenges due to the proximity to the airway hilum, along with limited access to paediatric bronchoscopic expertise, necessitated multi-institutional coordination for surgical biopsy. Histopathology confirmed pulmonary mucoepidermoid carcinoma (PMEC), followed by lobectomy with negative margins and an excellent prognosis. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of paediatric lung nodules and the importance of multidisciplinary and cross-institutional coordination when procedural feasibility and specialized expertise limit diagnostic approach.

articles.title: Phenylketonuria worldwide: geographic genotype and phenotype structure, birth prevalence and newborn-screening context.
articles.abstract: Phenylketonuria (PKU), caused by phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) deficiency, comprises a continuum from mild hyperphenylalaninemia (MHP) to mild and classic PKU. We characterized the contemporary global geographic and epidemiological landscape of this spectrum using an international genotype-phenotype database and a structured synthesis of birth-prevalence and newborn-screening evidence. The database contained 24,718 unique anonymized individuals representing 4867 distinct biallelic PAH genotypes. Phenotype was classified in 24,470 individuals (99.0%); PheMax was available in 10,456 (42.3%), BH4 response in 4821 (19.5%), a valid country identifier in 23,750 (96.1%), and a valid region assignment in 24,027 (97.2%). Phenotype categories were source-derived; PheMax comparisons were treated as descriptive because untreated Phe concentrations may have contributed to the original phenotype assignments. Geographic genotype enrichment was assessed using minimum-count thresholds, leading-location share, location quotient, Fisher exact testing and false-discovery-rate correction; national genotype-frequency profiles were compared using cosine similarity with bootstrap, equal-size subsampling and alternative-metric sensitivity analyses. In the full dataset, classic PKU accounted for 58.3%, mild PKU for 22.2%, MHP for 18.4%, and phenotype was unavailable or invalid in 1.0%; 6599 individuals (26.7%) were homozygous. Five genotypes met conservative country-enrichment criteria and 14 met region-enrichment criteria, with prominent signals in Iran, Russia, Southern Asia, the Middle East and Eastern Europe. Country-profile analysis identified a Central/Eastern European cluster that was supported by resampling and Jensen-Shannon analysis, although attenuation after exclusion of the most frequent genotype indicated that the cluster was partly driven by a shared high-frequency genotype. The preferred regionally weighted global birth-prevalence estimate was 0.84 per 10,000 live births (approximately 1:11,905), but country-level comparability was limited by variation in screening coverage, thresholds and true-positive definitions. PKU displays marked geographic genotype and phenotype structure; database frequencies and country similarities should be interpreted as population-structure and ascertainment signals rather than unbiased national frequencies or directional migration evidence.

articles.title: Transformations in play. Dyadic work inspired by psychoanalytic infant observation.
articles.abstract: The article explores the psychoanalytic foundations of Watch Me Play! (WMP), an applied approach first developed to promote understanding of the needs of babies and young children in care, now more widely used to support parent-child relationships and child development. Watch Me Play! is derived from psychoanalytic infant observation and underpinned by key concepts in child development research such as mind-mindedness, joint attention and contingent responsiveness. The relevance of the central psychoanalytic concepts of attention and time in the thinking of Freud, Bion and Birksted-Breen is illustrated in clinical examples from work with the group for whom the approach was first developed: infants and young children who have experienced abuse, neglect and disrupted attachments, together with their foster carers or adoptive parents.

articles.title: Time in psychoanalysis.
articles.abstract: By recognizing the existence of conservative infantile amnesia, psychoanalysis introduced a new category of temporality: timelessness. The contents thus subjected to amnesia escape the influence of time. This unconscious psychic reality is established to counteract the regressive force emanating from the id, in order to fulfil a function: that of thwarting the tendencies to revert to a prior state, even to the inorganic, which are inherent in every drive, and to prevent the disappearance of libidinal cathexes into a 'traumatic timelessness'. Through the regression of sleep, dream work can use this tendency towards extinction to create new psychic content and regenerate narcissistic and object-related cathexis. The dream is the time machine, the fountain of youth available to human beings. The oscillation between experiences of disappearance and those of regeneration, between an endo-perception of discontinuity characterized by experiences of disappearance and eternity, lies at the origin of the notion of temporality, as well as of many devices designed to create the illusion of continuity. Extinction cannot be represented; it is perceived through the traumatic emotions of terror and anxiety. This is why time can only be embodied by the devices that measure it - that is to say, by a method consisting of retaining that which tends to disappear.

articles.title: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making.
METHODS: Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds.
RESULTS: Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

articles.title: Intraoperative active warming with or without active prewarming on maternal hypothermia in patients undergoing elective cesarean delivery with spinal anesthesia: A randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal hypothermia affects up to 60% of patients undergoing scheduled cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia and is associated with maternal and neonatal morbidity. Although intraoperative active warming is standard, the effect of preoperative warming to improve zero-flux core temperature remains unclear.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 78 women scheduled for cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia received intraoperative forced-air warming and warmed crystalloids. The active group received 20 min of preoperative forced-air warming. The primary outcome was zero-flux core maternal temperature on arrival to post-anesthesia care unit. Secondary maternal outcomes included intraoperative shivering and in post-anesthesia care unit, maternal hypothermia (core temperature < 36 °C), thermal comfort scores in post-anesthesia care unit, and neonatal temperature. The Mann-Whitney U test and the Chi-Square test were used for analysis.
RESULTS: Median with interquartile range [IQR] core temperature on arrival to post-anesthesia care unit did not differ between the active and control groups (36.6 °C [36.45-36.85] vs. 36.6 °C [36-36.75]; P = 0.99). Hypothermia incidence was 5.1% in the active group vs. 15.4% in the control group (P = 0.161). Shivering incidence was 10.3% in the active group vs. 28.2% in the control group (P = 0.06). Thermal comfort scores were significantly higher in the active warming group (52.05 ± 6.56 vs. 43.84 ± 10.91; P = 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: Adding 20 min of preoperative forced-air warming to active intraoperative warming did not significantly increase core temperature or reduce hypothermia upon arrival to post-anesthesia care unit. However, active pre-warming significantly improved maternal thermal comfort.

articles.title: Magnetic Ureteric Stents After Kidney Transplantation: A Systematic Review of Retrieval Success, Cystoscopy Avoidance, Safety, and Resource Utilization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ureteric stents are routinely used after kidney transplant to prevent urological complications; however, cystoscopic removal can be associated with discomfort and high costs, particularly in the pediatric population where general anesthesia is often required. Magnetic stents offer a novel method of bypassing cystoscopic retrieval. Here, we synthesized evidence on feasibility, safety, and service delivery of magnetic stents after kidney transplant.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA, evaluated magnetic ureteric stents in kidney transplant recipients. The primary outcome was successful non-cystoscopic stent retrieval. Secondary outcomes included failed retrieval, removal time, pain, quality of life, urinary tract infection, urological and transplant-specific complications, cost, and service delivery measures.
RESULTS: Our study included 9 studies: 2 randomized controlled trials, 2 prospective nonrandomized comparative studies or abstracts, 1 audit abstract, and 4 noncomparative cohort or feasibility studies. Seven studies involving 251 recipients reported extractable retrieval outcomes, with successful non-cystoscopic retrieval achieved in 244 cases, corresponding to a crude success rate of 97.2%. Need for cystoscopic rescue occurred in 7 of 251 cases. Removal times were short, and magnetic retrieval was well-tolerated. Comparative studies did not show clear superiority for pain, quality of life, or stent-related symptoms. No clear signal of increased urinary tract infections or urological complications was identified. Cost and service delivery outcomes generally favored magnetic stents when the full removal pathway was considered.
CONCLUSIONS: Magnetic ureteric stents after kidney transplant appear feasible, well-tolerated, and associated with high rates of successful non-cystoscopic retrieval. Main benefits appear to be cystoscopy avoidance, pathway simplification, and potential cost savings, rather than clear improvements in pain or quality-of-life. Current evidence is limited by small study sizes, heterogeneous designs, and incomplete reporting, thus remaining underpowered for transplant-specific outcomes. Magnetic stents may be useful in selected transplant pathways, provided that cystoscopic backup is available.

articles.title: Childhood and adolescent changes in sleep spindle trends across the night.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Sleep spindle trends across sleep cycles provide clues to factors that influence these distinct EEG waveforms. We describe cycle trends in spindle density, frequency, amplitude, and duration, and we determine how these trends change across childhood and adolescence. Furthermore, we test how the trends in spindle density are related to trends in slow wave (delta) EEG incidence.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A computer program detected and measured sleep spindles in central and frontal EEG from 1944 nights from our longitudinal dataset of semiannual recordings from 97 participants, ages 6-18 years.
RESULTS: Spindle density and duration increased steeply between cycles 1 and 2 with smaller increases across subsequent cycles. The magnitude of these increases decreased with age. The spindle density cycle trend was strongly related to the delta cycle trend, but the age-related change in the density trend was not related to changes in delta. Spindle wave frequency shifted from an increase across cycles in children to a u-shaped trend in older adolescents, whereas central spindle amplitude shifted from a u-shaped trend to a linear increase. The trends in frontal and central spindles were, on the whole, similar with exceptions suggesting later maturation of frontal circuits.
CONCLUSIONS: The age-related changes in sleep spindle measures across sleep cycles cannot be attributed solely to thalamocortical pruning but must also be affected by myelination and circuit reorganization. The age-related changes in cycle trends for spindle frequency indicate a shift from a strong homeostatic influence in children to greater circadian influence in late adolescence.

articles.title: Draft genome sequencing of Burkholderia cenocepacia strain DC660 isolated from a chronically colonized patient with cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: We have isolated the Burkholderia cenocepacia strain DC660 from a chronically colonized pediatric patient with cystic fibrosis to develop a bacteriophage-mediated decolonization treatment to improve candidacy for lung transplantation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed antimicrobial resistance genes, consistent with the multidrug resistance observed in antimicrobial susceptibility testing, as well as several prophage-associated regions.

articles.title: Achalasia Cardia Unmasking 4A Syndrome in an Adolescent.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achalasia cardia is an esophageal motility disorder characterized by impaired relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) and absent peristalsis, leading to progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Often isolated, achalasia can occur as part of rare syndromes such as 4A Syndrome, which includes achalasia, Addison's disease (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]-resistant adrenal insufficiency), alacrima, and autonomic dysfunction.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 15-year-old male presented with 1.5 years of progressive dysphagia, initially affecting liquids and later solids, along with retrosternal chest pain, regurgitation, and 6 kg weight loss. He had a history of recurrent dry eyes since birth and symptoms of fatigue, dizziness, and skin darkening over the past 2 years. Examination revealed diffuse hyperpigmentation, dry eyes, hyperemic conjunctivae, and bilateral weakness of ankle dorsiflexion with diminished ankle jerk. His BMI was 17.53 kg/m2, indicating undernutrition.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) raised clinical suspicion of achalasia cardia, demonstrating a dilated esophagus and a tight gastroesophageal junction; high-resolution manometry (HRM) confirmed the diagnosis. Corticosteroid and ACTH tests indicated ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease). Schirmer's test confirmed alacrima. Genetic testing revealed mutations in the AAAS gene, confirming 4A Syndrome. Nerve conduction studies showed motor axonal neuropathy.
TREATMENT AND OUTCOME: Pneumatic dilation with 30 and 35 mm balloons resulted in a reduction of the Eckardt score from 7 to 2. Hydrocortisone therapy (10 mg morning, 5 mg evening) improved skin manifestations and weakness. The patient gained 3 kg in weight over 6 months, indicating clinical improvement.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the rare co-occurrence of achalasia cardia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, alacrimia, and peripheral neuropathy in 4A Syndrome. Early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary treatment approach led to significant improvement, making this the first reported case of 4A Syndrome in India.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative Postpartum Bracelet Pilot.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of a pilot project implementing postpartum alert bracelets to support the timely identification and treatment of maternal complications.
DESIGN: Program evaluation.
SETTING/LOCAL PROBLEM: Seven urban, regional, and community hospitals in Alabama participating in the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative. Inconsistent recognition of recent childbirth status in emergency settings and limited retention of discharge education can delay diagnosis and treatment.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients who recently gave birth (n = 1,237), Mother-baby unit (MBU) nurse leaders (n = 10), emergency department (ED) nurses (n = 35), and emergency medical technicians (EMTs; n = 79).
INTERVENTIONS/MEASUREMENTS: The intervention included distribution of silicone postpartum alert bracelets designed for continuous wear, standardized patient education, and staff awareness efforts. Surveys assessed patient acceptance and perceived safety and ED nurses' and EMTs' awareness and perceived utility. Semistructured interviews explored nurse leaders' implementation experiences.
RESULTS: Patient acceptance was high (81.3% would wear; 79.9% felt safer). Compared with non-Hispanic White respondents, non-Hispanic Black respondents (odds ratio [OR] = 2.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.67, 2.43]) and Hispanic respondents (OR = 2.23, 95% CI [1.78, 2.68]) were more likely to report willingness to wear the bracelet and perceived safety benefits. Awareness was 100% among MBU nurse leaders, 40% among ED nurses, and 19% among EMTs. However, both ED nurses and EMTs agreed that the bracelets could support timely recognition of complications and potentially reduce maternal mortalities.
CONCLUSION: Postpartum alert bracelets are a promising, low-cost intervention highly accepted by patients. Statewide implementation requires standardized distribution and targeted education for patients, ED staff, and emergency medical services.

articles.title: Self-medication in dermatology: Prevalence, motivations, and associated risks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-medication in dermatology is a common practice, driven by the perceived benign nature of skin conditions and easy access to nonprescription treatments. However, it may lead to significant clinical risks.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence of dermatological self-medication and identify associated motivations, commonly used products, and related risks.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted between January and May 2025, using an anonymous online questionnaire. A total of 346 complete responses were analyzed.
RESULTS: Self-medication was reported by 68% of participants, predominantly young, female, urban, and highly educated individuals. The most frequent conditions were acne (57%), seborrheic dermatitis, hair loss, and eczema. Topical antibiotics (41%) and topical corticosteroids (28%) were the most commonly used products. The main motivations included consultation cost (42%) and perception of the condition as benign (34%). Adverse effects were reported by 26% of users, while medical consultation remained limited.
CONCLUSION: Dermatological self-medication is highly prevalent and associated with preventable risks, highlighting the need for improved patient education and public awareness strategies.

articles.title: Differential expression of PD-1 and CTLA-4 in vitiligo: A pilot case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitiligo is a chronic, acquired depigmentation disorder characterized by the progressive loss of functional melanocytes, potentially resulting from immune dysfunction. This destruction may be attributed to dysregulated T-cell-mediated immune activity. Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) and programmed death-1 (PD-1) function as immune checkpoints that suppress T-cell responses.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the mRNA (messenger ribonucleic acid) expression pattern of PD-1 and CTLA-4 in vitiligo patients.
METHODS: Thirty-four vitiligo patients and 16 control subjects were included in this pilot study. Blood samples were collected. Gene expression analysis of PD-1 and CTLA-4 was performed using relative quantitative real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction to assess mRNA levels of the target genes.
RESULTS: This study demonstrated significant downregulation of CTLA-4 mRNA and marked upregulation of PD-1 mRNA expression in patients with vitiligo compared with healthy controls. Moreover, expression patterns differed between vitiligo subtypes: CTLA-4 expression was significantly higher in segmental vitiligo (SV) than in non-segmental vitiligo (NSV), whereas PD-1 expression was considerably lower in SV than in NSV.
CONCLUSION: Elevated PD-1 and altered CTLA-4 mRNA expression in patients with vitiligo indicate a dysregulated immune checkpoint profile that may contribute to melanocyte-directed autoimmunity. Further studies are required to confirm their significance in the development or limitation of the disease.

articles.title: Treating hair loss related to pregnancy and lactation: A literature review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hair quality and quantity can be negatively affected during pregnancy and the postpartum period, including lactation, and the psychosocial effects can be profound. Common causes of hair loss in this period are androgenetic alopecia (AGA) and telogen effluvium (TE), which may be exacerbated by stress and hormonal shifts.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the safety of hair-targeted pharmacotherapies for AGA and TE during pregnancy and lactation.
METHODS: Guidelines from the United States Food and Drug Administration, Briggs Drugs in Pregnancy and Lactation, the American Academy of Pediatrics, Hale's Medications & Mothers' Milk, and the National Library of Medicine's Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed) were reviewed. Additionally, relevant articles were identified through PubMed using a combination of keywords, including treatment names, "hair loss," "alopecia," "pregnancy," "lactation," and "breastfeeding."
RESULTS: Topical minoxidil, oral spironolactone, and topical tretinoin may be used for AGA (and TE for topical minoxidil) during lactation, but not during pregnancy. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo is recommended for AGA in pregnancy or lactation but is unlikely to be effective for TE. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections may be considered for AGA or TE during pregnancy or lactation, but all 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs) or supplements with 5-ARI activity should be avoided. Vitamin D and iron supplements are recommended when deficiencies are present.
CONCLUSION: Hair loss during pregnancy and lactation is common and, despite often being temporary, can have a substantial psychosocial impact on quality of life and well-being. Several therapies may be considered, including topical treatments, supplements, and PRP, while others are not recommended owing to safety concerns or insufficient evidence.

articles.title: Distribution of Malassezia species in patients with atopic dermatitis and psoriasis on biological agents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malassezia yeasts are lipid-dependent fungi that normally colonize human skin but may contribute to inflammatory disorders such as atopic dermatitis (AD) and psoriasis through immune modulation. This study evaluates Malassezia species distribution in patients with AD and psoriasis undergoing biologic therapy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the distribution differences of Malassezia genes and species between the scalp and the face of patients undergoing biological therapies for the treatment of atopic dermatitis and psoriasis.
METHODS: This study included 60 patients, including 24 with AD and 36 with psoriasis. Samples were collected from the scalp and face using swabs. DNA was extracted from the samples, and 10 Malassezia species were detected using specific primers in a real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction.
RESULTS: Malassezia species were isolated from most patients with AD and psoriasis, with M. globosa being the predominantly isolated species in both groups. There was no significant difference in the distribution of Malassezia species between male and female patients. However, M. sympodialis and M. restricta were strongly associated with psoriasis.
CONCLUSION: There was no significant difference in the distribution of Malassezia species between male and female patients, skin with and without lesion, or among different treatment groups. However, there was a significant difference in the distribution M. restricta between patients with psoriasis and those with AD. This association was not sufficient enough to clearly establish the role of Malassezia species in psoriasis.

articles.title: Retinoids for the treatment of autosomal recessive or X-linked congenital ichthyosis: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital ichthyosis (CI) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by impaired skin barrier function, hyperkeratosis, and scaling. Severe subtypes, including autosomal recessive CI (ARCI) and X-linked recessive ichthyosis (XLRI), often require systemic retinoid therapy, which is associated with significant long-term adverse effects.
OBJECTIVE: To identify topical and oral retinoids reported as effective and safe in treating ARCI and XLRI.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review between November 1 and December 1, 2024, using the PubMed database. Studies reporting clinical outcomes and adverse effects of topical or oral retinoids in ARCI and XLRI were included. Data on disease type, treatment, patient outcomes, and adverse events were extracted.
RESULTS: Fifty studies were included, comprising 14 clinical trials or cohorts and 36 case reports. Topical retinoids, such as tazarotene and isotretinoin formulations, demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing scaling and improving skin quality with mild adverse effects like irritation. Oral retinoids, including acitretin and isotretinoin, were effective for severe cases but were associated with adverse skeletal and muscular effects. Systemic retinoids improved survival in neonates with Harlequin ichthyosis when initiated early.
CONCLUSION: Oral retinoids remain essential for severe cases but carry notable risks. Topical retinoids offer a safer alternative, with emerging formulations showing promise. Further research is needed to establish standardized treatment protocols.

articles.title: Metabolic risk factors on pediatric hidradenitis suppurativa: A retrospective multicenter cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder that affects a clinically significant proportion of pediatric patients. Metabolic syndrome has been associated with HS in adults; however, its influence on disease characteristics and healthcare utilization in pediatric populations remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the relationship between metabolic comorbidities and pediatric HS outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX collaborative network. Patients aged 0-18 years with an HS diagnosis were categorized into HS with metabolic components (HS+MetC) and HS alone (HS only). Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, and age at diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, treatment patterns, and healthcare utilization outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 4,392 HS+MetC and 3,783 HS only patients were identified prior to matching. HS+MetC patients were diagnosed at a younger age and were more likely to be Black/African American or Hispanic/Latino. After matching, HS+MetC patients demonstrated significantly higher rates of emergency department visits, ambulatory visits, hospitalizations, surgical interventions, and most therapeutic treatments.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric HS patients with metabolic comorbidities experience higher healthcare utilization and more intensive treatment needs. Early identification of metabolic risk factors may support earlier diagnosis, improved disease management, and reduce morbidity.

articles.title: Dyadic Self-Care Types Among Older Adults with Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease and Their Care Partners: A Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract: Although self-care is an essential component of the effective management of individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD), little is known about ways older adults and care partners navigate CKD self-care together. We conducted an exploratory mixed-methods study that qualitatively examined dyadic self-care typologies and quantitatively assessed self-care adequacy among 15 care dyads comprising an older adult with non-dialysis-dependent advanced CKD and their care partner. Most demonstrated within-dyad congruence by agreeing on the "collaborative" type. Compared to congruent dyads, incongruent dyads described reluctant shifts in established relationship patterns (e.g., parent-child role reversals). Patients achieved the cut-point for adequacy on each self-care scale, but care partners did not. Collectively, these initial findings provide novel insight into dyadic CKD self-care with the potential to inform the design and delivery of relevant interventions.

articles.title: Adapting the international classification of cognitive disorders in epilepsy to Shwachman diamond syndrome: a feasibility study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Shwachman Diamond syndrome (SDS; OMIM#260400) is a rare multisystemic ribosomopathy associated with prevalent inherent neuropsychological issues. Understanding cognitive phenotypes remains limited by disease rarity and substantial heterogeneity in neuropsychological performance. The International Classification of Cognitive Disorders in Epilepsy (IC-CoDE), provides an innovative approach to harmonize data using universal cognitive domains. We evaluated its adaptability for SDS (CoD-SDS) to better characterized cognitive phenotypes and support future international collaborative research and ultimately enable more precise patient care.
METHODS: IC-CoDE was adapted to address SDS-specific concerns. Using established IC-CoDE guidelines, we: determined impairment thresholds of -1 and -1.5 standard deviations for tests scores; defined domain disruption as impairment on two or more tests within each domain; and classified cognitive phenotypes based on the number of impaired domains. Neuropsychological data from 32 children with SDS were analyzed.
RESULTS: -1.0 and -1.5 SD thresholds revealed intact phenotypes in 1 and 9 patients. Single-, bi-domain, and generalized vulnerabilities were evident in 5 and 9, 8 and 4, and 18 and 10 patients, respectively. All patients with impairments showed vulnerabilities in executive functioning and/or attention/processing speed.
CONCLUSIONS: Applying a cognitive classification methodology to children with SDS accentuated individual performance and underscored the cognitive morbidity hidden by group means. This feasibility study supports the development of a consensus-based SDS classification system for larger international cohorts that could be harmonized through the SDS registries. Its implementation will be critical for defining the nature, frequency, severity, and correlates of cognitive vulnerabilities to inform precision health and achieve optimized outcomes.

articles.title: LZTR1 functions as a two-hit tumor suppressor in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
articles.abstract: LZTR1 negatively regulates RAS family proteins via proteasomal degradation. Germline loss-of-function variants cause Noonan syndrome, with emerging evidence implicating LZTR1 in predisposition to childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), though its role in hematopoiesis remains poorly defined. Screening of 1587 children with ALL identified LZTR1 variants in 44 patients (2.8%). Germline variants were detected in 32 patients (2.0%), a frequency comparable to that observed in the general population (1.75%; 1925/110,017; P = 0.50). Somatic LZTR1 alterations were identified in 22 patients (1.4%) and were predominantly bi-allelic, arising through either a germline-plus-somatic or a dual somatic configuration. They persisted at relapse. Despite enrichment in favorable-risk subtypes (ETV6::RUNX1, high hyperdiploid, and ERG/DUX4), bi-allelic LZTR1-mutated cases showed delayed minimal residual disease clearance and higher late relapse risk, identifying a subgroup unsuitable for treatment de-escalation. LZTR1 expression was increased in most wild-type leukemias, consistent with a compensatory response to aberrant RAS pathway activation. Bi-allelic LZTR1 inactivation abolished RAS regulation, leading to deregulated canonical RAS expression and ectopic expression of the non-canonical RIT1 protein, whose involvement in ALL has not previously been reported. These findings establish LZTR1 as a classical tumor suppressor in ALL via a two-hit model. Monoallelic alterations show insufficient signaling perturbation and low germline penetrance, whereas bi-allelic inactivation acts as a driver event linked to a high risk of late relapse despite favorable genomics.

articles.title: Early Childhood CASPR2 Autoimmunity with Prominent Autonomic Dysfunction: Diagnostic Challenges and Effective Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: CASPR2-associated neurological diseases cover a broad clinical spectrum, with limbic encephalitis and Morvan syndrome representing the most characteristic autoimmune phenotypes. We report the case of a 2-year-old boy who presented with abdominal and generalized pain, refusal to eat or drink, weight loss, loss of mobility, and behavioral changes, including sleep disturbances. Further clinical evaluation revealed pharmacoresistant arterial hypertension and hyperhidrosis. Extensive diagnostic testing excluded infectious and toxic causes. CASPR2 antibodies were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid. Initial therapy with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins resulted in only minimal clinical improvement. Significant clinical recovery was only achieved after escalation of immunotherapy with plasmapheresis and subsequent B-cell-depleting therapy with rituximab. At the most recent follow-up visit, seven months after the first rituximab infusion, the patient showed complete recovery without residual symptoms. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of CASPR2-associated autoimmunity in early childhood and highlights the importance of early recognition of this rare but treatable disease.

articles.title: A neonate with hepatosplenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopaenia, and a characteristic X-ray finding.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteopetrosis is a rare bone disorder with a wide clinical spectrum ranging from very mild to severe disease phenotypes that are fatal in the first year of life.
CASE REPORT: We report the clinical course of a neonate with a severe form of congenital osteopetrosis who presented to our hospital with hepatosplenomegaly, severe anemia and thrombocytopenia. The diagnosis was established by bone marrow biopsy, and confirmed by genetic analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: In addition to infectious, metabolic and malignant etiologies, it is important to take osteopetrosis congenita into the differential diagnosis in young children with profound hepatosplenomegaly.

articles.title: Oculogyric crisis as a nutritional recovery phenomenon in severe infantile vitamin B12 deficiency.
articles.abstract: Severe Infantile vitamin B12 deficiency classically presents with pallor, developmental delay or regression, skin hyperpigmentation and hair changes. Oculogyric crisis (OGC), a paroxysmal dystonic eye movement disorder usually linked to anti-dopaminergic drugs, has not been described in this condition. This case series reports four breastfed infants of vegetarian mothers with nutritional vitamin B12 deficiency who developed OGC within days of starting hydroxocobalamin therapy. All had macrocytic anemia, three showed very low serum B12 and elevated homocysteine, and maternal B12 deficiency was documented in two. Associated neurological manifestations included distal limb tremors, orofaciolingual dyskinesia and, characteristic "batwing" upper-limb dystonia in one child. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated cerebral atrophy with basal ganglia changes consistent with metabolic insult. OGC and other hyperkinetic movements resolved with continued vitamin B12 therapy and nutritional rehabilitation in three children, while one infant died due to aspiration unrelated to withdrawal of treatment. These observations suggest that OGC may represent a nutritional recovery phenomenon in infants with severe vitamin B12 deficiency.

articles.title: A Homozygous SLC39A8 p.Asn369Thr Variant in an Infant With Leigh-Like Encephalopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biallelic variants of SLC39A8 cause congenital disorders of glycosylation Type IIn (CDG-IIn, OMIM #616721), a rare autosomal recessive condition characterized by impaired manganese (Mn) transport, defective glycosylation, and secondary mitochondrial dysfunction. Affected infants present with developmental delays, hypotonia, seizures, and symmetric basal ganglia lesions on brain MRI.
CASE PRESENTATION: An 11-month-old girl, previously developmentally appropriate, presented with new-onset seizures and regression of motor and social milestones. Examination revealed global hypotonia, poor feeding, and faltered growth. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral, symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensities with restricted diffusion in the caudate nuclei, putamin, globi pallidi, subthalamic nuclei, and cerebral peduncles, with sparing of the dentate nuclei and no contrast enhancement. Whole exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous SLC39A8 variant, NM_001,135,146.2:c.1106A > C (p.Asn369Thr). Each parent was a heterozygous carrier, confirming autosomal recessive inheritance. This variant is absent from ClinVar and gnomAD and is currently classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). The clinical phenotype and neuroimaging pattern are compatible with SLC39A8-CDG; however, the identified variant remains a VUS, and biochemical confirmation could not be obtained because the relevant tests were unavailable. Confirmation would require functional studies. Supportive testing would include transferrin glycosylation analysis and blood manganese measurement; a normal conventional transferrin result alone would not exclude the diagnosis. If SLC39A8-CDG is confirmed, manganese and galactose supplementation should be considered only under specialist metabolic supervision with appropriate biochemical monitoring. This case suggests a possible phenotype-genotype association but does not establish the pathogenicity of p.Asn369Thr.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited.
RESEARCH QUESTION: In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation?
STUDY DESIGN: and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis.
RESULTS: When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type.
INTERPRETATION: In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

articles.title: School-Related Factors Associated with Oral Health Behaviors among Adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the associations of academic achievement and school stress with oral health behaviors among adolescents to inform school-based oral health education and preventive interventions implemented by dental hygienists.
METHODS: Using data from the 21st Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-Based Survey, this cross-sectional study included 54,170 middle and high school students. Oral health behaviors were defined as brushing teeth ≥3 times daily, brushing teeth before bedtime, and visiting a dentist within the past 12 months. The analyses adjusted for sex, grade level, household economic status, smoking history, and alcohol consumption as confounding variables. Data were analyzed using the Rao-Scott χ2 test and complex sample logistic regression.
RESULTS: Academic achievement was significantly associated with all evaluated oral health behaviors (p<0.001). Students with high academic achievement were more likely to brush their teeth ≥3 times daily (odd ratio [OR]=1.25), brush their teeth before bedtime (OR=1.14), and visit a dentist within the past 12 months (OR=1.52) compared with those demonstrating low academic achievement. School stress was significantly associated only with brushing teeth before bedtime; specifically, high levels of school stress correlated with a reduced likelihood of this behavior (OR=0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.77∼0.87).
CONCLUSION: Academic achievement served as a critical factor associated with all measured oral health behaviors, whereas school stress correlated selectively with brushing teeth before bedtime. These findings highlight the need for tailored, school-based oral health education and preventive interventions that account for students' school-related characteristics.

articles.title: Association between Sleep Quality and Perceived Oral Health among Adolescents: Analysis of the 2024 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined adolescent sleep satisfaction and its association with oral health.
METHODS: This study analyzed data from the 20th Youth Health Behavior Online Survey (2024), ultimately including 54,653 adolescents.
