Subjective oral symptoms were defined as tooth pain when consuming hot or cold foods or beverages, aching or throbbing tooth pain, and gum pain or bleeding within the past 12 months. Sleep-based fatigue recovery was assessed based on self-reported responses regarding the extent to which sleep during the past 7 days was sufficient to recover from fatigue. A complex sample design with weights, stratification, and clustering variables was used for analysis.
RESULTS: Female students, high school students, adolescents with lower parental education, and those reporting lower subjective economic status and academic performance were more likely to report insufficient sleep-related recovery and to experience oral symptoms (p<0.05). Insufficient sleep-related recovery was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of experiencing oral symptoms (odds ratio=1.538; 95% confidence interval: 1.471∼1.608).
CONCLUSION: Insufficient sleep is significantly associated with oral symptoms in adolescents. To improve oral health, interventions should address sleep-related breathing disorders and strengthen tobacco control strategies, while implementing programs to promote healthy sleep habits alongside existing oral health education.

articles.title: Subjective Mental Health and Oral Health of Korean Adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess the status of subjective oral health and mental health among Korean adolescents using data from the 2024 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-based Survey (KYRBS), and to examine the independent associations between mental health indicators and oral symptom experiences.
METHODS: Data were analyzed from the 20th KYRBS, comprising 54,653 adolescents. Subjective oral symptoms were categorized as: (I) tooth pain when consuming hot or cold food/beverages, (II) throbbing or aching tooth pain, and (III) gum pain or bleeding. Mental health variables included perceived stress, feelings of sadness or despair, and loneliness. All analyses accounted for the complex sampling design (weights, stratification, and clustering).
RESULTS: Among participants, 49.3% reported experiencing at least one oral symptom in the past year. Mental health issues were prevalent: stress (84.5%), sadness/despair (27.7%), and loneliness (55.6%). Adolescents reporting poor mental health had significantly higher prevalence of oral symptoms. Notably, loneliness showed the strongest association with oral symptoms (odds ratio=1.922, 95% confidence interval: 1.860∼1.985, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Poor subjective mental health was significantly associated with increased oral symptom experiences among adolescents. These findings underscore the importance of integrated health strategies that concurrently address mental and oral health to support the overall well-being of adolescents.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sacrococcygeal teratomas are the most common fetal teratoma. When ultrasonographic parameters deteriorate at early gestational ages at which preterm delivery is not feasible, intrauterine treatment methods have been indicated. This study aimed to assess the perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251238039). We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL for studies published from January 2000 through November 2025, with four or more participants reporting minimally invasive intrauterine interventions for sacrococcygeal teratoma. The primary outcome was fetal death; secondary outcomes included perinatal mortality and preterm birth. Risk of bias was assessed using Downs and Black.
RESULTS: Five studies met inclusion criteria (three retrospective cohorts and two case series; n=4-22 participants) across six countries. Procedures included radiofrequency ablation, percutaneous and fetoscopic laser ablation, cyst aspiration, and shunting. Fetal hydrops and cardiac compromise were the main indications for intervention. Among studies with a comparator group, survival ranged from 40.0-75.0 % in intervention groups vs. 12.5-100 % in expectant management. Neonatal mortality reached 50.0 % in two studies, and preterm birth before 32 weeks occurred in 25.0-100 % of intervention cases across the five studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive fetal procedures are a feasible option for fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma complicated by hydrops or cardiac compromise, but the available evidence is limited to small retrospective studies subject to severity-based selection bias and does not allow conclusions regarding their effect on survival. Preterm birth was frequent after intervention.

articles.title: Elongated Fibroepithelial Polyps of the Anterior Urethra With Prominent Elastic Fibers: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urethral fibroepithelial polyps are rare benign lesions, usually occurring in children and often arising from the posterior urethra; adult cases, particularly in the anterior urethra, are uncommon. To our knowledge, fibroepithelial polyps with prominent elastic fibers have not been specifically described.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man underwent right radical nephroureterectomy for renal pelvic urothelial carcinoma, requiring repeated rigid cystoscopic manipulation. Three months later, two elongated polyps, absent on preoperative cystoscopy, were found in the anterior urethra. They remained unchanged for 6 months and were resected concurrently with a recurrent bladder tumor. Histological examination showed fibrovascular cores covered by benign urothelium, with abundant elastic fibers on Elastica van Gieson staining.
CONCLUSION: Elongated anterior urethral fibroepithelial polyps with prominent elastic fibers may develop in adults, possibly in relation to urethral instrumentation, although causation cannot be established from a single case. Close cystoscopic observation, with resection when clinically indicated, appears reasonable.

articles.title: Frequency of sensitization and co-sensitization to foods and environmental allergens IgE-mediated in children and adults with suspected allergic disease at a Costa Rican hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prevalence and patterns of sensitization in children and adults with suspected allergic disease.
METHODS: A retrospective, descriptive, observational study based on the analysis of laboratory records from the San Juan de Dios Hospital in Costa Rica, involving patients evaluated for allergies between 2019 and 2024. Tests were performed on automated platforms; sensitization intensity was classified, and co-sensitization patterns were explored. Descriptive statistics were used for data analysis, calculating frequencies, proportions, and means. The chi-square (χ²) test was applied, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Co-sensitization was assessed using dual-positivity matrices and graphical analysis, including heat maps and network diagrams generated in Python using matplotlib, seaborn, and networkx.
RESULTS: A total of 1815 patients with specific IgE determinations were analyzed, and 64,889 tests were evaluated across the respective platforms. Females accounted for 73% of the cohort, and 28% were under 18 years of age. On average, each patient tested positive for 3 allergens. Dust mites were the most frequent (45%), followed by Hymenoptera and animal dander. Among children, sensitivity to shrimp (28%), milk (17%), and octopus (20%) was notable, whereas environmental sensitization predominated in adults. The most common combinations for co-sensitization were dust mites with animal dander and dust mites with shellfish.
CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms the distinct pattern of higher food sensitization in childhood and the predominance of aeroallergens in adults. The high prevalence of dust mite sensitization and the unexpected sensitization to Solenopsis (fire ant) venom reflect the influence of the tropical environment and underscore the need for further clinical studies to guide public health strategies.

articles.title: Congenital ovine goitre in northwestern Argentina: Clinicopathological and immunohistochemical characterization in natural cases.
articles.abstract: Congenital goitre is an important cause of neonatal mortality and reproductive losses in sheep raised in iodine-deficient regions. However, integrative clinicopathological studies remain scarce, particularly in South America. This study characterized congenital ovine goitre in a flock from northwestern Argentina through endocrine, morphometric, histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Serum total thyroxine (T4) concentrations were determined in 20 adult ewes and 22 neonatal lambs, and 14 lambs that died spontaneously underwent complete post-mortem examination with thyroid morphometry and tissue analysis. Serum T4 concentrations were significantly lower in lambs than in adult ewes (P <0.001), and thyroid enlargement showed a strong inverse correlation with circulating T4 concentrations (Spearman's ρ = -0.71, P <0.01). The thyroid weight:body weight ratio reached 21.14 g/kg, confirming marked thyroid enlargement. Histological examination identified both hyperplastic and colloidal goitre within the same flock. Hyperplastic goitres had a proliferating cell nuclear antigen index of 42.8% and a caspase-3 apoptotic area index of 2.6%, consistent with a predominance of follicular cell proliferation over apoptosis, whereas the colloidal goitre showed a contrasting profile compatible with an involutional stage. The combined findings strongly support iodine deficiency as the most likely cause of the outbreak and demonstrate that congenital ovine goitre may encompass different morphological and biological stages within the same flock. By integrating endocrine, morphometric, histopathological and immunohistochemical findings, this study provides a complementary characterization of naturally occurring ovine goitre in an endemic region and highlights the value of combining functional and tissue-based assessments for its diagnosis.

articles.title: Association between Prepregnancy Obesity and Adverse Birth Outcomes among Mississippi Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prepregnancy obesity is associated with increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including preterm birth and cesarean delivery. However, limited evidence exists from Mississippi-specific populations despite the state's high burden of obesity and adverse birth outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the association between prepregnancy obesity and adverse birth outcomes, including cesarean delivery and preterm birth, among Mississippi women.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study using data from the Mississippi Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System, 2016-2022. The exposure was prepregnancy obesity (BMI ≥30.0 kg/m2), and the outcomes were cesarean delivery and preterm birth. Multivariable logistic regression analyses estimated the crude ratios (ORs) and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for covariates.
RESULTS: This study showed that among Mississippi women with live births (7,016), 51.6% were primarily White, and 53.4% were unmarried. About 57.3% had higher school education, 42.0% earned ≤$20,000 annually, and 77.5% had insurance before pregnancy. There was a statistically significant association between prepregnancy obesity and cesarean delivery in all the models. Mississippi women with prepregnancy obesity had higher odds of cesarean delivery (AOR = 2.09; 95% CI: 1.86 - 2.42) compared to women without obesity, after adjusting for covariates. Although prepregnancy obesity was associated with preterm birth in the unadjusted analyses (OR = 1.29; 95% CI: 1.11 - 1.51), but the association was not statistically significant after adjusting for covariates (AOR = 1.10; 95% CI: 0.93 - 1.31).
CONCLUSION: Prepregnancy obesity is an independent predictor of cesarean delivery among women in Mississippi. These findings may inform public health practitioners and policymakers in developing interventions that promote preconception weight screening and obesity prevention.

articles.title: No impact of gluten-free diet on glycemia, growth, or quality of life in asymptomatic celiac disease with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Evidence is limited on longitudinal health outcomes with a gluten-free diet (GFD) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and asymptomatic celiac disease (CD) identified by screening.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of the GFD on glycemic management, anthropometrics, gastrointestinal symptoms, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and nutritional intakes in patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.
METHODS: Celiac Disease and Diabetes Longitudinal Follow-up and Evaluation Study (CD-LiFE) was a prospective follow-up study (NCT03122093) whereby 62 participants aged 8-45 years (77% adult, 23% pediatric) with T1D and screen-detected CD were evaluated annually over a 2-year study period.
RESULTS: 51.6% of participants were GFD-adherent (daily gluten intake < 10 mg) at study baseline. After 2 years, rates of GFD adherence increased (72.7%) with only 15.2% transitioning to a gluten-containing diet (GCD). No differences were seen in mean HbA1c levels between individuals on a GFD and GCD (Δ = 0.1%; 95% CI: -0.6 to 0.4; P = .613, weight (Δ = 0.2 kg/m2; 95% CI: -2.3 to 2.8; P = .848) or BMI among adults (Δ = -1.1 kg/m2; 95% CI: -0.4 to 0.6; P = .149) nor BMI Z scores among pediatric participants (Δ = 0.91; 95% CI: -0.34 to 2.16; P = .136), number of acute GI symptoms (IRR = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.6 to 1.5; P = .810) nor longitudinal differences in HRQoL with respect to generic (Δ = -0.4; 95% CI: -4.0 to 3.3; P = .840) nor diabetes-specific HRQoL (Δ = 1.5; 95% CI: -2.9 to 5.9; P = .505).
CONCLUSION: This 2-year follow-up study demonstrates adherence to a GFD does not impact glycemic control, anthropometrics, GI symptom development, or HRQoL in adult and pediatric patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.

articles.title: Current Status of Fetal Cardiac Care in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology Perspective: A Consensus Statement on Behalf of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology.
articles.abstract: Fetal cardiology has become an important subspecialty in Pediatric Cardiology. It includes prenatal detection of congenital heart defects and arrhythmia as well as prenatal therapeutic procedures, planning of perinatal management, and the important part of parental counseling. Currently available methods to diagnose congenital heart disease prenatally, major requirements for parental counseling, available prenatal treatment options, and perinatal care of fetuses and newborns are outlined. A risk-stratified level of care classification system is proposed. This consensus statement of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology gives an overview about the current status of fetal cardiology in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology perspective emphasizing that detection rates in Germany stay behind in international comparison due to the minimal requirement of displaying a 4-chamber-view only in screening guidelines according to the "Mutterschaftsrichtlinie." We require mandatory views of the outflow tracts and the 3-vessel-trachea view in the 19 to 22 weeks' examination.

articles.title: Sport-related concussion.
articles.abstract: Sport-related concussion (SRC) is an issue affecting common clinical practice across medical specialties. Accurate diagnosis, therapy, and prevention are essential for acute management and the athlete's long-term health. The sixth international consensus statement on SRC (Amsterdam 2022) introduced updated tools for recognition and assessment: the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool-6 (SCAT6) and the Sport Concussion Office Assessment Tool-6 (SCOAT6) - both available in pediatric versions. These tools incorporate strategies for Return-to-Sport and Return-to-Learn. However, other reliable diagnostic methods for recognizing SRC are lacking. In this context, the significance of neuronal and glial damage biomarkers (e. g., GFAP, UCH-L1, NfL, tau) is being investigated. Thanks to ultrasensitive technologies, these can be measured at low concentrations even in peripheral blood. These biomarkers have the potential to improve diagnosis, monitoring, risk stratification, and return-to-sport decision-making. However, their routine use is not yet part of standard care for injured athletes. The aim of this article is to provide an overview of current international recommendations and the current state of the art in the field of SRC based on global consensus. The goal is to familiarize the reader with these recommendations, provide practical guidance for the care of athletes with this injury, and present the risks that SRC entails even in the long term.

articles.title: Variant interpretation and reporting approaches in the GUARDIAN study of genomic newborn screening.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate and scalable variant interpretation is a critical component of genomic newborn screening (gNBS).
METHODS: As part of ongoing quality improvement efforts in GUARDIAN, we compared our originally reported GUARDIAN results for group 1 sequence variants, including select variants of uncertain significance, with an alternative, easily scalable analysis that limited variants to ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic consensus variants. Additionally, the phase for 2 heterozygous variants in the same gene was predicted using the gnomAD co-occurrence tool. Results were categorized as true positive or false positive based on orthogonal testing and clinical assessments.
RESULTS: Among the first 12,500 enrolled infants, the original GUARDIAN analysis reported a total of 319 variants, while the alternative analysis identified 292 variants. Using the gnomAD variant co-occurrence tool, 70% of identified variant pairs had predicted phasing with an accuracy of 97%. The original GUARDIAN analysis was 97.5% sensitive and 99.6% specific, while the alternative analysis was 98.6% sensitive and 99.9% specific. When G6PD cases were excluded, the original GUARDIAN analysis was more sensitive (97%) than the alternative analysis (91.1%). Variants in several actionable conditions, including hypothyroidism, Wilson disease, and adenosine deaminase deficiency, were not prioritized for return in the alternative analysis. Eleven cases harbored variants not previously reported in ClinVar; 10 of these were in individuals of non-European ancestry.
CONCLUSION: Restricting gNBS variant interpretation to ClinVar consensus pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants can improve specificity but at the cost of missing clinically actionable diagnoses. Balanced interpretation frameworks that integrate multiple evidence sources are essential to optimize sensitivity while enabling scalable gNBS.

articles.title: Parental experience and satisfaction receiving genomic sequencing results in safety-net NICUs.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evaluate parents' understanding, satisfaction, and experiences receiving rapid genomic sequencing results from neonatologists with varying levels of genetics support.
METHODS: Using a mixed-methods approach, we examined the perspectives of English- and Spanish-speaking parents with infants in safety-net neonatal intensive care units enrolled in the Virtual Genome Center for Infant Health study. Parents received disclosures of rapid genomic sequencing results from neonatologists with or without genetics experts present. We surveyed parents within 35 days after the disclosure event and conducted semistructured interviews with a subset of parents. We used descriptive statistics for survey results and analyzed interviews iteratively until thematic saturation was reached.
RESULTS: Of 389 parents, 196 (50%) completed the survey (172 English, 24 Spanish), and 28 parents participated in an interview (23 English, 5 Spanish). Of the 196 respondents, 179 (91%) reported that the amount of information provided in the disclosure was "just right," and 168 (86%) indicated they understood the results mostly or very well. The rate of understanding "very well" was lower for positive results than for negative results and variants of uncertain significance. Qualitative analysis demonstrated that parents appreciated rapid access to genetic information, perceived neonatologists as highly competent in delivering disclosure results, and trusted neonatologists because of their familiarity with their infant's medical course. Parents valued the convenience of how the disclosure occurred (virtual or in person at the bedside).
CONCLUSION: Parents in neonatal intensive care units reported positive and satisfactory experiences receiving rapid genomic sequencing results from a neonatologist. These findings support a health care model in which neonatologists with variable genetics expertise provide disclosures for rapid genomic sequencing with virtual support.

articles.title: Paradigm-shifting MECP2 findings from genomic newborn screening: What population-based screening teaches us about Rett syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Genome sequencing is increasingly being implemented in research studies to evaluate its role in newborn screening. Early Check, a statewide, consented study in North Carolina, offers genomic newborn screening (gNBS) to evaluate both the feasibility and implications of population-based sequencing for actionable childhood-onset conditions.
METHODS: Using residual dried blood spots from public health newborn screening, Early Check performed genome sequencing for approximately 200 genes, including MECP2, associated with Rett syndrome and related neurodevelopmental phenotypes. Infants with pathogenic variants received confirmatory testing and family follow-up.
RESULTS: Three infants were identified with pathogenic MECP2 variants among 5143 screened, representing an unexpectedly high prevalence compared with published estimates. Parental testing revealed 2 previously unrecognized adult females who were heterozygous for a pathogenic variant and an unprecedented case of paternal transmission of a pathogenic MECP2 variant. These findings raise important questions about penetrance, inheritance, and counseling for families identified through gNBS.
CONCLUSION: gNBS can uncover unexpected genetic and inheritance patterns, including asymptomatic individuals with pathogenic variants and novel transmission events. Although based on a limited sample, these results highlight both the potential and complexity of incorporating genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, such as MECP2, into population-based gNBS programs.

articles.title: Clinical presentation of Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch in an adolescent.
articles.abstract: We describe a 14-year-old boy (weight 32 kg, height 148 cm), who was brought to a tertiary care facility in North India, with complaints of progressive exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, and chest pain with a recent episode of moderate haemoptysis. Imaging findings include Chest PA-view demonstrated cardiomegaly with abnormal great vessel contour, prominent superior mediastinal shadow, and increased bilateral pulmonary vascular markings, suggestive of a single large arterial outflow tract. Similarly, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a large outlet ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a dilated single arterial trunk overriding the defect. Cardiac CT angiography confirmed a large outlet VSD and an interrupted aortic arch, with no continuity between the ascending and descending aorta. The right and left pulmonary arteries, descending aorta, and left subclavian artery arose directly from the truncal vessel, while a separate ascending aorta bifurcated into the right brachiocephalic and left common carotid arteries. This particular case brings a remarkably unusual paediatric presentation with Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch and emphasises the effects of late diagnosis. Due to the patient's severe pulmonary arterial hypertension, palliative care was the only option for treatment, and definitive surgical repair was not feasible.

articles.title: Association Between Lifestyle Habits, Anxiety Levels, and Bruxism-Related Signs in Undiagnosed Adults.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Bruxism-related signs and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) symptoms may occur even in individuals without a formal diagnosis of bruxism or temporomandibular disorders (TMD). This study aimed to investigate the association between lifestyle habits, anxiety levels, and bruxism-related clinical signs in adults without a prior diagnosis, and to determine whether these associations persisted after adjusting for potential confounding factors.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: This cross-sectional study included 188 adults aged 18-60 years attending routine dental examinations with no previous diagnosis of bruxism or TMD. Clinical findings, including occlusal tooth wear, TMJ pain, maxillofacial pain, joint sounds during mouth opening, and parafunctional signs, were recorded. Individuals completed a questionnaire assessing smoking status, alcohol and coffee consumption, exercise habits, antidepressant use, and anxiety levels using the Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale. Categorical variables were analysed using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests (p 0.05). Multivariate binary logistic regression models, adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, alcohol use, coffee consumption, antidepressant use, exercise status, and anxiety category, were subsequently constructed for each clinical sign to account for potential confounding.
RESULTS: Occlusal tooth wear was significantly associated with older age and higher smoking frequency, and remained independently associated with older age and smoking status after adjustment. Morning TMJ pain and higher-frequency smoking were also significantly associated after standardising cigarette consumption into clinically interpretable ranges, although this association did not persist after multivariate adjustment. Stress-related headaches were more common in women and in individuals with higher coffee consumption, and these associations persisted after adjustment. Antidepressant use was associated with increased TMJ pain, maxillofacial pain, and occlusal tooth wear in bivariate analysis; after multivariate adjustment, the associations with TMJ pain and maxillofacial pain remained significant, while the association with occlusal tooth wear was attenuated, suggesting it may be partly explained by the older age of antidepressant users. The bivariate association between older age and TMJ pain similarly did not persist after adjustment for antidepressant use. Anxiety severity was significantly associated only with stress-related headaches.
CONCLUSION: Bruxism-related signs may be present in undiagnosed individuals. Lifestyle-related factors and antidepressant use showed independent associations with specific objective clinical findings after adjustment for confounders, whereas anxiety severity was more strongly related to subjective symptoms such as stress-related headache. These findings underscore the value of multivariate analysis in disentangling overlapping lifestyle, pharmacological, and demographic contributors to bruxism-related signs.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation in patients with severe oligodontia associated with ectodermal dysplasia: A retrospective case series with a follow-up period of up to 30 years.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oral rehabilitation in patients with ectodermal dysplasia is complex due to severe oligodontia and extreme alveolar ridge atrophy. This retrospective case series aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for the oral rehabilitation of patients with ectodermal dysplasia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 13 patients (8 men and 5 women; mean age 20.5 ± 1.9 years) with severe oligodontia (mean 18.4 ± 4.4 missing teeth) were included. The cohort included 12 cases of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia and one case of Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome. The protocol consisted of orthodontic treatment until skeletal maturity, restoration of the vertical dimension of occlusion via fixed temporary restorations supported by natural teeth and/or interim implants, 3D bone reconstruction using autogenous bone (iliac crest or intraoral bone blocks) via the split bone block technique, and placement of dental implants followed by definitive prosthetic rehabilitation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were assessed over an observation period of 14.4 ± 7.0 years (median 13 years; range 5 to 30 years).
RESULTS: A total of 147 implants were placed (79 in the maxilla and 68 in the mandible). All patients were successfully rehabilitated with fixed implant-supported prosthetics. Three patients were lost to follow-up (non-attendance) after a mean observation period of 19.0 ± 3.6 years. The implant survival rate was 100% over the entire observation period. All grafts integrated successfully. Five patients required secondary free gingival grafts to manage soft tissue shrinkage. At the final follow-up, all sites were free of inflammation with stable marginal bone levels.
CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this small patient cohort, the described approach, consisting of orthodontic treatment, fixed provisionalisation, autogenous bone augmentation and implant placement at skeletal maturity, demonstrated high long-term predictability, even in patients with Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome.

articles.title: Hyperlipidemia: Pharmacotherapy for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction in Adults.
articles.abstract: Hyperlipidemia management is key to overall cardiovascular risk reduction. Validated risk calculators, including the updated PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation and Pooled Cohort Equations, should be used to guide lipid-lowering therapy in adults without known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Lipid-lowering medications have shown benefit for primary and secondary prevention of ASCVD, supported by guidelines from the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association, US Department of Veterans Affairs/US Department of Defense, and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Statins remain first-line agents for primary and secondary prevention, with consistent evidence demonstrating reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events, myocardial infarction, stroke, and all-cause mortality. Statin therapy is recommended for primary prevention in adults 40 to 75 years of age with diabetes, chronic kidney disease stage 3 or higher, or HIV; in patients with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels of 190 mg/dL or greater; and in those with elevated 10-year ASCVD risk. Current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guidelines expand the recommendation to 30 to 79 years of age. Nonstatin therapies should be considered in patients who cannot tolerate statins or do not achieve adequate low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction. Adjunctive therapies may be appropriate for secondary prevention in certain patients. Older adults, younger adults with elevated lifetime risk, and patients of childbearing potential require special considerations. Lipid-lowering therapy should be individualized based on risk assessment, guideline thresholds, and shared decision-making.

articles.title: 2026-2027 Influenza, RSV, and SARSCoV-2 Immunization Recommendations for Nonpregnant, Immunocompetent Adults and Health Care Personnel.
articles.abstract: This immunization guidance from the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP) addresses nonpregnant, immunocompetent adults 19 years and older and health care personnel. For other populations, see guidance from the American Academy of Pediatrics (for individuals 18 years and younger), Infectious Diseases Society of America (for individuals with immunocompromise), and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (for pregnant individuals). Recommendations in this document are guided by the AAFP Adult Immunization Schedule. Where AAFP guidance differs from other organizations, the AAFP recommendation should be followed. AAFP immunization recommendations are reviewed and approved annually.

articles.title: Measles: Rapid Evidence Review.
articles.abstract: Measles is one of the most contagious, vaccine-preventable viral infections, capable of infecting up to 90% of exposed nonimmune people. Respiratory droplets and aerosols from people infected with measles remain infectious for up to 2 hours. Infection in unvaccinated people can lead to hospitalization and death. Approximately 1 to 3 of every 1,000 children with measles will die from complications. Measles-mumps-rubella vaccination is highly safe and effective at reducing infection risk and preventing community spread. Population-based studies have found no association between vaccination and autism spectrum disorder or other neurodevelopmental disorders. Although measles has been considered eliminated in the United States since 2000, outbreaks have recently become larger and more common because vaccination rates in many states and counties have fallen below herd immunity thresholds. Symptoms include cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and fever, followed by erythematous maculopapular exanthem. Family physicians play a key role in increasing vaccination rates and reducing risk of community spread through appropriate suspicion, early diagnostic testing, and isolation of people who are infected. Vitamin A supplementation may reduce mortality rates in hospitalized children with severe or complicated measles but should be used only under medical supervision to avoid toxicity; it should be avoided during pregnancy. Management of measles outbreaks requires isolating people who have been exposed or infected, discerning which people who were exposed have presumed immunity, and providing postexposure prophylaxis to nonimmune people with vaccination or immunoglobulin infusion.

articles.title: Prevention and Treatment of Drowning.
articles.abstract: Drowning is a major cause of injury-related deaths worldwide. Drowning causes approximately 4,300 deaths annually and is a leading cause of death in children 1 to 4 years of age in the United States. Other risk factors include male sex, poor swimming ability, inadequate supervision, not using a personal flotation device, and alcohol consumption during aquatic activities. Drowning typically causes respiratory arrest before cardiac arrest; therefore, conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation with rescue breathing is recommended. Initial management focuses on airway support, artificial ventilation, high-concentration oxygenation, and cervical spine immobilization if spinal trauma is suspected. Diagnostic evaluation is guided by clinical severity, and the primary focus should be respiratory function. Prevention strategies involve physical, behavioral, medical, and community and government methods. Evidence-supported methods include enclosed pool fencing, consistent use of properly fitted personal flotation devices, alcohol avoidance during aquatic activities, attentive supervision of children (including touch supervision for nonswimmers), and swimming lessons for children older than 1 year.

articles.title: Impact of co-occurring maternal nicotine use, depression, and anxiety on perinatal outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nicotine is the most commonly used substance in pregnancy, and the prevalence of mental health disorders in pregnancy is rising. In this study, we analyzed the association of nicotine use and depression and/or anxiety disorders, separately and together, on perinatal outcomes, an understudied area.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using California linked vital statistics and hospital discharge data (2008-2020). Patients were categorized into eight categories: (1) no nicotine use or depression or anxiety (reference), (2) nicotine use only, (3) depression only, (4) anxiety only, (5) depression and anxiety, (6) nicotine use and depression, (7) nicotine use and anxiety, and (8) nicotine use with depression and anxiety. The maternal outcomes measured were hypertensive disease of pregnancy, preterm delivery <37 and <32 weeks, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), and non-transfusion SMM; while the neonatal outcomes were neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, small for gestational age (SGA), respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), infant deaths, and hypoglycemia. We included 4,897,855 singleton, non-anomalous gestations delivered between 23 and 42 weeks and excluded individuals using other substances or diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Results were analyzed by chi-square tests and multivariable Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: Of the pregnant individuals included in this study, nicotine use was present in 1.4%, depression alone in 1.1%, anxiety alone in 1.2%, and combined depression and anxiety in 1.2%. Among maternal outcomes, SMM demonstrated a statistically significant association with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 2.20 [1.29-3.75]). Hypertensive disease was higher in groups with anxiety: only anxiety (15.3%), depression and anxiety (15.4%), and nicotine and anxiety (15.4%) compared to the reference group (7.7%). Among neonatal outcomes, infant death (aRR, 3.96 [1.66-9.46]), RDS (aRR, 2.03 [1.20-3.43]), and hypoglycemia (aRR, 1.67 [1.82-3.92]) were each significantly associated with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety. No other statistically significant increase in groups with nicotine use, depression, and anxiety were found in the other outcomes measured across the statistical analyses used.
CONCLUSION: Nicotine and depression/anxiety combined was associated with a higher risk of SMM, RDS, hypoglycemia, and infant death than each alone. These data can inform mechanistic research into the interaction between nicotine and mental health on perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: Non-invasive risk stratification of congenital cytomegalovirus infection using extracellular vesicle biomarkers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is one of the most common infections during pregnancy and can result in congenital CMV (cCMV) infection and long-term sequelae. In utero diagnosis of cCMV requires amniocentesis. In this nested case-control study, we investigated the use of fetal neuronally derived extracellular vesicles (fNEVs) in maternal circulation to characterize fetal brain alterations following primary maternal infection and evaluate their association with cCMV infection and disease severity.
METHODS: We used stored plasma samples from women enrolled in a multicenter randomized trial of CMV hyperimmune globulin (CMV-HIG) (n = 98). We isolated fNEVs from maternal plasma prior to treatment randomization (Gestational age: 20.04 ± 4.2 weeks) and 8 weeks later, and measured EV biomarkers of neuronal injury/injury response: synaptopodin (SYNPO) and Bcl-2-associated factor 1 (BCLAF1), both normalized to the EV marker CD81. We assessed the associations of these biomarkers with neonatal infection or symptomatic status using generalized linear mixed models and predictive performance analysis.
RESULTS: Fetal CMV infection was associated with higher pre-randomization levels of fNEV SYNPO (p = 0.001) and BCLAF1 (p = 0.040). BCLAF1 levels were also higher in symptomatic subjects (p = 0.029) pre-randomization. The combined SYNPO/BCLAF1 model demonstrated modest discrimination for fetal infection (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.713; 95% confidence interval [CI] = [0.612, 0.815]). We observed a decrease in SYNPO levels over time in symptomatic cCMV (p = 0.006). In symptomatic subjects those exposed to CMV-HIG had higher SYNPO levels than the placebo group (p = 0.004). Commonly, acute injury is associated with decreased levels of SYNPO, while increased SYNPO suggests a chronic response/repair state. Taken together, our findings suggest that noninvasive risk-stratification of CMV infection/symptomatic infection may be possible with testing refinement.

articles.title: Menstrual Disorders: Premenopausal Abnormal Uterine Bleeding.
articles.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding is a common and distressing concern for reproductive-aged females, potentially leading to long-term consequences such as iron deficiency anemia if not properly addressed. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics defines abnormal uterine bleeding as bleeding occurring outside the normal frequency of every 24 to 38 days, with additional criteria based on cycle length, regularity, and flow volume. Etiologies are classified using the PALM-COEIN system, which separates structural causes (polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, and malignancy and hyperplasia) from nonstructural causes (coagulopathy, ovulatory dysfunction, endometrial disorders, iatrogenic factors, and conditions not otherwise classified). Transvaginal and transabdominal Doppler ultrasonography are the recommended initial diagnostic modalities for structural etiologies, and magnetic resonance imaging may be used if findings are inconclusive. Endometrial sampling is indicated in patients at increased risk for endometrial pathology, including those with obesity, chronic anovulation, a family history of malignancy, or age of 45 years or older. Management options include medical and surgical therapies. The levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system is a highly effective medical treatment, whereas hysterectomy remains the most definitive option, particularly for patients who have completed childbearing. Medical management adequately controls symptoms for many, although structural conditions often require procedural or surgical intervention.

articles.title: Moisturizer Pearls and Pitfalls: From Routine Recommendation to Patient-Centered Precision.
articles.abstract: Advising patients to moisturize is among the most reflexive recommendations in dermatology, yet moisturizers are not interchangeable, are not appropriate in every clinical context, and can themselves cause irritation, sensitization, or occlusion-related adverse effects. As marketing claims such as "hypoallergenic" and "for sensitive skin" are unreliable, this brief report reviews moisturizer fundamentals-humectants, emollients, and occlusives, along with the surfactants/emulsifiers, preservatives, and functional/bioactive additives that accompany them-and provides practical, patient-centered recommendations for normal skin, infants, eczematous dermatitis, infection, and other dermatoses. Routine daily moisturization has no clearly established benefit in healthy, asymptomatic skin; infant emollient trials aimed at atopic dermatitis prevention have yielded conflicting results; and most best-selling moisturizers contain at least 1 common contact allergen. Also warranting consideration are the impact of vehicle choice on drug delivery, increased susceptibility to irritants and allergens due to an impaired barrier, potential aggravation of follicular disorders by occlusive formulations, barrier protection in moisture-associated dermatitis, and cautious use of exfoliating actives in vulnerable skin types and conditions. Selecting a moisturizer deserves the same scrutiny given to prescribing a topical medication.

articles.title: Fragrance Safety in Atopic Dermatitis: A Clinical Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate fragrance safety in atopic dermatitis (AD), with a focus on regulatory definitions, labeling practices, allergen exposure, and the clinical implications of synthetic and natural fragrance ingredients.
METHODS: A structured PubMed and Google Scholar search for relevant articles on clinical implications of fragrance and scented ingredients in AD was conducted using the search terms "fragrance," "atopic dermatitis," "contact dermatitis," "essential oils," "botanicals," and "sensitive skin." Regulatory guidance from the United States Food and Drug Administration, International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients, and the National Eczema Association was also reviewed.
RESULTS: Fragrances are complex mixtures of natural and synthetic compounds and are a common cause of allergic contact dermatitis in both adults and children. Terms such as "unscented," "fragrance-free," or "no fragrance added" remain poorly standardized and may mislead patients. Additionally, natural compounds are not inherently "safe," as they can trigger adverse reactions.
LIMITATIONS: Inconsistent product labeling, variability in product formulations, and limited patch testing panels impede allergen identification.
CONCLUSION: Optimizing patient outcomes requires standardized fragrance labeling, exploring naturally scented ingredients, and greater product transparency.

articles.title: GLOBAL CLINICO-EPIDEMIOLOGIC CHARACTERISTICS OF OCULAR CANCER AND ITS IMPLICATIONS FOR GLOBAL HEALTH POLICY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ocular cancer refers to a group of rare but serious malignancies that affect the eye and its surrounding structures. Although ocular cancers account for less than 0.1% of all cancers globally, they represent a significant public health challenge because of their impact on vision, quality of life, and overall patient?s survival. The most common forms are retinoblastoma in children and uveal melanoma in adults.Improving global outcomes requires integrating ocular cancer control into broader health policies, expanding research, and specialist care capacity. Stronger collaboration and equitable access to eye cancer care can reduce disparities and improve survival.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review underlines the global epidemiology of ocular cancer and discusses its implications for global health policy.
METHODS: This narrative review utilized secondary data sources obtained through a thorough literature search of relevant articles on multiple electronic databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, and Web of Science. All published books, journal articles, and other published materials that were written in English were reviewed for the purpose of this study.
RESULTS: The global burden of ocular cancer is rising, influenced by longer life expectancy, increased ultraviolet radiation exposure, genetic mutations, and unequal access to healthcare services. Key risk factors include inherited mutations such as RB1, BAP1, and TP53, viral infections like HPV and Epstein?Barr virus, immunosuppression, fair skin pigmentation, and environmental conditions. Preventive measures include the use of UV-protective eyewear, early screening, public health education, and genetic counselling.Diagnosis relies on advanced imaging, histopathology, and molecular testing to guide personalized treatment. Management typically requires a multidisciplinary team involving ophthalmologists, oncologists, pathologists, and radiologists. The treatment includes surgery, chemo-radiation therapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Importantly, the role of research in limiting burden and improving care cannot be overemphasized.
CONCLUSION: Although ocular cancers are rare, they are associated with significant morbidity. Therefore, modern diagnostics and therapeutic techniques are hugely required for better treatment outcome.

articles.title: ENABLING FACTORS FOR THE OPTIMAL VACCINATION OF INFANTS OF ADOLESCENT MOTHERS IN URBAN SLUM COMMUNITIES IN IBADAN, NIGERIA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants of adolescent mothers often have suboptimal vaccination, exposing them to vaccine preventable diseases and the attendant morbidities and mortalities. Understanding the factors that contribute to the optimal vaccination of infants of deviant adolescent mothers could provide insights which may be valuable in addressing poor vaccine uptake among infants of adolescent mothers in disadvantage settings.
AIM: This study explored the enabling factors for optimal vaccination of infants of deviant adolescent mothers living in urban slum communities of Ibadan, Nigeria.
METHODS: Exploratory qualitative study with embedded design was used. Twelve deviant adolescent mothers whose infants were fully vaccinated had in-depth interviews. Data were transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis guided by the attitude-social influence-self efficacy model.
RESULTS: Mean age of participants was 17.92?1.08 years, 2(16.7%) were married, and 8(66.7.0%) were cohabiting with their partners while 2(16.7%) were single. The adolescent mothers had good attitude towards infant vaccination as seen in their confidence in vaccine efficiency, priority given to vaccination and belief in the secondary benefits of vaccination. They also enjoyed tremendous support from their social circles and had a positive social norm for vaccination. These mothers also had good self-efficacy through their strong personal agency and efficiency in navigating the vaccination processes for their infants.
CONCLUSION: The optimal vaccination of the infants of the adolescent mothers was the result of their good attitude towards infant vaccination, strong social support and high self-efficacy in navigating vaccination processes. Replicating these factors among other adolescent mothers may promote optimal vaccination of their infants.

articles.title: EFFECT OF A GROUP OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY INTERVENTION ON DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, LEVEL OF OCCUPATIONAL PARTICIPATION AND FUNCTIONING AMONG IN-SCHOOL ADOLESCENTS IN ABEOKUTA, NIGERIA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Impairment in occupational participation and functioning can negatively affect adolescents' activities of daily living, academic performance, self-care, sleep, leisure, and mood.
AIM: This study examined the effects of a structured occupational therapy intervention on mood, occupational functioning, and social participation among in-school adolescents with depressive symptoms.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A two-stage design was employed, comprising a crosssectional survey followed by a one-group pre?post intervention study. In the first stage, 345 students from four schools completed the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI). Ten students with scores of 18 and above were recruited into the intervention phase and completed the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire (SMFQ), and Wellness and Life Satisfaction Questionnaire. A five-week manualised occupational therapy programme was delivered, and complete pre?post data from ten participants were analysed.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 14.9 ± 1.2 years, and 26.1% scored within the significant depressive symptom range. Females reported higher depressive symptoms than males (p = 0.02) and the mean BDI score for the screened sample was 11.61 (SD = 10.23). Post-intervention analysis showed significant reductions in depressive symptoms and improvements in occupational functioning and social participation, with large effect sizes.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that school-based occupational therapy interventions are feasible and may improve functional and emotional outcomes among adolescents with depressive symptoms.

articles.title: Association between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and infantile vascular anomalies in the Collaborative Perinatal Project.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) affect 10%-22% of pregnancies globally and are characterized by vascular dysfunction. Yet, their influence on fetal vascular development remains incompletely understood. Port-wine stains (PWS) and infantile hemangiomas (IH) provide a compelling model for investigating this gap. As the most common vascular anomalies of infancy, affecting 0.3%-0.5% and an estimated 1.5%-4.4% of infants, respectively, their clinical manifestations appear at or within weeks of birth, minimizing the latency between intrauterine exposure and outcome. PWS are congenital vascular malformations appearing at birth as red-to-purple birthmarks most commonly on the face and neck, while IH are raised, bright-red postnatal vascular tumors emerging in the first weeks of life on the face, scalp, and trunk. Both cause significant cosmetic and functional morbidity when located on the face or airways, and PWS may additionally signal underlying neurological involvement. Using data from the Collaborative Perinatal Project (1959-1966), a prospective cohort of 59 391 pregnancies across 12 US centers, we examined whether HDP are associated with PWS and IH. HDP were classified into five categories (normotensive [reference], chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia/eclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia/eclampsia). PWS and IH were ascertained through standardized physician examinations through the first year of life. We estimated adjusted relative risks (aRR) using log-binomial generalized estimating equations with inverse probability weighting for selection bias and propensity score weighting for confounding. Among 59 391 pregnancies, 312 (0.5%) developed PWS and 797 (1.3%) developed IH. Superimposed preeclampsia/eclampsia was associated with PWS (aRR, 2.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-6.75). No HDP type was associated with IH.

articles.title: Measuring maternal mortality and mortality disparities: a health-adjusted approach.
articles.abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities in maternal mortality are well known, especially the higher rates for Black and Native American women. However, the underlying causes remain unclear. These disparities may stem from disparities in background health across groups or from factors specific to childbirth and maternal care. We examine maternal mortality disparities using a novel method that controls for population differences in overall health. Unadjusted maternal mortality rate (MMR) ratios for Black, Asian, Hispanic, and Native American women relative to White women, measured over 2010-2022, excluding COVID-19 deaths, are 2.7, 0.91, 0.88, and 2.58. In contrast, adjusted ratios are 1.83, 1.31, 1.27, and 1.24, respectively. Poor background health contributes to the high maternal mortality risk among Black and Native American women, while better underlying health among Asian and Hispanic women masks their elevated adjusted maternal mortality risk. We also document substantial cross-state heterogeneity in adjusted MMRs and racial/ethnic disparities in these rates. In some states, minority women face substantially higher maternal mortality risks relative to White women, while in others-notably California-health-adjusted disparities are small.

articles.title: The contemporary and historical burden of arrhythmias in patients with congenital heart disease.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmias constitute a significant concern in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) but temporal trends remain unknown.
AIMS: To describe the burden of arrhythmias and dissect the impact of era of birth, lesion complexity, and age in both children and adults with CHD born in Sweden.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In a population-based cohort study, patients diagnosed with CHD (n = 63 431) born in 1970-2017 were identified in the Swedish National Patient Register. Each patient was matched by age and sex with 10 control subjects (n = 583 100) from the general population. Fine-Gray competing risk and Cox proportional-hazards regression were used; risk estimates were compared with matched controls. During median follow-up of 19 years (total range: 0-53 years), 1895 new events of supraventricular arrhythmias were registered, yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 8.0 [95% confidence interval (CI) 7.6-8.5], along with 371 new ventricular arrhythmias (HR 13.0; 95% CI 11.2-15.2). Complex CHD was associated with higher risk, irrespective of type, than non-complex CHD, and patients born in 1990 or later displayed lower risk for both supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, irrespective of age and CHD complexity, than those born before 1990. Patients aged 18-39 years with non-complex and complex CHD born before 1990 displayed HRs of 6.9 (95% CI 6.1-7.8) and 23.9 (95% CI 19.4-29.5) for supraventricular arrhythmias, respectively, versus 3.2 (95% CI 2.7-3.9) and 13.9 (95% CI 9.8-19.7) in those born in 1990 or later.
CONCLUSIONS: The risk of arrhythmias was generally high across the CHD population and increased with increasing age and lesion complexity. Importantly, patients born in 1990 or later demonstrated lower risk for both supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias than those born before 1990.

articles.title: Can self- or caregiver-administered nasal spray influenza vaccination improve outcomes? An agent-based model using the framework for reconstructing epidemiological dynamics.
articles.abstract: Newly licensed self- or caregiver-administered nasal spray live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV), available to order for home delivery, may improve vaccination coverage (VC) among adults aged 18-49 overall, as well as among those in this age group who live in households with school-aged children. Using the agent-based Framework for Reproducing Epidemiological Dynamics, which simulates influenza transmission in US census-based populations with defined household structures, we modeled the impact of: (1) 5%-15% VC increase among those aged 18-49 through self-administration and (2) household-based strategies for ages 5-17 and 18-49 that may occur from home LAIV orders. The household strategies included vaccinating children aged 5-17, followed by their 18-49-year-old head of household (HH) (kids + HH), and vaccinating children aged 5-17 and all household adults aged 18-49 (kids + adults). A 5%-15% VC increase in adults aged 18-49 reduced symptomatic cases in all adults by up to 10%. Among household strategies, kids + adults yielded a higher VC increase (9.2%) and greater reduction in symptomatic cases (5.7%) among adults ≥18 than the kids + HH strategy. The convenience of self-administration and household-based LAIV strategies in homes with school-age children may enhance adult VC and reduce influenza burden.

articles.title: A case of the Mondays? Pollution exposure and delayed care in pediatric asthma hospitalizations.
articles.abstract: Pediatric asthma remains a leading cause of preventable hospitalizations in the United States, with environmental triggers such as fine particulate matter (PM2.5) playing a key role. However, hospitalization timing reflects not only biological exacerbations but also healthcare access and care-seeking behavior. The "Monday effect," marked by higher early-week admissions, raises questions about whether short-term pollution drives asthma morbidity or whether access-related delays influence when exacerbations are observed. We analyzed more than 4.5 million ZIP code-level daily observations from Illinois Medicaid (2012-2021), linking asthma hospitalizations with PM2.5 and meteorological data. Fixed-effects logistic regression models estimated associations between short-lag PM2.5 exposure and hospitalization probability, with day of week modeled as both a covariate and an effect modifier. Short-lag PM2.5 exposure (0-1 day moving average) was associated with increased hospitalization probability on Mondays but not on other weekdays. PM2.5 concentrations were higher on weekends, while asthma hospitalizations peaked early in the week. With longer exposure windows, weekday-specific associations were attenuated and pollution effects were suppressed on weekends. These findings suggest that short-term PM2.5 effects on asthma hospitalizations reflect both environmental risk and healthcare access, underscoring the importance of accounting for care-seeking patterns in environmental health research.

articles.title: Current Status of Communication Activities to Raise Awareness on Antimicrobial Resistance and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: An accurate understanding of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is essential for its prevention, and for the development of this understanding, sustained, systematic communication and education are needed. This report reviews the recommendations from World Health Organization (WHO) on AMR awareness and education, examines related activities in the Republic of Korea (ROK), and proposes future directions for the promotion of behavioral change.
METHODS: WHO recommendations were reviewed. Major AMR awareness and educational activities in the ROK were summarized, including public communications, education for children and adolescents, education and training for healthcare professionals, and inter-ministerial collaboration.
RESULTS: WHO emphasizes evidence-based, audience-specific communication; diverse approaches to media; education and training for students and professionals; and continuous evaluation to develop awareness into behavioral change. In the ROK, communication materials for the public and healthcare professionals have been disseminated through various channels, particularly during the World AMR Awareness Week (November 18-24). Further, educational materials and parent newsletters tailored to different school levels have also been developed and distributed. In 2026, preparations have begun for joint inter-ministerial communication and pilot school-based education and awareness campaigns.
CONCLUSIONS: AMR awareness activities should go beyond information dissemination and toward behavioral change. Future efforts should strengthen audience-tailored communication and education, connect communication channels across ministries and organizations, as well as improve applied strategies through continuous evaluation and feedback.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes and Predictors of Mortality Among Preterm Neonates in a Tertiary Care Neonatal Unit: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth remains a major contributor to neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries. This retrospective study evaluated clinical outcomes and predictors of mortality among preterm neonates admitted to a tertiary-care neonatal intensive care unit. Data from 153 preterm neonates were analyzed for maternal characteristics, neonatal profiles, morbidities, management, and outcomes. Respiratory distress was present in 95.4% of neonates, predominantly due to respiratory distress syndrome. Sepsis occurred in 65.4%, with gram-negative organisms being the most common pathogens. Overall survival was 85.6%. On univariate analysis, lower gestational age, extremely low birth weight, surfactant use, positive pressure ventilation, and septic shock were associated with mortality. Multivariate logistic regression identified the requirement for positive pressure ventilation as the strongest independent predictor of mortality. These findings highlight the central role of severe respiratory failure in determining outcomes among preterm neonates and underscore the need for improved antenatal care and strengthened infection-control strategies.

articles.title: From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Sleep disorders are among the most common but frequently underestimated comorbidities in patients with epilepsy, with major manifestations including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness, restless legs syndrome, and periodic limb movements of sleep. A complex bidirectional interaction exists between epilepsy and sleep disorders: sleep deprivation, disrupted sleep architecture, and sleep-disordered breathing may increase seizure susceptibility, whereas nocturnal seizures, interictal epileptiform discharges, antiseizure medications, and mood comorbidities may further impair sleep continuity and daytime alertness. Although mechanistic links and individual sleep disorders have received increasing attention, a practical outpatient pathway that connects sleep-related complaints with screening, phenotype recognition, objective testing, and subsequent intervention remains insufficiently defined. From a clinical phenotyping perspective, this review proposes a complaint-based framework for the identification, tiered assessment, and integrated management of sleep comorbidities in epilepsy. The framework translates common sleep complaints into major actionable phenotypes, including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements of sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes, while incorporating life-course and syndrome-specific considerations for children and adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults, patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, and older adults with epilepsy. This review organizes dispersed evidence on sleep and epilepsy into a clinically oriented conceptual framework linking complaint-based entry, tiered assessment, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment. The framework is intended to facilitate recognition and structured clinical reasoning, while its feasibility and effects on patient outcomes require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Frequency of Readmission of Pediatric Patients With Respiratory Diseases in the PIMS Hospital of Pakistan: A Study of Cause and Effect.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital readmission with respiratory diseases among pediatric population remains the leading concern for healthcare services due to their increased morbidity, burden on healthcare and resource utilization. Understanding the factors related to readmission may help improve outcomes and lessen preventable hospitalization. This study was conducted to determine the rate of rehospitalization among pediatric population and to identify the risk factors for hospital readmission.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study of pediatric patients with respiratory diseases was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan from 1st January 2024 to 31st December 2024. Data was collected from a medical record through a structured proforma. Variables like age, gender, diagnosis, severity of disease, previous hospitalization, compliance to treatment, and length of stay in hospital were analyzed. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS 27 version.
RESULTS: During the study period, there were 2123 pediatric admissions among which 583 admissions were related to respiratory diseases. In the duration of one month (30-days), the readmission rate in total pediatric admissions was 6.92%. Readmissions were significantly associated with younger age, compliance to the treatment, disease severity, and previous hospitalization. Among respiratory diseases, bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and asthma were significantly associated with readmission.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric respiratory readmissions were significantly associated with younger age, disease severity, poor treatment compliance, and previous hospitalization.

articles.title: Nutritional Therapy in Malnourished Children With Cancer: Response Among Hospitalized Children in Northern Tanzania.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malnutrition significantly compromises treatment tolerance and outcomes in children with cancer. Although nutritional therapy has been incorporated into pediatric oncology care, its effectiveness remains unevaluated. This study assessed the effectiveness of nutritional therapy and predictors of poor response among malnourished children diagnosed with cancer in Northern Tanzania.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among children aged 6 months to 18 years diagnosed with cancer from January 2023 to December 2024 at a zonal referral hospital in Northern Tanzania. Children receiving palliative care were excluded. Nutritional therapy was initiated among children with acute malnutrition. At 6 months, nutritional response was determined by comparing changes in mean WHO z-scores and by assessing differences across cancer types using the independent t-test. A good response to therapy was defined as a WHO z-score > -2 SD at six months, while a poor response was defined as a WHO z-score ≤ -2 SD.
RESULTS: Of 190 children diagnosed with cancer, 117 had acute malnutrition. Among these, 77 completed six months of follow-up, 37 died, and 3 were referred out. Nutritional therapy significantly improved mean WHO z-scores by 2.347 (p<0.001). Predictors of poor response included age below five years (AHR: 1.99, 95% CI: 1.05-5.46), combined chemotherapy and surgery (AHR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.09-1.99), and neuroblastoma diagnosis (AHR: 1.47, 95% CI: 1.10-2.43).
CONCLUSION: Nutritional therapy significantly improved the nutritional status of malnourished children with cancer. Better response was observed among children older than five years, while poor response was associated with solid tumors and combined chemotherapy with surgery.

articles.title: Survival Status and Predictors of Mortality among Neonates with Birth Asphyxia Admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Units at public hospitals in the Central Zone of Tigray, Ethiopia in 2024, a Post-war Crisis: A Prospective Follow-Up Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine survival time and predictors of mortality among neonates with birth asphyxia admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Units at public hospitals in Central Zone of Tigray, Ethiopia, in 2024.
METHODS: A prospective follow-up study was conducted among 220 neonates with birth asphyxia from February 20 to June 30, 2024. Participants were selected using systematic sampling. Data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed. Adjusted hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals were used to identify predictors.
RESULTS: Over 2,299 neonate-days, 25.9% (95% CI, 20.5%-32.1%) of neonates died, incidence rate of 24.7 per 1,000 neonate-days and a restricted mean survival time of 20 days. Low birth weight (AHR = 2.86), blue staining (AHR = 2.71), mild-to-moderate asphyxia (AHR = 2.40), severe asphyxia (AHR = 3.17) were predictors of death.
CONCLUSION: Early identification and management of neonates with asphyxia may substantially improve overall survival.

articles.title: Machine Learning in Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome: From Early Warning to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), driven by pulmonary surfactant deficiency in preterm infants, is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. This narrative review synthesises machine learning (ML) applications across the NRDS spectrum-from prenatal risk stratification to long-term complication prediction-appraised against the TRIPOD+AI (2024) framework. Reported discrimination is high but heterogeneous (AUC 0.78-0.99); the most robust estimate is the prospective Korean Neonatal Network study of 13,087 very-low-birthweight infants across 76 hospitals (full-model AUROC 0.9187; testing 0.9216). Ensemble methods and deep-learning architectures tend to outperform logistic regression, often by modest margins. Emerging modalities-lung-ultrasound radiomics, cry-signal analysis (∼95% accuracy, controlled datasets), and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy-remain research-stage. Reporting deficits are near-universal: <20% report calibration, none conduct prospective fairness audits, <15% release code. Clinical translation requires federated-learning consortia, explainable AI, prospective external validation, and structured implementation science.

articles.title: The Effectiveness of Parent Educational Program on Knowledge and Caregiving Performance for Children With Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease is the most common type of congenital defect.
OBJECTIVES: This research was conducted with the aim of the effectiveness of parent educational Program on knowledge and caregiving performance for children with congenital heart disease.
DESIGN: This clinical trial study was conducted on 86 parents who have children with congenital heart disease. The samples were randomly divided into two intervention (43 people) and control (43 people) groups using a permutation block design.
METHODS: The data were collected using a demographic information questionnaire, a knowledge assessment questionnaire, and a caregiving performance assessment questionnaire. The collected data were analyzed with SPSS22 software and using paired t-test, independent t-test, chi-square, and covariance analysis.
RESULTS: The findings of the research indicated that after teaching the intervention group, the average parents care knowledge increased significantly compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Also, there was a statistically significant difference between the average parent Caregiving performance in the intervention group compared to the control group (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Based on the results of this study, the implementation of the educational program is a suitable method to increase the level of knowledge and parent Caregiving performance for children with congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Sociodemographic Correlates Among Children with Chronic Kidney Disease Attending a Nephrology Clinic in the UAE: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe health-related quality of life and examine sociodemographic correlates among children with CKD attending a nephrology clinic.
METHODS: This study included 92 children aged 8-12 years recruited from a nephrology outpatient clinic. Children completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory Version 4.0 Short Form.
RESULTS: Mean (SD) scores were 38.53 (10.39) for total HRQoL, 35.76 (13.05) for physical functioning, 40.08 (15.97) for emotional functioning, 42.84 (21.02) for social functioning, 36.78 (21.30) for school functioning, and 39.92 (13.39) for psychosocial health. Domain scores differed modestly, F(2.705, 246.140)=3.478, p=.020, partial eta squared=.037. Only the physical-social comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction (mean difference=-7.08, 95% CI -11.85 to -2.32; adjusted p=.024). The regression model was not significant, F(7,84)=0.547, p=.796, R squared=.044; no individual predictor was associated with total HRQoL.
CONCLUSION: Participants reported low mean HRQoL scores, with small within-child differences across domains and no identified sociodemographic correlate.

articles.title: Mortality and Its Predictors Among Preterm Neonates in a Conflict-Affected Low-Resource Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study From Syria.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is a major contributor to neonatal morbidity and mortality, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings. This retrospective cohort study assessed mortality and associated factors among preterm neonates admitted to a tertiary neonatal unit in Damascus, Syria, between January 2022 and December 2023. Data were extracted from medical records using a standardized data collection form, and CRIB II scores were calculated retrospectively. Of 480 records reviewed, 330 neonates were included after exclusion of 150 records. Among them, 208 died (63.0%), with a mean time to death of 10.2 days. Higher CRIB II scores (HR 1.093, p=0.017), respiratory distress (HR 2.4, 95% CI 1.8-3.1; p<0.001), and hyaline membrane disease (HR 1.79, p<0.001) were associated with increased mortality. Maternal parity of five or more was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.559, p=0.026). Mortality was high, highlighting challenges in conflict-affected, resource-constrained neonatal care. CRIB II may support early risk stratification.

articles.title: Management Practices and Clinical Profiles of Pediatric Pneumonia in a Tertiary Referral Setting in Ethiopia: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumonia remains a major cause of hospitalization among children in Ethiopia.
OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical characteristics, treatment practices, and outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional chart review was conducted between November 2023 and March 2024 (n=207). Descriptive and exploratory regression analyses were used.
RESULTS: Severe pneumonia accounted for 93.7% of cases, with community-acquired pneumonia predominating. Ceftriaxone was the most frequently used antibiotic (32.2%), while paracetamol was the most commonly administered supportive medication (84.8%). More than half of patients (55.1%) were hospitalized for 1-2 weeks. A history of pneumonia, comorbidity, recurrent respiratory illness, and acute malnutrition were associated with prolonged hospitalization. Blood culture testing was performed in only seven patients. Overall, 92.8% of patients recovered or improved, while 7.2% experienced poor outcomes. Regression findings were interpreted as exploratory given the small number of poor-outcome events.
CONCLUSION: Severe pneumonia was common, with substantial use of broad-spectrum antibiotics and limited microbiological investigation.

articles.title: Trends in Neonatal Disorder Burden in Afghanistan, 1990-2023: A Global Burden of Disease 2023 Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal disorders remain a major cause of preventable child mortality and health loss, particularly in fragile health systems. We assessed trends in neonatal disorder burden in Afghanistan from 1990 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive secondary analysis of GBD 2023 data for neonates aged <28 days, with analyses for early (0-6 days) and late (7-27 days) neonatal periods. Outcomes included deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), years of life lost (YLLs), years lived with disability (YLDs), prevalence, and incidence. We reported numbers, GBD-reported rates, 95% uncertainty intervals, subcause contributions, sex differences, and endpoint percentage changes.
RESULTS: In 2023, neonatal disorders accounted for an estimated 19,469 deaths and 1,752,536 DALYs in Afghanistan. YLLs comprised approximately 99.95% of DALYs, indicating an overwhelmingly mortality-driven burden. From 1990 to 2023, GBD-reported death and DALY rates each declined by 42.3%, whereas absolute deaths and DALYs increased by 76.8%. Neonatal encephalopathy due to birth asphyxia and trauma was the leading subcause, contributing 44.5% of deaths and DALYs. In 2023, 77.8% of neonatal disorder deaths occurred during days 0-6, and male neonates had higher death and DALY rates than females.
CONCLUSIONS: Afghanistan experienced substantial declines in neonatal disorders, but the absolute burden remained high and was dominated by premature mortality. The concentration of deaths in the first week and the dominance of birth asphyxia/trauma highlight priorities for skilled delivery care, emergency obstetric and newborn care, neonatal resuscitation, timely referral, infection management, and care for small and sick newborns.

articles.title: Beyond just survival: updates on adult congenital heart disease care.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
articles.abstract: Survival into adulthood is now the norm for individuals born with congenital heart disease, with over 90% of children reaching adult life. Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity. In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains: lifelong care models, diagnostic techniques, management strategies, genetic and precision medicine, and machine learning. We highlight the pivotal role of specialized, multidisciplinary care in improving outcomes, and the need for structured transition programmes to ensure continuity from paediatric to adult services. Emerging priorities include reproductive counselling, exercise prescription, and psychosocial support. Advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, electrophysiological mapping, and four-dimensional flow imaging now offer unprecedented anatomical and haemodynamic insights. Recent trials have demonstrated encouraging results for novel heart failure therapies and pulmonary vasodilators in lesion-specific subgroups, while transcatheter technologies continue to expand therapeutic options for patients with complex anatomy. Genetic testing and machine learning are beginning to reshape risk stratification and workflow efficiency, though challenges remain in their implementation. As this population ages and acquires new comorbidities, care models must evolve to move beyond just survival, but towards improving quality of life, preserving organ function, and anticipating future needs. This review aims to support clinicians and researchers in meeting these challenges and advancing the next era of ACHD care.
